product_title: Razor E300 Electric Scooter
review_headline: Razor creates a practical, kid friendly package
review_body: Razor creates a practical kid friendly package which combines ease of use, safety, and reliability. I have driven my e300 scooter over 1,000 miles in the last two years. I can truthfully state that this scooter has never treated me wrong. But there are some minor gripes I have about this scooter. The ride is very stiff, partly because of a strong steal structure and hard tires. Deflating these tires doesn't make the ride softer it only slightly numbs the ride and gives the normally stiff ride a rubbery jiggle. Unfortunately even with deflated tires hard impacts still come through and handling is compromised and feels as if you are skidding when you are not, which will diminish confidence in some riders. Braking is marginal at best and lock up is extremely common and in emergency situations it doesn't inspire any confidence. Due to these braking short comings your rear tire will probably only last about 200 miles before it blows out. However there are many great things too. This is a zippy way to get around town and is built like nails. After over 1,000 miles I have had the batteries replaced once free of charge under warranty. The battery reset switch and the rear tire. Battery life is good at about 7 miles on flat land and the motor may make a lot of noise but has hardly aged because it still goes 15 mph for me. I can say this scooter has been through snow sand rain and has gone on mountain bike trails, and has done it with flying colors. I have only fallen off the scooter once. It was on dry pavement and I just skidded in a turn on some sand. This is a really good Christmas present for someone in 6th or 7th grade

product_title: Xtreme Bright Escape Tool Light, Multi-tool LED Flashlight with 12 Tools Including Glass Breaker & Seatbelt Cutter
review_headline: I Wish That I Could Give It 10 Stars!
review_body: I wish that I could give the Emergency Automotive Escape Tool from Xtreme Bright 10 Stars!  I am so impressed by how many tools they have included all in one product.  I say I am impressed, but not surprised. I have other products from Xtreme Bright and in my experience I have only ever received quality, impressive products from them.  The box that the flashlight comes in also has a picture diagram to illustrate all of it's features. They've included so many that  I wasn't completely familiar with each of the features and actually had to read up on a few to understand how they worked. You will need to put in 3 AAA batteries for the flashlight and it's pretty much a matter of unscrewing the top half and inserting them into the chamber.  The flashlight has 3 settings including a regular full brightness, a reduced brightness and a flashing mode (blue emergency beacon) mode.  The light is also "zoomable" up to 2000X as well. 2 awesome car escape features are the seat belt Cutter (the blade is set way into the body of the flashlight so as not to accidentally cut anything and it is designed so that you could easily fit and slide your seat belt into the slot) and the second one is a window glass hammer.  The glass hammer pops out when you push down and unlock the release button.  On the end there are additional features which pull out and include an ice pick, screwdrivers, knife, scissors and bottle opener. The body of the flashlight and all the attached tools are definitely quality made, you can just feel it when you hold it and work with all the tools.  Although I anticipate that this product will be very durable it does also come with an unconditional lifetime guarantee as well.  I will be putting this in my oldest son's car.  He recently started a job that involves a lot of traveling in his car.  I will feel a lot better knowing that this flashlight with all it's useful tools is in his glove compartment.  I really truly love this multi-purpose flashlight!  I think I will also be getting one for the other cars that we own as well.  I was grateful that I received this product at a discounted price during a promotion in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

product_title: Coleman Woodsman II Chair
review_body:
I am not sure how this one got so many decent reviews. Usually reviews on Amazon are a bit more helpful as far as avoiding disappointing products goes. Oh well. Here are some of the things that make this chair a failure. This may be the first one star review I have ever given.

1. I am a normal sized person and my rear end barely fits on the butt part. The positive is that it fit my skinny 6 year old kid's butt perfectly.
2. The most disappointing part of this chair is that the back rest part is useless. If one were to rest their back on it they would be resting so far back as to end up resting their entire body on the floor. Ouch! In other words, not only will it not support an adult, it is too far back to be of any use anyway. You mine as well get a stool. Many reviews mention adding pieces and parts jammed places to get the back rest part to be useful. Nobody should have to rig a chair to make it work.
3. This thing weighs nothing at all. It is possibly the lightest chair I have ever owned for camping. But wait! That's a positive right? Well, think about it for a few moments BEFORE you sit on it. There comes a point when a chair is so light that it doesn't feel stable and isn't comfortable and that was on a level surface in my home. Not while camping in the soft dirt on an angle in front of a roaring fire.
4. This chair is not comfortable. My 6 year old kid sat on it and then went to get two couch pillows. She put one pillow on the seat and one on the back and THEN she said that the chair was comfortable right before the pillows slipped off and we all laughed. That was fun. I guess that's a positive.

So are there any positives to mention? The color is nice for camping.

product_title: Allen Sports Premier Hitch Mounted 4-Bike Carrier
review_body:
I bought this bike carrier for our family vacation. I needed to carry two adult bikes and one child bike. This carrier fit my needs well.

When I was shopping for a carrier, I was shocked by the price of some of these. They are a bike carrier, not a nuclear contraption. Thule was mad expensive and I honestly do not feel that any of those high end carriers are justified in their costs. I bought this for $158.64 Prime and thought that this was a little on the expensive side for me...now I see this selling for $200.35(including shipping) I realize that I got a deal on this.

I was a little concerned when I first purchased this because the box had a whole in it and part of the rack was protruding from the product box. When I opened the box, I realized I had nothing to worry about. There was nothing wrong with the carrier.

Assembling this couldn't have been easier...three bolts, one plastic cover, and finished. Attaching this to your vehicle was one more bolt, which is necessary to prevent it from wobbling.

This carrier is well made and easy to use. Squeeze the back of the neck, it will raise the bar holding the bikes. Lift the red lever, and the entire carrier tilts away from the back of your vehicle. This is extremely helpful when you realized you need to get something out of the back of your vehicle and your bikes are already loaded.

I like that this has rubber straps, not velcro holding my bikes on the carrier. It puts me at ease when I have a long drive carrying my bikes. This carrier has a nice little feature...not sure if it was intended to be used that way, but it was certainly useful. There is a spot on the carrier that you can use a bike lock to lock your bikes on the carrier. It is useful as added security just in case the straps are to fail. It is also nice to know I can leave the vehicle for a little bit and not worry about the bikes being stolen.

There are two issues I've had with this carrier. The first issue I had was you should be able to use a hitch lock on these carriers, so you do not have to worry about your entire carrier, bike and all, disappearing. The second problem I've had with this was putting a child's bike on this. With two adult bikes, it was almost impossible to get the child bike on. It worries me that adding a bike for my daughter would never work with this carrier.

After using this on vacation, I did see someone carrying a child bike upside down on their carrier. It seemed to work well, so I will have to give it a try next time I need the carrier.

review_headline: Great little light for the cheapest price in the world (just don't expect miracles or to last forever)
review_body:
I give this a 4 star rating, NOT for the quality, but for the price and it's ability to handle the 14500 batteries (3.7 volt AA). The price can't be beaten. It's that simple. Buy several to have kickin around your house, vehicles, hunting or hiking. Chances are, out of a half dozen, 1 or 2 won't last a year (or maybe even 6 months). Very small and extremely portable. Note: go with the Nitecore 14500 batteries, NOT the UltraFire (they're crap and have a very short life span).

Can't give it the 5th star, because some of the Chinese components are cheaply made and inferior quality. I've had 2 of these lights die on me within a few months. Now obviously, if they produced a higher quality light, the price would increase. So, there is your trade-off. I've also bought a couple J5 brand lights and those ARE of a higher quality and haven't died on me yet. But, they're also twice the price.

You decide.

review_body: The order arrived a bit early, that's OK, a pleasant surprise, but the contents weren't what was shown! Which would you rather have attached to your rod?  At any rate, shortly after we expressed these concerns, we received a message from the seller.  They apologized for the mixup, and offered either to accept the returned "Yomores" and credit our account, or to take 1/2 of the purchase price off the bill, and allow us to keep both reels. product_title: Full Nylon Pack Cloth Lobster Bags with Coated Handle and Mesh Bottom (for Drain), 2 popular sizes and optionable D-ring
review_headline: this is probably the best bag there is
review_body:
i don't remember where i ended up getting this bag, i think it was given to me at some point. it's an older version, no coated handle, otherwise looks identical. luckily, this is probably the best bag there is. if you try enough bags, eventually you'll realize that mesh is the WORST thing to have in a lobster bag. it does nothing but tangle them up. they get stuck in there and it makes loading it up and unloading terribly difficult. with this, they slide in and out of the bag. every now and then their feet will poke through the mesh at the bottom, but that doesn't hinder anything. i never really kept count, but i've had about 15 lobster in mine at once. and i had more room, just got heavy. with that many i'd definitely recommend supporting it from the bottom as well, not just the handle. something might tear.

only negative i have is inherent in the materials used, but is also a positive at the same time. since the nylon acts like a sail in the water, sometimes moving directions you don't want it to, or acting a bit like a drift anchor. definitely creates decent amount of drag. the positive side of that is that you can open the bag quite easily by cracking it open so the water flows in and it'll inflate the bag making it very easy to load it without getting caught on stuff.

and a separate note, inspect the mesh as the bag wears down. i had a small tear in the corner and lost two lobster before noticing, and was only able to recapture one of them. easy to fix with a zip tie, but just keep an eye on that. the nylon is way more durable than the mesh and you may forget that even though the bag looks new, the mesh could be wearing out.

product_title: Outdoor Research Women's Helium II Jacket
review_headline: Amazingly Compact Jacket that is still Waterproof and Breathable
review_body:
We've been using the Patagonia Houdini Jacket for emergencies. It's the smallest jacket I had ever found and it worked in a pinch. But I found out the hard way that when they described it as "water resistant," that meant water resistant for about 5 minutes of rain. The jacket works great for other things, but waterproof it is not. So I've been searching for a waterPROOF jacket that is as small as possible to keep in my purse for emergencies. I'm so glad I found this jacket. I came upon this jacket when reading reviews on an outdoor gear site. Listed as one of the best women's waterproof jackets, I found that it's small size and light weight (Houdini Jacket weighs in at 3.6 oz, this weighs in at 5.5 oz) make it the perfect jacket in a pinch. Actually, it's the perfect raincoat when not in a pinch.

I also had the opportunity, if you will, to try this out in a rainstorm. We were walking down the street watching the rain across the bay. Within five minutes, the storm had formed above us and the rain started pelting down. We had our jackets clipped to our shorts and pulled them on. The jacket worked perfectly: I stayed dry. They did not, however, protect us from the lightning.

If you are considering this jacket, consider it carefully. They have pared it down as much as possible to save on space and weight and it will not have all the bells and whistles that a heavier jacket would have. It has a very specific purpose and that purpose is to be as waterproof and breathable as possible in as little space as possible. They took out hand pockets and there are no velcro straps at the wrists. It's also shorter than the average rain coat. My arms did get wet because I was messing with my hood when it started raining. On the other hand, they have a way to tighten the hood down, and that was a really great feature. The hood fit really well. It fit better than the hood on my Patagonia Supercell jacket and I could easily see my surroundings when it was on.

I should also add that I was having a tough time deciding on the fit. I called Outdoor Research and was connected to a customer service representative within a few touch-tone selections. He was incredibly helpful. For anyone wondering, it appears there's a one inch difference in the length of each jacket as it goes up in size. There's a one inch difference in the length of the sleeves and a two inch difference in the girth. I ordered both a small and medium. The medium was too large, but I found the small very close to being smaller than I'd like. The sleeves were a tad shorter than my preference and I found the length to be wanting. But I eventually tried the small on with my North Face Thunder down coat and it fit under the jacket fairly easily. Even though I won't likely be layering a down coat under this small a rain coat, I figured I didn't need it any larger than that size, so I went with the small. For reference, I am 5'7" and weigh around 130/135. 32B/34A chest. Most of my weight is in my hips. So I am a smaller person up top, but my height, just above average, makes it tough to find jackets that are smaller with the right length and arm length. In this case, I chose getting the one that fit better around my torso over getting one that was the right length. I also compared it to my Houdini jacket, which I own in the Medium. The Outdoor Research Helium II in SMALL was just about the same size overall - in every measurement - as the Patagonia Houdini in MEDIUM. It was also very similar in size to the Patagonia Supercell in SMALL, except the supercell is much longer, which made it harder to compare. Outdoor Research calls this the "standard fit," so think that it will be a little bit on the larger side. Also, I found that like most jacket companies, I wouldn't have minded a slightly smaller waist and slightly larger hips but it was actually a really great fit considering I don't have the average female body shape.

In all:
PROs:
-Stores in its own pocket - super small
-very lightweight
-waterproof
-breathable
-great for keeping in a purse or backpack. Great for a trip where you aren't sure about the weather

CONs:
-does not protect from lightning ;)
-does not have any bells and whistles. (If you are looking for hand pockets, wrist velcro, neck reinforcement, etc., this is not your jacket. Don't complain that it doesn't have all the bells and whistles - that's not the point. The point is to be as small as possible while remaining waterproof and breathable.)
-sizing can be a bit awkward, you may want two sizes to choose from

product_title: Nitecore MT10A Tactical Flashlight by IMR 14500 Battery UM10 Charger EASTSHINE Wall Adaptger Battery Box
review_headline: Incredibly versatile, compact, and powerful flashlight....4.5 stars....
review_body:
Summary: Super powerful flashlight requires special, but not hard to find batteries - top buttons for mode changing make it much easier to use. Overall I'd rate it 4.5 Stars...rounded to 5

Here's the deal - if you really want a super small and super powerful flashlight these days, you have to go with lithium batteries - no 2 ways about it. Most of the more powerful lights use what's called an 18650 - it's a laptop battery and at 18 mm in diameter and 65 mm long, it's not that small. However, there exists the 14500 which is, not suprisingly, 14mm diameter by 50 mm long and it's nearly the exact same size as a AA battery. They typically hold only 700-800 mAh, but it's at 3.7 volts instead of 1.2-1.5. With the 14500, you can put out a stunning amount of light with something you can easily fit in your hand.

The 14500 does require a special charger - this set includes a charger which works off a wall plug, a car plug, or even from your computer. This kit comes only with 1, but I've got a bunch of the Ultracell brand - just search on Amazon for 14500 battery and you can find them at a reasonable price for extras.

Enough about the batteries and the charger - this flashlight is really top notch. It has an antireflective lens. It has 3 strobe settings (fast, SOS, emergency beacon) It has a red LED for maintaining your night vision and not waking everyone up in a tent or darkened room. It has a great beam pattern - a broad beam with diffused central spot, giving a very usable light that throws a good beam about ~100 feet when on Turbo. It's not super focused, so after perhaps 120 feet or so the lighting drops off pretty fast, but for something you can easily fit in your pocket, it's astounding..

Is it bright? Unbelievably so. While a lot of the flashlights will CLAIM to have 1000 lumens or more, many are simply lying or exaggerating. For example, the CREE specifications for the XM-L2 U2 claim it can deliver a maxiumum of 1052 lumens, under ideal conditions which you can really only meet with a cooled heat sink the size of a dinner plate, but many less reputable vendors will say they are getting 1200 lumens or more from this. The FL-1 standard 920 lumens from this flashlight is a claim I would fully believe. The flashlight gets very warm, and will automatically switch to a lower power after about 3 minutes.

Sorry to repeat, but the user interface is really handy and quite intuitive and the flashlight remembers the prior setting. It even tells you what voltage your battery is at - a pretty slick feature!

So why not 5 stars?
The first complaint I have is that the pocket clip isn't nearly as stiff as I would like. I ended up removing it to re-bend so it didn't wobble as much. Even then, it isn't enough that I'd really trust it to keep the light from falling off - just enough to keep it at the top of a pocket.

The second complaint is that the tail switch stands slightly taller than the shoulders, making the tail stand, even on a hard, flat surface, precarious. That's really unfortunate. Bouncing a light off the ceiling is the fastest, easiest way to get general illumination in a dark room.

product_title: Coleman Fold N Go Portable Grill
review_body:
I bought this because it's getting expensive to use charcoal to cook a simple meal for one person. I wanted something portable, easy to use, and reliable. This grill seems to fit the bill perfectly.

Assembly is easy but here are some tips. Don't drop the screw into the foot prior to installing it. You will go crazy trying to get it in the hole. If you don't have a magnetic screwdriver, simply hold a #1 screwdriver vertically by the handle. Carefully place the screw on the end of the screwdriver and then lower the plastic foot of the grill onto the screw. Voila! It does take a little torque but just tighten the screws till the feet are snug. There is no reason to tighten further - one reviewer tightened the screws right through the plastic and then blamed the product...

I fired the grill up and cooked some brats. It did a pretty nice job and the cooking was fairly even. I used medium heat with the lid open, rolling the bratwursts around for even cooking. They were pretty yummy. The lid on my grill didn't close but it was because I hadn't put the drip tray back in correctly. It appears that the rear most edge was not sitting back far enough. But there really is no need to cook with the lid closed... The meat is only a few inches from the flame and closing the lid would quickly overcook most any food at any temperature.

Clean-up was easy, but then again I cleaned the grill and drip tray within 30 minutes of cooking. I did not have to soak either piece. Just some Dawn soap, a green sponge, and water was adequate.

Overall I'm very impressed with this cute little convenient appliance. It's going to reside in my cargo / camper van in a little drawer under the bed. It's small enough to go on any camping trip and powerful enough to cook a great meal.

One last thing... The drip tray was said to be very sharp ... so be careful. My was not but I can see where it could possibly cut the skin. The edge will be filed down just in case I forget to be cautious. (I'm the goofy fisherman who leaves fillet knives in the sink and has the occasional OOPS).

product_title: Coleman Back Home Instant Screenhouse
review_headline: Great product! Worth the time to set it up.
review_body: This is a great screen house. We used it for 4 days of tent-only camping at a bluegrass festival (our car was half a mile away where we didn't have ready access to it), and it became a comfortable "living room" to our tent "bedroom" accommodations. It was hot and buggy out, but it really did the trick of letting you sit out comfortably and not worry about bugs or a few light raindrops.  The assembly on this screen house is very straightforward. It still takes time to get it all together (the roof, the tent screen, the pop-up legs, staking it down), but if you take your time, it really goes up quite simply without a lot of struggles. And be sure to stake it down; don't learn the hard way. Love that it comes with the stakes that you need to secure the whole thing. Also, note that it is rather heavy for transporting. But it is well-worth dragging it along to have a comfortable "living room" when you are out camping in the woods. Also recommend throwing down a tarp for a floor. It helps keep the bugs down. Great product! I would recommend it.

product_title: Clevr 2-in-1 collapsible 2-Seater Baby Stroller Jogger / Bicycle Trailer w Pivot Wheel
review_headline: Great as a stroller and rolls really well!
review_body:
I mainly purchased this trailer because it has the large front 12" swivel wheel. We have gravel trails by us so this was a must for us. I also like how it looks good as a stroller and not like a bike trailer with a little dinky wheel on the front. I've only had it for a short time but these are my first impressions-

Pros-
Super sturdy
Very well built
Glides super easy
Swivel jogger front wheel
Plenty of room inside and in the storage area

Cons-
Frame is entirely steel, non of the frame pieces passed the magnet test.

No recess for helmets, but I don't think any of them do.

Not sure on parts availability

It's a little heavy, weighed 36lbs as a trailer, front tire is 5 lbs so 41 lbs as a stroller. Although we took it over some gravel trails and it glided super well didn't feel that heavy and my son fell asleep! It did feel as a trailer that it gave a little more of a tug when your gaining speed than a burley trailer I recently tried.

They should make an aluminum version, but this trailer fits us well and I'm really happy with it. If you plan to do many miles of bike riding you may want to consider a lighter trailer, but I didn't find it too heavy while rolling on flat ground.

review_headline: You really do get what you pay for.
review_body:
You really do get what you pay for.
Bad wheels, bad bearings, deck is ok, but no grip to speak of whatsoever; it's like standing on an ice-block that's rolling on the ground. The bit of flex in the board helps out a little, but over all, not great. You may not see it in the picture but it has a little kick tail, if that helps anyone.

review_headline: This is pretty easy to install
review_body: I bought this rack for my Sondors Fat Tire eBike. This bike has enormously wide almost 5" tires. I wanted a bike that had a more rugged look. I would have purchased one of the other Ibera models, but the other owners of this bike had made a run on the suppliers and none were available. With the design of this rack, the two chrome brackets that go from the rack to the base of the seat post (not the seat post itself, but the frame) will need to be bent into a arc. This is pretty easy to do with only a little extra work to get the two brackets into the same arc. I went ahead and painted the two brackets to match the rack and my black frame.  My only issue with this rack is that there aren't any good spots to hook my Panniers to the rack. Other models from Ibera and other manufacturers have a loop or park of the frame that will accept a S-hook on a bungee. This rack design doesn't have that. And if you look at the picture, you will see that anything hooked onto its frame will slide around. I am sure I will be able to fabricate something, but at this time I haven't figured it out.  One detail I forgot. The M5-0.8x12 bolts were a little small for the spot at the bottom of the rack. I bought four of the M5-0.8x16 bolts and used the other two where the chrome brackets connect under the seat. I wanted stainless steel bolts, but my big box hardware store did not have them in stainless. In the user group for my bike, others mentioned that they found stainless. The black bolts do blend in nicely though.

product_title: One Hand Trekker Ns Camo
review_headline: A nice every day carry pocket knife, with some extra tools; excellent value for the price
review_body: The One-Hand Trekker is a very nice knife and multipurpose tool. It’s not as awesome as the top-of-the-line every day carry (EDC) knives like the Benchmade Griptilian, but on the other than, the Trekker is much less expensive and includes lot of other tools. I have a number of other Swiss Army/Victorinox multitools, and they’re all relatively fragile and gimmicky. This one is well built. I purchased it from Amazon in 2006, and carry it often.  (Note: There are two Trekkers. The One-Hand Trekker one has the thumb hole, and that’s the one I own and am reviewing. There is also a plain old Trekker, without the thumb hole on the main blade. Because it doesn’t have the thumb hole, it presumably takes two hands to open it. I have no experience with that knife.)  You can see my Trekker next to the Griptilian.  What I like about the Trekker:  • It’s a good pocketable size and not too heavy.  • I like the thumb opener on the main blade — as you can see, that’s the configuration I have on the Griptilian as well.  • The blade comes reasonably sharp and holds its edge. I have not attempted to sharpen it, and it would be difficult with the serrations.  • It’s nice to have the extra tools. I have used some, like the bottle opener and the tweezers. I haven’t use most of the others like the wood saw and screw drivers, but it’s nice to have them.  • I like that it has a locking main blade, which is crucial for any sort of knife. The liner lock feels quite sturdy.  • It’s quite inexpensive - can’t remember what I paid, but Amazon is listing it now (August 2015) for $38.13. That’s a bargain. See more about that below.  What I don’t like about the Trekker:  • I don’t know what type of steel it is. Not that it matters, but once you get into knives, you care about that.  • No pocket clip. I wear most of my EDCs inside my pocket but clipped to my pocket.  • The grip is slippery; most of my other EDCs are rougher and easy to hold.  • I dont like the serrated edge. That’s my bad because that’s what I bought. In retrospect, I should have purchased a no-serration version, which would be easier to sharpen.  Bottom line: Were I to lose the Trekker, I’d replace it with an NS version. And make no mistake, I would replace it immediately if lost.  Let me clear about my advice here. If you are looking for an EDC because you want a knife, get a knife-only EDC. If you are looking for a sturdy EDC-quality knife AND a multitool, this is the best one I’ve seen. It’s a real knife and a real multitool.  HINT: Shop around on Amazon! Lots of vendors are offering the knife at lots of different price points, and some of the prices are ridiculous.

product_title: Sigma BC14.12 - 14 Function Cyclometer
review_headline: Okay, but you probably can find something better
review_body:
Bought this model mainly because it is wired -- no more problems with lights interfering with the signal -- and because of the altitude feature. The altitude feature is fun, but I pretty much get the same info from GPS, so not really a strong argument for buying. I also bought the computer interface; it's not that great. I'm not sure how one resets ride data between rides without the computer interface; it's probably in the picture guide that serves as the only manual. It does attach/detach quickly from the mount, but don't ever put it in upside-down -- very difficult to get back out. I seem to have some problem getting consistent distance readings. On my old Cateye, I fine-tuned the circumference number after a few rides, comparing with GPS each time; have tried to do that with this one, but the numbers aren't stable. Unsure why.

Lots of reviewers mentioned that their device was DOA. Maybe so. I read such reviews before buying the device. When I got it, I couldn't get it to turn on. Figured I got one of the DOA ones too. My 12-year old daughter then read the manual and turned the device on for me (got it out of deep sleep mode). Not saying that's what happened with the other reviewers, but if you buy one, be sure to read how to turn it on!

Then while at pogopalooza in Philedelphia, I was able to try the new V4. The difference between the V3 and the V4 is amazing! it is like bouncing on a cloud compared to the already amazing V3. I ultimately decided to get a V4 and I am very glad I did. Everything about the stick is incredible! The aluminum construction is insanely durable and will take any beating that a person can inflict on it. I've taken many hard falls while attempting new tricks. In the process, I've slammed my pogo stick against concrete, ashphalt, rocks, down stairs, you name it and my stick has been tossed against it with no damage done at all. The construction of this pogo stick makes it unlike anything else on the market. The ability to replace every part on the stick and the ability to clean and lubricate this pogo stick with the removal of a few bolts is also a huge benefit. All the parts can be ordered and replaced with a single tool unlike other spring sticks which means that this pogo will last forever! The volume of air added to the V4 versus the V3 completely changed what I was able to on the stick as well I went from bouncing four and five feet high on the V3 to being able to reach six to seven feet and jump off from even higher objects on the V4. The added air makes it much smoother to do many new tricks that I wasnt able to do on the V3 and when I want to just have fun just bouncing around for a workout, it is much smoother and more enjoyable. The ability to change the air pressure in the cylinder makes this pogo very versitile. If i want to go really high and do bigger tricks I can pump up the air preassure and then i am able to do so, but when i want to just hangout and bounce around i am able to lower the pressure and have a smooth, enjoyable ride. The customer support at Vurtego is amazing as well! WheneverI have any questions about my pogo stick, Ian responds very quickly and always helps me with whatever questions I have, and their shipping is insanely fast. I would recommend this pogo stick to anyone looking for extreme sport action, a great fullbody workout, or a casual and fun activity for the whole family.

product_title: Ferrari Long Slide Skateboard,scuderia Ferrari Writing Across the Board
review_body:
I can't believe that Ferrari would have their name on this badly constructed, poor quality board. I don't know what kind of skateboard the first reviewer (notice it isn't a "verified" purchase) was riding but the truth of the situation is there isn't much to like about this skateboard. There is nothing "great" or even remotely "high quality" about it. Let's start with the "high quality" claim shall we.

The construction of this board reminds me of an airwalk board you would buy at Walmart. It has that particle/pressed board look to it from the side showing anyone who knows anything about skateboards that this is as cheaply made as you can get. This board is definitely made for show and not for go. The trucks however, are even worse than the board itself. Simply put these trucks are not only a joke, they're actually dangerous. The pivot cup is WAY too big for the pivot pin, meaning the trucks just slosh around and no amount of tightening will ever change that because, well once again, the pivot cup is twice the size of the pin. This is inexcusable, especially for a board with something like "Ferrari" on it. It's just shameful by whoever is manufacturing this board and by Ferrari for lending their name to something this bad.

The bolts holding the wheels to the trucks were twisted on so tight that I stripped out a skate tool trying to get them off. I had to put penetrating oil on all 4 bolts and let them sit overnight before I could remove them to look at the bearings. I've been putting skateboards together for nearly 40 years and I've never had to deal with nuts put on anywhere near that tight. As you can imagine the bearings were completely crushed by the incredible force that was used on the nuts so they were completely useless but being the standard 608zz bearing they weren't much good to begin with.

The graphics look OK but on the bottom of the board they were applied very badly. There are wrinkles and bubbles in the design, it's just awful. I've dealt with 1000's of boards over the years and I've never seen one with the graphics applied this poorly. The top graphics seem to be done much better and it's got some kind of clear grip on it. It looks pretty cool from the top, however the paint started coming off onto my hands just from touching it, so I doubt it would be very durable for any type of riding. The wheels it came with were red and quite soft, perhaps 82/84 duro wheels. Not what you would expect on a standard skateboard but they look alright. I noticed when putting the new bearings in that they too are not manufactured very well, the bearings do not sit tightly in the pocket at all so spacers are a must.

So take it from someone who actually bought this board, there is nothing great or high quality about it. The list price for this board is beyond laughable and should be a crime if they get someone to actually pay that. The reality is, it isn't worth any more than the cheapest boards you can get at any department store and if you can get it for that price it would make a great display and/or conversation piece. You definitely don't want to buy this board if you intend to have something to ride on though

product_title: Cygolite Hotshot 2-Watt USB Rechargeable Taillight with USB Cable
review_headline: Excellent Light, Charging Port Needs Relocation
review_body:
I purchased this at my local bike shop in order to support them.

This light has great brightness and cars are a lot more respectful of me when I use it. They give me much more room when they pass me. Some will patiently wait for me to move further to the right, or for me to wave that passing me is okay.) The light output remains bright even with just a weekly recharge. My daily commute to work is 45 minutes each way so I'm really impressed with the light output. This light is worth every cent I paid for it.

My biggest complaint is that the USB charging port is located on the bottom of the Hotshot. This makes it extremely difficult to get a charging cable plugged into the port. Why can't it be moved to the sides of the Hotshot? I would like to see that feature a lot. If the charging circuitry were set up so that one or two USB cables can be plugged in to ports on the sides of the Hotshot, that could speed charging. (I charge from a powered USB 2 hub which is connected to a wall outlet.)

As others say, seatpost mount needs a lot of improvement. If you have a short seatpost and a rear rack, which I do, there is very little room to swivel the Hotshot on an up-down axis. And to swivel it at all, you need to have a Phillips screwdriver handy to loosen and then tighten the mounting screw.

product_title: Grand Trunk Skeeter Beeter Pro Mosquito Hammock
review_headline: Absolutely love it. Costs way less than ENO (Eagle's Nest) ...
review_body:
Absolutely love it. Costs way less than ENO (Eagle's Nest) brand but essentially same nylon material.

My buddy has an ENO double without the bug nest and it already cost more than the Grand Trunk. Comfort wise, he couldn't tell the difference.

I used it on 4 camping trip including desert and Lake Tahoe. Temp ranged from low 40's to105. Performed very well. The key is to set the right sag (30 degrees pitch when you're in it). I use a "structural ridgeline" at 80-85% of the hammock's length to give me this perfect pitch. With the ridgeline, I could cut the shock cords into 2X 20in sections and tie the bug nest directly to it instead using the entire 20ft length to tie to the trees. Save weight and space in the bag.

The other upgrade is I bought two climbing carabiners to swap out the Dyneema loops at the end. Saves some bulkiness and makes hooking/unhooking to the strap very effortlessly.

Sleep at an angle, feet to one side and head to other. This will give you a flatter lay. If you have no clue what i'm talking about, look it up in youtube or hammock forums. Cheers.

review_body: Just received this in the mail.  It is mildly different from the display photo, particularly as regards the smaller pot/lid:  The bottom edges are less rounded.  Presumably this is a solution to the 'tipping' problem described by other owners.  I have not observed this phenomenon with my own set..  The coating appears to be of a nonstick variety, rather than anodization.  Absent field testing, my fear is that scratching from heavy use will encourage aluminum oxidation in a very short period of time.  The size is odd.  Approximately 6"W x 7"H, this is somewhere between one and two person cooking.  It's really too large for minimalist or solo hiking, and too small for groups.  While it does accommodate my thermos bowl and all condiments and utensils contained therein, it will not also hold my alcohol stove and stand; it's one or the other.   The set is very light, but seems fragile; e.g., easily dented, warped, etc.  Again, absent field testing, this cannot be confirmed.  The accompanying mesh bag is approximately two inches too long in length, and does not securely hold the lid to the pot. held together; all contents fall out.  Additionally, the bag itself is of inferior quality netting and manufacture, and has numerous points at which threads stray.  I will publish field testing results as I conduct them.  Preliminary opinion?  This set costs about twice as much as it's worth.

product_title: Fenix CL25R 350 lumen USB rechargeable camping lantern / work light (Black body) , 18650 rechargeable battery with Two back-up use EdisonBright CR123A Lithium Batteries
review_body:
A modern and very powerful lantern. The unique design has made it my favorite.

First the light output. With the unique design with the battery in the middle of the body the LEDs that shine out produce a wonderfully even 360 degrees of light. The frosting creates a very even light with no hot or cold spots. The button turns the lantern on after a 0.7 second press and additional presses change the light output. At low it makes for a nice night light - there's also a red mode that could be used for this too. At the brightest it makes a good task light lighting up an area for cooking or eating and puts out a large amount of light. There are a couple of useful modes in the middle trading run time for illumination. The memory remembers the last setting and returns to it when you turn the light back on.

Next the construction. The lantern is small, about the size of those smaller sized 6 ounce soda cans. It seems tough enough to not worry too much about it in a tool box or bottom of a backpack. There's a metal top loop for hanging that folds down flat. The on/off switch glows-in-the-dark and remains illuminated when the light is on or charging. The bottom is flat but there's a couple of unique features. There's a powerful magnet in the middle which will hold the light attached to a piece of ferrous medal like the side or hood of a vehicle. There's also a standard 1/4"-20 threaded hole which will allow it to attach to a camera tripod. I use one of those JOBY GorillaPod flexible camera tripods which allows me to wrap the legs around a tent pole.

Finally the battery and charger. The lantern charges from a USB socket using the same sized jack as a standard common (non-Apple) cell phone. The lantern can charge from AC or DC using the right USB adapter which are common and cheap. The batteries are included and the standard rechargeable 18650 or a pair of A123R batteries will work.

I've run my lantern overnight for 10 hours one the second lowest setting and come morning it showed no evidence of giving up.

I have a couple of Fenix flashlights in my collection so when this unique lantern came out I had to give it a try. I was so happy with the performance and quality that I bought a second one. Most highly recommended for use in camping, emergency supplies, or just around the house.

review_headline: Great little unit.  A little tricky to keep altitude calibration from shifting.
review_body:
Great little altimeter. Purchased for hiking in Washington's Cascade Range, as my old altimeter had died.

-- Sturdy construction
-- Seems accurate, as much as a small mechanical altimeter can be

These things are actually barometers, with a moveable dial for converting barometric pressure to altitude. You calibrate this by turning the moveable dial when at a known altitude, such as a landmark whose altitude can be read from your map.

Slight problem with this unit is the moveable dial moves around when the unit is in your pocket or pack, so you lose your altitude calibration. The old one's moveable dial was just about impossible to move by bumping the unit. I compensated with a piece of Gorilla Tape on the body, holding the dial, but this was less than a perfect solution.

Unit was also slightly larger and heavier than I'd guessed from the Amazon page.

It does the trick though, and I anticipate carrying it on hikes for years to come.

I first learned of Scrubba in 2011 and helped fund their first crowdfunding effort. I received my first one in 2012 and it changed my backpacking life forever. Fast forward to the future and I've ordered their new model which is a far cry from their original. The improvements are amazing.

The Scrubba bag is now super flexible, the cleaning "knobs" are rounder yet clean far better than the original. There are no worries that they will tear up my clothes. There is a great viewing window which certainly helps.

It wasn't super clear initially as to how much water to add to it. You don't need a lot, but you need enough to "slosh" a bit. Jeans are a bit of a challenge, but I'm mostly just washing lighter clothes anyway.

A must-have for backpacking and through-hiking but I now live in an Airstream so I'm particularly happy about this product. No longer do I have to wait for a big pile of clothes before going to the laundry mat. It's safe, great for small loads, cheap, and very environmentally friendly. Pair this with a great soap like Dr. Bronners or Coconut Oil soap (my fav) and you've got an easy and environmental way to wash clothes. No longer do I have to feel guilty about water or electricity use; it's truly easy being green with the Scrubba.

They are currently crowdfunding a dayback version of this. Needless to say, I'm going to be a part of this funding round as well. Here's where you can view their new crowdfunding: http://igg.me/p/scrubba-the-most-functional-travel-daypack/x/10974649

product_title: TETON Sports Oasis 1100 2 Liter Hydration Backpack; with a New Limited Edition Color; Free Rain Cover Included
review_headline: After 2~3 monts of hydration pack research, I finally found my perfect pack
review_body:
I needed a hydration pack that would be great for long hikes, had plenty of storage for a few survival essentials and not be bulky because I have a small frame of a body. It also needed to be lightweight because I wanted to be able to run with it for my longer runs and not have it weigh me down. It also had to be inexpensive. I was able to find packs that offered at least one of those criteria, but what I wanted was the whole package. I looked at the size, it was about the size that I wanted, and it offered adequate storage for my needs. I looked at the price and it was in my budget range. I liked everything about this pack and decided to go ahead and buy it.

Pockets:
The pack has four zippered pockets the biggest used for the hydration bladder and it has a Velcro strap to hold the bladder in place. There are also two openings near the top at the start of the shoulder straps for the bladder tube to reach through. The second zippered pocket is just a normal storage pocket. You can put your workout clothes, food, and electronics; just about anything, you might need for a run or long hikes. I use it to keep an extra bladder just in case I might be out for a longer time. The next pocket is big enough for your wallet, keys, protein bar, flavored drink mix ex. The last pocket is bigger than the smallest pocket and it can be used to keep you cell phone or small electronics in place. There are two elastic pouches as well as a clip in this pocket. On the outside of this pocket there is net made of elastic bungee cord that can be used to hold various objects in place.
There is one more pocket that contains a rain guard for the pack. It is located on the bottom of the pack labeled "RAINCOVER". It is a Velcro pocket and it is easy to miss if you do not know what to look for. This is actually great because it does not draw attention away from the pack.

Accessories:
The pack comes with two side elastic water bottle holders. It has various clips that can be used to tighten or loosen the pack to help make carrying various objects a breeze. There is a clip that I used which can unfold the last pocket. I used to keep my towel in place. It can be used to store climbing rope or other items. The back of the pack has two sturdy 1-Centimeter thick foam pads that run down along the pack. They are covered in breathable material in the form of net type structure. The shoulder straps are really thin and have thin foam with large surface area to allow breathability. There are two stability straps. One runs along your chest are and the orange buckle used to secure the strap has a built in survival whistle which is quite loud. The second strap runs along your waist and ahs generous amount of slack to accommodate varies waist sizes. There is also a strap on the very top of the pack that can be used to hang the pack. One little thing that many people do not know about is on the very bottom of the pack there is a "V" shaped hole. It is in the pocket that holds the water bladder. That is there to allow for drainage of water if your pack becomes wet.

The stitches:
I have gone through and observed the stitching on this pack and I can safely say it is really well done. The stitches are barely visible and they use the color thread according to the pack color you chose. It is actually very beautiful.

The verdict:
I do my best to provide helpful reviews and I try to go into as much detail as possible. I make it a point to be unbiased and all my reviews are written and rewritten to insure I give the most update information. I ordered and tested this pack on a few hikes as well as running and found it to be one of the best inexpensive hydration packs out on the market. I ordered the green pack because Green Is my favorite colure and the pack itself is beautifully constructed.
I am inclined to order another pack if anything happens to my first one as well as recommending it to friends and family. I enjoyed this product and I give it full five stars.ends and family. I enjoyed this product and I give it full five stars.

product_title: 1-1/4" Thick - 12" Wide - Bicycle Seat Cover / Gel Pad-Wide
review_body:
I have a Schwinn AD4 Airdyne, the "last of the big wheel versions." I love the Airdyne, however the seat was killing me. I'm rather broad in the beam, but I have one of the flatter tushes around for my size. I'm older and arthritic too and stuff hurts in places that it didn't used to hurt.

The Schwinn seat that comes on the AD4 is rather slick on the surface. It feels like it would be soft enough to the touch, but when I sat on it, it could have been a rock it felt so hard. Plus I slid around and hard to re-position myself on the seat every couple of minutes. Be the time 20 minutes rolled around, I was miserable, and my rear would get so sore that I'd have take days off to let the soreness pass.

So I bit the bullet, ponied up the bucks, and bought this seat cover with high hopes, and after my first ride, I am not disappointed! By the way, the seat cover arrived in two days, and I'm all the way on the other side of the US from the seller.

This seat fits my AD4 seat perfectly. It's snug and takes a bit of time to get it installed, but my prior experience with other seat covers is that you WANT a snug fit, otherwise it slides around and does not work well. So I got it on the seat cinched down tightly and then proceeded to take my trial ride.

And I did not have to reposition myself at all, not even once, no sliding around at all.... Plus, no more sore hips, it was thick and comfy and felt absolutely heavenly on my rear!

I don't know how this seat pad will wear over time, but I was impressed with the qualify and I'm optimistic that it was worth every penny I spent on it.

PS: I suggest that you get ready to lower your seat by a notch, because the padding is very thick.

I no longer dread sitting on my bike, no longer have a sore tush and hips, and no longer sliding around on my seat. I was attracted to This particular item for the carabiner clip at the top that will allow me to clip these to racks, handlebars, and belt loops. I can also clip it to my backpack when I use it for hiking. Sometimes when traveling through the forest we cannot get gps signal under the tree cover and there just isn't cell phone signals to be had so if an accident happens help can be hours away. Two carabiners, cord, and a thermal blanket can make a shelter and it comes with everything to make a fire. I have over 100 acres in my immediate area around my house so the whistle comes in handy when I have to call in my labs from their adventures since they are yellow and so are the weeds! All in all these are handy and I am sure I will find even more uses for them in time. I thank True Valor for giving me the opportunity to try these at a discount for my review, and supporting families of fallen/injured law enforcement with the proceeds of my purchase. product_title: Stansport Small Hurricane Lantern (Red)
review_headline: I know it's ridiculously easy to overfill tubed hurricane lanterns and get them to ...
review_body:
Short version: Pass on this. Buy a Dietz or Feuerhand or Kirkmann or other quality lantern.

Long version: I'm an experienced kero lamp and lantern user. I've owned lots of lamps and lanterns from multiple manufacturers for years. I know it's ridiculously easy to overfill tubed hurricane lanterns and get them to leak; even a quality lantern will leak if overfilled. That's not what happened here.

The base seam of the font isn't fuel tight. After leaving the lantern sitting with fuel in it for a couple weeks, liquid fuel has leaked out of the seam, wetting the seam and the workbench under it. There is no trail of fuel residue from the filler cap or the side tubes leading down to the seam, the seam itself is leaking. There are other areas of lacking quality that can be compromised on, but a fuel leak is not one of them.

I threw mine away.

product_title: ExOfficio Men's Boxer Brief
review_body:
As a men gets older, we learn something women have already learned waaaaay before us. The perfectly fitting/comfortable kind of underwear do not come in packs from Walmart. To get the most comfort out of something you are most likely wearing 90% of the time, you need to do some digging and trying out different brands.

These are OK boxer briefs. The legs do indeed stay in place and they are made to last for a very long time. They are breathable thanks to the holes in them, but the holes never expose anything. They are perfect for wearing in all situations. Hiking, walking, running, or binge watching something on Netflix.

-fits as expected unless you require above average room in the back
-comfortable
-breathable
-stays in place
-made to last a very long time
-simple washing, only requires time in a washing machine. . . Or heck, you can even wash it in the shower with you due to the fabric's nature

Now for why these are just OK. Fabric softener instantly ruins these and turns them into a normal pair of cheap boxer briefs, like the kind you buy in packs at Walmart. That means the legs will no longer stay in place and the front/back parts become lax, making them feel like normal boxers without much support. Putting them in the dryer also has the same effect. You can accidentally ruin these 20$+ pair of boxer briefs if you aren't careful, which is easy to do as a busy adult who's rushing to finish laundry while doing 5 other things. So be mindful! The worst offense is the lack of a curvature in the front. I still felt comfortable, but I didn't exactly feel grade A support like I'd expect from a 20$+ pair of boxer briefs.

-pricy
-easy to ruin if not cared for properly
-no curvature for maximum support

If these work great for you, then yay! I personally like them since they're better than Hanes or Fruit of the Loom. But I find Uniqlo boxer briefs to be cheaper and way more comfortable..

review_headline: NOT EVEN CLOSE TO "US MILITARY". VERY "STINKY" CHEAP MADE IN INDIA KNOCK OFF.
review_body:
1. Item description has "US Military" in it. As a veteran and someone who is fond of "genuine MIL-SPEC" items due to their stringent manufacturing and quality standards, I find the “US Military” label insulting and is blatant false advertising.

2. These are "Made in INDIA" and compared to the genuine “US Military” issue blankets made by PEERLESS TEXTILES or FARIBAULT WOOLEN MILLS, these are junk and would not even meet the lowest MIL-SPEC standards and would be rejected immediately as trash.

3. With the above being said, the price is fair for a blanket that you could throw in the trunk or the back of a pick up for an emergency or to cover the carpeting in your SUV when hauling dirty junk.

Be prepared to wash them at least twice with lots of detergent if you want to get rid of the "chemical stench" and the couple of extra pounds of wool that will shed off of these cheap knock offs.

Make sure you clean the washer and/or dryer lint trap after each washing. It will seem as if you have just sheered an entire "Green Sheep"!

product_title: Phantom Aquatics Impulse 1500 LED Aluminum Dive Light
review_body:
While the price point is high, the Phantom Aquatics Impulse 1500 is a really great underwater flashlight.

Though we haven't been able to take it on an actual dive yet, we've done a fair amount of work with it in the pool (during both daylight and nighttime hours) and are really pleased with the overall performance. The Impulse 1500 gives a great range of vision underwater at night (probably a good 20 feet in clear water) and is easy to use and really functional.

The rechargeable batteries work better than I expected, as I've not had great experiences with them in the past. But the ones that come with the Impulse seem good for a nice long charge (they've yet to run out on us, even after an hour of dedicated use). It may be a bigger issue if you don't have the ability to bring the charger with you, but the Impulse 1500's simple, but effective, packaging should eliminate that concern.

Overall, we've really enjoyed the Phantom Aquatics Impulse 1500 so far, and while a bit expensive, is certainly worth it.

product_title: Manitou Match Comp QR-D 26" fork, 100mm - black
review_headline: Wow. Nice fork at this price point.
review_body:
My frame of reference is the Rockshox XC28 & XC32 (coil and solo-air) and the Suntour 3030/XCT/XCM coil forks.
The Manitou Match Comp is torsionally stiff (a very good thing) but relatively heavy, although not as heavy as the Suntour XCM. It's comparable in weight to the XC32. The coil is plush and the action is very smooth. Spring preload is noticeably progressive, rather than on-or-off. The rebound damping is also noticeably progressive and quieter than expected at this price point. What really sets this fork apart from the sub-$300 field is the Absolute-Plus compression damping. You have several clicks on the drive-side, crown mounted dial. I began to notice the compression damping at 3-4 clicks. One click shy of lockout is ideal for climbing with a little suspension action remaining. The fork is completely locked out at the end of the dial. This is a wonderful feature. You don't always have the opportunity to disable lockout right after a climb. Having a firm but still active fork can be very handy when starting your descent.

I have no regrets and I would heartily recommend the Manitou Match Comp as an affordable, low maintenance solution for the casual XC/singletrack rider.

product_title: ThruNite Ti4 penlight series, Using 2 x AAA, IPX-8 Waterproof, 4 Modes from Firefly to Turbo
review_headline: Best Penlight I have ever owned.
review_body:
I really like this Penlight.

Conclusion first instead of last: High quality, great price, best Lumen “spread” between settings, the most functional Penlight I have ever owned.

My previous favorite pen light was my Preon P2. However this Thrunite Ti4 is far more functional for me. The low output (0.3 lumens) of the Firefly setting is perfect for finding my way around the house at night without losing what little night vision I have. It's enough light to avoid stepping on pets or toys during the 3am trip to the toilet, while preserving my limited night vision once it is off. My Preon P2 has a low setting of 2.2 lumens, and to keep from losing my night vision I have to partially cover it with my finger.

The middle setting is 24 lumens (2 less than my Preon). This is more than enough for all the other times I need a light. Whether looking for a dropped screw under my desk during the day, or looking for doggie land mines in the backyard at night. And everything else in between.

The high setting of 252 lumens is 54 more than my Preon. 252 lumens in a Penlight! Awesome! I almost never use it though. Mostly only go to the high setting when I’m showing it off. But if I ever really need it, and don't have a tactical light, it’s there.

review_body:
I bought two pairs of these for zip-lining, and they were really amazing. The fit was really good (I could've technically fit into a Small, but the Medium gave me just the right amount of grip and room.) They reminded me of the tactical gloves I used to wear in the Army, although these held up better, gripped better, and fit better.

The picture makes them look a bright pink, but it's more of a rich, medium pink. I would've preferred the beige color, but these don't look ridiculous or out of place when you're wearing them.

Edit: I've had these gloves for about 2 years now, and I use them two or three times a week for indoor rock climbing. They've held up well and saved my hands several times from getting caught in the belay device. They've also saved me plenty of rope burn and gave me extra grip when I was still learning how to belay.

The only downside is that Outdoor Research doesn't make these gloves (or any women's gloves) anymore, so if you can get a pair, count yourself lucky.

product_title: XLC PD-S01 Pedals 2016
review_headline: The pedals worked fine for about the first 3 years and I'd been ...
review_body: I bought these pedals about 3 years ago because of the price. These were maladjusted, as other buyers have noted, but I did not bother loosening the bearing adjustments because the spindles seemed to me to spin freely enough for use. The pedals worked fine for about the first 3 years and I'd been thinking I'd gotten a pretty good deal. But a couple of weeks ago one of the spd clips broke. When I took a closer look, I discovered that the BOTH screw heads had sheared off on the front part of the clip. Conclusion? Those screws were BOTH defective. The screw shanks are pretty tiny--too tiny for an easy-out. And what's more, they've been coated with thread-locker (as they should have been) before being run in. Long story short, I've discovered that it will be impossible to unthread those broken-off shanks. So one of my set of pedals has been turned from a combination platform/spd pedal into a quill pedal. And the logical conclusion? These pedals are junk and are not worth the $25 I paid. Don't buy them unless you intend only to use them as quill pedals.

review_headline: Great chair design, I won't count on it lasting me long.
review_body:
When I sat on this chair for the first time, I became a man who is very comfortable outside his house.

First thing that I loved about this chair was the way it carries in backpack mode. It's a very comfortable carry. All the weight (heh this chair weighs a feather) is on your back and straight down. It is symmetrical so it does not affect the way you move. I hate, hate, hate, hate the burden of carrying an oddly-weighted whatever labeled portable. This is the opposite of that. The people who designed this chair hate those things as much as I do.

This chair is low and leans back maybe 30 degrees. It's comfortable enough. I could probably take a bit of a nap between lunch and afternoon work on it.

The one thing I don't like about it is the quality of the materials. It's serious sad. Like I could have bought this on Alibaba for better material quality. The chair arms have this rubber nub (arm feet?) at the end so that it's not just bare metal getting sleeved in to the arm rest. One of those just came broken. Just split. One arm had a broken nub so I zip tied it down. Seriously you guys, fix that s***. It's a great chair otherwise.

product_title: Giro Hoxton Gloves
review_headline: Amazingly comfortable with no uncomfortable gel blocks to make my hands numb, but concerned about longevity
review_body:
I have been cycling for about a year. I ride between 50 and 100 miles a week, but as my rides have gotten longer, I've found I'm not liking to Pearl Izumi Elite Gel Gloves that I bought when I first started riding. I guess I was about 30 miles into my last ride when my left hand went numb. I realized that the little "gel" pocket was pushing into a nerve on my hand and it was painful every time I grabbed the hoods of my bike. It's like the padding is in just the wrong spot. Spurred by that issue, I decided to try out a glove with perhaps a bit less "gel" type padding, but with an overall comfortable palm.

These Giro Hoxton are just awesome, and I could feel it from the moment I put them on. My hand measures about 8" around (the palm, measured inside the thumb), so I got the Medium. The gloves themselves have a wonderful feel - extremely soft and comfortable, even when I ride in 95 degree Baltimore summer heat. The palms have small ventilation holes, and the padding is generous flat double-stitched overlay, rather than stick-out gel blocks. As a result, nothing pushes into my palm.

The gloves come off easily with 2 convenient loops on the fingers, but fit comfortably and don't slide during riding. The actual wool used is minimal - just enough to give them a nice feel. The palm is 94% polyester and 6% spandex. The top is 87% acryl, 9% wool, and 4% PU. I've finally found gloves that are comfortable for my longest rides, cushioning my hands, absorbing sweat, but not making my hands numb.

So why 4 stars? After just 2 rides, there is some fraying on the ends of the finger tips. It seems they should have finished them a bit better because it is WAY too soon to see the fraying start. I'm afraid these gloves might not last more than a few months, whereas my Pearl Izumi gloves lasted a year before i saw stitching start to come out.

Otherwise, awesome and recommended.

product_title: White Sierra Women's Bug Free Zip Hoody
review_headline: For me this hoodie is a great bang for the buck
review_body:
For me this hoodie is a great bang for the buck. I took it on a trip to an area where mosquitoes were unusually abundant this summer, and it did the job keeping them away. Being able to put the hood up over my head, tighten the strings, and cover my ears, was also a lifesaver against some dive-bombing flies.

It's easy to clean and stands up to odor, but only when you have something on. I wore it one day with a tank top and no deodorant to the beach and it reeked pretty badly within a few hours. I washed it and wore it again with a tank top, this time with homemade deodorant (coconut oil, baking soda, arrowroot powder, a drop of lavender oil) on a hot afternoon and it smelled fine.

The reason I gave it 4 stars is because I did get hot wearing it in the heat (polyester) even though it's mesh and very thin, and feel it might be better blended with a high-tech cooling agent/fiber.

Otherwise, very satisfied. It kept bugs away as advertised and protected me from sun burn. Would recommend it.

If you are looking for a hiker wallet that will hold everything a regular wallet holds, this product is not for you.  I am more of a walker and/or "tourist hiker."  I am not going out for three day treks through the back woods, I am going out for five mile hikes through the countryside.  All I usually carry with me is a key, an ID and a $20 bill.  For this purpose, the wallet works perfectly.  I especially like that it has a carabiner that I can hook into a loop in my hiking pants/shorts or the inside of my rain jacket pocket.  Being able to hook it in provides an extra level of security from loss (and probably from pickpockets when travelling).  It is not incredibly sturdy, but it should be fine if not overstuffed.  I am happy with the product.

product_title: Lowpricenice Professional New Mini Set Stove for Camping/hiking Cs-b02
review_headline: Much better than a beer-can stove
review_body:
I made one of these a few years out of an empty beer can, but it was always such a pain to use. This stove, on the other hand, is really easy to operate. The fact that the lid makes a tight seal means that you can leave unburnt fuel in there, put the lid on, and re-use it the next time you need to cook. With the beer can, I had to dump it back into the fuel container, which always made for a mess. The addition of the stand/pot-holder is a major plus. With the beer can, I always had to balance my pot/pan on some rocks around the can, which always posed a challenge.

I've been testing this out and it has met all of my expectations so far. I used it with my camping coffee pot and it brought 40 ounces of water to a boil in about 17 minutes using about 2.5 tbsp of denatured alcohol. I also put a large, heavy cast iron pan on this thing and cooked up 3 eggs all in about 10 minutes from lighting the stove to putting my eggs on the plate using about 1 tbsp of 91% isopropyl alcohol. The fact that you can do all that with something that fits in the palm of your hand and only costs $15 is impressive.

My only complaints are that the simmer ring doesn't really fit on the stove when you use the included stand. The handle gets in the way. Otherwise, it's perfect. The included carry case is a bonus.

product_title: Emergency Lights, TaoTronics Portable Led Lanterns, Camping Lantern Collapsible, Battery Powered Camp Lights for Fishing, Hiking and Outdoor Adventures, Camping Gear
review_body:
This is a great little light! I didn't expect much going in based on its size and shape, but I was definitely pleasantly surprised.

We immediately took it camping the day after receiving it and while it's not as bright as larger lanterns, this is perfect for hanging in your tent. It's great to have two different brightness levels, depending on how much light you need. The flashing feature is neat, but I can't think of a situation where I would need to use it. The built-in handle combined with a spare carabiner makes for an instantly usable hanging light, just about anywhere you have the ability to hang it. Aside from camping, I think it would be a great little utility light to keep on hand "just in case". The batteries last for quite some time, it's compact enough to store it in a backpack, glove box or center console in a vehicle, or in your toolbox. The focused beam is bright, but casts a halo that tints the light output so color accuracy should not be one of the things you expect from using this light. When expanded, the light is quite white, probably along the 6000K-6500K color temperature or close to it.

Overall, I've really enjoyed this light. I got it for a great deal on Prime and can honestly say that I don't think there's one thing I don't like about it, and as long as you manage your expectations appropriately, I think you'll be happy with it, too.

product_title: iGadgitz 3 in 1 Pop Up LED Camping Lantern + Flashlight + Emergency Light
review_body:
I have worked with several camp lanterns and I have seen a good variance in features, strength of the output light and power source. This is a small and compact camp lantern that works well and serves well in a couple of capacities.

This little lantern compacts down to about the size of a baseball. When expanded it stands approximately 5" tall and it exposes a nylon mesh over a spring. The mesh serves as a light diffuser and it casts out a gentle but bright light when powered on. It has three operating modes - bright, very bright and flashing. The flashing mode is great for attracting attention and acts as a beacon.

This lantern has a lens on the bottom which is close to the actual LED. When the lantern is collapsed the light coming through the lens comes out very bright and concentrated and the whole unit can be used as a flashlight. When expanded, the light instead diffuses and it casts a light glow which lights the area underneath the lantern if it is hung somewhere.

It requires 3 AA batteries to power this lantern which do not come in the box. I am not sure how long the burn time is for this unit before the batteries are drained as I have not run it that long to find out but it should last several hours with no trouble.

Because of the ability to use this as a flashlight, this is a good unit to keep around for emergency use. It is very lightweight, it is weather resistant and it is very bright. I am very pleased with this light.

product_title: Kelty TN 3 Person Tent
review_headline: Almost 5-stars, but gave 4 due to the zipper flap design, which is prone to a sticking zipper
review_body:
This is a high-quality, lightweight and very compact 3-person tent. It features a 3-4" bathtub-type floor, for when rain might puddle and the clear plastic window and half-on, half-off rain fly is a nice touch for looking outside or seeing WHAT is outside without having to actually open the rain-fly.

This was easy to assemble and I appreciate the green-colored tips and webbing to help decide where to put each end. Since there's 2 main poles, you only need to know where to put 2 ends to figure out the tent without instructions. The center pole is obvious.

We also appreciate the fly/tent pull-back clips to hold the door open, etc. and clip them. This is one of the easiest and most compact tents I've put together. I've also used the tents that you throw up in the air and they are done practically, but those are extremely heavy and not compact whatsoever. This is the best of both worlds.

The reason I gave 4 stars is the zipper flap design. I've used tents from Eddie Bauer to Coleman to REI and even their simple tents have better designed zipper flaps. I DID assemble this in the living room as a test prior to some outdoor 4th July Firework watching and my daughter caught the zipper in the zipper flap (not well designed). Basically it was stuck for her. I thought it was her, until it happened to me.

You don't need a zipper flap that is that close to the opening/closing of the zipper. Start the seam of the zipper flaps about 6 inches away and use velcro or a clip to cover the zipper. Or velcro to hold the flap open OR use a thicker material that won't slip in under the zipper mechanism. Or...don't use a flap, if your zippers are waterproof.

If the zipper didn't get stuck for my daughter and then, myself, I would have easily given this 5 stars!

review_body:
My teenage kids ordered this for me on Amazon for Father's Day, and I love it! After reading all the reviews first to prepare myself for riding, I was ambivalent about learning and got ready for the worst, because most people said it took 1-3 weeks to learn how to ride. However I ride Rip Skates and Orbitwheels, and I was happy that it took me less than 3 minutes to figure them out! If you ride Orbitwheels, you can ride these with no problem! Within 3 minutes I was doing laps in the inside of our underground parking garage, and went non-stop for a full five minutes before stopping on my own accord. I'm 49 and will celebrate my 50th birthday in less than two months, so if I can do it anyone can (and I'm not a trickster, just basic riding)! Here's a good tip I discovered: Instead of using a stationary wall or railing, find a shopping cart (the residents keep lots on hand in our underground parking). Hold on to the long side of the shopping cart in front of you as your "hand rail" (perpendicular to the cart handle), and you can keep going without falling, even if you veer off course. This should make the learning curve faster.

The reason why I gave it less than 5 stars is because they arrived pretty scuffed up, like they had already been used (only the wheels and the grip tape looked new). Don't know why they came like that. Otherwise, pretty pleased with the product. Don't know if I'll ever learn those tricks you see in those videos. But even regular riding is fun. Happy skating!

review_headline: Probably okay for some folks, but communication is good
review_body: I recently purchased the 2.5 L hydration pack did not never used it after first filling and testing the bladder. I could not draw any water from it until I had held the bladder up about chest high and then the mouthpiece leaked. Both issues reportedly have been corrected by the vendor who did send out a replacement mouthpiece when I told them of the problem. However, the deciding factor against this bladder was the handle/ring that attaches to the bladder snapped off the first time I tried to fill it. Although it easily snapped back into place, it easily snapped back off and it was evident that I could never use this as a holder to fill the hydration bladder (the best I could see is that three or four small tabs on the ring hold it onto the bladder). Once the fill lid (attached by tether to the handle/ring is tightened to the bladder you easily can use the handle for support. Communication with the vendor was easy and prompt. They told me to let them know of any problems. I let them know of the leaky mouthpiece and they sent out a replacement (that I never did try). After I emailed about the handle/ring issue I was told they would send out a replacement bladder if I needed one. However, when I said that there was no need to send out a new bladder if all handle/rings snap off, communication seemed to stop. That is until several days later I received an email asking if I had received my "Thirsty Monkey" Hydration Monkey Pak. What? Yes I had and I let you know of problems. The last email appeared to be a canned email but in fairness it did go into details of problems they had cured with leaking mouthpieces, etc. Anyway, if I need to insert my fingers/thumb into the bladder to fill it instead of using the handle because the handle and ring attachment that connects to the bladder cannot support the weight, then I'll shop for a pack that does as this one is being sent back (unfortunately on my dime). I had no issues with the pack itself. Again, I did think communication with this company was very good (at first) and was willing to give them 3 stars just for communication.  UPDATE: I mentioned I was willing to give them 3 stars for communication so I upgraded it from 2 to 3 stars. Reasoning: I received another email stating that they pulled the bad units from Amazon and wished they could have corrected it for me. Therefor, I do believe this Monkey Paks will work with any buyer. None the less, prior to this email I decided to go with a military-grade hydration pack.
