product_title: Sigma Sport Double Sided Docking Station
review_headline: the best solution is to ignore the apparent issue
review_body:
First Impressions: I had no trouble downloading the software and getting the device to synch with the program, but the instructions that came with it were not very helpful.
Some reviewers have mentioned difficulty locating the driver for the docking station. Based on my experience, the best solution is to ignore the apparent issue: I installed the program (Sigma Data Center 4.0) on my computer (Windows) first, then plugged in the docking station. The little arrow spun endlessly looking for a driver. I clicked on the stop looking button, there still seemed to be no driver, but as soon as I plugged in my Rox 6.0 to the docking station, it found the driver immediately and downloaded the data.

My complaints: The software is either not customizable, or if it is, I can’t figure out how to do it. There does not seem to be a good manual for the 4.0. A PDF of the manual for the 3.0 is available online, but I could only find it with a Google search. There does not seem to be a “help” tab or “preferences” tab in the program. Most particularly, although the ROX 6.0 can be programmed to display the date in miles and speed in miles per hour, the data center only displays metric data. Dates are backwards in European style. Not only is distance only in kilometers, speed is in minutes/kilometer instead of kilometers/minute, so the lower the number the faster the speed. It would appear altitude is in meters also, but no actual/starting altitude displayed from my first ride (? because this was entered as feet). The uphill distance did display in meters.

Also be aware, the device, at least the ROX 6.0 which I have, does not store trip data after you clear it out to start a new trip; so you have to download the data after every single ride if you want to keep a record of all of them.

Bottom line: If you want to keep track of heartrate and calories burned or details of every lap, this could save a lot or writing down, but ifyou are American and mostly just want to keep track of distances and speed in a familiar format, you might be better off just plugging them manually into a spreadsheet. The folks at Sigma should show some sympathy for their American users and provide the option of non-metric measurements.

This is a serious backpack with the update to be able to take a hydration bladder. My old Kelty was so minimal (it's what, forty years old?) and backpacks have become so much more in the last few years. For one thing, the back is padded so you can wear this all day. It's a top loader, so grabbing a change of clothes for weather situations is easy.

The belt has mesh pockets to hold water bottles (if you aren't using your hydration system, or if you have mixed up some energy drink) and there are all kinds of loops and handles to hang gear.

Best of all is the detachable daypack. Pack your backpack as heavy as you can carry to hike into your campsite, then detach the daypack for food and sundries on the trail that are all you need from your campsite.

This is not a pack for books and laptops. This is hiking equipment. I've had Kelty packs before and they last forever--my forty year old one, I finally donated to Goodwill. It was in amazing condition.

product_title: Schwalbe Big Apple Tire 29x2.35 RaceGuard Performance Series
review_headline: I've been running these amazing tires on my single speed Kona Unit 29er for ...
review_body:
I've been running these amazing tires on my single speed Kona Unit 29er for 3 years and 2,500 miles now, and whenever these decide to give up the ghost, rest assured I will be obtaining another set. For the first half of their life with me, I ran them in a desert climate, parked outside all day everyday in 120 temps, roads covered with desert debris, sharp plant material, glass, etc. and sub freezing temps all winter long. I rode washboard dirt roads, rocky and rooty trails, rain storms, mud washed roads, and a lot of searing pavement.

For the past few months I have been running them in a big city as a bike courier 5 days a week approx. 30-40 miles per day. The streets are full of potholes, uneven streets, cracks, curbs, cobblestones, bricks...you name it, it's got it. I ride hard every day and these tires are still going and show no signs of letting up yet. The tread compound is super hard wearing. I did finally get my first flat about 3 months ago...it was a black roofing nail that I never saw until I heard the thump thump of the head striking the pavement as the wheel rotated. I pulled it out, threw a quick patch on the tube and rolled away again in 5 minutes. No more issues since then.

In the city, I run these at full pressure for maximum speed and they are still quite lovely and cushy. My bike is rigid front and rear, so this is the only suspension I have, but it's really all I need. On days when I ride easy with my wife or putt around on the greenway, I'll drop 10-20 PSI and I'm floating on a cloud.

Best. Tires. Ever. More than worth their price.

review_headline: I'm super torn about this watch
review_body:
I'm super torn about this watch. It really is a great looking fit/smart watch. However, it is so very confusing. The instructions tell you the basics, but that is about it. The application doesn't explain anything very well either. It took me several minutes to figure out even the basics. Took me 20 minutes to figure out, you don't set the time, the application does that for you. So this is my biggest complaint for it. It doesn't have enough instructions PERIOD.

Other than that, it's a great watch. The time is clear, and the display shuts off after a few seconds. Meaning you have to hit the button to get it to show you the time. You can switch between time, pedometer, sleep mode, and a couple other features I haven't quite figured out yet (again, better instructions please). From what I can tell you can set alarms on this. For waking up, sitting too long, drinking as often as you should, etc. I just haven't quite figured out the application either. When I get more time I am going to play with this some more, and I will share my version of some instructions for y'all.

The adjustable-ness of this watch is pretty awesome. There are plenty of slots for the snaps to go into. It feels tight and snug on my wrist, and I don't think it will go anywhere. It's a very sleek design and I love it. The application doesn't seem to take up too much space on my phone. However, it does require bluetooth to work with your watch. I have to turn my on and off, because the bluetooth feature drains too much battery from my phone otherwise. I wish there was a way to plug this into my phone, instead of being forced to only use bluetooth. However, some folks probably prefer the bluetooth feature.

Overall this is a great watch, despite the lack of instructions and I do recommend it for those looking for something similar to a fitbit, without the fitbit cost.

review_headline: I feel like the vast majority of 4-5 star reviews must be ...
review_body: This is a long term review.  I feel like the vast majority of 4-5 star reviews must be people who have used the mattress infrequently.  Yes, it's comfortable (for an air mattress), and after the first night we too thought it was a good buy.  However, we needed a mattress to get us through a 2 month period where we were moving, and we've now been sleeping on this thing for about four weeks, nightly.  Last night we developed our fourth hole.  All of the holes have come up on the "flocked" top side of the mattress, and it seems like this must be some sort of basic flaw.  Whatever material they put on there to make the top soft and fluffy also appears to make it very prone to forming holes. The smallest are pinprick-sized, the largest I could fit my thumb in.  We have been pumping this using the recommended Coleman pump, and have experimented with both overpumping and underpumping-- doesn't matter, either way we get holes.  If you buy this mattress, have a ready supply of packing tape and krazy glue, and be prepared to spend a lot of time crawling over the mattress searching for holes!

product_title: Klean Kanteen 12-Ounce Wide Insulated Stainless Steel Bottle With Loop Cap
review_headline: Great large capacity, shows wear quickly
review_body:
This if for the 20oz size. I got the double pack.
It's not the best heat retention I've experienced in a vacuum insulated cup, but it doesn't do too bad. The main draw for me was the large 20oz size, larger than most insulated vessels. The wide mouth is useful for ice cubes and for cleaning. Heat retention from almost boiling to 'warm' is about 5-6 hrs with the lid not opened, 2-3 hrs if you like to drink it hot but not scalding. You will need to close the lid tightly and then more tightly to prevent hot liquids from leaking when the bottle is left on it's side. Cold will keep ice until the next day at normal temperature, about 10hrs in a hot car. If you want really awesome cold/hot retention I recommend Zojurishi, but it's hard to find the large capacity bottles.
The stainless steel is soft though and dents really easily compared to some of my other thermoses. The paint on the colored ones also started showing wear and tear in the first week (discoloration, chipping) and I'm not that hard on my thermoses. Really they take a ride in my purse from home to work, and then back again. It's great if you want to have alot of liquid on you, but not the prettiest if you like to keep your things looking 'like new' or 'pristine'.
Also there is no grip or indentation to hold it, so I usually hold it by the cap. I wear a regular small size in nitrile gloves and the bottle is too big for me to hold comfortably around it's body when it is full.
If you're looking for an even larger capacity, HydroFlask make a 32oz insulated I believe, but it's really a giant and very heavy when full.

product_title: Eberlestock Water Bladder Polymer Green
review_headline: Well made, but could be better design with newer version with quick disconnect tubing.
review_body:
I'm giving this a 3 star review overall due to being well made materials, but took off two stars due to that I received the older version without the QMT quick disconnect on the tube parts. The tubing on the older version is fixed in place, which doesn't dry easily as it should when hanging to dry completely. This is a critical to inhibit mold and bacteria in the long run. Even though they do have antimicrobial lining, it doesn’t guarantee germ-free growth especially since it is easy to leave water behind in the tubing for a long period of time). This product also really isn't Eberlestock's own, but made from Source Tactical Gear. The one I received didn’t even have the Eberlestock logo on it anywhere which I don’t care for anyways, but if you search on Amazon for Source Outdoors WXP SQC QMT Storm Valve-IRR Cover, that’s the newer version and cheaper too. But it's partly my problem for purchasing it without researching more and comparing versions and options.
For this review, I won’t argue the fixed verses quick connect tubing parts as I think they both can offer advantages and disadvantages (if only slight). For example, fixed usually means one less failure point such as coming off unexpectedly or some seal leaking, but the QMT disconnects are made well to prevent this.
My main issue was when I went to dry the bag, I did it by the instructions, opening everything up, but with the fixed tube, water will hold in it if not blown through very well. The instructions recommend to fold the tube inside the bag while drying upside down with top clip open, (which opens the bag up more inside to allow better air movement) however this makes it so the tube will hold water inside it’s bend. Even without putting the tube inside the bag, you would not have good air movement in the tube as one end is in the bag. All in all, this is still a good made hydration bladder, but would like to have had the quick disconnects and less confusion on item versions and manufactures.

review_body:
Finally got around to testing out our new stove and I must say this things works great for not having any liquid fuel to worry about!!

We bought this stove to take on camping trips and have for an emergency. You essentially can use this stove forever without ever having to worry about any liquid fuel as long as you have plenty of sticks, pine cones, fire pellets, etc lying around. It is a bit on the heavy side even with it being only the size of a nalgene bottle. I have a small butane propane stove that I use when we need to travel light as the stove and a small fuel bottle weighs less than this stove.

Back to the Biolite Stove, it comes with the metal stove canister/stand, the orange fan/battery unit, a usb to usb charging cable to initially charge the fans lithium battery, a triangular pot stabilizer, and some fire starter sticks. As I mentioned, when you first open up the stove you need to charge it with the provided USB cable so that you can always have a small charge to start-up the fan before the fire gets hot enough to recharge it on it's own.

Lighting this stove is very easy, first you need to put a good amount of small sticks and twigs into the stove then you have to take a half piece of a fire starter stick that came with the stove, light it, and place it in the middle of the sticks. The stove lit right up and after about 30 seconds I turned the fan on low to really get this thing heating up. The fan is slanted so it kind of acts like a fire whirlwind which makes the flames very hot! The initial pile of sticks we loaded up in the stove lasted about 5 minutes which is about how long it took to boil a small pot of water. After maybe 8 minutes of adding a few twigs here and there, you'll get a green LED light bar which means you can turn the fan on Hi and charge up your USB device. When the stove is set on Hi and you continue to add sticks to keep it nice and hot, you will get about a 1% charge per minute with an iPhone 5S. It's pretty slow, but when you're in the woods and have nothing else to do then it's better than nothing. I think you can also charge up a portable power bank with the stove then use that to charge an phone much quicker.

Overall I love this stove and can't wait to take it on our next camping trip in the mountains! review_body:

Not too much, but if you plan on putting things you want dry in there I'd recommend a "dry bag" the kind you get for kayaking/boating to ensure your stuff will be dry when you are done using the float. I'm always surprised how it inflates in about 20-25 minutes max compared to floats that are bigger and hold the same capacity of people. It's held up great, there are two compartments to inflate an inner circular tube around the mesh circle and an outer one, so you are able to pump both compartments at once bringing inflation time down to about 15 minutes before you're ready to roll.
There is also areas to tie rope too to chain additional tubes in case you have a large party.

Beware, smoking can cause holes in your tube from the embers/ashes...my last party float died that way after getting a few of them, so if you like your toys you spend money on I recommend telling your friends to hold off on lighting up on your float.

product_title: Schwinn Men's Wayfarer Hybrid Bike
review_headline: Far better than expected for its price - perfect for casual city and path riding
review_body: If you understand what you are buying, this bike is a fantastic value. It has a lightweight steel frame that features beautiful welds and a nice paint job. Handlebars and quill stem are high quality items.  V-brakes are excellent, but of lower quality, as is the rear derailleur. Chrome fenders and rear spring-loaded rack are decent quality and attractive. The saddle is closer to a size needed by a 12 yr old vs. an adult.  The bike's geometry is a bit of a puzzle.  I am 5'11 and have a 30" inseam and I can barely stand over it flatfooted. Yet the top tube is very short - similar to a 53 or 54cm bike - which would be appropriate for a 5'6"-5'-9" rider.  So it demands a very upright riding position for anyone that is over 5'10" and I would expect it to feel very small for anyone 6'1" or taller.  The other head-scratcher is the gearing range.  As a 7 speed, I would expect to use one of the middle gears (3/4/5) when riding on a flat, smooth road.  Not so - on my first 10 mile ride on city streets, I spent most of the time in 2nd gear and had to switch to 1st gear on more than a few occasions.  A hill of moderate slope will require you to stand and pedal as the 1st gear will not be of much help.  It has a 44T front chainring, that is unfortunately a single piece crank design, making it a harder chore to replace/upgrade.  A 42T or 40T chainring would have been a better choice.  All that said, it is a nice riding bike.  The steel frame is compliant and reduces road vibrations and the 700c wheels with 700/35 tires give a nice soft, smooth ride while being relatively fast rolling. Bottom line it is a sharp looking bike with a great frame that would be worthy of a few component upgrades.  But even as-is, it represents an excellent value for the casual bike rider.

product_title: Bell Memory Foam Saddle
review_headline: Best seat I've ever sat on riding a bicycle... amazing comfort and padding.
review_body:
Man oh man... this thing is amazing compared to the stock 'tiny' Giant seat that came with my Revel 2. I used to have the Bell seat cushion that went on top of the stock seat, but this thing is SO much better. It took me about 10 minutes to install it after i figured out how the whole stock seat setup worked. Just took a standard allen wrench to take of the one bolt, then took the original seat off the bracket, and this one fit the existing bracket without any special parts.

I'm 6'6" 280lbs so a bigger seat was a must for me. This isn't "too" big, but it's just right for me. My 3 mile ride with my dog was so much better than before! The bumps are much easier to ride over now and I came home without the dreaded bike "inner leg" pain. Bicycle shorts with the padding aren't even needed now and this seat provides a much more comfortable ride than padded bike shorts do with the stock seat. If you're thinking about getting a more comfortable seat and you're a larger person like me, you will NOT regret getting this for the price you pay for this... HIGHLY recommend this seat.

product_title: Coleman Back Home Instant Screenhouse
review_body:
This screened canopy is very well-constructed. The metal components are light but sturdy and the canopy has a silvery lining that makes it feel noticeably cooler under a hot sun. While one person can set this up, 2 or 3 people will make it much faster and easier and put less strain on the structure during assembly or take-down.

The screen is applied separately and if bugs are not an issue it can be left off. If the screen is installed, the zipper closures on the screen work but are slow to open and close. I chose to hand-stitch a magnetically-closing screen (AKA "Magic Mesh") into the opening, leaving the zipper unzipped. This makes entry and exit as simple as walking in or out--important if you are carrying a tray with both hands.

Be sure to anchor the legs with the provided stakes. The structure is very light and it will blow over and be damaged if not secured.

review_body:
I received this product at a discounted rate in exchange for an honest review.

I just received my headlamp and I'm super excited. I went camping earlier this year and everyone had their own headlamps, except for me. The package itself can be held in the palm of your hand. Inside it comes a carry bag, three triple A batteries and the headlamp itself. What I like most about the headlamp is the ability to have he headpiece shine down and not just always forward (see photo). I find this option super useful. I'm not sure if the package came with directions but there are two buttons on the top. The right (if from wearing on head) is for the bright led lights. It has about 3 or 4 options. Going from brightest, to bright, dim, and blinking. The left button is the red light and I think has only 2 options- red light and red blinking light. I really like that there are many options for the light. The brightest feature is super blinding for others (I shinned it at my bf and he confirmed). I like the red light as its dim but still gives you some light. I'm still trying to figure if I like how the headlamp lighting works I the sense that it gives of a general light and then in the center is a spotlight that shines brighter (see my photo for explaination as I'm not describing it properly). I guess I would like it to be a universal even shine.

I took lots of photos in the dark and not in the dark. In the photos I have a photo in the dark with the lamp off and then with the led and red lights on for comparison.

product_title: Xtreme Bright Illumilock Blade Bike U-Lock (Inside 16cm x 7cm) Bicycle Headlight & Tail light Combination All-in-One
review_body:
When I first received this, I was disappointed, but it served my needs adequately. Barely 5 months later and the light portions are simply nonfunctional. The taillight may just have a bad battery. The headlight on the other hand is a disaster. First of all the mount is made up of two pieces, the mounting bracket that plugs into the light, and the mount with wraps around the bike. These two pieces are screwed together, and that screw comes loose, causing the headlight to flop around. And the screw is underneath the light so you have to remove it (with the key) in order to tighten the screw. It's not very convenient, so I end up letting it get pretty bad before I fix it. Also in this short amount of time the connection between the battery and the light has gone bad. The light flickers on and off (mostly off, momentarily being awoken from the dead by a sharp smack). On top of the original downfalls, I really regret buying this.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
I read the reviews that said it was small, but I was still shocked at how narrow the U is. I guess that is so the headlamp doesn't get crazy long, I see no other real reason why it couldn't be wider. Living in Oakland, I have to use two U-locks anyway, so I only use this one to lock my front wheel to the frame; while relying on another lock to secure my bike to a rack. The lights are nice a bright. The headlight is front facing only, it doesn't have any light on the sides like some other headlamps do. The taillight does have side visibility though. One strange thing I noticed is that I can not pull the key out of the headlight without securing it to the U/taillight, or it's mounting bracket. Not really a bad thing, as I usually don't remove my key from the lock while locking and unlocking anyway. The headlight mounting bracket is ok, but (for me at least) the taillight mounting bracket is completely useless. Firstly, it is flimsy plastic (the headlight bracket is also plastic), such that the light flops around and I can actually pull the U out of the bracket without pressing the release button, totally insecure. Secondly, the angle and size does not fit on my bike, so even if it wasn't insecure, I wouldn't be able to use the bracket on my bike. Instead I have it clamped in to my spring loaded rear rack, this makes the position of the button for the taillight on the bottom of the light, less than ideal. This mounting itself is less than ideal, with the vibration from riding switching the button to turn the light off. All that said, this lock/light combo still does the job for me.d I can actually pull the U out of the bracket without pressing the release button, totally insecure. review_headline: What You Should Know Before You Buy!
review_body:
I was provided a BUBM Portable EVA Travel Organizer Case (Black, Medium) for testing and review and was asked only to give my honest review, so this is what I found.

What You Should Know Before You Buy:
♦ Zippered case that is made for carrying lots of small electronics and cables in an organized manner with several different elastic loops.

♦ I chose the Medium sized case and it was able to hold a ton of items including a large 14000mAh Power Bank.

♦ Not just for electronics. Great for just about any small items that you need to keep organized.

Conclusion:
Overall, this was a great organizer case. It has a single zipper and a separator flap inside with several strong elastic loops. It worked great for storing and securing a bunch of electronics. My girls and I went on an all day trip to run around with the grandparents this past weekend. They both have gotten into (obsessed) with Minecraft on their iPad Minis. Unfortunately, that game just kills battery life, so I needed some backup for them since they like to play in the car. I grabbed this case to give it a try. I was pleased to see that it fit a pretty large power bank perfectly ([[ASIN:B00G0NXUKI Floureon 14000mAh Power Bank]]) along with a couple of Lightning cables on one side of the flap and several additional items on the other side. It was the perfect grab-and-go case to organize small electronics. I plan to use it as my grab-and-go case on my next flight for work. I always have a single bag where I put everything I need for a flight. I like to get to my seat and pull a single item out of my carry-on before storing so I am not fumbling around with stuff and blocking traffic of people boarding. This is perfect for that. Easily fits a power bank, ear buds, cables, pen, small notepad, mints, gum, etc. Really any small items you would need for a flight in package small enough to fit in a seat-back pocket. The build seems good and the zipper works smoothly. product_title: Coleman Green Valley Cool Weather Sleeping Bag
review_headline: Really great price, quality is average but more than worth the cost.
review_body:
Great price. Average quality.
The stitching is coming loose on some of the quilting on this after only a few nights of use. This won't affect its usefulness unless more comes out and it starts shifting around.
It has no pamphlet or instructions so I'm still not sure what the little pocket inside is for. The other features I had to figure out through trial and error.
It has toggles and loops to hold the sleeping bag together in half when you roll it up which keeps the layers from slipping as you do it.

The strings to tie it/wrap around it when rolled up were hard to figure out. We had to re-roll the thing 4 times until we found the right direction to fold and roll it to make the strings work right. I imagine this would get easier with practice but it probably won't be used often enough for us to remember.

It does not roll up very small. We are thinking of getting a compression sack but since you can't store a bag in those long-term we probably won't. Just something to keep in mind.

Even with the few issues, it is worth the price! We will only need it for sleepovers or summertime car camping where we won't need to carry a ton of gear and it won't be very cold at night. Most sleeping bags cost $50-$70 and for our needs, that was just too much for what we wanted out of a bag. This will fit our son's needs perfectly and was his favorite color too!

product_title: EcoCity Lightweight Multipurpose Packable Daypack(Trip,Hiking,Camping,Sports)
review_headline: The EcoCity is an ultra-cool, self-contained day bag to carry along all those extras ...
review_body:
There are a lot of really cool, interesting items out lately and the EcoCity backpack / daypack is one of them. It’s not a heavyweight canvas, but rather like a really tough, lightweight nylon. If you have a heavy-duty windbreaker, the material is similar, but ultimately much more durable. It has what’s called a “ripstop” material, a pattern that has a tight weave and deters a sharp instrument or edge from penetrating the material. I’m sure there are exceptions, but this is some durable.

The size of the EcoCity is about the size of a small first aid kit, but once I pulled the backpack out of the back and filled it, it was hard to imagine it coming out of such a compact compartment. The backpack, when folded, has actually been tucked into part of it’s own structure. It starts out compact, but ends up being a great little bag that can hold quite a bit of stuff. I do like the compact nature because I’ll probably toss this into the trunk of my vehicle for when it’s needed.

It’s very well-made and everything about it spells quality. There’s not a stitch out of place and I expect this bag to last for a long time. The zippers are synthetic, slide easily, there’s sturdy piping, a loop on the outside to attach a carbiner to if you’d like, and it’s water-resistant. If there’s a heavy downpour, I do believe the EcoCity will keep my electronics safe until I can get to shelter. I tested the bag by putting it under a stream of water and it simply beaded off.

The EcoCity is more like a daypack, a perfect one for toting around those items you’ll need for the day. If you’re forever forgetting your reusable shopping bags, you could possibly add the this very handy to your repertoire. If you’re going to need more carrying room when you get to your destination, simply toss it in your backpack, suitcase, or vehicle. It’s going to take me a bit to learn how to fold it back up, but I don’t think the process will take all that long. Awesome little pack!

product_title: JOTO Universal Waterproof Case CellPhone Clear Dry Bag for Apple iPhone 6S 6,6S Plus, 7 SE 5S, Samsung Galaxy S6, Note 5 4, HTC LG Sony Nokia Motorola up to 6.0" diagonal
review_headline: Waterproof, solid seams, great locking mechanism.
review_body:
I was proved a sample for evaluation and here are my thoughts:

First off, it's a PERFECT fit for the Note 4 (in a phone case). I've tried a few similar cases and none fit just right (far too big or a smidge too small), this one fit like a glove. I've attached a picture for your reference.

I've done a little testing with the case and it's quite waterproof as advertised. Filled it with paper, put it in a cargo pocket on my swim shorts and went swimming with the kids. After an hour of diving in the pool, throwing the kiddos and general roughhousing the paper was removed bone dry.

I've used other waterproof cases and this one is a bit different in the way it locks down. The others used a twist lock that weren't as solid as the lever type lock this case uses. Feels much less likely to accidentally come open.

The case has a bit of black piping around the bottom and sides that adds a better feel than cases that are just sealed flat. Not sure if it adds any integrity to the strength but it does feel better in the hand.

The only issue was the included lanyard is junk, I pulled on it to test it's strength and it fell right apart with no effort. If you're planning on keeping it around your neck get a better lanyard.

So far, this is the best waterproof dry bag/case I've tried and am thankful for the free sample. I would recommend it.

The down side to me is the concave seems too deep in my opinion. I haven't measured but it is much more than my Sector 9 Barge and more than my Landyachtz Osteon Billy Bones model board. review_headline: Dangerous  ... both tires exploded en route from gas station,  Terrible customer support.
review_body: I purchased the Glide Go Glider Balance Bike for my 5 year old son.  When the bike arrived both tires were flat.  I assembled the bike and aired the tires 2 blocks from home.  On the way home both tires exploded in my trunk.  Both my son and I were disappointed when we open the trunk to see both tires flat and pieces of the plastic rims broken off.  Instead of sending back to Amazon, I called Glide Bikes customer support to see if I can get the tires replaced.  Instead  I was asked to send pictures of the "damage".  What damage? The tires exploded ... not one but "both of them!!!"  My son hadn't even ridden the bike and yet they wanted pictures of the damages instead of just sending the tires and rims,  I ordered the product for next day delivery and now Glide Bikes wanted me to waste time taking pictures of the proposed "damage" and send to them.  I guess I blew out the tires on purpose because maybe I didn't like them and wanted new ones. By the way, thank God my son was NOT riding the thing when the tires exploded.  If you purchase the bike and need to air the tires, who knows how much to put in the tires before they explode because there's not documentation on how much air is required.  As a seasoned cyclist, I had an idea on how much air to put in the tires and yet the tires exploded.  I'm giving a 1 star because the potential danger of the tire blowing while children are riding and the terrible customer support from the company.

product_title: Morakniv Allround Multi-Purpose Fixed Blade Knife with Carbon Steel Blade
review_body:
I got a new girlfriend and her name is Mora!
With 45 years experience fishing and camping behind me, I can honestly say that no knife has ever made me happier...and I haven't even had a chance to use this one yet...lol. The sheer quality and simplicity leaves me zero doubt that this knife will last me the rest of my life or until I lose it. If one appreciates simplicity of form, functionality, and a nice sharp edge, one will immediately fall in love with this blade. I am NOT a "knife guy" . I am a professional chef and avid outdoorsperson with a strong appreciation of well made tools, and this knife is exactly that. I returned a defective Bear Grylls Gerber folder that did not meet my very realistic expectations and decided to just give in and finally tryout a Morakniv fixed blade with my credit from Amazon. Even though it is a very different beast, I am extremely happy with putting this knife into duty as my primary camp knife.
After receiving my 5.8" carbon steel Mora, I immediately took a few pics, cleaned the blade with acetone, and proceeded to put a "forced patina" on it with an 8 minute soak in some hot white vinegar. A thorough rinsing and cleaning with a soft cloth and a light rub with mineral oil, and my knife was ready for use. The simple task of bias slicing a few pan seared 1.75 inch thick prime rib-eye and strip steaks for dinner tonight will be a fine initiation for it.
The knife came razor sharp and I will admit that the vinegar soak reduced that sharpness just a bit, so others should be aware of this if they plan to do an acid soak on their own knives(which I still highly suggest). I plan on touching up the edge with just a few strokes on a diamond stone and then a quick wipe with room temp vinegar on the new sharp edge. EDIT: Before forcing a patina on this blade I searched online hard for any info regarding how this might effect the sharpness of the edge and if a sharpening would be required after theprocess. I could find no definitive statements on the matter, other than a warning not to soak too long in hot straight vinegar as it could eventually eat away the entire blade. Despite my earlier statement that the edge was slightly dulled to the touch after the process, I am very happy to report that I did NOT have to lay this knife against a sharpening stone to restore its original razor sharp edge. All that was required was to use this knife very briefly(cutting steaks as mentioned below) and I was surprised to find that was enough to hone the edge halfway back to its original state. Seeing(and feeling) that, I stropped it against my blue jeans on my thigh(very,very carefully) for about fifteen seconds to get it all the way back to its razor edge. I am already planning on getting Morakniv carbon 4.1" Robust and 8" multi-purpose knives as well as a stainless filet knife, and the Morakniv camp axe is on my list too! I don't plan on becoming a "knife guy", but I can definitely say that getting my Mora cherry popped has already made me a Morakniv guy...lol.
The body of the sheath itself is also fantastic. The knife slips in smoothly with the blade stored without contacting the interior and it is very well retained. It sets into place with a comforting snug but easy fit and great haptic feedback letting you know it is in its final safe resting position. The belt loop is black leather and how well this piece of the package holds up is the only thing that will be a question for time and use to answer. I treated the small soft leather loop first with a small amount of neatsfoot oil, and once that was fully absorbed, I wiped up any excess and put on a final treatment of Sno-Seal beeswax gently melted in with the help of a hair dryer. I don't care if I look silly tonight, but I'm putting away my Chinese chef's knife(my daily use all around kitchen knife) and will be putting my new toy through its paces.
Here are some baby pics for y'all to enjoy.
Pics of knife in original state, after vinegar soak, and then lightly oiled. Rated hard R, sexy.

product_title: Zackees LED Turn Signal Gloves for Cycling with Spare Rechargeable Batteries + Charger
review_headline: Important SAFETY ACCESSORY for bicyclists - espeically commuters and urban riders!
review_body: Zackees provided a pair of these gloves in exchange for an unbiased review.  These gloves are an excellent safety accessory - especially for those who commute or ride in an urban environment like I do. (Dallas, Texas)  Operating the gloves: When you move your thumb to make contact, the arrow flashes very brightly. I had a friend follow me in his car and the flashing arrows are easily seen in bright sunlight, and at night.  It took riding a few times with them to get used to signaling a left turn with the left hand and a right turn with the right hand. It's easy to learn to use them without thinking about it - which is important when riding in traffic. You don't want to have to think about what you're doing. After riding for a few hours with them, I was signaling and activating the arrows automatically without thinking about it.  The arrows activate reliably every time and you don't have to look to see if the signal activated. (This was a BIG problem with the Ohuhu and Joyiqi gloves which I am also reviewing here on Amazon.)  The Zackees gloves are designed so you can signal with your hand up to alert cars behind you and with your hands on the handlebars to alert cars in front. Being able to sginal with your hands on the handlebars is especially  useful to alert oncoming traffic when making a left hand turn.  The gloves are washable, but I haven't washed mine yet, so I can't comment on how well they will hold up in a washing machine.  I can tell you this: I took these gloves to Fran, the owner of Transit Bicycle Company in Dallas, Texas. I asked him what he thought about the quality of the gloves. He wears the same glove size, so he was able to try them out. I thought the Zackees were well-made. Fran agreed and said they are on par with the other premium bicycling gloves he sells. Transit Bicycle Company specializes in commuter and city bikes and accessories. Fran also agreed with me that these are a useful safety accessory and pointed out that the gloves would be much more effective than bicycle mounted turn signals because you can put your hand up so that drivers who wouldn't see a bicycle mounted turn signal would see them. Additionally, the arrows are nice and large - which works perfectly on the back of your hand, while similarly large arrows would be bulky and clumsy if mounted on the bike.  Everyone in the store thought the gloves were "cool".  I received the gloves and the rechargeable batteries with charger. For those of us who are concerned about the environment, this is important. The only other turn-signal glove on the market has a built-in battery and the gloves must be discarded when the batteries run-down. The only complaint I have is that the charger has two lights, but no explanation of what they do. I inserted the batteries in the charger and one light came on flashing red. I expected both lights to come on (one per battery, like my other battery charger). It turns out that when the batteries are fully charged, the second light comes on (green) to indicate that the batteries are fully charged. It works GREAT once you understand how the lights work on the charger.  I compared these gloves to the Joyiqi / Ohuhu turn signal gloves manufactured by Gaciron. The Joyiqi, Ohuhu, and Gaciron are the same glove with different branding. Please check out my review of the Joyiqi and Ohuhu gloves, which I believe are a safety hazard.

product_title: Cobblestone Mini Ultra Bright LED Lantern – Best Portable Camping Light!! [ Flameless Candle ] Perfect for Camping, Hiking, Climbing, Boy Scout and More!
review_headline: A powerful little lantern that really delivers on its promises
review_body:
The ShuoFang Cobblestone Ultra Bright LED Lantern is an impressive little multi-purpose household lantern. It's small (about the size of an orange) but mighty. Inside the box came a nice user manual and three AAA batteries, so I could begin using the lantern right away. I love it when manufacturers supply the battery - it's the sign of a conscientious company. The lantern is also resistant to dampness like splashes, so if you're camping and it's raining, it reassures that the lantern is durable. It was so easy to activate, that my 9 year old grandson installed the batteries himself. Made with a combination of polycarbonate and rubberized plastic, this lantern is light and attractive. There is a hook at the top that will allow the user to hang it, or it folds into the lantern so you can set it on a table top or chair or other hard surface. You can easily toss it into a bag or purse or the glove compartment of your car should you ever need it in an emergency.

What is truly amazing is the fact that such a small lantern can shed such a powerful light. It is an LED light which can be adjusted in strength. Depending on how bright you set it, the lantern will run between 10 to 160 hours. I have used this to read at night, or for extra light when working in the kitchen. It also makes an amazing little emergency light during power failures. It even comes with a 3 year warranty.

In summary, this is an incredible little lantern that is not only attractive, but really does all that it promises. Long lasting, durable, splash resistance, and with a multitude of uses beyond camping, I highly recommend this quality product. I am very, very impressed!

review_body:
Nothing says “cool” like wearing the Sturgeon Men's polarized square aluminum at night. Not only do you feel like a rock star but look like one also. I sport these bad boys and you don’t know if I just dropped my debut album or I’m guarding the president. I could bust out break dancing to New Kids On the Block or put on a butt whupping exhibition.

1) You run into things. Put a rubber band around your head to hold glasses on when you fall down. If you are husky like me then kneepads help with falling also. Or you could just walk around with outstretched arms like a blind man. But that just looks dumb. Go with rubber band on head and kneepads.

3) Eye hand control. If you try to shake hands with a guy and miss, you touch his junk. BAD things happen after that. If you try to high five and miss then you hit your own junk. Just as bad.

Final tip: Couple this with a baseball cap worn sideways to increase coolness factor. Mine has a little propeller on it. UBER COOL! Like level 57 Dungeons and Dragons cool. Yeah…. I just said that.

product_title: Rollerblade Spitfire XT Adjustable Kids Inline Skates
review_headline: They run narrow and maybe a bit short.  Order accordingly.
review_body:
My son wears a US size 2 sneaker, so he tried on the size 2-5. According to the size printout in the package, his foot comfortably should have fit into a size 2. He was complaining the size 2-5 were too tight, so we extended the size from 2 to 3. Still too tight. So we extended to the 4. Still tight. Hmmm. We then went to the size 5-8, set it for size 5. I visually couldn't tell the difference between the length of the size 5 and the length of the size 4. However, the size 5-8 pair looked obviously wider all around, roomier in the front and ball of the foot in particular. Well, at size 5 they fit perfectly, no complaints from him. I was easily able to get the ankle snug enough so they don't wobble.

I have to say I'm quite pleased that he can start with these at the bottom of their range, rather than start at the top end of the smaller size. But for ordering online or not being able to try them on, just assume they run very small. In particular, they have a narrow/small toe box. It's also important to note that they don't adjust in width, only in length.

I have yet to see how he actually performs in them. He has only just tried them on at the store. Will report back with anything unusual.

While I rarely use flashlights – the DH keeps 2 or 3 in his work kit – as he uses them frequently. Compared to his current favorite (900 lumens, waterproof casing) this light feels sturdy, solid and is about the same weight, length (about 7” fully extended) and diameter.

Positives:

uses 3 AAA batteries or one 18650 we use rechargeable batteries and the light was full strength for several days with repeated use.

Solid-feeling construction, easy to manipulate

decent battery life, bright control (on.off) button

Negatives: lanyard cord connection TO flashlight feels as if the threading (actual connection from light to strap) is not as durable – feels like fishing line, so expect that the strength is there – but would have preferred either aluminum clip or lanyard threading with strap materials to make it feel more substantial

overall: a good value for the money, and well worth the investment in rechargeable 18650 batteries – be sure to use with enclosed plastic cylinder to eliminate the ‘rattle’ and secure the connection

product_title: Kelty Mistral 20-Degree Right Hand Sleeping Bag
review_body:
Bought two of these so at a local store for camping with scouts and YMCA activities. We finally got to try them out at a YMCA outing where the temps got down to about 40F at night sleeping in a cabin.

I wore shorts and a t-shirt to sleep and was very comfortable. I went to sleep with it a little more than halfway zipped. During the middle of the night I woke up a bit chilled and zipped it up almost completely and cinched it around my head. I woke up a few hours later too warm. A minor adjustment and I was good to go.

Things Daddy Likes:

- The velcro tab at the neck that allows you to keep the bag close around you but allows you to leave it partially unzipped to avoid overheating
- I'm not a small person (260+) and the bag had more room than I expected. Enough that I could shift comfortably and constricting enough to position my arms well for sleep.
- The pillow pocket. I stuffed a camp pillow in it with a little something to give it more cushion and it kept the pillow in place all night despite my rolling around.

Things Daddy Finds Less Than Perfect

- Tough to stuff back into its sack. I suppose I will get better with practice.
- Sack does not have compression straps
- Bag does not compress very well

Given the price point (I paid $68 for one) the above three points are nitpicks. We aren't hardcore campers or backpackers, so the above points shouldn't really be too big an issue for us.

product_title: Ritchey Snap-On Bicycle Rim Tape
review_headline: They can cause inner tube failure.
review_body: Revised rating from my original five stars.   I had two brand new Serfas thorn resistant inner tubes fail shortly after installation. The culprit: These rim strips. Their stiffer construction and slightly wider footprint actually caused friction against the inner tube. The first inner tube failure was a 1/2 inch tear near the inner rim. I thought I had a defective inner tube with a weak spot and installed a new inner tube. Two days later, failure again. This time, not only a small split, but a progressive cut forming in excess of four inches in line with the rim strips. This happened on the rear tire which carries a heavier load. There's no question in my mind that it would be only a matter of time before the front inner tube suffers the same type of failure. Back to the older type of rim strips.   Original review:   I didn't have any difficulty installing them as some have said, you just have to pull it a bit to get it over the rim. I think it's actually better because then it's really making a solid contact. What I found helpful was after they were installed, I took a semi-wide flat head screwdriver and placed it under the edge of the rim and lifted the strip up. Then, slide the screwdriver under it so only the round shaft made contact between the strip and the wheel. I pulled the screwdriver continually around the rim. It it allowed the rim strip to fit perfectly centered. It's also a very easy way to realign the valve opening on the strip with the rim valve opening.

product_title: Coleman Retro Rechargeable Battery Powered Lantern (Family Size)
review_body:
My first impressions:
When I took the lantern out of the box, my first word was... WOW! This is a piece of art. The red color reminded me of a Ferrari, so the title Ferrari of lanterns. It looks great on my desk. I will buy one more to keep on my office desk just to impress my colleagues :)

My first instinct was to unscrew the fuel cap. And yes it did unscrew and opened. There is a plug inside that you can unscrew as well and opens a hole. Hmm... "Fancy, but looks real..." I said to myself and screwed them back in. Turned the light on and VOILA! There was LIGHT! Yes, the battery came charged. (QUICK TIP: Charge for 18 hours for the first 3 cycles.)

There are 3 modes :
NIGHT LIGHT: Lights a dim greenish yellow light on the fuel cap. The plug I mentioned earlier is actually a bulb :)
HIGH : Lights the fluorescent bulb at high. (*Runtime up to 6 Hrs.)
LOW: Lights the flourescent bulb at low. (*Runtime up to 9 Hrs.)
* Printed on the box

Charging:
A 12 volt cord with a mini cigarette lighter plug is stored on the bottom inside.
A 120 volt charger is included. (does not fit inside lantern)
There is red LED indicator that glows while charging.
NOTE: The lantern will not light while charging. But the Night Light works.

About the people who are complaining that the lantern stopped working, you should understand how a lead-acid battery works.
Simple rule of thumb: DO NOT LEAVE THE LANTERN DISCHARGED FOR AN EXTENDED PERIOD OF TIME. This applies to all lead-acid batteries.

READ THE INSTRUCTION MANUAL.:
"Do not leave the lantern turned on after the battery has stopped, as overdischarging the battery can cause problems in recharging the battery to a full charge. If this occur, immediately switch the lantern off and recharge for 40 hours. After an extended period of storage (more than 6 months) recharge for the full 16 hours or more"

Final words: I bought this lantern for two purposes.
1. For my tent during camping.
2. Turn off all electrical lights in my room, turn on the Coleman lantern on my desk, read a book, switch off and go to bed, Good Night!!!

And it serves me well.l words: I bought this lantern for two purposes.

review_body:
Having not had a bike for the past seven or so years, i was looking to get back into the habit of riding to and from work and around town. For a commuter bike, this fits the bill perfectly.

Installation: The bike arrived packaged properly and i was able to put it together relatively easily. I did adjust the brakes a bit and of course filled up the tires, but other than that the bike was pretty much good to go.

Ride Comfort/Performance: I was surprised that the seat was fairly comfortable (for a stock seat) and the gears shifted smoothly. The bike runs fast and smooth! I am able to go up a somewhat steep incline no problem and I love to coast on this bike as well.

Overall i would recommend this bike if you are looking to get back into riding a bike, but without spending a fortune. I think that for the money, this bike is well built and comfortable.

product_title: US GI Military Original Issue E-Tool Entrenching Shovel
review_body:
This is a phenomenal tool for camping and in my opinion, a must have for any wilderness adventure.
I just returned from a four day fishing and backcountry hiking trip in the Adirondacks. With 50+ lbs of gear and a canoe over a 4 mile hike, I was hesitant to bring this along due to the extra weight. Showing up at the trailhead with this beast garnered more than a few laughs from my buddies. By the end of the trip, they were thanking me for bringing this along.
This has been written about in many reviews, but the strength and versatility of this e-tool is amazing.
Throughout our trip, we used this for clearing heavy rocks from our firepit, stoking our fires, clearing branches from firewood logs, leveling our tent sites and most importantly, digging latrines for proper waste handling. There are some great reviews on Youtube about this tool, but the fact that the spade head pivots securely to 90 degrees allowed us to use it as a seat for a makeshift toilet and for lounging around the campfire. To my knowledge, this is one of the only if not the only e-tool that has this feature. Pivoting less than 90 degrees also enables you to use it as a grappling hook, perfect for fastening it to rope to assist in setting up your bearbags. If it's good enough for our US Military, it is certainly good enough for me, but I highly recommend having this on any outdoor adventure.

product_title: Stainless Steel 304 Spring Snap Hook Carabiner with Screw Lock, 2 1/4 Inch -Set of 4
review_body: Although carabiners are one of the primary tools of trade in climbing, they have a wide variety of uses they can be used for outside of climbing. Such is the case for this STAINLESS STEEL 304 SPRING SNAP HOOK CARABINER WITH SCREW LOCK SET. There are some carabiners that are sold that are not designed to actually carry any weight. That isn’t the case with these carabiners. However, these carabiners are not designed to carry people. Instead, these are carabiners that a person might use to help carry equipment (they should hold up to about 100 lbs of weight). Besides using these carabiners to lift equipment, some other ways they can also be used include as a latch (instead of a lock) to keep a tool box shut, to attach a waterbottle or camera case to a backpack, as part of a dog leash, and as a key chain. These carabiners are slightly better than the spring snap hook carabiners without a screw lock: the screw lock adds a small, but important level of safety to the carabiner. Overall, the STAINLESS STEEL 304 SPRING SNAP HOOK CARABINER WITH SCREW LOCK SET is a nice set of 4 carabiners that can be used for a myriad of purposes. I was provided a sample of this item from the manufacturer for examination and possible review.

product_title: Black Diamond Neutrino Carabiner, Purple
review_headline: Lots of value for the money.
review_body: This is about 3 inches long, light, and has a strong wire gate.  I own about a dozen locking carabiners (some costing far more than this one) and many small $1 "toy biners" that I use when camping. This may be the best of both worlds.  Unless you want a locking carabiner for safety, or a steel carabiner to attach to metal, this is strong enough (24kN) for climbing, but light and inexpensive enough for general use.  It is overkill for a key ring, but a perfect choice for any camping use where strength is required.  While the $1 biners have their place (where strength is meaningless), spending a "few dollars more" means having a carabiner that is unlikely to fail.  I certainly would not use this towing a car, but strong enough for nearly any general task.  For hanging a hammock or a "bear bag", this thing is the way to go.

I know - you're not supposed to drop your flashlight, but I use mine several times every day, usually while on a concrete floor, and it gets dropped.  So this is about the 4th small flashlight I've wrecked by dropping it.  The first two were by another manufacturer, and the second two were by Olight.  So I just ordered an Elzetta A-113.  The Elzetta light is about 3X the cost, but I'm going broke replacing $50 flashlights.  From every review I've read and watched, the Elzetta lights are indestructible.  I have a two cell Elzetta mounted on a 12 GA shotgun, and it has never failed.  Hopefully the A-113 will be just as tough.  If you don't drop the S10R, it's a great little light.

product_title: OGIO Gambit 17 Laptop Backpack
review_headline: OGIO Gambit 17 versus OGIO Renegade RSS
review_body:
I purchased both the OGIO Gambit 17 and the OGIO Renegade RSS so I could compare them in person. The are nearly identical with respect to the pockets. I noticed three main differences:

1) The Renegade has a tighter weave than the Gambit. I think the Renegade looks nicer (higher quality) when viewed next to the Gambit, but by itself the Gambit still looks nice. Both seem to be good quality and should last a long time, although due to the tighter weave the Renegade might be slightly higher quality.

2) The Gambit does not have as much padding in the laptop compartment compared to the Renegade. I considered this negligible in my comparison, because the Gambit is (IMHO) well-padded-- just less so than the Renegade. Unless you are unusually rough on your belongings, the Gambit's padding should be more than enough.

3) The zipper on the Renegade's laptop compartment only goes down about 20% of the height of the pocket. I have a 13" laptop and because it is fairly small, it does not fill up the entire pocket. I have to reach deep into the pocket to pull my laptop out, which is extremely difficult because it's a narrow pocket and it hardly unzips. The Gambit's design differs in that the pocket unzips all the way to the bottom; you can open the pocket completely. That makes it a breeze to get laptops in and out.

Difference #3 was a deal breaker for me. It made my decision to keep the Gambit and return the Renegade an easy one.

UPDATE (7/4/15): I've been using this backpack for a couple months now and love it. A few things to note:
1) When packed about 80% full, it fits under the seat of a small airplane (CRJ900). It would probably fit when fully packed.
2) The one thing I dislike about it is that I like to keep my keys, wallet, phone, etc. (i.e. stuff I want quick and easy access to) in the front pocket so I can keep the backpack on one shoulder and swing it around for access. The front pocket goes up a bit higher than on my previous backpacks and it's difficult for me to unzip it while wearing the pack.
3) There are so many pockets in this backpack that it's easy to lose things. On the other hand, it's really easy to keep things organized.igher than on my previous backpacks and it's difficult for me to unzip it while wearing the pack.

product_title: Sea to Summit Coolmax Adaptor Traveller Liner
review_headline: Excellent for abroad travel in hot and chilled conditions.
review_body:
First, I am giving this item 4 stars only because there is a smell associated with the insect repellent. However to combat this I left the liner hanging out for a week in my office and then when packing it for my trip I sprinkled lavender oil all over the liner before stuffing it. This helped somewhat as my husbands bag (who didn't do anything for the smell) was noticeably smellier than mine.

The liner itself is amazingly soft at the end of the day. We were in rather hot weather (80-90 degrees at night) and in the northern highlands of Nicaragua, with some chilled weather (~60 degrees at night) and the liner was comfortable in both conditions. Even though it was uncomfortably hot at night, we were in some sketchy hostels that I preferred not to make skin contact with the mattress or sheets :-) and like the liner promises with the CoolMax technology it was great for both conditions.

As far as using it as a liner in my sleeping bag I cannot speak to that since I only used it as a liner.

I do not have have sensitive skin and did not have any reactions to the material nor to the insect repellant within the material. Though the thought of skin to insect repellant creeped me out because of the cautionary tale I just wore light pj's for the duration of usage. :-)

On the road it works well as an office. just open it up and set it down. Everything is within easy reach.  I have one of those business-class laptops- great for the road, but ridiculously bulky. the soft center panel accommodates and protects it with ease. My iPad can nestle up right next to it on the other side of a soft panel.  The corners have elastic, too, which means when you cinch down the top flap, it's basically waterproof. I have yet for rain to leak in, despite getting caught in a couple of showers.  The only improvement I'd make is to the strap. product_title: Burley Travoy Bike Trailer
review_headline: Awesome and unique product and a crowd pleaser as well :D
review_body:
Having never owned a bike trailer of any description, I literally read every review and blog related to the Travoy before I purchased this expensive item. I wanted to make sure it was the best option available for my needs, and after using it a couple of times, I think it definitely is. I just got back into cycling and converted my hybrid into an ebike. I chose the Travoy instead of investing in a rear rack and panniers. I just rode 50km yesterday and didn't have a problem with the Travoy, you really have to keep checking behind you or your shadow to make sure it is still there, as you don't even notice it. I have gone up and down curbs without any issues. It loses a star because the Tote bag can rub against the wheels if it is loaded with a wide item. I saw one guy create little cardboard side rails to protect the bag. Also, I believe all the market/transit bags are too expensive, especially because they are not waterproof. The way I have mine set up now, I have my old Osprey Atmos 35 backpack at the bottom of the Travoy, with the upper compression straps twisted around the metal of the travoy and then I buckle them. The aluminium back frame on some of the Osprey models are perfect for the Travoy, as the rigidity really helps it stay in place. If I need more storage, I can remove the Tote bag from inside the Atmos, and attach it to the top section so I easily have 75L of storage without spending a dollar on bags, but I will need to buy some rain covers.

Initially the quick release was really hard to use. I was really struggling to get it out the first few times. I used a little bit of chain oil to lube it up and now it is a breeze to unclip.

I also bought the Joubert Smart Bungee system thinking that would be needed to attach my Osprey (or larger Gregory Baltoro) but so far I haven't used them, but would recommend using your own bags and bungees as a good option instead of buying the expensive bags.

I wish there was some sort of security so you could leave it with your bike, but the beauty of the trailer is you can carry heavy chains with no problem. I bought an Abus 8KS Chain 8mmx110cm and while I haven't used it to secure the Travoy yet, I could easily loop it around the Travoy and my bike frame.

One day, I was only carrying a few things so I took the Atmos backpack on my back instead of the Travoy. It felt like such a hassle riding with a backpack, you lose a lot of freedom of movement. I really don't see myself riding much with a backpack again, taking the Travoy is so much easier.

The Travoy definitely gets noticed quite a bit, it is a conversation starter, as I think I am probably the only person in Melbourne, Australia with a Travoy. When the weather is better, I definitely see a first date involving bike rides and a picnic being lots of fun and easy to pull off :D

product_title: Schwinn 5 in 1 Floor Pump With Gauge
review_body:
I loved this pump from the moment I took it out of the box. It was packaged well and anything that could have come loose was zip tied together. I was a little concerned about issues with the pressure gauge as had been noted by another reviewer, but so far it's been nothing but perfect.

It's easily one of the most efficient and quick pumps I've ever had. It is designed well with a very large gauge and the rod comes back quite far. It takes pretty minimal effort to pump up my bike tires. I ride at around 80-85 psi, and it usually takes around 5 or 6 full pumps to get my tires from around 40 psi up to where I need them. So I'd say maybe count on 8 to 12 full pumps to fill a road bike tire from empty. It really doesn't require much strength or effort to push down, and given how far the rod comes out it really is a short process.

The base has plenty of room for your feet to stand comfortably and I really particularly like the fact that the tube clips into the handle which allows you to carry the pump by the handle without the rod extending out. Essentially by clipping the hose in, it locks the handle down. The head (or whatever you call it... the part that clips into the valve) is pretty large and feels solid. It isn't heavy at all, but gives a feeling of ruggedness. The little flip lever that locks the head onto the valve works perfectly. It locks on tight and holds without issue. The head also has little compartments built-in on either side to hold the ball needle and little cone shaped thingy which come with it. It's also got two holes; one for shrader valves and one for presta. The gauge goes up to 160. And the colors are exactly as shown.

I've only had the pump for about a week, so time will tell whether it holds up to my initial impressions, but so far I couldn't be happier with it. It feels superior to every other pump I've seen at this price point.

I'd definitely recommend scooping one of these bad boys up ASAP.

product_title: G4Free 130 PSI Bike Pump - Premium Portable Mini Bike Pump With Hidden Flexible Hose - Aluminum CNC Construction - For Mountain, Road Or BXM Bikes - Bike Frame Mounting Kit Included
review_headline: Lightweight Compact Pump Does a Fine Job Without Stressing Valve Stems
review_body:
After testing this pump on some bike tires, I visited a local outdoor sports store's bike department to compare this pump with other models. This pump, which was sent to me in exchange for an honest review, cost about half the price of most of the pumps in the store but appears to be just as well made. One small pump in the store had a pressure gauge, but most did not. This pump, of course, does not have a gauge.

Once the rubber end-cap is removed it exposes a knurled fitting that unscrews to release and extend a flexible hose. The hose is designed to fit the two most common valve stems on US bikes and enables operation of the pump without stressing or bending the bike's valve stem which is especially important with the more fragile 6mm Presta valve stems. Once the desired pressure is achieved, another twist releases pin pressure on an 8mm Schrader valve while the hose is still attached, so no air is lost when the hose is unscrewed from the valve stem. I really liked that clever feature.

This pump will obviously take more strokes to inflate a tire than a large upright hand pump, but the best pump is the one at hand. With the pump holder and pump mounted with two screws on the frame of the bike, this pump can always be ready to use. I was able to inflate my bike tires to their maximum working pressure without excessive effort. The included holder uses a heavy rubber strap to secure the pump. It is easy to attach and release. The pump is small enough to be packed in large jacket pocket or backpack when the bike is parked. Otherwise the pump would be easy pickings for a thief.

I was able to fit the tent back in the bag with a small amount of difficulty. Folded it longwise then folded it again to 1/2 that size where the length was the size of the bag then just rolled it over and inserted the accessories into the middle. product_title: Olight S10R II Baton rechargeable 500 Lumens CREE XP-L LED Flashlight EDC with RCR123 Li-ion battery , Charging Base and EdisonBright CR123A Lithium back-up Battery bundle
review_headline: Very satisfied. Works exactly as advertised
review_body:
Very satisfied. Works exactly as advertised. S10R is a great EDC light. It's the perfect balance of small and bright. The rechargeable battery is a HUGE plus as one of the most common flashlight problems is that it's always out of battery when you need it. The housing is tough and durable. The recharging platform is USB and micro USB so it can be daisy chained for your iPhone with one outlet. The bottom of the light is magnetic which can be used to secure it while on (like an open trunk while you dig around) or with another Olight baton battery extender for longer use. The clip is sub par. It's hard to use and it won't grab all of whatever material you're fastening to--but it's not terrible. In the box you get the light, normal battery, rechargeable battery, quality lanyard, and docking station and cable. Approx. run times are:

-"Starlight" .5 lumens for 136 hours
-5 lumens for 36 hours
-80 lumens for 3.5 hours
-400 lumens for 50 minutes

While 50 minutes is not an incredibly long time at full power, the reality is that most (not all, most) applications do not require longer than that (unless you are military or police). Additionally, the battery recharges so the light can be used at that power setting for 50 minutes daily without a problem as opposed to a light where the battery lasts longer but can't be recharged and you never know when it will burn out.

product_title: Light & Motion Taz 1200 Bike Light
review_headline: On-road/Off-road: bike and run at night just like you would during daytime
review_body:
Broad field of view, bright light, secure strap. NIGHT TIME TRAIL RUNNING: I can run over any terrain with this light. I wrap the strap around my middle finger and secure it as if on a handlebar, keeping the light clutched in my loosely closed hand. That's one advantage of the rubber strap mechanism, in contrast to other mfr's that use a multi-positionable-swiveling clamp mount: you have to hold those lights tightly, but the TAZ strap stays secure in your palm without having to clench your hand. BIKING: ON-ROAD, even where there is no ambient light, I can still bomb down hills at 45 mph with the same confidence as during the daytime. OFF-ROAD: same confidence level (no, I don't ride 45 mph off road). The broad field of view lets me see beyond the edges of the trail (& any glowing coyote eyes in the brush) and far enough ahead so I don't need to change my speed as with other, less intense lights.

NOTE: the comments about the strap being unsecure likely result from the user not reading the instruction manual. As you can see from the picture, the strap must wrap around the bar, then up and over the clip; you should pull the rubber strap tightly to get engage the hole furthest from the end of the strap; if properly attached, the light is extremely secure and allows the rider to firmly push the control buttons to change the intensity of the light as needed to conserve battery life. At full power, the light lasts for more than 90 minutes; several hours at low power.

COMPLAINTS: I wish the battery pack was ejectable so I could keep an extra, charged battery with me to swap out.

We were initially looking into the single speed version of this bike (22lbs), which was almost the same weight as the Brompton, but decided to go with this because the single speed had coaster brakes. We can now fit this bike along with the Citizen Tokyo and another kids bike (non-folding) into the trunk of our 99' Rav4!  Pros: * Lighter than Citizin Tokyo * Easy to fold * Very good ride quality * Gears shift well * Very well made seat, which is relatively comfortable * Solid construction * Very reasonably priced. product_title: Twin Sized SoundAsleep Dream Series Air Mattress with ComfortCoil Technology & Internal High Capacity Pump
review_body:
The mattress is marvelous! They are all they are claimed to be online as the "best of the best". I bought two to replace my old and very expensive Thermopedic, just to try out whether I wanted to shift to a Sleep Number "glorified air mattress" type bed, and because I could use them for my family's visits after my "experiment". I had noticed that when I stayed at my sisters' homes and slept on their air mattresses, (for at least 2 -3 weeks at a time), I never woke up with a back ache, as I was on my Thermopedic. So I decided on this little experiment. I achieved amazingly restful sleep with no back pain upon awakening! I found the quality of your mattress outstanding! It held the air almost perfectly and to the extent it needed slight topping off, I am sure it was due to temperature changes in my Florida condo from outside air to air conditioning, ( I know that can account for density of molecules). The built in inflating mechanism with just a dial and the speed with which it inflates and deflates is nothing short of stunning to behold for this old, experienced camper and traveler. The height is perfect, the top flocking is wonderful, and made up, it feels like a "real" bed that I will never feel that I have to apologize for to my overnight guests.
So, overall, I give these excellent air mattresses (I bought two!), a FIVE STAR Rating on all counts. I have one suggestion, however, for improvement: they could use handles!

product_title: Victorinox - Forester Swiss Army Knife (Black) 083633
review_headline: Good Size, Excellent Selection Of Useful Implements
review_body:
During a 1998 trip to Switzerland had Swiss fondue at a sidewalk café, bought Swiss cheese, Swiss chocolate, Black Death cigarettes, and a Swiss Army knife just like this but with the red scales instead of black.

As I recall, I paid more for it in Swiss Francs at an official Victorinox sales outlet than Amazon has it listed for here.

All the other items are but a fond memory, but this knife soldiers on.

I carry this knife all the time, so much so that the painted-on shield with Swiss cross has long since worn off. If I have my pants on, this knife is in my left-hand front pocket.

I like the larger size; it feels more secure in my hand, and I particularly like the locking main blade - it's not going to close until I want it to.

I've used every implement a zillion times and they all work well. I'm not crazy about the can opener, though it does open cans just fine. But ... as if to make up for the less-than-ideal can opener, those clever Swiss included an implement that lets you OPEN WINE!

I don't have occasion to use the corkscrew as often as I did when I was in Europe, but I like to use it just because whenever I have a bottle of wine with an actual cork instead of a twist-off aluminum cap.

If you could only have one pocket knife, this would be the one to have.

product_title: Energy by Optimus Gas
review_headline: Works as well as it could
review_body:
This is a review of Energy by Optimus Gas, 8oz.

My recently acquired ultralight camping stove needed some fuel so I decided to give this a try.

Perfect.

I have used this in temperatures as low as 40 degrees and it works reliably. Since the stove has a big part in how you might assess fuel, it's difficult to say whether everyone will have the same experience using this. All I can say is that my stove which has a 1' hose/valve connected to the fuel perfectly. I got a consistent burn no matter what flame height I was using. Compared to some other fuels, this seemed reasonably priced. Based on my experience with this so far, I'd definitely buy again. My preference is to buy the 8 oz containers rather than the larger sizes. I'd rather carry several smaller canisters and distribute them among the camping party than just have one or two bigger canisters. In case there is a problem with one of them, I figure it's better to have a backup or two. You do have to buy from the right seller to get the best pricing.

product_title: Adventure Two Pot Prep + Cook Set
review_headline: Compact kit that stows your cook needs in one place
review_body:
I can't say enough about this nesting system. When you open it for the first time and you see sitting right beneath the lid a tri-fold cutting board/serving platter, you know this is a company who thinks of everything!

Not to be confused with other Stanley models, this item includes two nested pots with lids and flip down latching handles, the cutting board, two large bowls, two large vented lids for those bowls that double as very small plates, and the most ingenious interlocking ladle and spatula I've ever seen.

The entire setup is incredibly sturdy. There was nothing about any of the components that looked like they could have been better quality or would easily break. Unlike my inexpensive aluminum mess kits, these don't give the impression that they'll scratch or dent easily. The handles are long enough that you can easily cook with this over a propane stove or a campfire and not have to reach practically over the flames to retrieve it.

Like most of the camp cook sets on the market, my only gripe is that there are only two bowls! That's hardly Stanley's fault, but I rarely get to go camping with just one other person. Even with this handy set, I would still need to supplement it with additional bowls and plates. I hope Stanley sells the bowls/plates so that I don't have to worry about which of my kids is going to complain about having the red bowl instead of the green one like his siblings! :)

It is important to note that this item is very sturdy but rather on the heavy side. Someone taking an extended backpacking trip might reconsider some of it. HOWEVER, if two people are going, you can easily split the kit up to save on weight, which would also probably give you enough room on the inside to stow your microstove and fuel. Otherwise, this set is the perfect item for car camping, extended base camping, fishing trips where you reached camp by canoe, and anywhere else where weight was a little less of an issue.

I know some people have balked at the price, but I've never had a Stanley product that a) wasn't worth every penny and b) didn't last longer than any of my other gear. The same people who produced that amazing, legendary vacuum thermos have put their know-how into this set, and it shows./>I know some people have balked at the price, but I've never had a Stanley product that a) wasn't worth every penny and b) didn't last longer than any of my other gear.
