product_title: RAD Cycle Products Indoor Portable Magnetic Work Out Bicycle Trainer
review_body: Great product for the money. Simple to assemble, relatively quiet and gives just enough resistance using the bikes gears to adjust your level of effort, just like on the road.     I have read other reviews that say the assembly instructions were not much help, so here are some that might.    There are just 3 items in the box, the trainer, a steel quick release for the back wheel (so the axle clamps don't gouge up you expensive alloy quick release)and a small steel barrel with an indentation in it.   I am using a beater bike on the trainer and it already has steel quick releases so I didn't need to use the one that came in the box, I'm guessing most people won't either. So all that leaves is the barrel, which goes on the bare end of the roller tension adjuster bolt for the wheel roller.    When you look at the big black plastic piece that the roller is attached to you see an indentation in the \\"ribs\\" on the underside (the side the roller is not on). Place the barrel on the end of the roller tension adjuster bolt and set the roller carrier (the big black plastic piece) down on the barrel so that the barrel nestles into the indentation in the \\"ribs\\" and the trainer is assembled, easy as that!    Now look at the picture on the box and see how the bike fits on the trainer and copy that. Once the clamping bolts are tightened on your rear axle bolts or quick release and the locking wing nuts are tight against the outer ends of the clamping bolts, turn the bike pedals by hand and adjust the roller tension bolt until you get some resistance from the roller. Get on the bike and pedal. If the rear wheel spins too freely hop off the bike and tighten the roller adjuster a little more. If you can barely pedal at all, loosen the adjuster bolt. Experiment until you get it just the way you like it. Now get on the bike and start sweating... Enjoy

Reading the reviews, I decided to stick to my usual size and ordered a 9.5. With a medium weight sock, the boot fits perfectly. My old boots were the lace-up style and I was always on the fence about metal laces that you ratchet up with the BOA system.

I took them out last weekend for their first test run. For about 2 hours of riding, they performed pretty well. The sole does have these weird knobby things sticking out of the inner side, I'm thinking so maybe the binding doesn't rub directly on the boot? Not sure, but that added width, tiny as it is, made it so the boot almost didn't fit in the binding, but they fit, just barely. It was mid 20's out and they kept my feet warm. You can cinch these up pretty darn tight, and even if they loosen a bit, I found that it wasn't noticeable on the runs and it's just a quick couple twists to the knob to tighten them up again. I especially like how easy they are to get off, at least compared to my old boots!

Also, I like my drinks with ice... after visiting Disney World and Universal Studios, I found there are 3 main types of ice machine ice shapes: the flat square, the cube with indent, and the cylindrical. If you stick the bottle underneath the ice dispenser: For flat square, about 1 in 4 will make it in (ppl will look at you like you're an idiot). For cube with indent, about 1/2 will make it in (no weird looks here). For cylindrical, if you put the ice in a cup first and pour it in, this is the best way because the cylinders will align themselves and all of the ice will make it in. They need to make one with bigger opening.

product_title: Currie Technologies eZip Women's Low Step-Thru Trailz Electric Bicycle
review_headline: This Bike Tried to Kill Me
review_body:
Buyer Be Ware!!!!

I bought this bike because I live in the city and wanted to be able to commute to work on it, but have the electric option if I got too tired or too hot so I didn't show up to work a sweaty mess. The reviews of this bike were mostly positive and though people said it was heavy no one said it was dangerously heavy, and the bike is marketed to women so how heavy could it be, right? Wrong, oh so very wrong.

The bike came and my husband had no trouble putting it together and it charged quickly over night. I had ordered a light and alarm for the bike for a little extra security in the city. First, the frame was larger than normal and the accessories would not attach to the oversized metal frame. The oversized frame added to the weight of this bike, plus the big tires, heavy battery and motor. This bike weighed a ton, there was no way I could get it in and out of the house on my own, or lift it even a little, a big negative, but I was still willing to work with it, I had my husband to help after all.

I spent some time in the parking lot getting used to the controls, the different speeds and options for full power or assistance were easy to use and I mastered them quickly. My husband and I decided to take a short trip to the local story and see how it handled for commuting. On the way home I had a small balance check after hitting a large crack in the pavement. I stopped and put my foot down which should have been fine, except the bike tilted when I did this and the bike is very heavy. The weight of the bike leaning against my leg took me down with the bike falling on top of me. If you are not strong enough to handle the inertia of 70 lbs DO NOT RIDE this bike. The bike was too heavy and I was trapped under it, in the middle of a busy street. My husband came to my rescues and bravely pulled the bike off of me. This turned out to be a mistake. The bike was actually so heavy that the inertia from the simple act of tipping over caused the brake handle had IMPALE my left thigh about six inches into my leg, and you should never remove something like that before going to the hospital.

At this point I am in no pain; shock is a wonderful pain blocker... The ambulance rushes me to the trauma ward of the local hospital, where there is a team of doctors waiting in full surgical gear and splash guards over their faces. It was like a scene from the ER, only scarier. I was lucky, the handle missed my femoral artery by the smallest fraction of an inch and I was not bleeding out. It did, however, tear a whole in my muscle, and it took two months to heal. I have a pretty serious scar on my thigh and it looks like I got in a knife fight when I wear a bathing suit... All in all, I am lucky to be alive. This bike is now in storage, it has been cleaned of all my skin, fat, blood, and muscle and is ready to be ridden again, but NOT BY ME. If you think you can handle the weight of this bike, or want to gift it to your enemy let me know I am ready to sell this bike, but be warned I do not think it's thirst for blood has been quenched.

review_headline: Easy to set up,comfortable and private...we love it!
review_body: I love this screenhouse!  I initially bought a cheap Walmart pop up shelter that we ended up returning because it was too small and flimsy. We set it up with 3 people in the middle of a wind storm and it wasn't hard at all (you'll need 2 people at least to set it up). It offers protection from the rain and privacy. It does get hot like all tents but I do recommend to set it up under some shade or tree and when you open all the windows it offers ample ventilation. It's lightweight and uses a little space in your truck or van. Don't forget to spray sealer before you use it for the first time so you will be twice protected from the rain ( better safe than sorry :) and when you get back from your vacation spend a little time and wash it and dry it so you'll have it ready for next season. The last tip,be gentle with the zippers so they last too. If you need more space you can buy the large version, this one is the medium size. Happy Camping!

product_title: US Military 4-PC Weather Resistant Modular Sleep System with Waterproof Gore-Tex Cover
review_headline: Tall guys and winter campers, these are the answers you seek on your quest to become one with nature
review_body:
If you want a sleeping bag for extreme outdoor camping, or want a sleeping bag for normal camping with the option to go extreme in the future, this is the best deal you will find for the money. It is a steal compared to what similar systems cost brand new. Note that this is military overstock. It is not fresh from the factory. That is why you will get it for a fraction of the cost of a brand new modular sleeping system, fresh from the factory. I bought from Black Star Surplus, and the item came in a box, tied up in its drawstrings. It smelled like it had been in a warehouse for some time, but not musty or moldy at all. You could simply tell it had sat around for awhile. Everything was clean, unused, all buttons and zippers were in perfect working order. Again: this is military overstock, not factory sealed, as listed in the description, which I read, so unlike some reviewers, I was not surprised. I would recommend buying through Black Star Surplus, because my friend let me try theirs before I bought mine, and his was from Black Star as well, and both arrived in perfect condition. I would recommend buying fast, however. I waited and the price went up in a week, and has gone up since. These bags are a great deal, and it's only a matter of time until they are priced closer to what they are actually worth.

I would not hesitate tent camping at temperatures below freezing in this setup because I have and I'm no Bear Grylls. There are three parts to this system, a black thermal layer, a green normal bag, and the Goretex, waterproof shell. Research online, you will not want to put the Goretex portion in the washer and dryer, even though the cleaning instructions on the bag say it's okay. I just aired mine out in the sun after it arrived, then threw it in the car and went camping in October. I used the black bag and the shell and slept barefoot inside a tiny tent with temps in the 20s. I had to unzip in the middle of the night because I was too warm. This was my first time tent camping, and I slept like a baby in windy conditions below freezing with heavy frost. I don't doubt that with all three bags together, I could lay exposed on a tarp at zero degrees and sleep soundly while the snow falls around me. You can cover your face and everything with this setup, and there is extra insulation around the feet to keep even people with poor circulation toasty. You could throw down in a snow-filled field without a tarp, I would simply recommend a tarp to keep moisture and dirt off the bag. This really is an all in one setup. Add a thermal foam pad and a folding lounger, and you will be living a life of luxury. You just might sleep better than you do at home. An excellent solution for troubled marriages in the winter time. Spouse getting on your nerves? Just grab this bag, and sleep in the yard under the stars!

This package comes with a bag to hold everything so you can backpack easily, which is next on my list. I was concerned when it arrived that being wrapped up so tight the insulation might have been crushed, but trust me, there is more than enough insulation in this thing. It really is the only option I would ever consider if you're considering winter camping. And if you're only camping in the summer or fall? It will work great for that too, just leave the black bag behind, that thing is an oven meant for crash landings on the planet Hoth.

The single biggest concern I had was being a tall guy, I wondered if I would fit. It seemed to be a topic of hot debate everywhere I looked online for people over 6'. I'm a strong 6'2", and can say this bag is designed for people 6'. However, I can just squeak by and fit. My feet are flat at the bottom, and the hood covers without being too uncomfortable, but I am definitely maxing out the height on this. I scoured the internet for a tall version, and apparently it exists, but is crafted by mythical woodland elves who live beyond the rainbow, manufacturing camping bags strung of unicorn hair for tall gods and goddesses who secretly camp with us mere mortals on weekend escapes from Mt. Olympus. I could not find the tall size version of this sleeping system, though according to forums, they are out there. Even if I could have, it would have easily cost triple what I paid. Not worth it if you're 6'2", because I can verify this *will* work. If you're 6'3" or taller, gather your Lucky Charms and happy hunting, hopefully you know someone in the NSA, those darned elves be an elusive lot.

As the picture suggests, this is a tight setup. You won't be doing the dirty with anyone in this bag, but there is enough room for me to roll from side to side within the closed inner black bag, so you shouldn't have any trouble, even if you're broad shouldered. It's tightest around the feet, tapered to promote warmth, so if you have The Shaky Leg, this might interfere with your RLS, or cure it, who knows, worth a shot either way.

In conclusion, I'm a tall, nerdy scifi writer who camped in this in below freezing conditions and loved it. product_title: Trangia Mini Windshield with Spirit Burn
review_headline: Simple and functional.  Tweaked to work with narrow cooksets.
review_body:
The picture on the product page is misleading. It shows the mini Trangia cook kit. This product is the Trangia Spirit burner and the mini windscreen/pot stand ONLY. I understood that when I ordered the product, so I have no issues giving it five stars.

The burner is the original, time tested Trangia Spirit burner. It is a bit smaller than the military burner that can be found at some surplus stores. That is a good thing, since all the aftermarket pot stands and whatever are designed for this burner, not the military one. While the Trangia burner is not ultralight and not the most efficient stove out there, it is very tough and carries its own fuel; enough for an overnighter at the least if I'm doing simple hiking grub (for two).

In addition to the included Trangia windscreen, I have used the Spirit burner with the Esbit pocket stove (designed for either Esbit fuel tablets or a Spirit burner), Vargo Hexagon woodstove and more recently with the Emberlit Fire Ant woodstove. The Esbit pocket stove works GREAT and is very compact (folds flat). For the Vargo woodstove I recommend elevating the Spirit burner for a better burn. I use the screw lid for this. If you're worried about heat, remove the o-ring from the lid first. The Fire Ant is an ultralight woodstove first and a fuel tab/alcohol stand second. But if you don't care that your burner weighs much more than your snazzy new ultralight wood burning pot stand, have a ball.

I like the windscreen/pot stand because it is stupid simple and also very rugged. I have two very narrow cookpots: a Snow Peak Mini Solo cookset and a single wall Snow Peak 600 mug. Neither is very stable on the mini windscreen. So I grabbed some pliers and bent the top 1/2" of the peaks inward. Through some amazing miracle I got them level. That made the windscreen the most stable stand I have for my Snow Peak stuff. Bending the windscreen peaks reduced the distance from the top of the burner tothe bottom of my cookpot. I'm sure that made the burner less efficient, but not by enough for me to care.

Bending down the points of the windscreen also made it less likely to snag on stuff. Although the windscreen does not fit inside either cookpot, it fits nicely (and snag free) in the mesh stuff sack on top of the Mini Solo cookset. My trail kitchen and most of my food for an overnighter fits inside the cookset, so I'm happy with how it packs.

Warning: bending the pot stand peaks any more than 1/2" will make it difficult to insert or remove the burner. You would probably feel stupid. Or blame me. Either way that would be bad. So try this at your own risk, and only if you're sold on using a narrow cookpot. And bend as little as you need to make your narrow cookset stable.

I rate the windscreen highly, and I like it. But it is not perfect. For starters, the windscreen is too small to effectively use the simmer ring. It will still snuff out the burner just fine though. And while it provides enough wind protection for mild weather, in windy conditions you'll need to carry a separate windscreen or take some other measure to protect your cooking area from wind. Lastly, the windshield does not collapse. Since it houses the Spirit burner that's not a big loss of space -- but there are plenty of more compact options on the market. None of that really bothers me, but your mileage may vary.

Bottom line, this is a tried and true alcohol burner paired with a simple windscreen/pot stand. The mini Trangia is about as uncomplicated as trail cooking can get. I recommend this compact little set.

product_title: Coghlan39;s Trekking Umbrella
review_body:
I have just received this umbrella and I am reasonably pleased with it. I bought it for lightweight backpacking and this gets me there. It weighs 12.0 oz complete with cover and 11.5 oz without. Unscrewing the last inch of the handle (which holds the flash light and battery compartment) the weight drops to 11.25 oz. By further timing the handle and cutting of the second velcro tab for the top part of the umbrella I believe you could get this down to 11.0 oz but I don't think it could be lightened up much beyond that with out messing with the functionality of the umbrella. Would I like it to be lighter, sure, but for $20 I think this is a great place to start. I'm hoping that I can leave my rain gear at home and just supplement this with a very lightweight poncho for those extra windy days.

The 42\\" canopy fiberglass handle and vented top are nice features and once I get a chance to try it out on a windy wet hike I will update my review with some performance details.

product_title: Glove.ly Cozy Touch Screen Gloves
review_headline: There are some disappointments that should be addressed
review_body: Conclusion: Product doesn't necessarily oversell its prime abilities (it's a glove - it lets you use your smartphone with a glove on), but there are some disappointments that should be addressed.    Pros:  - Touchscreen compatibility works as advertised. Very accurate response and easy to place finger on the right virtual keys.    - Good overall construction quality(*).    Cons:  - *Disappointing finger cutouts. While the construction was good, the finger cut material for the pinky was too short. It brought the webbing material between the ring finger and pinky up too high making the glove fitment awkward and uncomfortable. I wear a Large and my fingers aren't usually long. I could tell if I went a size up, the pinky would have enough room but  the other four fingers would have too much slack.    - No traction surfaces on the palms or lower fingers. The glove material is slippery. I didn't realize how much I missed silicone stripes/dots or a stitched palm pad until driving or trying to hold onto smooth surfaces. My steering wheel felt as if I was trying hold a semi-polished stair bannister.    - Although advertised as \\"Cold Gloves\\" they're not very warm. Below 30 they do a so-so job.    - The lining only does an OK job of blocking the wind. When a strong gust comes, the wind cuts through them and you feel little icy needle pokes on your hands & fingers.    - Magnet clasp is largely worthless. I have refrigerator magnets that are stronger. They should have used a more secure method of attaching the gloves to one another (plastic snap clip is just fine) or a small, stronger magnet (neodymium?)

product_title: STABILicers Maxx Original Heavy Duty Stabilicers Ice Traction Cleat for Snow and Ice - Traction cleats for Boots and Shoe Ice Cleats
review_body:
I've been wearing these daily for the last 10 days while managing a small outdoor skating rink. The Stablicers have provided great traction on the ice. After proper adjustment I've had no problem with them staying in place on my boot. They go on and off my muck boots much quicker and easier than the rubber type Yak Tracks that I've been using since last season. One of the wire wrapped thin rubber pieces of my Yak Tracks broke so I needed to replace them.

Once the toe strap has been initially set, I leave the toe strap alone, slide my boot in, then secure the ankle velcro straps. I've also worn these in snow covered ice and haven't had any issue with snow build up between my boot and the stablicer as some others have. I've ben keeping an eye out for loosening screws since some reviewers have had a problem with that. None yet but I'll keep checking tightness after every few uses. Hopefully occasionally tightening them will be the solution to lost screws.

As far as sizing the Stablicers when ordering, I googled Stablicers and size 13 muck boot. I found an ice fishing forum where a guy said his XL Stablicers fit on his size 13 muck boots just fine. I ordered the XL and they fit just fine like he said.

I've been very happy with these so far. I'll know more after using them for a full season or two to see what kind of durability they'll have.

review_headline: I love this stun gun but it's power charge will die ...
review_body: I love this stun gun but it's power charge will die if you don't check it regularly, which is understandable but if you forget that it has a rechargeable set of batteries and try to unscrew the cap to replace the imaginary batteries inside, you may ruin the tool. Operator error confession here. My wife said her stun gun had lost power and I forgot we had a plug in charger somewhere. So I began the usual task of screwing off the cap. Starting with the rear, where most battery compartments are, I couldn't budge the rear threaded cap. However, during the task, I noticed the front threaded cap would come off, thinking how strange for the batteries to be up there, I shrugged it off as a new design. What was happening was, I was twisting the lense area and the wires were being twisted out of their connections. I hope I haven't ruined it completely. I removed the pointed pins in the head of the gun to remove the semi-circular plates, which allowed me to remove the plate and see how the wires connected. Only the 2 wires that feed the shock elements were slipped out of their fittings and it seems as if they just slip into 2 holes and float in the space under the sharp pins, Now, I just have to find a new charger, as I can't find the original one. Once charged again, I can test my repair to see if it still works as intended. The power is great, it has a loud noise associated with it which would deter most folks without the shock. The flashlight comes in handy too. Beech Island, SC. The reason for 4 stars rather than 5 is there needs to be a dummy safety device designed to prevent damage to the unit.

product_title: Sportube Series 2 Double Ski Hard Case
review_headline: Wheels need to be re-engineered but overall a good product.
review_body:
I've had this product for 8 years now; purchased when my wife and I finally bought our own skis. We use the tube to check skis on the airlines and for car top carry.

First, let me say that our skis have never been damaged, despite the indifferent treatment of the airlines. The tube has had one corner bashed in with no loss of integrity.

Second, there is a specific technique for strapping the skis to each other, "like a pair of shoes" according to the manufacturer, then to the box itself. To pack it yourself takes a few minutes but is not difficult. However, God forbid you have to stand in line watching a TSA agent open the case to examine your contraband cargo, then try to re-pack the skis! Of course TSA won't let you touch your bag after handing it over to them, so all you can do is coach the agent on how to do it. We went thru this once, in Denver, for checked bags.

Where this product could be better is the wheel/axle system. After a few uses (and baggage handling drops, no doubt), the axle bends and the wheels no longer roll properly. Thus, they wear out prematurely and in a conical shape, and rub against the plastic. Makes it more difficult to schlep the bag across a big airport to your rental car. If the axle were beefier, or if it were supported at the ends as well as the center (add a small bracket), this problem would not occur.

The manufacturer will sell you a new wheel/axle set for $15 but it retains the original, inadequate cantilever design. I have suggested to them that they sell an upgraded wheel support system, but they politely blew me off.

product_title: Coleman Hooligan Tent
review_headline: It has a FULL fly - this is the one you want
review_body: I am very pleased with this tent. I wanted something a bit larger for times when I'm not using my smaller 2-man backpacking tent & footprint. But it can be hard to find a 3-man with a full fly (to the ground on all sides) and vestibule. This Coleman tent is well-constructed and roomy. It is NOT a lightweight tent, having quite a few fiberglass poles. It is also a bit complicated to set up. But once you have it up it is very comfortable for two people and downright luxurious for one person.  I have used it in wet and windy weather and the fly kept the tent absolutely dry. The integrated tarp-style floor worked as expected. The vestibule door zipper feels like it will hold up well.  This is a great tent for car camping in all types of weather.  UPDATE 08-2015: Everything is holding up well and I still like this tent. For hot weather, venting is a bit of a challenge during direct sunlight even with the top vent open. The tent does cool off after the sun goes down. The vestibule entrance is a bit igloo-like. For most adults, it's a crawl-in door which might give you dirty knees. The tent door is much larger than the vestibule door. This is not an issue for me, so no change in rating, just something to consider if you're a person with knee issues. Keep in mind that during a rainstorm you'll appreciate that small opening because unlike many tents, you can get in without exposing the tent interior to weather.

product_title: NITECORE P12 2015 version 1000 Lumen high intensity CREE XM-L2 LED long throw tactical flashlight with Genuine Nitecore NL189 18650 3400mAh Li-ion rechargeable battery, Nitecore i2 intelligent Charger, Car Charging Cable and 2 X EdisonBright CR123A lithium Batteries
review_headline: VERY bright - Rechargeable battery sold me on this one.  No more buying expensive cr123's!  Best light for the money.
review_body:
I have been an owner of all types of compact flashlights including everything from surefire, streamlight, ATN, and the chinese cree LED's.

This light is the brightest, most durable, most feature-packed compact light I could find for the money.

Build quality:
The aluminum feels sturdy as hell and the black finish seems pretty solid so far. As a volunteer firefighter, a hunter, and avid outdoorsman, My devices see a ton of abuse. So far this light has held up solidly through pouring rain, freezing conditions, and getting covered in mud.

Function:
The light includes several modes. ranging from low to high, and three strobe-style modes: strobe, SOS, and pulse.
I love the fact that there's a separate button to cycle through settings instead of using a half-press on the same on/off button as many other manufacturers use. This means when you turn it on, you use exactly the setting you intend to use.

The low light function is bright enough to help me walk to my treestand during dark mornings without spooking any game. The brightest setting is a beam style, but has a good amount of flood around it. There is definitely a concentrated beam, but the surrounding area is very bright as well. I'd say at 75 yds the beam really torches up a good 5 yard circle, but you can still clearly see a good 20 yard radius outside the beam as well.
At the highest brightness setting this thing is the brightest flashlight I've ever used for this size.

Accessories:
The rechargeable battery is what sold me on this thing. I am absolutely sick of paying a for CR123a batteries every few months. The charger can be used with wall outlet or car charger. The charging unit is not the most compact thing in the world, but battery life is VERY good so I keep mine at home anyway. On the low-med brightness settings you could run this light for several hours. I've charged the battery just once in the 3 months that I've used this flashlight and it wasn't because it was dead, I just like to be fully juiced up and prepared. Every weekend for the past 3 months of hunting season the light has seen a few hours of use and I haven't seen any brightness decline whatsoever.
The light also comes with a velcro pouch that I attached to the Molle on my backpack so it goes everywhere with me without taking up space in my go-bag. The velcro pouch secures it nicely.
Also included are a belt-clip and a stand so you could use it as a torchlight. Both are removable.

The light is small enough to fit in your pocket, and bright enough to temporarily blind someone (though I would NOT recommend shining this thing directly in anyone's eyes). The beam is effective at distances well over 100 yards.

I don't really see any cons for this product. Perhaps the only thing missing is a smooth 1" diameter section to allow weapon mounting systems to be used, but depending on your intended use, there's other light solutions out there for that purpose.

I will update my review as my use continues. I am of the belief (based on previous flashlight experience) that LEDs deteriorate over time and lose their brightness. If this one maintains the durability and brightness I've experienced so far, I'm planning on getting one for my pops and brother for their birthdays next year.

The headrest did not clear my handlebars and cannot be removed.

Very disappointing. I got it because friends use it and love it on both of their bikes. I have no idea how you could be sure that the headrest will clear your handlebars without trying it on the bike.

product_title: Demon Snow Azzpadz D30
review_headline: Great Product - Great Piece of Mind
review_body: I fell very hard on my tail a few times while snowboarding this season. I took a couple weeks off to heal and ordered this product. I'm a 49-yr-old intermediate snowboarder who is a bit daring; riding blues, blacks and terrain parks... So of course I fall at times. I really can't afford a broken tailbone, so today I put the Azzpad to the test. Keep in mind, my tailbone was still slightly sore. Of course I fell on it due to icy conditions here in the Northeast and a shear lack of snow. The first fall wearing this did not cause pain at all and I was so relieved; however I fell another three times and found that, while I'm certain this product is great if you haven't yet fallen on your tailbone and are snowboarding in ideal conditions, it just does not give you immunity to the pain of this type of fall. Perhaps it may have shifted slightly, although it seemed to have stayed in place. Again, I give it a 5 because had I not already busted my tailbone up, there would be no problem. So, my advice is to certainly invest in this product to prevent a bad fall in the first place and to make certain its tight and in place when worn. It is lightweight and very low profile under a generous pair of snow pants. I will continue to use this product knowing that my tailbone will not break and it helps me to be a little more daring. Please also get the Demon wrist guards as well. They are amazing...and some knee pads too. Now that you have all that going on under your snow pants, go out and hit the slopes.

product_title: Metropolis Patterson Crankset
review_headline: Low Granny Gear For Your Tadpole Trike or Mountain Bike.
review_body: A Patterson SRC drive to replace your front crankset with a 2 speed drive. These replaced my single sprocket and gave me enough low speed to pedal my heavily loaded KMX tadpole trike up those steep 15% grades. Something like 15 to 84 gear inches after installation - pretty low gear. Patterson offers a more economical method to get that Granny gear,  when all you had before was a single speed gear.  I am waiting for the shifter  and have the Patterson wired for low- gear only now.  I am afraid to be without the exercise and adventure of the daily trips to the wilderness park, all uphill and straining the old body. Pretty nice looking bicycle/ tricycle part and I love bike parts.  There is little info for we beginners and it makes a lot of this, a mystery. This Patterson drive is made for bikes with a 68 MM WIDTH pedal hub ( where the ball bearings for the pedals live).. You will need some tools to remove the retainer cups that hold the old BB assembly and I had to use a heat gun to soften the locking compound and get it to release. Likewise, you will need to fabricate a little angle bracket to keep the patterson backplate from rotating. Normally these are installed on bicycles and the anti-rotation plastic blocks won't work on the KMX without fabricating a simple aluminum angle bracket that interferes with rotation of the backplate ( a stop to replace the large black plastic block that hits the frame tubes on a bucycle but won't on a tadpole trike). I am surprised that  Sam Patterson does not talk about this in his video- see youtube re Patterson SRC drive installation. Tadpole trikes are still the exception. Utah Trikes wanted $20 for an adapter and there is a mysterious fog around all this information What does it do, Why Explain it to me please- just like a kid.

product_title: ATV LOGIC SB-6B Tank Saddlebag For ATV'S (Black)
review_body: These have proven to be a good economy option for my snowmobile.  I put these on a 2015 Ski-doo and they work pretty well.  I would say that the materials are of moderate quality, but I feel that the quality is on par with the price point.  The contour of the snowmobile means that they don't hang quite perfectly, but I haven't had any problems with them flopping around even without using the adhesive tape.  I have yet to stuff the bags, but they hold everything I needed them to hold with space left over.  I store a steno pad, a small spiral notepad, some hand and toe warmers, a pair of work gloves, and some small personal items and have plenty of space to add more.  The drawstring pocket holds my 12 oz. vacuum coffee flask well; in fact, it fits completely inside the pocket.  The zippers have cord on the pulls, so it's easy for me to open the pockets even in my arctic down gloves.  This also makes the zippers easy for ravens to open, unfortunately, so I have clipped them together with small carabiners.  The double zipper pulls make this possible, and the birds haven't figured out how to defeat that yet.  The pocket opposite the beverage holder does have a mesh inner pocket for smaller things.  One of the things I like best about this is that it's easy to pull off the machine and take inside at the end of the day.

product_title: Intex Pillow Rest Raised Airbed with Built-in Pillow and Electric Pump
review_headline: This airbed is firm and keeps me off the ground so I feel as though I'm sleeping in a normal bed like a civilized person
review_body:
I was sleeping on a small, ratty mattress my last roommate gave me when I moved out, and this is certainly a step up. I plan on moving 500 miles back to my home state of New York, and I want to limit the eventual hassle. For me, that means staying portable and not buying a bed frame or new mattress. This airbed is firm and keeps me off the ground so I feel as though I'm sleeping in a normal bed like a civilized person. The pump is loud but fast, and although I haven't deflated it yet, the option of using the pump in reverse is appreciated.

My main concern was longevity, since I'll be using this as my permanent bed for the foreseeable future. In addition, I'm a freelancer working from home, and I like to use my laptop for work in bed. I'm going to put this through more use than most people, easily. I've only had it for a few weeks, but it's holding up as well as expected, requiring top-off only very occasionally.

It took a little getting used to. It's not uncomfortable, although the ribbing that runs the length of the bed can be slightly annoying depending on your preferred sleep position. The sides are raised higher than the rest of the ribbing, which I suppose for me is a unique annoyance because I have to carefully place the clipboard I use to rest my laptop mouse on. Also, the raised pillow area seems quite unnecessary.

A good mattress is impossible to beat, but this isn't too far behind, and the utility of a portable mattress is phenomenal. Even after I'm sleeping on a normal mattress again, I'll be eager to take this camping with me, if I can find an adapter for my cigarette lighter. I miss camping, but I wouldn't miss being separated from the cold (and possibly wet) ground by little more than a sleeping bag.

UPDATE: Nope, this thing didn't even last three full months. I can fill it before I go to sleep, and in the morning it'll be half deflated. I'm not kidding when I say I put it through constant use, so it may be fine as an emergency guest bed or for short trips away from home. However, this won't stand up to regular use.

product_title: Swagman RV 2" Bumper Adaptor
review_body:
Attached this to the bumper of our self refurbished 89 coleman popup bumper. The bolts themselves I wish were threaded with an extra 1/2 inch of thread (rear bumper of camper is on the short side of the 4" vertical), but was able to use a 1/2 metal 'shim' and it tightened perfectly. Front to back, our bumper actually has a thin sheet metal knockout at the lower part of the bumper, but a slight modification (two holes to accommodate the bolts) in that thin piece of metal, it attaches perfectly. Other small snag is that the bumper on our camper is snug up against the plastic back panel of the camper. This was also not a problem as the plastic was flexible and my wife & I were able to push the flexible plastic back enough to put a 1x2 on either side of the work area, allowing room to install the bolts. This thing is a solid (read sturdy) piece of metal with strong bolts and strong metal lower plate. We purchased a four bike bike rack and it inserts and secures rock solid! Love it for the price!.

One minor negative (minor at least to me).. The hole for the trailer hitch pin was too small to accommodate both of the hitch pins that I own.. both of which fit fine in the Curt hitch I had on my CRV and fine with the hitch that comes with my Tacoma.. I own a dremel that has a grinding bit.. A few seconds shaving (and I mean very little) the interior of the hole and pin was snug and secure. If the hole was perfectly sized to the standard pin size, I'd have given a 5 star..
As it stands I would HIGHLY recommend this for anyone who needs to add a basic (minor load) hitch to the back of their camper to haul their bikes, so long as you have a little bit of handy in your blood to make minor tweaks. ;-)

review_body:
I just got back from a five day, four night hunting/camping trip and I have to say that this mattress was definitely a high point of the trip. I actually got out about a half hour late on the second day of whitetail and hog hunting in a central Florida Swamp because I didn't want to get out of my comfortable bed.

It sets up easily with the included pump (I still haven't had to charge it yet) and is comfortable. So, why did it lose one star? To adjust the firmness or softness of the mattress you have to use the pump as there is no other valve. This means letting out a little air, trying the mattress and repeating as necessary. Also, I had to add air after two nights due to loss of air. I know that no air mattress will hold air forever, I thought it should have lasted all four nights.

I used it for camping, but it could be used for house guests or even lying in front of the tv. I keep it in the hall closet instead of with the camping gear just in case I need it for one any of those reasons.

review_body:
This is an incredible flashlight. A must have! It is so powerful and lightweight, I will never buy any other flashlight. I've had several rechargeable big bulky lights that ultimately failed over time.

UPDATE - Jan 12, 2015

After only having this flashlight for a couple weeks, it stopped working. Replaced the batteries thinking it was the batteries.

Nope, for whatever reason this flashlight just stopped working. It wasn't dropped or damaged, it just stopped working after the batteries died in the flashlight. Which brings me to my next complaint. After using the flashlight steady on for about 15 minutes the batteries died and ultimately the flashlight now will not work at all.

Terrible product and I was so impressed out of the box...guess I should have waited a couple weeks to write my review. I won't make that same mistake again.

Bottom line -- Save your money and find a flashlight that contains rechargeable batteries and lasts longer than two weeks before it stops working. Truly Disappointed. I won't be buy this item again.

product_title: Energizer Light Fusion Technology
review_headline: Started with a "BAM"...ended in a wimper....
review_body: I purchased two of these lights, one from Ebay one from Amazon. These were tested to be reviewed on my youtube channel. I was so impressed at first with the slim design, bright light and the escape from D battery lanterns. My first light from Ebay lasted one day before it would not stay on for even 1 minute, you could count to 10 or 100 between battery changes and it made no difference in the lights ability to stay on. Wanting to give Energizer a fair shake before reviewing I purchased a second light from Amazon, this light lasted 4 days before it too began to malfunction. It was very promising at first, a nice throw on the light throughout the room, the ability to raise and lower the light closer or farther from the reflector to get the perfect light for your desired task, and ability to use AA batteries to boot. The built in kick stand was a great feature that folded away when not in use. The red carry handle was comfortable in hand. The quick and simple turn of the standard bolts to change batteries was great no worries about screws falling out or getting lost. But again this unit failed to stay on as well. Brand new batteries were used, each time a 10 second pause was used before replacing batteries to no avail, the light just would not stay on. It would shut off in seconds, some times a minute or two but no longer. I'm very tech savvy and this was not a user error! LOL. This could so be a hit out of the park for Energizer if they could fix the bugs and provide reliable lanterns to all or even most customers. Like quite a few companies the design is Great but the execution is lacking consistency. 2 stars is all I can give based on 2 attempts to get a solidly working lantern. It seems some customers were lucky and received working lanterns as per the reviews here on Amazon, but not all. Other site reviews also have a hit or miss on getting a consistent working light. I hope the company is not satisfied with this result and attempts to resolve this issue, as it left these customers with a dis-satisfaction with not only the product but the QC of the company as well. I would be happy to purchase again in the future once Energizer steps up and puts more time into Quality Control of this unit. Sadly I cannot recommend this lantern to any of my subscribers, and will have to find another product that hits the mark. I truly hope Energizer addresses this problem, as it is a really cool design that could change peoples opinions on buying modern lanterns to replace those old bulky heavy "D" units of the past. My wife's hybrid with the fat aluminum mixte-style frame also fit poorly since it had a very wide top tube and widely-spaced seat stays. It still works. My 80's Schwinn 10 speed with thin, chromo, horizontal top-tube fit perfectly. If you had 4 bikes like that with plain diamond frames and skinny, level top tubes, this rack would be a breeze to load. As it is, I do not think you could expect to load 4 bikes of various shapes and sizes and not expect some scuffs and minor damage from the bikes rubbing against each other. I suppose if you have very valuable bicycles, you probably transport them on a rack in a van or truck, well-spaced apart.

Threading the bolt to lock the swing-away carrier is a bit tedious. It could be faster and easier if it was some sort of cam-lock device. The bolt is at least safe in that it is unlikely to come undone and is backed up by the pin.

product_title: Oceanic ATOM 3.1 Wristwatch Dive Computer, Transmitter, USB
review_headline: Works . . . If You Can Figure Out How To Use It!
review_body:
You know that you're in trouble when the company wants to charge you $10 to download a "training course" in how to use your dive computer. I am a new diver and this is my first dive computer. Although it apparently works by default when you enter the water and displays what you need (except for the water temp), and therefore presumably does what you need it to do, the owner's manual is completely worthless, and I am a very technologically savvy consumer. Seriously . . . the owner's manual is absolutely incomprehensible as a guide to using this dive computer. It is not intuitive at all, and the fact that the company has the nerve to write such a useless document and then charge you $10 for a "training course" is just insulting. Other pet peeves: the "ocean log" software is a free download, but the "full" version that would let you set alarms and other settings on the dive computer by using your computer is $24. Really? Yes, it is an inexpensive and apparently functional option if you want air integration, which is the reason that I got this, but to charge you to learn to use it and provide free crippleware and charge you for the "full" version is just unacceptable. Oceanic apparently thinks they can get away with these shenanigans, and the only way that I know of to convince them otherwise is to return this product and not buy from them. For example, Suunto offers a similar functionality in the Vyper (at about $100 more and has a compass), but gives you a comprehensible owner's manual, free video training and free fully functional dive software. If for no other reason, I would pass on the Atomic 3.1 and patronize a company that does not treat their customers like suckers to be milked of even more post-purchase money.

Bottom line: it works, it's relatively inexpensive compared to other dive computers with seemingly similar functions, and I took it on a dive and it worked, but I wouldn't know what functions Ican use, because I can't figure out how to use them!

I had to go with a size larger than I expected because my hips were too wide. That shouldn't be a problem for a man. After finding it in store I found a much better deal on Amazon and bought it here. product_title: Diamondback Bicycles 2015 Atroz Full Suspension Complete Mountain Bike
review_headline: Quality Frame With Quality Components. Great Entry Level Full Suspension Rig
review_body: I live in North Texas where the terrain is flat. Local trails are man made for the most part consisting of small uphill and downhill areas near dried up riverbeds and small valleys. I've rode both 26 and 29 hardtails from different companies such as Trek and Specialized. A full suspension bike isn't necessary here but I wanted to give it a try. I also wanted to see what the 650B/27.5\\" hype was about. My budget was $1000. If you're familiar with the current offerings, well there aren't many in that price range. I found this bike while checking out 2015 lineups on a mountain bike forum and discovered it was priced at $839 here on Amazon. There isn't much information out on this bike or the model up (Atroz Comp) yet so I'll do what I can to share my experience here.    Diamondback has a reputation with some of the elitist bike crowd as being a Walmart bike, stating the company makes junk. If you're considering this bike then you're probably not part of that crowd that thinks a bike needs to cost $3000+ to be worth their time. Let me assure you this bike is built with quality components.    First impressions.    The bike arrived mostly assembled and fairly well packaged. Some assembly is required (handlebars, pedals, seat, front caliper) but all of the tools needed are included. If you have basic mechanical skills you'll have no problems getting it put together. If not, just take it to your local bike shop and pay them a little bit to assemble it and fine tune it.    As I was adjusting everything on the bike I noticed the fit and finish on the frame was very clean. I used to weld so whenever I buy anything that has been welded, that's usually one of the first things I check out. The welds between all of the joints and the rear shock mount looked good. I've seen more expensive frames with sloppy welds that made me question overall quality. I don't have that concern at all with this frame. It's not the lightest bike in the world, but a sturdy frame is more desirable thana light, fragile counterpart. The frame is built with a 66 degree rake and looks very aggressive. I'm not certain how this will affect handling. I ordered the 18\\" medium frame. I'm roughly 5'8 with a 32\\" inseam. I barely clear the top frame rail when standing flat footed.    Next I checked out all the painted surfaces and decals on the bike. When I first saw pictures of the bike I wasn't a fan of the yellow Diamondback decals and planned on removing them. Now that I have the bike in my possession and have been able to thoroughly look it over, I've found out that everything on the frame is painted on or at the very least decals with a heavy coat of clear to protect them. I didn't expect that kind of finish on this bike to be honest. It should be noted that all lettering you see on the lip of the wheels and fork are decals. I've already pulled all the decals from the wheels, looks much better in my opinion.    I haven't taken the bike to the trail yet so I'm only going to briefly review the components on the bike.    -Suspension:  This bike is built with a Rockshox Monarch rear air shock (Approximately 4\\" of travel). Rockshox makes quality parts and this doesn't appear to be any different. This shock compresses smoothly and goes right back to where it was without bouncing around. It feels firm and shouldn't kill too much torque when your pedaling hard.  The fork is a Suntour XCM 120mm (Approximately 4.5\\" or so of travel) with 30mm stanchions. I don't have any experience with Suntour forks. First impressions the fork feels too bouncy and somewhat like a pogo stick. The rebound is adjustable and I plan to dial it in. With that being said, I do plan on changing to a Rockshox air fork in the near future. I'll play with this fork for a little while though and update this review when I get more time with it.    Wheels and Tires:  The wheels are Diamondback's SL7 27.5\\" (650B). The wheels don't feel like anchors but they aren't featherweight either. Lightweight wheels are notcheap. I don't plan on messing with these unless I damage one beyond repair.  Tires are Kenda Nevegal 27.5x2.35. These tires have a nice fat width to them and pretty aggressive tread. They should hold up just fine on the loose dirt/powder on my local trails.    Driveline components:  All components are SRAM, excluding the crank and front derailleur. Shifter feels smooth and chain transitions easily on the rear derailleur. Rear Derailleur is an SRAM X5 9 speed mid cage and uses an SRAM 9 speed shifter. This bike is built with a single 32 teeth front ring. Your gear selection is therefore 1x9. Because of this the area around the front ring is clear of clutter and has fewer moving parts. Some may see this as a downside. I only plan on riding this bike on trails with lots of turns and few straights where high speed is possible. I never used the full range of gears on previous bikes so this is perfectly fine with me.    Seat and Seatpost:  Not much to be said here, other than the post looks nice with the Diamondback lettering all the way around as well as numbered notches on the rear for height adjustment. The seat has very little padding and is not particularly comfortable. That being said, I've never really found any mountain bike seat to be comfortable. I didn't buy this bike for comfort so it's not a concern of mine.    Brakes:  The brake are Tektro Aries mechanical discs. Diamondback lists the rotors on their website as both being 160mm. This information was incorrect, at least on my bike anyway. My bike had a 180mm front rotor and 160mm rear rotor. The front caliper included an adapter to accommodate the larger rotor. This was a nice surprise as I was not expecting a larger front rotor. Like I stated earlier there is not a lot of up and down on my local trails. The majority of the braking I do is on flat surfaces so mechanical discs are plenty sufficient. Hydraulics would be a nice upgrade if your terrrain consists of longer descents.    Miscellaneous Components:The handlebar is a Diamondback \\"Pro Bar\\" measuring 750mm wide. Handlebar feels light and looks nice. Grips are Diamondback 135mm \\"Kraton\\". They feel like decent grips and will get the job done.    Overall this Diamondback Atroz is a quality bike. You aren't buying junk if you choose to purchase this bike. Keep in mind, this is an entry level full suspension bike. This is not a $3000+ downhill bike but it's still a nice quality frame built with plenty of quality components to make it a nice overall bike. I'll try to help out and answer any questions I can. I'll be updating this review as I continue to ride the bike and upgrade certain components.

product_title: ENO Eagles Nest Outfitters - DoubleNest Hammock
review_headline: Great hammocks, Tons of Uses, I use mine daily! Own 6+
review_body:
Super Hammock! I have been using eagles nest products for years and own about 6 hammocks.. My first hammock was a single nest but I quickly realized I would like the space in a doublesnest better.. These hammocks are made of very very durable nylon and I have never had one fail or wear out..

I would strongly suggest anyone that purchases these hammocks to also buy straps for them.. My first hammock I didn't buy straps but after my first use I quickly went back to my local specialty store and purchased straps! Straps make these hammocks very easy to string up!! You can do it in under 1 minute with straps! Ropes stretch, are hard to use, hard to adjust, and more! Straps are the way to go.. If you don't want to purchase ENO straps, just buy some webbing and make your own!! Ends up being much cheaper!

There are tons of uses for these hammocks, you can sleep in them, throw them in a day pack and string them up on a hike to take a break or just relax, you can string them up as chairs... The uses are endless.. I even take mine with me to school and string it up outside the school to lounge around and study!! They are so lite that you will not even notice carrying them with you everywhere!!

You can toss the hammocks in washing machine with no issues (I wouldnt recommend drying and would recommend using an organic soap or something that isn't very harsh)

Remember to buy a top or tarp if you plan to use it camping!! Never fun to get wet :-)

One last tip, on a cold night, bring an extra blanket or pad to line the bottom of the hammock.. the open air under them does cause it to be very cold on cold nights.. much colder than tents!! I like an extra blanket rather than pad but I have friends who just use their pads

product_title: The North Face McMurdo Parka Style: A8XZ-62X Size: XL
review_headline: Decent construction and design, with a couple of caveats:
review_body: Purchased this McMurdo Parka for more or less casual use, while working at night on Mauna Kea, Hawaii- temperatures are generally near or just below freezing (say around 20 F - 35 F), but it is frequently windy (20mph - 45mph), and the physiological effects of altitude make you feel colder than you might at sea level (14,000ft elevation- all your blood goes to your brain and torso, leaving your limbs feeling very cold). I don't spend a lot of extended time outside, but enough to want something warm to wear when needed...    This parka is suitable to my needs, but probably not warm enough for someone spending long periods outdoors in truly cold climates (as IE below 20 F or -10 C).    The construction and design seems generally decent- very comfortable to wear, and lots of large pockets in useful places. I have removed the hood, which I probably won't use much, so I don't have much to say about that.    I do have a couple of issues with this parka though:    The zipper is a full length nylon YKK, that zips up one way only from the bottom. It's not a \\"big beefy\\" zipper- it has a small one-way slider that I find it a little awkward to start, way down there at mid-thigh level... Probably not a big issue if you just zip up once and leave it zipped for hours, but if you are getting in & out of it many times a night (my case), somewhat less than convenient. It has snaps on the zipper wind cover, which I use instead of the zipper, but the snaps are small and require a bit of two-hand fumbling to get snapped- and would probably be even more difficult with gloves (as would the zipper!).    The pockets have no insulation on the outside, just a fabric shell, so there is not much cold protection there for your hands, if you are not wearing gloves.    Other than that, this parka seems sturdy and well suited to my own needs, so far. For colder climates, I think I would recommend the Canada Goose Expedition (at twice the price!), which appears from the reviews I've seen to be a better design, and better suited to truly extreme conditions. For me, this parka does the job, at a reasonable cost.    A note on fit: I'm 5'10\\" and a bit portly (>200lbs), and the XL fits me pretty well- snug but not tight, with only a shirt & T-shirt under, for layering. Layered more heavily (heavy sweater or vest), I might need to go up in size.

review_headline: Good quality, perfect size, destroys credit cards
review_body:
I've had this for about 2 years, and it's held up pretty well for a $25 wallet. It's nice and thin, and has the perfect number of pockets, compartments, dividers, etc. It's a really great wallet. With one exception.

During this two year period, for various reasons, I've had about a dozen brand new credit cards come through my wallet. Every single one of them went in new, bright, and shiny. 2 weeks later, it looked like I'd been carrying it for 5 years. The fronts get a little scuffed up, but the biggest problem is that the silver on the numbers is destroyed. Every card I own has little to no silver left on the raised numbers, and has been like that since a couple weeks after getting it. I'm not sure what the rubberized coating inside the card slots is made of, but it's not friendly to credit cards.

I know, it's not a huge deal, but when you get a nice, new, shiny card, it's always nice if it stays that way for at least a few months. It's kind of depressing to get a new one and put it in your wallet, knowing that it will never look like that again.

The manufacturer wasn't terribly helpful. To quote the email I got when I wrote them about it: "We sent your original email to our corporate office to see if this has even been an ongoing issue. As far as they are concerned, this do not happen often."

product_title: Optimus Windshield
review_headline: Great tool, helps in windy environments.
review_body:
This is a great windshield that is generally stove agnostic.

Basically it's two quarter slices that bend where they meet, allowing you to hook the base onto any gas canister (100gram or 220-240 gram canisters).

I tried a few stoves with it, and the basic results for fit are:

- Snow Peak Giga Power: Yes. The low height of this stove means great win protection.
- Soto Compact: No. The pot stand portion hits up against the edge, forcing an angle. Probably still could use small cups, but limited.
- Soto Windmaster: Sorta. The included pot stand works, but the optional quad-arm pot stand is too wide. Also, the tallness of this stove means the stove is about level with the upper rim of the wind screen, so while it might help a little, I'm not sure how big a difference it would be.
- Snow Peak Litemax: Yes. in fact, I think this might be the best fit for this screen.

Low and wide pots won't fit very well on this, but just about any cup or liter sized tall and narrow pot should do just fine.

- Terra HE Weekend. Yes
- Snow Peak Trek 900. Yes
- Snow Peak Hybrid Summit. Yes
- Snow Peak cookset. tight and off center, but sorta
- Toaks 1600. tight and off center, but sorta.
- Terra HE cookset. Not really. Too wide.

Overall, this is one impressive wind screen, and it's a bummer that it isn't sold in more places.

If you already use a compact gas stove, don't want to do an additional investment in a jetboil, MSR Reactor, or a Primus ETALite, and depending on which compact gas stove you own, this might be perfect for for problems with wind.

product_title: Arcteryx Atom AR Jacket - Men's
review_headline: The LT is an amazing jacket. I just love it
review_body:
I own the Atom LT hoodie and the Atom AR jacket. I also ordered the hooded version of the AR jacket to compare. I'm 5'6 150 lbs. here are my thoughts. If I could have done everything over again I would have ordered the LT in a small without the hood, and the AR in a medium with s hood. This is the reason. The LT is an amazing jacket. I just love it. It also is great to layer. The small fits perfect. It would be even nicer to layer underneath the AR hoodie because it breaths so well. The problem is having the hood on the LT makes it more challenging to do it. I mean you can but you have this spare hood tucked in under your jacket near your back. Since I had purchased the LT before I already have the hood so kind of stuck in that situation. Seemed kind of silly to order another hooded one, but the medium hoodie in the AR was so nice to layer underneath. Ok, so I sent back the medium hoodie and kept the AR jacket. Thoughts on this is its very warm, but the small does not fit as well on me as the small LT. It's a heavier jacket and quite right fitting. A medium would be much better for a stand alone. So why did I keep the small? Because I got it without the hood I'm using it for layer. When I put this under my shell I'm super toasty. So to recap. If you don't have an LT yet the best combo would be to get an LT jacket and get one size larger in the AR. You can then use the Lt to layer underneath which breaths better than the AR, and then use the AR as the outer shell on dry days. If you want to use this jacket as a standalone in dry conditions and you aren't going to put it under another jacket for layering, get the hood. The hooded version of this was just lovely, but I didn't have as much use for it personally. I hope this helps.
The good: warm
The bad: a lot tighter fitting than the LT

product_title: Microfiber Towel for Travel, Beach, Bath, Gym, Camping - XL Extra Large but Compact, Antibacterial and Quick Dry with small Carry Pouch
review_body:
I wanted to try this towel as a replacement for the bulky terry towel that I had been using when going to the local swimming pool. When I received it, I was stunned at how thin it was and was concerned that it would not be absorbent enough. The truth is that it is amazingly absorbent - much more so than my enormous terry cloth towel. I'm not sure how this is managed, but it actually gets you dryer than a conventional towel.

The only thing about this towel is that it feels very different than a conventional towel. It has a good deal more friction (likely because of the microfiber). Even though it has a soft, velour feel to it, it has more "drag" when you pull it across your body. What I found is that you shouldn't drag it, but rather you should do what I've long heard you should do with all towels - pat, don't rub. If you do this, it works a dream, takes up much less space than a conventional towel and dries faster.

After trying this, I wonder how it is that we haven't all transitioned to these types of towels. I'm guessing that it has to do with just not being used to their look and feel and having to learn to get used to something better and different. At the very least, I'd say get one of these for situations in which you have to carry your own towel.

product_title: Camp Chef Outdoor Camp Oven
review_body:
We used the campstove/oven in October. I've used a lot of camp stoves before and never found one I like much....except maybe the Camp Chef River Guide I used before. The burners on most camp stoves either stay too hot or not hot enough. Therefore, I wasn't expecting much with the stove top on this unit, but I gotta say this is the best, most adjustable stove I've ever used. The burners are big enough...you can tell they didn't skimp on space much, and I even cooked in moderate winds with no problems.

The oven: this thing is absolutely great. Don't pay any attention to bad reviews saying things like normal pans won't fit in there...of course large oven pans won't fit in there but you will be surprised what will fit in there. The pan you see in the picture is 10x15\\" (outer dimensions). As you can see I cooked two Cornish hens in there....with no problems (yes, I used a meat thermometer). There's your proof. You know if it will cook Cornish hens it will do great for breads, pastries and pizzas.

It does take this oven a while to get to temperature for cooking meat, but I found it to be almost as easy to use as my home oven, and better than lots of home ovens I've used. I would much rather have the problem of slow heating, than getting too hot since you can't control that. Honestly, that was my biggest worry with the oven and stove top; getting too hot and having to constantly adjust the controls or having to constantly open the oven door to let heat out. But, No problems at all. I love this thing

product_title: CamelBak Podium Big Chill 25 oz Insulated Water Bottle
review_headline: Great Construction Leads to Long Lasting Endurance
review_body:
Simply said, I love this water bottle. I purchased two in January of 2013 and have been using them every day since. I refill each of the bottles an average of four times daily, and I put them in the dishwasher every night, needless to say they get a lot of use. After about 13 months the silicone caps ripped in half from bite wear, but removing them did not impede performance in any way. Both of the bottles fit securely in my bicycle frame, and are pliable enough to squeeze with one hand while riding. In the first year the bottles were great at keeping all sorts of drinks cold, but I have noticed as time has progressed that the bottles' ability to keep drinks cool has diminished.However, this is a very minor issue considering the duration and scope of use. These bottles have held up very well to the abuses of an active young man.I am very pleased with the quality of CamelBak's product. Unfortunately after almost two years of faithful service the "JetValve" on both bottles has started to leak, but it was quite impressive how long they held up. I will no doubt be purchasing the newest model of the Podium Big Chill.

Some Stats:
4 refills X 25oz water= 100oz per bottle per day
4 refills X 675 days= 2700+ refills per bottle
4 refills per day X 25oz water X 675 days= 525+ GALLONS OF WATER per bottle
675+ dishwasher cycles on "sanitize" and "high heat" modes

product_title: Kamp Rite Double Self-Inflating Mattress
review_body: The mattress self-inflates well.  With a little work it does roll back up to fit in the bag, with two of us rolling together.  It's a bit heavy and bulky, though, and took up quite a bit of room in the car. If you have a truck (or lots of car space), no problem. We ordered ours on September 25 from the Amazon warehouse, and later found that Amazon's return window expired on October 27, just before our camping trip.  We found this out when we had a problem with our first one and Amazon said it was too late to return it, after just a little over a month.  But Kamp-Rite's customer service saved the day and promptly sent us another one after we sent them a photo of the problem.  They said the manufacturing defect (a seam that separated) was rare and took it on themselves to send us another one.  This seems to be a company of real people who care about their product.  We will not hesitate to do business directly with Kamp-Rite when ordering again.  Be aware that Amazon's return policies are not what they once were.

review_headline: It was EXACTLY what I needed !!
review_body: I purchased the Condor MOLLE Large Utiity Accessory/Mag Pouch-Black to have a way to securely attach and carry my Bushnell Legacy WP 8x42 binoculars to my gear using its MOLLE attachment system.  I got the pouch's dimensions and compared them to my binocular's dimensions inside the soft, padded Bushnell factory carrying case.  It looked like it would be a pretty snug fit, but that was what I wanted, with the factory carrying case providing the cushioning and ease of removing / re-inserting my binoculars and the Condor Large MOLLE Utility Accessory Pouch-Black providing the secure attachment and carrying of my binoculars on my gear with the MOLLE attachment system.  When I got the pouch, I opened the elastic tension cord all the way out, pushed my hands inside the Condor pouch to open it up as much as possible, and slid the Bushnell factory carrying case containing my binoculars and their cleaning cloth into the Condor pouch.  It was a snug fit, as I had expected, but the binoculars inside the factory carrying case fit perfectly!  The strength, durability, and overall quality of the materials used and very good workmanship found in this Condor pouch is what I have grown to expect from them, with Condor making all of my magazine pouches, both 9mm and 5.56mm, my 3-Day Assault Pack, H-Harness, Tactical Belt, HHR Pouch, EMT Pouch, and other assorted Condor gear pouches I use.  With lower prices than the \\"well advertised and recognized\\" gear manufacturers, Condor is one of the best values in tactical gear I have found.

product_title: Squirt Long Lasting Dry Lube, 4 oz bottle
review_headline: Have used this lube for about 55,000 miles
review_body: My wife and I each ride about 5,000 miles/ year and have used it for a number of years.  I like it. It is thicker and you can apply it 'accurately' -- it does not run and drip all over like thinner lubes like white lightening or petroleum oils.  Chains are quiet. Rain does not seem to effect or remove it.  I get about 24,000 miles use of a chain ring with it and about 15,000 miles out of a rear cassette. Meanwhile, my wife's cassette with this lube lasted 22,000 miles and the chain ring at 22,000 miles still looks acceptable. Chains also last proportionately as long.  I do take a towel and clean the chain before applying say every 100-200 miles because it does build up and looks dark and still sticks. I only put water on the towel.  Because it's a milky color you can easily see it on the chain to make sure it's applied completely.  Shake it, and let the sun hit the bottle if possible in cool weather before applying as it is thick and needs help to flow.

review_body:
I may of done it wrong but this did not work for me. Attempted to revive a skiing shell that lost it's DWR.
Ran through the front loader with the tech was as instructed and then followed with the TXDIRECT wash in.
Then used the bucket handwash method on the clean jacket following the directions closely. Attempted to use it on 2 jackets and 1 pair of snowpants.
Let dry for a couple days and it's like the jacket is only half DWRed.. It wets out in small spots and beads in others right off.
Read how other people use it with success and am disappointed. Especially since this seemed better for my lungs then the heavy duty spray on stuff.

I am happy with Nikwax wax for leather so I was surprised I couldnt get this to perform equally well.
May try to use another bottle of direct wash in after the tech was is gone and I'm out of my spray on water proofer that is used for boat canopies since it's idiot proof and works super well even though you can't breathe the stuff in.

product_title: Source Tactical Gear Magnetic Tube Clip (Black)

Since there are two Source brand items and this one is specifically called Tactical, I expected this one to better size match the tactical tube. Since it fits so tightly, there is no way to slide it to adjust it, you have to remove it to reposition it. Once you get it where you want it you really should never have to take it off again, so this isn't much of an issue. If I don't plan to use the clip I just leave the "clothes" part of it, I never take off the hose part. The magnet is strong and no problems with it falling off, but I haven't gone commando with it either, just hikes and bikes. If you want any alternative to consider, or a cheaper option, there's a non-magnet style with a spring-clip one I've seen, here we go Blackhawk and Platypus make one, http://smile.amazon.com/BLACKHAWK-Hydration-Tube-Positioning-Clip/dp/B000WV62JA/ref=sr_1_8?ie=UTF8&qid=1417542475&sr=8-8&keywords=hydration+clip and http://smile.amazon.com/Platypus-07717-Lapel-Clip/dp/B000J2KEUK/ref=sr_1_7?ie=UTF8&qid=1417542475&sr=8-7&keywords=hydration+clip

product_title: Topeak Shock N Roll Hand-Shock Pump with Gauge (Steel, 9.8 x 1.9 x 1.5-Inch)
review_body: There are so many things wrong functionally & mechanically w/this pump.To make this easier I'll identify the main parts:1) hose, 2)valve screw,3)gauge,4)shaft & 5)handle. To begin. If I hadn't actually got it to air the tire, I would say it's junk but it does work; it's just MANUAL LABOR to do so. I pumped a completely deflated bicycle tire w/a Schrader stem, it took > 10 min. & I felt like I'd broken my arm & my palm was actually bruised. I ACTUALLY BROKE A SWEAT!!! FUNCTIONAL ISSUES: 1)Handle DOES NOT bend perpendicular(like a "T")to the shaft (to comfortably fit in hand) but rather stays erect & thus DIGS into your hand while pumping & is VERY PAINFUL as the tire gets full.2) Switching between pumping tires/shocks involves twisting the pump shaft, however, it DOES NOT LOCK IN EITHER POSITION so when attempting to use the pump it will twist out of position causing the pump to fail & air to bleed out of the pump. This happened to me > 5 times on both tires! 3) pump doesn't withdraw out enough to allow sufficient air into every pump; IT'S INEFFICIENT! MECHANICAL ISSUES: 1) Handle doesn't bend perpendicular to shaft, 2) valve screw doesn't easily thread onto the stem, 3)Shaft doesn't lock in either shock/tire position, 4)There needs to be a twist stand build into this to allow it to be placed on the ground to assist in pumping. CONCLUSION: DON'T BUY, yet. this is a great concept that just fails in application. THERE'S A SIMILAR SCHWINN PUMP (just tire not shock), $10-$20 that addresses all the faults the Topeak pump has. Topeak PAY ATTENTION! Topeak's quality control dept. obviously didn't use this before it left the factory.

product_title: Kelty Gunnison 2 Person Tent
review_headline: Great Tent - Just know that a 2-person tent is a TWO person tent!
review_body:
Only used a couple times so far, it is mainly for my yearly camping trip out at Laconia, NH for bike week. I have an older Eureka! tent that holds 4 adults comfortably and is tall enough for a 6ft person to stand up in, but I only need a tent for myself and my gear. The Eureka needs a second person to help me set it up properly.

The main points:
-Gunnison 2.2 is very sturdy and waterproof
-Sets up quickly and easily (only one person needed)
-Has 2 doors and 2 vestibules to store my boots/helmet/etc which is very handy.

**Please understand that the 2-person rating is meant for backpacking/camping. For myself and my gear, the 2.2 is fine, but when you are adding more than just 2 backpacks, you are going to get tight. The other reviews are correct. If this is for you and your wife/gf or child, then no problem. If you plan on using this with one of your buds from time to time....look into the 3 or 4 person version. The two of you will be shoulder to shoulder or head-to-toe. Your gear is meant to be outside in the vestibules.

These are backpacking tents that are meant to take up the least amount of space/pack for long travel. Just keep that in mind, and you won't be disappointed. There is nothing so far that I can see wrong with this design, I just want potential buyer to understand the space constraints before purchase. I have read quite a few reviews of others being upset that space is tight. They list the sq-ft/dimensions, consider what you need before you buy.

review_headline: Easily beats out other lights for lumen output
review_body:
Impressive little light. Those fins do shed heat. On "high" you could use this as a hand warmer. On the back are three lights indicating how much of a charge is left. It has a built-in circuit that lowers the light intensity to save the battery, but just push the button and it goes right back up to BRIGHT. Easily beats out other lights for lumen output. I've had mine on high for 5 hours and the last indicator has been blinking for 20 min. that it is about to die.
This probably should not be used on a mountain bike. The light mount is a very sturdy rubber-type band but doesn't look like it would hold the light from turning around the handle bar if there is lots of jarring/bouncing. Easy to take off the bar, but easy to steal as well. The battery pack has a separate charger and is also mounted on the handle bar. The kit even comes with a head-band for mounting the light on your forehead, but I'm pretty sure I'll never do that because of the "less than cool" factor. I've had many lights over the years with the best being made by Serfas (terrific company by the way). That said, this is very well thought out and constructed. I will outfit all my bikes with them.
