product_title: LuminAID Solar Inflatable Light, Version 1
review_body:
This little invention is AWESOME. No, I haven't yet had a chance to take it out camping and truly use it to its full extent. However, I have run all around my house with it and I love it. I love the idea of it, the usefulness of it, the compactness of it, the design team and rationale behind it, and that these are so simple. So the design team idea behind this was to create cheap and quick light in the wake of national disasters (I believe I read that right in the article). This solar-powered light packs to a shape the size of the panel in the picture (the solar panel and bright white part with the logo). The rest of the inflatable bag folds behind it and is secured with a tab, making it very easy to transport. Once inflated (which you pinch to inflate and when not pinched, it does not lose all its air), it's easy to hang and the space makes a brighter "bulb" to reflect light. I hung them in my dining room to catch light through a sliding door and then slung them over the backs of the chair. Up close, I could read by their light in the dark room, so they are useful for doing tasks close to it. Because they are so bright, they cast dark shadows, so doing tasks farther away was easy, but reading was harder. I also like that you can turn it on and off. I didn't do a stringent test but it seemed these charged well in somewhat ambient light. However, more testing would be required on that.
I would buy these again in a heartbeat, and I plan to use these for camping. I love my headlamps but get paranoid about using battery power. These would make GREAT stocking stuffers for anyone concerned about a bug-out bag or zombie apocalypse-sort of thing.

The wind caused tent problems which is why I had to cut my camping short.

I stand about 5'10" and have fairly wide shoulders. I had to wiggle around a bit to "stretch" the bag to fit me but once I did, I slept like a rock (other than when there was a strong gust of wind that caused tent poles to smack me in the head). The bag was so warm, I ended up stripping down and opening the bag a little to cool off.

I am very impressed with the quality of the bag and especially the price PLUS, contrary to the name of "Suisse" , the bag is made in the USA. I feel very comfortable in knowing this bag will keep me warm and comfortable when I camp again.

review_body:
The LED lamp is solidly built and performs very well in three modes (Bright, Normal, Flashing). The USB rechargeable batteries are a great innovation for being removable, allowing a fully charged spare to be carried on a long ride. Rugged construction, the product is packaged with great care showing evidence of a highly committed small company.

I would definitely recommend this USA made product.

Pro's:

Lamp Mounting - Very secure, and fits well on large and small diameter handbars
Lamp Performance - Bright Blue ceramic LED - The ability to set wide and narrow focus is excellent
Construction - Rugged!

For the manufacturer: Two recommendations for product improvement:
1) When the focus is set narrow, the lens housing rattles just a bit on the threads. While not severe, it's just enough to have drawn my attention during the ride. It was silent when the lens was "tight", but that wide angle is a bit rude (IMHO) to oncoming traffic because the lamp is so very bright.
2) Why not include just one tail-light that can be recharged as well. The disc cell batteries are expensive, and your competitiveness would certainly improve for having a "one stop shop" kit.

product_title: Buff Merino Wool Headband
review_headline: One of the best accessories I've ever purchased
review_body:
I travel extensively and often go from crazy climates to another. Sometimes I need a cap to keep my head warm, or sometimes I need to cover my face because of cold or pollution. Sometimes I just need a scarf to cover my neck. But I don't want to carry excessive things in my pockets or bag that I'll never use. A number of years ago, I bought a polyester buff because I saw "Long Way 'Round" and it came in very handy. It kept sweat out of my eyes and the sun off my neck in South America and in Asia, and it kept pollution of out my nose and mouth in China. And it held up through years of abuse.

Now that winter is coming and I need to prepare to exercise outdoors, I need something that will serve multiple purposes. In the few weeks that I've had the merino wool buff, I've used this as a winter hat to cover my head and ears and I've used this as a balaclava while cycling to keep my nose/face/head/neck warm. The fact that this has so many uses and it's versatile means this will be my go-to accessory when heading out in brutal midwest winters.

It's a great accessory and you can't go wrong with it. Worth the investment.

product_title: Timbuk2 Wingman Suitcase 2013
review_headline: great carry on bag for travel in europe
review_body: I bought this for a trip to Europe where I would be taking a lot of those discount airlines between countries that are really picky about the volume and weight of your carry on baggage. This suitcase was more than enough for 3-4 days worth of clothes and toiletries. It was also great not having to role a bag over European cobblestone, and the backpack straps came in super handy when running to catch trains and buses. It always fit into overhead bins no problem, and I think it is specifically made to fit the dimension restrictions on small airlines while maximizing space. The second time I used it was for a week of traveling in India. Again, plenty of room for a weeks worth of clothes, toiletries, my iPad, etc, and so convenient to lug around. The third time I used it was on a multi-day camping trip. It worked wonderfully and was way for accessible than a duffel or backpacking bag, while still being tough, durable, easy to cart around (backpack straps for the win!) and moderately water resistant. I still use my rolling suitcase for most domestic trips because it looks more professional, but abroad, this thing is amazing. It can also be flattened and put in a bigger suitcase if you think you might need to whip it out for a short excursion within a longer one, as I did in Europe and Asia. Unlike many minimalistic bags, it still has a lot of pockets. I trust the laptop compartment with my mac air. One thing I wish it had was better weight dispersion when wearing it like a backpack. Perhaps a waist or chest clip would help because all the weight of the bag is on your shoulders, so it's definitely not meant for carrying like a backpack for a long time. Otherwise, I'm super enthusiastic about the bag, and you will be too if you buy it.

review_headline: Looks nice, feels nice, is nice.
review_body:
I bought this pack for a two week trip to Nepal. I didn't want to risk losing my bag on a sketchy airline, as had had happened on a previous trip, so I was looking for something big enough to carry what I needed, yet small enough to use as a carry on. This fit the bill. I bought the S/M, and it fits like a charm. I'm 5'3 and 120 lbs.
Ironically, on the first domestic flight of the aforementioned trip with this bag as a carry-on, I had to gate check it. In the process, a door must have gotten closed on one of the clips, as it came back to me broken. I finagled a caribiner to do it's job while abroad, and then sent it in to Osprey when I got home. They fixed it and sent it back for free within a couple of weeks. 1 point Osprey, 0 points American Airlines.( I also bought a nylon bag that I can put the pack in at the gate so the same thing doesn't happen again.)
Overall, this bag is a good investment for anything from a large day pack to a small world-traveling pack. I've used it for both, and many trips in between. I'd buy again in a heartbeat!

product_title: Mirrycle Incredibell Adjustabell 2 Bike Bell
review_headline: The sound of this bell is extremely sharp.
review_body:
I personally hate the sharp sound of this bell and the thumb mechanism to flick it, but I guess it will work. I just installed the bell last night. it went on my Mtn bike bars okay. I don't think this bell can be taken off to be reused on a different bike once it's been installed.

The sound of the bell is *extremely* sharp to my ears -- so much so that I can tell I'm going to hate having to use it because it makes me cringe. I'll have to try it outside and see how effective it is and see if the sound is less bothersome there. Inside the house, which is where I tried it, the sharpness of the sound made me want to smash the bell to pieces. It won't surprise me if I end up choosing a different sounding bell. Yes, It will get the attention of people in your way, of that I'm sure, and yes that's the purpose of any bell you put on a bike. But it is not a pleasant sound at all, so just be aware of that if you're going to pull the trigger and order this one.

product_title: Visol Iceman Chrome Matte Torch Flame Lighter
review_body:
Upon initial opening of the package, this looked like an "odd little duck" for a lighter. The igniter button is a modernistic looking device, but after using it, it's very functional and the lid gets "out of the way" for the big ring sticks. The lighter is very well made and has a nice solid feel to it. This should be a durable lighter. As this lighter has a single flame torch, it's excellent for toasting a cigar and doing pin-point touch ups. I really like this feature. (Some of the multi-flame lighters can get can get a little out of control when doing touch ups.) The flame adjustment screw is accessible with any small flat-blade screwdriver (including the Visol purging/adjusting tool). Unfortunately, it cannot be adjusted with a finger nail, so unless you carry a screw driver or the Visol tool with you, it's going to be very hard to adjust it on the fly. As far as fuel capacity, this lighter, due to its thin profile, is very deceptive. Its very miserly in its use of fuel as I've now toasted and lit (throw in 3 or 4 touch ups in too) over 12-54+ ring sized cigars and it's still going strong. Huge plus for a cigar lighter. My only issues with this lighter, that would raise it up to a 5-star rating, is the lack of a fuel sight glass and the difficulty in adjusting the flame without a screwdriver handy. All in all though, a solid-feeling, interesting looking lighter. I'd highly recommend it to anyone.

Pros:
Miserly use of fuel
torch lid moves out of the way for large-ring sticks
solid feel metal body (no plastic in sight)

Cons:
Almost impossible to adjust without a screwdriver
No sight window for the fuel.

product_title: ALPS Mountaineering Zephyr 3-Person Tent
review_headline: If you're spending more on a tent you have to sit down and ask yourself why. This tent is great.
review_body:
This tent is the best I have owned yet. When factoring in the price i don't think it can be beat. I bought and tried this tent on a quick overnight in the middle of South Florida summer. Anyone camping from april to october in Florida can tell you the importance of ventilation in a tent. Two main reasons, one of course, airflow so you don't sweat to death in an hour. The other is moisture control at night. (If you think back to most childhood memories of tent camping and remember the wetness of touching the inside of the tent) This tent handled both really well due to the full mesh double wall design. The mesh breaths very well with any air movement at all and the fact that the fly never touches the mesh made for a cool (as cool as florida can be in august) and very dry experience.
This was all a test run for taking my girlfriend to the blueridge parkway for a long weekend of camping/biking/hiking and seeing the leave change.
The tent did great, it had plenty of room for both of us with a bunch of cold weather sleeping gear. Two things i have to give this tent praise for is one: the way the air flows. It comes around the bottom and is taken up the sides of the fly and out the top vent. This did some nice things for us like take the moisture out without noticing cold air rushing straight on to you.
The other praise worthy feature was how it took to in-climate weather. The fly stakes out great, kept my gear dry under vestibules (shoes, hiking bags, firewood, and fireball) and didn't flap or bow in on us when the winds picked up to forty knots with freezing rain on top of a mountain. We woke up in the morning to everything dry and still staked down perfectly.
All this comes with the added bonus of being able to easily pack in my small hiking bag with sleeping pad (klimate static v), down comforter (light fill) camping pillow, biolight stove, , cloths, extra blanket and food. No other tent i looked at (researched a month on amazon) met these kindsof amenities and was truly a hiking tent size.

For hiking or car camping this tent rocks.
The only "con" i could give it if from my girlfriend and her request was that it have more than the one little window in the middle of the "A" on the rain-fly.
If you do purchase this tent do yourself a favor and get the custom alps footprint for it. It makes setting up, ground moisture control and rain-fly installation super easy.

Plus, you won't have to deal with heavy towels weighing down your load because these towels are light weight and fold small enough they could fit in your bag/purse! product_title: Zippo Butane Fueled Lighter, Vertical Chrome
review_headline: Bad first impression but please read my update
review_body: After reading A LOT of bad reviews about Zippo's butane lighters I figured I would take a chance on a product from a company with a long history of making reliable fire... bad move on my part. This lighter is outstanding if all you want to do is make sparks with no flame. I read all the included directions from Zippo before filling this lighter with \\"super-special\\" Zippo brand butane and it just doesn't work worth a darn. I did manage to get a flame out of it here and there but even then the flame was never reliable. I'm not sure sending it back to Zippo for evaluation and repair is even worth the headache. I was really looking forward to owning my first Zippo butane lighter but what a disappointment this product has been. Hopefully the good ol' Zippo windproof lighter that's on it's way to me will work better. We'll see...    UPDATE: This lighter has been sitting on my kitchen table since I bought it. Everyday, just to remind myself never to buy another Zippo Blu butane lighter, I would pick up my lighter and try five times to make it light up and stay lit. Each day I would be disappointed by seeing sparks with no flame at all other than a flash of flame every now and then. Things went on like this until one day the flint wore down to the point it was keeping the striker wheel from turning. I replaced the flint per the instructions included with my lighter and now this thing works like a champ! I've still been picking it up off my kitchen table everyday and now it lights up fast, hot and strong. Once in a great while it takes two attempts to get it lit but that has been rare. This lighter of mine now lights up so reliably it's almost boring. I even tried leaving it in my refrigerator overnight just to see if I could get the butane cold enough to keep it from lighting up. No luck, the lighter still fired up although the flame was much smaller and weaker but I expected that. I would have never believed that simply changing the flint would make such a big difference in the performance of my lighter because the flint that came in the lighter was throwing plenty of sparks into the butane that I could hear flowing. Go figure. Anyhow, I hope this update helps someone out there who may have experienced the same initial disappointment that I did. As honest as my review was in the beginning, I was very reluctant to write it because Zippo is a great American company and we need all those we can get these days. I can honestly say that I'm impressed enough with how my Blu lighter is now working that I may just purchase a second.

review_headline: too bad. A slide with a snap would be better ...
review_body: I waited a few months before writing to see if any issues developed.  Shortly after using it, the lasers became so dim you could hardly see them even at night.  I discovered the cause a week later when the non-rechargeable batteries died.  I put in new batteries and the lasers came back to life.  If your batteries are getting low, there is not enough voltage to turn on the lasers. Put in new batteries!  Pros: the mount is attached to the seatpost with a thumb-screw clamp and the taillight slides into the post clamp.  I remove the light every time I leave the bike as I had the previous taillight stolen. It really is quite bright. Cons:  AA batteries would improve the somewhat short life of the AAA batteries.  You need a very small phillips-head screwdriver to change the batteries.  So if they die on the road, too bad. A slide with a snap would be better and would allow a tool-less battery change.  Pedalling does get in the way of the lasers.  They need to be a little longer and set wider.  It would be nice if the unit could be raised one foot to make the beams longer and wider. Overall rating; 4 stars.  Basically I am quite pleased; just a few minor shortcomings.  I would recommend this light.

product_title: Diercon Personal Water Filter
review_headline: ☼ Versatile Filter for the Hiker or for your Emergency "Bugout Bag" ☼
review_body:
I like the design of this filter. It's reasonably compact, it has an estimated filter capacity of 1,500 liters and it comes with accessories that facilitate drinking directly out of a water source from the end of the filet, using a tube for locations where you may not be able to bend down and use the filter directly, and a ways to drink directly out of a bottle or bad that you've filled with water.

Short of sending a dirty and filtered sample of water to a lab for testing, there's no way to know for sure exactly how good the filter is. I am supposed to be getting a dissolved solids meter in very soon and plan on using it to at least see what kind of difference the filter does with that type of contaminant. I did test it with some unfiltered tap water. The water in my home is pretty disgusting, so we use a whole house Culligan filter that makes a huge difference taste and odor. I have an outside spigot that isn't filtered and used that water to test and compare with the filtered water in my home. The quality of the water filtered with the Diercon filter, to my taste buds anyway, seemed to be on par with the water filtered with my Culligan filter.

All things considered, this seems to an excellent product, and at under $18 (at time of review) and a service life of 1,500 liters, this appears to be a very good buy.

product_title: Orp Horn Light Black, One Size
review_body:
I do not recommend this light for the following reasons:
The mounting strap is difficult to put on and take off the handlebar.
The charger is not a standard mini USB and its difficult to plug into the light.
The light is very bright and there is a lot of flashback along the edges of the front lens which radiates 45 degrees from the forward position and blinds the rider if looking down. Its very distracting.
Most importantly, the horn, even though is loud, is not recognized by pedestrians or cars as anything worth paying attention to. I have been completely ignored using both the polite "chirp" and the shriller "tweet". A loud vocal "on your left" or "bike coming through" is more effective and quicker than trying to reach for the horn which is usually not ergonomically in the best position for a quick reaction maneuver when faced with a sudden errant vehicular error in judgement.

As an aside and I'm not sure this if completely true, someone told me that the Amazon price is twice what is offered if purchased in Portland Oregon where it is manufactured.

Bottom line, use your voice….its much quicker to use and more effective. If you are truly looking for an effective horn, get the Air Zound, 115 db, Horn. Bulky, but extremely loud.

product_title: Keen Kanga Covertible Daypack Tote
review_headline: Good bag for yoga and around town, not for travel.
review_body:
This is a good bag but it could be a lot better. To begin with, most "convertible backpacks" are wearable three ways; as a backpack, a shoulder bag, and a messenger bag. This bag can only be worn as a backpack or a shoulder bag. The straps are not long enough and it lacks a mechanism for using it as a cross body or messenger bag. This would be ideal for using it for travel. That way you can carry it hands free and still have access to the contents of the bag. Also shoulder bags are very easy to grab and run off with, if one is traveling to an area where that is an issue. Finally, the mechanism for converting it from shoulder to backpack is a flimsy plastic slider, I don't think it would hold up to hardcore use.
This bag is made to carry a yoga mat so it may be more for that than for travel, but still I found it lacking. Aside from the complaints I listed, the bag seems well made and fairly aesthetically pleasing. Water bottle pockets are nice.

product_title: Generic 26" Hyper Havoc Full Suspension Men's Mountain Bike, Black
review_body: I want to start my review off with saying I did not get this bike on Amazon. I bought it from a very recognizable retail store and for less than the seller is asking for on Amazon. When I first got this bike it was the first bike I had in a few years, so I was just happy to have a bike when I first got this one. After 10 months of use I can say I am not satisfied with this bike. The brakes work better than any other bike I've had, even the ones that costed quite a bit more money. The shifting gears are horrible if you shift them to fast or to slow the chain falls off a part of the bike. The handlebar is my main problem and was what caused me to dislike this bike. I let someone borrow this to do some downhill riding and the handlebar came off WHILE he was ridng down a hill. I would not recommend this bike to anyone however if you are just looking for a bike to have for occasional riding, this might be good for you. If you are one to do downhill mountain biking or trail riding like myself this is not for you. This bike doesn't have the quality to ride trails or downhill for long. Something will always happen to it. There is to many things to criticize in this bike that I couldn't post them all. Spend the extra money and get a good bike. Not much just more than this.

I staked the tent down using the stakes that came with the tents and had a completely sleepless night because the wind kept lifting the tent up and the stakes did not hold. I pitched the tent for the second time in about 20 minutes, this time in the light, and used the new thicker stakes. product_title: Phantom Aquatics Air-Ease Swimmer's Snorkel
review_headline: It is a very useful tool for practicing freestyle (front crawl)
review_body:
It is a very useful tool for practicing freestyle (front crawl). I was a complete novice, had the sloppiest form imaginable, and with this gadget I was able to work on proper technique without having to worry about breathing. I still haven't mastered breathing out of the side of my mouth, but my form is solid now. In 5 weeks or so I went from not being able to swim at all to being one of the fastest swimmers at my gym.

The only drawback with this snorkel is that if you use proper head positioning, which means keeping your eyes parallel to the center line of the pool and not lifting your forehead, the snorkel can get some water in it. Not always, but often enough. There is a cap (sold separately)to eliminate that, but it requires hot water to attach and re-attach, which means it will be tricky to take it off once you hit the pool. The cap also restricts breathing significantly, which means your lungs will be getting a great work out. Whenever I get water in the snorkel, I make like a whale and give it a good air blast to clear out, then I'm back to swimming like Michael Phelps. Kidding, but I am very happy with this purchase.

product_title: BMS Bi-Metro XLT YELLOW Gas Single Cylinder 4 Stroke Semi-Auto Moped Scooter
review_headline: You get what you pay for...
review_body:
Bought one of these and these are my experiences:
It was delivered in a metal crate which had a significant dent but the bike appeared undamaged. Took me an hour or so to put together. It came with some clunky add on turn signals in front that mount to the mirror mounts. Presumably the DOT must dictate a certain distance between them so they added these to the US model. I removed them and found that the build in turn signals were not plugged in so I disconnected the plugs from the add-on turn signals and plugged the build in ones in and they worked as expected.
Then I found that the head and tail light did not work and after riding it I noticed that the battery was not charging either. After some diagnostics with a multi-meter I found where the wires were going; the wiring diagram in the included manual was of not much use since it had the Asian wiring I presume and was quite different. The head light was plugged into a red/white wire not shown on the wiring diagram. Finally worked out that the rectifier unit was not grounded due to a loose wire in the connector that plugs into the rectifier. Fixed this and the headlight works and battery is charging. I have technical knowledge and the tools to diagnose this "good luck" to the average user on this. Rode the bike around the block and noticed that it pulled to the right; found that the wheels were not aligned fixed this as well. Rode it to work a few times and noticed strange noises which I found were coming from the chain case; found a plastic guide that is supposed to stop the chain from rubbing on the swing arm mount. Bad plastic it was disintegrating so I removed it. Noise gone.
The bike has a semi-automatic (they call it) gearbox. Annoyingly I find it harder to ride the thing smoothly than a bike with a standard clutch. The clutch disengages automatically when stopping and engages when opening the throttle, this is fine but shifting down you have to blip the throttle or better still wait until the revs are quite low or the backwheel may lock for a moment. It appears that the clutch disengages when depressing the gear lever but then engages rapidly when releasing the gear lever. Takes quite some practice to ride smoothly and annoyingly the gear lever works in reverse to a normal motor cycle down is up and up is down going through the gears. Finding neutral takes stabbing the gear lever three or four times, thank goodness there is a light for that so you know you have reached it.
The gearing is way too low and first gear is for walking pace only; presumably on bad roads in Asia and with the bike over loaded perhaps you need such a low gear but in the US it is useless; also at 30 MPH it already feels like it is revving quite high and the bike would bebefit from a fifth gear or needs to be geared up. Others I see online have replaced the front sprocket with a 16 tooth unit replacing the 14 tooth standard one. I am in the process of ordering such a thing which has to be custom made the importer does not stock such a thing.
All in all the unit is somewhat poorly made and quality control is not too good. Ofcourse you get what you pay for and better quality bikes similar to this one can be had for well over 2000 dollars. product_title: EDELRID - Boulder Chalk Bag, Oasis/Night
review_body: I purchased this on July 27th, 2014, and I am currently still using it as my main bouldering chalk bag as of October 11th, 2014.  I boulder around 2-4 times a week anywhere from 2-4 hours a session.    I am a relatively new climber and this is my first boulder bag. I only have experience with one other prAna chalk bag that I still use for rope climbs.    Having not used any other bouldering bags, it is hard for me point out any advantages or disadvantages it might have when compared to other bags.    I haven't had any problems with chalk leaking out of the twist closure, though my bag has rarely been upside down. It is easy to twist open and close and takes about 5 seconds. The Velcro stays connected to the sides of the mouth and keeps the lining of the bag out of the way.    The main area where the chalk is held is plenty big for me.  I fill it to probably 1/4-1/2 of the way full to avoid any extra chalk poofing out and I don't have to refill it for quite some time, even when I occasionally climb with my brother who chalks up to prepare for chalking up.    The included brush is nice, its got a bigger end, probably a little big bigger than an average toothbrush, and a much smaller end. I usually use the gym brushes and rarely mine but it's nice to have my own when I need it.    There is a spongey thing connected from one side of the bag to the other side, and hangs about an inch above the bottom of the bag. I rarely use it and don't really know what it's for but it's convenient when I need to clear extra chalk off my hands if I chalk up and then realize I need to take off my shoes or check my phone.    The bag has a mesh pocket on one half of the bag. I've never put anything in it so I cannot speak for how well it secures things.    The only negative I have with this bag is that when the chalk level in the bag gets lower the sides of the bag start to slightly cave in.  They haven't caved in to the point where chalk dips out and I am usually able to poke around the sides and straighten it out but I imagine if it get's any worse it may become more of a problem. I also don't know if this is a common problem with boulder bags, having never used any other bag.    The sides beginning to cave in are my reason for giving it 4 stars.    12/12/2014:  I left the bag in my car as I usually do, except for this time it was upside down and all scrunched up.  I took it to the gym a few days later and it still worked perfectly.  I no longer have worries about the sides caving in.  Rating changed to 5 stars.    Overall I am happy with this bag and view it as a good purchase.

review_headline: Great Flashlight, best I have found.
review_body:
I am a home inspector, so a good flashlight is essential to me. Over the years I have gone from the huge 4 D battery Maglite, to a nice small tactical led that cost well over a $100. A year or so ago, I found the $10 orange and black Cree led flashlights. They turned out to be twice as bright as the expensive one I was using at that time. So I switched.

I had three issues with these cheap led lights. 1) Several arrived defective. 2) They would get dangerously hot if left on for any extended time. 3)They tended to stop working (something in the switch mechanisms I believe) after a month or two. But with the low cost, I figured they could be replaced as needed.

Then I came across this Simon Cree LED. At the $26 I paid for it here on Amazon, I would still consider it to be inexpensive. After using it for a couple of weeks, I am very impressed. It is probably twice as bright as the cheap Orange/black ones I was using. It is much more solidly built. The focus ring is nicely designed. It seems to stay cool (still gets warm) during extended use. Time will tell as far as durability and longevity, but so far I am very happy with it and will probably pick up a couple more.

Now a side note about/to the Simon company. They appear to be very interested in customer service (or at least getting reviews.) Though I have had no reason to test it. I would suggest that they simmer down a little on their request for reviews. I am a business owner. I understand the value of good reviews and I truly appreciate good CS. I take the time to leave reviews on products that I like or don't like, because other peoples reviews are valuable to me. However, I cannot help but feel that receiving two emails (one before I even received the shipment) requesting reviews is a little much. Wait a month. Yesterday I received a phone call wanting a review. Honestly, while I tried to be nice to the gentleman on the phone who was just doing his job, this was a little over the line to me. I really did not appreciate getting a call, during business hours, pressing me a third time to leave a review of a 25 dollar flashlight. I am not sure how they got my number from Amazon, but I don't really want contact like that from vendors.

So, the flashlight is great. Hopefully, the CS would be too, if it were needed. They just need to chill out a little on their solicitation of reviews. product_title: Princeton Tec Remix LED Headlamp
review_headline: Nice light, bright enough, but batteries need to be replaced weekly
review_body:
After reading hundreds of product reviews on Amazon, I ended up with this lamp, because of brightness, weight/usability, and price. My 2 year-old Energizer Trail Finder lamp is no longer bright enough and requires that I really concentrate on the trail surface ahead of me. Getting older also means that things further away become more difficult to see in low-light conditions.

I took the light out on the trails about 1/2 hour before dawn this morning. It is not quite a new moon yet, but there was not much natural light either. Here are my first impressions.

- brightness: definitely brighter than my old light, but only in the highest setting and not by as much as I expected. Still, I can see the trail ahead comfortably, even on steep down-hill sections.
- mechanical construction: the light stays in place and does not bob around, which has always been a problem with the old light.
- tilt mechanism: the vertical adjustment is difficult to change with bare hands when the light is on your head and probably impossible to change with gloves. The range of angles works for me. I have to tilt it down as far as it goes for my trail runs and the light is about there where I need it. The good news - once it is set, it will not change the angle on its own.
- stray light: almost none, even when angled down in the furthest position there is very little stray light in my face
- battery life: obviously don't know yet, but I'd trade more brightness for a shorter battery life any day

Overall, I think this was a good investment. The price is high in comparison to the Energizer Trail Finder (more than twice) - with only 15 more lumen it is not that much brighter, but it is a solid little device and a useful addition to my running gear.

Update after week 1: I stepped outside this morning for my pre-dawn run, put the lamp on my head, pressed the button, and ... nothing. Batteries dead. This is a first and has never happened to me before. I don't think this lamp turns itself on when nobody is watching, so I must have turned it on by accident while it was at rest, sitting next to my desk with the GPS watch and the charger.
I am used for the batteries in my head lamp to last between 6 months and 1 year. If dead batteries is the new norm with this lamp, the Princeton Tec Remix and I will not be partners for long. I can't give it more than 2 stars now. Luckily the old Energizer Trail Finder eagerly came to the rescue.

Update after week 2: the new batteries are dead again, after only about 90 minutes of operation. I don't know how this happens. The on/off switch is easy to operate and it is exposed. I handled it with care after this happened the first time. Apparently the weight of the lamp is enough to switch itself on. I have no other explanation. I am reducing my rating to 1 star and I seriously regret my purchase.

Final update after week 4: I used to rinse the lamp in the sink after my runs until I noticed condensation inside the lenses. I don't know if this could have caused the rapid battery drain, because I stopped doing this and also started to remove the batteries from the lamp when not in use. The battery door is stiff and not robust enough for frequent open/close cycles, so this is not really a solution. It does however seem to make the batteries last longer - the 3rd set has been lasting 2 weeks now (about 3 hours of operation) and the light is still strong.
Unlike the claim in the product description, the lamp is not waterproof and I would not use it in rain. Another thing that I don't like is the single Maxbright LED. A single point source of light creates an image that lacks 3D information. My brain is relearning how to process this, and it is having a hard time figuring out for example how high I have to lift my feet to clear a branch that fell across the trail. A multi-LED lamp is better suited for nightly trail running because there is more 3D information in the resulting image. Amazon dropped the price of this lamp, but alas I cannot raise me rating. I have no reason to believe that I have a defective unit, but it is just not working as expected.but alas I cannot raise me rating. product_title: Coleman 30-Can Soft Cooler With Hard Liner
review_body:
I went camping with this last weekend, and it was great to have. The adjustable strap makes it very easy to carry. It's also much roomier inside than I pictured. The hard bucket inside is great because it comes out and can be washed separately. It can also be taken out if you just don't want to use it at all. There are several pockets on the outside that came in very handy for flatware, napkins and condiments. When zipped up it's totally leak-proof.

However, it didn't stay as cold as I had hoped for the trip. My friend brought one of those traditional plastic coolers, and the next day his ice was all intact still, and mine was mostly melted. So I wouldn't recommend this for more than one night, and don't put anything in it that can spoil easily.

Overall, it's a stylin' little bag, and you could probably even use it for regular storage if you needed to.

review_headline: 'Comfort' bikes don't all fit as intended...
review_body: My family has 3 bikes, so I bought the 4 bike rack just to be safe.  Glad I did.  We have 'comfort' bikes, so all bikes have a smaller amount of space between the down tube, seat tube, and top tube when compared to a traditional 10-speed design.  The bike in the video is obviously ideal to easily fit/feed through the two pronged bike rack system.  The only way I can fit all of the bikes on the rack is to have 2 bikes with the down tube resting on top of the rack holder vs. feeding the bike rack through the space between the tubes.  So, the one rack prong goes between the seat tube and top tube and then I rest the down tube on top of the rack.  After we tie it down with the accompanying strap, plus the rubber holders, it certainly seems to be secured, but it is definitely not mounted as intended.

product_title: Energizer Carabiner LED Area Tent Light
review_body:
I was looking for a versatile lighting option to serve dual duty as a camping/night hike light. This little light is uniquely equipped to serve well in both roles.

First off as a camping light, the built in loop and included carabiner allow for me to hang this on any elevated position such as a tree branch, lantern stand, etc and the bright LEDs on each side illuminate a respectable area in all directions. My tent comes with fittings on the inside to accommodate lanterns hung from the ceiling, this is a great option to use as a tent lantern as well because it's lightweight design and the dual lantern modes means you can dim the light in close quarters settings like a tent.

I also do a lot of hiking in the evenings after work which of course means I hike in the dark a lot. My ideal setup for this is to have the unit clipped to one of the utility/accessory loops on my backpack's shoulder strap which creates a little cone of light when using the flashlight mode. The lantern setting does not work well obviously as the bright light so close to my face obscures my vision completely.

My only complaint is that there is only one power button shared between the flashlight and the lantern forcing me to first cycle through two lamp modes before I can use the flashlight.

product_title: Sundome 2 Person Tent (Green and Navy color options)
review_headline: Great for one person!  Very easy set-up, good quality, compact tent.
review_body:
I did A TON of research and read a lot of reviews here on Amazon before finally deciding that this was the tent I was going to purchase. I was looking for a decently priced, easy to set-up, portable tent for one person. I wanted to use it for backpacking as well as other campsite adventures. I just used it for the first time this weekend so I don't have experienced feedback yet I suppose, but thought I would share my findings so far while they're fresh.

This tent was great for my needs! I have camped several times before so I am not new to it, however this was my first time where I would be sleeping in a tent alone, therefore transporting, setting up and taking down the tent myself. I took it on a up north camping trip in the woods this weekend in northern Michigan with some friends. Extremely easy to set up! You really can do it in minutes. I took my time with it while having a beer though, so maybe 10-20 minutes for me. Everything you need to set up comes with it.

I did not use the rainfly because there was no rain in the forecast but I'm sure it works great, this "awning" type is what you want. I also didn't put it on because I wanted to be able to look up at the stars at night, and let me tell you, that was AMAZING. Such a clear night and in the woods of northern Michigan you can see an insane amount of stars, along with the Milky Way! That was just too cool to be able to look at them through my tent ceiling. The windows of the tent were great too. I'll see if I can post a photo of my awesome spot in the photos section.

Although it did not rain at all (yay!) there was still a ton of moisture from the air/dew. So much that if you left your sleeping bag out (like my friend did) in the open for an hour or two, it will literally become wet like it did rain. My sleeping bag that I put in the tent right away still got some moisture on it, but there is nothing you can do about that if there is that much moisture in the air. May have been better if I closed the windows and put the rainfly on but it really was no big deal at all.

As for the actual sleeping space inside, it was totally fine for me. I am a little over 5'7" and I would say medium weight, not fat but not skinny. It was exactly what I was looking for, just enough space for me to sleep and my backpack. I would not recommend this as a two person tent though unless you are using it with a sig. other and want to cuddle all night and look at the stars=) In my opinion, it was the perfect amount of space for one. Two adults would probably be tight. Also, I used one of those self-inflating sleeping pads (regular size) and that fit well in there too.

Although my walk to this particular site was not long at all (only 5-10 minutes) I would definitely use it for backpacking. (That was what I had in mind when I first purchased it.) You would need a backpacking backpack, it won't fit inside a regular sized backpack. I'm sure you could strap it on the outside of a regular one though. Doesn't come with straps but the bag has handles so you could strap it on by putting a rope or whatever through those.

review_headline: Wish they got the order right... But I still went surfing! They were 12s @ head- head+1/2 high.

The Single Soft would be better suited for wider boards, such as a SUP, not a Surfboard... The strap buckles are welded units, but turn sideways when tightened and end up scrunching the webbing up in the buckles- undesireable (especially when it happens driving, as it loosens the hold on the board) but functional enough still for a 100 mile drive from Seattle to the coast. Overall it (the Single Soft Rack) is made withe quality fabric and Cams, comes with a nice carrying bag for storage, and didnt scratch the car. I still wonder about the lifting on the outer 4-6 inches of pad, and longevity due to the "strap rings/buckles" bunching and creating a pinch point.

product_title: GMC Denali Road Bike
review_headline: Hard to beat the speed/effort to price ratio on this, but definitely not perfect
review_body:
Ok - picked this up about a year back when I finally got the itch to resume road biking and wanted something that would get me a bit more speed than my beater mountain bike. A year later, I've since snagged a decent racing bike as I've upped my mileage, but I still use this as my city commuter and figure I'd post what is good, bad, and ugly about this beast.

The Good -
- The price paid was pretty amazing (roughly 170 in wally-world) and doesn't require me to lose sleep when locking up the bike in more shady areas of town.
- Once tuned, the ride is pretty smooth (as the 700cx32 tires are great for smoother gravel trails along with roads),
- Although it is heavy at 30lb, it only goes about 1 mph slower than my nice 19lb race bike at comparable levels of effort/HR (keeping it at 17mph on flats is pretty doable without sweating through my clothes)
- No issues/extra vibrations when above 30mph on longer downhills
- With the stickers off, it actually looks pretty nice (the black/yellow model looks great parked around the 'burgh).

The bad -
- Brakes are pretty weak and require you to be in the drops to fully squeeze (replaced pads for another $18 to help).
- Front handlebar area between the click-shifts aren't a standard width, so some normal handlebar mounted components won't easily mount (i.e. computer, lights)
- Original handlebar tape comes loose pretty quickly
- You'll want to tune up at a local bike shop after the first few long rides, as the click-shift gears need some fine tuning (can find youtube videos if you want to DIY), the wheels need some initial truing, and it is susceptible to flats until you put on some good wheel rim tape
- Downtubes on the frame are also a bit thick, making it hard to find areas to mount lock holders
- Gearing is comparable to what you'd see on a mountain bike (28/38/48 on the front crankset), so it is great for climbing super-steep hills (letting you do 5mph at 80rpm on the easiest gear combination), but it will limit your top-end when going downhill

The Ugly -
- Tires started splitting within a few hundred miles, so I needed to replace very early ($30 for kendas on here).
- Bottom bracket area needs to be tightened periodically as the crankset area starts making crunchy noises after lots of hard pedaling (roughly $50 if you want to fully replace the bottom bracket w. parts/labor from an LBS for a more permanent fix)
- Front crankset gears have hairline cracks in them now between some teeth

Otherwise, after about 1,000 miles of use, no big regrets as it got me off my ass, relatively efficiently down the street, and most importantly after having 2 other bikes get stolen in the past few years, I'm not losing sleep when locking it up in shadier parts of town.

product_title: Trangia 27-8 Ultralight Hard Anodized Stove Kit
review_body:
I am pleasantly surprised with my new cook set. I knew it was a good set when I bought it because I have looked at these sets for several months and read dozens of reviews. I was still concerned that this set, the 27, wouldn't be quite big enough at the end of a long day of cycling and seriously considered buying the 25. The manufacturer states that the 27 is designed for one or two people and the 25 for three or four. But, most camping gear seems designed for 0.5 people. That is, a one person cook set might feed a child, a two person tent will fit one adult, etc..

My fears were unwarranted. This morning I was able to use the 27's kettle to boil enough water to make a normal size cup of coffee and have a 2-serving sized bowl of instant oatmeal plus have just enough hot water left over to wash things up. For lunch, I made a grilled cheese sandwich on the frying pan then heated tomato soup in one of the pots on the same fill. For dinner, I boiled some pasta, refilled the stove, and then dry baked a blueberry muffin (using a jiffy-foil pan) for dessert. I managed to burn the outside of the muffin (my fault - too much heat) but the inside still tasted great! After the muffin was done the stove still had enough fuel to heat more water for a cup of hot chocolate.

I think the 27 set would be at max capacity for two people but for one 150 lbs. male touring cyclist I think it will be great.

product_title: Topeak Glueless Patch Kit
review_body:
I had this for 6 months or so unused since I bought it, it was only because my tire didn't get flat.
So the opportunity came and I tried the first patch. I made a 7 miles round trip to a store for the test, and it worked out fine, when I got home, the pressure was still nearly full. When I took the bike out for a ride a few hours later, the pressure was already about half. So, I took the patch off, cleaned it and re-repaired it with regular patch kit. Everything in good order now. In another word, the Topeak patch is worthless.

My experience with the different kind of patch kit in the past:
I've used bicycles to get around for over 30 years. I started repairing flat using regular vulcanizing patch kit because it was the only kind available. It worked but thing I didn't like about it was the waste of the patches. I get to use only one patch and the rest is waste because by the time you need to repair the second one, the glue is already dry(unless you get the second flat within a week).
So, when I found out that there was a new kind of patch kit that doesn't use the glue, I had to try it. It also came in very small package takes up only a minimal space in my bag. It was called Park GP-1, and it stayed on the spot and did its work near permanently(for years and thousands of miles).
Then Park replaced it with GP-2. It was more rigid than GP-1 and less stretchable, make it easier to handle than GP-1. It held the pressure only for a few miles. I tried a few more in the kit but the result was the same if not worse.
I went back to the vulcanizing glue patch kit, only this time I started using rubber cement(school project glue), so I didn't have to waste the patches. It works but not for on-location repair. I'd rather keep a spare tube.
Then came the Topeak glueless patch kit. I won't repeat the result here(see top of this review) but I was very disappointed to say the least, because I had a high hope thinking somebody finally figuredit out. I was wrong.

I wish I had bought more of GP-1 when it was available.

product_title: Mad Grip F50 Thunderdome Impact Gloves
review_headline: Yet another work glove worth buying
review_body:
I haven't had these for very long but at this point I don't care. They're not going to blow up tomorrow, so I'm probably going to get my money's worth out of them. Further more, I don't know what all this flip flopping on their sporting purpose potential is all about because I've been using them for work, ie stuff that real people actually do. I guess if you wore these for a game of pickup football, you'd be a really awesome WR. Just don't try to throw with them. Moving on.

Yeah, these gloves give you magic super grip. I'm able to easily pick up ~100lbs in the form of four boxes of screws...from the sides! Today, I helped someone move some large appliances. Helping move washers and dryers is a cake walk with these on. Just grab on to anything and you have grip. Smooth enameled surface? Whatever. These gloves sure don't care. It's basically harder to let go than get a decent grip on something. The thick backing is also nice for protecting your hands from getting rammed and crushed into stuff. In short, these are perfect for things like box handling, appliance moving, so on. Really, if loss of grip directly correlates to loss of strength in what you're doing, these gloves might be for you.

On the other hand, they're not perfect. Aside from the obvious jobs that soft gloves aren't suitable for, these things give you some serious sausage fingers. Yes, you'll drastically improve in box handling just by having these on. You will also drastically suck at opening boxes because your big clumsy fingers won't be able to fit into slots and openings to pull tabs. And while it probably seems obvious, don't handle anything abrasive with these on...such as a file. I'm not sure that these gloves are particularly good for any task requiring tools, for that matter.

And finally, concerning the fit. Not bad. My hands are fairly ideal for the typical China made size L. These gloves expect a slightly longer finger, so they can be a little bit uncomfortable. I could also see how wearing these for a really long duration might make your hands tired.little bit uncomfortable. I could also see how wearing these for a really long duration might make your hands tired.

product_title: Car Inflation Bed, Multifunctional Air Bed, Extra Thick Travel Air Mattress, Back Seat Extended Mattress
review_body:
I have already reviewed a similar car air bed from this company, which is specifically designed for rear SUV use and i was thrilled with it. This particular model is made of the same high quality materials (with a really nice flocking!) however it is smaller in dimension for smaller vehicles / mutil use purposes for the back seats.

By doing this it omits the main reason I was really excited by the other unit - it was practically a custom fit where this one is not in all dimensions but in function instead. This just means the product may move a bit or may need the use of additional props to keep it in the same spot. If this is an issue it will depend on personal preference and think it is the need for this type of design which isn't to imply it is a negative rather just a necessity. I'd imagine the back seat area in most cars would be similar but would leave some room for adjustment so it is something to note but it is designed specifically for that area so it is going to be of a far more secure fit than a standard air mattress under the same use. Still, this unit is easy to make fit, and has worked well in the back of my own car. It also is a lot more comfortable the just lying on a seat!

However, If you have ever tried to sleep in the back of a car on the seats (i have done so many years ago) you would realise that a unit such as this would make if far more comfortable. No more seat belts digging into you like they are trying to prove a right wing political argument, no more arching your neck at 90 degrees attempting impressions of Regan from the Exorcist. Sure by its nature you will have to make compromise purely due to the physics and general width of a car but it at least makes those physics of simpler equation - Is the person awake or asleep in the back seat of the car.... or both at the same time? This example may may also apply to a cat in similar context and possibly your pet if you let it sleep in the back of the car. Regardless it will be in far more comfort with this device in any given state :)

The unit itself comes with its own pump that connects to the cigarette lighter, a couple of repair patches with glue, and also a couple of pillows which are a nice touch. As mentioned the flocking is very nice and my overall impressions of this product are it being of very high quality.
Another really nice product that will have its uses and provide a much more comfortable environment if circumstance requires a rest on the road in the back of your car.

product_title: RUBBERMAID - Blue Ice Mini Pack
review_body:
My husband and I still consider the \\"Rubbermaid BLUE ICE Mini Pak\\" to be one of our better investments (as well as it's larger cousin the \\"Rubbermaid BLUE ICE Block\\"). While the thick plastic, Blue Ice product line from Rubbermaid is not the most attractive, I believe it is the most functional reusable ice pack on the market.

Before purchasing the Rubbermaid Blue Ice Mini Pak, we fell for the gimmicks of the soft plastic ice pack products, which did not keep cold, melted quickly, and leaked soon after purchasing. Garbage.

The Rubbermaid Blue Ice Mini Pak, by comparison, is a wonderful size for lunch boxes (approx. 4.5\\" x 2.5\\" x 1.5\\"), and stays cool for almost a whole day of activities when inside an insulated container. We simply store our Rubbermaid ice packs in the freezer, so they are ready to use at a moments notice.

The Blue Ice Mini Pak is also great for icing injuries; we just wrap them in a small towel, and they are good to go.

Another application we've found for this product, is inside coolers for long car rides or trips to the beach. There is no mess like filling your cooler up with a bunch of ice, and no extra purchase.

Overall, the Rubbermaid BLUE ICE Mini Pak has come in handy for a multitude of uses, and has not broke or leaked after a year of regular use. Great product, great price. You'll be happy you made the purchase.

product_title: Dahon Vitesse D7HG Folding Bike, Navy, One Size
review_headline: Too heavy and awkward for everyday use
review_body:
Bought this for my wife to commute in Washington D.C. However, the bike proved too heavy for her to fold up and carry onto the Metro every day. It's also awkward to carry--packing up and down stairs/escalators would be tough, especially if you have anything else with you like a briefcase or purse.

Finally, to fold it up correctly, the handlebar and seat must be reset to their fold-up positions which you then need to re-adjust every time you want to unfold and ride. With a lot of practice, it could probably be folded up and unfolded quickly, but my wife never got to that point. Now it sits in our garage as a reminder of what could have been.

The quality is good--the bike is nice and solid. But for anyone thinking this will quickly fold up into a compact unit to easily carry onto a train, think again.

product_title: Selle SMP Stratos Saddle
review_headline: and find it quite comfortable for long rides
review_body:
I had my seat bone structure measured, and chose the Selle SMP Stratos seat as a compatible size. I have had the seat for a year, and find it quite comfortable for long rides.

I did have initial problems with the seat position migrating aft on every ride, but replaced my original stamped seat post/stamped steel bracket with a Race Face Revolution (machined) Seatpost which has held the seat in place since installation about six months ago. The Race Face Revolution Seatpost was easy to adjust and find a comfortable seat position.

I am still impressed with the quality and workmanship of the Selle SMP Stratos seat after a year of use.

My only reservation about the seat is the extended seat rail, which can allow the seat to migrate aft, and into a position where the seat bracket interferes with and causes chafing with my inner thighs, so to me the added forward extension would be useless, and I would personally prefer a traditional seat rail structure.

product_title: Northwest Territory 12 ft. Screenhouse
review_body:
I have had this screenhouse for several years and have gotten good use out of it. But not without problems. The thing to keep in mind is that we camp on Assateague Island, which does give gear a hard workout.

Pros:
The size is great! It fits over a large picnic table with plenty of room to move around. The sides are fairly straight, so the roof is large enough to give ample shade...extremely important on the beach. The doors are large and well located. And, a favorite feature, the skirting around the bottom can be covered with sand which really helps to keep the insects out. The metal legs are nice and sturdy. We actually string clothesline around from leg to leg to hang wet swimming clothes on to dry with no problems. Setting up is usually not too bad, at least in calm weather (see cons). I have done it alone. But it is definitely easier with help. Also, a major plus, is that there appears to be very little UV damage after several years.

Cons:
It does not do well in bad weather. Rain pools on the roof, weighting it down and eventually breaking the roof poles. Every roof pole on our tent has had to be repaired. In stormy weather, we have learned to lower the roof down onto the table to prevent breakage if we are not using it (such as at night). If we wish to be in it during heavy rain, it is helpful to use expandable clothesline props to help hold up the roof. If the screen house is set up in calm weather, it will remain up straight for the duration. However, It is impossible to set this screen house up in windy weather and have it end up standing straight. Even with four or more people helping, it will end up slanting away from the wind for the rest of the trip. It holds up fine, but definitely looks funny. At the same time, our Colman sleeping tent went up completely straight with far less trouble.

Conclusion:
This would be the perfect screen house for camping if the roof design were made more sturdy. This would almost certainly also improve the wind resistance. Would I buy it again? Only if I can't find one with a sturdier roof, with as good shade coverage, in a similar price point. Unfortunately, most screen houses have such slanted sides that they become almost useless for shade. For now, this one serves our purposes well enough.

product_title: Stainless Mountain Bike Cycling Bicycle Shift Cable Gear Shifter Inner Wire
review_headline: Good cables, better than OEM - can't beat the price
review_body:
I ordered these cables because I needed to replace the front derailleur shift cable on my mountain bike. There is one cable per package, it's 1.9 meters long, more than long enough for a front or rear derailleur. At the time I ordered this it was $1.99 each with free shipping. Delivery time was about 3 weeks since they shipped from China. I thought this was very quick considering it came from China.

This cable looks exactly like the OEM cable that cable that came with the bike. One end of the cable has the cast metal \\"knob\\" that fits into the shifter, the other end of the cable seemed to be spot welded together to keep the individual strands form fraying. This made it very easy to route the cable through the ferrules and housings. The welded area was the same diameter as the rest of the cable so it went in with little effort. It took a total of about 20 minutes to install the new cable and adjust the derailleur. Bike shifts like new again. For about $2 each and free shipping you can't go wrong. I ordered extras to have spares on hand.

review_headline: It can be put up by one, but....
review_body:
It's great for the price. It took four of us a while to get it up in the sea breeze. At home, I did it alone (no wind) in a fraction of the time. Here's how: put all the post together. attach the base (make sure alignment is correct to lock in place) to an arch and Velcro it to the canopy; let it drop. Velcro another arch (with base) to the opposite side of the canopy and attach the center dome post. You might need to put a few temporary stakes in (I didn't) depending on the wind. Velcro the other two arches, stick them in the bases, then connect the two remaining dome pieces.
PS - I was able to push the pole connectors that came out with a flat tip screwdriver.

product_title: Onyx M-24 Manual Inflatable Belt Pack Life Jacket, Black
review_body:
Tested this life jacket in a pool. Jumped in the deep end and went to the bottom tumbling upside down. Pulled on the red handle and nothing happened. Pulled a second time as it requires a hard pull to activate. Probably a good thing to avoid accidental activation. I was floated to the surface promptly. I was a little concerned about putting the inflatable bladder over my head while in the water. (the reason for the test) It turned out to be very easy. The vest supported my 200 lbs easily and comfortably (age 59). The manual inflation tube is easy to use while in the water. It only takes about 6-8 deep breaths to fill via the inflation tube.
Video of test can be seen on youtu.be/EQYMcP1gtQU

The manufacture recommends for adults over 80 pounds. I would not recommend for children because of the hard pull to activate.

Rearming with new CO2 was super easy. Follow the repacking instructions and you will be ready to use again.

I plan to used this vest while kayak fishing. Haven't tested the comfort while fishing from a sit-on-top kayak.
Purchased in a big box retail store.

product_title: YayLabs Play and Freeze Ice Cream Ball Ice Cream Maker, Pint, Blue
review_body:
I'm very please with the ice cream I've turned out from this ice cream ball. I've used it four times now, and each time I've tweaked the recipe slightly, and each time turned out delicious ice cream. A couple of things I learned:
1. After you open the lid on the ice-cream end to stir it, make sure to wipe off the rubber gasket on the lid and refasten it very tightly, otherwise you may get some slight leakage. Same goes for the ice side, especially if you're using table salt.
2. The ball gets VERY cold and frosty on the outside. I usually lay it on a bath towel and roll it back and forth.
3. Do not fill the ice cream ingredients to the brim! The ingredients need room to expand as they freeze. Leave at least 1/2" of space at the top (more if you can).
4. The ice cream freezes pretty hard to the metal cylinder. I've had good luck using a butter knife to scrape it away from the sides when its finished.

product_title: Osprey Transporter 60 Duffle
review_body:
Just used this bag for the first time as a carry-on for a 10 day trip. Like another reviewer pointed out, I thought I received the wrong item when it arrived because the bag folds up into itself into a small sack. Living in a condo with limited storage, this was an added bonus.

Anyways, after receiving it and examining the quality and features, my wife wanted one so I ended up ordering a second one so that we could both use them as carry-ons for our upcoming trip. So we have a very active 2 year old that makes travel difficult, trying to manage him, a car seat, etc. so a carry-on that can be worn as a backpack to free our hands was a must when looking for a versatile bag. Most backpacks are not this big and the duffel design makes it easier to pack and easier to access stuff when placing and retrieving items. There are also several carry handles that allow the bag to be carried horizontally or vertically which makes lifting, loading, and carrying in various positions very convenient. The 2 small outside pockets are convenient for keeping boarding passes, wallets, keys, etc. available for quick, easy access.

The backpack straps were comfortable for long walks in the airport and store away conveniently in their own zippered compartment. We only packed 1 large checked bag that was right at the 50lb limit, so we needed something large enough to hold the rest of our stuff and still fit in overhead bin or under the seat.

Well... we accumulated significantly more things for our return trip home and my wife and I had both of these bags completely stuffed in order to keep our checked bag under 50lb. I use a digital luggage scale to weigh our bags before leaving for the airport so we don't have any expensive surprises at the airport scale. This Osprey bag was stuffed for our return trip. My bag weighed 28lbs and my wife's weighed 27lbs! I was worried about these being too large for the plane being stuffed this full, but to my surprise, bothof our bags fit in the overhead bin. Granted, it was a tight fit but I think the two tension straps helped compact the bag as much as possible. The bag was also great for a couple 3 day excursions that we took while away and easily could have accommodated a couple more days if needed.

I can't comment on the long term durability since this was our first trip with the bags, but even with the bags bulging at the seams for our return trip, I saw no evidence of potential tears or damage. The material seems very strong and the stitching as well. The zippers were flawless and all of them have small lanyards attached with a rubber grip area that keep all the lanyards in a loop shape, making it very easy to grab and maneuver each individual zipper.

The only complaint my wife had was that the bag didn't come in any more color options and didn't look feminine. That being said, she was impressed with the versatility and convenience of this bag and was happy to sacrifice some aesthetics for function. We were very impressed with everything about this bag and although not cheap, it was worth every dime in my opinion and I hope it lasts a long time, as I anticipate it will.

product_title: Coleman Deluxe Camp Grill
review_headline: Where's the rest of the grill?
review_body: I looked at this grill at the store and I was thinking what the heck? Did they try and skimp on materials and trying to save a few cents by having large gaps in 1/3 of the grill and two more gaps at the other side? I see no logical reason to have a grill grate designed this way. The grill is small for starters so you can cook very little food on it to begin with. And with the inconsistent gaps in the grill you have even lesser usable cooking surface or whatever your cooking had better be a large piece or you have to use a pan. You will lose a hot dog here and there and portions of your burger will be lost due to them drooping down into the wider gaps. Also on one end of the grill they couldn't even weld another rod to it to close off the protruding ends of the grill rods so the pointy tips of the rods will get caught on things or scratch or poke holes in you or other things that come into contact with it. You also have to worry about the skinny pointy legs also. A few more rods is not going to add that much cost or weight to this tiny grill. And on top of that I question the tiny spot welds holding it together. A few more added rods to the grill surface would of helped in the strength also. But with the skinny legs that are just simply crimped to loop around a grill rod it will not be able to handle much weight anyways. So again you are a limited on what you can cook. Yes it is more compact than a Texsport grill or something but the design of the unusable cooking area and the exposed end of the rods and such make it an awkward useless grill. If you do most of your cooking with small pots and pans then I guess you can overlook the bad design of the grill for space and weight.

review_body:
My wife and I bought this stove as part of "just in case" kit that we have in the house, and also as a summer-time cookstove, to help use up all of the sticks that are left when I prune our two fruit trees. Yesterday, we tried it out for the first time.

It took us a a while to learn to tend the fire correctly. The key is to have fewer sticks, rather than move, and to be constantly pushing them forward under the chimney. As you can imagine, the fire needs a lot more attention than does your usual campfire or charcoal grill; but that's a small price to pay for such efficient burning. Because we had the stove on the ground, cooking turned into a two-person job - one to cook, the other to tend the fire. Putting the unit on a table would allow one person to do both jobs, which is what we'll do next time.

The first part of our test was to boil two quarts of water in a round-bottomed cast-iron pot. From striking the first match to boil took a little over 20 minutes. If we had waited until the fire was fully established, it probably would have taken less.

Next, we tried baking pita bread on a cast-iron skillet. We did a batch of eight pitas, from dough my wife had made the night before. They turned out beautifully - though we did have to watch them carefully, to avoid scorching on the hot spot in the middle of the pan.

Finally, we fried five cheeseburgers for our supper. Frying in the cast-iron skillet went quickly, and well.

Total fuel consumption for all that - boiling, baking, frying - consisted of one sheet of crumpled-up newspaper, a cupful of dry wood chips (to get the fire started), and approximately six feet of half-inch-diameter stick. That's an astonishingly small amount of fuel, given all that we did. Afterwards, there was about a half-cup of wood ash left in the Rocket, which shows how efficiently it burned the fuel. The bottoms of both the pot and the pan were sooty; the pot more so, because we put it over the fire before it was fully established, and smoky. Both cleaned up quickly with a little hot water and detergent.

Granted, our is just one use. Time will tell whether the EcoZoom is rugged enough for repeated usage. And it doesn't compare with our kitchen gas range in terms of cleanliness and convenience. But so far, we're very happy with the EcoZoom, and we look forward to using it for the rest of this summer, and in summers to come.it over the fire before it was fully established, and smoky. product_title: Osprey Farpoint 55 Travel Backpack
review_headline: Worked great for my trip to Europe!
review_body: This backpack worked great for my trip to Europe.  I didn't think I'd use the daypack much, but it came in handy when we decided to rent bikes in Amsterdam, since my cross-shoulder purse would've made it difficult to ride a bike.  Overall, I could fit about as much in this backpack as I could in a normal carry-on suitcase.  I used 1 small ebags packing cube for socks, underwear, & PJs, and 1 large packing cube for shirts & pants.  Since it was summertime, my clothes took up much less room than if I had to take full-length pants & long-sleeve shirts.  Even without the daypack attached, it is slightly larger than the allowed carry-on size, but I was able to use the daypack as my personal item, and the larger backpack as my carry-on.  The huge jets that go to Europe from the states have plenty of overhead space, so it wasn't really an issue.  I had trouble shutting the overhead bin door without turning it on it's side & slightly angled.  As we were traveling from train stations to hostels & vice-versa, I sometimes had the daypack attached in front of me, and sometimes left it on the main backpack.  It works well either way.  Being able to take the daypack off also helps with fitting it in tight spaces.  We took a night train to Scotland, and the only storage for luggage was under the bottom bunk.  I was able to take the daypack off & fit it under there, but my friend didn't have that option, and her bag wouldn't fit under the bunk.  On my way home, I checked the large bag.  It was great that I could cover up all the straps & carry it like a suitcase.  I definitely missed having a rolling bag, but that would've made it bigger & heavier, and also would've been harder to maneuver through all the places we went, so I am still glad I decided to go the backpack route.

review_body:
This review is after about 2 weeks of riding this bike daily.
When it first came it was super easy to assemble and everything came pretty well adjusted. My only problem is that the rear brakes on my bike are leaning to one side and i cannot find a way to make them right. They work but are very underpowered. I will be taking it in to the local bike shop for them to fix it as soon as i get the money. Anyway with that said this is just an absolutley great bike so far. Im a big guy
6'6" 330 lbs and ive tried out several bicycles over the last year,keeping my eye out for that perfect one. I have had schwinns before and even though they are probably cheap chineese made products i still like them the best. I saw this bike at a fred meyer but the one at the store was all ding-ed up and looked like it was assembled poorly. Also it cost nearly 300 dollers
But i really like how it looks and feels so i ordered it through amazon. The color and style is really nice and mature but also doesnt look something you would find at a retirement home. The seat has a beautiful leathery look to it and it is very very comfortable. The rack on the back is also very helpful and strong and the gears shift really nicley. Ive always had problems with gears that make clicking sounds or get stuck on gears but not this one. After a little adjusting these gears work fantastic. I bought myself a bicycle speed/odometer and so far have racked up about 60 miles. Since my truck gets 9 mpg this bike is going to save me alot of money in the long run. I usually dont go very fast but on this bike you dont need to. Its a perfect mix between street bike and cruiser but also a little rugged so it can take some tough terrain. Given the choice between this bike and a thousand doller street bike i would choose this bike any day of the week. I always forget how much i love biking and how good excersize it is, and this bike just reminds me of all the fun it can be. If your on the fence about thisone or are just starting to consider it i highly highly recommend it. Its very comfortable and versatile and just looks absolutley stunning right out of the box
Thanks for reading!

product_title: Spotlight Speck LED Light 15 Lumen Water Resistant Micro Light
review_body:
Due to its tiny, low capacity button cells, the Spotlight Speck only maintains decent brightness for about 1 minute, going from about 140cd to about 70cd. Afterwards, the output takes a steep nosedive and settles down at about 9cd of brightness. For comparison, a LRI Photon Freedom on 2x cr2016 cells starts at about 150cd, and maintains about 15cd after 1 hour, uses commonly available coin cells, and its lithium cells have a much longer shelf life.

The light comes with spare batteries, but the result is no different than the first set of cells. I even ordered a pack of new lr521 batteries online, which measured 1.52v out of the box, but the story always ended the same way - 1 minute of decent light, and then a steep drop to low output. Also, I could not find these cells at my local pharmacy, next to the overpriced lr41, cr2016, and cr2032 cells.

The unit itself is not bad in terms of build quality and produces light with a semi-decent (not ugly purple) tint, but for the money there are much better options, like the Streamlight Nano or the Photon Freedom. This light literally pales in comparison, and for anything other than short bursts of light, I'd actually be better off using the LED on my phone.

product_title: Israeli Shoulder Backpack
review_body: This is a British P-37 Small Pack modified by the Israelis . Israel used a lot of British and French Equipment when they started out as a Nation. This pack is one of those items just released to surplus. The one I received is in excellent to mint condition for a 60+ year old pack. Mine has a stamp of 1974 which was probably the year it was modified. The modification I have are the Shoulder Straps are sewn on. The original Pack used an "L" Strap which was abandoned to simplified it use. There is also a Shoulder Strap attached. One side sewn and the other side has a slide buckle. There are 3 Straps on the top and sides to hold a rolled up Blanket / Poncho "Horseshoe" style. The Israelis also added a 2 hole tab on the Pack flap to hold a US Style E-Tool. The inside has 3 dividers. One was originally used for the rectangular British mess kit. The other for Rations and a Water Bottle ( Canteen). This is a cool Pack to carry small items like Bino's and Range Finders. This is a cool piece of History and a practical little Retro Bag.
