product_title: Hydro Flask Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle, Wide Mouth, 40-Ounce
review_headline: Ice cold water, no more watered down ice tea - NO SWEATING!
review_body:
Love! Love! Love! One of the absolute best purchases I've made yet through Amazon. We live in Kauai where even standard double-wall cups sweat like you wouldn't believe. Ice melts almost instantly and I had to resort to putting an actual sock on my double-wall SB cup to keep from creating lakes on whatever surface it was sitting on. I've seen quite a few people using the Hydro Flask here so I decided to ante up the not-super-cheap asking price and hope for the best. And it far exceeded my expectations!

Zero sweating. Not even the tiniest drop.

No more ice melting in 10 seconds. My ice tea stays cold all day and night and most importantly, doesn't get watered down by melting ice.

I'm drinking more water which is great! I hate water that's not ice cold - I fill this with my filtered water and a few ice cubes and voila! Ice cold water that is refreshing and easy to drink.

I'll now be purchasing 1 for my hubby, 1 for our son, and I'm thinking about making this Christmas a Hydro Flask one for all my siblings and their spouses. Honestly, if you're looking for a drink bottle, this is the one to get!

::::::: updated December, 2014 :::::::

I ended up purchasing 2 of those - 1 in purple for myself and 1 in the stainless steel for my hubby. Unfortunately, the SS one actually began to rust on the outside of the bottle almost immediately. Totally random too - like a spot here and another spot there. On the body, near the top, at the bottom. I know that things rust here in HI but to develop rust w/in a matter of days was totally ridiculous. But Amazon saved the day. I was able to return the defective one and have a new one with black coating shipped out. It's been months and no problems with that. Hubby loves it and is drinking far more water than he did prior to the HF.

Overall, this is still a solid 10 out of 10 in my book. Just be aware if you live in a climate or area that has salty air, the stainless steel is not going to work.

product_title: Manhattan Portage Cornell Messenger Bag
review_body:
PROS:

- Durable. I purchased my first one of these 6 years ago, and it is only now showing minimal signs of wear (threading) and I put it through all of the elements, as well as stuffed it to capacity on many a spontaneous grocery trip.

- Water resistant. Keeps things dry inside. Exterior dries rather quickly after walking around in the rain.

- Light. Because there is no padding, this bag is inherently super light. It feels like nothing at all if empty on your shoulder.

- Small (but not too small) footprint. Doesn't look like a giant-ass laptop bag. Also doesn't look like a purse. Yet, I've squeezed a naked 15" MacBook pro in here (not recommended), as well as its cable, a water bottle, and a hoodie. All at the same time. Can easily put a 13" laptop in a sleeve in here.

- Single inner compartment. You can jam whatever you want in here. There's an outer compartment that comes in handy for things like a newspaper. A few other zippered compartments under the strap of various sizes as well, for change, gum, whatever.

- Neutral. Looks great whether I'm wearing a suit, or a t-shirt and jeans. There are fancier looking bags, but they don't seem to fit whatever outfit I'm wearing. Not this one.

CONS:

The strap. The strap sucks. When it tangles, it's a huge pain in the ass to untangle. Seriously. You have to sit down and mess with it and twist it back around with brute force. Also, when used over-the-shoulder, the strap slides down a lot. I would recommend finding a different strap, one with a shoulder pad if possible.

No handle. You have to use this in strap mode. And as previously mentioned, the strap sucks.

No padding. I'm actually okay with this most of the time, since it lets me squeeze more in and keeps it light, but when carrying around a laptop, be sure to put it in a sleeve.

VERDICT:

This bag is super durable, reliable, and great for daily use. I'm only replacing mine now after 6 years of serious city abuse. I would imagine it would last longer for someone not constantly jamming stuff in there, walking around in the rain, and throwing it on subway seats. I would give it 5 stars if it came with a good strap.t for daily use. I'm only replacing mine now after 6 years of serious city abuse. product_title: Overland Equipment Women's Isabella Hiking Daypack
review_body:
I *love* this bag! For such a small bag it is amazingly capacious--when necessary I can tuck a water bottle or a travel umbrella into the main compartment. Because of shoulder issues, I do not carry bags over my shoulder, but the Isabella hangs nicely from my forearm (with my elbow bent) without dangling too low. It is light enough for me to wear cross-body if I don't have too much crammed into it. But my absolute favorite feature is the buckle, which allows me to wear it securely around my waist/hips. This allows me to have both hands free (SUPER helpful--and secure--for all kinds of shopping and crowded public events!) and full range of arm motion (without any weight on my shoulder), and it looks *way* more stylish than a "fanny pack"! It is the perfect size for my everyday necessities (phone, keys, pen, lip balm, tissues, etc.), plus the front section under the flap serves in place of a wallet. I have it in the dove gray, which is beautiful and looks nice with everything in my casual wardrobe. I will definitely be purchasing it in additional colors!

(As another reviewer mentioned, it can be a bit difficult to find small items in the bottom of the main compartment because of the opening being smaller than the bottom of the bag. I try to keep small items in the pockets of the main compartment, and find that the annoyance of occasionally having to dig for something is far outweighed by the positives of this bag. If Amazon allowed fractional stars, I'd probably rate this bag as 4 3/4 stars for this issue.)

review_body:
Energy efficiency (reduced heat transfer) and cost are my top priorities, yours could be different. I bought one of these a couple years ago ($50) and it is holding up well, I have used it a lot. it has an excellent volume to surface ratio and lots of insulation. I have still had ice left after a 4 day festival (I started with a lot). This is also the largest size I can lift into my pick-up by myself. I am willing to deal with the shortcomings. My new one was $39 (the old one still works fine but I have even more stuff to keep cool now).

SHORTCOMINGS:
- Cubic shape makes it less stable (more tippy) than conventional rectangular shape.
- No \\"tie-downs\\" to easily secure it in the back of the truck.
- Light duty wheels - not for extended or rough use.
- Light duty handle that must be down to open the lid.

HTH, YMMV ;-)

review_body: Previous reviews mentioned problems with installation leading to exploding inner tubes. I should have given more credence to these reviews. I have lost 3 inner tubes trying to install these tires. at about 70 or 80- lbs (within rated range) the tire explodes. I assumed the first time that I overinflated the tire. I tried again with 60 lbs and was able to ride for about 50 miles. I assumed that maybe the tire hadn't seated properly the first time so I increased the pressure to 80 lbs. product_title: Grand Trunk Skeeter Beeter Pro Mosquito Hammock
review_body:
Yeah! I wish I had gotten one of these things sooner. I saved so much space and weight in my pack carrying this hammock rather than carrying a tent and a sleeping mat.

I set this up in 100 degree weather in the shade at Enchanted Rock and was able to nap in this thing for a couple hours without feeling the heat too much. Since the hammock is suspended in the air and the material is breathable one can be sure to get the most out of any breeze that might come through.

The mosquito net is awesome. I've seen videos on youtube where people modify their Skeeter Beeter to get a better suspension of the mosquito netting. After experiencing the standard setup I find that it is absolutely acceptable as a bug barrier. I had a wasp or bee wake me up when it was buzzing by my head, I didn't even bother to open my eyes, I just smiled and went back to sleep. I also read a few reviews on here where people broke the zipper or the netting after getting in or what not. I don't see how this could happen unless one just improperly suspended it or straight up abused it.

I was a little cautious when I first got in but soon found out that my worries were unfounded. The material feels so thin but to me seems extremely durable. I weigh about 190 pounds and am about 6' tall and didn't feel like I even came close to breaking this thing. The steel clips and rope seem strong enough. As long as one takes care of it and doesn't plop down into it this hammock should last a while.

The bottom line is that this thing is good in hot weather, its durable and does a great job at protecting you from insects, just don't forget to spray the bottom side with repellent.

review_body: Got this for my 13 birthday. Absolutely LOVE it! I had tried regular skate board before and did not do well (probably because I had to keep taking my foot off and pushing, but no problemo with the RipStik and it's "twist 'n go." So obviously it is harder to balance on than a regular skateboard with only 2 wheels, but the trick is (get this) the FASTER you go, the EASIER it gets to balance! Don't stand on the board and try and balance while holding onto the counter or a chair, this board was not built to stand still on -It would be like trying to stand still on a bike, no feet on the ground. So start moving on it and sort of push yourself around on it until you get the hang of standing, then try and do not holding onto anything, after that master pushing off and turning. I learned this in 3 afternoons, and am zipping around like a pro now! This is for you if you want a challenge and don't expect to quit when you fall once or don't think you can stand or push off and go fast. When you fall, get back up! review_headline: This product really doesn't deserve the one star I gave it!!!
review_body: I had been looking for a chair that I could carry to soccer games and use for camping, so this seemed ideal. Also, I not only threw the box out (I was so optimistic), I also misplaced my receipt, so I am stuck with a one-armed piece of fabric with metal legs.  I certainly won't be ordering any items from Victorian Trading Co. again.  I really could have forgiven the shoddy bag material, but having to throw away the chair away after one use is something I can't overlook.  All of my purchase was in the trash can before my credit card bill arrived, and in all fairness, I should have been able to use this product for more than 2 hrs,  even though I may be able to salvage the fabric to make a pillow cover or maybe a nice placemat.

product_title: NIKWAX Nubuck and Suede Treatment
review_body: I used this on a new pair of hiking boots with medium tan nubuk leather.  Used as directed the sponge applicator completely flattened and darkened the nape so that it looks like regular smooth dark brown leather.  I believe it flattened the nape because of the applicator.  I also tried Obenaufs pump silicone spray (for suede and other items) on a casual but dressier pair of very light beige suede shoes; it did not flatten out the nape but left them a darker tan with a somewhat uneven dirty look and the original vibrancy of the brushed leather was no longer there.  Both repelled water.  If your concern is just water repellency either will work and both are environmentally safe.  If you prize the original new look of nubuk or suede you are better off not applying any after market waterproofing agent, especially on lighter colored leather.  Just brush and clean as needed and wear something else for wet and muddy conditions.

I ended up returning it and picking up a Zebralight H52fw.  Yes, it cost more, but the light it produces is superior in every way. Better tint, and better, even beam.  Plus it's lighter weight because it only uses 1 AA.  And it has better runtimes at equivalent outputs.

product_title: Finish Line Dry Lube 8oz Aerosol
review_body: I like to detail my bikes after 100 miles of riding.  I clean all moving parts thoroughly with Finish Line Degreaser. product_title: Bravo BTP 12v Mano Inflation Pump
review_body:
I first bought the BP 12 but quickly learned that going cheap was not a wise move. I immediately replaced it with this BTP 12 and I am so glad I did. The BP 12 is a one-stage pump (high pressure/low volume) that only produces 150 liters per minute (150 L/min). The BTP 12 is two-stage and produces 450 L/min (low pressure/high volume) until it gets to about 1 PSI and then switches to 150 L/min (high pressure/low volume). This is not just an issue of convenience and speed. Air pumps tend to overheat after about a half hour of continuous use. The life of the BTP 12 will be much longer because it does not have to overwork like the BP 12.

In addition to two inflatable SUPs, I have an inflatable mat/dock that is 10’x13’x6”. It takes about seven times longer to fill to 14 PSI than a SUP. Even with the BTP 12 I need to fill it in two stages (30 min and 20 min) with a cool down period in between. With the BP 12 it would have taken hours and the pump would likely have burnt out in a few weeks (or an angry neighbor would have smashed it to get some peace and quiet).

An added plus for me with this vendor (Wahoo Inflatables) was that it came with an adjustable Halkey Roberts valve adapter that fit nicely on the hose without the need for fittings or clamps.

product_title: Kelty Women's Redwing 40 Internal Frame Pack
review_headline: Perfect daypack/small camping pack for a woman's frame
review_body:
This is a big pack for everyday, in-town tasks, so it is probably overkill, but it is a FANTASTIC pack for moderate hiking.

This backpack has one main zippered compartment, which is plenty big enough for a weekend's camping gear and clothes (other than a tent,and sleeping bag/mat, of course), with another smaller zippered compartment on the front (in which is an organizing panel and a key fob). Then, on the very front of the pack, there is a very small zippered compartment that is big enough for a phone, GPS unit, or small camera. There is also a daisy-chain and carrying handle on the very front of the pack.

On each side of the pack, there is a mesh waterbottle holder and a vertical zippered compartment big enough to hold a rain cover (that's what I keep in one of my side pockets), more water bottles, or other small gear.

This backpack has an internal frame, so it is somewhat of a hybrid between a traditional daypack and a camping backpack. The internal frame can be bent to fit the wearer's body, and directions are included to help the wearer figure out where to adjust the backpack to make it comfortable. There are pads on the back of the pack to protect the wearer's spine from being irritated by the center stabilizing bar.

The straps on this pack are well-padded and quite comfortable to wear, but the backpack offers two additional ways to make the pack more stable and comfortable-- a great waist band and a sternum clip. The waist band on the backpack is very comfortable and very stable. To further stabilize this pack, there is also a sternum clip.

The entire back of the pack has "Dynamic Air Flow" to make it more comfortable to wear, especially in hot or humid climates.

There are several straps and compression straps to further personalize the backpack. On the bottom, there are two straps that *could* be used to secure a sleeping mat or *possibly* a one-person tent, but I don't know that I would trust the straps to hold much in the way I use the pack.

I have several different backpacks that I use for different purposes, but this has definitely become my "go-to" for hiking, canoeing, and traveling. It is a great backpack that is very comfortable to carry.

review_body:

It goes up pretty easily, though the instructions are not very helpful.
I only wish that the little orange 'gear locker' that bumps out had a zipper on it so you could easily access stuff without stepping inside.

TIP: Don't fully extend the side poles. Keep the last segment collapsed. THEN hook the tent to the supports and finally RAISE it into position by extending the last section of the uprights. Otherwise, unless you are 7ft. tall, you won't be able to hook the center part of the tent to the peak once the supports are extended.

PROS:
- Steel cables connect the poles together, rather then just bungees, so the construction quality is very high.
- Goes up pretty easily with a helper. 1 person can do 90% of the work. The 2nd person is only needed on the very last step to extend and raise the tent.
- Doors on both sides
- Very roomy
- Fits 3 queen sized air mattresses easily.
- Lots of ventilation
- Really stable, even without using the guy-wires.
- The tent can actually fit back into the included duffle bag, though just barely!
- Directions on how to put on the rainfly are lacking.
- Hard to figure out how to put on the rainfly (still haven't figured out how it goes, luckily it hardly ever rains in the Sierra Nevadas during summer)

product_title: Victorinox Farmer
review_body:
The venerable Farmer is up to $30 now. That's a bit high, but the quality is still there. The Farmer is 3-5/8\\" long when closed and is 7/16\\" thick. It weighs 3.7 ounces. The liners are aluminum, as are the ribbed Alox (aluminum oxide) handle scales. The ribbed texture gives a better grip than the smooth Alox, and it hides scratches and wear better. On the back is a small (3/4\\" by 1/4\\") smooth rectangle so you can engrave something on it. The standard Victorinox split ring is attached, which is just a 3/8\\" diameter steel split ring. The Farmer is basic, but very capable. None of the blades or tools lock, just so you know. Here's the tool layout, sorted by the layers:
-The knife blade. It's a little larger than a standard Swiss Army Knife blade, at 2-3/4\\" long with a 2-5/8\\" cutting edge. It's 56 on the Rockwell scale, and is pretty easy to sharpen. It's your basic Victorinox blade: easy to take an edge, very stain-resistant, and low to medium edge retention. In truth, if you dull the blade before you can touch it up, you probably should have brought a more appropriate tool. The blade opens via nail nick.
-The reamer. It's 1-1/2\\" long and sharpened to poke holes in things. The arm of the reamer is sharpened on one side as well, enabling you to use it as a fire steel striker. A small lip allows you to open it. I wish this were the standard reamer on all Swiss Army Knives and not just the Alox models, but I see why the flat awl makes more sense on the others.
-The middle layer houses the wood saw. It's 2-7/8\\" long with some very aggressive teeth. They're kerfed, meaning the teeth are thicker than the spine so the saw doesn't get stuck in wood. They will cut on both the push and pull stroke. The saw is a little flexible, which you want in a saw. The spine is sharp, giving you one more option to strike a ferrocium rod if you have to. A few people don't like the keyring attachment's placement since it digs into the hand while using the saw, so they file it off. I've never experienced this problem, but if it bugs you, that's a quick fix.
-The last (or first, if you're looking at the Victorinox shield on the handle) layer has the bottle opener / wire stripper / large screwdriver. It's 1-1/4\\" long and just over 1/16\\" thick. The bottle opener works just fine. The large flathead screwdriver is 1/4\\" wide, so you can get some torque in larger screws. This tool also has a detent in the halfway position, allowing for even more torque. You can use this tool for light prying, although Victorinox doesn't warranty that.
-The other tool on this last layer is the small screwdriver / can opener. It's 1-1/4\\" long and will open cans of food quickly. The proper technique is to cut forward, but either way will work. That flathead screwdriver tip is just under 1/8\\" wide, and it will work with most #2 or #3 Phillips screws as well.

Overall, the Farmer is a great tool. I think the price is getting a bit high, but it's still worth the cost. There are other colors available from time to time: red, blue, and even black. product_title: Aquamate Solar Still Emergency Water Purification Inflatable Kit
review_headline: Great design, they thought of everything.
review_body:
I'm not going to review the rate of water output as it varies greatly for different situations.
Everything else about this device exceeded my expectations. Every little part of the design has been well thought out, down to the straps, strings, and plugs which prevent loss of any separable parts. There are instructions and a quick survival guide printed on it, ENGLISH ONLY, telling you important information like how to conserve energy, how much to drink, and not to inflate the device fully or else it may burst when the sun's heat expands the air inside.

You can't really see from the picture, but spread above the 'dirty water' reservoir is a black heat-absorbing fabric layer which has some of its parts dangling down and dipping into the dirty water, so that it sucks the dirty water upwards through capillary action, and then spreads the water over its large solar-heated surface area to accelerate the evaporation of the water. Since the dirty water in the lower reservoir easily loses its heat to the rest of the ocean or ground just below it, this black fabric system is essential for thermally isolating the "currently evaporating hot water" from the rest of the "dirty cold water reserve".

This solar still has its practical advantages and disadvantages to a pump-type desalinator, and since these should be apparent to anyone doing moderate research, I won't touch on them. However, when it comes to sustained use beyond the one-off life raft situation which these products seem to be designed for, I can't say if this indefinitely-reusable solar still triumphs over the high-maintenance-limited-capacity (few thousand gallons) filters and RO membranes, because I'm not sure how resistant this solar still is to UV degradation, it being a solar device and all. Only time will tell.

product_title: ActivFortis - Front Bicycle Light - Ultra Rugged and Durable Bike Light Using Aircraft Aluminum - Shock and Water Resistant - Adjustable Focus Beam - 5 Modes - Easy to Install - Taillight Included
review_body:
I've only had a few days to try it but so far I must admit I'm rather satisfied with my purchase. I've already tested it under a heavy thunderstorm without any issues. Build quality seems on-par with other premium flashlights I own. The light brightness is also on-par for its type and size. There are other much brighter headlights but they're bigger or more cumbersome with external batteries. I particularly like the fact I can easily adjust the beam pattern. I ride all across the city so the street lighting goes from well-lit to poorly-lit in the same ride. Moreover, I can go through hi-traffic streets to barely populated areas as well. Therefore, this feature allows me to set the pattern on the fly depending on the conditions. I don't want to blind oncoming traffic with a pattern that is too wide. It has 3 power settings, strobe, and SOS mode. Additionally, the unit will remember the last mode you were using so when you turn it on again it will default to that mode. Many other multi-mode lights require you to cycle through all the modes until you find the one you need. It's very light and compact so even going over bumps and potholes rarely disturb the position I set in on at the beginning of the ride.

Since there are many other lights with similar features as this one, the universal mount finally convinced me to get this light. This is a truly universal mount that can be installed on any handlebar. One of my bikes has an odd design and I always have trouble securing a headlight to it. Not with this mount. The fact that it uses velcro makes it super easy to attach and detach. Moreover, as there are no screws or elastic bands you will find it hard to over tight and break anything on the mount. For the same reason it's very easy to remove the light without changing the position of the mount. Not to mention you can use it as a regular flashlight. And, if I ever need to, I can also use any of the other tactical flashlights I own with this mount. Overall, I'm very happy with this headlight.

By the way, it also comes with a rear safety light, spare o-rings, an adapter if you decide to use a rechargeable battery instead of AAA, and a red on/off button. The tail light is not the very best out there, but it's still very bright. It actually saved my ride the other day as the tail light I was planning to use didn't fit on my new bike's seatpost.very happy with this headlight.

product_title: Pyle Waterproof Underwater Snorkeling & Diving Multi-Function Water Sport Wrist Watch with Dive Mode, Chronograph, Stopwatch, Water Temperature, Dive Depth & Duration
review_body:
I was pleasantly surprised when this dive watch arrived. In my opinion the picture doesn't do it justice. I haven't used it in the water as yet but from a cosmetic and \\"build quality\\" overview the product looks and feels like something that costs 5 times as much. I will update this review after I do some diving with it.
The case is solid stainless steel and the battery change compartment is screw down with a built in recess to use a coin to unscrew and change the battery while maintaining water resistance. I bought this as an everyday wear watch with built in depth measurements while free diving and as a backup depth gauge during my SCUBA diving. The large digits look like they will have great visibility in poor water conditions. The form factor is a perfect fit for my wrist since the included strap seems of high quality with the right amount of pliability vs resistance along with many holes placed closely together to get the perfect fit around my wrist.
Another reviewer mentioned the color did not match the picture but I got the exact color as the picture (blue with red accent in the 12 to 3 o'clock position). I am so pleased with the watch itself from a cosmetic/ergonomic standpoint that I would buy it again even if the depth feature didn't work as planned. I'm a bit of a watch guy with many more expensive units that have failed to impress as much as this one has. In my opinion the watch has just the perfect amount of weight to give the feeling of being substantial while not being too bulky. The profile is slightly higher than a normal high quality digital watch but it is not too much so. If it works as advertised this watch is a much better deal than many costing 5 times as much. If Pyle could fit a decent full dive computer into this exact form factor I would buy it in a heartbeat and then it would compare to true dive computer watches costing 10 times as much!
The dives will be the final test! I really hope it works as advertised becauseIMO dive watches are ridiculously priced and it is about time a manufacturer came in and shook up the playing field! I hope to dive with it very soon.

---Updated 4th of August, 2014-- Post Multiple Dives
Well I've had a chance to dive with the watch on two separate occasions and my 5 stars still stand. The watch is excellent as a free dive computer and as a backup depth gauge. The accuracy is perfect. One of the things that kept me from getting this watch sooner was a review that talked about the \\"5 second sample time\\" read somewhere in the manual. I wanted a watch that gave near real time updates. After diving with the watch and conducting experiments I can attest the depth response of the watch is near instantaneous. The 5 second time may be in reference to when the depth sensor first engages the depth function. Once the watch is in depth mode it registers changes immediately with depth change as little as two inches. I've tested this on free dives where I held on to an object and moved up and down the water column. As I have moved the depth has accurately moved up and down. So 20 free dives later and I have to say this watch is a real winner. This is exactly what I was looking for, just many hundreds less than the competition.

product_title: Discraft Weekender Disc Golf Bag
review_headline: Quality beginner bag, some minor annoyances
review_body:
As of right now, I only have 9 discs that I use regularly. They all fit rather nicely in the bag, but it is a little bit tight due to my putter being slightly thicker than most. It is an old disc, so if I had another style, I'm sure all of them would fit adequately with enough room to sort through them without having to pull them all out. The front pocket is shown as another slot for a disc, but I find it better suited for a bag of trail mix or other snacks. In any case, the pocket is just as well made as the main compartment. The drawstring that cinches down around your water bottle is a little weak, with the string already starting to come apart. A minor annoyance, but easily remedied. The main drawback is the shoulder sling. The plastic piece that connects the non-adjusting side to the bag has no texture or other method of blocking strap shifting, so after 30 seconds of wearing the bag, it slides so the piece is positioned vertically instead of horizontally. This might eventually be a problem for the strap, but so far it's just an irritation.

All in all, this is a good quality bag for a beginner, enough to hold several starter discs, but be wary of a few design choices that might interfere with optimum performance.

review_headline: Perfect bike for teen/adult with Down syndrome
review_body:
I was going to give this bike fewer stars after struggling for hours to put it together (awful instructions, missing screws, etc.), but now that we've had it for several weeks, wow, this trike is great! We bought it for our 16-yr old daughter who has Down syndrome. She never cared for the 2-wheel bike with training wheels she's had for years. I'm guessing it was just too much to worry about keeping the bike upright while coordinating pedaling and braking and everything else.

This bike is PERFECT for her! She all of a sudden loves biking and asks to ride it every day. Any time the family goes out--to a restaurant, shopping, walking the dog, etc.--she asks if she can ride her bike. It's great! Next purchase will be a bike rack for the car so the family can go on biking adventures together. When folded, the trike does fit in my little car (Nissan Leaf) with the back seats folded down. Also, to make it fit, the handlebars need to come off, which is fine because they have a quick-release mechanism. (The seat is also quick-release, which is handy, since all of our daughter's friends are wanting to try out the trike and it's easy to raise the seat.)

I'm glad we got the 16-inch and not the 20-inch. It's plenty big. My daughter is 4'8 and 100 pounds and she uses the seat at its lowest level. And kids/adults much taller fit on it fine with the seat raised.

product_title: SE Bikes Heavy Hitter BMX Frame 20.75" TT 100% Cromoly Headset White Gold
review_headline: So Far, I Like The Frame.
review_body:
Got this frame in May, 2014, so my review is based from what I've experienced in the two months I've owned the frame. I've ridden this frame mainly at skateparks and trails, specifically Lake Cunningham Regional Skatepark and Calabazas Trails in San Jose, CA.

Pros:
-Easy to assemble.
-Once you've taken off the stickers, it looks pretty cool.
-Pretty light.
-Fairly strong, but it's too early to tell. (I've let people ride my bike and they've done 360 whips, truck drivers, various grinds etc. and it has held up)
-Really reasonable price for a full chromoly frame!
-Comes with an integrated headset, and free stuff is always fun.
-Made it easy to learn tricks like hop 360s, hop barspins etc. (currently trying to learn tail whips)
-you will be inclined to want to learn how to whip-to-surf, or x-factor any and everything.

Cons:
-If you run pegs and the Primo hub guard, drive side, those washers that keep the wheel from slipping aren't very helpful.
-When the frame develops chips and scratches on the powder coat finish, the frame looks cracked. But I think that's expected of all powder coated frames.
-The screw on the integrated seat clamp broke on mine, but then, I over tightened mine, so that was probably my fault.
-No welded gussets on the top tube and down tube.
-Doesn't have the street cred that some of the other frame companies (Fit, CULT, Federal, Volume, Subrosa, etc.) have, so you might get some negative feedback.

Overall: Get this frame if you are a beginning/intermediate bike rider looking to upgrade, on a budget, and looking for a bike that looks pretty cool, is pretty strong and is light. The frame is full chromoly so its definitely an improvement than hi-ten steel frames or hybrid chromoly/hi-ten frames.

PS: If you really want to see the abuse that this frame takes, watch Big Daddy ride in Road Fools 17 and 18 on Hulu.

product_title: Coleman WeatherMaster 6-Person Screened Tent
review_body:
I did a lot of investigating before buying this tent and wasn't completely convinced it was the right choice until we pitched it for the first time. This tent is wonderful.
My wife had never truly camped before I took her into the CatSkills and at that time I had a small two person tent which was extremely cramped for two adults. After two trips to the woods she was ready for something else.

The first setup took about an hour. We are down to 15-20 minutes depending on the where the tent is being pitched (rocky areas take a bit longer in general to stake). It has enough room inside for me to stand up straight, a queen air mattress (for those glamping trips) and enough room for a couple folding stools for changing and room to walk around.

The construction is fantastic and should help the tent last many years/trips. The ventilation is awesome. The door on this thing is something else and I don't know if I could own another tent where you have to zip in and out.

The screened ceilings are amazing at night whether under trees that reflect the firelight on leaves or under an open sky with brilliant stars shining down on you. One night there was a full moon and it was actually too bright for me.

The rain fly keeps you dry and is SO easy to install. Just make sure when you stake the tent it's fully stretched so that you can avoid pooling but that's true for most multi-pole 4+ person tents.

The screened room we haven't taken full advantage of yet but our last trip it rained and we moved our chairs and table inside and played some cards and ate snacks while watching the forest get soaked. It was quite cozy. Usually we just put our gear in this room for the night or when we leave the site for the day. The screened room does attract quite a few insects which get trapped at the top after entering through the sides at the bottom. This could be due to poor staking (we don't take too much time to stake this part of the tent) causing the tarp flaps along the bottom to welcome curious bugs.

As with most tent gear I struggle to get everything folded up and back in the box so simply roll and tie the tent and throw it in the back of the car while the canvas bag w/ box holds the remaining gear and a few other items like extra stakes and tarps.

You will not be disappointed with this tent.

My one complaint is that due to its size and the lack of a shoulder strap (only hand straps) you will struggle to take this and other essential gear to a secluded site in one trip.) causing the tarp flaps along the bottom to welcome curious bugs.

product_title: CatEye - Strada Slim Cycle Computer
review_headline: This model intermittently blanks out (shows 0.0 mph) while you are riding. Do not buy.
review_body:
No. Absolutely do not buy this. I have ended up with two of these over the years. I bought one and then returned it. I ended up with another one on a 2ndhand bike. In each case, I have had the same problem: every 40 minutes or so during a ride, I'll look down and notice it has stopped sensing wheel rotation. A smart "smack" to the face of the unit restores it to proper function.

Yes, I have ruled out the possibility that there is user error. I have taken great care to put the sensor in the right place near the wheel, etc. I think this is simply a bad design. Others have also had this problem, and have gotten CatEye to replace these under warranty. What a hassle.

FWIW, my go-to bike computer is the PlanetBike computer, because it never blanks out, and because it shows way more info on a single screen. Even if the Strada didn't intermittently blank out, I'd still hate it because I don't enjoy pressing the button over and over again just to scroll between data points. I shouldn't be staring at an LCD, I should be watching the road, right?

product_title: Pelican ProGear 35 Quart Elite Marine Cooler
review_headline: Best bang for your buck!  All my other coolers are headed to craigslist...
review_body:
I have the tan 45qt. Pre-cool the cooler for a day or so in the house, pack with ice the day before to keep the cold the longest.

Bottomline up front: This is a great cooler that is built like a tank. Beats out the Yeti, Engel, Yukon and others by a long shot!

So why is this one better?
1. US made product which is lower priced than the competition. $100 less for a better item!
2. LIFETIME warrantee. Not sure what you could ever break on it but its not a 3 or 5 year warranty, its for life (unlike the Yeti).
3. Latches and hardware are much better. Solid click latches and SS hardware, this thing opens smooth as can be and closes solidly. No rubber to dry rot.
4. No rope handles. This has solid fold out handles that don't let the cooler swing around when loading it. Also has solid built in handles that mean you don't have to lift so high when loading into a lifted truck or Jeep rack.
5. The ability to fit chaffing dishes is great and means you can keep your beer ice cold and your food cold (but not water logged or frozen). All brands seem to offer overpriced baskets but the chaffing dishes are cheap and SS so you can have more than one size depending on your adventure needs.
6. It actually holds 45 qts (the yeti 45 is woefully overrated).
7. Sloped drain that drains quickly and seals tight. No more holding up one end and waiting to drain!
8. Grippy feet. Some remove these to allow the cooler to be slid in and out of truck beds. Personally I like how well they hold the cooler in place. They also keep the bottom off the ground prolonging your ice.

Other reviewers have noted this is a heavy cooler. If you are looking at coolers in this price range and style you probably knew that. In the world of coolers light weight = light duty. If a 35# cooler is too much weight then a $50 igloo is what you want. After all this wasn't designed for backpacking or tailgating, this is a serious piece of gear for keeping things cold for long periods of time in extreme conditions.

I'm already planning to buy another for extended trips.

Now I realize that every time you ride you're riding over new conditions to a certain extent. I was having my bike tuned up to get it in shape to return to the mountain biking trails I've not ridden in the past couple years. The second time out riding I got a flat with the new tubes, I repaired the places (3) that were leaking and threw the tube back in the tire. The next morning I went to the garage and just by coincidence I happened to be there to hear one of the patches fail. In frustration I threw out the garbage tube and threw in my old slime tube, and until it fails I'm holding strong at 5 stars. Maybe there's just a hint of bike shops not wanting to sell this product because they end up selling less tubes,... just sayin'.

product_title: Kelly Kettle Large Stainless Steel Base Camp Basic Kit
review_headline: Aluminum Rivets + Stainless Steel Container = Galvanic Corrosion and Failure
review_body:
I bought the Kelly Kettle last year for camping and backcountry hiking.

It works great for boiling water. Depending on the type of fuel you're using, it can boil the full volume of water in about 7 or 8 minutes. It seems to work best with actively burning fuel (anything that's actively emitting flame), smoldering coals don't seem to heat as quickly as little twigs and branches... Though I should note that I live in AZ and most of the small brush available as fuel here is extremely high in oil and very dry so it burns hotter and a bit longer than a similar volume of wood might in wetter areas. You're mileage may vary.

I've never tried cooking above it, so I can't comment on its utility as a \\"stove\\".

That all having been said, if you're not careful and you happen to forget to empty the kettle, as you might if you're using it as an additional water container and happen to leave it in the trunk of your car for a couple weeks after filing it while hiking/camping...You're likely to find that the rivets have corroded and left a nice milky residue of aluminum oxide all over the inside of the kettle. When you try to remove the corrosion you may find that the rivets leak. And if you try to remove the scum inside the kettle with vinegar you may get lucky enough to have the rivets completely dissolve, pop out, and spill boiling vinegar all over your stove. You'll have a really clean stove top...but your house will stink for a while.

At the end of the day it was a really poor or perhaps lazy decision by the manufacturer to use aluminum pop rivets in a stainless steel container. My guess is that they make the steel unit on the same line they make the aluminum one on and never thought about galvanic corrosion.

It is a really cool piece of equipment, but DO NOT under any circumstances use this thing to store water for any significant length of time or leave even a small amount of water in it after use (dump it all and leave the plug out after every single use).plug out after every single use).

I put a temp gage in the wire basket and left it. The first 24hrs I checked the temp 40 degrees and the ice had done little to melt. The next 5 days I did the same. The temp in the box was 45 degrees in the basket the ice lasted a full 6 days.
Now nothing else was put in and not close to being full of ice or anything else. All I can say is WOW!!

I will use the cooler for keeping fish cool as I surf fish on the outer banks of NC. I have fished there for more than 25 years.
I don't have to worry about the fish any longer. I am getting a 35 QT for my food and cokes. Only thing I wish I would have done so sooner, God Bless and enjoy..

review_body: I bought this pack (blue color) from a local store several months ago, and I am very satisfied with it so far. Not only is it a wonderful all-day pack, I just used it last weekend for a two-night backpacking trip, on which I carried 30-35 pounds of gear, food, and water. I don't necessarily recommend that you buy this pack for backpacking (its 27-liter capacity is barely enough for a two-night trip), but it shows how versatile and tough it is that it can be used for that purpose in a pinch. I plan to use it for another two-night backpacking trip (this time to Mt. Whitney) in a couple weeks, and I'm confident it will do the job once again. If I want to do longer summer backpacking trips or spring/fall trips with more clothing, I will probably need to find a larger pack with at least a 47-liter capacity.

review_headline: The bike needs a lot of adjustments and tuning once that is taken care of the bike rides great. With the price of the bike you c
review_body:
I bought this bike a little over a month now and I do not not normally write a review. However for this bike I want people to be aware of what they are buying. So far I had to replace the cassette, had two major tune ups and the peddle arm came loose and came off while on long ride. The bike needs a lot of adjustments and tuning once that is taken care of the bike rides great.

With the price of the bike you can not go wrong. I am 260 lbs (logged in as my wife) and I find the bike one of the smoothest rides I have ridden in a long time. I bought the bike to loose weight and get back into mountain biking. I ride ski trails, single track and on the roads. The bike does great for what I use it for. I am planning on replacing the bike for a good full suspension Trek in the next year or two. This bike will get me through till that time.

Over all the bike is a high end "Mart" bike and a good deal for the price. If your looking to be a little more aggressive then I would highly recommend spending an extra $100-200 and go to your local bike shop and get a bike you can upgrade.

product_title: Razor A5 Lux Scooter
review_body:
I used to have a Super Scooter when I was younger and I always loved flying around on that thing, but once I got into skateboarding my scooter days were over. Fast forward 20 years and now I have a son who loves riding his scooter and I'm left walking around like a commoner. Needless to say I needed a scooter so the research began. I originally ordered a Razor Black 3.0 because I wanted a sturdy scooter that would handle my weight and allow me to do tricks as I got better (hoping up curbs and whatnot). Unfortunately the handles came up to a few inches above my knees which was unacceptable.
Once the A5 arrived, I knew I had the scooter I needed. The wheels are 7.5" in diameter and handle the sidewalk anomalies with ease. The foam grips are way to narrow though so I replaced them with a pair of Odi grips. I had to cut off the flange part of the grips to make them fit (they were too long), as well as drill a hole in each end cap to allow the elastic line to pass through them. To slide them on, I applied rubbing alcohol to a toothbrush and scrubbed the inside of the grips. This allowed them to slide on with ease. Next I fed the elastic line through the hole in the end cap, tied it in a knot, and installed the end cap into the bar. This is a WAY better solution than the stock foam grips.

product_title: Bell Spotter Trainer Wheels for Bicycle
review_body:
Don't buy these. If you already bought them take them back. If you can't take them back don't ever go back to the store that sold them.

If you already have them with no hope of getting your money back, here is how to make them work.

The problem: If you look close at the manufacturer's picture of them installed, you will see that the axle sticks out past the bike frame by about an inch on each side. That leaves plenty of room to remove to simply remove the outer nuts, slide the training wheels with bracket over the axle and tighten everything back up. News flash Bell, bikes don't come with oversize axles. They come with axles that are long enough for you to put a nut on, that's it!

Instructions: Pull the rear wheel completely off the bike. There will be two nuts that hold the axle in place. Remove them. I had to remove one nut then use a pair of locking pliers to hold the axle while removing the other nut. At this point, the axle was gouged to the point that it would not go back in the wheel. If this happens to you, use a file to smooth them out again. Then wipe the metal filings off so they don't ruin your bearings. Put the wheel back together sans nuts. Send your kids to their room so they won't hear you swear. Now put the brackets on either axle. The flat side faces the hub, the tab faces out. Put the training wheels on now. Put the outer nuts on. Tighten them just enough that the training wheels don't fall off. Put the chain back on the sprocket and try to get the assembly back on the bike. Having someone hold the bike frame while trying to wedge the wheel back on helps. Tighten the nuts and don't ever buy anything from Bell again.

product_title: Mountain House Just In Case...Breakfast Bucket
review_headline: Great instant breakfast for camping or hiking but lots of sodium!
review_body:
My family and I enjoy the outdoors so it's convenient to have some instant breakfast readily available.

Likes:
*Easy to prepare, just add water.
*Tastes alright for on the go, outdoors meals.
*Good assortment of breakfast flavors.
*Comes in a convenient plastic bucket with 16 individually sealed pouches.
*The suggested shelf life is ten years but even after that, the instant meals are still edible, just the taste has deteriorated.

Concerns:
*While the \\"Breakfast Skillet\\" provides a good 400 calories, the other three flavors only provide around 190-250 calories, with over half of the calories from fat in the meals with eggs. 190-250 calories for breakfast is really on survival mode for most healthy adult males (2500 calories per day recommended).
*With the exception of the \\"Granola with milk and blueberries\\" (65mg), the other three meals with eggs have 640-930mg of sodium per serving (27%-39% of daily recommended sodium intake). High Blood Pressure, anyone?
*Our kids are finicky and only liked the \\"Granola with milk and blueberries\\".

Overall:
A nice tasting instant breakfast meals for outdoors activities. Also great for emergency meals but extended storage in hot and humid conditions deteriorates flavor and shelf life. Not good as daily meals due to high sodium content in the meals with eggs.

review_headline: Both knives are very sturdy, equally capable
review_body:
This is a review of the Izula 2 compared to the the Kabar BK 14. I own Both of these knives and will compare these two very similar blades. Both knives are very sturdy, equally capable, light weight knives in this review I will list the advantages of the Izula 2 over the BK14 and the reasons I think the Izula 2 is a better purchase.
Handle and length: 1/2 inch extra of handle on the izula 2 makes it much more comfortable to use than the BK 14 and really fit well into my size XL glove hands. The wide micarta handles included with the Izula 2 Help make the Izula 2 a better value as neither knife can be used comfortably without a Handle, even para cord warped handles don't cut it for large hands.
Sharpness: The Izula 2 came sharper and is easier to sharpen thank the BK 14. The BK 14 seems to have a less fine grained steel than the Izula 2, I could not get the BK Shaving sharp but with the same tools I can get the Izula 2 sharper than shaving sharp, wicked sharp? As sharp as my Mora can get. The Izulas sharpness is likely due to its Rowens heat treatment ESEE has.
Weight: the Izula 2 w/ handle scales is less than the BK 14 without handle scales.
Fit and finish: MY BK14 has uneven edge grinding getting worse at the tip and was missing blade coating in several very small spots. The BK14 also was only working sharp when delivered. The Izula 2 shaved hair on my arm when delivered and after using it on a backcountry camping trip as our only knife. Handle scales fit perfectly.
Blade coating: The blade coating on the Izula 2 is less abrasive and stays cleaner than the BK14's coating. It seems more durable and was more evenly applied than on the BK14.
Sheath: The Izula 2 has a better sheath hands down. It's smaller, has better retention, has no rattle and is much lighter than the BK14 sheath. MY BK14 doesn't snap into the sheath like It did upon purchasing.
Blade geometry: The spine of the blade of the Izula 2 has more of a downward curve and IMHO it gives the knife better ergonomics, cutting ability and fine control. While the BK14 has a longer blade IMHO it does not seem any more capable and it's wide blade hindered its ability to do fine wood carving. See images I uploaded comparing the Izula 2 and BK14's blades.
Heat treat and steel. The Izula 2 is made from 1095 steel with a Rowens heat treatment all ESEE knives have. The BK14 is 1095 chromium vanadium steel with a not quite as good as Rowens heat treatment. 1095 cro-van steel is better on paper but according to many people heat treatment is more important than steel chemistry at least to a point. After using both practically speaking I like the steel of the Izula 2 better because I can get it sharper than the BK14 steel.
Warranty: ESSE has the best warranty in the knife business, a unconditional if you break it you get a new one warranty. Kabar BK has a good warranty but not unconditional.

Is the Izula 2 worth the extra $30? I think so. For $30 more than the BK14 you get 1/2" extra handle, better ergonomics, better fit and finish, mythical Rowens heat treat, comfortable micarta handles, a unconditional warranty, a better sheath and more effective blade geometry. review_body:
When I first went to install this, I thought it could not support my bike's 29\\" wheels. The settings only go up to 27\\". Then I realized you can enter the circumference instead. This is probably the better thing to do even if your wheel size is listed. The result will be more accurate. The easiest way to do this is to mark your tire with chalk, grease or paint and ride it straight forward. Measure the distance between the marks the tire makes on the ground. That will be your circumference.

As for the computer itself, it has the basic functions. I wanted a simple one to give me speed and distance traveled. This also has average speed, elapsed time, max speed, a clock and a pace arrow. Unless you are a pro, what more could you want? The screen is also easy to read.

product_title: Mirrycle Original Bicycle Mirror
review_body:
I've known about the Mirrycle for decades, but decided that I could use more safety. I've tried helmet-mounted mirrors, and found them unsatisfactory.
Once I got the mirror mounted, it exceeded my expectations -- it gives a wide, stable view, and has enough flexibility for adjustment that I think any size rider can set it to his/her needs.

Beware that the installation can be tricky. The instructions have sections for 4 possible brake lever types. The first listed was Shimano 600. That's what I have.
I removed the front brake cable per instructions, removed the nipple that held the cable in the brake lever. It's no longer needed.
But the hollow bolt (through which the brake cable must be threaded) wasn't long enough to accommodate the supplied lock nut on its end. (boo)
But the installation kit included a threaded brass insert to use on a Gran Compe or Shimano Z style brake. Not what I have, but it looked likely. (yea)
But the insert had too large a diameter for the hole in my brake lever bracket. (boo).
But the instructions said that for some brakes, you may have to drill the hole in the bracket to 1/4". (yea)
But the hole was already 1/4" (boo)
So I measured the diameter of the inset (5/16"), and drilled the hole out with that size bit. (yea)
Went to thread the brake cable through the brake housing. But the housing was kinked and the brake cable was frayed. (boo --But after 29 years of use, that wasn't too surprising).
Made a trip to the local bike shop with the old cable and housing, and got new ones, with the housing cut to size by the tech, who advised me not to trim the bike cable until after installation and adjustment. (yea)
Threaded the cable thru the housing and the brake shoe clamping screw. Couldn't get cable tight enough with just two hands. (boo)
Remembered I had a "third-hand brake tool" to hold the calipers shut while the cable was being tightened (yea).
The screw threads that hold the pieces of the mirror stem together have an extremely tight fit (which is a good thing), but I needed to use a rubber jar-opening grip (appropriated from the kitchen drawer) in order to complete the fit.

In summary, I needed extra tools -- third-hand, jar-opener, portable drill with 5/16" bit, small adjustable open-end wrench -- beyond the two Allen wrenches supplied in the kit -- plus a trip to a bike shop for replacements for worn parts.
I still have to say -- it was worth the trouble of installation.

product_title: KRYPTONITE KryptoFlex 7 ft. Cable
review_headline: Easily cut with a bolt cutter - spend the money and get a REAL LOCK!
review_body:
I purchased this as an "added protection" for my bike, as we have many that we have locked on out porch (each of us own 2-3 bikes), and sometimes it's easier to loop them all together. I live in Burlington, Vermont mind you (by no means a "major US city") and looped the open end through a much beefier Kryptonite Series 2 chain lock. The bike that was locked using the Series 2 was fine, but the thief made off with a brand new, high-end mountain bike that was locked up using this one. Silly and naïve on my part, I guess. But I had just purchased the bike and waited a couple weeks too long to buy a proper lock. Mistake!

So, just be aware - I don't really know what this does to actually protect your bike. There are many other thefts in Burlington where the person comes around in the evening and clips these flex cables.

I'm about to buy a Series 4 Kryptonite bike lock to protect my bike from further potential theft. When you look at it as a one-time purchase, it costs relatively nothing to protect your bike. Far cheaper than even an okay renter's insurance policy and so worth it. I am thankful for having the Series 2 lock on my other bike, but this flex cable was apparently useless.

Really, it's worth it people - don't think... oh, $30 vs. $50 vs. $80 vs $100 - it's a one-time purchase to protect your bike. If you even own a bike worth $500, it's so worth it to just buck up and get the Series 2 or 4 locks. Those actually come with a protection policy from Kryptonite if the locks are compromised by a thief. Spend the money!

product_title: Big Agnes Slater UL 2 Plus Tent: 2-Person 3-Season
review_headline: I have used Big Agnes products before and always like the quality
review_body:
I had/have high expectations for this tent. I have used Big Agnes products before and always like the quality. Plus there are based right here in Colorado so that is a plus.

First to address what other people have said, no this is not a free standing tent, and no it does not work correctly unless staked down to the ground to get maximum square footage. Anyone who did research on this product, or have been on any serious backpacking know that most tents in this weight range are the same way... and the design eliminates a lot of weight. In my opinion tents should always be staked down, it's the only way, with any tent, you get maximum floor space and get the rain flys to work properly.

Now onto my problem with the tent. Even though the material feels light and thin, it is good quality. Proper handling will allow this tent to give you many years of use. However, when inspecting my tent out of the box, I saw a mistich/thin area at the very foot of the tent by the pole. I am going to chalk it up as a quality oversight, but none the less I am concerned. I have returned the tent for a new one, as I feel this tent deserves another shot in my book.

The tent is super light weight, has a very large fly space, seems are excellent quality and covered for leak proof. The tent also has a double layer door which will really help for warmth and you do not see on many tents in this class. The ability to completely seal up the tent, will also be nice for camping in areas with dust.

I am giving it three stars now, because of the quality oversight, but will report back after I receive my new one.

***UPDATE****
My second tent arrived quickly, as most always with Amazon prime items. I really was looking forward to getting the new tent setup and see if the quality and defects were not there, and to my great disappointment... the same problem as above was present in the new tent, just a different area. I really wanted this ultra light tent to work out, however I am going to be returning this one as well, and opting for a more rugged tent sacrificing a little bit of weight.

I still think Big Agnes products are good quality. I am not sure if this was a bad run off the production line or what. I don;t buy tents very often, averaging every 8 years now since my last investment. product_title: Slumberjack Big Tall Steel Chair (Khaki)
review_headline: The Best Lawn Chair I've Ever Owned!!!!
review_body:
I purchased my and my husband's chair last weekend and using Amazon Prime, we received them two business days later.

We were excited to try it after having read so many great reviews about it... and the reviews didn't fail us... the chair is WONDERFUL! It took us a moment to figure out how to open and close it the first time, but wow, is it ever nice. I used it this past weekend at both a picnic and RC racing event two days ago and just loved it!! It's tall enough that I no longer have to channel a turtle getting out of regular lawn chairs! I sit up so tall, and I'm a short lady (5'3). I didn't know if I would use the footrest, as many didn't, but I ended up using it a lot. It isn't as rigid as a solid steel footrest, but it did the trick for me. Although there was a tiny sag, I took my flip flops off often and sat my feet on the footrest. Nice feature because my feet don't really touch the ground (although they could if I sat towards the edge of the seat a bit) and it was great to rest them on the footrest. What I love equally as much as the height of the chair was the tightness of the seat. My goodness!!! Was it ever tight!! Unbelievable! There is absolutely NO SAG in the chair of this seat!!!! It is firmly tight and the fabric is rigid enough to be tight, but of a quality that it is soft and comfortable. I'm just awed... and so very happy with the purchase. After sitting in his, my hubby (who is 6'2) suggested that we get one for his father, who is also 6'2 and is struggling with getting up and down. He noted that the handles (which are of a quality steel material) are strong enough to support him comfortable. I work in hospice and I would agree... this chair would be wonderful also for seniors needing a little additional lift when trying to stand. As a matter of fact, at the flying event, one older woman, who was using a cane, sat in my chair and said, "This is really comfortable." And she had no problem getting up. She loved it as well. It is the best lawn (or director's) chair I've ever owned!!!! What a wonderful product!

product_title: Wilderness Systems Tempest 170 Ocean Sea Touring Kayak
review_body:
OK but....
I have owned this yak for a few years. This yak cuts, cruises and holds a line well. It is for a skinnier person. I am 6 foot, 160 lbs, slight, 34 waist. Although I do not find the yak tight if I were any wider or bigger this kayak would be uncomfortable and difficult to get in and out of as the cock pit is not very wide. It is a sevelt yak. I am not an ocean yaker so this yak is longer than I need. I would prefer a 14. I would not buy a yak with a skeg again. Skegs have holes that penetrate the bottom of the yak. The two holes used to attach the skeg are underwater and leak. A skeg is also somewhat limited to helping a person go straight and hold a line. Next time I will get a rudder which can be used to hold a line or turn and generally do not have holes that penetrate the bottom of a kayak. Having said all that I do like the yak and enjoy paddling it and cruising in it. I do think my 14 foot Dagger Savanna is faster , holds a line better, is lighter and easier to toss around and transport. It is also a bit easier to get in and out of. Would I buy the Tempest again, no; however I might consider it if I were actually on the ocean and fighting big swells. Wilderness does seem to use good plastic and are very well built and thought out yaks. I have a friend with a Carolina and that seems like a very nice yak as well. Between the Tempest and my Dagger Savanna, the Savanna is my go to yak.

product_title: Coleman 2000016462 Camp Oven, 13.5 x 12.9 x 3.3 Inch
review_body:
This one is nice. It's somewhat heavy in order to retain heat, but not too heavy that you can't pack it in your gear easily. Folds up and out easily. Rack clicks into one of the five indents - so pick your height. I would have liked to have 2 racks - we could have fit more trays for baking at once. Fits nicely over a single burner. You'll have to pull back the wind flaps or somehow get it figured out, because this unit really sticks out. You can use the second burner for a small pan, but not medium like you'd normally be able to, with this in place. Temp gauge on the front is super nice. It's tough to get it exact with propane, but close enough for baking, if you know the recipe and have a timer. Be sure to slot ALL the tabs on the top or bottom. If you miss one, then the sides will bow out a little and you'll lose heat.

I've never had an actual oven before while camping, and this one works well. I'm going to be be on the lookout for a single burner unit just for this oven, or maybe a good deal on another two burner portable stove. This oven really does take up a fair amount of stove real estate when deployed.

It does cool down quickly, so you can move it off to the side easily. Beware, the top handle is metal as well, and it's hard to grab with an oven mit. So be inventive with a fork or a knife and safe and you'll be good.

review_headline: I’m still glad to make this purchase because just having a way ...
review_body:
Purchased for a trip to the Yucatan, but wasn’t necessarily needed as since the places we stayed (a major resort) had purified ice and bottled water. We went on many day trips to outlying areas and the 2 liter bottle full of hotel water and tour bus bottled water was enough for the day trips to Mayan ruins or other scenic sites.
On one excursion to the Coba ruins I had to refill my bottle from a restaurant’s blue cooler, and just for peace of mind I went ahead and treated that water. But being in a touristy area it was probably plenty safe and my treating it wasn’t necessary since getting tourist sick is not their intent.
I’m still glad to make this purchase because just having a way to purify drinking water whether camping or due to some concern with local water supply makes owning a SteriPen worthy. It will go with us on all future overseas trips.
Two problems surfaced on our purchased item, one was the bottle would not seal properly and unless it was upright it would drip. It was missing a seal and it was promptly resolved by the manufacturer with a phone call when we got back home. The second issue had to do more with me the user than any product defect. Trying to purify the water a second time I couldn’t get the SteriPen wand to work, a red light kept coming on. My first thought was the lithium batteries drained from one use, so I replaced them but still got the red light. Then I thought the humidity had affected the electronics but eventually learned to turn the wand on outside of the water and then insert in order for it to perform correctly.

product_title: Timbuk2 Classic Messenger Bag
review_headline: Older Timbuk2 Classics models are still the overall best bags for me
review_body:
I have at least 5 active Timbuk2 bags that I use from time to time. Among them are 3 classic messengers, the old model, the last one and this 2014 one. I wanted to like the bag because I like the improvements I read and saw online. But it was not as I expected to be when I got it.

Pros:
- Side mesh pockets for water-bottles, harddrives, portable batteries, and more!
- Buckles are now inside the flap (for a change)
- Top holding flaps come free (albeit very thin one and not the padded you get on custom orders)
- Retained the napoleon pockets in front

Cons:
- Major gripe, less pockets, specially on the inner zipper lining! I use that for personal stuff and now it just jiggles around inside the zippered compartment.
- Straps are now thinner and just smaller than the 2013 and before models. It feels a little 'weak' on my chest. I want the old wide and thick ones :(
- Shoulder pads are now fixed. I have lots of strap pads I orders from Timbuk2.com and I still use it to mix and match from what I wear. I don't know why they didn't made these new ones removable with velcro.
- I'm not sure about the new Cordura fabric. It's much durable and abrasion resistant from what I read but I still prefer Ballistic Nylon just for the the overall heft and thickness.
- The tightening and adjusting system of the straps doesn't work for me yet. It's now smaller and might take me a while to get used to.

For me the older models still has the better build and just the robustness and compartments that I need. The post 2010 and pre 2014 models were the best in my opinion.

Just an update: You can check out a youtube video I did about the comparisons here: http://bit.ly/1YqCIUy

product_title: SILICONE SWIM CAP FOR BEST SPORT PERFORMANCE - New easy-breath comfort swimming apparel for kids and adults
review_body:
This has been a great swim cap for the several weeks I have used it. It keeps my mid-neck length hair out of eyes and helps hold goggles in place without getting tangled in hair. If put on correctly, it keeps hair relatively dry - just be sure your skin is dry when donning cap as wet skin prevents obtaining a good seal. It secures to dry forehead, temples, ears, neck quite well, and stays in place for "regular" swimming (no diving, splashing, underwater gyrations). I swim laps in an indoor pool, and this cap works very well for me if I don't try to re-adjust fit when I'm already in the water.

As soon as I leave the pool I rinse my swim cap in cool tap water to remove chlorine, place a soft rolled up hand towel inside to hold form and allow to air dry. When thoroughly dry, fold and place in protective zipper pouch that came with the cap. With proper care (as suggested by Swimculture) the cap still feels and functions like it's brand new.

review_body: I wanted a small, light weight, easy to set up sunshade for times when I take one dog to a dog show or agility trial for just one day. It took 10 minutes. The hardest part was getting the last pole into its pocket without the end of it ripping the mesh sleeve. I do agree with others who said they wished the sleeves were sturdier material.  The size of the tent is perfect for me and my dog (in large crate) and another person. Unlike other sun-umbrellas, you can sit in a full sized lawn chair in this one. Ventilation is very good with the huge back door that can be opened to screen or totally open. You can easily zip the front panel up if you need privacy for changing clothes. I do have a large silver mesh tarp, and will still take that with me to increase shade on really hot days (I have Siberian huskies, and heat is our enemy). I came up with another use for this 1/2-a-dome tent, too--it is perfect to set in the backyard to put a little cot in it to sleep outside on summer nights when you'd prefer to be outside (it will keep the dew from forming on your sleeping bag). To avoid frustration in setting it up, I did **mark the pockets where the BLACK poles are inserted** which really eases set-up..no questions as to where the 3 poles go when it's all floppy and laying in a heap on the ground. There is one design flaw I discovered outside on a rainy night...The back door has the rainfly on the inside. Why did they do that? ha ha...had to drain water out in the morning. Otherwise, I am very happy with this purchase. Hope this critique helps someone.

product_title: Fenix HP25 360 Lumen LED Headlamp (Yellow or Iron Grey), Flood/Spot Combination Flashlight with LegionArms AA Batteries Pack
review_headline: Last Headlamp You'll Need OR Want! *perfection*
review_body:
I've been using a cheap Rayovac headlamp for many years now. It was never a bad light, but I opted to upgrade it with this Fenix headlamp for the hiking trip on the Appalachian Trail that I went on a few weeks ago. After I pulled it out that first night on the trail when I went down to pump some water from a stream with my Katadyn Pocket... I laughed when I turned it on because though I knew it would be bright, I didn't realize that the flood and spot options on it were absolutely perfect for so many things I use a headlamp for while I'm camping or hiking.

The flood light saw more use because it provides 4 different lighting options, which meet most of my needs while outdoors. From lighting up our entire campsite & shelter at night, to putting it on the most dim setting for reading a book at night in my ENO JungleNest Hammock... this light did all of it with perfection!! I only utilized the spotlight function to either show off (yeah, I like comparing the brightness of flashlights & headlamps) or use it when a crazy hiker decides to jump up at 3am and run around the campsite while blowing an airhorn, all because he saw "green lights" floating around and flashing into his tent. lol

Overall, this light outperformed every single flashlight I own, along with my old headlamp. I have no complaints whatsoever... heck, even the cheap no-name batteries that came with it lasted the whole trip and never once left my headlamp going dim on me, so I had no use for my spare set of Duracells. If anyone asks me about getting a headlamp, I'll immediately direct them to the Fenix HP25... unless of course they decide to release a newer "better" model, which I honestly don't think is even possible. Kudos to Fenix!!!

product_title: Nebo 5581 220 Lumen Redline Tactical Flashlight Strobe S.O.S
review_headline: Why this crappy 1-star flashlight has a 4-star rating!
review_body:
The current 4 star rating on these flashlights is misleading. I'm guessing practically all people rated them almost immediately after they received them. After opening the box I would have given these flashlights 4 stars too. But a couple months of use exposes just how cheap these flashlights are.

I initially thought this was a great little flash light. However, after a few months of use I found out how fragile it is. The metal construction is durable. However that red ring you see in the photo connects the body of the flashlight and the lens. The ring is made of cheap plastic and has brittle threads to make the connection. I bought 4 of these flashlights. The threads on the plastic ring has broken on two of them causing the lens to fall off. The threads broke during normal use (i.e. twisting the head of the flashlight to adjust the beam size). One even broke while I was carrying it around in my pocket. None of these flashlights were dropped.

I urge you to check other low ratings and see just how many people had this same problem. This kind of breakage is not an exception. It's systemic. Steer clear of this flashlight and try to find something with an all metal design.

review_body:

With 2 liters of water in it, snacks for the day and some lightweight rain gear I am constantly having to pull it back up on my waist. On the trail I find myself stopping every few hundred yards to fiddle with some of the straps, trying to improve the way the pack rides on my body. None of the adjustments seem to satisfy for more than ten or fifteen minutes. And no matter how tightly I cinch it down I can't stop the load from bouncing. Very annoying. Compared to the Tour and Day TLS the waist belt is very narrow. So narrow that it digs into my gut. The narrow belt combined with having to keep it super tight so that it doesn't keep sliding down just makes for a miserable hike.

It is large enough to double as a small book bag or as a personal item for air travel (check with your air carrier). I like it better in urban environments than on a hike.

This is a super light, minimalist type bag. If I respect the Daylight's design limitations and keep it lightly loaded it can be a pleasure to use. Heavily loaded it's miserable. For me, the Tour is the best riding of the Mountain Smith series with the DAY TLS being second. Both bags are far heavier than this one and with much more padding.

I am 6' tall and about 10 pounds overweight. A thinner person might have better results with this bag.

product_title: Okuma Crisium Graphite 2-Piece Fly Rod
review_body:
I bought this rod through amazon warehouse deals for a third the listed price. It is a two piece, 8'6\\" graphite 6/7wt flyrod. The rod looks great and casts very well. I already have a 5wt fiberglass rod and a 8wt fiberglass rod so I really wanted to get a graphite rod for a good price in a different weight that I did not have. I had previously owned an 8wt graphite rod but the rod was over 30 years old and broke during a fishing session.

My first impressions is that this rod even though is a two piece, is very sensitive. I could feel the fish through the rod even if they gently took the fly and when fighting the fish I always knew I was hooked up. This rod also casts extremely well. It loads then propels the line through the guides so smoothly you need less effort to cast. With my fiberglass rods you really have to bend the rod with the flyline forcefully to get a similar result. My 5wt is the same size and number of pieces as this Okuma rod and the Okuma rod is superior in every way.

I really enjoyed my first few hours of fishing with this rod. Great sensitivity, great casting and at a great price. I will update with more information soon after I get a few more hours of fishing with this rod but initial results are good.

***UPDATE***
10/27/2014
I fished a couple of more times with this rod and I have to say I like it a lot. The one complaint I have is that the reel I am using with this rod does not stay in the reel seat because the tightening ring on the rod does not stay tight. I have a 100 dollar rod that has two tightening rings for the reel and that seems to be the best but I have not had this problem with my other rods that have only one ring. I never want to over tighten but I may have to. The reel has never fallen out but after fishing for about 15 minutes the reel kinda rattles in the reel seat so that I have to tighten the ring again. This is just my experience with the rod on a few occasions that I have taken it out. Otherwise this is a great rod. Casting is effortless but I am using an 8wt line on this rod just because I had either 8wt or 5wt to try it out and the 8wt seems great. I will have to update again when I try a 5wt line with this rod.this is a great rod. Casting is effortless but I am using an 8wt line on this rod just because I had either 8wt or 5wt to try it out and the 8wt seems great. I will have to update again when I try a 5wt line with this rod.
