product_title: Skatecycle (Black)
review_body:
So...this free rider is a microcosm of society. It's not easy and most will give up and quit. Those same people will create excuses and reasons why they could do it...design flaw! No..it's user flaw. See...there are people who can do it...so it's NOT an issue with the skate cycle, it's an issue with you. I know that's is super difficult to accept and comprehend....it's not the free rider..it's you.

It took me all of 20 minutes to figure it out...

Was it difficult? Yes....

It took me W A Y longer to learn how to ride a unicycle, but I stuck that one out also. There's this word called perseverance...look it up.

So, if you want to learn to ride this \\"flawed\\" item, here are some secrets...

1. The front of your ankles should NOT come in contact with the stirrups. You actually BALANCE on the wheels. The balls of your feet must be directly over the wheels.

2. You don't really lean to balance and recover, you turn your feet in and out. I am not saying you don't lean at all, but the key is pointing your toes if you are falling forward...and your heels if falling a bit back. The item is incredibly well balanced...once you get the hang of it, when you come to a stop, it literally will just stand there for a bit.

3. You need a slight downhill to initially learn....or a wall or corner you can push off with your hands. Just like a bicycle, it's way easier when you are moving at a decent speed than being still...get it?

4. To pump yourself, you need to get a snowboard glide type motion...the upper part of you body starts the flow and the lead leg does the carve...the back foot follows and keeps the pump.

5. It helps to point your back toe towards the back...and heel closer to middle...gives,you more leverage on pointing toes.

That's it. It's not easy. It's nothing like a ripstick. \\"Oh...I can ride a bike, maybe I can do a wheelie on a motorcycle!\\" It's a separate deal and one does not ensure you can do another. If you are a parent, your kid will have to put some effort in...just like schoolwork, making a sports team or learning a guitar solo. There is NOTHING wrong about this item...just typical parents who can't accept that maybe. JR. Isn't the most hard working or coordinated tyke on the planet.

If you are into balance and challenges, this is for you...of not, go buy an uber challenging ripstick...or maybe play with chalk.

product_title: Ibex Outdoor Clothing Men's Arrivee Bib Shorts
review_headline: I really wanted to like these!
review_body:
Have bought Ibex stuff before, several shirts of great quality, plus the wool dramatically improves the inevitable sweat funk of summers in the SE USA. Bought these cycling shorts recently and was very impressed with the construction quality the breathability of the wool fabric -- they also have the first wool-based 'chammy' I've seen and use an alternate fabric for the seat area to keep the nice wool safe from seat contact pilling. The first commutes with the shorts were a beautiful thing, the 17 miles each way were very comfortable and my office was distinctly non-stinky (well, maybe a tiny bit of wet sheep smell).

But when I tried a multi-hour ride I ran into a problem; the wool inner pad cover bunched up along a seam and started to rub on my inner thighs. After 25 miles I had a burning abrasion area an inch in diameter on each side and had to cut the ride short, by the time I got back to my car at 40 miles I was not having fun.

Got in contact with Ibex (noticed that another purchaser had reported the same problem), and while they would swap the now used shorts, the construction would be the same for the replacements. This issue will probably not affect everyone, but for at least two of us they are expensive shorts that don't work for long rides.

product_title: Victorinox Swiss Army SwissChamp Pocket Knife
review_body:

The logo is cheaply printed, the little lines extending out from the sides of the cross are too fat and the crest and cross color are incorrect and slightly faded in places, doesn't look original, probably a used repair job. The plastic is deformed in several places. The pin is missing and the main blade is not factory sharp. The awl is barely retractable. Numerous little scratches on the metal of the back side of the tool layers, once again suggesting that this is either used or rebuilt. To top it off there is no warranty card or handbook.

Will be returning for a refund from Global Kingdom Holdings. They were, thus far, quick to respond to my return request.

product_title: Mongoose Expo Scooter 12” Wheels
review_body:
I have two sons and just bought 2x of these babies. It's pretty easy to put together--not sure the issues with the brake lines ppl are stating. All that you need to do is undo the screw that fastens the metal wire and pull it out and retighten. Do that a few times until you reach the level you want and you're set. Took me five minutes.

Now for the issues. Both scooters were missing the same parts (I got them from Walmart online). I had no front brake cable nor the nuts with hooks that keep the wheel attached to the frame. I called mongoose and they were extremely helpful and shipped them out immediately. A+ for customer service.

Now for another issue--the rims are garbage. There is a constant and loud squeaking sound from the cheap spokes. It's insane tbh. I'm now looking on ebay trying to find some plastic mags to avoid this issue. In addition, I didn't put on the pegs. It looks like they'll rip up your ankles and my kids are young. Maybe in awhile they'll get one.

The scooter itself looks sharp--much nicer in person than in picture. I was hesitant on this color over the blue--but I'm glad I got this. The rotor for the brake lines is an A+ feature. Kudos for this feature. Minus the super cheap rims, this will turn out to be a nice scooter as soon as I buy some Mags.

Regardless, even at it's worst, there is no competition between this and the razor scooters. I'd tell your kids to walk before handing over one of those.

product_title: Sawyer Products Premium Permethrin Clothing Insect Repellent
review_headline: Be aware that the trigger Spray bottle not a spray like the aerosol can
review_body:
I have used this product for years and agree with all the positive reviews as to its effectiveness, lack of odor etc.
I had previously used the aerosol cans which may not be the most economical way to apply the product but allow you to do so evenly over all surfaces.
The trigger "spray" is not a spray, but a stream. Unlike most spray nozzles, you cannot switch from stream to spray - just off to full stream.
This makes it quite awkward and messy to apply and impossible to evenly distribute. Further, if you treat clothing hanging vertically, the liquid tends to runs down.
I can see no advantage to a stream vs spray dispenser for this product and, indeed the name is misleading.
For those who have not used this product before or those like me who might consider switching to the bottle from the aerosol, you might want to be aware of the difference and decide if it is worth the savings.
I want to emphasize that the 3 star rating is for the dispenser and not the product!

product_title: Adidas Women's Outdoor climacool Boat Sleek Water Shoe
review_body:
I ordered the Adidas Outdoor Climacool Water Shoes along with the Teva Women's Fuse-Ion Water Shoe.

These are my findings in directly comparing the two:

The Adidas are more minimal than the Teva and indeed are as cute as the photo but don't appear to be as well made or as substantial. They are also no where near as comfortable as the Teva. I wore each of the above sets of shoes all day long, first the Adidas because I received them first and then a week later, the Teva. On both occasions I had to walk across a wet lawn (to retrieve a hose)... in the Adidas, water seeped-up into the shoe through the bottom the second I hit the lawn, while in the Teva this was not the case. Although the Teva soles are obviously thicker and this may be why, I want to think the drainage holes are one way, aka, water that goes in through the top of the shoes goes out the holes but are not as easily infiltrated with water through the bottom..... ?? I don't know and it's pure supposition on my part but either way, they are far more useful as an all day water shoe that you won't have to change after your done with the water portion of that same day and say, are walking to that restaurant for lunch.

Another superior design feature in the Teva is the tongue that is incorporated in the top of the shoe versus the Adidas that have a separate, more traditional tongue that has to be intermittently pulled up and moved to the center when you first put them on and when you are moving into awkward positions that cause them to move such as when I was sitting on my folded legs while I was loading the dry hatches of my sit-on-top kayak...

Overall, for my purposes, the Teva are better because I can kayak with them, walk in the water as I get the kayak to shore and investigate tide pools without cutting my feet (they are really slip resistant) and not have to bring an additional pair of shoes to change into (because I'm camping at a site only accessible bynon-engined water vessels and traveling light is paramount...).

The Adidas are much lower profile, more of a responsive sole (you can feel the ground allot through the shoe, almost as much as my rock climbing shoes, so I guess it just depends on what you are going to use them for... You be the judge.

product_title: Doggyhut Medium Pet Bike Trailer / Jogger Kit Dog Bicycle Carrier Red 7030101
review_headline: Quality, Affordable Option That's Opening Up My Old Dog's World Again
review_body:
My 13 year old, 35 lb. (what we think is an) Australian Kelpie just fits in this trailer/stroller but that's fine. Training has been a cinch since she was crate trained as a pup. I say the usual, \\"Go in your crate\\" as I toss a treat in. We've yet to attach it to a bike but I've jogged and she's nothing but relaxed in there! It has really re-opened her world again. And I don't have to carry her home if her leg/shoulder gives out. [I'm no spring chicken myself...]

I bought this with the beach in mind. She can still enjoy a short swim but as of last year the walk from the house to the beach and back is too far so I started to drive her the 1 block. But getting over the dune boardwalk, across the beach and into the water and back to the car is too far this year. So, I can now stroll her right from the house, over the dune boardwalk and park the buggy at the end. Ah, if only the wheels were WheelEez!!! Also, in the general neighborhood she is strolled to her favorite sniffing spots, gets out, walks a bit, takes care of business. If/when she limps: back in she goes for the stroll home. I ride her over to a neighbor's fenced yard where she hangs out with 2 dog friends too!

Considering the arthritis issue it took a bit of trial and error the first few times entering and exiting to arrange the best method. Getting in is less of a problem. Exiting is best with one of 2 strategies depending on where we are. If we're home I back the stroller up to a step with a large landing area and an outdoor rug. This way she steps straight out and perhaps down only a few inches. If we're out on a walk with no option like that available I ensure her step down will be onto soft ground and assist her with my arms to gently lower her down.

It's with hesitation that I'm giving it 4 stars instead of 5. I feel it would work better for an arthritic dog if the whole top unzipped. But consider that 1 star down is just a smidge! This little cart is a potential life-changer for $110!!!!

review_body: I recently got back into roller skating. These looked like a decent, inexpensive buy. They were. Once I found the button, (too me a minute) the adjustment works pretty decently, and they roll pretty well. All things considered they are decently padded. I don't pull them out very often, but so far they seem to be holding up decently. These aren't exactly a high end set of skates, but they work well for the casual skating I do. I would certainly recommend these to a friend.

review_body: I am disappointed in this purchase. It arrived and there were absolutely no instructions. No pictures, no drawings, no nothing. review_body: I purchased the Camelbak Eddy Glass bottle in June 2013. I thought I was going to have to get a whole new bottle but was very please to be able to purchase just the bite valves and straws. Now i can continue to use my favorite bottle!

product_title: Sundome 4 Person Tent (Green and Navy color options)
review_body: I bought two of these for my scout troop.  I generally buy Ozark Trail brand because it is generally a little cheaper, but is still pretty good.  However, I pitched out the extra $10 and got this four man tent.  i set it up when it arrived and it was made of much more sturdy and durable material.  You could tell the walls were thicker.  There is an extra vent at the bottom which helps with hot days.  The poles are much thicker than Ozark Trails'.  Another feature I like is the e-port has a zipper on it.  Many of your cheaper tents don't have that.  I've owned many different kinds and brands of tents in my life.  This one is one of the best.

product_title: White Lightning Bike Chain Cleaner Kit
review_headline: Don't pay more for the other cleaner kits!
review_body: This bicycle kit, although low in price, provides an excellent method for cleaning bicycle chains. Not only does it come with enough cleaning solution for 4 cleans, it also includes written and video instruction guides! Although the bristles are not very strong, they are not any different from the other cleaning kits that cost between $25 and $30. This kit is excellent for cleaning bicycle chains.

product_title: Polarmax Women's Light Weight Tech Silk Pant
review_body: My wife bought these to take on an Alaskan cruise. They are very comfortable and warm, especially when the wind is blowing.

product_title: McNett Tactical Gruntline Deluxe Multifunctional Elastic Cord
review_headline: Wonderful convenience for hand-washed items and wet swimwear
review_body: With all of the weight restrictions on airlines I decided to pack light for my trip and wash underwear and socks out in my hotel sink. I bought two of these and they came in very handy. I had no problem finding ways to hang them in my hotel bathroom and between swimwear and hand-washed articles I used them daily during my 2-week vacation. Spend a minute to practice pulling a bit of the wet item thru the braiding and you are set to go.

product_title: Henschel Burnished Hand Stained Raffia Western Straw Hat with Wooden Beaded Band
review_body: Nothing special either.  I bought it as a summer hat for yard work and the beach.  I took a star away because I really did not like the silver plastic beads on the band.  So I broke it down and remade the band using stronger string, leather and bone beads from a broken Buddhist prayer necklace I had.  Looks much nicer now. product_title: Earth Jamboree Military Style Aluminum Cot
review_body: after getting the second one I'm pleased. the first one had holes in the canvas and had to return it.

product_title: Rainkist Adult Poncho-Unisex One Size
review_body:
Please be aware that most of the posted reviews are for products other than the RainKist Poncho. This RainKist poncho is the perfect poncho and has all the features I wanted. It has the extra brim on the hood so it has a large overhang which is valuable when you wear glasses! It has 2 snaps on the placket at the neck so it's easy to get on and off for people who wear glasses. It snaps up to my neck and it's a perfect fit - not too tight or too loose. The hood has cords for cinching it tighter. The poncho comes to just below my knees (I'm 5' 3\\") and the \\"arms\\" almost cover my fingertips. (My husband is 5' 9\\" and the poncho comes to just above his knees and the \\"sleeves\\" stopped at his wrists. The hood and the neck also fit him perfectly when both placket snaps were snapped.) There are 2 snaps on each side of the poncho to create the armholes. I think this is the perfect weight (100% PVC) and it seems durable - not like those ponchos with the thickness of plastic bags. I looked at a large number of ponchos and this is perfect. I bought it for an October European vacation but plan to keep it in my car for our rainy season of 5 days in September! It's a lot better protection than an umbrella! I purchased the yellow poncho and love the color - it's a rich, deep, school bus yellow. The pouch is clear plastic rimmed in yellow with one snap and is envelope shaped. It was larger than I expected (10.75\\" across x 8\\" height) but that aids in easier packaging of the poncho!

UPDATE JUNE 13, 2014:
I really like this poncho and ordered the navy blue for my husband from the same supplier the yellow one came from - Cambridge Select. I received an umbrella! I returned it and ordered the blue poncho again - from Cambridge Select. This was a mistake because I received an umbrella again. I've now ordered the navy blue poncho a third time but from a different company. Cambridge Select had no problems getting a yellow poncho to me but having their navy blue umbrellaslabelled as ponchos presents a big problem in getting a correct order in that color.

product_title: ChillWarmer Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle - Chiller 2.0 (Stainless)
review_body: Keeps my water ice cold on bike rides.  Doesn't leak and is very easy to drink from while on the move.

product_title: Sawyer Products Mini Water Filtration System

These seem to work pretty well in home tests (haven't tried them in the actual wild yet). Great peace of mind for emergencies for now, but I'm hoping to actually try to use them for a hiking or camping trip soon.

A bit disappointing that I actually found them at one of the big stores at a cheaper price than I got them for here on Amazon.

product_title: Camelbak Podium Big Chill 25 oz Bottle
review_body:
I just bought two of these to replace my old 17 oz Camelbak bottles. There was nothing wrong with my old bottles I just wanted to the larger bottles to use on my longer rides. With the larger bottles it is like having an extra bottle with me which is good on long hot rides. I am an avid Camelbak user because they are the quality products that do a great job. Since upgrading to Camelbak I have been very happy with how long they keep my drinks cold and my new bottles continue to do a great job for me.

As an Amazon Prime member this purchase qualified for free two day shipping and my package arrived on time and in perfect condition.

product_title: Backpack Cooler
review_body: Cheap and fell apart. Of course, 10 days past the return date. I'm not happy at all! Save your money.

product_title: Carlisle Standard Polyethylene Clad Aluminum Canoe Paddle with T-Grip
review_body: These are green. They make my canoe move. They work. They have a nice T handle that you can palm. I haven't lost one yet. I haven't tested them as a weapon. I was able to use one to retrieve a wayward beer can so I guess they are versatile.

review_body: This tool will get you out of a bind on the trail!  I can't see spending crazy amounts of money for a multi tool unless you're a road racer who absolutely needs a few less ounces.  Perfect for me on the trail!

product_title: Goson Classic 57mm Mirror Lens Aviator Sunglasses
review_body: It looks and feel good but it is only good to look at sun! otherwise you can not see anything trough the glasses. It is very dark and you definitely will have problem specially if you are driving. I think that explains the price!

product_title: Kali Protectives Avatar MTB Helmet
review_body:
Well built helmet with great graphics. Sized a bit large. Padding for M.B. helmets are different than M.C. helmets in that they are spaced out with large open areas in between. This requires the helmet fit to be smaller because there is less padding to compress.
Interior fabric, chin strap and edge moulding are all quality materials. The graphics are actual paint, not stickers. The red is metal flake: very cool.

product_title: Campfire Roasting Forks with Coated Handles 33-inch, 4-pc Set
review_body: There work great for roasting marshmallows over the fire. The handle stays cool and its great that you can use the two prongs to hold the marshmallow onto the stick. They are also super easy to clean by heating up in the fire.

product_title: Ibera Bicycle Triangle Frame Bag
review_body: I use my old Specialized 26er as a get-around town rider and occasionally do some light trail riding. I purchased the medium sized bag and it fits perfectly. I just wanted something to put important things (wallet, keys, weed pipe, etc) into as I ride. This seems to work well. The velcro attaches to the frame securely, who knows how it will last long term though. I usually have it empty besides those small things, but I tried it with my toolkit inside (pump, tools, levers, patches) and still had plenty of room for my wallet (and weed pipe...hehe). My only complaint is that sometimes it can get in the way of your legs, but it's no big deal. I can live with it.

product_title: USA Leather Classic Mens Black Leather Hip Length Jacket - 5X-Large
review_body: This jacket is made of quite soft and flexible cowhide, still quite a bit more durable than the lambskin products that I have known.  Before purchase, I wondered if it might be more of a motorcycle jacket, fairly thick and hard, or more of a street jacket, thinner and softer; it is the latter.  It meets my needs because I wanted something that was light enough to wear when it is not very cold, but also heavy enough to wear when it is quite cold (which the liner accomplishes), and something that would breathe while also being an excellent wind barrier - leather does those two things.  The length is great, dropping low and keeping the wind out.  It has one inside pocket and two outside pockets, and no pocket zippers, as a slight downside.  It is comfortable to wear and light in weight, so I think I will enjoy it most of the time that I wear a jacket.  Buying XXL for my XL frame runs slightly large, but it is a comfortable fit.

product_title: Coleman Montana 8-Person Tent
review_body:
I purchased this tent because of the door and size. There is enough room for my family, four of us, and our luggage. After camping for the past forty years, I'm amazed that it took so long to design a door that is useful with children going in and out. The first thing that goes on almost any tent is the door zipper.
I do not purchase anything but Coleman nor does any other family member

product_title: Fireking Reusable Firestarter
review_body: Makes starting a camp fire so easy.  Keep using the FireKing over and over. Must add more lighter fluid.  Very efficient use of lighter fluid.

product_title: The Compact Towel Reusable Multi-tool. Weighs only .5 oz. Quick Dry, Waterproof Packaging, Super Absorbent, Antibacterial, Soft, Perfect for all Outdoor Activities- 3 Pack 12x24" Lightload Towels
review_body: I purchased these for my GO bag and for camping. These towels are amazing and work better than expected. Do yourself a favor and pick up a pack today.

product_title: Cycling Bike Bicycle BMX Chain Whip Wheel Sprocket Remove Tool
review_body: For those of you who do at home bike mechanic work or like to switch out your rear cassettes. This is the tool to have, this one is pretty basic and does everything I need it to. It's very basic, no frills and cheap. So far I have changed out three cassettes and the chain whip is still doing it's thing.

product_title: Schwalbe Delta Cruiser HS 392 Reflex Bicycle Tire - Wire Bead
review_body:
I bought the brown Delta Cruisers to go on a classic Trek touring bike with cream sks longboard fenders. They look so beautiful and the ride is smooth and light.

Replaced my old schwalbe marathon touring plus with these, and so far have been very pleased. They are a little wider at 35c and lighter and the difference is notable. So far no punctures, just a smooth easy quiet ride.

I also bought cream Delta Cruisers on an old german Hercules with chrome fenders, and love those as well. They get a little dirty on the high tread, but so much prettier than standard black especially with softer colored frames and fenders. Given the choice, why not try cream or brown? So I did, and am very pleased with the choices. Next time i might try the little big ben, which is even wider. Width doesnt slow down at all, just gives nice cushion in the city.

product_title: Snow Peak Giga Power Stove
review_body:
Smaller and lighter armour but also likable. Pack King too.
And serve as a wonderful backpacking stove.
It's hard to get fine thermal throttling.

product_title: Xtreme Bright Portable Work light and Power Sports Zoomable LED Headlamp Flashlight with 3 Light Modes
review_body: I needed something like this for closeup work and it fits my needs perfectly. There were dozens to choose from with prices all over the place. This seemed to be the best for the buck. Best thing about this is the ability to shift the lamp at different angles pointed downward.

product_title: Coghlan's Nylon Mesh Organizer Bags, 3-Piece Set
review_headline: Great supplement to expensive packing cubes!
review_body: Actually, the large and medium bags are direct substitutes for packing cubes and will easily hold a weeks worth of rolled tshirts and underwear respectively. (However, I will note that these are solid black rather than having yellow trim - making them harder to find in the dark.) The smaller one is an excellent ditty bag for small gear like charging hardware, cables, adapters and related items (and it actually is yellow). The set of 3 costs less than a single packing cube - making them a value winner for the frugal traveler.

product_title: Fox River Therm-A-Wick Sock Liners - Unisex
review_body: Great for keeping your feet dry in the warm, hot weather and warm in the cool and cold.  Make sure to purchase more than one pair...these wicking socks will become a favorite fast.

product_title: Royal Scout Complete Dirt Scooter
review_body: My son has this and he loves it. It has nice bouncy, wheels. You do need to air them though and monitor that just as you would a bicycle. He does trick jumps with it, as well as his Eldorado and his kick scooter, and he likes the softer landing. It's not has hard on the joints. Although it is heavier due to the off road riding ability. It is a great scooter. Very well made. Nice long, wide deck, good grips on handlebars

product_title: Sunlite Standard Schrader Valve Tubes, Black
review_body: Perfect fit and delivered to my front door. What more could you ask for?  The quality seemed great for what I needed and it appears to be holding air and working fine.

This shirt feels great (material), but wrinkles and stays wrinkled, I hope I can reurn it.

product_title: Independent Trucks Stage 11 Silver Trucks - Pair
review_body: The description and title for this product is very incorrect as others have pointed out. I received 1 truck, not a pair of trucks.

product_title: Hydro Flask Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle, Standard Mouth w/Loop Cap
review_body:
I love this water bottle! It is attractive and comes in great colors,but best of all, it really keeps your liquid at whatever temperature it was when you put it in. I have put cold water (no ice, just cold water) in this bottle, left it in the hot car (I live in Florida) for hours and come back to find the water was just as cool as when I put it in the bottle. Amazing!! My daughter does use ice in her water and hours after filling her Hydro Flask you can shake it and still hear the ice in there, even if left in the heat.

I also love that these flasks leave no metallic taste in your drink like you get with some other metal drinking bottles. Plus, the outside of the bottle stays at room temperature while the liquid inside stays at whatever temp it was when you put it in there. I really dislike picking up a bottle that is ice cold on the outside. This one is comfortable to hold (both in temperature and in texture. I love the feel of the outside of this bottle - just enough grip that it won't be slipping out of your hand).

These bottles are a bit pricey, but I have never found another that works as well and I think it is worth every penny! I highly recommend these flasks!

product_title: Energizer Weatheready 3-LED Carabineer Rechargeable Crank Light, Red
review_headline: I bought 8 of these flashlights, 7 great, 1 dud
review_body:
There are lots of good reviews already here. For the most part, I had an experience similar to the positive reviewers. The lights seem sturdy and are plenty bright. They are compact in size and we have them in the cars and emergency kits.

One of my flashlights will not stay lit for more than a half second. It flickers on and off and only works if you hold down the power button. Still, the others work well so I'm going to just chalk the bad one up to a fluke.

product_title: Panlong Roswheel Bicycle Bike Front Tube Top Tube Cell Phone Bag Frame Bag-4.2 Red
review_body: Nice to find a bag were I can see my phone the whole time. Wiah I bought the next size up buy awesome bag.

product_title: Swagman XC Cross-Country 2-Bike Hitch Mount Rack (1/1/4 and 2-Inch Receiver)
review_body: We live on a dirt road that is less than smooth most of the time. This rack holds the bikes in place very well. Would recommond this bike rack to anyone.

product_title: Solo Pot 900: Lightweight Stainless Steel Backpacking Pot for Solo Stove and Other Backpacking & Camping Stoves
review_body:
I received my stove and pot set just in time for my two-week cross country trek to Yellowstone NP with my son. He is working there this Summer and I wanted to get a simple cookset for his free time. I've used the Solo Stove for well over a year, but was just able to get the Solo Pot as it was not available when I bought the stove.

I love the stove! Not having to carry fuel simplified a lot of what we were doing. Finding a few handfuls of twigs and branches was easy. For just the two of us we no problem first heating water for a hot drink in the morning and then some instant oatmeal. Usually for dinner it was either heating water for pasta sides or instant rice along with a can of tuna or chicken. Occasionally we went and heated a can of chili or soup. Usually each meal was ready in under ten minutes. On a couple of nights we had daylong rain, so we did use a small alcohol stove inside the Solo Stove.

As for the Solo Pot, I really like it. It holds more than my old pot, which has a small skillet as a lid. I found I have never used the skillet part as it is so small and not with the effort. Back to the Solo Pot, I appreciate the measurements stamped into the side which can be read from the inside. Takes a lot of guess work out of the mix. I also like the folding mug style handles. They make it much easier to pour the hot water out. Plus the pour spout was dripless for me. Not true with other pots. The steel is easier to clean off the inevitable soot build up.

All in all, I really like this stove/pot combination. I'm sure my son will get great use of it this Summer. I look forward to his return so I can have it back for the upcoming Fall schedule of scout trips.

product_title: Hydro Flask Stainless Steel Insulated Drinking Bottle, Narrow Mouth
review_headline: These type of flasks don't get any better.  Its great.
review_body: My daughter bought me the first as a gift and I have since bought many more to give away as gifts.  These are truly good insulated containers.  I can keep something cold or hot in them most of the day.  The smooth stainless steel inside does not allow bacteria to build and with a simple wash of water and mid liquid soap the container is clean with no lingering smells.

product_title: Hydro Flask Insulated Wide Mouth Stainless Steel Water Bottle, 32-Ounce
review_headline: Hot or cold this keeps liquid perfect
review_body: Liquids are kept hot or cold for hours. The flask is easy to clean and is the perfect "grande" or medium drink size.

product_title: Continental Gator Hardshell DuraSkin Folding Tire
review_body: These with a German stamp manufacturer have been some of the best buys I have ridden with. In 1500 miles only one glass flat and perfect combination of a tire that wears long, resists flats and is not too heavy. I will buy them not only for training but put a new set on a week before races to get them tuned in and set.

product_title: Petzl Tikka 2 Plus
review_headline: This headlamp has seen the outdoors and the server room.
review_body:
It has served me well. It can be upgraded to accept a programable USB rechargeable battery pack. That extended my love and use for this headlamp, as it made dayly use of it trouble free and nearly cost free also.

It's so simple to use. If you get the battery pack, it takes seconds to convert it back to using AAA batteries, so it's great for emergencies.

It also can recharge off a solar panel with USB power out.

product_title: Survival Magnesium Flint Firesteel Fire Steel Starter by efuture
review_body: I've used this fire steel to light fires in my backyard fire pit. It is easy to use, and seems pretty sturdy. My only complaint is I wish the magnesium rod was a little bigger, so I took 1 start off for that, but I gave it back because it was >$2 with shipping.

review_body: This bed is surprisingly comfortable.  I use it for all my house guests and they love it.  I wish I had purchased the full now.

product_title: Coleman Somerset 8-Person/Man Tent Hinged Door
review_headline: Great Tent but wish the Rainfly Allowed more Airflow
review_body:
I purchased this tent from Amazon and was just able to take it on a 3 day camping trip with me. The tent is very easy to set up and take down and is the typical solid Coleman construction. The tent is super roomy inside and I'm able to stand up fully in it being 5'10" tall. The only complaint I have about it, and hence the 4 stars instead of 5, is that the rainfly is almost too good. It literally covers the entire tent, not really allowing any airflow and it got quite hot inside during the middle of the day. I was camping in California with 70-80 degree weather so in colder climates, this would probably not be a detractor but a positive instead. Also, this is a bulky tent and so should be used accordingly.

Pros:
Decent price
Thick tarp flooring (takes a better beating)
Solid Coleman construction
Plenty of space
Easy setup and take down
Hinged Door is awesome
Rainfly creates a patio in the front perfect for storing gear

Cons:
Rainfly covers entire tent so little to no airflow
Pretty bulky

product_title: Sea to Summit Solution Traveller Soft Racks
review_headline: Sea to Summit Soft Rack for Kayak
review_body:
Great solution to carrying a kayak or two on the roof of your vehicle.
The Good:
*Well made - no chance of deflating like some of the other soft racks available (just my opinion...not based on experience)
*Covered buckle tie straps
*Large rack can hold 2 kayaks
*With adequate tie down straps, through the car rather than attached to the rack itself, I was able to do 70mph without any worry about it coming off the car. Must be very careful to secure it properly however, including bow and stern lines. Highly recommend feeding the tie down through some point in the kayak also. I feed my through the sidewall of the seat for added security. I have one set of tie downs that attach the kayak to the rack and one set that go around & through the kayak and feed through the door jam, which ratchet inside the car. Very secure!
Not so good:
*If it rains, you may leak water in the car where the straps run through. This is not usually excessive but be prepared
*Read instruction on placement of pads and don't over-tighten rack or boat to car or you will see your roof dent (pops right out after you remove the boat however)

Overall, very happy with this rack and would recommend this to anyone no wanting to use a permanent rack system or on a budget. I own a Chrysler 300, ordered the Large rack and I can fit 2 recreational kayaks perfectly!

product_title: Super Lithium 1300 Brushless Electric Scooter "BLUE"
review_headline: This is by far the worst experience I've ever had on Amazon,,
review_body: The shipping time was good, and it arrived with no damage, unfortunately that's where it ends. Puts together fairly easily everything fits where it's supposed to go, it's pretty straight-forward. So,,, after unpacking and putting it together I put it on the charger; took a few hours to charge up, by then it was nighttime. I woke up the next morning and was very excited to get on and ride. I drove about 15 minutes out when out of the blue the motor started to smoke, and then just quit within seconds of noticing the smell of smoke. I had to walk the bike back home, which was NOT easy because the motor was providing resistance. It took me over an hour to walk the bike home. 15 minutes of driving, over one hour of walking. Without using expletives, words cannot tell you how disappointed I was. I talked to the owner on the phone and told him that I had never purchased a product at this price and had it completely fail within the first 15 minutes of owning it. Now,,, I know it's not a Harley-Davidson, and I didn't spend $25,000, it is however expensive enough to last more than 15 minutes. Instead of receiving an apology for the horrific experience, I received a sad story from him about a Nissan that he had to replace an electric window motor three times on it. After listening to his sad story about replacing a window motor after I just walked over an hour to get home, I knew I could not do business with him any longer. An owner that wants to go tit for tat when it comes to disappointing experiences to say the least, is in my opinion no way to run a business. If we were friends just shooting the breeze; fine I would listen to him all day long, but we're not friends, I'm a customer who was expecting an offer to send out a new bike right away. I was not expecting to hear, how do you feel about replacing the motor? After listening to his sad story, which was an attempt in my opinion to get me to fix the bike myself.... There is no way that I was going to replace the motor, itis in my skill set to do so, but after witnessing the motor go up in smoke on a 15 minute drive, I also suspected that there could have been other inferior parts on the bike as well resulting in hidden damage to the scooter. Maybe there was maybe there wasn't. I do know that I could not deal with him if there was hidden damage to the power control unit or even worse, the battery. I wasn't going to listen to another sad story of his to compare to mine. So I returned the unit, and have taken my time to tell anyone who reads this the true events that took place. People should know before they buy what the level of service they're going to receive is. PS,,, there are a lot of first-time comments on these bikes, it's a little more than suspicious. I say suspicious, because I have no proof, only my gut feeling. Good luck, I hope this helps you in your decision making. Thank you for your time,,,,

product_title: 3 Gallon Reusable Water Bottle- BPA free
review_body: We used to get 5 gallon bottles of water for our crock until my husband had an injury.  I looked into switching to 3 gallon jugs, but when I saw that the price was almost as much as for 5 gallons, I balked.  I had ended up getting 1 gallon jugs (one or two at a time)and pouring them into the crock, using a bowl to close the opening.  I had found a source of good, cheap water that I could  only get in the gallon size.  This was more economical, but I had to collect those gallon jugs and return them for the bottle deposit.  I decided to get a reusable bottle, and try refilling it at the water kiosk at the supermarket.  This bottle doesn't fit inside the dispenser (and the shelf where the bottle sits didn't look adjustable).  But by tilting the bottle and using a funnel, I can fill it just fine.  Instead of filling it full, I decided that 2 gallons was a more manageable load to carry.  Two gallons bought this way were the same price as the one gallon size I had previously been buying.  And I don't run out as fast, since whatever doesn't immediately go into the crock sits above the water line in the bottle.

product_title: Ducati Corse 2012 Backpack
review_headline: Awesome Backpack. Can Fit A Lot. Flashy
review_body:
I ride a 2009 Ducati Hypermotard and wanted a backpack that matched. This was perfect and it was surprisingly a lot less money ($70) than the similar Alpinestars backpack ($150) I wanted.

Storage: It can store a lot of items. The main storage is huge and has a smaller zippered pocket for my wallet. There is also a headphone hole on the side. The smaller front storage can fit a lot too. There are also 2 waist/kidney pockets that can be secured together. I usually leave this empty but can easily fit 2 bags of Skittles or 2 energy bars in each pocket. There is a mesh open pocket large enough to fit a liter bottle of water for easy access. This backpack had enough room for a weekend Las Vegas trip. 2 pants, 3 shirts, board shorts, dress shoes, 3 socks, 3 underwear. I easily fit a toothbrush, toothpaste, soap, cologne and other toiletries fit in the 2 kidney pockets.

As for riding my motorcyle, this backpack is secure and doesn't move. I ride canyons and ride on the freeways in So Cal with this often and it doens't shift due to the chest strap and buckle. The kidey strap and buckle also provide a secure fit. I secure the double zipper tabs with a caribiner.

Styling: The Ducati patch is stitched on to the rubber front. The red is highly visible and the small white rubber part is somewhat reflective to that's an added safety feature at night.

Quality: It's a $70 backpack. Obviously it's not heavy duty. But it will last a long time if taken care of. And do not store any sharp items in the bag alone. Put sharp objects like your pens, tools, etc in a plastic cylinder and secure the lid.

Summary: It's worth every penny and people will notice. Let people know you ride a Ducati or just love the brand. It's perfect for anyone who needs a backpack.

product_title: Allen Sports Deluxe 3-Bike Trunk Mount Rack
review_headline: Do NOT buy an Allen Bike Rack - WILL CAUSE DAMAGE to your car!!!
review_body: I purchased an Allen Bike Rack, that carries up to 3 bikes, that is meant for the trunk of a car. I now have $600+ in damage to the body of my car. It worked for over a year, when it was being used for just one bike, with no problem, but as soon as I used two bikes on the rack, I immediately got impression marks from the bumpers that stayed right under neath my license plate. Apparently, even though I was following the directions for the rack, the weight distribution caused by the rack wasn't meant for more than one bike. Then, just a few weeks ago ( I continued using it because at that point the impression marks were made, I figured it couldn't get worse, which was a MISTAKE), when I put 3 bikes on the rack for the very first time, and hit a bump at 40 mph - THE ENTIRE RACK lifted up and scooted across the trunk of my car, leaving further paint and ding damage to my trunk. The body shop says it will cost upwards of $600 to fix all the damage. I contacted Allen about this, and I got NO response to my customer service email. Not even a "sorry for your problem". Just nothing. Don't waste your money on this brand, unless you are looking to be sorry.

review_headline: Built Like a Tank with All the Right Adjustments------------
review_body:
Tough,...Beefy Torch Holder with 3 Handy Adjustments + adj. Cushioning Thicknesses., May 29, 2014
By carefulShopper

Verified Purchase(What's this?)
This review is from: Universal Bike Bicycle LED Light Flashlight Torch Lamp Mount Clamp Stand Holder

I needed a torch holder for my new bike. But after reading all the reviews of the pro's & con's, didn't seem like there was a good one out there. So t tried to rig something up myself to hold my light. The light fell off . So I redoubled my efforts to find a quality torch holder & back to Amazon I went.

I finally settled on this one from `buyinsoon' but I hesitated; there were no product reviews & who wants to be the first?? Couldn't find out what city they were located, maybe on the other side of the world so customer service is probably non-existent. I might get stuck with junk. But since non of the other bike mounting clamp reviews were convincing to me, I studied the pics & limited description hoping it had the flexibility /toughness I was looking for. So I gave it a shot & ordered.

Eventually I found out yes they are in Fujian, China (I try to buy USA) & shipment comes directly from there with a return address and phone number on the shipping label which is good. After ordering I was informed projected arrival date was 6-8 weeks & I was spazzing!

But they had shipped so quickly I could not cancel (which turned out to be good). So when the mount arrived in only 9 days via USPS (free shipping) I was relieved. When the package was a bubble soft pack. There were no instructions in the package, but none are needed.

It was instantly clear this 5.45$ flashlight holder is high quality, strong, beefy, with all the right adjustments. The mounting strap for the handlebar has two removable inner hubs of rubber that grip the handlebar. If your handlebar is larger or smaller than standard simply remove one or both for best fit.

One of the cushion hubs is thin, about 1/16 inch. The thicker cushion hub is about 1/4 inch. So it gives a good combination of thicknesses to fit a wide range of handlebars or even other applications if u want to anchor to something other than a bicycle handlebar. I have a standard bike handlebar so I mounted it as it came right out of the package. This set up provides a very secure grip.

The handlebar clamp is secured by a long black metal bolt (fine thread) with a round knurled flared end that's easy to access, grip and turn. This easy-turn knob lets me dial-in exactly the holding tension I want. It's also handy to twist this knob for adjustment on-the-fly while riding. An easy turn of the knob allows a quick up/down light beam adjustment from the drivers seat then twist to re-clamp. Easy peasy.

At the other end of the knob is an actual shiny metal nut (not plastic) in a recessed cavity so it can't turn when tightening or loosening the bolt. Good design. From what I can tell, the bolt is metal (not plastic) and has fine threads for max holding power. Can't tell if the shiny metal is stainless (probably not) or just polished. But the metal looks refined & not cheap.

You'll want to trial fit your light before clamping everything down because the second (of 3) adjustments is inside the ring that attaches to the handlebar. Underneath the two rubber cushioning rings is a metal screw at the base of the light clamp stem. After setting the best left /right aim of the light beam, tighten that screw then it up & reinsert the cushioning rings. There is a handy hole in the outer ring to allow a screwdriver to be inserted for best torc on the screw. Good engineering.

The third adjustment are the jaws that actually clamp the flashlight barrel,...it's built like a tank! The jaws are thick, well contoured and pretty much as pictured. They easily grip the 7/8 inch barrel of my 700lum light. Both sides of the two jaws are slightly tapered starting at about an inch widening to 1 1/4 inch at its widest.

The jaws are wide and strong with a threaded shiny metal rod & an adjustable flip-over lock down lever. The end of the rod is a \\"T\\" pin, metal hinge going clear through the locking clamp to the outside of each jaw making it the strongest possible.

Sugg not over tightening the flip-over locking lever. It's fully adjustable & beefy so unless you're careless it should last for years. I was impressed with the lockdown jaws, flip locking lever, metal in key places, and the whole design. Nice!

This clamp is great. It is easy to pop the light on/off in a second. The adjustable clamp looks as if it could comfortably accommodate a larger barrel 1.5 inch or even larger. The flexible and beefy design allows me to try out different flashlight barrel sizes and styles of lights.

I did not notice any odd or offensive product oder as some had reported from their mounting clamp. This clamp has the same quality /color as my other bike accessories so it blends right in. I will update again if I have anything significant to add. Best five & a half bucks I ever spent! Highly recommend.

product_title: Klymit Inertia X Frame Ultralight Backpacking Pad
review_headline: Great first impression, but needed to earn my trust
review_body:
Bottom line: Mine failed the second night had it in the field, but the first night exceeded my expectations.

I really like the X-frame concept. It removes a LOT of unnecessary weight, yet provides a good level of comfort. I'm a tarp and bivy kind of guy, and I was excited by the prospect of putting this pad to use. My first night out with it I was very pleasantly surprised by how comfortably I slept. I'm 6'4\\" and it worked just fine for me. Comfortable sleep and it held air all night.

My second night with it was a different story. It wouldn't hold air for more than a couple hours. I have been careful to follow Klymit's instructions and not lock the cap while inflating, so I didn't pop a seam. I also made a point to examine the seams and could find no evidence of failure. While I haven't done a submergence test to verify it, I'm forced to conclude that I'm seeing a valve failure that's giving me a slow leak. It's slow enough that I can't hear a leak from either the oral inflation valve or the inflator's valve, but I'm convinced it's happening.

So, I'm going to be returning this one and asking for a replacement. I'll post an update after taking it out a few times.

UPDATE: My second night experience seems to have been due to some sort of debris in the oral inflation valve. I called Klymit customer service (good experience, FWIW) and have an RMA all ready to go. Having several days between receiving the RMA and being able to get out and ship my pad back, I decided to do some testing. I've pumped it up three nights after work and checked it the next day when I got home. It's held pressure for 24 hours each time. I've got a motorcycle camping trip coming up and can carry both the Recon and my old Thermarest pretty easily, so I'm going to give the Recon a second chance before making the decision to send it back.

2ND UPDATE: I'll be keeping mine. I spent four nights at a motorcycle rally using a fixed location as a base camp. I pumped up my pad once and it held air until I deflated it to head home with absolutely no issues.e camp. review_headline: Entry level road bike for the casual rider, student...
review_body: Entry level road bike. I got this bike to run errands, casual riding. I didn't want to ride my Bianchi road bike for short trips to the store. I knew what I was getting, an inexpensive ride. This bike is not for someone who wants a performance or high fitness ride. But one certainly can burn some calories on it. The Denali comes well packed. It is relatively easy to assemble. Comes with an excellent manual. I would recommend a bike shop put it together for you if your not handy. If you do build it yourself, a second person would be helpful, but is not necessary. I took pictures of it packed, in case I wanted to return it, repacking is not easy. Keep all packing material. Take your time building it, took me about an hour or so. It is important to fit it correctly and make all the brake and shifter adjustments. I put 50 lbs pressure in the tires for a smooth ride, they take 85 lbs. Don't over tighten the nuts or screws. A bike shop will build it or set it up for you. Call around to find one if you don't know how. WD-40 for chain and moving parts, etc. Good quality, rides smooth and nice. Great for tooling around, errands or on the campus. I added toe clips, and a cyclometer. You will need a spare tube, plastic tire removal tools (do not use a screw driver to remove tires), and a frame mounted pump. Carry a small adjustable wrench to change a flat. Put all that in a seat pack. It takes awhile to brake in a new bike. Adjustments are common on all new bikes. Brakes are good, shifts well, rides stable. I have a high end bike for long rides. I got this bike for whatever else. One thing I like to do is go to events, concerts or the stadium and will throw this in my jeep. I'll park a ways off and ride in and save on parking. Great for a bike to keep at work and ride to lunch. If you want a performance bike, be prepared to pay 1K or more. If your on a budget, and want performance, check out the Kent International 700C Mens GMC Denali Pro bike. All in all, I'm very happy with my purchase. Update, I've put 1800 miles on this bike as of 5/16/2016. Added a bottom bracket cartridge, derailleur, brake pads and tow clips. Still very happy.my purchase. product_title: Axiom Journey Tubular Alloy Rack (Black)
review_headline: Caution for adding to steel frame bikes; dinky reflector mount
review_body:
As everyone else says, it's super sturdy yet light weight. The extra, looping rear bars (which the Topeak, Planet Bike, and Blackburn racks lack) keep nonrigid panniers and saddle bags from swinging into my rear wheel spokes. I've carried high and low loads exceeding 50 pounds on this rack with no drama whatsoever. So no complaints about its performance or design, except...

1.) The strong, adjustable bars that connect the rack to the upper seatstays have to be bent if your bike has a short rear end/chainstays, and they are quite difficult to bend evenly.
2.) The reflector mount, in contrast to rest of this burly rack, is a dinky afterthought that will take ordinary reflectors--but most screw-on taillights use a different mounting system that doesn't work with this. The only exception I've found is the Serfas Stop Sign Taillight which you can also find on Amazon.

If you intend to mount this, or any other aluminum accessory, to a steel frame then be aware that there could be accelerated rusting (oxidation) wherever the aluminum touches steel. This is due to the electrochemical properties of steel and aluminum. My solution has been to install galvanized steel washers between the aluminum rack mount points and the screw holes on my bike frame. That way the washers, rather than the frame, will take the contact oxidation and can be easily replaced.

review_headline: Boils like a champ, makes fire starting a breeze.
review_body:
First thing first, this is only first impression and not a full review. We used this kettle only once in the field, so there is no way I can review its longevity or ease of use in a less friendly weather/environment. However for the first use it performed incredibly well, and if the seams hold up, I don't see any reason why it would disappoint in the future.

Ok, first and the only negative thing about this thing is that its relatively bulky compared to small camping stoves, however...

You are carrying a great water container, that can be used to get and carry water to the camp.
You are carrying a stove to cook on and a pot to cook in. Turns into a small grill once you boiled the water and got some coals in the base.

Gets the fire going really fast. I haven't tried it on damp materials yet, but we had some greener firewood last time camping, which sometimes is a pain to get going, but this thing roared and got those sticks nice and hot in seconds. I see no problem using this to actually get a fire going inside with marginal (wet) wood, and then once its nice and aflame, transfer it to the main camp fire to start that.

Boils water in record time!

This is the medium size, which turned out to be a perfect size for two people. It boiled water by the time the fire dried out the sticks and finally combusted the smoke and roared in the chimney. Blowing into the hole in the base really angers the fire and the sound is incredible!

We haven't tried the cook set yet, just boiled water for some tea, so can not comment on that. Pot seems to be ok, but I doubt the lid will be very useful as a skillet.

Really smart design. I'm sure it will prove itself to be useful time after time and compensate for its bulkiness.

product_title: Coleman WeatherMaster 6-Person Screened Tent
review_body:
I bought this tent last summer (2013) after my old and beloved Ozark Trail 4 person dome tent leaked on my girlfriend and I during a trip into the Missouri Ozarks. I needed something that was big enough to keep all of our stuff and the both of us dry. I also have wanted a screened porch because I've always thought they were kind of cool. We took it to Wisconsin for a three day camp and it made it through a good sized storm with no leaks, and it went through another, larger storm about three weeks ago in north western Missouri.

I bought a 10x6 outdoor carpet to put in the screened porch area, as that doesn't have a floor. There's enough room for a couple of camp chairs and that's about it, although you can use the front room area to extend the porch. Chairs, coolers, and a table with a camp stove will fit just fine if you do that.

Pros- enough size to keep my girlfriend, our dog, and me dry and comfortable. It can fit at most 8 people but that's pretty good for keeping that many people out of the rain. Windows are wide (although the rear window could be a bit bigger for hot summer nights). The side hinged door is genius. Don't need to zip it up to keep out the bugs, as it closes nicely against the tent.

Cons- It's pretty heavy. I ended up buying a big plastic case to haul it in, as the zipper on the case it comes in split on me. I can set it up by myself, but it really takes two people to do it quickly.

It's a really neat tent, great for car camping. I wish I could take it on overnight float trips, but it's too big and unwieldy to set up and take down every night. Coleman really did a great job with this tent.

product_title: Mountain House Just In Case...Breakfast Bucket
review_headline: It's OK, just be aware of limitations.
review_body:
First, this was delivered to me via UPS and dropped at my doorstep. A little while later a severe thunderstorm hit my area and drenched...DRENCHED...the package Although the box was so wet that lots of water made it inside, the bucket protected the contents, so if you're looking for something that will stand up to a downpour, well, this seems to do it.

Now then, this is a product that's useful for lots of people. Whether you're a camper, hiker, or just plain want to have some emergency "just in case" food available, this isn't a bad choice. Indeed, shelf life is outrageously long. The ad copy suggests 30 years and the science behind that claim seems sound to me...it's freeze dried, so no moisture, and the packs are sealed quite well so no air.

So no, I don't have an issue with shelf life (the manufacture date of the bucket sent to me was Jan 2013). My issue is with the product itself, and one should be aware of the limitations of this product so one isn't frustrated with it when you actually have an emergency.

See, you're buying this to either tide you over until you can get fresh supplies (aka an emergency) or you're using this when you're away from Normal and are hiking or camping. In either event, I think it's safe to assume you're pretty active...you're moving around, you're looking for shelter or whatever, you're hiking, camping, recreating, all of that. The problem with the product is twofold: it advertises 29 servings but you're two servings per pouch, and each of those servings has very low calories.

Take an example: The scrambled eggs with ham. The bucket includes four pouches, but each of those pouches is two servings. Each serving is 2/3 cup (prepared) and you get 190 calories out of it. Now if you're out being active, that 190 calories is NOT going to hold you. Even if you ate the full pouch (380 calories) you're not going to last.

Keep in mind the main rule of thumb for hiking... your weight should NOT fluctuate more than one or two pounds while you're out. If you are losing weight while you're hiking (without meaning to, that is), you have to reevaluate your nutrition strategy because you aren't eating enough!

-----

EDITED TO ADD: I read some other reviews mentioning the calorie thing and there was some discussion about these meals being intended for 'survival,' eg holding you over until you get rescued, so calorie intake isn't intended to support active people. I had to call my doctor for an unrelated issue today and I decided to ask him about some of this. First I asked what a "normal" calorie intake would be if you were looking to maintain weight. He said it's dependent on a lot of factors...if you're active you require more calories than if you're sedentary, younger people tend to need more calories than older people, men tend to need more than women, and so on. However, a good midrange for weight maintenance for sedentary people is around 2500-2800 calories per day. That's if you're sitting around doing nothing. For me at a moderate level of activity he says weight maintenance is going to be closer to 3,500 calories per day. I therefore think these meals fall short of providing you a "normal" caloric intake.

I then asked about weight loss. He says for overweight/obese people, weight loss is obviously ideal but it has to be done properly. You run the risk of doing damage if you are on crash diets or "The Biggest Loser"-style things. The best thing to do is lose weight gradually via eating nutritious, well balanced meals and exercising regularly, but not overdoing either one. He says weight loss that stems from "surviving" on these meals has the potential to create problems.

Lastly I asked about the sodium. He says the guidelines exist to ensure you receive ENOUGH salt in your diet...your cells simply won't function properly without salt. In other words, it isn't a ceiling but a floor. In normal humans who have functioning kidneys and are well-hydrated, excess salt just get flushed out of the body. For that reason he's not ipso facto weirded out by the salt content, assuming we're talking about an otherwise healthy person who is getting enough water.

My takeaway...this product can fill a role in an emergency kit or other use, but it would be a mistake to rely on them as one's sole source of nutrition. The salt thing isn't that big of a deal assuming you're healthy and you're well-hydrated. In other words, don't just buy a bucket or two and think you're set...you won't be.

---------

That said, the Breakfast Skillet pouch comes fairly close, at 400 calories per serving, but even at that you have to keep something in mind...these are 2 serving pouches, so you're either sharing with someone OR you're eating the entire pouch yourself...saving it for later isn't a viable option, especially on the trail since the entire pouch is prepared all at once and carrying delicious-smelling food in your pack for later means your pack smells like Breakfast and, well, bears. This means the packaging won't let you stretch this out 29 days if you're single...you get two weeks.

Now that I've got the critical stuff out of the way, and assuming you're OK with all of that...it's a decent product. You aren't going to mistake it for Sunday brunch at The Ritz, but then it's not the worst tasting food either. As another reviewer said, it's amazing how The Trail turns food into a delicious meal.

So my recommendation - it's a good product, but you're likely going to want to buy twice as much as you think you'll need...the servings number is wildly understated in my opinion. It's a little bulky for backpacking but the storage life supports a "stow it away until you hopefully never need it" emergency food strategy. product_title: Kelty Coyote 80 Internal Frame Backpack
review_headline: Little heavy but lots of room
review_body:
I grabbed this at REI on clearance 50% off and additionally marked down because it was a returned item missing some pieces. For $80 you can't beat that deal but not sure I would pay full price for it if I had more gear to tie down (see con). It's a little heavier than packs in its price range or $50 more but it is made pretty sturdy. It isn't cheap/thin fabric.

That being said, I've used this pack on three 30+ mile trips over 2-5 days each. Fully loaded at 55 lbs (without water added in) on my 3 day trip in the Grand Canyon this bag performed very well. I had no hot-spots from it rubbing me and I had no sore areas from it being too tight/loose or just not fitting well. You can adjust the height of the back, the placement of the shoulder straps, the placement of the cross-chest strap, and the waist strap. After some custom adjustments before using my first time I was able to take nearly all the weight off my shoulders and place it on my waist. So much more comfortable on long day/multiday hikes. Make sure you do this at home, preferably with someone to help you. Load it down with all your gear and then some extra. When you find a good spot, move around a lot or have your helper shift the weight a bunch to simulate you sitting or tilting sideways (more than standing straight up). After this, re-fit it again. After this mine was a perfect fit. Haven't changed it since other than the quick straps on the shoulders/waist/cross-chest when I take it off/put it on.

There are numerous tie-downs which help keep your insides from shifting which is a plus. Nothing worse than having to take your pack off because your heavy items moved from the middle all the way to one side.

My biggest con for this pack other than it's slightly heavier weight, is the lack of external tie-downs for items like a sleeping bag/pad, or whatever. Many other day/overnight packs offer 2-5 sets of tie-downs and this offers 0. You do have a few loops in thecenter strap down the back but it doesn't work well to keep larger items from spinning or flopping around. Thankfully the top pouch has adjustable straps and I can loosen them enough to put my sleeping bag and pad in there and tie it down with the top-pouch over it.

product_title: G704-G Green Handle Folding Knife Camping Knife Hunting Knife EDC Pocket Knife w/G10 Handle
review_headline: Great Knife, Just Doesn't Cut Anything.
review_body:
I saw a lot of good reviews on this knife on Amazon and UTube so I decided to check it out. It was only $20 and I wanted to check out an Axis lock. There is a whole lot about this knife that is very nice considering it is a $20 Chinese copy of an expensive Benchmade knife. It took about 4 weeks to get delivered from China.

The handle scales are G10 and are quite nice, I would say a little less than medium traction and I like the texturing pattern. I got the OD Green color and I like it a lot. The Desert Tan one looks very nice as well. The handle is also comfortable with no hot spots or sharp edges.

The pocket clip is good. It is black and not big or funky and it has about perfect retention. It can be moved for left or right handed tip up carry only. Overall it feels very solid.

One small negative of the knife is that it is quite heavy. This is because the blade is extremely thick for a folding knife of this size. The stainless steel liners are pretty thick as well and are not skeletonized at all. I tried to drill out some holes in the liners to lighten it up a bit but the steel was very hard to drill through and I gave up after the first hole.

I mainly took the knife apart to work on the Axis lock on the knife. Out of the box it was quite stiff and rough. I took everything apart, the problem was that the guide cutouts in the liners for the lock were rough and unpolished. I took some emery paper wrapped around a small screwdriver and polished up the cutouts down to a smooth surface as well as cleaned up and oiled the blade pivot point and now the knife opens and closes and the Axis lock works silky smooth. I did about 20 minutes of work on the knife to get it this smooth.

The blade shape is very sharp looking and overall the knife looks great. The thumb studs are nice and easy to access, they work very well. The blade bushings are plastic.

As I said at the beginning, there is a lot about this knife that is extremely nice for the $20 price tag. Where this knife falls down is the blade steel. They claim it is 440C steel. Maybe it is, but if so then they heat treated it with a BIC lighter. It was not very sharp out of box so I sharpened it up on a ceramic rod. It cut paper nice for the first 3 cuts and then it started tearing the paper. I pulled out the Lansky sharpener and put a crazy edge on it. It made 7 or 8 nice cuts in paper and then started tearing the paper. How 8 paper slices could dull a blade that much is beyond me. It is a shame too because other than this the knife is awesome for a $20 knife. I played around with it a few times and can get it very sharp but it dulls instantly.

Bottom line, for $20 to $25 there are a ton of excellent knives from Kershaw, Byrd (Spyderco brand), CRKT and others that are sure things as far as quality goes. Only real complaint is the snow cuff is not very tight. It does not cinch over boots; I eventually began tucking it INSIDE of my boots to wear the pants in extended outdoor activities.

product_title: Zulu Highperformance Glass Water Bottle
review_body:
I have purchased so many items on Amazon, yet have reviewed very few. I felt compelled since it seems like a struggle to find the perfect water bottle and a glass one at that!!!!

First, I must say that I purchased this bottle on sale yesterday from a local retailer for less than $15.

The first thing I noticed today when testing this bottle out was that it did have an awful plastic taste seemingly from the lid as other reviewers have stated. This may fade over more washes, but only time will tell. I am a big fan of flip top lids and they can be difficult to find, especially on a glass bottle. This one seems very sturdy, however it does make a pretty loud pop noise when opened. Not a deal breaker for me. However, I did have an issue with the carrying cord getting stuck in the the lid when closing the lid this morning. I didn't realize it until I went to take a drink and the lid was stuck. It could have been the way I re-looped the cord after the bottle went through the dishwasher.

I washed the bottle last night in the dishwasher on the bottom rack since it is rather tall. Also, I normally wash glass and silicone bake-ware on the bottom rack. After using the bottle for a while this morning, I noticed that all the grid lines on the bottle were peeling off the bottle. This may be due to my washing the bottle on the bottom rack, but I am also skeptical of the long term durability even if the bottle was washed on the top rack. I am also guessing that the grid line decorations are plastic.

I also purchased a Lifefactory bottle yesterday. While I haven't washed it or tested it out yet (I was more excited about the Zulu flip top), I did check over a few points this morning after having the issues with the Zulu:
Lifefactory: Dishwasher safe - No restrictions listed on the silicone sleeve that limit washing to the top rack.
Zulu: Top rack dishwasher safe.
Lifefactory: Bottle: Made in France, Cap: Made in Poland, Sleeve: Made in the U.S. 100% silicone, Assembled in the U.S.
Zulu: Sleeve: Made in China, does not state that it is 100% silicone.

I am planning on returning the Zulu bottle that I purchased.

Hope this review helps you decide!

product_title: SE Lensatic Compass
review_headline: Fun $5 Toy For Kids, Not For Serious Navigation Use
review_body:
This is a good looking, fun toy for kids or a young teenager's first compass. If you are 8 to about 13, this looks COOL.

Made In China. It's a plastic copy of a serious Cammenga type military compass that costs $45 to $85. But it's only a copy, and many of the features don't actually work. It won't glow in the dark, the lens doesn't magnify, and it may or may not even point North reliably.

As a compass, it's about the same quality as the $1 dollar store or flea market dime-sized compasses that slip on a wristband or keychain. It's better than nothing, but not accurate to within 10 or even 20 degrees. And some don't work at all.

So get this as a cool toy for a kid, but don't get this thinking you can depend on it to navigate around in the woods or on a boat. It's just a toy. You wouldn't take a plastic toy gun out deer hunting, either.

And don't overpay. But for $5, and guaranteed free return shipping if you don't like it, you could have some fun.

product_title: Sigma Sport BC16.12 16 Function Bicycle Computer
review_headline: It is actually a quite complicated little device. The Enigma of the Sigma
review_body:
It is actually a quite complicated little device, in terms of, user friendliness. There is a learning curve. It does require that you sit down and dedicate time to learn how to use this. Pencil and paper. There are a few zigzags in the note taking. But, once you see it then you will say, \\"Ah, ok I can manage using this now.\\" But, simply trying to figure it out on your own on the fly without studying the available information and instructions I don't recommend.

Modification 1:
As it pertains to working in conjunction with the Docking Station...
Obviously requires drivers that do not automatically download nor can be found at the manufacturer's website nor can be found by Google search. I know the Europeans and they may not be all too impressed with Americans...perhaps this is why all of the mental gymnastics for this bike computer. Between trying to decipher the operating instructions for the computer itself to the Data Center to the drivers for the Docking Station...either one huge learning curve or a prank joke on Americans. It is instructed that if the drivers do not automatically download to install them manually...

So what was that manual solution? Usually a manual solution for installing drivers means going to the manufacturer's website and clicking download or finding the drivers on the CD for the Data Center neither of these seems to be an option as I have combed the manufacturer's website. Though I haven't bothered to check the file for the CD for the Data Center. I am no stranger to Computer Coding, though not a Rock Star at it, but this does not seem very user friendly, even for me.

Modification 2:
I finally got it to work this particular Docking Station does not work with the Sigma BC 16.12 through the 2.1 DataCenter. However, once I figured out how to register online...and literally, I felt like the process was made to make me feel like I was in an episode of being Punked or Pranked...then the Download for the DataCenter 3.0 was made available. Upon downloading that I reconnected the Docking Station to my computer's USB Port and attached the Bike Computer to it. The drivers for the Docking Station/Bike Computer were engaged, finally. The data, then was able to be imported to the DataCenter...but, again only the DataCenter 3.0 version will recognize Sigma BC 16.12. I am now able to chart my stats.the DataCenter 3.0 was made available. Upon downloading that I reconnected the Docking Station to my computer's USB Port and attached the Bike Computer to it. The drivers for the Docking Station/Bike Computer were engaged, finally. The data, then was able to be imported to the DataCenter...but, again only the DataCenter 3.0 version will recognize Sigma BC 16.12. I am now able to chart my stats.

product_title: RAD Sportz Kayak Hoist Quality Garage Storage Canoe Lift with 125 lb Capacity Even Works as Ladder Lift Premium Quality
review_body:
First, the main reason I got this system are the pulleys. They are good. The pulley blocks are made of very thick metal and are super strong. They also have strong screws for mounting to the joists. I shopped around and found nothing better.

Knowing other reviews about buckles failing and ropes fraying, I went straight to the local hardware store and got some good quality nylon rope. Get braided rope for pulleys, not twisted. Braided wont stretch and will roll in the pulleys better. With the rope that came with the product I used it as a safety harness for the buckles in case they fail, though I don't honesty think they will if they are properly latched. Anyhow, I have kids and don't want to take any chances, so in addition to the straps the added a rope safety harness for each strap gives me piece of mind. There is no way the Kayak is coming down.

Last mod I did was in tying the rope. Per instructions, you tie the end of the rope to the shaft of a bolt inside the pulley block on the ceiling. I was concerned that the knife edges of the bolt thread would, in time, cut through the rope, so after the bolt was in place, I wrapped it several times with electrical tape before tying off the rope to it.

So with the added safety of the rope harness and upgraded rope. This is a great system. I give it 5 stars, because you just cant by this quality a pulley that mounts to the ceiling as nicely anywhere else.

Last word, the rope locking mechanism works, though as another reviewer pointed out, it is bit tricky to operate. But your'll figure it out. You must only operate one rope at a time when lowing, holding the other rope steady to stop the locking mechanism from engaging. Consider wearing gloves when letting down and wrap one rope around each hand so you can operate both ropes independently. You are going to have to be reasonably strong to do this depending on the weight of your kayak btw. The pulleys give a mechanical advantage of2:1, so if you have a 80lb fully rigged tandam Kayak as I do, you are handling 20lbs with each hand.
