product_title: Seattle Sports E-Merse Clear Dry Audio Case, Patterned Black
review_body:
I found this locally while looking around for a case for an upcoming kayaking excursion. The only real criteria included being a good fit for my large Samsung Galaxy S4 and preferably clear so I could take photos. That this one had an audio pass-through was frosting on the cake! Although I had to remove my phone from my wonderful Trident case (look for that review here), the phone fit fine in the dry bag naked. It's not easy to get it in, mind you. First you need to connect the 1/8" plug, then somehow get the plastic sides of the bag to not stick to the phone while dropping it in. This requires a shaking technique that looks pretty silly. I had tried it at home the night before kayaking, so I knew what I was in for. I removed a star in my review for this, but will update it if the phone goes in and out more smoothly in future. Anyway if you have an S4 or similarly-sized phone, you'll need to put the phone in upside down. I'm pretty sure the audio cable is too short to reach the top of the phone if you don't invert it. Even if it was long enough, how would you connect it after the phone is already in the case? Anyway, inverted works well: you can wear the cord around your neck and simply flip the phone up for use.

How was the trip, you wonder? It was great! 2 1/2 hours spent between canals and an open bay, and I was able to snap many pictures (anytime the wind wasn't pulling my kayak off course). I went out with friends, so I didn't utilize the earphones jack, though in testing it worked great for music and calls. The downside of the audio cable is that it shifted inside the dry bag due to my paddling and the wind, putting the cable near the camera lens and shading one corner of my later photos. I didn't notice while I was out, as I couldn't see my phone very well due to bright sun, sunglasses and water everywhere. The heavy winds were sending salt water all over the place. When I was paddling through the shaded canals, I could see the screen just fine, as if it wasn't in the dry bag. The water also made my touchscreen difficult to use, again not a fault of the dry bag.

The reason I got this is I had gone on a trip for my birthday a few weeks back and had to leave my phone in the car. I have a sordid past with cell phones and water (look at my other reviews for details), so I'd rather play it safe without a dry bag. Anyway, on that trip we saw gorgeous views of land, water, sky and nature but have zero pictures to document it. I'm glad I have this dry bag now, so I can use my phone when I really want to.

There are a features on the packaging I don't see in the ad copy:
-submersible to 10 feet
-use device through case
-secure slide bar seal
-cold weather compatible
-breakaway lanyard
-eco-friendly construction

Specs: Internal dimensions of 7" x 3.25"
Perfect size for: Samsung S4, HTC One, Phablets & most other smartphone models
There's also a link to a video: YouTube.com/SeattleSportsCoTV

Speaking to the other review, I can't imagine any iPhone would have trouble fitting in this case.

Buy it on Amazon - I paid more locally, since I sought it out only 12 hours before my trip.

product_title: Trek Tents 218 Polyester Taffeta 6 Person Family Dome 10' x 10' Tent
review_body:
First, the good news:

1) Set up: It was very easy to figure out how to set this tent up and, with two people, it can be set up and taken down quite quickly (in theory it could also be set up by one person, but it's big enough that this would be tough to do if there's any wind at all).

2) Ventilation, ability to look out: It has large windows on all four sides and a large screened section (4-5 feet by 4-5 feet) in the top of the ceiling). On nights when you are pretty confident it won't rain, you could leave off the fly and be able to look up and out of this tent really well, while still being protected from mosquitoes. This is a big plus for me.

3) Packing: It's light and compact for it's size when set up.

4) Cost: The cost is quite reasonable for a tent of this size.

Now, the bad news:

1) Protection from rain: The rain fly the tent came with is not even remotely water-proof. Because the top of the actual tent itself is mesh, that means that even a light rain will come right through the rain fly, through the mesh at the top of the tent and onto your stuff. I think there may also have been a little bit of leakage around the seams between the floor and walls of the tent and/or along the seams between walls (near the bottom) on one or two out of the six nights it rained, but this didn't seem to be too bad.

A couple of more minor issues:

1) Window zippers: The way the zippers work, it is not possible to have the window coverings adjusted so that just the tops of the windows are open. You either have to have the window covering completely closed (which makes the tent stuffy, even with the large ventilation area in the top of the tent), or you have to have it open at the bottom on at least one side, which is a problem if it's raining.

2) Instructions: The instructions said that one of the pair of tent poles (or was it one of the pair of fly poles?) is longer than the other.This is incorrect. They are both the same length and work fine that way.

Overall: The fact that this tent is not water-proof is a big deal, but I actually still have a lot of hope for it. I'm going to treat the fly and the seams along the floor and partway up the walls of the tent to try to make it waterproof. I may also try to add another slide to each zipper, so that the window coverings can be partially shut in such a way that only the top of each window is uncovered. If this tent can be made waterproof with a reasonable amount of effort and extra expense, it's positive attributes (4 large windows and a large mesh area at top of tent, ease of set up) will make it a terrific tent for the price.

review_body: I looked at a number of other kits before I ordered this one.  It came to me as pictured and included instructions, which were adequate for making the bracelets.  I would add to the instructions: don't over-tighten the weave or the final product will be too stiff and will distort.  Also, I found it helpful to build a simple loom to hold the two ends in place while weaving the paracord.  And, finally, don't cut the ends off until you make sure the bracelet fits the wrist for which is was intended and that the weave is just right and not distorted.  If you don't cut them until you get it right, you can go back and re-do it as needed.  I thoroughly enjoyed making these and I like wearing them.  They look good and are a very practical addition to the other wearable survival gear that is part of my everyday carry array.

product_title: WeeRide Co-Pilot Bike Trailer
review_body:
Some points:
1) this bike is ridiculously heavy to the point I would be afraid to go a steep hill. And going up hill you would probably blow out a knee.
2) the cranks are humongous. My five year old (70 percentile height and weight) can barely do the pedal rotation. These cranks are really for older kids or adults. My daughter also has a 16 inch trek and when compared to this bike the cranks are almost half the length of this bike.
3) the four bolts that come with the clamp to attach to seatpost don't reassure me. why not throw in some safety nuts or a redundant plastic strap in case of bolt failure.
4)If you have aluminum or any non steel seat post I would not attach this bike to it. The shearing force produced by the weight of bike and rider on the seatpost can be significant and could lead to catastrophic failure.

To sum things up, I got bike on a Monday and listed it on craigslist on Wednesday. After assembling bike I didn't want to disassemble and repackage to send back to amazon. just not worth the time and effort for me.

product_title: Primus Micron Lantern
review_body: By myself, I've always been perfectly content with my headlamp. I bought this thinking it'd be a cool toy for plush backpacking trips with my girlfriend/non-hiker friends. After all, the weight penalty is negligible if I'm already carrying a canister. After using it just a few times, however, I am reluctant to leave it behind even on my solo trips.  It creates a lot of natural looking, ambient light.  Its a strangely comforting effect, whether I'm setting up/tearing down a tent, eating dinner, getting ready for bed, or packing up before dawn. Much preferred to the blue, shadow-less spot light from a headlamp.  One thing that would be kind of nifty would be a way to adjust the length of wire/cable/thing, so you could adjust the height that it hangs down when suspended.  Also, to keep the cable from getting as hot, it seems like a non-metallic spacer could be added, but I'm not sure if that would help, and it would certainly add weight. The lantern itself does get very hot. Like, it glows red for a few seconds after you turn it off.  Also, down below 15-20 degrees it kinda craps out. It sputters and shoots flames out the top and whatnot, but that's kind of inherent in the design. Perhaps a generator tube could added like on cold weather stoves... that would be  pretty cool.  *Dropped from 5 stars to 4. After about a year (probably a dozen backpacking trips) the piezo igniter stopped working. It was difficult to light with a lighter or matches until I removed the igniter entirely. This left a space large enough to allow the flame of a lighter to reach the globe.

product_title: Minus33 Merino Wool Men's Acadian Lightweight Boxer Brief
review_headline: Not bad, but did not fit right on me
review_body:
Being deployed to Afghanistan, I was looking to an alternative to the UnderArmor boxer briefs due to the "high melt factor", should I be inadverdently exposed to an explosion or a fire. After doing some research, I discovered that wool underwear is moisture-wicking and somewhat fire resistant. After viewing and reading the reviews of the various brands offered on Amazon, I decided to try the Minus33 boxer briefs. I ended up trying two different sizes, large and extra-large. All of the rest of my underwear is sized large, in variuos brands. The Minus33 large is somewhat tight in the waist, but fit acceptably almost everywhere else. I returned them for an XL, which fit well in the waist, but it felt like there was excess material in the legs which caused them to bunch up.

The other issue that I had was that my "junk" would randomly fall out of the fly. I am Joe Average White Guy, so it is not like I can use my junk as a tripod leg for support or anything like that. However, with both the LG and XL briefs, it felt almost like there was not enough material for the fly to fully close, so the material in the fly would move around and gap open.

I would probably consider buying these again if:

1) the waist on the LG was about 2 inches larger or the material in the legs on the XL was slightly reduced, and
2) there was more material added to the fly, or the fly was eliminated altogether. (seriously, why do men's underwear even HAVE flys? In 33 years of wearing underwear, I have never actually used one, and all of my male coworkers say pretty much the same thing)

product_title: Yepp - GMG Maxi Bicycle Child Seat
review_headline: Great Seat - Some details caught me off guard...
review_body:
UPDATED 7/7/14 to correct model name.

This seat is fantastic. It may or may not be better than other less-expensive seats (this is the only unit I've tested) but it totally meets and exceeds expectations. That stated, there are a few things I've learned in the past month of use that will inform future decisions on carrying children on bikes.

Some Background: One child, 9 months old (at time of review), 19 lbs and 28.5 inches long. Prior to family life I was regularly bicycling 5,000 miles per year, almost entirely commuting to work. This seat is mounted to a Surly Long Haul Trucker (a touring bike), size 56cm with a 73 degree seat tube angle. That probably won't mean much to most readers and that's ok, but for the bike nerds it may provide some reference.

Rear weight bias: The biggest surprise to me with this seat is how much it shifted the weight of the bike to the rear. When dismounted, the bicycle is very rear-heavy (with baby in seat) and it doesn't take much effort to lift the front wheel. When riding there is no problem - i've tried to wheelie or otherwise unload the front wheel enough to test the limits and can't - which is good. No issues on inclines. In fact the overall ride of the bike isn't that much different at speed; stopping and starting take a little more coordination and that's where the weight comes into play most. But back to the rear-bias - I'm just a little bit curious what will happen when my son gets older & heavier. This issue probably isn't unique to this seat, and honestly it shouldn't scare anyone away from a purchase. Just something to be aware of.

Front-to-Back Seat Leveling: The adapter (included) which mounts to the seat post can be adjusted slightly to ensure that the seat is level front-to-back. Some reviewers have noted that on some bikes there it's not adjustable enough. I want to confirm that the degree of adjustability is limited, and with the 73 degree seat tube on my bike the seat is close to level, but not completely. the base is slightly higher in the rear than front. For me, it's close enough though.

No helmet interference for smaller children: I was concerned that the high seat back would interfere with my son's helmet and force his head forward and down. At his height his head is still largely below the top of the seat back. I've found that this is not an issue however.

Tail lights: If you are accustomed to a seat-post light facing the rear, you may need to find a new location to mount your light. It would've been nice if this seat was designed with some kind of light bracket mount (it has all kinds of reflectors already), but i've found it's easy to clip a light that has a belt-clip type of attachment (PlanetBike Super Flash, for example) to the seat back just below the hand hold. It feels secure and works.

Rear Panniers on a rack: If you have a rear rack and are used to mounting a pannier to it you might have trouble with clearance. the integrated skirt on the seat that works well to keep your kid's legs out of the wheel spokes takes up lots of lateral real estate along my rack, and I've found it difficult (but not impossible) to continue to use a rear pannier. Not a deal breaker, but it caught me by surprise. I may end up moving towards regularly using front panniers, but that's a lot less convenient.

Longbike / Xtracycle notes: (UPDATED 6/30/14) I've recently installed an Xtracycle FreeRadical on this bike. This product works fine with the Xtracycle meaning that it fits over the flight deck without issue. I want to point out however that it still has to attach to the seat post - that won't change. There isn't an adapter that will allow the seat to attach to the top of the flight deck; if that's what you want you'll need to purchase the Yepp Maxi Easyfit seat. The good thing with this setup is that the seat/baby weight doesn't count towards the 200# weight limit onthe FreeRadical (honestly though, 200# out back plus another 50# seat/kid plus my own weight is really pushing things, so this may be a moot point). The main drawback in utility for me is that because the Yepp is mounted to the seatpost it takes up space just above the front of the flight deck - this is the part of the deck that can carry the most weight and where you'd put an adult if you wanted to carry both a baby and an adult on the Xtracycle. The long stays (behind the rear axle) are only rated to 50 lbs will bend under the weight of an adult. If you want to do something like this, get the Easyfit and mount it at the rear of the flight deck so you can carry an adult towards the front.

Overall I'm very pleased. I poured the purified water into the OKO and then ran it through the filter. It raised the ppm from 13 to 364. The maximum TDS for tap water is 500.

When I contacted OKO and told them this, this was their reply:

"Thanks for your email.

Our bottles a re used for filtration of cysts, bacteria and some viruses form mostly open water
sources, but also tap water. They are not used as a purification system which generally improves
condition of safe water."

So if you're looking to "purify" your tap water, look elsewhere.

product_title: Thule Sonic Cargo Box
review_headline: Great added space and looks good on my car!
review_body:
Turned 40 and just couldn't handle the mini-van mom persona anymore......traded for a Highlander, but lost all our space!!!! We bought the Thule Sonic L a couple of weeks ago for a trip to the beach and was amazed at how much it could hold! We piled 3 duffles and a suitcase in there and stuffed the 'holes' with jackets. Many reviews question whether this cargo box is waterproof....the Oregon/Washington coast proved them wrong! Our stuff stayed dry through monsoon-like conditions.

The box was easy to install, no tools required and fit onto our factory racks and crossbars perfectly. If I had a complaint, it would be that it does encroach on our moonroof just a bit, and when open, there is added wind noise. Not a problem though, it is so easy to install and remove, we can store for the warmer months and when we are not traveling with a bunch of stuff or dog in tow.

Another plus, the locking mechanism. The lock won't let you remove the key unless fully secured. It can be a little challenging if stuffed full and the locks are pressed by luggage, but once you get the hang of it, no prob! We looked at the competition, the key turns in a key hole leaving the key vulnerable for bending or snapping. The Thule locking system engages the entire locking mechanism. If the key won't turn, it cannot be forced-you have to align the locking points.

People say it is flimsier than expected.... I agree, but in order to keep it lightweight, aerodynamic, while sturdy, something's gotta give! I think the material is much more resilient than it presents itself..

In summary.... great fit for the vehicle size, love the amount of storage for family of 4 (and doggie) and it looks good!

product_title: EasyStay 4-N-1 Single High Airbed – Twin/King
review_headline: A twin + a twin = a king
review_body: Pretty novel concept. I basically bought two twin mattresses with a zipper in the middle. Kinda wish the \\"conversion\\" to the king made the mattresses join together as one mattress but stuff like that only happens in sci-fi movies.......or something...anyway. Great mattress, no leakage. The reason other people say these mattresses leak is probably because they aren't pushing in the air intake valve after they fill it, thus allowing air to seep out of the \\"cap\\". Push the valve in and you have a solid (well more cushy than solid but you catch my drift) air mattress that doesn't leak. Also some tips on having a firm compared to a soft mattress. For a soft(er) mattress, use the D-powered air pump and it will fill to capacity but not more than. For a more firm mattress, use a manual hand pump (Coleman offers both pumps) as the manual pump allows you to fill the mattress as full (and as firm) as you want. product_title: Allen Sports Deluxe 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack
review_headline: Did what it was supposed to do
review_body:
I bought this to bring my bike to campus and it has been highly functional and useful for what I need. The car I use it on is a 2007 Honda Accord.

This product overall worked well enough for what I needed it to do. Installation and assembly was simple and straightforward. It holds 2 bikes, but I've only done it with 1. I keep the bike on the rack closest to the car and the wheel does turn into the car when driving but this hasn't damaged the car in anyway and is probably like that on most racks.

Some disadvantages is that it doesn't "feel" secure. I've never had the product fall off while driving thankfully but it doesn't always feel like it's safe and secured to the car. There are 2 hooks that go on top of the trunk lid. They don't always line up symmetrically and 1 hook seems to do a lot more of the work than the other.

Another caveat is that the bottom hook isn't always stable and can fall off the bottom bumper. It's partly due to my poor skill perhaps because I have adjusted the tightness so it grips it better but I can't shake off the fact that it doesn't give me the 100% confidence and safety knowing it will secure the bikes. However, I've used it many times and have had no problems. Never fallen off. Other pluses are its cheap, portable, small and easy to store. Good product overall, no problems yet after 2 years.

review_body:

product_title: Therm-A-Rest Z-Lite Regular Coyote/Gray
review_headline: Indestructible, light, cheap - best foam sleeping pad I have ever used
review_body:
I have used a few different foam and inflatable pads, and this is the best *foam* sleeping pad I have ever used. Five starts because:

- Unlike the inflatable pads, this is indestructible. Rip off a piece? Still works. Burn a hole into it at the campfire? Doesn't matter.
- Thanks to the ribs, it is much more comfortable than a flat foam mat of the same weight.
- The folding is ingenious. The ribs on the pad nicely slot into each other (like a stack of legos), and it uses roughly half the space of a comparable rolled mat.
- It's cheap.
- It's light.

Let's be clear here, it's not perfect. Negatives:
- Any inflatable pad which packs to half the size will be thicker and more comfortable.
- I haven't used it too often yet, and I think that over the years the ribs will deform a little, making the pad effectively a bit thinner / less comfy.
- Due to its square shape, it's a bit more annoying to attach to backpacks than a rolled pad.

I ordered this for my son, and so far it's worked out very nicely. The day it arrived, we rode 7 miles to a Boy Scout meeting, then returned home after dark...and he's had another opportunity or two to use it after sunset since then. So, limited experience thus far, but it seems to be working great. When I rode with him, I was using a wimpy little $5 wrap-around-the-handlebar light mainly for the sake of me being seen, not for being able to see, so on the really dark patches I rode right alongside or slightly off his front quarter—and kept thinking it was a car headlight right behind me. But it was just my son and his new light.

So, we’re quite pleased all-in-all, especially at having taken a chance on something that's not a "major name." I own another great hi-intensity flashlight from FourSevens, but at least one thing I like better on this light is being able to toggle through all the modes with “soft” clicks. (On my FourSevens light, you have to slightly unscrew the cap and go through a few other gyrations to change the modes—so this ActivFortis light is actually better for use “on the fly.”) This one has good heft, construction seems solid. Nice to know it's waterproof if it starts drizzling before you make it home.

The mounting block is pretty stable and uses Velcro straps which I could conceive might be easier to replace than rubber or plastic should that ever become necessary. I feel like I can get them cinched down very nice and snug. Standard road vibrations don't cause any slippage of the light's position on the handlebar. Can't speak to how it might do on a trail, though. You have the option of using 3 AAA batteries versus investing in a single rechargeable one. Just involves adding an extra 1/2" extension piece to the barrel.

Can't come up with any negatives; would definitely recommend to friends. (This is Dad of three; Mom just shows up as the main gal on the account name...)

review_headline: more foot room than phase 2 but 2 pounds heavier. tires were only 50 psi and clamp only 2 bolt. rides great

Royal Scout Highs: Large foot room (usa foot size 13 plus). Fits tall 6'2" rider. Neutral steering with straight high quality forks. Stoppie ready. High quality gloss paint. Very intelligent x-bar downtube design enabling the stoppies and footroom. Brake is very thin and keeps large foot area.

Royal Scout Lows: 13 pounds is 2 pounds heavier than phase 2. Plastic rims. 50psi tires will not enable high speed use with heavy riders. Wiggly if you wobble wheels back and forth from factory. Factory clamp only had 2 bolts. Brake works but not great (rely on your foot on the tire which works good but wears out your shoe if you do any downhill braking).

Phase II John Radtke Highs: 11 pounds. 3 bolt clamp. Nice blue paint. Cool art design sticker on bottom. 80 psi tires enable high speed (necessary for big offroad stunts). Metal wheels. Nice grips. Plastic slider on rear sides. Brake works well even downhill, very safe if you like your foot never to touch the tire. High quality.

Phase 2 Lows: Came scratched in the box. Matte paint on handlebars and forks is ok. Brake keeps your foot from ever touching back tire, brake mechanism takes up 2cm more space of footroom causing limited footroom. My size 12's compete for space more than on the Royal Scout.

product_title: Sigma Sport Spokes Magnet for Wired Computers
review_body:
I tried these on a set of HED Ardennes which use a relatively small bladed spoke. They attach as well as the screw-in variety by slipping the metal shield over the rubber magnet and pinching the rubber to the spoke. My Garmin speed and cadence sensor didn't want to pick it up at first, so I flipped it around several times. The rubber part is the magnet and there is no indicated up or down. You'll just have to play with it until your sensor finds it. It's a relatively weak magnet, so I had to position the sensor arm within 1/8\\" of the magnet for it to work.

If the blades on your wheels are really wide, this may not hang on well enough. The slit is clearly made for a round spoke and, in theory, the rubber magnet could be oriented towards the sensor. With a bladed spoke, the spoke will never fully seat in the rubber slot, consequently the rubber portion will be like a fan attached to the blade rather than perpendicular to the sensor.

Bottom line is that it works okay and has a unique attachment system that is better than the screw on variety. They could have made the slot deeper to accommodate bladed spokes, and the magnet could be stronger.

review_body:
This bag is great as a lightweight bag for late spring and very early fall. I live in MD.

I used this bag in 40 degree nights of March and I was way too cold. Wouldn't use it under 55 degrees. Probably use it as a quilt by June.

This thing is very small when packed. It fit in my old Big Agnes pad sack (minus the pad). The silkscreened Logo wasn't on properly and had a few spots of ink on the bag. I don't really care though. Just saying if you're some kind of fashion hiker then you might need to inspect upon arrival. I got it for 55 bucks on an amazon sale.

It will serve its purpose until the end of June. Probably carry it again starting September.

product_title: Tour de France Double Pannier Bike Bag
review_headline: Decent Bag for a good price.
review_body:
I spent $28 on these bags and picked them over some Axiom bags because I only needed them for a short time and they offered a better price.
There are plastic sheets which slide into pockets of the panniers which help them keep their shape. Some of the stitches in the pockets have broken or become loose, however they still work well. The bags also are somewhat difficult to attatch to your pannier rack. I used zip ties which have done the job. The clips which attach the inside of the bag to the rack are questionable. While I was riding my spokes caught the bag and tore a hole in one of the bags. I patched it with duck tape and all is well. They are pretty spacious as well.

product_title: Yakima Landing Pad
review_body: These do not have a lot of contact with the paint. My only issue is the locking mechanism on the for the bars that can be a pain at times. I pinched my finger pretty hard and the description for screwing them in is pretty poor so you should be careful not to screw these into your car paint.

product_title: Kelty Grand Mesa 2 Footprint
review_body: Yes, the size is prefect matching with my Kelty Gran Mesa 2 Tent!  However, they forget... the pole has its angle when setting up the tent, and it's not pure vertical...  So, it's not possible to make final prefect matching when you set up the tent.  The design will need to enlarger a little for making the RIGHT matching...  In addition, Kelty Gran Mesa 2 outer cover created extra area.  I will be even better if this foodprint is able to cover that area.

product_title: BV Bicycle Light Set Super Bright 5 LED Headlight, 3 LED Taillight, Quick-Release
review_body: Would give 5 stars to headlight and 3stars to tail light as only 2 of 3 led lights work. FOR Tor the price not worth returning.

product_title: Pearl Izumi Men's Elite Inrcool Shorts
review_headline: Great Short, Maybe not the best value
review_body: They're great, and the ventilation definitely helps in hot weather. I also like the white side panel, which is more visible than just all-black. One thing, though, I do not see a huge difference in comfort from the cheaper Attack short.  I regularly ride 50-75 miles and haven't noticed a difference.

product_title: SPACE SAVER MUG HARD ANODIZED
review_body: This mug fits over a Nalgene bottle perfectly. I see where it makes scratches because of the rivets, but that is not a deal breaker. Its for camping anyway! One thing I did notice is that the handles seem to extend too far away from the cup a bit. It just doesn't "feel" right to me. No problem, I made smaller handles with a coat hanger! Now, it's the  perfect mug.

review_body: I bought the hat as a gift and he lives it now he says he wants a nother one I don't blame him.

product_title: Micro Maxi Kick Scooter, Orange
review_body: I now have to jog to keep up with my 3 yr old when we head to the park.  And, he's figured out how to off road on this.  For my 7 yr old I have to flat out run to keep up.  They love these.

product_title: Kinetic Road Machine 2.0 Fluid Trainer
review_body: With all the heat we are having in S California I am so pleased I got the trainer.  Santa Anna winds and 90's just don't make for good riding.  Kinetic sets up easy and with fluid turbine I am able to get my climbs in while watching some playoff hockey and basketball.

product_title: Silicone Mouthpiece w/ Color Tab Replacement Scuba Regulator Comfort Fit Mouth Piece
review_body: it is more than I expected, in fact it seems better than what originally came with my set. Thank you so much.

product_title: Suunto Core Standard Strap All Black One Size
review_body: I have the sunnto core all black military and this is the exact replacement for it. My original broken strap is much darker then this one. Which does not make any sense. Not impressed for being 40 dollers you think it would be the exact same strap. This strap has a greyish black tone when my original strap was like really dark back.  absolutely annoyed

product_title: Trident One Handed Opening Lobster and Game Bag Scuba Dive Diving Diver Gear Authorized Dealer Full Warranty
review_body:
no zipper to fail in bottom easy to open and fill with bugs....perfect game bag!!

for the price a great deal!!

product_title: Velo Orange Moderniste Polished Stainless
review_body: I purchased this for my Wabi Classic single speed road bike. I wanted something that looked a little more classic/vintage to match the look of my bike. But, I also wanted something light and functional. This bottle cage is perfect! It looks great. It's very light. And, it is more functional than any of my bottle cages on my other three bikes. It holds bottles tight with no rattling. But, it also allows you to pull the bottle out with ease. I truly love this bottle cage. If you're looking for something class/vintage for your custom build, look no further. This is it!

product_title: Gore Running Wear Women's Essential 2.0 Lady Tights
review_body: First pair of tights i have found that actually reach my ankles. I measured according to the gore website, brought a large probably would be better in the medium bit saggy around the thighs but they are still so good, and warm!!

product_title: Sunlite Willow Bushel Strap-On Basket
review_headline: This basket works great on my gf bike
review_body: I got this for my girlfriend when the car was in the shop. It has two straps that hook on to the handle bars, set up in less then a min. it is a great size and pretty sturdy. Plus it makes the bike look super cool

product_title: Pink Pennant 8 x 18" Bicycle Safety Flag with Rear Axle Mounting Bracket
review_headline: Fits perfect and just what we were looking for!
review_body: We bought a used tag-a-long bike and the flag was missing. I loved that we could get this in hot pink for our daughter, since it not only helps keep her more visible, but it's also more fun than the typical safety orange colored flags.

product_title: BIGBANG GIYONGCHY G-DRAGON GD favorite type knit hat
review_body: Love it! it fits perfectly,great stitching and the material is high quality. A great purchase for any GD/Big Bang fan!

product_title: Earth Products Jamboree Military Style Folding Cot with Free Side Storage Bag System and Pillow (Green)
review_body: When I received mine, the packaging of the product was decent and looked great. Then I opened it out all the way and realized they skipped out on quality control. The seems on the one I received where ripping in multiple locations already and the pillow is laughable, but better than nothing i guess when you need it. I figure I still give it the benefit of the doubt and give it a try by laying on it, which caused some of the seems to undo even more and even break (heard those pooping sounds when string breaks) after that decided its not going to work and starting packing it up. When I got to the point of putting it back in the carry bag, while i was shoving it back in, the handle completely came off, not so much a carry bag anymore. My experience with this has not been good, I could have just received that 1/1000 defect that went through inspection, but I probably wont be buying this again. I was able to return mind thanks to amazon and got a full refund.

product_title: Dare2b Men's Oscar Pereiro Waterproof Jacket
review_body: I can't speak for the performance or quality of this jacket because I was unable to use it. I ordered a large, which is what I wear in 90% of clothing items - and I'm on the smaller side of large so the other 10% of the time I wear a medium. Well this Large fits me like a Small, I could barely fit into it and couldn't even come close to zipping it up! Needless to say I ended up having to send it back for a refund. Don't know if I got one that was labelled incorrectly or what, but I am hesitant to get it another shot.

product_title: Hot Chillys Women's Rose Low Volume Poco Socks
review_body: Exactly what I expected. I'm very happy with the quality and the overall ordering experience. This was definitely worth it!

product_title: Bushwhacker Ketchum Black - Bicycle Frame Bag Cycling Triangle Pack Bike Under Seat Top Tube Bag - w/ Reflective Trim
review_body: for wallet, cell phone and keys - but does make it a challenge with water bottle.  Velcro straps are HUGE - but didn't flap in the wind once i cut them down.

product_title: Portable LED Camping Lantern with Ceiling Fan, Outdoor Camping Lantern 2-In-1 Combo 18 Super Bright LED Light and Fan
review_headline: Great fan and excellent light. Cant wait to go camping. I got 2
review_body: Nice fan and real handy. My boys will love it. I always get hot no matter what the temp is.

product_title: Palm Springs 10 X 20 Heavy Duty White Party Tent Gazebo with Sidewalls 002
review_body:
Very thin weak pipes connect this flimsy junk tent, which snapped in minutes of being set up.

Total junk!

Do not buy this tent...

Rent a tent with 2-3 heavy metal pipes and rope that connects to huge ground spikes for $200 for the day rather than this flimsy bending pipe tent with little tiny strings that connect to itsy bitsy metal spikes...

I can't believe anyone wrote a positive review of this garbage

product_title: Greenfield SKS2BC Rear Mount Kickstand - 285 mm - SKS2BC
review_body: I got a new road bike, and it didn't have a place to attach a standard kick stand, so I bought this.  This gives the bike such good balance that I bought one for my hybrid bike as well.

product_title: Park Tool Home Mechanic Repair Stand - PCS-9
review_body:
This is a great bike stand! I've used it for adjustments and fixes on Electra Cruisers, a Diamondback and Raleigh comfort bike, an old school Schwinn, and a Cannondale mountain bike. No problems with any of them.
The stand itself is a good weight. I can pick it up and move it around with no problems, yet it's sturdy enough to not fall over. It looks to be well made and last a long time.
There was one slight problem with a plastic piece being misshaped when I bought it, but a 5 minute call to Park Tool and a new one was on it's way. I was very happy with the prompt replacement and ease of contacting their customer service.
Well worth the money spent!

product_title: Shaun White Supply Co. Skateboard Composite Deck
review_body: As the package comes, the board is near impossible to ride. It would not turn, it takes a lot to break in the bushings. The stock wheels are very average and function fine, and the bearings also take a while to break in. This board is very durable, has taken a beating many times by me and still rides decently. I out fitted my deck with aftermarket wheels that are slightly larger, and better bearings. The trucks on this deck are horrible and I would suggest upgrading to penny board trucks. Then again, I like to modify things. If you want a quality deck from the get go, this is not for you.

product_title: Coleman 40 Quart PowerChill Thermoelectric Cooler
review_body: My husband uses this cooler in his semi.  He's extremely pleased with it.  Lots of space and keeps everything at the perfect temperature.  Highly recommend it.

product_title: Canari Women's Cross Sport II Tank
review_body:
Good stuff - fits is small so order 2 sizes up. I wear a medium n most tops, the XL fit snug but, looked great! I wore this to run our Flying Pig Marathon - the rear pockets were so convenient.

Bad stuff - this color is not yellow it is neon green. I returned it to the seller the first time because I thought they sent me the wrong color. However, when I received the second top, it was the same color. I called the seller who told me that their yellow is actually a "highlighter yellow". Noooooo, your "Killer yellow" is highlighter GREEN!

Nevertheless, I wore the top and matched a pair of neon green running socks with it and it was okay. I wanted to give this a four/five star rating but the yellow is so completely off plus the sizing is two sizes off.

product_title: Hyperflex Children's ACCESS 2mm Back Zip Spring
review_headline: Length ran small based on chart
review_body: My daughter is 5y old. I ordered this in size4 based on the reviews here but the size ran small. We couldn't get it up her shoulders! Had to return it for a larger size. Otherwise product was good.

product_title: 65mm Blank Pro Longboard Skateboard Cruiser Wheels (Black) + ABEC 7 Bearings + Spacers
review_body: If you want cruiser wheels get these. I was sceptical at first but when I got the package it was worth it. The wheels are good, the bearings decent, and it comes with shock pads and hardware. The wheels itself id buy for 20$ this this is a great buy.

product_title: Mares Tropic She Dives 2.5mm Shorty
review_body: Great wetsuit! Fit like it was supposed to. Good quality materials and workmanship.  The sizing is very accurate which is important when ordering things online and not being able to try on.

product_title: Advanced Elements Double Action Hand Pump with Pressure Gauge
review_body: I like the gauge so you can tell how much you're inflating..Sturdy and works well. Lightweight. I am pretty happy with it.

product_title: Pack of 8 Aluminum Tent Stakes Y Beam Design with Pull Cords - Includes Carry Bag
review_body:
I just can't stand the stock stakes that come with most tents and shelters. I've been switching all my gear to these type of stakes. Maybe it is the places I end up camping but these always seem to hold up well and are super light weight. The only issue I have with these is the notches in the top. For guyline staking these are great, or if your tent as guyline loops or steel rings at the bottom of the stake points, but if you have 3/4" or 1" strapping at the stake points these may be a little challenging to work with.

Several of the red string ties were completely off their associated stakes when I opened the package and the others had very loose knots that all needed to be retied.

product_title: econoLED US Army 3L 3 Liter (100 ounce) Hydration Pack Bladder Water Bag Pouch Hiking Climbing Survival Outdoor Backpack US
review_headline: Item is not as shown in picture or as described on item page
review_body: I purchased this to use for a hiking trip. When I received the package in the mail, it was a tiny pouch with no pockets, no straps, NOTHING. It was a cheap 50 cent plastic pouch. Please be careful when ordering from "GGXSAM". You're better off spending a few more dollars and ordering from a legitimate website or from Amazon.com directly and not through this re-seller. Horrible experience!!!!

product_title: 2014 Fox Head Men’s Dirtpaw Race Glove
review_body:
I have bought two pairs of these gloves (lost a glove in the first pair), and they have worked brilliantly both times. My friends that I recommended this to likes them as well. They fit well, are snug, and properly pad my hands when biking.

The only minor thing I have experienced is the palms of the gloves might scrunch slightly when in heavy use. It does not affect my riding or comfort, but it is something that occurs sometimes.

product_title: iMeshbean® 24V Scooter Battery Charger For Razor E100 E125 E200 E300 E500 USA Seller
review_body: The second time I used the charger there was a pop and charger no longer works ??? Would not recommend.

product_title: Razor V-17 Youth Multi-Sport Helmet
review_body: I ordered Razor V-17 Youth Helmet, but I received a Razor  8+ youth helmet. Can I consider they are the same?

product_title: River Tow Tether
review_body: The Kokatat River Tow Tether is exactly what I needed. It fits perfectly in the elastic and mesh sleeve in a Kokatat Maximus Prime rescue vest. It is light weight with quality stitching. Best of all is that the tether stores neatly and securely out of the way, which greatly reduces any snag hazard.

product_title: Magnesium Flint Fire Starter - 3 Pack - Survival Firesteel Blocks with Striker, Camping Emergency Equipment by The Friendly Swede
review_body: I love these little fire starters ...  They require no experiance or technique ... just strike, strike, strike and you have a very hot little fire burning in no time.  I keep one in the car and one in my camping stuff ... and the price is so low that they make great Chrismas stocking stuffers for the kiddies ....  I even give out dozens of them for Trick or Treat at Halloween instead of cavity causing sugary candy !!!!  Why poisen our children when you can teach them some usefull survival skills ????

product_title: 2PCS Bicycle Wheel Spoke Tire Wire Tyre Valve LED Light
review_body: I bought these on a lark (under a dollar with free shipping? heck yeah) but they've actually been great. They're still working, months later, and make me more visible when I'm biking at night. This is actually cheaper and more effective than putting reflective tape on my bicycle and helmet, and more stylish to boot. For less than a dollar, you can't go wrong.

product_title: ESI Chunky MTB Grip
review_headline: Great grips, light but still comfy!
review_body:
I was using lock on grips on an AL bar and switched to carbon. Someone gave me a tip to check these out and I'm so glad they did. They're very light, but I must say more comfy than standard rubber grips. Once they're on, they're *ON* and any worries about slippage because of the material is misplaced.

That's actually the only real downside of these grips. They are extremely tight and difficult to put on and taking them off? Haha, I'll just cut and buy some new.

FWIW I installed them using soapy water and some zip ties through the grip. Slipped them on, then pulled the zip ties out.

product_title: Therm-a-Rest universal repair kit
review_body: If you are like me you have some very old and some new thermal-rests. I have no idea what model they are. The instructions say there are different methods for different mattresses. They don't say what the differences are so you can't really just wing it. Only comes with three fabric patches. I'm not sure what to use and already confused before I even start. Bad instructions, unclear.

product_title: Sunday Afternoons Sprinter Cap
review_body: The description pic of the item shows it standing tall like a firm hat. It is very flimsy and thin material. Not good for putting a company logo or any other company advertising. I bought these for my pest control employees that work in South Louisiana humidity...but the hats don't seem to work any better than a normal baseball cap. Nice idea...but not very functional for anything but carrying in your pocket or for runners wanting to limit additional weight.

product_title: Princess Quad Skate, Size J10-J13
review_headline: Saved my daughter from breaking her legs
review_body: I love these skates, they are a little heavy but extremely durable and completely adjustable for years of wear.  She may just wear them out before she grows out of them as I can't get her out of them.  So the first day she got her skates she puts them on and skates in the basement and I told her not to wear her skates going up and down the stairs, so what does she do, 15 minutes after first putting them on she climbs up the stairs and falls down them.  I ran down and her legs looked like they were twisted by the way the skates were, but because of how they are made they cannot tighten as much as a lace-up skate (still tighten enough to stay on and do not fall off during normal skating), so her foot had twisted inside of the skate and did not twist her leg and snap the bone, and the other leg because of how she fell had come off her foot in the process so that was okay.  Had she been wearing her sister's lace up skates I believe she would have twisted her ankle or worse broke her ankles or legs.

product_title: Schwinn Toddler Classic Microshell Helmet
review_headline: Love that it is so easy to fit to head!
review_body: My daughter loves to wear her new helmet.  Makes bike riding even more fun.  It is easy to adjust to fit her head.

product_title: Retrospec Bicycles Fixed-Gear Track BMX-Style Foot Retention FGFS Velcro Straps with Reflective Fabric
review_body: For the price I really cant complain.  I am sure if you wanna spend 35$ on a pair straps go for it, but these seem to work fine for around 10$.  If you live on your bike then I guess get something else, but if your a weekend warrior these seem to be just fine for riding around on if you arent constantly having to stop for traffic.  Takes some practice getting in and out of them on the good.  Overall, I'd probably buy again.

product_title: Suunto MC-2G Global Compass
review_body: This is one of the better made compasses on the market today.  It is pricey for what it does.  The MC-2 Pro is exactly the same but the gimbal mount for the magnetic needle is different and does not allow as much verticle movement so it only works in the hemisphere you buy it for.  Unless you are traveling and exploring in both hemispheres, the less expensive version is just fine.  I would recommend either one of these, depending on wheere you plan on travelling.

product_title: Croakies Original Eyewear Retainer
review_headline: Love It, Love it, Love it.
review_body: Only have had a few days, but what a world of difference with how my glasses fit.  I have had problems with glasses and them causing sores on mu nose.  So far the TiKi Koa has made a world of comfort available I have not had for many years. They are also stylish from the back of my Head.

product_title: LuxuryLite UltraLite Cot Sleeping pads
review_body: very expensive, just heavy enough that i'm not sure i would take it on a long treck.  that said it makes sleeping on the ground a pleasant experience.  i would definately take it on a trip if i were cycling, canoeing or horse back riding.

product_title: Top Seller Newest Motorcycle Fleece Neck Hat Winter Ski Full Face Mask Cover Cap
review_body: l used one this winter and was very good if set right will keep  your face warm, and  your breathing warm air back into your mouth  then the very cold air that could make you sick, only issue I had was to short could be 5 inch long and the one adjustment cord came out of the hood, I made it work by putting the cord  on out side of the hood area!

product_title: Animal Essentials AS-9000120-2 2 oz (Pack of 2)  Detox Allergy Blend Dog and Cat Supplement
review_headline: Makes my old kitty feel much better.
review_body: This formula works very well to relieve my cat's arthritis pain.  She used to limp and avoid walking too much.  Now she's up around way more, and the limp is gone.  She is a fairly picky eater, and tolerates the drops in her food quite well.

product_title: Coleman Instant Canopy with LED Lighting System
review_body: I ordered this canopy to use for the beach.  I have not used it yet, but it does seem of good quality and nice.

product_title: American Athletic Shoe Women's Quilted Patent Leather Figure Skates
review_body: Love the look of the skates, but they felt cheap, thin plastic, little padding, and were very uncomfortable.  Ended up returning them.

product_title: SHIMANO Deore BR-M615 BL-M615 Hydraulic Brake Set Front and Rear Black
review_body:
It was not mentioned in the specs, but the left lever controls the rear brake, and the right controls the front. Like many I don't run my levers this way so I had to swap them. Beware if you don't want to bleed them. If you don't already have them, you will also need to buy a bleed kit, and new olives.
That said, after swapping the levers and bleeding them they work great. They have more stopping power and a better lever feel than my Hayes Mags, and 9's.

As long as you don't mind the lever setup or bleeding, these are great brakes.

product_title: Swagman XC Cross-Country 2-Bike Hitch Mount Rack (1/1/4 and 2-Inch Receiver)
review_body: I'm in the process of assembling this bike rack, and it's been one frustration after another.  I tried to return it but the window for returning has expired. This rack is clunky and it seems as though the engineers never bothered to assemble the unit after building it as there are multiple obvious flaws with the pieces fitting together.

product_title: Pelican Baby Single Back Sleigh, Beige/Red
review_body: It is the best winter gift for a small boy. You could see the smiling face and hear the giggles in those snowy days. We used it for a couple of times without any issue. It works pretty well and quality is good for lasting.

product_title: Slouchy Beanie Slouch Skull Hat Ski Hat Snowboard Hat Ribbed Beanie,One Size,Heather Dark Grey
review_body: It didn't have any of the listed special features, go go gadget nothing. No Bluetooth, no Wi-Fi, no microwave. It'll keep your head warm, I guess

product_title: Columbia Men's Silver Ridge Long-Sleeve Shirt
review_body:
Columbia makes some really great outdoor and travel clothes. This shirt is the best shirt they make. The fit is great, roomy without being baggy, sleeves that are just long enough with plenty of buttons at the cuff and a slightly longer cut so if you do tuck it in, it stays tucked in.

The material is simply amazing! It feels great and has a really nice high-tech weave. Three factors make this shirt my favorite: 1. Stain and smell resistant. I can wear this for several days without any problems 2. Keeps me cool on hot days. Also protects my skin form UV 3. No iron ever. It never wrinkles.

I am ordering more in different colors.

product_title: Pure Water Straw-Advanced
review_body: Definitely did not receive what is shown on the ad. Not sure if this is a fake, but looks similar, but no color and no tip as shown. Shipped in bulk packaging clear bag. Does come with a small container with another filter insert (when opened black crushed charcoal? went all over the place) . Main beef is while it does have a small paper 'instructions' it does not even tell you how to use it. Also you cannot tell which end is which... one side is like a sports bottle pop top, and the other is a flattened flute mouthpiece looking part covered with a cap... Im assuming that is the mouthpiece and the poptop is the intake.

product_title: Nemo Equipment Cosmo Insulated Sleeping Pad (Orange, X-Large)
review_body: This pad has been awesome for me. I have taken it on numerous hikes, including a 12-day Trek at Philmont Scout Ranch, and it always provides me with a great night's sleep. With this sleeping pad, you will never have to worry about that tree root or rock poking you in the back all night long.

product_title: Magnesium Flint Fire Starter - 3 Pack - Survival Firesteel Blocks with Striker, Camping Emergency Equipment by The Friendly Swede
review_body: they work great just scrape the powder coat off the striker.everyone needs these,matches,and lighters dont last long.these will keep you building fires for a long,long time.

product_title: Fenix FNX-E01BK E Series LED Flashlight, Black
review_headline: Great Keychain or Emergency Close Lighting in a Tiny Package
review_body: This light is so small and featherweight that it's easy to drop or have it fall to the bottom of a pocket or bag. But when you turn it on it explodes with so much white light for its size, you can use it for just about any close-range lighting. It is waterproof and pretty tough, too.

product_title: Suisse Sport Adventurer Sleeping Bag
review_body: Comfortable bag, very collapsible. Zipper is very cheaply made, it has not broken yet, but I find myself struggling to zip it up without damaging the zipper. I would not recommend this for someone who is going camping or intends to use it multiple times for the long term, but for someone who wants a cheap, very portable bag that they can toss in the closet for when guests come over, this may be the thing.

product_title: Street Surfing Amped Pro Scooter with Colorful Customized Graphics
review_body: i hate this scooter. the grip tape fell off, the wheels de hubbed, and the bars bent.not worth it at all. terrible scooter

product_title: Chaos Men's Dylon Wool Blend Trapper Hat
review_body: Stylish and warm. I haven't been able to wear it much because I live in So Cal and I normally run hot. But, I really like the hat.

product_title: Black foldable bicycle bike cargo trailer cart Large carrier 0016BL
review_body: I purchased this trailer to pull my dog. I enjoy riding trails and I have a Lab that is only good for half the distance. The trailer is a joke! Made in China cheap, the inside diameter is quite small and it weighs a lot. Everything about this item is cheap. You get what you pay for. If you have the money look at the BOB trailer.

product_title: Zippo Hand Warmer 2012
review_body: Excellent product, have had similar ones in the past and this lived up to my expectations.  Would suggest it to anyone.

product_title: Pearl iZUMi Men's Quest Cycling Short
review_body: Sizing is as stated and item is good quality - this is the second pair we have purchased and would recommend this to others

product_title: Nitecore Sens Mini Cr LED Flashlight with Active Dimming, Black, 190 lm
review_body:
I bought this light 2 to 3 months ago because I wanted a small keychain light that was powerful. I was aware of the active dimming and was a little skeptical of it, but after reading the answers to my question (above) I was comfortable that I could avoid that feature. Well, turns out that the dimming feature, and the ease with which it can be used or not used, makes this keychain flashlight the perfect keychain flashlight in my opinion.

First, it is a VERY bright little light. Very bright. Prior to this I had a little nano light - which is physically very small, but almost nil on light. This SENS Mini light is a little bigger physically but 20 times brighter - it throws a serious amount of light.

Now about that active dimming capability - it is really easy to use/control, and extremely helpful when working really close up and don't need a lot of light.

If you want to use the active dimming feature, simply turn the light on while holding it straight up and down, with the lens facing down. That is all there is to it.

If you want full bright regardless of how you point the light, simply turn on the light in any position OTHER THAN straight up and down with the lens down.

This is a fantastic light. I have it on my keychain at all times and it is really nice to be able to work with a very small amount of light when I want to, but also be able to throw a serious beam what I need to.

You can't go wrong for $25. Get one. It's terrific.

product_title: Glove.ly Cozy Touch Screen Gloves
review_body: I was a bit hesitant purchasing these after reading some negative reviews. Make sure you get the proper size and do measurements, etc. The closest fit for me was a medium pair. The finger tips may extend slightly further then where your finger actually is, I believe this is due to the inner warm lining and design. Doesn't bother me. One thing to note is sometimes if your hands are warm/sweaty it is difficult to take off the gloves without the inner lining falling towards your wrist. It's not a big deal, and you can just carefully pull up one finger tip at a time to hold the lining there, and then pull the whole thing off. Oddly this only seems to happen on my right hand and hasn't been an issue with my left. The smartphone function works as advertised, just dont expect a perfect response as no touchscreen glove this thick and warm will offer you that. I have a light weight (not warm) pair of touchscreen gloves and although are better at controlling the screen they do not keep my hands warm at all. The compromises of this glove are worth it to me. I look forward to see how they hold over the next year and cold seasons. Additionally, note.. perhaps some of the gloves have quality control issues (so return them?) or users reviewing expect too much for these gloves.. This may be what's going on with the intense negative reviews.

review_body: Has held up over the years and serves its purpose. Wouldn't recommend for a new vehicle as it scratches the paint.

product_title: Built U.S.A. Seattle Sports Camp Bucket (Blue)
review_body: This is amazing addition to any campers utensils, although my wife thinks otherwise. The construction is very sturdy and you can be confident it will stand without collapsing or tipping over when full. The strap is very firmly attached making it very easy to transport. product_title: Solo Stove Tripod: Compact Lightweight Aluminum Tripod w/ Adjustable Hang Chain. Works with Solo Stove Titan and Campfire. Perfect for Camping, Backpacking, Survival
review_body: I have the solo stove pot and I was impressed with its quality so I was confident that the tripod would also exceed my expectations. It did. Its very wall made and surprisingly light. Under a pound! It collapses and comes with a carrying case. But best of all it has a great easy to use adjustable hight chain and pin. This makes it so easy and versatile to use. product_title: kahtoola MICROspikes Footwear Traction
review_body:

Even gave some to Grandpa, he loves them too!

product_title: EcWorld Enterprises 7732326 8 In. Replica Desktop U.S. Navy Mark-V Brass Diving Helmet
review_body: This item was perfect. It was a birthday gift for a Navy diver, and exceeded expectations. It's proudly displayed on the fireplace mantle.

product_title: Sigma BC 509 Bicycle Speedometer
review_body: This speedometer is great  and easy to install. I use this on a city bike mainly for exercise on neighborhood asphalt road conditions. review_body: I was impressed with the amount of light this gives off.  I haven't had it for long so can't speak to the battery life but the light output is great and it's very easy to use.  The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is that it's not particularly comfortable.  The piece on the forehead is only cushioned by the elastic band holding it on your head.  Not significantly uncomfortable but wouldn't want to wear if for any length of time without something in between the light and my forehead (would be fine on a hat or something). Overall a great solution for night dog walking, trail running, emergencies or any situation when you need the use of your hands and don't want to have to hold a flashlight.

product_title: Coleman 5 Ft. High-Pressure Propane Hose and Adapter
review_body:
It Did exactly what

product_title: Coghlan's Inside/Outside Camping Mat
review_body:
The measurements on the product page are clearly wrong, so I rolled the dice and hoped that it wasn't really 1x1x1-inches. It wasn't. But it was smaller than I expected.

I don't have the exact dimensions, but it's a little smaller than a doormat. I had hoped it might be a little bit bigger, but it's serving the intended purpose...a place to remove our shoes prior to entering the tent.

I use it outside and it does tend to get covered in dust and dirt, but it shakes out easily. It's small enough that the kids sit on it to deal with their shoes while the adults use it more to keep socks and feet out of the dirt.

It rolls up and is very compact.

review_body: These suck. I'm on a road bike for 30 minutes to 2 hours, and these just suck. There is NO padding on the front of crotch and very little on the rest of the crotch. There's a ton on the butt though, and I don't sit back that far on a road bike. The seams also seem (ha) to hit me right where they chafe on the inner leg, which I haven't experienced before. They fit great and I love the material, but the padding is way too far back to be useful for road biking.

product_title: Princeton Tec Fred Headlamp (45 Lumens)
review_headline: A well-designed headlight for casual use

review_body: I had been searching for a nice flashlight for a while.  I have several of the cheap $5-10 LED flashlights around the house, but they never seem to really get the job done. I used the highest level last Halloween to light up pathways that my kids were walking up to homes.  It really worked well. product_title: Vanquest JAVELIN 2.0 VSlinger Right-Shoulder Slingpack (Coyote Tan)
review_headline: Needs some tweaks, but well made, practice pack
review_body: 1st of all...this is a great looking pack and can be customized with any moral patches or pins that you see fit.  This is the first pack that I needed to use a few times, and play with to learn how best to wear it.  The snaps are very tights and tough to snap open or closed, so had to "break them in", continuously snapping and unsnapping until they loosened up a bit.  Now they are great, though still holds secure.  I could have used a large area of shock cord to carry cast off jacket but there are options to add to the pack for this purpose if you feel creative. I did not like the two step main strap buckle, so took a razor blade to it and shaved down the middle knob that needed pressing down to open and release.  The two side levers are secure enough - no child is going to accidentally open on you.  Now that I have adjusted it to my liking, it is the most comfortable sling pack I have tried on.  I have taken a few hikes in the Smokey Mountains with it, and it rides well, not bouncing around when I run, and fits all I need.  Now all of this adjustment sounds like too much work for a new pack, but I liked the flexibility it gives me to make this pack MY pack.  You can make it YOUR pack.

product_title: American Trails Ozzie & Harriet Double Person Giant Sleeping Bag
review_headline: Why does Amazon keep getting this wrong?!
review_body:
I've ordered 2 used bags (only had cosmetic damage to the box) and one new bag, and ALL THREE were only half of the bag. Part of what drew me to this particular sleeping bag was that it could turn into two one-person bags in addition to being able to connect for a two-person bag. After three attempts though, it's not worth trying again. This is the third time I've had to contact customer support (who admit that this is a recurring problem.) If you guys can't get this right then please stop selling it. You're not selling a two-person sleeping bag at this point; all you're selling is one-person frustration.

* The bag itself seems fine despite the frayed edges that have to be cut/burned. For the price it should be as comfortable of a bag as you'll need for weekend camping, if only they could get it right during shipping.

Using a 1/2 inch socket wrench ADAPTER with the "stem" thin enough to fit into your VARIABLE SPEED drill (I use 1/2 x 3/8), insert the crank stem into the 1/2" socket adapter. Start the drill slowly, turning the crank until you quickly get the hang of it. Once you get the idea, go as fast as you're comfortable with, but don't go much faster than as fast as is intended (Aagood, fast as you can HAND/FINGER speed. 5 seconds = 1 minute if you're the fastest spinner alive; 20 seconds if you're 100 years old. 2 minutes later you'll see a much brighter flashlight than it would take around 15-30 minutes of boring, monotonous & finger-cramping cranking to do. review_body:
Aesthetically, this is a very nice water bottle. The colored metal construction with attention to detail, like finger grips, give it higher end appeal.

It's slim enough to fit into a regular size cup holder, though tall enough to wobble in a moving car, so I put it in the larger cup holders.

The spout is hard plastic, which I prefer to the bite valves of some other brands. The spout folds for travel and there's a carry handle. Also included is a straw.

Instructions say to hand wash, but I'm lazy. After a few hand washes, I threw it in the dishwasher to see what would happen. Nothing happened, so I've been happily washing it in the dishwasher ever since - everything including the straw.

So far my biggest disappointment is the insulation. There really isn't much, if any. I have another water bottle that is insulated. When it's filled with ice water, I can barely feel the cold. After three days, there's still a smidgen of ice inside. Not with this water bottle. It feels ice cold to the touch the minute I fill it with ice and water, and the bottle starts sweating right away. In fact, it sweated so much, water was dripping onto my electronics in the car. Note to self: cool drinks only, not too much ice.

This is a great water bottle if you don't need to keep your drinks ice cold. It's attractive, not too fat for the cup holders, and I don't need to bite to take a sip.

This product was provided for review by Hydracentials.

review_headline: This is a great, lightweight jacket.
review_body:
I have to admit that I purchased this jacket because it was the only black jacket I could find in my size that didn't picture a logo on the left side of the chest and I needed to put a work logo on it. This one advertised the logo on the left arm. When I got the jacket in, the logo was on the chest! Luckily the embroidery company saved the day and was able to stitch over it, but I was initially pretty disappointed when I saw the jacket was different than the picture. That is the only reason for the four stars. Other than that, I would definitely give it five!

It's been a super jacket overall. I'm 5'6 and 129 pounds and the small fit me very well, just a hair tight in the shoulders, but not enough to bother me. The waist and sleeve length were perfect, and I always have trouble finding garments with long enough sleeves.
I have worn it out on windy days in the 40's with only two light shirts underneath and it did a very good job of keeping me warm. I haven't noticed any wind getting through the fabric and if I'm wearing it inside for too long I start to get hot- and I'm always cold!

If you're in the market for a water/wind resistant lightweight jacket, I would definitely recommend this one. I'm glad I spent the money on a more expensive one; it's worth it.

product_title: FILLABLE CAULKING TUBE, 2 per pack
review_body:
Standard empty caulk cartridge. Product recieved was exactly as pictured. Came in what appeared to be a factory-sealed clear plastic bag. Should last many, many uses for my purpose. I bought these to load with sausage, squeeze out into 3/8" x 1 foot long logs, freeze, then cut into 1/2"-long bits with a knife and cook to make my own sausage 'crumbles' for breakfast dishes. Works great and costs less than half the price of that brand name pre-packaged version.

Another reviewer mentioned using an air compressor to force the end/plunger-cap back out once the filling has been emptied and you want to reuse the cartridge. I don't have an air compressor and that method seems potentially dangerous and destructive to me. Instead, I just bought a 1/4" x 36" solid aluminum rod for $4 at my local hardware store, inserted it into the nozzle, and carefully pushed the end-cap back out (wooden dowel works fine too). If you need a smaller opening in the nozzle tip than 1/4", you may be able to get away with down to a 1/8" rod to push out the end-cap but it would need to be a stronger metal like steal or brass. Also, the end-cap is pretty thin plastic so I found an empty plastic bottle with a thick/heavy bottom, cut out a disc (from the bottom) that was just slightly smaller diameter than that of the caulk cartridge, and I insert it in front of the end-cap after filling the tube so when I push the end-cap back out with the rod, it pushes against a good thick bit of plastic that I'm not going to punch through. Note: make sure the push end of the rod is flat, not rounded or pointed.

product_title: UCO Anodized Original Candle Lantern Kit
review_body:
I was sent two, one came minus the metal base under the candle - needless to say not worth the trouble to get replaced - I made one out of a tin can bottom. The spring under this cap that feeds the candle upwards seems weak. Why does this matter? Well not all candles are perfectly shaped which means the flame is not pushed upwards, then the heat builds inside the tube causing your six hour candle to melt into a puddle in the bottom of the housing in 1 hour instead of six.
With all the bad out of the way onto the good - the candle provides nice light with some amount of heat if needed. (top of candle vent plate gets very hot) The candle is largely windproof and stays lit outdoors and when operating correctly burns consistently. It comes with a small hook and chain to hang up. Disassembly is quick and easy, clean up is not difficult even though I read reviews where that was said to be a problem. I had a complete melt down due to the afore mentioned weak spring - cleaned it out in minutes.
The candle is lightweight and comes with a nice case easily carried in pack. The reflector is odd. It does not fit inside the case - it does add some light for reading but largely seems unnecessary.
I love this lantern when it is functioning correctly - I intend to make a few changes to the spring and for the price think it is still a good buy.

review_headline: LOVE this simple little product-- my kids can FINALLY handle their own ski gear
review_body: I bought a pair of these KlipSkis at a mountain in VT- Jay Peak. I bought them because I am FOREVER looking for a way to let my kids be self sufficient and carry their own gear. And thankfully, THEY LOVE THEM! This is the last ski/pole carrier that I will ever buy (believe me, I've bought them all). They are SIMPLE, SIMPLE and durable too. I've tried the straps with Velcro and I end up spending a ton of time untangling them when we get to the mountain not to mention the 15 minutes or so getting them on and adjusted. These take me and my kids seconds to attach. Also, it's great having the two clips on each side of the bindings (verses a velcro strapping in the middle) because you can use your poles as the handle which makes the weight of the skis equally distributed and they don't tip forward or backwards.. (GENIUS!).... so glad to see them available on Amazon because I am going to get a few more pairs for my nieces and nephews. Next year I'm definitely thinking about them during the holiday season as stocking stuffers. They would be an easy, neat, usable gift for anyone in my opinion. And, apparently there is a problem with their \\"contact us\\" sector of their web site which they claim is being addressed. They also promised prompt shipment of my requested 4 lids - grateful, again, for their prompt attention and favorable response to my request. I am raising my rating by one star for excellent customer service (2 of the 3 stars for apparent high quality materials, design, and construction of the bottle and 2 stars off for the lid: low quality materials and poor design and construction.

UPDAE 4/4/14: Lids arrived in just 2 days (FL to AZ); and, the seller included one of their HydroValve sports bottles for free - now that's customer service! Thanks, Randy. I'm increasing my rating by another star for follow through and above/beyond customer care - and the fact that only the lid remains questionable but would likely hold up under careful use.

product_title: FlexiFreeze Ice Vest
review_body:
I just went for my first run outdoors in a long time that didn't leave me wrecked for a week. I've got Multiple Sclerosis, and if my body temp gets to high for to long, I literally feel like I've been run over by a truck. (Having actually been run over by a truck, I know exactly how it actually feels and am not exaggerating.)

I wore a light running shirt under this, which is pretty much required as the nylon mesh would remove skin if you attempted to run in it otherwise. On a 40 minute run, in 82 degree weather, it kept me comfortable, and let me push a lot harder. I would say that it probably had another 15-20 minutes of 'Cold' left in it when I finished the run.

It's no fashion statement, and certainly isn't going to last 3 hours under load, but for pushing your workouts a bit harder? Yeah, it's exactly what I needed.

product_title: Coleman Instant Screenhouse
review_body:
It's hard to write a single review for this product, because it performed great in some ways and not so much in others.

Successes:
-Easy to setup. Even that first time out of the box, tired, and confused- it went up quickly. With many memories of shoving tent poles through nylon, this shelter was a breeze. (don't forget to use the anchor lines so it doesn't get taken away in the breeze). It does start INSIDE OUT. Thank you reviews!
-Lots of mesh screening keeps away the majority of the bugs. You're outside, some of the darn buggers are smart and will find their way in. Many of them will be kept out however. 4 sides of mesh means 360 degrees of viewing.
-Lightweight and easy to transport.

Failure:
-Not exactly a shelter from the elements. My camper and the attached canopy are a shelter, since they keep out rain/snow/sleet/etc. The shape of the tent is much more like a dome than a square, so only 1-2 people can stand next to each other out of the rain under the canopy. Everyone else is under a screened area, soaking wet.

review_headline: Klean Kanteen Stainless Bottle 18 oz. - Mostly Pretty Good
review_body:
This is mostly what I was looking for, specifically trying to get away from so much plastic, which tend to add a bad taste. This Kanteen type is meant to fit in the normal bike cage bottle holder, but I could tell that it was going to get scratched up pretty quick using the aluminum tube-type of bottle holder. So I switched out my bottle holder with a plastic type (looks more like a cup holder), which works better with this 18 oz. Kanteen bottle.

Lastly, the rubber cap I hope will lose it's smell. There's that characteristic rubber tire smell in the little valve and while it doesn't taint the taste of the water necessarily, you can smell it as you drink so it's kind of the same thing. If you remove the top and taste the water, the water is fine. So maybe, over a short period of time, the top (rubber valve), will become scent free.

review_body: I actually purchased this to prevent our dog from getting mud all over the car seats. I found it to be just what I was looking for. Easy to put on and take off, making washing super easy. I added an elastic strap with clips to hold the part that covers the seat a little better as our dog is pretty excited when in the car and managed to work the cover off. There is a backing on this cover that is rubber like and makes it stay in place really good, but an 85 lb german shepherd can manage to get it off......lol. I just ran the strap under the seat and attached on both sides, stays in place great now. I love that I can take it off easily and wash. And if you need to remove it on the go, no pulling it off over the top and working up a sweat. Very easy and protects your car seats.

product_title: Himal Packable Water Resistant Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Hiking Bag 30L
review_body: This is a nice collapsible backpack.  It's not a good as the nicer packs of course, but if you happen to have on hand with no fancy pack its good. It has a nice amount of pockets but I probably wouldn't buy again if I had seen it in person before.

product_title: Selk'bag Original 4G
review_headline: Get one. You know you want to.
review_body: I haven't had this out to field test it yet, however the materials used and the construction of the bag are well above what I expected. Design features of the bag are great with velcro straps in the right places for personal adjustment. Pockets, vent zippers, and hand access holes seem to be well thought out and crafted. This will be the perfect companion for my hammock camping setup. No more fussing while trying to get situated in a mummy bag in the hammock. The only addition that I might suggest to Selk'bag, add in a drop-seat for those middle of the night nature calls.

product_title: Solo Stove 3 Pot Set - Stainless Steel Camping & Backpacking Cookware Great for Use with Solo Stoves. Lightweight Aluminum Pot Gripper Included.

Overall rating I give is 4 stars due to the bulkiness and no increment marks on the inside of the back.  However, you can't go wrong with adding the set to your gear.

product_title: Timbuk2 Snoop Camera Insert
review_body: I had been looking for something that I could put my camera gear in that was transferable to another bag relatively easy. It fits well in a back pack or a large shoulder bag.  Glad I have it and have considered buying another when I have to travel with more gear.

product_title: ExOfficio Women's Exo Dri Lattice Tank
