product_title: Yaktrax Run Traction Cleats for Running on Snow and Ice
review_body:
I Really wanted to like these. I have run in Yaktrax Pros and loved them. As soon as I got the Run version, I went out for a 5 mile flat trail run entirely on packed snow and ice. After a mile or so I noticed that my left forefoot was slipping just a little, so I checked the fit. Nothing amiss. But the slight slipping happened for the entire run. When I got home I found that I had lost the right one. The straps didn't seem to be genuine velcro, and just didn't hold. The revealing thing about the slipping I'd been experiencing during the run was that the bare shoe that the Yaktrax had fallen off got better traction than the shoe with the Yaktrax still on. The forefoot plastic that the teensy little spikes are on is slippery. Furthermore, a couple of the little spikes on the one that had stayed on were bent. I had run only on packed snow and ice--no road at all.

I contacted Yaktrax and they wouldn't refund my money since I hadn't bought it from them directly, but they sent me a free pair of the Pros--which I already knew are GREAT. I'd mistakenly thought the Runs would be an improvement over the Pros--they are NOT. I notice that Amazon currently has a note about these that says this product is \\"Under Review.\\" Stay away. Get the Pros. If you think you need something more than the Pros, get the Kahtoola Microspikes, which I think securely handle more radical conditions and terrain than the Yaktrax Pros, but are MUCH heavier.

product_title: Seirus Innovation 1426 Womens Ladies Xtreme All Weather Form Fit Waterproof Gloves - TOP SELLER
review_body:
I am a huge fan of the Seirus Hyperlite gloves, but unfortunately I am also an expert at losing them. After losing yet another pair, I decided to give these a try since they're thicker and seemed a bit warmer and better suited for this bitter winter we've had. I'm a cyclist and a moped junkie and low-profile, windproof and weatherproof gloves are paramount to keep my hands warm while I ride. Too bulky and I fumble with brake levers and controls and my keys when I lock my ride up. Too thin and I have to endure the excruciating pain of near-frostbite. The Hyperlite gloves do the job but I wanted something a liiiiiittle bit warmer and much more waterproof. Plus, the Hyperlite gloves don't have that little clip that holds them together when you're not wearing them, which is such a nice thing to have when you're a serial glove-loser like myself.

After having these for about a month now, I've decided I really don't like them at all. They're too snug and don't really allow for any necessary air circulation to keep my fingers warm. They're definitely windproof but that really doesn't matter when there's no way for your fingers to maintain their warmth. The liner on the inside is annoying and bunches up. They're difficult to get on and off. After a long moped ride I wanted to throw them in the trash. They are just too snug to be warm.

I fear it may be too late to return these for a bigger size, which sucks because they were not cheap. I think that if I were to get a size bigger then they would be okay, but the liner is still really annoying. Plus, all gloves should be made nowadays with touchscreen-sensitive fingertips, IMO.

I love Seirus' products, but skip this one. If you live somewhere warmer (I'm in the Mid-Atlantic), stick with the Hyperlites.

product_title: Condor Solo Sling Bag
review_headline: Medium size tactical sling fits the bill
review_body:
I bought this bag new from an ebay store after searching all over for this size tactical sling bag to use everyday, carrying just basic items I like having at the ready, as well as my lunch for work, a rain shell, pair of gloves, field glasses, etc.. I own a Maxpedition Jumbo Versipack that is a wonderful EDC shoulder bag, but the main compartment is too small for what I need, especially in the winter.

This Condor is very well built, the fabric is heavy, stiff, and durable just like all other high quality tactical bags from the top companies. The zippers are big, plastic zippers that are functional, but not as good as the heavy duty zippers found on Maxpedition bags. They aren't quite as smooth and strong as I would prefer, but should be more than adequate.

There are two long, skinny pockets on either side that I haven't yet found a regular use for, but I like that there are small storage areas you can get to from either side without taking it off. The outermost panel that zips open almost the full length of the bag is useful, there are many pockets for small items, the zippered mesh compartment on the inside face of the panel is full length with no partitions or pockets. I don't find it useful yet, perhaps I will.

Inside the main compartment there are two full width zippered mesh pockets on the inside of the outer panel, one on top and one on bottom that are pretty handy. On the back panel there is a full width, padded sleeve big enough to fit a letter size file folders, and would work well for a small laptop or tablet.

The sling strap is well secured at the top, and wide, but very stiff. It tends to dig into my neck a bit no matter how I have it slung, so I wish it were softer or more flexible. It works equally well slung from either side due to the strap system. Since I never use the other strap and connection to secure the pack, I took the top buckle on the strap off and tucked the bottom strap into the handy little sleeves behind the back panel for just this purpose.

There is a web strap sewn into the shoulder strap that routes under the top handle, and connects to a sewn "Y" strap on the front panel. I imagine this is to help stabilize the load & pack when it's full, but I don't use it with what little I carry every day, so it's in the way for me. I imagine others who put more in their pack might find it useful, but I'm considering cutting it off. There molly attachment loops all over the front and sides of the bag are flat and don't snag. I don't use them typically, but I like that I have the option since they're not obtrusive in any way.

Since this is a concealed carry bag, there is a zippered panel just inside the backpanel, with zips on either side to access your pistol from either side you sling the bag - herein lies the bags biggest fault if you are considering this for carry: The zippers for the concealed panel are smaller and more delicate than the already not so perfect main zippers. These should be the biggest, heaviest, smoothest zippers on the bag, like Maxpedition bags, because you need access to that panel quickly & reliably if you need it at all. In addition, instead of a full velcro lining for attaching a web sling holster, the velcro patch is only 3"x5", which doesn't allow you to put the simple web sling holster in any position you prefer.

For these reasons, I would not recommend this bag for carrying. If that's what you need your bag to do, look to the other, more expensive bags out there that are very well designed for this purpose. If, like me, all you want is a good looking, slim yet roomy, versatile, shoulder bag to organize your daily use stuff, this is a pretty good option for the price. While it doesn't truly compare to Maxpedition and other serious tactical bag manufacturers, it is well made, and the only bag I have found that is not bulky, but can carry a lot of gear easily.

product_title: Hutchinson Fusion 3 Tubeless Road Bicycle Tire
review_headline: Great tire - tips for easy mounting
review_body:
I have been very happy with these tires: they handle very well, they are comfortable and you don't get flats. The only negative is that my first rear tire barely lasted 2,000 miles while I used to get well over 3,000 miles from Michelin Krylions.
The big fear that held me back was all the talk about how hard they are to mount. After doing a bit of research and experimentation, here are a couple tips that make the process quite easy:
1- Use valve stems with removable cores
2- Start mounting the tire like any other tire. When you get to the hard part and it feels like the last few inches will never get over the rim, the trick is to use heat (I use a hair dryer) around the tire/rim. Using gloves with a rolling motion also helps a lot (there is a good video on YouTube on this). The tire will mount in less than 5 minutes
3- Use a CO2 cartridge to quickly inflate the tire and seat the beads (they make a very recognizable popping sound)
4- Once sure that the tire holds pressure well, deflate it, remove the valve core, and inject the sealant (I use Stan's injector). Put the core back, inflate the tire, rotate to spread the sealant and you are ready to ride.

product_title: Sawyer Products Mini Water Filtration System
review_body:
I purchased this filter to use while backpacking. I had formerly used a Katadyn Varil that worked quite well, but is much larger and much heavier. This filter does a great job of removing dangerous bacteria from your drinking water and is extremely lightweight. Perfect for backpacking. The 16 fluid ounce pouch that comes with it is on the small side, but works quite well. You might want to consider a second (larger) pouch if you plan to use the filter for more than 1 or 2 people. I especially like the ability to backflush the crud out of the filter using the supplied syringe.
Testing of water flow shows really good flow when "rolling-up" the water bladder to force water through the filter. I'm really looking forward to using it on the trail this summer.

The only potential downside that I see is that the filter does not remove bad taste from the water (it does not contain activated charcoal like my Katadyn). As I see things, this is an acceptable tradeoff in order to conserve weight. If taste is a big concern for you, you might consider placing a small charcoal filter in-line following this one to improve the taste.

Bottom line, great filter and I highly recommend it.

product_title: Outdoor Research Stormbound Mitts
review_body: Okay, so I was hoping that these would be \\"the\\" mittens. I have chronically cold hands and the recent arctic temps here in Long Island sent me searching for warmer mittens. I have other gore-tex insulated mitts and gloves, but my hands were still always cold. Enter these babies with primaloft AND down fill...I thought my hands would be good and toasty, but really, not so much. First of all, the sizing is misleading. I thought I was ordering women's L (based on the info available on the Outdoor Research website and the color:purple), but I really got a unisex L, had I known this I would have sized down as they are on the big side for me. Then the warmth factor comes in and unfortunately, unless the temps are in the high 30s plus range, they really don't keep my hands that warm. Let me clarify, the back/top of my had stays warmish (even in colder temps), but because there isn't any (or seemingly any) insulation in the palm, my fingers are quickly cold from things like gripping a cold steering wheel in my car! Also, I specifically bought mittens because I like when my fingers are free to move around a bit, BUT these have fleece finger separators inside the mitt (I did not see this listed anywhere when I purchased them). Then to make things a little more annoying, the pinkie of the right mitt inner fleece glove always gets stuck or inside out or in some strange position (I really haven't figured out what's happening there), so every time I put that mitt on, I have to fiddle around to try and force my pinkie into the right spot! All in all, these were not worth the high price tag. I thought I was investing in warm hands, but that does not seem to be the case. I would have returned, but testing them in the cold means wearing them.

product_title: Bushbox Outdoor Pocket Stove
review_body:
Tested this stove out at 3600' above sea level, in WV, at around -20 degree Fahrenheit, during the 2014 'Arctic Surge'. Using dead pine branches and old cuttings from a rose bush. Using the Stanley Adventure Camp Cook Set, I was able to boil 20 oz of water from just above freezing to a rolling boil in 19 minutes and 20 seconds. I was not using a wind screen. I later used a folding aluminum windscreen and at around 19 degrees Fahrenheit, using the same materials, was able to boil about 20 oz of water from just above freezing to a rolling boil in 12 minutes 40 seconds. This is not a bad little stove at all. One caveat, keep fuel close by, it can go out quickly if you're not using a windscreen. It folds very flat, about the size of a large deck of cards, and is easy to pack.

UPDATE: I later used this stove, in similar conditions, with a Trangia Alcohol burner, and got water to boil in about 6 minutes. When using an alcohol burner, such as the Trangia, or a penny stove. remove the upper 'floor' of the oven and set the alcohol burner on the lower 'floor' or ashplate. This puts the 'sweet-spot' of the burner flame in the correct place and whatever is on the stove will boil even faster.

product_title: Thule CX1 Child Carrier for Stroller
review_headline: Worth Every Penny and Here's Why
review_body:
With just "reasonable" care I honestly think the Thule Chariot CX Single Stroller may be the last stroller you're family will need for several generations. It is that well made. Everything about the fit and finish of this stroller screams quality. From the design to the sewing and ease of setup, this chariot preforms exceptionally well.

I normally don't talk about price in my reviews, but on occasion the cost of a product requires it be taken into consideration when assessing it's quality. You could buy half a dozen decent strollers for the cost of this one, so why lay out so much money for the Thule?

1. Exceptional design
2. Ease of setup and use
3. Quality of materials and workmanship
4. Flexibility
5. Safety
6. Longevity

Putting the stroller together is as easy as it could possibly be, especially considering the advanced features and design. Everything is designed to "snap" and "click" together. Don't let that ease of assembly fool you. I never got the impression of any connection being "flimsy" or loose. Every point at which one part connects with another feels like it was welded together. This thing is incredibly sturdy.

The Thule Chariot CX Single Stroller is designed to allow conversion from the standard stroller to other configurations (i.e. jogging, cycling, etc.) by the use of conversion kits sold separately. The "VersaWing Bracket" system on the stroller allow for easy, quick conversion from one configuration to another. The connections are made via an arm and sleeve setup with a spring loaded thumb and release button system that really couldn't be easier to use and quicker to accomplish. While I have not ordered one of the conversion kits, the connections are the same as the base stroller design and they couldn't be easier. The conversion kits are also designed to store on the chassis of the stroller when not in use through what the company calls the "click and store" system. It is basically the same concept as storing accessories on a vacuum when not in use.

The wide "wheel base", low center of gravity, oversized rear wheels and front caster wheels make for a very stable ride and incredible maneuverability. The disk brakes and adjustable suspension make for a very comfortable feeling roll and the stroller absolutely stops on a dime. The parking break allows for stable secure parking. Everything on the stroller is adjustable from the handlebars to the suspension.

The stroller has an incredible amount of storage space. The main "trunk" in back holds a ton of stuff. There are also pockets and straps inside and out that allow for even more places to put stuff. There are velcro straps on the back to hold accessory wheels, but they can also be used for diaper bags or other cargo. The venting, sunshades and main opening are accessed via velcro closures and make for a very versatile setup. The five-point harness system locks the child in place and is very quick to engage.

When it comes to portability, I would have to disagree with some of the reviews that say this is a problem for this stroller. The rear wheels pop off in literally one second and the main body of the stroller folds down to a compact package. It does take up more space than the "umbrella" type folding strollers, but any comparison with those things is strictly apples and oranges.

The difference between this stroller and you're average child carrier is the difference between a European sports car and a rusty old beater. In other words there is no comparison. The Thule Chariot CX Single Stroller is truly a marvel of Swedish design and craftsmanship. product_title: Scott USA Men's Fuel Mitts
review_body:
I lost my lobster gloves right before we were forecast to experience a bout of sub-zero temperatures, so I needed something to keep my hands warm on a bike. Since I lost my (more expensive) lobster gloves so easily, I wasn't sure I wanted to pay that much this time, and since these were a little less expensive, I decided to try them instead. I was pleasantly surprised by how warm they are. They are thick and worked well, even during our -15 degrees F lows I had the privilege of experiencing. They are actually warmer than my lobster gloves, which I think is mostly because they have more insulation, though the fact that all my fingers are together probably also helps. These aren't *quite* as good as lobster gloves for biking since you loose some dexterity and it makes shifting more awkward, but it's still do-able and a small price to pay on extra-cold days for some added warmth, I think.

In addition to the above, they appeared to be well made. (I'm sure I will manage to lose them long before I notice their condition deteriorating.) Other reviews mentioned they ran a bit small. I was a little worried, but I have average hands for a male, and the medium fits me just fine. The wrist area of the glove is a little tight, so I can understand the problem others may have. This can be slightly remedied by loosening the strap on the glove that goes around the wrist, but there is also stitching in that area that makes the glove tighter there. They fit fine for me even if I wear thin knit gloves underneath (which I do so I can take these mittens off to use my keys and not have my hands completely unprotected--not because I need added warmth underneath these gloves).

In summary, these gloves appear to be well made and are very warm. I've used them for biking and walking without problem. If you're at all worried about size, you may wish to order one up, but they were fine for me (just a little tight around the wrist when putting them on).

product_title: Doggyhut Large Pet Bike Trailer / Jogger Kit Dog Bicycle Carrier Red 7030201
review_body:
We were looking at several dog trailers and decided to give this a try. Our dog has hip problems, so we're hoping this helps with taking him places with us on our bike.

The Good:
-Easy to Assemble & Disassemble
-Lots of room for our dog to sit down, stand up, lay down, stretch out, & turn around
-Seems well built
-Has built in leash that you can hook up to your dog so you can use trailer with the windows open.

Cons:
-Front wheel doesn't spin - can't make sharp turns - though I think this actually helps make the cart more stable for the dog (so it's probably a good thing)
-Doesn't have wheel locks, so you need to hold the cart steady when loading in and out your dog.
-Wish it folded up smaller when putting it away, but I'll take big and bulky if it means stability and quality for my dog.

Word to the wise:
- Our dog is a medium sized 38 pound Aussie. He has plenty of room and more to breath in this. I would be cautious of using it with a large dog.
- You have to take the time to train your dog to like the cart. We started our dog on the cart with no wheels. Then we started taking him on walks using the jogging kit. This was pretty easy & for this reason I would recommend the jogging kit. We are slowly getting him used to riding behind the bike with someone walking next to him - This is taking a little more work and a lot of positive reinforcement (IE: really good treats)
- Get the jogging kit, it's helpful in the training process even if you end up not using it in the long run.

product_title: Vuelta Corsa Pro Crankset
review_body:
I'm not sure what cranks usually weigh, but these are lighter than the steel cranks they replaced. For a limited comparison I weighed a few of the sets I had.

-This aluminum crank set weighs 40 ounces exactly (I have the 3 gear 170mm option)
-The aluminum cranks I have on the front of our tandem weigh only 32.8 ounces, but they are compact and welded together with no spider, so naturally they should be lighter.
-The Steel crank set this one replaced which only had 2 gears, rivets, and no spider weighed 49.5 ounces (glad to be rid of them).

I bought these to add some more range to our tandem and also shave off a little weight. So far it's working wonderfully.

There are many reasons to consider this crank set: If your compact set is not allowing you to go fast enough, if you need some cheap bolt on chain rings, or if you need to lose the weight of steel cranks. I wouldn't get these if you're wanting something lighter than a set of aluminum cranks you already have, or if you're wanting a really small granny gear.

--Edit--
In working with this crankset I've noticed it holds the chainrings out about a centimeter further than the other cranks I have. I bought some longer chainring bolts and some washers to move the rings back in. This doesn't bother me since I need the extra room for my timing ring, I just found it kind of odd.

I bought an FSA crank off ebay for the captain's crankset that weighs a few ounces less, but it looks noticeably weaker, so I'm glad I have this one for my stoker.

product_title: NiteCore EA8 Caveman 900 Lumens LED Searchlight, Black
review_headline: Disappointing - though stupidly bright as one can get with standard AA batteries
review_body:
My cousins and siblings remember me as the one with batteries in all of my toys ( 1950s & 60s). I've had a thing for flashlights since Eveready advertised a cat w/ nine lives on the wrapper of their batteries. Caution! - Do not look into the beam! Avoid mirrors. I can't give you a range for useful illumination, but this will serve as long as you are not airborne. The maker's discussion of heat-sink design is quite justified. Quite a bit of heat can be felt in front of the lens. After going through the first two sets of alkaline batteries, I opted for 3rd Generation Enloops. Have fun!

April 14, 2017
Deeply disappointed and embarrassed…
I was impressed by reading that Nitecore was a member of PLATO, an industry group trying to hold to a given standard of performance regarding brightness, beam range and output. After my first purchase – the EA-4 – I was delighted in every way.
Then it died when the batteries leaked, ruining the flashlight. Lesson learned, don’t store with batteries installed unless they are rechargeable lithium like Panasonic Enloops. I bought another – what fun and actually very useful.
I bought the EA-41 and it was even better – I gave the replacement EA-4 to my brother and he was impressed.
Time goes by and I bought the EA-8 for the improved reflector and longer run-time. Stunning! I was able to – and I am quite serious – outrange the headlamps of the heavy haul truck at work when navigating in the ND boonies driving to location.
That was so much fun I bought the ‘Hammer’ - now discontinued - for its increased output and added to my stable of rechargeable batteries. I bought the AAA TS-2 for my keychain.
Then they started to die.
I had written glowing reviews on Amazon and cleaned and checked and tried different batteries… and one by one they have all died except the Hammer which is stored without batteries in a drawer.

During this same period I had purchased aStreamlight that was acceptable for use in hazardous locations that ran on the same AA batteries. It actually delivered many more hours of use than all of the Nitecore flashlights put together – and continues to do so.

I am embarrassed by my earlier reviews and my unwillingness to admit I was overcome with enthusiasm.

When new these are bright, fun, work on reasonable batteries and are just cool. BUT THEY DON’T LAST.

review_body:

They are too thick, so I'm kind of kicking myself for not spending the extra $30 on the \\"World Cup\\" model that can accommodate skis of any thickness and has more angle options. If you are serious about tuning and plan to be working on more than one or two pairs of skis, I would definitely recommend spending a bit more and getting the next model up. But if you are only an occasional tuner working on your own skis, these will get the job done.

Another note: the glue holding the rubber pads to the vises is not terribly strong. Both pads on the center vise fell off within a couple uses and I have had to re-glue them. The thicker pads on the outer vises have not fallen off yet, but I can see that they are starting to a bit. I can't speak to the build quality of the World Cup model as I haven't used it myself, but I would imagine the quality control might be a bit tighter.

product_title: Kestrel 3000 Pocket Wind Meter
review_headline: Great Travel Companion for the Outback
review_body:
I got this for primarily for my adventures in the Arizona outback (summer & winter); and it is a good little combination meter, with one caveat. When going from one environment to another very different one, it can take a very long time to get an accurate temperature reading - unless you employ some tricks. For example, when my unit arrived, the outside temp (including the UPS truck) was in the single digits. 10 minutes later the kestrel's temp reading was still 10 degrees lower than my indoor ambient. Once acclimatized, I then took it back out, with the same results: 10 minutes later, it was reading 10 degrees too high. The reason for this is that the temp sensor is housed in a cavity in the fairly solid meter, which is good for protection. But it remains sensitive to the heat, or absence thereof, in the surrounding body of the meter. My solution started with a test: hold it out the window of my car while moving, and an accurate temp was achieved in less than 10 seconds (5 degrees F, at the time). Now, when I change environments I sweep the meter in an arc back and forth for up to 20 seconds and then I get a pretty accurate reading. You might think that being a portable meter an accurate reading would be faster, or that the manual would mention this and advise accordingly - but not so the manual that came with mine. {Note: I subsequently found that the online pdf manual at the kestrel site does cover this - and their info matches my experience closely.} Because, unlike my Fluke digital meter with remote thermocouple, if left to itself in still air, it can take quite a while to arrive at the correct temp - unless you speed up the process in some way.
Other than that it works very well, and its form factor, including the lanyard that passes through the excellent travel case, makes it a very practical travel companion.

product_title: Fenix Remote Switch (TK12, TA20, TA21)
review_body:
First, I will start this review off with a confession and that is I am a big fan of Streamlight and EagleTac products. It is my opinion that you can't beat either one of those manufacturers for quality and price. However, after reading numerous glowing reviews about Fenix lights, I decided to give them a try with the intent to mount one on my Armalite AR 10A4 carbine. After looking at several options, I chose the Fenix TK11 (I will review this item separately). Obviously, I also wanted a remote pressure switch. After doing the appropriate research, I landed on this Fenix switch as being compatible for the TK11.

Upon receipt, I was initially quite impressed. This switch is well made. The light cord is heavy and is quite long which is nice for a larger AR platform such as the AR 10. The pressure pad is oversized which is extremely nice. Especially when the light is mounted on the side of the weapon. I utilize a Magpul AFG and I have the pressure pad mounted right above it. My hands are medium sized but having the pressure pad large enough to merely move up the side of the weapon, like playing a guitar, and operate the light is extremely convenient. What I found really unique, and completely different than the Streamlight and EagleTac products, is in addition to the pressure pad it also has an on/off button on the cap. So, if the user doesn't want to utilize the pressure pad he/she can just turn the light on or off by using the button. This is a nice feature if the user wants to keep the light continuously on.

Now for the disappointing aspects of the product and why I down graded its rating. With Streamlight, the purchaser is provided with different sizes of zip ties for securing the cord to the weapon. In addition, and most importantly, you get heavy duty velcro adhesive strips to apply to the pressure pad and weapon. With the Fenix switch you don't get any of those items. I ended up having to raid my parts box to cannibalize a UTG SCP-LS269 green laser to snag the velcro adhesive strips. In addition, I used extra Streamlight zip ties I had to secure the cord. I think for the price of this Fenix product the purchaser shouldn't have to do this in order to mount the item properly. I confronted the same issue with the TK11 itself when, for the price, the light didn't come with any batteries. The lack of the little things is annoying.

Overall, as I previously stated, I really appreciate the quality of this product. It is well made and has unique, as well as differentiating, features. However, for the price, I just expected more little things. Everything to use the product effectively should be provided. The consumer should not have to supplement the item in order to elevate it to where it needs to be.

product_title: Fashion Moda Women's Wool Cashmere Winter Noble Long White Jacket Coat
review_body:
I ordered this coat before any reviews were written... and then watched in horror as one person after another came in and left these awful one-star reviews. I was sure I was going to have to give the coat back, and started looking into how to file a claim, etc...

But the coat arrived yesterday, and it's not bad. I don't know what happened to the other people's coats... it looks like the one in the picture, it is the size that I ordered; it says dry clean only, which you'd expect for a wool blend...

The main thing is, it is just 30% wool. The rest of it is polyester. This is a lower percentage of wool than you'll find by people like Anne Klein (usually 60% wool).

The second thing is that it's advertised at $65.99, then they charge you $35 for shipping... so was this a $100 coat? I guess I'll see how it holds up. But bear in mind that an Anne Klein coat at 60% wool sells for $200.

I tried the coat on over a sweater. I'm a US size 8, and I bought the XL, and it worked well.

All in all, it's a bit of a bargain, and anyone who was hoping to get 100% wool/ cashmere for $65 is a bit silly, in my opinion... but here are the facts: 30% wool, compared to designer brand 60%; $100 compared to $200. The XL fits a size 8 US very nicely.

product_title: Filzer Chain Cleaner
review_headline: Easy to use by one person and it gets the job done very quickly
review_body:
I found this easy to fill with cleaning solution and then turn the crank of the bicycle to run the chain backwards through the Fitzer. The design is a good one that makes it no problem to hold the lower half of the unit in place and then put on the top and slip over the clamp. I had very dirty chains on my bikes and after running a couple batches of cleaning solution with the first bike it became a simple process.

It took a couple minutes to realize that I needed to keep it in alignment with the chain or it would work like a derailleur and the chain would slip off the large chain ring.

I used a 50-50 solution of Simple Green and water and found that it was very frothy so I diluted the solution to a 25% Simple Green and 75% water and it worked much better.

Cleanup was easy, pulling out the two foam blocks and then running hot water over the Fitzer.

For the price this is an excellent tool that is both well designed and well made and it comes with clear illustrated instructions.

review_body:

review_body: Handy little bag for throwing a camera in. Could do with a couple of extra small pockets maybe. It's also a little too big for what I need but that's my problem/fault I guess for not bursting out the tape measure and measuring it. It is certainly exceptionally well built externally and I'd imagine will outlast the camera comfortably. Maybe a little more padding inside would be nice. Removable padding perhaps that helps those that maybe don't need all of the case and thus, stop the camera from moving around too much. I guess the crux is am I glad I bought it? Yes. Would I buy another one? Yes.

review_body: I bought this item for my boyfriend, he wears it all the time. The hoodie came in perfect condition and fits well.

product_title: Timbuk2 Wingman Suitcase 2013
review_headline: Lots of space, convenient backpack style, packing cubes are a good companion.
review_body: I needed a bag for overnight work (field) trips and I picked the Wingman for three reasons: simplicity, convenience, and because it´s a Timbuk2. I don´t like duffels because things "disappear" within the bag and get wrinkled; in the Wingman everything is on sight and organized. Although the medium size has enough room for several pants, shirts, t-shirts, undergarments, and one or two pair of shoes, it works for my overnight work trips because I carry several extra items needed in my field work. Now, I would appreciate more small pockets within the large ones; the laptop padded compartment is too large (who carry a 17´´ laptop these days?) and the front pocket could be divided into three smaller ones. I also bought packing cubes and realized that they are very useful with the Wingman because this bag doesn´t have good support. The Wingman can carry two large cubes or one large, one medium and one small cubes. The best combination, however, would be two medium (for clothes) and one small (undergarments or toiletries) cubes. So far I have used the Wingman as a carry-on in an international flight and in one of my field trips here in Costa Rica. It was a good purchase and I would recommend the medium size together with packing cubes.

product_title: Childrens Balance Bike No Pedal Push Bicycle for Girls or Boys
review_body:
For 2-4 year old kids, this thing rocks. It is easy to get started, just put them on the bike and they'll start walking/hobbling around on it. A few rides later, they're balancing with their feet up.

Here are some more useful details: if your kid is smaller than 30 inches, this thing is probably too big (even though it looks so tiny). If your child is over 42\\", s/he is probably too big for it. So somewhere between 30-40 inches is my opinion of a good size range.

You'll love the airless tires and how light the bike it (it's gotta be something like 5-6 lbs). It's super easy to transport around, it'll fit in even a small trunk of a small car. You can't go wrong.

OH, it took about 3 mins to assemble!

product_title: Primus OmniFuel Stove
review_headline: Absolutley the best stove I have ever used!  With a few additional accesories I can burn any fuel on this bad boy.
review_body:
I had 3 other MSR stoves I got rid of after getting the Primus Omni fuel. Love it so much I bought a second to keep on hand or take out when I'm travelling with a large group.

Pros
- Will burn pretty much anything! Will even burn butane canister fuel in liquid mode so I can run those in sub-zero weather with no issues.
- I can use the smaller jets in the Omnifuel Ti service kit to really stretch my fuel economy. I can boil 2 cups of 45deg water consistently only using .20oz of white gas, or .30oz of butane.
- I can use the same 3.6mm jet for everything from White Gas, 4 season canister propane/butane, 1lb green liquid propane cans, and the 8oz butane cans you can get at the grocery stores for the little omelet burners. So no need to change jets between those fuels.
-Look for the Kovea propane and butane adapter that will allow you to connect to those fuel sources. The cooktop butane cans run you about $5 for 4 8oz cans compared to that for a single 4 season camp stove canister. And since can run butane in liquid mode you don't need the propane mix for winter weather. But if you want you can get the propane adapter that will let you run the 1lb green cans.
- Will simmer great and adjustable from a candle flame to an afterburner. I can go from making eggs over easy and pancakes, to ratching it up to hash browns or stir fry's.
- Will melt ice chunks in subzero weather (-7deg) and bring to a full boil in about 5-7mins.
- Very easy to maintain with only a single jet and very few parts.
- Love the fuel pump design that means I only have to flip bottle over to evacuate the fuel and in the line and allows me to bleed the pressure out the bottle so I don't get fuel all over me when disconnecting the fuel line or taking the cap off.
- I can remove the burner from the stand and use it in my Trangia alcohol stove set. Just get the Optimus adapter and it works well. So now in the worst of winter weathermy Trangia is absolutely bomb proof.
- Fuel hose is very flexible unlike all of MSR's lines which are like rigid brake lines. I can move my fuel bottle around and I don't need a perfectly flat spot for everything to work right.
- Primus makes a super small 0.35l fuel bottle which is great for a solo camper that is out for only the weekend.

Cons
- Pricey, but I found a very good deal on Amazon for both of mine just at 100.
- Does not come with as many repair/service parts as MSR stoves do new.
- Optional repair kits are not as complete, cheap, or widely available as MSR' or other stoves.
- Can be a bit loud at full flame, but not as bad as my dragon fly. But I do a lot of high altitude cold winter camping. So when its minus 20deg with a 45mph wind that burner at full throttle is the sweetest sound of comfort of a hot meal in a very short time.

With the Omni Fuel I've greatly simplified my cook setups to these and a few Trangia Alcohol burners. Used to be a MSR guy but got sick of the stiff fuel lines and stoves tipping over, and having to have two separate style stove to run multiple fuels and still have true simmer ability. This is the do all stove for me!

review_headline: Small, Light, Useful, Great for Youth Understanding

None real bad.

4 stars because the poor thing is made in china, had inappropriate paint on it, sits unevenly, doesn't close tightly, and proves to be a tad small for a serious fire for any length of time without constant feeding when considering its thermal retention qualities. GREAT VALUE FOR THE PRICE THIS THING CAN KNOCK THE FREEZE OUT OF A CLOSED UP 20x20 GARAGE NO PROBLEM IF HANDLED CORRECTLY

Want to hear about it? Keep reading...
Got it a day sooner than the delivery date suggested in the orders menu on Amazon. This time,the package came in a van rather than a box-truck or step-van type vehicle. It is one of the heavier items I have ordered. At a little over 20 lbs It comes in a plain colored box that claims "stove" and other things on the side that make it clear to whats inside, so Heads Up if you are trying to be discreet.
Easily taken out of the box, I did so outside because the sealed up box said China all over it so I wanted to be upwind and in a field when I let the air out of the box. I had looked around to see where the stove was manufactured and rest assured its Made in China after seeing the print and whatnot on everything. The company that sells them is out of California. All parts were included and went together after I took a small hammer and made some reasonable noise forming the tops of each flu pipe.

See, the flu pipes fit together because there is a flange, or a stretched bigger round hole, on the bottom inch or more of each piece of flu pipe. You get four of these and there is an obvious way they fit together, but as mentioned before, they might need influenced a bit with a hammer or mallet of sorts. IT fits right onto the barrel of the stove and off you go after putting the legs on.

The paint would take a good 2 to 3 hours of a solid fire to burn off. It stinks like a chemical paint/plastic-burn-smell and I imagine will set some individuals off into a headache or make it unattractive to use to those who don't understand it needs to be completely entirely red hot for a good 10 minutes to get that smell from ever happening again (unless you cause it). the paint comes off in little black flakes and get everywhere like ashes would so do it outside. Good temperature-rated paint that will spiffy up the gear should suit some, as to others it looks completely fine as a raw finish, but should still be painted for rust protection and possible thermal benefits.

The stove has a fixed grill type insert inside in the bottom, creating a space for ashes to be raked out with the handy tool that was purpose built just for this sized job. The ashes can be raked out the front by pulling them towards you or opening the slots up located in the very back of the chamber and having ashes fall out that way. The stove is made of a comparatively thin metal, and will not hold the temperature of the fire much at all. The fire can be raging in the back quarter of the stove red-hot for hours and the front be cool to the touch as to handle feeding the fire without gloves. I thought it was nice, but I have plans to harvest the heat before it gets awayinto the air. Far from cast iron with its heat retention properties. Well done for the price in function and availability, I will consider again after we put her to some real testing and customization. I may update sometime in the future and even post a picture or two to the user photos thing If I'm feeling up to it. Thanks for reading. Stand up for the Constitution.

product_title: Selk'Bag 4G Lite +45 Synthetic Sleeping Bag Shadow XL by Mountain's Best Gear
review_body:
Be a yeti!

This bag is GREAT. Really great. Received it as a Christmas present and I have been using it out on my screen porch to enjoy bowl games on TV. I took a nap in my hammock wearing this as well. Elderly neighbor has been peeking out the window at me. Confusing my neighbor is worth the price alone. Love this yeti suit! Awesome to not be confined as I am in my mummy bag.

The chest does unzip on both sides if you get a little warm, and there is a small opening so you can get to your pocket which is handy.

The legs are LONG, but you can move around by pulling up on the sides when you walk, or cinching a string around the ankles. Sure it would be nice if these were built in, but honestly, problem solved with two $2 straps. The "colder" versions of these do have leg straps built in.

As for the review that this is just a good "fun" bag. I disagree. I am a very experienced backpacker. I would suck up the extra weight on the trail to have the freedom of movement. I could see hitting the trail with this and a tarp. This bag is well made and comes with an awesome compression bag. Quality construction and seams throughout. Compares well to my regular bags. Hood is great. This is not some kind of "slanket" that is mass produced and cheap. Well worth the price for the quality. This will last for years.

It packs down really small. It can go down below 45 degrees with a sweatshirt and long undies underneath.

Not designed for jogging, but you can walk around in your sleeping bag, and how great is that!

Hands are easy to free if you need them.

Downsides, and remember I am thrilled with this overall:

Could use a leg zipper so you could vent your legs if they get hot.
Could use straps built in on the legs to make it easier to walk around, but I fixed that.
Could use a bit more insulation on the bottom of the feet. Feet get a little chilly without big socks.
Would love to be able to remove feet. I think the colder versions let you do that. Then, you could wear with boots etc.

product_title: Gore Bike Wear Men's Countdown Gore-Tex Gloves
review_body:
I really wanted to like these gloves. They look good and are made by a solid company, but the overall build is just not up to snuff. I should start by saying they are warm, comfortable, and do keep the wind and water out. I also found that the finger articulation was good. I had no problems shifting and even wore them in a few cyclocross races. They're a little too bulky for fine motor needs, i.e. getting something small out of you jersey, but I didn't expect that from winter gloves.

However, they do have a couple of fatal flaws. First there are two interior liners that bunch up and make it challenging to get your fingers in the gloves when your hands are dry (I know this because I had to cut one of the liners out ...more on that later). When they are wet from sweating it's practically impossible. So, if you take the gloves off on a longer ride, say to get out some money for a snack, or to change a flat and you can kiss the gloves goodbye for the rest of the ride. Fortunately, I usually I had a second pair of back-up gloves I could throw those on a in a pinch. I finally grew so frustrated by these gloves that I cut out the first fleece liner to see what was causing the bunching. The problem is that the two interior liners are only sewn in at the wrist so they get pulled out partially when you remove your hand. When you try to put your fingers back in the gloves, invariably one or both of the liners are so bunched up, there's no way to get them worked back in.

The second flaw is that after a couple of months the gripping layer on the palms and fingers began wearing away in small flakes making it more challenging to shift and making the gloves look horrible.

Finally, they do run very small. I usually wear a large or XL sometimes, for these I needed an XXL.

For the price I expected a LOT more. I definitely wouldn't recommend these gloves if you're going to be riding for any length of time.

product_title: Diamondback 2013 Insight 1 Performance Hybrid Bike with 700c Wheels
review_headline: Just Ok - requires upgrades for longevity.
review_body:
I have the 2010 version of this bike which is pretty similar. You might actually dislike biking if you own this.

7 speed with Shimano Altus derailleur and Suntour crank. The shifting is really poor which is why I'm upgrading components. Lots of noisy shifting, you may feel unsteady if you attempt to stand up on the pedals.

The frame won't take a rear rack without some spacers to allow it to clear the rear dropout area. I wouldn't plan on using a rack unless you want to do some fun tricks with little washers or spacers.

to date I have upgraded:
- seat post; the existing one has only one bolt which allowed my saddle to move out of position.
- wheel set; "Weinmann;" broken spokes and out of true most of the time. The hubs are very poor and not turning smoothly.
- tires, need upgrade. Lots of weird flats & problems until I upgraded the tires.
- grips. These move while riding. I find even on some of the more expensive bikes this is also a problem. Buy locking grips.
- pedals. The plastic ones cracked right through.

I have upgraded the Insight to a 9 speed with new wheels, shifters, brake levers, crank, chain, derailleurs, and a bunch of time and energy. I've been told the V-brakes on this are junk also. This might make you consider getting a nicer ride to begin with. Look at the Fuji Absolute for $500 if you want a good hybrid.

Some good:
frame geometry feels comfy.
Avenir saddle is comfy to me.
Handlebars, stem, fork are ok.

product_title: Energizer Weatheready LED Lights
review_body:
This is the second LED Lantern I have purchased. The first was a \\"Rayovac Sportsman LED Lantern (SE3DLN)\\". They each have strengths, This lantern's is the green on button. It cycles from bright to dim to glow and then off by pushing it. It's kind of rubbery so I'm not sure how it will hold up long term (as in years). I like the concept of using either AA or D batteries. It accomplishes this by including a \\"cage\\" that holds the AA batteries (included) in place. I'm not a battery expert, but I would think the D batteries would be brighter, last longer, etc. But I haven't checked this out. When the AA batteries die, I will probably remove the cage and replace with D batteries. Then comes the quandary, where do I store the cage so I can find it if I want to use AA batteries again? I did not find it as bright as the Rayovac, but it's possible this is due to the battery difference. The batteries are accessed by unscrewing the rubberized bottom, a process I found rather awkward, I'm not quite sure why. Overall, it's pretty decent, I just happen to like the Rayovac better.

8 Jun 14 update. I had to do some work in the attic and used this lantern. I had to hold it fairly low so that I could see the joists buried in insulation for my feet. Maybe about a 5 foot radius of light. The only advantages over a flashlight was the handle and the fact that it could sit on the floor next to the work area. Otherwise, worthless. As a result of my experience I have dropped it to 3 stars.

review_body: I'm a bald guy, so finding good sun protection is important. This hat meets all expectations. product_title: Style Eyes Block Polarized Lens Sunglasses
review_body:
I already owned one pair and bought two more. That's how much I like them. I have a style I'd worn for years, DIRTY HARRY black frames. They're cheap. I buy them by the dozen for under fifty bucks delivered. See, I have this axiom regarding eye wear vs price. IF I buy a $130 pair of Ray Ban Aviators, within a month they will be lost or sat on/destroyed. IF I wear my under five buck a pair Dirty Harrys...I wear em until the lenses get funky and I just toss them and pull out another pair. This could be a year or more. So, what have we learned? That the length of time you will own a pair of sunglasses is inversely proportional to the price of the glasses. In this case, the Style Eyes glasses are in the middle ground, so I'm sure I'm good for at least nine months. :-)
Seriously, they're great shades. What I like is that they are not so dark as many others, letting in considerable more light without bothering my eyes. I also like the style A LOT. GREAT VALUE.

product_title: Jetson Electric Bike Eco-Friendly Lithium-Ion Powered Scooter
review_body:
When you first look at this bike compared to other items on Amazon you will see it's at the higher end of the price range. Initially that had me looking at other cheaper E-Bikes but what kept me coming back was the reviews. When looking at other options I found there seemed to be more complaints than anything else. But review after review people were commenting how wonderful their Jetson bike was. I spent about 24 hours going back and forth on what I would buy but finally decided to go with Jetson. Boy am I glad I did, and I'll explain more of that below.

Ordering/Delivery Process:
Ordering from Amazon was easy of course and the delivery company (JB Hunt) contacted me the next day to set up a time. They gave me a 4 hour window and was there right when they said they would be. As the back door of the truck opened up I saw this large box with a full color picture of the bike. It was freezing cold that day and part of my wanted to run back into the house while they were unloading, but I was too excited to leave!

Packing Job
Inside the cardboard box the bike is secured in a two part steal frame.It took me about 5 minutes to unlock the bike and lift the top of the frame off. I was then able to roll the bike right off.

Initial Inspection
What can I say, the bike was in perfect shape and absolutely beautiful! I was pleased to see so many heavy duty components on it. For example, this thing has better disc brakes then the $1000 mountain bike my friend just bought. The manual was straight and to the point, and as a benefit has instructions on how to take apart anything you wanted on the bike, step by step. I was surprised when I opened up the seat to see the battery, it was pretty light given the power it has. I could easily disconnect it and carry it inside work with no problems at all.

Use
I was going to charge the bike for the 4 hours they recommend but the display said I had a full a charge so I just had totake it out for a spin. One word..... FUN. At the time I was out my daughter was walking home from school and I zipped past her and her friend and honked the horn. All I could hear and I drove away was \\"DAD!!!\\".

I think the bike drives well, has all the functionality of a scooter, but I can go places a scooter can't. You can be driving down the street and decide to take a shortcut down the bike trail. There's no license plates, no DMV registration and no insurance. The goal of this bike was as a replacement for a car when going to and from work. Without any doubt I believe it will do exactly what we intended.

I've had myself and my 14 year old daughter on the bike at the same time, and still had no problems zipping down the street at the 20 mph it states. For those people who don't 20 mph is quick, I would disagree. Usually during the summer I bike 30-40 miles per week on my mountain bike. I use a GPS to see my speed and location. I couldn't possibly keep 20 mph as an average speed, so this Jetson really moves.

Overall Comments
I believe this bike is way ahead of the others I researched online, and worth every penny. I've already emailed the company twice with general questions and the person who answered my emails has requested very quickly. Irving even followed up with me when I was unable to respond in a timely manner, thanks Irving!

I did agree with another reviewer and ordered a metal license plate that says \\"E-Bike\\". These are new, and people are not used to seeing them. For the $9.00 I spent for the plate (ordered right here on Amazon) I figure it might save some questions down the line. Also, since the bike has a mount for it that lights up (nice touch) so why not get one.

I believe this bike is a good purchase and have already recommended it to the people I work with. I work at a University and the students seem to really smile when it drives by. This is the first E-Bike I've seen on campus in the17 years I've worked there. With the reactions I've seen driving by, I believe there will be more people making the switch.

Always remember that most people won't write a good review, but they will complain and complain when something isn't right. If you look at reviews for this bike the vast majority are all positive. I myself usually don't write many reviews, but this bike is so cool that I can't pass up the opportunity.

If you order the bike I hope you enjoy it as much as we have. The only regret my family has is that we didn't order two of them! I know how to share, but when it comes to the Jetson.... Mine... Mine... Mine...

review_body: I've been spending a lot of time outdoors and it's been pretty cold in the Northeast, this is a lifesaver.  It fits perfectly, breathable, soft, and warm.  It covers my neck great which keeps the cold air from running down my back as well.  I thought I might be worried with condensation forming on the inside when I breathe but the material actually wicks the moisture away from your skin.  Very good purchase for any outdoor enthusiast or for anyone that spends a lot of time in cold temps.

review_body:
Seems sturdy and works perfect on my racing bike that doesn't have any lugs by the axle to mount your regular support arms.

Lightweight, well engineered, geat low price, includes a adjustable bungee cord and easy to install. 5 Stars!

product_title: Kijaro Dual Lock Chair
review_body: This chair is very comfortable for watching the kids sporting events. It is larger than most, but that makes it sturdier. It keeps you from slumping down in the chair, MUCH more comfortable to sit in than the regular fold up chairs. It also locks closed so that you don't have to put it in the bag to carry it if you're in a hurry. I would buy this chair again.

product_title: Best Choice Products® 16" Unicycle Red Chrome Unicycle Wheel Cycling
review_body: Great cycle! My 8-yrs-old grandson loves it. It was easy to assemble. The color is vibrant red. Excellent quality! The stand is also great. The unicycle rests in it sudeways. Took a minute to figure that out.

product_title: Wahoo Blue SC Speed and Cadence Sensor for iPhone, Android and Bike Computers
review_body:
This sensor has enhanced my training considerably. It's one thing to ride my bike on the trainer (which is what I do with it most of the time) but having the feed back to measure distance, cadence, pace, etc. makes it infinitely more useful (and fun!)

I've paired the sensor with the Map My Ride app and when I took my bike out on the road for a ride, I was also able to map the route, elevation gain and a bunch of other stuff.

And, Bluetooth is definitely the way to go, especially if you are using it with something like a smartphone app. Much cleaner than the old-fashioned wired models.

product_title: FAB Starpoint Big Boys' Transformers Bumble Bee 16 Inch Backpack
review_body: The back pack was a little bit more than I wanted to spend, but it's halfway through the year now and it has held up really well. My son loves it too. The only thing that has ripped is one of the side pockets for water bottles and admittedly my son isn't the most careful one.

product_title: Klean Kanteen Stainless Steel Water Bottle
review_body:
I was hesitant at first to use one of these reusable water bottles. They're significantly more work. But you save some money and reduce the clutter in your life.

I've hiked with these, and I use them in my day-to-day. They can get pretty beat up on hikes, resulting in the occasional dent and chipped paint, but the bottle remains intact. Most plastic bottles can't standup to the slightest abuse.

NOT FOR HOT LIQUIDS. I didn't but it for this purpose, but I figured I would try it with tea. There is no insulation, so instead of having warm tea, you'll have a burned hand. Also, I'm sure whatever lining is inside shouldn't get hot.

Pros: Saves money, environmentally neutral, probably safer, super durable. Also, no aftertaste after a few uses. Minimal cleaning.

Cons: Cap ring wears eventually, cap occasionally whistles.

product_title: point6 Hiking Tech Light Cushion Crew Socks
review_body: This is a nice weight sock - comfy and warm.  I don't know how they will wear, but so far, so good.

product_title: Intex Deluxe Pillow Rest Raised Airbed with Soft Flocked Top for Comfort
review_body: Easy to inflate and deflate. You wont regret the purchase at the price. Comfortable to sleep on. YOu may have to top it off sometimes as the weather can deflate it a bit. All you do is plug it in and hit a switch. Much better than the old ones you had to do bu hand.

product_title: Thermor Bios Indoor/Outdoor Digital Suction Cup Thermometer (White, 4.25-Inch x 5.7-Inch x 0.9-Inch)
review_body: I love this thermometer.  Stays stuck to window.  Make sure you gave a porch light behind it if you want to see it at night.  I like the high and low temp of the day feature.

The cap is a double layer with a very soft inside. It fits comfortably and kept both my head and ears warm.

review_body: I got this for a ski trip and it was great. Size was great, and it was very comfortable. product_title: Betty Rides Women's Headbanger Band Snowboard/Ski Beanie
review_body: I love this headband. It goes with EVERYTHING. Mine has lasted a few years, but the button just fell off.

review_body: The skates look great. I was thinking the bearings would be better and the wheels but it should be good to start off slow then if she wants I will buy fast wheels and bearings for them which should fit. so yeah its her first set of skates and I think they are going to work great.

review_body: I had heard that SmartWool was getting worse in workmanship, and this was my first experience in seeing it first-hand. I will darn it and keep wearing, but really? No, I do not have needles for toenails.

product_title: Horny Toad Women's Oolong Sleeveless Dress
review_body:
I own this dress in two colors, the gray-ish color and the brown color. Horny toad doesn't seem to use solid fabrics, they generally have a blended fabric with a color and gray mixed together. I'm not sure if this is a style preference or a material requirement (their clothing is very soft and comfotable) but be aware that the color is blended and once you have the item in your hands you can see the color blends.
I own several horny toad dresses, tunics, and leggings. This is the first one I've needed a large in. I'm a DD but a 8 on the bottom. I generally wear a medium in Horny toad so that things fit without being skin tight on top or majorly loose on the bottom. The cut across the top looked better on me in the large, so I simply sized up in this item. Because of that I'd say this fits somewhat small in comparison to other horny toad articles of clothing. The medium to large didn't have a huge size difference, I could have gotten away with either, but the large sat nicer and I think I look more slim in it.

This dress is thin, but not sheer, not overly clingy, and very comfortable. I wear it to walk to dog and window show downtown. I generally wear this dress with birkenstocks, it's a very relazed look. The seams are on the outside at the chest, so the dress is more casual.

product_title: Black Diamond Spot Headlamp
review_body: This headlamp is very bright and has an option for a focused beam or a more widespread, less intense brightness. Bought it for my husband, who investigated several brands and this was the most powerful he found.

review_body: pretty cheap.  not enough velco to make it truly adjustable. my daughter is 5 1/2 and all of the items are quite a big too big for her, just for a size guage.

product_title: Faux Fur Animal Hats Hoods Ski Red Wolf with Mittens Unisex Gloves Scarf with Paws
review_body: We bought this to use for a Halloween costume, but will keep using it all winter, super soft and cute!

product_title: Wide Angle Lens for MagicShine, Gemini, and many other Bike Lights / Headlight. Includes O-Ring
review_body: This is great when mountain biking at night.  I added this to my cree light mounted on my handlebars.  I also have a light mounted on my helmet that does not have the wide angle on it.

review_body:

product_title: ChicoBag Reusable Hobo Repete Shopping Tote
review_headline: Great bag to go or diaper bag!
review_body:

I use a bag organizer inside which organizes all the little things and wipes, etc. It has a big outside pocket that's secured by a magnetic snap. The inside which has the little pocket (that's the pocket that the whole bag fits into) is great for storing my cell phone, keys or backup money, etc. The drastrings on the side allows you the adjust the size of the bag.

product_title: Razor A5 Lux Scooter
review_headline: If You're On The Fence, Red Model Is Better
review_body:
I may have gotten a lemon but I feel like the blue model of the A5 just isn't as sturdy as the red. While I rode my Red into the ground over the course of 2 years I never once felt it was chintzy or unsafe. The same cannot be said about the Blue I purchased a little over 2 months ago. While it has improvements, like a kickstand, the steering column, almost out of the box, came loose and has to be tightened all the time. Worse, it came loose WHILE RIDING nearly spilling me into traffic. And after another adjustment the column is now off center and I cannot get it straight again.

While I LOVED my Red A5, 5 stars all the way, I'm not nearly as thrilled with Blue. Prettier is not necessarily better.

product_title: SoundAsleep Dream Series Air Mattress with ComfortCoil Technology & Internal High Capacity Pump
review_body: Bought this mattress for my son to sleep on while home on college break (during our house renovation). He loved it, said it was very comfortable. I like that it has smaller pockets on top instead of the big 'tube-like' ridges on other mattresses. I put sheets on and they actually stayed on all night. Inflation was really fast and effortless.

product_title: Cressi Dry Snorkel

review_body:

I would have given this 5 stars but one of the units I bought was made bad so when you tipped the light downward it was so loose it wouldn't stay where you set it and instead it just fell all the way so it lit straight down making it unusable. The others are all working well.

product_title: Jagwire Bag of 4 Non-Crimp Brake/Derailleur Cable Ends
review_body: These not only do the job for which they are intended, they look nice while doing it.  Plus, I like the fact that they can be removed without having to be cut off the cable, and can then be put back in place without damage.  Sure, it's a small detail, but still one that adds to the overall look of a bike.

product_title: Kelty Redtail 27 Backpack
review_headline: Great backpack for weekend outings at zoo.  Needs more ventilation.
review_body:
This is an awesome backpack. I bought it for my son who's in 2nd grade. I found myself dumping his stuff out to use this pack on weekend zoo, renaissance festival, Sea world outings. It's light weight and comfortable to wear with the nice wide traps.

It is a little warm and not as ventilated on the mesh for the back side for warm/humid day. My Kelty MAP 3500 performs better in this area. Taking 1 star off of rating for this.

product_title: Intex Deluxe Pillow Rest Raised Airbed with Soft Flocked Top for Comfort

product_title: HopOn Slacklines - The Original - 49 ft and 82 ft (15m and 25m)
review_body: The Original HopOn slackline is a fantastic line that I would recommend to anyone because of it’s wonderful features. Also the fact that it is two inches wide also helps with stability. On the fitness front this slackline is great. It is a killer core workout with all the balancing, and it also gets your legs and arms. It takes a lot of balance to walk all the way across this line. I think this line is great for any level of slackline enthusiast.

product_title: Mountain Hardwear Micro Dome - Men's
review_body:
There are two different sizes. Standard & Large.
I tried on a standard at a local retailer. It didn't cover the entire ear.
Order the large and it fit perfect.

I'm going to order one more.

Hope this helps.

product_title: Svord Peasant Fold Knife Red, Poly Handle, Swedish high carbon tool steel blade
review_body: I did not pay enough attention to the reviews that mentioned the size of the knife (I did note them, but didn't believe them), but those reviews are accurate. product_title: Fenix Bike Mount (Fits lights with 18-28mm Diameter)
review_body: The design of this mount results in a multitude of options to mount a light on a bike. I use this to mount a Streamlight 68201 4AA Propolymer LED Flashlight with White LEDs, Yellow (Amazon Product: B00069PJLA) onto the handlebar on my Voodoo Marasa Hybrid bike. The bike's handlebars have a tapering design rendering most mounts useless. This mount allows me to set the light at an angle that results in a neat beam of light in front.

product_title: Dakine Heli Pro Backpack, 20-Liter
review_body:
This bag fits perfect in all aspects, it has plenity of space for all equipment, food and also for an extra pair of boots,
the diagonal ski carry is a bit unstable but nothing out of normal. very lightweight, and it can also fits perfect in the city.

product_title: Global Vision Eyewear Escort Safety Glasses

product_title: Columbia Boys' Alpine Action Jacket

I wish I had just started with Columbia to begin with. My son has no problems with zippers getting jammed or fabric caught in the zipper and he is staying warm on his walk to school in our current 4 degree weather. Hopefully it's just as warm for him in January when we dip below zero! He also LOVES all of the pockets!

product_title: Helly Hansen Men's HH Dry Glove Liner
review_headline: Good gloves for a good price, runs big
review_body: The gloves are somewhat larger fitting than expected. They are good quality and made well though. I bought them for a costume, but will continue to use them under my boarding gloves.

product_title: Darn Tough Vermont Merino Wool Over-The-Calf Cushion Sock
review_body: These are great !!!  My mother bought a couple pairs for me three years ago. Still hold shape, look like new and wear very well. product_title: Mad Grip F100 Pro Palm Knuckler Gloves

product_title: Carabiner Water Bottle Holder Clip Camping Hiking Outdoor Travel Buckle Aluminum
review_body: My son is always putting his water bottle in his pockets or leaving it around so this is the best stocking stuffer for him! Thanks for the fast shipping!

product_title: Dakine Rider's Gear Duffle Bag, 51-Liter, Nebula
review_body: I am in love with this bag. Perfect size to use as a carry on bag for the plane. Super sturdy and roomy. Also, the nebula color is great. I will definitely considering buying more of these kinds of bags when looking for luggage in the future.

product_title: Bluewave Lifestyle Large Tritan BPA Free Water Bottle Jug with 48mm Cap
review_body: Like other customers, we had an unexpected floor cleaning exercise when all 5 gallons flooded after setting the bottle on the kitchen counter. The bottle is thin and breaks easily.

product_title: Origin8 Compe Lite Bar End
review_body:
Very easy to install and a great price vs the local bike stores. Saved almost half.

Made my hybrid bike at lot more comfortable to ride with another optionally place to set my hands.

product_title: Fenix PD35 Flashlight

product_title: 4MyCycle Bike Cover 210T Extra Heavy Duty – Bicycle Cover Waterproof Outdoor – Suits Mountain Road, Electric and Cruiser Bikes – Black & Silver
review_body: The covers fit fine. Easy to use BUT we notice some condensation on seats when we remove covers. Not enough it can't be easily wiped up but not what we expected. Since we had lots of rain one time and no rain another time we believe this moisture is from condensation. I wonder if the bag was a closer fit at the bottom if this might solve the problem?

product_title: Thule Archway 2 Bike Rack
review_headline: One of the few workable bike rack options for our son's car
review_body:
Our son likes to bring his mountain bike with him whenever he comes home from college. He drives a small sports car so the bike won't fit inside. Plus his drive is 9 hours round-trip; so it was important that we find a bike rack that was sturdy, safe, and dependable for the long haul.

We narrowed the search to the brands Yakima, Saris, and Thule; and each company offers a very helpful \\"fit my car\\" function on their website for finding the ideal rack that will work with the specific exterior design of your vehicle. Our son's car is an Infiniti G35 coupe with a spoiler detail. That rear spoiler really limited what was already a small window of options for the G35 and pretty much narrowed down the workable choices to one Saris rack and three Thule racks.

The Thule Archway was the highest end of the three recommended options and we chose it because of the locking cable. In hindsight, the quality and functionality of the lock wasn't worth the extra money, though. We are pleased, however, with the design and fit of the actual bike rack.

The Archway rack provides lateral support to prevent side-to-side movement of the rack and its anti-sway cages prevent bike-to-bike and bike-to-vehicle contact. The molded rubber pads that come in contact with the vehicle's finish seem to be of adequate size so far to prevent denting.

product_title: Zippo Chrome Lighters
review_body:
Simple, sturdy, refillable, replaceable wick... stamped "BRADFORD, PA. MADE IN U.S.A." which is always nice to see. :-)

What's not to like? I've had and lost a few Zippos over the years... but I've never had one break or fail. Just have to remember to top them off regularly with lighter fuel, which is quick and easy to do. The fuel is the standard-issue stuff like Ronsonol Lighter Fuel you can get at hardware stores and gas stations, and it's pretty cheap if you buy a larger container. The 12oz Zippo brand fuel available on Amazon is also a pretty decent deal--that's quite a few refills and will last a while unless you like using your Zippo as a lantern to read by or something. Which probably wouldn't hurt the lighter any... might get hot, though.

If you're not prone to losing things like I am, a lighter like this one might save you a bit of money over its life vs buying replaceable ones or matches all the time.

Be aware that these lighters are not pressurized like a butane lighter. So the flame does not "jet" out the tip. It's more like a portable candle. So it blows out easily, and if you hold it at crazy angles it might burn your hand. I mostly use it for starting campfires, lanterns and candles, and as a backup portable light source. At those kinds of tasks it is ideal.

product_title: Princeton Tec Remix Pro MPLS Headlamp
review_body: This is one of my favorite headlamps.  I prefer the remix pro, but the MPLS version is also very handy.  The mounting bracket fits solidly, but the mechanism feels just a little cheesy. product_title: BV Bicycle Commuter Rear Carrier Rack  For 26" and 28" Bicycles Frames, Carries Up To 55 lbs, Frame Mounted , Fender Board
review_body:
We bought our daughter a 24" bike for Christmas, and thought we'd get her this carrier rack and a separate back to take the place of the front basket she had had on her "little girl" bike. Even though the description clearly states this rack should fit a 24" bike, the only way to make it fit was if we lifted the seat up all the way. Of course, with the seat that high, there was no way our daughter was going to be able to ride the bike!

To be sure, we tried to attach this carrier rack to our son's bike, also a 24", but made by a different manufacturer and since he is taller, his seat is adjusted a bit higher. We found the same problem, the rack would only fit if the seat was all the way up.

The rack seems well made and would have been more than sturdy enough for what my daughter would have used it for, it simply didn't work for our needs. The two-star rating is because the title of this item plainly states the rack is for 24" bikes, but that is misleading, and ended up wasting our time.

Amazon's return process is painless enough, but it is still a bummer. We didn't replace it, we'll wait until after Christmas and take her bike in to a local bike shop and see about purchasing a carrier rack there.

A special note to anyone that has a bigger bike and intends to buy this rack, it does NOT come with all the necessary hardware that you need for installation. I'm not sure if that is standard practice for bike rack manufacturers since the bicycles themselves vary so much as to how wide the frames are and how the seats are shaped. You will need to set this rack in place, perhaps even bending the two arms that attach to the seat, and then see what size nuts, bolts and washers you will need to work with your bike.

I am not reducing my rating because of the lack of hardware, but any buyers should know they'll be making a trip to the hardware store.

review_headline: These are a necessity for me
review_body: Living in Colorado, these are absolutely an essential piece of gear for me. I am quite clumsy by nature, and there have been times where had I not been wearing these I would have been in some truly precarious situations in the backcountry. These give me the traction and confidence I need to continue hiking all winter. Love how lightweight they are, too; very packable, even when you aren't sure you'll even need them. I've gone many places where I thought for sure the ground would be clear and gotten there and been so grateful I threw these in my backpack! The only reason I deducted one star is because after only one year they croaked. They are still usable even though one part on each snapped, but after a particularly steep and disconcerting hike today where yet another rubber part snapped, I placed an order for a new pair. Not worth the risk to me! I wish they were more durable; even for their reasonable cost, I'd like to see these last through two winters before needing to be replaced. I do admit to wearing them sometimes when there wasn't snow (sudden clearings on the trail), so I am sure that contributed to wearing them down sooner. I will try and be more mindful of that for my new pair. All in all, love these and will continue to purchase.

review_headline: So So So PLEASED with this stroller!
review_body:
Well, unlike the customer who didn't know how to put the front wheel on, this single mother had no problem. Easy to assemble, and very lightweight. Folds easy go throw in the back of a minivan and those trunks are small! I have a 3 year old 35 lbs and a 1 year old 20 lbs and it pushes with such ease I enjoy running now.

Ok so I've read all the bad reviews for this stroller now, and I have to say this is a user issue not a product defect. If these customers read the instructions, they would know to stop, flip the lever, let the wheel flip back and click into place before they continued to run. You CANNOT let that front wheel SWIVEL (like it says in the name) back into the locked position (which means it will at some point be perpendicular to the street). It is just common sense. It is totally safe once you have put the wheel in the locked position, in fact it is absolutely impossible for the wheel to \\"collapse\\" because it is underneath the stroller at that point. You wouldnt close the top to a convertible while you were driving, and you can't lock a front wheel as you are running. It does take a second to get it in place, but I assure you this stroller is not defective and is very safe. If, God forbid, this stroller does throw my kids to the street, I will update my review. As of now, I have put hundreds of jogging miles on this blue baby and had zero problem.

I looked for the perfect stroller with shades that adjusted and cup holders for the kids and myself and I am so glad I picked this one. My ONLY complaint is it doesn't fit in some doorways, but it does fit through my front door. Actually complaint number 2 is the basket underneath sucks... But I love this stroller and it was worth every minute of research. The first review posted on Amazon by the marathon family sold me on this stroller and they weren't lying. This is the perfect stroller/jogger!
