product_title: Energizer LED Keychain Light
review_body:
These keychain lights are fantastic. They are extremely powerful for their size, and I've had more than a few keychain lights in the past decade or so. The shape is comfortable in the pocket, if you keep it there, and it's easy to turn on in the dark. I gave these out to my entire family at Christmas, and everyone has reported back with positive comments - and we all have them on our keychains currently.

They are a very well made and solid, which does make them a bit heavy if that concerns you.

The three modes are 1. always on bright 2. always on dim 3. flashing. I only ever use the first mode, but even at that, it isn't too annoying having the other two modes; if you use the first mode for more than a second or so, the next time you press the button it automatically switches off (instead of making you flip through the other two modes). I guess the dim move would be okay if you had to conserve battery life. The blinking mode might be useful in an emergency signaling situation.

Battery life is a couple of years of brief nightly use and counting.

My last endorsement - the bright mode is bright enough that you can activate it in the dark, let the light dangle down and use a key attached to the keychain to open a door - the light will be strong enough from reflection to allow you to see easily without having to point the light at the lock you're opening.

product_title: Verso Cologne 7-Speed Aluminum Folding Bike, 20-Inch, Blue
review_body:
I purchased this bike on sale for sub $250, so this is reflected in my rating. I think at over $300, I would consider something a little more durable, like a Dahon Uno.

The Bad:
The bike is heavy, has cheap components, and shifts horribly. Shifting cable tension does not stay consistent in any way even after aligning, so my bike only has a few usable gears that won't clink and randomly skip while riding. I've adjusted the max/min of the derailleur, but I rarely can get it into the 7th gear. Not a big deal as that yields a decent speed on a bike like this on level ground (I usually ride in 6 at about 15 mph). After about 4 months of riding, the rear tire blew out. I don't recall over-inflating the tube, but this could possibly be my fault. Also, the left pedal slowly started to get bent out of shape and had resistance to spinning, making pedaling difficult, so I tossed another pedal on there.

The Good:
The brakes work really well, the bike folds very easily, and it doesn't take long to get used to riding it. The 20" wheels make dealing with potholes not much difficult than normal bike wheels. I think most importantly, it has for the most part stood up to some pretty decent abuse for 6 months. I ride, consistently, 40 miles a week on this thing in Chicago weather, so the bike has put up with humid heat waves, thunderstorms, and blizzards. With proper care and maintenance (cleaning/oiling chain, inflating tires, etc.), it has still been going strong besides the issue I mentioned in the cons.

Summary: Cheap components, but folds up nice and does the job with proper care at a very affordable price point.

product_title: Bolle Vortex (Photo Clear Gray, Shiny Black)
review_headline: Good for Night Riding as well as day
review_body: I often bike at dusk/twilight/night and wanted photochromic lenses that would get clear enough for riding in the dark (prime bug-in-the-eye time...).  These do the trick.  The lenses get only moderately dark during bright daylight and those blinding sunsets, but dark enough for me.  Most important, they go completely clear once the sun goes down (which many - most? - photochromic glasses do NOT).  Very lightweight and comfortable.  The little vents in each lens do help a little bit to evaporate sweat on the eyes, but not as much as I'd like.  Oh well, that's the inevitable tradeoff: to protect your eyes you have to give up the cooling effect of wind  ...which on warm days means sweat dripping onto the lenses and murking up your view till you stop and wipe them clean.

product_title: BioLite CampStove 1- Wood-Burning Small Lightweight Stove with Internal Fire Starter, Generates 5W of Electricity for USB Charging Using Excess Heat, 1st Generation, 5 x 5 x 8.3 Inches, Silver (CSA)
review_body: A bit intimidated on a first date with a somewhat exotic, very outdoorsy girl, I needed to find a way to find the right balance of wholesome, fun, natural, and unique...I decided that we would take a hike together in the woods nearby, find a nice spot overlooking a scenic view, park ourselves, make some coffee and enjoy some afternoon snacks. Here is the where the BioLITE Wood Burning Campstove saved the day. I was able to pack it into my bag, along with a small pot, some coffee, sugar, and water - and I was set. When we finally came to our romantic spot of choice, the BioLite served as the ultimate medium to cut the awkwardness of the moment. She was so floored by the concept of a campstove that was not gas-run. Furthermore, rather than sitting together in silence, we had a great time looking around us to find the perfectly sized twigs, wood chips that could properly ignite the stove so that we could boil our water together. Within a few quick minutes we had a pot of delicious coffee, the sun started to set and we were off to the races. Thanks BioLite for enabling me to catch the eye of the girl of my dreams. I know what I'm buying my girlfriend for our first anniversary, the BioLite Kettle Pot - so that our coffee making experience can be complete!

review_headline: Great light output. Modifications needed to work reliably.
review_body:
This light is wonderful for the price.

The light output will beat out a lot of 200-300 dollar lights.

The only issues I have found so far is with the hardware and some of the internal assembly.

The mounting screw came loose on the third ride I took it out on. The solution was to re-install the mounting screw with a drop of loctite on the screw threads. Since then, I haven't had an issue with the mount.

The second issue I had was with some of the soldering on the circuit board. I read a lot about the capacitors rattling loose. What I did was fill the base of all the soldered connections with globs of hot glue. I have used this light on 8 trail rides total and have not had any issues at all. Very happy with the light after the "modifications" I made.

product_title: Magnesium Flint Fire Starter - 3 Pack - Survival Firesteel Blocks with Striker, Camping Emergency Equipment by The Friendly Swede
review_headline: Will last for a long long time.  Fun way to make a fire.
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:mo1FIOLPDVEATOQ]]Just perfect for my son who is a scout. One of the most basic element for survival is to be able to make a fire.

Unlike other magnesium fire starter that looks like an over-sized key, this pack gives you three big 3\\" x 1\\" magnesium bars with embedded flint on one side. This will last for a long time.

Also included are steel chains to chain the magnesium and the striker. The striker can also double as a small saw.

Magnesium is highly flammable as a powder or shavings but not in solid form. So this makes it a safe fire starter compared to matches or lighters. It is waterproof and practically indestructible. Not only it is very effective, it is also a very fun way to make a fire.

How to make a fire:
The only trick is to makes sure you have an ample amount of shavings. About the size of a penny should be sufficient. Have your tinder or paper ready and with just a couple of strikes and you can start a bonfire.

A sample of this product was sent to me for review purposes.

product_title: Pearl Izumi Men's Elite Barrier Convertible Jacket
review_headline: Great Top Layer for Winter Cycling
review_body:
I bought this to act as the top most layer of my winter Cycling kit. Sizing chart was accurate. It's a great top layer, well designed with detachable sleeves for the inevitable warm up you get once underway.

Pretty decent water repulsion. It's good for 20 mins of light rain with little seepage, but the heat retention goes a long way to mitagate the chills of being caught within a deluge.

Honestly, It might be too warm for the gentle Georgia winters. I've worn it a half dozen rides this winter season, and I've take it off ( entirely ) on all but once. Most of these rides have been ~ 45 - 50 degrees. On the 25 Degree ride, I kept it on the whole way.
It's compact and light enough material to cram into the center/back pocket of the jersey underneath, detached sleeves no problems.

Only complaint = I bought two of these, one for myself and one for my wife as we cycle together and she feels strongly that we match... ( both White Jerseys ). The pattern and layout of the ladies version is cooler looking than the men's, not sure why.

-Bruce

review_headline: Very Good Instant Hand Warmer & More
review_body:
Bought one of these for my hunting trip & was a bit skeptical at first because I needed a reliable handwarmer that gets hot & stays hot for long periods of time even out in the fridge weather. My first thought was its alittle on the pricey side for a hand warmer but after trying it I realized how well it suits my needs.

Its Heat not only survives the cold it regulates how hot it actually gets to prevent from getting burned. Has some kind of sensor that triggers the warmer to pulsate the heat in short intervals, which I found pretty cool.

The On Off switch is very handy when Im not using it, great idea for extending the battery life throughout the day. I am impressed how fast this quickly warms up even out in the cold once I need it.

I do use my old fuel hand warmer sometimes but have been getting spoiled with this battery warmer. It is nice not having to deal with smelly fuel leaks & spills anymore. Maybe time to retire it.

Definitely a bonus having a cell phone charger feature too. Haven't used this feature much yet but it is nice to know I have the option if I get in any emergency situation.

This device is well worth it. I would highly recommend it.

product_title: Gil Hibben Alaskan Survival Knife with Sheath
review_body:
Yes it is 420J2 but this knife is going to hold up to some tough use The blade is thick and heavy great for chopping, out of the box sharp enough to cut paper smooth but not shave hair. Some quick fine tuning on the stone brought it right up to a razor.

Cut halfway through a 16" fallen tree in the back in under 15 minutes just clean sharp cuts, no mashing and no dulling to the blade at all. It was very easy to control the cutting. I got one of my cleanest V shapes ever. The grip was very comfortable and if this knife slips wet or dry, your doing something wrong because the finger cuts allow you to hold it tight. No chips or nicks on the blade. if you move forward and use the finger guard you have all the control you need for finer work. This is a well designed knife.

This Knife batons well and took no damage from the Baton. Strikes my Fire starter just fine. This is a true survival knife and much more than just a pretty face. I recently purchased a Schrade SCFH9 and this knife matches up well in every way. This is a well designed knife. Try it , you'll like it.

product_title: Atlas Series 10 Snowshoes
review_body:
irst off I am a big man. I am 6' 6" tap and weigh 270lbs. Bought the biggest snowshoes I could find.
Pros: -Very light shoes
-Strap clips hold well. Never noticed any slipping while walking in the snow.
-Shoes seems to be made very well. Almost every part is riveted together. Tubes seems to big good metal. Straps are good quality. I think these shoes will last for years to come.
-Fit my large snow boots. Size 12.
-Stay in place well walking. Never had strap fall off boot or boots shift in the snowshoe. Watch tube video on how to put on shoes.
-crampon bites deeply. Grabs great as you climb hills.
-heal lifts work great as you climb hills. Feels like your climbing stairs. (though was a gimmick but they work great)
-good floatation. Thought with my weight I would sink far into the snow but they seem to float well. I sink about 4-8 inches depending on the density of the snow. If you are 250+ pounds do not buy shoes shorter than 35 inches.
-snow slides off shoes nicely.
Cons:
-strap loose on top can easily be caught on branches when walking through brush
-release clips are hard to open with winter gloves on.
-Boot bindings are little annoying to get into. They curl in and make it frustrating to get boot into the binding. Maybe after more use the bindings will stay open better.
Love the shoes. For the price think they are hard to beat.

product_title: MSR PocketRocket Stove
review_body:
I ordered this MSR Pocket Rocket Stove and what I received was a beat-up knock-off in a ratty, coming apart at the seams "Shanyou" bag. (I have no idea what Shanyou is, but it's not MSR.)

If you order this stove, inspect it carefully when you receive it. It should not have a domed top piece, Instead the top should be flat with a wind guard divided into thirds. The arms should not be bent, and the stove pipe should be shiny steel, not black something else. It should also come with a red MRS case. If you suspect you got a knock off too, call Amazon and report it. No one needs to have a malfunctioning stove when they get out in the backcountry.

product_title: HealthPro Ultra Lightweight Super Strong Folding Titanium Spork
review_headline: It's lightweight & durable but the handle pops off the spork if you're not careful
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:mo3UU4HMVISZFVP]]The HealthPro Folding Spork is so light you'd think it would snap in half when you use it like a plastic spoon or fork frequently does. But it won't because the spork is made from Titanium which makes it light and strong.

The folding spork is easily packable, only 3.5 inches long when folded and unfolded it's 6 inches long. The handle is not titanium however since it is attracted to a magnet. I believe the handle is stainless steel.

The relatively short length makes it less than ideal for eating out of a freeze-dried food pouch. I also had a persistent problem of the handle coming detached from the spork because the handle ends aren't quite long enough nor bent enough to keep them attached to the spork when you press the sides of the handle in to fold it.

This is otherwise a nicely priced titanium spork that is well-suited for camping and hiking adventures where weight is a prime consideration. It's also at home in a lunch kit as it is reusable and durable, unlike plastic utensils.

This is dishwasher safe, has no taste in the mouth and since it does not conduct heat very well, can be used during cooking without buring your fingers as you hold it,

I was provided a sample for testing and review. If you have any questions please leave me a comment and I'll do my best to answer.

product_title: Tour Hockey THOR BX-PRO Inline Hockey Skate
review_body:
I skate recreationally but I'm almost as good as the average roller hockey player. I wanted something that was more agile, so I got these.

My first pair of hockey skates. I typically wear a size 10.5-11 shoe, and the 9 fit snug. More snug than my shoe. Do consider, you want a skate that fits tightly around your foot. You don't want to feel pressure from all sides on your foot, but I think it's good that most parts of my foot are touching the skate, as if it were harnessed in well. Then the boot really functions as an extension of me rather than a handicap

I mixed the stock wheels with an older pair of rink rat hornets. I think the rink rat hornet is a better wheel, but I only have 4 so I mixed it up. The Milleniums that come with it are really nice too. Better than most hockey wheels out there for indoor, in my opinion. They have great grip and everything. I think the Rink Rats will out last and wear better than these though, and they flex a bit more and get slightly better grip and feel a little nicer since they flex more. But they're almost 2 times the price.

Also am skating on Swiss bearings. These abec 9's just werent up to my standard.

I'm probably still breaking the skate in. everytime I go, it's more comfortable and less work to adjust to my liking and fits better each day. I've only gone to the rink maybe 6 times by now and it's starting to actually be moderately comfortable, whereas the first day on them was somewhat uncomfortable. You gotta give these skates a real chance. Will probably have to re tighten the laces about 3-4 times each time you go to the rink on the first few days. I only do it 1 or 2 times now. I expect these to be more comfortable and maybe even fully broken in with another 6 times at the rink or so. Haven't baked them...might later on

For the price, I think these skates offer a lot! Just wear some socks that go above the skate a good inch or two and you're set to get started.

product_title: Kodiak Canvas Flex-Bow 6-Person Canvas Tent, Deluxe
review_body: It looked like a good quality canvas tent.  It's that, and so much more!!  If you're looking for a heavy duty, easy to deploy tent, built with quality precision, this is it!!  I had a Coleman tent that was passed down to me for years, but it finally had seen its better days.  I opted for the cheaper nylon tents for a few years and had good luck with a few of them, but decided it was time to try and find another heavy canvas tent.  I've used it several times, since ordering, and have zero complaints regarding its quality and design.  The Flex-Bow concept minimizes the need for multiple support poles and makes for an easy, one man deployment and take down.  The key is in getting the floor stretched tightly and having solid anchor points at the stake locations.  Adjustable poles for the awning would be the only improvement that I might consider to allow lowering during heavy rains.  They can be tilted back, but it compromises the door access.  It's seen HEAVY rain and I experienced no leaks.  The adjustable side vents are a nice feature to circulate fresh air with the window flaps up.  All in all, in my personal opion, this is a great tent.  10' x 10' is a lot of interior space, plenty of room for two cots, a table, folding chairs & gear.  The organizers that are included are a nice feature too.

product_title: Topeak RideCase II iPhone 4/4S Holder

Uses about 12% battery on a 40 minute commute while the display is on the whole time. The case turned out to be perfect for videoing the kids on a mountain bike trail, just tilt it up to vertical and turn to landscape then video while riding. The iphone image stability takes out the jitters.
In every day use the case protects the corners of the phone and has slightly raised edges to keep the screen from sitting on a table surface when face down.
Mount and case are well made. Only used on road and slow trail rides to date.

product_title: Suspenz EZ Wheel Step-Up for Kayak
review_body: This did not fit our car tire.  It says it is adjustable, but wouldn't fit under our wheel well. Otherwise, it was sturdy, and seems like it would be a great piece of equipment to help hoist a kayak on to your vehicle.  I only wish we could have used it.

product_title: Smith Optics Tenet Sunglass
review_body: i recently purchased a pair of costa del mar zane from west marine. i bought this as a backup fishing sunglasses. and now the understudy is dominating all my fishing trips.

product_title: Hydro Flask Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle, Standard Mouth w/Loop Cap
review_body: i love this item so much more then the Klean canteen.  The rough outer coating makes it must more appeasing.

product_title: Mac Coupler Propane Bottle Cap MacCaps
review_body: Well made brass caps for small propane bottles - which I occasionally refill so I need to keep crap (scientific term for extraneous debris) out of the valve area

product_title: Ultrafire® Cree 7W 300LM Mini LED One Mode Flashlight
review_headline: Not 300 lumens, but it's still bright!
review_body: And for 4 bucks or so, who cares? Granted, I would prefer that (not sure if it's the seller or Cree who are full of it)they just be honest about the brightness. It's a great deal for the $$, regardless. I think I have 5 of these now...Will  be ordering more so I can give them as gifts this year for the holidays I think.

product_title: Electra Wicker Quick Release Bicycle Basket
review_body:
I bought this a my local bike shop along with a 7-speed Nirve Island Flower bicycle. I was able to attach the hardware without issue and the basket fit fine. It is well made, sturdy and a really nice size. It looks really cute on this bike. [[ASIN:B000QFQA4O Nirve Island Flower 24 Inch Cruiser]]

However, the weight limit is ten pounds. Another issue is that it sits rather high. You will not be able to mount a headlight on your handlebars while using this basket.

If you don't plan on carrying anything heavy and will not use a handlebar mounted light then go for it. It's a very attractive basket. Great for a sweater, water bottle, and small purse. This is the most I ever carried on it. Don't plan on using this if you intend to go grocery shopping, unless you are buying very few things.

product_title: Black Diamond Trail Compact Trekking Poles
review_headline: Strong and light with great ergonomics.
review_body: These are lifesavers on the knees on backpacking missions and long day hikes in the mountains. Makes climbing and descending rough terrain much much easier. The flick-lock feature makes it easy to adjust and the handles don't seem to wear quickly and stay comfortable all day.

product_title: Darn Tough Men's No Show light
review_body: better than smartwool quality merino wool mountaineering socks.  double strength for appropriate layering and strength.  never heard of the brand.

product_title: Lezyne Alloy Floor Drive Pump
review_headline: Probably the best floor pump for the money
review_body: This pump is consistent and well made. It works very well and I have no complaints except that it makes a little squeeking noise when you pump. It functions perfectly well for the price point, though.

product_title: Grizzly Grip Paul Rodriguez Grip One Size Black
review_body: Great item just why does it come with grip tape I was Tripped out at once , but I highly recommend If you like P-ROD

product_title: Morakniv Bushcraft Carbon Fixed Blade Knife with Carbon Steel Blade, Black, 0.125/4.3-Inch
review_body: This is a great knife. This thing was scary sharp when It arrived.  The blade was thicker than the companion model and will hold up real well. It works well with my fire rod. The price was good and it arrived very quickly. Everything I wanted.

product_title: Saris Bones 805 (2-Bike) Trunk Mount Rack
review_headline: Does what you need it to do for a good price. Using it with a Toyota Corolla 2005.
review_body:
I am still glad I bought this product, but BE AWARE, this is a VERY plasticky product. Especially the tightening screws that hold the arms from being able to move horizontally across the bar. Fortunately the vertical movement is limited by a more robust system, otherwise I would worry.

It works fine with my Toyota Corolla. Takes me about 5 min or less to mount once I got used to it after putting it up 1-2 times. Holds the bike VERY securely. I took a 3 hour road trip with two bikes on it when it was brand new, made me pretty nervous as a responsible driver, but it worked really well. I checked the bikes and the rack once I arrived and nothing seemed to have loosened at all.

product_title: Bike Pump by Geared2U - Mini, Compact & Portable - For Road, Mountain Or BMX Bicycles - Presta & Schrader Valve Compatible - Premium CNC Aluminum - Extremely Lightweight
review_body: Great little pump. Attaches easily and works great.  Need extra pumps (does't push a lot of air each pump...but it's small) to fill to pressure, but it's easy to get there.  Great product.

product_title: High Sierra Freewheel Laptop Backpack
review_body: I bought it for my son so he can wheel his books around. I plan on buying one every year till he graduates.

product_title: Swiss Gear Cirque 2 -4LB Rectangular Sleeping Bag (Green/Blue/Beige)
review_body: I got this for my niece's 10th birthday.  She was so excited that she opened it up and rolled around in it...just to get the feel for it, she said.  Very warm and easy to roll up.

product_title: Problem Solvers 7/8" to 1" adapts 22.2mm Handlebar to 25.4mm clamp diameter stem
review_body: Does the safety critical job without drama. No concerns for safety or reliability in a VERY abusive motorized bicycle stock to useful handlebar adaptation.

product_title: TETC CREE XML T6 LED Flashlight 5 Mode Zoomable Torch with 1600 lumens + 2PC 6800mAh Rechargable Battery + Dual Charger + Flashlight Holster
review_body:
I think the people complaining about this light not being very bright are not using the proper batteries. You MUST use the 3.7V Lithium Ion batteries for this light, and you will be VERY pleased with the light. As with all Chinese lights, the lumens are exaggerated. But next to my Surefire 600 lumen, ($150.00), it is not that far off. I would say around a solid 400 lumens, which is terrific brightness for the money. So, this is an amazing light for a package with TWO Lithium Batteries- AND a charger- for about $17.00! with shipping. GREAT value.
Well built, all aluminum, only 11 days delivery from China. This is one Chinese made and shipped product that I am very pleased with.

product_title: Yens® Fantasybag Urban sport sling pack, SB-6826
review_body: The bag is easy to carry, but it disappointingly does not hold very much. Its flat triangular shape limits the items that can be carried.  I have a 'fanny pack' that holds almost as much. I would not buy it again.

product_title: Alpha Electric Igniter Portable Propane Gas Stove Range Camping
review_body: Gas stove range...we had a difficult time igniting until we adjusted the igniter device at the bottom of the burner.  Other than than it worked well and ignited without a problem.  I don't like the red tube because it's thin and cheap looking but it did the job.  We will consider changing this part on the range. This is a large and heavy duty cast iron stove range it holds large pots. I'm very satisfied with this product. We placed a small wire grill on top because the pot we used was smaller than the range.

product_title: NiteRider Solas Tail Light
review_body: I got this light just in time!!  Caught in a rainstorm and my taillight was the brightest and most visable of the group of riders.  The different flashes are attention catching.

product_title: 6pc Throwing Knife Set & Wrist Sheath
review_body: This set is not bad.I mainly got them for utility work.They work well when cutting paper with the tip , I checked the sturdiness in them and i wasn't 100% happy with them. I wouldn't try prying anything with them using the blade part, I guess you could use the handle for that.The sheath is ok but try not to raise your hands up, or they will slip out. All and all it was worth the cash and they will work for what I need them for.

product_title: Diamond Plate Mens Plus Leather Embroidered Patches Outerwear Vest
review_body: Fit perfect. Look awesome. I ride every day to my job with out any problems. A lot of people ask me about it to buy one. Thank you.

product_title: Pedco UltraPod II Lightweight Camera Tripod
review_headline: Just as good as the original!
review_body:
I've owned the original since 2004 and use it A LOT on GoPros, PNS cameras, microphone mountings, slave flashes and many other things.
This one is just BIGGER, not that much heavier at all! Velcro strip on this one is removable though. I like that!
VERY STRONG AND STIFF. This is awesome! I honestly can't believe just how light, durable, strong and reliable this thing is!!!
And it's MADE IN THE U.S.A.

CONS: None! But I do have a tip for people who use ANY Ultrapod of device with rubber slip overs for feet:
SUPER GLUE THEM ON. ;)
That's it! That's THE ONLY issue I have. I say this because my Ultrapod (original form 2004) slip off sometimes and superglue fixed that. With the UlraPod II I have NOT had this issue AT ALL.

Great company.
MADE IN U.S.A.
Strong
Light
Dependable
LOVE IT!

product_title: Brand New Taya Women's Cycling Underwear with 3d Padded Coolmax of Riding Pants (L (26"-27"))
review_body: These are great.  I wish I could find a pair without the bike padding just to wear around the house!

product_title: Under Armour PIP Escape Lightweight 1/4 Zip II
review_body: Fits well and the little pocket is very convenient. Keeps me warm without getting hot during a longer fall run.

product_title: JCS Glass Filled Delrin (Plastic) 3-Slot Belt Buckle
review_body: plastic clasp is stron and has never broken on me, but clasp doesn't stay secured when closed (using nylong belt) PROS: it's plastic and wont rust, seems to be strong enough that it wont break, just doesn't offer enough pressure to stay closed.  Has come lose on me on more then one ocassion and I constantly need to retighten several times during a dive.

product_title: SeaSense Deluxe Canoe Carrier
review_body: The foam blocks have good firmness to them but could be a bit softer. I did not need the strap but it was included anyway. The cutout in the blocks were a bit narrow for the ridge of my canoe, so I had to trim them wider and deeper.

product_title: Stanley Stainless Steel Classic Mug
review_headline: A great dishwasher safe easy to clean mug.
review_body: This is a great desk mug.  The large base relative to its short height make the mug very stable.  This stability combined with its lid means no worries about spills.  The double wall stainless sides are ok for heat retentsion however if this was truly a concern it would probably be more efficient to have a smaller lid resulting in less surface area there to loose heat through.

product_title: Continental Grand Prix 4 Season Road Clincher
review_body: Most don't think it makes much difference but having top notch tires not only increases speed more than one might think, but also greatly increases traction and safety.

product_title: Dakota Green Mini Clip Microlight Watch
review_body: I got this watch for my 13 year old grandson.  He loves it and wears it everywhere.  He likes that it clips to his belt loop.  It's a good looking watch that has so far (three months and counting) stood up to the normal wear and tear of a 13 year old boy.

product_title: Third Eye Bar End Bicycle Mirror
review_body: Works good. Super easy install. I'm just wondering if a little more convection would be better...I'm tempted to stick a car wide angle mirror to see if its better...might be to much, things might be to small.

product_title: Ultimate Survival Technologies BlastMatch Fire Starter
review_body: I have never used a flint to light a fire in my life. I had a fire going right after I got the blast match out of the packaging. Great quality & easy to use even for beginners.

product_title: Gatorade 32 ounce squeeze water bottle
review_body: this was the best water bottle ever. used it for everything. it was really cool and fun. blah blah blah

product_title: Pearl Izumi Women's Select LTD Sleeveless Jersey
review_body: Oh my gosh!  This jersey is SO cute!  I bought the Maui Flamingo and couldn't wait to put it on; the pink flower pattern is so pretty and feminine.  For hot days it is very cool and on cool days I just wear my Pearl Izumi Infinity Shrug over it to cover the arms and shoulders for a really cute combination.  I'm 5'6' and 127 lbs and the large size fits me perfectly. I just LOVE wearing it!

product_title: Streamlight Stinger XT / POLY STINGER Flashlight Open Top Leather Belt Carrying Case Holder for Police / Security Duty Belts
review_body: the leather is too loose for my stinger flashlight. The light seems to fall out of the pocket quite often.

product_title: Kryptonite KryptoLok Series 2 Integrated Chain Bicycle Lock
review_body: This is an extremely beefy and impressive lock.  I own a nice bike that I park daily on a huge University campus, and tend to look around at what other bikes are using.  Trust me, bike thieves are gonna go for any other bike on that rack before they mess with this bad boy.  It is heavy, but I'm big guy anyway so an extra 8 lbs doesn't really matter to me.

product_title: Topeak Hexus II Multi-tool
review_headline: Like a Quality Swiss Army Knife
review_body:
Nice quality to it. Only light on number of features. Perfect for what i need.

Note: If u want only the stuff you need this may be for you.

If you want something that has everything you need, and all the otherstuff that you may forget that you need and then some, then this isn't for you. (like the the difference between Victornox Swiss Champ vs the Victornox Tinker).

product_title: Magnesium Fire Starter: Spark The Fire LLC
review_headline: Great for all sorts of outdoor activities requiring quick and easy fire!
review_body: This fire starter is a reliable tool. Every time I tried to strike the two pieces together, sparks immediately flew out in the direction I was striking. My only complaint is that after using the starter repeatedly, the magnesium portion of the starter seemed to be whittling down a little. I don't expect this to be a problem for most customers, however, as most will not use the product as vigorously. The coating scratches off very easily and then proceeds to strike just as effortlessly. I would recommend this Magnesium Fire Starter to anyone who needs at least a back up plan for starting fires as it is incredibly easy to spark.

product_title: Slackers Value Series Zipline Kit
review_body:
I put this up between two large oaks, 60 feet apart. The cable was as described more than long enough, instructions were clear and all the parts were there. It took only a short time to put this up with simple tools. One area that needed addressing was the excess piece of cable that I cut off at one end. I used an angle grinder so it wasnt difficult but its something you may need to do (or you could wrap the excess up in a coil and hang it on the tree).

The pulley/trolley was excellent and all metal, I bought a disc seat and hung it from the trolley (I had to enlarge the hole slightly to get the carabiner through)

Compared to going to the hardware store and trying to build this from scratch this was much easier and probably about the same price.

Im 180lbs and it handled me just fine across our 60 foot span, I dont doubt for a minute that it would be fine across the full 90 feet.

100% satisfied

product_title: Tribe Provisions Durable Diamond Lock Rip-Stop Nylon Adventure Portable Hammock
review_body: I purchased this as a camper in a region of the country with plenty of trees and uneven, rocky, or overgrown ground. The thought of being able to carry my bedding in and sleep off the ground between two trees was enticing.  First thing I did after its arrival was to test it by setting it up under my second story deck, climbing in, and taking a nap.  It is strong, double-stitched for durability, lightweight, easy to set up and use, and comfortable.  I am thoroughly impressed so far and anxious to get out and use it somewhere a little more wild than my back yard.

product_title: Portable Pro Aluminum Mechanic Bike Repair Stand Bicycle Workstand
review_headline: A great workstand for the price
review_body: The workstand works well. Adjusts easily to grip different seat tubes. It's light weight and folds up for easy storage. Being able to raise the bike to different heights is a great convenience. The tool holder and handlebar support are useful. The only thing that could be improved would to be to have the base a little wider and more stable.

product_title: Neosport Mens 2mm Sock
review_headline: Good value, would buy thicker next time
review_body: The socks were comfortable and sized just about right. Hard to go wrong for the price, but in the future I would purchase a thicker set of socks, at least 3mm. I can't call to the durability of the socks, but they never felt cheap.

product_title: Vapur 0.5 Litres Anti-Bottle
review_body: my wife uses this more than me, she fills and carries in her handbag and when empty rolls it up so takes no room. we like it so much going to get a larger sized one as well. Recommend

product_title: Ledge Sports Gooseberry Hydration Pack
review_body: Bought this in anticipation of Tomorroworld. It pretty much saved my life for the 5 days that I was there. I put so much stress on this bag and abused it horribly. The only reason I took off one star is because the top ripped at the seam after the 5 days. Otherwise the water bag did not leak and the zipper was solid. Good product, would definitely recommend at this price.

product_title: Aqua Lung Sport Diva Lx / Island Dry Snorkel/ Trek Fins / Snorkel Set - Teal, Small
review_body: After spending the entire summer trying to find a true no-leak mask and dry snorkel I purchased this set. Perfect! Perfect fit mask with no water leaking in. The snorkel is as it is described, no water in there either. The fins are awesome because they are short enough not to cause problems getting back in the boat, wide enough to keep you moving even against a medium current, and oh so easy to take off and put on.

product_title: Royal Robbins Women's Gracie Tank Top
review_headline: best shirt ever!!! If there was a Royal Robbins store in my town, I would be there , , , , , , all the time - seriously great!!
review_body:
SERIOUSLY NICE FABRIC, WASHES UP GREAT, IS LIGHT A BREEZY AND DIFFERENT AND WONDERFUL
AND I DON'T USUALLY BOTHER TO WRITE REVIEWS!!! LOVE THIS BRAND

product_title: Goal Zero Whisper USB Powered Fan
review_headline: It is USB powered.  Fan, Not so much.
review_body:
Pay close attention to the size listed.
This fan barely moves the air at all.
Would not buy it again.

product_title: Schwinn Child Carrier
review_body: It was a perfect fit for the bike and my Grandson, all safe and sound for a nice bike ride with Mom.

product_title: Arctix Women's Insulated Snow Pant
review_body:
These were described as having an adjustable waist so I went with a medium .
The waist was not adjustable however and the pants had a good bit of extra room in the waist I was not expecting .
I decided to keep the medium anyway and tuck upper layers inside .
The length was fine for me at 5ft. 6 inches .
I had this brand of snow pants before & they wash beautifully and come out ready to wear .
I wore a layer under them in frigid weather and found them to be warm and comfortable unlike the stiff snow pants that make you feel like a stuffed robot .
You cannot go by the measurements but I would recommend these .

product_title: Ding All Sun Cure Sanding Resin
review_body: My skim board bottom was peeling and I smothered it in this and it seemed to do the trick. Good product.

product_title: HDE® Grenade Shaped Aluminum Tire Valve Caps - Set of 4
review_body: Love the grenades, but are a little larger than I thought and stick out a bit farther than I would like.  Other than like them a lot.

product_title: Snow Peak Titanium Spork
review_body: We use these sports for pretty much everything.  They are perfect for ice cream - especially if you have a tendency to bend your spoons.  The shape is nice, the tines perfectly pointy, and the bowl can still handle soup!

product_title: Spyder Men's Troublemaker Pant
review_headline: Aewsome fit and great winter clothing line
review_body: Product fits as expected and is very flexible and keeps your legs warm on the coldest days, very well priced

product_title: O'Neill Wetsuits Men's Epic 3/2 mm Full Suit (Black)
review_headline: Does what it says it will do. Great price
review_body: This is my first wetsuit and I am very happy with it. I don't have anything to compare it to since it's the only one I have but it works exactley as described. it was extremely tight the first time I went out but after a few outings it fits perfectly. I use it mostly for kayaking so I'm not submerged for long periods of time but just to test it out I went for a swim and was warm in 58 º Water. I also bought the oneill heat booties and got them and the epic for under $150. The booties run really small so get a size or two bigger. This suit is way better then I thought it would be. Looks good. Killer deal too.

product_title: Kuhl Men's Rydr Pants
review_body: Kulh really does make a superior product.  I now own two pairs of the Rydr pants and find myself neglecting my other pants.  Well, reinforced with a great fit.  *** One Item of Note: This pant comes in Khaki but it is not as pictured.  Kuhl's Khaki in this pant is more of a green color.

product_title: Chums RPS Nylon Rope Eyewear Retainer
review_body: I use them daily, easy to find my glasses. Wish they were a little longer, but they do the job.

product_title: Camelbak Eddy Bottle 0.75-Liter/25-Ounce
review_body: This water bottle is perfect! I love the color and how easy it is to drink from. The bite-and-suck mouth piece is a perfect design to help prevent leaks. It is also lifetime guaranteed by the company which is awesome!

product_title: Igloo Marine Breeze Roller Cooler
review_body: Used it on the beach and it worked well. Rather small but we knew that going in. Good value for the price.

product_title: Craghoppers Men's Nosilife Convertible Trousers
review_body:
I have say that these pants are just brilliant! Having just completed a trek to Everest Base Camp, when they were worn for 12 days straight, I can honestly say that these pants were perfect for their design brief.
They are extremely comfortable, both in fit and over a large range of temperatures and environments - although they are definitely made for slimmer framed people. They do wick moisture well, dry quickly when wet and the insect repellent system does work.
The pockets are well located and good for carrying a range of items, the zip off legs are well made and easy to remove and reinstall.
The small touches, like a dry bag pocket or the extra belt loops that unclip to allow hanging of caps etc, show how much thought has gone into the practicality of these pants too.
I highly recommend these to anyone planning some serious trekking.

product_title: Bell Dawn Patrol LED Headlight
review_body:
It's a nice light to be seen on your bike. Don't expect to see the road with it though.
The CONS:
-the ON button is too sensitive and this light frequently turns ON in my bag/pocket, which can drain my battery faster
-too bad you need a screwdriver to change the battery.
-the lock to fix the light to the holder did break in no time. Hopefully the light still stick on the holder even with the bike vibrations due to the bad roads in Chicago

product_title: Coleman Heritage Big and Tall Sleeping Bag
review_body: Just like the old Coleman bags I finally retired after 20 years of faithful service. If the materials are as good as they appear to be the new ones should last just as long.

product_title: Big Skinny Men's Curve Bi-fold Wallet
review_headline: Wallet GOLD front pocket carry for those of us who hate sitting on our wallets all day long.
review_body:
I have had a few big skinny wallets, this one like the others does not disappoint.

The curve really does help with front pocket carry. The slots are deep enough and seem to work well, the rubber coating is great and everything is nice and secure.

Pro:
SLIM
Lightweight
Holds a lot and keeps a low profile.
Curve works great with jeans or dress pants to help reduce the awkward square front pocket wallet carry
Rubberized inside works great keeps things nice and secure. No issues with cards falling out (I had another big skinny for almost 3 years and when cards started falling out a quick clean of the wallet solved the problem, they are seriously high quality).

Con:
The curve has one less pocket than the previous ones I have owned, but its not an issue all my stuff still fits.
the little logo (raised little rubber logo) on the front is supposed to be to help you grip and pull the wallet from your pocket. I have never needed it and don't like it, it gets caught on other things (like a phone) in my front pocket. While it may void my warranty, I remove it first thing (its sewn on). I have talked to other big skinny customers who leave it and others who remove it, its all personal preference.

product_title: Magnet Steel Bike Bicycle Indoor Exercise Trainer Stand by FDW
review_body: This did exactly what I wanted, allow me to ride my bike when outside is inconvenient. Sturdy, easy to assemble even though the picture instructions were not the best.  Would recommend this to anyone.

product_title: Chicago Women's Rink Skate
review_body: Price is right, quality is right, shipping was prompt. They look good and fit well. Ordered one size smaller than I normally wear based on reviews and recommend doing so. Very good basic skates for casual use.

product_title: Phantom Aquatics Adult Speed Sport Mask Fin Snorkel Set
review_body: Finally found a swim mask that fits!  Good quality, nice case, used it all summer in our pool and at the lake, and really like it.

product_title: Coleman Cooler Soft with Hard Liner Mix
review_body: I got this cooler for work. I'm a delivery driver and the summer months are brutal. It has been impossible to keep my lunch cold in a 120 degree truck.  This cooler keeps it all cool. No more warm Ham sandwiches :)

product_title: NowAdvisor®Q5 CREE 240 Lumen LED Bike Bicycle Headlight Torch
review_body: Really useful when biking at night. It lights much better than other bicycle lights I've used and uses less batteries.

product_title: Outdoor Research Alibi II Gloves
review_body: very comfortable,we will see how they hold up,seem to be well made and seem to be a good warm glove.

product_title: Shimano CS-5700 105 10-Speed Cassette
review_body: I have been using Ultegra and more recently SRAM cassettes.  Admittedly, I didn't look up the specs for the 105 cassette, so it shouldn't be a surprise that it felt somewhat heavy.  I picked it over the SRAM 12/27 simply over price.  In retrospect, I should have spent the extra money.  The spacers are a lot thicker than both the SRAM spacers and Ultegra spacers.  Granted the spacers are probably just one element that makes it feel a little bit heavier than other cassettes in my inventory.  Oh, well... it's just a cassette for a training wheel, so I think it will be fine.

product_title: Hydro Flask Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle, Standard Mouth w/Loop Cap
review_body:
love it!

i have only used it for hot contents so far. not sure if it keeps the temperature quite as long as they say it would. but definitely still very happy with it. the orange colour is a bit darker than photo.

the standard mouth size is a bit too big for me. will consider buying a second unit with a narrow mouth instead.

product_title: RAD Cycle Products Bike Lift Hoist Garage Mountain Bicycle Hoist 100LB Capacity (2-Pack)
review_body: Product works great!  Hooks seem a little flimsy but have had no issues with this item yet.  No problems! Great

product_title: Platypus SoftBottles with Push-Pull Cap
review_body: lighter than most bottles, when empty, takes up little space. I have not used it long enough to know if it is a pain to clean, but excited to have it with the features mentioned above.

product_title: Suisse Sport Yosemite Tent
review_headline: It withstood high winds at the beach
review_body: We camped among motor homers with hundred thousand dollar rigs at the beach last month.  Big winds came up in the middle of the night.  Next morning all the nice RVers came to check on us.  They were amazed that this Suisse Sport tent held up.  The winds were probably 28 mph sustained with gusts to 50 mph.  Of course, we had brought some big-time tent stakes with us from Summit Hut.  Also, we purposely kept the screens open to let the wind through; thus, we got sand and grit inside; but simply swept it out next day.  We had our tall Coleman air bed, queen size, in the tent and there was still room for a huge cooler and all our bags.  I like that you can stand-up in this tent, even with a queen size mattress.  We did not use the cloth room divider; only little kids would appreciate that item.  Can't comment on water resistance - we had no rain.  This 5 person tent is a taj mahal for 2 adults.  We plan to use it about 4 times per year for 4-5 days per trip.  I expect it to last 2-3 years; and for the price, I'll be very satisfied.  Re putting it up - yes, it needs 2 people to get it up in 9-10 minutes.  One patient person can get it up in 20-25 minutes.  Whether one or two people, just be patient and enjoy the craft of tent camping!  Everything that was supposed to be in the box was IN this box upon arrival and we got it back in the original bag, too.  Si se puede.

product_title: Reelight SL100 Flashing Compact Generator Bicycle Headlight and Tail Light Set
review_body: Needed to bend the magnets closer together so they could connect and took 1 hour to install. Works great though after installation. Flashes every time the magnet goes by the light if it is close enough. No charging or batteries needed.

product_title: Arbor Fish Cork Skateboard Completes, 38 x 8.75 x 27.75-Inch
review_body: As a family of 8, we can never have enough long boards. We own 2 Arbors including this one and they have proven to be favorites with everyone. I purchased this originally for my 13 year old, but her 15 & 17 year old brothers fight her for it. Great build and performance right out of the box!

product_title: Serfas Thunderbolt USB Headlight
review_headline: Very nifty, unique, and bright light.
review_body:
Pretty nifty light. I only removed one star, because they should have attached the rubber straps on both sides, not just one. Sometimes when removing the light, the straps will fall off. A minor annoyance, but I don't see why they have to be detachable on both sides except to be replacable. But they could just have the holes on one end be somewhat smaller so they could be removed, but wouldn't fall off by themselves.

product_title: Blank Slate Slim Climbing Trainer
review_body: See updated update below.  I don't like to leave a less than stellar review, because this seems like a nice company, and the construction and design of this are very good.  However, it isn't really suiting my purposes because the doorways I would like to use it on are close to a corner, and the cross bar on the unit is too wide, and hits the adjacent wall of the corner, so that it won't fit in place.  Only works on doors with about 5 1/2 to 6 inches lateral clearance beyond the door opening.  I have only one door like that in my apartment, and it isn't the one where I want to use this.  I'll go buy a length of oak 2 x 2, drill some holes, and use it instead of the metal tube cross piece. Note:  I have one of those common, inexpensive pull up bars of similar doorway hang design to this.  The cross bar for that isn't as wide, and works in every door of the house.  Blank Slate-- change the length of your cross bar!  Update.  Rather surprised to have experienced continued frustration.  Got a 2 x 2 wooden cross piece narrow enough to fit in the doorway (clears the adjacent corner wall), replaced the manufacturer's metal crosspiece with it, and discovered that the torque on this thing (when used with a Metolius hang board) is high enough that no matter how hard I tighten the bolts on the crosspiece, they slip under pressure.  Multiple hours into this thing, and I still don't have it working.  I suppose plan C is to get a hack saw and shorten the metal crosspiece, but this will be a serious pain.  Update to update:  The BlankSlate company, upon seeing this review, contacted me and arranged at their expense to send a 36 inch cross bar.  They are seriously cool, I would urge anyone to do business with them.  I understand they will consider changing to a 36 inch cross bar as standard for their product.  You maybe should check with them if you are hoping to use this in a corner doorway.  Update to update:  While I still commend the company for their customer service, after anextended time I'm unhappy with the thing.  As was stated by other reviewers, it just isn't stable, and the torque on the thing is very high when you hang from it, causing the bolts to slip no matter how hard you tighten them.  Also the cross bar destroys the door frame, again due to the high forces.  Nice try, but this thing really isn't suitably functional.  I took it down and mounted my hang board directly on the wall.

product_title: Aeris F-10 Free Diving Watch V2
review_body:
Once this is setup it is great.

The Bad...
The alarms(beeps)are a little hard to hear if there is background noise. A passing boat or school of parrots nibbling will over-power the beeps. They should have put the alarm on the front by the LED.

The LED could also be brighter same with the dial. Also the entire dial should blink if the alarm triggers. The dial light should have used UV LEDs and with a florescent background. That would have been much brighter than the \\"night lite\\" luminescence.

The band .... The band is too inflexible and not at all adjustable. My Helix band snaps on and then has a ratchet to tighten down to the correct tension. I get the feeling this band will break every time I put it on and take it off.

And finally the controls....Designed by someone who thought that complex is good. The controls are NOT intuitive. Make one button for mode another for steps and another for adjustments. This is easily the worst part. The instructions a real laugh. Also like complex... cryptic must be good. The time each button or combination of buttons are pushed also sets the modes. No simple way to go back a steep.

Go to youtube and watch the tutorials to get the best ideas how to set the computer and the best startup settings. It is easy to chain the dives together into one dive so check out the vid's they are great. (BTW the links from the install disc are broken!!!)

NOW the GOOD...
This is what you got it for. The best variety and quality of alarms and data. Depth alerts (3), Dive time....yada yada. Tons of great alarms. I couldn't get the first depth alarm below 10 meters so that must be a default.

The surface interval and most other aspects (too numerous to mention) let you have a ton of information during and after the dive. Sitting at the plate and getting feedback is easy. There is a historical recall of the last 100 dives and it tracks the current dive number, so it is great to track for training and safety.

Anyone who has used a watch or scuba computer will really enjoy this dedicated computer for freediving.

There is a shoulder strap on this bag. The sewn sections on the end of the bag that the strap clips to are not holding up to the weight of my gear, and I can already see the stitching starting to tear away from the bag.

The reason I didn't give this bag a 1 star, and almost gave it a 3 star, is that for the price I wasn't expecting too much. But if I had to do it over, I would get a different bag.

product_title: Hammer Single Serve Gel Packets (Pack of 12), Chocolate
review_headline: Almost as good as unicorn tears...
review_body:
No really. If you are a distance athlete, you know what I mean about the almost spiritual aspect of mid-race food when you really need it (credit to The Oatmeal for the unicorn thing).

I struggle, because I hate carrying stuff with me when I run, but almost all the conveniently packaged sport \\"food\\" (gels, shot blocks, etc.) make me really sick. \\"Real\\" food--like a peanut butter and jelly sandwich--would be ideal, but those tend to make a giant mess when you try to pull them out of your fuel belt and nosh on them at the same time you are weaving and dodging other runners on a hilly course. Most of the time I just suffer, and struggle through the massive wall I hit without food. However, a couple weeks back, I was running a race that I really wanted to hit a PR on, so had to figure out nutrition to prevent the bonk.

This did it. I won't lie and say you should buy 12 to frost your next birthday cake with (no, it's not quite that tasty), but it's pretty yummy when you are 50 minutes into a hard run. It's very easy on the stomach. I drank a small cup of water on the course to wash it down, and didn't have any problems. I had one \\"dry\\" (i.e., without any water) on a long run last weekend and still didn't feel like it upset my stomach at all.

If you are experimenting with different gels, give this a shot. I like it better than anything else I've tried, and I've tried A LOT of brands looking for something that didn't make me hurl. This is pretty much the holy grail of sport nutrition as far as I'm concerned.

product_title: Opinel N Degree8 Boxed Garden Knife, 8.5 cm Blade
review_body:
I bought this as a curiosity and a bit of nostalgia because I remember my grandfather owning the traditional No8. I was pleasantly surprised when the knife arrived. The fit and finish exceeded my expectations and the blade was sharp enough to shave my forearm clean of hair. I have carried this knife for a few weeks as an EDC blade as well as whittling. I have been impressed enough to order a second opinel with the traditional blade and handle shape that I have been carrying for the past week.

Out of the two Opinel designs, I prefer the spear point blade shape as well as the tapered handle of the No8 Garden Knife to the \\"traditional\\" opinel. Because of the blade and handle shape, I am able (with a bit of practice)to open and close the knife one handed. I am considering adding a thumb stud to make one handed operation a bit easier (at this price point, why not experiment with it...).

A great knife, well worth the price.

product_title: Pedego White Comfort Cruiser Classic Electric Bike with Red Rims and Black Balloon Tires
review_body:
I love my electric bike. While living in Austin it saved me an incredible amount in gas, time and traffic frustration. In fact, the year I used my Pedego I only filled my truck up four times. That's it ... all year. Four tanks of gas.

Now for the downside.

The tires needed an immediate update. While riding on the usual Austin trails, sidewalks and bike lanes I was always getting flats. Five over the course of the year.

The underside of the seat is made of plastic ... one side of which broke so I was constantly riding a bit sideways until it would pop back into the slot. There's no way to fix it. I'll eventually replace it. How'd it happen? I'd been incorrectly grabbing the seat and the handle bars to pick the bike up with .... apparently that's not how it's done. You have to grab something beside the seat to pick up the nearly 90lb bike. The bike has a weight limit so make sure any of your larger friends know that. I'm pretty sure the plastic seat is why.

It's a little on the noisy side taking off. Something, somewhere scrapes .... shang ... shang.. shang. shang shangshangshang ....... quiet.

You'll eventually need fenders.The lack of fenders on a bike this expensive seems a bit cheap to me. Until you get fenders you're going to get wet ... it'll happen. Mark my words.

After only 8 months the ignition / locking mechanism on the battery is starting to get finicky about when it wants to turn. Luckily I've moved from Austin and don't have to lock it up as much as I used to so the issue hasn't been rising to \\"problem\\" status of late.

The flipping kick stand spring mechanism broke on one side and started tilting. So now the bike tens to stand when it wants or fall over other times. It's parked in a garage now, leaning against a wall so it's not going to fall over now but be careful of the plastic part of the kick stand.

Thats all I can think of for now.

It's still a greatbike but it has some issues.

product_title: Park Tool FR-5G Cassette Lockring Tool with Guide Pin
review_headline: Not Shimano ten speed cassette compatible.
review_body:
I could barely get this to grab an alloy lock ring for a ten speed Shimano cassette installed on my Sturmey Archer CS-RK3 3 speed internal gear hub with cassette.
So at first I assumed it was because of the cone nut inside my hub; but alas the alloy ring was stuck to the tool once removed and was barely fitted inside it.
Bottom line: it's a well built tool that works great for brakes and probably works good for older Shimano lock rings; but it is not what you need for a ten speed Shimano M-771-10.
It will work in a pinch for the cassette; but will mar your lock ring.

product_title: Granger G-Max Footwear Universal Waterproofer
review_headline: Great job protecting hiking boot leather
review_body:
About nine months ago, I began doing weekly day hikes in the mountains - 6-10 miles, 1,000-2,000 feet elevation gain. I bought a really good pair of hiking boots with Gortex lining so they would be water proof for the numerous stream crossings and wet vegetation along the trails. Many years ago, our family had been serious backpackers and we all used Sno Seal to waterproof our boots. Before applying Sno Seal to my new boots for added protection, I did some research and learned that Sno Seal treated boots cannot be resoled as the heavy wax in Sno Seal prevents the resoling adhesive from working reliably. Several hiking websites recommended Granger G-Max so I decided to give it a try. I am happy to report that G-Max works great.

I spray a heavy coat on my boots every 3-4 weeks and let it dry overnight. There is no need to wipe it off though keeping a towel under the boots is a good idea as the excess G-Max will run off a bit. Prior to using G-Max, I noticed that the leather in my boots absorbed quite a bit of water on wet days and during stream crossings though the Gortex lining kept my feet dry. After using G-Max, the leather does not absorb the moisture likely resulting in longer lasting leather. The G-Max treated leather gets surface wet but not soaking wet as happens with other hikers boots on the same trails. G-Max really works for me and I certainly will continue to use it.

The screen comes off with enough force, I think this is a good thing in event of crash to prevent facial lacerations. There's no obstruction to vision whatsoever and I forget I have a screen in front of my face sometimes. It's ride-able at night but I wouldn't recommend it due to its slight darkening (very slight). The sun shading is not quite as effective as sunglasses but much better than the naked eye, plenty for my normally sun sensitive eyes. It's very nice not having to put sunscreen any where near or above your eyes!

My head is 59cm and I actually went with a medium (large was just too big). It's extremely tight, but wearable.

Hopefully more Casco helmets will be available in these here United States, I want them all.

product_title: Stansport Lantern Wire Mesh Globe
review_headline: wish i'd have found this years, and many glass globes, ago...but might not be good for ice fishing
review_body:
i can't tell you how many glass globes i've broken. the last one made it almost 6 whole hours. i was pretty ticked off and when i searched for some sort of relief from my clumsiness, and i found this.

it worked great. it did everything you'd think it would. if it cut down on the light any, i couldn't tell. i feel like propane lanterns are crazy (often annoyingly) bright anyway. the screen did get discolored from use, but who cares? i will say that i have not yet tried it in heavy wind, but will come ice fishing season. i'm pretty sure some aluminum foil will fix any issues i have. and, for all the money i'll save on glass globes, i can buy a wind screen.

oh, and i put this on a standard coleman 2 mantle propane lantern. it also fit some cheap ozark trail 2 mantle propane lantern i had kicking around as well.

edit: 3/21/14

after taking this out ice fishing this year, i found a weakness. it was pretty cold, close to 0 deg F, and my lantern just wouldn't go. the other lantern, with a glass globe, worked fine...like every other lantern i've ever used on the ice. what actually happened was ice must have built up somewhere inside, b/c after repeated attempts to light, it finally did...by the knob on the valve. not cool. i took it home, disassembled and cleaned it, and got it to work fine in the garage. i think it was just too cold.

i'm taking off a star because not working in the cold is no good, but only one because i imagine this won't be an issue for most people.

Contacted the seller and they took forever to respond then made no concessions on the error.

product_title: Go Plus Outdoor Pop up Tent Portable Changing Tent Camping Toilet Room Privacy Shelter
review_body: If you tent camp this is a must have!  We bought this for our annual spring break trip (have two teenagers).  We used as a shower house.  We bought a portable shower head and pump and we didn't have to go without taking showers.  The teenagers thought it was a great idea. review_headline: Featuring subtle but juvenile gross out comic motifs. Fun helmet!
review_body: Great looking graphics.  So, it's a helmet.  It can only look so good.  I measured my head and according to the extremely specific Bell sizing chart that I found online, I ordered a large.  It fits perfectly.  Wear a helmet so you don't spill yer brains.  I recommend this one.

product_title: Zebra Two-tier Tiffin Box and Food Carrier (12 cm)
review_body: I usually bring my lunch to work and I found myself bringing two or three separate containers which just was inconvenient and felt disorganized.  This two-tier tiffin was a great purchase because it holds more than I expected and it's really easy to use.  This is my go-to lunch container.  It's great that it's made of stainless steel, not plastic that leeches who knows what chemicals.  I even get people commenting on it and asking where I got it.  I will probably get a second one for my husband.  Just make sure to keep it upright if you have liquids and wash with a soft sponge or cloth, scour brushes might scratch its beautiful finish.

product_title: K2 76 mm Wheel (8-pack) /Abec 5 Nylon Spacer
review_body:
Initially I chose K2 over other brands because my previous set of K2 wheels (78mm 78A) served me for ~6 years. I skate about 20 minutes each week (until recently), so I was quite happy with those wheels. I had to change because they were starting to wear out: friction increased between bearing and wheels so that the wheels make huge noise when I skate, and speed obviously is impaired.

I had expected these new wheels to serve me, if not for 6 years at least for one or so, but after ~2 weeks of use the surface cracked and they were quite slow (observable friction when you turn the wheels by hand), some even slower than some of my 78mm 78A wheels. Maybe it's because now I skate 1~2 hours each week outdoors on uneven, asphalt surface, but still, quite disappointed since these wheels are not cheap.

product_title: SanWay Waterproof Bike Light LED 3-Mode Bicycle Tail Light Lamp
review_body: Just as described, REALLY bright!!!! Can even see them glow in daylight. My kids love them!!! Can't beat'em, for the price.

product_title: Nintendo Reversible Mushroom Backpack
review_body: My daughter loves Mario. She is a H.S. freshman, this bag holds her 3" binder, a couple of folders & lunch box. She loves this bag!!

product_title: JanSport Classic SuperBreak Backpack, Hedge Green
review_body: Just as described - perfect for my Junior, even with all their books!  lasts well and is sturdily made.  Definitely recommend this backpack.

product_title: The North Face Womens Arctic Parka Black Size Medium
review_body: Item received in a very timely manner, even for being overseas, it arrived faster than I though it would.  Won't have a chance to try it out in cold weather while I'm still here in Kuwait, but I expect it will keep me very warm through New England winters upon my return back to the states.  I'm 5'7, 150lbs and bought a medium in order to have room for layering if need be.  It fits well, not snug and not too loose.  Material looks and feels like it's high quality.  A bit more than I wanted to pay for a coat, but am sure it's one that will last me a few years.  The one draw back is that the hood isn't detachable.  I would prefer to have the option to take the hood off as the fur feels a bit itchy.  Other than that, it's an excellent coat, would definitely recommend to others.

product_title: Limited Edition Water.org CamelBak Groove Water Bottle (Blue)
review_body: Let me start with this.....This water bottle is pretty awesome.  I fill it with the water from the water fountain at work (which normally tastes like metal) and voila!, no more metal taste!  The only problem is that it's hard to suck water out, although it's not too bad; when you are really thirsty, I suggest drinking from a cup.  Other than that, I'm happy with my purchase, I can't even tell you how much money I've saved by using this bottle instead of buying bottled water.

product_title: SealLine Baja Dry Bag
review_headline: Durable, well priced, and does the job!
review_body: While some of the smaller SealLine bags are a lighter material, this has the feel of a thicker, rubberized material. It does the job very well. Floats while fully loaded, keeps out any and all moisture, and is made of a very durable material that I cannot imagine wearing out any time soon.

product_title: JanSport Sliver Shoulder Pack
review_body: My daughter loves this bag it's a good size for a 4 th grader.  She can fit all of her things in it

product_title: EagleTac D25C Clicky Titanium Neutral White XM-L2 LED Flashlight
review_body:
One of the brightest and smallest pocket/keychain lights you can buy. Period. Compare the lumens and size to other lights and you will have a very difficult job finding another light of keychain size that puts out anything near what this light does. It has a extremely simple to use, yet very diverse interface (lots of modes all extremely easy to remember and quick to get to). It is made of top notch material and build construction. It has a gorgeous neutral white beam (floody like you would expect from a light this size, with big wide hotspot and tons of spill all around). You can pretty much light up everything directly in front of you...out to about 40 yards or so. The light dissipates very rapidly after that (you can't expect a lot of throw distance with such a small reflector, not even with this much light being thrown out). It also has a top notch pocket clip (low profile, bolted on so it isn't coming off, in jut the right place to put it deep in your pocket, and just the right tension).

And, the icing on the cake is that it is build from solid titanium polished to a mirror finish...GORGEOUS to look at.

If you want one of the best EDC (everyday carry), pocket, keychain lights on the market, then get one of these. You will not be disappointed. And, if you want the benefits (strength, corrosion resistance, etc.) and beauty of titanium, then get the titanium version of the Eagletac D25C clicky.

I would also recommend getting some 16340/RCR123 rechargeable batteries. They will increase the brightness even further (nominally to the naked eye), and could increase the runtime (they have them up to 750 Mah). AND, you are going to want to use this light, play with it, show it off, etc. so rechargeable batteries give you guilt-free use (you don't have to throw them away and buy new ones everytime you run them down....just pop in another rechargeable, and throw that one on the recharger).

This is currently my favorite light....it really is that impressive.

product_title: Pearl Izumi Men's Cyclone Gel Glove
review_body: These gloves are great in temperatures down to the low 40's.  The are thin enough and flexible so that there is no problem feeling the breaks and operating the shift controls.  The gel pads have reduced numbness in fingers and hands when riding for long periods.

review_body: Son was into the "Brony" thing for a little while (2 months) and then got over it. It's a fine shirt for a fad, but don't expect it to have much lasting value.

review_body: Bought this to feel prepared for any need that arises where I will need the basic need of man, FIRE.

product_title: 2013 SR Suntour XCR Bike Fork Remote Lockout Disc V Brake MTB 26" 1-1/8" Black
review_headline: great value fork for upgrading that non-dampened pogo-stick
review_body: My bike an a super low end budget fork from the factory (nothing more than a coil spring) so do damping to speak of. This fork is miles better, the remote lockout is super easy to use (but don't forget to unlock it for the rough stuff, ouch!) One neat thing that many of my buddies that ride higher end bikes hadn't seen before is the ability to lock the forks in the downward position. This is insanely awesome for super steep climbs where the bike wants to wheelie over backwards. I can't describe how much easier it was to pedal up some hills that I previously had to walk up. They aren't super fancy and they aren't made for jumping, but if you just want something to take some of the abuse off your arms, this is a great mid-range fork.

review_body: I bought this Dakine Garden Day Pack to use for work. It's just about the perfect size (not to big)...although I wish it came with just one extra compartment. It's very stylish and feminine without looking too girly. I work at school as a teacher's aide and found this bag to be just the perfect way to carry my lunch, a book, a cellphone, sunglasses, my kindle, pens & a few smaller items. I wish it came with a cellphone pocket on the strap...then it would be absolutely perfect. If you need bag to carry lots of books, this might not be the best choice. It's a very cute smaller bag.

product_title: Coleman Basin 20 Degree Sleeping Bag
review_body: It is a nice sleeping bag.  I bought it for my child who likes the plush foot area and the cozy hood.  My child will be out in a tent this weekend in 42 degree Fahrenheit weather.  I am hoping that it will keep my child warm during an outdoor camp out.  I'm not quite sure it is thick enough, it feels like old fashioned polyester batting, but maybe it is some new high tech fill.  The down side is that it barely fits in the stuff sack.  More over, it has to be stuffed into the sack since there are no cords to tie it or loops to hook together the sides.  The Coleman brand usually has these useful packing tools on sleeping bags, and it is one of the reasons I went with this product.  I am a bit disappointed.  I was also disappointed that there seems to be a white dried drool mark near the head opening and a few bits of tiny twiggy debris in the foot area.  The box was clean though and the warranty paper came in the box.  I would probably have exchanged it for a new bag, but I was to last minute ordering it-- my child needs it this weekend.  I'll just give it a good wash and add an extra blanket to my child's pack.

product_title: Schwinn Discover Women's Hybrid Bike (700C Wheels),White,28"
review_headline: Incredible deal for a great bike
review_body:
This is a perfect cruiser /leisure bike and an incredible deal! I bought this for my girlfriend and she loves it. We've logged a few hundred miles on a few dozen trips already. Her cruiser actually requires less maintenance than my mountain bikes that come with 10X the price tags.
I'm used to doing bike maintenance and I'm relatively handy so assembly was a breeze. It came mostly pre-assembled. I had it together in 10 minutes and it took another 15 minutes to tune-in.
Hybrids are pretty difficult to shop for and I checked everywhere. Other alternatives were just bulky road bikes or jenky mountain bikes. It's a great blend of practicality. Everything is intuitive on it's use. It does well on hills and flats.
I would recommend purchasing head and taillights if you ride in low visibility. Additionally, slime tubes for the tire size are hard to find, but amazon sells those as well.

product_title: ExOfficio Boxer Brief Mens
review_headline: Confortable and fast drying like the advert states

I washed them in the sink and hung them to dry without rolling in a towel and they were ready to go in the morning. I blotted with a towel but didn't roll and stomp like the instructions in a humid area and they were still dry by morning. Good find, I'll get another pair for the next trip.

product_title: South Carolina Gamecocks Kolder Kaddy Can Holder
review_body: Of course girls love glittery things... especially when your favorite team is included! I would recommend this can holder, great buy!

product_title: Smartwool Kids' Hike Medium Crew
review_body: These fit pretty large on my son's size 9.5 foot, but with hiking that's ok. They look really worn really fast, as other smart wool products do, but they are durable so far.

product_title: Howard Leight Laser Lite Foam Earplugs No Cords (20ct)
review_headline: Leaves a pink stain in your ears.
review_body:
Functionally speaking, as earplugs, I have no problem with this product. They fit my ears well and block out an adequate amount of noise. I did not experience any discomfort when using them.

However, the next morning, a cotton swab from my ear came back pink. The next time I wore the same pair, I checked this again, and it happened again. So, clearly, these plugs are leaching some sort of pink dye into the ear canal, which is somewhat disconcerting. I'd love to assert that this is probably harmless, but I'm unqualified to make such an assertion.

In retrospect, I would have preferred to have purchased an earplug that did *not* leave some sort of chemical dye behind in its wake. No other earplug I have tried has ever left a stain inside my ear canal. Thus, I do not recommend this particular earplug, unless pink ears is what you're going for.

product_title: Big Agnes Whiskey Park 0-Degree Sleeping Bags (Quallofil)
review_body: Listen, I DO Love this sleeping bag BUT there are definite 'issues.' Mostly it's that you NEED a sleeping pad with it, to fill in the back of the sleeping bag which is nothing but thin parachute material, however if you do have something in between you and the ground such as a sleeping pad (insulated for sure in the winter because of the backs thinness) or bed, rest is SWEET. Also, it's pretty bulky and takes up quite a bit of room in your pack unless you have an amazing condensing bag (which I have yet to find for the size I got which is Large and Long). All in all though, I really love this bag. I love Big Agnes and am very pleased with it's quality, durability and delivery. I've slept with this bag out in the snowy cold winters of Oregon and am very satisfied with the warmth that was kept with an insulated pad in it's perfectly fitting back. The zippers are awesome, if they catch the material it's easily released! I just love that in products. Any who, try it out test it for yourself, as for me I'm satisfied.

product_title: P-Mate Female Disposable Urine Director
review_body: I discovered these a few years ago. I am ancient and find they are so helpful not just in the wild but on the airplane and airports. Because of my age it is difficult for me to get up and down. With P-Mate I don't have to sit and don't have to worry about getting on my feet. Don't leave home without them.
