product_title: Tower Paddle Boards Adventurer Inflatable 9'10" SUP Package
review_headline: 2 extra inches thickness really worth it
review_body: I own a sevylor samoa inflatable and now just got the tower adventurer. Im not a heavy person (170 lb) but im really glad i moved into a 6\\" thick board. The tower adventurer doesnt flex as much as the sevylor and is way easier to use. Would definately recommend, although i am not sure whether the Tower will be as durable as the sevylor (the material is a lot lighter and thinner), only time will tell, but so far ano excellent board.

product_title: Topeak Dyna Pack DX with Rain Cover (Black)
review_body: I have been using this pack for about 6 months and 1300 miles and I can really say that it is great.  I've put a gallon of milk and a couple other items in it, and I usually carry work clothes and spare tubes, CO2 cartridges, tools, etc.  I do have to leave a pair of shoes at work because those will not fit in the bag and I'm afraid it might overload it if I stuffed some in there.  But for those not wanting to get panniers for their bike or their bike doesn't have the proper mounts for panniers (like mine) then this is a very lightweight and affordable alternative.  I have also posted a picture for a size reference.

product_title: Zippo Brass Lighters
review_body: This Zippo is as advertised. Made of high quality brass. Nice feel and balance, heavy duty and well made. The Zippo lighter is classic!

product_title: The Friendly Swede Carabiner Grenade Survival Kit
review_body: Not sure what's in it, not sure if I wanna open it, but I am so glad to have this as a back pack. It is small light and convenient.

product_title: 10-Piece Galvanized Steel Tent Pegs - Garden Stakes
review_body: I used these to stake my tomatoes and peppers for stringing.  No problems at all and they are galvanized so I will reuse them for years to come.

product_title: Light My Fire Swedish FireSteel 2.0 Scout 3,000 Strike Fire Starter with Emergency Whistle
review_body: Hard to get a fire going with this. Took many strikes and a lot of tries. Ended up using something else.

product_title: Zippo Wallet - Genuine Zippo Brushed Stainless Steel RFID Blocking Wallet
review_headline: Good concept, didn't quite do it.
review_body:
It's a good concept, really. But I see two real problems with it, one of them potentially really bad.

The annoying problem is that the cards are really difficult to insert and remove because the rubber is way too grippy. It needs to be grippy to hold the cards in, but it's one step away from tape.

The BIG problem I see is that the card-holder causes your credit/bank cards to be bent at really bad angles. especially when you have it in your back pocket and sit on it. This will quickly break down the card and cause it to break, which is something I have experienced with another wallet.

Overall, it's a good try on an RFID-safe wallet but it missed.

It holds just about the same amount as the Sharkk (and other similar branded) metal wallets, so this just ends up being an awkward, albeit flashy, version of those.

I personally am returning mine for a refund just because I really don't like it.

product_title: Coleman Jug 1-Gallon Insulated Jug
review_body: It seemed fine the first few times I used it, but then I noticed a leaking problem when I poured it.  I don't know if I just didn't have it screwed on properly, or if there is an actual problem.  I haven't had a chance to use it since then.  Other people have commented on that, so I thought I better mention it, also.  I do like it, though.

product_title: Giordano Libero 1.6 Men's Road Bike-700c
review_body: The Giordano Libero 1.6 Men's Road bike provides new-moderate level cyclists a great bike for all situations. Whether it's climbing, sprints, or leisure riding, this bike fits the bill. I've owned this bike for well over four months and it has performed beautifully. I definitely recommend it.

product_title: Coleman Airbed Cot - Queen
review_body: We used it this past weekend on a camping trip and absolutely loved it! Granted, we've only used it once; however, it worked great for our purposes. The mattress held air very well (no need to inflate during the night) and it was nice being off the ground. Time will tell if it holds up to repeated use, but so far we're impressed.

product_title: Thermacell Outdoor Mosquito Repeller plus Lantern, Multiple Styles/Colors
review_body:
I didn't get to many chances to use this this year but when I did I was very satisfied
It is a little pricey but it saved my friends from being eaten alive
Helps if you remember to turn it off when your finished !!!
I would recommend

product_title: Mountain House Breakfast Skillet
review_body: Used with Tortilla shell for breakfast burritos.  Very easy to make and taste good.  Will use again on next trip!!

product_title: Global Vision Eyewear Escort Safety Glasses
review_body: Great glasses,  can't wait to take them out to the range and make use of them. Recommend anyone interested in a solid pair of over prescription shooting glasses to check them out.

product_title: GSI Outdoors Glaicer Stainless Percolator with Silicone Handle
review_headline: Old school yes... delicious coffee YES
review_body: I bought this percolator primary for camping trips. It's stainless steel and with care should last many years. I was really surprised by two things. First, it's durable. I've used this to make coffee all weekend on an open fire (using a cooking grate) at times the silicone handle was right over flame and I thought OK this thing is done. No way! The handle did not get damaged at all and the pot, It got blackened on the bottom and nice patina on the sides which cleans off easily if you like. The 2nd thing... this makes awesome coffee. I used your basic canned coffee like Maxwell house and everyone on our camping trip was commenting how awesome the coffee was. I lost power recently and the power company was estimating 2 hours for restoration, but of course it happened early in the morning as I was about to make coffee. Instead of firing up my generator, I made coffee in this percolator on my gas range and it was great. I've gotten my money's worth 10x over on this baby already and it still looks new.

product_title: Tifosi RX Adapter f/Podium, Podium S, Podium XC (49535)
review_body: These lenses can be more big, in order to fit the screen of the sunglasses. Something you see them when your view is more open

product_title: FSA Control Center computer mount, 31.8mm
review_body: I mounted this to my Giant Escape 3 bike for my LED Headlight. Fit perfectly, easy to install, allowed for perfect positioning of my Schwinn LED (in the center!). Looks great!

product_title: Hollis LED 3X focusable Light
review_body:
It's small, but at the same time powerful.

product_title: Kool Stop Eagle 2 Canti Threaded Dual Compound Brake Pads
review_body:
Put these on my bike after a number of daily hills destroyed my other brakes. I've had them for a couple months now riding daily and I've had no problems, including in rain. review_body:
I've looked at several bike racks and this is by far the cheapest and most sturdiest one I've encountered. Most of them had a weight limit of 20-25lbs and cost $25+. This one is 55lbs weight limit and almost half the cost.

It didn't fit my cruiser bike, and it wasn't meant to. I had to bend some parts and ghetto-fasten it with a few cable ties (zip ties), but it's holding like a champ.

Make sure the screws and nuts are tight. It uses Metric Hex screws, so keep that in mind.

review_body:

review_body: I've only used it once. Light rain and very warm conditions. It kept out the rain and kept me cool. Easy to set up. Can't wait to use it again.

Can be installed anywhere inline with a standard Camelbak drinking tube, or equivalent. Allows you to quickly snap on other attachments without stressing and pulling at the hose.

To disconnect, just push the yellow button. The half with the button has an automatic valve that closes when disconnected to prevent leaking, so make sure you install that part on the supply side.

product_title: Schwinn Quilted Wide Cruiser Saddle
review_body: On my bike, made riding more comfortable for my rides.  Quality is excellent.  Merchant ships fast, very pleased with this product. Quality above my expectations.

product_title: Wellgo Road Bike Pedal Toe Clips Medium + Straps

review_body: These came in a little more than a week, so I was happy with that. They were easy to install, the right size, good leather strapping to fit a wide range of shoe types, and the chrome is pretty darn durable too. Sometimes in the course of getting my foot in and out of them, they unavoidably scrape on the asphalt, but the chrome still looks like new even after a couple of months of what should amount to some wear and tear. product_title: Outdoor Research Sombriolet Sun Hat
review_body: I'm pleased in every way -- it's exactly what I had hoped! The reviews were absolutely correct. The fit is generous, so don't order any bigger than what you normally wear.

product_title: Coleman Oversized Quad Chair with Cooler
review_body: works good just like it should. was new is package and is everything that I thought. thanks for the sale.

product_title: JanSport Big Student Backpack
review_body: Jansport is really the best. I used one in the 70's 80's for school. 90's to treacle the world, and now my kids are using them. Classic brand great bag.

product_title: Sunlite Cloud-9 Bicycle Suspension Cruiser Saddle, Cruiser Gel, Tri-color Black
review_body: As someone posted earlier, this is a large seat, and if you looking for something sleek, sporty, forget it, but if you are looking for a very comfortable seat that takes the bumps like a charm, then this is what you need, especially if like me, you have a bike that has front suspension, but not rear.  I was getting some heavy back jars from biking, but now this padded baby with the suspension underneath the seat , is just what the doctor ordered.

product_title: Thermacell Portable Mosquito Repellers, Multiple Colors
review_body: First and foremost, it works. It won't keep everything away, the strips won't last a full 4 hours, and the effective radius is much smaller than advertised. But it does work. I was Dove hunting last weekend and it was 90+ degrees and bugs were out in full force. I was getting bitten and stung by all kinds of bugs and bees. Honestly, I got stung by a sweat bee within the first 5 minutes of setting up. I don't think I even had my chair set up before I got stung the first time. Once I got this thing going I didn't get bitten or stung again. Bugs would fly close, but nothing would land on me. I had it pretty close to me so I imagine the giant radius they claim is grossly exaggerated. However, it works. It's great for one or two people hunting very close such as in a blind, but probably not for a full patio of people in the backyard.

product_title: Reliance Products Bio-Blue Toilet Deodorant Chemicals (12-Pack)
review_body: I only used one while using the portable toilet, but perhaps I should have used more.  These do work as the waste liquid was a normal green; perhaps if I had used more it would have been a darker green.  Either way, this product works well with the portable toilet.  These deodorizer packets last under stress also, so I am highly satisfied with these as well.

product_title: NiteRider Lumina 500 Light
review_body: This light is wonderful! I bike commute 5 miles and this light is SO bright, does a great job of showing potholes and such, even in the rain, and being able to recharge it makes it very cost effective. I've used this in bucketing rain and it still shines through, no problem. I usually just have it on the low setting because I don't NEED it as bright as it can get. Only negative is people walking toward me on shared paths are a little blinded by it (I've noticed they occasionally cover their eyes) so I try to use my hand and deflect the light away from them a little as I go by.

product_title: Coleman Rechargeable Quick Pump, Colors May Vary
review_body: So glad I bought this nifty little pump. I bought the coleman queen double high bed with a built-in electric pump, but the campsite we went to didn't have any electric hookups so I purchased this rechargeable pump. It worked perfectly with the double valve coleman pump. Now we don't have to worry if the campsites we book have electric or not. This is lightweight and one good charge lasts the whole weekend. Extremely useful with the deflating function as well.

product_title: Mongoose Gel Bicycle Seat Cover
review_headline: Seat Cover is OK, not great
review_body: I would give this seat cover a B-, perhaps C+.  I'm a 50+ year old fat guy, and I had a bicycle seat that was killing my rear.  I bought this seat cover, and it definetly helped, but  I could still not ride as long as I would have liked due to my sore bum.  With this seat cover, I could ride for perhaps 25 minutes before I had to quit due to a sore backside.  I got the Cloud-9 saddle, and I could ride for 45 minutes.  In fairness, I am very out of shape.  I'm sure if I were in better "bicycle shape", those sore bum would not have been an issue, and this cover may have done just fine.  I do love the way this seat cover slips on and off so easily,  and it stays on the bike while riding with no problems.  I also like the fact that, unlike the Cloud-9 saddle, I can easily use this seat cover on different bikes.

product_title: High Sierra Curve Backpack, Purple Pattern, 18.5x12.5x8.5-Inch
review_body: Love it.its everything I wanted.Very pretty and well made!!Lots of room and love the design,Love the color.i would remanded this!

product_title: Sportz Truck Tent Blue/Grey
review_body: This tent works great!! It survived Hana, Maui's monsoon rains. Stayed good and dry all night. Set-up was easy enough for the first time without reading the directions. Probably a snap if you read the directions. Shipping was quick. Good choice in a truck tent. Next trip will be on the beach.

product_title: Eagles Nest SingleNest Hammock Khaki / Rose One Size
review_body: Purchased as gift for niece.  She loves it.  She can crowd the hammock with cousins and it always withstands the extra weight.

product_title: Nite Ize Gear Tie - Assorted

product_title: ALPS Mountaineering Lightweight Series Self-Inflating Air Pad
review_headline: Good, but smaller than I expected.
review_body: Overall I'm happy with this pad.  It is comfortable and easy to inflate and doesn't have a strong plastic or other odor.  That said, if I had it to do over I probably would have gone with the 'long' size.  The actual usable space is closer to 70.75\\" long by 19.25\\" wide when it's inflated.  The length is almost perfect (as a ~6' male), but the width feels a bit cramped and I often wake up with part of my body off the edge.

product_title: Coleman 40-Quart Wheeled Cooler
review_headline: Cooler kept ice frozen for 15+ hours!
review_body: This is a great cooler. I filled it with ice before 5PM and had it outside on a warm day. At about 11PM, I brought it back inside and left it alone. Around mid morning the next morning, I went to clean it out and the bags of ice were still mostly frozen. I was impressed!

product_title: UCO Candles for Candle Lanterns, 3.5-Inch
review_body: For the price I was expecting wonderful things such as the mentioned \\"pleasant aroma\\". But as I write this review I'm burning one of these beeswax candles and I don't notice any aroma at all, pleasant or otherwise. As a matter of fact to my normal nose they don't smell any different when burned right along side one of the citronella candles that also seem to have no aroma or odor. As to their ability to last for 15 hours this is yet to be seen. For the price I think I will stick to the standard UCO white candles.

product_title: 5 GAL Portable Camp Toilet Camping Flush Potty
review_body: When camping. the wife does not want to go out side the tent at night ... so this unit works great... just needs sturdy floor...

product_title: Fox G.I. Dog Tag Silencer Black
review_body: Were as described. Although be advised, they don't come in packs of 2; they are packaged individually so buy accordingly.

product_title: SODIAL(R) Waterproof Double Red LED Light with Black Silicone for Bicycle
review_headline: Takes a lot of time--but so worth it!
review_body: I'll admit, I'm not a huge fan of waiting but if it's for a product that I know is good, I'll wait. Boy am I glad I did. I received this early in the arrival date range and started using right away. This is so worth the wait.

product_title: Morakniv Craftline HighQ Robust Trade Knife with Carbon Steel Blade and Combi-Sheath, 4.1-Inch
review_headline: Steel of a deal on Amazon!
review_body: I have been picking Mora knives up when prices dip. You will have a hard time finding a better value than a Mora. Get over the plastic sheath, you can always buy a leather one if that is the issue, but you just cannot buy too many of this brand.

product_title: SportLite Beach Towel and Travel Towel in 3 sizes
review_body: We took a 39 day road trip and used these as our towels.  They are a really nice size (I wrapped mine around myself quite a few times as a cover-up).  They are absorbent.  Although they are not fluffy and cozy, I did not expect them to be.  They were perfect for camping & hiking and dried quickly, too!!

product_title: Sunlite Sprocket Remover/Pedal Wrench
review_body: Worked great with the other tool to remove cassett from Trek.  Watched a video on youtube to learn to use it.

product_title: Zoic Men's Black Market Plaid Bike Shorts with RPL Essential Liner
review_body: My boys are much happier now during a bike ride. They stay comfortably in place rather than bouncing around like they are part of a lottery drawing or bingo game. And the ladies love how they look on me. I've gotten so many cat calls while riding down the street. In fact, one lady lost her dentures while whistling at me!

product_title: Bell Liquid Flat Repair Sealant, 8 oz.
review_body: This was very easy to install. I removed the cores from my presta tube valves, and squirted it in. it was quite easy and it should help prevent punctures.

product_title: Seattle Sports Frost Pack 40-Quart Soft Cooler
review_body: This cooler is built well.  One of the best features is the thick, solid straps and handles.  I could strap the cooler on the boat easily.  It also has a double zipper, which is helpful for quick in and outs.

product_title: Texsport Self-Inflating 54-Inch by 22-Inch Mattress
review_body: I had to get a self-inflating air mattress for a field trip. I admit that I don't like to rough it that much. I like camping, but I can no longer sleep on the ground. This air mattress works. It does not fill on its own. I had to fill it manually. It does not take much at all. Overall, it worked great. My hips are what hurt the most when sleeping on the ground and I did not have this problem. The air mattress in not small but not heavy either. I would recommend this for light backpacking.

product_title: ExOfficio Women's Give-N-Go Full Cut Brief
review_body: These are the best briefs I have ever owned . The fit is great. Easy on and of when sweating play golf. Quick dry

product_title: Klean Kanteen Classic Single Wall Stainless Steel Water Bottle with Leak Proof Loop Cap
review_body:
Build Quality = 5 Stars
Water taste = 1 Stars
Overall Rating = 2 Stars

I have no idea why anyone who is not doing hiking/camping etc would ever buy this product. Water has a very bad metallic taste which is hard to get rid of no matter how many times you clean it with soap or cooking soda etc. Water tastes even bad the longer you keep it in this bottle. I returned it and got Lifefactory bottle which is made from good old glass. Now water tastes like it should, not like steel or whatever weird metal.

product_title: Coleman LED String Lights, 10 Lanterns
review_body:
These are awesome lights for camping or backyard. Have 2 sets now. They are bright, no heat, safe to hang on the tent. 3 AA batts, last for a very long time. Box that batts housed in, a little heavy, 3 AAs weight. But hangs easliy with a camping clip of any kind. I used reusable rubber twist ties.
Took my 9 yr old daughter into the Manistee National Forest tent camping along the Manistee river in Mich a week ago. We were pretty much the only ones along the river, 40 mins back off the main road. It was dark! But 3 nights on for a bit of security night light for her outside and still working fine off same batts. Would totally recommend for anyone looking for a fun, easy to use, camp site nite light.

product_title: Sunlite Standard Schrader Valve Tubes, Black
review_body: I purchased a Beach cruiser Bike with 29 inch wheels because I am 6ft. 4 in. tall and need a big bike. I read where people bought this bike and complained that Wal-Mart did not sell the tubes to fit it. 29 inch bikes are just beginning to become popular and this bike requires tubes with a 48 to 54mm fill valve, you won't find that at wall mart or even some local bike stores. I bought a pair to have on hand so when that flat occurs I will be prepared. Haven't had to use them yet, I hope that I haven't just jinxed myself

product_title: Cgecko 3l Military Maximum Gear Cycling Hydration Pack Camping & Hiking Reservoirs U.s. Army Style
review_body: I bought this product to use for airsoft and for jogging. I must say I love this camelbak, looks like the picture. I would recommend this to anyone looking for a good camelbak for a decent price!

product_title: Razor E90 Electric Scooter
review_body: I bought this for my 6 year old's birthday and it made his year.  The wide base helps him to balance so it's an easy and safe ride.

product_title: Outdoor Research W's Rocky Mountain High Gaiters
review_body: I wore these for my Kilimanjaro trek in August 2013 and they did a good job. I liked the elasticized bottom, it seemed better for keeping out the dust and scree. They kept my boot tops, socks and lower legs pretty clean, although quite warm. Don't be surprised when you take them off at the end of the day and they are sweaty inside. I gave them only 3 stars because the top buckle broke at the end of day 6 (of 7), it was made of plastic so I wasn't super surprised. Otherwise, no complaints.

product_title: OD Green Hydration Pack Drink Tube Cover
review_body: Dont waiist your money, very cheap product. No insulation and did not fit my particular camelback model. Started to fray immediately. Rips very easy on branches

product_title: 2015 Cool Women's Bike Cycling Sexy Lucky Phoenix Breathable Fabric Specialed Ventilated Jersey L size
review_headline: Love the pattern but runs small
review_body: I'm finding a lot if the items ordered from china run smaller. Perhaps their sizing standards are different. It's a pretty top and overall I like it however order a size up from what you would order in the USA.

product_title: Ogio Brooklyn Women's Purse
review_body: Love the color (black, but looks like a dark blue almost), love all of the pockets and love the price! Would definitely recommend for anyone with a tablet. My kindle fits great with lots of room. Made very well and should last a long time.

product_title: Liberty Mountain Aluminium Guyline Adjuster, Pack of 10
review_body: Once you have walked into a set of tent pegs in the dark with your bear feet and messed up the rigging, there Guyline adjusters allow for a quick resetting of the reflective guy lines

product_title: Dakine Women's Accessory Case
review_body: My daughter was looking for a pencil holder for school. She needed something roomy, that looked good and would hold up all year. We purchased this Dakine case and are very happy with it. It looks great and it's made well.

product_title: Advanced Elements 5 Gallon Summer Shower / Solar Shower
review_body: I purchased 2 based on previous reviews claiming faulty manufacturing. I got lucky and the one we used worked great. Plenty of water for two people. I think it was a little pricey, but no where as bad as the shipping charges.

product_title: Roswheel Bicycle Frame Pannier and Front Tube Cell Phone Bag
review_body: The product is good, I use it all the time on my pedicabs. I work as a pedicabs driver in Houston, Texas for Ready 2 Roll Pedicabs and use it all the time. It fits my iPhone with the case on it. It is useable with the plastic face and it has room to put other stuff in a separate compartment, like sun glasses. I would give it 5stars if I didn't have to wait for ever to get it, it ships from China and take at lest 2.5 weeks to get to you.

product_title: Ergon BioKork Grips, Large
review_headline: It is comfortable well-designed, pleasant to the touch
review_body: It is comfortable well-designed, pleasant to the touch, easy to install, resist shock, I recommend it, came the order on time without problems

product_title: Columbia Kaleidaslope Windbreaker Jacket
review_body: This jacket is a nice color and feels like it will be warmer than a basic shell, but still perfect for a layer. Size is accurate. Pleating looks a bit retro, but not off-putting.  Zippers might be wimpy, but overall a good buy for the price. Trying it out on a long day hike in the golden rockies this weekend!

product_title: Intex Fabric Extra Wide Camping Mattress
review_headline: Deflated twice in the night -- urgh!
review_body: This mattress stayed inflated when we tested it out at home (we didn't sleep on it all night) but on the first night we used it camping, it deflated twice!  We had flat ground and it was in a tent (with a tarp below the tent) so there were no sharp objects to wreck it.  It just didn't work!  I guess we'll stay with using two therma-rest backpacking pads.

product_title: niceEshop Liquid Filled Magnetic Camping Mini Compass(24pcs,20mm)
review_body: Not exceptional but very cheap and perfectly usable. All 24 compasses worked well enough to be helpful in an emergency. They are better quality than I expected. And perhaps the best feature is that they are not liquid filled. I have purchased way too many cheap button compasses that didn't work because bubbles in the liquid kept the dial from rotating properly. I have added them to mini survival kits for my family and given as gifts. The usable compass you have with you is worth more than the super accurate orienteering compass at home in a drawer.

product_title: Columbia Men's Backcast II Water Trunk
review_body: I bought these for my husband and he loves them. He really likes the pockets. He actually wears them as every day shorts rather than swim trunks.

product_title: High Sierra Envoy Lumbar Pack
review_headline: Great but a little too big for my taste.
review_body: In the picture it looks smaller that what it actualy is but a great product. I will make it work for me.

product_title: Rio Brands 6' Sunshade Umbrella
review_body: No complaints about this umbrella...it's not made cheaply as the price might suggest.  The only advice I would offer is to consider buying a larger one.  If you're the only one in your group who was smart enough to bring an umbrella to the beach, 6' is not going to accommodate all the family and friends who try to glom on to your shade.

product_title: UVEX MP-VI Melanin Polorized Sunglasses
review_body: These arrived just today. Viewing out the window with these and with my $300 REVO pair, the view appears to be the same. I will report back if it isn't after trying them out driving. Otherwise, they are a good look, appear to be well made in spite of the fact that they are \\"slight\\" (meaning the material they are made of is not thick and chunky) so do not know how they will hold hold. For me they are wide so if you normally wear a smaller frame they may be too big. I wear small Ray-Ban aviators as the regular ones are too large.  Arrived quickly, appropriately packaged in a box with a care sheet and pull-string black bag for storage. At 10% of the pair I am replacing, these may be a good deal. Will update later.

product_title: Columbia Men's Aruba IV Pant with 30-Inch Inseam
review_headline: Columbia Aruba IV Convertible Pants PFG Omni-Shade
review_body:
I write a review when I feel strongly about something. I LOVE THESE PANTS.! I know these are Men's, but I'm a woman about 5'6\\"-150+lbs and these pants fit and feel great.(yes, I did cut out the Nylon Web Support insert) I'll now outline the details why I love these pants.
1) WAIST: 3 components: a) wide elastic WAISTBAND (Approx 1-1/2in) that is not-too-tight, probably designed just to keep the shape / pants up with-out a belt; b)drawstring CORD that is run thru the waist band if you want to tighten them; c) BELT LOOPS securely stitched 2-1/2\\" x 1\\" for a belt, or in my case to securely clip a D-Ring with keys, etc.
2) WICKING Material: a) in Hot/Humid weather I wear wicking boxer briefs underneath and I was keep quite cool and dry even though I was sweating b) in Cool temps, I wear long wicking \\"thinsulate\\" underwear and I was comfortable. c) in RAIN I was amazed that after walking in the pouring rain, and entered an air conditioned building I was not cold and I swear these pants felt dry.! are they water resistant.? or just dry that quickly.?
3) POCKETS: front pockets are deep, nylon web pockets that I have placed my cell phone in one and wallet in the other, and still have comfort. back pocket on right rear, is secured with a zipper. I have driven long miles in a day, with these on, and very comfortable.
4) CONVERTIBLE pant legs: a) I cant even feel the seem/zipper, I forget I can remove the pant legs. I wear Columbia Silver Ridge Shorts. (love them too) So I can't rate how they are as shorts.
RECOMMENDATION: Would like a MAP Pocket on the Right Leg with a Zip Close, more comfortable than using the right rear pocket.

product_title: High Sierra Impact Backpack
review_body: this is a cute, handy backpack for Kindy through about 4th grade. It fits a lunch box, sweater, and a few folders/notebooks with a bit of room to spare. It's not too big for a 5 year old to carry but would be too big for a preschooler. Not big enough to fit a kid who needs to haul textbooks back and forth. Very sturdy material and pretty.

product_title: Hennessy Hammock Expedition Series
review_body:
I've owned this for a couple summers now. I bought my 9yr old one as well. We typically go on 1 or 2 night hikes and this thing allows it by letting us skip the tent. My son can carry ALL of his gear on his back, including his \\"shelter\\", and still be under 20lbs. I really don't think he'd be doing 10 mile days, with elevation, without this hammock.

Its completely waterproof, and mostly windproof if set up correctly, and once you've used it a few times, you get better and better at changing clothes, getting into the sleeping bag, etc. Like one of the other reviews said, under 50 degrees and you'll get cold quickly, and the underquilt seems expensive to me.

I hadn't camped in years, and finding the Hennessy has brought me back in....

product_title: Schwalbe Marathon Supreme HS 382 Touring Road Bike Tire (700x35, Triple Nano Folding, Reflex)
review_body:
Really? You read the name of this tire and you still need to read some words describing their magnificence?

Look, if you have the money to blow on a quality tire that will probably die after you do then stop looking. 16,000 kilometers with only two flats. One flat was the valve breaking away from the tube. The other flat was from being run over by a drugged-up lady in an SUV. Sixteen thousand. If you ride these that far then you deserve a new set. If not then these tires will look nice on the bike hanging in your garage and be ready for your children to ride if you haven't damaged them too much.

product_title: Space Saver Cup
review_headline: Great cup, but a few minor issues.
review_body:
Used 2 of these on a 5 day canoe camping trip.
The actual capacity of the cup is probably about 20 oz.

As noted by others, they don't fit snug enough over the nalgene bottle to stay on without help. I put a rubber band around the bottle to fill the gap and that worked. They are NOT light (being good quality stainless steel) so if weight is important you may want to look elsewhere for an alternative.

They worked great on the camp fire, and had markings on the side for measuring. Bonus of stainless is that it can be sanitized over the fire (vs plastic cups) and holds heat better than aluminum.

product_title: Minoura King Carrier Front Basket Large
review_body:
This is a nice front bike basket. It looks nice, it looks and feels like it was made with quality components. It is heavy but not that heavy. It will alter the handling of you bike, especially when you have it loaded down. Keep that in mind when you're crossing intersections. Nobody can accelerate as quickly as they think they can when you are loaded down with an extra 10-20 lbs. The bottle opener is upside down. You have to almost pour your drink out as you open it. It does the job though so alcoholics without driver's licenses need not worry.
The biggest downside is the only two choices when it comes to the centerline mounting bracket. Other people have commented already about this. If you think that you'll be able to pull it out of the box, put it on your bike and be riding in an hour and a half think again. Odds are the bracket will require significant modifications. I had to take a hacksaw and a drill to get one of them to fit. It took me 7 hours from start to finish. And that didn't include the time it took to ride to the hardware store. It is probably best installed by a reputable bike shop unless you are pretty handy. I like it but I'm probably going to have to have the bracket replaced by something custom fabricated. The basket is big enough that is strikes me as a big safety risk if it were to snap a any significant speed.

product_title: Planet Bike Superflash bike tail light
review_headline: Bright, but didn't stay attached to the bike ...
review_body:
I had this light for about two months. Now, I can only hope that some lucky person is now happily using the light. Unfortunately, the clip for this light may not securely attach to your bike bag or bike and you may find that when you arrive home that it is missing. I apparently did not hear it fall off during my ride. While the light was quite bright, there is not a way to more permanently lock it to the bike. What would have been perfect if it had a small clasp that I could have used to make sure that it didn't bounce off the bike. My ride this morning consisted of rural black-top roads in Southern Wisconsin ... while not smooth, certainly it wasn't a mountain-biking experience. Bumps, dips, uneven pavement.

While I still owned this light, I occasionally would set off riding and realize after a few minutes that I had forgotten to turn it on. Unfortunately, there's not a nice mechanical style switch that provides much feedback when you toggle the light between \\"on\\" and the few different modes it offers, so you may be left guessing whether it's actually on, if you're like me and you just reach back and push the button once firmly.

So, while it's bright and reasonably inexpensive, it's not so inexpensive that I'd consider it disposable. I'll be looking for a light that will more securely attach to my bike bag (I have a small saddle bag that makes a light attached to the seat post not useful).

product_title: Diamondback 2013 Overdrive V 29'er Mountain Bike with 29-Inch Wheels
review_body:
Really good bike for taller riders. I am 6'3" and this is the only bike I've ridden, so far, that properly fits me. I do have a few minor complaints though.

Setting up the gears is a bit challenging. The instructions are a little difficult to understand, and those of you who are not mechanically inclined will need to take it to a bike shop for the initial set-up.

The handlebar grips have a great texture, but are very firm. I had to purchase gloves after just 2 rides, as my hands were so uncomfortable.

The seat is like sitting on a boulder. I have a gel seat pad, but it's still uncomfortable for me. I plan on purchasing a cushioned seat in the near future.

Overall, a great bike, and I get many compliments from my friends. For this price range would definitely purchase again!

product_title: TETON Sports Scout 3400 Internal Frame Backpack; with a New Limited Edition Color; Free Rain Cover Included
review_body: At the moment almost everything I need to live is inside this backpack. I have enough clothes to last me about 2 weeks, a small tupperware full of detergent packs, a towel, a blanket, a pillow, a few books, all my toiletries, and a few other things here and there. I hang my shoes off the back. It's kind of an unconventional use, but it's what I'm doing to get by while I look for a job and couch surf.  Basically, this thing is pretty spacious and it's comfortable. Even loaded to the brim with things hanging off of it, it may be tiring walking around with the weight, but it's not uncomfortable or painful or anything like that. A great buy for camping (I hope to use it for that someday), but also for things like going to the grocery store on your bicycle or living a minimalist nomadic lifestyle.  -----------------------  Update April 2015: After having used it for a while longer in a variety of situations, I'm still very satisfied with what it offers, especially at the price. The only thing I'll add is that the more expensive packs are definitely nicer in quality, most noticeably because of the strings on the back. They're gotten stretched and frayed and now they get everywhere. It doesn't take away from its functionality, but it's annoying enough to be a hassle.

product_title: Schwinn Gridlock Men's comfort bike (26-Inch)
review_body:
I bought this bike for my high school son because that's what he wanted. It has had many problems and is the worst, least-reliable bike I have ever owned. Great styling. Terrible engineering. This bike is VERY comfortable but VERY heavy. Here are some of the things that failed in less than a year.

* Pedal broke and had to be replaced.
* Gears need too-frequent adjustment.
* Brakes need too-frequent adjustment.
* Brake wire mechanism at wheel easily pops loose leaving you without brakes.
* Three of the cables (for aesthetics) have a bare-wire segment running down frame. Those cables holders do not hold the cables very securely so they often become detached thereby causing the brakes or gears not to work.
* Brake cables are too long (probably to look retro/cool) so they get caught on stuff (especially in the garage or at the bike rack) so the cables frequently come off thereby causing the brakes or gears not to work.
* Seat comes loose and needs to be tightened with an Allen-wrench every few weeks.
* Kick stand has to be tightened to frame with a large Torx-bit on a ratchet wrench every few weeks or else it becomes loose and bike falls over. (I tried putting Lock-Tite on the threads but that didn't help.) I doubt that many people have a Torx bit big enough to do this job.
* Kick stand has a slip-on rubber base pad that fell off, thereby causing the kick-stand to become too short-- which causes the bike to fall over. Had to buy a new one and glue it on.
* Kick stand pivot eventually wore out and sags so that the bike falls over. I had to buy a new kick stand.
* Both shiny black fenders quickly faded to an ugly powder finish and no longer match the shiny black frame.

This bike has been a maintenance nightmare. I am so sorry that I bought it. My daughter has a mountain-bike style Schwinn that has essentially been maintenance free for several years, so not all Schwinn bikes are bad. Thisone is.

product_title: Von Zipper Feenom Goggle
review_body:
I have to admit that I didn't purchase these goggles from Amazon. However, I've had my Feenom's for at least 4 years now and I absolutely love them still. Here is the short breakdown:

Pros:
-Excellent build quality (lasted me through 4 seasons, probably 5 - it's been so long I don't remember exactly)
-Very comfortable to wear
-Wide and tall fit to not get in the way of your peripheral vision

Cons:
-Replacement lenses can get pretty expensive
-The goggles itself is pricey given so many other choices available
-Fit might be an issue for some with smaller faces

I purchased my pair during a sale at my local store and it was a pretty hefty price even at that. But, the deciding factor in getting these was the fit. It was wide & tall which really gave me an unobstructed vision in all directions. Previously, I've had less expensive goggles from Sc0tt and Spy, which served their purpose in keeping my eyes dry and open. But the biggest issue I had was their smaller frames which just got in the way. I don't know if my head/face is the issue but I have to say these goggles were what I've been missing (I would say my hat size is some where around 7 3/8\\"). I know there are some other goggles out there that also has the great vision aspect of it. But I just can't seem to get myself to buy a different pair, especially when my goggles are in their excellent condition.

That brings me to my next point: Build Quality. Like I said, I can for sure say I had these for 4 years now, going on 5, and they are absolutely excellent in how they've endured the slopes during the years. Now, I feel the most problematic areas of goggles would be the lense and straps. I don't know if I've ever heard of the frame breaking for whatever reason (I'll still point out that the frame is fine and feels the same as the day I got it). As far as the lense goes, I believe it's the same for any pair of goggles, not just Feenom's. The lenses have to be taken care of, especially the chrome versions, since they tend to get scratched very easily. I definitely have some minor scratches to mine since it's been 4 years but it really will depend on the care taken. My other lense, yellow for night riding, has been fine and you really can't see the fine scratches as much since it is not chrome-material. Also, the other aspect which I point to would be the straps. My goggle's straps have remained elastic and maintain their desired length without any issues. This was not the case for my previous pair of Spy's. The strap tore during the season, which was part of the reason I looked for another one, not to mention how it lost all elasticity. I've had none of those issues and I feel I definitely got my moneys worth in these goggles.

I would definitely recommend this pair for anybody that wants a very good quality pair of goggles. It is definitely not for the price sensitive rider or smaller riders with small frames. Definitely try on a pair, if you can, and you'll see the difference in vision and fit. I'll probably keep my pair for at least another 2 seasons before I even think about getting another pair of goggles.

product_title: Pedco UltraPod II Lightweight Camera Tripod
review_headline: Compact, lightweight, suprisingly versatile -- great for my Fuji X20 and Panasonic LX100!
review_body:
I bought the Pedco UltraPod II to carry with me on photo hikes and while backpacking. I prefer to pack light and keep my gear simple, but functional. I carry a Fuji X20 or Panasonic LX100, microfiber lens cloth, ziploc bag (for rain protection), spare battery, and this tripod, all packed in my Golla Salmiac G1018 case. It's an excellent lightweight setup and the UltraPod II significantly extends my shooting options, allowing for long exposures, action/family shots that include me in the frame, etc.

Initially, I expected to use the UltraPod II only in a pinch, but now I find myself using it regularly, even when I have a full size tripod relatively close at hand. Besides the basic tripod functionality (which is great for razor sharp photos), the integrated strap allows you to fasten the camera securely to railings, flagpoles, small tree trunks or branches, sailboat masts, handlebars on a bike or motorcycle, chair legs, ceiling fans... almost any secure mounting location of 3" in diameter or less. As you get more familiar with creative ways to hang it, it opens up a whole new world of possibilities for creative angles/shots.

The strap-ability of this tripod also shines when shooting video. When I was making a video about sailing our sailboat, I was able to get dozens of different angles that I could not have gotten with a regular tripod or hand-held. For example, I mounted the camera high up the mast, on the foredeck, on the tiller, down in the leg wells, on the side rail, on the back of the outboard, etc. These creative mounting possibilities resulted in a really engaging video, and I enjoyed the creative challenge of thinking up new ways to mount the tripod/camera. I was also able to use the tripod as a moderate extension arm, making it possible to hold the camera higher or further out than I would normally be able to reach--again allowing for greater variety in camera angles and some really cool, smooth shots with the camera held low down by the surface of the water.

Obviously, since it's such a short tripod, you have to find a chest-high mounting location if you want to capture eye-level photos. Thanks to the strap, that's not difficult, since it doesn't necessarily have to be a flat horizontal surface like a picnic table or wall (a slender tree trunk will do just fine, for example... just strap the tripod around the trunk at the desired height). It also allows you to capture some really cool low angle shots since the tripod legs can hold the camera much lower to the ground than a fully collapsed regular-size tripod, and is a lot easier and steadier to use than trying to prop the camera up with a sweatshirt or whatever you can find.

All in all, I think this is an excellent mini tripod. Very stable, very functional (especially with the included strap), and quite compact. Also, the non-slip vinyl feet work great. I set the tripod on a damp, bouncing sailboat deck (in windy conditions, no less) and it stayed put just fine. I would have no concerns placing this on a modest slope, though obviously you'll still want to be smart about it and perhaps tie a safety tether to the camera in situations that could destroy your camera if the tripod slips.

I don't know how this tripod would do supporting a large SLR size camera (possibly fine), but for a large point and shoot like the Fuji X20 or Panasonic LX100 (or Fuji X10, Sony RX100, Canon G15, etc.) it is terrific and very solid. Highly recommended!y the surface of the water.

product_title: Intex Fabric Extra Wide Camping Mattress
review_headline: Not just a great value but a great mattress as well
review_body:
I had bought several of the smaller INTEX mattresses and had to return them all because of inferior valves as well as being too narrow. I thought instead I'd try these extra wide ( INTEX ) mattresses. I was sooooo glad I did. These mattresses have a totally different valve. The smaller mattresses had a valve like a beach ball. A small nipple that you push in on after inflating. These mattresses have a heavy duty nylon valve that's recessed in a deep pocket on the underside of the pillow section.

This mattress is extra wide ( about 3 feet ) and it makes you feel like you have a lot of extra room. It's almost like a twin bed size. For camping or sleeping anywhere this mattress is great. The mattress deflates much easier too. Just unscrew the valve and all the air will come out in seconds.

One thing I would like to suggest is not to over inflate this or any air mattress. Only inflate it to the point where you're hip or butt isn't touching the ground. It's actually more comfortable than being fully inflated. I believe that the biggest problem causing leaks in air mattresses is due to over inflation. If you blow these up tight ( like a balloon ) you put a lot more stress on the bladder. It's not any less comfortable if you only inflate the bladder about 75 % of the way. Being so low to the ground it doesn't make any difference.

Of course the inflation advice doesn't apply to the large thick air matresses.

I would highly recommend this extra wide mattress to anyone looking for a good quality air mattress for camping or anywhere on the ground.

For $17 you just can't beat it.

product_title: Lightweight Large Burner Classic Camping and Backpacking Stove. For iso-Butane/Propane Canisters
review_headline: Spectacular value for casual / occasional users.
review_body:
I like to live by a corollary of Murphy's Law - roughly "The more prepared for something you are, the less likely it is to happen." This was purchased as Disaster Repellant® and it'd be hard to be more pleased with it.

For my expected use cases, a stove like this primarily needs to boil water. It will do that quite rapidly. I didn't time accurately, but I'd guess boiling enough to rehydrate a bagged meal takes about 2 or 3 minutes, even uncovered. (250ml water was too hot to touch after less than 1 full minute in a 1 quart thin-wall stainless steel pot) As advertised, the flame will also adjust lower - so high quality pancakes, fried spam, etc. can also on the menu.

It's pretty large compared to similar stoves, but I wouldn't trust it with any pots or pans larger than about 3 quarts - depending upon how shallow and wide they are, and also the weight. Bigger heaver stuff is less stable, especially when perched on top of a tallish canister.

There's enough heat coming out to use a thick-bottom pan, like a cast iron skillet. Of course heating the heavy pan means burning extra fuel. But I'm not packing it in on my back anyway, or expecting a canister to last a month, so no biggie.

The flip-out arms are basically useless. On my unit, the one pair is significantly lower than the other, offering no stability improvements. In the few minutes I've used it so far, I've left them retracted.

The "handle" on the adjustment valve is serviceable but be careful not to leave it sticking up close to the flame or you may have trouble turning it off without pliers. (yes, fire is hot)

This item's quality and performance are great, and it's totally worth the price I paid. When I was in the local big box store picking up a fuel canister (cheaper there than to get shipped) I compared this unit to a moderately respectable brand's competing stove priced at $22.95 and was quite pleased at what I didn't spend.

tldr; this thing is great for the money

product_title: JanSport Big Student Backpack
review_headline: Once a Jansport always a Jansport
review_body:
I bought this product to replace my older Big Student Jansport backpack that I've had since 2006. That's 7 years now! My older backpack was used heavily during this time in all weather conditions. It's gone through rain/sleet/snow/100+ heat and -20F temps and hasn't faded. It can sure fit everything you need in there. While my old big student backpack could keep going, I think that after so many years of use it would be a good idea to replace. The bottom part of the bag is getting real thin, mostly because of setting it down on hard concrete a lot.

Something to note...
There is no compartment for laptops. You can fit up to a 17\\" laptop in the bigger compartment, but it will be a tight fit. Laptops 16\\" and under will fit fine, but there is little protection for them so don't drop the bag.
There's only 1 side pocket. Wish there was another side pocket so we could place another water bottle or an umbrella.

Since I did have an older model Jansport Big Student backpack, I can see some changes. A minor change is the color of the interior. The older model was light gray and this one is darker, which is better so I'm not complaining. The biggest change was to the straps. The older model straps were a bit bigger thus provided a bit more support. Straps on older model are 3.5\\" wide at the top, 2.5\\" wide in center, and 1.75\\" towards to bottom. This newer model is 2.75\\" top, 2.5\\" center, and 2\\" bottom. Still haven't been able to test whether comfort has changed so I will update this review in a few weeks if I notice discomfort.

Overall, I hope this newer version lasts just as long as my previous one. For the price, you sure can't find a better backpack. Check prices often as sometimes the price dips under $30 (as I bought mine). Highly recommend.

product_title: SUPERIOR SUN PROTECTION: ezShade Canopy Sunshield BLOCKS 99% UVA/UVB rays - DOUBLES shade, keeps you COOLER, and INSTANTLY ATTACHES to ANY 10x10 nylon/poly canopy, CANOPY NOT INCLUDED

review_body:
We got this product as an add-on to our canopy for use while at the beach. I set it up at home before using it to make sure I got everything secure. The extra shade provided when the sun is low in the sky is incredible. It keeps you from having to chase the shade throughout the day, and I believe it even provides extra shade when the sun is high in the sky. My one complaint about the product is how it attaches to the canopy. The wall uses velcro strips that attach to the canopy and the sidewall with an adhesive backing. Unfortunately, after our first day on the beach, the sun caused the adhesive to melt, allowing the sidewall to drop. Fortunately the side of the wall attaches more securely, so we did not lose the wall completely.
I am planning on purchasing some 3M adhesive to see if it will stick better. If the wall was able to attach more securely, then this would easily be a 5 of 5. However, over all, aside from the headache of continually re-attaching the adhesive strips, the product worked well.

product_title: Kamp-Rite Compact Extra-Large Tent Cot, 44x10x10-Inch
review_headline: There are actually 3 things to review here...
review_body:
Like a previous reviewer, I set mine up in the living room the day I got it, and I'll update this when I actually get into the woods, so these are just first impressions:

Cot: This thing is built like a tank. Excellent design, easy to setup, very sturdy. And as a previous reviewer mentioned, it is about 22 inches off the ground (didn't measure, just eyeballed it). A nice touch was that the center support legs have a bit of compression to them (about 2\\") which might help on uneven ground... or cushion a quickly approaching butt! It really shows that this cot is made in USA (Go Team!). The equipment hammock underneath is.. well, maybe useful. An air or foam mattress might help a bit, I'll use one for fall/spring camping to separate me from a space blanket under it to keep the body bottom warm. I'd give the cot 5 stars.

Tent: Well, the tent is another story. It's made from the lightest material I've ever seen in a tent. The zippers are the weak point. The first time I zipped the tent to the cot, the already zipped part came undone. It took an hour to get that straightened out. And this is in the house, not out in the woods at sunset. Treat them gently and they'll be ok - but very gently. The tent interior is fine - the dome design is definitely the way to go. I'll give the tent 3 stars, it might go up or down after the first camping trip or two.

Rain-fly: Unfortunately, the rain-fly is a different story entirely. I can't speak yet to it's water repelling qualities, but due to the dome shape, the vents at each end have a kind of gable sticking out to keep rain from entering the vent. Well, the rain-fly goes into a crush sack, and the feeble support(?) for this gable is rendered useless, the gable falls against the vent underneath cutting off nearly all the air flow. It may be a asphyxiation hazard.. personally I would not trust it without some kind of fix. I'll be using a detached tarp for now. I'd give the rain-fly 2 stars without a fix.

I'd still buy it, but it's nice to know in advance what you are getting. Good Luck.

product_title: Hyperflex Wetsuits Men's 3mm Access Split Toe Boot
review_headline: Size does matter; IMPORTANT SIZING INFORMATION
review_body:
The quality of the boots is at least as good as you'd expect for the price. It might take a few years before I can tell how well these hold up, but for now, they seem well made.

UPDATE: The inside of these boots list the size in cm, the EU size and the \\"US\\" size. I checked the size in CM with a standard shoe size chart to see what was going on. The size in cm corresponded correctly with the women's EU size. It also came close to the women's UK size. But the boots don't say \\"UK.\\" They say \\"US\\" and the description says men's. In other words, if you pick a size 7, you are getting about a size 7.5 women UK, which is equivalent to a US size 9.5 women which is about a size 8 for men.

The original pair I ordered and returned was listed as size 8. I didn't note the size printed inside it. But using the same calculations, it would come out to about 9 to 9.5 men's US, which was about right for how big they were compared to how they were supposed to be. In summary, if you take the size listed, add about 1/2 size to it, find out the equivalent length in cm of that size in women's UK size, and figure out the US men's size for that same length, you will get the correct size if they are consistent.

I know this is complicated, but their size 7 is 25.5 cm, and you can look that up on a table to see what it really is. Since I can't come up with a table of sizes without seeing each of their boots, the best I can recommend is buying 1.5 to 2 sizes smaller than what's listed.

I will post a question here so perhaps others who already bought these might list what size they bought and what size in cm or EU was printed inside.

product_title: 85w/65w/45w+sos/strobe HID Xenon Flashlight Torch 8500lm Real 7800mah
review_headline: Yes, it's bright enough to be of safety concern.
review_body:
I'm glad I got it, it exceeds all expectations. The battery has a led lamp, equal to a keychain led flashlight.

Pros: It is much brighter than the two accompanying pictures portray. Upon doing the calculations, this is considerably brighter than both blue high beam headlights that idiot drivers use to blind oncoming traffic. Intensity approximates an aircraft landing light or railroad engine light.

Cons: Sorry, Amazon, there is another source with a much more reasonable price.

Safety: Staring into this flashlight is like staring at the sun. If you do, then you need to make your appointment to visit an ophthalmologist. After that you'll get a tax break for being legally blind. Don't shine this at aircraft or on-coming traffic. Add an aluminum foil or sheet metal barrier between the lamp assembly and the foam molding of the case, to dissipate heat and avoid melting the foam molding. If you want to touch, handle, or press the lens after light has been on a while, go ahead, but get familiar with first aid for burns first.

Hardware integrity: Allow 30 seconds for full brightness. Wait at least 30 seconds before turning it back on. You are not supposed to flash it, on and off. Mine does not have strobe or SOS, for good reason, flashing it is abusive to the High Intensity Discharge (HID) bulb life. If you need strobe, buy a separate 1000 lumen LED flashlight.

Enjoy!
