product_title: Schwinn 20-Function Bike Computer
review_body: don't buy.  the sensor needed to be a hair width away from the magnet and it still dropped signal after any little bump.  waste of money.

product_title: Park Tool Wrench Combo 6-17mm Set
review_body: The blue makes them the fastest wrenching tools out there.  The assorted sizes just make things confusing though.  I would have liked a manual.

product_title: Big Skinny Men's Magnetic Money Clip Slim Wallet, Holds Up to 12 Cards
review_body: I've had this thing for a few weeks now and I couldn't be happier. It holds a bunch of bills with no problem, none of my cards have ever fallen out, and my butt looks great without a huge bulging wallet obscuring the view! It's slim, practical, and best of all, it's not made of dead things. This is absolutely the best wallet for me and I plan on buying another if this one ever wears out. It takes a lot of abuse and still looks like the day I got it.

product_title: Coleman Oversized Quad Chair with Cooler
review_body: Got 2 of these for my son's football games, the beach etc. We tested them out in the house and seems to be very comfy and roomy. My husband is 6 ft and I'm 5'7" so it's nice to have a slightly bigger chair then the cheap $10 ones they sell in the stores.

product_title: Limited Edition Neon Blue Mini Kick with Pink Brake and Blue and Pink Hand Grips, by micro
review_body: We looked and looked for a good scooter for our daughter. This one is very versatile and was very easy for her to learn to use it.

product_title: SPORTSSTUFF 53-2223 Super Mable Towable
review_body: My  6 and 4 year old grandchildren can ride on Super Mable between 2 adults and love it. Two adults and one child at a time. They also use it as a raft for jumping into the water

product_title: New Bike Bicycle Cycling Frame Triangle Front Tube Bag Blue
review_body: Great product, especially for the price, but the ZIPPERS!!! jeez, you would think that an item from China, the zipper capitol of the world, would get it right. but they just make a lot of noise, so replace the metal grabs with some string, or something, and you're good. shipping was extremely fast

product_title: NeoSport Wetsuits Premium Neoprene 2.5mm Sport Cap
review_body: The strap was so long that the cap wasn't functional. Unfortunately, I was unable to wear it during the dive.

product_title: Camelbak Eddy Bottle 0.75-Liter/25-Ounce
review_body: It sweats....a lot. I gave it 5 stars because other then the sweating I love this bottle! I would highly recommend it.

product_title: Shaker Bottle 28oz with Blender Ball
review_headline: A Gym body is not a gym body without a good shaker
review_body:
Comes with a blender ball, top part which i don't know what to call, and is pretty durable. i hate the plastic that bends, this is like a rock. Haha

This shaker will take me places

product_title: Coleman Premium Double High SupportRest Airbed w/Built in Pump
review_body: The price is right, super comfortable, and takes about 4-5 minutes to fully inflate. Easy to deflate, fold, and put back into the storage bag. Normally you can never fit something back into the original packing bag but this was done easily.

product_title: Underwater Kinetics SL4 eLED Crevice Light
review_headline: Awesome light for the right price
review_body: love my light for my Scuba adventures. Great little switch on the front to turn it off and on. Perfectly fits in my hand.

product_title: Emergency Zone Folding Shovel with Pick and Compass, Multifunction Survival Tool
review_body: this is a pretty cool tool but i dont know how well it would hold up in a real zombie attack (lol) but i got it for my dad for father's day and he said he likes it a lot. just one of those things you can pack while tenting if you need a multi purpose tool.

product_title: Louis Garneau Men's Tri-Lite Triathlon Cycling Shoes
review_body: These shoes worked great in transitions.  Easy on and easy off leaving them clipped in.  I got a size 43 and these seem a little larger than my bontrager 43's.  I might want a 42 in this shoe if I were going sockless.  I feel like these shoes were a good deal at the price for an age grouper triathlete.

product_title: Razor E100 Electric Scooter
review_body: came on time,packed real well ,easy to assemble  ,my kids love it ,it looks like my kids will enjoy it for a long time

product_title: Topeak Sport II Floor Pump
review_headline: Excellent value for a very useful pump
review_body: I don't understand the earlier reviews that complained about the difficulty of locking the pump onto long presta valves.  I have 60mm prestas on my road bike and the end chuck locks on and seals fine.  I can easily pump the tires to 120 psi.  I can't comment on its longevity (I've had it less than a week) but I can certainly testify to its functionality--a very good pump at a very good price.

product_title: Bell StowAway Bicycle Seat Bag
review_body: Others have mentioned the shortcomings with the strap on this.  There has to be a better way to design it.  The bag itself seems great and I figured for the cheap price it was worth a shot to get it.  I made a few minor modifications to the straps by reconfiguring the velcro so it makes a little more sense when putting it on the bike and also makes it sturdier.  It's difficult to get a snug fit with the straps as they come so I made it significantly more snug.  I think it might be better if the strap was one whole loop that went around the bag and had one end that velcros around and on the top.  I would recommend it but be sure to read others descriptions of their issues securing the bag to the bike before you make a decision.  Maybe hit one of your local bike stores or dept stores to see if they have it then try it out to see if you like it.

product_title: Energizer Weatheready 3-LED Carabineer Rechargeable Crank Light, Red
review_headline: Very handy light for the right price.
review_body: This rechargeable crank light, flash light works well in my camping/bug-out bag I put together.  It is the smallest crank light I could find available.  The cranking of 3 LED lights is my only trouble.  The handle is small and feels as if it could snap off.  Other materials are made well, and for the price, you should want one if in need of a self-powered light source.

product_title: Coleman 12V Electric Trolling Motor
review_body:
I purchased this for my Sevlyor 360 6 person raft. It fits easily and moves along at a good pace. The reverse never seemed to work that great, but I never really needed it.

Operation was easy, but it required me to sit in a fairly awkward position. We were out on the lake for quite awhile when the wind picked up. The motor could not get us moving into the wind. We paddled back in, but I blame the wind more than the motor.

My only real complaint was that the clips didn't match up well with the Sevylor 12V battery.

product_title: MGgear Messenger Cross Body Outdoor Biking Backpack - 2 Color
review_body: My grandson loved the look of it, but the first time he tried to use it he found that the zipper of the main compartment was broken. Also, one of the seams had a break in it.

product_title: Avenir Excursion Rack-Top Bag (830 Cubic Inches)
review_body: I looked at this bag and a bunch of more expensive bags and decided to try this one. It is easy to get on the bike rack, easy to take off, and holds a ton of stuff. It has a strap for carrying once you get off your bike. The weight is good, even full, I can't even feel in on back there. It does keep things cold for a while and it keeps things from getting wet. I like that it expands.

product_title: Ibera Bicycle PakRak Clip-On Quick-Release All Weather Single Pannier with Rain Cover
review_body: Easy to clip on and off. Perfect for my commute to work and picking up groceries. Good quality. I like the front pocket for keys and phone while the inside pocket is big enough for lunch, water bottle and change of clothes.

product_title: High Sierra Vivian Tote Bag Backpack
review_body: This bag is big enough to fit all of the stuff my wife needs for her day including her lunch and water bottle, but it's not overly large. It's pretty compact in fact, and it looks nice. It kind of looks like a big purse.

product_title: Arbor Pin Skateboard Completes, 46 x 9.5 x 32.25-Inch
review_headline: Very nice for riding but the paint was thin
review_body:
I love riding it its surprisingly very agile for such a long board. Has a lot of flex which is nice. The trucks were loose which gave the board a nice turn. I love riding it.

One thing I noticed though that made me rate it one star less was the the paint was very thin, so much so on some parts of the graphic you can see the natural wood color underneath it.

Other then that I recommend it.

product_title: Kelsyus Wave Beach Canopy Chair
review_body: Very comfortable. Love the top. Easy to carry. Worth the cost. Was on the beach and got caught in the rain put the top up and stayed dry.

product_title: KLOUD City Grey Polyester Waterproof Bike Bicycle Cover
review_body: I thought it would have a more options depending on the bike - my bike is hanging and I could not get the cover completely as I would like.

product_title: Bravo Sports Shade Tech 144 Canopy (12X12-Feet)
review_headline: cheap frame and horrible customer service
review_body: We took this canopy to the beach. A gust of wind came, and the frame snapped in half and the whole thing collapsed. I talked to customer service and they said that the manual says not to use it when its windy.  So wind damage isn't covered by the warranty. We spent $150 on this shade, used it for an hour, and now its a mangled piece of crap.

product_title: Kelsyus Tropical Island Shade Shack
review_headline: Broke the first time I used it
review_body: Though lightweight and portable, this broke the first time I used it. I was putting it away and a joint snapped. The plastic joints and poles are very fragile. Bummer because its a cool design.

product_title: Sigma BC 509 Bicycle Speedometer
review_body: This item only lasted 150 miles and 4 weeks.  All the steps in the troubleshooting section of the manual were performed and the unit still does not work.  I will be contacting Sigma since it has a 2 year warranty and is only 1 day out of the Amazon 30 day return policy.  I have owned Cat Eye products and never had any of them fail.

product_title: Blackburn Voyager 3.3 + Mars 3.0 Bike Light Combo
review_headline: The absolute best bang for the buck !!
review_body: I gave this 5 stars because this lighting system is like a cars headlight, it's that bright, as well as the rear light which is very bright as well.For $35.00, that is cheap for the safety of a human life.It came earlier than the date estimated which was nice for me, and i would say get this if you want to not only be seen, but to also be able to see the road at least 20 feet ahead of you.

product_title: Osprey Packs Poco - Plus Child Carrier (2015 Model) (Bouncing Blue, One Size)
review_headline: Parents & baby both luv this pack
review_body: Very happy with my purchase. Perfect to take the whole family to the dog park, farmers market, and eventually some day hikes.  More convenient than a stroller by far.

product_title: Picnic Time Portable 'Ventura' Reclining Stadium Seat
review_body: This is both fashionable and functional. My wife and I have used ours for approximately two months and no issues but I question its durability. Worthy of the purchase.

product_title: Cosmos Assorted Color UV Protection Cooler Arm Sleeves 4 Pairs for Bike/Hiking/Golf (Black,White,Gray&Light Blue Color)
review_body: They fit great and keep me warm under my scrub tops in my cold office. Then I can just take them off if I get too hot, unlike wearing a long sleeve shirt under my scrubs. Great idea!

product_title: Yukon Outfitters MG10501N Parachute Hammock with Net
review_headline: Good but not great. Description is WRONG!
review_body: Nice hammock for the money. Not great, but good. Item description is wrong. This is NOT a double hammock that is 11'6\\" long x 6'4\\" wide. It is a SINGLE hammock that is 8'9\\" long x 4'8\\" wide with a weight rating of 275 lbs. Ordered from \\"thegrape\\" and got the single hammock. Their response to my inquiry was basically that Yukon only makes a single hammock and they didn't seem eager to refund my money. I think the hammock is worth the fifty bucks, but order from someone other than \\"thegrape\\".

product_title: SMOKEH BIG CHIEF TOP LOAD SMOKER
review_body: I've smoked 3 batches of delicious Copper River Sockeye Salmon so far and each one has been outstanding!  Surprisingly, it gets done in 3 1/2 to 4 hours. I like the design with the 5 trays. I can get 30+ pieces of salmon in there!

product_title: Cheng Shin C637 Road Bike Tire (Wire Bead, 27" x 1-1/4", Black Wall)
review_headline: You get what you pay for
review_body: I installed these tires 4 days ago and already one is getting a bulge in the tread (cord failure). Even at this price I expect any tire to last longer than this. This is my first and last Cheng Shin purchase.

product_title: NowAdvisor®Q5 CREE 240 Lumen LED Bike Bicycle Headlight Torch
review_body: I bought this light to replace a Bell and the improvement was immediately noticeable.  It is bright enough to use in total darkness.  On the wide beam setting it provides enough light to see a wide area on both sides.  This light also projects light far ahead, allowing me to increase speed a little.  The mount is easy to install and sturdy.  A great bargain for it's price.

product_title: RockBros Bike Pedals MTB BMX Pedals Cycling Pedals 9/16" Red
review_body: I am very pleased with these pedals! I put them on my Specialized HardRock Sport and have no complaints. Light weight, huge studs for great grip on shoes, my feet have not slipped off these pedals once! Plus these are just as nice as some $80 pedals out there!

product_title: Diamond Willow Walking Stick 4-6 ft
review_body: I was under the impression that you would get four(4) 6ft sticks for that price. but instead receive one. It should read one, 4ft-6ft stick. Now that I could of understood clearly.

product_title: Life is Good Coin Tire Cover
review_body: Easy to slip on the tire.  Happy message.  Love it.  It seems to be holding up nicely in Florida sun and rain!

product_title: Igloo Stainless Steel Hinges
review_body: Very solid and well made. Comes two to a pack, so if you have a three hinge cooler order accordingly.

product_title: Cosmos ® Black mesh/gel cycling/bike gloves (size:L)+Cosmos cable tie
review_body: These gloves work ok and the reason they don't work better is probably my fault. I bought them as summer motorcycle gloves to reduce vibration and they do that, but not very well. They may work fine in the application they were intended for, bicycling, which doesn't have the vibration associated with motorcycling. I would suggest that you read what bicyclists have to say about them if that is how you plan to use them.

product_title: Thule Load Straps - 2 Pack
review_body: Well made straps, sticking was in good condition with no breaks. It came with a buckle cover to protect the item being strapped down.

product_title: Women's Black Braided Knit Arm/leg Warmer Fingerless Long Gloves
review_body: At Daiso for $1.50. I mean, it kept me warm during the cold seasons and they were stylish. So yeah.

product_title: Zoic Men's RPL Essential Padded Cycling Liner
review_body:
I waited to review these intentionally-
I am an avid bike rider and have rode with: integrated shorts with liners, thick spandex shorts with pads, and other liners similar to these.
The best set up I found (for me) is to wear a liner under some surf shorts, and the Zoic RPL is the best thus far.
I ride a single speed road bike and a mountain bike that is set up for downhill.
I have found other liners chafe and/or bunch up - and integrated shorts slip down and show my plumbers crack - and although the thick spandex don't have those problems, going straight to the pub after a ride and cat calls from chicks in cars test ones modesty ;)-

product_title: Intex Pillow Rest Raised Airbed with Built-in Pillow and Electric Pump
review_body: I purchased this one and also the Sealy Never Flat.  This one is much cheaper than the Sealy, but it works just as well.  I like the never flat pump, but for the money you can't beat this one! It does make some noise when you move around...

product_title: Columbia Men's Dry Ice Bandana (Omni-Freeze ZERO)
review_body: This is perfect for hot days, kept me cool while mowing all summer.  Now using it while coaching football, complete life saver.

product_title: Commemorative US Armed Forces Colt .45 M1911 100th Anniversary Zippo Lighter
review_headline: It's a Zippo with a Colt 1911 on it, what more could you ask for?
review_body: This is a great commemorative Zippo.  It's a Zippo with a Colt 1911 on it.  There's not much to say really.  It's just awesome.

product_title: AIRHEAD AHCI-1 Cool Island
review_headline: fun for the day flat the next....
review_body: Used this raft once...when we went back to use it the next weekend it was flat.  My husband found two spots in the seams that was losing air.  Hard to patch the seams. Factory defects. Felt like we wasted $140!

product_title: Sta-Tru Silver ST725 36H Rim Rear Wheel (700X25)
review_body: Purchased this wheel to complete an assembly of a road bike using left over parts in my collection. Excellent product despite the under $40 price. Would recommend this as a replacement for an older or extra bike.

product_title: One Direction Messeger Bag
review_body: My Granddaughter loved it so I will say all went well, she was thrilled! it was a good buy also.

product_title: Wald 1216 Bicycle Training Wheels (12 to 16-Inch Wheels)
review_headline: Wald 1216 Bicycle Training Wheels (12 to 16-Inch Wheels)
review_body: Didn't work with the bike that my daughter was riding. She couldn't ride on gravel or dirt. She would get stuck.

product_title: TETON Sports Scout 3400 Internal Frame Backpack; with a New Limited Edition Color; Free Rain Cover Included
review_body: Looks and feels durable, haven't tried it but looks like it can fit a lot of things and sturdy, slight weight to it even empty

product_title: Saris Bike Porter 2-Bike Trunk Rack
review_body: Works very well on my vehicle. The adjustable rubber cradles are great for bikes that have curved top tubes like my Trance X 29er.

product_title: MSR WhisperLite Stove
review_headline: For One or Two People, WhisperLite Does the Trick
review_body:
I owned a WhisperLite for many years though now I have the [[ASIN:B002IAJ5VA MSR Dragonfly Stove]]. I had it with me backpacking through Spain, England, W. Germany (yeah, that long ago it was still East and West), Wales and in my home area of Virginia. (Lot of piecemeal Appalachian Trail time there.) I believe it got lost during a move from VA to NC. Regardless, if you're cooking for yourself and one other, the WhisperLite's the way to go. It's almost idiotproof, does a good job and packs up easily.

The windbreak, in my opinion, is probably the drawback of this stove. I ended up tossing it out and manufacturing a better one out of an aluminum pie plate.

product_title: Minoura Tool Alloy Set Tire Levers
review_body: I ordered these assuming they'd be useful for something.  I literally laughed out loud when I got the package.  They are just the cutest little things.  I suppose maybe for small or easy to mount/dismount bicycle tires they 'may' do the job.  But they're awfully soft and easy to bend also.  I really don't see them being useful for anything.  And the item description says nothing about size or material.  I basically laughed it off..and threw them in the back of the tool box as a poor decision and maybe a novelty gift at some point..

product_title: Solrx 71446 Sunscreen Orig. Formula
review_body: My husband is a roofing contractor and once we discovered Solrx is been a world of difference for him.  We swear by it and recommend it to everyone we know.

product_title: Coleman Folding Double Wash Basin
review_body: bought it a few weeks ago and have used it twice (both 3 night trips with 4-6 people and lots of dishes) and it has held up quite well. The plastic seems thick and tough and, with obvious mindfullness regarding sharp objects, should hold up for quite awhile!

product_title: Horny Toad Women's Empirical Dress
review_body: This dress is great. I'm 5'7 average build and I love it.  I purchased the medium and have worn it several times.  Didn't shrink when washed and looks just as good as it did when I first got it.  So versatile, I can wear it to pick the kids up from school with some slip on shoes or dress it up with jewelry and wear it for a night out.  Honestly, you could probably sleep in it, too. It's is worth the money. You'll get many miles out of this dress.

product_title: Minus33 Merino Wool Men's Isolation Midweight 1/4 Zip
review_body: This product is amazing.  Thin, breathable fabric that is unreasonably warm.  Extremely soft and a quality make.  Couldn't recommend it higher.  The product seems to fit as advertised.

product_title: Camelbak Eddy Bottle 0.75-Liter/25-Ounce
review_body: I had one, but it got stolen at the gym... had to rebuy one because they make drinking water easier while working out. No more tilting your head back gasping for air. It came in perfect condition. The tip click when you put it down and stays down. Gentle bite on the tip and drink up! I dropped my old one many many times and it just scratched it slightly but didn't do any real damage.

product_title: Sigma Wired Speed Sensor Kit w/Cable - for computer models using CR2032
review_headline: works for a 2nd bike mount if?
review_body:
I ordered this mount and speed sensor kit to use on a second bike with the sigma 1609 computer I also ordered at the same time. I received this product along with the computer on July 10, installed everything on two bikes and could not get the
second bike feature to work. The instructions that came with the computer mention almost nothing about the second bike function
that I had begun to think it didn't have a second bike feature, and the sensor and mount kit didn't have any instructions about
using it for a second bike.
Last night I was reading the amazon review for this mount and sensor kit thinking I had gotten the wrong one when I read one reviewer had the same problem and solved by moving the left hand lead one notch over. I tried this and it works now on my second bike. I wish Sigma would have put that in their instructions some where, it would have saved me a lot of time.
All in all I have to say that I really like this mount and speed sensor kit it should work as either a replacement for bike1
or a 2nd bike mount depending on where you put the left hand lead.
Thank you to the amazon reviewer for informing me on what Sigma did not.

product_title: The Flying Wheels Bolt Bike Brake Pads (Bag of 4)
review_body: Had some time hardened pads on an old classic Murray 26". Replaced with these and I am quite happy with them. They need to be "burnt in" to get the hard coating off them when new.

product_title: Columbia Women's Bahama Long-Sleeve Shirt
review_body: I'd like it better if it had snaps instead of buttons but overall, it's a good shirt. Fits well, looks good.

product_title: Fytto Thermal Therapy Pack, Large Leak-Proof Cap, Condensation Resistant Fabric
review_body: A useful and attractive basic product of good value. I plan to use it to dull the pain of my frequent headaches. You usually can't go wrong with the judicious application of ice.

product_title: Single Hammock by Trek Light Gear - Pioneering Lightweight Hammocks
review_body: This is a great hammock that is on par with ENO and their stuff, but the end hooks are lighter than ENO's carabiners.

product_title: Stansport Hammock Tree Straps
review_body: Heavy duty straps. They hold up to my friends kids bouncing and swinging all over the hammock. They have a 300(?) pound weight limit as does the hammock. But they held up to a very little extra weight. Longer than expected but work perfectly.

product_title: Coleman 12V Rechargeable Battery
review_headline: Held enough charge to get us around for hours.
review_body:
I really am quite happy with this purchase. The charge held very well, and I never ran it out of juice.

I would love to see a charge indicator. I was also disappointed with the way my Sevylor trolling motor and this battery clipped together. The connection was barely secure.

product_title: Klean Kanteen Double Wall Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Tumbler Cup with Tumbler Lid
review_body: I received one of these as a birthday gift from my son.  It keeps drinks amazingly cold!  I can make an iced latte at 7AM and there will still be ice cubes in it by 3PM.  Also great for a super cold beer!  I immediately bought one more for my husband and another for my brother!

product_title: UCO Candles for Candle Lanterns, 3.5-Inch
review_body: Very little candle for the money. I think you could do better, wish I would have. Never again.  Why does this require me to keep writing to submit this review??

product_title: Texsport Deluxe Privacy Shelter/Shower Combo
review_body: I was renovating my bathroom. it took four months. So my family used this for showering. It worked great. It was handy that it included a heater so we could have a hot shower.

product_title: Avenir Resin/Alloy Pedals with Toe Clips and Straps, Black/Silver, 9/16 Inch Axle
review_body: The pedals are much lighter than I expected! My only complaint is that while you can take the back reflector off, the front one is a part of the plastic cage so it can't be removed. Not a huge issue.

product_title: Wahoo Blue SC Speed and Cadence Sensor for iPhone, Android and Bike Computers
review_headline: Love it, but took a minute to install on Cervelo S2
review_body: This is amazing. I have my heart rate watch, this and my iPhone and I get all the data I need. Took a minute to install because the magnet mounted on the spokes was to close to the sensor. To solve I put the magnet on the opposite side spoke but slid the sensor forward or closer to the bottom bracket (place that pedal arms attach to the bike). This allowed the sensor to be lined up with the magnet that was toward the end of the spoke so close enough to the sensor. Have the crank magnet about half way down the crank arm and they all line up nicely. Great product and work without any button pushing or anything. Just open the iPhone app and get on my bike and go. Love it.

product_title: VR TT Adjustable Multi-Position Armrest Triathlon Handlebar Aero Bar with 8 Backup Rings and 2 Elbow Pads
review_headline: Easy to install, but will take a few rides to dial in for the proper comfort.
review_body: New to long distance riding, and I'm training for a non-race century this fall, looking for something to start with, and these will do the trick.  They were easy to install, but no directions.  If you can install a bike computer around your handlebars, and do a little google browsing, you will have enough knowledge to install these bars.  It is helpful to have a stationary trainer and riser when installing so you can sit on the seat and get the grip distance properly before trying them out.  They are highly adjustable, forward/back, and the arm rests have a lot of adjustability for distance, and space between, angle etc.  I added bar tape to the ends for a better grip if it's wet.  It will take me a few rides to dial them in, and I plan on carrying the allen wrenches with me if I need to do an on-road adjustment.  I was surprised at how light they are.

product_title: Sea to Summit DryLite Towel
review_body: This towel was purchased for camping due to space saving design. The towel is very absorbent but I still bought the large so my wife could "wrap" herself in it to give it a better feel. They feel different than cotton but are actually more absorbent & dry quicker.

product_title: Schwinn Turismo Swivel Double Jogger
review_body: We love this stroller we use it for running and for long days out and about. Runs smoothly and easy to push. We use it for a 1 and 3 year old. Over all no complaints. Great stroller.

product_title: Coleman RoadTrip Grill Cover
review_body: The quality of this cover was a surprise, its much better than I imagined. I've bought over the counter covers and they would last a month at a timer. I'm very pleased.

product_title: Jagwire Mini Inline Bicycle Cable Adjusters w/ End Caps - 2 Pieces
review_body: Works as advertised.  Simple matte black works with any color cables.  Easy to work with and high quality as with all other Jagwire products.

product_title: SunSport Sunglasses Sport Style with Polycarbonate Lens (Smoke/Blue, Black)
review_body:
I've had these sunglasses for about a month, and am about to throw them away.

First, the good parts:
These sunglasses were extremely inexpensive, fit OK and are lightweight and comfortable.

Now, the bad:
The only thing holding the lenses in place is two little tabs on each side which fit into slots on the lenses. The frames are very flimsy, so if you take them off with one hand, you bend them enough to pop the lens off. The color on the lens is a film so thin that within a week, it had rubbed off in spots.

product_title: Light & Motion Taz 800 Light
review_body: This Light and Motion Taz 800 WILL light up the road ahead, aside, and around. I have not yet even tried it on the highest setting. I think it is easy to use, but don't forget it because someone will take this thing in a second.

product_title: Mirrycle Incredibell Original Bicycle Bell
review_body: The harmonics of the brass bell is not only pleasant but also gets people's attention. A truly pleasant and effective way to alert pedestrians to share a multi-purpose pathway.

product_title: Hydro Flask Insulated Wide Mouth Stainless Steel Water Bottle, 32-Ounce
review_body: I have been waiting for a water bottle that is stainless steel that has a wide mouth for easier cleaning and drinking..the smaller mouth style you have to unscrew the top and remove it,, not exactly driver or user friendly.. this wide mouth model replaces the toxic plastic bottles I have been using for years. Its Extremely durable and I read a review about clean canteen models that said they left condensation because they were not insulated,, this one is and it does not sweat,, its everything I was looking for and more thanks. With the sling I now have everything to fit to my life style.

product_title: Slime COMP02 12-Volt Tire Inflator
review_body: This is a good product it does beat the hand pumps, might be limited do to having to plug it into the car but that can be worked around

For the minimalist camper, this is a perfect one cup/pot to carry.

On a side note, I want to use every available space so I store my Primus stove (excluding the fuel canister) inside my GSI cup when not in use or when hiking or kayaking. So that the stove doesn't fall out and get lost or damaged, I use the plastic lid from a Gatorade powder 18.4 oz container to secure it. product_title: Starlyte Stove by Zelph Stoves
review_body:
I have built alcohol stoves for years, and bought stoves from several stove builders Tinny, Smokeeater908, Zellph, Batchstovez, Intense Angler, etc.

This stove is AMAZING. it is very light weight, and very fuel efficient and could not be easier to use. Pour the alcohol in the stove and light. If you cook pot in a Titanium cup, Glacier cup, or GSI Minimalist; this stove has a perfect size flame pattern.

I have only used this stove a few times; so I am not sure it will give a fast boil but the fuel economy is GREAT. the only stove with the same fuel economy to the Starlyte stove is the MAHALO stove that I designed.

UPDATE: I used this stove for the third time, and this time I timed the test.

The Starlyte IS slower than my MAHALO stove. The MAHALO takes 6:30-7 minutes to boil. The Starlyte took a little more than 8 minutes: so my MAHALO is the clear winner for speed. I think the reason for the slower boil time is that the Starlyte is a wick stove, and the MAHALO is not.

I still think the Starlyte is as efficient and possibly more so because in optimum conditions 15 ml Heet boiled two cups tap water with some alcohol to spare. Next time I am going to try 12.5 ml alcohol to boil two cups.

If you are new to alcohol stoves; you cannot go wrong with the Starlyte.

Using the Starlyte could not be easier. Measure the alcohol in the plastic 1 OZ measuring cup. Pour the alcohol onto the screen. Set the pot on the built in pot stand. Light the stove and you are cooking immediately without dealing with priming pans, waiting for the stove to blossom. With the pot stand you NEVER have to worry about cold pot flame outs.

One last thing most alcohol stoves are good for cooking meals for 1 or 2 people. You will not be cooking a spaghetti dinner for 6 people.

As long as you have realistic expectations for the stove; alcohol stoves will serve you well.

product_title: Kelty Ignite DriDown 0-Degree Sleeping Bag
review_headline: So far, so good - more stars likely after some more outtings
review_body:
So far, this bag is great. Very light and comfortable to sleep in, it lofts up quickly after removing from the stuff sack. The construction seems top quality so far, but I haven't had the chance to really put it through its paces yet. Compared to the North Face Snow Leopard 0 degree (synthetic) i had been using, this bag is by far superior. For the first trip we camped at about 8500-9000', night time temps were probably in the low 50's and we were very close to a substantial creek which added a good bit of humidity to the air for Colorado. Wearing light flannel pants and a T to sleep in, this bag was extremely warm - really didn't need a 0 degree bag this trip, but better safe than sorry. I left the bag unzipped all night and essentially used it as a blanket with a foot sack. On top of my 3" sleeping pad, I was very warm and actually sweated most of the night but the bag didn't get damp inside and stayed lofty.

I highly recommend this bag to anyone debating down vs. synthetic - if you're worried about it getting wet and not working, keep it dry - not that hard really. But after sweating in it all night, I would say the DriDown coating seems to work just fine and the aspect of it being down seemed to let it breathe better than synthetic without sacrificing warmth.

Some reviews claimed the 6' bag was a bit confining, so I went for the 6'6" just to have some wiggle room and to be able to stash some clothes in the foot area to keep warm over night and I'm very pleased with the roominess (I'm pretty much 6' even with very broad shoulders), I could turn and roll about and not get all bound up in the bag.

Zipper can get snagged if you don't pay attention to what you're doing but not really an issue (happens easier when you zip it up from the outside - when in the bag it didn't happen once), and doesn't seem to be a threat to tearing the bag.

In short - great bag, solid construction, comfortable and light. Get a waterproof compression sack and it will be flawless for backpacking into even the most inhospitable weather. If your tall or broad or a violent sleeper, go 6'6", you'll be glad you did, and no real extra weight for the added comfort. Forget synthetic that will break down and loose loft faster. With proper care and upkeep, this bag should last for some time. (If you can, always try to hang it loose for long term storage). Now get your butt out there and camp!

product_title: Critical Cycles Dutch Style Step-Thru 7-Speed Shimano Hybrid Urban Commuter Road Bicycle
review_body:
I'm not a bike expert nor have I ever assembled a bicycle before. That said, the bike itself seems great but assembling it was more work than I had originally thought.

Pros:

1. Great manufacturer customer support. There were missing parts that I emailed the manufacturer about and they sent the missing parts right away (very impressive!)
2. Bike looks great. The components seem very high quality, and everything arrived without scratches or dents. I haven't been able to ride it yet due to the problems listed below.

Cons:

1. There is no manual and you will need a decent set of tools as the all-in-one tool that comes with the bike won't cut it.
2. Some parts can have trouble fitting. One of the pedals was not able to screw in at all and contacting customer support recommended that I bring it to a bike shop to have it installed.
3. Even with good packaging, some parts are still misaligned (eg. back tire rubbing against something). This is understandable given that it was shipped in a box but it isn't obvious to me how to fix it.

To quote the manufacturer's website: \\"To insure that every component on your bicycle is working properly, Critical Cycles recommends that all Critical Cycles bikes be assembled by a qualified mechanic. Improper assembly of your bicycle may lead to premature wear or failure of individual components such as headsets, crank assembly, drivetrain, brakes, and wheels.\\" In the end, it feels like it would have been a better idea to buy this bike fully assembled in the bike shop rather than online. Or one should factor in the cost of bringing it into a bike shop to get it assembled and tuned properly.

product_title: CAMP CHEF 14X32 Italia Artisan Outdoor Pizza Oven Accessory, Silver
review_headline: Not true Neapolitan, but still very good!
review_body:
First of all...

I am a true pizza fanatic, I own a 48" wood fired oven and use it to make true neapolitan pizza. As such, I have a fair bit of experience with "artisan" style pizza as well as many others.

I have had a camp chef EX280LW for two years now along with several of the accessories and have been happy with its performance. When I saw this oven pop up, I knew I had to have it.

I must admit that I was very skeptical, a lot of pizza oven claim to be able to make neapolitan style pizza but very few can live up to that claim. I was especially dubious of the design having a large open front as well as instructions that stated a proper cooking temperature of 600F - way too cool for neapolitan pizza which I bake at 800-900F.

However, with a camping trip coming up, I went ahead and ordered one anyway. After the oven arrived, I was fairly pleased with the construction, including a large stone and a stainless "dome". It is not heavyweight and there is no insulation, so the oven is not exactly oozing in ultra high build quality. However, since it is designed for camping, I appreciate the cost effectiveness as well as the portable weight of the design. I may try to add insulation to the top of the dome as well as cover some of the front opening, but that is down the road.

For the camping trip, I prepped 24 8oz dough balls and brought loads of toppings to try. I went ahead and fired up the EX280LW at medium heat, it took a little bit to get the temps regulated but after about 20 min, I had it figured out. Out of my personal preference for high temperature pizza, I went ahead and fired the little oven almost as hot as I could get it. The stone floor temp was about 750F according to my IR thermometer and the dome was a little over 800F.

Overall, the event was a success, for some reason though, even though my temps were high, it took the pizzas about 3 min to bake, I hope to tweak my process and get those bake times down to 2min or less.

What I learned...

This oven is not a miracle worker, it will not replace my wood fired oven for any of my normal pizza needs, however, it is a very easy, convenient solution that allows excellent pizzas to be made on the campsite without transporting a heavy mobile oven or expending the money needed for such an investment. All in all, it performed nearly as well as I hoped, and better than expected.ss and get those bake times down to 2min or less.

product_title: Zebralight H502W - Neutral White LED
review_body: Let's set the record straight from the start... This isn't a typical flashlight.  It's Better!  O.K. so it doesn't send a laser-bright beam of light down-range 300 yards. It's a FLOOD light.  It's good out to about 25 feet (9 meters to our friends across the pond, and to the north, south, and well everywhere else...) but in that distance, it brightens everything within a 120 degree swath.  It's incredibly useful as a work light as the immediate area you're trying to illuminate is evenly lit and you're not staring at a retina-melting hot spot.  It's WAAAAAY less fatiguing to your eyes!  As far as build quality, Zebralight is in a class of their own!  Exceptionally made, extremely well thought out design except for one little thing, you pretty much have to remove the pocket/shirt clip to get it in the headband for use as a headlight.  Not a huge deal, as it's easy to do, but it's also easy to misplace said pocket/shirt clip... oh well, almost perfect!  I've read reviews where people have complained that this type of wide beam flashlight, and specifically the Zebralight H502 isn't good for walking around the woods at night... which is nuts!  If you need a light that you can use to count the rings in a coon's tail from 100 yards, up a tree... this isn't it.  But for lighting up EVERYTHING out to 25 feet in front, to the side, above and below in one glance, this light is PERFECT!

product_title: Texsport Jumbo Easy Set-Up Folding Sleeping Camp Cot
review_body:
The instructions that came with this talk about velcro on one side which allows you to easily set this up and adjust the tension of the canvas for comfort and also for setting up. There is talk of that in the product description when I bought it and at the time of this writing. I quote: "with VELCRO-brand wrap around closure for quick setup"

Unfortunately, I am unable to find any velcro on this unit and have no idea what the "wrap-around closure" is I should be looking for. The pictures in the instructions seem to have no relation to the product I actually have.

I did find it difficult to put together, but I think I figured out the trick. Since a lot of reviews complain about difficulty in putting the unit together, this is what I did:

1) Slip the small rod through the canvas on one side; and pop the holes into place. This should be easy; since you don't have any tension because the other side isn't secured yet. I did have to push down on the cot to get the rod to click into place.
2) Put the longer rod through the canvas on the other side. You'll notice that the holes are not even on the longer rod. One hole is close to the edge; and the other has a lot of space between the edge and the hole.
3) On the side of the rod where the hole is closest to the edge; click it into place. This will be less easy than step 1, but still doable.
4) On the other side of the rod; you now have a handle between the hole and the end of the rod. You can put one hand on the cot and one hand on the space between the end of the rod and the hole. This is your leverage; and you should be able to use it to secure the final hole into place.

product_title: NiteRider Lumina Handlebar Mount
review_body:
I have a NiteRider light and the handlebar mount it came with always left me wondering if it was going to fall off. Or it would constantly tip downwards bit by bit with every bump I hit. I decided to see if I could find a more secure way to keep my light on my handlebar and after a bit of searching I found this. So far it seems to work pretty well.

There was a period of time right after buying it that I thought for sure that it was not going to work. The rubber gasket that it comes with is very thick, and lets the mount clamp down very securely onto smaller sized handlebars very effectively. However, the gasket is way too thick to use with oversized handlebars, which is what I have right now. I tried using the gasket off of the original mount, but even that was slightly too thick.

Finally one day I scrapped the gasket idea altogether and simply clamped this thing down with no gasket. Voila! It worked. I had to snug it down pretty tightly to keep it from slipping/tipping with the light on. But, I was able to find a tension that worked well enough without making me think I was going to compromise my handlebar. So far it has held up admirably and kept my light secure without tipping.

I would give it five starts but for that simple fact that I had to completely go without the gasket on oversized handlebars. Using a gasket would make me feel better about the amount of friction keeping it in place, and also prevent it from scratching the finish of my handlebars. As it is it works well, and fits, if just only.

product_title: InStep Quick N EZ Double Bicycle Trailer
review_headline: Just Okay, Not Sure How To Improve Though
review_body:
This gets four stars for flexibility, though it is probably a 3-star on comfort for 2 kids, and a 3-star as a jog stroller.

I'm an avid runner and a former cyclist, so I was looking forward to having some flexibility when pushing / pulling my three year old and my five year old. First things first: it's cramped in there with two fairly 'lean' kids, with a combined weight under 70 pounds. shoulder-to-shoulder is the issue...though it's fantastic with a single kid back there. I don't know if I would want a wider trailer (due to narrow sidewalks), so I'm not sure there is a solution to this problem.

If the tow arm is stowed, make sure you 'convert it' before you load the kids up. The tow-arm stows underneath the trailer, and you basically have to lay the kids on their backs in the trailer to get to where the arm stows.

The hook-up is a spring that bends 90' to jack into a 'port' that you install on your rear wheel hookup. Downside... Because there is so much tension in this spring, you have to turn the bike sideways when hooking it up, or your bike will likely fall over. Hookup is otherwise easy and quick. the spring adds 'give', which makes makes it a bit more forgiving for an uneven pedal cadence.

Pushing it is an adequate experience, but coming from a real jog stroller (I think mine is a babytrend), this is only \\"meh\\".

Storage is pretty bad, especially if you're used to a no-kidding jog stroller, though there is *some* storage in the back, poorly segregated from the passenger compartment.
The cover comes over it for rainproofing, and the plastic shield doubles as a good insulator for chilly fall weather, which is good.

product_title: Sevylor Spare Parts Kit
review_headline: For the Sevylor kayaker that has everything.
review_body:
This repair kit came with a bunch of stuff you hope you will never need, bust must have if you do. I figured for the price it was worth keeping in the dry box for river trips. Hope for the best but be prepared for the worst I always say.

UPDATE - I am raising this kit from 4 stars to 5. That's because I just came back from a river trip with a thorn in one of my K79 Tahiti kayaks. It happened at a class V takeout trail that was completely overgrown with blackberries. (NOTHING will puncture a Sevylor K79 Tahiti Classic kayak quite as easily as a darned thorn on the river bank!) Fortunately the included PVC glue and patch material fixed it right up as good as new. I also like that the patch material is clear, so you hardly even notice the finished repair. I wish I had had this material for another thorn hole I repaired several years back on another boat with whatever material I had on hand. That patch worked great too, but it doesn't look nearly as good as this one.

I have three Sevylor Tahiti kayaks for class II & III river tripping with friends and family. And I ALWAYS take along a small dry box packed with repair items one might need in case of a hole or valve malfunction. The Sevylor Spare Parts Kit isn't EVERYTHING you might need, but it is certainly a very important part of a good emergency plan.

The glue and patch material with this kit is more for permanent, home-based, over-night repairs than for emergency ones on a river bank, but it is good stuff. For quicker, \\"emergency\\" repairs check out the Sevylor emergency patches that have a peel-off backing and then go on like tape.

review_headline: Lightweight, convenient travel size when deflated, easily inflated
review_body: My buddy and I recently  took the Conquest Dyad inflatable kayak for a 2 day camping trip in Northwest Washington at Lake Cushman. Let me just say this thing was great! We were skeptical at first about purchasing because we didn't know how heavy it was going to be or if it was going to be too big to carry with us, but we were extremely satisfied with the purchase! We switched off carrying our backpack full of camping gear and the inflatable kayak and I'm not going to lie the inflatable kayak was much lighter and better to carry than our camp gear! Also comes with two paddles that break down very for very easy stow. Inflating this bad boy was a breeze with the pump thats included with it. My buddy and I are somewhat big guys (6'1\\" - 210lb, 6' - 195lb) and we hopped in this and it took us out on the water for a full day of kayaking adventures. Not once did we run into any issues with having to re-inflate due any air leakage and it kept us afloat for HOURS of paddling. One of the coolest features is the clear bottom on this inflatable kayak, its awesome being able to look down under the water as you paddle around. When we eventually set up camp we just set the Dyad aside leaving it inflated overnight so we could get any early start and when we through this beast of a kayak back in the water the next morning it was almost like we had just inflated it. No air loss, no signs of a full day of use the day before. Great quality, great product, I've checked out Conquest's website (conquestadventuregear.com) and am now very interested in their Inflatable SUP, considering buying it sometime this month. After the satisfaction I received from the Dyad inflatable kayak, I'm sure it won't disappoint.

review_body: I keep one in my golf bag.  When gnats and mosquitoes are out I can play comfortably.  I like it so much better than deet which feels hot and oily and stinks. review_body: I purchased these pedals so that I could optionally wear my mountain biking shoes. I find them hard to clip into while riding because they have to be flipped. The clips protrude a lot so even when you are wearing flats you have to flip the pedal or it becomes uncomfortable. Maybe there's a technique to letting go so that the pedals are in the correct position when they spin around?

product_title: The North Face Vault Backpack, TNF Black, One Size
review_headline: Perfect size for high school senior to use
review_body: This backpack is made very well. It looks good. It is very sturdy and we anticipate it will last the entire school year - (not like some of the other packpacks we've bought in the past).

product_title: Handlebar DELTA SMART PHONE HOLDER
review_body: Bought one originally and liked it enough to buy a second for my other bike.  Fits my iphone 5 while in an otterbox case.  Not sure how long the shock cords that keep the 2 sides together will retain their integrity but so far, I like it.

review_body: The strongest DEET on the market by far.  You cannot buy this strong in the stores.  It works like no other insect repellent.

product_title: Allen Sports Deluxe 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack
review_body:
I recently purchased this bike rack, and so far, it's done its job. It requires very minimal assembly (you have to insert two metal supports into holes in the upper bracket in order for the rack to support itself--be careful, though; I almost lost a finger trying to wrestle the support into the hole, as my finger got pinched), and the instructions are easy-to-read. There are also instructions for rigging the rack if your car doesn't have proper support under the bumper like it shows in the picture. My beef with the item is thus, and just nitpicky things: 1) I've been pulled over by law enforcement twice because the bottom part of the rack inconveniently goes right across the license plate and obscures the numbers--no, I wasn't doing anything illegal, either. 2) My bike is a Schwinn cruiser and the frame assembly near the seat is too wide to fit properly into the support, but the nylon straps are long enough that it fastens, plus, I use the straps that attach to the top of the trunk as extra security and wrap them around my frame at various points as added security. 3) Speaking of the supports and straps, it can be a little tricky undoing the straps. To secure the bike, you thread the strap through the plastic buckle and tighten. When unfastening the straps, it gets a little frustrating, but my previous rack had a flimsy rubber \\"buckle\\" and the straps were velcro, so obviously, after a while outside in the elements, the rubber broke down and actually gave out one day while trying to fasten my bike, plus the velcro was starting to lose its grip, so like I said, this is just a personal gripe. 4) When my bike is on the rack, again, a nitpick, but my back tire sticks out from the back a little too far for my comfort, and when driving down narrow residential streets, I fear hitting other vehicles with my tire, but so far, this hasn't happened yet.

All-in-all, this is a good product for the money. It gets its job done. I'd recommend this product if you're looking for an inexpensive way to get your bikes from point A to B.

product_title: Louis Garneau Men's 12c Air Gel Cycling Gloves
review_body:
These are extremely well designed, comfortable gloves that include lots of thoughtful features such as tabs to help take the gloves off and a well placed, thick chamois that makes it easy to wipe sweat off the brow. The padding is in just the right places, and (in concert with some Ergon bike grips) has made it possible for me to ride much longer without any numbness in my hands.

About the only complaint I can lodge against these gloves is that due to all that padding, they're not the best choice for rides on hot/humid days.

product_title: Bones Bearings Reds Bearings
review_body:

product_title: Shimano Cycling RevoShift 18 Speed Shifter Set SL-RS35-R/L - 58751112SET
review_body:

review_body: The tent quality, overall, is good. Good summer tent. Nice and airy at night. For those that said the rain fly leaves you exposed, you put it on wrong. Easy to set up. review_headline: Well Designed, Brief Use So Far

product_title: KiDooo XEME Triangle Bag
review_body: Love the color, and high quality. Stores tools, two tubes, screw driver, pump, and I still have room. Would highly recommend!

product_title: Camp Chef Everest High Output 2 Burner Stove
review_headline: Works well, especially with a bulk tank.
review_body:
the heat output is excellent. it works consistently and will boil water quickly.

Like most camp stoves the heat settings really go from "high to really really high" but with that expectation and a bit of care it is really easy to cook with.

I suggest getting the bulk tank adapter and using the larger tanks as the smaller ones end up getting frosted up more easily... options help.

The only real downside was that the manufacturing of the cover is a bit on the flimsy side. This appears to be a common complaint but when I looked it over I didn't consider it a dealbreaker.

product_title: Helly Hansen Girl's K Synergy Jacket
review_body: We love the look and the colors of the jacket. This will be our second winter with it and it is still in good shape.

product_title: Victorinox Swiss Army MiniChamp Pocket Knife
review_body:
This particular model of knife has everything I want and nothing I don't use.

The main blade is very sturdy and sharp, as it should be. The nail file and cuticle pusher are probably my most frequently used tools, as I enjoy clean, well shaped fingernails. The ball point pen is one of those things you don't appreciate unless you know what is feels like to carry one so handy with you. All of the tools, though, are fantastic. The tool itself feels just the right size, not too thick but not at all lacking in grabable (made up word) surface area.

My friends joke and call it a "feminine" knife, because I myself am a woman and this knife's tools suit me so perfectly. This was a great choice for my first Victorinox product and will definitely be looking into the large knives soon! A very nice product.

product_title: Origin8 Pro Cork Handlebar Tape
review_body:
I was hoping it would be a little cushier, and a little darker orange, but works just fine. Easy to install...I did it myself and had never done handlebar tape before.

I would call the color a "light orange".

It's cushy, especially compared to the decades old tape I had before, but I was hoping it would be a little cushier. No big deal though.

review_body: I have a 2013 Trek Marlin, with 29 inch wheels and disc breaks, and this stand fits it quite nicely.

product_title: Thule 9001 Raceway 2 Bike Rear Mounted Bike Rack
review_headline: Easy to get on car. Getting bike on is a different story.
review_body: I have a Mini Cooper and a big 20" Trek Alant. Female, with Thule frame adapter. After some thought and experiments, I found an ok position with the front wheel off so that nothing pokes out too much or hangs down too far and nothing can touch the car. A bit hard to close the hatch with rack mounted, and instructions on where to put the straps could be clearer. However, no dents or scratches after first use (10 miles in city). Held up fine in an all out emergency stop from 40 mph and a few potholes. The straps are fun: no fabric to flap around or tie down or cut to steal bike.

product_title: GSI Outdoors Glacier Stainless Bottle Cup/Pot
review_body:
People with experience with camp pots will know what to expect, size wise. But this came very small. Small is good. It's the size of an oversize coffee cup, and holds a 40 ounce klean kanteen (with maybe a slight wiggle, barely). I used it to boil water, and it did perfectly.

Some people complain about the handle. I find them to be perfect. They're small and lightweight, and didn't heat up while I boiled water. They tuck perfectly against the sides of the cup, keeping it's profile very small. Very thrilled with the purchase.

A tip for any of you new campers: if you place this on a wood fire, it will blacken with soot. They all do. It can be washed off, but is a pain. Bring along some dish soap to rub along the edges when you cook, and it makes cleaning the black stuff off VERY easy. The soot wont cling to the cup, and water will rinse it off very easy. Enjoy!

review_body: I've been using this pump a few days every week for nearly 7 months now.  I haven't had a problem in any form and the gauge works as great.  I'd buy it again no question.

review_body:

During the middle of the night I was so hot that I just unzipped the sleeping bag and laid on top of me like a quilt and was perfectly comfortable.

I'm 6'6" 215lbs and it's barely long enough and wide enough for me, but I was still pretty comfortable inside it. Any bigger though and I wouldn't recommend it.

Some have complained about the smell, but I only noticed it because I put my nose right on in and smelled. You can definitely smell the duck when you do that, but while lying in it I can't smell anything.

The only annoying thing about the bag is that the zipper gets caught quite easily so you have to be careful when zipping it up, but I would definitely buy this again.

review_body: This saddle has given the relief desired, which means I can ride longer with more comfort. It was easy to install and has given me the pleasure of biking again.

product_title: Takara Kabuto Single Speed Road Bike
review_headline: Some May Like It, Not for Me. Kind of Unsafe.
review_body:
So I purchased this bike after reading some really great reviews. After two weeks, and about 6-7 rides of various lengths, I'm returning it.

The Good- Looks nice, great price, easy assembly, seem reliable.

The Bad- The stock brakes are pretty weak and would need an upgrade.

The Ugly- a prior reviewer mentioned this, but I missed it. On any sharp turn of the front tire, whichever pedal is forward can and will hit the front tire. I'm not sure why I didn't notice this at first, because it's pretty serious. This isn't a huge deal if you're at a stop or cruising in a straight line, but on my last ride, I cut to avoid a car pulling out, the tire jammed into my foot/the pedal, and I wiped out pretty bad (thankfully wearing my helmet and fell out of traffic's way). I wasn't sure what had happened at first, but after picking myself and my bike up, it's pretty clear that the front tire doesn't turn freely and will hit a pedal and your foot. If you ride in the city, I'd be wary.

Other reviewers seem to like this bike, so maybe this is just me, but I don't feel any kind of safe on this bike. I haven't had this problem with any other bike I've owned (more than a few), and I won't be keeping this one.

product_title: DuPont Teflon Non-Stick Dry-Film Lubricant
review_headline: Slightly Waxy, But No Oily Residue
review_body: Almost all the other Teflon sprays have some oily residue or prominent waxy residue. This spray is good in that it is the most dry or the dry Teflon sprays. It doesn't go on thick, but that can be good. The carrier liquid evaporates quickly. I did try to use it to slick up the inside of a holster. It did stain the leather a little and the white Teflon residue on the weapon was annoying. On other uses where you need a dry lube, it is works well. product_title: Profile Design Cork Wrap

product_title: Coleman 10 x 10 ft. Swingwall Instant Canopy
review_headline: Really like the tent, but maybe somebody could have re-read the instructions before printing them!
review_body:
This was our first pop up tent and this one is sweet...once you get it to its full open position. Maybe others who are more tent savvy didn't have the learning curve issue with the instructions. Having the fold down wall is a great option as is the air vent at the top.

The only other downsides (besides the poor instructions) we've seen are 1) the lack of space for the folded tent roof inside the rolling storage bag and, 2) the ability to actually roll the darn thing. The center of gravity combined with the awkward handle when rolling the bag makes it unlikely that one will roll it much. review_headline: Warning: this product is total junk, DO NOT BUY!!! Coleman brand means nothing here.

I bought the Coleman Hot Water On Demand and used it for a camping trip worked fine for 2 showers then the unit completely died. It was under 30 days so Amazon took it back and let me have a new one. I tested out the new one on arrival and it worked fine. A few months later we went camping and it was dead on arrival. It exhibited the same problem many other reviewers talk about: it shows the battery is dead even though the battery is fine. I tried connecting the spare, fully charged battery and it still thinks the battery is dead. Now Amazon won't take it back and Coleman is giving me the runaround. My cost for 2 showers was over $250! PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE avoid this product at all costs. It is scarey to think such a great, trusted brand as Coleman could put their name on such garbage.

I read up on the Mr. Heater water heater which is similar but clearly more advanced, like digital temperature readout, you can use a car lighter (can't do that with Coleman), and it has separate water outlet for the shower. That will probably be my replacement.

product_title: NiteRider Lumina 650 Light
review_headline: Now THIS is a bike light!
review_body:
I'm doing mostly urban riding nowadays, I can usually get someplace nice and not crowded but there's no way to avoid spending some time on busy roadways. Being Boston, these roads have unusual intersections, and are usually pretty narrow. I want to make sure I'm visible, and since I end up returning in the twilight or dark some of the time I also wanted a light to let me see in the only occasionally lit park paths.

Originally I got the [[ASIN:B00CQU00EI Planet Bike SuperFlash Turbo Bicycle Tail Light]] for the rear, and the [[ASIN:B0015R1NE4 Planet Bike Blaze 2Watt LED Headlight]] for the front. Planet Bike came well recommended by REI and has a good reputation. I eschew multi-LED lights and care about run-time, so these two seemed like a good fit for me. I have nothing bad to say about the Superflash Turbo, battery life is exceptional and the blinking pattern is very noticeable. Bright enough to catch the attention of cars coming from behind even during the day, and extremely annoying at night which is perfect. The Blaze 2W seemed pretty good at the time, and honestly if I never found myself biking in the dark it would probably be fine. The batteries last long enough and are easy to change, it's bright enough to catch notice, and the mount and light are pretty well built. However, when it comes to actually needing to light up the path ahead it's not going to find you those potholes until you're already on top of them.

The NiteRider Lumina 650 comes well reviewed, and now that I have it and have taken it out a few times (once biking along the Esplanade and through Jamaica Way / River Way park after 10:00) I have to say there is simply no comparison. I have some other high end flashlights from Surefire, and the Lumina 650 is definitely in that category.

First of all, it is bright. I find that the medium setting (3 hours run time) is plenty for partially lit trail riding, although riding along the road where street lights and cars are common I liked using high (1.5 hrs runtime) to see into shadows cast across the road. Low (5.5 hrs runtime) is plenty for slower riding or where it's for real dark (not in a city). The blink mode appears to be full brightness and is incredibly aggressive, maybe two flashes per second, will catch anyone's attention during the day or dusk but frankly disorienting at night. I prefer the blink mode of the Planet Bike Blaze 2W since it is more random, has variations in brightness, and is less disorienting as a result. I would say the Planet Bike's High setting is approximately equal to the Lumina 650's low setting, but that's not really even fair since the Lumina 650 casts a much more even and wide beam. This light makes the Planet Bike seem like a toy.

Secondly, the light quality of the Lumina 650 is exceptional. The color is rather blue-white, not so much that you notice on its own but really like an HID headlight - it makes other lights look yellow. The beam itself is very even, a wide beam with great peripheral illumination that is a good match to the field of view needed when cycling. I had to turn a pretty sharp low-speed corner to get out of the beam, otherwise I never felt myself searching beyond it. The center is brighter, and if you aim it right it will provide extremely consistent illumination well down the path ahead of you. I was unable to out-ride this light on flats, and only a little bit going downhill where streetlights reduced the relative brightness of the Lumina 650. Really great optics and good choices all around. Even if the Planet Bike Blaze 2W was much brighter it wouldn't be as usable as the Lumina 650 since its beam is so narrow it just doesn't light up enough of the street so you're always out-riding it.

Thirdly, the build quality is very good. The light appears to have a cast, anodized aluminum frame that secures the battery and optics. Surrounding much of this frame is plastic that seems pretty durable to me. The activation switch is positive and well protected, as is the USB charging inlet on the bottom (which is protected by a rubber gasket, retained at one end). I would have no qualms about subjecting this light to normal abuse, and while I wouldn't go swimming with it I can't imagine it having a problem in any kind of weather. Feels very good in the hand, I would even toss it in my backpack for an overnight hike.

Of course, no light is perfect, so while I believe that this is a Real Damn Light that you should seriously consider spending the extra money for, I have a few complaints. The mount is well built, but the light is not secured to it as well as I'd like: I can bump it off the mount if I push my body against the handlebars - no problems with releasing on very bumpy trails though. Also, tightening the screw that clamps the mount onto your handlebars too much with cause it to release, easy to avoid but it remains to be seen if the light will stay in place and not slide down my tapered bars. The recharge time is also considerable, not a problem if you can leave it overnight but don't expect to be able to recharge it fully in a few hours at a friend's house. My main concern with this light is that I strongly prefer replaceable batteries. The light is regulated and will provide constant illumination until it's close to running out of juice, at which point it will make it clear to you that you'd better hurry up by changing the color of the light in its activation switch from blue to red. That said, I can easily charge it before any big rides and I cannot imagine the run time will be a problem - but if you're a forgetful person you may want to carry a cheaper backup. There are brighter lights with longer run times but then you need to have an external battery pack, which I definitely didn't want.

Long Story Short: This is a well built light with enough output for any situation the average road and park rider may find themselves in. Well worth the quite reasonable price tag, and leaps and bounds ahead of anything cheaper.ion switch is positive and well protected, as is the USB charging inlet on the bottom (which is protected by a rubber gasket, retained at one end). I would have no qualms about subjecting this light to normal abuse, and while I wouldn't go swimming with it I can't imagine it having a problem in any kind of weather. Feels very good in the hand, I would even toss it in my backpack for an overnight hike.

Of course, no light is perfect, so while I believe that this is a Real Damn Light that you should seriously consider spending the extra money for, I have a few complaints. The mount is well built, but the light is not secured to it as well as I'd like: I can bump it off the mount if I push my body against the handlebars - no problems with releasing on very bumpy trails though. Also, tightening the screw that clamps the mount onto your handlebars too much with cause it to release, easy to avoid but it remains to be seen if the light will stay in place and not slide down my tapered bars. The recharge time is also considerable, not a problem if you can leave it overnight but don't expect to be able to recharge it fully in a few hours at a friend's house. My main concern with this light is that I strongly prefer replaceable batteries. The light is regulated and will provide constant illumination until it's close to running out of juice, at which point it will make it clear to you that you'd better hurry up by changing the color of the light in its activation switch from blue to red. That said, I can easily charge it before any big rides and I cannot imagine the run time will be a problem - but if you're a forgetful person you may want to carry a cheaper backup. There are brighter lights with longer run times but then you need to have an external battery pack, which I definitely didn't want.

Long Story Short: This is a well built light with enough output for any situation the average road and park rider may find themselves in. Well worth the quite reasonable price tag, and leaps and bounds ahead of anything cheaper.

product_title: Coleman Elite WeatherMaster Tent - 17'x9' 6 Person Cabin Tent with LED Light System & Screenroom
review_headline: It LEAKED, but Coleman replaced the tent.
review_body:
I liked the tent except for one major problem - the bottom leaked. Otherwise, it is very well designed. Very nice front alcove design, nice stiff \\"D\\" door design, good LED lighting. The product is great except for its primary reason for existence - the inside gets soaked. It may be a manufacturing defect, but the Customer Service number NEVER PICKS UP. The Coleman web site recommends an online submission for replacement, but THEY HAVE NOT RESPONDED after 2 weeks. End result: Poor product support of a terrific idea which has a fatal flaw.

ADDENDUM: July 30, 2013; replacement tent from Coleman arrived. Their warrantee process is a bit convoluted, but they ultimately stand behind their product. Instead of one star, I will give it three for Customer Service, and if there are no leaks when camping, I will give it five stars.

ADDENDUM #2: July 8, 2014. We pitched the tent before Hurricane Arthur passed by, and despite hours of unrelenting deluge, there was NO WATER in the tent. Five stars.

product_title: Native Eyewear Silencer Polarized Sunglasses
review_headline: WARNING! For "Moss," wrong color is stocked! Box is incorrectly labeled!
review_body:
I have attempted to order these glasses from Amazon a total of three times now. Each time I have received a box with a label that says \\"Frame Color: Moss; Lens Color: Silver Reflex\\" on the outside, but the actual glasses inside are dark brown with a brown lens. (I see that at least one other reviewer has had this problem but apparently still thought that the color was \\"Moss\\"...?!). The first time this happened, I returned them for a replacement, but the second pair were also mislabeled. At that point, I called Amazon to inform them that they must have an entire shipment of glasses that are labeled incorrectly. They assured me that they would contact their supplier and fix the problem. They said that the glasses in \\"Moss\\" would be temporarily unavailable on the Amazon site, but that they would be able to restock the correct color within about 7 days. A couple of days later, I checked back on the site and saw that, indeed, the color \\"Moss\\" was no longer available. Once it became available again, I waited well over a month before attempting to order them again. Guess what happened...yup, I received another mislabeled pair. I called Amazon again and told them the entire story from the beginning. The service representative assured me that he would personally see to it that I received the correct color glasses. I emphasized to him that someone needed to physically OPEN the box and LOOK at the glasses inside; that the box would say \\"Moss\\" but the color inside would be dark brown/black. He assured me that it would not happen again and arranged for me to return the wrong ones at no charge. He also said that he would send out the replacement pair via 1-day delivery at no extra charge. That was just this afternoon.

Amazon has been very responsive, but so far they have not actually fixed the problem. If they did get another shipment in from their supplier, somebody dropped the ball by not checking it to make sure it was the correct color. I'd give them long odds forbeing able to get it right this time, but since it wasn't costing me anything for the shipping back and forth, I decided to take a chance. The replacement pair should arrive tomorrow. Check back here for an update!

UPDATE! Can you guess what I received today? You got it...The box says \\"Moss,\\" but the frames are dark brown/black with a dark brown lens. I am now giving up on Amazon and going elsewhere to purchase these sunglasses.

My advice: DON'T BUY THESE FROM AMAZON if you want the frames in \\"Moss\\"...

product_title: Columbia Men's Coolhead Cachalot Hat (Omni-Freeze ZERO)
review_headline: Coolest hat ever! (Plus a secret for XL sizing)
review_body:
This is one of the greatest hats ever! I usually don't like wearing hats for two reasons, 1. They usually make me sweat and overheat, 2. They usually don't fit my (very) large head!

1. This hat has so much Omni-Freeze material that it's covering all the bases for cooling. The top of your head has venting and swelling cooling material. The sides of the sweatband are triple lined with cooling fabric and the bill even has the same material to keep it from baking in the sun.

For those of you that haven't seen them around, the Omni-Freeze material is similar to the \\"cooling towels\\" and neckerchiefs that hikers sometimes wear. Having it cover your ears and neck keeps you from burning your ears and the flapping sensation actually cools you off very quickly.

2. If you have a larger than normal head/hat size, use this tip:
Turn the hat upside down, fold out the sweatband, make a small incision near the end of the \\"shock cable\\" elastic band.
You should be able to remove it completely with out a trace afterwards that it's missing... and an immediate upgrade to an Extra-Large cooling hat!
