review_body: I really like these pants, but when I ordered them, I was replacing a Large and moving to an XL, but the XL was too small. I ordered a new pair in a XXL and they were hanging off of me. I wish there was more adjustment in the waist. Other than that I like them.

product_title: Lizard Skins Clear Skin Chainstay Protector
review_body: This item is perfect, just the right thickness to roll on smooth and bubble free. Extra protectors will come in handy when I find the rubs on my new bike. Super fast and priced right .

product_title: Sea Lion Junior Floating Fins
review_body: I did not want to spend a lot for a pair of flippers for a growing child. This is made of wonderful quality. Bought a pair for my 7-year old son, weighs 55 lb. The size I got which is size CHILD 1-3 fits perfectly and stil has room to grow another size. My son wears a size two rubber shoes. Hope this helps for new buyers in guaging which size to get. You will not be disappointed.

product_title: 1000 Lumens Tactical Flashlight,Asben T6 High Powered Handheld Torch with Rechargeable 26650 Lithium Ion Battery and Charger, 5 Modes Zoomable …
review_headline: The Best Flashlight I Have Ever Owned
review_body:
I backed this product when it was just a Kickstarter effort, and I honestly can say I have never regretted doing so. While the fact that I can program this light is awesome--and has prompted some jealousy from my coworkers at the engineering firm where I work--the real value of this light is in the quality. It produces stunningly clear light for quite a long time, and you can pretty much drive a car over this thing and it won't be appreciably harmed. (As someone who tends to toss everyday tech into pockets and backpacks a little more haphazardly than she should, a nigh-indestructible product is of considerable value to me.)

If you are looking for a good flashlight small enough to fit in a backpack or satchel pocket, bright enough to use in pretty much any situation *and* sturdy enough to stand up to whatever abuse you can throw at it, I highly recommend the FLEX.

product_title: SimplySleeper SS-27Q Inflatable Full Air Mattress Bed with Built-In Foot Pump (Inflates in 4 mins) - Best material in the market!
review_body: Im a big&tall guy and weigh over 500. This not only supports my weight, but it feels like my bed at home (if not better). Its designed very smart and does not "wave" at all. Each side is divided down the middle instead of the cheap airmatress way of tubes that go the full length of the matress. It makes a HUGE difference. Also it has a built in pump so no more blowing, no battery powered pumps, just pump it for a while.. and presto. I use it every weekend at my camp. It hold air great. I have only pumped it up once and its held it for 6wks of camping no problem. I love it and always tell people that its awesome. My friends envy my tent setup because I have a Camprite double cot and this SimplySleeper matress on top! Its really great! BUY IT, BUY IT, BUY IT!!!

product_title: Tilley Endurables LTM6 Airflo Hat
review_body:
Great hats. Lightweight, washes great, can be worn year round. I own 2, one for working outside and the other for trips to the mountains or beach or just going to town. I bought another for a retirement gift for my brother-in-law. He loves it!
Best hat you can buy!

product_title: TETON Sports ComfortLite Self Inflating Pillow; Free Stuff Sack Included
review_body: Very comfortable, easy inflation/deflation, excellent price. The only minor complaint is a slightly large pack size/weight but I knew this going into it and the trade-off is with it. This is my fourth product from Teton sports and they just keep on continuing to impress.

product_title: Sea to Summit Lightweight Dry Sack
review_body: The dry bag worked as advertised. My gear remained dry during a 7 day canoe adventure.  I used it to keep my sleeping bag and some other misc gear from getting wet.  It is easy to use and durable for scouters.

product_title: Black Diamond Voyager Lantern
review_body: I just used this on a family camping trip and then a few weeks earlier on a scouting one! It works excellently and casts a good light!

product_title: LotFancy 24V 2A Scooter battery Charger with XLR connector for Ezip Mountain Trailz Schwinn 4.0 S400 S500 Jazzy Power Chair
review_body: Purchased this for a personal mobility device. It hooked up perfectly and charged quickly. What else could I ask for.

product_title: Women's Cycling Biking Pants Underwear Bike Bicycle Padded Shorts
review_body: I liked these a lot but the Large was more like a Small so I gave the item to a petite friend.

product_title: Outdoor Research Men's Helios Sun Hat
review_body: This sun hat met my expectations and is of quality construction.  The waterproofing works well and the brim has stood up to moderate use over the last month.

product_title: Shimano Unisex PD-M520 MTB SPD Pedal
review_body: I use these pedals on both of my road bikes.  They are easy to clip, not too heavy and seem very durable.  I also like that this style clip and cleat seem to be pretty universal.  I can use the same bike shoes on a spin bike.

product_title: Victorinox Swiss Army Classic SD Pocket Knife
review_body: Much thinner than a normal SAK.  Hardly notice in my pocket.  Nice finish.  Sharp.  Looks professional and high quality.  I recommend

product_title: Montado en la pared abrebotellas, Plateado
review_body: This thing is solid, and it has four screws to mount it to what ever you decide. I attached mine to the inside upper left corner. Works like a charm.

product_title: Black Diamond 300 G Refillable Canister
review_headline: Chalk was all busted into powder.
review_body:
As the title says, I did receive my order very quickly. However, all of the "blocks" were busted upon delivery, I had nothing but a canister of pure powder. Needless to say, this was a massive waste of money. I am trying to get the seller to make it up but they will not.

Consider yourself warned.

product_title: Riedell Skates R3 Roller Skate
review_body: We got these for my daughter. She loves them. They roll very smoothly. They suggested going down a size because they run large, but that wasn't the case for us. We had to exchange for a size up from her normal size and there was just a little room to grow.

product_title: Shimano Acera SL-M310 Rapid Fire Shifter, Right (Black, 7-Speed)
review_body: I needed to replace an old shimano handlebar shifter on an older style Specialized mountain bike.  I researched the product, found a great price, purchased, and had it installed @ a local bike shop.  The bike now functions great!  Very Happy!!

product_title: Texsport 3/8-Inch Tent Pole Replacement Kit
review_body: This is an excellent kit that you can assemble the way you want - to do exactly what you want.  The poles are quality material and all of the little doo-dads to make them work are included.

product_title: High Sierra Evolution 28-Inch Drop Bottom Wheeled Duffel
review_body:
I wanted to wait to post my experience with this bag.

Every time I travel I always go over the allotted 50 pound weight limits for flights, but I am happy to announce how much I love this bag! Not only was the price great, but it saved me $$$$$....I was 20 pounds underweight! Well, not me personally but my bag! Woo Hoo! Excellent bag! I had two connecting flights going and three connecting flights coming home and it looks perfect....not a mark, tear, nothing. I was worried when I read some of the ratings, but for me....not a problem...Did I mention how much I loved this bag? :=)

product_title: Sunlite Cloud-9 Bicycle Suspension Cruiser Saddle, Cruiser Gel, Tri-color Black
review_body: This is the most comfortable set you can buy for a beach crusier like mine for those who carry a lot of weight like my wife then a seat like this is most comfortable on any bike.  So throw away that banna size seat that is built for pain and get yourself the Cloud 9 and save your fram from the pain of riding.

product_title: Outdoor Research Women's Oasis Sombrero Hat
review_body: I went to Ecuador with a group of Master Gardeners to work in the Andean Highlands. We were told to bring hats for sun protection. This hat served me well. It's light weight and the broad brim covered my face and neck as I worked.

product_title: U.S. Divers Admiral LX, Island Dry Adult Premium Snorkeling Combo
review_headline: Fits even on my big head
review_body:
I have a 2xl head size, and this still fits fine. I bought these for goofing around in the pool, and they totally make it more fun to swim around. The bite guard does tend to make your mouth tired if you are using it for a prolonged duration, but its nothing worse than if you chewed gum a long time. It could be because i'm new, and biting down harder than i should.

I have tried to go underwater with this, and it does plug the top perfectly each time, and no water can get in. Even if it did, you can blow it out easily. Very ingenious device.

product_title: Liberty Bottleworks Straight Up Aluminum Water Bottle
review_body:
we like large mouth bottles to be able to get ice cubes in and this works great.
the cap seems sturdy so far and seals well.

product_title: XLC Alum MTB Pedals, 9/16"
review_body: These were a great replacement when the original (!) WellGo pedals on my 1985 Bianchi  Alante finally started to wear out. When I saw these here and read in one of the reviews that they were also WellGo, and the price was so reasonable, I tried them out and to date I am very happy with them. They grip my athletic shoes great (I don't use clips) and they look great on the bike. No problem installing them. Just one complaint, which I have seen in other reviews: the reflectors are flimsy and one broke off after only two rides, and I didn't do any rough stunts. Amazon has some replacement reflectors that use metal bolts rather than plastic plugs, so I will probably replace the reflectors with those. But overall a great replacement product for a very reasonable price!

product_title: Coleman Max #95 Insta-Clip 2 Tube Style Lantern Mantles Pack of 2
review_headline: You have to like the brightness
review_body: I don't find the usual tie-off mantles to be difficult.  If anything I thought the clips were a little fiddly on this one.  But it works amazingly well in the Northstar lantern line.  I can't speak to their longevity because I rarely use my lantern, more of a rare camping/emergency supply for me.  I don't see any reason to pick a different mantle.

product_title: Sierra Designs Men's Microlight Pant
review_body: These pants keep me dry - they fold very small in my saddle bag for easy access in case of a downpour

product_title: Coleman Road Trip Propane Portable Grill LXE
review_body: buy it....... a must for everyone who camps. you wont be disappointed. great buy for the money. quality is great

product_title: Coleman Egg Container (12 Count)
review_headline: But at Walmart for half price
review_body: These didn't work amazing but better than a cheap egg carton turning soggy one hour after being in the ice chest. The main complaint that I had was walmart sells the identical thing for half the price of amazon. I felt like an idiot when I saw them sitting on the shelf for $2 and I had just payed $5 for one on amazon.

product_title: ExOfficio Men's Give-N-Go Brief
review_body: They are dry within 4 hours, which makes them perfect for travel. Also they seem comfortable & as good as the cotton underwear I normally wear.

product_title: Premier Kayak Paddle Splash Guards. Greatly reduces paddle drip. Sold in Pairs.
review_body: these work great if you use them as marketed. Otherwise its kind of a pain to deal with. Hubby is a big stroker with his paddle and these do nothing to help him, while my small easy strokes are perfectly suited with this product.

product_title: Mini Headlamp Headlight Flalshlight Torch
review_body: This product has more value for the price. I used it for my camping and it worked like a charm. The zoom feature is working as described. Visibility up to 15 feet in pitch black. 3 AAA battery is required but not sure about the life. Overall, it's worth five dollars I spent.

product_title: AO Coolers Water-Resistant Vinyl Soft Cooler with High-Density Insulation, 12-Can to 48-Can
review_body: Nice looking ice chest. Holds the ice pretty good. So far no leaks but I've only used a few times

product_title: Intex Pull-out Sofa Inflatable Bed, 76 inch X 87 inch X 26 inch
review_headline: Poor quality, it didn't even last for 2months..
review_body: I would not recommend folks to purchase this product and waste money on it. Better try another quality solid product.

product_title: Camelbak Delaney Plus 24 oz Hydration Pack
review_headline: Disappointing performance, and picture hides front pouch.
review_body: Right out of the box I was surprised to see a pouch sewn to the strap on the front. I guess this would be a nice feature for most people but I wouldn't have ordered it if I had know it was there. I got this for triathlon so I have to put it on quickly and the simpler the better. The other and far more aggravating problem is that the adjusting straps do not hold and the pack loosens very quickly when running. This was so irritating that I had to ditch it on a short training run and pick it up on the way home. Perhaps one could do up the velcro roll up straps so it was not adjustable but then it wouldn't be adjustable right?  It is fine walking so I will probably give it to my mom but I was disappointed.

product_title: Heavy Plastic, Trike Cover
review_body: it was something that my mom was alking to me about  at  my place that i should be able to get as long as i have a lock and key for to be on the safe saide so i can be able to cover my bake so it would not get wet on

product_title: Smartwool Women's Best Friend Sock
review_body: I purchased 4 pairs for my wife, she LOVES THEM!  Comfortable, and safe to put in the dryer without them shrinking.

product_title: HO Sports Hot Shot Child Toddler Life Jacket 2012
review_body: Before purchasing this life jacket for our great-granddaughter, who's 2 years old, I was not aware there are ratings for flotation device safety.  This particular life jacket is not rated to keep a child face-up if the need arises.  We'll use this life jacket when in a swimming pool and we're holding her, but will not risk her in our Kayak if it should capsize.

product_title: Little Tree 20 Junior
review_headline: warm enough but very, very bulky
review_body: I chose this based on the kelty brand but have not been impressed. It's really bulky and no good for backpacking. Car camping or summer camp maybe.

product_title: KMC Z33 NP Chain 5/6 Speed 1/2" x 3/32" x 116L Nickel Plated

product_title: Pearl iZUMi Men's Quest Cycling Short
review_headline: Once you wear cycling shorts, nothing else will do.
review_body:
I got these to try out, as I've never worn cycling shorts like these before. I figured with the decent price, if it wasn't what I wanted, I could just move on. Well as most of you already know, cycling shorts like these make biking much more comfortable. I liked it so much that I bought a second pair of more expensive Pearl iZUMi's and to me, they both seem to work about the same, so save your $$$ and just buy these.

product_title: OGIO Locker Bag
review_body:
This is my second Ogio Locker Duffle bag!
Would not buy any other, my first one lasted over 10 years!

product_title: Seattle Sports Kayak Wall Cradles
review_body:
Hubby wanted to 'build' a kayak rack, but I talked him into these...am I ever glad! So easy to get the boats on and off. He did swap out the screws provided for sturdier ones, though.
Rapid delivery..sturdymproduct.

product_title: Strider ST-3 PREbike (Red)
review_body:
Well made and very lightweight- I was surprised to see my 2.5 year old son pick the bike right up off the ground and walk it off the deck and over to the driveway. Nice paint, robust hardware, and good looking welds make me feel confident about the quality of this bike.

We had a Schwinn pushbike for about 10 minutes and I took it back to the bike shop for a refund... it was way too heavy, poorly made (the seat spun about the seatpost because it was fastened by a single sheetmetal screw that was overtightened at the factory which caused the plastic to crack- which is completely unacceptable engineering if you ask me) and more expensive than the Strider. You can tell by looking at the design that the Schwinn was just a pedal bike sans the crank, but the Strider has definitely been purpose built as a pushbike.

product_title: Oury MBRD Brown MX Grip (Perfect for Machines with Twist Throttle)
review_body: These look great on my Triumph Scrambler.  very vintage and the brown matches my brown leather seat well.  decent vibration dampening as well

product_title: Absolute Outdoor Onyx Adult Type II Life Jacket
review_headline: Cheap way to please the law
review_body:
I just bought 3 of these to abide by the personal life vest law on boats. Have a 12 foot V bottom fishing boat my buddies and i take out. We just toss these in the boat and go fishing. Sometimes I use one as a seat cushion. We all know how to swim, so we never had to actually put one on, but again, they are cheap, they do actually fit, im a 29 yr old 185lb male, and this fits me fine, although not very comfortable, but none of these orange cheap special vests ever were .

if your looking to head out onto the lake for 4th of july weekend, and need some quick life vests, just order these.

product_title: Finish Line Shop Quality Bicycle Chain Cleaner Kit with Lube and Degreaser
review_body: Simply does not clean the chain very well and isn't worth the price vs cleaning with a brush and rag.

product_title: Men's The North Face Half Dome Hoodie Charcoal Grey Heather/Krypton Green Size Large
review_headline: In the Northwest wearing the North Face
review_body: Great hoodie for all of the elements around you. I live in the great wooded northwest and have found this hoodie to meet all of my comfort and warming needs

product_title: Shimano CS-HG20 7-Speed Cassette
review_headline: Wide gear ratio, heavy steel gears
review_body: This enty level casette provides a very wide gear range which has advantages and disadvantages.  The largest gear (34 teeth) provides a low gear for very steep hills. What you loose with this very wide range is that the steps between each gear is several teeth which results in a choice between pedaling very fast or slowly with more effort to maintain your desired speed vs. having more choices that are closer together when you use a cassette that does not have such a wide spread.  I switch between a 28-12 cassette and this 34-11 cassette depending upon whether I need the larger 34 and 30 size gears for very steep hills.  This gear is made of steel and because of the size of the large gears, it quite heavy.  The steel may rust if you get it wet and don't clean it and keep it well lubricated.

product_title: Schwinn Women's Sanctuary 7-Speed Cruiser Bicycle (26-Inch Wheels), Cream/Purple, 16-Inch
review_headline: Bike is great, assembly is terrible
review_body: This bike itself is great.  I love the look of it and it rides really comfortably, but it arrived with the front fork and brakes installed backwards.  I had to take the whole thing to a bike shop and have it reassembled.  Which sucks since I could have gotten the bike locally for a little more money and the extra expense of having it repaired before I could even ride it means I didn't save anything at all.  So I'd definitely recommend the bike itself, but I'm not sure online ordering is the way to go.

product_title: ful Unisex Adult Ditty Mini Backpack
review_body: I wanted a 'Goldilocks' backpack.  One that was not too big and not too small,, this one is just right!

product_title: Glow in the Dark, Water Resistant Rubber Coated Body Super Bright 9 LED Flashlight. Pack of 2
review_body:
When my wife sent me an email with the link for these flashlights and said she wanted to purchase them I became really excited. I was having a pretty tough day (anxiety issues, but I won't get into THAT) and the thought of these little guys was just the pick me up I needed. I must have clicked on the link 20 times over the two days it took for them arrive, thinking about all the ways I could use a little extra light. Check out the basement for any critters, look under the bed for missing socks, I mean, I had all kinds of plans for them.

I had been showing the kids the pictures of the flashlights, too, and let me tell you they were excited with a capital X when they arrived. I let the oldest open the box because the 4 year-old ALWAYS cuts himself with the box cutter when I let him use it. Soon the kids were having a field day with the flashlights. They were having as much fun with them as I was. They did this cool thing where they turned out the lights and used just the flashlights for light. I was dying. So everything was going pretty good with the flashlights for a week or so when one suddenly disappeared. Not like into thin air or anything like magic, but just gone. We used the other flashlight to look for its mate but we couldn't find it anywhere. I'd estimate we spent about 12 hours in total looking for the light.

Just having the one light wasn't the same fun as having both of them and it became kind of a downer every time I saw just the one so I threw it away. I'm considering ordering a new set but would hate to go through the same ordeal. I'd recommend to the manufacturer to add some sort of locking mechanism to the flashlights so they won't become separated. It'd also help if they were longer, maybe 14\\" so they'd be easier to find. I'd also be interested in downloading an app for my smartphone that allows me to track the location of the flashlight if it becomes lost.

product_title: Green Guru Recycled Climbing Rope Key Chain
review_body:
A very solid build and doesn't add to much bulk in a pocket. Just the right size.

Downside would be that you dont get a choice of color. I ended up with neon pink but as an easy going person I'm just going to pretend i'm making a statement and tell myself its easier to find in a bag.

product_title: Conquer Road/MTB Endurance Short Sleeve Cycling Jersey
review_body: Good jersey.  Pretty big for a cycling jersey, I know it supposed to be "club fit" but it's still really big in the shoulders, even with a compression shirt under it. Zippered pocket is too small to fit an iPhone in it.  Jersey is made of good material and is machine wash, which is nice.  Decent jersey for cooler weather riding, especially if your going to wear something under it.

product_title: Panaracer RiBMo PT Tire with Folding Bead, 26 x 1.50-Inch
review_body: Haven't got any problems so far. Rode it on rocks, dirt, hot road, wet road. Still looking good and safe.

product_title: 1000 Lumens Tactical Flashlight,Asben T6 High Powered Handheld Torch with Rechargeable 26650 Lithium Ion Battery and Charger, 5 Modes Zoomable …
review_body: This is the coolest flashlight I've ever owned.  It is very bright and very high quality. Having a rechargeable battery and being programmable is a huge bonus.

product_title: Camelbak HydroBak 50 oz Hydration Pack
review_body:
I recently ran the Tough Mudder near Allentown PA and this was a life saver. It was over 90 degrees that day and without the water it would have been even more of a bear. This is a 1.5 liter unit and was more than enough to last between the water stations. Great for runners and hikers!

If I had to write one negative thing it would be that I think all versions should have the chest strap to help prevent the back from bouncing around while you run.

product_title: Magnet Steel Bike Bicycle Indoor Exercise Trainer Stand by FDW
review_body: I really like this trainer. It works very well, and is not too loud. This was a great product for this price.

product_title: DoggyRide Mini Dog Bike Trailer
review_body: This was easy to assemble and my dog loves it.  We used his dog bed to put in the trailer instead of the pad.  That way he is familiar with it and knows the surroundings.

product_title: Cannondale Men's Women's Classic Gloves
review_body: The gloves were advertised as men's and women's gloves, size large. The gloves were so small that only a child could wear them. I had to return them to Amazon.

product_title: Shimano Sora Crankset - Triple
review_body: This Shimano crankset was an upgrade to a crank on one of my bikes. This is a great looking crankset. Shimano products are very high quality.

product_title: Kent Dual Drive Tandem Comfort Bike
review_body: It has too low of gears I thought it was a touring bike not a mountain bike you have to pedal too fast and get no where. I am going to change the gears on it should be fine then if you liv3we in the hills this is a great mountain bike for two but if you want to cover come country be ready to put the old style 10 speed  gears on it

product_title: Osprey Stratos 26 Backpack
review_body:
I have a bigger osprey for hiking and purchased this one for day walks. If they had of included some straps for a sleeping mat it would have been great for over nighters.
Fits good and does allow your back to stay dry with the space between the pack and frame.
Just another good quality product from osprey.

product_title: Dirt King Children's Tricycle (Green)
review_body: This is a very well built trike. We bought it for our first grandson but I think it will last through all grandchildren we may have (and possibly great grandchildren). Everything is built of heavy duty materials and quality craftsmanship. Even my son in law rode it and he is a BIG man. And it is ACTUALLY made in the U.S.....no kidding. Huge plus there. This may be a bit more expensive than some of the others but you will never have to buy another one unless they start fighting over it.

product_title: Victorinox Swiss Army Grip Series - One Hand Forester Knife
review_body:
This is a terrific Swiss Army Knife-- really, a SAK 2.0. I like the redesign a lot-- very ergonomic, the main blade opens easily and locks securely, as does the screwdriver/bottle opener. It is a more serious blade than the one on the old-style knives. It's silly, I suppose, but I do miss the toothpick, tweezers, and scissors. Everything else is first-rate.

I bought one for myself, and once I used it immediately bought another one for my dad.

product_title: Pearl iZUMi Men's Quest Cycling Short
review_body:
I couldn't find a bike seat that I liked, so I bought these to try and get a more comfortable ride. The cushioning seems to be high quality, and hasn't broken down (like some other shorts I've had).

Highly recommended, and good value for the price.

product_title: Soap Holder
review_body:
Clasp button broke almost immediately after I got it, and I was careful.

As inexpensive as it is, it's not worth the annoyance.

product_title: Axiom Appalachian Rear Pannier (1220 Cubic Inches, Black with Silver Reflective Trim)
review_body:
I use this bag on my commute to school, which involved a mixture of off- trail and pavement riding. I can fit my 13 inch macbook, two textbooks, a notebook, and a binder, as well as extra layers and lunch. In the smaller zip pouches I keep pens, pencils, a 6 inch ruler, and a calculator. The other carries bug dope, sunscreen, and my reflective anklets with. All of this and there is still some room to spare!
The only reason I do not give it 5 stars is that there is still room for improvement, but for it's cost this is a small factor.
I looped a shoulder strap under the center so that when I get to school all I have to do is unvelcro and unhook the bag then grab the shoulder strap and then I can use it like a messenger bag. Even when I'm not riding I will still bring the bag with me cause it's just so good at holding my stuff.
Things will rattle around and there is no way to cinch the bag when there is extra room, so make sure you have a good leak proof water bottle and fragile things should be wrapped with a jacket or something.
So far the bag has never affected my center of gravity and has never gotten all up in my spokes. An excellent product!

product_title: Descente Men's  Pro Sock
review_body: Descente used to be THE name in cycling apparel, but over the years, Descente left cycling, and came back, but never really recovered.  The quality, however, is still top notch.  I already have two pairs of these socks and plan to buy more.  They fit tight, but not too tight, and are extremely comfortable.  The fabric wicks away sweat very well.  I've used my other two pair quite a lot, and after a year, they look almost like new.

product_title: Tenn Mens Burn MTB Shorts
review_body:
I liked these in the picture and I love the fit when on.
I don't however know why they are called cycling shorts. The happy zone pad is hardly a there.
So if you are looking for good looking shorts that fit awesome you have found them.....
However if you are looking for shorts that will be provide comfort to the tween area, during a long ride... Not so much.
But at least you will look good while walking funny!!

product_title: Michelin Lithion 2 Road Tire
review_body: I like the weight, feel and comfort of the Lithion tire. I also like the puncture resistant belt it has.

product_title: ExOfficio Women's Give-N-Go Lacy Thong
review_body: These are great for wearing on hot days. I wear scrubs at work and can get so hot and sweaty in my nethers from a long, hectic day of running around. This thong miraculously kept me cool and comfortable. The lace is really pretty and I love the lilac color. Just hope they last a while -- the fabric seems pretty delicate. I've been washing on the delicate setting and hanging to dry; so far, so good.

product_title: 3pcs Flexible Collapsible Foldable Reusable Water Bottles BPA Free (3x paisley)
review_body:
These foldable water bottles were perfect for the use I plan--they will be added to Christmas shoeboxes (a project of Samaritan's Purse) which will be delivered to children in many different countries. In many countries, it is difficult to obtain containers to carry water from its source to the child's home so these are not just a fun item but a necessary item. And the fact that they are collapsible means they will take up less space in the shoeboxes, leaving more room for school supplies, toys, t-shirts, etc. etc.

And the service was great--received them very, very quickly!!

product_title: Pearl iZUMi Men's Quest Cycling Short
review_body: I ordered  the XXL and they fit but really needed the XL which I have ordered. They wear well and are comfortable on the ride.

product_title: MB Booyah Large Pet Trailer Pet Bike Trailer & Jogger with Shocks - Blue
review_body:

product_title: Sunlite Bicycle Tube, 700 x 18-23 (27 x 1) 32mm PRESTA Valve
review_headline: All 4 Tubes I ordered Leaked at the base of the Valve
review_body: I bought four of these about a month or so ago. To make a long story short, ALL four had a tiny, less than pin hole leak between the intake valve unit and where it attaches to the tube's base. Do NOT buy these tubes. Of course the leak was very gradual and I didn't discover the cause until the last tube died. The tube would hold up for a ride or two (didn't go more than 10 miles each trip) and then the next time I took out the bike, the tire was flat. (Note that I only road one or two times a week.) I had inspected the tire with a fine tooth comb after each tube died but couldn't find anything in the tire that would continue to cause a flat. Finally, duh, on the last tube, I inflated it and put it in some soapy water to see where the leak was. When I found it, I dug out the other spent tubes (I had dumped them in a box in my basement) and sure enough all had the same tiny leak in the same spot.  Why I didn't check the first tube instead of waiting for the last, is because life bees that way! Leaned two lessons: 1. make sure you find the cause of a flat the first time; and 2. never buy Sunlite tubes!

I could probably wear a medium but I'm more comfortable in the large. It's a pro-cut jersey so it's supposed to be tight. It's not skinsuit tight though. Quality is top-notch and the fabric is super comfortable and very lightweight. It's a hot weather jersey. I wear it during the hottest part of the summer here in SW Florida and it's my coolest jersey. It's so lightweight that I have a hard time wearing any of my other jerseys because they're so much warmer. The extra zipper pocket is a nice bonus even though I'll probably never use it and the sleeves grip nicely and are just the right length. My only complaint is that the Castelli logo/badge is a little annoying if you're wearing shorts instead of bibshorts. The straps of my bibs line up to where the badge is so you don't feel the logo. But if you're wearing shorts you can feel the badge through the shirt and it's itchy and uncomfortable when you first try on the jersey. However, after just one washing this went away. I'm very happy with this jersey and plan on buying another.

product_title: Big Agnes - Pumphouse, Multi-Use Dry Sack & Pad Pump
review_headline: Could have a better nozzle, but does a good job and keeps moisture out of my mattress.
review_body:
QUICK PUMP INFLATION: It takes only a minute or two to fully inflate my Big Agnes using this pump sack. I prefer this method to breath inflation, because I want to keep moisture out of my mattress, for two reasons: 1) moisture trapped in the mattress increases its weight, and 2) moisture in the mattress, especially moisture that just came from human lungs, might breed nasty stuff inside of the mattress, which I do not want to be touching my mouth to via the valve.

VALVE: My one complaint is that the drawstring nozzle closure, designed to clamp around the mattress valve, could get a better seal. It seals sufficiently to make quick work of mattress inflation, but I think it could be improved.

LIGHTWEIGHT: The sack is very light. I don't use it to carry anything I won't definitely be taking out of my pack for bedtime, such as a tiny camp pillow. I like for my camp gear to have long-term homes in their respective sacks, and don't want a slew of items sitting around while I use the pump sack. I also don't want to wreck this specialized tool, as it's not the most heavy-duty material. That's fine - it's a very light addition to my pack, and I can use other stuff sacks to carry things.

product_title: Brooks B17 Standard Black Steel Saddle
review_headline: What happened to the discomfort I was supposed to feel in trans-continental touring?
review_body:
When I built a touring bike from the frame up and planned on putting a few tens of thousands of kilometres on it, I wanted a saddle that could go the distance. The Brooks B17, a handmade leather piece from England, is the most acclaimed touring saddle in the world, and I too have been completely content with my purchase.

After positioning the saddle on my seatpost at an ideal angle and setting off on a 500 km tour, I experienced only the tiniest discomfort as the saddle slowly conformed to the shape of my posterior. By the end of that tour, I hardly noticed the saddle was under me, so smooth was the ride. On a longer tour where I lost a few excess kilos, there was another brief period of adjustment, but the saddle again adapted to my new sitting posture. Before I got into touring, I had heard stories from cyclists of horrible sores, pummelled sit bones and the need for constant application of vaseline, but with this saddle I've never come close to such horror stories. Riding a bike for hours a day, for weeks in a row, is no more uncomfortable than sitting in a car or train.

The saddle should be oiled occasionally to keep the leather supple and help it break in. Be sure to purchase Brooks's [[ASIN:B001O35F2A Proofide solution]] at the same time you order the saddle (don't order the so-called [[ASIN:B0010AJU46 maintenance kit]], it's a ripoff). Also, although Proofride will protect the saddle from slight accidental contact with moisture, the B17 *must* be covered in rain. Brooks sells a [[ASIN:B0018PPWV8 saddle cover]] separately that is a must-have. The saddle does come with a special wrench that should be used to tighten the saddle after a few months of riding, in order to maintain its broken-in condition and keep the leather from sagging off the rails.

product_title: Fizi:k ICS Seat Bag
review_headline: Right side of hinge on ICS bracket prone to breakage
review_body: I am compelled to write my first review because of this product. I was attracted by the design, price and ICS integration with my Fi'zi:k saddle. I packed the saddle bag with one spare 700X18-23C tube, 2 16oz CO2 cartridges with valve, 2 nylon tire levers, a Park patch kit, and Lezyne SV5 multitool with room to spare for a grand total of 338g (.75lbs) of gear inside, not excessive in the least for long solo rides. After a handful of rides and in the middle of a double metric century a fellow rider behind me noticed the right side of the bracket near the hinge cracked & separated and the bag was hanging by just the left side of the bracket. After experiencing this failure I became aware of 3 other owners of this same bag who have the same exact issue. I duct taped the bag to the seat rails at a control to secure it for the rest of the ride and placed an order for a different bag (Arundel Dual) after reading several other reviews of owners experiencing the same problem (lesson learned). My advice is to avoid this saddle bag or risk losing your bag during a ride.

product_title: Marzocchi 44 LR Switch TA suspension fork 1 1/8" diameter steerer 120/150mm travel, gloss black
review_body:
This item arrived and it has a 15mm diameter axel bolt. Much too large for my wheel hub. Following this up I realize I will have to order a different hub and have it installed. The specs should be amended to indicate clearly that it is a QR15MM axle.

Following receipt of the appropriate axel and successfully mounting it on the front of a 2009 jackal hard tail with a rohloff 14 gear hub I recognize that my review was not fair but rather a knee jerk reaction to my disappointment at not being able to use it immediately. Yes the full specs did indicate the axel size but I overlooked this as it should have been included in the header specs. Like Brock says I am an idiot but only for not looking further and then reacting impetuously with the review. As far as aftermarket comment is concerned we all live and learn by immersing ourselves in what we love and this is the best way to get an improved ride. Rides well, price is good. Happy rider. Thanks Brock.

product_title: Topeak Aero Wedge Pack with Strap Mount
review_body: With the expansion zipper opened on this bag I can carry 2 tubes, 3 CO2 cartridges, a CO2 inflator, 3 pry bars, a chain tool, a multi-tool, cleat covers, a pocket knife, a tire bead jack, gels, an energy bar, an iPhone, arm warmers, leg warmers, and a vest. I think I could even cram my jacket in there. With the expansion zipper closed obviously you can carry slightly less but even then you can still hold a ton of stuff. This bag is so big that it’s really too big for most uses. For a serious roadie or mountain biker  it’s out of the question. Aside from looking ridiculous and hanging too low it’s so large that it’ll rub your legs. The velcro strap that goes around the seatpost is also too long and you’ll probably need to trim it. Also, the straps that connect to the saddle are made of a thin, lightweight fabric so getting this bag high and tight against your saddle is difficult if not impossible. The back of the bag has a strap/loop for you to clip on your tail light and the light stays upright which is nice. Like I said, I think this bag is too big but if you really do want a huge saddlebag I prefer the Expandable Wedge Pack by Inertia Designs. That bag is just as big if not bigger but it doesn’t rub my legs and holds tighter and closer to the saddle.

product_title: Halter Home Mechanic Repair Bike Stand - With Work Tray And Handlebar Holder
review_headline: You get what you pay for
review_body:
So, I just needed a stand to do basic bicycle maintanence in my garage...and I saw some stands I really liked from Feedback Sports but since I'm not a bike shop or true mechanic, I didn't want to spend a ton of money. So I bought this.

The stand itself is fine: sturdy and stable. The clamp is terrible. The blue plastic is hard...I have to clamp the seatpost on my carbon-fiber road bike to protect the frame. The only way to adjust the clamp is by a flimsy, plastic, turn-knob which works fine but there is no quick way of getting the clamp open or tightened quickly: it's very time consuming and forearm burning.

So, it works fine. But you get what you pay for.

product_title: Guide Gear 10x10' Teepee Tent
review_body:
This is my bushcrafting setup. Sturdy little set up. Plenty of room for an individual. I could probably fit 3 full sized cots in this tent, if placed in a triangular manner, but wouldn't leave much room for maneuverability. As for the individual, this is amazing. I had my military grade cot, my guitar, my cooler, and a bunch of misc stuff and had plenty of room to enter one side, exit the other, and get around the tent for each item needed.

Takes a few times of tripping over one of the ten tie downs before you realize you gotta stay aware of where they're at. For some people, or people with toddlers, this might be an issue. My niece tripped over them a few times, but she's a trooper and usually laughed about it lol.

If I could change anything about the tent, I would change *will change eventually* the hooks and rings used for the tent. They're all made of a light plastic. The rings are fine, but the hooks are pretty flimsy and I managed to snap one of them during the initial setup. Never-the-less this tent has earned a 5/5 stars from me. I'm very happy with it.

Once you get the hang of it, setup and take down can be done in about 10 minutes.

review_headline: Great if you can get it blown up
review_body: First let me say that I love this thing and my kids and i have had a blast on it.  We also have \\"real\\" kayaks\\" but after shlepping them on and off the roof rack a few times I find the inflatable a great treat and well earned break. I promise you, you can.  This sleeping bag is lovely thick and fluffy and incredibly warm when the nights are most certainly not.  Best part is that it is long enough that most adults can literally hibernate inside the bag - pull the top up over your head and hide from the *brrrr* deep inside your Teton cocoon!    Update: October 2014: used the bag for the third time... And the right side zipper separated. Tried to re-zip from the bottom and it simply separates any time any pressure is applied, resulting in very cold air finding warm flesh (which SUCKS!!!). I've contacted Teton to see if there is some way to address this obvious quality problem. Will keep updated..l

product_title: Planet Bike A.R.S. Standard bike seat - Men's
review_headline: Excellent seat for the money; excellent for short commutes (under 10 miles)
review_body:
I'm male, 5'8", 220 pounds. I have extensive cycling experience, including a one-day, 100-mile ride on a mountain bike and hundreds of 50+ mile rides on a road bike. I have used the Planet Bike 5020 on my commuting bike, a Jamis Coda, several times since receiving it last week.

I commute to work every day: 5.5 miles each way, 11 miles round-trip. The stock seat on my Jamis Coda had become too painful and I realized it was affecting my decision to ride each day. For the money, the Planet Bike 5020 is an excellent seat. It's quite comfortable. I put it on the bike, rode around the block, adjusted it, and that's been it. So far, worth every penny.

There are assuredly better seats out there, but I don't do the really long road rides anymore and I'm a pretty cheap guy. For $45 (cost + shipping) I think this seat is an excellent investment. It keeps the ride happy, which means I ride more, exercise more, and save more money by not driving.

review_body: The plaid is more of a turquoise and brown than it looks on my computer.  The interior is a very bright medium turquoise color.  This is a solidly built small pack. This is not the right pack for someone who wants frills or interior organization-- there are no little sleeves to hold your pens or pencils, no little key ring, nothing.  It does have 2 exterior zippered pockets-- an upper smaller one with a lightweight fleece lining for sunglasses and a larger one beneath that easily holds my large-ish cellphone, my ipod in a plastic box, keys, tissues and other small bits and pieces.  The larger main compartment has two zippers with matching fabric pulls and easily holds a small purse, a lightweight sweater, a tablet or kindle and still has room leftover.

product_title: Paradise Tattered Flowers Complete Longboard, 8x40-Inch
review_body:

I love the graphic, the griptape (speckle spray) is insane. I've never had griptape be so gritty. For the deck itself its great. Other than some molding flaws on the bottom layer I've always liked heavy 9+ ply longboards . With a hardcore concave this thing looks mean. The wheels and bearings that come on it are sick. Nice bigfoots with smooth fast bearings.
Now the only gripes I have about this board is that its sitting on no name trucks. With that come the crappiest bushings I have ever seen. after some riding and no improvement I decided to give her some nice bushings and now its gliding on butter.
IF YOU ARE LOOKING TO GET SOMEONE THAT JUST RIDES A NICE BOARD THIS IS A GOOD CHOICE. THIS IS MADE FOR CRUISING AND BOMBING STRAIGHT DOWN HILLS. THIS ITS NOT A SLIDING FREESTYLE DECK. AMAZON SHIPPING IS BOSS, THIS IS A NICE COMPLETE FOR CHEAP.
4/5

review_headline: IF I COULD GIVE A 0 I WOULD

product_title: Onguard Akita Resettable Combo Cable Lock
review_headline: So much better than the Kryptonite
review_body:
I live in an apartment and have to store my bike outside chained to a fence covered with bushes. The only way to secure it is with a long cable snaked through the bushes to the fence. My first bike cable lock had a key which worked for about 9 months until the lock stiffened up and I broke the key off in the lock; that lock then had to be cut off. I bought a Kryptonite combo lock and after only two weeks of use it would not open, and it had to be cut off.

My third lock is the OnGuard combo lock which is much smoother to operate and to use than either of the two prior bike locks. After several months outside including getting cold and rained on several times it's working fine. So far it hasn't stiffened up even after a couple of freezes.

The guts of the Kryptonite were plastic with plastic pins that were very difficult to depress while simultaneously setting the code. The OnGuard has metal guts, and it's a breeze to set the code and to use the lock. The lock appears to have much better materials and construction quality. I would recommend spending a couple of extra bucks for this lock.

product_title: Harmony Stowaway Cart
review_headline: Good Product After you learn how to strap it correctly
review_body:
I got these wheels because I live by the beach. I have a 13 ft sit on top ocean kayak. I needed something that would roll on sand and over a large dune. My kayak has scupper holes. If your Kayak doesn't have scuppers, I don't know that I would buy this particular set of wheels. There were no instruction stating the best way to strap the thing down. I tried several different methods: going around the entire body of the kayak with both straps, going around the entire body with one strap and through the scupper holes with the other strap, going through the scuppers across the width of the kayak and cris crossing through the scuppers. None of these worked, as soon as I hit a dune or had to turn on the sand it would fall off the wheels. Embarassing and nearly cause me to chuck this unit in the trash. I was sweating and covered in sand constantly tying to re-align the thing.

The Good News (and i don't know why it took me 6 tries to figure this out, perhaps smarter folks figured it out quicker): if you strap through each scupper and under the wheel bars length wise to the kayak (not width), this thing will work perfectly. It has been great ever since I started strapping it that way. I've never written a review before, but figured I may be able to save somebody the experimentation. If you don't have scuppers, you won't be able to strap it length wise and I have no idea how they would work unless you get ratchet straps and really tighten the kayak down.

product_title: True Utility FireStash Lighter Multi-Tool
review_headline: Great for backup; might get lost
review_body:
I knew this was small; I could tell from the pictures. But it wasn't until I had it in my hand that I really understood how tiny it is.

This is great as a backup or emergency lighter. It's small capacity, along with the fact you have to screw the top off, means it won't be your go-to lighter for daily use. But that top does seal with an O-ring, helping to prevent the fuel from evaporating out, like with regular Zippo lighters.

Edited to add: I just pulled my keychain out specifically to get this lighter for a smoker friend who lost her regular lighter. However, the FireStash was missing. The cap, which actually attaches to the key ring, was there, but the lighter itself, which screws into the cap, was gone. It wasn't in my pocket. I don't know how long it's been missing, nor do I have any idea where it is. I've looked in many places but haven't found it yet.

This is actually the second time it's unscrewed out by itself. The first time I did find it in my pocket. I wasn't so lucky this time.

I see from other reviews that I'm not the only person to lose his FireStash this way. I do also agree with other reviews that point out it's difficult to tell how much to screw it into the cap. Once you hit the O-ring, it will keep screwing in, but you can see the soft O-ring getting squished out the more you tighten.

product_title: Wenzel Pine Ridge Tent - 5 Person
review_body:
So far I have used this tent on two camping trips, with decent results (26 y/o male). Both trips were weekend trips to the mountains of south central PA (just south of Raystown Lake). This was car-type camping. A friend of mine's relatives have a few acres in the middle of nowhere out there, so we try to camp there 2-3 times a year. The first was in early February, the other was last weekend (early May '13). In both trips the tent fared well. During the first trip, I did not actually sleep in the tent, but set it up to house some gear and to use as a backup if our (me, and three friends) handmade tipi around the fire failed to adequately shelter us. The weather that weekend did not rise above 20 deg. F, dropped to the single digits at night, and was pretty windy, with sustained winds of 15 mph and gusts up to ~25 mph. Oh yeah, and we got about 1/2\\" of snow one morning. The inside of the tent was dry and it seemed to handle the winds quite well. During the second trip it was raining the majority of the weekend. ~65 deg. F in the afternoon, ~50 deg. F at night, with medium intensity showers for the area and light wind (~15 mph). This time my wife and I slept in it for two nights (didn't spend much time in it otherwise). This time, a very little bit of water got in. It was all just inside the door and could be picked up with a few paper towels. I think it got in because of two reasons. 1 - the rain fly did not completely cover and shelter the door. So, I think some got in when we opened the tent and climbed inside to retire for the night. 2 - I noticed a little bit more water on the floor when I woke up mid-way through the night. I suspect a little more got through at the bottom of the door where the two zippers meet. I suspect this is because the rain fly didn't cover the door and the zipper-to-zipper interface leaves a small gap. The encroachment of water was minor, but perceptible. Let me throw out a few more pros and cons:

Pros:
Price - I think I remember buying this thing for ~$65, which is pretty cheap for a tent of this size.
Floor - The floor of this thing seems much more durable than tents of a similar size/price, and I have not had any water leakage issues.
Capacity - I think this is one of the few tents whose capacity is advertised at close to what might be comfortable to an average set of campers not using air mattresses. Four of us laid down in the tent to test the claim, and we were satisfied.
Simplicity - Dome tents of this style are very simple to set-up and pack. Being of this kind, it is not an exception.
Color - Yeah, this shouldn't matter much, but it looks like it fits in in the woods.

Cons:
Zippers - Most of the reviews mention that the zippers on the doors frequently get caught on the orange weather protection flags. This is true, but as long as you and everyone else using your tent knows this and is mindful and careful, you shouldn't have much trouble if you take your time. My zippers have gotten caught a few times, but I have always been able to un-snag them with little effort.
Rain-fly Coverage of Door - As I mentioned before, the rain fly does not completely shield the doors in the front. So, if you are entering/exiting the tent when it is raining, a small amount of water can enter the tent. It would be great if the rain fly just extended ~6\\" further. I assume this problem could be mitigated by strategically placing the entrance away from the wind. Because of spatial concerns, I did not have that option. Other than not completely covering the door, the rain fly adequately covers the other mesh window/vents on the sides and back of the tent.

Rain-fly Coverage of Door - As I mentioned before, the rain fly does not completely shield the doors in the front. So, if you are entering/exiting the tent when it is raining, a small amount of water can enter the tent. It would be great if the rain fly just extended ~6\\" further. I assume this problem could be mitigated by strategically placing the entrance away from the wind. Because of spatial concerns, I did not have that option. Other than not completely covering the door, the rain fly adequately covers the other mesh window/vents on the sides and back of the tent.

All-in-all this is a solid tent for the price.

review_body: This heater does what it says. Whether in a deer blind, or camping, or in the dugout at a baseball tournament, this heater produces steady, comforting heat. review_body:
My wife (5' 8\\" approx 160 lbs?) put her thin inflatable ALPS camping pad on top of this cot and her bad back did very well for our 3 night camping trip! Our kids love to 'camp' in the loft with just their pillow and a blanket and sleep on this cot, but that's a little too stiff for my wife's liking. (almost 40!)

It does make some slight creaking sounds, but it really is pretty quiet, probably no more sound than our inner-spring mattress in our bedroom!

We've used it on 1 campout and several 'campins' (that's when the kids sleep in the loft). probably 20 to 30 nights of sleeping on it (mostly kids) and assembled/disassembled 6 or 8 times, and it really doesn't show any signs of wear. It still looks brand new.

product_title: Hydrapak Elite Quantum Clip
review_headline: Great addition to any bladder pack.
review_body:
I bought this for my Camelbak after seeing one on a friend's and have since used it a number of times for single-track riding. It's nice to know exactly where the valve is when riding hard and not have to spend any time finding the end of a moving hose.

I've not used any other setups similar to this one, but the clips are very easy to install and neither move once in place. The only thing is that the magnet could be a little stronger. I have the strap clip attached on the chest strap furthest from where the hose comes out of my pack so it's at a pretty good bend. Even still, with the hose clip up against the valve so the valve can't bounce around on rough terrain, it seems to be working just fine.

I figured I'd try this vs making my own, and it looks to last. I'd recommend to anyone who's doing activities that require quick reactions but won't be moving/contorting their bodies too much as it would probably cause the magnets to break free.

product_title: Blackburn CP EX-1 Disc Rack
review_body:
The manufacturer claims this is a universal rack that fits bikes with a 700c frame. It may fit some bikes of that size but not all - despite the use of the word \\"universal.\\"

For many bikes the rack requires that the extenders (used to stabilize the rack by securing it to the frame) be clamped to the seat stays. Unfortunately, the size of the clamps are very small and do not allow the rack to be installed properly on a bike whose seat stays have a circumference of more than 9/16 of an inch. This pretty much rules out many higher end bikes. I contacted Blackburn thinking they must make some clamps in larger sizes but they do not. So, buyer beware. Unless you have small seat stays, or a place on the frame where the extenders can be bolted on, this rack will only frustrate you. Do not buy it.

review_body:

Prior to ordering this I had a flat and fixing it while the wheel was still attached turned out to be rather tough.

This little tool fits in my emergency pack.

I have used it on the road twice. Despite being fairly short, it is very tough and I was able to undo the wheel, get the tire off with a combination of the lever end and a pair of Pedro's levers, fix the flat, CO2 my tire back to ridable, bolt it all back up and get on my way in less than ten minutes.

product_title: Bliss Hammocks Gravity Free X-Wide Recliner with Canopy Shade and Cup Tray
review_body:
Just purchased the Bliss Gravity Free x-Wide recliner and could not be more pleased.
In fact it is the Jacquard color black/brown shown here and it is lovely. It took just a few
minutes to put the cup holder and canopy on and voila it was done...could not be simpiler.
The canopy is sizeable and flexible, so easy to manage and will allow you to have all the shade
you could ever need even here in the strong Arizona sun. I bought this to use inside and outside
the house, but I might have to get another for outdoors...it is just that comfortable! I have a
$700.00 recliner, but truly because this recliner elevates far higher then my recliner, I will only
use the Bliss from now on while reading and watching TV....the Bliss Gravity recliner is SHEER BLISS!
I am a senior and my ankles swell later in the day and a few minutes in this chair and like magic
the swollen ankles are normal. It is worth its weight in gold and one of the best purchases I have
ever made bar none.

product_title: Explorer Rack Without Spring, Black
review_body: It would have been perfect with ALL THE SCREWS IN THE PCKAGE, it was kind of disappointed when I found out!:-(

product_title: Coupler Attachment - InStep & Schwinn Bike Trailers
review_body: Perfect fit in 3 minutes flat by removing 1 nut. I put it in upside down to give the trailer an extra inch of height.

product_title: Street Surfing Kazari Tilt Scooter (Black/Red)
review_body: My 13 year old son loves it. Nice solid scooter! Even I rode it and it perfrormed well. Nice job.

product_title: Coleman 2000016527 Replacement Tent Pole Kit
review_body:
I ordered these replacement poles for my husband, who wanted to use them to make a canopy for his Sevylor Fish Hunter Inflatable 6-Person Boat. They were priced well, arrived quickly, and he was able to use his engineer brain (as well as the rivet gun that I wrongly predicted would never get used) to put together a really nice canopy so that we can fish all day without getting fried.

As an added bonus, this project kept him busy for two entire days.

Recommended!

product_title: Malone SeaWing Saddle Style Universal Car Rack Kayak Carrier with Bow and Stern Lines
review_body:
I bought these wings about two years ago and they are the best device for me. I tried the \\"J\\" racks but I am a small woman and could not get my boat up high enough to clear
the lower part of the rack. I then went to the wings and now load my boat from the back of my vehicle and this works perfectly. I have several kayaks and these wings fit all
of my boats without a problem. I own a Rav4 Toyota which sits a little higher than a sedan type auto so for me this is the best set up and I can load my boat by myself so
I don't have to depend on someone else if I want to paddle alone. The only reason I gave these racks 4 stars was because I do not like the straps that come with them. They
seems sort of cheap and when the red of the straps get wet, the dye runs.

product_title: Thule 9001 Raceway 2 Bike Rear Mounted Bike Rack
review_body: Although I didn't pick this up from Amazon, I can say it's a solid bike carrier,worth its price.I do not entirely agree this is a one person operation if you have a CUV, or SUV cargo door.It's much easier to have another person steady the arched frame as you place the top hooks onto the upper edge of the cargo door.Once this is done,it really is a one person operation.I've used this rack with the Thule adapter bar TH982XT,and it has worked well with a ladies,or hybrid frame.Reasons to own one: garage over head clearance,no need to remove your bike before entering; better aerodynamics; storage,folds down in one  self contained piece;access cargo area with [empty]carrier on the cargo door

product_title: eGear Survival Essentials Ceramic Knife Sharpener
review_headline: eGear Survival Essentials Ceramic Knife Sharpener
review_body: I can not believe how sharp I was able to get my knives, this item is handy when you do not have a big sharpener to use, and it can be carried with to the Lake when you go camping to keep your fillet knives sharp when you get your catch.

product_title: Nalgene Tritan 12oz Grip-N-Gulp BPA-Free Water Bottle
review_body: We love these Nalgene bottles for little ones.  Great for toting around when you are out and about.  Pending that the valve inside the cap is properly attached, we have not had any issues with leaks. Ours have taken quite a beating from lots of use and they are still in good condition. Only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 is because I wish that it came with a cap to protect the mouthpiece. Great product!

product_title: Y-volution Yfliker F1 Scooter - Pink
review_headline: Every child on the block loves it!
review_body:
We bought this Fliker for my daughter for Christmas. She is about 45lbs, and about 46 inches tall. She was seven years old at the time. She jumped on it and figured it out in the first two minutes. My younger daughter who was four got a scooter. She has ditched the scooter and always insists on riding her sister's Fliker too. My four year old took a few tries before she got the swing of it. But loved it immediately. Both of them can ride bikes without training wheels which was our requirement before they got scooters. We have about 15 school aged kids on our block that play together. Each of them have tried it out and love it. Even the older boys about 10 years old are asking to ride the pink Fliker. The least coordinated child on the block just got one for her birthday and while she cannot do the tricks the other kids can do, she loves hers. A little 11 year old girl neighbor rides my daughter's around the backyard. She is about 80 lbs and 4 ft 8. It's a little short for her but she do not care. The weight limit is around 100 lbs, so I always ask the kids how much they weigh before they hop on.
I even tried it out...I am 125lbs. It is really fun. I'm a little jealous. I am now on line ordering my younger daughter who is five the same Fliker.

product_title: EDELRID - Python 10mm Dynamic Climbing Rope
review_headline: Edelrid Python 10.0mm Dynamic Climbing Rope - 70m - Flame
review_body:
I'm fairly new to climbing and rappelling so I did a lot of research into all brands , sizes and quality of ropes and after reading reviews , specs and talking to rock gym owners about different brands of ropes I have gone with Edelrid Ropes and right out of the package these ropes are very supple , smooth and strong and for the prices here it's a steal , their literally almost half the price of other ropes and the same quality and comparable specs of the other ropes .
I recommend Edelrid ropes to anyone who doesn't want to spend a small fortune and get the same quality as the higher-priced ropes.

product_title: GasOne Butane Fuel Canister (12 Pack)
review_body: Perfect for use on our Sea Ray 240 Sundancer.  Great price! Love the fact that I won't need to buy more for several seasons. Store surplus at home.

product_title: Tilley Endurables LTM6 Airflo Hat
review_headline: Pricey, but it is a forever hat
review_body:
I do art shows for a living and have been trough many hats. I finally broke down and bought a Tilley. So glad I did! When using the straps as per the instructions, this thing will stay on in 40 mph wind. It is not waterproof but will keep the rain off of your face during a downpour. It is so comfortable that I forget that I am wearing a hat.

Pay close attention to the sizing instructions on the Tilley website. The first one I bought ended up being 1/8 too small, went up one size and it is perfect

product_title: Jagwire 5mm Brake Housing
review_body: Awesome brake cable for a great price the color is bright and brilliant they make mike bike look great and have performed very well

review_body: the product is made with excellent quality. I wear pant size 39-40 and believed and X-large sufficient, but it is to small!! suggest to consider a table with dimension to select this product.

product_title: Ogio Rebel Laptop/Tablet Backpack
review_body: This item is really just what I had looked for in a backpack. The backpack is well made and very handy, easy to use for my laptop computer. I would recommend and purchase again.

product_title: Topeak Pocket Rocket Master Blaster Bike Pump
review_body: Great Product!  The product is flawless and performs as designed and as desired.  I would buy again either same or like products.

product_title: Nite Ize Spokelit Bicycle Light (Amber)
review_body: I ordered 4 of these (in all differed colors) and 2 of them did not work from the moment I got them.  The kids love the 2 that work.  Save your money and buy an LED that is brighter and use rechargeable batteries.

review_body:
recieved on time

product_title: Lezyne Femto Drive LED Light-Pair
review_body: These are very simple and small, and work as advertised.  They're not obtrusive, but provide plenty of visibility.  Bought two sets.

product_title: BICYCLE REPAIR STAND Bike Adjustable Heights 360º Rotation w/ Lock & Tool Tray
review_body: I'm just beginning to repair and maintain my bikes, so I wanted my own bike rack.  This one holds my bikes and I've done adjustments and chain cleaning now. It holds the bike up for what I need and it was reasonably priced.  However, it came with no instructions or directions for use, just a complete parts list with a drawing.  Also, one of the base holes to attach the legs was stripped, so instead of using a provided part for assembly I used a nut and bolt. No real big deal.  Interestingly, one can also buy this same rack through Amazon for $82.88 with free shipping or ,I think, $29.99 with $9.99 shipping.  The listing for $82.88 has a video review that shows how to assemble the rack.  So, obviously, in this case "You get what you pay for." doesn't necessarily apply.

product_title: Nubutte Chamois Butter
review_body: This chamois cream works great to prevent chaffing on long rides.  It goes on easily and stays until you wash it off with soap and water.  It does not come off from perspiration as you ride so it works great on long bike rides of 50 and more miles.  Will be using this all summer as I prepare for RAGBRAI.

product_title: Dakine Mens Pipe Snowboard Bag
review_headline: looks nice, but split a little the first time i flew with it
review_body: I understand that the airlines are exactly gentle with your luggage, but it should have been durable enough to withstand more than one flight.  It is still usable, so I gave it 3 stars but the fabric is splitting a little bit after only flying with it once.

product_title: Advanced Elements AdvancedFrame Convertible Inflatable Kayak
review_body: Used boat twice thus far and have enjoyed it thoroughly. Easy to set up and pack in. Made from quality materials and tracks well for an inflatable. Looking forward to many more paddling adventures this year, urban and remote locals.

product_title: Ski-Lash ski carrier. The Easiest Way to Carry Your Skis & Poles!
review_body:
Got this for my wife, but the lash would slide together and not be able to hold onto ski poles.
I have been able to use it with my larger skis because I can put one end of lash outside the bindings and other end inside of bindings to minimize movement and hold onto poles. Other handy feature of lash is that its soft and easy to carry around in pockets while skiing.

review_body: Lightweight, strong, and looks good. I've compared this product to the actual carbon fiber ones in a local bike shop and appearance-wise, it's hard to tell the difference. It's about as light as well. Why spend 3-4 times more than you need to?

product_title: Petzl E49 PNG TacTikka Plus NVG Headlamp with Green Lens
review_body: Very bright lamp. Looks durable enough in construction and light enough you forget you are wearing it. A bit disappointed not to get a red light filter.

product_title: Allen Sports Tension Bar Bicycle Cross-Bar Adaptor
review_body: I got this so I could mount my wife's bike on my car.  It works very well.  Very easy and dependable.

product_title: Stansport Black Granite Steel Mess Kit
review_body: I will admit, I haven't cooked anything significant yet.  I've only boiled water with this set on an Esbit stove--and it boiled long before the cube was finished burning.  I do feel they are of good quality and very sturdy.  The pot holds almost exactly 16 ounces of water.  Everything nestles well, and I just keep a dish sponge inside of the set when it is all folded together to eliminate any rattling.  Also, I have added a set of utensils, a camping sized salt and pepper shaker.  It doesn't come with a cup so I bought a metal cup seperately that fits over the end of my water bottle so I didn't have to sacrifice any space.  I  feel good about this purchase, and it's a LOT better than the last mess kit I bought for nearly the same price.

review_body: The best part about this set is that it comes in a handy storage bag.  It doesn't take up a lot of space, the pieces are durable and easy to clean, and camping with these is a breeze!  My son and I both own a set now since we camp a lot with his Boy Scout troop.

review_headline: Great bottle, but can make a squeaking sound...
review_body: Overall I love this water bottle. The only reason I took one star off is because if I hold it in a certain way it makes this odd squeaking sound while drinking. If this happens to you, just adjust the way you hold the bottle and it should stop.

product_title: Penny Australia Classic Complete Skateboard
review_body: I love longboards but i needed something that i could store in my room that does not take up to much space. I have had it for about a year now and it still is a great board. I got the rasta one because i would be able to put different colors on it if something needed to be replaced. I have size 13-14 shoe and i have no problem riding a 22 by 6 inch board. The wheels are really great and the board has alot of flex but not to much. I had to loosen the trucks when i first got it but the trucks are really good. Is the best board i have ever owned and the fastest. I recommend this product. 4 and a half stars

product_title: Lightload Compact Reusable 12x12" Towels weighs .2 oz.  (2 Pack )
review_body: These towels worked perfectly for my backpacking trip! We hiked to Supai Falls (Grand Canyon) 10+ miles. Lots of running water and waterfalls! These small towels can be used for pretty much anything. Their small size is perfect for times when weight is a factor on your trip. Can be used to clean up messes and washed out to be reused again! The different size options for these towels are a plus! Innovative and required for any trip!

review_body:
I have used this product for a month as an overnight water bottle on my nightstand and a daily drinker at my office. Unfortunately, I can't recommend it because I don't believe it was designed to be used with ice.

There are several reasons to like it, bpa free, lightweight, filter, great handle for grab'n'go; however the biggest problem I had is that condensation would form on the outside of the bottle if you used it with ice because it is not double-walled. review_headline: Happy to be back to foam grips on my bike
review_body: My old bike for the most part was something I did not like.  However, the grips on it were foam which I loved.  The new bike had rubber grippers.  I replaced them with these and am very happy to be back to foam grips.  Wetting the inside with water made them very easy to install!
