product_title: Bike Multi Bicycle Tool Repair Rescue kits Folding Hex Wrench Set (16-Function)
review_body: Small and good. Perfect size to put in the pocket, it does not take a lot of space. So far so good.

product_title: GasOne Butane Fuel Canister (12 Pack)
review_body: I got this to go with the Nature's Quest Deluxe Portable Gas Butane Stove. Worked in the product as described. Have no complaints!

product_title: SRAM PC 1 Snaplock Bicycle Chain (Single-Speed, Silver)
review_body: I didn't pay attention to the snaplock and thought it was like the newer chain connectors.  Nope, snaplock has both pins on one plate and you have to flex the chain to force the pins into the other plate, which isn't ideal.

product_title: Water Filter Straw, Frontier Emergency Water Filter System for Emergency Disaster Preparedness, Survival Kits, Survival Packs, Survival Gear, Camping,
review_body: This straw is excellent for backpackers or packs for disaster preparedness. I put them in plastic ziploc [quart or gallon size] bags, so you have a filtering straw in a container for holding water. Space saving way to ensure good safe drinking water.

product_title: Fire Puck Matchless Firestarter-Pack of 6
review_body: This fire puck works excellent, but you have to strike it on a striker to light it. There is nothing wrong with that, but you have to strike it pretty hard or the striking materiel will just fade away and you only get about 2 good tries imo. Once lit though this thing burns very hot and starts a fire very fast without the need of smaller wood pieces. 4 stars cause the striking material ran out on one of mine, and in a emergency situation that would suck if this was your only method of fire.

product_title: Elastic Head Strap Black Full Frame Mesh Goggles Pair
review_body: these are good quality mesh goggles for the price. near vision needs getting used to but far vision is great.

product_title: WeeRide LTD Kangaroo Child Bike Seat
review_body: Me my husband and my daughter love it! Highly recomended! Only thing is the weight limit on it but other than that we ride to school everyday

product_title: Filzer Chain Cleaner
review_headline: love this thing, a must have for regular bike maintenance
review_body:
i've had this chain cleaner for over a year now and i can't imagine going back to the old method of cleaning a chain. i hated using the spray-on degreaser and using the hand brushes. it doesn't really work that well and you end up getting your hands pretty dirty if you don't wear gloves. time and time again, i've used this chain cleaner to restore rusty and encrusted chains to looking pretty good. i find that if you clean a rusty/dirty bike chain repeatedly a couple weeks in a row, you eventually break through all that and have you chain looking pretty new-ish again. the cleaner has over 100 brushes (128 i think), a fairly large reservoir for degreaser and a removable handle. holding it all together is a strong clip at the top to make sure the brushes clamp and really get in there.

you might find a cheaper chain cleaner. filzer is a canadian brand that they don't normally sell in retail here in the US, but it was recommended by a couple websites and i don't deny its quality. over a year and it's still working well. perfect purchase in my book.

product_title: KLOUD ® Silver & Black 190T nylon waterproof bike / bicycle cover (size: LL
review_body: i live in apt complex and have to keep my bike outdoor. it fits over the mountain bike perfectly. i have a 26in mountain bike. it also covers my rim driver for my bike as well.

product_title: Wenzel Kodiak Tent - 9 Person
review_body: We got this tent for family camping, and we love it! It is the biggest tent I have ever seen, which is great when camping with kids and all their gear. I definitely recommend placing a tarp or pad of some sort under the tent as the bottom liner is very thin and could be easily torn on a rock/stick/root etc. Also, we hung a huge tarp over the tent (strung up in trees, not touching tent) because it was raining, and this prevented any leaking issues. We are very pleased with this tent and look forward to many more camping adventures.

product_title: Light My Fire Swedish Firesteel Mini 1,500 Strike Ultralight Fire Starter
review_body: For its size it is unbeatable compared to other small firesteels, gets a lot of sparks in a small package.

product_title: Diamondback 2013 Kid's Mini Viper BMX Bike with 16-Inch Wheels  (Blue, 16-Inch/Boys)
review_body: Just started using it, I hope it was good. For this brand I still very much believe it. But after all, no one hundred percent things, so good luck.

product_title: Outdoor Technology Turtle Claw Clamp
review_body: Just recieved it in the mail. I have 2 other portable speakers. The jbl flip and cyfi wireless bicycle speaker. The jbl flip  beats the turtle in loudness and clarity . Loudness ,by my opinion, 15 percent difference. The turtle beats the flip in bass and battery life (havent tested batterry yet, but in theory). My jbl will last at about 4.5hrs on the loudest setting on consistent play. My cyfi is a great size for my bike. Its light, water resistant and will last about 3.5 to 4hrs. The cyfi is not as loud as the turtle. the turtle is 30 percent louder t my cyfi in my opinion. The turtle is going to be clunky when I attach it to my bike.....but its going to be the loudest weather resistant bike speaker out there. I havent tested the clamp yet but looks good for my odd shape handle bars and may even work with my gopro.

product_title: Zippo Flex Neck Utility Lighter
review_headline: Finally a lighter that isn't plastic junk
review_body: I love this lighter so far, got it about a week ago.  I was looking for something that I could refill with fluid & that would last. I feel this just may be the one. At first it seemed to be a little hard to figure out how to light because of the child safety feature, but I can live with that. I'm just glad to see a quality product I don't have to toss after a few months. Good job Zippo, as usual.

product_title: Avenir Octalink Crank Puller
review_body: The crank puller worked great. I needed to remove the inner screw to remove my crank from the square shaft. The entire process of rebuilding the crank took less than twenty minutes. I would recommend this product to anyone.

product_title: White Sierra Men's All Seasons 4 In 1 Jacket
review_body: This is good and meets my requirement. I love wearing it and it is comfortable and easy to use. overall it is 5

product_title: Kryptonite Evolution Mini Bike U-Lock
review_body: I have been using this plus a cable to lock up my bike behind my house in the city. My housemate's locked bike was stolen and mine wasn't, so it's at least a good deterrent. It has gotten rusty inside so be aware that it will rust if you let it get wet.

product_title: Princeton Tec League Flashlight
review_headline: Do Not Buy- Light Floods Immediately!
review_body:
Do not buy the Princeton Tec League 100! The light housing flooded on the very first dive I took it on (to about 100ft). The light was half full of water when I got back to the surface. The dive shop apologized profusely and replaced it, no questions asked. The next dive I took it on was a 40ft night dive. The replacement light died about 5 mins into the dive! With no light, I had to end my dive. Way to ruin a great dive.

The Princeton Tec League 100 makes a better water bottle than underwater flashlight.

product_title: Giro Monaco Road Gloves
review_headline: What I had been looking for
review_body: The gloves not only match my bike in color scheme, but are comfortable and do not hinder my ability to operate the bike's control, but are also light enough that you can answer a cell phone with them on.

product_title: Razor E200 Electric Scooter
review_body: My daughter decided to save all her birthday money from friends and family and use it to buy the E200 (with just a little more help from Mom & Dad).  She researched the E90 and E100, but decided to go with the E200 because she didn't want to "out-grow" it. review_body: Keeps things pretty chill. I should have gotten 2. It holds water. What else can I say! I also like the cap's ability to lock out.

review_body: The battery was dead on arrival. Accessories broke during installation. Think again before purchasing this. Instructions were useless. Too bad.

review_headline: Quirky Design With The Quality You Expect From Zippo
review_body: Ordered this Zippo pipe lighter directly from Amazon.com and it arrived expiditiously andr packaged very securely as always. The lighter looks exactly like a traditional Zippo wick lighter except it has a hole in the middle(as seen in the amazon product pictures). It works great and lights instantly. Great price for great craftsmanship.

product_title: Columbia Sun Goddess Booney Sun Hats
review_headline: Columbia Women's Sun Goddess Booney Sun Hat
review_body: This item is one size fits all and is easy to adjust to one's head.  The lining is grey and serves to protect and soften the sun's glare. It is well made and I love the color.  My spouse can always find me in a crowd.  I have used it while we were sailing in the Sea of Cortez, MX and it more than serves its purpose.  My face is protected, the glare from the sun is diminished, and the hat is comfortable to wear.  The strap to keep the hat on is essential during sailing conditions and it was very easy to adjust.  I highly recommend this product to anyone. As a matter of fact, a friend of mine loved my hat so much, I ended up giving her one just like mine for her birthday.

product_title: Camelbak Day Star 70 oz Hydration Pack
review_body: I am using for commuting.  It is nice and compact but I can fit my clothes, shoes, make-up bag and incidentals! Love it!

product_title: Coleman 5-Gallon Solar Shower
review_body: I love this!  I fill it up, leave it in the hot car and when we leave the beach it provides great warm shower cleaning to get all the sand off.  Holds plenty of water for myself, daughter and two grandchildren to ride back home feeling "non-sandy"

product_title: Timbuk2 Phoenix Cycling Backpack
review_headline: Straps squeeze neck & it doesn't zipper closed at the top!
review_body: Believed the good reviews; my mistake. Not comfortable and EXTREMELY impractical because the top closes ONLY with a foldover velcro flap -- no zipper, not even a drawstring. I doubt the 17\\" size would fit under an airplane seat as another reviewer said it would; maybe he was reviewing a different size? That was a big reason I ordered it, and now that I've seen it, even if it would fit there'd be too much risk of everything falling out the top. Shoulder straps set way too close together at the top -- and I'm not a large girl -- such that they uncomfortably (and bizarrely) squeeze the neck and rub against the skin. Also, material, particularly of neck-attaching shoulder straps, is really stiff. and there's no tag saying where it's made -- it just says \\"made with pride worldwide,\\" and what does that even mean? Made in China but not wanting to admit it?

product_title: Sea to Summit Compression Sack
review_body: I'd personally been recommended Sea to Summit compression sacks from a multitude of friends. Living in the high country, I end up camping on the weekends and have been looking for a hardy compression sack to live up to my frequent travels. The sack made it to Moab, but upon packing up I realized that the size L compression sack could not hold my 3.15 lb sleeping bag. The bottom of the compression sack separated at the seams after just one use. I will be returning it promptly and was highly disappointed in the quality. I would not recommend this compression sack.

product_title: Extreme Pak Digital Camo Bag
review_body: One of the straps began to tear after a couple uses. I would be okay with this if I were carrying extremely heavy objects often; however, the heaviest thing that I had put in my backpack was a spiral bound notebook and a laptop and within a month, one of the straps began to tear at the base. Also, the inner "rubber" (or w/e that material is) inside the bag began to flake since day one and it has been flaking for nearly 3 months. There seems to be an infinite supply of this flaky material because it just doesn't stop flaking. The problem with this is that if you have anything rubbery or leathery inside your bag, this rubber material will get all over that and it is nearly impossible to get off. I also carried my laptop inside this bag and all of the rubber flakes got inside the laptop and caused problems for the laptop. Finally, after it flaked in a certain spot, i realized that the material that the bag is made out of is incredibly thin. I can literally see through the bottom of the bag because of how thin the material is. I would not trust the structural integrity of that.

product_title: Solo Scientific
review_body: This item is a study in wasted potential. Even the o-ring can't stop slipping around all over the place, and the lanyard holes aren't anywhere near large enough to fit paracord. This could have been great, but instead I'll be using my $.99 firesteel instead, because it actually starts fires. Save your money, and hope they make the necessary adjustments to what could be a fine product.

So if you have a Durango, save the extra charge for the "SUV" size mattress and just get a regular full.

product_title: Smart Air Beds Raised Ultra Tough Inflatable Mattress with Rechargeable Pump
review_body:
This air bed is very different from any others I have used or bought. It is strong in ways that you feel a confidence and a comfortable awareness that it will not let you down. It can be made super firm, I found adding a 3 inch topper
makes this air bed in competition with standard mattresses and is so much better than most.I apply silicone around all the seems of any airbed, in the past, it has always been a busted seam that takes the bed down. It is almost a Queen size, falls a few inches lengthwise, no recommended for anyone 6 ft. Something memory foam beds can't do is adjust the feel or increase firm or softer. This bed is fully in your choice to adjust it in any degree that suits your sleep. The pump is super strong, pops this baby up in 3 minutes and has pressure to reach full firm. Some pumps push just enough to inflate to a somewhat firm feel, but never get the mattress to feel solid. I also don't want any air bed to have an internal pump, if it goes, so does your bed. Also if ever a leek comes to play, this mattress can be sealed and tested in a pool as there is no electrical parts to get damaged by water. Many pumps will do the job of providing inflation, it is size appropriate for different pump inserts. I have found that I sleep on this air bed more than my memory foam mattress. I can get it perfect for my choices. The air mattress looks regal and solid, cross beams and dual air chambers that are separate help make this bed transcend the ordinary air bed, and as all air beds will leak some, this one holds for almost a week and topping up happens in seconds with the pump included. I have has smart beds that self destructed into strange shapes, yet the company worked hard to bring raft caliber material to create a more deeper degree of safety from punctures and leaks. The seams are computer scanned and electronically sealed sealed then scanned under pressure to test strength. This is my experience with this new generation smart bed and we are seeing technology bring us closer to best mattresses for 1/10th the cost of memory foam, and you are in charge on how you want it to feel. Great mattress, and the company responds to customer needs within the warranty period.

product_title: Shimano SL-M410 Alivio 8-Speed Shift Lever Set
review_body:
I am building up an 8 speed touring bicycle and was hoping to use these as my shifters. After opening the box and prepping the shifters to mount onto my bicycle I ran into some trouble. I decided I’d swap the stock cables to some nice Teflon coated cables that I’d bought of the exact same dimensions as the stock. After switch the cables and testing both shifters I noticed the left shifter jammed the cable. Alright I have had a cable jam before... no problem I'll just take it off, open it up and pull the cable out like I would any other shifter. Here's where I started having trouble... the thing is impossible to open! I removed every screw I could to try and get my jammed cable out but had little luck. After an hour under a magnifying glass with a set of pliers, a small screwdriver and a bit of force I managed to get the cable out. I had figured that removing the cable would fix the jam, but the shifter is still jammed even now! It also stripped the Teflon coating on my new cables. So now I have a useless shifter that I can’t open up and that I can’t shift and a stripped cable.

If anything I am glad that I had the problem now rather than later while on a bicycle tour. This is a really poor shifter design in terms of maintenance and fixing. I had enough trouble at home trying to remove the twisted cable I can’t imagine what I’d do on a tour. Maybe I’ll take it to the LBS and see if I they can figure out why it’s still jammed. I ended up putting the other shifter on my around town bicycle as an upgrade, so far it’s worked great on that bike.

In the meantime I am in search once again for a pair of 8 speed shifters for my touring bicycle… If you’re looking for easy to fix parts and plan on changing your cables a lot these are not the shifters for you. If you’re using your bike around town for the occasional trip you’ll find them ok. I probably wouldn’t buy them again though.

product_title: Texsport Saguaro Bivy Shelter Tent
review_body:
First, I'll state I had not been backpacking before and was looking for an inexpensive tent for my families first year to see if I enjoyed backpacking before investing a lot of money into equipment. I bought 2 of these tents for my family. They are great for the price.
Cons:
The clips for the poles needed to be replaced was the only issue. The clips broke the first time out and I will add rings or an S clip for the next time out, was able to fix with some extra rope while camping. I did not mark the rating down because at the price I paid (under $40) this tent is great, the clips were an easy fix in the woods (I used extra rope that a brought and tied the poles to the tent).
I will probably get better stakes in the future but these worked just fine for where I was camping. They are a little flimsy and might cause a problem on really rocky ground.
The poles do seem fragile but I did not have a problem with them. I had another person help so we supported the poles in the middle while setting them in place on the sides.

Pro:
PRICE!! Under $40.00 and pretty light weight!
It was really easy to set up.
Stayed put through a major wind.
Roomy enough for myself and my partner.
Warm enough I had to unzip my bag...I'm always cold and dress in lots of layers!
The tent survived my two children!! That in itself is impressive at any price!

There were some cosmetic issues where the tent looked like it had not been sown correctly and was resown in areas but this did not appear to affect anything as far as I could tell. I would purchase this without a question again.
I set it up in a grassy area and didn't have an issue with the flooring, if I was going to be in a rocky area I would use something under it because it is a very thin floor material. For the price of this tent it was an excellent deal.

review_body:

They cut the blurring glare of sunlight, make it tolerable, and bring out the detail of your surroundings. They lose a star because I like to see the color of things and these give everything a yellow/orange cast. The side shields do a great job of blocking that sneaky side ray that likes to reflect at you from the inside of a sunglass lens. Love the side shields. Can't wear them over my corrective lenses so can't wear them to drive.

The frame is a bit heavier than I expected as well. If you're a regular user of full frame sunglasses, you may not notice that. My corrective lenses are mounted to a very light frame so I have a low tolerance for any weight on my nose. Like the neck strap that came with them too. The case is a nice add as well. It has a clear top so you can see at a glance which pair is in it. The ear loops won't adjust for me. Maybe they need to be heated to change their shape. I haven't tried that, but that's how the arms of other glasses are changed. These arms are too long for my head so the ear loops are about an inch behind my ears. Not very effective for keeping them on the bridge of my nose but I'm not really doing anything other than riding in a car when I wear them. Nice shape and size for sunglasses. They do look nice on me. My husband prefers them on me instead of my round goggles. I just wish they fit a bit better.

review_body:
I have only used it about 4 times so far but I like it. Especially compared to other beach carts I have owned. This one works pretty well, and is the best I've found thus far. It doubles as a drink table when unloaded.

My only complaints with this cart, is that the base is narrow with braces just above the wheel, that prevent me from fitting my cooler on the bottom. In other words, you have to start your stack on the cart with something kind of narrow, or more of a smaller, cube shaped cooler. Also, the netting used to hold items, if full, makes stacking other items difficult, almost rendering the netted pocket useless, but not a big deal.

The size is nice, it is somewhat tall, which adds to the functionality, but makes fitting in my trunk a little more difficult, but it does fit. The wheels are nice and big and sturdy, and I had no issues rolling on the sand. I paid a hundred bucks for it at the beach store but it looks considerably cheaper on Amazon of course. Beach carts seem to be one of those items that you kind of need to inspect in person, and difficult to assess online.

As far as the quality that other reviewers are complaining about, I haven't experienced it yet, and I suppose only time will tell. But this cart seems about the same quality build as the other few that I've owned.

product_title: Fenix LD41 Flashlight
review_headline: Truely a legitimate, sturdy, quality light
review_body: This is my second Fenix light and I am again impressed with the build, quality, looks, and output.  Really love that it takes 4 AA which are cheap compared to the specialty batteries.  Without a lumenometer, I'd definitely back up Fenix's claim that it is over 500 lumens comparing it to another unit with similar qualities.  It really fits nicely in my hands which are not large.  I like that it is smaller than my other 500 lumens light, and is all aluminum and not plastic.  The power and mode buttons, which are separate, are easily activated and appear very distinct.  Although it is a 500 lumens light, it fits nicely in my pants pocket for carrying, but does come with a holster as well.  Light beam is not adjustable and I'd have to say it's more of a spot light than anything, which is one of the reasons I purchased it.  Besides the holster, it comes with an extra \\"O\\" ring, and rubber power and mode buttons but NOT batteries.  If there were any cons, I'd have to say I'd prefer the power button on the side rather on the end, but that's just personal preference.  I strongly recommend this light to anyone that wants a powerful, sturdy, and easily held quality built flash light.

product_title: Gransfors Bruks Splitting Maul
review_body: By Odin's beard, I swear: this Gransforth Bruks is the +6 Vorpal Blade of wood mauls.  Never again shall I venture forth into the Grimswood Deep with an inferior maul from a giant box blacksmitherie.  Why, even as I unsheathed it from its bubble-wrap packaging, I felt my biceps grow by two sizes, splitting the sleeves on my Carhart tabard.  But the proof is in the pudding, as they say, and this pudding is tasty indeed. Facing half a cord of ponderosa yester's eve, I hefted this finely balanced tool and with a single blow each, sent round after round popping apart like goblins' heads below a broadaxe.  Standing back and wiping my brow after the exertion, I found myself surrounded by every wood-nyph and dryad within a league, each begging me to mate with her so that she might bear my progeny and I might spare her woodland home the wrath of my fine wood maul.  But we shall see, we shall see.  There is so much wood to split, and Winter is Coming.

product_title: LE 1000lm Dimmable Portable LED Camping Lantern 4 Modes Water Resistant Light Battery Powered Lamp for Home Garden Outdoor Hiking Fishing Emergency
review_headline: One of the worst products I have ever purchased.....
review_body:
This looks and feels close to the 4W green one with the same features I have made by someone else. I'm game to try new things, and thought I might save a couple bucks with this one. Sometimes when we try new things they work out and sometimes they flop. This one FLOPPED......

The first one showed up and worked fine with good light output compared to the green one (I found the light output of both on high very good, by the way, and about equal), BUT the low light setting flickered badly - guaranteed to give ya a headache. Plus, knowing electronics - if it is flickering now, it will likely fail completely later. NOT good for an emergency light. If I needed this in a survival setting, I would already have quite a headache and be irritated enough, thank you. If camping and trying to relax, this would be highly irritating. :)

Soooooooo, thinking this was a fluke, I promptly packed it up to return to Amazon, and went and bought a second one from Amazon. It showed up fast, though packing left something to be desired, BUT when brand new batteries were installed it did NOTHING. Nothing. I made positive the batteries were installed the right way, and even tried the wrong way. NOTHING. I tested the 3 batteries and all 3 had excellent charges.

SO this one showed up with a DOA circuit board and was only useful for a paper weight. Nice.

Back to Amazon with TWO of these, with the customary North Atlantic merchant vessel crew creative language - while taking the time to re-pack/tape/label and get to UPS, AND the return shipping costs, AND being disappointed in the same product TWICE in a row. NO MORE of these for me. Back to the green one at just $3 more as of today.

Sometimes a bargain isn't.

product_title: NeoSport Women's Jane 5/3mm Triathlon Wetsuit
review_body: I have been in 1 olympic distance and 7 sprint distance triathlons, and the last 2 events have been cold enough to need a wet suit.  I decided I needed a wet suit just 5 days before the first triathlon of the year this year when the temps were in the 50's and the water temps were only 68-70.  I ordered this suit because it was inexpensive and looked exactly like what I was looking for.  I had only worn a wet suit for scuba diving previously, and didn't think I wanted long sleeves as I thought they would impede my swim.  I ordered a size 12, though I wear a size 6-8 in actual clothing, because I went onto the NeoSport website to see what they recommended for sizing.  I am 5'10" and the smallest size they recommended for my height was the one I ordered.  Being a Prime member, it got to my house as guaranteed.  I ordered on a Sunday night and it was here on Tuesday.  The neoprene is the softest I've ever felt, and the suit slips on so easily, and comes off just as easy.  The inside is a different feel than the shiny outside and is really soft, almost like a soft felt.  The seams of the arms are rounded and soft, so they haven't chafed me at all in the two races I've worn it in.  The attention to detail at the neck and with the long zipper leash and it's velcro attachment on the backside are perfect.  The openings at the calves make a very easy on and off.  I even wore 5-toed Vibram shoes for my swim during this last event, and the suit came off with no problem, and the shoes stayed on.  I would definitely recommend this wetsuit for any level of triathlete.  I don't see a need to spend big money on this item when the quality of the NeoSport suit is so great.  As a side note, I LOVED performing my swim in a wet suit!!  I seemed to go faster (my times were better), and it was so nice to float without effort!

product_title: GSI Quality Waterproof Camping Tent, Closed Sun Shelter, With Fiberglass Frame And Carrying Case - For Camping, Hiking, Picnics And All Outdoor Activities
review_headline: Good for very dry conditions if you are short
review_body:
This tent is very light and the poles are surprisingly sturdy. However there are more negatives than positives IMHO which is why i gave it 2/5 stars.

First the size is just small enough to be uncomfortable for me and I am not tall (5' 9\\"). I am unable to lay in the tent lengthwise without my feet being propped up on the walls and my forehead touching the opposite wall. I have never had this issue in any other tent since I am not really a tall man. If you are 5' 6\\" or shorter the size will be good for you.

Second, the material feels, looks, and performs cheaply. It is basically translucent and I don't think it provides as much UV protection as it claims. The seams in the wall are poorly constructed, stretching the material to the point that there are visible holes. This was right out of the box. The walls absorb water and cannot repel light rain even after I treated the whole thing liberally with sealant. On the plus side, the floor material seems to repel water and moisture well (contributing to the 2 star rating).

Lastly, the stakes it comes with are worse than the cheapest Walmart quality stakes (nothing against Walmart). They are lousy and unusable even in the softest soil. I immediately had to replace them with better quality ones.

In conslusion this tent does have some positives. The light weight, cheap price, and good ventilation in DRY conditions is nice but there are too many things about it that make it nonviable as a piece of equipment. I would NOT re-buy... save your money and buy something better in the $50-$75 price range.

product_title: CatEye Adventure Wireless Bicycle Computer CC-AT200W
review_headline: Best thing about it is it's long running time
review_body:
So, I've been brevet riding; which is to say I've been on the bike for longer than 12 hours per ride. This computer's ride clock will go to 99 hours before it resets, whereas the previous computer I had, a VDO A8+, reset it's ride clock and trip milage after 10 hours. Data collection shut off/ reset after a determined elapsed time is also a problem for many GPS devices.

I find the display easy to read especially with a helmet light and the pace arrows helpful while riding alone. I find myself switching displays between clock and distance while riding the most with distance displayed. It's numbers are on the smallish side, but are still readable with tired eyes; I find it more difficult to read a route cue sheet.

I find the second distance collection valuable. Resetting Distance2 does not affect the first distance or any time settings. I used this during a recent 600k ride while riding at night. I reset the distance at a known turn then at every turn after. It was an extra level of data we were using to concur with a GPS and paper route sheets.

The sensor setup was straight forward, as were the clock and wheel settings. It's easy enough to adjust wheel size to match a route sheet's distance, ride a segment, compare and adjust. However, I have yet to set the altitude base settings, they seem to require closer attention to the instructions; this section kinda reads like 'stereo instructions'.

The supplied mount supposes that you have bar space or a long stem. I don't really have either as I use a handlebar bag and short stem. But the mount separates from the mount band so, I tapped the stem cap with 4-40 screws and shaped the computer mount to angle the computer with good viewing angle and drilled and countersunk holes in the mount. I haven't found any Cateye stem mounts. While the computer collects data and displays while in a map pocket on a bag, it's not possible to change screens with one hand, the main button is on themounting side, I would have considered a bag mount solution if the button was atop the computer.

Overall, so far so good. I'll know about water resistance later this year, but it seems to be well sealed.

Computer works well
easy to set up basic functions
easy to read in daylight and under LEDs
trip timer goes to 99 hours

mount options could be more flexible
altitude setting explanation could be more clear

product_title: Future Fins - Large Carbon Fiber Black Keel SUP Fin Stand Up Paddleboard
review_headline: Seems Like a Really Well Thought-out Design
review_body:
I haven't gotten it yet, should be here tomorrow, but this looks like what I would make if I could somehow make whatever kind of fin that I wanted to.
This is a rather significant product and I was disappointed with the lack of reviews or pictures of it, or even the dimensions, on the internet. I will be updating this review tomorrow and adding customer photos.
I'm really excited about this keel and have high hopes for it making my water-sport experience better.

Update: got the fin, and it seems well made and the design seems to be good for creating the least amount of drag and still be functional for the real world environment, and its intended use, on something you want to generally go in a straight line but still be able to turn when needed.
One of the things I was concerned with was exactly how deep into the water this fin would extend. My best estimate using a long ruler and a tape measure, is about six and three eighths inches, off from the fin box.
I did order a fin box to go with it but haven't gotten it yet. And I should note here that when I ordered the fin box, I was debating whether to get the seven and a half inch one, or the ten and a half inch one. I made the right decision to go with the longer one because the part that goes in the box, on this fin, is about seven and three-quarters inches long.
Got the fin box and put more photos up here. There is another, nice photo of the fin in the box, on the box's product page for: 10.5\\" Standard Longboard Surfboard Fin Box (Bayne Style).
It seems that the method for holding a fin in the fin box is that the screw pushes the fin down into the bx so that it bottoms out, then the friction between the fin bottom and the box bottom keeps it from just sliding up and down the box. There is only a small amount that the screw can move the fin because of the close quarters inside the box, with the slider piece that the screw threads into fitted in to a slot machined into the faceof the main slot that the fin slips into. So there are close tolerances involved where if the fin is not finished to the exact size, then it does not press against the bottom of the box hard enough once the screw is bottomed out, with the fin right up tight against the threaded slider piece in the small side slot. If it still can slide up and down the box with the screw all the way tight, then you can place strips of masking tape on the bottom of the fin to take up the slack. Put one piece on at a time, then put the screw in and check if it is tight yet, if not, add another strip. Keep doing that until you can't slide the fin down the slot when the screw is tight. As you do that, take a sharp razor knife and slide it along the fin bottom corner edge to cut the excess tape sticking out past the fin. The carbon fiber is pretty hard so the knife does not dig in, so the procedure is simple and does away with the false sense of being finished when you are really not, because of stuff on the side holding it, which wont really hold up in use. You have to have just the bottom holding in order to last very long.
The other thing I discovered is that the material the box is made of is slippery, so the bottom of the fin, or the tape placed on it, slides even if it is tight, if you pull on it hard. What stopped that for me was cutting a strip of masking tape to fit, and sticking it to the bottom of the box to add traction, so now it doesn't slip even if I pull pretty had on it.

We live in the Northeast. The cold snaps during the winter seasons are a way of life. As are the mounds of snow that appear at will during the waning months of winter. I originally bought these gloves for a company ski-trip and they definitely fit the bill. The conditions at Okemo were great, and all the other gloves I had wouldn't hold up in wet conditions. Wet, cold conditions are terrible on your extremities.

The inner liner was comfortable and nice enough to use without the shell. It also easily fit in the shell and stayed put. It stayed put so well that I had trouble extracting one of my hands quite regularly. I'd have to shimmy out of the shell with the liner still on my hand. The other hand didn't have this problem. It's nice knowing that it's not just large organizations that don't know what each hand is doing.

The shell is good at several things. Namely, keeping out moisture and wind, and giving you a good surface to wipe off your goggles. It also cinches up tight when you need to button up and keep the snow and wind out of your sleeves. They run up high enough to close over the cuffs of my Columbia jacket. With practice they're even easy to cinch up. Mind you, you'll lose dexterity with shells this large and bulky so it would be nice if they made the cinches and pulls easier to manipulate.

As a last note, I'm over 6'2" and have large hands and feet. The X-Large glove fit my hand just fine, and the webbing ran down to the base of each finger with no issues. I hate gloves that are too small. No problems here.

product_title: Yakima Raptor Upright Mount Rooftop Bicycle Carrier
review_body: I like these carriers based on the price. They do the job of transporting your bike on your roof rack. But I must agree with several of the other reviewers in that, one, it is not the sturdiest rack, and two, the inability to lock the carrier to the yakima cross bars makes me nervous to leave the bike(s) unattended on the car. The sturdiness is not a horrible issue, but it is a little disconcerting to see the bike through the moon roof sway back and forth as much as it does, but I haven't lost a bike yet. However, the inability to lock the carrier to the rack is much more of an issue. You can use the optional sks locks to lock the Q-towers/rack to the car, and you can use the optional sks locks to lock the bike to the carrier, but you cannot use sks locks to lock the carrier to the cross bars. Therefore, if you leave your bike on the roof of your car unattended, it is only a matter of loosening 3 wing nut style bolts and some one could walk off with your bike and the carrier and take it wherever to cut the bike free from the carrier at their leisure . I did know this due to the previous reviews before I purchased the carrier and resigned to the fact that I would, one, never leave the bike unattended if it was on the car, or two, I may buy a fairly robust kryptonite lock to lock the bike to the rack while the car is parked (but not while driving because I would not want the lock to scratch the top of my car). Number two is a bit of an inconvenience, but considering the price I was willing to deal with it. (Who knows how long it will take before I get annoyed with that routine and just wished I spent the extra money on a carrier that locked to the cross bars?) Total security while the bike is on the car would be the full five stars. But if you are looking for an inexpensive, decent carrier and can work around the lack of security, then I would recommend them. But if you have an uber expensive bike then I'd say look else where. Besides if you have the uber expensive bike I'm guessing you have the money to by an uber expensive rooftop carrier.

product_title: TRANGIA 27-5 UL Stove Kit
review_body:
Trangia mess kits are bulletproof. They'll cook in a stiff wind, everything is pretty compact, and the burner is both incredibly simple and reliable. If you're used to the mini jet engine that most canister stoves emit, the quietness of an alcohol burner is pretty astounding and a big plus point in and of itself. If you Youtube Trangia, you can find insane recipes for the trangia, from baking to frying to almost anything you can imagine.

The down side? It's not ultralight. Weighs a couple or three pounds, and for a lot of people, the kit is going to be overkill. A lot of packers will pretty much just want a burner to boil water and a cup to rehydrate things in, and the trangia, while capable of that, is slow and heavy. If all you want is an alcohol burner to heat water, consider one of the do-it-yourself stoves. They work well, are super light, and are pretty damn cheap.

So the Trangia is a good option if you actually want to cook. That being said, you have the 3 options of the traditional aluminum cookware, the non-stick, and the anodized aluminum. I opted with the non-stick for cost reasons, but if I had to do it over again I'd go with the anodized aluminum. It's slightly lighter and doesn't deal with the teflon or whatever they coat this kit with potentially flaking off.

So 5 stars for a bulletproof mess kit/cook kit, 3 stars for the nonstick which I know better (and have some plastic/silicone scrapers/spoons in the kit so I don't scratch anything up), resulting in a 4 star overall. Anodized would be 5 star easily. I suspect though that if you're considering a Trangia kit, you already know if you need it or not.

review_headline: A word of caution about the instructions...
review_body:
I have read many of the reviews on this item and have some information that should be useful to some who have had problems with this item. I purchased the pump and tried it out over the weekend. My first try was unsuccessful due to the problem of the pump head not staying on the valve when I attempted to pump air into it. After trying several attempts I aborted and planned to call Schwinn the next day. Seeing as I had a Schwinn Mountain bike and was trying to use a Schwinn pump, I figured they owed me an explanation on why thing was not working. When I got through to someone on the phone, a startling discovery was made. The instructions, which clearly stated that the thumb lever should start in the upright position, and then be flipped down once the pump head was placed over the valve, WAS WRONG. The rep on the phone said it was just the opposite. I double checked with her and she again stated that the instructions were wrong.
I hung up the phone, went downstairs and tried the process with the thumb lever in reverse and presto! It works!
I'm chalking this up to a possible mix up in translation, seeing that of course this item was made in China, but it is still a big proofreading error.
Hope this is helpful to some of you who may be still trying to figure this thing out.

product_title: Allen Sports Deluxe 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack
review_body: I bought this bike rack a few weeks ago and was kind of concerned it wouldnt be very good since the price was so low, but it is great actually.  It definitely does the job it is intended to do without any problems.  It is insanely easy to set up - just unfold, insert the pins that hold it open, two hooks on top of the trunk, one hook on the bottom of the trunk, tighten the straps to fit and youre done!  Loading the bike is easy too since the nylon stablization strap are easy to loop and easy to tighten (easier than the rubber kind that I dont think tighten as well).  The rack is very stable as I drive - even 80 mph on the freeway and over bumps. Turns are my only concern since this rack lacks alot of side-to-side stablization I take turns a bit slowly.  I also do not know if I would trust two bikes on this rack - more because I would worry about the weight the rack would apply to my car than because I think the rack couldnt handle it.  The way this rack is designed, the more weight it is carrying, the harder it rests on and presses into the trunk.  too much weight and I would be afraid there would be damage at the contact points.  But for one bike it is great and I havent had any damage to my car. The peddles do not scratch your car like some other review said and the rack does not swing.  I would suggest 3 or 4 bungie cords to help keep the bike in place on the rack and to keep the front from rotating back and forth and to keep the wheels from spinning as you drive.  If you just need a simple bike rack for getting your own bike from point A to point B, this is a great, handy little rack for a great price! If you need to drive very long distances, very curvey distances with lots of sharp turns, or you need to be carrying two bikes all the time, maybe invest in something heavier duty.

review_body: The Hasa 18 speed 20\\" mountain bike for kids is a great bike!  My husband is a avid mountain biker who was questioning wether or not to get a bike with 18 gears or go with a 6 speed mtn bike for our son who just turned 8.  After my husband got done examining bikes for 4 days he decided on the Hasa. Hasa quality is far better than Diamondback and GT! The Shimano components are great for a kid learning to ride with gears, they can handle the abuse kids put them through, plus they shift very easy and smooth.  The front forks are plenty of suspension for a kid.  The Hasa frame is welded very well and built with care.  The Hasa name was unknown to us but after seeing the other reviews we took a chance and are very pleased with the product.  Assembly was simple.  It took my husband about 15 minutes.  He said all he needed was a couple different allen wrenches and a phillips screwdriver,  and a wrench to put the pedals on.  If your kid has never ridden without coaster brakes, I recommend disconnecting the front brake until he/she gets comfortable using hand brakes, so they dont endo onto their face!  :) (My son did that! LOL!)  He's ok, got right back on it and is shredding trails!  The tires are kinda weak for the dirt!  If your kid is in the dirt, I recommend getting a more aggressive tread pattern after the first set gets worn out! The price was a little more but it should last a lot longer than the other bikes because the components and the quality of the bike are much better!  Amazon shipping (3 days) was good also, no scratches or dings.

product_title: Timbuk2 Spin Messenger Bag
review_body:
I thought this bag would be good for me when I go to the library once a week and take my knitting and sometimes a laptop or Kindle. I had been using a bag with handles and I'd stuff everything into it, making it kinda tough to find things. This messenger bag is large (the small/medium) and the strap can be adjusted to where you feel comfortable wearing it over your shoulder. There is also a padded section on the strap than can be moved to feel more comfy. It has two compartments inside, one for your laptop and the other for misc. There are also some small pockets inside where I have put lotion and spray cologne and you could also put items like a cell phone, ipod or mp3 player; they are open pockets however so things could fall out. The outside has a zipper pocket and an attached cord with a ring to snap your keys to so you won't lose them. There is also an open pocket on the outside.

This uses velcro to close and has large strips to hold it so it definitely will not come open unless you want it to. Two things I have found when taking this bag to the library - when I open the bag the velcro is very loud so I have learned to open it slowly. Also, I found that velcro and yarn don't mix; lol. But I do like the fact that I can hold so much stuff in this bag that I've been putting my yarn in a smaller bag inside this one.

Like other reviewers have mentioned, some padding would be nice. When I sit it on the floor it tends to collapse. This is my first Timbuk2 product, so I can't compare it to others of the same brand. Tuimbuk2 must be very proud of their products because I think the price is pretty high for what the bag is. But according to their info on the bag it has a lifetime guarantee. They also write they have seen their bags outlast jobs, relationships, and a few pets. :-)

product_title: EnergyFlux Ellipse Rechargeable Hand Warmer 5200mAh / USB Portable Charger Power Bank Battery Pack
review_body:
The EnergyFlux is an extremely useful tool, and it's a great idea to have it handy at all times. Be mindful that the warming feature takes a while to work, and that you can't charge and warm at the same time. It doesn't really get warm enough to substitute gloves in the winter, but it works great indoors or in one of your pockets. Unless directly exposed to freezing cold, it will get as warm as it can get without causing pain.

The charge feature is enough to charge the iPhone 5 at least 3 times. It will charge just as quickly as it would with the wall charger. This is a lifesaver for people who use smartphones a lot. No more dimming the screen!!

The only thing that I don't like is that the device itself will take roughly 4-5 hours to charge, which is a while, although partial charges are much quicker.

It is great and I highly recommend it, but I might look into it's bigger brother, the EnergyFlux HEF (which includes a flashlight). It's almost the same price anyway, so you might want to look at it.

product_title: New Wave Enviro Stainless Steel Water Dispenser, 2.2-Gallon
review_headline: No leaks if you follow these simple directions!
review_body:
I have never written an amazon review before in the many years I have been a customer. I felt compelled to do so after seeing all the bad reviews this product has unfairly received. I studied all the good reviews and bad reviews before I bought this and I gave it a try. I've had it setup for a month now and it works PERFECTLY. Not a single drop of water has leaked.

The secret to making sure it doesn't leak from the faucet tap is to follow the advice of another reviewer who had success with this method and posted it. I used his technique and it worked just as he said it would. When you install the faucet you will find that you are supplied with two rubber gaskets that go one on each side of the metal housing of the dispenser body. You will notice that these gaskets are flared out with the flared end facing away from the metal on either side. The secret is to make sure that it is tight enough that these gaskets are no longer flared but flush on either side. If they do not appear flush or almost flush, it's not tight enough and it might leak! Hand tightening is not enough, you need to use a pliers or ideally a 1-1/10" socket over the nut and turn that by hand. If the gasket is still not flush or you want to be extra sure, fill the tank with HOT water up to the top of the nut and let it sit for 5 minutes. Carefully drain the hot water and immediately take your socket and tighten it again. You will find you will get another half turn out of it at least. Obviously, be careful not to over tighten or you could bend the metal.

So to summarize, if the gaskets do not appear flush its not tight enough! It may leak. It's that simple folks. All the jokers who are saying the good reviews are paid reviews or there is no wrong way to do it are fools. These are not paid reviews, it's common sense and yes there is a wrong way to do it. As far as it leaking out the seams as some have suggested I have no seen that and since those are all old reviews I think it's safe to assume the manufacturer has since corrected any of those kind of defects. I highly recommend this dispenser. For the ultimate combo buy the no spill cap that works for crocks. Works great.

UPDATE: Over 2 years and 4 months later and not a single drop has leaked from either the tap or the seams. We use it every day. Fantastic product.s safe to assume the manufacturer has since corrected any of those kind of defects. I highly recommend this dispenser. For the ultimate combo buy the no spill cap that works for crocks. Works great.

UPDATE: Over 2 years and 4 months later and not a single drop has leaked from either the tap or the seams. We use it every day. Fantastic product.

product_title: Victorinox Swiss Army Skinning Knife wih Blade Guard
review_body:
We love a good multi-purpose knife in our house, especially the kitchen where we spend a lot of time preparing meals. I have difficulty throwing out old knives that have dulled beyond use so when I get a new one it can feel like quite the discovery. I've never actually used a skinning knife in the kitchen so I thought I'd give the Victorinox Swiss Army Skinning Knife with Blade Guard a try. Here are my thoughts;

Pros

+ Sharp and durable high carbon stainless steel blade. Great for peeling fruit and vegetables as well as slicing meat.

+ Ergonomic grip and non-slip handle.

+ Manufacturer lifetime guarantee.

Cons

- Blade guard feels a bit flimsy and can be tricky to snap on and off. You need to be very careful of the blade when attaching it. A locking sheath would have been much better and a lot safer.

- A bit too small to be used as a proper skinning knife. Really only good for small jobs such as gutting and cleaning pan fish.

- Not really dishwasher safe. I'd hand wash it only.

Overall the Victorinox Swiss Army Skinning Knife wih Blade Guard is a pretty impressive little knife for the cost. It's sharp and cuts through most anything with ease. Although the blade is a tad smaller than I would like the knife serves its purpose. Also, for the price point it would be difficult to find a better utility knife. In the end the Victorinox Swiss Army Skinning Knife with Blade Guard is a welcome addition to our kitchen.

product_title: 26 inch Folding Bike
review_headline: easy to assemble. good bike for the price
review_body:
here is my YouTube video of me unboxing and assembling the bike.
[...]

I have only ridden this folding bicycle twice so far as I have only had it 2 days. I will do a real review of the I-Ped after I ride it for a while. This video shows me unboxing the bike and how easy it was to assemble.
However, my preliminary opinion is favorable.
I was impressed with the construction and finish,and how easy it was to assemble. It took longer to remove the plastic wrap than to assemble the bike.
I did not read any directions. You do need a 6mm Allen wrench to attach the handle bars.
I have a stationary exercise bike that I never use as it is so boring and since it takes up a lot of space I bought the I-Ped folding bike to exercise more.
I like the fact I can put the bike in my car or trunk. I know places where it is good to fish but there are no places to park the car, or it is too expensive to park, so I can park the car farther away and ride the bike to the fishing spot and not have to pay for parking. In the video I did not remove the handlebars and it still fit in the backseat.
I have not ridden a bike in a very long time and this bike seemed a little slow, but at my age and weight and state of physical fitness, I am thinking it may not be the bike.

I looked at a lot of other folding bikes and this was the best one I saw for the price with 26 inch wheels, or even the smaller 20 inch wheels.. I bought this new for $149. I looked on Craigslist for used folding bikes, and saw very few used folding bikes that were cheaper than the price of this bike new, and many used folding bikes that had rust on them were still as expensive as this one.

Now, if the bike only had a sail.

product_title: Texsport 9 Cup Stainless Steel Percolator Coffee Maker for Outdoor Camping
review_headline: Nice backup coffee pot for home, great for camping
review_body:
We first tried percolated coffee on a camping trip. It was great. At home we use a Capresso grind and brew which is simple to use, makes great coffee, but wastes a lot of coffee beans since they went to the non-inverted pyramid design on the filters. Oh well, that's progress.

This percolator makes very good coffee, uses far less coffee than our electric, cleans easily, and is a great backup for when the power is out, since you can brew with any heat source. I recommend trying it a few times before you go camping, so you get the timing and amounts set to your taste. The result is FAR better than instant coffee, which has its place as a backup that's fast and can be made very strong. Like most foods, coffee comes in ORGANIC varieties, and those are strongly recommended since coffee is usually contaminated with chemical residues.

The only downsides to this device is that the handle is insulated with wood, and as I have demonstrated from time to time, campfires can get too large and burn the handle if you are not paying attention first thing in the morning. There is no cover for the spout so it's also possible to get ash in your coffee at the same time, but these issues are easily avoided if you are not hung over and paying attention, or just use a camp stove and not try to emulate Daniel Boone.

review_body:
I've had two Break Aways. Each was my primary bike for a couple of years, so I've done many miles. And I'm 200+ pounds and a masher. So my experience may be extreme.

Anyway, what happens is that over time the clamping coupler needs to be re-torqued as the clamp get looser. The ends of the clamp get a little closer to each other. Eventually, they touch and obviously you have a problem. I have tried filing down the ends of the clamp to restore the gap and full clamping tension again. But after doing this, I can still feel the tubes move in the clamp as I apply torque by standing on one of the pedals. The riding is experience is not great either at this point, especially on bumpy descents. Sprinting is out of the question as the rear end moves around alarmingly.

So what happens? Ritchey says the clamp stretches, but I don't think so. Otherwise the filing trick would fix the problem. What I think happens is that the relatively hard tube flanges work space into the V-shaped interior surface of the softer ferrous clamp. So the surface become more like a U than a V, and things can move.

Fortunately, the flanges seems to hold up well and a new clamp puts things right again. It's money well spent. In fact, even if you still have a gap in the clamp ends, test for flex and replace the clamp if you can sense any movement.

By the way, the clamp itself gets only gets 3 stars because it needs be replaced every so often. But maybe this is better than what might happen if the clamp were made of something harder (like damage to the flanges of the frame tubes).

review_headline: Really helps my cat with his bladder tumor
review_body:
I have a 15 year old cat with a benign bladder tumor/polyp. He's doing generally OK, but would periodically have \\"episodes\\" where he'd be experiencing a lot of bladder/urethra irritation and he'd go into frantic peeing mode. This stuff, while it can't do anything about the underlying cause, has greatly improved my cat's quality of life.

A few words of caution... firstly, the bottle says that the dosage for cats is \\"10-20 drops or .25-.5 ml 1-3 times daily.\\" Well... I didn't realize at first that the ml were marked on the dropper, so I was just counting drops, and apparently my drops were much bigger than theirs because when I finally did see the markings on the dropper I realized that I was actually giving him twice the recommended dose!

Also, be aware that several of the ingredients have a diuretic quality, so your animal might end up peeing more frequently than normal, and in greater amounts, so don't freak out if you notice that.

product_title: Victorinox Swiss Army Huntsman Pocket Knife
review_body:

I debated between this model and the tinker which comes with a phillips head screw driver but settled on this one because how else could you open a bottle of wine without the corkscrew? You could use the flat heads to turn phillips screws but without the corkscrew your only option to open a bottle of wine is to break it. Plus the phillips doesn't have a lot of reach because it folds out from the middle of the knife and not the end. So if you needed to unscrew something that was more than an inch away, which is usually the case, you couldn't even use it anyway.

I bought this knife for an upcoming camping trip but started using it immediately just because of its overall usefullness. Situations kept arising were this knife was the perfect tool. Can't wait to take it camping and I would suggest that everyone have one of these just because they are so useful.

product_title: Four Seasons Survival Tinder-Quik Fire Tab
review_body:
I got a small pack of these to try out before buying a larger pack for a camping trip. They work great & the best thing is you can squash them almost as flat as a credit card & fit them into little containers to bring along. For example I put a couple in the handle of a survival knife, and a couple inside a waterproof match tube I have tied to my magnesium stick/flint firestarter. They are not just fluffy stuff, they seem to have some kind of waxy fuel or something in the middle that helps them burn, yet there's no smell or anything, nor are they toxic. So supposedly even if they're damp they will still assist in getting a fire started.

Even if you do it the easy way & use a regular old lighter to start your fires instead of striking flint trying to do it the "hardcore" way ;) you can still use these things to get a fire going. A lot of times when it's damp, it's fine burning slightly wet wood once the fire is roaring, but getting one going can be a real pain when all the grass and tinder-type stuff is wet. These little tinder tufts hold the flame long enough to get some thicker stuff burning. I wouldn't go camping without them, now.

product_title: SidePaq: Travel Undercover With All Your Essentials
review_body:
tl;dr:

Pros:
Well Made
Discrete
Fits under jacket

Cons:
Small outside pockets - could be a matter of opinion as other reviews say it has larger pockets than competitors.

Improvements (I would like to see):
Larger outside pockets to easily fit smart phone.
Separate zipper for each section on sides.
Possibly a \\"left\\" and \\"right\\" version with flat/no outside pockets on the back (might be more comfortable/less bulky when sitting).
Additional mesh pocket on inside - I found the one is pretty useful and the \\"ID Holder\\" not so much.

Ramblings:
I'm still torn on returning this item. I bought it to travel figuring I will wear it under a light weight jacket to add a bunch of pockets. I like the idea of having chest/jacket pockets for important things (passport, tickets, wallet) while still having easy access to them. I looked at some travel jackets (Scottevest.com), but they were much more expensive, plus I figured this would be more versatile. I didn't want a cross the chest one so it would be more discrete and easier to take off through security.

The problem I have is that the outside pockets are just too small to be as useful as they could be. You can squeeze your iphone in if you don't mind the pocket open and the phone hanging out. It does fits in the inside mesh pocket as well as the zipper ones.

If you wear it on your left, you have a third outside front pocket, but the zipper sections are smaller. The right has larger sections in the zipper section including the one for your glasses where they have made that section deeper, but you loose easy the third outside pocket (but they are small as I said). I would also have liked the zipper sections to be/have separate zippers. Maybe it's just me, but I feel accessing stuff in the lower section exposes you to dropping stuff from the upper ones. I can't say I have enough experience (yet).

Again, it' is well make, has been comfortable on my \\"test\\" wears, but I'm torn. As stated in a couple of other reviews, there is no size adjustment (though it has a buckle/clip on the side for some reason), but seems to fit me (5'8\\", 44R suit, 36\\" waist - I know, diet time).

product_title: Serta Raised Air Mattress with Never Flat Pump
review_headline: Best Air Bed on the Planet!
review_body:
I do not know what beds they use for sleeping on Mars, but here on Earth this air bed is out of this world. I have been sleeping on air beds for over five years now. All of them leak! But, I love the support of an air mattress.

1. This is the first air mattress I have ever owned, and I have owned five or six now that does not leak. Awesome!
2. The never flat pump is the perfect design, some people complain about the noise but that is like complaining about the house settling or hum from your TV. The Central Heating and Air system makes ten times the noise that the little pump makes. Plus if you put it at the foot of the bed I can't hear it at all.
3. The Never flat pump ran the first day while the bed was stretching and I have never heard it run since.
4. Tip: When you buy the bed set it up and leave it inflated for couple of days so it stretches out. After that once it is filled up the pump will shut off quickly.
5. what is really cool is that all you do to set it up is turn the pump to the firmness setting you want and walk away it will turn off the large inflator pump automatically.

The Bad: All air mattresses will suck the heat right out you at night, so you need a memory foam topper to stay warm or at least a few blankets under you. The raised twin is a little wobbly as it is a bit tall for its width, it took me two nights to get used to that - However it is still the best bed ever. Without a memory foam topper it is a bit bumpy and is cold at night.

The Good: My roommate bought a $2500 bed as he was in a bad car crash and needs a good bed. After trying out the Serta he returned it and love the Serta Never Flat. But he reports the he can hear the pump run for a little bit in the morning after he gets off of it. But he weighs over 200 lbs so I'm sure it releases a bit a air when he lays on it. (I know I would).

Buy this bed its great.

I spent a lot of time eyeballing these in town and online. When I saw the price The Wonderful World of Amazonia(tm) was charging for it and read many of the reviews I was sold.

This cooler did what we needed to do. We camped at that one place for four days. I loaded it up with ice ONCE and kept it outside under the shade of the bedends. I won't say there was 100% of the ice remaining, because there wasn't. What there was remaining was enough ice to keep the melted water cool to keep the items in the cooler cool.

For what it's worth, I'm a retired chef. I know all about HACCP. I know what needs to be refrigerated for how long and at what temperature. I wasn't worried about this cooler and my food in it.

I am not built like a cyclist (I am a little bulkier in the chest and shoulders).  This jacket fits great.  Maybe an inch long in the sleeves but I would rather that than too short.

product_title: Timbuk2 Wingman Suitcase 2013
review_body: I bought this bag as a gift for my partner who travels a lot.  It works great for him because he usually has clothes at the places where he travels, so he doesn't need to pack a ton of them.  The bag is smaller than I expected it to be, which is the only reason I didn't give it 5 stars.  It has nice compression straps so you can fit more clothes, so that defiantly helps.  Overall, this is a great bag, but a little pricey.  The quality is great and Timbuk2 has a lifetime warranty, so it is a  bag you can essentially own forever.  I don't regret the purchase at all and it is a great carry on bag, if you have enough items that you would check a bag, this is not large enough to hold them.

product_title: Comfort Zone The Heat Solution Instant Portable Heat Pack
review_headline: Not practical for overnight or all day outings
review_body: Worked great the first time but only lasted about 20 minutes.  When away from a pot of boiling water all day it is impractical, and the second and third time we used it it barely got hot for more than 10 minutes before going cold.  Not sure what this is good for, most people looking for a heat pack or handwarmer would usually need it for more than a one-time 30 minute use.

product_title: Rhode Gear Highway 2 Bike Rack
review_headline: I've had mine for over 10 years
review_body: I've had this rack for well over ten years and still use it regularly.  I had to replace the velcro straps one time, other than that, no problems.

product_title: UCO Stormproof Matches, Waterproof and Windproof with 15 Second Burn Time - 50 Matches
review_body: I bought these as spares. I've had no problems with this manufacturer. They work great and they work as advertised. Every home should have them in case of an emergency or if you go camping.

product_title: Optical Corrective Scuba Dive Snorkeling Mask Prescription Lenses
review_body: Just luv them.  Got them quickly and they fit beautifully.  Will totally check out their products in the future next time.

product_title: Columbia Sportswear Brewha Short
review_body: I have another pair that I bought years ago and still wear all the time. Bought them for our vacation.

review_body:
I really like this bike.
Its the first bike I have ever bought and I think,

product_title: Sram X.7/X.9 Derailleur Pulley Kit Pair
review_body:
Confirmed fit on 2011 X.9 11T.
During routine maintenance, I noticed my lower derailleur pulley was broken (cracked). Although the bike still rides well, the part will leave you stranded if it breaks on the trail. I'd rate these SRAM pulleys 3 stars. Heres why... These are on 1 of the 3 bikes I own. I've only put 500 miles on them before one failed. The design is weak and the pulley that failed is roughly 2 yrs old. I've worn pulleys from other manufacturers out before breaking one. I've now had this happen twice with SRAM derailleurs. Never with Shimano.. Have only had to replace theirs due to wear. In my experience SRAM components perform very well, but their durability have always been questionable. Maybe I've had bad luck with SRAM, but this has been my experience over the years, hence my 3 star rating. Your mileage may vary.

product_title: White Sierra Boy's Snow Day 3 In 1 Jacket
review_body: It was perfect! The color, quality and fit plus the company was excellent to deal with. I would highly recommend this product and company.

product_title: Giro Factor Shoe - Men's
review_body:

review_body:

product_title: Jagwire Slick Stainless Derailleur Wire, 2300mm Shimano Head
review_body: Jagwire makes some really great stuff. these cables work well for me. I actually can feel smoother shifting especially on the front derailleur which makes that long push on the shifter a little less work.

product_title: Rhode Gear Highway 4-Bike Hitch Mount Rack
review_headline: Rhode Gear Highway 4-Bike Hitch Mount Rack
review_body: Purchased this product and was very impressed with the fast delivery and quality. My only complaint is the inability to place the rack in a downward position when not in use. I replaced the bolts and nuts with bolts and pins in order to remove the top portion when the bikes are not being transported.

product_title: Phantom Aquatics Adult Speed Sport Mask Fin Snorkel Set
review_body: I bought this as a present for my daughter, who is going on a cruise.  So far she just loved it.  Cruising soon, then I guess she will have a better opinion.

product_title: 2011 Ronix District (143cm)
review_body: So I am a beginner wake board.  My setup prior to this board consisted of the ronix parks modello and parks bindings.  Love the parks bindings, but after attending the boarding school in Orlando, I had the opportunity to try a bunch of different boards.  This board was one of the beginner boards but all in all it is solid.  Handles well.  Easy to cut in and out.  Would recommend to a friend.

product_title: ExOfficio Men's Give-N-Go Boxer
review_body: I am a little big fat man, am over-weight for sure, but in spite of my fat waist line, the waist band on these boxers stretch to fit and are very comfortable.  I have probably about a 46-47 inch waist x 5ft 11-1/2in tall and i can wear these (XX-Large Size) all day without any discomfort.  They are especially good in warmer/hot weather.  And i think that even if i lost some weight the waist band would probably still hold up the shorts and i would not need to buy a smaller size.

product_title: Yakima RocketBox Pro 12 Cargo Box
review_headline: Easy install, fits (barely) a full size stroller, and a loud as I expected.
review_body: I bought this box to give me more cargo space for family trips. I measured our stroller to compare it with the box dimensions and determined that there was plenty of room. Once I got the box installed, however, I found that it barely fit. The box doesn't open very wide, which made squeezing the stroller in a little tough, then when I went to close the lid, I had to force it closed because of the contours of the box lid. The lid is taller on the sides and is shallower in the middle. My stroller deformed the shallow middle of the box lid and pushed it up a little. The box still closes and our last trip was much easier due to the major increase in cargo space. I remove the box when not needed - it's easy for me to do by myself.

product_title: Frogg Toggs Dri Ducks Trail Pac Rain Suit
review_body: The suit fit great, have'nt been in the rain with it yet but im sure it will be okay.Thank You!!!

review_body: I own Oakley sunglasses for sports and these Nike Karma stack up against them very well.  The ventilated nose grip and textured grips on the end of the glasses keep them in place.  Amazon price cannot be beat!

review_body: Glasses appear to be counterfeit as sold by Amazon. Amazon sells these as real, but with zero paperwork, no OEM box, no warranty, I think they are fake

product_title: Hotronic Battery Pack E4 2014 1153
review_body: OK I will admit it I am a weenie when it comes to cold feet. I had the whole Hotronic foot heater system installed in my ski boots about 5 years ago. I'm very pleased and my feet are very happy. The boots are so comfortable that I am no longer anxious to take off my boots at lunch or days end. I also have great fitting boots...that helps a lot! I don't notice the pad or wire in the boot at all. Careful how you attach the batteries to your boot. I have my batteries on my outside ankles attached to the top strap. Sometimes I am careless in the way I clip the E4 battery pack onto the top boot strap and had a battery fall off the first year. Believe it or not I checked the lost and found at peak 8 at Breckenridge and someone turned it in. I have my name and cell # on the new ones I just purchased.  By the way this year I found that the old batteries would not hold a charge. That's about 5 years. I'm an above-average lifetime skier and the old batteries were scratched up and took a beating.  The charging system is simple and works well. They would get 5 stars if they attached a little better. Now if they only made a battery to make my wife ski just a little faster! Oh well I guess I'm lucky to have a wife who is willing to ski with a maniac like me and my friends. HA!

review_body: I work outside so always pack a lunch and bring plenty of water.  I have tired numerous different ice chests and lunch totes.  This is the one.  My ice packs fit in it perfectly.  The little storage on top is great for a quick snack or to pack silverware, napkins etc. I wish it came in red!

product_title: Insta-Bed Queen Raised Air Mattress with Sure Grip Bottom & Built-In Pump
review_body: This is a great product and perfect for taking care of guests in a room without a bed. It is also portable for easy storage. Very pleased.

product_title: Ritchey Quick Disconnect - Brake (each)
review_headline: Works well, may save you effort
review_body:
This allows you to split the cable in two parts for collapsible bikes, like those with S&S couplers. You need two cables, one for the brake lever and another for the second half of this splitter as it uses the same cable end as a road lever. It is larger and beefier than the shifter version and the rubber o-ring keeps it from rattling on your frame. Two set screws keep it very secure.

You likely need only one of these because the front brake stays in place when collapsing the bike.

However, you might not need one at all if you have cantilever brakes. Can you separate the cable yoke from the straddle cable?

product_title: Dora the Explorer Plush Backpack Bag
review_body: My daughter loves Dora and of course this backpack was the perfect gift for her.  She likes to put her TY Boots in it along with other random items to go on trips with! 5 Stars!

Liked: Fine mesh, breathable, large enough to cover cot, kept mosquitos out (used in Haiti)
Disliked: 6 connection rings along the top, forming a rectangle, hard to manage if you don't have the right support system. I connected multiple rings to one support and seemed to work ok.

product_title: RAM Zinc Coated U-Bolt Mounting Base with 1 inch Ball
review_body: This is excellently made and held up to my super vibrating XS650. That included hardware was easy to install and excellently made.

product_title: Hydro Flask Insulated Wide Mouth Stainless Steel Water Bottle, 32-Ounce
review_body: This bottle is fabulous! It keeps my cold water cold overnight and throughout the day. When packed with adequate ice, it will last me two days easily! Great shape, awesome product!

product_title: Kelty Redwing 50 Internal Frame Pack
review_body: Has held up nicely. Originally had the next size down but it was stolen on vacation so I replaced it with this one. Great for hiking, I also use it daily to carry my laptop, portfolio, coffee mug, some tools and supplies for work.
