review_body: Got one of these bottles previously and tried and tested it to confirm the claims. It works great! keeps cold or hot for longer than my needs. So now bought one (blue) for work and 2 (red and orange) for the kids to take to school on hot days. I might even get the smaller one for coffee too. By the way, the orange colour looks the best :)

product_title: Wald 135 Deep Sized Grocery Front Handlebar Bike Basket
review_headline: Great product and straight forward installation instructions
review_body: Very sturdy construction and clear installation instructions.  I especially liked the pieces of rubber included to protect the handlebars from friction damage.

product_title: Intex Raised Downy Airbed with Built-in Electric Pump, Queen, Bed Height 22"
review_headline: Tried it twice, both times ended in heartache
review_body:
For awhile, this was the highest rated air mattress on Amazon. When we got it, we loved the height, it's quick inflating, deflating, and packing up. After several months it got a leak and you couldn't sleep on it for more than an hour or two without saggy towards the middle of it, requiring a middle of the night inflation. I spent a couple of long sessions listening and feeling for a leak, but never found it, so it never got fixed. Then, the cat peed on it, so we got a new one.

Round 2, we bought this guy yet again, and we thought this one would last a bit longer, but no! It actually got a leak much sooner, which was equally impossible to detect.

Now I've ordered http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B006OU4ERA, and I'm getting ready to walk these bad boys out to the dumpster.

product_title: Pure Comfort Raised-Profile Inflatable Air Mattress with External Air Pump, Extra Long Queen Sized Bed
review_body: This has lasted many a sleep-overs with guests. Thrilled with the quality and the product's durability and I love the thickness.

product_title: Intex Deluxe Pillow Rest Raised Airbed with Soft Flocked Top for Comfort
review_body: I purchased this item to go in my storm shelter to use as seating/bed whenever bad weather happens.  It is the perfect size for the space.  It is comfortable.  It is well made.  I think it would also work well to bring into the house as extra bed for guest. It folds up nicely to be stored away until needed as extra sleep bed.

product_title: Coghlan's Magnesium Fire Starter
review_body:
I think everyone should have this for an emergency. I will never forget a time in the far northwoods on an ice fishing trip, we had a strong heavy storm and our lake cottage lost power. We hade no wood burner and no way out as the snow was just too much.
We had this item and we were able to build a campfire using snow soaked wood. It really made the job easy. Having a warming fire made all the difference. Lots of fish were caught until the plows came 2 days later.

product_title: Sunlite Standard Presta Valve Tubes, Black

review_body: I have used the Shimano Alivio FD-M413 derailleur on 11 builds with 22-32-44, 28-38-48, 30-39-50, 30-42-52 and 22-39-53 crank sets without problems.

review_body: It stays for a month max, the stitches/finishing are not that strong/ air starts leaking here and there. it is not something you can patch it up. Don't waste your money on this please.

product_title: Suunto A-10 Field Compass
review_body:
1. I wouldn't use this compass for Orienteer Racing. The needle is slow and the dial is a little loose in its base plate mounting. However, for Boy Scouting or general use it's a great buy. The three star rating is for the compass itself.
2. The product isn't as pictured when I bought it--it was pictured with metric scale. The scale on the product I received was in English miles, not meters like I expected it to be. I wanted it in meters for doing Orienteering events which are typically done in meters. I contacted company listed as the seller and explained that they didn't advertise it correctly in the picture. They were gracious, apologized and gave me a refund, but the experience wasted my time and energy.

product_title: Stearns Puddle Jumper Deluxe Life Jacket, Crab, 30 to 50 Pound
review_headline: Great for pool, not good for ocean
review_body: Although this is coast guard rated I would only use it in a swimming pool. Heaven forbid your child ended up on their own in moving water (ocean, river, etc...) this could/would slide right off. I ended up buying a life jacket with a strap under the crotch for use in moving water and this will be reserved for use at the local pools. The local indoor pools require floatation devices to be coast guard approved so this fits the bill!

product_title: Ostart 3 in 1 Flint Fire Starter Lighter + Whistle + Compass - Yellow
review_body: Good firestarter, average compass, crappy whistle.  The whistle is basically useless, you might as well discard it and the striker half of the tool if you carry a knife, otherwise, a good BOB addition.  Cheap, too.

product_title: Light My Fire Swedish FireKnife with 9.5 cm (3.75 Inch) Sandvik Stainless Steel Blade and Swedish FireSteel Fire Starter
review_headline: Very practical to have in the wild
review_body: First, 10 cm is just under 4" not 3" and that is what this blade is. That is a happy surprise. 3" would be a little short for a knife like this. The fire starter fits very securely in the handle, which is not completely obvious from the pictures. The knife also clicks pretty securely in the sheath, so it won't come loose in your pack. It is very well made and and even the color helps keep you from leaving it behind when you stop. It's just extremely practical and a handy size. I may carry a big Bowie or short machete in addition to this for wilderness treks. It would be hard for one knife to do everything you might encounter. This will probably do 90% though and weighs very little. The only comment I would make is that the belt clip fastens very securely--almost too securely. Seems it would be very tricky to get it off you belt. Better a little fussing than losing it I suppose.The sheath is made of polypropylene so should hold up well and not break. The tip of the blade has an unusual tapered grind which I think would weaken it. Probably shouldn't be prying with a blade this small though. Blade thickness is about 2 mm. All in all I'm very please with this knife.

product_title: SI Predator Jacket - Gray/Black - L
review_headline: really like this coat and the maker!!
review_body: Kept me plenty warm with a long sleeve shirt in below zero degree weather,  the reflective stripping is coming offafter just two months of use which I really liked that feature for walking around in the dark in remote villages in Alaska.  I think the worse comditions I actually went out in temperature wise was a of -25 or so with blustery winds on the snow machine for a quick ride to the store and back.  I had a cotton tshirt and fleece sweater on and was plenty warm.  Walking to quarter mile with same stuff on and I was roasting and had to take off my sweater and open the vents.  The sleeves were plenty long so I would just keep mitts in my pockets for when my hands would get cold again.  I liked all the pockets too.  Going out in the blowing snow and my iphone never got wet,  I spoke directly with the man who created this line of coats and he was so helpful with how it should perform and what size to get as I am a woman and so sizing is different.  I am 5'7\\", 265lbs with a chest measurement of 55\\" and the 3XL was plenty big.  Lkke I said the arms were long but with the velcore closres they were fine.  I really am satisfied with this coat.  My only complaint would be that after opening the arm vents the wind would come through the right arm after both vents were closed.  I imagine it was coming through the teeth in the zipper.  Not a big deal but weird to feel a slight breeze on one arm in back when vent was closed.

product_title: Dakine Women's Lux Beanie
review_headline: Love the fit of this hat!
review_body: I have a smaller head and have always had a difficult time finding hats that fit.  This hats fits perfectly!  I just ordered the white one as well!

product_title: Columbia Women's Freezer II Polo
review_body: This shirt is very thin (nice, aqua not see-through) and cut large - my fault, I ordered the wrong size.  Color is pretty and washed nicely.  I've worn it only once but it looks like it would snag easily; so far, so good though.  I wouldn't order more of this one but will keep what I have and make it work.  I have other Columbia shirts that are MUCH better.  Sizes just aren't consistent.  Amazon is the best!!!

product_title: Red Lion I Care Arm Sleeves (Sold as Pair)
review_headline: Great in a pinch!! - Well priced!
review_body: I purchased these to tide me over until I can afford a custom compression sleeve.  They have been great during this time and very helpful in reducing numbness in my hand from lymphedema following removal of all lymph nodes on one side.  Hand washing them as recommended is VERY important.  I made the mistake of throwing one in my laundry basket.  It has shrunk and become 'pilly'.  My only comment for improvement would be that it come in longer sizes.  I'm 5'9\\" with appropriate length arms and at the sleeve's pre-shrunk length it was too short.  I would purchase them again and recommend them to a fellow lymph nodeless friend.

product_title: Projekt Fixie - Fixed-Gear Crank Single-speed Road Bicycle Forged Crankset 44T, 46T, 48T 170mm
review_headline: My thoughts on the Projekt Fixie 44T 170
review_body:
I recently bought a 2012 SE Draft, and have set about upgrading parts that I feel could be better. One of the first things that had to go were the heinous plastic pedals with the reflectors (what, am I 12 years old?) - and I was glad that I came across this crankset.

The bike looks great with the new crankset, the pedals are a great match if your in the market. I would buy these again without a hestitation

product_title: JanSport Driver 8 Core Series Wheeled Backpack
review_body: I'm in nursing school and I have a lot of books to carry to class. I had it over a year now and its amazing. I have no regrets buying it. It holds all my nursing books and more. It even has a compartment for my lab top. Its very spacious inside and has numerous compartments. The wheels never fails.

I got it as a gift after I passed my NREMT so it sits next to my certification on my bookshelf, collecting dust.

product_title: ExOfficio Men's Give-n-Go Boxer Brief
review_body:
If you're in doubt because of the price, try them. Once you give these a try you'll never wear anything else. Expensive but worth it. I now have six pairs. Very durable and well made, yet stretchy and soft at the same time. I took three pairs on a two week trip and washed them in the sink and hung them to dry in the shower. Three is plenty, two would be fine. It took a full day to dry one pair in the humid Florida air so I'm glad I had three.
If you have any problems chafing or getting road rash from running these are a great solution. I have tried so many different brands. These offer the best protection for active people. I get burns on my inner thighs at the top from running or walking 54 holes of golf on a weekend. I can wear out a pair of cotton jockeys boxer briefs in one or two days worth of wear cycles. Not these. They are extremely protective and don't show any wear after almost one year and many miles on the first pair. Because They are stretchy and fit your form well without sagging, they stay in place. I have had other athletic undershorts that did, too. The difference is that they were tight and compressive. I had to constanly adjust and tug to stay comfortable. The ex officio brand doesn't give me any issues with that. I always wear xl, but tried larges for golf. That fit just as we'll because the fabric is forgiving. I can kneel down and read putts and not have to stand up, pull up and rearrange my belt line with these.

I'm a big athletic guy with a baseball player rear end. I have done a lot of squats over the years so my thighs are touching. I will tell you this. When your thighs rub together and get a rash so bad that it burns to move for a week or so each time... You skip golf or jogging until you recover. So, you spend a lot of time and effort looking for a product like this so you can stay active. This is that product. Amazon has the best price, too.

product_title: Cygolite Expilion 350-Lumen USB Rechargeable Headlight
review_headline: Great Light with at least TWO flaws
review_body:
I find the light itself to be wonderful. Very bright, easy to use/intuitive, etc. I also really love the fact that the light can pivot slightly left or right on its mount. This is really handy in sharp corners.

The problems I have run into are as follows:

1. The mounting system. The mount is really designed for a round bar. My bars are oblong - sort of streamlined front-to-back like a plane wing - and thus the mount has a hard time. It tends to move, allowing the light to swing downward over time. I'm going to try and fit some foam into the mount and see if that helps, but the design could clearly be improved.

2. The charger cover. This is a small rubber piece that is supposed to be fitted/squished into the rectangular slot where the USB charger connects. The problem is that it is constantly coming out for no apparent reason. I'm not touching it or riding on rough terrain, etc, and I make sure it is fully seated. Despite this, the thing is popped out more times than not after my rides. I worry about it because I don't want moisture getting in there.

Also wish I had purchased the version with the helmet mount included, but that's my fault :)

**UPDATE: The charge port cover has now completely fallen off! I am not hard on my stuff, and I have no explanation for what happened. It was constantly unplugging itself (see above), and now it's simply missing, which means I have an open hole into the circuitry of my light. This worries me, particularly in the rain. -2 stars = down to 2 stars from 4. :(

product_title: Palm Springs Outdoor 10 x 20 Wedding Party Tent Canopy
review_body:
This is my first review ever after purchasing something on Amazon- I'm doing it because I was so back and fourth about this tent and then I went ahead and pulled the trigger.

Okay- so first, I'm giving it 5 stars not because it is fantastic quality, but because for just over $100 it is a great tent!

I set it up with 2 other people and it took around an hour, we (as another review told us too THANK YOU reviewer) duct taped every connection that there was, we used white duct tape (again, per the reviewer) and it went up pretty well.

Some people complain about the directions, but a simple picture is all it takes to put up a tent.. so no worries there.

I left it up for 3 days, with very little wind (no more than 10 mph) and a very little bit of rain, but the thing held up just fine! I had no problem taking it down myself and after all the duct tape came off it looked good as new.

I've got 2 recommendations for you guys-- USE WHITE DUCT TAPE to help support every connection, it will help... also, get a (1) small, but long (prob 4') wooden dowel (I used super thick knitting needles) to support the center top connection- You'll thank me if you do both of these things.

So- to summarize- you're buying a super cheap tent, so don't expect that you get a super sweet set-up, but treat it kindly and it will return the favor!

product_title: Exped Bivy-Poncho UL
review_headline: Technically perfect, but a little pricey......OK alot pricey.
review_body:
This is hands down the best poncho you'll ever buy. There are already several excellent video reviews of this product on YouTube, so I wont go through all the details of it here. I will say that it functions true to its word, and that an impressive amount of thought and careful design went into every aspect of what is usually a pretty basic piece of kit.

It can cover both you and your pack when in poncho mode, is more comfortable and restricts movement less than most ponchos, forms a truly excellent emergency bivy bag, and is large enough to cover me completely when set up as a shelter (I'm 6'1\\"). And that's the whole idea; this thing replaces several pieces of gear with one super light and compact piece. If you are an ultralight backpacker or the like, this product was designed specifically for you.

That said, the price point on this one hurts. I don't care how cool it is, paying $100 bucks for something that could technically be replaced with a heavy garbage bag REALLY stings. You could quite easily buy a real bivy bag (new Gortex military surplus on Amazon about $30 bucks), a couple tarps ($10 ea), and several cheaper ponchos (dollar store) all for less than what you spend on this one item. The \\"ultralight\\" market amazes me sometimes.

That's where you'll have to make a judgement call. If you care about packing light more than anything else, then there is simply no better piece of weather protection that you could get. Or if you're a shameless gear hog (me), buy this thing and bask in its multi-function awesomeness. Expect a slight twinge of buyers remorse, you'll get over it. Also, several ponchos can be snapped together to form a larger shelter, so there is some value in the idea of your whole family or group being equipped with these. Again though, a simple large tarp will do the job better and cheaper, but not lighter.

On the other hand, if you are not an ultralighter and will be hauling a tarp or tent anyways, thismight not be your best bang for your buck when it comes to rain gear. I stand by saying it's the best poncho ever made, but it's SO much more expensive than a regular poncho that it's hard to justify.

All in all, I would say skip this one if you're still in the process of building your kit. Get your basics covered first, then circle back to this one farther down the road when you're looking to upgrade your gear and have some money to spend. It's absolutely a 5 star product, I love it and take it everywhere, but it is just plain unrealistically priced.

The only thing that made me give it 4 stars instead of 5 is that since it came in plastic with a stapled cardboard to seal the opening, there's no instructions, whatsoever. It doesn't exactly tell you how to properly lock the little plastic "screw" that comes with it. Common sense said to try and turn it righty-tighty after pushing it inside the reflector to actually lock it in place. This required the use of a flat head screwdriver, or a really thin allen wrench. I have read reviews saying how the reflector doesn't stay in place, that it rattles, or that it's loose, but once I managed to turn the plastic "screw", it held its place very securely. All in all, this is a very good, basic reflector.

product_title: Thule Complete CrossRoad System
review_body:
I bought this roof rack to go on our 2010 Honda Odyssey minivan, primarily to hold a cargo box on the roof to alleviate crowding inside the van on our summer road trips. In general, it's solid and I don't worry about any of the mechanical parts failing while I'm driving 75 MPH down the interstate.

Strengths:

I like the square shape of the rails. When I bought these, I was comparing them with the equivalent product from Yakima, and I do prefer the square rails to the round ones. Sure, the materials each is made with will have an impact, but I feel like the square would take more abuse before failing than the round would.

From a mechanical perspective, the design of the feet is good. Using rubber straps to go around the vehicle's roof rails is a clever solution to fitting may different types and shapes of rails. The curved base of the feet looks like it would fit just about any shape of rail as well, without undue pressure on any one point.

The way the rails slide freely within the feet is very nice. It makes it easy to put the rack on vehicles of different widths. When the rubber straps securing the feet to the roof rails are tightened down, the bars are also secured in place, meaning that no side-to-side motion will be possible while driving down the road (as long as the straps are tightened). This is essential.

Others have criticized the gearing inside the feet (for tightening the straps) as requiring too many turns to tighten. I disagree with the criticism, and appreciate the higher gear ratio. This allows the straps to be made much tighter without the risk of them \\"backing out\\" on their own with the jostling and vibration of the highway.

The hex key being a part of the locking handle is very nice. I don't have to worry about finding the right size hex key and having it with me on our trips. It's plenty long enough to allow for ease of use, and stows away nicely when the locking handle is attached.

Weaknesses:

While I appreciate the rubber strap design, as mentioned above, I do see it as a potential weakness, from a security perspective. It seems to defeat the purpose of having locks on each of the feet, if one could simply take a sharp cutting tool and circumvent the lock.

The locks themselves feel particularly cheap. It feels like I have to be careful when inserting, and especially removing the key if I don't want to bend the keyhole mechanism. The action of the tumblers inside the lock feels gritty, so I wonder how it will hold up over time and with frequent use. One of the locks also seems very reluctant to relinquish the key when I unlock it. I'm not sure which component inside is to blame, but it is rather annoying.

The rubber part of the feet that actually makes contact with the vehicle's roof rails seems a weak link to me. It tends to come out of the slot where it attaches to the foot if the strap is overly tightened. This isn't a major problem, but I think over time it will tend to deform the rubber and perhaps impact its functionality. I like my straps really tight, though, and perhaps others may not see this issue if they don't tighten the straps as hard as I do.

The endcaps are plastic, and are likely to pop out eventually. Not a functional concern, but a cosmetic issue if it happens.

I like the plastic coating on the rails because it keeps them from damaging whatever is being placed on them. I do worry about its resilience as it comes into contact with metal brackets, though. If the plastic fails, rust could become an issue.

The rails do add some wind noise when I'm driving around with nothing on the roof. The solution to this is either to take them off when they're not being used, since they're pretty easy to put up and take down, or to buy the deflector shield.

The Bottom Line
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
This is a solid roof rack system to fit onto the factoryroof rails that come with many vehicles. While my only experience with them has been on a Honda Odyssey minivan, the shape and size of the rack makes it an adequate choice for most vehicles. The straps can be tightened securely, and there appears to be no risk of them loosening on the road. The feet are well-designed, and won't scratch the vehicle or the roof rails. The locks could be better constructed, but they get the job done. Aside from the worry of a few possible cosmetic issues over time, it seems like a pretty good setup. It earns 4 stars for the overall solid nature and effective design. It could be a 5 star product with upgraded locks and a stronger rubber base for the feet.
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

product_title: Sweat GUTR Sweatband
review_body:
First the good news --- Is the GUTR effective? Yes. Does it keep 100% of the sweat out of your eyes? No.

Overall, I'd say that the GUTR diverts about 75% of the sweat, which is WAAAY better than nothing. I found that it was even more effective if adjusted to be super-tight, but that was also uncomfortable.

The bad news is that it broke after just 6 months, or the equivalent of 40 bike rides. I know silicone should be very resistant, but I nonetheless hand-washed the GUTR diligently after every ride or two to avoid the potential caustic effects of residual sweat. But the other day, when washing it during my post-ride shower, it simply broke in two. There seems to be a weak point in the design just to the outside of the gutter, since I noticed a break was beginning in the same place on the other side as well.

It seems to be a pretty good product overall, but surely should last longer than half a year.

product_title: Humangear cap cap wide mouth replacement cap
review_body:
I loved this cap while it lasted. It dented easy, but no big deal. The opening was just right, the texture was pleasing to touch and everything held together nicely, no leaks.

Then I left it in my bag with a lunch I forgot to eat. Ugh. The smell of bad food while trying to sip water was unbearable.

I washed it. I scrubbed it. I salted it and scrubbed it. I let is soak in vinegar for a day. I used a quarter of a bottle of dish soap. I gave it more elbow grease than I had ever given a dish in my life. Each fix got me minutes of fresh water before the nasty food smell would creep back. Ugh. I finally gave up.

This is a great cap, but you MUST. KEEP IT. CLEAN. The material it's made out of will absorb any smell. You put juice orange juice in your cup once? Everything tastes like oranges. You put it in your foot locker? Sucking on your toes. Left it in your backpack with a sandwich you forgot about? Moldy bologna will lurk in your water whenever you use it.

Keep it clean and all will be well!

----UPDATE 7/19/2014----
WOW!

Customer care reached out to me about my review, reminding me about their lifetime (!!!) warranty. I gave them my new address and they sent me a new cap. It took it three days to get to my place in MA from CA! On top of that, I had forgotten to tell them what color my cap was, so they covered their bases and sent me THREE CAPS with different colors!

Super pumped. I love this cap. Fantastic customer service from this company as well!

product_title: Shimano CASSETTE SPROCKET CS-HG62
review_headline: Nice Casette for the budget oriented.
review_body:
I got this to go on a spare set of wheels that have City Tires mounted.

The idea being that I can ride my 2x10 mountain bike on the street without wearing down my dirt tires or driving myself crazy with the noise and resistance from the dirt tires.

My dirt setup is all XT, but for a cheap set of wheels it seemed like overkil to get a cassette that costs more than the wheel that I was attaching it to. So I ordered this (11-34) figuring that at worst it would be 'OK'.

First things first, it is heavier than an XT item. I have no idea how much, it does not matter to me as I am not exactly lightweight.

Secondly I totally defy anyone to tell the difference in shift quality between this unit and the XT unit that I have on my other wheels.

Shift performance is identical. There is no difference at all

The ratios are exactly the same as the unit I use on the dirt too.

But it is half the price.

I have a couple of hundred miles on it, I've never missed a shift, never actually noticed any difference between this and its $80 cousin.

Save yourself $40 and get this one, it is lovely to ride...

review_body:
I love this back pack. It is the perfect bag for daily use. Commuter use, school, travel, ect... It has a comfortable waist strap with hip padding and a chest strap.. I use it for school, small weekend trips and when I am riding my motorcycle. A couple months ago I was on a circular on ramp on my motorcycle. I looked back (dumb mistake) because my friend had stopped and I hit the curb. I flew over my handle bars at 40mph. I landed on my back (Dakine Backpack) and slid all the way across the opposing lanes of traffic. I had no scratches and the backpack received minimal damage. The buckles were scratched and there was a small road rash hole in the front. thats it. I was wearing a tshirt so I would have been in the hospital with some serious road rash without this backpack.

I'm not saying this backpack will save your life but the quality is high enough that it can withstand sliding across multiple lanes of concrete roads with a 180lb flailing guy strapped to it. I will definitely buy another Dakine.

Since I have purchased this item I have noticed that:

The cradle (which is tightened with a plastic 'screw') has slowly become loose causing the light, including cradle, to move up or down when I hit a rough part in the road. Fortunately it's easy to tighten even with gloves on.

The rubber band that holds the light onto the cradle is a huge weak point for this light. I have been able to use hair elastics when I misplace the piece but I think it would be better to not have this extra piece to lose.

All in all it's a decent light, but for the price it is now (I paid less than the current Amazon price) I think I would look at other options on the market.

product_title: Schwinn Turismo Swivel Double Jogger
review_body:
We have owned this stroller for a little over a year and have taken it EVERYWHERE! We have 3 children, ages 9 months, 2 and 4 (and one on the way)! I researched for many months before purchasing this model, and have no regrets!

PROS
1) pushes sooooo easy! We have had all 3 children on this thing at one time (short-term and NOT JOGGING, of course) in different configurations and it has moved like a dream!
2) fits each of my kids well and they are of average size
3) fits through every doorway since we have owned it
4) shock absorbers make for a nice ride for the kids on bumpy terrain
5) doesn't get dirty easily...the fabric is durable and our stroller still looks new after a year of nearly daily use!
6) \\"lambskin\\" inserts for infants are easily removable and reversible (and washable!)depending upon what season it is!
7) 3 words: adjustable. sun. shades. NICE!
8) maneuvers on sand fine (we have taken to the beach) just lock the front wheel and/or pull backwards. great in the snow, too, for those treks to the best sledding hills! (of course, the snow can't be too deep!)
9) travels well--we have checked it at the airline gate twice when travelling x-country and it held up great!
10)love the open/close snack tray for easy in/out
11)safety straps are comfortable, adjustable and durable!
12) it folds up nicely (yes, it is a bit bulky and heavy when storing; however but it IS a double stroller and MUCH lighter than other doubles we have owned) and it fits beautifully in the back of our minivan.
13) there's plenty of ways to haul extra stuff on it if you don't have enough room underneath...we've hung beach chairs and a beach umbrella, winter coats and sleds across the top of the sunshades, extra bags, a potty, a cooler--YES with children strapped in and it STILL pushes easy
14) we have received many compliments on it as well--very stylish!!
15) the handlebar has a silicone(?) covering on it right where you place your hands so that it's not too cold in the winter
16) the adjustable handlebar is handy for adults or the child who wants to help push!

A few CONS:
1)the carrier underneath drags and nearly made a hole...we fixed the problem by lifting it up with a luggage strap which does not interfere with folding and storing.
2)you must remember to recline the seats fully before folding or it will not fold/close properly...after a year it comes naturally for us to do so now ;-)
3)key holder/box to store things between the cupholder is not big enough to hold my iphone, but I just place the phone in a cupholder (there are plenty of those to go around)
4)the two separate foot brakes are a bit annoying....would prefer a single bar foot brake, but they work well and are trustworthy!
5) the speakers are worthless, but also not necessary for an enjoyable ride!

Overall, we are very pleased with this stroller and anticipate getting quite a few more years out of it!

product_title: SCOTT Women's Groomer Mitten
review_body:
I bought these mittens for a trip to Quebec in February. Needless to say, it is extremely cold in Quebec that time of year (drops into -45 F). These gloves were great. They are mittens, but they actually have individual finger slots inside. It is fleece lined and the outside is grippy (so its easy to catch yourself and hold onto things) and waterproof. There is a small pocket on the back of the hand, which I thought would be a good place for a hand warmer. The hand warmer certainly fits in the pocket without a problem, but because it was as cold as it was in Quebec, the warmer it the pocket was not helpful. Eventually I transferred the handwarmer to be actually inside my mitten (at my palm) and it helped a lot. I guess the pocket would be great for something like chapstick or money. I think that in warmer temperatures (and by warmer I mean to about -5) these mittens would probably be perfect, but of course my hands still got cold. The one change I would make if I could is to actually get rid of the individual finger slots. My fingers probably would have been warmer had they been about to touch each other.

All in all, these are really great mittens. Would be perfect for skiing, playing in the snow, and other winter activities.

product_title: Zippo Hand Warmer 2011
review_headline: Warm enough for the Alaskan outdoors
review_body:
I was looking for something that would keep me warm while stationary in the woods. I would stay there for hours, but after awhile I started to get cold, which forced me to head back home. These Zippo hand warmers really fixed the problem perfectly.

For Fuel I used Ronsonol Lighter Fuel, It's the Same exact thing as Zippo, just a lot cheaper.

I've heard a lot about this being hard to light, it's actually quite easy. It takes about 30-60 seconds for me to light one.
The only time I hear it gets hard to light is when the platinum-catalyzed glass fiber burner starts to ware out.

The only thing I don't like about this hand warmer is that the burner falls off if you're moving around a lot. For example I was climbing a side of a mountain and I noticed my warmers were no longer warm. I took cap off and noticed the burner was off.
I fixed this problem by using a small screw driver and making the indents on the burner tighter.

As far as tips go, don't forget to let the just lit hand warmer(s) sit out in the open for at least 2 minutes, or else they will not get warm enough. I had this problem for the first 2 days. I noticed my hand warmers were never that warm. I was not to happy about this. After I Googled my problem, I found that this was the reason why they never got warm enough.

Just make sure to handle with care, because after those 2 minutes I went to pick one up and burnt myself.
But after that, my hand warmers have been my personal heaters, very reliable and warm.

Also, you can stop the burner once it's lit. Simply take off the burner (careful it's hot) and let it sit for 5 minutes, then put the Zippo hand warmer in an airtight bag (prevents fuel evaporating). To re-light, take the hand warmer out of the bag, put the burner back on, and light as you normally would.

Bottom Line: Yes, I would recommend it to anyone that likes to stay warm on a cold day.

I hope my review has made your choice to buy this item easier!

product_title: Smartwool Women's Best Friend Sock
review_headline: It is the worst purchase ever from Amazon
review_body:
I heard so much about Smartwool sock so after much consideration I decided to order one pair of Smartwool Women's Best Friend Sock as a trial. I have looked forward to receiving it so I can wear as the winter is about to end soon.
Usually my feet is very cold during winter so I have been looking to find a kind of sock that can keep my feet warm, and Smartwool was ranked as top brand among these high quality of socks for winter. I took a chance as basing on all the positive reviews and go ahead purchased this pair of sock.
To my disappointment, these socks did not keep my feet warm at all and worst, they even made my feet colder than when I wore the cotton socks. product_title: Kelly Moore B-Hobo-I Shoulder Style Small Camera Bag - Heather Grey
review_body:
I just bought this bag and I love it! I've used the same backpack for my camera gear for several years now, but I dislike having to take it off every time I want to change lenses or put my camera away for a bit, so I was really looking for a bag that would allow me easy access to my camera and lenses and still allow me to carry them comfortably. I looked at a few different messenger-style bags, but they all seemed kind of boxy and I really wanted something that didn't scream \\"camera bag.\\" This bag really fits the bill.

First of all, it doesn't look like a camera bag - it looks like a purse (as you can see from the photo). I purchased the gray one. It's slightly darker than the picture seems to indicate, but it's a light gray and has a lavender interior, which makes it easy to find your gear inside. (My backpack has a black interior, so it's hard to see what's in there.) It comes with both a shoulder strap and a messenger strap.

There's also plenty of room. Currently, I have my DSLR (with short lens attached), plus my 70-200 lens, plus my camcorder (about the size of large lens), and there's still room for another lens (although it would have to share a compartment with my camcorder). The interior dividers are removable, so you can configure the area as needed, and there's a space for a tablet. I use that space for my wallet. There are two zippered pockets in front for memory, etc. There's also a zippered pocket in back that's perfect for travel documents. The main compartment zips shut for security. The top flap has a hidden magnet to keep it closed, or you can fold it back and leave it open for easy access to your equipment while you're shooting. There's a side pocket on the outside that is supposed to be for your phone. I keep my phone inside the bag and use this pocket for a lens cleaner and pen.

I love using this bag with the messenger strap because it sits right at my hip, giving me easy access to my camera whenever I need it.If I want to change lenses, it's just as easy to switch those out. With my camera out and the middle section empty, it conforms nicely to my body. Even with my camera in the bag, it doesn't look or feel bulky or awkward. I find the strap with the pad comfortable, but I haven't carried it for extended periods. I'd imagine it would get a little uncomfortable after a while if you have heavy equipment, but any bag will.

Overall, I'd highly recommend this. I'd drop half a star if I could because I think it's a little bit pricy - it could easily be about $30-$40 cheaper. That being said, I haven't found another one that matches this for appearance and comfort, so I'm willing to pay a little bit more.

Set up is incredibly easy and it only takes a few minutes for the bed to fully inflate. Sleeping on the bed was very comfortable for the one night I stayed on it. review_body:

I went ahead and purchased a multitude of other Icebreaker items after wearing this one.

**I will never again buy any polyester material clothing.

Wool, especially merino is the best material available. It has been worn for thousands of years and is not man-made.
The design and color (mine is admiral) are immpecible as well as the zip collar and the thumbholes (huge plus). I can't seem to find any reason why I would ever dislike the shirt. My girlfriend says it looks great. I wear it for all purposes too - rather around town or when winter mountaineering in the Adirondacks.
I will always be a fan and rave about Icebreaker products. I first heard about the brand from reading reviews of hikers on the Appalachian trail, they and I can tell you - It is worth every penny. I even recently read a backpacker review on the brand and it trumps smartwool, raab, and ibex.

product_title: Park Tool Home Mechanic Repair Stand - PCS-9
review_body:
I bought this repair stand locally from the original owner and am very impressed. This is an entry level repair stand with big ambitions and compares favorably to more expensive stands. I have been considering purchase of other brands but am glad I found this one, it is very sturdy and well-built..

The clamp mechanism is very simple and quite solid. When I mount my bike in the stand there is no sag at all with the clamp in the horizontal position. With the clamp in the vertical position there is just the slightest amount of sag, barely noticeable at all. Pretty impressive for an entry level stand. There is some plastic but it is very heavy and should last many more years.

It does fold up and is portable, although not as easily as some of the more expensive stands. If you are going to be setting it up and breaking it down a lot, it might not be the best stand for you, you'll have to decide that. For me, that is not an issue so I am more than happy with it.

One issue with some of the non-Park tripod stands seems to be that the metal is not as sturdy and the stand flexes enough under the weight of the bike that the pedals come close to hitting the upright when the rear wheel is turned. Not even close with this stand. With my bike mounted there is a good 8 inches of clearance, no chance of the pedals hitting the stand upright.

After using this stand I am definitely a Park fan and will consider Park first if I need to upgrade. For now it is all I need, Thanks Park!

Follow Up:
I want to share a couple of simple enhancements to the PCS-9 that you might find useful. A number of buyers have noted that they wished the stand came with a quick release clamp on the stand upright used to adjust the height of the bike clamp, instead of an allen head screw that requires a tool for adjustment. Well, I went out to the garage and found a quick release seat clamp from an old bike. It fit perfect and was free, problem solved.

Another thing I noticed was that the ends of the handle that tightens the main clamp are a little rough. A very simple and cheap fix is to buy a couple of bolt thread protectors and push them onto the bare ends of the clamp handle. The green ones fit perfect. Protects the hands and gives a nice finished appearance.

The last thing I did was buy a clamping knob (cost about $4) to replace the allen head screw that tightens the clamp base onto the rear of the stand upright near the floor. Now, no tools are needed to set up the stand and it makes for a professional appearance.

I hope you find these tips useful.

If you want a little luxury with snapping magnet go for helium. Helium also thinner strand that hold your head in the back. product_title: SportRack A30850 Folding Hitch Basket
review_body:
The package arrived in perfect shape, with all parts included. Fit and finish are extremely solid. Assembly is straightforward, though the instructions do not explain the purpose of the \\"extra\\" short screw that was left over for me -- turns out that it goes into the threaded piece that came already assembled (hidden) inside the long bar that slides into the hitch receiver. As others have pointed it, this seems a bit dodgy as the screw does not fit all the way through the hitch, plus it is not lockable (and would be super inconvenient to take off later as it requires a wrench). I simply gave the plastic piece inside the long bar a few taps with a screwdriver to push it out of the way and am using a standard 3rd-party hitch lock ([[ASIN:B0009V1WS4 Master Lock 2866DATSC Swivel Head Receiver Lock, Chrome]]) to secure the basket to my hitch.

Some people have reported that the basket does not fold up for their particular vehicles. I'm pleased to report that it folds up perfectly on my 2003 Chevy Trailblazer. It just touches the bumper (no room to spare) but does lock vertically without a problem. This feature is the main reason I chose this product over other similar hitch baskets, and I'm very happy with the result.

A few tips/observations:

- Some people have complained about the cotter pin that secures the basket position up or down. Indeed, it is a tight fit, and at first I also thought it wouldn't fit at all as I could not fit it through by hand. However, I gave it a few soft taps with a hammer and it slid right through the hole. After a few times pulling it and reinserting it that way, I can now insert it by hand, though it's still a tight fit. I actually view this as a feature -- it is perhaps the most solid cotter pin connection I've ever seen, and I like that it attaches so firmly.

- The hole for the bar that secures the basket position is ever so slightly misaligned in both positions (literally just by a millimeter or two). It's just enough that the bar doesn't quite clear the inner frame by default, and I found that I have to slightly lift up on the basket when inserting the bar in either basket position. This is a very slight inconvenience, though not really a big deal and not enough to detract from my overall positive rating.

- When assembling the basket, you have two plates that join the two halves of the basket together -- one plain one, and one branded with the company's name (as shown in the product photo). If you put the branded plate on the side facing your car instead of the back, you can decorate the plain plate with a sticker or something more interesting than the basket brand name (it's the perfect size for a school mascot sticker). This did not occur to me until AFTER I had it fully assembled...

Overall I am extremely happy with this purchase so far.

product_title: Mavic Ksyrium Elite Clincher Wheelset
review_body:
Great prize and super quick delivery. To my surprise, it came with matching tires/tubes. The website did not mention anything about it. I am very satisfied with them and they roll nicely and increased my average speed by 1 mph.

Update: 3/15/2013.

The front tire - Mavic Yksion Griplink Tire - Clincher that came with the wheelset has only 600 miles, I am riding on smooth roads and the tire started to de-laminate. In another words, the tread rubber at the center - where it is the thickest and suppose to have most wear,... Well, it is coming apart with only 600 miles.

The rear tire Mavic Yksion Powerlink Tire - Clincher, it is wearing very well at 600 miles.

Needless to say... I will never buy the Mavic Yksion tires. No wonder they are having a sale as low as $29.00 for the GripLink. They originally sold for $60.

When I discover the issue, I had 50 miles to head back home, no issues... I removed both tires and replaced them with the trusted tires that I have used for a long time - Vittoria Rubino Pro III Fold Tire (150 TPI).

product_title: Sigma BC 1609 Cadence Bicycle Speedometer
review_headline: More of dissatisfaction or shifted expectations
review_body:
I chose this one because the reviews were quite good + it's topline + cadence + thermometer. I've been using it every day for almost two months now.
Pros:
-cadence
-number of functions
-easy mount
-backlight
Cons:
-every time I need to do reset I need to wait 4-5sec and even after that I should go to \\"trip up/down\\" and hold buttons for 3 more seconds to reset that. Really over-complicated reset procedure for every day.
-it turned out that it doesn't display temperature below -10.0C (in winter it's around -15-30 here), so it's a big con for me. In addition, it takes over 15 minutes to adjust. My usual ride takes about 10 minutes, so it's just insufficient time for the thermometer to measure, also a big disappointment.
-backlight will only turn on for about 3 sec and no way to customise that period (usually I cycle in dark, so having possibility to have backlight on for at least 10 sec would have been great, alas...).
-doesn't remember the last used screen mode, so every time there's a need to select (in my case clock or cadence) again and again. Quite annoying.

To sum up - a good computer but way too far from being called \\"top line\\". Main con: too complicated reset process. However if the cons that I've mentioned aren't important for you - go for it.

product_title: SPOT Personal Tracker
review_body: Here is an article with pictures on a recent rescue of three snowmobilers:    ksl.com January 12, 2013     SALT LAKE CITY - A trio of snowmobilers in Wasatch County are lucky to be alive Friday after finding themselves trapped in a massive winter storm overnight.    As the snow came in and day shifted to night Thursday, the situation quickly became dangerous. After hours of being trapped in the snow, enduring bitterly cold temperatures, and early signs of frostbite, the men say it was a miracle they were able to make it out.    Kory Boyd, Randall Hild, and Aage Giessing were snowmobiling in Wasatch County when the storm approached. They quickly realized they needed to get moving.    \\"We need to get out of here because we could get into a situation that could be life threatening,\\" said Giessing.    Hild say they were caught off guard. They'd somehow gotten turned around - lost in the back country.    \\"We're losing energy really quick,\\" he said. \\"Then you see the storm come in and we really had no idea. I never knew where we were.\\"    Landmarks faded into the snow, which faded into the darkness. The men say it was difficult to stay composed.  Should you become caught outside in a violent winter storm or blizzard...    \\"I was a little panicked thinking, this is really happening to us,\\" said Boyd.    Eventually they found shelter under some trees and built a fire. There was no cell phone service and little food. But the men did have something that would ultimately save their lives - a satellite tracker, (SPOT SATELLITE PERSONAL TRACKER-See Pictures in article) thrown into a pack at the last minute.    \\"I wasn't planning to bring it,\\" said Hild. \\"I actually kind of forgot that I had it. Hadn't set it up, then yesterday morning, logged in, set up the account on it and threw it in my bag.\\"    He activated it and the three men waited. They kept foraging for firewood, trying to stay warm.    \\"Throughout the night, we just kept doing that,\\" said Hild. \\"Somebody would rest, somebody would walk.\\"    A few hours later, the men heard the faint sound of snowmobiles in the distance. It was the Wasatch County Search and Rescue Team. They had received the distress call and come to the rescue.    Boyd, Hild, and Giessing would make it home.    \\"(We're) just thankful,\\" said Boyd. \\"They saved our lives. Who goes out at nighttime in a blizzard in crazy terrain and puts their own lives on the line? It was awesome.\\"    Eight men from the search and rescue team guided the men home. They had ventured 37 miles off course.    Rescuers say there's no indication the men would have made it off the mountain on their own in the extreme weather.

product_title: Refuge Eco 2 Person Tent - Ecru - A Frame Tent
review_body:
This is a minimalist 2 person backpacking tent that requires 2 telescoping hiking poles. I use my Leki's. The tent that I purchased came out in 2012 and I have heard that there is an earlier discontinued model with the same name. The tent weighs about 2.6 pounds making it nice for those who are looking to lighten their backpack. Setup is pretty easy, but you do need a larger clear ground space because of the tie-downs and end guy lines. This not a free standing tent. It must be staked down. There is no seperate tent fly. It is one piece. There is a vestible and zippered door with netting on each end even though it is stated as 1 door (at least that is the way mine came).
The inside is really quite roomy for such a lightweight tent and I can easily sit up and change my clothes inside the tent. There is a ridge line cord that runs the length inside to hang clothes on. The floor appears to be tough and waterproof. There is some potential for dampness inside during humid conditions with the end doors zippered closed. The tent includes a dry bag roll up storage bag. The tent does not pack up really tight for those who use very small backpacks, but because it is light, it should strap on the back of many packs without a problem. In general, this is a decent value for a lightweight minimal 2 person tent (which most people actually use solo).

product_title: Rokk Bell Rock Two Room Family Dome Tent - Sleeps Up To 6 (Blue/Grey)
review_body:
I received this tent for Christmas. I set it up in my living room. It's a very nice tent.

First, I can stand up in it easily, and I'm six foot two. The inside is spacious, and I probably wouldn't sleep six people in the tent, but two double air mattresses fit inside easily with extra space for coolers and gear. Length wise I think it's at least twelve feet and width wise I can lay down and stretch my arms up and that's the width, so it's also a decent width.

I really like the two doors at opposite angles. Setting it up isn't bad, but easier with two people (and likely I won't be setting it up with anyone else, so I proved it's possible to set up alone - better be somewhat tall though!). The inside has a combination of running poles through the seams at the top and snapping the tent onto the poles further down. I would rather see just snaps, but you do get the best of both worlds (easier setup with snaps and more space with running poles through the seams).

Speaking of seams, I suggest doing what the instructions suggest, find seam sealer and use it on the inside seams. You may want to put down a tarp before putting down the tent to prevent holes in the floor. I also use a tarp to stop the Sun's rays from eventually damaging the tent, so I really like the anti-UV feature of the tent's fabric.

It should last a long time. I will post an update if something goes wrong after I use it awhile (and I don't anticipate it) but it's a very good price for a very good tent. It even fits in the bag after you roll it up again! lol Seems like Bell Rokk thought of everything. By the way, everything appeared to be straight from the factory new (one reviewer complained about an apparently used tent).

However, when you want a walking staff that easily fits in your backpack for car, plane or train travel you can't beat a good aluminum collapsible. This Alpenstock Walking Stick is made by Kabuda. This staff is comprised of three sections which closes down to 26 inches and opens to 53 inches. It extends farther then I would ever use and I am 5'10\\". The materials look well-made, the aluminum is solid, the fittings lock well, the candy-apple red looks great, the handle is contoured hard rubber with a three inch section of foam below it on the shaft, rubber footing with a two inch diameter snow cup, a 3/4 inch wrist strap and a tiny compass on the top that I would not bet my life on.

Overall you it would be hard to beat the price and value. I own a backpacking hiking stick that cost one hundred and fifty bucks. Although it has lasted me years it was not worth it. The price is a fraction of other aluminum hiking sticks and for the life of me I do not know why. Earlybirdsavings ships directly from China so plan ahead if you need this for an upcoming trip.

review_headline: Best I've Tried With One Concern
review_body:
I've used this mirror for years and really loved it. It gives a more stable, less shaky view than any of the helmet mount mirrors I've tried. It's flat, not convex like so many, which gives a much better view of cars approaching at a distance.

I always had some concern though. The mirror is hard plastic with sharp edges, not something you want that close to your eye. A recent crash where I fell on my left side brought home that concern. I can't say if it was the mirror or glasses or a combination that caused the injury. Luckily I didn't lose vision in the left eye but there were numerous facial cuts, a black eye and the white of the eye was no longer white but blood red. The music wire, brass tube and sharp plastic are not very yielding and it holds the glasses frame tightly, potentially dangerous. I'm torn now whether to replace it or go with one of the less effective helmet mirrors with their more flexible extension and mount.

Is the greatly improvevd rear view worth the possible danger? I'm thinking the answer is probably yes ... with fingers crossed!

product_title: CoPilot Ski Trainer Learn-to-Ski Harness to Teach Kids to Ski
review_body:
If you want to teach your kids to ski I highly recommend this system. I have three kids, all skiers. The first two learned without a harness when they were 5 and 6. The third child was 4 when he started in earnest. After watching so many little kids wearing tethered vest harnesses slumped over like rag dolls on strings, I really wanted to give something else a try.
I used the CoPilot with my soon-to-be 4 Y.O. at the beginning of the season last year. We had skied one or two times the previous season without any harness. He didn't show a lot of interest so we didn't push it. The next season it took just two half-days with the copilot tether for him to get the hang of skiing on gentle wide beginner slopes. At the end of the second day we were skiing without the tether on green runs. On the third day we were on intermediate slopes using the tether for steeper sections. Initiating turns is very instinctive: give a little tug on the right foot and he starts turning right, tug on the left and he starts moving to the left, pull back on both to snow plow.

I think I used the copilot periodically for five days total then carried it in my pocket for insurance for a few more days. It was the best $40 I ever spent. I anticipated we'd spend half the season splitting time between the kids, teaching the youngest to ski. Having the whole family skiing together (independently) so quickly was priceless.

We used a different ski tip connector (Lucky Bums Easy Wedge) rather than the velco strap that comes with the copilot. I'm not convinced the velco, when wet, would be strong enough. However, the optional copilot lift halter works great. Its handy for picking kids off the snow and getting them back on their feet, plus it makes learning to get on and off the lift much safer. He still wears the halter so I can pick him up with one hand when I need to.

My advice is to start on a wide dedicated beginner slope with a chair lift. Avoid narrow slopes witha mix of fast and slow skiers. Use a strong ski tip connector. Anticipate the tip connector breaking at some point and carry a spare. If they slide off the tips frequently, drill a ¼\\" hole in each ski tip and thread them in directly into the ski. Have fun.

Just going to town shopping here in North Dakota can be a chilly adventure, and I get sick if my feet get cold, so they are a Godsend.

I went online to stock up and found that the prices everywhere are several times higher than local prices. Tomorrow I will call the local hardware stores and see what their regular prices are. They are probably about $1 a pair. Next fall, when they go on sale, I will buy at least 40 pair!

This is a wonderful product, but wearing them every day at online prices could be expensive. They aren't heavy to mail, and I wonder why they are so high priced online.

product_title: Coleman Big Basin Extreme Weather 15 Degree Fahrenheit Sleeping Bag
review_body:
I live in my car, and it's nearly perfect for my needs this winter. However, the face hole isn't very soft; it can jab into your face at times. I prefer to close the hole as tight as I can in very cold weather so that some air can get in (leaves about enough room for a hand to get through at its smallest) and the cold incoming air mixes with the warm air inside the bag to make a decent sleeping experience.

In temperatures below 15 F, I plan on putting my other, more standard Coleman bag inside this one to make a double sleeping bag--and since this one has the Big Basin, this is possible. I love the size, and the fact that I can double up is going to possibly save my life this winter.

The fabric on the inside by your feet is fuzzy--since I wear single or double layer socks in sub freezing temperatures, this feature isn't particularly necessary. And since I tend to wear no socks when it's above freezing, and I'd prefer the feel of the slick fabric against my feet rather than the fuzzy fabric, I don't particularly need it. But otherwise, it's great.

product_title: Kinetic by Kurt 2013 Road Machine Indoor Bicycle Trainer
review_headline: Easy set up. Hides away. Quiet. Makes indoor training during the Winter more bearable.
review_body:
I began bike riding again this past May. I would take long rides on the weekend, and ride to work 2-3 times per week. Then the snow hit, and riding home after work meant pitch black roads. I stopped riding as often and the results were... let's just say undesirable. I ordered this trainer after looking at literally dozens of training options.

I will update this review over the next several weeks as I gain more experience. The summary of my experience to date is:
Pros:
-Quick setup - comes mostly assembled
-Easy to fold away and store so you don't need a dedicated place for it like you would for a stand alone exercise bike
-Your existing gear shifters allow you to adjust resistance
-Solid - able to support my 240 pounds easily
-Comes with a rear wheel spindle optimized for the trainer, but works fine with my existing spindle.
-QUIET
-Allows me to maintain my biking workouts through the cold and dark of Northeast Winters

Cons:
-None discovered yet

Post 1: December 5, 2012
Received the trainer yesterday. I was expecting a complicated setup process. Fortunately the trainer comes mostly assembled. I just had to attach the resistance unit to the frame. That took less than 10 minutes, and no tools were required. Attaching my bike the first time took a bit longer. The trainer comes with a read wheel spindle optimized for the trainer. I have a rear rack on my road bike which needed to be removed if I wanted to change out the spindle. In the end I just decided to leave the existing spindle in place. Once I made that decision, the bike fit in VERY quickly - it's not optimal, but it works very well and doesn't seem likely to cause problems with the trainer or my bike. I tightened both side screws (again, well-designed knobs), then tightened the resistance unit against my back tire using the well-made and placed knob, and I was ready.

I'm a big guy - 240 pounds - and there was absolutely no problem with this unit carrying my weight. I rode for 40 minutes, varying resistance using my gear shifters, and really enjoyed myself. I was VERY surprised at how quiet this trainer is. My wife in the next room didn't even hear me using it.

Tonight I am planning on a longer ride - long enough to watch a movie that I have been wanting to see.

Post 2: December 9, 2012
Have used this for 3 hour+ rides in the past several days. The unit is still working without a flaw. I have learned a couple of things along the way.

First, my desktop speakers were not loud enough to watch a movie with lots of dialogue while riding on the trainer. I was watching [[ASIN:B008OHV49W Safety Not Guaranteed]] and I was missing some parts of the conversations. I ended up using in-ear headphones with an extender cord. I will also probably end up upgrading the speakers to [[ASIN:B0053T4PHC Bose Companion 20 Multimedia Speaker System]].

Second, biking in one place for extended periods of time tends to produce puddles of sweat. I never noticed this while biking outdoors. I ended up setting up a fan to blow on me during the ride but I also ended up having to lay a towel down on the floor. I am going to experiment with some other options over the next several weeks and will write more.

Finally, I thought that I ended up buying a used sheet music stand which I use to hold books, my iPad, etc while I am riding. It's helpful to have it on the side of my bike and I ended up riding longer once I set it up as I could change my focus during the ride without interrupting the flow.

Post 3: December 19, 2012: Took the bike off of the trainer on Saturday as we were having guests and I wanted the kids to be able to play in the room where I had the trainer set up. Loosening the back screws that hold the wheel in place took less than a minute. The trainer folded up and I put it in the closet. Setting it back up last night took 5 minutes.Very happy.Very happy.

product_title: Knog Boomer USB Rechargeable Rear Light
review_body:
Knog strikes me as a company whose product designers sometimes try to fix what ain't broke.

My first rear light from them, the Gekko, was a great (for city riding at least) rear light, except for the hair trigger sensitivity of the on/off. I'd clip it on my bag, accidentally brush the button, and run down the batteries. I bought a Skink, which was almost the same light as the Gekko, but with a much improved button. I liked the loop attachment design of both the Gekko and the Skink: easy on and off (since I don't leave my lights on my bike when its parked outside), but secure, whether on my seatpost or a bag loop.

I bought the Boomer mostly for its USB rechargeability, since I dislike disposable batteries. That part of the Boomer's design I love. But, why? why? why? did they change the design of the attachment? The attachment seems secure enough on my seatpost, but I'm pretty sure the first time I strap it to my bag will be the last time I see my light. By comparison to both the Gekko and the Skink, the Boomer's attachment seems much less secure.

product_title: Joos Solar Orange Portable Solar Charger
review_headline: Good Attempt but misses the mark
review_body:
I have to say I love the idea of this unit and love everything about it except for the connection they chose to put in for the charging system.

I got my first unit and it never made it out of the house. The pathetic excuse for a connection named Micro USB was the culprit, it was horrible. You had to push in the cable and sort of bend it just right for it to get a connection. Well I was within warranty still and sent it back.

They sent me another one, luckily I got it right before a kayak trip and as able to take it on the trip. I was very, very careful with this one in hopes that the connector would hold up. It made it through the trip, only just though.

When I got back from the trip, the same thing happened. I am sort of done with it at this point, really frustrated at this point since the same thing that happened with the first one happened again.

I really wish this thing would work and I am hoping for the Joos 2.0 that would come out with a much stronger connector to hold up to the rigors one would expect a product of this type to go through.

It has no problems holding up a ContourROAM2, even on uneven ground, and allows me to perfectly position the camera so I can always get that perfect shot.

review_body: Had been looking for a big boy bike for our son and came across this one. Easy to assemble and he absolutely loves it!

review_body: I bought this base layer t-shirt as a wicking layer for cold weather bike riding.  I selected it in part because of the polypro blend which I thought would be very quick drying.  Unfortunatey in use I have found that during activity this base layer shirt absorbs more moisture and is slower to dry than most other base layers I have used.  It does seem well made and I have had good luck with Gore's Fusion pants.  One other note is that you should be aware that this shirt is very tight fitting.  It is a stretchy material and has a compression style fit similar to some of the Under Armor base layers.

product_title: Sunlite 1-Piece Chainring w/ Double Chainguard, 3/32"
review_body: Appropriate value.  Used this to simplify my son's Magna Excitor 20 inch bike;.  Had a 3 sprocket chainring (current model no longer does), which proved a bit complex for my 8 year old, who is learning to ride and is easily frustrated.  Frankly, with 20 inch; tires, smaller front sprockets are not needed.  Gear range is more practical with this single, which is 2 teeth larger than the largest sprocket from the triple.

product_title: Diamondback Sound Pedal, pack of 2
review_body:
I do heavy duty commuting and shopping trips in a busy urban area. After several frustrating experiences with cheap to average plastic pedals I found these and decided to give them a try. Most appealing is the all cast metal, heavy platform and sturdy construction. The type of riding I do demands having my feet off / on the pedal in a split second, but also a steady grab of my shoes on the pedal without straps or special clips. These pedals do the trick. After two years they still work well and didn't need repairs or overhauling so far. They're the best choice for the \\"un-racing\\" urban biker, in my opinion, and the higher price is well worth the quality. HINT: Before you order make sure whether your bike needs 1/2 or 9/16 inch pedals- this measurement refers to the thread with which the pedal is screwed on the crank. Contrary to the image the pedals I ordered came with their (legally required!) amber reflectors.

UPDATE January 2014: Actually I bought 2 pairs of these pedals. One went on my MTB and is still going flawless and strong, and I am happy with it! The other was for my trike, and a different story... it got bearing troubles like described by several other reviewers. I have to take it apart and see if it can be fixed. (I use the trike only occasionally; the MTB gets everyday use). Will keep posted, stay tuned :-)

review_body: I am not pleased with the sizing of this product.  The wrist guards are too small for my 8 year old son. (The elbow and knee pads seem to fit fine.)  He can hardly fit his hand in them and when he does, the velcro straps are too short to fasten, it is as if they were made for a much smaller child and/or toddler.

product_title: Columbia Men's Majik Wand Glove
review_body:
I bought these gloves on the strength of my experience with other Columbia Omni Heat products. While the jacket and beanie pass muster in sub-freezing weather, not so much the gloves. In 20°F or less, my fingers were numb after 15 minutes, even during some pretty brisk exercise. I don't have the same problem with my old Grandoe Volcanos which these were supposed to replace. There's far less insulation in the Majik Wands than in the Volcanos, and considering how well the jacket and hat work with virtually no insulation, I wasn't surprised. Loosening the straps to allow the crotch to sag a little helped out enough to make the snugness a non-issue.

Wore them out to make snowmen today, which entailed crawling around the yard on my hands and knees, and my knees were bone dry when done after an hour in the snow. I wore them over a pair of lined blue jeans, and I was quite toasty in the 32 degree weather today.

In summary, don't let the low price fool you, for playing around outside with the kids these are more than adequate. If you need to impress someone with a brand name or amount spent look elsewhere. review_headline: Still looking for the perfect product
review_body:
I bought these based on the reviews and on other websites. Before, I used the packed ice to keep my drinks/food cold, but it was a pain emptying the cooler when the water melts. And when I use my smaller cooler (not plastic) the water would soak threw. I then went with the blue ice but those were bulky and took up a lot of space, and even though they worked, they didn't keep the drinks really cold.

I bought 8 sets of these sight unseen based on the reviews. I soaked them in cold water, letting each cell fill up to about 3/4 of an inch, and they put them in the freezer. You can cut these into smaller pieces as needed. They seem to work pretty good, better than the blue ice, but not as great as real ice but they don't melt so you can use these in the hard plastic coolers, or the smaller coolers and not worry about water soaking threw. However, as some people said, there is a film on them that sort of makes the can feels oily. I have used these for BBQs and they do work but just note they do take a small time to prepare for first use (took me about 30 mins) to presoak the 8 sets and you have to squeeze them to get the water in them initially. I did cut mine up to fit smaller containers but I am still looking out for better products out there.

product_title: Cressi Frog Open Heel Diving Fins
review_body:
I got these to replace my two year old Atomic Aquatic Liquid Blue Splitfins(~$180)[[ASIN:B004OV18N4 Atomic Aquatics Splitfins High Performance Scuba Diving Split Fins]] which just did not work that well for me in strong currents. I managed all right using the Atomic Splitfin for two years but this year we dove in some really strong currents.
I tried other fins such as Mares Quattro[[ASIN:B0077FH6Z8 Mares Avanti Quattro Open Heel Strap Fin]], Tusa Liberator[[ASIN:B003JOS470 Tusa Liberator Xten Open Heel Scuba Diving Fins]], Force Fins, Dacor Turboflex, and Unidive. I liked these Cressi Frogs the best. They are reasonably priced, not too flex or heavy but satisfyingly substantial and effective. They feel light but not too light. I have not experienced any leg cramping with these fins.
Note that this model might be discontinued. If I couldn't get this I might have tried Cressi Reaction fins or some other traditional paddle fin.
I'm very happy with these fins. My only non-positive comment is that the straps are not as easy to adjust as the Atomic's. Still, I don't think I could have gotten a better fin for 50-60 bucks.
Just FYI, I use dive booties with open heel fins like these. Without booties they would be loose.
I wear Women's Size US 9 in shoes and the Small/Medium size of these fins fit me well.

product_title: Pedco UltraClamp Assembly Camera Mount Accessory for Cameras, Scopes, and Binoculars
review_body:
I bought this clamp based on the reviews of others ranting and raving about how great this clamp is and I bought it for a small portable light fixture (less than 4 lbs) since it was light and as everyone else said: “strong”. I’m a professional videographer and I know a thing or two about clamps. This clamp is rated at 6lbs which is a complete lie and it is advertised for using with round bars which is also a lie. These clamps is only good for teenagers with 50 gram cheap point and shoot cameras, nothing less, nothing more.

If you are buying this clamp for use on motorcycle (dear god) or bicycle, STOP. This is a clamp that will send your camera flying before you know it. If you are buying this for a DSLR camera - STOP. If you are buying this for anything other than a disposable camera, look somewhere else.

I recommend Manfrotto Super Clamp or their Mini Clamp. They are the industry standards and only $3 more expensive. Manfrotto clamps will last you for the rest of your life if not your grand kids.

I wouldn't recommend this clamp to my enemy.
