review_body: I bought this lighter to have with me when I go out camping, hiking or just about any out door activity. It is rugged and lights easily every time. I have not had one problem with it. A good butane is key. I have read many reviews for many torch lighters that they stop lighting or don't light properly and I realized that there is no substitute to using quality butane.

product_title: Giro Feature Mountain Bike Helmet
review_body:
I went to the Giro site looking for MTB helmets and i had my eye on this helmet and the HEX. I selected the Feature because of the rugged look and fit. Construction is exceptional and the color choices are unmatched. I would recommend this over most MTB helmets, you just feel like you can take a good tumble and get right back up.

I'm 6'2 and 180lb; Using measuring tape, i measured my helmet size at 58.25 cm which is a Medium. I could probably have gone with a Large, but using the GIRO Helmet Sizing Chart on their site, it showed me more at the top end of Medium. It fits perfect.

product_title: Nantucket Bike Basket Co. Classic Lightship Basket
review_body: Beautiful product! I am so pleased with my basket. It looks perfect with my pink Electra beach cruiser. The basket is good quality and I highly recommend.

product_title: JanSport Big Student Backpack
review_headline: I like the weight and size but
review_body: There are just two many pockets.  That is a convenience for most people but I'm always looking for things in it.  Some of the divisions don't go all the way down and things migrate from one section to another.  I expect to keep it for a long time because it is so well made but next time I by a backpack, I'll buy the same one with few compartments.

product_title: ALPS Mountaineering Comfort Series Air Pad
review_body: These pads work incredibly well. I used them for a week camping in and around the Everglades. Make it sooo much more comfortable to sleep. They seem very well-built and durable. The do need to be manually inflated after being compressed for a while, but it is fast and easy. Long was the perfect size for me, and I am 5'8". I bought two and would buy more. Best value in sleeping pads.

product_title: Canari Cyclewear Men's Velo Padded Cycling Short
review_body:
I mean they made my butt look big in a good way. I've worn this pair on a number of rides. Whether it's an easy 20 or a century ride these shorts keep my junk from going numb. I can peddle for miles with this pair on.

Drafting!

product_title: Worksman Port-o-Trike Three Speed Adult Tricycle Blue
review_body: The stability was not what I expected or needed. Riding it on the streets of my residential neighborhood it always felt like it was about to tip over as the streets slope down on either side for the gutters. A big disappointment as it sounded so cool.

product_title: XLC bike tools crank tool TO-C02
review_body: I liked the ease of use. No other adapter needed. Got the bike repaired in a blitz. Worth the buck.

product_title: Katadyn Water Purifier Tablets -- Military 10 Pack
review_body:
These are light, compact for you backpack. It is great for you 72 hr bag. FEMA tells us to have a emergence bag. Food, water, radios etc. You can only carry so much water. In case there is a water source you are not sure about. Just drop 1 of these tablets in your water bottle.
Look at the N.E. when Hurricane Sandy hit. They lost power which in turn lost water. You can't go very long without water. The cost, weight, size, it is a no brainier that this product is a must have.

Earthquakes,volcanoes, and just bad weather are getting more frequent now days. If anything were to happen to your water supply can you still get water? If so, can you trust the water source with your health?

product_title: Salomon Men's Snowtrip II Pant
review_body: great pants goes best with the jacket that they where made for ... i got them somewhere else which i love too

product_title: Spyder Men's Leader Jacket
review_headline: REAL skiers wear Spyder-wannabees wear N---th F--e
review_body: You might pay a lot more for Spyder ski wear, but their stuff is very functional with all the bells and whistles. If you are outdoors and it's below 20 degrees, Spyder is the way to go! Don't believe it? Next time you see the Winter Olympics, check out what the pro's are wearing. Spyder, of course!Their stuff WILL keep tou toasty!

product_title: Sunlite Standard Mesh Bottom Lift-Off Basket w/ Bracket
review_body: I strongly recommend this item great for holding all your stuff you have to cart around from place to place.

product_title: Allen Sports 102S Premium 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack
review_body:
This was the first bike rack that I ever purchased and it works perfectly.
It takes me less than a minute to mount it on my 2010 Toyota Camry. I keep the top straps fixed and only adjust the bottom straps for mounting and removal. While on the road, only the front wheel and handlebars move around, the main part of the frame is very sturdy and doesn't appear to bounce. I once took it on the road while the bottom straps were not tightened and didn't have a problem. Great rack for the value.
Take the rack off when you're not using it. I've seen the plastic and foam parts of racks deteriorate from weather and changes in temperature.
It would be helpful if the product description had a list of all the compatible make and models like there is on the outside of the rack's box.

product_title: Camelbak Podium Chill Bottle
review_body: I have tried many different cycling bottles and these are the best by far. It keeps the water cold and it doesn't drip. My kids are even using one for school. It's perfect!

product_title: Sector 9 Portal Platinum 38.1" Drop Through Complete Longboard
review_body: It was what I was looking for!!! I would recommend it. It was a good gift for my child !

product_title: Columbia Men's Shimmer Me Timbers II Hooded Jacket
review_body: This jacket has exceeded all expectations.  I'm 5'11" and 200 lbs and the large fits great even with a fleece underneath.  It's very warm but breathes well.  It is very rain resistant and super light.  I wouldn't hesitate to buy this jacket.

product_title: Emergency Zone  Personal Water Filter Straw (Pack of 2)
review_headline: Really cruddy straws, Filters seem okay
review_body:
I would give these a better rating, given the small size and the low price point for the two of them, but both of the plastic straws split at the seams when they were inserted into the filters. (It's going to be kind of hard to draw water up through them, given those large splits.)

If you're serious about having something that will work if needed, you might want to try another brand of personal water filter. But if you just need something to throw into a pack, in case the worst ever happens, and you don't really think the worst will actually occur, go ahead and get these for the portability. (And bring along some duct tape to repair them.)

Do plan on spitting out the carbon dust on first use. (The water will be black. Don't freak out.)

(Note: 1/4 inch OD Tygon tubing fits inside perfectly, making a better straw. Bit more work to suck through it, of course, due to the smaller inner diameter, but Tygon tubing is practically indestructible.)

product_title: Surf One "Pakala III" complete skateboard (KXL, 9.25-Inch x 43.75-Inch)
review_body: I wanted a board to kick around the neighborhood with and stay in touch with the feel of surfing when I couldn't make it out to the break.  This board is plenty sturdy and rides great.  The wheels are large and smooth, and the trucks are nice and wide.  It carves easily and the kick tail helps to get over any obstacles.  The paint job is stylish/old school.  Overall I am loving this skate board.

product_title: Jandd Frame Pack, Black
review_body: Just what I needed to carry my masterlock chain on my Cannondale road bike. Fits perfectly and isn't bulky at all. Straps keep it tight and secure my 7 lb chain with no signs of give or wobble. Can't think of anything better for carrying a big chain or other items.

product_title: Topeak F66 Fixer for Phone Pack, Tool Bags & Moonshine 3H/HID Battery Mount
review_body: Putting the F66 on my stem was the perfect solution to figuring out where to put the phone pack while I ride.  Frees up space on the handlebar for other attachments.

product_title: First Aid Kit Hard Red Case 326 Pieces Exceeds OSHA and ANSI Guidelines 100 People - Office, Home, Car, School, Emergency, Survival, Camping, Hunting, and Sports

This pair is great, even with the unanticipated lightly padded chamois. I used them in a Sprint triathlon just last month and I had no complaints! product_title: Halo II Headband Sweatband Pullover
review_headline: Moisture Boy mountain biker gives it two thumbs up!
review_body:
I grew up in Atlanta and when playing basketball in high school, I would sweat so much and drink so much water that my friends called me \\"moisture boy\\". I could play ball for 20 or 30 minutes and I would look like I stood under a shower head with all my clothes on. Fast-forward 15 years and 50 plus pounds, and I am still moisture boy, but I live in Colorado where it is usually pretty dry. I like to mountain bike several times a week and was finding that the constant river of sweat out of my helmet and into my eyes and onto my sunglasses was one of my biggest discomforts with riding. I bought a Halo earlier in the summer and now I never ride without it. It works well as advertised under my helmet and fits comfortably. My sunglasses are sweat free and my eyes stay clear *most* of the time. On longer, hotter rides I wring out my Halo when I take a break, much to my wife's dismay. I put it back on, and it is good for another half hour or so. If I don't wring it out on longer rides I start to get some leakage, especially if I bend my head down (e.g. to tie my shoes or something) and lift it back up.

The bottom line for me is that I am a heavy sweater and the Halo is a home run and goes with me on every ride. I have yet to test it in a humid environment like Atlanta, but based on my hottest and more humid rides here in Colorado, I think it would still be worth trying one in any environment.

product_title: CatEye - Micro Wireless Cycle Computer
review_headline: Best Cycling Computer In Price Range? Read more below....
review_body:
DON'T SKIP THIS REVIEW BECAUSE IT IS LONG!!! I will answer questions that the other reviewers did not answer. Also, at the end of this review, I have written simplified instructions that are much easier to use than the complicated flow chart manual that the computer comes with. Read on!

QUICK REVIEW: The Cateye Micro Wireless is an excellent wireless bike computer because of its high value price, features, and reliability. I bought this computer for a new bike, but I am still using the excellent and reliable Cateye Strada Wireless on my mountain bike. The Strada has survived extremely technical and jarring terrain, heat, cold, and torrential downpours of rain. I haven't been able to extensively test the reliability of the Micro Wireless yet, but I'm sure based on the Strada and it's similar design, that the Micro will give 100% reliability and satisfaction.

WHICH SHOULD I BUY? CATEYE STRADA WIRELESS OR MICRO WIRELESS?: If you want a computer that is easier to setup and use, go with the Strada wireless. If you want a computer with a backlight for low-light situations, a separate stopwatch, the ability to choose something other than \\"current speed\\" for the primary (non-changing) upper display, and the ability to limit which parameters(avg, max, dst, time, etc) are displayed as you cycle through the computer, go with the Micro Wireless. The Micro takes more time to learn, but its upgrades make it a much more functional computer than the Strada, especially considering that it is cheaper than the Strada at this time. When I use the Strada, I have to wear a sports watch so that I can time laps and sections of the trip separately from the trip timer.

CUSTOMIZABLE DISPLAY: I want to clear up some confusion about the Cateye Micro Wireless and its customizable display. There are three spaces for items to be displayed--the upper, middle, and lower parts of the screen. The upper part of the screen can be preset to any parameter youdesire, even the stopwatch. It will always be displayed. The blue middle screen is FIXED to display \\"time of day\\", will continuously be displayed, and is NON-CUSTOMIZABLE. The lower part of the screen can cycle through all of the parameters and will stay on your last selection. Basically, once you choose what to display on the upper screen, the upper and middle screens never change while the lower screen can cycle through the other parameters by clicking through them. In a nutshell, you can only customize the upper and lower displays.

SIMPLER MEANS SAFER: One feature of the Micro that I really like is the ability to limit which parameters are shown when you cycle through the computer. When I am riding with traffic or mountain biking, I don't want to cycle through 7 different parameters to find what I need because that's too distracting. The solution? Turn the parameters off that you don't use and limit the lower display to 2 or 3 options to cycle through. By doing this, you can quickly cycle to what you want without even looking at the computer, then take a quick glance down when it is safe to do so.

Below, I have included some instructions that will make using this computer MUCH EASIER than reading the complicated manual or trying to figuring it out. I can't explain everything here, but I can save you a lot of frustration with these tips:

INSTRUCTIONS SIMPLIFIED:

The Micro has essentially 4 buttons--the AC (\\"all clear\\") Reset, Mode, Menu, and SSE (soft tiny button).

The AC button resets and deletes all of the information on the computer to factory default.

The Mode button has two functions. Quick clicks cycle through whatever is flashing. Holding the Mode button down for 2 seconds either allows modification of something while in the menu, or turning the backlight on/off while riding. When riding, hold down the Mode button for 2 seconds to open the backlight option, then quick click between on/off, then hold down for 2 seconds again to exit back to normal operation. Note: When the computer is attached to the bike's stem/handlebar, the Mode button is depressed by the mounting bracket when the bottom of the computer is pushed down.

The Menu button has two functions. It obviously enters the menu and also functions as a back/save button when an item has been modified or when exiting the menu is desired.

The SSE (soft middle) button does not function on its own. When the computer is mounted to the bike, pressing on the SSE also clicks the Mode button. THE SSE BUTTON WILL NOT DO ANYTHING ON ITS OWN. IT WILL ONLY FUNCTION WHEN PRESSED AT THE SAME TIME AS THE MODE BUTTON. KEEP THIS IN MIND WHEN USING THE COMPUTER AWAY FROM THE BIKE. When quick clicked, it start/stops the stopwatch as well as the trip time when in manual mode (\\"AT OFF\\"=manual mode, \\"AT ON\\"=automatic start stop caused by motion of the wheel). When held down for 2 seconds, it also clears the data currently being displayed. \\"Distance 2\\" and the \\"stopwatch\\" must be cleared separately from the other parameters. The other parameters (AVG SPD, MX SPD, TIME, DST) will ALL BE DELETED when any one of them is displayed and cleared by using the SSE button for 2 seconds. If either the \\"stopwatch\\" or \\"distance 2\\" are in the upper display, they can be reset by cycling to the current speed in the lower display and holding down the SSE button for 2 seconds.

Now that you know how to use each of the buttons, you can figure out the rest. It just takes some time. I hope this helps and saves you some time and frustration. Keep riding!

review_body:

This is extreamly dissapointing, as I don't always want turbo mode, often just a little light to see the door key slot. Also, if you have had a few of the other bright lights with several modes, it will take you a little while to get use to the way this one works(only with a AA battery)
Most lights you click on, then lightly push to change modes, with this one, you lightly push to select mode then click on. I can't see where this is any better, you would have to click it off to change mode, then click back on. This way takes much longer to change modes, and you will be without light for a moment, sometime, that could be bad!
It will come back on where you last used it if you just click it. Many of the cheaper ones come on at a different mode each time or always start on high. Another problem it has, trying to get it to stand up is too hard, the back is not flat, it will stand, but this needs to be fixed.
When they fix the design flaws, it will be a 5 star no doubt. In the mean time, mine will go back. It had a great life for 1 day though. It was able to sit beside my olight, fenix, surefire, streamlight and many others. Jetbeam, listen to your customers.

product_title: Pearl Izumi Men's P.R.O. Pittards Gel Gl
review_headline: Decent after 2 years; Giro Monaco better.
review_body:
Got these October 2011. Retiring them now October 2013 after 5000 miles. Generally I am a big fan of PI cycle goods. Have jerseys, shorts, jackets, hats, gloves mostly at the Elite level and some Pro. Prior set of gloves were PI Pittards Carbon Leather 2008 glove. Great glove. Alternated between two pairs of PI Carbon for three seasons. PI stopped making them so went with these... the PRO Pittards Gel since both Pittards and Gel are desirable features.

These look good and are a minimalist design without the standard velcro wrist tab. As a result, the glove does not come far up your wrist. They also ride cool... hands don't feel excessively hot and sweaty.

On the downside, after a couple months, the stitching at the thumb-wrist interface let go. So became like riding with previous gloves but with velcro tab left open. Not too much of a hassle, but annoying. My main complaint is that you can't get the gloves off quickly enough after a ride. The lack of the velcro tab is not compensated by the pull tab on the third finger. I'd be struggling for a couple seconds to wiggle my fingers and hand out, which never happened with PI Carbon Leather (or any other glove). Doesn't sound like a big deal but after a ride, gloves need to come off first before getting the rest of your gear off (and grabbing a beer and a shower).

Instead of buying another pair, replaced these with Giro Monaco gloves. Monaco's also feature Pittards leather and gel (3M Technogel). Also have pull tabs, but two... on second and third fingers - on the top instead of on the side; top being clearly superior. Also Monaco's have a svelte velcro wrist strap. So these gloves come off the fastest ever of many pairs of gloves I've ever had. Downside, the glove is a bit longer than the PI PRO... riding further up your wrist... so not a minimalist... and not as temperature cool. But clearly superior. Going to buy a second set to alternate between.

product_title: Pearl Izumi Men's Thermal Lite Glove
review_body:
These gloves are great, especially for the price. Here's what I like:
- Fit matches the sizing;
- They are thin and fit snugly, so there's still good feel, and not bunching up;
- They are nearly wind-proof, even at 30 mph, so my hands stay warm;
- They have some thin, rubberized grips on the thumb, index, and middle fingers.

I needed some gloves for cool-weather road-biking and these fit my needs. There is ZERO padding in these gloves, so don't expect pads. I didn't want padding, just protection from cold, and that's what I got.

They are thin and do not look like they would withstand much abuse, so I'm waiting to put them on until I'm on the bike, ready to go, and taking them off as soon as I'm done. So far, so good.

UPDATE: After several months of use, they are still good, but one of the cuffs is unraveling. If you look at the zoomed view, you'll see the cuff trim. Well, mine had loose threads. I tried to pull one off, which was my mistake. It began the unraveling process, and now, half the cuff trim is hanging loose.

Additionally, the gloves are showing some wear all over. They still feel really good, but I don't think they will last very long, maybe a year?

product_title: Light Rear Cygolite Hotshot 2watt Usb+wall Charger
review_body: This light is unexcelled.  It has several modes and a another adjustment for speed of flashes.  One mode is perfect for day riding on highways, consisting of a cresendo/decresendo pulse that is visible for miles--literally.  If anything, this mode is too bright for night, when I use one of several pulsing flash patterns. A couple of those are maddening strobe effects that demand rapt, involuntary attention.  The Nightrider Solas 2-watt, a new light also available on Amazon, is the sole competitor I have found, and I have looked far and wide. I suppose there may be others, but I have not found them.  I continue to be amazed by the number of riders out in the daytime in heavy traffic who have either no rear light or very dim and ineffective ones. This light has an effect that is impossible to avoid or deny. I always wear a yellow fluorescent vest that is very effective in the daylight. Between this tail light, an E-3 Supernova dynamo front light, reflective tires that came on my Townie, wheel reflectors and copious 3M red  reflective tape on my Townie Electra, all topped off by 3M blue tape on my helmet, I have enormous respect at night from drivers at night. Some approaching virtually stop and pull over, many refuse to budge at 4-way stops until I either motion for them to do so or go on across myself. Those coming up from the rear move into another lane.  Hey, the point is to stay alive. If you have to look like a fire truck to do it, that's fine. Even the police nod and wave approval to me and incredibly, a fire department ambulance rushing into my geezer neighborhood recently braked heavily for me at an intersection. You only have one set of bones; don't scrimp on your own safety.

product_title: Takara Kabuto Single Speed Road Bike
review_body:
I purchased this bike based on the great reviews and good prices. I like several things about it:
1) It is a fixie / one speed
A) This reduces weight, maintenance, messy-derails, and price
B) It is fashionable
C) There are other virtues of fixies on which I will not elaborate
2) The colors and general design are fun. Everyone was admiring my bike when I showed up to a class picnic. I mentioned it was a single speed, someone asked what speed that was, and I replied \\"fast\\". Everyone laughed and looked upon my bike admiringly.
3) The parts seem to be of good quality. Some previous reviewers have said the breaks were made of plastic. That was not the case for me, so perhaps they updated the bike since the older reviews.
4) The tires are hybrid, which means they give you a fair amount of speed (like with road bike tires) but you won't waste much time replacing them when they pop as you go over a bump.

WARNING --
1) Many nuts and bolts need to be tightened. For example, the foot-clip (is that what they are called?) bolts were a little loose so one fell off when I was riding. I promptly tightened the others and haven't had any problems since. Similarly, the handle bar slipped a little (about the axis going left to right), and needed to be moved back and tightened. This is not a big deal and is easily addressed, but it will be more convenient for buyers if they know about it when they are first assembling their bikes. Tighten everything.

Great bike, super glad I purchased it.

product_title: Kool Stop Dura 2 Brake Insert
review_body: If you read forums like [...], and find threads where people are asking what brakes to upgrade to to improve performance, the standard answer is ''don't replace the brakes, all you need is some koolstop salmon pads''. Fit into 'shimano' cartridge shoes (you can buy them with the pads).

product_title: TETON Sports Explorer 4000 Internal Frame Backpack; Great Backpacking Gear; Backpack for Men and Women; Hiking Backpacks for Camping and Hunting; with a New Limited Edition Color; Free Rain Cover Included
review_body: Good product for the price. Seems to be pretty well made and was comfortable with a 25lb load on a short hike.

product_title: Aftermarket HJC HJ-09 visor shield for CL-15, CL-SP, CS-R1, CS-R2, FS-15, CL-16, AC-12, Kawasaki ZX, Kawasaki ZXSP, IS-16 and Joe RKT101 and RKT201
review_body: The picture doesn't really show the pink/purple rainbow effect it has opposite the light teal green. If was darker then this would be awesome. product_title: Red Running Sunglasses Exchangeable 5 Lenses
review_headline: Comfortable, good option for the price
review_body:
I've had these for a couple weeks now and like them just fine. They're comfortable on my face, the lenses are easy to change out, and the hard case for the extra lenses is nice. The dark and the blue lenses are great for commuting on the road, and the clear is good protection for mountain biking. review_body:

Much much lighter than my old bent gate dog leg snap links

review_headline: Ahead of schedule and some welcome light.
review_body: I ordered two of these on the Saturday evening after Sandy struck and had them delivered to a relative's address in NJ that was still without power. review_body: This is my first pair of resin pads, having always run metallic pads.  The resin is silent compared to the metallic.  Don't know about heat dissipation, pad life, or wet performance yet, but my first impression is great.  Will update if performance or wear isn't good.

product_title: Dakine Coast Cooler Pack
review_headline: Comfortable for long trips and SUPER useful Backpack
review_body:
I bought this backpack because I have two small children, ages 1 and 3, and we are out and about just about every other day. We'd spend a fortune eating out or would have to rely on snack type items if it weren't for a product like this. It's wonderful to be able to make our own, healthy meals and stay out for as long as we want which is great for days at the zoo, small hiking adventures, etc.

I love that this backpack as a separate compartment for the cooler. I use the top part as a diaper bag basically and it's even big enough for a picnic blanket! I'm a chronic over packer, so needed something a bit bigger than what's available in the form of actual diaper bags.

The bag also looks great and is very comfortable to use for extended uses. My only complaint is that your back get a bit sweaty because the material is not breathable, but I wouldn't let that deter your purchase if functionality is most important!

review_body: I needed it for an outdoor table top heater that ran on a small gas propane tank. It hooked up in seconds to a 20 pounder and worked great.

product_title: Athena Brands Soladyne 7-Inch Mini Solar Lantern
review_body:
When I received this I cranked it for a bit, and tested it. It worked fine, so I left it in a bright window for half the day while I packed for a camping trip. At the camp site, the light was noticeably brighter than just hand cranking. The next morning I saw that the red \\"charging\\" light was on. So it even charged inside the tent. As the pictures show, this is a small lantern. The product description says to use for ambient light, and that is what I used it for, inside a tent and around the camp area. It weighs 8.6 ounces. I had some jealous friends who brought heavy and giant lanterns which weren't really necessary. I also agree with another reviewer that noticed that the solar charge was brighter than the hand crank.

I would definitely recommend this for tent camping, and as an emergency light. The small size, and solar panel was my main reason for purchase.

review_body:
This product was what we were wanting. Very very happy with this product & would suggegest it to anyone.

I'm able to fit all my gear in it for the hike out to the dive spot and clip my fins to it with a carabiner. I just wish it had backpack straps for the hike to the dive spot and back, it would make the weight of all the catch/gear easier. Great strudy design.

product_title: High Sierra Chaser Wheeled Backpack
review_body: I bought this for my 6th grader.  Now she doesn't have any problems bringing her books back and forth from school.  It rolls easily and smoothly, doesn't tip over.  It is large enough for all her books, lunch and gym clothes.  It even was $20 cheaper here than at the store (JC Penny).

product_title: Coleman 70 Quart Xtreme  5 Cooler
review_body:
I've had this cooler for a couple of months and hadn't used it. I thought I'd give it a test to see how it performs.

I had ice in plastic lock & lock containers in the freezer, it had to come out to make room for food. I had two one gallon containers, and several smaller 12 oz containers full of ice. plus a couple of zip lock bags 12\\" full of ice cubes, that had been in there a couple of months.

It filled just over half of the cooler, I didn't put any food or drink in there. I shut the lid and opened it five days later, which was today.

The ice appeared to be melted, but it was icy cold water. I emptied the containers out into my watering can to water the plants (waste not want not!)

I was surprised there was a two inch lump of ice in one of the gallon containers and a small piece in one of the small containers, and a few small pieces of ice in one of the zip lock bags.

I now know that this cooler works really well, after five days all that ice water, there was over four gallons! If I'd had frozen food in there, it would have been ice cold too.

I usually turn the electric off before going on vacation. Now I'll be able to turn the fridge off a few days before my trip, so I can clean it out, and I'll put the food in the cooler, so I won't be doing it at the last minute.

I'm very happy with my cooler, it is a nice size. I bought the one without the wheels, because reviewers said the ones with the wheels are a bit smaller, this is just right.

product_title: WAYLLSHINE(TM) 500LM CREE LED Flashlight Torch 3 switch Mode: Strong Brightness / Normal Brightness / Flashing for Riding, Camping, Hiking, Hunting & Indoor Activities
review_body: This is no cheap plastic flashlight!  Solid and heavyweight, I was pleasantly surprised at the quality.  Will probably order a more powerful version from the same company.

product_title: Outsunny Two-Person Double Wide Sleeping Bag
review_body: The inside is not slippery like the outside. So when you roll over the material sticks to your clothes. Only one side and bottom zipper. So you can only get in one one side and only 1 person can have their side folded down. But it does roll up really well very compact.

product_title: Global Vision Eyewear Escort Safety Glasses
review_body:
These Global Vision Escort sunglasses got many good reviews, so I ordered a couple (yellow and gray). They fit over my glasses nicely and are surprisingly comfortable.

The yellow makes the world look much brighter! But your eyes adjust and it seems to help lessen the glare of sunshine. And curiously, they do not make my brain change colors (when I take them off, the world is not purple!). They will make a beautiful blue sky look washed out greenish blue, like an old faded color photo.

The gray makes me feel like I cannot see quite as sharp, which really bothers me. I suppose that's \\"normal\\" but I found it unacceptable.

While these GV's have a small peripheral window, I found it was not suitable for riding a bike or hiking where I need to see everything around me. I picked up a pair of wrap-around amber Solar Shields at WalMart for $20, and the peripheral vision on those is excellent. Plus they look almost cool.

If you want these GV sunglasses for indoor safety use, they would be quite acceptable, I think (and I think many of the reviews have that use in mind).

product_title: Lightspeed Outdoors Quick Canopy Instant Pop Up Shade Tent
review_headline: Pretty fantastic... when there's no wind.
review_body:

I was a little disappointed to discover that I needed to use the guide lines and stakes if there is any breeze at all. The unit just isn't solid without them. I havn't used this at the beach yet, and I'm wondering if the sand \\"pouches\\" will really be enough when there's a breeze.

I like the open design, as you stay cool and comfortable. There's just enough to give you some privacy and keep out the glaring sun, but open enough to get some air and not feel like your in a zip lock bag. The built in \\"floor\\" is convenient, and seems like it is reasonably durable. Just be careful with anything sharp. We throw down blankets on top anyway, so really its more or a moisture and yuck barrier for us.

Very compact. I leave ours in the trunk and it's always ready for a spontaneous getaway.

Setup and takedown really is very easy. One person can do it in minutes. Great design. Overall I'm very happy with it and I will recommend to friends and purchase another when this one is ready for retirement.

product_title: Gramicci Men's 30-Inch Inseam Original G Pant
review_headline: These aren't the Gramiccis you once knew and loved...
review_body:
I originally wore Gramicci pants in the 1990s, and they were great. They were a little more dressy than sweatpants, but a little more athletic than jeans, and they lasted for years and years. They were the perfect weekend pants for cool outdoor activities. (At that time they were made in the U.S.A.--California, I think.)

Flash forward 20 years, and you'll find that the \\"Gramicci\\" pants are now simply made-in-China junk. They tend to fit a little strange--the front now sort of \\"poofs out\\" as if they were pleated. The material is much more stiff--now they really feel like plain ol' denim jeans, more or less. And the quality has gone to (heck)--I now get about a year out of a pair of Gramiccis.

Foolishly, I recently bought 3-4 pairs, and some are already wearing out. The hem on one pair has shredded, and the velcro rear pocket closure has torn out in another pair after a couple of months.

If these were twenty-dollar pants from, say, Target, okay fine. However, why would anyone pay forty or fifty or sixty dollars for these ill-fitting, poor-quality pants now days?

If Gramicci would bring back that original quality--even if the pants were a hundred bucks--I'd buy them in a heartbeat. But now, well, \\"Gramiccis\\" don't really exist.

product_title: Shimano PD-M540 SPD Pedals
review_headline: The PD-M540 is okay but the PD-T400 is safer and better
review_body: The PD-M540 is an okay pedal that many people really like but it has some serious safety flaws.    First of all here are my objectives.  1) A peddle that I can get into and out off quickly that will help me get more power on the upstrokes. 2) A peddle that is safe where it will quickly release to prevent a fall during an unforeseen stop.    The PD-M540 peddle doesn't meet these objectives.  It takes time to learn how to enter and exit this peddle.  I fell many times during the learning phase which is typical.  But I also fell after many rides when I was more experienced.    It also comes stock with the less forgiving single release SM-SH51 cleat.  Thus, if you really want this peddle, you should immediately discard the stock cleat and buy the multiple release SM-SH56.  That judgment is backed up by Amazon reviews on the two cleats and the peddle instructions.  Spending extra money to replace a cleat only suitable for advanced riders really bothered me.    I called Shimano and asked tech support for recommendations.  They told me that based on my objectives, to buy their brand new Shimano Click'R PD-T400.  It comes stock with the multiple release SM-SH56 cleat and it is uses lower spring tension to enable easier entry and exit.    I checked expert reviews on the PD-T400.  Experts claimed that not only was entry and exit easier than the PD-M540 but the peddle did not unintentionally release even during extreme upstrokes.  Yet it did release predictably when you wanted it to using barely a thought and to prevent a fall.    Here is the product description for the new PD-T400  [[ASIN:B00A2I0PPK Shimano Click'R Trekking SPD Bicycle Pedal - PD-T400]]:    Click'R design has a much lighter step-in and release action. Step in action is 60% less than SPD. Release action is 50% less than SPD. Built-in reflectors for visibility make them perfect for urban/commuting use. Adjustable spring tension can be set to your preference. Outer cage offers additional support and security when not clipped in. Chromoly spindle. 507g.    Here are the drawbacks of the new PD-T400 peddle.  1) It doesn't look as cool as the PD-M540 because of the plastic platform surrounding the metal peddle.[[ASIN:B002LBNEVI Shimano PD-M540 SPD Pedal]]  3) So far, I am one of the few bike riders to write a review. 4) Some riders may feel that they are too advanced for this peddle (I disagree. It is a superior peddle for any skill level from Beginner to Advanced.  If you wish to do trick riding switch to the single release cleat.)    The PD-400 peddle has exceeded my expectations.  When I ride on the sidewalk to avoid heavy traffic, I must avoid light poles, hydrants, etc, that can cause serious injury if I hit them.  This is the only peddle with a toe clip or binding that will release quickly enough to allow use on congested sidewalks.  It is also great on the open road.  I have never had an unintentional release during riding.  But entry and release are far easier when they are intentional.  That's because you cannot release this peddle by lifting up at the toe.  Even releasing by lifting the heal is non-trivial.  But release to the side or upward angle is fast and easy.    1/13/2013 Update on PD-M540    I still love the T400 peddles and have never regretted my switch from the M540.  The negative comments on my review on the M540 are from bike riders who didn't test the T400.    Let me broaden this discussion with a similar argument that may have been going on about about 50 years ago.    From Wikipedia: The first downhill ski binding was invented in 1929.  It was nicknamed \\"Bear Trap\\" which refers to the deathlike grip of the binding that lead to many injuries.  They were replaced by heel-and-toe \\"safety bindings\\" in the mid-1960s, but remain in use in cross-country skiing to this day.    Clipless bicycle bindings are not safety release bindings but for the first few months of use, they may feel like \\"Bear Trap\\" bindings.  They do not release in an emergency to prevent anaccident. Why not?  Because no manufacturers has developed that capability.  Current bindings require a conscious decision by the rider to release the binding.    If you make a panic stop, can you release one of your bindings in under a second to prevent a fall and possible serious injury.  If your answer is yes, the PD-M540 is a fine choice.  If your answer is no, it takes 1 or more seconds and I might fall, you should switch to the T400.  It is as close as you will be able to get to a safety release peddle binding.    What are the downsides to the T400 over the M540?  There aren't any.  Although some sources call it a beginner's first clipless binding, what does that mean?  It means that a bike rider new to clipless bindings can learn how to use this binding faster than with other bindings.  It doesn't mean the the bike rider will outgrow this binding and want to move on to more \\"advanced\\" bindings.  The M540 binding will not hold any better than the T400 but the T400 will allow faster entry and exits and provide a faster learning curve.    Read the following review from a British Cycling Magazine: [...]    Them go to your local bike shop and take a test ride with both the M540 and the T400.  If they don't have a testing program they probably will allow you to buy and return each within 30 days.  I did this at REI and it didn't take me long to convince myself that the T400 was a major improvement.  One of the advantages of REI is they have an unlimited return policy.  If you think you might outgrow the T400 in a year or two, you can return it.  To me that is worth the few extra dollars they charge.  But I don't think that most bike riders will \\"outgrow\\" this binding.    It is an  underrated superior binding.

product_title: Quik Chair Heavy Duty Folding Camp Chair - Grey
review_body:
The chairs arrived and I immediately noticed how bulky they were. I was expecting them to be big but not that big. I didn't play too much attention to the bags as I don't use them and discarded them. First impressions were good. I'm 6 foot and 190lbs and found the chair roomy and comfortable. They looked strong but I don't think 500lb strong. They have thicker tubing than a regular chair but it has the same plastic connectors.

My problem with this chair is with the armrests. In the past all the chairs I've had have the back of the armrest attached to the rear leg with a metal ring sewn into the fabric. The ring slides down and locks in a position resulting in a horizontal armrest.
This chairs armrest is designed to be more flexible. There is no locking metal ring, there is just a rubber ring sewn into the fabric. You can slide the rubber ring all the way down to level of the seat if you like. Some may like their arms at that angle but I don't. The problem is when the weather heats up or you are near a campfire etc the rings expand. They then slowly slide down to the level of the seat, sometimes resulting in a slow spillage of an adult beverage. I don't like the fact that the rings are rubber in the first place; rubber breaks down easily over time especially out in the sunlight.

product_title: SteriPEN Adventurer Opti UV Water Purifier
review_headline: Do you want to die from water? No.
review_body: I initially debated this purchase, as it's not inexpensive, but it's a total win. My debate centered around version, price, weight and fragility. I trust the science behind it.  I'm notoriously sloppy with water purification, drinking tap water in Mexico, ice cubes in Myanmar and river water in Colombia. In preparation for an expedition to cross Madagascar, where water sources would be unknown, I decided it was time to consider my health. My last big gear-buying spree was in 2005 - it's pretty amazing the advancements since. For any hardcore trip where you risk destroying water tablets, using up iodine on other activities or serious dehydration...get a SteriPEN.  Key moments I was particularly thankful for SteriPEN:  1) When porters topped off a group pot of water we'd boiled the night before, which we realized as we went to tank up for the day. Wait 30 minutes for purification tablets, or, re-purify starter bottles with two wands for immediate consumption? Easy.  2) When I ran out of water and found a river an entire village used to wash dishes, laundry and bathe. I ran through the purification process twice, just for fun, drinking within five minutes.  Since returning from this trip, I've undergone multiple blood tests- the only bacteria strain found was contracted pre-SteriPEN. Having this, I am much more likely to drink wisely on future trips.  The weight was nominal and, while you certainly want to use the included case, it's sturdy enough. I had it in the outer pocket of my pack much of the trip. I used it in multiple 40oz Kleen Kanteen metal containers, which the math was a little tricky on, but I just over-purified when in doubt. Also "works" on Camelbak sacks. I do agree with various other reviews noting it's a little awkward to ensure the wand is submerged while you're stirring (otherwise it shuts off), but it's not a big deal. The signal light is easy enough to keep an eye on, but it would be nice if placed at the end of the handle. A lot of folkswarn of contamination around the lip or mouthpiece of your container. Slosh it around while you're purifying or rinse your mouthpiece off with a purified bottle. At the end of the day, my bottles were being dragged through rivers and muck so there are really only so many preventative measures one can take.  Like any tool a life might depend upon, I tested it before departing to at least verify the light remained on through a full cycle, etc. I would encourage anyone to do the same.  October 2016: I still recommend SteriPEN as your primary method of water purification. Also great for extended trips or living abroad.

product_title: Rollerblade Spitfire TW Boys Inline Skates Size 11J-1
review_body:
I recently replaced the skates my children had with these Rollerblade Spitfire TW skates. My son is 10 and my daughter is 6, and they have been skating for the last two years. They previously had gender-specific versions of the Bladerunner Phaser skates, which are a good, cheap, entry level skate. While the Bladerunner brand is owned by Rollerblade, the Spitfires are far superior to the Phasers. The Spitfires are very well made, and I am told by my children, to be very comfortable. The construction is sturdy, and the boot bindings are very easy, especially the \\"speed lacing\\". The fact that these skates are resizable is huge; a child's feet can grow quickly, and these Spitfire skates will grow with them for 4 sizes. I purchased the \\"Boy\\" version of these skates for both of my children, and nobody has complained yet. The styling of these skates is very nice, and gender neutral, and frankly my daughter already has enough color in her wardrobe. Better still, once my daughter out grows her skates she can step up to her brother's skates, and I bet she won't even notice!

The sizes for these skates are as follows:
* Y11-1
* 2-5
* 5-8

Buy with confidence. Recommended.

product_title: Guerrilla Packs Airporter Travel Backpack Duffel Hybrid with Detachable Daypack (50-Liter + 10-Liter)
review_headline: Excellent travel bag not really for small people
review_body:
I bought this bag for my most recent trip to Spain, where we flew in to Madrid and planned on going to various other cities via rail. The large bag holds so much, yet still fits carry on specifications. The daypack attached to it is perfect - exactly what you need if you leave the main bag at a hostel/hotel and go exploring. Also on a plane, you can put the main bag up in the storage and keep your snacks/important documents/book/etc in the small bag on your lap. The straps that clip it to the main bag look a little bit flimsy, but they held as I was running for trains several times.

The only problem I would have with this bag is that although its straps are adjustable, I don't think they can fit every body type. I am pretty small (5' 0\\") and even though I had the straps at their tightest, the bag was still hung and wasn't fully supported on me. After a couple hours of carrying it, I could definitely feel it, so if I planned to take it hiking or something, this might not cut it for someone my size. The other thing is that it is pretty wide for a backpack. Definitely wider than my body, a bit difficult to walk around things with. Finally, the little laptop sleeve that comes with it only fits 13in laptops, so is pretty much a throwaway if you have something bigger.

Overall, the Airporter is an excellent bag and I love it!

product_title: Tire Boots 3 Pack
review_headline: Does the job well - could be easier to apply
review_body:
I had not heard of these previously either - wish I had about them a month ago when I got a hole in my old tire - could have kept it going!!! Had a flat the other day and couldn't get the object completely out so used this to cover and prevent a new flat. The big complaint about these is that they aren't sticky - at all - when you first apply them. I cleaned the tire with alcohol before using, but after pausing to get the tube ready, found the boot had fallen off of the tire. Tried again with the tube in place - the adhesive barely stuck enough to resist sliding a little bit until I got the tire in place. In fairness - if I'd stuck it on with the tube in place and immediately sealed it up, it probably would have held long enough to get the tube in position the first time. But that's awkward and risks contamination of the tire with dirt - not to mention making it hard to place the boot perfectly over the hole.

BUT. I opened this tire back up the next day to replace the large \\"boot\\" with a small tire patch. The adhesive was now stuck VERY strongly, and like someone else said the adhesive stayed on the tire. So it's probably activated and/or improved by road heat.

Definitely a large patch - I'd recommend keeping at least one whole one in case you get a big blowout - but you could probably cut this up into some smaller patches *before* you go out on the ride. It's probably too tough to try to cut cleanly on the road.

product_title: Stearns Men's V2 Life Jacket
review_headline: Good quality life vest budt design could be better
review_body:
Since the Amazon site does not list the chest size applicable to the relevant size, I have taken the liberty of indicating it based on what is listed on the \\"sizing\\" tab of the product-specific web page of the manufacturer's web site at stearnsflotation: small (32\\" -34\\"), medium (36\\" -38\\"), large (40\\" -42\\"), XL (44\\" -46\\"), 2XL (48\\"-50\\"). Note that the manufacturer's web site also has a web page on general sizing for all their products, which you should ignore, and instead use the sizing as indicated on the manufacturer's product specific (Stearn's V2) page. The sizing ran true for me and it is great that there are so many different sizes which mean that one can pick a prefect size to conform to one's body.

I like the fact that the manufacturer on its web site description has openly and honestly stated that the V2 is made in China. However, rest assured the quality is very good and I am sure that it will be durable. I also like the fact that it has just one color (black) and is therefore unobtrusive unlike other life jackets, so it is not embarrassing for one learning to swim to wear it in a swimming pool. I wish the product was sleeker than the overall look, which appears like a bullet-proof jacket that you see on TV. One person even said he thought it was some kind of brace for the back and was surprised when I said it is actually a life jacket.

It is not bulky like a typical life jacket but it is not sleek either, presumably because it needs to provide a specified level of buoyancy to meet U.S. Coast guard type III PFD certification. The two buckles and zipper are of exceptional good quality. The zipper is on the side rather than in the center front, and there is a convenient small opening so one can place it on a hook to dry. The life jacket is comfortable and the space for your arms is large allowing for freedom of movement.

I purchased the item to aid in learning to swim and to serve as a substitute for the flotation \\"noddle\\". The Stearn's V2 suited that purpose. It also provides slight warmth which is great especially since the water temperature of most pools is on the cooler/chillier side.

I would have given this product a 5 star rating but am deducting a star because there are small portions of the jacket that seems to have a vinyl-like material and a slight shine (such as the portion that goes over your front shoulders (you can see it in the picture). The chlorine in the swimming pool water also tends to settle on the vinyl causing minor temporary dis-colorization requiring an extra step of the user having to rise the vinyl. Had this vinyl-like looking portion been substituted with neoprene (which is used elsewhere in the product), this well- made product would have been easily met the \\"top notch\\" standard. Perhaps the manufacturer/designer will take my suggestion when they decide to make the next version (V3?) of the product (i.e, get rid of the vinyl!!!). I also wish the life jacket was 1 or 2 inches longer so that the entire back (including the lower back (just above the pelvis) can be covered/supported. If you read the reviews for the Stearn's women's V2 version of the product you can also see a comment calling for the jacket to be a bit longer.

Bottom-line advice for designer: Consumers are looking for the sleekest and lightest type III certified life jacket. Why don't you make an \\"all (i.e., 100%) neoprene\\" jacket with the slimmest inner padding to achieve this purpose?

Overall, I rate the life jacket 4 stars. After just 4 days of swimming in a pool for the first time, I can now swim in the deep end of the pool knowing that there is a zero chance I will sink.

product_title: Pearl Izumi Pro Softshell Lobster Glove
review_body:
last winter was the first full winter i rode through. and, to be clear, what i mean by \\"ride\\" is that i did daily 30-40 mile loops on a road bike at about 20mph or faster (because this matters; wind chill becomes a significant factor when it's this cold and you're really moving). i usually rode until at least the freezing point. after that, i would only go out if i was sure there wouldn't be left over water on the road that would freeze and take me down. so what i'm talking about are regular daily temperatures ranging from 25-40F, coupled with wind and me moving at 20mph or faster; which is really about an actual temperature well into the teens or single digits.

for the first couple months, i SUFFERED with my hands. nothing i tried worked. i bought some super nice, very expensive softshell gloves and those only got me to about 40F. awesome dexterity-wise, but not warm enough. i tried some assos baselayer gloves under those and that only bought me another couple degrees. the guy at the LBS talked me into the Gore \\"fusion\\" gloves. which have two chambers (one for warmth, one for wind-blocking) and are a neat idea, but really didn't get me to any lower digits. i even tried those goofy-looking and very awkward to use \\"bar mitts\\" and had about the same results as with everything else: every day i was coming home with freezing hands, running them under hot water for several minutes in agony, etc.

then i finally decided i'd try a new solution: a warm layer and a wind-blocking layer. i mean, this works for my torso, why wouldn't it work for my hands? so i grabbed a pair of the wool defeet gloves for warmth (which are about $20) and a larger pair of these pearl izumi pro softshell lobster gloves to block the wind. BINGO! that did it. now i'm very very cozy out there for at least a couple of hours. i did a three hour ride in 35F with an average pace of 19+ last week and didn't even THINK about my hands. which is exactly what you want.this system got me through the rest of last winter and it's looking great so far this year.

there are some downsides to these gloves, of course. they're bulky. but they're lobster gloves and they're THICK. what do you expect? you get used to it (shifting with SRAM is easier than shimano with these, fwiw). it's better than not feeling your hands and THEN not being able to shift (been there before; not fun). and yes, the bottom velcro enclosure is a little tricky to do up. but it's secure and once they're on, you don't have to think about it. no big deal.

a couple notes on my \\"system\\" described here: 1) i was careful to have a decent air layer between the two glove sizes, so that some air movement can go on. you don't want them to be tight and constrict blood flow. the defeet gloves are tight, the lobsters are roomy. 2) the nice thing about this system is that if i flat or need some extra dexterity while stopped (to eat a bar, check my phone, change a flat, adjust my bike, etc.) i just take the lobster gloves off. i still have the wool defeet gloves on to keep me warm and those are nicely form-fitting so they're almost like wearing no gloves. and my hands won't freeze like they would had i worn a single-glove system (which would undoubtedly also be very thick gloves) and taken the gloves off for dexterity.

overall, i'm quite happy with my solution and with these gloves. hopefully someone else will find this information useful and can avoid some of the painful suffering i endured.

product_title: Sweat GUTR Sweatband
review_body:
The Sweat GUTR works. I've used it on several +70 km road rides and on long mtn bike adventures with varried terrain. My only issue is that it can slide downwards and be a little uncomfortable on the ears. With glasses, the GUTR, and helmet on- it gets a little busy and things can shift a bit. A quick stop and adjustment does the trick. Glasses and eyes were free of sweat every time. The plastic feel was OK, but not really great. It could be a distraction for some people with sensitive skin.

I also have the HALO sweatband, which is more comfortable and stays put. I used it on the 94,6km Birkebeiner mtn bike race in Lillehammer, Norway- because during a race you don't want to stop and mess with gear. Glasses and eyes were also free of sweat. Yes, the band does saturate, but not so much that the performance was diminished in any way.
My first choice would be the HALO, and the GUTR would be in my backpack as a backup.

product_title: GORE BIKE WEAR Men's Alp-X 2.0 Gore-Tex Active Shell Jacket
review_body:
1 YEAR UPDATE: Still in PERFECT condition! Like new, zipper are still good, elastic is good, everything is still water tight. It has only gotten dirty, and you can wash it just like regular clothing so that's not an issue. Couldn't be happier.

Original Review:

SHORT STORY: Great if you are a cyclist. 1 pocket in back and breast pocket. 100% waterPROOF. Very durable. If you just want a fully waterproof jacket, save your money and get something better that has more practical features like front pockets.

The bad first. Yes, this jacket is expensive. Do not buy this if you are not a very frequent cyclist. It does NOT have front pockets. Only a breast pocket and a back pocket. Both are very good, however, and waterproof. They are mesh inside. The jacket is absolutely 100% waterproof, and suprisingly warm, as I have worn it (while biking) in 50 degree weather by itself and that makes up for it. However, I would have preferred front pockets, and a little more insulation I suppose. Maybe a real lining.

Now for why I gave it 5 starts. It is extremely thin, high tech fabric, and is comfortable to wear on your bare skin. The hood is detachable, (It comes with the fully gore-tex red one, NOT THE GREY one in the picture up there) but I use it and slip it under my helmet for extra warmth, as the whole jacket is windproof and waterproof, including the hood. The jacket has a longer back already, but if the ground is wet, this jacket has an additional few inches to cover your rear end from road spray, and believe, me, this works very, very well. I got mine in red for $279.99 here on amazon, in size XL. It fits be perfectly. I am 6 foot 4, wide but fit build, and arms as long as Micheal Phelps'. The jacket's arms and torso length miraculously still fully, and comfortably cover my huge body.

This jacket is truly designed for cyclists and can be a great year round jacket to last you many years. It is designed specifically for the cycling position. I ride very aggressively (position very forward) and have had no problems. It has elastic on the waist, velcro on the wrists for sealing yourself off or locking down gloves, and a restraint system for tightening the hood as well, but it could be better. The hood is small enough to get under a helmet without much extra fabric. It will not go over a helmet. The shoulders are reinforced for hitting trees while mountain biking, as this is actually made for mountain biking in my opinion. The reinforcements are also slightly rubberized, making backpacks less likely to slip around on the otherwise slippery surface of the jacket. I have a chrome citizen and it doesn't slide at all, or interfere with the breast pocket. The back pocket is roomy, and easy to access while riding unless you have a backpack which comes far down your back. My Chrome Citizen doesn't interfere but that is a messenger bag which sits high on my back, so think about that.

It should also be noted that the entire jacket folds, and zips into the back pocket.

Also, for the record, this is the new model for 2013. I bike commute in NYC every day and have seen no one with this jacket except a professional bike messenger, but even he had the old model. Once again, this is 100% waterproof, windproof, and extremely durable. Great visibility and it looks good too. The red that I purchased is slightly on the flashy side for me, but its nothing to unusual and I would rather be seen on the road than in danger of not being seen, and that's the trade-off I make.

product_title: Gregory Baltoro 65 Technical Pack
review_body: As a lite traveler and inexperienced trekker, I think the large size (65L) just gives an excuse to fill up with extra stuff I wouldn't otherwise be carrying in a 55 or 60 pack instead.  With this minimalist mindset, I at first thought the Baltoro had too many pockets and straps and whatnot for my liking.  However, after 2 months of travel through Nepal including a week-long trek, all the pockets were used, and I wouldn't have preferred any other backpack.  The straps are as sturdy as I've seen, the rotating hip and shoulder straps are worth their weight.  I was torn between the Baltoro 65 and the Savant 58.  I preferred the Savant carrying up to 30 lbs., and the Baltoro over 30 lbs.  My dealbraker was the unquestionably stronger straps and lumbar support of the Baltoro, and I couldn't be happier with this decision.

product_title: Katadyn Quickfill Hydration Pack Adaptor
review_body:
The picture provided by Amazon is not correct--it does not show all of the adapter pieces that come with this kit (3 pieces). It also does not show the best location to install the adapter.

This adapter is significantly more compact and better designed than the Camelbak adapter.

If you want to be able to attach your water filter to your water bladder without having to take it out of your backpack or even take your backpack off, this is the adapter to use. It is easy to install. Once installed, there's no quicker or more convenient way to refill your water bladder from your water filter. Also, unlike the (Amazon provided) picture shows, this adapter can be installed anywhere along your hydration pack hose--at either end or anywhere in between.

product_title: Go-Ped GTR46i Trail Ripper Interceptor Gas Powered Full Suspension Off Road Scooter
review_headline: Goped GTR 46i Trail Ripper Intercepter is the finest!
review_body: This is the second stand up scooter I own.  The first lasted ten years and is still going strong!  I wanted the Trail Ripper because of the full suspension and high performance motor.  This machine is very strong and well built but also very light in weight.  The performance is outstanding! After a break in period of two tanks I now enjoy the use of full throttle and let me tell you to hang on when this thing takes off! Acceleration is strong and if you pull up at full throttle you will lift the front wheel easily. This scooter, like all gas powered scooters, will require periodic adjustments to keep things properly tuned.  I have needed to make some carb and brake adustments and one chain adjustment since the break in. The brakes are really good and the tires provide amazing grip. I just can't wait for spring so I can ride again! If I had to make any complaints, I would say that the kickstand could use a redesign as it is very weak and will fold past its down position and let your $1000 plus scooter fall right on the motor. I will be making a warranty claim with Goped about the kickstand.  Overall I think this scooter is amazing and would make any gearhead happy.  Keep in mind that you will need some mechanical skills to keep things set. If you avoid the maintenance and adjustments, you will do damage so I am not sure this is good for kids. I know this scooter costs more than most, but I have never had this much fun for the price.  I recommend to anyone looking for a thrill ride you can fit in your trunk!

product_title: GSI Outdoors Flask
review_body: Ok, so we can send a rover to Mars but we can't build a flask that doesn't leak? I purchased this with the intent of using it as a small water bottle, something with a small footprint that I could carry around in my messenger bag. The size works well, but unfortunately, the flask leaks. It was on its side in my bag and the lining of the bag showed a wet area beneath it, indicating leakage. Anyways, to the manufacturer's credit, the flask is not advertised as being leakproof, so maybe I'm asking too much. Maybe it's only meant to be carried upright, but that defeats my intended purpose of throwing it into my bag. I'll try the Nalgene flask next to see if it is leakproof.

product_title: HIAEFIRE Q5 CREE 240 Lumen LED Bike Bicycle flashlight Torch +1 x Bicycle Holder +3 AAA batteries + dual charger
review_headline: Overpriced compare to Planet Bike Beamer 3 LED
review_body:
I buy this light with the [[ASIN:B000HU11ZG Planet Bike Beamer 3 LED Bicycle Light with Quick Cam Bracket Mount]].
both produce about the same lightning, this one is marginally more powerful.
The Beamer 3 is more folding type when the Blaze 2w is more focus.
But for more than twice the price ($50 vs $20) you do not get twice the punch.
I found the flashing mode of the Blaze 2W better than the Beamer 3, more powerful.
The Beamer 3 get a 100h of runtime vs only 5h or 12h for the Blaze 2W.

Both light are good for safety lightning, but when the path is really dark they do not produce enough light.

I move now to the [[ASIN:B0054N48WY MagicShine MJ-872 1600 lumen LED Cycling Bike Light 2011 version with improved MJ-828 LCD battery pack]] at $130. It's 2.5 more expensive, but you get 10 times more light.
The difference is really like \\"day and night\\" compare to the 2 Planet Bike.
The only side bike I found for the moment is the 2h of runtime on max output (but 50% output appear more than enough). You basically need to recharge the battery after every trip.

My conclusion is the Beamer 3 is perfect (power/price) for a safety light (especially with 200h of runtime).
If you really need more light, skip the Blaze 2W and move directly to the MagicShine MJ-872.

product_title: Coghlan's Sierra Saw
review_body: I carry Coglan's Sierra Saw with me on my weekly recreational horseback trail rides.  It's lightweight, compact, and comfortable to handle.  Even though it's considered a light-duty tool, I used it one winter to cut through two 6-inch tree trunks that were blocking the trail.  I took about 15 minutes, but the saw did the job.  For something so inexpensive, it's a remarkable value.  The only caution I would offer is that it cuts on the pull stroke and must be used with care--don't force the blade, but take your time.  This is not the only good, small folding saw around, but it's a winner.

product_title: Bell iPulse LED Bike Torch
review_body: Works as described by the seller and the reviewers. It has bright light. The only reason for not giving 5 stars is that the mount was kind of small for my bike (Trek 7.3) and I had to push it to the side of the handlebar to fit it. But now it's fine. I liked it closer to the middle of handlebar.

product_title: UCO Candlelier Candle Lantern Deluxe Kit, Black Bag, Blue Lantern
review_body: So,I've had one of these candle lanterns for years and they are simply amazing. I LOVE mine. In the process of looking for a case for it, I found these here cased and ready to go. Decided they'd make super christmas presents so I purchased a few for family and friends. The problem is that they are soooo snug in their case that it is a REAL struggle to get the lanterns out of the case (and back in for that matter). The cases just need  like a quarter of an inch more room or perhaps a tiny hole in the bottom to relieve the suction issue that is created by the snug fit.  I'm worried folks won't want to go to the hassle of getting them in and out of the case to use them. It's problematic.  I could see a looser fit with a draw string to make it snug once inside of the case or something. Basically, it's just a poor design. Slightly bummed about it.

product_title: ALPS Mountaineering Green/Clay Crescent Lake +20 Degree Mummy Sleeping Bag
review_body: My 13 year old used this for a weeklong sleepover in the woods as part of a survival trip for his school.  It was perfect for those late spring nights in the mountains. It was warm and very comfortable. He was one happy 13 year old.

product_title: Shimano Unisex PD-M520 MTB SPD Pedal
review_headline: for mountain bikes, but im using them on road bike
review_body: they are not the lightest nor the quietest, but they work. i like being able to clip into either side. having no issue with heat build-up on bottom side of foot due to small clip. when i step up to a better road bike, at that point i may invest in lighter single-side clips

product_title: Serfas USB 3 Ultrabight Rechargeable Headlight (Black)
review_body: It's great for the city when you want to be seen.  It's not the greatest for seeing when it's pitch black out, like in the suburbs (which I've done).  You can get by at around 15 miles/hr safely (in pitch black) but anymore and you'll want a brighter light (for the city, it's more than enough).  The really nice thing about this light that connect be overstated though is the quick release and size.  It's so easy to take it with you when you've locked your bike up in the city and you don't need to install some mount to your bike first.  Sometimes I go on camping trips with my bike and I'll take the headlight off and use it as a finger flashlight.  It also comes in handy when you have to change a flat at dusk or you're looking for where your inner tube has a leak.  I would definitely recommend this light, price and convenience are its major attributes.

product_title: Ventura Standard Carrier Rack
review_body: I bought it to carry stuff instead of packing junk in a back pack, in the future I plan on buying saddle bags for it for when I go on extended rides. It fits two of my bikes so if I had to I could switch it over if needed.

product_title: Dimension Road 26.0 40cm Double Groove Black
review_body: This bar seemed well made, and few 26.0 bars are available these days.  However I purchased it to shorten the reach on my bike, but the drop and reach on the bars I received was nearly identical tho what I was replacing.  I had chosen this bar over another because customer reviews indicated that they were \\"not as described\\", or they did not give specifications.  In the end, I spent more on shipping them the bars were worth.

product_title: Nutcase Dots Bike Helmet
review_body: This helmet works very well. Though reviews of bike helmets didn't list this one as the best, it does a good job protecting my head. I like the dots design. The helmet is a bit heavier than my Bell Helmet but that's okay. I like this helmet and will continue to wear it.

product_title: Yens® Fantasybag Urban sport sling pack, SB-6826
review_body: This bag is well made, the zippers appear to be strong enough for my meeds. Love the many accessable pockets. My water bottle fell out twice, which surprised me - guess I need to have it higher up.

product_title: Camping Lantern With Compass
review_body: not as big as I thought but it works fine, lighting was good, handy to hold, great for table top

product_title: ExOfficio Women's Give-N-Go Full Cut Brief
review_body: I took this on a trip and got along great with this product. Fit nicely, comfortable and is easy to pack.

product_title: UCO Stormproof Matches, Waterproof and Windproof with 15 Second Burn Time - 50 Matches
review_body: I haven't used them yet, but they look like they would do the job...  I have these matches as part of my survival kit along with a few Bic lighters, flint fire starter, and a magnifying glass...  Better safe then sorry

product_title: Serfas E-Gel Hybrid Bicycle Saddle With Cut Out
review_body: Very comfortable and the springs in back add extra shock absorption.  I'll probably get one for my MTB as my old Serfas gel sadle on it got partially eaten by my cat.

review_headline: My sons Birthday, and he wasn't able to ride his new scooter
review_body: I purchased this product for my son for his birthday, I charged it the day before his birthday and he tested it, It would go up the block,But he had to walk it back to the house. So I charged it again over night, he wanted to try it again before he went to school because he was so excited. It still went up the block and again he had to walk it back to the house. The look on that kids' face had me upset at this point... It's been in the box since it arrived before the weekend, and Monday I assembled it, Tuesday which is his Birthday, I have to take it to a local shop. Because it says do not return to store..

product_title: Sunlite 4-Bolt Unicycle Saddle
review_body: I really like this seat because it is really comfortable. I had to buy a new seat post, but it was still cheaper than some of the other seats. It has gel so it is very comfortable. It is a bit heavy, but sturdily built. It is also thinner in the middle, so the insides of your legs wound hurt.

product_title: Coghlan's Bear Bell with Magnetic Silencer
review_body: Makes just enough noise to avoid spooking anything that may be around the corner while I'm hiking.  Not too loud to become annoying.

product_title: Cygolite Expilion 170 USB Rechargeable Headlight
review_headline: Bright enough to see where you're going, not just so people can see you
review_body: I currently live in a village in Africa, and sometimes have to bike after dark down very bad roads where there are of course no street lights. This light lights up the night! It's brighter than most flashlights I've owned. Not only are others able to see me coming, I can easily see pedestrians, rocks, ruts, potholes, and other hazards. It takes a long time to charge (especially through a USB port; I have better luck charging through a wall/USB adapter), but once it is it will last for hours. Just to see, I left it on overnight, and although by morning it was too dim to be useful as a headlight it would still be visible by others so they could see you.

product_title: Little Hotties 8-Hour Hand Warmers
review_body: I have been buying \\"Little Hotties\\" for years now with a lot of appreciation and reciprocal joy! Putting a smile on the face of your co-worker, friend, mailperson, service person working outside, or anyone who is a skier, traveller, or just chilly is a wonderful feeling. product_title: Camelbak Fairfax Hydration Pack

We are very satisfied with this table. We used it on four car camping trips this summer. It's light weight, and folds up flat, making it easy to store.
