product_title: Icebreaker Women's Bodyfit150 Ultralite Leggings
review_headline: Some info on Icebreaker's wool weights, ranges, and sizing
review_body:
Because some of Amazon's listing descriptions for Icebreaker items have very few details about the products, making it difficult for the customer to make an informed purchasing decision if he/she is unfamiliar with this brand of clothing, below I'll type some information and personal impressions about Icebreaker clothing.

Note that my review is quite long and usually only the first half of it is shown on this page. If this happens on your screen and you wish to read the second half, all you have to do is press the \\"read more\\" button at the bottom of the review and Amazon will show you the rest of it. :-)

----------------------
OVERALL IMPRESSION

Icebreaker's marino wool items are generally made well, last a long time, are easy to care for, feel fantastic on the skin, are \\"natural\\", don't get smelly easily like polarfleece does, let the skin breathe, etc.

Many of my Icebreaker items have been worn and washed several hundred times and are still holding up much better than would be expected.

I am a BIG fan of this company's products. For my overall experience of them from around 2000-2010, I would give them a solid \\"5 stars\\"!

However, I regret to say that my opinion of the items I have bought from Icebreaker in 2012 is not as high. In the last 2 weeks (late 2012), I have bought 7 items from them and I decided to return all of them because they aren't as well-cut as the very \\"same\\" items that I bought in the 2000s (which I still have and wear, so I can make like-for-like comparisons easily).

Based solely on my 2012 experience of Icebreaker products, I would give them 3 stars, \\"it's ok\\". For me, this is not good enough to command prices of $50 - $100+ for quite simple items, even if the basic wool material itself is outstanding and long-lasting.

For my star-rating on this review, I will average the \\"5\\" I give Icebreaker historically and the \\"3\\" that I would give Icebreaker in2012, and give them a \\"4\\".

---------------------
MY EXPERIENCE WITH ICEBREAKER

I bought my first Icebreaker clothing about 13 years ago when I needed some long underwear for skiing.

Up until about 6 years ago, I had been buying Icebreaker items very sparingly, due to the eye-watering prices at London UK sporting goods shops . Then, I discovered that Sierratradingpost sells various Icebreaker styles (usually discontinued items from years past) on their site for a discount. Fortunately, for a couple of years after I discovered this, they had a large selection of women's Icebreaker stuff, so I bought quite a few things for great prices. (These days, Sierra's Icebreaker selection for women appears to be smaller, and the prices comparatively higher, than before. I expect that there are more discounters they have to compete with now, to get that kind of stock.)

In addition to bricks-and-mortar sports shops and Sierratradingpost, I have also bought Icebreaker items from several sporting goods online retailers, Amazon, and the Icebreaker website.

I still have almost every Icebreaker item I've bought. Even the discounted items have been somewhat pricey, but the quality and longevity were worth the initial investment.

In the last two weeks, I have tried to replace a few of my key Icebreaker items but found the fit and cut of the current versions of the same items to be sub-par. I will keep using my old items for another year, and hope that next year's fit and cut will be better-suited to my body shape.

----------------------
CAVEAT

What I have written below is based on my current knowledge about their products, but it is possible that I have misunderstood some aspects of the brand.

If you wish to better understand their product offerings, I would absolutely recommend that you have a look at the Icebreaker official site to view their entire range and gain more clarity about what items are for what purposes, what the wool weights are about, what the quality levels of the different clothing collections are, etc.

(Unfortunately, their website, while snazzy, does not fully explain these things, leaving it up to the customer to piece some of the puzzle together.)

----------------------
ICEBREAKER WOOL WEIGHTS:

Icebreaker's marino wool items generally come in four weights of fabric: 150, 200, 260, or 320. This is \\"grams per square meter\\".

150 is quite thin.
It provides light warmth.
The material is generally see-through. (I wouldn't wear items of this weight out and about in public without anything over them, but some reviewers have said that they do.)
It's good for a first base layer, for strenuous exercise, or for sleeping in.
Their items of this weight, especially in the ranges intended for athletic use, tend to be really form-fitting in one's typical size.
All Icebreaker material seems VERY resilient and long-lasting to me, but because the 150 wool weight is pretty thin, it is the likeliest to be torn, develop holes, get \\"runs\\" (like pantyhose). I don't think this happens too much with it, but I've seen some reviewers mention it (most often talking about how they accidentally poked holes in it with long fingernails), and three of my 150-weight leggings have developed runs in them after several years of heavy use.

200 is slightly thicker, but still on the thin side.
It's pretty warm.
The lighter colors are definitely see-through, such as grey and cream. My older black and brown items made out of 200 weight wool don't seem to be see-through, but some of the newer dark-colored ones might be.
It's good for a base layer or mid-weight layer, for exercise, and sleeping in.
Especially in the ranges intended for athletic situations, their items of this weight tend to be form-fitting in one's typical size.

260 is on the thicker side.
It's definitely warm, a cozy weight.
None of my 260 items are see-through. I can wear tops made out of this weight on their own (without anything over them) and not worry that my underwear or too many lumps&bumps will show through.
It's good for a mid-layer or top-layer, and sleeping in (if you get cold at night, like I do).
Items of this weight tend to fit looser than items of the same size in the 150/200 weights do. This may have something to do with how much naturally-stretchier the thicker fabric is, but it also seems that they cut these 260-weight items bigger because this weight is often worn as a top-layer or middle-layer, instead of as a base-layer.
I like this weight the best. I think that the company says that this is their most popular weight across the board.

320 is thickest, of course.
It is quite warm, very toasty and sturdy.
This weight is generally a top-layer, so items made out of this material are relatively loosely-cut.

--------------------------
ICEBREAKER LINES / RANGES / \\"COLLECTIONS\\" OF CLOTHING:

Icebreaker makes different ranges - some intended for wearing as normal underwear (like panties and sports bras and tank tops), some intended for wearing as thermal/long underwear, some intended for wearing as everyday clothing, and some intended for wearing as athletic wear.

Even though at first glance most of their items appear VERY similar to each other, there are different feelings to the fabrics (even in fabrics of the same wool weight), different quality levels, different cuts, and different design details amongst these different lines, so it is good to check their website about the particular Icebreaker item you are thinking of buying to make sure that it is intended for the activity you want it for.

Two of the popular ranges at the lower end of the Icebreaker price scale are:

Bodyfit
The Bodyfit range seems to be for athletic situations, but also casual-wear and sleeping-in. The knit of this range's wool is usually flatter and less stretchy than the knit of the ranges that are for underwear or purely casual wear. Items in this range are usually cut to fit relatively snugly.

Everyday
This range is made of a looser, thicker, stretchier knit than the Bodyfit, and is more for general sleeping-in and casual long-underwear needs, not so much for athletic situations. (However, I'm sure that they would be okay in many athletic situations, and I have worn them skiing and hiking.) Everyday items tend to be made of a stretchier knit and cut to fit more loosely than the Bodyfit items. I wear a size below my ordinary size in this range.

Other ranges
Their other ranges appear to include: Black Sheep Collection, RealFleece Collection, Pure Plus Collection, Journeys Travel Collection, Premium Underwear Collection, GT Technical Sports Collection, GT Bike Collection, Technical Base Layers Collection, and Technical Mid Layers Collection. Please see the Icebreaker site for more information on their ranges.

Frankly, I feel that they've made this aspect of their brand over-complicated and too confusing for the average customer, and I have not been able to locate any overview of the various collections on their site or on their product packaging materials.

-----------------------
ICEBREAKER COLORS:

Icebreaker tends to make most items in black, as their basic universal color.

Many items are offered in about 2 to 8 other colors, as well. There is often some version of blue, red, grey, and green - sometimes a pink, sometimes a brown or purple, etc. Often the colors are skewed towards the cool end of the spectrum (which I notice because my coloring is on the warm end of the spectrum and cool tones look awful on me).

The different weights of wool and/or different ranges (e.g., Bodyfit, Everyday, Journeys Travel Collection, etc.) will tend to have their own mini-set of color options. (For example, the current grey color in the 200 Bodyfit is a medium-grey and is called \\"blizzard\\" and the current grey color in the 260 Bodyfit is a dark-grey and called \\"metro\\", and they don't offer those particular colors in other weights of wool or other ranges, as far as I know.)

They change their colors every year or so (I think), and some colors tend to sell out mid-way through a season and are not restocked, so if you see an item in a color that you love, or there is a matching set (of long underwear or something) and you want both pieces in the same color, you probably should get it at the time, because it's not guaranteed that it will be available in the future.

---------------------
EXTRA DESIGN FLOURISHES:

A couple of their ranges, mainly the more athletic lines, feature \\"pops\\" of contrasting color in a certain part of the garment, such as a stripe running down the sleeves or down the sides, or a triangle of bright material at the ankle. Most internet retailers' photographs of the garments do show these features because the areas of differing colors are pretty obvious, but it pays to read the item descriptions (and check out the manufacturer's site for confirmation) if this kind of thing is not what you are looking for.

In a couple of their clothing ranges, mainly the underwear, 150-weight, and casual-wear lines, some of the tops and bottoms have printed patterns (like floral motifs or abstract swirls - sometimes in contrasting colors) on the sleeves or in the hip-region. This *can* escape your notice when the only images of the item you have available to you are the tiny product photographs that most internet retailers provide, so do double-check the customer reviews of the item, and maybe the Icebreaker site's own full description of the item, if you want to know for sure if the item comes with a printed pattern on a section of it.

---------------------
ICEBREAKER SIZING:

Sizing and fit are so variable from person to person and from brand to brand, but in case it may help, I'll talk about my experiences with Icebreaker clothing.

For reference, generally I am usually a women's size 4 or 6 in US sizing, a women's size 8 or 10 in UK sizing, and a small when it comes to small/medium/large sizing. This goes for both tops and bottoms.

---
Sizing of Tops

Almost all of my Icebreaker tops from the last 13 years -- crew tops, long-underwear tops, turtlenecks, and zip-up jackets -- are women's size small.

The only tops I have in size extra-small are from the Skin range (which they phased out in 2006, but the sizing and type of material used for the Skin range appear to be very similar to those of the current range called Everyday).

Generally, I know that an Icebreaker small top is probably going to fit me.

The main issue that I've had with their tops is sleeve length (too long). This is not uncommon for me, because I do have arms that are on the petite side: most suit jackets I buy have to be shortened a little in the sleeves, and I often have to turn up sweaters one turn at the cuff. And one feature of some Icebreaker tops is a thumb loop which necessitates that the sleeves are meant to be about three inches longer than the wrist - I understand this, and just roll those tops up a turn or two. However, I've read quite a few reviewers' comments that mention that Icebreaker sleeves tend to be long, and I do think that their sleeves are longer than normal. [\\"Normal\\" being subjective, of course! ...the only women I've met from New Zealand actually did happen to be tall, lithe, and willowy, so maybe that's normal there. :-) ] Last week, I bought a 2012-made Icebreaker \\"Oasis\\" top in a size small, and while it was too tight in the chest area (which is normally NOT a problem for me with Icebreaker), the sleeveswere a crazy four or five inches past my wrist, even though they didn't have thumb holes and therefore were meant to end at the wrist. I had to return it.

---
Sizing of Leggings:

I have run into inconsistency in Icebreaker legging sizes. I have some in extra-small, some in small, and some in medium. (And in one 2012 collection, the extra-smalls are a little too big for me but there isn't a smaller size to go to.)

I have not found Icebreaker's official sizing chart (available on their site) to be terribly accurate for leggings.

For the leggings, it seems to me that one must experiment in each Icebreaker clothing range and wool weight to discover the best size and fit for oneself.

I will spell out below the ones that I have tried. Because the sizing of the \\"same\\" leggings sometimes has varied across the years, I will mention what year I got them.

1. BODYFIT range

1a. Bodyfit 150 leggings

2006 or 2007 Bodyfit 150 leggings
Size medium. The label says \\"slim fit\\" (possibly back then they had different \\"fits\\" within the Bodyfit range, but they don't seem to now).
Fit me snugly, but well.
Waistband comes up to the belly button, feels secure.

2008 Bodyfit 150 leggings
Size small.
Are a bit too small for me this winter - they fit me when I'm about 5-to-8 pounds less than I am at the moment.
Waistband hits 1 inch below the belly button, feels okay.

2012 Bodyfit 150 leggings
I decided not to buy new 150-weight leggings in 2012 because after a few years of heavy use, my old Bodyfit 150 leggings developed some un-mendable \\"runs\\"/\\"ladders\\". I still wear them and love them, but they are slowly self-destructing. It is comparatively easy to snag them on a rough surface or to poke a fingernail through them when pulling them on or off.

Actually, I've just looked on the Icebreaker site (December 2012) and they don't list ANYBodyfit 150 leggings. The only 150 weight leggings they list are the \\"Sprite\\" leggings from the Premium Underwear Collection. Also, I think that the \\"Nature\\" leggings (which are a discontinued style) were of 150 weight, and I have seen these still on sale on a few websites.

1b. Bodyfit 200 leggings

Current suggested retail price of around eighty (discounted price of around sixty).

2008 Bodyfit 200 leggings
Size medium.
Fit me, and there is extra room in them - I probably could go up 5 to 8 pounds and they would still fit. When I purchased those mediums, I tried on the small size and found it to be way too small, especially along the tight and narrow waistband that these leggings were made with at the time. (I think it was a reaction to the consumer response to that waistband that they made the newer waistbands really wide and soft.)
Waistband comes up to the belly button, feels secure.

2012 Bodyfit 200 leggings
At first, based on the Icebreaker official size chart, I ordered a medium in these. They were too big, so I exchanged them for a size small.
The small fit relatively well - snug, but acceptably so.
Waistband came up to 2 or even 3 inches below the belly button. This is a more \\"modern\\" position for a waistband, of course, compared to coming up to the true waist, but I prefer \\"athletic\\" base layers to cover my entire body - neck to ankle, to enable the base layer shirts to be securely tucked inside the base layer pants, and to feel really secure when I'm moving around -- but this waistband was so low on me, and so wide and stretchy that it felt like it was about to slide down to my hips at any moment because the elastic wasn't very tight.
Not only from the practical side was this low waistband a problem, but MAN, the whole cut of the upper part of these leggings seemed to be designed to make my tummy area look as flabby and unattractive as possible! I tried my old leggings on when I took these off -- just to check that it wasn't bad lighting or post-Thanksgiving excess weight that was to blame for how these made me look, but my older Icebreaker Bodyfit 200 leggings looked a lot better on me than these leggings did.
I had to return them. I have decided to wait until next year's production, to see if they alter the cut of the waist area.

1c. Bodyfit 260 leggings

Current suggested retail price of around ninety (discounted price around seventy-five).

2012 Bodyfit 260 leggings
Size small.
Fit relatively well - snug, but acceptably so.
Waistband came up to 2 inches below the belly button. They had the same issues as the 2012 Bodyfit 200 leggings did - waistband too low, too loose, too wide, and quite unattractive in the belly region!
I also had to return these. I hope next year's will be cut higher on the waist.

2. EVERYDAY range

2a. Skin 200 leggings (discontinued 2006) - the Skin range was probably similar to Everyday.

2005 Skin 200 leggings
Size extra-small, yet are the largest I own - I could gain 15 pounds and they would still feel okay. But they fit me nicely when I'm at any weight - 10 pounds less or more than my present size - they are simply the coziest and softest that I own.
Waistband comes to about 1 inch higher than belly button, feels secure.

2b. Everyday 200 leggings

Current suggested retail price of around sixty (discounted price of around forty-five).

2012 Everyday 200 leggings
Two weeks ago, I bought them in size small which were too big, so I exchanged them for an extra-small. Even the extra-smalls had extra material in places on the legs, which is unusual because my legs are not toothpicks (this kind of legging is not supposed to be baggy, so the cut of these must have been off).
Worse, the upper part of the extra-small leggings was cut strangely - the waistband was in a deep V, so that the middle was 3 inches below my belly-button (which is way too low for me), but the sides rose up 3 inches higher than that (it wasn't a curve, it was a visible V). Yet the waistband elastic wasn't tight enough, so the tall sides wanted to sag down and bunch up around my hips -- strange. (And that was not the way the smalls I tried on the week before had fit my waist area! In fact, I think the smalls of last week fit me better generally than the extra-smalls of this week.) I don't have the energy to go through the rigamarole of ordering a different pair of extra-smalls, but maybe I just got a bad apple.
I had to return the extra-smalls.
I was very disappointed because they were the 7th Icebreaker product I've tried in the last 2 weeks. This Icebreaker shopping quest has taken up a fair bit of my time lately, but I have nothing new to show for it. I've given up trying to get anything now and will wait a year and see how their 2013 production fits me.

3. OTHER ranges

Their other legging types are more expensive than the Everyday and Bodyfit, and seem to be geared towards high-tech athletic use, or constructed to be worn on their own as pants/trousers. Some have Lycra in them. Check out Icebreaker's site for more info.

--------------------------------
OTHER TIPS

The other main retailers of this kind of product sometimes offer free shipping on their Amazon listings of an item but don't offer free shipping on the exact same item when sold through their own site (even when the price of the item itself is the same on both sites), so it can save you money if you pay attention to that.

The best selection BY FAR is available from the manufacturer's site, but the prices there are generally higher. However, they have discounts from time to time, such as their \\"Black Friday\\" sale when they offer 30% all items that are black in color.

Amazon sometimes calls the Icebreaker Bodyfit range\\"BF\\" and sometimes \\"Bodyfit\\", so if you are searching here for Icebreaker's Bodyfit range, do a separate search under each of the two search terms to get the most accurate results.

In terms of merino wool socks, I prefer Smartwool socks over Icebreaker's. Sierratradingpost is one retailer which often carries a large selection of them at good prices. Those socks last a really long time. I wear them almost year-round because the lightweight ones breathe really well even when it's warm out.
The Smartwool women's small size is the only sock I can find that truly fits my feet (which aren't even that small, all things considered!) without bunching up inside my shoes.
If you have a smaller foot (size 7 or less) and are female, note that the Smartwool unisex socks in the small size are bigger than the smalls made just for women, even though that company's size guide says that they both are meant to fit the same range of women's shoe sizes.

product_title: AlpineAire Foods Dehydrated Chopped Onions (Gluten Free)
review_headline: Gluten and wheat allergies?  Buyer beware!
review_body:
While AlpineAire Foods state in their titles that they are gluten free, the back of the packaging needs to be seen. The packaging for AlpineAire Foods Dehydrated Chopped Onions (Gluten Free) actually states on the back that food is processed at facility that processes peanuts, tree nuts, wheat and gluten, among other high-risk items for those with dangerous allergies.

I have no problem with the food itself, but I don't have an allergic reaction to wheat or gluten. If you feed this to a child with an allergy to nuts, wheat or gluten, the consequences could be deadly. Likewise, if ingested by an adult with such an allergy, it would be less than pleasant to put it mildly...especially if this food is ingested while hiking or camping.

If you're just looking for a healthy alternative to snack food or something to throw into the backpack before trekking, this is a great option. However, please keep in mind where it's processed if this is desired for someone with an allergy to nuts, wheat or gluten. Thanks!

product_title: Dahon Speed Uno Folding Bike, Shadow
review_headline: Easy Commuting in and around a Small Town
review_body:
My main reason for purchasing a folding bicycle was for convenience, as well as wanting a way to protect the investment of purchasing a quality bicycle. As bicycles seem to be a \\"hot\\" item for thefts in the small town where I work, I wanted to purchase a bicycle that I could easily store within my office. Folded, this bicycle has a very small footprint, and fits perfectly under my desk on the side, leaving still plenty of room for my feet. My typical commute is to the local residential treatment center as well as to the local hospital, which are less than a mile from my office. Initially, my only hesitation in purchasing this specific model was that it only has one speed. However, that concern quickly dissipated after realizing the comfort and ease this bicycle is to ride. I've added a rear rack, so that I can easily transport my briefcase and iPad.

It was challenging to find a rear rack at my local bicycle store, until one of the mechanics at the bike shop made the comment, I think a rack for an incumbent bicycle would fit.... And it did fit, perfectly!

It's already clear I will be taking this bicycle along with me to out of town conferences for work, as well as vacations. It's just fun to ride, and gets a lot of second looks. I've had so many people stop me around town asking what brand of bicycle this is, and they can sense the pride when I say, \\"It's a Dahon!\\"

product_title: InStep Quick N EZ Double Bicycle Trailer
review_headline: You get less than you pay for
review_body:
We own both this trailer and the Burley Bee (the equivalent no-frills trailer by Burley). What a huge disparity in quality between these two! This is a good trailer if you need something quick and cheap for a few short rides, but it won't last for more than a couple of seasons. The component are cheap and flimsy. This is NOT a durable product!

The Burley costs twice as much (or more) so here are the major differences and you can decide for yourself:

Burley vs InStep

FABRIC: Water and abrasion resistant nylon cordura VS. soaking wet and torn to hell nylon
FABRIC ATTACHMENTS: Rubber rings and plastic clips VS snaps that rust and pop out of the fabric within a couple of weeks
BIKE ATTACHMENTS: Plain and simple, compatible with almost any bike VS oddly complicated, compatible with only certain bikes
FRAME: Lightweight aluminum VS heavy steel
WEIGHT: light (~20lbs) VS heavy (~33-38lbs) (See above)
BRAKES: None VS Yes
WHEELS: Traditional aluminum rim with spokes VS plastic wheels, smaller diameter
SAFETY: Child rides higher in seat, suspended above frame VS child rides so low in frame (plus smaller wheels) that his/her arse gets soaked whenever you ride through a puddle, also potential to get smacked in kiester if you ride over a curb/large pothole one wheel at a time
STORAGE: Pain to fold VS easy to fold
VERSATILITY: bike trailer only VS also makes a lousy stroller (front wheel will not cooperate--very difficult to maneuver or even wheel in a straight line)

product_title: Texsport La Paz Fabric Single Hammock
review_headline: Quality product, rope asymmetry over time, too large for a collapsible stand
review_body:
I bought this a few months ago to deal with back pain and joint stiffness caused by lying flat on a regular mattress. I've probably slept in it thirty times indoors.

A few thoughts:

* This style of hammock is dramatically preferable to anything with spreader bars. It's more comfortable, it molds around your body, and it's much more difficult to fall out of or flip.

* This hammock is designed for people under 6' tall. I'm a little above that and found it slightly short for general use. Despite that, it's physically quite long. I have a large Coleman collapsible metal stand of the sort you might take car-camping. The ropes on this hammock were about two feet too long. It's really designed to be used outdoors (temporarily) or in an enclosed porch.

* Hammock sleeping isn't flat. There's a curve in the middle and the two ends are elevated, even if the hammock is suspended tightly. I couldn't get used to having my head at an upward angle, so I'd scoot down until my back was in the hump, which meant my legs were elevated and hanging off the sides or on the ropes. Not ideal. You'll like this better if you're used to sleeping in a recliner or the like.

* Over time, the cotton suspension ropes on one side stretched more than the other, so one side of the hammock is elevated at rest and it tilts about five degrees when I'm in it. The tilt is not objectionable and it hasn't caused me to fall out yet, but there isn't any way to adjust this. Weight capacity is otherwise high; at 175 lbs, I never felt at risk of damaging it.

* The relatively thin hammock material allows a lot of air circulation. If you're prone to cold, you'll want more blankets or a bottom sheet. If you overheat, you'll like it.

As far as my sleeping issues were concerned, I had mixed success. The first few nights, I'd wake up after a few hours and transfer to my regular bed. After a week or two, I could sleep through the night, but still woke up stiff because you can't shift around much in a hammock. I wasn't getting the upper back pain from before, though, so that was an improvement. I've since returned to my regular bed and have had decent rest after modifying the pillows I used.

This hammock is an excellent value. I wouldn't expect it to last outdoors, though. It should taken in when not in use, or at least coated with a spray waterproofer. You can buy metal snap-clips and eye-screws at any hardware store that'll make it very easy to mount and dismount.

I understand that there needs to be a good seal so you don't suck in air in the process. But I think slightly sturdier straw would make this a superior product.

I went and bought some 1 gallon water jugs that, as we all know, taste like plastic. Not to worry. Here comes the Aquamira to the rescue. I can taste the difference before and after. Once, I know the filter is working, I begin to drink out of the tap water. It tasted pretty good too.

For small volume and short duration, this filter is the preferred choice. If you are going to be out of water for a long while (> 1 month), get the lifestraw instead because it has a lot higher capacity (1000liter as opposed to 25 liter for the aquamira).

Happy drinking! (water of course)

product_title: Cane Creek 3G Thudbuster Short Travel Seatpost, Black
review_body:
I use this post in conjunction with a [[ASIN:B001F6Y52C ISM Adamo Typhoon Saddle]] on a 2007 Fuji Absolute SX (aluminum frame with carbon fork/stays) flat-bar bike for both commuting and occasional use on both paved and limestone trails. At 190 pounds I'm at the high limit for the medium (blue) elastomer, and once correctly set up for me this combination provides the most comfortable seating of anything I've used in 45 years of adult riding, at a weight penalty of only 190g over the stock seat post.

However, if you are considering the ST, or the ST over the LT (which I've not ridden), you need to understand that (at least in my experience) the STs effect on ride is quite subtle, enough so that you may not be immediately aware of a significant difference: the ST does NOT mimic or even approach the shock absorbing characteristics of a rear suspension, and at first I was not sure the ST was making a difference at all.

Instead, I gradually become aware of what I was *not* experiencing - or at least experiencing to a far lesser extent - the constant small, quick \\"blip\\" sorts of feedback, for example from riding over a long series of patched cracks in asphalt or ruts in a compacted limestone surface.

The resulting ride is not \\"plush\\" (as described by some users of the LT posts in reviews here), and NOT similar to a full-suspension mountain bike; instead it's just \\"smoother\\". Not so much a \\"shock absorbing\\" effect over things like .50 to 1.0 inch displacements in slabs, but a \\"damping\\" effect on the .125-..375 displacements typical of city streets and well maintained limestone (as opposed to \\"mountain type\\") trails.

*Over a distance*, I found this to be a substantial improvement: after a few miles on city streets I realize that my hands and wrists are feeling the \\"normal\\" effects of this sort of \\"vibration\\", but my \\"butt\\" is not. (IMO the next Thudbuster product should be a suspension stem, assuming this is practical and useful).

And, other than weight, I found this improvement to be pretty much \\"cost free\\": except as noted above unlike a front or full suspension bike I was *not* aware of the \\"energy eating\\" aspects of the \\"suspension\\" system - I noticed no difference at all between the \\"feel\\", \\"handling\\" or \\"performance\\" of the bike with or without the TB.

So I'd say that the value of the ride improvement with the ST TB goes up along with the distance traveled: a mile commute, not much difference. Five miles, a noticeable difference. Twenty miles, I *definitely* notice and appreciate the difference. Riding a century or touring? Never done either with this post, but if I did, based on my experience I would consider the ST (at least) TB a \\"must\\".

For me, that level of improvement is worth the cash and weight.

product_title: Garelick/Eez-In Universal Boat Seat Swivel - Standard - 6" x 6"
review_body: These removable swivels are very sturdy and hold up my Wise Big Man seats very well, so overall I am satisfied, but I had a lot of difficulties installing them, and I have reservations as to how long they will last. First of all, they are supposed to fit most standard seat mounts, but they did not. The mounting holes were about a quarter of an inch too far apart to fit the mounting holes in the seats, so I had to mount them to a piece of plywood and mount the plywood to the seats. Secondly, the plastic tracks that mount to the boat and receive the swivels are separate pieces, so it is up to the installer to judge how far apart they should be so that the swivel slides in easily without binding or being too loose. I tried to err on the side of avoiding binding and ended up feeling they were a bit too loose, but they seem ok. Thirdly, the metal part of the swivel that slides into the plastic track is not completely smooth, so I am concerned that over time it will wear down the plastic tracks. After one installation I found some plastic shavings lying around. Lastly, the metal release lever, which is also not completely smooth, sticks out enough that when you turn the seat you can scrape your leg on it. As I said, as very sturdy product with some design flaws, but after all is said and done, I am satisfied.

product_title: Ogio Newt II S Laptop/Tablet Backpack
review_body:
I bought this backpack on amazon for college. I did a lot of research before my purchase, I didn't want my backpack falling apart on me again!

This backpack comes with several compartments, one for your laptop, sunglasses, plane tickets (I use this one for wires), tablet sleeve, and a nice compartment at the top for other smaller electronics such as a phone or camera. I use all of these compartments and they are wonderful. They are each lined with some fuzzy material to prevent scratching. I don't even need a laptop sleeve anymore! (Perfect for the electronic maniac like me.)

This backpack has some serious stitching, I pack everything in here and not one seem out of place. It has foam lined straps and foam lining the back area (where the backpack rests against your back). This can be a real life saver when your campus is over a mile long.

Overall it is top of the line quality. There is one fairly large compartment for storing textbooks and what not, and it's all I really need. It may be a bit small for some, this is no camping backpack. I'm able to fit two full sized text books, and four notebooks in there. This compartment also has the tablet sleeve in it.

I'm not sure if I'm missing anything... The material is of great quality, it doesn't show stains much (it rains mud where I live), I haven't attempted washing it or anything yet. Still looks brand new and I've had it for about four months.

All in all I highly recommend this product. Order in advance m the shipping can take a while, but it is well worth it.

Edit 6/10/2013

I've had this backpack for just about a year now. I've taken it with me everywhere. I've even been using it for light travel. Nothing has torn, nothing has ripped. Everything still looks fairly new. (And this is after I brutally drug it through a dusty canyon)

During finals, I maxed the crap out of this backpack with equipment, and still had room to spare. Camcorder, camera, wacom tablet, nexus 7, 15 inch laptop, 3DS, safely stored safey goggles in the sunglasses compartment, game controller, loads of pens, and arts supplies in the front pocket, 2 one inch thick textbooks, and up to 4 notebooks (bounded). I could have possibly fit even more. The weight was tremendous, yet I didn't experience excruciating back pain as the weight is distributed well. The straps can help move some of the weight to your center. The strain of all this weight for my previous backpacks would have left them in shreds by the end of the week (I mainly used Swiss backpacks through high school).

The backpack is easy to surface wash, and the color I purchased (cereal) shows little dirt. I accidentally got melted crayon on it at one point, but that all came out without an issue with just a warm wet cloth, same goes with pen markings.e

The only issue is the soft material that lines electronic pockets has began to wear down. That's really it. If you have electronics that have exposed screens, such as a tablet, then I would eventually get a case for it, just to be extra careful not to scratch the screen. (I still don't use a case for my laptop, as the built in sleeve still works wonderfully)

Now let me just say that after I while, I tend to get very rough with my backpacks. It's typical for a backpack to last me just over a semester before I end up using a cheaper, and even worse quality bag to get me through the year. I throw them on the floor, sit on it, grind it up on cement, load it up with as much crap as possible, sling it around everywhere, jog with it, brutally shove sharp notebooks in, you name it. However, despite all the abuse, this backpack still looks brand spanking new, and I am not purchasing a new bag for the next academic semester. This is the first time I've ever had a bag that will probably last me 2, even 3 or more years. The material they use is of very durable quality, and the stitching is just beyond impeccable.

I'll be uploading pictures of my bag so check them out.d impeccable.

product_title: Mr. Tuffy Bicycle Tire Liner.
review_body:
I am giving this product 5 stars because it does indeed protect against punctures caused by the vast majority of road or trail objects that you will encounter.
A word of caution: Don't think that your tires are bulletproof because you have liners installed. I was distracted by a car that was driving way too close to me, and I didn't see what must have been a big piece of a broken bottle. I heard glass breaking, and was immediately riding on the rim. The glass had cut my Bontrager Hardcase tire bead to bead, and cut clean through the Mr Tuffy liner and the tube.
When I removed the tube and the Mr. Tuffy liner, it was evident that the liner had prevented several small pieces of glass that had previously penetrated the tire from puncturing the tube.
To summarize: Don't sweat the little things, but keep an eye open for the big ones.

product_title: SRAM cassette PG 730 7-speed
review_body:
I wore out the 7-speed cassette on my mountain bike and installed this one as a replacement. I found out I needed a new cassette when I installed a new chain and it slipped on uphills. The cassette gear cluster and the chain tend to wear together. The cluster usually outlasts the chain for a while but this was my third chain and the gear teeth were just too far gone. Installed the new cassette easily. (You'll need a tool like this [[[ASIN:B0028N57UU IceToolz Cassette Lockring Tool with PIN]]] to remove the cluster.) The slipping ceased and the chain is much quieter now. Shifting is smooth. Guess the old cassette was more worn than I realized.

Build quality is okay. This is an inexpensive replacement suitable for entry level or casual use bikes.

This SRAM is a 12-32 tooth cluster. It replaced a Shimano 14-28 tooth. The larger 32-tooth gear gives me a noticeably lower ratio for hill climbing, a bit of a granny gear, which is a nice bonus. I did have to adjust the front derailleur for chain clearance due to the larger gear.

Note this is a cassette cluster, not a freewheel cluster. A freewheel contains the ratcheting mechanism and threads onto the hub body. A cassette cluster slides onto a splined ratcheting cassette and is held in place by a lock ring.

SRAM and Shimano drive train components are interchangeable, except for shifters + derailleurs, which should not mix brands because they use different ratios of cable travel.

product_title: Rokk Palisade Two Room Family Dome Tent Sleeps Up To 8 (Blue/Grey)
review_body: I LOVE this tent! The space is fantastic! There were only 2 of us in the tent which was perfect as far as I was concerned. We had 2 queen size mattresses leaving an isle so I had a table in there as well, plus space down at either sides of the door for each of our stuff /gear. The \\"shoe\\" doors are excellent to have which I also used for my 8# dog to go in and out of too! No leaking from the torrential rainstorm we had the first night either! On that note, make sure ALL the guylines are staked down, and the \\"bay windows \\" are zipped up completely! The built-in \\"mudd flap\\" served as a swimming pool with the rainstorm but no water got into the tent thanks to the raised lip going in and out of the tent. So because of the torrential rainstorm the first night, (9-8-12),was 42 degrees out - it was cold! Due to the spaciousness of the tent make sure you have the appropriate sleeping bag/blankets & long underwear and flannels! Oh yes, the corner pockets were very handy for stuff especially a flashlight. The pocket made it so easy so as not to have to fumble in the middle of the night when having to use the facilities.  Also, I had no issues with the stakes(they are plastic ) but I know in general that there can be issues with anything plastic . So I also purchased titanium stakes just in case. Now,  the directions for putting up the tent they did not mention \\"sleeves\\" that the poles go through. There are sleeves - look for them! That all being said I wouldn't trade my tent for anything!

review_body: Mounted on side rail of rifle makes it very ergonomical. Well constructed durrable product. Soft button is a nice feature allowing to switch from and to \\"high beam\\" / \\"low beam\\" / strobe light.

review_body: Hubs doesn't think I notice the fact that he wears this shirt ALL. THE. TIME.....but I do. Oh yes, I notice. At least he looks hot in it. :-) Seriously though, this is such a cool shirt. review_body: I thought this was gonna be a really good board the first day i got it, made for a nice cruiser. product_title: d.light S10 Solar LED Lantern
review_body: My main reason for purchase was to reduce electric energy, and help the environment. It charges well, even during cloudy days.  It has a red light that will let you know when is charged.  Charge lasts. I didn't really find any difference between the 2 settings. The higher the location you place it, the better lighting coverage.  If you place it on top of a table, well, it will just light a small area. But, place it high, above your height, and it does a very good job.  You can look things around.  Don't expect the same brightness or intensity as an incandescent bulb, but it does well for the tiny bulb and being solar. The handle will let you hang it at different places.  I used it mainly as a night lamp for my bedroom, and when I want to look something around, I hang it high.  I personally don't recommend it for reading, that's why the sell the reading lamp alternative.  It rained while charging it outside, and it was fine.  I unscrew the bottom (it unscrews to the right), let it dry and screw it back (to the left). I don't know what they refer to a mini tool box on the description, maybe is just the bottom part that can be unscrew, but not sure. Nice lamp for power outages, camping, etc. Fluorescent pushbutton switch.  Overall, good investment.  Will update in a near future.

product_title: Aluminum Cycle Pro Mechanic Bicycle Repair Stand Rack Bike
review_body:
.
I had been looking at a stand from the Blue company for about a year; the one with a 10 in the model number. Never could quite convince myself to pull the trigger on that one knowing that some of the profit would go to the PRC.

When I happened to check to see what was the hottest seller on stands on Amazon I found this one was at #1.

With good reason, this is not only a serious piece of gear; it passes the \\"Prissy Test\\" Ha-Ha!

Seriously now, I have to say that I rely on my lovely wife to tell me frankly when something we're considering purchasing - or in this case - have purchased - looks \\"nice\\". She says this is a handsome piece of gear and I totally agree.

Taking the price of a tray into consideration, this stand is just a little more than half the cost of that Blue 10 that's now made in Commie China...

So if you've been waiting for a good price on a great stand OK, YOU CAN JUMP NOW!

PROS:

-Head flips back to give the folded unit an extremely compact footprint
-Tool tray has a magnetic center to keep stuff you've removed handy
-Rotates a full 360 degrees AND can be canted to allow it to be used on a slope [driveway for instance]
-Made in a nation with representative government
-No assembly required
-German engineered [instructions come in two languages only; English & German]
-Great customer service [I had a technical question to ask pre-purchase via email and the U.S. rep for CyclingDeal got back to me in way less than 24 hours]

CONS:

-None that I can see; I'm a little wary of the pin lock mechanism on the rotating head; no problems so far but I just got the stand today; will update in a few months

CLOSING NOTES:

While its true that a bike store professional stand is a LOT HEAVIER and thus should be a LOT MORE DURABLE I can see myself using this stand, taking reasonable care particularly to not abuse it whenmounting a bike on it, for 10-15 years no problem.

Like most of you probably do, I have a few carry bags left from the currently popular folding chairs and a couple of those bags are from \\"Big Boy\\" models. I plan to match one of those larger bags up to the stand in order to have a good travel protection method.

Cheers!

product_title: Allen Sports Deluxe 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack
review_headline: Fits great for my 2011 Nissan Versa HB
review_body:
This product works great for the price. The box has fitting sheet, but it only goes up to 2010 model cars. I was scared if it fits my car, but fortunately it did. My car is kind of bubbly in the end, so bikes sit diagonally.
As one person's review I read after the purchase, the bars are far apart. That makes the system more sturdy, but also it makes it harder for smaller bikes to fit. My bike is not small by all means (I am 5'7\\"), but I emailed the company (five starts on quick reply) about not being able to fit it on the rack. They gave me links to youtube videos; one to show me how to put my bike without a tension bar and the other to show me how to put a tension bar if I own one.
I have been using the rack without a tension bar for a while, but because I don't have a cross bar that is parallel to the ground and I use a diagonal body part onto the rack, it started pinching my gear/brake cables. After a while I started noticing my gear shift acting badly (slipping to next gear when going over a bump, etc.). So now I know I will need to get tension bars.
Each tension bar costs about $15. I need two. That raises the price of this rack by $30. Had I known that, I could have purchased lower end racks of Thule. But then, I may have had to buy a tension bar for Thule anyway...
I am happy with the product now that I am comfortable using it, but I had to contemplate for a while.
It's your choice!

review_body: I ordered this and the fahgettaboudit lock but ended up keeping this one. I like the extra length of the kryptonite because it gives more leniency when attaching bike to rack. review_body: Hands down the best camo pattern on the market for hunting out of a tree stand in any season. Mossy Oak this. Real Tree that. They look real good.....up close. But at 20-50 yards? review_body: I wish these were a little longer. I put them on my oakley sunglasses and wish they weren't so tight around my head. I have a few inches to work with but if you plan on wearing a hat with them just forget it.

product_title: Victorinox SwissTool
review_body: I've owned several Multi-tools over the years, including a Gerber and a Leatherman Supertool.  I never really liked the Gerber due to the slide-out plier configuration, and I really liked the Leatherman tool until I lost it. I purchased with the intent of returning it if I didn't like it, but I can tell you that didn't happen.  This is a very useful tool with the best build quality I've seen in a multi-tool.  And I'm a huge fan of the fact that you don't have to open it up (like the Leatherman), to access all the tools. Easy to access individual tools, useful tool selection, great built quality, and the lifetime warranty make this tool my new favorite.

product_title: Shimano Ultegra CN-6701 Chain
review_headline: Easy to install. Change your chains often so you won't have to change other parts...
review_body:
I get Ultegra because it's worked for me for the last few years. I've got an Ultegra cassette and front gear and front derailleur set. The rear-derailleur is Dura-ace, but I find it hard to fork over the dura-ace price of a chain when my Ultegra chains have worked great for as long as I can recall.

A few years ago, i rode about 2,000 miles without checking anything. Had to spend a bunch to change everything... Now, I change my chain promptly, and I have been riding with the same rear and front gears for the last 7,000 miles or so with no noticeable wear.

Get a chain wear gauge such as the [[ASIN:B000OZFIMQ Park Tool Chain Wear Indicator CC-3.2]] and check the wear on your chain. Once the 0.75 side gets in, time to change your chain. If the 1.0 side gets in, time to change your rear cassette (pricey). If the 1.0 side gets in and is wobbly, time to change the front gear as well (even more pricey).

To install this chain, you will need a chain breaker such as a [[ASIN:B003RZPIBG Park Tool Mini Chain Brute Chain Tool - CT-5]] and put it in your under-saddle bag. If you ever have a chain break on a ride, you will be able to fix it enough to get home...

product_title: Intex Raised Downy Airbed with Built-in Electric Pump, Queen, Bed Height 22"

If it wasnt for losing the indent problem, this bed was great.  It plugged in and had a built in pump for easy filling and deflating.

product_title: Sparehand Systems Black Wall Rack
review_body: I had recently bought two kayaks and found this product to be exceptional for strogage. Easy installation and sturdy. Keeps my equipment dry and utilizes minimum space.

product_title: Shimano A530 SPD Pedals
review_body: These are the first clip-in pedals I've used and they work as advertised - I love them!  As recommended in at least one other review, I adjusted the tension to the lightest point and it is fine - easy to get in and out, and my shoes are firmly attached when riding.  I've also had a couple of opportunities to ride with running shoes using the non-clip side and have no complaints there either.  You would definitely want to have rubber-soled shoes to use on the non-clip side as the pedals do not provide much friction.

review_body:
The shipping was really fast .i am super happy with the quality of the hammock ,worth the price! Fabric feels good ,like a dry cotton . The hammock itself comes in an extra bag to travel with ,it's nice ,small and compact ,once folded up.
Holds easily me and my son and my puppy dog.but fairly narrow hammock !
Beautiful pattern and when wet it really dries up fast

product_title: Osprey FlapJill Pack
review_body: The backpack is cute and practical. It's not oversized so you don't kill your back, but it still holds everything I need! love it.

product_title: Schwinn Meridian Adult 26-Inch 3-Wheel Bike
review_headline: Workhorse But Handles Differently than A Bicycle
review_body: This Tricycle is a must for anyone having trouble hauling weight on their two wheeled bicycle.  The heavier rear can accomodate 60-80 pounds of weight (it's best to add a bike trailer if you plan to haul 100 pounds or more of weight.  Although the rear axle is heavy steel, why risk banging it up?) Just remember that a trike drives differently than a bike.  My two wheeled bicycle can weave in and out of rush-hour traffic, as well as go on uneven surfaces, hilly terrain, etc.  The Schwinn Tricycle is best on flat surfaces and can't weave in and out of heavy traffic easily (it is not designed as a racing bike because of its heavier rear).  It is a very good tricycle FOR ITS INTENDED USE.

product_title: Nutcase Pretty Pink Matte Bike Helmet
review_body:
I never wanted a helmet. I find helmets irritating, but love my brain. So...it's pink. It fits well. It's not horribly heavy, and does not look as dorky as many. If I can find a hat to cover it, all will be wonderful.

Yes, it causes helmet head. I love my brain, so I have it. :)

product_title: Sleeping BAG Adult Size 20+ Degrees Bright Grass Green Gray - Carry Bag NEW
review_body: Ordered this item one year ago.  Have use it a few times. Packs very easy.  If I am staying over for a short time at family or friends, a pillow, air mattress  and this sleeping bag does the trick.

review_body: This was a really great purchase. Comfortable breathable, lightweight and looks pretty snazzy too. Haha. I wore it on long rides short rides and raced with it, it's durable and safe. HIGHLY recommended..very pro ;)

Maybe coat the inside with the wax like these are so it doesn't come apart while you're peeing???  That would really be great. product_title: Maxi Kick Scooter - Black with T-BAR Steering
review_body: My husband and I purchased the Mini for our daughter when she was 2 1/2 years old for Christmas. She caught on really quickly to riding this scooter unlike the cheaper scooters that most kids constantly fall off of. She is turning six this month and it's time to upgrade to the Maxi, although she still rides the Mini with ease. Fortunately, we have a son on the way and we plan to keep the Mini for him. The price was not a negotiation for our daughter's safety and it has paid for itself more than twice. I can't recall an accident on the scooter and l love how easy she maneuvers around corners. The scooter also travels with us almost everywhere.

product_title: Park Tool CM-5.2 Cyclone Chain Cleaner
review_headline: fastest & easiest way to apply lots of degreaser but cheaply made
review_body: I hesitated buying this because it seemed overpriced and unnecessary. Then I found out that my local bike shop uses it so I decided to give it a try. Now that I have one I love it. It's worth the money. Yes you can apply degreaser with a rag or a paintbrush and I still do a little of that but this device completely immerses and soaks your chain in seconds. The device snaps apart, you fill up the degreaser compartment, snap it back together with the chain inside it, run your crank a bunch of times, and then empty the chamber and repeat. Most people probably don't need to do the repeat part but I'm crazy like that. After my chain is soaked from the Cyclone I then use rags and scrub brushes to further clean my chain. Once again though, that's probably not even necessary. I then soap my entire bike with a sponge, rinse, dry everything with a clean towel, and then let it all air dry for about 15 minute. Lastly, I lube my chain and apply bike polish. The only downside to this device is that it is messy. You will leak and spray degreaser so if you're doing it indoors make sure you have a tarp laid out. I do my cleaning in my yard so this isn't an issue. I wear an apron to prevent spray or splash on my clothes. Also, you will go through a lot of degreaser. I buy the cheap gallon jugs of Zep Citrus degreaser from Home Depot so this isn't an issue for me. I've only been using mine for a couple months so I can't attest to its durability. UPDATE: as of 8/16/13 my cleaner has fallen apart and I can't really use it anymore. I still love what it does but unfortunately I had to remove a couple of stars from my rating and can no longer recommend it because of how poorly it held together. I'm going to try the Finish Line cleaner next. Hopefully, that too won't be a waste of money. UPDATE 9/24/13: The Finish Line chain cleaning tool is even worse!

product_title: Rio Brands Deluxe Wonder Wheeler Wide
review_body: This beach cart was just what we needed! I had owned one before, but without the wider wheels...perfect for the beach. We carried a cooler, 5 chairs, a beach umbrella, 2 beach mats, 2 beach bags filled with towels, toys and sunscreen! Amazing! And the price was roughly 25-30 dollars less than other sites. Thank you

product_title: Park Tool Vulcanizing Patch Kit - VP-1
review_body: I had to use this the other day when my rear tire got a leak, worked like a charm and held pressure. Would have been nice to have a few more patches though.

product_title: ENO Eagles Nest Outfitters - ProFly Rain Tarp
review_headline: Great tarp, cords frayed on me though
review_body: I really like the tarp. Good design, light weight, strong, pitchable in various configurations. Used it as a sunshade for the family at the park (with some tent poles). But the cordage for they guy lines is kind of 'weak' and has started to fray on me after only pitching a couple times. I will probably look for a replacement cord for mine, otherwise a great tarp for hammock camping.

product_title: Rothco Portable Commando Cooker
review_body:
I thought the pricing for this item was pretty decent, I wanted it because it didn't take up much space and I could fit fuel cubes in it (turns out it can fix 6), and if I ran out of fuel cubes I figured I could use it like a mini wood burning stove, just put it upside down, start a fire underneath with natural materials and put a little pot or pan on top, perfect right?

Most likely only in theory.

It is flimsy, when I took it out of the box and started opening it, motion was not smooth,and even being careful I could feel that too much pressure would make it bend, the metal moved really easy, also the little metal eyelets look pretty thin and fragile, I find myself already trying to figure out what im going to do to replace them when they break (if I don't buy something sturdy or make my own similar device).

I really like the design itself, but the \\"product features\\" a rugged steel design. The box it came in said steel plating. If there is any steel in this thing at all it has to be some sort of minimal amount with as weak and malleable as this thing feels.

I bought it to shove in my bugout bag which I also camp out of , it's thin and lightweight, but far from sturdy, and I am very curious and a little concerned about how much heat it can take before it starts warping the metal, not to mention they wasted their time painting it because I took it out of the box and the CARDBOARD rubbed some of the paint off.

I suppose I will have more to say after I use it firsthand , but at the rate things are going I may test it out with a fuel cube as well as a little kindling and such before I even think of taking it out camping with me and I will definatly keep everyone updated.

I gave this item 2 stars because the design and idea I like, but the material and workmanship in holding it together I find to be lacking.

I know it's a pretty cheap item, and people are usually happy to say that for the priceits a good item, but when I read rugged steel design, I expect it to at least not bend.

As it stands before testing, If you are looking for a portable stove type device to use more than once or twice for a good price, If you happen to have one and you put it in a bugout bag, take it out and find something better.

*edit*

Ive used it twice now, the first time it seemed to work out just fine, a little residue from the single fuel cube I used, just used it a second time today, again, used a single fuel cube, and I have to say, its possible some warping occurred during the first use, but it definatly jumped out at me today after I used it again , it's thin, and susceptible to heat. I thought that I might be able to use it as a mini stove setup using small bits of wood and tinder but after using a second ever fuel cube on it id have to say there is no way I would bother.

It would be great if it was made out of iron or steel, I would gladly pay twice as much if it were (even though I think the price as it is, is overpriced for the material. It's a great idea overall, but unless they make it out of something more heat resistant and sturdier, you are paying for a gimmick that lost it's potential in production.

Which leads me to unfortunately lower my rating of this from two stars to one, because im not paying for what this \\"could\\" be.

review_body: Stylish, warm, comfortable, reasonably priced here - what's not to like.  Columbia at full price are overpriced but frequently available at good sale prices unlike Northface (NF), which are comparable/good quality but are always way overpriced. review_body: I bought this to pump my road bike tires which require 125psi. If this is your intention please save your money. I used this 6-10 times before purchasing a plug in pump. This will get you to 125 psi but it will take a while. On average it took me 10-15 minutes per tire, this is definitely not a quick pump. It is a little awkward to use, and you would probably be better off with a standing pump or an electric pump.

product_title: Arm Warmer Cover Uv Protection Cooling Sleeves Coolmax - Pair
review_body: I bought a pair of the white sleeves as a gift for my wife, who loves her early evening bicycle rides but is extremely sensitive to the sun. review_body: This is a great kids sleeping bag. Sturdy, comfy, warm and easy for kids to pack and unpack. Highly recommend this as a starter sleeping bag for sleepovers or campouts.

Ran into a problem with the standard light mount positioning the back of the light too close to your fingers.  The fingers WILL hit the back of the light under recoil.  This very solid offset mount lets you move the light up and along the axis of the barrel out of the way of your fingers and allows you a full grip on the forearm. review_body: We use two of these blankets on our bed to protect it from the cats while we are not at home. They work very well and have been a very good purchase. I just bought two more so we have two sets to switch between while one is cleaned.

The amount of space you can see in the mirror,  the balance of staying positioned vs being able to be knocked into a new position after bumping something, the small extra lateral profile it adds to your bike... this is the very best.

product_title: Kenda K850 Aggressive MTB Wire Bead Bicycle Tire, Blackskin, 26-Inch x 2.10-Inch
review_body: I was going to get stock replacement for my Trek but decided to go with these. They were a really good price is the first reason I bought it. They shipped quickly. After installation I had to go for a test drive! Took them out that same day I got them. They are great! Little noise on the hwy but tons of grip off road. I have had no trouble out of them, great brand and great tire. I would definitly recommend to a friend or fellow rider.

product_title: Nalgene Tritan Grip-N-Gulp BPA-Free Water Bottle
review_headline: Hard to drink and easy to break
review_body: I brought two of this bottles due to the overall positive feedbacks on Amazon.com. Unfortunately, one of them broke today, after merely two weeks of use, when my two years old accidently dropped it from her shopping cart seat in a store. The bottom totally cracked and water got everywhere. We have been using them without the insider small piece on because it's almost impossible to drink from them while that piece is on. product_title: Bushwhacker® Moab Black - Bicycle Rear / Front Pannier Cycling Rack Pack Bike Bag - w/ Reflective Trim - Sold as Pair
review_body:
For those not looking for enormous panniers, or those who do not want to spend 100+ dollars on totally waterproof ones, these are great panniers. I use them for everyday getting around town and avoiding sweaty back syndrome. They're made of heavy, but lightweight cordura and they don't take up much space -- I easily cram my (full) average sized backpack into one, which is about a full load for one side. If I'm not mistaken, these are made in the USA, which is another plus. I have a pair of waterproof Axiom monsoons and I like these better for every day use (plus they're less likely to get stolen).

I should also add that I have the Jandd Economy Panniers, which are about the same quality (a tiny bit nicer), and cost approximately DOUBLE.

product_title: Supernova Black E3 Rear Light w/ Direct Mount
review_headline: Worth it, but read the directions.
review_body: The Supernova products unbox like an Apple product...the metal box and packing material are first-rate. Attaching the light to the bike was a little difficult for me only because I mounted it to an incompatible reflector housing.  The predrilled holes on the light itself will flush mount to a trunk rack without incident.  The light is very bright, and the only recommendation I have is to read the full set of directions.  When you are connecting this light to the front headlight you have to stagger your connections so there is no chance of the wires and connectors making contact and this also ensures that the shrink tubing fits over the wire and wire connectors.  Bottom line: I would absolutely recommend this product to others looking for a hub dynamo lighting solution.

product_title: Sigma Wired Speed Sensor Kit w/Cable - for computer models using CR2032
review_headline: Product works well, Instructions are poor
review_body: The original wire connection to the BC 1609 computer is quite different from the universal bracket. The purely pictogram instructions leave lots to be desired. Whereas the original wire connects by sliding the wires over pins under the computer, the universal wires have slots to set the wire ends. Study pictogram 5 carefully.

product_title: DAKINE Girl's EQ Duffle Bag
review_body:
I've had this bag for two years now and it's still in great condition. It's very durable and it's comfortable to carry around.

This bag is probably a bit big to use as a gym bag but it's great to use for travel and you can use it as a carry-on bag if you're flying. It's roomy and can actually hold a lot of stuff. I'm a girl with small clothes and small shoes so I can fit all of that in the bag. I could probably fit a week's worth of clothing in there, if not more. Perfect for camping as well.

When you're storing the bag, it can easily be flattened or folded without ruining the bag. It's not too stiff but can still maintain shape when the bag is packed.

product_title: RAD Cycle Products Heavy Duty Bike Lift Hoist For Garage Storage 100lb Capacity Mountain Bicycle Hoist
review_body: I bought the 2 pack to raise our Mtn Bikes when not in use. Thankfully I read several reviews to make me aware of the limitations of this inexpensive lift. The first thing I did was to lose the supplied rope and replace it with more substantial rope. Next I bought new screws for mounting. I had a finished ceiling to deal with so a mounting board was necessary. I bought a 1X6 board and cut it to 50 inches to screw across three joist members. The instructions say use a 2x4 and I decided that it would be too narrow and the depth too bulky. The 1x6 worked perfectly and left room for mounting through the drywall. I assembled the pulley mechanism on the board since it is easier to do it that way before mounting on the ceiling. To be safe I then used 3 inch deck screws to mount the board through the drywall into the joists (two screws in each stud). Getting ready to lift the bikes, I bought 4 short bungee cords to secure the hooks to the handlebar and the seat. That worked great. I would not suggest trying to raise a bike without securing the hooks to the bike. The brake system seems to work fine, but safety requires mounting the cleat on the sidewall and tying the rope off. Fortunately I have a 12 foot ceiling in the garage so the bikes are plenty high to avoid interfering. All in all it cost a little more than the price of just the lift, but I have the result I wanted with the bikes out of the way and safely hanging.

product_title: Slumber Sack, Sleeping Sheet, White, 92" x 42" Inches - Hypoallergenic - Organically Treated Fabric That Kills Bud Bugs And Dustmits And Preventing Infestation - Independently Tested, Laboratory Certified
review_headline: gives peace of mind during an infestation
review_body:
Bought this item during an active bed bug infestation in our home. Since it is recommended that one sleeps in the same place that one did before the infestation, so as to not spread the problem, I treated the area around me and then slept in this sleep sack for several nights. Since we were very aggressive in treating this problem, we controlled it very quickly, but during our treatment stage, I did not receive one bite while I slept in this. Although I cannot attest to the effectiveness of the \\"organically treated fabric,\\" the peace of mind I got when sleeping in the slumber sack was well worth the money. I bought an extra two that I am saving for our next hotel stay (the source of our infestation).

By the way, the best way to launder these is to secure them in a pillowcase.

product_title: CatEye - HL-EL135 Headlight
review_headline: Not As Bright As I would like
review_body:
I don't love it but I like it. It lights the dark patches of the road when going home at night. It makes me feel more confident when traveling through wooded areas with little street lights. It allows me to see the road. It is water-resistant. It is cheap. It works. That's pretty much all I needed.

Now, it could be better. The light isn't quite as bright as I hoped it would be. That means that light from other sources such as streetlights and car headlights it will overpower the light. It does, however, cast a unique color light into the dark. It is more akin to white light than any other artificial lighting that I have ever seen. Which is neat. However, since that light is weak it isn't as nice as I would like it to be.

Finally, there is a setting on this light that I do not get. There is a strobe setting that you get by lightly pressing the button. Beyond calling extra attention to yourself I do not get why you would have it. I don't use it.

It is definitely a buy, however, I would not spend anymore than 20 dollars for it. Anymore than that and you are wasting your money. Be smart and only pay 20 dollars.

product_title: California, Northern
review_body: Very useful and well presented.  Easy to find exactly what you are looking for, particularly scenic attractions and various points of interest. It also has mileage charts and campgrounds and is a good resource to use in planning a trip to Northern California.

product_title: Clear2GO Water Bottle with Filter
review_body: I purchased two of these bottles recently. The bottles are made from a very soft plastic. Right from the start they leaked like a sieve. I am not talking about a trickle, this is a soak your clothing type of leak. The water pours out around the screw cap. There are no instructions to indicate how to rectify this problem, and I have tried all of the suggestions from other reviewers to rectify the problem with no luck. I cannot recommend this product.

product_title: Currie Technologies eZip Women's Low Step-Thru Trailz Electric Bicycle
review_headline: Scary to ride downhill and can't return--beware!
review_body:
First, the worst thing about this bike is that once you order it, you can't return it, even if you haven't opened the package, due to the \\"hazardous\\" nature of the bike's battery. The battery is considered safe enough for Amazon to ship via UPS but not safe enough for the customer to return via the same method. If Amazon offered a local drop-off location for returns, that would still have been acceptable to me. However, neither option is available so once you buy it, it's final. It's been my biggest regrettable purchase this year!

The second worst thing is that the bike is super heavy and its battery makes it even heavier. If you live in a hilly area like me, it will pretty much be impossible pushing this bike uphill should the battery die. However, I haven't had the chance to test that since I'm too afraid to ride it downhill. The bike's weight plus its lopsided battery position (on one side of the bike) makes it too scary an endeavor to try riding downhill with. Uphill, it was fine, albeit jerky, but downhill was scary. The bike's heavy, lopsided battery threw me off balance and I jumped off the bike within seconds and walked it downhill. My husband, a 150-lb man, found the bike's engine too weak to carry him uphill so I don't know how most people would fare with the bike uphill.

Would I buy this bike again? No way. Would I buy another electric bike? Probably not, but if I did, I would definitely get one that was designed better and weighed a lot less. However, I think a traditional bike is probably best and if it doesn't suit your needs, a scooter may be better.

review_body: I bought this backpack for my 2 year old grandson. He loves it so much. He packs things in it and puts it on to go to the park or wherever. I showed him how to use the zippers and he caught on real quick.

product_title: Stereo Vinyl Cruiser Plastic Complete Skateboard (22.5x6-Inch)
review_headline: fun to ride, but major adjustments needed first!
review_body:
I bought two of these - one blue with red wheels, and one black with green wheels (for my girlfriend). We are used to skating regular boards, so we thought these would be fun to cruise around on - and they are! HOWEVER, the blue one required major tweaking first. Other reviewers have said you need to replace the bearings - Replacing the Bearings is NOT Necessary! They come with ABEC 7s, which are good. What IS Necessary is loosening the nuts on some of the wheels if they are tight (I did this on the advice of the skate shop owner where I purchased the boards - he had every reason to try to sell me the Reds I was asking about, but said replacing the bearings would not be necessary). On the Black board, loosening two of the wheels and adjusting the truck tightness was all that was needed - it skated great after that. Great speed and control.
On the blue one, there were 2 wheels that were still not spinning properly after that small adjustment, so I took them off completely and found that the inner bearings were not inserted all the way! On one of them, the bearing was stuck to the truck itself - I was able to pry it off and found a bit of extra welding on the truck, which was holding the bearing in place and not allowing it to stay in the wheel. I scraped the welding off, put a drop of oil on the truck, and reassembled the wheel. It worked great.
Another problem was that the trucks on the blue one were not the same trucks as on the black one (the trucks on the black were stamped \\"Stereo,\\" while the trucks on the blue were blank). The kingpin nut was not the standard size (kingpin on black board was standard), so I had to use an adjustable wrench instead of my skate tool. The bushings were super loose and the metal washer at the top of one of the bushings was actually broken (chipped). I took them apart hoping to find an easy fix, but no. So I tightened them with the adjustable wrench and hoped for the best. It ended up riding great, not much different at all than the black one.
Final word: I would recommend these to moderately experienced skaters looking for something fun and light to cruise around on. I would Not recommend these to beginners UNLESS you have a good skate shop nearby - skate shop workers will usually help you adjust your board for free, so you'll need to do that if you don't know your way around a skateboard. If you buy the board AT the skateshop, they will definitely adjust it for you for free.

We have notify you the shield you ship back is not our product, We will need to received the product we ship to you to be able to exchange it. Our exchange/return policy is for any purchase within 30 days and it is now over the 30 days period. Sorry we can no longer assist you on this matter. You may provide us with prepaid shipping label if you need the shield you send to us mail back to you.\\"

product_title: Sevylor Inflatable Party Island
review_headline: Not very durable, but fun nonetheless
review_body: We had a lake party planned for the upcoming weekend, so I was very excited to order and receive the Sevylor Inflatable Party Island.  After opening the box and unfolding the item, I was pleased with the large size and layout of the product--it easily fit four people laying flat around the center hole or 6-8 in seated positions.  However, on its maiden voyage, I discovered a small puncture in the base of the raft.  It did not lose air quickly, and we were able to salvage the rest of the day on the raft with only having to re-inflate it one time.  However, this was not the durability and quality I expected of a raft of this price.  I called Amazon the next day, and they agreed to send me a replacement item with one-day shipping (no questions asked!), so hopefully I'll be able to continue to enjoy the new raft for the rest of the summer... I just hope the next one comes without any holes!

product_title: Overland Equipment Special Edition Donner Shoulder Bag
review_body:
I couldn't be happier with this bag. It's just what I was looking for - an all purpose shoulder bag that is just the right size and super functional. I'm a small person, and needed a smallish shoulder bag that would still fit everything I need for a tennis game or a daytrip. It can be worn over the shoulder, or adjusted to be worn messenger style. This bag is so well designed! I love the pockets on either side that can be used for water bottles, lotion, sunglasses, etc. When you're not using them, they stay collapsed and you won't even notice them. When you need them, they expand nicely. The front flap has a velcro closure and contains multiple pockets where I keep my ipod, lipbalm, pen, kleenex, advil, etc. There's one pocket that's lined with soft material just for your sunglasses. The main compartment is roomy and has a single pocket which I use for my wallet. My datebook easily fits, as do snacks, a can of tennis balls and there's still room left over - I agree with the other reviewer that it's like Mary Poppin's bag - it seems like you can endlessly fill it and yet it remains a compact size. There's also an open back pocket that's flush with the bag -perfect for easy access to my keys and cellphone.

The extra shopping bag that comes with the Donner Special Addition is a real bonus. It's so handy to have when shopping. And when traveling, to hold the sweatshirts that you or your kids are no longer using.

I was uncertain about the color so I ordered both poppy and dove to compare. I thought the dove color was pretty dull but I love the poppy. I was worried that the poppy wouldn't be neutral enough to go with everything but the color is surprisingly versitile.

The material is durable but soft. Looks like it will be easy to clean. I expect to be using this bag for many years to come!!
