product_title: Coleman Camp Axe
review_body:
This camp axe is not going to win any competitions for being made of high-tech materials, carbon fiber handle, handsomely crafted, or other such things, but it will not let you down. You can pick these up pretty much anywhere that tools. The head it a high carbon steel that is very durable, and the axe head has a good heft to it making it good at driving a split. I have had one for 8 years, in which time it rusted a bit, but I dug it out of storage and used some vinegar and steel wool and sharpened it up to a fine edge and it works as well as any of the \\"tacticool\\" hatchets.

I have a SOG fast-hawk, and a Cabela's throwing hawk which is better for throwing (this would not work good as a throwing axe due to its weight, if you are looking for a thrower) but I grab this little juggernaut for anything that I need to actually do some chopping with. Its extra weight and large wedge shape make it ideal for chopping. Being heavier is actually a good thing in a axe designed for chopping as it increases the impact. The only thing I am not particularly fond of (and this is a personal preference) is the curved handle. I would have preferred a straight grip rather then a curved one. The rubber grip however is comfortable and absorbs shock well. Works excellently as a camp axe when you cannot bring a large 2 handed wood axe but still need to chop some logs. just coat it with oil occasionally, and sharpen it every year or so and its maintenance free. Sometimes you don't have to break the bank to have a good tool

I don't know how these tires would perform or hold up for long distance riding - I have Continental tires on my road bike that I take on rides like RAGBRAI (almost 500 miles), but I'd consider putting Vittorias on my road bike now that I've been so happy with them on my fixie for over 2 yrs now.

product_title: Victorinox Swiss Army Tinker and Classic Knife Combo,Red
review_body:
There are several reasons why I always go for the Swiss Army knife these days, and it has been my standard for about 50 years, with one hiatus when I got a two blade Buck knife, famous for their ability to hold an edge. I lost the Buck, probably because it lost its alure when the tip of the high carbon (brittle) steel blade broke off.

My first Swiss Army knife was bought in Switzerland. Got a matching one for my father. I still have it, but it succumbed to some of the ills I will note below. Just before my latest, I had a \\"Tinker\\" model, distinguished by its having a Phillips Head Screw Driver blade, but lacking a corkscrew. I believe I had that one for about four years, when it started showing the expected fault of a device which does so many things. The catch which locked the main blade in place began to loosen up, so that I could no longer trust it to stay open under a bit of strain. Upon retiring it, I also checked the scissors, and discovered it had lost its zing as well. It no longer opened when you closed it with the handles. Since there are no finger holes, the spring is essential. This, it seems may be a problem with most Victorinox Swiss Army knives. But I stayed with this brand for one crucial reason. It is one of the few which includes a key chain loop. I looked at Buck and Gerber and Smith and Wesson. Several looked like they were standard gear for the Special Forces, but no key ring loops. So, I stay with good old Swiss, but I never used the Phillips head blade, and I often wished I had the corkscrew. So, I went with the Climber II, which had the corkscrew, and it also had an improved spring on the scissors. My \\"Tinker\\" will not be discarded. It will become the fixture on the living room table for opening mail... and packages from Amazon.

product_title: 4 Oz Ounce Magnum Red Pepper Spray w/ UV Dye
review_headline: Just now received, and tried it out for a "test shot"
review_body:
Thank goodness, I haven't had to use it in ernest [that's why this is not FIVE STARS], but I did check it out, per the attached instructions.... and here are my observations:

Making sure that I had the \\"wind to my back\\" [very important to remember], I gave it a 1/2 sec. blast. What came out of the nozzle was a stream [not a cloud] of yellow/orange fluid, and at about 10', the spray was about 1 foot in diameter. Clearly, this spray is very selective in how you aim it. I also had pressed the nozzle when I was holding it about 18\\" in front of my chest, and in the process, I received a very, very small dose of a fine mist spray in my nose [not enough to sting, but clearly, enough to know that I wouldn't want to be on the receiving end]; that was due to the fact that I pressed the nozzle too close to my chest, and the air moving around me, from my back. To eliminate that, it would be advisable to extend your arm straight out in front of you, before spraying, to prevent any back draft. As the instructions mentioned, it's a good idea for the first time user to give it a practice shot; I would guess that the maximum conservative effective range will be at least 10'-13' feet.

Nozzle security: Unlike a paint spray can nozzle, this nozzle requires that you give the nozzle, a 1/8 turn with your thumb, before pressing down to initiate the spray. It's a reasonable safety feature, and easy to accomplish....although you still have to remember to turn it first, during a critical moment.

Physical size: The body [not the plastic cap] is 4-1/2\\" long, and 1-1/4\\" diameter.... about the size of a toilet paper roll tube. The plastic cap is 1-1/4\\" long.

Questionable info: Although the Amazon ad claims that this product contains an additional \\"UV Dye\\", there's nothing on the actual attached label that mentions that. All that's listed, is the active ingredients: Oleoresin Capsicum [Red Pepper], and pressurized with nitrogen. It does mention that it's not to be exposed to temps greater than 120*, so you might not want to store it in your car. The container also indicated an \\"expiration date\\" of 05/27/16, for what that's worth. Probably giving it a half second test shot every 6 months wouldn't be a bad idea.

product_title: TYR Hydrovision Water Sports Mask
review_headline: Never leak, comfortable, don't give you raccoon eyes
review_body:
I love these for swimming laps. After years/decades of swimming with small/medium/large \\"regular\\" goggles, I gave these a try and haven't looked back. They never leak -- even with a loose goggle strap. I put them on at the start of my swim and don't mess with them until I'm done. Another thing I love about them is that they rest along your brow ridge and lower on the orbital bone below your eyes, while \\"regular\\" goggles rest on your eye socket and/or just at the edges of your orbital bones. Since these TYRs don't sit on your eye socket, they don't give you the typical \\"raccoon\\" look regular goggles create on the sensitive skin right around your eyes. The pressure is also broadly and well distributed -- I don't notice any redness from where the goggles were after swimming.

Goggle fit depends on your bone structure -- especially with one-piece goggles. The only way to test goggles is to put them on. Regarding fogging, I apply anti-fogging gel every once in a while and never have to think about my goggles when I swim.

They are fairly odd-looking goggles, but hey, they never leak, they're comfortable, and they're easy on the skin around your eyes/don't give you raccoon eyes.

review_headline: Have been using this hammock since 2001
review_body:
I backpacked all over South East Asia, and Australasia with this hammock. I never really paid attention to how comfortable it was until I tried a few other hammocks. The cool night air always breathes right through the parachute-like nylon. I was swinging with it tonight, and noticed the tag in the pocket for the first time, so I checked it out on Amazon, with the intention of leaving a review.

So here I am. It's a great hammock, and my wife and I can sit in it at the same time. I got mine from Campmor.com in 2000, and have been using it since 2001, like I said. I also use nylon ropes, as a 3/8\\" rope is plenty. It's triple stitched in all the right places, and mine now has holes in it, but works fine. I don't know what the holes are from, but I would guess they are from campfires.

I know it's on it's way out, but it has had a great run. I don't have much to compare it to. It's in a whole different ballpark compared to a rope hammock. When I have this hanging under my pergola, and keep the ropes together, so my body is cradled, but when I backpack with it, I keep the ropes far apart so my padding doesn't bunch up and I lay flat. Anyway, I would recommend this hammock to anyone.

product_title: Super Turbo 1000watt Elite 36v Electric Scooter "Neon Green" (Now includes Econo/Turbo mode button!)
review_body:
Received this scooter today, took for a 6 mile test drive around Flagstaff, AZ. Went up several hills. Average speed seemed to be around 20 MPH. I will be using this scooter for commuting to work and eliminating the need for gas 5 days a week. Great product, arrived in great shape. Shipping package was well made. I really cannot find a thing wrong at all about this scooter. Fun and environmentally friendly. I need to buy the 1000 watt scooter now!

Update on scooter after several months of ownership: The idea of using an electric scooter to get around town and the service from the company selling them is great. Unfortunately you get what you pay for. This scooter is cheaper then alot of the others that have comparable power and range, but it IS made in China and has the design engineering to prove it. Within the first month I got a flat tire and realized at that point how hard it is to take the rear tire off of the forks and what a crappy design the wheel shaft and bearing assembly is. The shaft is a bolt. There are spacers on the bolt that keep it from spinning in the cheap bearings. If you dont align these exactly, they will eat the rubber shield and raceway of your bearing really fast. I had to replace these bearings and put in expensive(quality)bearings. I also made a proper shaft and used a different design to keep the bearings in place then a friggin spacer(which is just one more thing to have to get into place while your trying to get the chain on, align the wheel and tighten everything down). So the bottom line is, EXPECT to have to work on this scooter and to have to re-engineer it. If you can't do this work then you better have a good bicycle mechanic available who will work on these scooters. Otherwise it will not be on the road for long.

product_title: Timbuk2 Track II Laptop Backpack
review_headline: Great bag, wish Timbuk2 would allow us to customize it though!
review_body:
So far I've ridden my bicycle to Manhattan twice during rainy weather, and my iPad remains dry! There is a side-pocket that supports a water bottle or U-lock (mini, eg: Kryptonite), along with a helmet pocket! Could also stick gym clothes in there if you'd like! Now there are 3 compartments: front compartment is a zipper down which is large enough for keys, cell phones, wallets, etc. Second pouch is decently sized with an organizer inside which stores pens, pencils and the like. Third compartment is large and can hold your books along with a 15\\" laptop compartment that's padded.

Pros:
Water resistant
Has a U-lock & helmet pocket
Awesome
Cons:
There is only one side pocket! Why do this?? This is why we should be able to customize our bags!
Smaller then it looks but is that really a con?
Zipper down - This should be a zipper up to open, not down. I worry that as time goes on, the zipper will ride on down and open on it's own.
U-lock side pocket doesn't have a strap to secure the lock. (Yes it will hold your U-lock the entire ride, but sometimes you're in a rush and the U-lock flies right out of the pocket as you're putting on your Track II)

All in all, I'm happy with the bag and I would recommend it to those who commute by bicycle.

product_title: Columbia Men's Airgill Lite Long Sleeve Shirt
review_headline: Great Technical Shirt for Hot Weather
review_body: This shirt could be called the Columbia Tamiami \\"part 2\\", as it is very similar to Columbia's Tamiami shirt apart from the expanded air vent layout on the Airgill. The Tamiami and Airgill have the same cut and and style and are made of the exact same material, which is indeed very lightweight and soft and ideally suited to hot weather use. The cut is similarly quite loose - I am 6'2\\", 205 lbs, 17 inch sleeves, and I actually sized down on the Airgill from my regular XL to a Large.  It's still plenty big. The sleeves on this, like the Tamiami, are really long and tend to ride a little lower than I prefer when they're in the rolled up & secured position. I like the sleeves to sit above my elbow when rolled up, so sizing down helped to accomplish this. The numerous air vents on the sides and back give this shirt superior venting properties, but it is slightly odd looking for casual wear. If you're in a warm climate and spend much time outdoors, this shirt with the numerous vents is a winner - super light, comfortable, and cool. If you want something with a more versatile style that doubles as casual wear (in other words, something that doesn't look quite as odd when you're wearing it in the grocery store), go with the Tamiami with it's more subtly placed air vents. product_title: Dynacraft Transformer Optimus Prime Bike (16-Inch Wheels)
review_body: our twin grandsons wanted this bike but the first time the bike fell over due to the training wheels being so unstable, the cutsie plastic handle covers broke off, which sent them into a fit wanting it replaced....still having trouble finding the replacement cover for it.  Wish I would have read the review before purchasing 2 of these bikes.

product_title: Timbuk2 Phoney Strap Pad
review_body:
This pad is definitely comfier than the stock one. I have a large D-lux messenger bag, and this pad compliments it well. Even when I load up my bag with a lot of gear, this pad is long enough to be around my shoulder even moments after putting it over my shoulder. If I do have to adjust the placement, it's usually not much. The cell phone pocket works really well, and the velcro is strong enough to hold my HTC Incredible with an extended battery.

This phoney strap pad might not work so well for ppl that put their messenger bag up and over onto their right shoulder. Even putting the strap pad the other way doesn't work cuz the flap would open downwards. So take that into account if you are reading this and thinking about buying one. Aside from that... it's a great strap pad and the phone/mp3 pocket is a great lil bonus.

product_title: Columbia Men's Insight Ice Short Sleeve Crew
review_body: I bought this shirt to train in the gym. I sweat quite a lot in the gym and as I got sweaty the cooling effect of the shirt was very noticeable reducing the amount of perspiration and making the whole training much more fun!

product_title: Igloo Stainless Steel Cooler Latch
review_body: You are reading this because you already know about the problem with Igloo plastic latches and may have purchased a 'few' before reading this. The metal latches are far superion to the plastic and appear they will last the life of the cooler. After several plastic replacements and many complaints it appears Igloo finally decided to make a latch that will last. It should be standard on all new Igloo coolers. The latch actually closes and latches more firmly than the original 165 quart  one on my cooler when new. They are not cheap in price but appear to be worth it; time will tell. You need to use both the latch and the new post as mine would not work properly with the old post. Both are supplied with the new latch, but I was being lazy and frugal(spare parts) and trying the old posts, which did not work right. Don't purchase plastic replacements unless you like 1)frustration, 2)spending money, 3)getting 'stuff' in the mail. I noticed cheaper after market latches but decided to stay with the Igloo's praying that they realize a serious problem exists and are capable of a permanent fix. Four stars because 1 star was eaten by the reputation of the original latches right off the top.

product_title: Texsport Heavy Duty Over Fire Camp Grill
review_body: The first time i used this the black coating started to melt off the grill.  I put foil over it to make sure non of the paint got in the food.  I returned the grill no issue.  The product is good in theory and solid.  Would have been better if it were just steel.

product_title: Wald 520 Rear Medium Twin Basket (13.5X6.25X11)
review_body: Again, I turned to Amazon for my purchases. I have always wanted this basket for my bike as I live near the beach. It was VERY easy for a girl to install. I am quite happy with it. Delivery was fast too.

product_title: Klean Kanteen Wide Mouth Water Bottle with Loop Cap
review_body: I purchased this kantenn about a month ago. The insulation is fantastic - does as promised. However, I've had problems with the kanteen smelling. I've soaked in vinegar, soapy water, etc but to no avail. If bought, I recommend using it just for water and juice, but probably best to stay away from milk or food items.

product_title: Glide Bikes Mini Glider Balance Bike
review_headline: Lots of fun, except when assembling
review_body:
Our son really likes his bike, but there were a few quality control issues when we got it:
* There was no explanation how to get the plastic cover off the handlebar stem. After I laboriously cut it off, I realized that I should have loosened the stem bolt.
* The front fork was overtightened, and wouldn't turn smoothly. I needed to loosen the nut at the top of the frame about 1/4 turn.
* The rear axle was not fully seated into the frame; that would have been fine if I hadn't needed to install the kickstand, which wouldn't fit properly into its stabilizing hole. I had to loosen both the rear axle and the brake to move the wheel to its proper position.

A few ongoing issues:
* The kickstand is too tall; you have to turn the front wheel to the left when parking the bike, as the bike will fall over if you turn the wheel to the right or point it straight (we can't park the bike the way it's shown in the picture here).
* The belt brake seems to be impossible to adjust properly, so the wheel will spin freely but the brake will stop the wheel when squeezed. The instructions (and the bike's inventor, who answers the phone when you call for customer assistance) say the brake will break in after a few hours, but that's not our experience.
* The foot rest hangs down pretty low when pivoted into non-use position. My son likes riding over driveway speed bumps, and the foot rest often drags over the bump.

Despite these nuisances, it's a solid bike that works well, and my son is having a great time. He's a big 4 (almost 50 pounds), so we got this in part because it has a higher weight limit than some others. It's light enough that he can load it into our minivan, or carry it up a few steps. A couple of weeks after getting it, he can glide down inclines easily, and is starting to extend his glide on flat walks. He loves riding about every chance he gets. My other son (just turned 2) also has a balance bike (the two fought over the bike until we got one for each), and we turn a lot of heads as people see the two of them merrily rolling along.

product_title: BLANK Color Complete Longboard OLD SCHOOL Shape 33" X 10" skateboard
review_body:
I bought the black one and just decorated it on the bottom.
But it's so easy to get around campus on it. The wheels allow me to easily ride over the cracks of the sidewalk and the wide deck allows me to have better balance.

The thing I don't like about it is that if you loosen the trucks too much or lean way too sharply, you'll fall due to the wheels rubbing on the board. It is also heavier than I expected which can be a bit of a hassle if you're carrying the board up and down the stairs or if you're carrying it around indoors.

Other than that, I love my board. It's easy to ride and the parts are pretty decent.

product_title: Profile Design RM System 1 Black Water Bottle Cage
review_body: This mounting bracket was too wide to mount it on my road bike seat and was and too narrow on another bike seat.

product_title: Halo Headband Sweatband Skull Cap
review_body: i used it all the time when im working and repairing equipments at jobsite.perfect no more sweats running to my eyes.thank you halo.

product_title: Pedco UltraPod II Lightweight Camera Tripod
review_body:
It is a very great item for a relatively cheap price.
I had a huge dilemma between this and the Gorilla gp3 made for DSLRs.
This tripod serves perfectly on trips, and I actually use this more than I do my fullsize tripod.
Buy this w/o worrying about its quality.

product_title: Camelbak Lobo 100 oz Hydration Pack
review_body: Very compact yet lots of water and room for small stuff. I will use mine for hiking when I am away from my base camp. Highly recommend.

product_title: Innovations Ultraflate Plus CO2
review_body: I recieved it quickly and it works great. I tested on my bike and it only took a couple of seconds to inflate my tire. Note: the next day you should deflate that tire. The CO2 does not stay in the tire the next day it will be halfway solid. Just deflate and use your tire pump.

product_title: Lightweight Large Burner Classic Camping and Backpacking Stove. For iso-Butane/Propane Canisters
review_body: I bought this for a week long camping trip to make coffee. It exceeded my expectations for a single burner, very stable and held the pot securely.

product_title: Coleman 5319-700 MicroPacker LED Mini Lantern, Yellow
review_body: It's bright enough to use it in a 6-person tent, the slide at one side it a good design, kids can sleep in the dark side while I sitting on the bright side.

product_title: Triple 8 Brainsaver Glossy Helmet with Standard Liner (Black Gloss, Medium)
review_body: Works just fine.  It is a little small but I would rather have a tight fit knowing it won't come off.

product_title: Firewire Day Pack
review_body: Jansport went all out with this one!  All kinds of storage, well laid out, TSA compliant, and heavy duty construction!  What more could you ask for?

product_title: 25 Kids Large Rock Climbing Holds
review_body: These went up on a home made rockwall for my kids. They are great size with grip just perfect for their little hands so I feel comfortable with them climbing so high.  They have a roughish texture to them so they arent slick.  Great price for a great product.  Included the hardware to mount them.  Super pleased with shipping also.

product_title: High Sierra Loop Backpack (19 x 13.5 x 8.5-Inch, Yellow/Navy)
review_body: I have used this backpack on a trip to Europe, and so far I am very pleased. I really like the straps and side pouches for water bottles or other items. It would be easier to find items packed in the main pouch, if the zipper extended closer to the bottom of the backpack. While here in Europe, I expect to take it on a 10-day hike. For the price, I think it´s an excellent buy.

product_title: Sigma BC 1009 Bicycle Speedometer
review_body: Good product, easy to install, easy to use and sharp screen. There is not off switch if there are no movement for 1 minute only the time clock will show on the screen, I hope the battery will last for a year or two.  Highly recommend.

product_title: Descente Women's Ridge Short
review_body: I found the medium to be smaller than a true medium, but what really turned me off was the \\"liner\\" which was a separate nylon garment that was an extra extra small. I didn't even need to try it on to know that it wouldn't fit. The liner was so much smaller that it kept me from ordering the next size up to see if that would fit.

product_title: Avenir Shimano RM30/Weinmann XC-260 32H QR Rear Wheel with 8/9 Speed Cassette Compatible Hub (Silver, 700 x 24mm)
review_body: I liked it for the double wall construction as well as the stainless spokes (I broke my wall truing, and broke spokes regularly) it was also about 90% true when I mounted the tire - yay! We live in a world where cycling is about spending - not riding. Fancy shirts, and engineering changes so infinitessimal that only Lance Armstrong could notice, are regularly purchased by staus symbol seekers. If you want to ride and want to avoid spending a car payment's worth of cash on a wheel that will last a decade, this one's for you.

product_title: Coleman RoadTrip Sport Propane Grill
review_body: LOVE IT! Perfect for traveling! Just the right size for my balcony. I was worried that my complex wouldn't allow gas grills,but since this one uses the small cylinder tanks it's great! Clean up is a breeze. I just threw the grate in the dishwasher and it washed up like new!!!

product_title: Zippo Hand Warmer 2011
review_headline: great warmer but needs a shut off switch
review_body: love the concept of this warmer and IT DOES do it's job.  The only drawback to this little gadget is that the fuel has to run out before it will shut off.  Looks great and has a wonderful curvy exterior that really reminds me of my dad's old zippo that he used to flick open.  If you decide in invest in these, buy two--one for each coat pocket.  Great price!

product_title: d.light S10 Solar LED Lantern
review_headline: If you need them and don't have them....Well....
review_body: Going with my hit or miss criteria. These things are definitely a HIT. Had to use them twice for extended power outages due to bad weather. I own 3 and the smaller nightlight version. Safer than candles, long duration and easy power up with just a bit of sunlight. I'm going to be buying a few more of these as spares and for my cabin.

product_title: KOR ONE BPA Free 750ml Water Bottle
review_body:
Cobalt Blue? Try purple.
Only reason why I kept it was because its too much of a hassle to return it and get another.
Aside from that the product itself is great.

product_title: Coleman CPX 4.5 LED Tent Light
review_body:
I camp a lot and use a combination of led flashlights and a propane powered Coleman lantern. I got this light for inside my large six person tent. It works very well. the three light settings are a nice feature. I usually use the brightest setting which provides more than enough light to read by.
The night light feature is a cool addition for say families who have parents that might need to get up in the middle of the night. It provides enough light without being too much.

The magnet that attaches the light fixture is strong and holds well. One person can attach it, but you are somewhat limited to your reach. If two people are available, then the light can be attached anywhere on the tent. Since the light swivels, finding an ideal location was not critical.

As far as turning the wrong switch as others have stated, it is pretty straight forward as to which side the switch is located on and not an issue.

I def like this light and plan to use it on many trips!

product_title: Quik Chair Heavy Duty Folding Camp Chair - Grey
review_body: Mine must have been made on a Friday. Nice large size. Extra tall. But cup holder stitching was off causing a hole in the bottom and stitching on right arm was off causing the metal tubing to come out. I'm thinking they cant all be like this? Hince the three stars. product_title: Cycleaware Reflex Bicycle Helmet Mirror

review_body: This item is not returnable. So if you're a big guy you might not like the fit and be stuck with it. product_title: Allen Sports Deluxe 3-Bike Hitch Mount Rack (1.25 or 2-Inch Receiver)
review_body: Bought this rack to replace one that hooked directly to the car and it worked very well for us.  Easy to install and the bike rode so quietly we hardly knew it was there.

product_title: Coleman Road Trip Propane Portable Grill LXE
review_body: First time reviewing anything on here. I do wish when people review an item they would not rate it low because of things like slow shipping or poor packaging. The fact that it took a while to get or maybe UPS damaged it in shipping does not reflect the quality of the item which is what you are supposed to be reviewing. product_title: Kelsyus Original Canopy Chair

product_title: Comfort Zone The Heat Solution Instant Portable Heat Pack

product_title: Old Town Discovery 119 Solo Canoe Suitable for use with Kayak Paddle, 11-Feet 9-Inch

product_title: JanSport Unisex SuperBreak
review_body: i like the color and its style. It looks great with its appearance with $25 price. It's suitable for students.

product_title: Shimano SL-TX30 TOURNEY 3 x 6 Speed Shifter Top Mount / Thumb Pair.
review_body:
Wow! what a difference in the shifting. Makes my 20 year old bike seem new again. The old shifter was sloppy. Had to estimate what gear you were going to get next. This TX-30 is click-click crisp. No more chain off the derailleur gears.

Ignore the nano-print directions; just use your common sense and they install easy. Adjusting is just making sure they cover all gears. For my bike it was just a matter of setting the cable clamps at the right place. The rear derailleur needed a turn or two on the adjusting screw so it would catch top gear.

You need to take the bar grips off so have new grips to install if they need to be cut to get them off.

product_title: Kammok® Python Straps - Hammock Daisy-chain Suspension System (Stone Gray)
review_headline: Exactly what I have been looking for!
review_body:
I have been working on tweaking my hammock setup for about a year now. In that time I have tried several different suspension options, including the ENO Slap Straps, Hammock Bliss tree webbing, rappelling rings & rope, etc. My search has been for convenience, ease of use, and quick setup and takedown. Weight and size were not a top priority since much of my use is from a car, motorcycle, or canoe. Although I think for the convenience these could still be worth it for backpacking depending on your preferences.

I though the ENO Slap Straps were going to be the ticket, until I slept in my hammock hanging from them and woke up on the ground the next morning. They stretch way too much, which to me became a deal killer on them.

The Hammock Bliss tree webbing is also made of nylon, and when used with carabiners, rappelling rings, and climbing rope, still stretched enough to effect the hang on my hammock through the night. And it took a bit more time to setup this way (although not much).

Just plain climbing rope leaves the problem of tying knots and retying them to adjust the hang. Too much time and trial and error in setup for me, not to mention you are not supposed to loop the rope around the tree.

Finally I stumbled upon these Python Straps. They are Poly, not Nylon like all of the others I have tried and seen, so they do not stretch once you set them up. My first night in my hammock with them confirmed that. I was happy to wake up at the same height I went to sleep. Setup and takedown were lightening fast too. I replaced the rope from the ends of my hammock with a climbing carabiner, so to setup I just clip the biner into a loop. Repeat on the other side. Reverse to take down. It also rained the whole weekend I was testing these Python Straps, and I was please to see that the extra length of strap that hung down from my biner connection served as a drip line and kept water from travelling down to my hammock.

In short, these straps effectively provide the combined benefits of tree protection, hammock suspension, and drip lines, all in one easy to use piece of gear. When you factor that in with ease of use, I could certainly justify keeping them in a backpack, and it is a no brainer for car, bike, canoe, or kayak. Highly recommended.

product_title: Black Motorcycle Scooter Luggage Tail Trunk Top Hard Case with mounting hardware
review_body: Great value. The bottom line is I'm not crazy about the looks but it was the best of all choices for my bike CCW misfit (google it! ) It rattles a bit and is not superbly constructed but at this price point, I wouldn't expect more. product_title: Delta Cycle Leonardo Da Vinci Single Bike Storage Rack/Hook with tire tray (colors may vary)
review_body: I recently moved into a tiny little apartment where space is at a premium. I have a Specialized Tri-Cross and needed to store it taking up the smallest amount of space possible. This rack was very easy to install (I'm an idiot that can barely work a screw driver) and it worked out great. I have the bike hanging behind my front door and the door can open nearly the whole way without the bike getting in the way. It's also really easy to get the bike off and on the rack. I'm glad I found this product!

product_title: Binocktails Bev-Cam 5 oz Camera Flask
review_body: Made of cheap plastic and is very difficult to open. I can't even open mine to test it out. Others say it leaks but they fixed it with glue. If I could get mine open I'd let you know.

product_title: U.S. Divers Admiral LX, Island Dry Adult Premium Snorkeling Combo
review_body: If your even remotely serious about this sport or even hobby spend an extra 20 bucks and get one thats a bit higher end. The seal is very hit or miss and the way the its formed cuts into visibilty.To attach and remove the snorkle you have to thread it through the strap and thats annoying. Great for a pool crap for the actual ocean.

product_title: Igloo Island Breeze 28 Qt. Roller Cooler
review_body: This is perfect for our needs.  Keeps our drinks nice and cold as we sit and watch little league.  Also it makes a quick seat for my daughter when she decides to sit still.

product_title: Topeak Mini Dual Bike Pump
review_body: I've owned the Topeak Mini MasterBlaster for about a month now, and it has saved me on many occasions.  It does require some effort to get my tire pressure up to par (requires ~20 pumps from flat to 70 psi), but it works efficiently despite its small size.  The nozzle attaches and seals very well to my Schrader valves.  Overall, it's a great product - would highly recommend.

product_title: Dakine Girls Cosmo Back Pack
review_body:
So i basically needed something to carry my stuff when i go out. It can fit a small notebook, my sketchbook and pencils, my phone and mp3 player, a small novel, and my camera. It also has little pockets for cash and stuff. There are enough compartments to keep everything organized, which is nice.
It can't fit textbooks though, so I wouldn't buy it for school.
I haven't had it for very long but it seems pretty durable.
Overall I am very happy with this product.

product_title: Hoopla Hippie Stick Assembly Skateboards (7.75-Inch)
review_body: Received product promptly and 100% satisfied with my new skateboard. Although there was a little dent at the tip of the deck, but nothing too serious to worry over. THANK YOU!

product_title: Coleman Bayside 8-Person Family Tent - Orange
review_headline: waterproof the rainfly, THEN it's a great tent
review_body: If you purchase this tent, buy  a gallon of [[ASIN:B003CYTOAI Starbrite Waterproofing & Fabric Treatment]] and a pump sprayer along with it.  The rainfly of this tent leaks when it's brand new. After applying a PTEF Waterproofer to the rainfly, the tent was fantastic.

product_title: AIRHEAD AHMX-V2 Matrix Towable
review_body: I have used this towable for two seasons and have started on season three. It is very well constructed and is typically used with two to three riders. It pulls with ease behind my Honda Aquatrax PWC. I have had no issues with this towable and would recommend it to anyone looking for high quality, fun, multi-rider towable.

product_title: Insta-Bed Raised Air Mattress with Never Flat Pump
review_body: This is the cadillac of air mattresses!!  I had my doubt that it would perform as described due to our past bad experiences with air mattresses but this one has lived up to its claims!  It was wonderful not waking up six inches from the floor with the mattress in a V.  The never flat pump really works. I like having the pump built right into the mattress and it goes up to one of three different levels of firmness and deflates completely flat all at the turn of a dial!  Easy to transport in its carrying bag. The top is a little too bumpy for me with just a sheet over it so I think we'll get a piece of foam for the top or just use a blanket over the top to even out the dips.  Nothing beats being in your own bed but if you are traveling where you need a place to rest your head this is the one you want and I won't feel guilty putting extra company on this one!!

product_title: KAVU Sydney Satchel
review_body: Love this shoulder bag. Well made, sturdy and nice looking. The interior is made of a nice material and there is plenty of room and pockets for organization. I have room for everything I need plus extra space for a diaper & wipes so I don't have to lug the diaper bag around when out for a quick trip.  Kavu seems to make nice products.

product_title: Lightspeed Outdoors Quick Canopy Instant Pop Up Shade Tent
review_body:
I just received my new Lightspeed Quick Canopy today. It came quickly and the packaging was great. We imediately drove to the beach to test it and I LOVE it!!! I'm only 5'2\\" and was easily able to manage both set up and tear down all by myself, even in a decent breeze. It's so light and quick. Just like the name implies...
There is a small strap to clip around the rolled up tent to keep in together while you're putting it into the bag. I'll just have to make sure I don't loose it. But there are 4 mesh pockets in the front 2 'legs' up high enough to keep keys etc. out of my toddler's reach and out of the sand. A perfect place to stuff the sack, pegs and strap so they don't get lost!
The only comment I have is that it's really a purple colour, not the bright blue that I see on my screen. But it's a nice colour, and my 2 & 4 year olds love it. I hope it holds up, but it seems sturdy, so I'm very happy.

product_title: Big Agnes Air Core Sleeping Pad
review_body:
I bought this air mattress for a \\"bucket list\\" trip to the Boundary Waters Canoe Area just outside Ely, Minn. I'll turn 60 in 6 weeks and couldn't have survived this trip without a good cushion to sleep on. Big Agnes provided it. No problems with air loss at all.

As others mentioned, it's surface is a little slippery but I really didn't have any problems staying on it. Several reviews mention it takes a while to inflate. It inflated in under 3 minutes which to me was just fine. It packs small and light and comes with a patch kit in the flap of the case. (I didn't need it, but nice touch).

I'm 6 - 0 tall and bought the 78\\" size. That length was very comfortable. I was concerned about it being too narrow at first but that really wasn't an issue. I weigh 185 and it provided all the support I could have asked for.

I'm very pleased with this air mattress and would highly recommend it.

product_title: Rollerblade Men's Solo Tribe Street Skate
review_body: somehow i scooped these up while they were only $50 on amazon.com. at first these skates are a little stiff, and the huge soulplate takes some getting used to...but now i think i will never skate another skate. when you use the switch setup with the big wheels, the frame feels very tall and its hard to hit the backslide plates on royales, farvs, etc. with your favorite \\"normal\\" frame setup, though, this skate is a beast.

product_title: Sunday Afternoons Adventure Hat
review_body: This is the perfect sun hat for backpacking many miles!  I have another good sun hat that has a rather large brim all the way around, but cannot wear that when I wear my backpack because the brim in the back hits the top of my pack, hence I cannot hold my head up straight.  This hat has fabric in the back to cover the neck, and it does not hit the top of the pack.  Very quality product.

product_title: Fox Men's 360 Short Sleeve Jersey
review_body: What is there not to love about Fox products?  Do yourself a favor and buy some right now.  And remember that jerseys do run fairly big to begin with.

product_title: NALGENE Tritan OTG BPA-Free Water Bottle 24 Oz
review_body: I got this bottle for my wife. She had another style of nalgene before and she was afraid that she wouldn't like this one as well. Turns out she loves it. Uses it all the time.

product_title: Fenix LD22 190 Lumens Flashlight, Black
review_body:
The Fenix LD22 is an excellent lighting tool that can serve multiple roles. This little powerhouse can be useful in an office drawer, glove compartment, camping bag, or tool belt. The versatility of the LD22 is really what makes it a great performer not just among compact lights, but among flashlights in general. Here are some highlights as to the specifications.

Size/Weight- Length is 6.14 inches (156mm). Weight is 2.1 oz (60gm) without batteries. I thought the length would exclude pocket carry for me, but I was wrong. It fits comfortably in the front pocket of cargo shorts and the light weight makes it hardly noticeable.

Power/Run Times- There are 4 power levels. This is what really makes the LD22 so versatile. Low (3 Lumens/110Hrs) The most common setting for me. A great camping setting to find your way around, can shine across a room at night without blinding yourself in the process. Excellent for tasks that are close (dropped coin, key, etc.) and situations that do not require far throw or brilliant light. The ability for a light to go into low modes is often underrated. A super bright light is not always needed for common tasks. Fenix got it right with this setting that provides excellent light volume vs. runtime. Mid (42 Lumens/15hrs) A great general purpose level. Great search mode. Perfect for most functions that most would use their archaic 2D cell junk lights for. But the LD22 will far outperform given its smooth even light beam. High (92 Lumens/6hrs) Very bright. Easily shines up a room, gives excellent visibility outdoors with a decent throw distance. Turbo (190 Lumens/2.5hrs) This is where the magic happens. Blinding light that is good for tactical as well as searching at a distance. It's amazing the level of light and throw it puts out on just a couple of AA batteries!! I am able to use rechargeable batteries. For this reason alone this light will likely pay for itself in battery savings over some of my other lights requiring expensive CR123 batteries. It also has a strobe function that I like a bit more than a typical strobing light. It alternates the speed roughly every 2 seconds. It seems to be more effective than single speed strobe modes. There is also an SOS function that is not much use to me but it is there if you need it.

User Interface- The Fenix LD22 has some improvements over its predecessor the LD20. A side switch just between the body and the lens allows you to toggle between the various lighting levels. One click moves you through the modes, while holding it down puts you in the Strobe/SOS mode. Very easy. It could be a challenging button to find with cold fingers or gloves however. Orienting the pocket clip to \\"point\\" to the switch helps your fingers find it. The rear push button switch is very solid and simply turns the light on and off. The light has a memory and will come on in the mode selected before it was turned off. My particular light has the switch extending just past the tail cap, meaning it is not freestanding. This was not a concern for me, because if I were to use it as a lantern, I would likely hang it instead.

Carry Methods- The Fenix LD22 comes with a decent (not great) nylon holster. It has a Velcro closure on the front, and a loop in the back fitting a 2 inch thick belt comfortably. I doubt this holster would hold up under heavy use but for the average owner it would be sufficient. Someone using this light professionally on a daily basis would be advised to look for an alternative. It also has a pocket clip that is reversible in order to carry bezel up or down. It is solid, and grips securely to a pocket. I was also able to place it off center on the brim of a typical baseball cap allowing hands free operation. Fenix also supplies a lanyard but it is rather thin although stylish does not appear to be very strong. A solution to this might be to get a small ring attached to the light in order to connect to a more substantial lanyard made of 550 cord or other material.

Attachment Options- The Fenix LD22 has some excellent options available. A well constructed bike mount [[ASIN:B0040JRHG2 Fenix Bike Mount (Fits lights with 18-28mm Diameter)]] is made that will allow you to have a very capable bike light that is removable to use for other purposes. A filter kit that has an orange traffic wand, diffuser tip, diffuser lens, and red filter have been invaluable additions to this light. The filter kit requires a separate review, but well worth the 12 dollars on Amazon. [[ASIN:B003XP9IBQ Fenix Accessory Kit - LD and PD Series (4 Piece Kit)]]

Conclusion- The Fenix LD22 is well worth the money. It is an excellent tool that can be used in numerous ways. It's a bit of a multi tool of lights. You will not regret purchasing it. I'll probably be ordering another one soon.ade of 550 cord or other material.

product_title: Schwinn Thrasher Helmet
review_body: This helmet had pieces falling off of it immediately upon opening it. All of the plastic coverings were loose, and I suspect they would fall off with minimal use. Do not buy this product. It is faulty. Other reviewers have had the same problem.

product_title: Titan 65 Frame Backpack
review_body: I have only had one use but I already love this pack. Plenty of storage area's and the section for your sleeping bag (aka extra boots) is a nice addition. Also, several other reasons that I bought the bag were the rain cover and pockets on the hip straps. Both came in handy on my last trip. We got caught in the rain and I was able to quickly cover my pack up with the rain cover while by buddy's fumbled around with ponchos. My only complaint would be that the strap that goes around your waist is big. I have about a 31\\" waist and it's still loose on me. Other than that the pack is great!

product_title: JanSport Big Student Backpack
review_body: I bought this product online looking for a great new backpack. It looked so cute online but when it came i noticed that it is all navy blue and deep-sea green. Personally it's kinda ugly. It would be great for a boy though. Do not recommend if you are a girl buyer. It looks so different than online and is really hideous.

product_title: Perception Sport Swiftwater 10.5 Kayak (White/Blue)
review_body: My friend went the cheap route with a $225 Pelican kayak.  He took his out a few times before I was able to go with him.  His is lighter, with a MUCH smaller bulkhead and sat ALOT lower in the water which made it much slower and harder to paddle.  He's already purchased on of these for himself and given the other to his fiancee' who will use it probably twice a year.  Kayak was very stable on lake Ponchartrain in 1.5 foot waves and great for getting over submerged logs in the bayous. Spend a few buck and get something nice!

product_title: ExOfficio Men's Give-N-Go Boxer
review_body: I bought into the hype and gave these a try, but must say I don't get it.  Sure they are pretty comfortable but so are a lot of boxers for far less $$. I hang my laundry to dry and these take longer to dry than my polyester pairs, and about the same as thin cotton ones. On a recent vacation I tried out the hand-washing thing; rung them out but neglected to roll in a towel... they hung all night in a bone dry room and were not even close to dry by morning. Don't forget the towel step! Also they do not seem like they will hold up well... they will be fine if you plan to wash them in a sink/river but the washing machine appears to take a toll, even when washed on cold/delicate. After just a couple months they are starting to get a lot of fuzzy patches.  Don't even think about washing these if there is any Velcro in the machine. 4 stars for the shorts because they are pretty comfortable and good for hiking, but 2 or maybe even 1 star for the price vs. what you get.

product_title: Mirrycle Incredibell Original Bicycle Bell
review_headline: Great Little Bell, Keep Handlebar Size in Mind
review_body:
I've used these bells on a variety of bikes, and I find them very useful for busy days on the trail.
Only drawback (and one that is easily worked around) is that the bell does not appear to fit several modern road bikes. Specifically, the handlebar tube circumference exceeds that of the bell's clamp. The bell will still mount OK, but since it is not secured in place, it may rotate around the bar, which can be annoying when trying to ring it. This is easily fixed by employing a zip tie to secure it in place!

PROS:
Lightweight
Compact
Easy to hear from a good distance away
Black color works on pretty much every bike

CONS:
Adjustable sizing would be a welcome improvement

product_title: Solar & Dynamo AM/FM Radio with Flashlight
review_body: I got this awhile back from somewhere. Mine doesnt have the flashlight built in which is why I like it. Im trying to find a new one but cant find one that isnt a radio flashlight alarmclock ipod charger pocket knife all in one. I like it cause its a basic solar radio. Period. Its very basic. Its not loud reception is crap and hand crank would be for an EMERGENCY only. You can crank it for a min an get about 2 mins of battery time from it. But with rechargable batteries solar an a crank youre always good to go. I like it for the beach and lake cause with the sun out it will work non stop. It is VERY cheaply made so just be gentle with it. Its not a rugged piece of emergency equipment. I didnt pay for mine but I dont know why they want 30 bucks for it... mine doesnt have a flashlight so I cant say anything about that part. I would try and find one without it because the run time with a 1 inch speaker is shady I dunno how it would power a flashlight for more than 10 seconds.

product_title: ROCK N ROLL RNR Absolute Dry Lube, 16-Ounce
review_body: This lube is great at what it does. It goes on light, cleans your chain and provides silky smooth chain movement. But it is dyed red and the dye tends to stick on everything including the hard to reach areas in the interior of the cassette. It also seemed to permanently stain my plastic chainstay guard. Now instead of being clear, it's pink (stained red against a white paint job). I understand that the dye helps you distinguish between the products, but this seems to be a case of aesthetics getting in the way of function. I chucked the bottle in the trash after only using about half of it.

product_title: SimplySleeper Raised Air Mattress
review_body: I have owned many air mattresses and was reluctant to order yet another however, this one is \\"amazing\\" as my daughter said after sleeping on it for a week on a trip out of state.  The reviews by people in the armed forces helped me decide.  It's a bit pricey but truly worth it.  I've never blown up a mattress and thought it was too firm, but with this one it is easy to do.  You literally plug it in, turn the dial to inflate, wait a few minutes and it is fully inflated.  Too much air?  Just turn the dial to deflate for a few seconds until it is as soft as you want.  Completely supportive and you able to sit on the side and get off of it.  Not a chance of feeling the floor at any time!  Deflates in a few minutes and easy to fold/roll up.  It comes with an oversized bag that has enough room to hold a set of sheets and a blanket. It's bigger than your average sleeping bag for transporting, but well worth it.  Only down side is that the bag is beige and therefore shows dirt quickly.  There is not a chance you will be disappointed! Seriously, you should order yours now and quit researching products!

product_title: Wondershade II Portable Umbrella
review_body: Really easy to put up & take down. Easy to cary with the case. I LOVE this umbrella. Its a really great purchase.

product_title: Schwinn Discover Men's Hybrid Bike (700C Wheels),Black
review_body: Used to love riding bikes as a kid, never thought of riding one as an adult, but since  i prefer  riding one to work to save money i went with a cheap mongoose mountain bike (the ones found in walmart)that bike sure was a miserable ride to work & home. I  decided to get the  Schwinn Discover Men's Hybrid Bike and let me tell you it is  great! not only does it look nice its lighter (yet taller than the old bike) i can ride  faster and smoother. did not need to fine tune the bike...right out of the box the bike works just fine. Easy to install, the parts look more durable than the mongoose. Quick release seat and front wheel, you can carry  stuff in the back also. The seat is comfy, the speed snifters work great, and i mean all speeds unlike my other bike. I live in Connecticut and there are alot of hills, with the other bike i had to walk the hills, with the schwinn i can ride sitting down  will going up each hill without taking a break. For the price i think this bike is great, if your a pro rider then maybe you should go spend the big bucks on another. but for the casual rider this one is worth it.

product_title: Bell Child Barbie Roller Girl Multi-Sport Helmet + Mirror included
review_body: The  helmet is good - fits  my 5 year old daughter fine.  But the bell pictured did not not come with the helmet.  We got some cheap blue mirror that mounts on the handle bars.  Oh well, my daughter didn't seem to mind...but I'm waiting for her to ask where the bell is.

product_title: LEDwholesalers 51-LED 395nm Ultra Violet Blacklight UV Flashlight 3xAA, 7202UV395
review_body: I tried several UV flashlights, but this is the one that worked. Most of them are too weak to use with the slightest bit of light around if you're more than 6\\" from the thing you're inspecting, but this makes up for it with raw power. I use it to search carpets for spots to clean.

product_title: Mirrycle Incredibell Adjustabell Bicycle Bell
review_headline: Didn't even last a full ride
review_body: On the weekend, the trails I ride get busy so I thought to give a bell a try... \\"on the left\\" gets old... I was about an hour into the ride when I was searching for the leaver to ring the bell but it had broken off.

product_title: Snugpak Jungle Right Hand Zip Bag, Black
review_body: love this sleeping bag. it's very light weight and comfortable to sleep either in or under. side zip goes top to bottom as well as bottom to top. Also has a bottom zipper to allow you to open it all the like a blanket/quilt. Really like this bag and would recommend it to anyone who wants a lightweight bag for mild temps. Would have given it 5 stars, but there are a couple of downsides to it. First is there are two small strips of shoelace type things at the bottom of the bag and no idea of what to use them for. Also the bug net at the top needs something to keep it off your face. Otherwise it's a great bag.

product_title: Sunlite City Slick Tires, Black/Black
review_body: Easy to install. Formulated for greater dry-rot resistance and thus longer life. Rare sizes available. I am confident that these tires will last me for several years.

product_title: Camelbak Kid's Bottle
review_headline: My daughter was so excited to get this!
review_body: I have a bigger camelbak water bottle that I loved so much that I also purchased one for my two daughters. My youngest couldn't wait for this one to arrive! She loves it and it encourges her to drink more water.

product_title: Sector 9 Mama Say Longboard Complete
review_body: i have had it for about 4 months and i have never been happier with a purchase. i have rode it a lot and even in rain and through mud the whhels have been slick and easy. if you like long board i would suggest you get this one i love it!

product_title: VitalGrill Survival Stove
review_headline: Too cool for words!!! Actually hot!!!!
review_body: I saw this it seemed to good to be true.  I found videos on this thing. Everyone raved about the compact size, the output of heat (up to 20,000 btu) and the fact that it can be fueled by most anything that burns from wood to paper, to charcoal fatwood etc.  I was amazed that it did indeed boil water in a few minutes. The unit can handle up to 50lbs. of weight as well.  A wonderful addition, (that is on my wish list) is the grill unit for about 110 bucks that will grill, steam, or smoke your food. It too comes in a pretty compact unit. This Vital Stove is great for camping, tailgaiting, or an emergency stove at home in case you lose, electricity or gas.  An incredible marriage of form with function.  Highly recommend.

product_title: TETON Sports Camp Pad
review_body: This pad rocks!  If you want a good nights sleep this is it!  Cover makes it bomb proof and keeps the dirt out too.  Love it!

product_title: Pearl Izumi Men's Select Tri Sleeveless Jersey
review_headline: Improves My Hot Weather Bike Rides
review_body:
material is soft and lets air flow through and sweat evaporate away, armholes are the right size.
the rear pocket could be a bit bigger, but overall, it improves my hot weather ride by keeping me cooler.
sizing is true to other models of PI jerseys.

product_title: Sea to Summit DryLite Towel
review_body: I bought this for an extended backpacking trip, but recently got to test drive it on a 10 day trip. I bought a size large. I am 5'2\\" and 110 pounds, and it covers me with a wraparound but it's short, to give you an idea. It dries quickly and sufficiently. Obviously not a towel texture but it's not unpleasant, still kind of soft. It dries fast as well. Can't give an exact time because I wasn't paying much attention. It was also fine to wrap my long curly hair in to towel dry. I daresay it would be fine to dry my body off, dress, then wrap my hair with it, if I were say in a hostel that doesn't provide towels. I wouldn't want to carry 2 just to have one for my hair. But an all around great travel towel if a little pricey. Worth it if you need it!

product_title: Canari Cyclewear Men's Short Sleeve Sprint Cycling Jersey
review_body: Great bike shirt.  The shirt seems to cool as the wind picks up as you ride.  Fits well and looks good.

product_title: Hikker Poles HP-5 and BT409 are both Anti-shock Hiking Pole, 2-pack, Anti Shock Hiking / Walking / Trekking Trail Poles - 1 Pair With Compass & Thermometer, BT409 comes with a Flashlight
review_body: Ordered these poles for day hikes.  They have worked very well and provided the stability needed.  They are exactly what we expected and for a great price, too.

product_title: Bell iPulse LED Bike Torch
review_body: This is a very good looking unit that performs as advertised and provides adequate light for low light bike riding.  It provides light just over your front wheel path as well as in the distance.  As usual, the purchasing process at Amazon was without issue.

product_title: Avenir Wicker Bicycle Basket with Black Velcro (8 - inch x 10 - inch x 7.5 - inch)
review_headline: THIS IS A SMALL BASKET, NOT MEDIUM
review_body:
It's well built and good for the price.

The problem is it's labeled SMALL by the manufacturer. The product description says MEDIUM as of this initial review.

It's not that useful for grocery shopping but for little knick-knacks like a woman's small purse/wallet or bottled soda or camera would be fine. The MAXIMUM interior dimensions are approximately 10 wide by 7 deep by 6 high. Everything tapers down a little towards the bottom and all the corners are rounded off.

Although it has a handle I can't really see anyone taking this on and off a bicycle to do any real shopping. In addition to being too small to be useful for groceries it would be a pain to mount the velcro straps on and off the bike (especially with items in the basket). Also the strap on the bottom that mounts vertically on the head tube will rub on it constantly. I don't know if there will be long term effects but I would put a clear piece of tape to protect the finish if you cared about the paint.

Since this item is made of natural materials it will vary slightly from basket to basket. Mine was not very centered when mounted. I had to rethread one of the velcro straps through the wicker openings. Not a big deal but something to note in case you were wondering why it looked lopsided.

So in closing. If I had to redesign this product. I would want a quick release mechanism and more useful space. I may try the large which has the quick release but I think that may be TOO large which may throw off the steering especially if loaded with heavy stuff. I just wish there was a TRUE medium.

product_title: THULE WS2 Wheel Straps, 2-
review_body: I had a really old bike carrier on top of my pop-up camper, the strap broke and I had a bike bouncing down the highway at 70 miles an hour.  When I got home from camping I ordered these replacement straps, installed them and they worked perfectly on my most recent camping trip.

product_title: Monkey Light M210 - 80 Lumen Bike Light - 360° Visibility - Wheel & Spoke Light
review_headline: Fantastic, fun bike light! Total life saver!
review_body:
I love this light! I got it as part of the kickstarter project for the product, so have been using it for months. The light is compact, very bright, colorful, and the patterns are great! Better yet, for all us America types, is it's made in the USA! How cool is that!

The battery pack is situated at your wheel hub, so it doesn't unbalance the wheel the way some others might, this is a big deal, especially on larger circumference wheels. It still fits on smaller wheels though, I have mine on a folding bike with 20\\" rims. The whole thing is waterproof. I've ridden in the rain and through deep puddles without any light problems. There are lots of ways to set up the patterns, color cycling, selecting specific colors or patterns.

The light tends to create a colorful \\"light puddle\\" that you ride within, so as well as a very visible wheel, the entire area of roadway around you is illuminated. I wouldn't say it's in a spot to be useful for identifying road hazards, but people can _definitely_ see that there's a bike there, and I can be fairly certain that you are the most visible bike on the road. The day a cab driver stopped in the middle of the road to ask me where I got the light was the day I knew it was really working :D

My bicycle motto is: \\"put your money where it counts - in keeping you alive\\". Monkeylights help to do just that. I will _always_ have at least one on my bike.

product_title: Coleman Camp Axe
review_body: I order this item it arrived with the handle not aligned with the blade, the rubber part was rotate on the metal handle, making it completely useless.

product_title: Bicycle Bike Turn Signal Brake Light Horn
review_headline: Works, but made from cheap material
review_body: Setting it up was easy and works ok, but problem is that its very fragile. It feels like the whole thing can break if your bike hits a small bump. I would not recommend this product to anybody, your better getting something else similar to this thats not made in china.

product_title: Sierra Designs Convert 2 Tent
review_headline: A fantastic, light, strong, versatile, mountain fortress
review_body:
Six nights only I spent in this tent during the summer, but since virtually no one else has written a review on it, it is time for someone to weigh in on the Sierra Designs Convert 2. My experience was sufficient for me to have something to say. I used it in the Rockies at 2800 meters and 3100 meters during July of 09, which means relatively low humidity and cool, but not cold temperatures. My first impressions of this tent are excellent, and I am already thrilled I bought it.

The tent is roomy enough for two men 1.85 meters and 75 kilos each. If you are taller than 1.9 meters, then this tent is going to start feeling a tad short for you. There is a little extra shoulder room at the head (near the door) for the necessities that you need; the tent tapers toward the feet to save weight. There are a couple good internal hanging mesh pockets, and additional fabric loops on the inside, which certainly could be used for a larger gear loft or two, but which can be used for internal guylines to strengthen the tent in extreme conditions--something I have never heard of before, but a great idea.

Set up was a little tricky the first couple times, as you need to figure out which poles do what, and how to thread the two main poles so as to raise the canopy. I don't remember if this tent is advertised as freestanding, however, the tent without the vestibule is freestanding: it can be set up without stakes, and is taunt. If you are backpacking solo however, during set up, it is really a help to stake down the tent first, thread the poles all the way in the sleeves, and then with arms spread wide and a pole in each hand, to push on both poles simultaneously from the head of the tent in order to raise the canopy.

The ridge pole which holds open the venting \\"fly\\" (which I call the \\"minifly\\") on the very top of the tent was extremely difficult to remove at first: it was simply strung too tightly. No amount of snow which might build up on theminifly would ever collapse that pole. With time however, I have found that ridge pole has become easier to remove and now in 2012, its tension is just right. (It seems to me that Sierra Designs could have shaved another ounce by creating that pole at only half its present diameter. It is possible that Sierra Designs corrected this problem in 2010; I cannot tell from their website. They did make some changes.)

I had to stare at the instructions and the Jake's Corners themselves for a minute or two before I figured out how they worked, but they would seem to me to be an ingenious and significant contribution to tent strength. Inside the tent, I locked one corner with the JC and then pulled inward on that pole, exerting a lot downward pressure on it, and the Jake's Corner was not about to let that pole deflect. I was really surprised at how firm it was. Reminded me of JC's story of the house built upon the rock: when came the storm it stood firm.

Outside the tent there are also numerous (seven at least) additional guyline loops which, like the Jake's, are unnecessary in normal conditions, but which would allow you to really anchor this baby down in the strongest winds. Sierra Designs also makes an internal guy kit, which if you also used, along with the JCs, you would have nothing less than a fortress. Strength is one of this tent's fortes.

The Convert 2 has no rainfly: it is a single wall tent. As for myself, I was concerned about ventilation and condensation. So my first night in, experimentally, I zipped up the door all the way, and zipped shut the two, covered, ceiling vents (which have both mesh and fabric closures, which are separate), to put the breathability of the Drizone material to the test. About the only conditions in which someone might want to do this would be at about 40° below in an all out effort to keep heat inside the tent. (In regards to keeping heat inside the tent, I sense that the Drizone material would do this better than the average tent with standard nylon walls, yet I might be wrong as it is only a single wall.) I awoke at about 4am and did sense a big need for some fresh air, but surprisingly there was no condensation inside the tent, even with two occupants on a still night. I unzipped the top two vents and zipped the door part way down, and immediately felt a fresh air flow, even though there was no wind outside.
In a colder and more humid setting I found that in the morning, the inside of the tent felt moist, but was not actually wet. In other words, no moisture had beaded and I would not get wet when touching it.

Fortunately for this review, at my 3100m location, I got hit with a number of good rain storms and heavy winds. This tent never leaked a drop, and happily, no rain blew in through the open ceiling air vents under the minifly. Even when I touched the sides of the tent during the rain, they did not leak. There was no internal condensation during the rains, day or night. The air ventilation system catches and channels air and seems to create a power ventilation system. I was very impressed that a tent of this general shape was so taunt when no guylines were strung. In fair weather, you simply don't need them. The tent did make some rustling noise under some strong winds, and this noise decreased when I guyed out the sides and tightened the vestibule. The tremendous blasts of wind I experienced pulled out a couple of the needle stakes (the ground was soft) and moved two 7 or 8 kilogram rocks I had used as anchors to guy out the tent sides. That is how strong the wind was. (80kph?) No damage was done to the tent, and the tent would have had so much more to give if I had guyed it out everywhere and installed the Jake's Corners. The tent of course will shed wind best if you are able to pitch it so that the door or the rear is facing into the wind. If you have a strong cross wind, you need to have the air vents open to allow the air to pass through the tent. If they are closed in a crosswind, the air will get trapped underneath the minifly and exert strong upward lift on the tent. So, I suppose you will need to open the air vents at 40° below if you have 60 kilometer per hour cross winds. In short, in this tent I felt like I was sheltered from the elements: I was sealed in from the rain, and this tent can handle any wind I will encounter.

One really nice touch is the reflective piping. Once at night when I was trying to find my way back to camp in the forest with a dim headlamp, as I scanned the forest, my headlamp \\"shone\\" on the tent at about 50 meters out, and the reflective piping on the tent lit up like a roman candle. Even with the headlamp, I would not have been able to have even seen the tent directly at that distance, if it were not for that piping, and would have walked way past camp and really wondered where I was.

The vestibule was really handy: when leaving camp to go fishing I just threw all my junk in there, and it was all out of sight and protected from rain. Contrary to another review on this tent, you CAN get two full-size backpacks into the vestibule if you pack them so that they will stand up and if you place them right by the door. With the vestibule in place, you can leave the tent door unzipped for excellent ventilation and even a little star gazing through the clear skylight patch on the vestibule. One negative would be that without the vestibule (which zips off to stay at home), rain or snow will enter the tent while you do. Apparently, without the vestibule and the Jake's Corners, this tent weighs only 4 lbs 2oz. My advice would be that if you are traveling fast and light and far, breaking camp each day, leave those two at home. If you are going to set up camp in one place for a few days, or may face extreme wind, rain, or snow, take the vestibule and the JCs and laugh at the elements.

Let's summarize, negatives first.
CONS
Two minifly limitations:
1. With the ventilation flaps under the minifly closed (which would only be desirable in super cold temps), in a crosswind, the minifly will really trap wind underneath it, which will exert lift and pressure on the tent itself. (Head or tail wind, no problem.)
2. With the ventilation flaps and door closed, the air in the tent got noticeably stale overnight.
3. Without the vestibule, rain and snow, if coming from the direction of the door or coming straight down, will enter the tent when you open the door,.
4. The ridge pole which holds up the minifly at the tent's crown fit way too tightly, and is very difficult to remove.
5. Construction gaffs: a small piece of fabric of the vestibule was accidentally sewn into the door zipper seam, and thus not separable from the canopy. A simple cut of a tiny slice of non-necessary fabric cured that. Also at one fabric juncture, a flap of material was not stitched together properly. Some SeamGrip took care of that.
6. (2012 update) After three years of use, I just noticed that there are several small spots where the white Drizone coating on the inside of the tent is starting to wear off. I don't know yet if the tent will leak there or not.

PROS:
1. Door location: at one end. Better than one side door, as both occupants can get in and out without one having to climb over the other.
2. Strength: This tent withstood some ferocious wind, (80kph I am guessing) which I frankly think would have leveled most off-brand cheap tents.
3. Lightweight: Do any other sub-2-kilogram tents that are this strong even exist?
4. Waterproofness: nothing came in.
5. Low-condensation: I was surprised there was none on a still night with two occupants and the tent zipped up tightly. I attribute this to the Drizone material which, if not highly breathable, at least seems to do a good job of conducting moisture vapor to the outside.
6. Airflow: with the two ceiling vents open under the minifly, or with those open plus the door partway unzipped, the flow was wonderful.
7. Unprecedented Versatility: They say this is a four-season tent: I concur. Yet it is light enough and practical enough to take on any summer overnighter. I will use this tent all the time, everywhere, solo or with a partner, regardless of what kind of trip I am on, regardless of season, and regardless of conditions. I don't know of any other tent on the market about which I could say that. I found a winner.

product_title: Pop Up Tent (size:106"x65"x43") with inner tent
review_headline: a simple tent that sets itself up.
review_body:
This tent has three significant disadvantages and one significant advantage.

First the disadvantages-
1. while advertised as a two man tent, this really only has room for one. Two people would have to be either really friendly or really squashed to sleep in this thing.
2. the thickness of the tent wall needed to keep the tent itself from ripping on opening up also keeps the tent from being breathable. I would not recommend it for daytime camping anywhere that heat is an issue.
3. when taken down, the tent has a thirty-two inch flat footprint. Not really something that can be thrown in the back of a small car, or carried while backpacking.

and the advantage (and the real reason to buy the tent) -
It requires only minimal set up and take down. In non-windy conditions, the tent can be set up and ready to use in seconds with out any experience, just pull the strap and throw. In windy conditions, setting the guy-wires takes an additional two to three minutes. Take down requires a little practice, but is done in two minutes or less, even if you really mess it up.

product_title: Topeak Joeblow X.O. Full Metal Floor Pump (7.4X 10.5X 29.1-Inch)
review_headline: Does Not Work For Presta Tubes
review_body:
While I was hesitant to purchase a bicycle pump this expensive, I ride every day and fill tubes all the time so I decided to go for it. That was a mistake. The SmartHead ThreadLock pump head seems like a great idea, but it is virtually unusable on Presta valves.

There are two problems with this pump head:

First, it takes a large number of turns to fully screw on to a Presta valve. This is not a huge deal, but it takes much longer than a typical clamp-style pump head.

Second, when you unscrew the pump head it also unscrews the valve core and the tire completely deflates. Yes, seriously.

Almost all Presta valves these days have removable valve cores. These give you a larger opening that allows you to put tire sealant such as Slime into your tubes. I've never heard of them unscrewing by accident until I used this pump. To be fair, I have managed to use it successfully a few times, but after a valve core comes out once the success rate drops to almost zero.

Like the other reviewer, I emailed Topeak but have not heard back yet, either.

product_title: U.S. Divers Proflex II Diving Fins
review_body:
Out of any of the past fins I have owned these are the most flexible. But is this a good thing? It depends. The more flexible a fin is the \\"easier\\" it is on my muscles. For example. We have all ridden a bike. If you remember when the gear ratio was very low you had to peddle very fast just to get anywhere but your legs didn't suffer fatigue. But, when the gear was much higher just pushing the peddle one time required all of your body-weight, and you wanted to quit so you just lowered the gears back down. Well, that is how I see fins and like I said these are flexible (low gear ratio).

I bought the large pair (9.5-11-.5 mens). My foot size is 10.5 and pretty skinny. I was kind of concerned how these would fit because they are full fins without a strap. So as a precaution I bought 3mm fin booties:[[ASIN:B0057RHN6K Deep See 3mm Skin Smooth Neoprene Fin Socks]]. The fins fit taught, but I am kind of worried during long swims my feet may start to go numb in certain areas. I have only used them for max 30 min at one time and have had no issue with this thus far. The Neoprene fin socks will add greater comfort for those long hauls.

If you are a 9.5 get some kind of fin sock. These will be too loose which in turn will become very uncomfortable. Over 10.5: You will probably be alright. You might like the socks for comfort purposes, if you do, then get the ones without the grip. I bought the ones with grip and they are hard to insert into the fins sometimes.

Finally, the fins are great for being close to the shore and especially someone new to snorkeling. Because they are so flexible you will not be able to travel very fast. For those of you who enjoy traveling far out into the reef these may not be for you. Your friends may leave you behind and you may have to try harder just to keep up. I recommend considering these situations before purchasing. I contest, however, that these perform how I expected them to and will recommend my friends to buy them as well. Remember, these are $20 fins so do not expect them to perform like $200 fins.

For this reason, I think that these should come with some kind of attached tie to seal it off at the top.
