product_title: Thule Quest Cargo Bag
review_headline: Stylish, Big Lockable Zippers, Great Bang for the Buck
review_body:
Quick summary:
I uploaded a few pictures of the Thule Quest 846 I received. It's black and grey, a pretty stylish combination and looks like good cargo bag. Would buy it again having now seen it in person and checked out the zippers/material/stitching. Extra information that you may/may not want to read below.

It's Lockable:
I want to point out that I was afraid I wouldn't be able to lock the bag, but that's NOT the case at all. I am able to use my standard TSA approved lock on this bag through the zippers NO PROBLEM. Of course I won't be checking this bag in at the airport, I'm just trying to give you a general idea of the size lock that will work. Just go to any store and look in the traveling section, those small luggage locks work fine. This way I know for sure the cargo bag won't be coming open during our long trips.

It's Water Resistant:
Not water proof, and the booklet that shows you had to use the cargo bag clearly says this. I applied some Scotchguard fabric spray which repels water to add an extra bit of rain protection in case it rains, and will do the common knowledge \\"put your suitcase in a trash bag THEN put it in the cargo bag\\" trick. This way if rain does make it in during the trip, our actual suitcases will still be dry.

It Stores Nicely:
It folds up. From a fully stretched position, fold it forward at the 1/3rd mark twice (back 3rd over middle, front third under middle). It fits into the supplied storage bag securely and snugly. It doesn't take up that much room - which goes without saying it takes up a LOT less room than trying to store a whole hard cargo carrier. Most of the benefits of the hard cargo carrier, without the space issue. We can literally just store it in our trunk area and forget about it, and if we need to use it it's quick and very easy to put up.

It's Easy To Throw On:
As I just mentioned above, it doesn't take but a minute to take it out of the storage bag, throw it on your roof and run the straps. If you like extra security you can throw some ratcheting cargo straps on top as well. I use two ratcheting straps across the roof rack bars in a parallel horizontal setup, and two going in a parallel vertical setup. Think of it like a tic-tac-toe game. 2 running north/south, 2 running east/west. The cargo bag isn't going ANYWHERE if you do that, that's for sure! Of course you'll spend a few more minutes when you arrive at your hotel removing the extra straps, so it's really up to you if you wanna spend the extra money and time doing that. I think the straps the cargo bag comes with should be fine, but there's always a chance the bag could potentially rip and if you've got the extra straps everything should remain tied down (and with the extra straps I really don't see how the bag could rip because there'd be even less of a chance the wind would have any surface area to catch onto / rip).

product_title: Genji Sports Wheeleez Fishing Cart/Beach Cart
review_body:
I fish about 4-5 times a week, and this is probably the best \\"little rig\\" I've seen for the price. It's not fancy, it doesn't hold more than 50-60lbs worth of gear, but for what it is, it's awesome!

I have had absolutely no problems taking this thing over gravel, hard pack sand, dunes, or anything.

The only modification I had to make was the use of 2 bungee cords to strap my cooler and tackle bag to the frame. That's it.

Great product, decent price. I'm happy with it.

** UPDATE: so i've had this thing a little over a year now and it's worked fairly well, however, i'm dropping my 5 star review to a 4 star for the following reasons:

1) rust: the top clips and the bottom folding bracket are pretty well caked with rust...yes, i use this a lot and realize that salt water/air and sand are corrosive, however, for the price i paid for this i would expect better protection from the elements...and i rinse with fresh water and dry it EVERY time after use.

2) tires: it's not a huge deal as they still work, but be careful running the tires over pavement and/or gravel...since i don't have a 4x4, i have to park on pavement and walk to the beach...the tread on mine has pretty much worn off completely...like i said, it doesn't make a huge difference in efficiency, but it's just another example of something that didn't last too long.

3) rod holders: 3 out of the 4 rings on the top rod holders have fallen off...i realize i use this thing pretty hard, but it's not like i'm pulling or tugging on the rings for them to have broken off...i was able to re-attach them with duct tape...it's not pretty, but who cares?...it's a fishing cart.

product_title: Sea Eagle SE370 Inflatable Kayak with Deluxe Package
review_headline: Safe, comfortable but a bit slow
review_body:
I've kayaked since my teens but my wife had never tried it - she's a bit uncomfortable in small boats.

Our first outing was on a perfect day, almost calm, bright, and on a long, narrow lake.

Setup:
Inflation is quick and easy if you use an electric pump to get you 85% of the way there, then switch to the bellows to get full pressure. The seams appear well manufactured and straight, the valves install easily, and the simple pressure gauge is elegantly easy to use. The seats are nothing fancy but do the job just fine, likewise for the paddles. It really only takes about 10 minutes to be ready to go.

Under way:
Stability is good and there was no anxiety about a capsize while getting in. I'm 6'3\\" and my wife is 5'8\\"; we both had plenty of space. As we paddled away from shore I heard \\"this is easy!\\", which was a great relief. You'll get pretty wet as water drips from the paddles, but it doesn't amount to much even after a reasonable length trip.

Directional stability is good, with little wandering from side to side. We went from one end of the lake to the other and returned, about 2.5 miles in total. No problems with seating comfort the whole time.

All that stability comes with a price - this is not an especially efficient hull. When you both stop paddling you'll come to a halt quite quickly, and as a result it takes a fair amount of effort to keep moving - not enough to be a problem, but if you're used to sleeker hulls you'll feel like you're pushing through rather than gliding over the water.

Packing up:
We left the hull in the sun to dry after draining the small amount of water we'd collected from paddle drips. Remove the valves, roll the sides in, and fold ends to the middle - that's all we bothered doing. We stowed the deflated hull on top of camping gear across the back seat of the car, and I can easily carry it myself.

Summary:
A great success for us. It's an easy to carry, easy to use, confidence inspiring way of having safe fun on the water. Experienced kayakers might find it a bit slow, but for most people just wanting to have some fun it's the perfect ticket!

product_title: Schwinn Girls' Petunia 12-inch Steerable Bike,Pink/White
review_headline: cheap but so far so good
review_body:
I was hoping for a little better fit and finish from a schwinn product, but this bike is cheaply made and it shows.

I bought the bike specifically because I like the handle. And the fact that it comes with training wheels instead of that being an extra purchase. So far the bike is working, it does what it should, my girl likes it. I'm trying not to be negative since it is accomplishing the task that I bought it for... but I just can't get over how things are not as I'd expect. I would gladly pay an extra twenty bucks for a better product. Here are some gripes:

-The paint on the handlebar does not match the body of the bike. The paint on the adult handle is 2 different colors of pink (the handle is in 2 sections).
-The instructions to build the bike were a joke. The manual looks like it comes with every single Schwinn bike... it has instructions for BMX bikes and mountain bikes and everything. BUT it does not include instructions specifically for this bike. I think I got everything right... but I can't be sure, can I? There really aren't instructions included.
-The training wheels are hard plastic. I would have preferred rubber (even if not pneumatic)
-The adult handle is not in line with the front wheel. Meaning - when I'm pushing, the handle is cocked a bit to the side.
-The streamers are a joke. They will fall off the first time my daughter pulls on them.
-There is a badge glued on the front of the bike that says \\"Schwinn Quality\\" and the joke is - that badge was coming loose as I pulled the bike from the packaging. I'm sure it will fall off soon.
-It would be really nice to be able to \\"opt out\\" of the brakes while teaching my kid how to ride. She pushes backwards on the pedals because she thinks it's fun to stop. Every. Five. Feet.

All of that being said - it does the job. It's not a pretty as it could be, but I don't care so much about that. If stickers come loose and the handle'sa little crooked, I can deal. I still think it's a good buy. I just wish I could have found one used, or I could have paid a bit more for higher quality.

I was disappointed that the cable lasted for only a month. Considering all the 4 and 5 star reviews here on Amazon, I am hoping that this was just a fluke and the new one will last a little longer!

product_title: Ibera iPhone 4 Handlebar Bag with Stem Mount
review_body:
**Update 2 (6/21/2012)**
I did a century ride with it this past weekend and it was solid. Hit many pot holes and bumps, and was never a worry. This thing is solid. I'm even going to bump it up to 5 stars now, as its not very hard to remove from the mount now. Awesome product.

**Update**
I did a 16 mile ride on mainly paved surfaces (with some bumps and potholes on the way). I should also mention it is installed on a road bike, so i cannot attest to how it will hold up to mountain/trail riding. it held up very well. I was a little worried it would shake/rattle on bumps, and it didnt even seem to move. I didnt worry about it at all during the ride. Phone is easily accessed when needed. Agree it can get difficult to see, but thats not really the fault of the pouch/holster. All in all, great product.

**Original Review**
Full Disclosure: just received and installed it, so I've yet to ride with it. Will comment on it (and perceived durability) at a later date.

I had been strapping my armband (thats used for running) around the stem and handlebars, before i found this, so this was exactly what I was looking for. Mounts right onto the stem, and even provides a longer bolt to screw into the stem. Nicely positioned, i would imagine reading the screen would be relatively easy (outside of glare of lighting conditions, as mentioned in previous reviews). Install was a breeze. The pouch looked like it was going to be a tight squeeze, but my iPhone 4S fit effortlessly. I like that it is a pouch, and not just a holster, in the unlikely case it becomes separated from the mount during a ride. It was a little difficult to remove the pouch from the mount, so thats really where I knocked a star off. It might get easier with more use, who knows. But all in all, great mount for the price. We'll see if it holds up.

product_title: Coleman 2-Pole Sun Shade
review_headline: Solid performer in all kinds of wind
review_body:
We just completed a campout over the weekend, with 25-35 mph winds gusting to 45 mph. The canopy held the whole time, deforming under gusts, but holding true. I watched some other canopies fold over in the campground.

Of course, the gusts blew some hot ash on the canopy, and now I have a repair to do...

I would recommend a few good stakes (at least 4, attached to the pole guys). I used these stakes - [[ASIN:B0017TFPV2 Sierra Designs Y Tent Stakes 6 Pack)]], but other heavy duty stakes would work well too. I used some basic stakes for the other guys, and bend them in the strong winds.

It takes quite a bit to set up, vs. a EZ-UP or similar. You must stake down all the sides, which means 8 stake placements (2 on each pole, plus 4 stretching the canopy).

I'm definitely a fan, and would highly recommend.

*** Update ***

After e-mailing Coleman about how to fix the holes in the canopy due to my own mistake, they sent a repair kit to me for free! Coleman has my vote for excellent customer service, and I will be looking for their products in my future buys!

Cons:

- No outside pockets. Everything has to go in the main compartment. There is a very thin outer pocket that can only hold flat stuff. A few exterior pockets would be handy.

It seems to me this was designed by someone who takes their laptop to a coffee shop on their bike, not someone who commutes with a laptop to work every day. Nevertheless, it's the best option I've found.

product_title: Hollywood Racks HR1400 Sport Rider SE 4-Bike Platform Style Hitch Mount Rack (2-Inch Receiver)
review_body:
I have only had the Hollywood Racks HR1400 for a couple of weeks, however, based on what I know right now I am going to be extremely satisfied with this product. My first, and only, word of caution is that you must make sure that when you install the receiver tube into your hitch receiver that the hitch pin goes through the hitch tightening system within the receiver tube. Once you have the receiver tube on, the rest of the installation takes maybe 20 minutes. The majority of that time will be aligning the wheel holders to fit the bikes that you own.

What I love is that this rack is versatile. You can put an adult bike and a kid's bike with training wheels on the rack in 2 bike mode, and off you go. You can put 16\\" or larger bikes on this rack, assuming that you have the seat of the smallest bikes in a position where the frame hooks can go over the seat. The velcro wheel holders appear to be sturdy and help to ensure that the bikes do not move. The fold up and tilt down actions were very easy to accomplish; much better for you and your car than a trunk mount rack.

The 'no wobble' levers for the base unit and the 2 bike extension seem to be awesome. There is no 'play' in the connections and the rack seems to be secure. As previous reviews have stated, this rack is heavy. However, if you store it in two pieces there's no real issue dealing with the weight and length.

For my money it does not look like you will be able to find a better quality product for the money that will allow you to take 1-4 bikes with you on any trip, safely and securely. Also, Hollywood Racks does everyone a solid by including a locking hitch pin AND a 9' locking bike cable. Both locks use the same keys (at least for mine) so you can carry one key and be able to lock/unlock the hitch pin and cable lock as needed.

November 2012 Update:
After making several long trips with this bike rack, I can re-affirm the 5 star rating.

review_body: Shirt is awesome. Wore it trekking through the himalayas for many days in a row without washing and didnt smell too bad. Shirt fits perfectly, no complaints at all.

product_title: Pearl Izumi Women's Select Glove
review_headline: nice gloves but do not have enough protection
review_body: The glove fits me prefectly and looks nice.  but It can't protect your hand if you are going to ride your bike for a long time.  The part under the fingers do not have enough protection.

product_title: CamelBak BPA-Free Better Bottle with Bite Valve
review_body: We aren't an extremely active outdoor family but when I was researching for water bottles for my two boys, I figured these were a no brainer with all the high reviews. But not long after getting them, one of them started leaking water around the valve area on the lid. We figured it had something to do with the way our 6 year old was using it because our other sons bottle was doing really well. Then as I was sitting down getting ready to order myself one, we noticed the other one leaking the same way. We can't figure out why they would start doing this because they basically just sit out on the table or counter or sit in the car, no rough treatment. I was really excited to from such high reviews and was willing to forgive one cup as a fluke but not two. Sadly, I will be taking my business elsewhere.

product_title: Schwinn Rocket Comp Adult Dual-Suspension Mountain Bike
review_body: I bought this bike mainly because it had good reviews and it's wasn't too expensive. I made a mistake in doing so. When the bike arrived it looked great. After 50 miles of use and the left crank(peddle arm), fell off because the screw fell out. I put it back together making sure the screw was tight, but it keeps falling out every 20 miles or so. The gears on the bike don't switch smoothly and the front gear won't switch to first and the back gear won't switch to eight. The other parts seem ok. Barely rideable though.

product_title: Smith Optics Lineup Premium Lifestyle Polarized Outdoor Sunglasses/Eyewear - Matte Gold/Gold Gradient Mirror
review_body: I have been wearing Smith's (and plenty of others) for years and these are my favorite Smith's of all time.  They are not \\"aviators\\" and are classy and professional looking.  They are so light weight and comfortable it's amazing.  They wrap around your face unlike sunglasses of that shape.  Love everything about them.  Amazing value, style and performance lenses.

product_title: Topeak Pocket Rocket Master Blaster Bike Pump
review_body:
Wow, this thing is great... I flipped the little head so that I could use it with Schrader valves and it works perfectly.

The action is very smooth and I find myself counting out 100 pumps with no fatigue. Delivery end gets warm as you keep pumping but I just thought that was kind of neat. Friction?!

I just love the low-profile of this thing... I throw it in my backpack but it looks easy to affix to your bike.

Definitely recommend this for emergencies and regular use!

product_title: Trail-A-Bike Jr. Compact Folder (Silver)
review_body:
The bike had a large dent on the bottom tube right out of the box. While the dent won't affect the function of the bike, it is disappointing and makes me wonder if we received used merchandise.

I bought the compact trail-a-bike for my 3 y/o son who is 38\\" tall with a 15 1/2\\" inseam. His feet barely touch the pedals (flat footed) in the lowest position. Should be OK once we add some mini-clips to the pedals.

The 20\\" tire that comes with the bike has an extremely aggressive tread pattern like a full on mountain bike tire. Since the owner's manual states that the bike should only be ridden on paved or smooth gravel trails, I don't know why they include a tire with so much tread/ unneccessary rolling resistance. Isn't it enough that I'm towing a 28 lb bike + a 35 lb kid? A tire with a smoother/faster tread pattern would make more sense.

product_title: Nantucket Bike Basket Co. Classic Lightship Basket
review_body: I am very happy with the quality of the basket.  The size of the basket fits my bike and will hold every thing that I will need for a fun filled day with my Grandchildren.

product_title: Light My Fire Titanium Spork
review_body:
Strong, solid, good sized. Comfortable to eat ramens (where both fork and spoon might be needed). I am thinking about bringing it to the office for lunches (but then I wouldn't be having it in my backpack when going camping). Overall, it's a nice spork, I tend to use only it outdoors.

As time passes: I noticed that this spork can scratch some of your pots. So, I still take this spork with me, I no longer consider it my no 1 eating tool. I still keep in my backpack as a fork or as a replacement spoon for a buddy who forgot his, or when I need a second spoon, because my primary mideum-size wooden spoon is used serving the food. Same kind sporks, but made out of plastic, don't made the cut to me either, because they can melt when frying something.

product_title: Osprey HydraForm Reservoir
review_body:
I purchased this for trek up Kilimanjaro, where minimum daily liquid intake is 3L. Seemed like the perfect match for my Osprey Talon 33 day pack.

However, despite being clearly marked as 3.0L/100 oz., I can only get 2.5 liters into the bladder. Measured several times with same result - not sure how you sell it as 3.0L when it doesn't hold that.

product_title: Coleman Camp Towel
review_body: This towel is horrible and don't waste your money.  It does not absorb at all.  I bought two for a trip and they are worthless.  They are now going into the garbage.  Don't wast your time or money.

product_title: Camelbak Groove Bottles
review_headline: Need Filtered Water On The Go? Then This Is Your Water Bottle!
review_body:
I have had my Camelbak Groove for a year and a half now, and I have no complaints.
The filters do a great job and, other than your first sip after replacing a filter, I have never experienced any \\"drag\\" in pulling the water through the filter. Also, the filters are easy to replace and reasonable in price as compared to other filters.
The bottle itself is well made; I live on the beach, play roller derby, and work with kids, and despite being dropped a zillion times and thrown in and out of different bags my bottle works perfectly with no leaks or defects.
If you need filtered water but can't always have a pitcher near by to do it for you, this is the perfect solution.

product_title: ExOfficio Men's Give-N-Go Brief
review_body: I have two pair from many years ago that are great.  Bought two more.  Not nearly as good.  Seem more cheaply made, ill fitting, fly too low, not enough \\"up front\\" room.

product_title: High Sierra Chaser Wheeled Book Bag (20 x 13.5 x 8-Inch, Purple/Green Flower)
review_body: excellent product-backpack is spacious and sturdy,colors are nice, can fit a lot of things,it is easy to transport, I definitely recomend it

product_title: Osprey Talon 11-Litre Backpack
review_body: Used this backpack in the half Geoquest adventure race (160km trek, kayak, tubing, mountain bike over 48 hours).  The bag easily fits in all the mandatory race gear (med pack, thermals, gore jacket), food, 3L hydro port (bought separately) and other bits and pieces you'll need for a race.  The pockets on the straps are great for bars and gels as are the front pockets on the waist straps which also readily accommodate a compass. I've trained with this bag almost daily and it's been bulletproof.  The bag is easily adjustable and have had no back or knee issues with 2hr+, 9kg pack training runs in hilly national park terrain. The reflective material on the back and locations to clip in lights make it an ideal mountain bike bag as well. This pack is an excellent, tough pack for mountain biking and long (12hr+) adventure races.

product_title: Truvativ 20mm Offset 350/27.2Seatpost Holzfeller Single Clamp (Blast Black)
review_body:
I ordered this as I needed a two bolt style seat post to get enough angle adjustment for my saddle. It appears well built, is not very heavy, and the logos are fairly discreet. I ordered this over the Hussefelt due to the less obvious logos, and the lesser weight to a much smaller degree. I'm sure either would work fine, and based on how strong this one appears to be I have to guess that the Hussefelt seat post must be nearly indestructible.

As per the description it does have a setback, unlike the photo that Amazon has.

product_title: Pearl iZUMi Attack Low Sock 3-Pack
review_body: These are very lightweight and stay dry. I rode with them on through a rainstorm and they were bone dry by the time I was back inside. They're very thin (stretch to the point that they're transparent) so I don't know how long they will last.

product_title: Finish Line Wet Lube
review_body: The largest size is well worth it.  You save by purchasing it.  I have three bicycles and so I have used this for all of them.  It really does work so well and it does not run off of the chain. Goes on every well and adheres nicely.  I have used other brands before, but this is my favorite by far.  You also have to use a minimal amount of this product for maximum effect.  Your chain does not attract all sorts of dirt of debris either.  Well designed product for sure.

product_title: Schwinn Thrasher Helmet
review_body: It is cheap so I didn't expect much. My friend bought the Giro one and it is very similar in terms of build quality and features. The main difference seems to be the name and color selection. I bought this as I would not care if it was stolen and if I do have to use it in-case I fall it is cheap to replace. Helmets are only good for one fall. It fits comfortably, has an adjustable head strap in the rear and two adjustable straps for the ears. Of course it also adjust under the chin. Vents well. The only reason I didnt give it 5 stars is because the front clip doesn't adjust like other helmets but cant expect too much for the price. Overall I am satisfied.

product_title: Continental SuperSport Plus Urban Bicycle Tire
review_headline: So far, so good - but hard to install
review_body:
I purchased one of these at a local bike shop to replace a Bontrager Race All-Weather Hard-Case 700x28c rear tire that picked up a piece of glass.

I've only put 10 miles on it so far (commute), so I can't say much about it's reliability, but it's ride-ability is nice, so far. One thing I don't like about it, is that it was absolutely impossible for me to install on my rim - even with using tire levers. It's the first tire I've had to bring to a bike shop to have installed. I dread the day I get a flat, because I don't think I'll have any chance of replacing the tube road-side.

I'll write a follow-up in several months to let you all know how they hold up.

[edit - 10/16/12]
My nightmare came true - I got a flat the other day after about 900 miles on these tires. A tiny piece of very sharp, very rigid metal worked it's way through the center of the tread of the tire. This tire was so tight on my rim that it took me nearly 15 minutes just to remove it. While attempting to re-install it, I managed to puncture both of my spare tubes. This tire is nearly impossible to install without the use of tire levers - at least on the Bontrager rims that came on my bike from the factory (2012 Trek FX 7.5).

I was curious, so I installed them on a spare rear wheel that I had laying around - a 32 hole Mavic Open Pro laced to a Shimano Dura-Ace hub - It certainly wasn't easy to install, but it would definitely be doable road-side without levers, or chance of pinching the tubes. Great tire overall - just very tight on certain rims.

product_title: Camelbak Podium Big Chill 25 oz Bottle
review_body: I bought this water bottle 2 months ago for when I go mountain biking and I use it everyday. it keeps drinks cool for a long time and it has never leaked. It has fallen from my bike at about 20mph and it did not get damaged. it is tough. the only problem is that if you are going to have it in a waterbottle cage you have to find the right size because its weird shape makes it difficult to keep it from falling off. other than that it is great.

product_title: Potable Aqua Water Tablets
review_body: The product arrived when promised.  It is just the right size.  I haven't had to try it yet, but that doesn't matter. I will be getting more of this product.

product_title: Victorinox Swiss Army Huntsman Boy Scout Pocket Knife (Red)
review_body:
Our grandson just because a boy scout and we were so proud of him, that we bought him this knife.
He loved it and was so thrilled with this gift.
It's hard with teenagers to pick the right thing, but this was a winner.

product_title: Pacific Cycle Women's Oceanside Bicycle (Light Blue)
review_body: I got this bike for my girlfriend and she loves it. It's a beautiful bike and works great but it wasn't shipped with propped padding so theirs scratches on the bike in places.

product_title: Light My Fire Original Swedish FireSteel Army 12,000 Strike Fire Starter - Black
review_body: This is a MUST BUY for any survivalist or outdoors lover or you just like to go camping this little number will get your fire going no matter what the weather hot, cold, rain, or snow! this product is high quality and heavy duty and works exactly as advertised and using my hunting blade I was able to get an even better spark though the striker works fine and there is no need to use the knife at all the company shipped this item very quickly it was not supposed to be delivered until the 5th of July and it got here today on the 3rd of july now that is FAST shipping! If you are trying to decide which one to buy stop right here and buy this NOW! you will not regret it!

product_title: Polar Bottle Insulated Water Bottle - 24oz
review_headline: Not as good as  I thought...
review_body:
This is okay and I will keep it but it does not keep drinks cold for very long.
I don't know what product everyone else got but mine may keep drinks
cold for about 2 hours if that and that is in an air conditioned house.
I have yet to try it outside in the heat...Can't imagine it doing too well.

product_title: Eleven81 Lift-Off Wire Mesh Basket Silver, 14.5 X 10.25 X 9.625"
review_body: Wife wanted a basket large enough to hold her purse and a couple other items on rides on the beach or greenway. This one is almost perfect. We added some rubber pads to the bottom to keep it from scratching the front fender. A very practical unit. It was also well packed and arrived as predicted.

product_title: Mountain Hardwear Pinole 20 Sleeping Bag
review_body: I purchased this bag through Altrec.com.  I needed to get a sleeping bag that had synthetic fill due to an extended trip sea kayaking (if down gets wet, you get unhappy :-) ).  I used this bag for 4 nights during a trip to Anchorage in the summer time.  I was very comfortable and warm every night (in fact I had to wear minimal clothes inside the bag on occasion to prevent overheating).  The only drawback I would have is that it doesn't pack down quite as small as I would like (a little bulky).

product_title: Giro Indicator Sport Bike Helmet
review_headline: Great buy for the price!  Not 100% comfortable.
review_body:
This is a great buy for the price. It was a little uncomfortable, so I'm happy they included some attachable padding.
I put 2 pads in my helmet, and that has worked for 4 months now. I also am not fond of the location of the buckle to attach
the helmet under your chin. I should likely tighten it a little more but tighter is uncomfortable. But once I put it on I forget it is even there (that's good!). If it does it's job in an accident is what matters most.

Updated review on 5/25/2012: Feel off my bike last week, I hit the side of my head on pavement, small scratches to helmet absolutely NO injury to my head :-)

product_title: 2PCS Foam Road Bike Bicycle Handle Bar Grips Black and Blue
review_body:
Feels cheap for the price. You can buy tubes four times as long for half the price, cut them to fit four bicycles. They don't even supply end caps.

Fits one inch diameter handlebars. Just about all handlebars sold in the US are one inch. Exceptions are French bikes from the '80s and expensive Italian bars.

product_title: EveryDay Willow Organic Hemp Drawstring Backpack
review_body: its organic and great quality......simple and pure.....a very good size...we will be buying many more, great price! good for gifts

product_title: Darn Tough Men's No Show light
review_body:
My main reason for purchasing these socks was to use for hiking. So far I've had them on a couple of trips and the air circulation is especially nice with the vented tops. They have gotten wet during some hikes, but since they're wool, they tend to dry out fairly quickly.

I bought both the XL and L sized socks, and initially I didn't feel much of a difference, the XL comes up a little higher on the ankle, which I like. The L size fits me as well, but I prefer the XL size.

My shoe size is 11 US

product_title: Columbia 50 Can High Performance Rolling Cooler
review_headline: Great for on the go chilling!
review_body: This item is just what we're looking for. Works perfectly. It flattens out and becomes compact so it's easy for storage and very easy to expand. Can fit a lot of things in it to stay chilled on the go. I like that it's on wheels so we can roll it rather than lug it around. I also really like the color. I would highly recommend getting one of these :).

product_title: Big Scout 30 Degree Kids Sleeping Bag
review_body: We've used these sleeping bags several times this spring and the boys always stay snug and warm. We love them too because they sinch down small when in the bag! Perfect fit for our family while camping and canoeing.

product_title: Slumberjack Trail Tent
review_body: My family was a hardcore camping family when I was a kid. We had some excellent tents over the years. When my nephew was born I couldn't wait to take him camping! I had to find a tent that could withstand the elements because there is nothing worse than a tent that fails when there is the slightest bit of rain. We camped in my backyard the first time we used this tent. It was a nice night adn the tent was great! Nice airflow and a lot of space! When we took our first actual trip into the woods, we were gone 5 days, it rained three of those days. The first night it rained so hard I was worried the creek we were camping about 20 feet from was going to rise over the bank and we were going to need to evacuate. This tent stayed dry dry dry. I couldn't believe it! Even the best tent I've ever had (a Gander Mountain 8 person monstrosity that was solid as a rock) would have leaked a bit in that storm. The rain stopped around 1 AM and the tent dried over night so we had no issues when packing up to move on. I like that this tent has two doors, it extends the life of the tent. I hope there will be many more camping trips in this tent.

product_title: KAVU Women's Sydney Satchel Bag
review_body:
I have had this bag for months now, and carried it daily. It is chic, sturdy, and goes everywhere and with everything. I call it my \\"adventure bag\\" and all my friends are envious.

ADDENDUM: I am still carrying this bag even months later- I've had it for almost a year now, I think. It's been through several washes, and still holds up perfectly. This is such a fantastic bag, and I would recommend it to EVERYONE!

product_title: Bottle Top Cold Beverage Koozie, Set of 12
review_body: was hoping for all the colors shown in picture, but they sent me 4 boxes of the same color tops. other then that i like them.

product_title: Hikker Poles HP-5 and BT409 are both Anti-shock Hiking Pole, 2-pack, Anti Shock Hiking / Walking / Trekking Trail Poles - 1 Pair With Compass & Thermometer, BT409 comes with a Flashlight
review_headline: Good poles but compass & temp worthless
review_body: Used on a three day hiking trip.  The compass on each pole always showed a different direction for north (yes, I made sure I didn't put together) and the temp was always different by 5-10 degrees.  Will remove them on my next trip.  Poles are a bit heavy compared to my hiking partners, but worked well.

product_title: Texsport Deluxe Privacy Shelter/Shower Combo
review_body: Great shower for camping excellent size very easy to install it even has a shower bag and two towel racks the price was the best

product_title: Aosom Elite 2-in-1 Double Child Bike Trailer/Jogger
review_body: Purchased for my granddaughter's first birthday.  Easy enough to assemble.  She has to sit on a folded towel as the straps are a little high but she loves riding in it and there is plenty of room for toys and snacks!

product_title: Avenir Fixed Gear Lock Ring
review_body: it works great. i had no issues installing, easily threaded on and threaded right back off. keeps your cog secure.

product_title: WAYLLSHINE(TM) 500LM CREE LED Flashlight Torch 3 switch Mode: Strong Brightness / Normal Brightness / Flashing for Riding, Camping, Hiking, Hunting & Indoor Activities
review_body: I mistakenly gave this product a bad review because I thought the product was not operating correctly.  The fact is that I was not operating the product correctly.  I must have inadvertantly loosened the rear of the light where the tether wrist cord is attached. After I tightened the rear piece the light has been working great.  My apologies for mistakenly assessing the product in a bad light..no pun intended.  JD

product_title: Intex Pillow Rest Raised Airbed with Built-in Pillow and Electric Pump
review_body: Ordered 2 of these airbeds.  They came in really handy when my guests arrived.  I had no complaints.  They were comfortable and held the air very well. product_title: Azonic Outlaw Bicycle Wheel Set
review_body: good deal for a strong light set of wheels.. i have tortured these things for a few years now and they are solid...

product_title: Columbia Men's Permit Short
review_headline: best shorts I have bought online
review_body: Shorts are light weight, ripstop nylon, fit is very confortable. great summertime short and will pack and travel well. These shorts dry really fast, my cotton shorts in the Carribbean would still be wet after overnight drying.

product_title: High Sierra Elevate 28" Wheeled Upright
review_body: I looked at a lot of pieces of luggage before I bought this one. I really wanted something that was lightweight, had a side handle, and was a color that stood out on the baggage claim belt. This definitely fit the bill. The only negative is the lack of compartments/pockets. I took the luggage to Europe all ready and it was perfect.

product_title: MOLLE Medium USMC Assualt Backpack Pack-TAN
review_body:
Great Pack I have used it for several weeks now every day. It fits fine over a flak and sappies. Im 6'1\\" 205LBS. That post that said it didn't fit properly is probably a boot and needs a PME on how to properly wear a day pack. For $50 your not going to find anything better trust me.

Semper Fi

product_title: Nalgene Tritan 24oz On the Fly (OTF) BPA-Free Water Bottle
review_body:
I've used this bottle for at least 10 months now and it's wonderful.

Here are the reasons why:

1. There's no odd plastic smell to it
2. It's very easy to open (one-handed operation)
3. I can drink from the spout while doing other things and not worry about spillage
4. It's very light
5. Screw the top off and it's super easy to clean
6. There aren't a ton of nooks and crannies that get dirty and make it impossible to clean
7. It doesn't leak
8. I've dropped it a few times and it's survived well
9. The lid locks in place when opened so it doesn't hit me in the nose when I'm drinking
10. There is an additional metal latch to keep the lid closed when it's locked in place
11. I mainly use it for water and it never smells. Even when I've kept water in there for a few days.
12. I love the clean, simple design
13. It's easy to slip a single finger under the lid to carry. There's enough space for three of my fingers (a little cramped and very unnecessary).

The only thing that I don't like about it, and this is minor, is that the lid does take a bit of strength to close but it's not a problem for me. I can do it with one hand if I put a little muscle into it but with two hands, it's really easy.

I really love this bottle.

I returned to purchase another because someone washed it with one of those hard green scrubbing pads and scratched the interior. Now it smells and I have to wash it after every use.

product_title: Royal Robbins Men's Backcountry Shorts
review_body: My idea of the perfect lightweight short to show off my still decent looking legs around the farm.  They fit well but the belt seems to slip loose under strenuous conditions.

product_title: Essential Gear Pico Zipper Keychain Flashlight
review_body:
this one is supper. i had a coast nano one for a long time. it's pretty good. but i need one fit in my pocket key case better. this egear has similar diameter but half short than coast nano. the finish of both flashlight and key chain are shiney and decent, supper nice chrome like. light feels about the same as my coast nano. one better thing to say, this egear has a battery holder inside, which makes it much easer to change battery. my coast nano has no battery clip, a bit hard to line up 4 batterys and fit back in.

i'll still keep this egear in my wish list.

product_title: Schwinn Solar Combo Light
review_headline: Wish strap had better materials or better design.
review_body: My handle bars are tapered so the thing was always sliding loose.  Not any more, after a few rides the cheap front strap fell apart. Lights work okay.  If I did any real riding at night I would chuck the lot.

product_title: Shimano UN55 BB Square Taper Bottom Bracket
review_body:
I had an unsealed bottom bracket that was the absolute bane of my existence on my daily commuter. It creaked, groaned, popped, and felt like it was bathed in dirt. I knew I had to get a sealed BB. This was my first choice and boy was it a good one.

The bearings are smooth, although don't expect borderline friction-less smooth, but you won't notice when you are pedaling. There is no noise at all and the aluminum cups makes for a nice peace of mind without having to worry about any plastic becoming aged and cracking over time. Simple to install, easy to thread on, and sealed bearings are a must. Expecting this BB to last me quite a while!

product_title: Magnesium Fire Starter
review_headline: knock off. NOT genuine issue from Doan. [Updated]
review_body:
I ordered the \\"Doan Machine and Equip...\\" mag bar from Trail Explorers Outpost and it appears to be a knock off.
It has Doan impressed on one face as listed but DOES NOT have the patent # or the NSN for military ordering.
Additionally, it weighs a bit lighter than the genuine issue ones.

I would recommend avoiding this one.

Will cost too much to return. Going to relegate to a drawer and experiment with it.

[Update]
I have experimented with it and the one I have in my hand is NOT a legit mag bar.
While it has the Doan stamp on it I would not purchase one until I saw pics of both sides which have writing on them.
I shaved off a good pile and had sparks land all in it and around it with very poor results. The size of the pile should have blazed and it did not. Blowing on it just put it out.
There is no doubt that the bar has magnesium in it but it seems to be a poor mix.

It was hard to shave in good sized chunks (using the blade perpendicular to the bar and scraping) as compared to my known good bar. Don't try to shave chunks off like whittling.

I am not sure the seller is even aware that this is probably a knock off so I wouldn't send a scathing e-mail or call if I were you. Just let them know.

Mine came in a plastic bag and not in the packaging shown in the pics. Not a big deal just including for full disclosure.

I hope this helps. Buyer beware.

Lndcrsn

product_title: Genji Sports Pop Up Family Beach Tent And Beach Sunshelter
review_headline: Perfect on the beach, plenty of privacy
review_body:
We took this tent with us to Jacksonville to help keep our 10 month-old out of the sun. It's roomy enough for my family of four (including my 6'4\\", 200+ lb. husband). It looks so much smaller on the screen and I was worried about not having enough room, but there was space for our bags and our bodies to fit comfortably.

It also provided adequate privacy for me to nurse my son without dealing with onlookers. We threw a quilt down for comfort because the material would have stuck to our skin in the heat, and it was perfect.

The tent held up great, even with the post-Tropical Storm Debby winds. Set-up is very easy; just take it out of the bag and it pops right into position. We used the stakes to keep it in place instead of filling the sandbags. Putting it away is a bit trickier. We practiced before vacation, just to get the hang of it, and it took a little less time each time we closed it up.

It does get hot in there, but opening up the windows and/or the back flap is really helpful with that.

Overall, this is a terrific shelter and I'm so glad we bought it. Our son (and hence, we) would have been miserable without it. And I can use it in the backyard when we want to get outdoors to read or play. It'll get plenty of use.

I posted a photo above of my son in the tent so you can get an idea of how much space there is. I highly recommend this tent for the beach, Little League games, or the backyard!

product_title: InStep Quick N EZ Double Bicycle Trailer
review_headline: Great as a stroller and trailer!
review_body: We just got this in the mail a few days ago and so far it seems to be great. My husband put it together with ease.  We tried it as a stroller first with both kids (1 year and 3 years old) and it was great!  I was surprised with how smooth the ride was and how easy it was to push.  My kids liked it too.  They weren't even fighting!  There are two pockets on the inside for them.  Which we put toys in and it fits sippy cups too.  I hooked it up to my bike too and just took it out without the kids.  It seems to be very east to control and maneuver.  I think we will try it out with the kids on a bike ride tomorrow.

product_title: Disney Minnie Mouse All About Bow 12" Toddler Backpack
review_body: This was a present for my daughter's second birthday.  She loves it and carries it everywhere!  It has plenty of pockets for all the things she needs, diapers, extra clothes and even snacks, plus has room for the things she wants to bring along.

product_title: Schwinn Men's Varsity Carbon Bicycle (Black)
review_body: I've had this bike for over 3 years and haven't had any problems with it. I have ridden over 400 miles on it and it still runs like new. Worth every penny so buy it.

product_title: Fenix LD20 180 Lumen LED Flashlight
review_body:
These units uses the new Q5 cree led assembly. I bought 2 of them, more for their long battery life because of the forthcoming hurricane season.

It is optimized for NIHM batteries. If Alkalines are used, the low and medium is hardly distinguishable when the batteries are fresh. Also, due to the smaller diameter, the alkalines have a slight rattle which can be eliminated with a few wraps of paper.

The Fenix has a wide beam compared to a torch like the Led Wholesaler's 7224BK. Both are rated at 180 lumens but the latter's beam is narrow like a laser. The useful light is about 15+ yards further than the Fexix LD20s. I use these in a suburb so there is ambient light from homes, street lights and possibly the sky. Because the lights are from all directions, the USEFUl light range is only about 40 yards. Beyond 50 yards, it blends in with the other lights. Perhaps in a dark forest or an enviroment where are no stray lights, you will do better.

When the batteries in the unit are questionable, I'm thinking of using the high output. The Fenix is designed for constant output, there will be no warning that the batteries are weak. Should the light go out, I feel slightly more secure knowing I can drop to low and gain a few minutes.

product_title: InStep Safari Swivel Wheel Double Jogger
review_headline: You get what you pay for
review_body:
I researched many double strollers and chose this because the price was so reasonable and had many of the things I was looking for in a double stroller. Main things I wanted were: storage, easy to steer, something to fit my Graco Snugride infant seat, cup holders for adults and kids.

Pros
1)It came with a parent console with 2 cup holders and child snack trays/cup holders.
2)It folded down pretty compact and with ease and fit int he trunk of our mini van with room to spare.
3)I read in other reviews that it could hold the snug ride car seat while resting on the tray (not recommended by manufacturer though).
4)Seats recline almost flat. My 3 year old who is about 37 inches fell asleep comfortable in it several times.
5)The price is very reasonable.
6) The handling is pretty good for a double stroller because of the inflatable wheels.
7) Prompt response from manufacturer when we had to get a new tire lining and storage basket, although she was really grumpy.
8) Sun shields could fold all the way down to snack tray.

Cons
1) It was pretty heavy and awkward to pick up when folded.
2)When it folds, the whole stroller weighs down on the foot rest and it gets scraped up.
3) The cup-holders have a rubber lining inside which makes it really hard to pull disposable cups out of without them getting squished.
4) The tire lining popped within 2 weeks worth of use. The manufacturer replaced it \\"as a gesture of good will\\" just one time because the tires are not under warranty.
5) The storage basket underneath drags on the ground and tears the bottom. Manufacturer replaced this free of charge, but we were informed its only meant to hold 3 lbs!
6) Does not fit through standard doors. This proved to be frustrating because we had to take kids out and fold it up to get through some doorways.

Overall, for the price of the stroller, it is okay. I think it would be good for someone whois just looking to use it outdoors only for walks or jogging and not needing to use the storage. It is awkward and heavy to get up and down curbs and a tight squeeze through many doorways if it fits at all. The snug ride infant seat does not fit in securely and lays very flat when resting on tray. It will only fit on one side of the stroller because the level indicator window hits the tray and makes it lopsided on one side if place on the wrong side of stroller. I did not list this as a con because it was not really made to hold the car seat anyway.

We ended up returning this stroller because it was too hard to get through doors and the storage was useless and annoying because it made a scarping sound on ground. Amazon was wonderful about this and very prompt at responding to my request. We ended up purchasing the Britax B-agile double stroller which was almost $200 more, but hopefully worth it!

product_title: Vilano Aluminum Road Bike 21 Speed Shimano
review_body:
Short: It's light, enough, fast enough, and can take enough of a beating that you'll either be able to ride it for a year or two until it's really hurting, or you'll like it enough to invest in keeping it in good shape and it will last a long time.
Best bike per dollar I have seen. I can't imagine there's a cheaper bike that won't disappoint you quality wise. If money isn't a factor a more expensive bike would be lighter, faster, and probably tougher. You'll notice this one age, but it's great for starting out, commuting, or abusing.

Long: When i purchased this bike I got it in size small black for about $270. Considering that finding the same style bike just a few pounds lighter will jump you into at least $500 this is as light as my budget was going to allow.
The rear tire blew out a couple times until I replaced it with a more expensive Gator Skin, but that's to be expected in the glass riddled streets of nyc. The front tire is still hanging in there so the stock tires aren't total junk.

After a couple months the crank axle has gotten loose and started making some ugly noises and the front spokes are a bit out of whack, but after a trip to the shop it should be fine. The ride is fast enough that i think it's worth some money to repair instead or riding into the ground.
Again it was < $300 and i really beat on it so I'm not complaining.

This thing performs like an urban bike that should be at least $400 - $500, which is awesome. It's probably cheaper because over the months it's needed more maintenance than any of the antique 1980s/90s road bikes I used to ride in college, which is not so awesome, but I'm willing to deal with that since around here even an old road bike is often > $300 and a new one starts at $600

product_title: Coleman 2-Burner InstaStart PerfectFlow Propane Stove
review_headline: Great camping stove that is also handy for those emergencies that come along!
review_body:
We have had this stove for a while and it has been a good one. We don't use it often but it has always performed the way you would expect it to. We used to live in the county and we had numerous power failures and in one bad winter storm that meant 3 days without power. This little stove helped cook our meals and keep us going during that time period.

The stove sets up easy and the two burners are ideal to cook a larger meal with two things going at once. The flame controls work well and you have good control over the heat setting you want to use which is important whether you are trying to boil water or make eggs for breakfast. I also like how the cover and side wind shields lock together and help keep the flame steady and hold in the heat.

We always have some cylinders of propane around and they are inexpensive and easy to find. The grill features an InstaStart spark igniter but to be honest I always carry matches or butane lighter as a backup. The propane cylinder lasts a reasonable amount of time and the specs say 1.1 hours on high and 4.5 hours on low when using a 16.4 ounce propane cylinder with both burners going. We always got that same usage or a little better. This baby gets things hot fast and you don't need to use the full burner setting all the time.

We have been very happy with ours and it is ideal for camping or those emergency times when you lose power. This is a very good product and I recommend it to you!

product_title: Sip N Go USA Spill-Proof Bottle
review_body:
I haven't had this bottle for very long, but I wanted to write a review as there were no other reviews yet. I took it with me on a cruise, and it was very handy to clip on and carry along with me. It freezes very nicely. The plastic is very flexible but seems sturdy. So far it's held up well. It's ideal for air travel b/c you can empty it before going thru security, roll it up into a small package, then refill it at a water fountain before you get on the plane.

It may not be clear from the picture and description that the bottle has a snap to hold it in rolled-up position when empty. Nice feature.

I didn't have any trouble drinking all the water in the bottle. (Reviewers of some similar products said it was difficult to get the last bit of water out. No problem with this one.)

The only negative comment I have is that it's on the small side. That's subjective b/c it might be just the right size for some people! The mouth is small, so standard ice cubes can't easily be inserted, but the bottle itself can be frozen, so that's not much of an issue.

review_body: They hold pretty good.I had to go back and redo it one time but they seem to be holding good now.The white does get dirty no matter what I do.But after the ride I clean them off.Would I re order these yes.I do like the way they look on my bicycle.

review_headline: Leaked badly, made my back hurt
review_body: I bought a twin-sized bed of this brand a few years ago and it was perfect. I bought a queen-sized bed for use while waiting for my furniture in a long distance move. product_title: Scooby Doo 12.5in Child Backpack- Mr. Machine Scooby Doo Backpack
review_headline: Happy with decision to buy this item
review_body: I bought this backpack for my grandson who will be starting pre-school soon.  The description states that it is big enough for a standard sized folder.  The overall size is perfect for little kids. However, we found that most folders actually do not fit, the plain paper type folders work best.  The side pockets are nice for easy access to frequently used items.  The graphics are very colorful and the quality of the product is very good.

product_title: Bicycle Carbon looking Aluminum Bottle Cage, CARBON LOOK
review_body: I've had this on my bike for about a year now and I have no complaints at all!  The build quality is excellent and I see no cons.  It holds a variety of water bottle sizes safely and securely.  Being mounted on the underside of my full-suspension bike, it's even taken a few hits but never missed a beat. Excellent.

product_title: Mirrycle MTB Bar End Mountain Bicycle Mirror
review_body: I checked out the pictures and thought, by leaving out a part, I could mount it in the end of my bull bar. Sure enough, it mounts that way. Very happy. Strong unit.

product_title: NALGENE Tritan Wide Mouth 32oz BPA-Free Water Bottle
review_body: I have owned several of these. I wanted the green color so I paid what I thought was a little over priced for the item. I like the large mouth because it is easy to fill with ice and your favorite beverage. These things are durable as well. It was a replacement for one I lost skiing from my backpack!

product_title: Swiss Gear Smart Shade Sunscreen/Windbreaker for Canopy
review_body:
I bought this to use with another manufacturers canopy. It works well. I noticed that I had to raise the canopy height up a notch higher than I would normally to that the screen didn't hang on the ground. This also allowed me to use the hole at the bottom of the canopy leg to secure the last elastic hook on the screen. The screen did a great job of keeping the sun at bay while allowing enough light through to not be cave-like under the canopy.

Overall it was $20 well spent.

product_title: Innate Shiru Vacuum Food Container - 2012
review_body: I'm using this container to save tea leaves and it keeps them very fresh, I would definetely buy another one if I need it.

product_title: Cloudveil Men's Upstream Mesh Fishing Vest
review_body: I bought mine based on first review by Phil. It's totally accurate. I'm totally satisfied. I anticipate more Cloudveil purchases in the future.

product_title: Topeak Ride Case for iphone 4 and 4S (Black, 4.6 x 2.4 x 0.6-Inch)
review_body: I found that the mount and the case were very well made.  It is easy to install and holds my iPhone very securely. The phone condom that they supply doesn't fit all that well but it does look like it would protect the phone a light rain.  I'm not sure that it would stay dry in a downpour.  All in all it is certainly worth the money.

product_title: Outdoor Research Sunshower Sombrero Hat
review_body: Outdoor Research makes a great deal of top quality products.  This Hat is very comfortable.  It is very light and well made.  It has vents to help keep you cool and has a rain cover that can be used in a downpour.  Very nice foldable hat.

product_title: PHAROAH DLX BALACLAVA
review_body: I purchased this item needing to cover my neck for low temp motorcycle commuting. At first look you think it would not keep you warm as it is so thin, but it does, at least to 32 degrees, the real test is to see how it does in lower temps.

product_title: Bell Detonator 3.5 Foot x 20mm Bike Cable and Lock (Steel)
review_body: My bike was stolen using this lock. There appears to be a weak point under the plastic bits on either site of the combination lock. I originally bought it for the extra length and flexibility over a U-lock. In that regard it is a lot easier to use in situation where a bike rack is not available(on lamp posts, trees, etc) However these qualities so not outweigh its inferior security. I now know my mistake and would advise against anyone buying this lock.

product_title: Profile Design Ti Rails Tri Stryke Saddle
review_headline: Great seat at a really great price. I'm glad I bought it!
review_body:
The short version:
I like this saddle. The price is right. I'm glad I bought it. I recommend it.

Now for the longer version for those who are interested.
As a reference point, I'm about 5'9\\" & about 190 lbs. (Not exactly \\"fat free\\" but more of a broad & \\"meatier\\" build.)

What's a nice term for \\"that area of the human anatomy which doesn't like bike saddles\\"? Maybe I'll just call it \\"that area\\". \\"That area\\" likes this seat.

The price is right. If you're on a pretty tight budget like me, the price is a big issue. I'm sure the pricier saddles are worth the money - but if you don't have that kind of money available, it doesn't really matter how great they are.
The long nose of the saddle makes me able to \\"get forward\\" in the aero position like I want and stay there for a good long time. The padding is right - not super squishy & not hard. The rear portion of the saddle is fairly small but it's enough to \\"sit back\\" on when I want to. Like another reviewer commented, I'm not sure that the slot helps all that much but it doesn't hurt anything. If you're trying to decide between the version with & the version without the slot - I don't think it matters very much.

As I write this review, I've had this saddle for about 3 weeks & I've put about 320 miles on it. Not a ~ton~ of miles or time, but certainly enough to know if I'm going to hate it or not. I don't hate it at all. I'm glad I bought it. This is a good tri-specific saddle at a price point that regular folks like me can afford.

Another reviewer said that the seat quickly began to stink. I sweat heavily when I'm riding & I haven't experienced that problem.

review_headline: My embarrassment at admitting I own this product is outweighed by my appreciation that it exists.
review_body: What more can I say?  It gets the job done.  Comes nicely folded up.  Designed very well too.  You can imagine what could go wrong, but this is well designed, so don't worry.

product_title: Lock Alarm 8-ft Multi-Purpose Cable Lock with Built-in Alarm
review_body: I recently bought one of these in hopes of deterring a bike thief.  One crack with a hammer to expose the battery and a cut of the wire, my bike was gone.

product_title: Pearl Izumi Men's Elite Inrcool Short
review_body: the old adage applies; you get what you pay for and in this case you get a great, durable bike short at a very good price. Used these from mid summer to the present and you wouldn't know they they've been used.  Comfortable, cool in the heat and worth the dough.

product_title: Thule Parkway Hitch Mount Rack
review_body: If you have a road bike, cross bike and a mnt bike... or just 2 of the listed bikes- GET THIS RACK! then you can grab something for the road, something for a trail and friend w/ their bike and fit all four on the back! Go have some fun outside!

product_title: Coleman 12-In.Frying Pan
review_body: THIS WAS A GIFT FOR OUR GRAND DAUGHTER AND HER HUSBAND (THE COOK) THEY WERE VERY  PLEASE.  IT WAS JUST WHAT THE WANTED

product_title: Gerber Shortcut Mini-Scissor Tool
review_body: Dull knife and worthless nail file. Worst of all, the thing completely fell apart after about 10 uses. I tried to put it back together but it quickly became apparent that this should've been called the Geber Humpty Dumpty.

product_title: Nike Storm-FIT Elite Running Gloves
review_body: The seams came apart and it took a over a month to get them in the mail.  They keep your hands dry in the rain other than that they are food for nothing.  They dont even keep your hands warm.

product_title: Yakima WindJammer Airfoil
review_headline: It's a gamble if you don't know how it will work with your car...
review_body:
I know that not every review is perfect. I can't say this product is junk because it's technically not. It's a pretty simple design and can be easy to install if you are able to reach and pinch it together.

I have a 2012 Focus Hatchback and this WindJammer didn't seem to help. I have a sun/moon roof so it's simple for me to open that up and adjust the pitch of the WindJammer while driving. I was not able to find that happy medium which would make much of a difference.

It actually seemed like if I inverted the WindJammer so that it was backwards, I had better luck with noise reduction. I don't drive like this however since the thin snap together end shouldn't be facing the oncoming wind.

I'll probably keep this on my car and deal with the wind noise but I wish this had worked better. Perhaps purchasing 2 and placing them next to each other may help, but then you'd for sure have to remove them when adding a Yakima piece to the rack.

product_title: Bell Array Bike Helmet
review_headline: Awesome lid for the $$$  Giros are over rated!
review_body:
Just getting back into cycling after 25 years removed, on a budget no less (aren't we all?). I wanted a decent helmet for under $100, one that got good reviews, and one that matched the rig. I also wanted one that had the inner foam \\"finished\\" all the way down the back of the helmet. The ARRAY does all this. All the reviews you read about sizing are dead on- this lid can be dialed in to fit perfectly! FYI, unless your head is a pin or a melon, go for the \\"M\\" size. My measurement was at the upper end of the sizing range on the MEDIUM, but found out this weekend that I still had enough slack to dial it out to fit a tight cap on underneath due to the cold weather we're having. Also, the back \\"webbing\\" seems to come down a little further than other helmets, offering more protection and a more confident fit. For the $$$, you can't go wrong!

PS- Also found out that Giro and Bell are the same Co.!

product_title: Jansport Catamount Outdoor Backpack (Black)
review_body: Muy buen producto todo llego a tiempo y de la forma esperada. El vendedor es serio y cumple con lo ofertado

product_title: Case Trapper Pocket Knives
review_body: Bought this as a gift for my fiance; great idea!  He loves it, it's beautifully crafted & just the right size.

product_title: Under Armour UA Renegate Unisex Laptop Sports Backpack Book Bag-Geometric Pathern, 18" Small X 14" X 4"
review_headline: Bought Oct 2006 - Still using it today 6 years later!
review_body: This backpack is a classic! I use it all the time when I travel. Its just big enough to hold anything I'd need on a plane but not too big to get in the way or be too heavy once stuffed full. It has held up very well over 6 years and 10 countries. I'm sure I'll buy another one if this one ever gives up on me.

product_title: Blackburn Mars 3.0 Rear
review_body: Bought this to install on back of my bike - very bright, easy to install, good price, feels solid.  Bought same light a few years ago as a present for a friend and she still uses it.

product_title: iTP A3 EOS 150 Lumen 3 Outputs and Strobe CREE XP-G2 LED Keychain Flashlight 2016 Edition 1X AAA battery
review_body: I was looking for a small light to replace my Fenix Ld01 which i carry everyday and i came upon this light.  The specs seemed to be great and i like the fact that the mode sequence is different than my fenix, as this one is low med high as opposed to med low high.  It does not seem brighter than my fenix as it should be but not a main concern.  Build quality is ok the black finish is not that durable and will scratch easily.  The pocket clip which i use the most is not strong at all and it has fallen out of my pocket many times already.  One con is that this light cannot tail stand.

product_title: Planet Bike Borealis Fall/Winter Full Finger
review_body: These gloves single-handedly got me through winter biking this year. I love the design and the feel. And paired with the fleece liners, I had no problem biking with these in freezing temps for an hour or more. Below freezing, though, and my fingers started to really feel the cold after about a half an hour. As for the sizing, I'm a pretty average-hand-sized guy and the large was definitely the way to go. If I wanted to wear these without liners, a medium might have fit better, but I needed these to be big enough to fit over a liner.

product_title: ZÜM Balance Bike
review_headline: Nice concept, poor quality. Better brands out there.
review_body: We bought a Zum and a Skuut at the same time for our two sons, over a year ago, just  in case one was better quality than the other.  We are so glad we did.  The Zum has had the front bottom bolt/nut come off twice already (customer service sent us a replacement the first time, and we are currently waiting to see what they do this time), the red handles discolored in a few months, the seat cover completely wore off within months, the wood looks old, the nuts look rusty...  The Skuut is in much better shape. We store them in the same place and they have about the same wear and tear (the Zum a bit more, but not enough to justify the bad shape it's in compared to the Skuut).

product_title: Zippo Zipper Pocket Lighter, Black Ice
review_body: The lighter is great and it has an awesome design. Completely windproof and doesn't need a lot of fluid to light it.

product_title: Black Diamond Icon Headlamp
review_body: Was not my first choice but thought it was a good deal for the money. You do not get multiple mode as some others and I wish the LED light setting was brighter but it gets the job done. The bright lamp has a great beam that reaches very far. The straps are comfortable and provide a secure fit.

product_title: Sugoi Resistor Bootie
review_body: These booties are cheap and effective for rainy weather in Seattle. I spent last season soggy, so I was very glad to finally get a pair of these!

product_title: Razor Micro Force Bike, 16-Inch
review_body: My Grandson wanted a green bike for his birthday.  I looked all over for a well made, sturdy bike that could stand up to a 6 yr. olds abuse.  I knew Amazon would have what I was looking for.  And as always the delivery was quicker than anyone else can provide.  He loves his bike and he is now starting to rely less on the training wheels.  Great choice for a rough and tumble boy.

product_title: Powell-Peralta Pool Light Ripper Deck
