product_title: GORDINI Men's Challenge XII Glove
review_body: I use these globes for skiing. They keep my hands warm, dry and are very comfortable. They are soft and give a good grip.

product_title: Benchmade 147BK Nimcub Ii, Fb, Molded
review_body:
I'll spare you the details since the specs are listed above or on the Benchmade site.

This is a lightweight, extremely solid, serious piece of cutting hardware. It is not fancy, showy, or elegant. This knife commands respect only from those who are savvy knife users which is just what you would expect from a relationship between Benchade and the elite special forces.

The price of this blade is noteworthy. For a reasonable cost, one can have a defining knife that expresses all the elements necessary of a knife without the added baggage of a club or overt survival \\"knife \\"like the LMF etc.

If you are the kind of person who needs, no, demands the best in a fixed blade without having to shout out to the world about your inferiority complex, then this blade's for you. But if you need to make an obvious statement of \\"I've got a bigger knife than you\\" skip this one and search for Cold Steel, Sog, Ka-bar or Viagra.

product_title: Sierra Designs Men's Hurricane HP Jacket
review_headline: Terrific shell, might need to go one size larger
review_body: For affordability, purpose of use, and quality, this is a terrific piece of outer-shell wear. Design, materials, stitching, zippers, draw-string cords, pockets, hood, all the specs are good quality, and function well. Lightweight, too, and with its own stuff sack. Impressive.  If, after a few uses, however, this jacket ends up not keeping the rain off (nor the user inside it dry), I'll modify this review. But, so far, it's been a terrific addition to the gear kit. Mind you, this jacket won't be taken up Mt. Everest by its user, but will be used as standard rain-protective wear and for moderate backpacking, or in an emergency situation.  But, as with most waterproof gear, when it gets dirty, the jacket should be washed to keep up its waterproofing function, if not then also treated with a good, waterproofing spray. (Sometimes washing is all that's necessary to unclog the fibers and restore the material's waterproof protection.) At the time of writing this review, a Sierra Designs rep recommended using \\"NikWax Tech Wash\\" to prolong the waterproofing efficacy of their outer-shell wear; and \\"NikWax\\" or \\"McNett\\" waterproofing sprays for fabrics.  As for sizing, I don't know about other folks, but this purchaser had to go one size up from a normal large size, which is highly unusual for the person I bought it for. To be sure on the right measurements (length, shoulder room, etc.), you might want to contact Sierra Designs directly. They're friendly, courteous, and very helpful.

product_title: Emergency Poncho, Emergency Rain Gear, Weather Protection, Emergency Zone Brand
review_body: When it started to rain, I was using this poncho and it worked awesome. It kept me dry from the rain; however, it does not really work well when swimming in the lake. I was soaked instantly to my surprise. Do not purchase if you plan on using it for swimming.

product_title: Eureka! Scenic Pass 3XT - Tent (sleeps 3)
review_body: This tent is pretty good. It is lightweight, so it is good for backpacking.  It seems to pretty well constructed.  Has ample storage space.  My GF and I use it as two-person tent with gear and it is pretty good.  PROS:  -Lightweight  -well constructed  -doesn't leak  -good tent for 2 people plus gear backpacking  CONS:  -a little short for tall people  -condensation forms on insides where the rainfly doesnt cover.  Can be quite a bit of condensation.  Have been thinking about how to extend to rainfly to solve this problem.  Maybe a tarp.

product_title: GAS ONE NEW 10,000 BTU CSA List Portable Butane Gas Stove with Carrying Case CSA Listed
review_headline: Where's the carrying case and gift box?
review_body: I can't speak to the functionality as mine will be going back without being used.  The \\"gift box\\", whatever that was supposed to be, was not included.  Not a biggie as I didn't buy this for any bonus item they threw in.  However, the carrying case which it clearly states is included was not there either.  This is a deal breaker for me as it will be awkward to store, take tailgating, etc. without some type of case.

product_title: Tony Hawk Creep Boy's BMX Bike (20-Inch Wheels)
review_headline: last review is unfair to product
review_body: Both of my sons have Tony Hawk bikes.  They have been riding them for close to two years now and we have put any money into them, other than tires, and that is only because they ride so much.  I am only writing this review because i believe the only other one I saw here was unfair.  These Tony Hawk bikes are not built for competetion or for professional riding, they are meant for younger kids or kids that just want a nice bike to ride, and they are priced accordingly.  My kids have put ridiculous amounts of miles on thier bikes, and they ride them a little rough, mostly on paved surfaces, but they do ride through the woods, on trails and over small jumps.  Thier bikes have not broken once.  Bottom line, if you are going to do some serious bmx riding, or are a professional rider, then buy a professional bike.  If you are a parent looking for an affordable bike for your kid that is stylish and durable, this is the bike for you.

product_title: StrapGear Utility Strap with Matching Color Hooks 12-Pack
review_body: I bought a multi-size 12-pack at the Outdoor Show. These don't stretch as long as a bungee (only get to half again their original length,) so their uses are different than bungee. So far, they've worked well for attaching stuff to my mountain bike. With great result, I replaced some bungee's and string in my camping gear with some of the long ones. There are a couple in my shed holding stuff on the wall. I think when you find someplace where these work well (and if you're like me, you will) you will not want to use anything else.

product_title: Swiss Stop Disc #10 MTB Disc Brake Pads fit Magura Marta, Magura Marta SL.
review_headline: FAR BETTER Than Magura's Own Pads!
review_body: After going through countless Magura Performance(Organic) and Sintered pads...I have finally found the FINEST hydraulic brake pads for the (pre-2009)Magura Marta SL MTB brake system. Don't let Magura tell you otherwise - the Swiss-made Ceramic compound offers the best of BOTH WORLDS....with superior heat dissipation, wear, anti squeal and virtually fade-free downhill operation. These pads outlast Magura's own best pads a whopping 2:1! Don't let the slight premium deter you...they are WELL WORTH IT!!!!

product_title: prAna Hemp Chalk Bags
review_body: As a starting rock climber, I found this back to fulfill it's need in holding chalk. I've just been bouldering and at the place I go no one else has a bag like mine so I like how it's easy to find on the ground.

product_title: Pearl iZUMi Men's P.R.O Barrier Lite Cycling Jacket
review_body: It is a good quality wind jacket and packs tight occupying only 1/2 a rear pocket. My only gripe is that it flaps around a lot. I'm 5'11", 175 with a long torso and I got a large. Perhaps I should have gone for the medium.

product_title: Coleman RoadTrip Wheeled Carry Case
review_headline: The grill does fit in the case.
review_body: I've read many reviews about this case being \\"too small or \\"a snug fit\\".  If you remember putting your grill together, the handle slides in and locks into place.  If you press the two buttons that lock the handle in place and push the handle down, it will retract down further allowing for a perfect fit.

product_title: Sunlite Laser Streamers
review_body: bought to spruce up a secondhand girls bike. look great and go on okay but takes some strength to remove old grips .Since I bought new grips I just cut off the old.

product_title: Fox Men's 360 Vortex Full Finger Glove
review_body:
I love these gloves. I wear them for bicycling. They're very comfortable, fabric is just stretchy enough. Normally I need a 13 (XXL) because of big palms, but these as a 12 fit without much trouble.
The palms and fingers have leather (or leatherish) on them for good grip and comfort. The top fabric is fairly breathable, and keeps your hands nice and cool. They're good for biking down to about 40-50 degrees. I love the design, think they look awesome.

product_title: Cateye LD130 Taillight
review_body:
I bought this as a replacement for another (cheap) tail light that stopped working after one of many rides in the rain.
I didn't want anything fancy: just something to keep me safe for my evening commute. No one has hit me yet.

I was pleasantly surprised at the battery life and the security of the attachment (at first I was wary). Plus it's made it through a number of rainstorms without issue. Operation is very simple: the easily located side button means I can reach back and turn it on and off if light conditions or road conditions change.

The strap to secure it on the bike was too short for affixing it my seat post-- but there are usually other options. Overall it's a good light for the price.

Shipping was (as usual through Amazon) prompt.

product_title: Finish Line Grunge Brush Chain: Gear and Chain Cleaning Tool
review_body: it does the job nothing really special about it wish it was a bit thinner and came with a few replacement brushes. I cleaned my chain once with it and the bristles don't look like they will last much longer

product_title: Fenix HP10 7 Level 225 Lumen LED Headlamp
review_body: I do a lot of caving and all my chores are done in the dark and this light is awesome bar none. Good light close and great light far, good mix. I have had it for almost a year and if you want to see in the dark this is the light.

product_title: Flybar Foam Master Pogo Stick
review_body: I bought this for my 8 year old. He is a big kid, 82 lbs., but I think he is still a little too light for the pogo stick. He can't quite get a good bounce out of it. On the other hand, I love it! I can bounce and bounce and bounce.

product_title: Bridgedale Coolmax Liner 2-Pack Socks
review_body:
These socks are terrific! I've never had a pair of liners before and I can't believe I have lived without them.
My feet sweat a good bit throughout the day and this tends to leave me feeling cold. These liners do an incredible job of pulling that moisture to the outer sock. Incredible and very comfortable.

product_title: Ultimate Direction Classic 26-Ounce Bottle, Granite
review_body: I received this 26-ounce bottle few weeks ago. [[ASIN:B001KTQT5U Ultimate Direction Classic Bottle]]  Pros: The bottle design is so attractive.  Cons: Awful smells from inside of the bottle.  After received this bottle, I started to fight this smell. It is worst plastic container smell. product_title: Paracord Survival Bracelet with 20mm Compass Desert Camouflage 8 Inches (by Perpetual Revolution)
review_body: The bracelet arrived very fast and the quality is just great.(makes me want to learn how to make them myself!) The compass works great, and this is a perfect gift for a military person. (My hubby is a Marine and loved it)

product_title: Texsport Rechargeable Electric Air Pump to Inflate/Deflate Inflatable Boats, Mattresses and other Recreational Inflatables
review_body: This pump is a great size and powerfull.  It blew up a hi-rise twin bed in a couple of minutes.The only negative is the attachment nozzles do not lock on so I found they fell off easily.

product_title: Currie Technologies eZip Men's Trailz Electric Bicycle
review_headline: Pretty great for what I use it for
review_body:
My review will be short and sweet.

Pros:
Any round trip under 10 miles will be a breeze as long as you're doing some pedaling
The price is low
I've spent about $0.15 on electricity getting to and from work over the past two weeks while I would have paid $25 for gas.
I was able to put it together very easily with the included tools

Cons:
Any trip over 20 miles and the one battery is not able to sufficiently power the motor even to help negate the weight of the whole \\"electric\\" part
Its difficult to attach anything to the bike since it's a bit of a weird shape. I'm using a ULock, but I basically have it attached around the bottom of the seat with the \\"U\\" resting on top of the battery carriage. Attaching a rear light was awkward as well and I ended up mounting it to the very back of the battery carriage and I always worry I'm going to knock it off when I swing my leg over.
I do wish there was a better battery life meter rather than just the 3 lights

product_title: CamelBak 0.75- Liter Stainless Steel Better Bottle
review_headline: For months, this has been next to me
review_body:
I bought this bottle because of CamelBak's reputation, despite its expensive price tag. I also bought an insulation sleeve [[ASIN:B0019DCDIY CamelBak 0.75 Liter Insulated Bottle Carrier]]. This item was going to be my main source of hydration for everyday (and nightly) use.

After a couple months, I was surprised by leakage from its threads. One day, I left it in my car's backseat bench only to find a very wet patch of car seat. It seemed to become more frequent. It would drip from its threads while I drank from it in a tilted position every so often. I lost trust in this bottle-- it always had to be upright, never on its side. Keep in mind that this was never dropped or damaged.

I posted a message on CamelBak's Facebook page, and they contacted me very quickly. They sent me a brand-new sealed lid (and mouthpiece) at no charge for me. They are absolutely great in customer service-- for that, I would recommend their brand.

As for this bottle, even with a new lid, it began leaking again. I close it very snugly each time it gets filled. I should have bought an UnderArmour or different CamelBak bottle. I decided not to complain to Camelbak again. It seems my next bottle will be a different model, as this one consistently has leakage problems. Bottles are not supposed to leak.

I might mention that this bottle's mouthpiece catches dust and fuzz. This bottle is not easy to clean. You might consider buying replacement mouthpieces if you are a germ conscious person-- soaking it hardly seems sufficient. I follow their instructions on how-to. I put dish soap inside this canister, fill it with some hot water, and add its straw and mouthpiece. I shake it for 30 seconds then let it sit for 10 minutes. After rinsing it really well, I still taste soap, perhaps from its mouthpiece, which is hard to rinse.

I came back to edit this review because this product deserves even worse of a reputation. I switched back to my old (very leaky) lid, and it is very hard to suck for some unknown reason to me. This makes it harder to drink, which means I am drinking less-- that's not good. At this point, I would rather use a glass than my Camelbak .75L Better Bottle.se of a reputation. review_body: I purchased this jacket after testing products from Marmot, Patogonia and LL Bean.  I wanted a full-length (not a vest) down jacket with high-loft down that I could use for skiing, hiking, cold-weather dog walks etc.  I live in NC and its been so warm this year that I haven't really tested it in cold weather so I can't rate the performance here as much as I can the fit. product_title: Park Tool Tire & Tube Repair Kit - TR-1C
review_body:
I purchased my first PT (Park Tools) TR-1 repair kit back in 2007 and it has so far been the only set I have purchased. If you ask me how many times I have used them in the last 5 years, I can sadly say that it has been more than I would like. Not sure anyone enjoys changing tires. However, this trusty kit has never failed me once.

Negatives:
- Not enough patches?

Positive:
- I interchange my MTB with slicks and fatties constantly and without any damage to my spokes, rims, tubes, tires or the levers. My road bike has the same constant success. All three tire levers have lasted me 5 years and still going strong.

- The small metal plate within the plastic case is a life saver due to ensuring that you can safely scruff (to allow for better sticking power of the patch) the tube at the puncture site to ensure a longer but still TEMPORARY seal.

- I have had issues with the Slime patch kit I purchased after running out of the PT ones with the kit, however, I rarely made it home on one Slime patch. This has never been the case with these TEMPORARY patches from PT. They, unlike Slime patches, never slide around between the tire and tube. They hold strong even when it is over 100 degrees outside and with many more miles still to go.

Note:
Looking for a more PERMANENT patching system? You will probably be happier with the [[ASIN:B000JF2ZB8 Park Tool VP-1 Vulcanizing Patch Kit]].

If you have never used this type of item before then I would recommend this brand for the quality of the patches and levers. I would also say to practice changing tubes and how to properly locate a puncture along with feeling the inside of your tire. After-all, you might patch the puncture with talent but if you fail to get that piece of glass out, you will be getting some more practice as soon as you jump back onto the saddle. Take your time at first and you will notice that as the days go on it all becomes muscle memory and you can get yourself back on the road or trail quicker.

product_title: Jeep Compass Men's Hybrid Bike (700c Wheels, 22-Inch Frame)
review_body:
DO NOT BUY THIS BIKE, OR ANY JEEP BIKE!

I rode this bicycle for two months before returning it. The first problem I encountered was a clicking pedal. Kent Bicycles promptly mailed me two new pedals, which I installed. Curious, I took apart the clicking pedal. The manufacturer left out some ball bearings. It was a bad omen.

When I put this bike away, I often lifted the front wheel. While turning freely, the front wheel made odd noises too, inconsistent with ball bearing operation. After getting a flat from a thorn, I took the back tire off and patched it. While I was at it, I removed the front wheel and tried to disassemble the axle and bearings. The nut securing the racer was so tight I couldn't remove it, but ruined a thin bearing wrench. The other bearing race was 13 mm, while this one was 13.5 mm. One side had 9 ball bearings, the other had ten. It gets much worse. After putting everything back together, the noise persisted. It was necessary to tear the axle apart and clean all the grease and dirt thoroughly to see that the wrong race had been used. Bearings were running on the edge of one race instead of their proper channel. The bearing race was already damaged and ultimately would have failed and perhaps locked up the front wheel. Imagine that happening on a steep downhill at speed with potentially fatal consequences.

Such shoddy manufacturing is inexcusable in my opinion.

product_title: Mongoose Lark Girls' Bike (18-Inch Wheels)

Purchased this for my recently turned 7 year old and she absolutely loves the bike! She is 3'7\\" so she is one her \\"tippy-toes\\" with the lowest seat setting but she rides it perfect. The bike came partially disassembled (only had to put the front tire, handle bar set, and the foot pedals on) so assembly wasn't too difficult. review_body: We used these burners during a recent power outage and they worked perfectly. The only thing that could be improved is the case isn't big enough for the burner. review_body:

Jessica says: \\"Thank you for your email, the layback seatpost is fo BMX racing they are made to not be sat on for long periods of time, they are used for jumping. I have contacted amazon and told them to varify that in the listing since they have control of the listings and pictures. If there is anything else please let me know thanks and have a great evening!\\"

review_body: nice product, hooks could have a little more angle to them and directions could be a little clearer on exactly where to measure the hooks themselves, the rope could be a little thicker to catch in the locking system.  over all not a bad product.

product_title: Omega Pacific Figure 8 Belay/Rappel Device
review_body: Nice, smooth rope movement makes it a great device to use for a rappel, wide enough for double ropes. product_title: Camelbak Day Star 70 oz Hydration Pack
review_body: Bought this pack specifically for day hikes and I have not been disappointed. product_title: Thule 2193 Fit Kit for 400XT and Rapid Aero Foot
review_body:
I bought this fit kit when switching my Thule roof rack from an 09 Altima to a 2012 Honda Accord. First of all, Thule's website wasn't helpful at all when trying to find the proper kit to use. I somehow stumbled onto the proper kit from some other site. I am using the 400XT feet but Thule seems to think everyone is now using the Aero or Podium feet for some reason.
Installation should really take only about 30 minutes when changing over a roof rack from one car to another. Thule's instructions for the installation should be taken with a MAJOR grain of salt, perhaps even a 1 pound package of the stuff.That's why I took off 1 star. There were just two good measurements given in the Thule instructions: Distance from the windshield to mount the front feet and the distance from the front load bar to the back one.. If you move the feet to the suggested distance (side to side)on the load bars, you'll find it will be either too far apart or too short. My suggestion is to manually move the feet to the correct distance by eye and disregard what Thule says for this particular measurement. A helper during this part of the install would be great if one's available. The same is true with the rear load bar and foot positioning. Thule's measurement here was way off, too. OK, now that that's out of the way, let me continue... Once you're happy with the placement of the rubber foot pads, you can now attach the clamps to the underside of the door opening and to the foot. Keep in mind that the front clamps are shorter than the rear onces so be aware of the clamp numbers in the directions. At first, it seemed all the clamps were too short. But, once you insert the clamp screw and begin to ratchet it down, the clamp slides easily into place inside the foot. Once all four clamps are tightened down, you're finally in business!
This installation is the third one for this roof rack but somehow the most complicated. But, once it's finished, you can remove the entire rack, if necessary, just by unscrewing the four clamps and spreading them outward a bit. It didn't help, either, that it was about 28 degrees when I did this and my pinkies were getting numb!
A big thank you to Amazon! I am a Prime member and got this fit kit in just two days, from AZ to PA!ust by unscrewing the four clamps and spreading them outward a bit. review_body: I bought this grinder several years ago for home and camping use. The grinder is difficult to hold while grinding, since you have to fit it in a cup while turning the crank. I was sick of the awkwardness of grinding, so I never fixed it. IMHO, fresh ground coffee on the trail isn't worth the weight of the grinder. Just grind before you go, and get a nicer hand grinder for daily use. We've been happy with our Hario grinder. Nice and easy to hold while using.

product_title: Extrasport Children's Type II PFD
review_headline: Great life jacket for canoeing, kayaking or canoeing or for fidgety children who take off their life jackets without permission
review_body: I bought this for a 9 year girl who is 4'9\\" and weights about 70 lbs meaning she is pretty skinny for her age.  She outgrew her Stearns Heads-Up life jacket when she had a growth spurt and became too tall for it.  We went to the store to try on some life jackets but whenever I picked her up by grabbing the shoulders of the life vest, all of the vests in her weight range would ride up above her ears.  Many of them would slip right off of her if she held her arms up.  I was afraid that if she fell into the water, the vest would slip right off.  With this vest, we don't have that problem thanks to the crotch strap.  At first I was afraid that it would be too uncomfortable for her but she wears tight fitting swim bottoms which help her from getting a wedgie and she hasn't complained about it yet.  I also feel that she is safer in this vest with the extra flotation around the head/neck.  She plans on her wearing this vest when she is canoeing, kayaking, or rafting.  The inside of the life jacket says that it is not for high speed activities but has been rated for 50 MPH impact so I have no issues with her wearing it while tubing or other higher speed water activities.  I want to give a better description of this life jacket since the current one to me is incomplete.  Please note that even though you are buying this from Amazon, it is actually sold by Altrec.  The Youth model is a Type II vest not a Type III vest like the Mustang Youth Lil' Legends life jacket.  It is made up of a total of four of \\"Gaia\\" environmentally friendly foam pieces, two for the flotation collar and two for the front.  The front foam is very thick, probably twice as thick as the foam on the Mustang Lil' Legends, but it's not quite as large area wise.  It is shorter in length than other vests and the foam doesn't really go under her arms.    It might seem at first that this vest doesn't fit since it doesn't go down to the waist but it is more important for a life jacket to fit the chest so it doesn't ride up then the length of the torso.    On the inside right front of the vest there is a place to put the name of who the life jacket belongs to.  There is large white grab loop at the top (a bit larger than the Mustang Lil' Legends) for easy fishing and storage.  The white crotch strap buckles in the middle of the back with the excess just dangling.  The white waist strap is fully adjustable and the female end is connected on the left side near the zipper allowing for easier buckling.  The front large white teeth plastic zipper is easy to secure and won't corrode like a metal zipper.  The zipper has a loop on it so if you wanted to attach something like a lanyard or whistle you could.  Some important things the inside of the vest says: US Coast Guard approved wearable device for uninspected commercial vessels less than 40 feet in length not carrying passengers for hire, and for recreational boats.  Not approved for use on personal water craft, for water skiing, or similar towed uses.  Strength tested at 50MPH - Not tested for personal protection from impact.  Fasten all closures and adjust for snug fit.  Excessive ride-up will impair performance.  Out of curiosity, I put the life jacket on her, buckled everything up, then doubled up one of the ties, pushed it through the opening and used the other tie to tie and secure it off.  I then asked her to try and take off her life jacket.  She was able to unbuckle her waist strap quickly but then to unzip it, since I had tied it using the ties near her chin, it took quite a bit longer for her to undo the knot and get it unzipped.  It also took her quite a bit of time to be able to undue her crotch strap since it was high up her back and not easily reachable for her.  Fortunately my daughter does not mind wearing her life jacket, in fact she still likes to swim with one even though she knows how to swim, but if we have anyone over that wants to take their life jacket off this would be a good model to use.  Pros:  The crotch strap insures the life jacket stays in place under the water and not ride up above her ears which is difficult to find for her weight (50-90 lbs).  The grab loop on top gives an easy way to \\"fish\\" her out of the water if need be (which we had to do when she was younger) and also makes for convenient storage mechanism.  If you have a child that likes to take their life jacket off while you're not looking this has many features which deters them from doing that.  Additionally, each of these following pros makes it a good choice for when she is paddling.  It is a \\"shorter\\" vest which makes it much more comfortable when she is sitting down because it doesn't get pushed up to her chin by her legs.  Since the foam is concentrated at the chest, this means there is a lot of room under her arms along with less material in the back making it retain less heat and easier to paddle.  Reflective strips on the flotation collar and bright colors create good visibility of her in an emergency.  Cons: The vest is a bit more difficult to put on since the crotch strap buckles and adjusts in the back.  She will have to leave the crotch strap buckled, step into the strap and pull up the vest up if she wants to put the jacket on herself.  Also, if she is laying on her back the back buckle does dig a bit into her back.  With the flotation collar, it does make it a bit more difficult for her to sit in a high back chair, she has to flip the collar up to be more comfortable and again the back buckle can be uncomfortable.  Another thing, the ties at the top can \\"tickle\\" her chin.  Finally, Amazon only sold it in one color but you might be able to find it another color somewhere else.  We tried this out at the pool and it did flip her on her back when she started off face down in the water or jumped in the pool and relaxed.  This will be a good thing if we are ever in an accident and she is unconscious.  She swam around in it and it seemed to fit her well and not ride up.  After about an hour she companied that her back was hurting where the buckle connection was so we took of her vest and saw a small red mark there.  She was just wearing her swimsuit without a rash guard or something like that which may have helped.  She wanted to continue to swim so she put on her Mustang Youth Lil' Legends life jacket by herself and was good for the rest of the day.  She said that the Extrasport vest would be best for when we went canoeing, kayaking or rafting but prefers her Lil' Legends for other water activities such as swimming and boating.  I hope this helps, and remember, buckle them up.  Safety isn't always comfortable but it's necessary.

product_title: Smith Snow Goggles Scope Pro AirFlow Series Gloss White RC36 Lens NEW
review_body: I have been using Oakley goggles for years, but after I got a new Smith helmet, the Oakley's didn't seal correctly and left me with freeze head. I purchased the Smith Scope Pro goggles in hopes that they would be a good, affordable replacement and fit with my helmet better. They do fit the helmet shape, but they look rather cheap and are nothing special. I decided to return them and shop around for end of season deals. I ended up getting the Smith Heiress goggles for only $5 more. These goggles are probably fine for an occasional skier, but I would recommend an upgrade for anyone using them more frequently.

product_title: Columbia Women's Suspiciously Sweet Long Sweater Fleece
review_body: I was looking for a warm jacket for my wife that was not bulky or looked like we just got off the slope.  The jacket is light and very moveable even while driving, and can be worn to semi-fancy outings. When asked I am told the jacket is very warm and very light to wear.  This is an excellent jacket for women who want style without losing warmth.  It looks great, can be worn to different types of venues or functions and is extremely warm.  Well worth the price.

product_title: Spider-Man 28-Inch Skateboard, Helmet, and Protective Pad Combo Pack (Colors May Vary)
review_body: This was a great price for this package deal.  Got it for Christmas present and my grandson loved it.  Would buy it again.

product_title: Schwinn Airacuda Bike (Blue, 16-Inch)
review_body:
My wife and I bought two of these bikes for our 5yr old twin boys. These bikes are heavy and tire lugs are a little too much for a beginning biker. Our boys were extremely strong riders coming off their 12\\" Gary Fisher bikes. They are working through the extra weight but a less experienced little rider may be frustrated. The training wheels are extremely weak and have to be straightened after every ride. Our boys weigh 40 lbs and these will have to be replaced. One of the forks was bent and that made the wheel assembly more difficult.

Update...it has been almost 1 year since we bought these bikes. I upgraded their training wheels which they used through the summer. We recently took the training wheels off and they are riding on two (I added a kickstand). After initial reservations I am pleased with the bikes and they should serve them well over the next two years.

product_title: Suisse Sport Adventurer Sleeping Bag
review_body:
For those just skimming reviews:

Pros:
Very compressible, can get it to be nearly as small as a NCAA football
Very Lightweight

Cons:
Made for a small framed man or an average woman/child
Not warm unless used well above temperature rating
Zipper gets caught on fabric CONSTANTLY
Fabric near zipper tears VERY easily

This bag is a bargain if you are a small man or woman but I am a 6 ft and 190 lbs man... this bag is too small for me. I had a very difficult time moving my hands up to my neck without feeling like I was going to rip the bag.

Now, with it being a shrink wrap, you would think that it might at least keep you warm... No. It is incorrectly rated. This bag will keep you warm in 45 degrees and up but don't even try to bring it out when it is near freezing, I learned the hard way. I was stuffing \\"Hot-Hands\\" in my clothes and practically spooning my buddy to stave off hypothermia. Finally I got wise and gave up on the bag all together, donning my complete outer-wear suit.

Perhaps the most disappointing thing about this bag is that the fabric is very poorly put together. I am no expert on seams and stitching but seams should not rip on first use under normal conditions. The fabric constantly gets caught in the zipper too. I have had tons of bags where the zipper gets caught in the fabric, it is a common problem but none have been as bad as this one. You seriously cannot move the zipper an inch without it getting stuck and then good luck trying to get the fabric out of the zipper.

Overall: Only get this bag if you are under 150 lbs, don't plan on using it in cold weather, and you know how to mend seams. I think this bag is a great bargain for the wife or kid to use in spring or fall weather and so I gave the bag it's only 2 stars for at least fitting a niche but it lost 2 for not being advertised as such. This is NOT a winter bag for Men, it is a moderate temperature bag for women and children. The fifth star was lost because of product quality. There is no excuse for it ripping on the first use.no excuse for it ripping on the first use.

Not only did the mesh pocket inside the main pouch tear, but the stitching for the actual shoulder straps has started to come undone. I haven't bothered to put more than 20 pounds in it as of now, nor have I abused it beyond taking a quick jog. product_title: Tour Hockey Adult Grunt 50Bx Hip Pads
review_body:
These are not a replacement for the outer hockey shorts that you normally wear. They have the same function in that they have padding but I bought them and went to practice and they told me that I looked naked. Evidently sports teams use these and then they have colored covers that they put over them. For now I just wear them under sweatpants and that works fine, other than looking a little funny. You might still want to get some jocks that have the velcro on them to hold up your socks. (Don't work if you're wearing sweats, obviously)

As far as the product itself, I'd be careful washing it since the mesh seems a bit weak and flimsy, but for the price they're actually really good. They are very comfortable. I bought the small size. I'm 6' 1 1/2\\" 170 lbs. and that was a good fit although a tad on the short side they said.

product_title: Diamondback Edgewood LX Men's Sport Hybrid Bike (2011 Model, 700c Wheels), Burgundy
review_body:
It had been about 10 years since I'd ridden my 80's Schwinn World Sport road bike, and was very disappointed, after a few recent rides, to find my older body not liking it much anymore. So, I began looking for a new, more comfortable bike. I decided on a hybrid, and read reviews on every one I could find in the $200 - $500 range. I decided on the 2011 Diamondback Edgewood LX, 19\\". I checked and rode all the big time names in local bike shops, but the Diamondback gave me the most bang for the buck.

The comfort of the Edgewood is amazing after spending my life on a road bike. After 3 weeks and 60+ miles on pavement, and bike trails, I love it. While not as fast as my road bike, it moves very well, no problem maintaining 10 - 15 mph on fairly level ground, good for me at my age and state of fitness. :)

I'm 5'10\\" 32\\" inseam and the large size 19\\" frame fits me well. The 17\\" felt cramped. All of the components are working well, but shifters needed small adjustments after 2 weeks. Cable stretch?

Only one thing I'm watching, the front shocks have compressed a bit from when they were new, I'm not sure if this is normal, so I'll keep an eye on it.

Overall, I love the bike, it's a joy to ride. I like it so much, I've given the old Schwinn World Sport away as I can't see myself riding it again. I will miss that bike.

product_title: JanSport T501 Superbreak Backpack - Black/Verdant Green Break Beat
review_body: My daughter had been searching for the right backpack in our local stores and was unable to find one in-stock when she found one she liked. I decided to check Amazon and low and behold I was able to get her the one she originally wanted at a much better price.

product_title: Schwinn Men's Broadway Bicycle (Blue)
review_body:
Got my bike yesterday and it took me about an hour/hour and a half to set-up.
I really like this bike: it has a nice upright position (much nicer for my back) and even though it is not the lightest bicycle it is fast and the gear ratios are well-designed. Good value.

product_title: Bazoongi Special Edition Garden Cottage Tent
review_body: I ordered this playhouse for our 14 month old granddaughter--she is younger than the recommended age for this product, but is always supervised. She LOVES crawling inside things, and is crazy for flowers, so this seemed like a good choice.   We opened it up. All parts were there, and it easily assembled in about 2 minutes. Very easy. Colorful and bright, and the flowers velcro on, so they can be rearranged for fun. The fabric seems like a pretty indestructible synthetic.  The floor doesn't make a lot of sense. It's kind of slippery, and doesn't seem to add to the experience. We took it out, and placed the house on carpet, so it's secure to walk on and soft to land on.   The most important thing: the baby crawled right in, loved playing peekaboo with the doors and windows, and threw herself against the walls without harm to either the house or herself. (Again, we were there, ready to intercede!) This little house is a lot of fun for a really reasonable price.

product_title: Razor Rip-Rider 360 Drifting Ride-On
review_body: I order this for my sons 9th birthday right before Christmas.  He has really enjoyed it along with many other kids (even big ones). Definitely recommend, it was not hard to assemble either!

product_title: Planet Bike Superflash Turbo bike tail light
review_headline: Awesome quality light and worth the price. Very bright visible flashing pattern! But still has minor problem.
review_body:
Hi everyone
I have been using this light for already 1 year on my 28 miles round trip commute to my university 3 days a week and I am very satisfied with the brightness and the quality of this product. I tested the brightness of this light with a friend at night by having my friend ride about a mile away in a straight line. I was very impressed with brightest of this light because it can be seen as far as a mile away. I specifically only use the flashing mode on this light because I feel the strong point of the light is the flashing pattern. The steady mode is bright, but does not grab as much attention as the flashing pattern. The light and the mounting I feel is particularly sturdy because the batteries does not fall out of its casing and the light does not go off when I hit a bump because I had bad experience from buying cheap $1 light from 99 cents only store. Anyway the only minor flaw I experience like others who review this light is that the light does go out sometimes. However, I don't think it is the problem of the batteries coming lose from its casing. I think the problem is when the batteries power is very low after a long period of use. I check the voltage of the batteries myself with a battery measuring voltage device. After charging or changing batteries with new power, the light works like a charm without going off. I highly recommended you to buy this light because it can be mounted in different places and it can also be cheaper than the other rechargeable USB bicycle lights by using rechargeable batteries for this light. The bright and long last light will help for serious commuters who needs to be seen far away. Just be sure to check the voltage of your batteries and change them. Feel free to comment and ask questions. I will respond happily.

product_title: Mountain House Chicken Teriyaki with Rice
review_body:
I have been backpacking in the wilderness for almost ten years and go out every month throughout the year. So needless to say I have purchased dozens of different manufacturers dehydrated meals.

Mountain House is not only BY FAR consistently the best tasting brand, but their packaging is top notch as well.

The PRO series is worth the slight extra expense as it packs better, keeps better, is easier to cook and comes in VERY HANDY one person servings which most other meals do not.

With all of that said, the lasagna is my FAVORITE meal of all of Mountian House's offerings.

My only complaint is that the cheese sticks to your fork really well and is tough to wash off.

The overall flavor, quantity of meat, cheese, and pasta are all excellent.

Please note these meals are specially formulated for what your body needs in the backcountry after a long day of physical exertion. I do not recommend these meals for casual dining at home.

product_title: iBert Safe-T-Seat Front Child Seat (Green,38-Pounds limit)
review_body: I purchased our Ibert safety seat in 2008, for use with my then two year old daughter.  Before purchasing it, we used a burley pull behind bike carrier as well as a traditional rear mounted bike carrier.  The hills in Folsom are fantastic, so although she liked the single burley - I could not pull the weight up the hills on most rides.  Although the rear mounted bike seat seemed to be easy to use - my daughter hated it and it made every ride a chore.  From her very first ride on this seat to the last she loved it.  We were able to mount it on a trek mountain bike, a bianchi commuter bike and a beach cruiser - no problems.  I saved the seat when she moved into the tag along.  Now my son uses this very seat and he loves to bike.  I started riding with him when he was 10 months old.  The best part of this bike seat is you can upgrade it with the newer parts - there is a steering wheel, padding (ours was not padded) and a newer harness...  Now my bike is a bicycle built for three baby on front, momma doing the work, and daughter trailing behind on her tag along.

product_title: Avenir Coil Combo Cable Locks
review_body: Works really well! Keeps my bike safe, and allows me to change the combination freely. Only thing is that the holder doesnt fit on my bike, but I compensate for that by wrapping it around my bike's drink holder.

product_title: Pearl Izumi Women's Symphony Thermal Jersey
review_headline: Not what I was looking for..
review_body:
I actually returned this jersey because I ordered it in a larger size based on reviews saying it runs small but I found it to be true to size and therefore too big. I also was not a fan of the fabric, it was soft but it was that shiny almost basketball shorts type of material and I just did not care for that or how it looked on.
The quality of the product, however, looked great - I have a lot of Pearl Izumi cycling apparel items and like how they design them to fit AND flatter women!

product_title: Outdoor Research Peruvian Hat
review_body:
Be careful as there are two different items pictured. (with and without chin straps) I thought I was buying a decent-looking Peruvian Hat with ear flaps with a slightly rounded fuller dome. The black one with no chin straps. I received a black one but the item is the coyote-color version. (from the pictures). It's not round and full and has these elastic chin straps. Maybe I'm the fool for not realizing a Peruvian hat wouldn't have chin straps.

As far as fit goes, I have a large head and most micro fleece caps don't cover my ears completely. That's why I purchased this item. I will say though that if you purchase the large, it should fit a large head nicely. But the inside of the cap is kind of rough. At least rough for a guy with thinning hair that keeps it cut very short. The inside isn't micro-fleece. It feels almost like some kind of foam. The inside seams in my other fleece caps are stitched down smooth where you can't feel them on your scalp. The inside seams in this one stick out quite a bit. Nearly 1/4\\" or 4-5 mm. It was quite uncomfortable.

The elastic chin strap is probably effective in blistering cold winds, but it was also pretty uncomfortable.

Thank you Amazon for having such a painless return process.

product_title: ExOfficio Men's Give-n-Go Boxer Brief
review_body: These are awesome, they feel great, they're very breathable and really high quality.  Obviously you have to be a fan of boxer briefs to really appreciate them.  I'm actually torn between these and the Under Armor O Boxerjocks.  I can't decide which one I like better but I use them both equally, they're both very nice.  I think these have better airflow than the boxerjocks though.  I have noticed myself reaching for these over the boxerjocks when traveling, though I can't really explain why.

product_title: niceEshop SHOPPING Motorbike Alarm Security Bicycle Lock Moped Bike
review_body: This alarm is very cheaply made. While installing the alarm on my bike the nut actually tighned right thru to the other side.

product_title: Fox River Three Layer Ragg Glove
review_headline: Lifetime New England resident, wish I found these gloves sooner
review_body: I highly recommend these, I have never worn warmer gloves except for waterproof  ski gloves. These are amazing and the liner is so soft. They are pretty large, my guess is most women would need no larger than a small. Not attractive at all, but thats not why I bought them.

product_title: Paul Jr. Designs Coleman RoadTrip Grill
review_body: Really unique black and chrome grill. Impressed with the size for it being a portable grill, but still able to fold up very small. High quality.

product_title: Tacx Carbon Assembly Compound
review_body: ...if you have a newer model road bike. Any time metal is on metal, you need lube. When it's titanium, you need Ti prep. When it's carbon-carbon, you need TacX. The reason? Most lubes are hydrocarbon based. Put that stuff on carbon fiber parts, and it literally melts the carbon fibers. No kidding, it does. TacX is carbon paste compound, which has no HC's, so it prevents the parts from bonding, making disassembly possible. While it may seem expensive stuff, carbon bike parts are MORE expensive. So, as I said, you probably need this if you have carbon components on your bike. If you use regular lube or anti-seize, you're asking for trouble.

product_title: Avenir Regular Schrader Valve 700c Tube (700x25-35 27x1-1/4)
review_body: I have ordered Avenir tubes many times and have never had a problem with them. They are standard tubes, not the lightest or heaviest, and work well if installed correctly. I have yet to have any problem with them. Like any inner tube for a bicycle, you need to make sure the tire is free from debris or sharp objects inside the tire and rim before installing a new tube, as well as make sure your rim strip is correctly aligned. I use puncture resistant tires (Continental Gatorskins) so I rarely get flats. So far the tubes are holding up very well. I think improper installation or using cheapo tires will cause any tube to flat (nothing is 100%), and so far, these ones are holding up quite well after a few 100 commuting miles in the City.

product_title: 3/2mm Men's O'Neill Reactor Full Wetsuit - XX-Large (2XL)
review_body: He loves it.  Fits perfectly.  No stretching or sagging.  Molds to the body.  Also, very easy to clean.  Dries quickly.  Fantastic product.

product_title: Rollerblade Men's Fusion X3 Urban Skate
review_body: The skates are great, fast enough, very comfortable and the shock eraser really works, I recommend to use the break if you don't have any previous experience with skates because these ones are pretty fast.

product_title: Topeak Dual Touch Bike Storage Stand
review_body: I love this product! I've been using it for several months now and it's worked very well. I have it set up in the garage with a normal concrete floor and a slightly textured ceiling and it seems to be holding up very well. I initially had a minor issue. Contacted customer service and they were fantastic and went the extra mile to make sure I was satisfied. This was worth every cent.

product_title: Giro Skyla Sport Bike Womens Helmet
review_headline: Great helmet at the right pice
review_body: I was so glad to find a helmet that was small enough to fit my head.  I should have purchased a women sized helment before.  It is light weight, comfortable, and easily adjuste

product_title: 66 North Boy's Baldur Jacket
review_body: In general I'm a fan of 66N.  My son loves this jacket... so much we bought a second in the next size up.  Great quality and great style.  Well worth the $$.

product_title: Shimano Single-Speed Freewheels
review_body: Got this in the mail yesterday to turn my road bike into a single speed and I have to say it's great. Much quieter than the five geared freewheel that was on my bike before and is quiet as can be coast. I am a happy guy with a single speed bike now.

product_title: Lucky Bums Snow Sports Helmet
review_headline: Nice Looking Helmet - Size way off
review_body: Like many others have mentioned, the size of these helmets is way off.  Thinking that we'd be safe moving up to a Large for my wife whose head measures 58.5 cm, we were disappointed to find that it was still a tight, uncomfortable fit.  The dial in the back does hit your neck weird also.  I can' recommend the product based on fit, but otherwise a nice, inexpensive helmet.  But then again fit is a big deal.  We went with a medium Giro instead.  Night and day difference, but then again it was twice as much.  Happy wife - happy life!  We sent back the helmet and was refunded the purchase price without issue.

product_title: Solo Stove Lite - Compact Wood Burning Backpacking Stove
review_body: I ordered the stove on a Friday, and received it on Monday.  Does not get much better, especially via free non-Amazon Prime shipping.  The Solo Stove was well boxed, and was in perfect shape on arrival.  It is well made and will obviously last a long time.  I have been shopping for a third stove as I have a Primus EtaExpress and a simple titanium folding Esbit stove for a back up.  I love the EtaExpress, as it is a boiling machine, but wanted something a little more hands on and something I did not have to worry about bringing, or running out of, fuel.  I fired the Solo Stove with some Vaseline cotton tinder and some twigs laying around the yard and was impressed how quickly and efficiently the fire was up and running.  It did not take a lot of fuel to get a boil on and left little residual in the stove.  It is not as fast obviously as the EtaExpress, but I will be packing the Solo Stove most of the time.  The Esbit folding titanium stove fits inside the Solo Stove easily with a couple of tabs, in case I am to tired, or there is no wood around to use the Solo Stove.  Though, honestly, it takes very little wood, and in the Pacific Northwest there is no shortage of fuel laying around.  All in all, an excellent product which I easily recommend to anyone looking for a compact wood burning pack stove.  As a side not, while the Solo Stove will fit inside the EtaExpress pot, the pot will not stay on the cooking ring due to the radiator ring on the bottom of the Primus EtaExpress pot.  So sadly, I will need to buy another pot.  No fault of the product, just an observation for folks who may have similar gear as myself.

product_title: Fox Head Men's Bomber Glove
review_body: The gloves are pretty nice. it adds grip to my bars and now i cant stand riding with out them. they look amazing but they are kind of cheaply made. the stitching is good but the little finger tip things started to peel off the first week i got them. but the gloves get the job done.

product_title: Maxxis CrossMark UST Mountain Bike Tire
review_body: Purchased this tire for a second bike since I use it on my other bike.  I ride a Trek Top Fuel WSD and it is a good replacement for the very thin tire that came with the bike, which was fast but didn't have much for grip and flats happened too often.  Tubeless is a must if you are going to be racing offroad I think and this tire is easy to put on and holds up well when you use sealant to avoid flats.  This tread pattern roles fast and has good grip on corners since we mix gravel roads in with single track you need both and this works great for that.

product_title: Life is Good Women's  Crusher Shamrock Hearts Tee
review_body: I am Irish and wanted a shamrock shirt to wear on St. Patricks Day. I saw one in Amazon books and decided to order it on line. I couldn't believe how fast I received it! It beat the 5-7 days for delivery! I love my shamrock shirt. However, they must had ran out of the color \\"true blue\\" to make the t-shirt because the shamrock was on a \\"true grey\\" color. I don't like the color grey normally but I do love my shamrock shirt. I would had loved it even more if it was on \\"true blue\\" like the description said.

product_title: Suisse Sport Adventurer Sleeping Bag
review_body: This sleeping bag kept me nice and warm. I went camping in 30 degree weather and I did not freeze.

product_title: Zippo Camo Lighters
review_body: Easy to use. Good compromise for a girly girl who works with all men. Would have liked the directions to be more clear.  I had to go online to Zippo to figure out how to fill etc. I got tired of holding down the button for the disposable lighters. This lights and you don't have to hold anything down. Close cap, flame goes out.  Easy peasy

product_title: Primus Atle 2-Burner Family Camp Stove (Red)
review_body: My boyfriend and I have had this stove for five years now. We didn't get it on amazon, but at an EMS our friend worked at. It still works perfectly and is easy to clean (compared to other stoves I have had over years of camping and power outages) Also, the propane cannisters definitely seem to last a little longer with this stove.

product_title: Shimano SPD-SL Cleat Set
review_body: I just replaced my Shimano cleats (finally). Frankly, what took me so long. I had become used to my foot slipping around in the cleat, difficulty getting in and out of the cleats, foot coming out of the cleat on occassion and finally had enough. Wow! putting these new cleats on was like getting an entirely new cycling experience. Very very happy with fresh cleats. I also looked at the other reviews and my experience with these cleats. Seems that the fact is they are great when they are in good condition. So I am now conciously trying to not walk on them. Along with this purchase I bought cleat covers, which I have never used before. Carrying them in my back pocket and putting them on and off is a new habit I am working on. Hopefully that will extend the life of the cleats. Just for the record, I live in the Virgin Islands, ride 1-2hours most days and got about 2 years of life out of my last set. The roads here are rough and I probably walked too much on them on and off roads. One of my friends here covers his Shimano cleats religiously. They look like new and he has been riding them for years happily.

product_title: Ear Lock Sunglasses Retainer System - soft rubber earlock system, no more slipping glasses
review_body: Needed \\"something\\" to keep my galss'  in place. While walking, jogging, and working.  These little devices certainly did the trick...easy to install, maintain, and well worth the price!

product_title: Planet Bike BRT Strap Multi-Use LED Bicycle Safety Light
review_body: LED is red and quite bright.  The frequency of the flashing mode is too fast for optimum visibility, though.  On/off switch is easily accessible on the outside of the band.  Length adjusts easily using elastic and a plastic buckle.  It looks like the battery can probably be replaced by removing 4 small screws from the plastic housing behind the on/off switch.

product_title: Outdoor Research Women's Sensor Gloves
review_body: I just got these for Christmas and they seem very nice so far. They fit snuggly and seem just about as warm as you'd expect for a basic, light-weight, wind resistant glove. I am able to use my iPhone with little trouble. You shouldn't expect them to be just like using your bare hands, you're wearing gloves. Your finger tips are a little chunkier and it's easier to hit the wrong letters when texting. I'm sure with a bit of practice I'll have no problem. I've looked a other gloves in stores and these are the nicest sensor gloves I've seen so far.

product_title: NRS Z-Drag Kit
review_body: This is a quality made system, taken from rock climbing tools.  I would like to see a nice hi visibility waterproof bag with comfortable carrying straps for the set up. Also some provisions to add other pieces for emergencies.

product_title: Sunlite Thorn Resistant Presta Valve Tubes, 700 x 25 - 28 (27 x 1.125 - 1.25") / 32mm, Black
review_body: I used these for an ultracross race that was 80k long on fire roads in a state park. There were sections with rocks the size of your fist where the bike slammed up/down and back/forth. Within the first mile I saw other racers changing flats. I never came close to getting a single flat with these tubes in 35c Maxxis 'cross tires. They held steady and true through an incredible pounding in the race.

product_title: Paricon Lightning Sled
review_body: These sleds are awesome.  They are really sturdy and the kids loved them.  I am 6'4, 230lbs and fit in these things. I don't think the description was accurate they had them listed as a little smaller. We used them all day in packed snow that was a little icy in the morning and they held up, I don't think there is a crack or stress point on them.  Great buy!!

product_title: Snorkeling Scuba Dive Side-View Edgeless Mask DRY Snorkel Gear Set (9080)
review_headline: Mask won't fit many face types.
review_body: I liked the snorkel and the shape of the lens. Unfortunately, the mask frame made it impossible to use. The middle part of the frame extends too deeply into the mask and presses painfully against the bridge of your nose. The silicone nose compartment also seems too small for an average nose. It's a very poor frame design, because this mask has a lot of internal volume.

product_title: Extra Soft Road MTB Bike Bicycle Saddles Seat Black
review_body: The seat is pretty I do say it's got that look about it that tells peeps that it is race inspired. On that note, it is very firm. It is thin, if you're looking for a plush baby seat then this is not for you. I have mine mounted on a rigid mountain bike I use for trails and minor commuting. When I sit on the seat it is only for minimal amounts of time. It is mainly for looks and occasional rests, I'll be happy to answer any questions on the seat

product_title: Sanitation Equipment Visa Potty Model: 268 24 Liter with 2-level Indicators
review_body:
I have mixed feelings about it, first off I don't think it has a true 6.3 gallon resivoir, that would mean full it should weight about 42 lbs, but it did not weigh as much as a 5 gallon jug of water. It took me less time to fill it up than it did my previous 5 gallon bucket. I think the 6.3 gallon measurement is for the fresh water basin and resivoir. Mine did not come with a manual and I couldn't find one online nor could I find the manufactures web site. When I first started using it the pump leaked at the top, but I just had to tighten the ring around the base of the pump handle and it stopped.

The part that upset me the most was when I went to dump it, there is a red vent cap on the top that you have to push down before you pickup the resivior. I did not know this because I didn't have a manual and the ewww from the resivior squirted all over my leg. The valve itself is kindof chinsy too, it's not click lock, thread in or anything just slides open and closed. I didn't trust picking the thing up even after pushing the vent cap in.

The sanitization solution that comes with it was horrible too, didn't do anything about the smell when dumping it. The reliance Bio-blue worked much better at reducing the smell [[ASIN:B0011MXVD4 Reliance Products Bio-Blue Toilet Deodorant Packaged (12-Pack)]]
If you plan on using this unit without some sort of sanitization or deodorant solution I recommend buying nose plugs as well. The smell when dumping is enough to make somebody with an iron stomach vomit.

For as cheap as it was it wasn't a bad purchase, but you get what you pay for.

product_title: 25" Foam Snow Disc
review_body: Unfortunately the snow disks didn´t look at all like advertised, so we were really disappointed, when we got them.  Everything else was okay.

product_title: Liberty Mountain Nylon Gaiter
review_body:
I was trying to figure out what gear to get for a Mount Washington winter summit attempt. I was buying all the equipment for our group of 3 (from mountaineering shoes to cramp-ons and pick axe), so I tried my best to balance quality and price. This item matched exactly what I was looking for.

The first attempt ended up in failure. Complete white out and 100 MPH winds. Temperatures were hitting 15 below with the ridiculous wind chill. The second time we finally summitted with tons of snow and 50-60 MPH winds. In addition to be being extremely comfortable, the gaiters kept us all dry the entire time. For the price, this is the champ. I'd highly recommend this item.

product_title: Big Agnes Clearview Air Pad Mummy Sleeping Pad
review_body: Was excited about it until I opened it up. It is super thin and just as I thought. I filled it up and the next morning walked into the room and it was half empty. Maybe I just got a bad one, but I sent it back and bought a Thermarest pad. I just don't want to take a chance of one leaking out on me. Good luck to you if you get one, but I think I would invest in a thicker one though.

product_title: Intex Pillow Rest Raised Airbed with Built-in Pillow and Electric Pump
review_body: Got this inflatable bed so that friends could sleepover without taking the ground. It blows itself up quickly and stays blown up for weeks. This bed has started to double as a couch in our room. After deflating it, it may be hard to get into the tiny bag again. The bed may also smell a little (like plastic tends to) when first inflated, but if it bothers you too much, just wipe it down. Initially may deflate more upon first getting it, but the plastic is just stretching. For the occasional sleepover with an extra person (or for those with the desire for a couch, this bed is a great option with an awesome price.

product_title: Seattle Sports Kayak Wall Cradles
review_headline: Works but a great deal of hassle
review_body:
The Seattle Sports cradle worked for storing my boat, but only after a bit of small hassles.

I was trying to mount the Seattle Sports Cradles to the studs in my garage. First thing I noticed was how big these suckers are! They are a lot bigger in person than they appear in pictures. This was okay, they have to be big to fit a large range of boats but it did cause me to reevaluate where I was going to place the cradles in the garage. I see now that they make folding models. I think I would have liked to get these instead. Hind sight is always 20/20. My biggest issue with the Seattle Sports Cradle is that in order to attach them to a typical wall stud, with or without drywall, you need to either angle the screws in and hope you hit enough of the stud to hold or you can offset the brackets and use only one screw on each bracket. I went with this option because I wanted to know that screw was completely in the board.
This set up has held my boat just fine for a year now but I have to be careful when placing the boat in the rack or it bends the plates. My brackets are very wavy from being bent a few too many times.
I am starting to look for another boat and have been looking at some of the other options. I like the cradles but might pick a better designed and folding model next time. I wont be a cheap weasel twice.

product_title: Swiss Gear Adjustable Telescoping Hiking Pole (Red)
review_body: I BOUGHT THIS ITEM FOR A FRIEND BUT AFTER PUTTING IT TOGETHER AND TRYING IT OUT, I DECIDED THAT I LIKED IT AND NEEDED IT MORE THAN HER.  CONTRARY TO WHAT OTHERS SAID IN THEIR REVIEWS, I FOUND THIS VERY EASY TO PUT TOGETHER.  IT IS VERY STURDY.

product_title: Sigma BC 1009 Bicycle Speedometer
review_headline: not for mountain bikes should specify
review_body: just writing a review to warn future buyers that this will not work with a mountain bike. the space required for the wheel sensor is too wide for mountain bike fork and wheel setup, wish this would have been stated more clearly in item description. i am not the type of person to return things that only cost $20 so i guess i have a donation for the church garage sell.

product_title: Humangear capCap - Green/Gray
review_body: This is a great idea to create an easier way to pour and drink from nalgene bottles. Sadly, it's incredibly difficult to get open unless you leave the cap a little moose. If you do that though, you will have a leak on your hands! I still use it camping, but not as a daily cap.

product_title: CamelBak Fourteener 100-Ounce Hydration Pack
review_body: I have had this pack for several seasons now and can attest that it is very durable and the capacity can't be beat (I carry a lot of \\"God help me if I have to use any of these survival tools because I am in deep trouble\\" stuff in my pack. The bottom strap has elastic belts that tie around the straps when not in use and they sometimes come loose but no big deal. Well worth the $$. I bought it at the time because it was one of the few packs that had a 3 liter hydration capacity but am not disappointed with its quality at all. This pack is just what you need no matter how long that 14er summit takes.

product_title: 3/2mm Womens Roxy Syncro Full Wetsuit - Size 8
review_body: This is only my second wetsuit for scuba diving, but it has worked very well for me.  It fits nicely, looks good, and does its job of keeping me warm and protecting my skin underwater.

product_title: Trademark Global 72-72645GRN, Solar Energy LED Flashlight w/ Keychain - Green
review_body: I bought one of these little devices several years ago and I use it every night (to avoid turning on the lights when getting up late at night) and especially when I travel. It's great to know that if the electricity goes out it will recharge each day as usual. And it's a pleasure to use it without feeling guilty about consuming batteries. I've never tested how long the charge lasts but it's certainly adequate for all my needs, and it continues to work just like new. Decided to get a bunch for friends and family as holiday gifts this year.

product_title: SealLine Kodiak Window 5-Liter Purge
review_body: Just used for the first time on a kayaking trip. Protected cameras very well. Easy to open and reseal after placing something in it. Good investment to protect anything you do not want to get wet!

product_title: Nalgene Hose Kits and Valves
review_body: Arrived quickly and is exactly as pictured & described.  Was a bit hard to take the old valve off and put the new one on, but very secure now.  This is really great for tucking under my helmet so I can drink while riding without having to take my hands off the bars.

product_title: Smart Planet Ocie4 Eco Filtered Water Bottle Free Bonusfilter
review_headline: Love this bottle, works really well, read on for details...
review_body: This bottle filter works well for filtering clean tap water of its taste and odor. It should be noted that it takes moderate force to pull the water through the straw, however anyone who isnt a child or elderly should have no problem pulling it through.

product_title: Scuba Diving Dive Snorkeling Underwater Safety Whistle with Lanyard
review_body: It's a whistle, it's loud and piercing. Every diver should have one on their BC. Even hikers should carry one. When the emergency happens you will be glad you have it.

product_title: Coghlan's Electric Air Pump
review_body: This pump is small sized but very fast on inflating and deflating a queen size air mattress. I used a portable jump start battery so I could inflate the mattress inside the tent. You have to hold the adaptor in place to the mattress valve so there is no air leakage but it only takes about one minute to fully inflate or deflate my queen size. Great price and not that noisy either. Get two at this price!

product_title: Ergon GE1-L
review_body: This my second set of Ergon grips. They are perfect for my hand size . Before I used them I would end up with numb feelings in my hands, it really changed my riding experience. These grips are easy to install and have usefull markings on the rims so you can position them equally and also remember the exact position if you need to remove them. Great product.

product_title: HotHands Toe Warmers (40 Pair)
review_body: Sent them to Afghanistan. The guys are guard duty were pretty happy.Delivery was quick. It would have been nice to send them directly but that is not available at this time.

product_title: FireSteel Miniature
review_body: Proof that good things can come in small packages! It may be small, but works like a charm. Perfect for mini-survival kits - I made mine out of the ever-popular Altoids tins, and is a great addition to it! No excuse to not have a couple of these on hand as backups to your other fire-starting tools (or as your primary fire-starter if you like). Solid five stars.

product_title: High Sierra Swerve Laptop Backpack
review_body: I always place the product name in the title because Amazon does combine reviews at times. I had to return the book bag within 30 days because part of the zipper because exposed from the inside. It seemed like a good product at first. I am disappointed the product did not last very long.

product_title: XLC/Alex X-101 MTB Front Wheel 26" x 1.75, SRAM Hub, Silver/Black
review_headline: great deal on a great wheel
review_body: I really like these Alex wheels. I had similar wheels on my road bike and needed new ones for my mountain bike so I went with these. They are very high quality for the price and these ones come with some very nice SRAM hubs. This hub also has the 6-bolt disc brake mounts, but you don't need to have disc brakes on your bike to use them. If you are looking for some good quality wheels and hubs for your mountain bike at a reasonable price, look no further, my friend.

product_title: Wenzel Fleece Sleeping Bag Liner
review_body: For it's intended purpose as a light weight liner blanket it is warm and adequate for minimal occasional use. It was warm enough to cut the chill of a cold office environment.

product_title: Defence Technology First Defense 1.3% MK-9 Stream OC Aerosol
