product_title: Yukon Charlies Beta 930 Snowshoes
review_body: This is my first pair of snowshoes, had I know it was going to be this much fun I would have bought some years ago.  The bindings are very easy to use and operate flawlessly even with gloves on.  They seem stable in the snow and have excellent grip on the ice going both up and down hilly terrain.  I primarily got them to go walking with my two lab retrievers and so far it is a blast.  I am 240lbs and these were able to support me without any issues.  I will update this review as the season progresses, I live in northern Vermont, so there will be plenty of snow to really put these to the test.

product_title: GoLite Women's Demaree Canyon 800 Fill Insulated Down Jacket
review_body: I love the green color of this jacket, though they call it \\"Midnight Blue\\" and the photo depicting the color is quite accurate. The jacket has a very feminine, body-contoured fit. On cool days I wear it alone, but on freezing days it acts as a sweater-jacket underneath my bigger coat.

product_title: MOOSE Natural Longboard Complete 9" x 47" Pintail 76mm
review_body:
I was extremely surprised. I honestly ordered the longboard just for the deck. When I went outside to ride it with the trucks that are already one, this could have been a $200 board for all I known if I didn't buy it! I am very happy with this Pintail and now am a Moose fan for life. I also got a plain Moose skateboard, which is also amazing quality. I think the only reason this is cheap is because there is no art or big name printed on these. Think of an expensive board, strip the common printed art off of them, and this is what you have. Completely satisfied, thank you!

P.S. Yes, this board does ride smoothly and has pretty good wheels and bearings. Wheels aren't clear, instead they are black, but that doesn't bother me one bit!

product_title: Delta Cycle Michelangelo 2 Bike Wall Rack
review_body:
I've been looking at stands and reading reviews for a few months searching for the stand that would work in our house. I was looking for stability (bikes are expensive), looks (it's in the house,not the garage) and price (I'm cheap).

What makes this stand so stable, in my opinion, is the bikes that it holds and the floor surface. I'm not putting a lot of weight on the stand. On the lower rack I've got my heavier aluminum framed road bike, which still weighs less than mountain style bikes or cruisers. Then on the top rack I've got my CF frame 16.5 lb. bike. That's less than 40 pounds on this stand. The stand base rests on a carpeted floor and against the wall, with no extra anchoring. The base being on carpet means it doesn't move anywhere. I remove and replace either bike and the stand stays firm. No wobbling or moving forward off the wall.

As far as looks, I've seen better. But not at this price. This looks very nice up against our light gray wall. And if you're going to store your bikes in the house this should be a consideration (especially if you're married). We already have 3 bikes and a car in our single car garage so the pitch to get this in the house had to be good. And after putting the bikes on the rack, it kind of looks like a work of art (beauty is in the eyes of the beholder).

But the price is the first reason I even looked at this product. It was a sub 60.00 stand with good and bad reviews. But all of the stands I was looking at through bike outlets and the local bike shops, started out at 100.00 and went up from there. I almost purchased one on sale for 75.00 before I thought of looking on Amazon. After reading reviews, I decided to give this one a try and couldn't be happier.

But any review has to point out the cons and this one has a couple. First, even though this saves a lot of space by \\"stacking\\" two bikes. It still comes off the wall almost two feet. My brake lever/shifter is 21.5\\" off the wall. The legs are only 17\\" off the wall. But we don't keep this in an area where it's going to impede foot traffic. And secondly, although I like the looks, it could look better. But it's not bad enough to be a con. Let's just call it an ehhhh.

So all that being said, I would recommend this stand for a couple of light weight road bikes. If you're gonna stack a couple of Target brand mountain bikes this review might not be as helpful as others. Good luck in your bike stand search. I found mine.off the wall. But we don't keep this in an area where it's going to impede foot traffic. And secondly, although I like the looks, it could look better. But it's not bad enough to be a con. Let's just call it an ehhhh. So all that being said, I would recommend this stand for a couple of light weight road bikes. If you're gonna stack a couple of Target brand mountain bikes this review might not be as helpful as others. Good luck in your bike stand search. I found mine.

product_title: Fenix TK41 Flashlight
review_headline: Wow....they werent kidding, it is bright!
review_body: I ordered the TK41 on monday and received it today, nice quick shipping so I was happy with that. It came as advertised, nice plastic hard case with extra O-rings, lanyard and booklet. First let me say that I own a bunch of other brands of flashlights, I have a lot of MAG brand in all different sizes from AAA up to 4D cell, and several handfuls of Lawson products lights, etc....I carried my MAG 2 AA light for many, many years on the job and it was always my go to light. But the TK41 on its lowest setting is brighter, and throws the light further then any light I have ever owned. One of the primary reasons I bought this light was I am now living in an RV park in AZ for the winter, the dog run where I walk my 2 shelties is about 100 yards long, with a gate on either end. Some inconsideret folks will sometimes leave the far gate standing wide open, and if I let my dogs off leash in the park at night I had no way of knowing if is was actauly closed down on the far end or not. I can now see that gate on the lowest setting of this flashlight!! It is amazing now far this things throws the beam, med, high and especialy turbo are just crazy bright, I dont have to worry about my dogs running out an open gate now. Yes it is a bit expensive, but the safety of my 2 dogs is worth every pennie to me...I would highly recommend this to anyone needing an above average flashlight.

product_title: Pro-Tec B2 Danny Kass Men's Snowboard Helmet - M - Matte Black Reaper
review_body: MY son  loves this helemet this was his first season skiing and it was a huge hit with his friends they all wanted to know where he got it. Nice I recommend it. He says he feels so cool when he wears   it.

product_title: Seirus Innovation 2875 Polartec Winter Cold Weather Balaclava for Complete Head, Face, and Neck Protection
review_body: Got the x-large for my sons-in-law, but they fit tight on my small head. Cover well though.  I'm hoping they can stretch them out of the washer, and hang to dry. Very warm.

product_title: Gordini Toddler's Blizzard Mitt
review_headline: Small is too big for toddler
review_body:
The small is too big for my toddler, but she wears them anyway because they are so warm. At least we will get a long period of use out of these mittens!
UPDATE: One year later, these mittens are a perfect fit for my 3.5-year-old. She used them pretty much all last winter and they've held up well with frequent washing. I would definitely buy these again.

product_title: Children Bike Bicycle Replacement Kickstand Silver Tone
review_headline: i can't get it to keep the bike up right
review_body: This was a waste of money, too short even for 16\\" kids bike, you need to drill wholes use your own extension bracket. Metal is not strong enough to hold the bike, metal itself will bend

product_title: Insta-Bed Queen Raised Air Mattress with Sure Grip Bottom & Built-In Pump
review_body: This mattress is very confortable and looks as good quality. Very easy to inflate and deflate. I bought it for temporary use but I think it could be used every day as a regular mattress.

product_title: Those Who Wander Pocket Compass
review_body: The receiver of the gift loved it!  Perfect for the pocket and the small bag it comes in helps protect the exterior.  Great for hikers and campers that don't want a larger compass.

product_title: Schwinn Magnetic Bike Trainer
review_body: This trainer DOES NOT contain the skewer that you need. If it did in the past as the other reviewers indicate, that has changed. I started setting this up all ready to ride only to come up short when I discovered that something was missing. This was not a simple oversight or accidental omission either; the instructions state specifically that you need to go to a local bike shop or order from their customer service to get the proper type of trainer skewer. Needless to say, I was quite annoyed. I guess this was a cost-saving move.  I'm not saying this unit still may not be a good deal for the low price, but everyone should be aware of the omission.

product_title: Kelty Shadehouse
review_headline: Still in a sweat from failed assembly attempt
review_body: I read the reviews and, against my better judgment, still bought it. Wow. Whoever said it requires extreme force to get the pole ends into the grommets was not exaggerating.  Extreme force to the extent that I.could.not.do.it.  I got two poles in the grommets and after much huffing, puffing, heaving and hoeing, I gave up.  Thank goodness it was only an aborted test run and didn't ruin a whole camping trip.  Unless you are looking for an alternative to the P90X workout, skip this canopy.

product_title: JanSport T501 Superbreak Backpack - Black/Cabesa Blue Flitter
review_body: This is an awesome backpack!! I have had this backpack for about a year now and it still looks like new. I use this backpack almost everyday and it has held up well. I use this backpack to keep my planner in and as a school backpack. It's just the right size. I think for the price, you cant get a better backpack!! I would so recommend this backpack to anyone looking for a new backpack!!

product_title: ful Unisex Adult Collaborator 22-Inch Rolling Backpack
review_body: Couldn't make it to my Dj gigs without this backpack.  It holds all the essentials and it's very durable but I do wish they would have come up with a better design on the straps.  They're easily adjustable but tend to get in the way a little.

product_title: Storm Alert Whistle
review_headline: Best Simple Safety Device I Own
review_body:
I'd say this is the \\"Best Simple Safety Device I Own\\" for a few reasons. Before I go into my reasons, keep in mind I am a safety fanatic. 'Be Prepared' is even close to my life style (no offence to the Boy Scouts...they are GREAT, and I was an Eagle Scout. Here we go on this little device:
1. It is inexpensive
2. It is easy to carry and use
3. It works in all weather and conditions (all I could duplicate)- YES, REALLY works!
4. It never runs out of air or won't fail in cold weather (as do canned air horns)- GREAT for snowmobiling
5. It never will fail due to a dead battery ¡V GREAT for EMP attacksº
6. It works under water - GREAT for my SCUBA diving
7. It is a good and legal personal protection deterrent
8. It is loud as !@# and will get attention, if not hurt the ears of a person near you
9. Children can carry them everywhere (even at schools) as an extra safety product ¡V NOTHING more important than our children!
10. Last, but not least...it just makes sense and is the one single safety device that has cost me the least and does so much.
Need I say more? I will keep one in each vehicle, on my SCUBA BC, in my safety kits on my RV's & Snowmobile, and give to friends and family as a usable and practical gift. Kudos to the designer and manufacture!

product_title: MICRONET Microfiber Towel
review_body: This is the perfect towel to take on your travels. It folds up really small and compact and does exactly what it's suppose to do. It dries you quickly and dries fast. I got this towel for when I went backpacking in Europe and we were moving to new cities every couple of days. I had no problem with the towel being totally dry in the morning ready to be packed. I recommend this towel for all types of travelers.

product_title: Cygolite Expilion 350-Lumen USB Rechargeable Headlight
review_body: I got this light to increase the daytime visibility of our tandem. It does that exceptionally well. On our second mid-day ride with this light an oncoming driver gave us a thumbs up and yelled \\"great light!\\" It's very clear that motorists now use more caution around us.   This light does not interfere with my wireless flight deck computer like the 2W Planet Bike light does. It is also much brighter and casts a wider beam.   I no longer commute in the dark, but if I did I would have no need to go back to the rig I used to use for that, which was 2 halogen lamps - 15W and 20W - plus a 2 lb water-bottle battery. This little LED amazingly gives comparable visibility with a more pleasing whiter color.

product_title: Pearl Izumi Men's Elite Softshell Jacket
review_headline: Warm Enough by itself down to 50 degrees.
review_body:
I like Pearl Izumi products, even though they run a little small for their sizes. This Jacket is soft inside, has extra long arms and bottom back so everything is covered when you are stretched out over the bike. I have a 44\\" chest, so the large is a little snug. Therefore, I use this as a base layer if I'm biking in weather that's below 50 deg F. Check the sizing chart. If you are borderline, choose the larger size.
The zippered breast pocket is handy so you can hear your phone ring, or store tissues for cold weather runny nose (you can't hobo blow in a line of riders). The arms have reflective strips, which is a help in the dim and dark days of winter. The full length zipper is a must for me. I get overheated on long climbs, and zipping down helps cool my core.
The material wicks moisture and dries quickly -- if the jacket is not used as an underlayer. I chose black with red trim rather than the screaming red with black trim. Either way -- good jacket for bike enthuthiasts.

product_title: LEDwholesalers 51-LED 395nm Ultra Violet Blacklight UV Flashlight 3xAA, 7202UV395
review_body: Best we've tried yet! Works where others don't Made by the original makers don't be fooled by imitators. Buy some now!

product_title: Texsport 3 Person Hide-A-Way Camo Backpacking Camping Tent with Carry Storage Bag
review_body: This was a gift for two boys.  They love it!  Easy to assemble.  They have been camping in their living room since Christmas!

product_title: Planet Bike Superflash Stealth bike tail light
review_headline: super-bright, looks great on the bike
review_body: this is my third light. I used to have red super-flash for several years until I lost it on a very rough, bumpy road (broke in half). The white/clear one is more stylish, and works just as well. I now have two clear ones for my two bikes (used to swap back and forth). The amount of light superflash generates guarantees you will be seen from far away. It works great even in bright daylight. Very easy to turn on and off (I do it while riding, don't even need to stop pedaling).  Highly recommended.

product_title: O'Neill Heat 3Q Zip 3/2 FSW (Black)
review_body: O'Neill does it again.  I have been wearing O'Neil suits for over 25 years and they just keep getting better with age. Perfect suit for So. Cal. which is where I live, and even worked well in the Central Coast where the water temp is at least 10-15 degrees colder. (Kept me plenty warm) Plenty of flexibility here.  Easy to get on and off! Keeps you plenty warm with all of the \\"details\\" stated in it's description. Would (and have) already recommended it to family and friends.  Great Suit - nuff said!

product_title: Pearl Izumi Men's Elite Softshell Jacket
review_body: It fits nicely. I ride late at night after work, it keeps me warm. It moves with my body nicely. It is an excellent jacket, well worth the price.

product_title: Reebok Womens Sport Gym Bag Swim Bag Yoga Bag Pink Shoulder Bag Purse Nwt

review_body:
This is a great gym bag. It is large enough to hold light summer gym clothing and it is very light.
I previously bought a larger bag that hold gym shoes clothing and towels.
This bag will hold a small towel. i love the pink color!

product_title: Columbia Cougar Flats Six to Eight-Person Two-Room Cabin Tent
review_body: We were the proud owners of this wonderful tent for the last 4 years. Just last week, both door zippers finally gave out,  we broke too many poles (duct tape can only do so much!) and it finally started to develop leaks during the last rainstorm.  Overall, we were very pleased with it.  We used this tent approx. 10-12 days each year.  Going to purchase the newer version of the same tent from Amazon!

product_title: Sierra Designs Women's Hurricane Pant Petite
review_headline: Warm and Dry and Just What They are Supposed to Do
review_body: I've only used them once but it was during a three day weekend of long periods of cold rain and hail.  The part I liked best was that I had purchased a pair big enough to be pulled over my pants.  With the zippers on the side of the ankles, I get them over my boots then tighter them with the velcro to keep the rain and thick mud away from my feet.  Several other adults commented that they needed rain pants and I highly recommended these.  When I got home I dried them out and it was a quick rinse in the sink to get the dirt stains out.  They wear well and I can see many long years of use, though I'd prefer to camp in the sun.

product_title: RavX Chain TX 10 Function Chain Tool
review_body: You hope you don't have to use this out on the road or trail, but if you do, it works great.  Instead of a multi-tool, I use a set of three tools which weighs in at around 110g.  - RavX chain tool / spoke wrench  - Park MT-1  - King Cage Titanium Tire Levers  I've built and maintained all my own bikes (MTB, Hybrid, and Road).  Last Fall, I broke the chain on my road bike about 30 miles from home.  A bit far to talk someone into picking me up.  The RavX fixed it, no problems.  Luckily we were about a mile from a convenience store and my wife rode down and bought some hand wipes.  What a mess.  At home I use disposable painter gloves.  Now I also pack a couple wipe packets and hope it will be enough.

product_title: Intex Raised Downy Airbed with Built-in Electric Pump, Queen, Bed Height 22"
review_body: We bought this bed on two different occasions. Not because of subpar workmanship, but because my kids were poking at it. They jumped on it, ran into it flipped it over and it has not buckled one bit. We have a family member staying with us for a while and he should be thoroughly suprised at the comfort and size. The most weight it's carried has been over 400lbs; a couple of friends that slept on it while staying with us.  Not so much as a whistle.  And at this sale price...I'm getting another.

review_body: This fillet table is everything I could have hoped for and more.  Living in Washington state near the Puget Sound, you can imagine the salmon fishing is incredible!  This table made cleaning my days catch a breeze.  It's light weight and portable.  It also has a hole on one side built into it that you can put a bucket or trash receptacle under which makes fish cleaning a virtually mess free task.  So glad I got this so I can do it at the waters edge rather than bringing my catch home and making a complete mess out of my kitchen.  The construction of this table is top notch and the cost is well below others that I looked into.  Great product and a GREAT VALUE!

product_title: Eurosocks 0111 Patented Recovery Graduated Compression OTC Socks - Pair
review_headline: Best compression sock I've encountered so far
review_body: I've tried a number of compression socks to deal with my defective anatomy and nearly continuous shin splints while nursing myself through college track and field.  These brands include CEP, under armour, and CW-X.  These socks were my favorites- the most comfortable, and the most successful application of graduated compression.  I have relatively thick ankles and fairly monsterous calves from being a competative triple jumper and hurdler, yet the under armour and CW-X socks still didn't apply enough pressure and I usually wore an additional layer of ace bandage or tape wrapping beneath those socks.

product_title: Gci Outdoors Bleacherback Stadium Seat
review_headline: Good bleacher seat for football season!
review_body: This bleacher seat is very comfortable, and good for anyone who needs some back support for an extended time sitting in bleachers.  The strap that secures the seat to the bleachers (underneath) is an added bonus.  You can adjust how far back (or how straight-up) you want the seat back to go.  This seat also keeps you much warmer than sitting on a cold bleacher.  The only reason I gave this 4 instead of 5 stars is the carrying strap. . .it's not terrible, but I would prefer that it be adjustable to a slightly longer length (but there is a buckle that prevents the full strap from being available to put over your shoulder).  But I highly recommend this product. . .it's a great value!

review_body: Purchased this for the many camping trips scheduled for this summer with the intent of wowing the kids. What I've found, though, is the perfect fire starting tool. While showing the kids how to use it, I found that with the proper tinder (dry sage grass as an example) you are able to get first strike results. Impressive!

product_title: Chums RearView Mirror
review_body: This has a nice clip that can't slip off. We liked the retractable chord so the mirror is always attached and doesn't have to be unattached to use.  Overall, its a great product and very sturdy!

product_title: Wilderness Solutions Scout Fire Piston - Includes tinder and fire making materials

After opening the packaging and reading the instructions I was able to light the charcloth on the first attempt. I have since taken it to work and let some of my co-workers try it and they were successful and impressed. Also, I let my Ranger boys try it out last night in class and they were all able to successfully light a \\"birdsnest\\" of black moss. Its a very nice product and so far the quality is great after 7 ignitions.

review_body: I did a lot of research before buying this.  I like it because it is very light to carry around.  It really does not leak! The bottle should not be intentionally rolled, but left flat .

looks great, very grippe, overall I'm very happy with the grip tape and will order form this company again

product_title: Gransfors Bruks Splitting Maul
review_headline: You get what you pay for
review_body:
I've been cutting and splitting firewood ever since I was a boy, and many a calorie and cord I burned, much to the angst of my physiology. My father was the type who instilled in us such virtues as 'hard work builds character' and 'when the going gets tough, the tough get going'. My dad was a very good and wonderful man who has now passed on, probably because he worked too hard trying to also live up to those virtues. On the other hand, my philosophy, learned from past years of trial and error under the rulership of my dear parent, eventually led me down the road of taking the path of least resistance and \\"Doing less and Accomplishing More!\\" What I learned from Dad over all those pain staking years was; the kind of work I didn't want to do with my body, i.e. pushing it beyond it's limits to the point of injury. So, with that short preface in mind, I'd like to say, whereas Dad generally, but not always, went cheap combined with a lot of elbow grease, I now always buy the top of the line (at least what the pocket book allows so I don't go into debt) in any purchase I make. If the item is not priced high, in most cases but not all, it's probably not worth it, in my mind.

When we installed a Nectre \\"Bakers Oven Wood Stove\\" (a product I highly recommend also), in our kitchen, we did it because we wanted to heat (and cook more or less) exclusively with wood. We have plenty of dead and down timber on our property so all that was necessary for me to complete the plan was to get the fuel from where it was and package it for the stove. And since we live in the Pacific NW, it meant heating the abode with at least 6 months worth of fuel. So, if I was to be the provider in that department, I wanted to make it as \\"easy\\" as was possible for myself. I use Stihl chainsaws and my present one is a \\"440 Magnum\\", and as far as chainsaws go, as long as it's properly maintained, it does the job flawlessly. So, with everything else covered, all I needed was the right splittingtools. I considered a hydraulic wood splitter (and this may seem to conflict with my philosophy, but I'm also an avid exercise freak, race mt. bikes, so I like good upper body workouts, as long as I'm not \\"punishing\\" myself.) So, I thought how can I split logs without dislocating my shoulders and cracking molars in the process? I did my research and came up with the Gransfors Bruks Splitting Maul. Now I must confess, I was raised on a maul and wedge to do the splitting. Metal on metal takes it's toll. However, when I read that one could do most or all the splitting with just the GB Maul Splitter (based on certain conditions inherent in the wood being split, e.g. variety, size, moisture content, etc.) I was skeptical, at first, to say the least. Fortunately, I thought to myself, the opposite end of the GB Maul's face is a \\"Hammer-Poll\\" which is designed to be used as a hammer to strike a wedge into a log and split it that way. That's how I originally cut wood in \\"the old days\\" and that's why my shoulders crunch a bit today around my rotator cuffs. Anyway, I decided to purchase the Gransfors Bruks Spitting Wedge as a backup, just in case.

When I purchased the Maul and took it home, I was amazed at how \\"lively\\" the tool felt. It was so lively it felt \\"light\\", in fact, it felt too light. \\"This can't do the job\\", I thought to myself, \\"there's not enough weight behind it. Darn it, I'm going to have to use the wedge. However, even though I assumed I'd have to use them in unison, I looked over both the Splitting Maul and Wedge and I could sense there was something unique about these tools. Aside from their \\"liveliness\\" and \\"lightness\\"; they were both works of art. I read the owners manual that comes with both and was captivated by the history of Gransfors Bruks, the description of all their tools, their Mission Statement and the hearty looking staff who were instrumental in producing these hand made/forged products. I could tell, these tools I was holding, camefrom a tradition steeped in a culture where lives depended on reliable, finely crafted tools capable of doing the job, day in and day out. At that point I was buzzing inside and couldn't wait to initiate them on the spot, or at least outside.

So I put on my equipment; goggles with face protection (ALWAYS WEAR EYE PROTECTION WHEN SPLITTING OR CUTTING WOOD, ALWAYS!), boots, chaps (same ones I use with the chainsaw), gloves, ear plugs, grabbed the Maul and Wedge and proceeded outdoors to split some wood.

MY, OH MY!

It's hard to explain what my experience was without sounding a bit \\"out there', but what the heck, here's what happened. When the 'Maul/Axe' hit the log I could feel this energy from the swing transfer from my body, into the handle, into the face of the Maul, into the log itself, as if there was an electrical current of surging power intelligently guiding this 'charged\\" and eloquently designed metal object, effortlessly through the wood. The moment the maul struck the intended object it seemed to stop for a mini-micro second at the spot of impact, but then this remarkable device, magically, exploded with a conscious force that naturally and automatically split the log into two halves, proceeding downward from there and planting itself firmly into the base log underneath. I'm 6 feet, 160 pounds, with above average upper body strength, but even so, I could feel \\"The Power\\" (LOL to myself saying this), I could feel an energy, above and beyond my own, commanding this tool to fulfill it's purpose. Those guys, those distinguished Craftsmen back in Sweden, who have been forging these masterpieces for generations, 112 years in fact, guaranteeing every hand made tool with a 20 YEAR WARRANTY, do so because they know they have a truly unique and supremely made product and they KNOW what it takes to activate its 'subtle powers'.

I ended up splitting a few dozen logs that first day (when I had other things I was suppose to do) and I had great FUN doing it. In fact, since that day, I find immense, satisfying pleasure, throwing that extraordinary tool over my shoulder, heading out to spit wood and then allowing the tool to fulfill it's designed purpose. There was a time that I hated splitting logs; dreaded it, wishing never to do it again. However, since acquiring this work of art, I feel blessed to have made it's acquaintance, and together, we go out and do the job in style. It's a pleasurable adventure now, one that I highly recommend you experience for yourself. BUY ONE, you won't regret it.

One last note: I've only used the GB Wedge a couple of times when gnarly, irregular logs, took advantage of my smug cockiness, and made life difficult for a few intense swings prior. Enter: \\"The Wedge\\". Case closed! Log out!

After much research both online and in stores (yes, I am very picky), my 8 year old daughter and I finally settled on this one.  We are so glad we did! product_title: Nintendo Zelda Triforce Black Billed Beanie Hat
review_body: so i was expecting this beanie to be blue like the picture but it came in black and was very disappointed because its a christmas  gift for my boyfriend. he loves the colour blue, zelda and beanies...so a all in one combo right? not anymore

product_title: Earth Products Jamboree Military Style Folding Cot with Free Side Storage Bag System and Pillow (Green)
review_body: The materials used seems to be durable, the sewing strong and of a solid construction. The cot comes with its own carry bag. The all polyester pillow is about 8\\"x 10\\"and 4\\" thick so if you want more comfort bring your own. The side storage bags have hook and loop straps to attach to the cot and hook and loop strips inside the storage areas to close them to keep contents from spilling out. One bag is longer with various sizes of sewn stash areas plus a mesh area to spot contents quickly. The second shorter bag has storage on both sides divided down the long center. product_title: Shimano RD-M810 Saint Shadow rear derail, SS short cage
review_body:
I've never ripped a derailleur off but even my XC bike's derailleur has a few scars from close calls.

When I was building my new DH bike I wanted something fairly light but more importantly reliable and smooth. So far I have about .5-1 seasons of riding with the M810 derailleur and it's been great. The shifting is smooth & firm with zero problems with ghost shifting/chain falling even in rocky decent. When I shift it's crisp and fast and doesn't hesitate. It's survived a few crashes with just some marking. There is still a little chain-slap but I think this will be present for any bike that uses a derailleur. Honestly, I don't know how much the difference the mode converter makes but I like the idea of having it. It does bring the derailleur closer when using a road cassette. The overall compactness and the spring firmness are also impressive.

I have no real complaints to speak of.

At this point I would buy a second one without hesitation. In fact, when I think about it, I'm tempted to switch my other bikes to Shimano because of this derailleur.

product_title: Falcon friction ATB thumb shifters
review_headline: Not for winter, not for me
review_body: I got these to replace a broken Suntour shifter on my early 90's Giant Iguana, which I use as a winter bike due to its solid construction, diverse gearing and low street value.  I installed these on friday and was pretty impressed with their performance, especially given the low price and overall ease of install (this was my first time running bike cables, or swapping shifters and I had the whole thing done in about an hour).  Only 2 days after installing these, the plastic of the left shifter split causing the shifter to lose cable tension on my front derailleur. I glued the plastic housing back together as a temp fix, but its just really not a great design to depend on a small piece of plastic to maintain tension.  This probably would not have been an issue if I was not biking home in below freezing weather causing the plastic to get brittle, but thats what I need. If you plan on putting these on a cruiser or using them for a cheap replacement on a kid's bike, you will probably be fine. But, if you plan on hitting the streets in the snow, you may want to think again.

product_title: Swagman Bicycle Carriers Trailhead 4 Bike Towing Rack
review_body: There is a design flaw that does not allow you to tighten the hitch ball.  Neither a box wrench or socket wrench will fit around the nut on the bottom of the hitch ball because of the design.  The box is cut at a 45 degree or so angle, but it doesn't allow a socket to go around the nut.  Nor is the box itself wide enough to accept a hitch ball wrench.  I cannot believe this could be designed so poorly.  I called the company and they were less than promising with advice.  They admitted the design problem, but their lead \\"designer was away on a factory visit and could I call him back next week?  Swagman was aware , of the problem - you have to jam a metal bar against the nut and the inside of the tow bar box and tighten the top of the hitch ball with a channel locks in order to get the ball tightened on.  Not exactly a good way of ensuring a tow ball is tightened properly to safely tow a trailer.  They said they would stand by the product, but only gave me words of encouragement, not sound advice.  Do not buy this to tow anything.  Do not buy this.  It's simply not safe as designed to use with a trailer.  Secondly, I had to put spacers in-between the cradles to keep them from sliding  A plastic water pipe (1 ¼\\" inside diameter) cut to 4\\"pieces keeps the cradles from moving and the bikes form rubbing on each other.  Did I mention you should not buy this product?

product_title: Columbia Womens Silver Ridge Long Sleeve Shirt
review_headline: Very flatteriing, durable, comfortable, breathable - what more can you ask?
review_body:
This shirt is my all time favorite synthetic shirt. I use it for hiking, everyday wear, river trips, travel, you name it. By now, I have it in both the white and the fossil (for dirtier times on the trail or river) in long sleeve, and in the short sleeve and sleeveless in white. The white is still bright after many washings, and it really sets off the slight tan I can pick up (through sunscreen). These shirts have had a lot less piling than any of my other synthetic shirts, and I wear these a lot! And Amazon often has a good - i.e., sale - price on some colors and sizes.

There is just something about the arced seam across the upper chest and back that is very flattering. I'm not sure you can see this in the photos, but somehow it makes my shoulders look better, and everything below look slimmer.

It's a semi-fitted shirt, not all blousey like some of my outdoors shirts, and true to size. It ventilates extremely well, with areas of more open fabric where you need them. I generally can take a S or M in this sort of shirt, and either one fits me in this one. I generally like the M best because it gives me a little more room to move when I'm active, but I do have one small in white that I keep nice to go out in. Yes, it is that good looking that I reach for it on casual nights out when my activity level is not that key.

Note that at this point, this shirt would have a uniform 5 star rating if someone had not given it low marks because it got lost in the mail getting to her. That's not a fair basis to rate the shirt on, and I bet she found it in the end, but still her low review pulls this shirt's score down. Not right! This is a true 5 star product!

product_title: Bear Grylls Parang Machete

It's a Gerber product so you don't need me to tell you about the quality but I will anyway.  This is a quality made blade.  The weight and thickness of the steel is all you'd expect from a Gerber blade and more than you would expect from a machete.  This will certainly do the trick for camping, outdoors use, hunting, survival and yes the dreaded zombie defense.  This blade is a good addition to any \\"go bag\\" or camping gear.  The rubberized handle is comfortable in the hand and the curve of the blade makes it ideal for chopping.  The sheath is pretty good to although I would like for it to have more than one option for attaching it to the body.  Only the one belt loop which doesn't allow for either inverted attachment nor ambidextrous attachment.  The sheath also doesn't allow for quick or easy removal and sheathing.  Another drawback is that the bolts in the handle are TORX instead of hex/allen.  I would have liked for the bolts to be of the American or metric allen head variety but I don't foresee much need to remove the blade from the handle. I like the non glare color of the blade and despite the conspicuous orange of the grip, this makes for a somewhat tactical machete.  If you are a \\"zombie-phobe\\" like me you'll want this machete because the weight and lack of serration make it ideal for dispatching the un-dead or \\"Solanum\\" infected attacker when Z-Day arrives.  For the camper and or survival \\"prepper\\" this is also a great blade for you because you can use it in a variety of situations. The quality of the blade, the weight and the ergonomic design are what make this machete superior.  This machete is Ideal for chopping and comfortable to hold and swing. This machete is worth every penny of the $42 retail price tag but at less than $30 it's a steal.  Those familiar with Gerber knives will want this to add to their collection, gear or arsenal. product_title: Ultega Wireless All-Round Bike Computer
review_body:
Having read the reviews on this wireless bike computer before ordering (including a few sharply critical ones), I figured I'm taking a big chance, but I decided to gamble since it has so many features for the price. I was happily surprised after I mounted it and took it for a test ride for a few hours, which is why I decided to write a review to set the expectations right.
1. INSTALLATION: Pretty easy, although the user manual is virtually unreadable.
2. WIRELESS CONNECTION: very good. I didn't experience any of the reported wrong speed indications. In fact, the wireless connection between the sensor and the display worked perfectly, under what I consider trying conditions: I had my rear light blinking and I has my iPhone in my pocket streaming music to my headset over Bluetooth, and I didn't notice any problem with the wireless computer. At some point, my biking trail passes about 50 feet from a radar installation and, at that point, the Bluetooth connection between the iPhone and the headset broke, but the bike computer was still working perfectly.
3. AUTO OFF / MANUAL ON: no problem. Other reviewers complained about the fact that after the computer automatically turns off when you stop, it doesn't turn back on automatically. This is true, but I don't have a problem with it: I am checking my speed all the time, so even if I forget to turn it on when I restart, I would notice that after a few seconds, and press any button to wake it up.
4. ACCURACY: very good. The size of my tires is missing from the table in the user's guide, so I entered the numbers from the nearest tire size in that table. I took a GPS with me to check the bike computer's accuracy, and it was within 3% of the GPS, which I think is very good, considering...
5. FEATURES: very good. Besides the regular functions (speed, ride time, distance, clock, etc), I found the mode in which it shows the average speed and the current speed relative to the average intriguingly motivating: I was constantly trying to go above average, which makes a great exercise.
6. USER GUIDE: useless, which is why I'm giving it only 4 out of 5 stars. It is so badly written and spelled, that it's not even funny!
7. PRICE: great.

review_body:
I'm going to talk about the size since it seems to be a topic of discussion on this item.

3)I am usually an XS, I am 100 lbs, A Cup, 5'2 tall.

product_title: SportRack A30901 2EZ Hitch Platform 2 Bike Rack
review_body: I own this and the Xport 4 bike version of this rack and have had both for about 3 years.  Both work great.  I've used this rack with both a 1 1/4\\" and 2\\" hitch. The 2\\" requires the plastic adapter and I've seen some bad reviews with that.  I've not had any problems with it but have found that you need to insert the adapter opposite to the side that you insert the threaded hitch pin (this allows the metal rack to tighten to the metal hitch).  As long as you insert the pin from the correct side, it's very solid.  However, if you insert the threaded pin on the same side as the plastic adapter, you can't tighten it properly because it's metal on plastic and it shakes horribly.    I carry a couple XC mountain bikes (just about every weekend) on short drives to the trailhead.  I've also taken a couple long trips where I've driven 3+ hours with this and felt very comfortable with rack.  After 3 years, it still does the job and I've been very happy with this rack.

review_body: What are the odds on getting 2 lemons in a row from Conquest? Our first Dyad (which is a bladder-and-skin inflatable)had a major leakage issue along the seams of the outer cover; we would be ankle-deep in water within 30 minutes. We contacted the distributor, who was very accommodating after we sent a video of the water gushing out of the seams after we'd filled it with a couple of gallons of water (to see where the leaks were)  We were sent a new Dyad while our first one was still in transit. We took it out and...once again, ankle deep in water. In fact, the new one leaked more rapidly. Constant bailing is required, unless you want to be waist-deep in water in about an hour.  I would like to point out that we are both well experienced with bladder-and-skin inflatable kayaks (3 other brands we own and use do not have this issue) and do not push the weight or capacity limits; nor do we operate these kayaks in areas where the skin or bladders may be easily punctured.  The issue with the Conquest Dyad is the seam on the cover. It leaks, and badly. The rest of the kayak seems to be sturdy enough. Definitely not worth spending $450.-plus on, though.

product_title: VDO MC1.0+ Wireless Altimeter/Cycle Computer
review_body: I have been using this for about a month and so far it works really well.  The setup and installation were easy.  So far the mount seems sturdy - it clicks securely in place and does not come out easily.  While this works for me, others who want to remove the unit regularly may not like it.    The altimeter is quite sensitive (it even registers the change in elevation when you lay your bike down).  The readings are pretty accurate - I have compared them to one friend's Garmin Edge 800 and to another friend's Polar wristwatch.  Over the course of a ride with over 4000 feet of climbing, the reading for total feet of climbing is less than 100 feet different.  Actual elevations have been less than 50 feet different.    I have used this on two night rides where a handlebar-mounted light was also used and had no problem with it.  The only issue I have had is that actual elevation sometimes fluctuates over extended periods (several days) when the bike is parked but that may be due to changing atmospheric conditions.  The instructions even give the procedure to re-calibrate the unit due to changing weather.

product_title: Hand Warmers - HotSnapZ Reusable Round & Pocket Warmers
review_body: These are very good hand warmers, last about an hour - 90 minutes in really cold temperatures. If HotSnapz made a smaller version of the handwarmers, they'd be downright perfect.  I actually just put the hand warmers in my pocket and grab them when I need them, since they're just too bulky under a glove. I love that they're reusable, and resetting them by boiling them is really easy.

product_title: SEASON SPECIAL""NEW & IMPROVED!! HEAVY-DUTY OVERSIZE Oasis COOL CHAIR-TOP OF THE LINE CONSTRUCTION- 10 YEARS WARRANTY-A BONUS SOLAR RECHARGEABLE LED FLASHLIGHT INCLUDED WITH YOUR PURCHASE....BUY TWO CHAIRS AND RECEIVE A BONUS COOLER BAG!!!
review_headline: Love it; bought it for hunting
review_body: Thumbs up; very sturdy.  I researched many of these type chairs before buying.  Of the many similar-looking products, this is the lightest one at only about 8 lbs (due to the shallower seat depth) - vs. up to 13 lbs for identical-looking ones (you may need a larger one if you're over 250 lbs); which this light weight is why I got it; to tote into the woods to hunt with -- Tall enough to see and shoot OVER tall grass, which is a real problem for short and even normal hunting chairs, as you know if you've tried it.  Great product so far, but to be fair, haven't actually hunted with it yet.  Good price for $105 plus shipping I thought.  You can also buy this EXACT same product for $70 plus $48 shipping from the same seller from a separate listing, for some reason, but why would you pay $13 more total?  Weird.  Definitely the best deal among all the similar chairs, for the quality you get, I think - and yeah, the insulated tote that comes with it is alright, too - might be useful for toting hot or cold food when a guest at another house for a potluck dinner.  The little light? Sure, why not - it works; throw in the re-gifting pile...  Gonna sand this thing down, primer, then paint it in flat tan - the whole thing (the shiny aluminum and black seat).  For years I've hunted with stands and blinds, but stands tend to be very dangerous things as we age, AND aren't readily movable when you realize that the perfect spot is actually over yonder a ways, not rat-cheer where you originally put it.  Blinds can be moved quickly, but the really good ones are expensive, they can spook game if not placed a couple weeks prior to hunting, are not durable (must be replaced every few years), and blow away and shred in windy places, even if staked with 8 stakes, as I learned this season.  Plus, a quality blind is heavier to tote around than this chair, and a blind PLUS small chair, which is the acutal substitute for this idea, is much heavier and cumbersome.  I've harvested far more game over the years (dunno why) from just a folding chair on the ground in the open (no blind) - or from stalking - than actually IN the many many blinds and stands I've purchased, hauled, assembled, erected, maintained, sat endless hours in, and lamented the placement when I see game out of range. Short portable tripod stands are a good idea, and work pretty well, but they're much, much, MUCH heavier than something like this to tote around. Think of this as a portable tripod stand that is lighter than any on the market, and can be hauled a couple miles in, should you choose, and moved on a whim.  So, I'll have to sit still (as we always have to do regardless), but this chair will be the only stand or blind I'll ever buy again, with any luck - simplify your life, kiddos!  The frame base goes across the ground on either side, plus two rear legs, to keep from tipping, rather than simply 4 legs with no 'cross-beams' - I'm thinking and hoping this will keep me from sinking in soft ground - we'll see.  This is why I didn't buy the other kind without this feature, but otherwise similar - and somehow the ones with just 4 legs come in heavier anyway.  Oh, I will also use this when I sit at gun shows as a vendor; may come in handy there as well.

product_title: Super Pogo 1505 Pogo Stick
review_body: I bought 2 pogo sticks for Christmas.  One for my 13 year old daughter and this one for my Husband.  I had bought this because my husband is 230 pounds and this had the highest weight limit.  Not only does he use it, I have had fun with it too.  I am 5'9\\" and 140 pounds.  It has a strong spring and is built to last.  We were reviewing our daughter's pogo and realized what a fitness item the pogo had become for adults.  It is such a workout and soooooo much fun.  I did get bruising on the inside of my knees.  My husband bought self stick foam meant for water pipes for me.  Problem solved.  He did not have that problem.  I assume that it is the way I hold my legs.  I would not hesitate to buy this product.  It is much taller than the one we got for my daughter, so if this is for a child, you may want to take a look at the product height.  My daughter can pogo on this, but the spring is very strong and she doesn't get decent compression like she can on hers.  She is 90 pounds. The way your hand fits around the grip is different, and while very comfortable, it does need to be positioned to distribute the pressure properly.  If it doesn't feel good at first, play with the angle before concluding it doesn't work!  After hitting the streets with these for a couple of days, any discomfort in my hands has *dramatically* diminished and I'm very satisfied.

Also my shelter had been heavily used as could be seen by all the stitches in it. My only complain is that it is very difficult to maneuver (as manual states :) the safety metal pin when you slide the seat on the rack as this pin is on the bottom of the seat and it is somewhat difficult to make sure it is in horizontal position (it has the spring mechanizm to keep it in the vertical position to ensure that the seat is secured to the rack and not moving) when sliding the seat any direction. product_title: Royal Robbins Women's Classic Zip N' Go Pant
review_headline: High waisted, order a size down
review_body:
I'm 5'0\\" tall and have a 26.5 inch waist, which falls right between a size 4 short and a size 6 short. I decided to order the size 4 short, and I'm glad I did. The pants are generously sized. The waistband is perfectly fit. It doesn't gap open at the back, but the elastic in the waistband barely stretches unless I bend over. The pants are high-waisted so they DON'T bind in the crotch. The waistband is very wide so it doesn't bind like a skinny belt, and the tummy section is a little baloony. It's roomy enough that I considered buying a size 2, but decided not to. Some people may not like the extra room, but for me this is NOT a bad thing! Unlike a model in a catalog, I actually like to walk and move and bend over and pick things up and I don't care if I look \\"unfashionable\\" doing it. In fact these are the ONLY pants I've been able to wear in years (jeans are a disaster). The pant length seems long, but it's not. It's only a little long on me because I'm so short.

The material is very durable and dries very quickly. They are very cool, with mesh inner pockets. They zip on and off very easily, and they don't look too casual. There are plenty of pockets, one with a zipper. One drawback is that there is no hook for a key ring, but I can just sew one in later. I ordered the black pants and after a few washings they haven't faded at all. If you're looking for low-rise and high fashion, I recommend you hie thee to the mall. If you like to think about stuff OTHER than which of your internal organs your pants are digging into at that particular moment, these are GREAT pants and well worth the price. I'm thinking of ordering another pair.

product_title: Serfas Seca Wire Bead Tire with FPS
review_body: I have used these on my regular road bike in the past, and was pleased with their low rolling ability that were also very puncture resistant.  In the past I have used Hutchinson Top Speed (Which flatted a lot but are low end, I hope), and various Michelins, such as Pro Race 2, 3, and Lithion.  All are much better than the Hutchinsons, but all had flats.  The Serfas are tougher and seemed to be at least as fast.  I did a 100 mile ride in Wichita Falls with these - and no flats.  (Although there were many people who had them).  Recently, I got a couple of old steel bikes that I want to rebuild - a Miyata, a Steyr, and a Schwinn.  I had originally put Kendas on the Miyata (These are all 27\\" which is hard to find) and they worked OK.  Felt different in a hard turn - but usually ride a Specialized Roubaix with Conti 4000's.  So I thought I could actually try a comparison and see what the difference is.  I ordered Conti Gatorskins, the Serfas - and had a nearly new set of Kendas - the type sold for 27\\".  By far the Kendas were the heaviest.  Much lighter were both the Conti's and the Serfas's.  The Serfas is the lightest - it has a slightly smaller 'thick area' of rubber to help prevent flats than the Gatorskins.  I know how the Serfas holds up - there is a set on my wife's bike that has around 1,0000 miles and they look new.  1 flat.  The Kenda's are the hardest to mount - all have steel beads.  The Serfas were around 2/3 the price of the Conti's - and feel the same on the road to me.  These seem a high value tire - they look nice, hold up well, and handle well.  Yes, they cost more than the Kendas (Who make excellent tires) and are less than the Continentals.  While I suspect the Gatorskins are a bit  more puncture resistant, I know from experience the Serfas do well there.  Both are easier to pedal than the Kendas.  Both turn more securaly.  The Kenda's are softer - when I change them I get black stuff on my hands.  You won't be dissappointed in the Serfas.

review_body: Overall this item is not bad at all, especially for the mere $27 you pay for it.  It is fairly durable and you can feel the quality of the construction from simply wielding it.  Cons - Unfortunately the terrible coating they slap on there is weak and comes off easily, the blade (at least mine) came duller than dull, but this is no big deal and this thing can be as sharp as you want it so don't let that deter you. Other than those minor flaws, this is actually a pretty nice piece for a reasonable price.  Now if I can go a few months without it breaking I will be satisfied!

product_title: The North Face Flint 2 Tent Boxed
review_body:
After owning a too small Eureka Solitaire (couldnt even sit up) i bought this wanting something a little heavier but with much more space.

The poles are just sweet, very light, gold anodized, and being alum. they will not snap like my fiberglass poles did on my Eureka. This thing is also really waterproof, everything but the mesh has a really thick coating of some sort of silicone or rubber.

I like the colors a lot. I just want to mention i did my research on this tent, hours and hours, and for the price, this is a top contender imo.

The thing weighs 3-4oz over 4lbs, which crushes the \\"Eureka Tetragon 5\\" 2 man tent (5lbs 12oz). I took this on a short 20 mile hike over 2.5 days. One thing that impressed me was the speed of assembely, putting it up was quick but taking it down was super quick. The way the poles are designed you can just slide then away from the tent instead of unclipping the plastic tabs one by one.

The ventalation in this is good, i never woke up to any condensation like my last tent did. Also without the rainfly you get a very good view for stars out of the \\"no see um \\" mesh.

I dont know why theres no reviews on this tent yet, except for that i think this is a new model, but i just wanted to add my 2c.

product_title: Bike Pump - Genuine Innovations - Ultraflate Plus Instant CO2
review_body: Hi, I've had the ultraflate for two years, and used it several times. It's difficult to get full pressure with a frame pump, and i've had two right rotor cuff injuries in the last eleven years. A few tips for this CO2 inflator. Get your tube started with a hand pump, make sure the tube is in the tire properly or you'll blow up the tube. Don't worry about over inflating, there is an equilibrium between the liquid co2 and the gas pressure in the tire. Keep the CO2 cartridge pointed down so gravity holds the liquid in the cartridge, if you tip the cartridge upward, you'll squirt liguid co2 and not inflate effectively.  brrrrrrrrrrrrr  If you insert the cartridge properly, and lock off after use, i've inflated more that one tire with this inflator, it will hold gas pressure for some time.

product_title: KMC X9.93 9-Speed Bike Chain
review_body: Been riding with this new chain for 2 weeks now and the shifting is excellent, it fits my shimano drive train just fine, smooth, quick and precise shifting. So now I just hope that it will last a long time.

product_title: Shimano 105 PD-5700 Road Bike Pedals (Black)
review_body: I like these pedals. I am a recreational rider, but tend to ride competitively with myself; while I don't need the weight reduction/quality improvement of ultegra/dura-ace I like a durable and still, quality pedal. I got them essentially free when they accidentally ended up on a floor model bike I purchased (pedals unintentionally left off cost of bike), though having ridden the base model spd-sl pedals previously, I imagine I'd be alright paying for these (especially the discounted Amazon price). I've not used ultegra/dura-ace, so I can't compare. Over the spd-sl, though, I noticed the 105's tend to spin a little more freely. They are also much more secure. The clip in/out feels stronger and more solid without having adjusted the tension on the release. I haven't had problems clipping out for stopping, nor have I had my foot release under high torque (which happened on occasion with the spd-sl). Oppositely, they are easy to get into. They have a large target zone so mounting your bike in traffic isn't very difficult, and if you're not able to lock in quickly, the pedals are large/flat enough to use as a platform pedal until you've found time to properly secure your cleat. I've pedaled through a few turns and had a one hit the ground and minus cosmetic damage, they have not been phased (mechanically). The only issue I've found with these pedals is based on personal style. They have six degrees of float, which is comfortable, but for my style of riding, I've found the mechanism which returns your foot to the neutral position (center) is a little strong. I tend to run on the pigeon-toed side of straight, and have noticed that translates to my riding position. For shorter rides this isn't a problem, of course, but for longer ones I notice some fatigue. I know that riding style needs to change (and running for that matter) so I don't tear up my legs and it's something I'll work on it since I've become extremely aware of it. But for now, if you have similar tendencies, it's worth taking note if you're on a test ride or considering the 105s.

product_title: ALPS New 3 Section Adjustable Hiking/Trekking/Snowshoeing Poles with Carrying Tote Bag
review_headline: Not bad, especially for the money
review_body: I bought these poles to go with a pair of snowshoes I already owned.  They are adjustable, which is so handy because either my husband or I can use them.  They are reasonably easy to adjust, and the adjustablilty makes them very easy to store.  They also came with a small clip that keeps the two poles together for storage, which is nice.  And finally, they have rubber stoppers that go over the points at the ends, which are nice for storing and traveling.

product_title: Delta Cycle Delta Airzound Bike Horn , colors may vary
review_body:
I'm about to purchase my second AirZound horn. The first one was on my daily rider for about eight years (rarely used, but always ready). So you can't complain too much about the longevity.

And it is loud! It'll scare the bejesus out of pedestrians and stop an offending car in its tracks. It definitely performs as advertised.

My main complaints:

1. Trumpet too near cyclist's head. It would be great if you could mount the valve/button up on the handlebars and mount the trumpet down on the fork. As it is, it's painful to use - I never use it frivolously. Also, an Arkel-style handlebar bag blocks the sound from going forward, instead redirects it up to your head.

2. Horrible tone. Not only is it loud, it is obnoxious! It produces a really unpleasant piercing noise. It does get the attention, but it would be nicer if it were like the Union Pacific locomotives.

3. Breakaway valve assembly breaks away too easily. After about five years of use, the link between the handlebars and the valve/trumpet got a little sloppy. In fact, it was the sloppiness of this link that, after eight years, eventually relegated this unit to the cesspit. It's good to have the sucker break away in a crash, but this was the weak link for me.

Nevertheless, I am going to purchase another AirZound. Despite its faults, it's still the best horn out there. I tried the Biologic air horn but found the reservoir was too narrow to fit snugly in my bottle cage, as well as a little too long for my setup. Otherwise, the Biologic looks just about identical to the AirZound and is probably just as good a unit.

product_title: Velo Orange 700c 45mm Stainless Steel Fender
review_body:
I have been commuting with a pair of these fenders. They are a bit heavier than plastic or aluminum fenders, though the weight difference isn't a great as one might expect. On the other hand, these fenders are more durable and less likely to dent: a nice quality to have when a bike is parked in a rack among other bikes.

On most bikes, you won't need a fender flap, as these fenders are longer than most. And they give any bike a nice, classic look. They will look as good on a \\"retro\\" build as on a modern bike.

The only reason I don't give them five stars is that they're not the easiest fenders to install. Try to do the installation with a friend: another pair of hands makes the job a lot easier and quicker. And, while they can be bent or cut to shape, doing so isn't quite as easy as on aluminum or plastic fenders.

The overall quality seems very good. Priced only slightly higher than most plastic fenders, they are a good value, as other Velo Orange products I use are.

review_body:
I used one of these for many years tent camping and fishing in the California Sierras; and so I know that this is the sturdiest compact lightweight camp cot available in today's market. I wanted to buy one last year; but they were completely sold out everywhere. I have been sleeping in my mummy bag on ensolite pads in my four season tent these last twenty years here on the Kenai Peninsula in Alaska where I now reside; and it will be nice to get off of the uneven, cold ground and onto a level platform again. I cannot wait to use it. I have already put it together twice and laid down on it in my bedroom next to my queen sized bed and it is sure nice. I cannot wait to go camping and fishing this summer and fall. And thank you Amazon.com for providing this marketplace where hard to find items can be bought easily, securely and at fair prices electronically.

Aloha,

Dennis A. Rofoli
Alaska Fly Fishers Anonymous
Kenai, Alaska

review_body:
I'm a Army Reservist living in South Korea and I wanted something to use as a bug out bag in case things went bad with North Korea, or any other emergency for that matter so I was on the market for a big well made backpack. I had some requirements though that had to met which follows:

1. It had to have good organization.
2. I preferred something made in USA.
3. It had to be big 2500cubic inches/45Liter + range.
4. It had to be durable and from a reputable company.

The Camelbak meets these requirement. It has many pockets for organization, and the sewn on exterior pouches save money from having to buy extra pouches. It's \\"assembled in America with foreign and domestic components.\\" So it's not 100% American but the Cordura nylon, and ITW buckles are American. Amazon says it's cargo size is about 2900cubic inches but it's really over 3100 if you include the exterior pouches.

The BFM is well made, comfortable to use. The only pack I have used that is better in terms of craftsmanship, and durability would be Spec Ops THE Pack. It uses 1000D Cordura, metal D Rings, and has the straps running through the backpack. But it's also a lot smaller. It and the Camelbak are also very comfortable to carry.

The BFM is a great pack that I'm glad to have it. I eventually switched to using the Spec Ops THE Pack as my bug out bag, and use the BFM for my range bag, travel bag, and camping bag. The BFM's main cargo area is big enough that it can hold my IBA body Armor (with plates), ACH helmet, knee, and elbow pads. That saves me a lot of hassle when I have to transport my battle rattle to training. That kit is over 35 pounds, and it rides comfortably on my back.

There are some things I would like to see improved though. First I wish it had a higher denier because the 500D Cordura is strong, but it can't keep it's form. For example when opening the clamshell, the BFM's main area, the pack literally just flops down. This is annoying because say I have some gloves, flashlight, and night vision equipment in the top front pocket. When you open the main area the nylon folds on itself like a T-shirt or something. So I have to spend time straightening the front portion out so I can find my gear. The 1000D Spec Ops, and Maxpedition do a good job of keeping their form. On the plus side the 500D does make packing the BFM easy.

product_title: CamelBak BPA-Free Better Bottle with Bite Valve
review_headline: Worst water bottle I've ever had
review_body:
After several months of almost daily use, my Camelbak bottle mouthpiece broke today, and I thought I might share with you how thrilled I am to get rid of this worthless piece of junk and order a sturdy new Thermos bottle to replace it. The Camelbak mouthpiece structure is of extremely poor quality, which is one of the many problems with this bottle. The clear plastic mouthpiece/\\"bite-valve\\" itself is generally ok, but the hard plastic part it sits on is really poorly made. One of the really flimsy tiny plastic prongs on that part broke long ago and that part has never sat right, as a result of constantly having to disassemble several parts of the mouthpiece and filter in order to clean it. The result was crimping of the clear plastic straw (also poorly crafted) underneath the mouthpiece, making water flow into the bite valve difficult. I thought I could deal with that, since I had invested in several of the rather pricey carbon filters, but combined with the other disadvantages, it's really not worth putting up with.

It is an abominable pain to clean, for something that is top rack dishwasher safe. There are so many small parts you have to pull apart that it's simply maddening and takes up a lot of space in your dishwasher. You also have to take the carbon filter out of it to clean (what am I gonna do with this nasty looking gray thing? I guess I get to display it on my kitchen counter on a paper towel till the load is done... gross.)

This bottle also leaks like crazy. Don't put it in a bag or backpack -- even if it's positioned sturdily upright, water somehow manages to get out. You may as well bring a cup with you wherever you go, because this thing is useless for portability, unless you're carrying it upright in your hand. I gave up bringing water with me anywhere and just filled it up wherever I was. I thought the whole point of a water bottle was portability.

The carbon filters, while a good idea in theory, don't do a good job of filtering. I still get the water fountain taste that Brittas or Pur filters take out. Those pricey little carbon filters are just not worth it.

I think the only good thing I have to say about this bottle is that it is BPA-free. Fortunately, many other companies are making them that way now, so I never have to purchase a Camelbak again. Steer clear of this bottle and spend your money on something that will last, doesn't leak, filters, and isn't a pain to clean. Is that too much to ask, Camelbak?

product_title: Aosom 17R Mag Indoor Exercise Bike Bicycle Trainer - Red
review_body:
The resistance does not increase on its own. There are only 3 levels on the handle bar mount,
Which the bracket broke the first time installing. I just set it to the highest and left it.
It is not quiet, and develops an additional hum/resonance at certain speeds. A front riser is needed and a rubber mat of sorts for vibration.
Overall, it works. I mounted the bike and have been using it for 4 weeks of work outs 3+days a week.
Would shop around more, definitely try another brand.

Update: Since looking around at other indoor trainers, this is acceptable for the price. I use the gears on my bike and have ignored the resistance adjuster that came with it. Would not try to use it while someone was sleeping, but smooth tires reduce the noise and so does working on your form (smooth pedaling with even pressure all the way around, instead of just pushing down on the pedals).

product_title: Energizer Weatheready 3-LED Carabineer Rechargeable Crank Light, Red
review_headline: What a fun light and useful too
review_body:
This is not an expert review, I've never owned nor used a crank light before. I'm not a cave diver, mountain climber of any other kind of sport enthusiast who would know the ins and outs of the different kinds of equipment used for lighting. I just know that this flashlight produces a nice amount of light, enough to light up the sidewalk after dark thereby illuminating any doggy turds left behind (I seem to possess an uncanny knack for finding the slimy piles with my clean and colorful sneakers).

The crank is easy to use and sturdy enough that I don't worry that in my enthusiasm I might snap it off.

The light is small enough to clip onto a shoulder bag or off of a belt for easy travel.

The light has a nice sized grip handle and is pretty lightweight so that an hour's walk after dark doesn't leave you feeling that you need to work on increasing your upper body strength.

Last of all, it's fun to use. There's something kinda cool about winding the crank on this for light. I usually hand it off to my son and he's always a little over zealous in the winding, but like I said before, this is a pretty durable light.

product_title: Marker 21-Inch Wheeling Double Decker Bag with Boot Section
review_body: Enjoying so far.  Taken on a few trips and seems to work great.  I like the pockets and love the smooth roll of the wheels.

product_title: Morakniv Companion Fixed Blade Outdoor Knife with Carbon Steel Blade, 4.1-Inch, Military Green
review_body: There is no better knife... for the money.  And even then.  I have read glowing reviews on Mora knives for some time, but thought they looked cheap, like steak knives you'd buy from Target or K-Mart.  This knife is anything but cheap.  Price-wise, okay, but quality is excellent.  Excellent!  You have laminated carbon steel with a Scandi grind (that means the main bevel IS the grind, no small near-the-edge micro sub-bevel that you can never align on a sharpening stone).  Therefore, sharpening is easy, and the knife comes nearly razor sharp; I swiped it at some tough plastic packaging and it glided through as if cutting air, totally effortless.  Amazing.  For backpacking, camping, or just around the house/farm/ranch utility, this knife is as good as it gets and probably as much as you need.  Now, it is carbon steel and that means it can rust, so wipe clean and keep oiled and this knife should serve you long enough.  I have talked about the blade, but the grip is very ergonomic and superb and seems to be of high quality plastic, tang is 3/4 through the handle(which is an improvement over the recent 1/4 tang in the previous discontinued version).  The plastic sheath is good quality, better than I had expected.  Would like to see more colors other than O.D. Green.  Go get yourself a couple of these knives.

product_title: Currie Technologies eZip 500 Electric Scooter
review_body: I bought this for my 11 yr. old daughter for Christmas.  She loves it!!  Do yourself a favor and watch the video on how to assemble and you'll be ready to roll in minutes (after charging the battery first). Wonderful transaction from start to finish! This is one very happy customer!

product_title: CamelBak Insulated 0.75-Liter Bottle Sleeve
review_body: In our family, we each have a CamelBak water bottle; we love them, but love them even more with this cover. product_title: SPOT Satellite GPS Messenger unit
review_body:
I've used Spot for about 4 years now in the USA and Asia Pacific region in airplanes, boats, hiking, driving, and motorcycling. It's all but worthless unless you have a completely unrestricted view of the sky and its messages are often delayed by more than 40 minutes to an hour. This is better than nothing, but only just. It's kind of like cheap tools...sometimes you're better to never have them because one day you might count on them and they'll break or not work properly. While Spot may save your life, it could also encourage you to rely too heavily on it and risk too much.

Then there is the issue of customer service. The call center rep I talked to actually raised his voice with me and told me that I was wrong to try and adjust my billing info online when you can't do that. He said, that's why we're open 5 days a week, so you can call us. I was overseas and couldn't call internationally, but he proceeded to tell me what an idiot I am. I may not have done things to his satisfaction but he was rude beyond what I've experienced even in basic human conversation, let alone customer-mechant relationships. This experience was surprisingly the same as what I heard it was like back when I first subscribed. I guess they still aren't making customers a priority. I don't foresee ever using a Spot device again.

product_title: 1 Liter Better Bottle
review_body: VERY, VERY DISAPPOINTED. Top was broken when I received, one of the knob ends that rotates the nipple out was busted. to much hassle to send back. still works but will tip to the side. ANNOYING..

product_title: d.light S10 Solar LED Lantern
review_body: Highly recommend.  It is a simple design.  Purchased several lanterns for presents - received wonderful feedback.  Simple and realiable. Concerned about having a flash light ready if the power goes out - this is awesome.  I will purchase more.

review_body:
