product_title: Mantis Lil Maya 12 Kids Bicycle
review_body:
I originally purchased a 16\\" bike for my 3yo. This was a dumb mistake. The reviews of the 16\\" bike said that it was perfect for a 3yo. Those reviews were wrong. My daughter is in the 90th percentile for height, and she could not reach the petals. This 12\\" bike fits her perfectly!

Some people complain about its build quality. The bike is built very well considering its price and the fact that it will only be used for a year before my daughter out grows it. If you want a bike that will last for years, spend $200, not $60.

Like most bikes, it was easy to assemble and packaged well. It took me maybe 30 min to assemble it.

My daughter LOVES her bike. I feel safe with her on this one. Of all her toys this was one of our best purchases.

product_title: CamelBak Bottle Accessory Bite Valves (Multicolor, Pack of 5)
review_headline: A Necessity for CamelBak Bottle Owners
review_body: I absolutely love my CamelBak waterbottle. However, over time the white bite valve that it comes with ineviteably gets dirty and disgusting. These are great to have as you can eventually replace the bite valve on your bottle. Simple enough, and it comes in cute colors too.

product_title: Clean Motion Leopard Skin Capperz Valve Stem Caps
review_body: These are very stylish and added a nice finishing touch to our restored cruisers.  They are also a good size and make opening the valves much easier than the original/stock caps.  They were also a great value considering the quality.  I got the leopard print for my bike and 8-ball style for the hubby's.

product_title: TOPEAK Alien II Multi-Tool
review_body:
I got the Topeak Alien II after comparing this tool to others on their site and reading reviews about it. The only negative I could find that was relevant was about the plastic clip that holds the two parts together. Irrelevant negatives were about the included tools, not enough, too much, doesnt work with every bike (should be obvious), I find all three of those negatives to personal preference.

The clip that holds the two halfs together is plastic but I dont see it being a problem unless is gets dropped at least a few times (already dropped it once and it held together).

The weight of this tool is noticeable, but is too be expected with the number of functions that this device has. I would not recommend keeping this in your pocket while biking.

This tool is great as the numerous functions allow you to do your own tune up for your bike, but be careful with the spoke tool as if you use it improperly it can cause the most trouble, unbalanced wheels.

Check to make sure this tool has the functions you need as the other Alien tools that have less functions may work for your use (and be cheaper)

product_title: Limited Edition Water.org CamelBak Groove Water Bottle (Stainless Steel)
review_body: I use mine a lot, it keeps my water cold. Its easy to take with me. It keeps my water clean, I know nothing has gotten into it.

product_title: ABO Gear Instent Max Shelter
review_headline: A TOP PRODUCT THAT MUST BE IMPROVED
review_body: I BOUGHT THIS TENT TO TAKE MY FAMILY OF FOUR TO THE BEACH SO WE CAN HAVE A SHELTER TO PROTECT OURSELVES, SPECIALLY THE LITTLE ONES, FROM THE SUN WHENEVER IT GETS TOO STRONG.  IT'S PRETTY GOOD. IT OPENS UP IN SECONDS AND CAN BE INSTALED ALSO PRETTY QUICKLY ON THE BEACH AS LONG AS THERE IS NOT MUCH WIND, BUT I GUESS THIS WOULD ALSO BE TRUE FOR ANY TENT AT ALL.  BEFORE I RECEIVED THIS TENT I READ SOME USERS REVIEWS SAYING THAT IT WOULD COLAPSE AND ALSO THAT THE JOINTS ON THE POLES WILL BREAK WHEN INSTALED IN A WINDY PLACE. WELL, I HAVE TO SAY THAT WHEN I GOT IT I TRIED IT FIRST AT HOME AND, BEING A CIVIL ENGINEER AND A HANDY MAN, I DECIDED NO TO WAIT UNTIL THE JOINTS BROKE, SINCE THEY DO LOOK THAT THIS COULD REALLY HAPPEN, AND WENT AHEAD WITH MAKING SOME ALUMINUM REINFORCENTS FOR THEM. NOT THE FANCIEST ONES BUT THEY WILL CERTAINLY ABSORV MOST OF THE EFFORT PLACED ON A JOINT WHEN WIND HITS THE TENT. I BELIEVE THAT THERE IS A VERY EASY WAY TO MAKE A PRETTY EASY TO INSTALLL REINFORCEMENT FOR THIS TENT'S JOINTS SO THEY GET PROTECTED AND CAN WITHSTAND ANY WIND SITUATION BUT THIS WOULD BE FOR ABO GEAR TO CONSIDER. ALSO, RELATED TO THIS, ABO HAS INCLUDED FOUR PEACES OF ROPE, APROXIMATELY 6 1/2 FOOT EACH, AND FOUR NOTCHES SEWN TO THE TENT AT MID HEIGHT SO IT CAN BE SECURED TO THE SAND USING THE ALSO SUPPLIED STAKES. THIS IS A MUST ON WINDY SITUATIONS AND I WOULD SAY THAT, MOST OF THE TIMES, IT WOULD BE A MUST WHEN ON THE BEACH SINCE MOST OF THEM HAVE A LOT OF WIND, BUT I WOULD RECOMEND TO ATTACH THE ROPE TO THE POLE ITSELF AT EACH NODE INSTEAD OF USING THE SEWN NOTCHES SINCE THIS CAN BE DONE IN THIS THIS PARTICULAR TENT. I USED THE SEWN NOTCHES TO SECURE THE TENT ON THE BEACH AND, UNFORTUNATELLY, MY WIFE RAN OVER ONE OF THEM AND SOME TENT SEAM GOT BROKEN. ALSO SECURING THE TENT TO THE SAND AT NODE HEIGHT WILL TRANSFORM A SUBSTANCIAL AMOUNT OF FLEXURAL EFFORT AT THE NODE INTO SHEAR EFFORT (THIS PART FOR PEOPLE KNOWING ABOUT EFFORTS ONLY), WICH WILL ALSO HELP KEEP THE NODES FROMBREAKING DUE TO WIND HITTING THE TENT.  THE FIRST TIME I TOOK THE TENT TO THE BEACH ACTUALLY THERE WAS A LOT OF WIND AND I DIDN'T HAD ANY PROBLEM SINCE I USED THE NODE'S REINFORCEMENTS THAT I MADE AND ALSO SECURED THE SEWN NOTCHES TO THE SAND USING THE ROPE AND STAKES SUPPLIED WITH THE TENT. THAT DAY I HAD ANOTHER TENT BESIDE THE INSTENT MAX. THIS SECOND TENT WAS ONLY SECURED TO THE BEACH USING THE FLOOR GEARS AND IT KEPT BENDING DOWN ALMOST TO FLOOR LEVEL DUE TO WIND. THIS WASN'T THE CASE WITH THE INSTENT MAX.  FOR TENTS USING THE OLD POLES MECHANISM IT WOULD BE EASIER TO SET UP IN A WINDY SITUATION SINCE YOU CAN ATTACH THE FLOOR OF THE TENT TO THE SAND FIRST AND THEN OPEN IT UP, BUT WITH INSTENT MAX THIS IS NOT POSSIBLE SINCE GEARS ON EACH CORNER OF THE TENT FLOOR WILL LAY DOWN ON THE BEACH VERTICALLY INSTEAD OF HORIZONTALLY BEFORE OPENNING THE TENT SO, IN ORDER TO ATTACH THE TENT FLOOR TO THE SAND, FIRST YOU MUST OPEN THE TENT, WICH WILL MAKE IT MORE DIFFICULT TO SECURE IF WINDY, AND THEN ATTACH IT TO THE SAND; NEVERTHELESS I BELIEVE THAT IT CAN STILL BE DONE EASIER THAN WITH THE OLD POLES MECHANISN.  I DIDN'T HAD ANY PROBLEMS WITH THE TENT COLLAPSING OVER ME AND, FOR THIS, I DIDN'T TOOK ANY MEASURES DIFFERENT THAN TO TIE BOW WITH THE ROPE AT THE TOP OF THE TENT WHICH IS EXACTLY WHAT THE MANUAL SAIS. IT IS PRETTY QUICK AND EASY TO DO. SAND POCKETS ARE ALSO VERY USEFULL SINCE THEY KEEP THE FLOOR OF THE TENT PRETTY WELL SECURED TO THE BEACH.  ALSO, FOR THE MOST SUN PROTECTION BOTH TENT DOORS SHOULD BE PLACED ONE BESIDE EACH OTHER INSTEAD OF ONE IN THE FRONT AND THE OTHER ONE IN THE BACK OF THE TENT AS IT IS RIGHT NOW.  ALSO, THERE IS A WARNING AT THE END OF THE MANUAL SAYIN \\"WARNING:  DO NOT USE IN STRONG WINDS. THIS PRODUCT IS NOT A WIND SHELTER. ABO GEAR ACCEPTS NO RESPONSIBILITY FOR MISUSE OF THIS PRODUCT\\". I GOT, IN SOME WAY, DISSAPOINTED WHEN I SAW THIS. IT IS SIMPLY NOT THE CASE IN MOST OF THE BEACHES AND THIS IS SUPPOSED TO BE A BEACH TENT.  BOTTOM LINE  ONTHE UP SIDE  I REALLY LIKE THE QUICK SETTING MECHANISM IT IS PRETTY PRETTY GOOD  PRETTY QUICK AND EASY TO SET UP  CAN BE SECURED TO THE BEACH QUICK AND EFFICIENTLY EVEN ON WINDY SITUATIONS  YOU'LL HAVE MORE TIME TO ENJOY THE BEACH WITH YOUR LOVED ONES USSING THIS TENT  EASY TO FOLD BACK WHEN NOT ON WINDY SITUATIONS (ME, I JUST WRAPPED IT UP AS FAST AS I COULD AND PLACED IN MY CAR'S TRUNK. BACK IN THE HOUSE I OPENED IT UP AGAIN, CLEANED IT AND FOLD IT BACK INTO IT'S BAG)  ON THE DOWN SIDE  I BELIEVE NODES ARE WEAK AND WILL BREAK, AS READ IN OTHER REVIEWS, IF NOT REINFORCED (I HAVE TO ACCEPT I DIDN'T GAVE THE NODES A CHANCE TO BREAK BEFORE REINFORCING THEM. I THINK IT WAS BETTER THIS WAY)  BOTH TENT DOORS SHOULD BE ONE BESIDE THE OTHER INSTEAD OF ONE IN THE FRONT AND ONE IN THE BACK OF THE TENT (THIS IS FOR MOST SUN PROTECTION)  GOT DISSAPOINTED WHEN I SAW THE WARNING NOTE IN THE MANUAL ABOUT PLACING THE TENT IN STRONG WIND SITUATIONS (MOST OF THE BEACHES HAVE A LOT OF WIND.  !BOOOOO.....!)

review_body: I hate this backpack.  I've been using it daily for about 3 weeks and I can't stand it. God forbid I want to put something large in it because there's just not room in there since it's broken up into such a huge number of small pockets! The only thing I like about this product is the adjustable elastic on the water bottle pockets on the sides.    Save your money and go with any other backpack on the market because this one is just bad.  I will be putting all my stuff back in my broken 10yr old eastpack as soon as I get home tonight.

product_title: Swagman XTC-4 Cross-Country 4-Bike Hitch Mount Rack (2-Inch Receiver Hitch)
review_body: OK, so my choice of this product was, in large part, due to the reviews that were included on the site. I feel compelled to add my own two cents in hopes that it will help someone else as they weigh their decision.  Mine came with a locking hitch pin that also tightens it in the hitch to prevent wobbling. It also included a serious cable for use in securing the rack and bicycles to the car. The slick thing about this is that the cable appears to also utilize the locking hitch pin for securement: therefore eliminating the need for an additional lock. I'll try these included items and perhaps avoid the need to \\"upgrade\\".  I received the package (on time and with no shipping charge thanks to 'Amazon Prime') and have opened and unpacked all the parts. At first glance this thing looks rock solid. It is heavy and difficult to handle in the box, but I expect it to be more manageable once I get it assembled simply due to the fact that there will be more places to grab hold. The box is tough to handle because it is oversize with no grip points.  As another reviewer noted, it does appear that it will be simpler to assemble ON the vehicle. My reasoning is that the central parts will remain upright and stable while you maneuver the smaller parts into place. The instructions do leave a bit up to the assembler, but it appears painfully obvious what goes where after you have seen the assembled picture and the accompanied diagrams.  I'll update this review after full assembly and usage....TTYL

review_body: Comfortable for a small face, not very light, but flexible to shape. product_title: U.S. Divers Diva Women Snorkeling Set, Ladies Silicone Mask, Trek Travel Fins, Dry Top Snorkel + Gear Bag
review_body: This set was great to have for our honeymoon in Maui, not only because it came with a durable bag to throw wet gear in, but the open toes were perfect for comfort, the mask didn't leak, and the snorkel was pretty decent at keeping water out. review_body: Nice shirt, great color. I got the brown, I mean \\"Earth\\" color. Am going through a brown phase (I cycle between black and brown), and this is the perfect shade for me. product_title: Bell Wo Light Set
review_headline: cheapest lights to come with batteries
review_body: i used to own the zefal light set, which is only a few more dollars than this item and was very pleased with it. however, my bike was stolen along with all my accessories. so i bought a cheap replacement mountain bike. i figured i didn't want to spend a ton of money replacing all my accessories in case the same thing happened in the future so i bought these.  there were much better light sets that were only a dollar or two more, but the main reason i bought this item was it was the cheapest light set to also include batteries. all the other light sets i saw were clearly labeled 'batteries not included', except for the zefal light set i mentioned, which does come with batteries. if you factor in the cost of batteries, all the other light sets might cost you north of $20. for that money, you're better off buying the zefal set.  if you're looking for a light set to actually be able to see well in the dark, you're gonna have to shell out a few more bucks than this. if you're looking for a light set to be seen for the sake of safety, this'll do the trick. if you have (or have had) multiple bikes and don't want to shell out extra money for lights and stuff, go with this item.  another reason i bought this item is the 'no-tools necessary' installation. they clip on and off easily, which is ideal because i don't plan on leaving the lights on my bike when left unattended. there are much better light sets out there but if your situation/reasoning is similar to mine, this item will do.

product_title: Camp Chef HWD5 Triton Water Heater
review_body:
I love my new camp chef tankless instant water heater! The only thing I had to do was bend the tab up in the battery box so that the batteries made contact, after that it fired up as soon as I turned on the shower head.

It makes very hot water in mere seconds just as advertised. I have had a tankless water heater in my house for the past 10 years so I am familiar with how they work and this one works great.

But, the first camp chef that I received didn't work right. I called tech support in Utah and left a message with their engineer. He called me back and I discussed with him how the unit was malfunctioning. He decided to ship me a new heater and have Fed Ex pick up my old one. The exchange took place in just a few days and I am very happy with my new water heater.

product_title: 5.11 #74363 Men's TacLite EMS Pants
review_headline: Nice material and features for EMS work
review_body:
These were definitely created with the EMS worker and volunteer in mind. There is a pocket for everything. I bought a pair of the Taclite pants for myself (outside of our uniform buys which uses the regular 5.11 [[ASIN:B005L80XYY 5.11 #74310 Men's EMS Pant]] which have a heavier material and are just heavier all around. The TacLite material is a ripstop fabric and if you look closely, you can see the pattern in the material. But they differ so minimally from the regular 5.11 EMT pants that you really won't be able to tell the difference, but they are substantially lighter when coming to wear.

I like the TacLite material and it is Teflon treated and holds well up to repeat washing and drying. I have washed these about 10 times thus far and have had no fading to date.

A ton of pockets for many different gadgets from stethoscopes to penlights and pads of paper. You can carry a lot in here. My uniform consists of these pants, the [[ASIN:B005L6AYVI 5.11 #41060 Short Sleeve Professional Polo Shirt]] with my specific agency information and the [[ASIN:B003Z0KUWK 5.11 TDU 1.75-Inch Belt]]

Pricey but worth it.

product_title: Worksman Mega Bicycle Horn
review_body: As it has been mentioned before by other reviewers, this horn is loud enough to attract attention (most of the time, but when it doesn't, it's not the horn's fault). The quality, though, just horrible. Not only the mounting strap broke after a first ride (I've managed to rig it back), but the horn itself died in less than a year. I keep my bike inside, so the horn was exposed to the elements only during the rides. Granted, I ride in any kind of weather, but still... This is just another made-in-China piece of crap.

product_title: Timbuk2 The Snoop Camera Messenger Bag 2013
review_headline: Great quality Timbuk2 bag with a lot of room!
review_body: This bag lives up to the standards of every other Timbuk2 bag: great quality and durable. First off, I would have preferred the black version of this particular bag, but it was out of stock and I needed the bag for a trip to NYC. The green color is actually better than I had expected, and I have grown to like it as it is different than the typical black camera bag. Next: yes, this bag is quite large, but that is to be expected as this is the medium size (the largest size offered from TImbuk2 for the snoop camera messenger bag). I was able to fit my Nikon D300 with the 18-200mm attached, my 70-200mm 2.8, 50mm 1.8, 55mm macro, and my SB900, as well as my card reader, battery charger, spare battery, and cords in the empty space under the camera body, and still had quite a bit of room left. This did mean the bag was quite heavy, but manageable, and the included strap pad helps reduce any discomfort caused, but not eliminate it entirely. Some reviews mention how the strap sets the messenger bag too high on the body. If adjusted properly, I was able to get the bag to hang by my side, BUT, the point of positioning the bag higher on your body is to reduce strain on the wearer. Adjusting the bag to sit higher up on the body and on the back of the wearer puts the bag in closer proximity to the wearer's center of gravity and will help reduce any strain the bag my cause from wearing it. This did help in my case at least, and still allowed the bag to be easily swung to my side to access it. The strap pad makes the bag easy to swing from behind you to your side to rummage through the gear inside. The grab strap makes it nice when you want to remove the bag from your shoulder and carry it rather than wear it. Also, the velcro silencers are a nice touch, and allow the user to choose to solely use the buckles to secure the bag closed or a combination of the buckles and the velcro located just under the flap for a more secure fit. One pitfall I discovered, however, was the small capacity of the pockets on the front of the bag. They are capable of holding things such as memory cards and cords, but even when packed with something like a lens pen and a cord or spare battery (in just one of the pockets, mind you there are three pockets including one clear window pocket), the pockets would bulge. This is more of an OCD problem for me, and may not be a problem for others. I decided to put any spare cord in the space between the actual camera insert portion and the padded tablet/laptop portion of the bag. I still have yet to add in my 15\\" MacBook Pro, but I did carry my Kindle Fire in the padded part of the bag. All in all, I really like this bag, and would recommend it to anyone. While the size may not be for everyone, it suited my needs. The next size down (small) may suit others better, but I like having my gear with me in case I need it, even if it is slightly heavy.

product_title: Fox Head Men's Launch Short
review_body:
These under short MT bike protectors are great. They allow for a full range of motion and are only slightly more bulky than standard shorts.

The protection is quite effective. I've fallen with my upper thigh slamming directly into a root as my first point of contact and it barely hurt. I was shocked as I did the same thing last season and could barly walk afterwords. Defiantly worth the money!

product_title: 12 Premium SKY LANTERNS 40" Tall Hot Air Balloons - PINK
review_body: The lanterns were ok. At least 10 out of 25 were stuck together when opened, seams would tear and I had to tape closed so they would rise. Back to the Wish Lanterns we used last year.

review_body: The instructions could be better, however, the product does what it advertises... for the price, I cannot complain... At least the hardware came complete as opposed as a similar lift (same brand) for kayaks.

review_body: Despite the trouble of refilling every night before sleep for more comfort, this airbed is very similar to the real mattress. (I would suggest putting a comforter over it to make it more cosy)

product_title: U.S. Divers Diva Women Snorkeling Set, Ladies Silicone Mask, Trek Travel Fins, Dry Top Snorkel + Gear Bag
review_body:
When we got to Oahu, we saw this this level of gear was what you were able to rent at the Hilton Hawaiian village. So, not that high end a set. It's always a risk buying things like this online, and I have a few gripes, but here goes.

Fins:
They're short and, as such, you don't get as much power with them as you do a regular length fin. I knew this going into the purchase though. Nice for navigating in small areas but I miss the power of my other fins. My foot is a 9.5 women's (normal width) and my boot fit just fine. The bottom of my fin says (M 7-10 40-44). Hope that helps someone with sizing. Easy to adjust.
Now, I'm not sure what the boot is made of but I think it might contain latex as after the first 2 days of snorkeling, my feet are covered in red, itchy bumps only where the fin boots meet with my foot (seems like an allergic reaction and I \\"AM\\" allergic to latex). I've written to US Divers and they haven't replied to my inquiry two days later. On their site they say that it's some sort of composite...but a composite of WHAT?

Mask:
It's silicon but it leaks around the edges. Hence, a bad fit. I have a normal sized head so I'm not sure what the problem is. Fogs continually (and I'm an experienced snorkeler). Doesn't seem to tighten very easily. It has a single piece of glass on the front, but it does NOT have glass on the sides.

Snorkel:
Has a crappy clip - snorkel comes off of my mask CONSTANTLY. Nearly every single time I take my mask off my snorkel detaches from the mask. REALLY frustrating. This is a DRY snorkel - first I've ever used. It's a bit frustrating to use. Something I didn't realize about dry snorkels is that the breathing tube gets narrower towards the top - which means that you have to suck harder to get the air you need. If you're doing some serious swimming and need that extra air, you'll find yourself getting a bit winded. I also noticed that the top part would slap shut when I tilted the snorkel in a certain way, cutting off the air. (Maybe it was supposed to do this but it was always a bit of a shocker to me). If they could make a dry snorkel with the same diameter as a regular one, that would be really nice. I don't like to fight to get my air.

Bag:
Nice as you can sling the entire thing over your shoulder. Has room for a few extra things in there as well. It has mesh so water and sand fall right out. There's also a small pocket where you can put in a business card or something to identify that it's your bag.snorkel in a certain way, cutting off the air. product_title: Maxxis Ignitor Mountain Bike Tire
review_body: I've not ridden tires like these in a very long time. I used to race cross country and always was looking for tire that would grip like these do.  I enjoy going fast down hill and after trying the tires after installing I was pleasantly surprised with how good they perform. Low rolling resistant, great on tight and open turns regardless the loose, hard pack or rocky terrain.  I totally recommend them.

product_title: Nantucket Bike Basket Co Steps Beach Collection Oval Picnic Bike Basket with Quick Release (Natural, Adult)
review_body: I absolutely LOVED this basket.  Unfortunately Amazon didn't include the bracket used to attach the basket to the handlebars.  Customer service was absolutely NO help.  It seems they didn't think that bracket should come with the basket, but the manufacturer said that it is supposed to be with the basket.  How else would you attach it to the bike? product_title: Kinetic by Kurt 2013 Road Machine Indoor Bicycle Trainer
review_body: For twenty years I rode a mag trainer and tried other sorts thru friends...then I got the Road Machine. Quite simply, it is in a whole other league compared to other trainers...it is about as close to road riding as you are gonna get for winter training...and while it was twice the price of my old mag turbo, it is worth every penny. On the old mag turbo,I couldn't get off the bike fast enough when I hit my allotted training time...with the Road Machine, I enjoy it so much I do even more time...I find myself actually looking forward to the old dreaded winter training session. Unbelievably good trainer...get one and you won't be sorry.  A further note...they have about the best customer service I have ever experienced...had a slight problem with vibration and they sent me a new resistance unit and flywheel along with a prepaid box to return the other resistance unit...this way, I never missed a day on my trainer over winter...other companies, if they even back up their product, would have you return your unit and wait and wait until they sent you a new one...that and would most likely charge you postage...Kurt customer service really is the best!

product_title: Timbuk2 Griptex Messenger Bag Strap Pad
review_body: The construction of this pad is solid, the grip is efficient. It is bulky put still perfectly acceptable even during business trip.

product_title: Under Armour Men's RealTree AP/Timber UA Ayton Camo Fleece Pants
review_body: Love these pants. I hunt alot and I sit for long periods of time in various type of stands so I go for comfort. Can't beat these in that category. review_body: This seatpost does exactly what it should. product_title: Orage Girl's Thalia Insulated Jacket
review_headline: What an awesome deal on a great jacket!
review_body: I ordered this for my youngest daughter to wear next winter.  She will be skiing for the first time, and I wanted her to have a very nice ski jacket.  I noticed the price of this one kept going down more and more as summer approached.  Finally, I had to order it!  I saved about $120! product_title: duogreen Spork 4 Pack Magnetic Set for Camping Picnic Outdoor Activity Spoon Fork Combo with Peanut Shape Carrying Case
review_body: I bought these for our trip to Africa and only ended up using them twice. Loved that they have their own case to keep them clean. However took them to a hotel a month later and two snapped in half right where the magnet is. Only hand washed them and didn't try to eat anything tough. Super bummed they didn't last longer than six weeks and three uses.

product_title: 5.11 Tactical Holster V-Neck Shirt
review_body: In concept, this shirt seems to be a very good solution to conceal carry. Realistically, it's not so great. Like all products from 5.11, this is made with quality and designed to last long. I purchases this holster shirt for conceal carry while wearing dress shirts. I figured it would always be accessable right from my shirt buttons. I carry a Sig Sauer p220 compact, and it stores very nicely in the compartment. The issue I have is, it's not very accessable when you want to draw. The pocket design is very deep, I assume so it would accomodate most any handgun firearm, even the Smith and Wesson 500. Drawing the firearm is a bit tough through a shirt, as well as reholstering it one handed. The other issue I did not like about this shirt was the foam padding around the shoulders and chest. They act as an insulator and causes me to sweat a lot more in those areas - deeming this a very difficult solution in the summer. Now, if you were in law enforcement or military, and you had the physique to wear such a shirt and not look like a choking sausage, this shirt is perfect for you. Otherwise, perhaps it's better to move onto a different solution.

product_title: GSI Outdoors - Halulite Tea Kettle, 1 Quart, Superior Backcountry Cookware Since 1985
review_body: I bought this little kettle for an annual camping trip with some friends. It doesn't hold much water, but, it is enough for a couple of cups of coffee. And, since it does not hold much it boils super fast. I would definitely recommend to anyone that wants to bring a kettle camping and doesn't have much space to spare.

product_title: Exo-Science Powermonkey Extreme 5V and 12V Solar Portable Charger
review_body: This solar charger charges anything iPod iPhone any droid phone it charged my iPad twice w/out connecting to power the lithium battery is great and holds charge for a long time.charge it 110volt or with the solar it works great for me.

product_title: SPOT Personal Tracker
review_body:
I don't review products I purchase but I'll make this an acception. I bought the \\"low end\\" version of SPOT because my needs are simple. I hike county parks alone almost always. Family worries about me getting hurt, etc. This little tracker suits me pretty well.

Pros:

The \\"OK\\" feature works like a champ. The \\"tracking\\" feature works well enough that family members can see where I am A LOT of the time, but not always. Tree coverage greatly affects the signal. Recently, I was hiking on a path with heavy tree cover. Not one time did the tracking show up on the entire trail which is 1.2 miles long. Once I was in the open, it worked fine. It has a HELP button and a 911 button of which I hope to never have to use. I don't know how that function will work as of yet. It's lightweight enough that it easily hooks onto a strap on the shoulder of my backpack. I find that's the best place for this tracker to pick up satellite signals. It needs to be face up or at least vertical to work.

Cons:

In order to send an \\"OK\\" message, the buttons to do this on the unit is simple enough. But then, you have to manually changes the settings to have it start tracking. It cannot be set up to do both simulaneously. I find that annoying. If I can get a cell signal, I'll send an \\"I'm ok\\" from my smartphone and just keep the SPOT on tracking. If no cell signal, then I have to manually reset my SPOT to send \\"OK\\" message, then reset again to go to \\"tracking\\". I have to wait until the \\"OK\\" message goes through before I can reset to \\"tracking\\". This can take up to 15 minutes. The SPOT gives a certain signal once the \\"OK\\" message has been sent.

All in all, I am pleased with it. The contract per year isn't too bad considering it just may save my life one day.

product_title: High Sierra AT605 Carryon On Wheeled Backpack with Removable Day Pack
review_body: I was hoping this bag would offer me a super versatile solution - but found it's over-designed upon arrival. My intention was to use it to fly to a location and then hike for a few days (either staying in a hotel or not) but the bag is too wide when the backpack is attached.  Knowing how crammed overhead bins are these days - I didn't even bother.  The backpack portion has an odd pocket between the front and rear that is extremely narrow and the rear portion that rests against your back is also very rigid.  I promptly returned the item.

product_title: Maxam Italian Mosaic Genuine Lambskin Leather Belt Bag
review_headline: This is a good fanny pack
review_body: This helps you when you are shopping and so not have to take  much with you. You can just put your license and money and credit card in it and they will stay safe when you wear it.

product_title: Salsa Crossing Guard 44T 110mm BCD Black
review_body: Went from a 3x10 on my hybrid to a 1x10 including removing the front derailleur and shifter.  I was already using a chain keeper to ensure that my chain didn't fall off to the inside.  A local bike shop mechanic had warned me that without the front derailleur my chain might fall off to the outside.  I should have heeded the warning because on my first ride with the 1x10 setup that's exactly what happened.  Installing the Salsa Crossing Guard fixed the problem.  It works great and looks good too.

product_title: Schwinn Pillow Top Cruiser Bicycle Seat
review_body:
A vast improvement over the generic seat that came with my bike, nice and wide, offers great support and comfort for casual/long distance rides.
Install was less then 60 seconds.
Highly recommended. my wife loves having a soft seat for an hour of light exercise/cruising in the evenings.

product_title: Energizer Weatheready 3-LED Carabineer Rechargeable Crank Light, Red
review_headline: awesome little flashlight, very bright for the size
review_body: this flashlight is surprisingly bright for a its size and considering that it is crank charged. i really like this flashlight. it's so easy to use my 3 yr old son can turn it on and off easily. the charge lasts a long time too.

product_title: Adventurer Aluminum Survival Kit Box
review_body:
Big vs. small- Survival tin size depends on you! I have included shots of my Every Day Carry- BCB tin, self stocked!, for comparison. I like this tin, the size is great for a pack or car. First what I don't like- not a big fan of anodized anything, it's like the egg thing- first it's good then bad, would not want to boil my water in it. The BCB tin wins in this area as it is just plain old aluminum. Second I have to agree that the rollers are not the greatest and their rubber so melting is an issue. I have no issue with the inner lid seal as you can see in the photo, it fits pretty well and is not all messed up. It also has a sticker on bottom of it from the Adventurer series survival equipment on it, so guess you'll have to burn it off if you don't want it!

This fits a LOT of items in it depending on your idea of survival gear, still filling mine! I don't really worry about it breaking open if I drop it, probably more that I'll dent it. The more gear you pack in them the more durable they are. The lid fits pretty snugly and the metal reminds me of the Coleman cooking pots, ya know the ones from Wally world. A little on the thin side, probably for weight control. Check out the photo's hope they give you a clearer picture!

Bottom line: I like both my tins for different reasons, but either way you can't go wrong, happy with both purchases!

product_title: Wenzel Camp-Away Airbed with Comfort Adjust Pump
review_body: Has worked well for my mom, whom I purchased it for. She has been helping out at my brother's quite a bit and has been using this to sleep on during those occasions. So far, it's held up...

product_title: On Guard Bulldog Mini DT Lock 5015
review_body: As this lock is the only lock I've purchased, I'm unsure of how it ranks in comparison to other locks. However, for the purpose of protecting my bike from being stolen, this product excels.  Just a few days ago I went to check on my bike and noticed that my cable lock had been cut. I didn't ride my bike for a little over a week so I'm unsure of when the person attempted to steal it. Looking at what remained of the cable lock, it appears that it took very little effort to cut it, which is reasonable considering it wasn't meant to be the main theft deterrent. Looking at the u-lock, there appeared to be no damage done to the actual lock or perhaps the thief didn't even attempt to break the lock. However, I noticed that the side of the bike frame where I had connected the u-lock to was partially damaged indicating to me that the thief did put in quite a bit of effort to break this lock.  As for the actual lock, it's fairly small and heavy. You might have a little difficulty locking up your bike as did I at first, but you'll soon figure it out. It's really strong and durable and looks and feels like it can withstand a lot of damage.  Since I now need a new cable, I decided I might as well buy another set of the On Guard Bulldog Mini DT Lock 5015.   That being said, I bought this lock to keep my bike from being stolen, which it did. So, I'd say this lock was well worth the purchase.

product_title: Therm-a-Rest Trail Seat Self-Inflating Seat Cushion
review_body: Bought this to use in my kayak.  Price was right, packs up small, comfortable, light and easy to use.  Would buy another.

product_title: Topeak MTX Trunk Bag EXP Bicycle Trunk Bag with Rigid Molded Panels
review_body:
Purchased this item about four months ago, and I am so glad I did. I've been biking since the beginning of the year, but had been struggling along with a backpack. As I often make trips to the library, the backpack was doing a number on my spine.

This product has been hugely helpful for my chores. I can cram it absolutely full of books, and I've seen no wear or tear from all that weight. I even managed a phenomenally insane trip to Costco, which did involve some rope and carrying bananas by hand, but that was all my fault.

Be a bit careful if you load the bags up, as it will make your bike unstable while resting. That's just physics. But it seems like pure magic when you're on and going, because I've never noticed the weight added on by a full library trip.

Only criticism: doesn't come with anything to secure the back portion to your bike. I've been using a clip, and that's fine, but I'd have like a loop of velcro.

product_title: Pearl Izumi Women's Select Thermal Jersey
review_body: This is a very quality made piece.  I like it; however it is also a lot warmer then I thought it would be and I end up taking it off more often then not.  The sleeves are quite long and I have long arms, it is form fitted but looks nice on.  I like it, and got it for a good price, but now I need to buy a lighter weight one that I can wear when not so cold out.

product_title: Sunlite One Piece Crankarm Set, 24 TPI
review_body: Purchased this crank as a replacement for a badly mangled crank on an oversized adult-type BMX bike.  This crank is well made and appears very sturdy and durable.  It is a little rough along some of the ground surfaces but fits and works perfectly.  A very good product.

product_title: Timbuk2 Classic Messenger Bag 2013
review_body:
The bag is very well built, very solid, well constructed, many pockets.

It is a bit bigger than expected, because of it's depth and stretches sideways. So it's a bit bulky to carry.

I can pack 10 garments or 4-5 pairs of shoes in this bag easily.

product_title: Pearl Izumi Elite Barrier Jacket - Closeout
review_body: I wore this today in 19 deg F and windy (20mph) weather.  It is definitely windproof.  I think the slightly negative reviews regarding the \\"flapping\\" and weakness in the rear pocket closure are likely related to ordering too large a size.  I ordered a small (I'm 37\\" chest, 31\\" waist) and it fit like a glove.  I didn't notice much flapping in the wind and had no problem with my cellphone overloading the rear pocket.  (I would give it 5 stars, but haven't tried it in the rain yet.)

product_title: Kool Stop Avid Elixir Organic Disc Brake Pads
review_body: I use kool stop pads for 6 years and i never had problems with them.  I use it for all mountain riding, this pads have very strong stop power and they hold on for long time.  The pads start to work for the best after two riding.

product_title: Columbia Men's Bahama II Big Long Sleeve Shirt
review_body: This shirt is exactly as pictured and true to size, it looks terrific on!  Ordered 2 for my boyfriend and he loves them, looks great over a t shirt with jeans.

product_title: Schwinn 20-Function Bike Computer
review_body:
For under 13 USD, the value of this Schwinn bike computer cannot be beat. As a casual cyclist, this is just what I was looking for.

* Installation was simple.
* Instructions were clear and concise.
* Accuracy is perfectly in sync (speed and distance) with GPS.

I'd argue 20 functions when some of the functions were \\"reset trip, reset odometer, etc.\\" Even still, it is a very capable unit and a great value to boot.

product_title: Kryptonite New York Noose 1275 Bicycle Chain Bike Lock with Evolution Series-4 Disc Lock
review_body: First, let me say I was surprised at the size of this lock.  It is BIG, like in FAT and HEAVY....If you need top shelf security this will prob work for you.  If you need a EDC lock, this might not be the one, unless of course you need to protect your bike from thieves trying to steal your ride while you grab a cup of coffee...for me, I will use this lock if I have to leave my bike overnight somewhere or feel I need to keep Bane from stealing my bike...I ended up buying another krypto lock and am also happy with that, much lighter and better for my every day carry lock.

product_title: Krown Complete Longboard Skateboard
review_body: LOL I laugh at these reviews this board is spectacular I had an old nice board and I just switched the trucks up that's all u saw wrong with it you can easily learn on this and since it's cheap it's great because later getting a better board will be easie to ride

product_title: Pearl Izumi Women's Divide Short

product_title: Electra Bicycle Handlebar Flower (Cream Rose)
review_body: Great product..easy to put on,good item on old bike, it would look nice if it had a few water drops on it and scent. thanks

product_title: Zippo Pouches

product_title: Fox Labs Defense Spray- Flip Top Cone Fog (4 Oz)
review_body: Product arrived quickly and at the best price I could find anywhere.  I'm very pleased.  With a combination of service, price, quality, and ease of doing business that's beyond compare, I wouldn't hesitate in buying from this seller.  I'll be buying from them again!  Thank you!

product_title: Thule 669ES Mountaineer ES Rooftop Cargo Box
review_body: The container was easy enough to install and the straps to secure the ends was a good idea. Since I placed it on my motorhome I didn't need the special brackets that came with it. product_title: RockyMounts PitchFork
review_body: The Rocky Mounts PitchFork was simple to install (less that 20 minutes) and is super stable at highway speeds, even with strong cross-winds. product_title: Coleman SportCat PerfecTemp Catalytic Heater

product_title: G.I. Military First Aid Case / Compass Pouch
review_body: Great gift for my daughter's compass. Very rugged and well made. Now she can clip on her compass on our outings.

product_title: O'Neill Wetsuits Mens Reactor Reef 2mm Boot
review_body: These booties meet my needs in keeping my feet from getting cut on coral and rocks. The sole is also thick enough to keep those pesky sea urchin spines from penetrating my feet. The fit is true to size. Because they are low cut, they can let in a fair amount of sand and small rocks which can be irritating. Maybe some sort of bungee type closure would help.

product_title: Multi Color Tie Dye Zip Up Hoodie For Men & Women #35
review_body: Colors are loud enough to add to bicycle safety, and size was the medium I wanted. The package arrived on time and I wear it a lot.

product_title: Big Agnes Air Core Sleeping Pad
review_body: This pad is great for side sleepers (like myself). It distributes weight evenly so that digging your hip into the mattress will not cause you to touch the ground.  Inflation is easy but time consuming compared to a foam pad. 4 minutes of blowing into the pad will inflate it to a comfortable level. I slet on this pad for a 4 days straight without any issues. I use this pad/mattress for camping and it's the best I have ever owned.

product_title: Texsport Saguaro Bivy Shelter Tent
review_body: so i had just taken it out of the box and opened it for the first time, went into the back yard and set it up, the clip ons on the lower half of the tent, when i was snapping them on, and two of the clips broke.

product_title: Igloo Quick and Cool Cooler
review_body: This baby is HUGE and keeps everything I place in it at just the right temp forever, it seems. Love it.

product_title: Limited Edition Water.org CamelBak Groove Water Bottle (Blue)
review_body: First of all it's a CamelBak so what's not to like about it?  I already had the regular CamelBak water bottle so I was thrilled to see that they came out with one that contains a filter somimcam have filtered water with me wherever I am. The filter does a great job and makes the water taste delicious so I actually drink more water in lieu of soft drinks which is my goal. Thanks, CamelBak for such a great product!

product_title: Camelbak Octane 18X 100 oz Hydration Pack
review_body: This is my second camelbak and I love it even more than the first one.  They have improved the bag shape and function and made the tube to the mouth piece removable for easy drying.    This camelbak has plenty of room for a second water bag.  I had two reservoir bags in it at once for a 12 hour hike and had a mouthpiece routed down each shoulder.  Worked perfectly.  Even with two bags I had enough room for a small snack and basic first aid.  Great bag, very light, and more comfortable than other camelbaks I have used.  I use this thing every weekend for hikes, climbs, and any time I am headed into nature or just need lots of water for the day.    For cleaning I only empty the reservoir, wipe it out and let it air dry for the week on one of these:  [...]    If it gets really dirty, or you use something other than water in the reservoir you should drop some of these in to clean it:  [...]    and then use this brush to clean it out:  [...]

product_title: Columbia Men's Black Ice II Jacket
review_headline: Nice looking but has a poor fit and is cold...
review_body: I'm mad a myself for buying this jacket. It's cold and doesn't fit well around my neck to hold in the heat. The collar is stiff and abrasive to the skin. For a Titanium series I would expect way more. You would need some heavy baselayers to stay warm in this thing. I'm sticking with Spyder!

product_title: RockyMounts Clutch SD
review_body: I purchased this because I need a way to transport my mountain bike with my pickup truck. I have an '09 Toyota Tacoma (with bed rails) so to purchase an expensive bike carrier would be stupid. I found the perfect solution: the Clutch SD. It slides easily into the rail system in my truck bed and even with my tool box the bike fits perfectly and securely. If you have a rail system in your truck that you want to use to transport a bike, this is the cheapest and most secure device you can buy.

product_title: Platypus Hoser Hydration System
review_body: I used this for when I went up skiing (on a warm-er day) and it worked beautifully.  I got the smallest one (as that was the only size that would fit in my day pack).  It was slightly small, but almost got me through the whole day.

product_title: Curious Penguins Short Sleeve Cycling Jersey for Men
review_body: it looks fantasic and is made very well, but the main problem with it was that it took about 2 weeks longer then what was promised. I don't think I would buy it again.

product_title: SnowStoppers Kid's Nylon Waterproof Snow Colorful Mittens
review_headline: Great gloves!  A little tight around the wrist
review_body:
I ordered these for my 3 year old because he's a NUT about playing in the snow. They are fantastic. I love that the cuff come up so high on his arm so that the snow doesn't get to his skin. They are a bit tight around the wrist (which I know it's meant to be) and it makes it kind of hard to get them on him properly. Would have been good to have it a little less tight and just alow the adjustable strap at the wrist to cinch it up.

Overall...these are well worth the money. He played outside in single digit degree weather for nearly an hour and his hands were toasty warm when he came inside.

product_title: Camelbak Military Water Beast Omega Reservoir
review_body: Bought to upgrade my old reservoir bought many years ago.  Delighted to see many well thought out improvements, such as quick disconnect, sheathing for drinking tube, on/off switch.  Washed and tested and fits great in my Lobo pack.  Looking forward to more outdoor running & biking.

product_title: Timbuk2 Swig Bag
review_body: It's a nice looking bag, but after using it for about three weeks, I switched back to my broken down Keen backpack.  There's something off about how it sits on my back.  It's just not that comfortable when it's loaded.  For local, kicking-around-town use, it's fine.  For international travel, it's just alright.  I'll keep it as a backup, and keep looking.

product_title: Sea Eagle SE370K_P Inflatable Kayak with Pro Package
review_body: Wanted something to carry in the Motor Home. This is compact enough to fit in one of the exterior compartments and easy to inflate and deflate in a short amount of time. Bought for lake use but have used on the river as well. This is a very sturdy kayak. Plan on a class 2 in the spring to check it out. So far awesome experience!   My carry bag was not sewn properly at the seam so I had to repair. They sell some great fabric tape at Camping World. No big problem to fix.

product_title: Schwinn Artemis Adult Women Micro Bicycle Helmet (Colors and Graphics May Vary)
review_body: I have to return this one, I tried it on my 10 year old daughter and it can't even fit her and this was suppose to be an adult helmet.

product_title: Super Lithium 1300 Brushless Electric Scooter "BLUE"
review_body:
**UPDATE** 09/12/2012: I wanted to give an update on this review because I really do believe in this company. It has been a year since I bought this scooter. Now I have been using the higher torque and lower speed however not much lower. I have clocked it going 30 mph and I am 180lbs. In one year I have replaced the brake pads ONLY. Nothing has broken down and everything works great still. The battery life is still VERY good. Not quite the same as when I first got it. But still very good. I use this scooter mostly at school. I go to school at UCF and the campus there is very large, so I ride my scooter to all my classes in record time. Since my school is crowded I sometimes have to drive it off the sidewalk and on the grass. This scooter handles off roading wonderfully. I fell off of it once because I was stupid and my chain fell off my handle bars, but even though I wiped out, it hardly made a scratch in the paint. This scooter is not meant for children at all. My scooter got caught in the rain once because I live in Florida and it rains a lot here in the summer. It does not do well in the rain at all. But this is not the manufactures fault. It's electric and electric and water does not mix. When I was driving it back to my car in the rain it would kind of sputter and not get power. But once it was all dry it worked fine again. Still though do not drive this in the rain, it's not good for the part and the metal can and will rust. AGAIN this is a great product and I would recommend it 150%

Old Feedback during initial purchase:
I do not leave feedback that much, but all I can say is wow! The scooters got to me in two days. I live on the east coast in Florida so it got to me as expected. The box was pretty beat up, but there was no damage to either of the scooters. It took me about 15 mins to assemble one of the scooters, but the assembly went without a hitch. Chris even gave me an extra part because I could not decide if I wanted better torque or better speed. Chris called me right away when I called to ask questions about the scooters, and he was very knowledgeable. I played with the scooters for like two hours, on the econ mode and on the turbo mode. Even after playing for so long, the battery did not drain out that much. I have been on quite a few scooters and electric bikes, and this thing is by far the fastest electric bike/scooter I have ever been on. Thanks so much for such a wonderful product and shipping not to mention the customer service. Chris keep up the good work. And for anyone reading this, don't bother with the crappy knock off product sold on eBay, if you look at the specs, Chris's scooter has better made parts. Also do your homework, check the better business bureau, Chris has great ratings on the BBB, and however the seller at eastcoatswholesales has horrible BBB ratings. So do your homework and check ratings and reviews before deciding, but once you do decide, if you go with Chris's scooter you will see it is a much better product.[[ASIN:B005CEJUV4 Super Turbo 1000-Lithium Electric Scooter \\"BLUE\\"]]

product_title: Finish Line Grunge Brush Chain: Gear and Chain Cleaning Tool
review_headline: Unique design for easy chain cleaning
review_body:
The Grunge Brush head features 3 bristle heads that allows you to clean all 4 sides of a bike or motorcycle chain very quickly. However, it is not as tight of a fit as I'd like on my factory DID V6 chain for my Ducati. The bristles are very large in diameter, so they're not likely to damage the O-ring seals on modern chains. However, I still recommend using a quality degreaser or cleaner in conjunction with the brush.

The bristles are easy to change in the event they need replacement, but my biggest gripe is that there's no easy way to store the brush. I have to zip-tie or tie a loop so I can hang it on the wall in my shop. It'd be nice if they designed that into the handle somewhere or made it a bit more compact. The straight end bristle isn't very useful other than for spreading the grime all over your motorcycle.

Overall: 4/5 stars

product_title: Men's Felt Insoles 2 Pack: Blue, Size 11
review_body: I needed some insoles for a pair of woolly slippers. I actually bought four pairs, because I had done a lot of research and these were inexpensive, and I gave the extra pairs away. I have some very happy friends as a result. They are great. Keep feet warm.

product_title: Cheng Shin C1218 Street Tire, 26 x 2.125" Wire Bead All Black.
review_body: This is my 2nd set for another bike, since  they work so well. High quality rubber, true runout, no wobbles or other out-of-round issues. easy mount by hand, recomend slime in tires.

product_title: Pelican 8060 LED Flashlight
review_body: Description says it comes with a wall charger and base.  I ordered this twice from Amazon and no charger was included.  I returned the first one thinking that the charger was missing, but the second one arrived in the same condition!

product_title: Stansport Deluxe Freighter Aluminum Pack Frame
review_body: Works great for hauling Elk Quarters over long distances.  I used mine last week to haul the head and meat over a mile from our camp.  The suspension and harness work really good for distributing the weight, the only difficulty is initially standing up with the pack.  The pack is at least equal or superior to higher price ones!  Its a good buy.

product_title: Sun Dolphin 5 Seat Pedal Boat Mooring Cover (Grey/Blue)
review_body: My wife and I depended upon the cover to keep rain water out of our paddle boat.  We have tried various ways to keep the cover taut but each time an area collects water and drips into our paddle boat.  We have not been able to keep water out of the paddle boat.  I would not recommend this product to others.

product_title: Schwinn Thrasher Helmet
review_body: The Visor won't stay on. The helmet was great for about one week then the visor started falling off. I would not recommend as this should not of happened. I gave this a 2 star, as the rest of the helmet is still good but now has four holes were the visor should be.

product_title: SportRack A26395 Aero 1300 Roof Box
review_body: We've used the sport rack several times for camping and long trips on our Subaru Outback.  My biggest complaint is the hardware used to attach it to the vehicle.  They are kind of ugly and are very noticeable, but that's a minor issue.  We only lost 3-4% MPG when using it so it's pretty aerodynamic.  I haven't used it for skis yet, but all of our gear appears to fit without problems.

product_title: Level One Seat Belt Cutter X 2
review_body: It will probably never be used, but DOT requires them in our school buses, so whatever, these are cheap enough.

product_title: Mountainsmith Dog Pack - 2011
review_body: I was spoiled by a Ruff Wear backpack that I borrowed from a neighbor. But considering the uses I have for the backpack, I couldn't justify the cost of that brand.  My dog uses the backpack on walks in the neighborhood to get a little extra exercise, it also helps calm her down a little (she is quite hyper), and on rare occasions she carries a few groceries.  Ruff Wear is better for real backpacking because it has a separate harness system and is super tough. But the Mountainsmith is good for general use.  One reviewer mentioned that the straps loosen up, which is true.  However, any saddlebag system must be perfectly balanced or it will pull to one side or the other; it really doesn't matter how tight the straps are if it's unbalanced. Once you have the straps where you want them, you can tack them in place to prevent slipping. Another reviewer said that the backpacks run large, this is also true. I went to the Mountainsmith website and it recommended a medium for my size dog. When it arrived I knew it was too big, but I kept it because I wanted the capacity for groceries. I have already made some modifications, and I make sure to keep the weight balanced. It never slips and my dog seems just as comfortable wearing it as she did the $120 Ruff Wear.

product_title: Spring Blooms Scooby Doo Backpack for small children - Kid size Scooby Doo Back Pack
review_body: Bought this for my 5 year old daughter. She loves Scooby & it seems strong & just the right size for her age.

product_title: Blackburn Helmet / Head / Hat Mount Kit for Flea Headlight
review_body: At work, we have a campus bike program that gave us free Flea lights and mounts when we sign up....i haven't used the product yet but the packaging is AWFUL!! I literally had to tear it apart into pieces before the mounts and lights would come out of the packaging!!  The packaging alone was frustrating!! BAD PACKAGING - company should consider better packaging since the first impression of the product is frustration!!  Frustration from not being able to get the product out of it's packaging!!!  I can't imagine the scrap cost when people return the product if they change their minds since it cannot resold because the packaging is in pieces.....      The light seems cool - with the USB charger - but the USB charger can easily get lost as well - i know one of my co-worker lost his after the first day!

product_title: Storm Alert Whistle
review_headline: AWSOME LOUD WHISTLE COVER YOUR EARS!!!!!
review_body: Cover your ears.. this is the whistle i want with me in any event i am LOST. The others.. are garbage. they are gumball crap.

product_title: GSI Outdoors 4 Cup Stainless Mini Expresso
review_body: I'm currently on my 4th one in the last 12 years.  They work great and are well made.  I use mine most every day. (I wore the last 3 out) It's handy to use at the house, on the boat, or camping. (I even packed it to the condo in Hawaii)  You must remember to stand-by while brewing; if you walk away and leave it unattended, you will burn it up.

product_title: Mongoose BMX Bike Gel Knee and Elbow Pad Set
review_body: I thoroughly researched pads for my 5 year old.  These arrived and he put them on immediately by himself, amazing because he's autistic/ADHD and is easily frustrated.  They look cool, which is what motivated him.  He's learning to ride a 2-wheeler, so these are put to the test frequently.  The hard material doesn't even show a scratch from numerous wipe-outs on a pebbly rough blacktop.  They will last a long time and the strong elastic with qualty velcro closure will allow for growth. Great value, glad I went with these!  Highly recommend!

product_title: Timbuk2 The Snoop Camera Messenger Bag 2011
review_body: Was looking for a camera bag for a new DSLR, and came across the Timbuk2 Snoop bag.  Debated for a bit due to the price, but decided to take the plunge, and so glad I did.  The small size perfectly fits my DSLR, lense, and extra camera stuff.  But after refitting the camera insert, can fit even more stuff in the bag (change of clothes, book, magazine, etc). Took it on a few trips, and easily traveled without looking like that \\"guy with a cumbersome camera bag\\".  When not used as a camera bag, the bag is perfect for commuting with work or school stuff and easily accepts a 15\\" MacBook Pro in the bigger storage area (used an old sleeve from another messenger bag), folders, textbooks, and other stuff.  Got caught in the rain once, and the outside skin kept all water out and my laptop safe.  Pros:  1) Sturdy, reliable, quality product  2) Flexibility between camera and utility bag  3) Inconspicuous camera bag  The only drawbacks can see are:   1) Wish there was a grab handle for those times I can't describe  2) Lack of Pencil holders

product_title: Kestrel 2500 Weather Meter / Digital Altimeter
review_body: Bought this to use for raptor migration counting. Need to record weather conditions including wind speed and the Kestrel 2500 is just the ticket. Very easy to use. Built in protective case is really good also. Highly recommended.

product_title: Croakies Terra Spec Adjustable Eyewear Retainer
review_body: As i'm using a intermediate courier to ship to Singapore, the box they package the item is actually like a shoe box, and a size 10 one at that!  so the total cost shoot up although i paid a reasonable fee to ship to my courier. for a feather weight item , it really feels ridiculous.

product_title: prAna Henna Satchel
review_body: I bought this bag years ago and besides having a few stains, it's still in great shape! I use it every day! It's a great hands free way to carry everything you'll possibly neeed!  It's the perfect size and is well constructed... not to mention, ADORABLE! I would love to find another one in another color so I can switch it out.

product_title: Strong Durable Maxam Backpack for School and Hiking
review_body: I bought this at the beginning of the school year because my son's old backpack, after two years, was done. This backpack was done after the first day. The backpack started to rip at the seams after the first day that he came home with books. From there, it has be progressively worse. The shoulder straps looks like ti has been through a meat grinder.   I have to buy a new one after less than a month of use.

product_title: Texsport Lakeway Hammock
review_body: We love this hammock, my wife and i can both lay in it at the same time. It is as described in the add. i bought a stand for it and it fits great.

product_title: Thinksport Stainless Steel Sports Bottle
review_body: The bottle was a little disappointing.  It doesn't keep ice water cold but it tastes good.  My wife has a different brand which performs much better.  The screen at the opening of the bottle is a good idea but I haven't found it useful yet.

product_title: Heat Factory Premium Hand Warmers
review_headline: Kept me alive... well a slight exaggeration
review_body: These rock, they are great for backpacking... which is what I use them for. I went out in Febuary and hammocked camped in the Appalachian mountains. Quite honestly i wasn't properly prepared, I got to my spot late and was setting up during a new moon. This was not one of the better planned trips i had... no it wasnt. Anyway i brought a few of these along and stuck them in my socks. They were needed they kept my feet toasty warm. That night my tarp blew off and my shelter was compromised. It was 8 degrees, 0 with the windchill. I recommend these greatly if you plan on being an idiot in febuary like i was...    Recommend!

product_title: Blackburn Flea 2.0 USB Front and Rear Combo
review_body: The Fleas are well-named.  They're REALLY small and light.    I mounted the headlight on my helmet, and clip the taillight on the back of my helmet's adjustment strap.  I run the taillight in 2+2 flashing mode.  I find that cars give me a wider berth when I have it flashing.      Note that the combo comes with 2 lights (1 front, 1 rear) but only 1 charger.  I initially was disappointed, thinking that charging both would be tedious.  In reality, the units charge so quickly that it hasn't been an issue.

product_title: Sigma BC 2209 STS Triple Wireless + Alt Bicycle Speedometer
review_headline: Don't need a G.P.S.? I HIGHLY recommend the SIGMA BC 2209 STS Triple Wireless+ALT Bicycle Speedometer
review_body: If you don't need a GPS This is the bicycle computer for you.  The Sigma BC 2209 STS is PACKED with a LOT of functions (All it's missing is the G.P.S.)     I took off one star (should be 1/2) because The first time I tried entering my stats it was a little difficult(I VERY STRONGLY suggest that you purchase the sigma docking station (less than $19) when using any of the sigma products that will mate with it.) setup the docking station, and mate the computer with it  Then you can enter all of the stats through the program it comes with.              I can't state the features well enough so here is a link to SIGMA's web page for the 2209 sts+ heart rate monitor                 [...]     Once I got the computer set up the way that I wanted to however.......        There is a very nice sized display.  You are able to see what your present Alt, HR, and Speed are, PLUS either your trip distance, time, avg or max speeds, avg or present cadence, trip climb, max alt, Avg or max pulse, or calories burned.  You can have the present time, stopwatch, countdown, and total time on bicycle.  You can see your trip distance,  total odometer (bikes 1 or 2, or total millage 1+2) plus total altitude, AND present temperature.  The computer comes with a wristband that allows you to use it when you are hiking also.  You can get all of the same features, except those that are bicycle related (speed, cadence, mileage, )      You will need some patience getting it setup, that is why I took off 1 (1/2)star,  I can't say it enough times   I VERY STRONGLY suggest you invest in the docking station, the software it comes with makes it MUCH easier to set up, and keep track of MOST of the stats collected by the computer.    it allows you to set up the computer with a keyboard not a set of buttons.       If you are looking for a loaded computer that will help you get into (or back into) shape.  THIS IS WHAT YOU ARE LOOKING FOR!!!!!!!

product_title: Emotion Kayaks Paddle Leash (Black)
review_body: Bought these to make sure we don't lose our good paddles while kayaking and they're great.  They are easy to clip on and the slack in the string gives plenty of room for the movement of paddling.  If I need more, I'll buy these again!

product_title: AIRHEAD AHGF-3 G-Force Inflatable Towable
review_body: We live on a small lake and near a very large lake, and own 2 jetskis and a boat.  My kids keep me on the water pulling this thing.  It is very reasonably priced, extremely durable, and always the number one choice on the water!!!  In my opinion you just can't go wrong with this item.

product_title: Planet Bike 3044 Blaze 1-Watt LED Headlight
review_body: I read a lot of Amazon reviews before purchasing this product.  It was obvious that the Planet Bike brand had a very good reputation.  The challenge was to decide which light was right for me.  I have a mountain bike and generally ride on a paved bike path.  I need a light bright enough to light the trail in front of me at a speed of 11-12 MPH.  I however did not want it so bright that I might blind other bikers, walkers or joggers on the path in the early monring.  I decided I probably did not need the 2 Watt version, as reviewers said this 1 Watt version was bright enough to light a dark path at a moderate speed.  And it is!  I was able to point the light out a fair distance in front of me on the lower of the two brightness settings, and could see quite well and ride relaxed.  The blinking setting is interesting, giving 3 lower beam blinks followed by 1 brighter blink.  It does give quite the strobe effect, and can't believe anyone could miss you coming on this setting.  I wonder if it might be too bright or confusing for oncoming motorists, but the main point is that they definiltey will see you!  I do understand some of the complaints about the bracket not being tight enough to fit snuggly.  I adjusted the strap to it's smallest setting and it was still a bit loose.  However, I had bought the companion rear blinking light, and that came with a couple of rubber incerts, and I used one of them on this light, and was able to tighten the light snuggly to my handle bars.  Without the additonial insert, I'm not sure I could have connected the light snuggly to the handle bars.  It seems obvious that this has been an issue for others to, so hopefully the manufacturer will do something to correct this.  Overall I'm extremely pleased with this product.  It performs very well, seems to be made rugedly, and was very reasonably priced, with both this light and the companion blinking light on Amazon for about $50.00.  Highly recommend.

product_title: Eureka! Copper River 30-Degree Mummy Sleeping Bag
review_body: I recently went camping on a night when the temperature hit about 39 degrees and I froze my butt off in this thing even while wearing long underwear. It's simply not as warm as the manufacturer claims. Other than that, it works fine, but that's a big \\"other.\\"

product_title: Ultimate Direction 10-Ounce Fastdraw Hand-Held Bottle
review_headline: Nice size bottle for carrying during a supported race
review_body:
Addendum: after 4 years, this bottle is still going strong! I use it for most of my 5-6 mile runs, plus all my half and full marathons (refill at the aid stations).

I use this bottle (10 oz) during 10K + races for carrying a glucose drink and a gel pack. Then, at the aid stations, I take on water. It's relatively light, doesn't affect my arm swinging or stride, and tightens nicely about my hand so that I don't have to clench it.

What you don't want to do is leave a sugar drink in it for a few days. The stuff that starts growing is really hard to clean out because of the bottle's shape. Rinse it out after each use.

product_title: Osram Sylvania Battery Operated Mini Lantern
review_body: has high and low settings, casts plenty of light for large tents and to supplement other lanterns around the camp site. it's small, light and rugged and runs for hours before batteries need changing. our first lantern was purchased 6 years ago to help provide some reading light during power outtages and to take camping. i have yet to change the batteries! bought a second one as a backup.

product_title: Smokehouse Products Big Chief Long Leg Replacement Element, 450 Watt
review_body: I got this for a smoker a family member gave me. It had been burned out for at least 5 years, and I used it after buying this element. It fit just like original. Works like a charm.

product_title: Energizer Brilliant Beam Headlamp
review_headline: ENERGIZER SPOT FAILS AFTER A COUPLE OF YEARS!!!
review_body: This was the best headlamp I could find at Walmart over the period of about two years. I had lost a very expensive Petzl (regulated power supply) headlamp and was hoping to give up being a headlamp snob, to the ever lighter and adjustable beams of the constantly improving mass market options.    I have preferred Petzl headlamps for their durability and ability to clearly see whatever I was working on, day or night.     I wound up buying 4 of these Energizer spot lights. I am not exactly a fan of a large number of different lighting modes accessed from one power multi- switch, but it worked OK.    Then \\"it\\" happened, that first FATAL MECHANISM DESIGN FAILURE, which virtually guarantees every other Energizer 1 watt headlamp I own, and of an     inglorious and frustrating ending in the Sh*rtcan. Through Planned Obsolescence, by way of cheaper materials, the POOR DURABILITY OF THE PLASTIC RATCHET ADJUSTMENT FOR AIMING/HOLDING THE preferred angle of the headlamps beam, FAILS FIRST. (low angle for distance viewing or a more downward pointing angle) critical to illuminate work within arms reach. AS the loose headlamp hinge causes the lamp to fall forward, instead of clicking through intermediate settings moving the spot closer to oneself the light can fall all the way forward with just a little movement of one's head and point directly down, neither extreme positions are workable. I have tried locking the light against the headband aiming the light nearly horizontally, or using a wade of tape as a spacer behind the light, for a more useful angle, like walking at night or working with the hands. The ability to change the lamps focal distance is a requirement!                                                                                                                 ** If anyone should see a brilliant solution, to fix the worn ratcheting gears, which hold the lamp housing at various angles, changing the spot focal point, especially for critical close up work...   let meknow! I don't see any easily applied fix, but perhaps someone else can help out?     There is a new headlamp, the Energizer \\"7 LED Headlamp\\" w/ \\"4 modes\\" (45 lumens), from Home Depot, is advertised as an \\"Industrial\\" version. The batteries are not in the movable part/lens section of the hinge assembly, but are mounted in the headband side, So there is less weight from not having the batteries hanging out, putting stress on the ratcheted hinge assembly. It appears to be an improvement over the 1 watt Energizer lamp, In theory, anyway, since the ratchet seems also less robust than in the 1 watt. Only time and use will tell, if this common weak spot is going to wear out prematurely. The large field of illumination, not like an ordinary unevenly lit spot, makes for a larger evenly lit working area created by the intersecting LEDs. Also, the color of the LEDs is more evenly a white color light. The button pushing is more logical, with the Red LED illuminating first.

product_title: Mountainsmith Trekker FX Monopod (Single)
review_body: After looking at several monopod hiking poles I chose this one.  It was a great value and worked really well.  It collapses short enough to fit in my suitcase.  If you are looking for a hiking stick/monopod I would recommend this one.

product_title: ST LOUIS CARDINALS BOTTLE SUIT KOOZIE COOLER COOZIE by Kolder
review_body: This Cooler Coozie is perfect.  It shows my Cardinal spirit while keeping my spirits cold and refreshing.  It also prevents my fingers from becoming icy and uncomfortable.

product_title: Planet Bike Aquilo Cycling Gloves
review_headline: Not Particularly Durable  - Long Term Update:  Grey Suede Surfaces Have Significant Perforations after Three Seasons
review_body:
Despite being an enthusiastic owner of several Planet Bike products, I have been disappointed with the durability of these gloves. After three seasons (3 x 3 months = 9 months), the suede palm and finger pads have severely worn down. Currently, much of the grey suede material is missing and the gel pads in the palms have fallen out. Basically, this material is not suitable for bicycle gloves.

What is particularly surprising is that the grey suede on the right index finger has completely worn though to the underlying fabric. While the palm surface of any bicycle glove is susceptible to significant wear, the index finger should never wear through. By comparison, I have Trek winter gloves used for several years with virtually no sign of wear. My Trico mesh summer gloves have been used ten times as many hours as the Planet Bike fall gloves with little wear on the leather palms.

Planet Bike appears to have slipped up with the design of these gloves. My suspicion is that neither they nor their Pakistani supplier did any long term testing. Perhaps the material was picked merely for cosmetics? In any event, I would suggest avid fall cyclists seek other glove alternatives.

Cons
Flimsy suede surfaces

Note: Because these gloves were purchased in December 2008, it is impossible to say if the current gloves use the identical grey suede. However, my gloves look nearly identical to the ones pictured.

product_title: Zippo Hand Warmer 2011
review_headline: Fool me once, shame you on.  Fool me twice... doh!
review_body: I bought two of these together so really I only count myself as being a sucker just the one time :P  Product marketing guys really understand how important Amazon reviews are so I'm getting suspicious of all these great stars.  The first out of the box lit up and stayed warm for roughly four hours on a full fill.  The second fill lasted about the same.  The final fill lasted about six hours as I kept it in the the cover the whole time.  It burns longer, of course, if it's getting less oxygen.  On the flip side, it doesn't generate much heat as it burns slow.  So three lights and I've never got it to light again.  I thought maybe the butane lighter I was using to start it up may have damaged it so I actually bought a basic Zippo lighter to start up the second.  I'm sucha sucker.  I really wanted these to work.  The second has never ever started.  Anyways, during the three burns that I got out of the first, I experimented non-stop.  I was looking to these warmers to keep me cozy on a month-long trip to the desert; the days are usually all right but the nights can be miserable when duty keeps you exposed the full night through.  If you leave this thing out of the bag on a rock, or something, you'll have a pleasant amount of heat but only briefly.  The warmer has thin, metal walls with little mass so they dump their warmth on contact.  The more you cup your hands around it, the less oxygen it gets and the temperature is not maintained.  It radiates no heat whatsoever, only that bit of conduction.  I threw it into the bed hoping that it would make things all nice and cozy for me but there was only a slightly warm spot where the warmer undisturbed lay between the covers for two hours.  The bed was chill just three inches away.  Guess I'm going to be cold.
