product_title: Pewi Ybike Ride On Toy and Walking Buddy
review_headline: Perfect scooter as a child transitions into walking and beyond
review_body: We've had this product since our son was 11 months old. At first he pushed it around--he wasn't tall enough to sit on it and have his feet touch the floor--and it worked fine. The wheels move very easily in any direction, which is a bonus for a very practiced cruiser (freedom to go where they want), but makes it slip away easily for a child who needs help with balancing. I wouldn't recommend this for the stage where they are just beginning to cruise--you'll want a sturdier push cart for that. This small limitation shouldn't discourage you, though, because for us, the real joy of the bike came when my son could start to \\"ride\\" it as a bicycle. He was 13 months old before his feet fit firmly on the ground with his bum on the seat and then it was true love. At first, he couldn't quite go straight from one point to another, but he zig zagged around like a little speed racer, smiling and laughing the whole way. After a few weeks of seated riding, he could begin to maneuver it where he wanted to go--even if he was outside and his desired destination was 20 yards away. This was especially fun for him since he wasn't quite waking yet. It is hard to have a crawler outdoors, but this helped him play on rough surfaces without sacrificing his knees.    I am UPDATING this review at 15 months old. My son is now walking very well, and still loves his little bike. It works very well indoors and out, and it is hands-down his favorite toy and has been for the last couple months. It is so much fun that it attracts all sorts of attention from other children and parents. Whenever he sees it, he points to it and lets us know he wants to go outside and play. It seems like a great toy to keep him active and challenge his balance and coordination, and is definitely sturdy enough to survive multiple children. Much older children have ridden it, and I, myself, have sat on it with him. While I obviously wouldn't do that all the time, it did not crack or show any stress from the extra weight. Ido think it helped him become an independent walker a little bit faster than he would have otherwise.    For reference, my son was 27lbs and 31\\" at his 12 month checkup, and he grew into this at about 12 months and 3 weeks, after a bit of a growth spurt. I assembled it myself in about 15 minutes. He began walking somewhere around 13 months, 2 weeks, and he loved it before and after.

product_title: High Sierra Ridgeline Lumbar / Waist Pack
review_headline: Lousy bottle design, not that comfortable.
review_body:
I needed a pack to carry two bottles of water, some accessories (GPS, phone, gloves, and the like) and be comfortable. The thing has the room for accessories, but that's all I can say that's good about it.

Bottles - what are these for, soup? You have to unscrew the cap - then you're looking at an opening the size of the bottle. Why not bite or sip caps? So the bottles went into storage. Now, the pockets will fit standard water bottles - but if the bottles sweat, or you use frozen bottles to start the day, they'll slip out often. The elastic straps are useless. Forget the larger bottles - they'll fall out instantly. All that really works well are stubby water bottles.

Fit - You have to really cinch the straps down to achieve a good fit and comfortable ride. But with two full water bottles, the thing fill keep trying to slide down and rock backwards. Feels really awkward. Clip on bottles on my belt work better.

Bottles and fit - OK, you have the bottles in place and the pack cinched down. Now you have to remove a bottle to drink. Usually takes two hands - and the moment the bottle comes out, the entire pack becomes lose and slides down. Takes two (or three!) hands to put the bottle back. You can't just swivel the pack around.

Padding - in the pack itself, zero. On the waist/lumbar pad, it's about 3/8 of an inch.

Comfort - wore this for 6 hours on a hot, humid day. The lumbar pad trapped water and sweat. By the time the hike was done, the entire area by and around the lumbar area was soaked and chafing. The rest of me - not nearly so wet. The pad acts like a sponge and traps sweat. Just imagine wearing a huge sponge just above your butt, one that's constantly soaked and is keeping your upper buttocks soaked the entire hike. Taking off the pack allowed me to dry off. I really debated putting it back or just carrying it.

If I had to do over again, I would not purchase this pack. It's for transport - not use while hiking. Stop, take it off, have a drink, put it back on. Move on. Thirsty? Stop, take it off, have a drink, put it on.a drink, put it back on. Move on. Thirsty? Stop, take it off, have a drink, put it on.

product_title: Hydro Flask Stainless Steel Insulated Drinking Bottle, Narrow Mouth
review_body: This is the first Hydro Flask product I have purchased and quality control is lacking. On the backside of the bottle's label the company gives a caveat for their bottle being made in China, stating \\"Hydro Flasks bottles are made in China at meticulously chosen factories that practice social responsibility, fair labor, and strong ethics.\\"     Upon opening the bottle I noticed some oval debris stuck to the inside, looking to be the same color as the bottle and approximately 1/2\\" diameter by 1/32\\" thick. It looked like some stainless steal debris from the manufacturing process. Using water and a long handle bristle brush I was able to scrub the debris off the side, only to reveal a blemish on the inside the same size and shape as the debris that had been removed. The blemish is considerably darker than the rest of the inside of the bottle. Being unfamiliar with the manufacturing process, the only thing I can guess is that the inside of the bottle must have some sort of coating which is missing in the location the debris had been.     Although the bottle seems to be a somewhat standard diameter of 2-7/8\\" at the base and able to fit in a standard car cup holder, at about 11-1/2 tall (from base to cap top) it is a bit taller than I anticipated. I suppose this is due to the fact that it is double wall construction for insulation purposes, thus making the inside volume smaller than single wall designs having the same outside diameter.    Also disappointing is that the bottle is not to be washed in the dishwasher, although the instructions do not state the reason for this limitation.

product_title: Klean Kanteen Stainless Steel Water Bottle
review_headline: 6-months of constant use, still in perfect working order.
review_body: I bought two of the 27oz bottles. One for my wife and one for myself. We both use them daily to help increase the amount of water we drink, and stave off cravings for soda. It has now become part of the kit of stuff I end up taking everywhere with me. I fill ii up multiple times per day. The bottle isn't insulated, but I knew that going in. It can sweat quite badly in the humid air here in Texas, so you can't place it on any real wood surfaces. The water will reach room temperature in about an hour, longer if it is packed with ice.  The bottle is very durable. I have banged it and dropped it a few times, there is no scratches in the paint and just a small dent from one hard hit. The glossy finish is still bright. The plastic cap is still smooth and hasn't developed any brittle edges or flaking. The black cap does show hard water stains over time, but they clean off easily. Cleaning the bottle is easy since the large mouth lets a scrubber brush though.  The bottle doesn't change the taste of the water even when left in the bottle overnight.  A few cons: The sound the air vent makes when you take a drink. Its a sort of warbling, gurgling sound. I often press my finger against the valve to manually release it and quiet the noise.  And the bottle will leak if left on its side (The cap isn't rated as water tight in the first place though.)

product_title: Schwinn Men's Prelude Bicycle (BBWhite)
review_headline: Schwinn Prelude -- great for the price!
review_body:
I'm a 49-year old male that started riding in Jan '11 to get back into shape and for fun. After 2 months I transitioned from my 20-yr old mountain bike and zeroed in on this bike. I did not want to spend much because I was not sure I was going to stay with the sport for long. Since then I have ridden in a 2-day 150-mile ride from Houston to Austin, and last weekend logged over 100-hundred miles through the countryside west of Houston. This is in addition to probably about 400 miles of training rides. I am NOT a bike expert, but I can tell you that I feel like I got a great bike given what I paid for it. A few specifics...

I have had only a couple minor issues with the bike. First, the rear brake was not tight and on my third training ride it slowly came loose such that it ever so slowly tightened up on the rim, making it increasingly hard to pedal. The problem was easily fixed once I figured out what was going on. Second, the tires seem to lose air albeit slowly. Generally they seem to lose about 20% of their pressure per week. Not a big issue but clearly something is not holding, so I always have to pump them up before I ride on a weekend. Third, and most worrisome, after about 500 miles on the bike the bottom bracket started clicking as my left foot started back down while pedaling. I took it to the local bike shop and for $32 they took it apart and put it back together; they told me it had just gotten loose. It seems fine now.

The only modifications I've made to the bike was to replace the pedals with Shimano SPD clip-ins, which have worked great. It would be nice to add aero bars, but I don't think there is any way to do so given the way the shifters are laid out on this bike. I have seen some posts here that some people don't like the seat - I've not had a problem with it. It would be nice to have a few more gears and a quick-release on the back wheel, but those are nice-to-haves that you won't find at this price range.

As I stated, I was out on a very long ride this weekend and it performed without a flaw. I weigh 190 pounds, it got up to 95 degrees and ~40 of the 102 miles of the roads we were on were very rough, so the bike (and I) took a steady pounding. I don't know if more expensive road bikes would have absorbed the shocks better or not, but the Prelude certainly transferred every bump from the road to me. It did so, though, without anything breaking or the tires needing more air.

In summary I have nothing but positive things to say about this bike. For the $230 (not including tax) I paid at the local store for the Prelude I am delighted with my purchase. I highly recommend this bike if you want a very good entry-level bike to explore the sport. 5-stars for sure!

Update 3 July 2012:

I stand by everything I wrote earlier, but I did transition to a higher end bike as my riding has gotten more ambitious (and I'm down to 170 lbs) and the shifters on the a Prelude are a bit odd. That said, for various reasons I do still ride this bike on occasion and it continues to perform very well. I am yet to have a flat on it -- the tires and tubes may be \\"cheap\\" as some other reviewers have said, but they has served me flawlessly. I did lower the handbars 3 spacers recently, and after 2K+ miles this is still the most comfortable seat of the 3 I have. I did log a hard 16 miles on it last weekend at an average speed of 19.5 mph, so it can move if you have the legs to push it. Finally, though it is all aluminum and my new bike has a carbon fork, I think the Prelude the smoother of the two.

product_title: MagicShine MJ-816 1400 lumen LED Bike Light 2011 version with improved battery and charger
review_headline: Solid light, great for the money
review_body: This is a good light, and much cheaper than most of the alternatives. The only other bike headlight I've used is a niterider trinewt, which broke within the first month due to water damage (it claims to be waterproof). I sent that light back and bought this one. Not only is the magicshine brighter, it is also cheaper, and I've sprayed it from every angle with a hose and it still works. One note on water though: while the light still works exactly as advertised after being sprayed with water now, for about a week after I sprayed the light with water I could see little droplets of water inside the casing of the control button, and the light would occasionally flicker. It seems like the water that was inside the button must have worked its way out and dried away because it is no longer there and the light works just fine. I've also ridden in the rain and that has no problems. The light is very bright and the battery charge indicator is very useful. One annoying thing is that you need to mount both the control button and the light itself on your handle bars (they're both small and it works out fine), but the kit includes three DIFFERENT SIZED o-rings for fixing the light/button to your handle bars. Ideally there would be 6 o-rings with 2 of each size.     Bottom line: this light is bright, very bright, and is absolutely worth the money.

product_title: High Sierra AT3 Carry-On Wheeled Backpack
review_body: I bought this item a few months ago for a trip to New Orleans, and I'm absolutely in love with it. I have plenty of luggage, but I wanted something that would fit in carry-on, and yet be able to handle five days worth of clothes, shoes, toiletries, etc. It handled everything I brought with, plus quite a few souvenirs that I brought back.   Now to be fair, if you stuff this thing full there is no way that you will be able to fit it in an overhead. However, if you unzip the day pack the carry-on fits nicely in the overhead, and the day pack (even full) fits under your seat. Mine fit nicely under the seat along with my rather bulky laptop case. The only thing you have to keep in mind is that once you unzip that day pack the flight attendants see that as an additional carry-on. I didn't really have any trouble, and like I said, both the day pack and laptop bag fit nicely (not tight) beneath the seat in front of me, just something to think about.  I had no troubles with either the wheels or the telescopic handle, both of which are of sturdy materials, like the bag itself. The handles on the top and side of the bag are extremely comfortable to use, and I did use them a few times when things got crowded. I only had a problem with the zippers on one occasion, and as is often the case it had to do with the way the bag was laying, as soon as I rearranged the bag the zippers were again fine.   I now exclusively use this bag for all of my traveling, and frequently use the day pack for all sorts of things. I would definitely recommend this bag to anyone.

product_title: KMC X10SL Superlite Bicycle Chain with Missing Link (10-Speed, 1/2 x 11/28-Inch, 112L, Chrome Plated)
review_body: This is a great chain.  Never really considered a chain quiet before now, especially when the manufacturer claims it to be so. I am using the chain with Dura Ace 7800 parts, and none of them were new along with the chain.  No slipping, great shifts and it's much quieter than the wipperman chain.  The missing link was a little more difficult to install than similar styled chains, but it definitely felt secure once I was able to engage the pins.  I hope the chain is still easily breakable for cleaning, otherwise it won't be much different from a shimano chain.  Give this a try, it's definitely worth it.

review_body: Bought this for Mom and we love it!:) Great quality, soft and beautiful material..Love the stylish details with fabric gathers behind the neck and back, uniquely beautiful. *You can even leave it open and belt it with a beautiful dress underneath!:) Mom got compliments wearing it this way after going to church and needing a bit of warmth and a new stylish look:) Wish I had one myself!:) This is everything & more to Mom & I !:) In addition to wearing it for the gym or home workouts, or an \\"out & about\\" uniquely beautiful style that may get compliments.. product_title: Serengeti RX Eyewear Medium Aviator Sunglasses (Matte Black, Drivers Gradient)
review_body: I purchased the large version of the aviators from Serengeti first and they were too big.  I tried to go down a size and get the medium aviators.  The sunglasses fit ok, but not great. product_title: Black Diamond Center Bars
review_headline: Great for Semi Flexible Mountaineering Boots
review_body: These worked great in allowing me to use my BD Sabertooth crampons with my Kayland Apex Rock Mountaineering boots. They are quick and easy to change out with the rigid center bars.

product_title: Stearns Puddle Jumper Deluxe Life Jacket, 30-50 lbs
review_body: Having toddlers in the water is stressful as any parent knows, but this product puts you at ease.  We tried multiple products before discovering this one, and we cannot praise it enough.  If you go to a Walmart or Target, you may see these for sale.  They will just cost you more than on Amazon.  Also, we never saw the girl's version in the stores.  This product will support them in the water without much rolling or tilting.  Once the child is used to it, they will float in place without any problem at all.  No other product out there does the same.  You still have to be near them however in case they shift their body quickly or raise their arms, which will make their head lower into the water.  Our children have done that of course, and they will get water in their mouths.  It is not a disaster however.  As the product claims, this is a great way to help the child build confidence in the water too.  Our two toddlers have gone from fearful to confident in a very short time while using these.  Now they will float around on their own, and the position the float keeps them in promotes kicking their legs and moving their arms--the beginning steps to swimming of course.  They never complain about discomfort either, and the device is super easy to put on and off.  When breaks are called on the beach and it is adult swim only, the children will play with the floats on without complaint as well.  The single buckle is in the back too, so the child cannot mess with it and possibly disconnect it on accident.  The arm floats are sewn onto the base that wraps around their chest, and that keeps the arm floats in place and working as intended (compared to cheap arm floats that simply fall off and are extremely dangerous).  I highly recommend this product to parents with toddlers.  If you are buying any other device, you will eventually want this instead.  Save your money and get a Puddle Jumper first.  You'll love it!

product_title: Scuba Pro Jet Fins
review_body: Jet Fins are the best fins on the market. Period. I've taken different brands and different models out for test runs, and I've owned other models as well, but nothing comes even close to the simultaneous ease and power delivered by Jet Fins. They make diving a no-hassle, carefree joy. Being 100% rubber (instead of some rubber/plastic/neoprene blend), they are also incredibly reliable and durable. Maybe that's why the design hasn't changed in 40 years. Maybe that's why these fins are a staple of the tec diving community. Maybe that's why they are the official fins of the U.S. Navy SEALS.   That said, these fins are not for beginners. Like one of the previous reviewers correctly noted, you need to be comfortable with the frog kick - which means you have to your breathing and buoyancy pretty much under control. Otherwise, these fins will wipe you out. Scissor kicking with Jet Fins for an entire dive is like running a marathon with weights strapped to your quads and calves - it burns. More importantly, it completely winds you and devours air. So unless you're experienced enough I recommend getting a model that will make scissor kicking less of a pain, split fins for example.

review_body:
the foam material was too thick for my child who already doesn't like wearing these things and freaked out when I put this one on him since he couldn't move his head around.

product_title: OnGuard Brute STD 5001 Bike U-Lock
review_body: I've had several bike locks growing up, nothing serious and luckily never had any problems with stolen items.  So when this bike lock showed up in the mail, I was slightly shocked (in a good way) at how much of a beast it was.  This thing is a giant piece of heavy metal that will intimidate anyone thinking about ripping off my bike.  Its covered with a nonabrasive plastic sheath that keeps it from scratching the paint off your bike.  I bought two of them: one for my 7 year old son, and one for my wife.  My wife rides a large cruiser bike with the fancy looking frame, but the beast had no problem fitting around the frame to lock it.  We ride our bikes all over town now and lock the bikes together and we seriously have NO ANXIETY at all about anyone taking off with the bikes.    Unfortunately, the device that is supposed to hold the lock when its not in use does not fit anywhere on my wife's cruiser frame primarily b/c of the shape of the bike frame.  The holding device does not work on my son's bike either b/c his bike is too small (he's got a bike size appropriate for a 7 year old).  Luckily, my wife has a basket that accomodates both locks easily, but if you don't have the luxary of a basket on your bike, this heavy beast may be a bit difficult to lug around unless your bike frame is normal shaped (adult, noncruiser style).    Overall, I'm very satisfied with this purchase and would buy it again for myself when I buy my own bike.

product_title: The Bag of Holding Messenger Bag
review_body: I've had my bag for about three days. It seemed to be almost everything I hoped for - attractive, sturdy, and capable of fitting a large laptop, four law school casebooks (big thousand-page hardbacks), a small binder, and the minor sundries you'd figure would go with those things (pens, headphones, bandana, deck of many things) without difficulty.    Everything was going great until I tried to carry it through a wormhole. I understand that ThinkGeek cannot be held responsible for the loss of my laptop or textbooks, nor the fact that I'm currently lost in the Astral Plane. Still, a warning label would have been nice.    Additional Pros and description:   - It seems durable; with a little Scotchguard, as someone recommended, I think it will be pretty water-resistant.   - Most of the components are quite well-built.   - It really does hold a lot; I think it's in the 1,750 - 2,000 cubic inch category, around the size of most \\"large\\" professional messenger bags (though not the truly giant ones.)   - Compared to them it's inexpensive.   - The low-key grey canvas look seems quite handsome and professional to me, compared to the shiny and gaudy look of most good messenger bags.    Cons: These are all pretty minor; I mention them mainly for ThinkGeek's benefit in developing the BofH 2.0.    - The zippers on mine are fine, but I can see where the construction isn't ideal.  - There could stand to be a bit more tech in the straps. The main strap is actually quite comfortable considering, but a pad and D-rings would still be a good idea. It's great that it has a separate handle as well, but I'm not sure the handle will last as long as the rest of the bag. Not bad, but could be better.  - As others have noted, while the laptop compartment feels quite safe, having padding on all of the edges of it would be nice.  - The front pocket has a number of nice little pouches that are great for headphones and thumb drives and things, but it would be cool to have a couple that could fit pens or a typical geek cell phone.  - The magnetic clasps for the top flap do not work well when the bag is very full.    Like I said, these are all minor. I'm picky and so far I like this bag a whole lot.

product_title: Bell No-Mor Flats Bike Inner Tube
review_headline: Expensive - But More Than Worth It
review_body: was going home from work &  front tire tube valve stem ruptured. Green goop didn't stand a chance sealing it. Six miles left to get home is a long walk. It was evening so bike shops were closed. Decided to go to Wally World and the only size on the shelf was 26 x 1.95, exactly the size I needed. Bought one box thinking $20 was for two foam rings. Got home and learned it's $20 for one ring. Turned out to be more than worth it.    Used two plastic bike tire remover tools (sold in pairs at your local bike shop) and a flat blade screwdriver to install the ring (first one is a challenge to install, last few inches of tire bead is the hardest. Be careful to not gouge aluminum rims with the screwdriver blade. Also, be sure to refer to the install drawing that shows the ring orientation - the tapered seam MUST point towards the rim and not the tire). When installing, take your time and think about what you're doing and all should go well. By the time you reach installing the second ring you'll be a pro.    Once installed, it feels like 65lbs of pressure - perfect fit ! Bought a second ring the next day. Now, no more flats and no more concerns about picking up goat heads, broken bottle glass in the street, etc and no more concerns about having to walk miles during a late night ride home from work due to a ruptured tube valve stem. Sure, you can always carry an extra green goop filled tube but that's extra weight. At $8 a tube (plus labor, inconvenience, etc) it seemed wise to pay $20 per tire ring to never have a flat again {8^D    If you ride a lot (I do 15 miles a day commuting to/from work) these rings are a blessing and your employer will appreciate them as well since you'll never be late or miss work due to a flat tire.    It's a great product, seems expensive at first, but well worth every penny once they're installed.    Buy them with confidence.

product_title: Fenix HP10 7 Level 225 Lumen LED Headlamp
review_body: I purchased this headlamp along with an Energizer LED headlamp (3 LED) for a hiking trip.  In terms of brightness, the Fenix HP10 blows the Energizer 3LED away by a significant margin, no question about it.  But with great power, comes.. great... weight and power drain. The Fenix's battery pack is significantly heavier and the lifetime (per battery change) is significantly shorter on the Fenix at the higher intensity. Another characteristic of this headlamp is that it has a very focused beam, which I don't really need for my use.  In the end, with all things considered, I still use the Fenix HP10 with a diffuser lens as the main light for my night hike. The battery pack sits at the back side of my head to give a decent weight distribution and doesn't drag the strap down (i don't even use the top strap). The battery life span is more than enough for my 1-day trips at the lower intensities.  Another downside to the ergonomic design: although the buttons are clearly marked with bright-orange rubbers, they are not as pronounced when you're trying to reach for them with your fingers to your forehead without looking. They're probably only raised by 1/16\\" and surrounded by other similar indentation on the body of the headlamp.  I'm not 100% sold on the build quality, as the intensity selector button on mine gets 'sticky' after the hike. Maybe it was due to getting drenched in rain, or maybe it was a bad manufacturing defect.  Pros:  - Very bright, with 4 light intensity settings (+3 strobes)  - Very focused beam  Cons:  - Ain't cheap  - Battery pack is heavy for a headlamp  - Intensity selector button doesn't work reliably (on my unit)  - Build quality not super great  - Buttons placement not that ergonomic

product_title: Sevylor Inflatable Rio Canoe - Green
review_body: I bought two of these boats (Rio and Colorado) for moderate whitewater. They are the same boat and only differ in length to accommodate the number of paddlers. I have now ran 20 miles of mild rivers (Class I and II) with them without any issues. My wife paddles the Rio solo and I paddle the Colorado with my daughter in the front. I am very pleased with both the engineering and material of the boats but need to use them more to see how durable they are. I chose these over the Aire Tomcats because of price and so far I think I made the right choice. I expect the Aires to be better boats but for family use these should work great. If it is needed we will upgrade later on but based on reviews with some reasonable care we should be able to use these for many years. These are very stable but I suspect their limit to be rapids III+ or IV. We will do our first III run this weekend!    So far we have got these stuck in rocks several times (low water levels) with no visible sign of wear. The bottom of the boats is a very tough plastic and seems to be doing its job. As some other reviewers commented these are not really designed for flat water so paddling in flat water or slow moving rivers is manageable but tedious. They track reasonably well in flat water for an inflatable but if you expect hardshell kayak tracking you will be disappointed. The paddle choices depends on the number of paddlers. Two paddlers could handle the Colorado with canoe paddles but I would not want to paddle the Colorado solo or the Rio with a canoe paddle. If paddling the Colorado solo or with a child (my daughter weight 50lbs) you want to invert the seats and paddle backwards as this helps balance the boat lengthwise. It tracks much better this way. If you will only inflate one of these boat you can do with a manual pump but if you have two you definitely want to use an electric pump initially and finish the inflation with a manual pump. Inflating these to the correct pressure without a pressure gauge is extremely difficult so I recommend to invest in a pressure gauge. I bought a \\"Bravo\\" and rigged it to my Coleman dual action pump which is a great combo.    The correct kayak paddle length for paddlers irrespective of height is 240cms because of the fat and high side tubes. The problem with this was that paddles this long could not be found locally so we had to order online and wait for the delivery. If you insist in buying shorter paddles locally definitely don't go shorter than 230cms or you will not reach the water comfortably.    My operating procedure for these boats is the following: 1) unfold, 2) inflate main chambers for volume with a 12v pump quickpump, 3) inflate main chambers for pressure with a manual pump with pressure gauge , 4) Inflate seats with the manual pump, 5) tie seats, 6) launch.    After kayaking: 1) take out of water, 2) unplug drainage valve, 3) lift kayak to drain water, 4) dry with camp towel, 5) deflate manually, 6) deflate with pump, 7) dry again with camp towel, 8) unfasten seats, 9) fold, 10) drive home, 11) inflate for volume main chambers, 12) let dry for a day, 13) deflate with pump, 14) fold.

review_body: Ok, so it's a bottle and it holds water, simple thing that you can get anywhere. Well, maybe not anywhere, I looked this bottle up because I saw it in a movie and wanted to see how much it was. The movie was Iron Man 2 and it was Robert Downey Jr.'s bottle in that movie, (shameless product placement, but it actually worked on me.)     As for the bottle itself it does what was designed to, hold water. The lid/cap that folds all the way back flush with the bottle's side is great. The shape of the bottle is nice to hold and the rubber ring on the bottom is helpful in keeping the bottle from slipping all over.     I like the bottle but I don't like the price $20 plus for a bottle, is kinda ridiculous. Not to mention that the bottle does come with little round message stones that reveal a message when you look under the cap/lid. In reality they are just pieces of card-stock paper(or FiberStone® paper, according to the website) with a design on them. The fact that I got 3 of them for free with my bottle was good, but these \\"stones\\" are about $2 for a set of 4 and then you get to pay shipping too. My suggestion is outline the stones that come with the bottle & make your own.     The bottle does sweat when brought out from cold fridge to room temp or hot day, but I don't know many bottles that don't sweat, so no big deal there. To me water is water unless you are trying to drink hot water, The bottle is great for taking to school and use during classes. Fits in my shoulder bag just fine.    I only gave 4 stars because I think paying $20 plus for a water bottle is ridiculous, I know, I paid that much but I had a gift card that was going to expire so I grabbed the first thing that I wanted. Overall I'm happy with the buy, & speed of delivery, was very fast. This is a good product, if only too expensive. Do check to see what size you are buying because there are different sizes and they vary in price.

product_title: Sea Eagle SE370K_P Inflatable Kayak with Pro Package
review_headline: Incredible value for a very fun toy
review_body: If you want a sleek, fast kayak that will impress your friends ... this is not it. This is a fun little boat perfect for one large adult (or two children) on lakes, ponds, rivers and creeks, and any place that's not too windy. It is not fast. The wind has more of an effect on it than on a hard-shell kayak (naturally). And it steers a little differently, with more yaw, but you can learn to minimize that. The foot-pump works very well. I need to put about 60 pumps in each of the three big chambers, but it's not hard and it's good for my quads. The boat weighs only about 25 pounds, so you can inflate in the shade of a tree and then carry everything down to the water's edge. Very easy to get in and out. Holds a lot of stuff, like a cooler, umbrella, poncho, bug spray, etc. You could easily pack a tent. Seems almost impossible to tip this thing. And it's very comfortable, as you can imagine an inflatable would be. Best of all, it deflates in seconds. Then I wipe it off with an old towel, roll it up, and throw it in my Honda Civic back seat. I live in an apartment, so the fact that it fits in a duffle bag is great (and the bag that comes with it is excellent). The Pro Package has better seats. I've had a ton of fun in my Sea Eagle.

product_title: High Sierra expandable hydration pack
review_headline: Already used a bunch of times
review_body: This pack has been great.  Almost wish it held even more water.  There are places to hold wallet, phone, keys and even enough room for a decent size plastic bowl  so I can give the dogs water.  Take it on all my long hikes.  Very good product.  Easy to fill too.

product_title: Eureka! Tetragon 1610 - Tent (sleeps 9)
review_headline: Durable, versatile, tough as nails, great for family camping!
review_body: I've owned this tent for over a year now and have spent somewhere between 20-24 nights in it with my family (wife + 4 kids ages 5-12!!)  We have camped in hot desert conditions and cold shady mountain conditions.  We've had rain and dangerous micro-burst winds and never a stitch of fear that this tent was going to leak or collapse!  It is the BEST tent I've ever seen or used and so incredibly superior to any of the other tents I've seen others suffering with in the campgrounds we've stayed in.  Here are my favorite features about the tent:  1. EASY, EASY, EASY setup/breakdown!!!  Less then 10 mins solo, 5 minutes with two people (kids can do it themselves even!).  I have set this thing up and broken it down dozens of times now, even multiple nights in a row sometimes and it just couldn't be any easier.  Just 4 poles, completely intuitive design, and never had to read the manual except for a quick glance at the steps the very first time, and it fits nicely into a tiny bag the size of one of those fold-out armchairs!  2. Very versatile design!  3 doors makes it easy for the kids to sneak out their side of the tent in the middle of the night to use the bathroom without waking everyone up or crawling over people.  Screen windows on all 4 sides allows for great flow through of air to keep things cool and dry inside (no condensation buildup ever!).  Nice built-in storage pockets and loops to hang lights/fans/bug repellant fans, etc.  The entire top of the tent is a screen mesh, so you could fall asleep looking at the stars if you like, and this also makes it nearly impossible to have condensation problems inside the tent.  Most complaints that people have about \\"dew\\" leaking into their inferior tents are actually problems with their own hot breath filling the tent with moisture.  This tent avoids that by always letting the warm/moist air out of the top screen.  I've always used the fly cover just in case there was a midnight rain or heavy dew, but you could leave it off if you're comfortable with that.  Eureka also provides you with extra guy wires and tie-down loops in case you expect adverse weather conditions or high winds.  As you'll see below, we've suffered those and didn't even need the guy wires.  3. Tough as NAILS!  One day when we were camping in Zion National Park a storm rolled through and we suffered a horrendous microburst of wind at the front edge of the storm.  This produced several minutes of quick and powerful bursts of wind up to and exceeding 70MPH!!!  It nearly knocked us to the ground!  We watched as tents all over the campground collapsed and began flapping in the wind like torn flags while others just plain ripped up from their stakes and rolled away like tumbleweeds.  I had thoroughly staked our Eureka with metal stakes as usual, so it just sat there and took the brunt of the wind.  We were about 30 yards away from it on our way to the river so we just sat and watched as it easily weathered the gusts.  With it's low, tight, and crouched design, the Eureka wiggled a little back and forth, but never even hinted at giving in to the winds.  Not a stitch came loose, no seam damage, and the tent was still standing proud after the winds subsided!  3 of the tents around us actually suffered BROKEN poles from the bursts....not our Eureka!  LOVE that tent!!  That was impressive, but what's even more impressive is that it has withstood two summers of a family of 6 living in it for weeks on end!  The kids have had all out wrestling matches in this tent many times, we walk inside it with our hiking boots and shoes on sometimes (although we try not to), and the bottom has never shown a sign of wear.  One person wrote a negative review saying that the fly cover is too tight, but I actually think that's a benefit!  The fly cover acts as a shell to tighten and strengthen the structure of the tent and keep it from flapping in the wind or allowing water to pool up on the top like those cheapy throw-away tents.  This thing looks like a large turtle shell just hugging the ground and if you use all the little Velcro straps under the fly cover to attach it to the poles, it's even stronger!  GREAT DESIGN!  After all the things we've put this tent through, it is showing ZERO signs of wear!  All the seams and tie-downs and zippers are in tip-top shape!  4. Fits ANYWHERE!  We've had camp sites that were like half acre sections of woods and others that had puny 10x12 tent pads, and this large comfortable tent fits perfectly in them all!  I've been amazed at how a 10x16 tent could fit into places the park rangers weren't even sure it could.  Unlike the cheap box-shaped 9-person tents you can cheaply acquire, the low profile/domed design of the Eureka fits under low trees, next to picnic tables, and in between tree trunks very easily!  The poles are integrated nicely into the tent itself, so you don't need any footprint space outside the actual fabric of the tent itself.  Very versatile and easy to fit!  5.  PLENTY of room inside!  As I've mentioned, we sleep a family of six inside this tent.  We lay out a king size foam mattress topper for Mommy and Daddy, then sleeping bags with padding below each for the 4 kids and we have enough room left over for our bags, water bottles, and other supplies still.  I'm not an exceedingly tall man (5'10\\"), but I can stand up easily inside the tent without bending over.  It's deceiving from the outside as to just how much space is in that tent.  We have never felt crowded at all and although it is a domed design, there is plenty of adult stand-up room in the middle of the tent, which is easily half the floor space of the tent.  A few tips:  1. Most definitely use a high-quality seam sealer and throughly seal every seam on the tent and fly cover before you ever use it!  Also allow plenty of time for that sealer to dry and do not store the tent in an overly hot location or the sealer can turn gummy.  We did this and have not regretted it!  2. In addition to the seam sealer, I also sprayed a quality silicone-sealant over the entire fly cover and exposed corners of the tent.  Sure, this may supposedly \\"void\\" the warranty, but who's gonna need a warranty on a tent this tough anyway?  And wouldn't you rather have a dry night's sleep then worry about whether or not they're going to quibble with you about sealant if you DID need to use the warranty?  The water beads off my Eureka like marbles on a tile floor and I LOVE that!  We can sleep in comfort....and we've had 3 midnight storms while sleeping in the tent too....not a drop got inside the tent!  3. buy yourself one or two high-quality, double-layered, waterproof tarps to put under the tent.  I personally use one of those cheap $5 blue tarps on the ground, then a good $20 double-layered/waterproof tarp on top of that.  We found this was necessary especially in areas with moist soil to keep that moisture from getting the bottom of our bedding damp by morning.  Once we started using the high-quality tarp (and/or two, not sure which), we haven't had any moisture problems.  Overall I have found absolutely NOTHING wrong with this tent!  It is just perfect for us and we've loved making it our home away from home during the summers!  Every single feature is so well thought-out and designed, you just can't buy a better tent for the money!

product_title: XLAB Torpedo Carbon Mount (Black)
review_body: This is exactly what I expected it to be and what I needed.  Very simple to install and easy to use.  Even with an over sized 24 oz bottle, it does not hinder the use of my arrow bars.  I would definitely recommend this product to anyone looking to add another water bottle to their bike.

product_title: ALPS Mountaineering Mesh Weekender Seat
review_headline: Great seat pad with backrest for canoe or leanto.
review_body: I purchased this seat pad with backrest for a 5-day backpacking canoe trip into the Adirondack Mountains.  The back support was much better than a simple seat pad.  The ventilated back was a nice extra touch for a hot day in the canoe.  The only improvement would be more padding in the seat; however, that would add bulk and weight in the pack.  Overall, I was glad I bought and took this on the trip.  Good quality and good value at a good price.

product_title: Camelbak Unisex Classic Bottle Cap
review_body: We bought this cap to replace the cap the bottle came with (one of the ones with the straw/bite valve, that got moldy very quickly).  Works well, just as you'd expect.  It's a bit pricey for just a cap, though.

product_title: Dakine Campus Laptop Backpack
review_body: Thanks so much for the awesome backpack. It's perfect for what I need and I will definitely be able to use it all the way through college. Fast service and prompt feedback when I had some questions.

product_title: Wald 585 Rear Bicycle Basket (14.5 x 9.5 x 9)
review_headline: Will not attach to my rack
review_body:
This will not attach with the provided hardware to the rack on my Trek bicycle. I will have to attach it with zip-ties.

Otherwise the basket is fine.

product_title: Coleman 6-Person Instant Cabin
review_body: I went by the previous reviews of this tent and decided to trust that it was easy to set-up. It took us 90 seconds on the first try and then less than a minute on additional attempts. Rolling it up is a little more work but not bad. It easily fit back into the carry bag. We are happy with this purchase!

product_title: Manzella Women's Power Stretch Glove
review_body:
I was looking for new gloves made of fabric with minimal loss of dexterity. From the product photo and the product description, these sounded wonderful. They looked like they'd fit trim and snug, but have enough stretch to not be restrictive.

I measured my hands, and they are 7.5\\" at the knuckles. Bingo. Size Large fits 7.5\\".

Only it doesn't. These gloves are by no means snug. They are over-sized. The finger seams are crooked, and the thumb gusset sits too close to my thumb. Furthermore, the fingers are odd lengths. My fingers are rather short. The index fingers fit well. That means if you have long fingers, the index fingers of the gloves will be too short. The remaining fingers are far too long. In fact, the pinky fingers are nearly as long as the index fingers. These simply are not well-made. They feel strange on my hands. I've bought gloves that were too large or too small before, but I've never had a pair of gloves so oddly-shaped.

The fabric is decent. It isn't that stretchy, though. On the palm side, the gloves are covered with oodles of gripping dots. They'd be great if I could actually grip anything, with my thumbs being pulled away from normal by the gussets, and the fingers being so long.

I can't recommend these gloves. If the cut and sewing are typical of Manzella, I wouldn't even recommend the brand. I'll donate these to Goodwill.

product_title: Wenoka Squeeze Lock Knife, Blunt - Yellow
review_body: I've lost one knife (of another brand) by just moving my BC while on a boat and my wife has lost one (of yet another brand) getting out of the water - the knives simply fell out of their respective \\"locking\\" sheaths.  The Wenoka Squeeze Lock Knife can't be lost.  I've tried (out of the water of course) to make this knife fall out, slip out or be knocked out of its sheath and it stays put.  I even unlocked one side by tilting the knife in the sheath and it still stays put.  I can't even pull it out by force.  The only way it will come out is by squeezing both of the locking tabs.  So, unless you drop it into the depths while using it, this knife will stay with you in and out of the water.

product_title: Intova Digital Sports Utility Camera
review_body: The only thing good with this camera is the waterproof case, it is really good. But all the rest are rubish. Camera arrived with 3 dead pixels, the image quality very poor, video sometimes jumps about 0.5~1 seconds, it sucks the batteries and it can turn off at anytime. I am not happy at all. This camera can be only a toy for kids.

product_title: ALPS Mountaineering Zephyr 1 Backpacking Tent
review_body: Light, easy to set up, well-made. I camped for 10 days in the North Cascades in this tent and it served me well. The vestibule was just the right size for my (too) large pack. I like that it's not so small that you can sit up inside.

product_title: Camper RV Sheet Set Bunk 30x80 White with Mahogany Trim
review_body: Way better than the single bed sheets I used at the beginning of our RV experience. The primary problem I have is slippage -- the top sheet tends to slide toward the floor during the night and that is hard to combat because of the design of the RV. Actually, I would like to get more sheets before our next long trip to facilitate laundering. I would buy a higher thread count camper RV fitted bunk sheets if they were available.

product_title: Columbia FunRun Sport Swivel Wheel Jogger Stroller
review_body: I've been using this stroller for several years. Overall it's great. I had originally had a BOB stroller but sold it because the handle was too short (I am rather tall) and the front wheel didn't steer (very hard to maneuver). The Columbia stroller was much better as a replacement. It has held up well to hard use. The only flaw is the harness; the straps are floppy and tend to get twisted around.

product_title: Neewer 3 Mode Zoom R2 AAA LED Headlamp Headlight Torch, Light Weight Headlight for Camping Fishing Hiking
review_body: Anteriormente compre 1 de estos focos para probar, (era otro módelo muy similar) ese lo califique bien porque resulto muy bueno, con base en eso compré 2 de estos focos que anuncian son de 300 lumens, y en realidad son de 160 lumens, así me los enviaron....eso es PUBLICIDAD ENGAÑOSA, y aparte de esos, los 2 dan un tono diferente de luz, uno es más claro que él otro, los comparé con mi compra inicial y alumbran MUCHO MENOS, estoy sumamente molesto con esta compra.

product_title: Chums Floating Keychain
review_body: I ordered the blue keychain in the picture but I received a red one. My boat is blue, all the trim is blue, if I order blue why send me red? Save yourself the trouble of returning it.

product_title: Planet Bike Borealis Fall/Winter Full Finger
review_body: Received these last week and already worn them twice in 30 degree weather.  They have kept my fingers warm throughout the 90 minute ride (made before dawn).  Neither day registered over 33 degrees throughout the ride.  Fingers do get a little chilly when riding into the wind but its not bad -- would be the be all and end all of gloves if they were windproof.  Still, I can see using these (perhaps with glove liners) down to 15 or 20 degrees.

product_title: Alex X101 Rear Wheel MTB - 26 x 1.75"
review_headline: Good enough. Great store, necessary products.
review_body: This is a great place to find parts. I mean parts to fix your bike, not parts that are special and cost a million dollars. I just wish that you could go through amazon and have \\"chat\\" or some kind of question/answer functionality to assure you are getting the right combination of parts. Anyway the rim works great and I'm back in the saddle. I will return to this store. I have been there in person when business takes me that way and they are very helpful.

product_title: MSR Dragonfly Stove Pump
review_body: I own a first generation Dragonfly.  The original pump failed long ago, the brittle plastic housing around the plunger cracked, not from abuse or overuse, but from normal use.  The replacement was a significant improvement.  The housing is more flexible and durable.  Recently the on/off valve began to leak.  I was unable to affect a repair with the stove repair kit and my local outdoor store, Campmor, was also unable to fix it. It appears that debris from the decayed gasket may have cause the valve pin to wedge in a way that made its removal impossible. The stove has performed flawlessly in the field but this kind of catastrophic failure was disappointing as was the fact that there is only a $6.00 difference between sending it back for repair and replacing it.  I will continue to use the stove but now instead of relying on the ability to repair it in the field I will carry some type of back up.

product_title: CamelBak ThermoBak 3L Hydration System 100 OZ Desert Camo Military
review_body: This is a very simple hydration pack.    It does NOT have ANY extra pockets for small items you might want to take with you, however there are some \\"D-rings\\" you can use to attach other items or small pouches to it.    The hose comes with insulation so the water in the hose doesn't get warm too fast for that \\"first sip warm water gross out\\" and the bite valve comes with a little \\"clean cap\\" to keep dirt and crud off the part you put in your mouth.    The water bladder is not removable from the pack.  (WAIT: I WAS WRONG.  The bladder IS removable if you pull off the plastic ring that holds the lid on.  Thanks for the correction USMCgunrock.)  Interestingly: the bladder is made out of a black material while every other Camelbak I've ever had used a blue material for the bladder.  Doesn't really affect my opinion one way or the other.  Just curious.  And I hope there's no extra chemicals that might leach into my water, but with any plastics you never truly know.    I like the extra handle right below the filling port.  It is perfect for filling the bag under a tap and eliminates the awkwardness in filling many other types of Camelbak bags.   You can't lose the cap because it is attached with a loop of plastic.  Nice.   There is no waist strap, which is a bit annoying if you're used to having one, but really the bag isn't long enough to require one, so that's okay.    The only real bad thing about this bag is that there is NO padding on the shoulder straps.  If you wear this thing full of water on a long hike or jog the straps are going to start annoying you and cutting into your shoulders unless you're wearing a lot of other layers that act as padding.  When I'm hiking/biking/jogging I try not to wear a lot of layers so they DO cut into my shoulders.    All in all it's a good bag.    Very basic.  No frills.  (Except the insulation and the clean cap cover.)

product_title: NIKE BRASILIA 4 LG MESH BACKPACK (MENS)
review_body: i look every where and i could not fine anywhere whn school started so look at amazon and found just what i was looking for and it did not cost that much either..

product_title: Aquatec Duo Alert Aquatec Duo-Alert Air Powered Surface & U/W Signaling Device Scuba Dive Diving Divers BC BCD Gear
review_body: This tool is a must when diving. Technology is in your hand so why dont use it. I had one of these but only had the alert in the surface. Now with this new tool I have it also for underwater and also for the surface. Cant dive without it. It's better to have it and not need it that need it and dont have it. It can save your buddies life and yours..

product_title: Sixsixone Veggie Shin Guard
review_body: at first they looked a little small but after i put them on it was great.i use these for bmx freestyle and they worked great. I took them to camp Woodward and they survived. great protection plus they last a long time.Price is perfect for what your getting.the only bad thing is the ankle strap is a little small so if you are around 12-14 and have OK sized ankles then get a small. another cool feature is that it also connects to the veggie knee guards. i would definitively recommend these ,but i would also get the knee guards they work a lot better when combined.

product_title: Timbuk2 Commute 2.0 Laptop Messenger Bag
review_body: On the upside - this is an extremely well made bag, all the pockets and pouches are great.    On the downside:  (1) it is difficult to assess what size bag to buy based on the measurements provided on the Timbuk2 website - I chose a size small to fit my 14\\" laptop, which from the website I should have had ample space but with the actual bag it only just fits at a squeeze.  (2) with my laptop in the bag, the bag doesn't sit right by default when you sling it over your shoulder (it sticks out on an angle due to the weight of the laptop) - you need to adjust the clips where the strap joins the bag every time to get the bag to hang properly.    Even though there are a couple of downsides, I still use the bag everyday and quite like it, and recommend the workmanship of the Timbuk2 guys.

product_title: Kenda K850 Aggressive MTB Wire Bead Bicycle Tire, Blackskin, 26-Inch x 2.10-Inch
review_headline: Something went wrong with the size :(
review_body: I ordered this tire because it was by 2.10 but then when i receive it, the tires ends up looking like a 1.95 which is really thin.

product_title: Primal Wear Women's Sparrow
review_body: I love the style and design, its beautiful - I sized up, b/c of other posters comments, but would have been fine in my usual (bought a large, usually wear a medium), so I found the sizing to be true, not small (I wear an 8 in regular shirts).  The fabric is a lighter weight than others I have, so best for hot days.

product_title: High Sierra AT3 26" Drop Bottom Wheeled Duffle
review_headline: You get what you pay for
review_body: You will pay more for this brand but it is worth it.   If you have ever owned cheap luggage then you can see the difference in the thickness of the materials and how well the seems old up over time.    This is a great carry on that I travel with all the time and am happy with.  I highly recommend it if you are looking to travel light and get in and out of the plane fast.

product_title: Coleman 2-Pack Standard String Tie #21 Mantles
review_body: These Mantles worked fine on my very old gas lantern. Very bright and stood the abuse of a car ride after being lit.

product_title: O'Neill Wake Waterski Men's Superlite USCG Vest
review_body: I really like the yellow color scheme but all those buckles are a turn-off.  Does it not have a zipper?  It's 2 or 3 buckles too many seems like.  A mesh top seems like it'd keep you cooler if you were out kayaking   or fishing in the hot sun. But the colors would match my kayak so i hate  not liking this one!

product_title: Topeak Turbo Morph Bike Pump with Gauge
review_body: I just purchased this and have only tried it once.  The displacement on the pump is not large, so you will get some excercise getting to 70psi.  The plastic foot rest is not sturdy but can be used carefully to balance the pump while inflating.  The Guage is small but surprisingly accurate.  The unit is somewhat long and limits where on your bike you can mount it.  I opted for under my crossbar so I wouldn't have to sacrifice a bottle holder.  The Valve stem receptacle fit easily over the valve stem and clicked into place easily.  So far, I really like the pump, but if you value lightness and compactness, look elsewhere.

product_title: Summer Beach Cabana / Tent - Quick Setup and Floorless
review_body: I can not recommend this cabana to anyone who intends to use it on the beach.  We tried, for several days, to erect this cabana.  If there is the slightest wind, the legs will buckle and it will not stand as shown in the picture.  It is certainly not worth the money.  In fact, it is not worth any amount of money if you intend to use it on the beach.

product_title: Eureka Apex 2XT Tent
review_body: The tent is actualy quite good in terms of rain and wind coverage as well as is to make up. The problem that i found with it is that it look beat smaller than what it is as well as lighter. The tent it is said to be for 2 people but it is more for 3, you could even put in 4 people but they would be very messd up.  If you are planning to by this tent just consider that it is a very big tent to be for 2 people

product_title: Sunlite Top Tube Pannier, 2011 Model, Black
review_body: Exactly what I was looking for, worth a little extra $$ for a quality product. Roomy and good fit on my bike.

product_title: Garrity Power Lite 3 LED Crank Light
review_body: I bought this light for my emergency go-bag. It's not for everyday use, but I want assurance it will work when I need it. The crank is perfect for emergencies--when batteries would be clumsy and likely expired.     PRO  Reliable  Bright  Fine for car camping    CON  Quite heavy for its size -- not for backpacking

product_title: Scuba Dive Underwater Writing Slate 6" x 5", available for different style, w/ compass, and glow-in-dark
review_body: For the price of this slate it woks ok.  you are going to want to put a retracting device on it for ease of use and handing between to divers.  Very hard to see this slate in low light though.  great for a beginner diver.

product_title: ExOfficio Women's BugsAway Ziwa Pant
review_body:
First, I don't own but these seem EXPENSIVE!!
Second, you can get SAME results it would seem by buying Permethrin Spray [[ASIN:B001ANQVYU Sawyer SP657 Permethrin Premium Insect Clothing Repellent, 24-Ounce Spray]] and spraying your OWN existing clothing. Just think about it before you buy.

If you go to Insect Shield(tm) web site [...] they give you link to CDC / EPA-OSHA about insect protective clothing[...] which cites ONLY Permethrin as an effective garment treatment for protection against ticks, as it deals solely with Lyme Disease (tick borne), and I quote:

Use insecticides such as Permethrin for greater protection.
Permethrin kills ticks on contact.
Permethrin can be used on clothing but should not be used on skin.
One application of permethrin to pants, socks, and shoes typically stays effective through several washings.
Ref:[...]

Just so you know what you are getting ...

product_title: Giro Stylus Bike Helmet
review_body: The over all helmet is great. The only real issue that I'm having is that the dial that adjust the tightness on you head comes loose all the time. If I were to buy another helmet I think I may pay the extra money and buy it from a bike store and not Amazon. This way I could try it out before I buy it.

product_title: Crocodile Creek Kids Drinking Bottle - Daisies
review_body: My daughter carries this with her each day to school filled w/ water.  She does have to make sure to push down hard on the white part of the drinking spout so it doesn't leak.  I love that it has no liner, so no chemicals to leach into her drinks. It will dent if you drop it, but it's metal, so it's to be expected.

product_title: Sand Blaster Beach Umbrella
review_body: This  umbrella is more than I expected----for the price  Great for sitting in the sun at the beach---brought it for my daughter and son in law---They love it

product_title: U.S. Divers Cozumel Seabreeze Dry Proflex II Mask, Fins and Snorkel Set
review_headline: My husband LOVES this snorkel set!
review_body: I bought this snorkel set for my husband to use in the Bahamas based on the reviews.  It lived up to the great reviews.  My husband loved it!  He went on and on about how great it felt and how it performed.  Highly recommend.

product_title: Thermacell R-1 Mosquito Repeller Refill, 12 Hour Pack (3 Repellent Mats and 1 Butane Cartridge)
review_body: I hate to buy a product like ThermaCell without having refills on hand. Mosquitos have been so bad this year! Glad I found them!

product_title: Columbia Women's Silver Ridge Sleeveless Shirt
review_body: Love this shirt. Actually was in search of the cotton version. However, 8-10 washes in, found the shirt to be pilled up and kinda yucky.

product_title: ShelterLogic 13 x 20 x 12 ft. SUV/Truck Garage-in-a-Box™
review_body: Be very carefull about buying one of these or similiar items on line. They are very heavy (look at the shipping cost) and if parts are missing the company is slow (A understatement) to answer their phone and address problems.  Ours came missing 8 critical parts and 2 other parts were assembled and welded in their factory incorrectly.  I could not finish assembling the shelter without them. It took three days of waiting for a response from their help line (I both phoned and emailed) before I just dialed and let the phone stay on unit a live person finally answered after almost a hour.  You have to furnish a copy of your purchase reciept before they will do anything and I didn't find them very helpful, just made excuses for the problem and slow response. Lucky I was able to scan and email it. But, I have never received any notification that the replacement parts were shipped. You could have the same problem if buying locally, by the way.  But at least you have some one to talk to.  As to the product itself, it seems well designed and fit for it's intended purpose. Instructions are a bit sketchy in places, but not to bad if you have some general idea how things go together. If they got their QC in control, it would be even better.  Edit, almost 3 weeks after we received this item, we are still short parts. They finally sent and I recieved the shorted parts, but they only sent half as many as I was shorted.  I cannot recommend that anyone buy anything from this company. Their customer service is lousy to say the least. All my communication with them is documented and I requested what was short, but they still couldn't get it right.

product_title: Coleman Fold N Go Stove Grate
review_body: I received this accessory for Christmas last year. This accessory works great for using the fold n go grill as a camp stove. So far, I've used it to heat a camp oven. Can't wait to use it on my next camp out.

product_title: Bones Skate Bearings Cleaning Unit
review_headline: The best service for the best bearings
review_body: This bottle is great, helps you clean your sistems with NO MESS AT ALL, great product, tuff built, it helps a lot when you need it, just place the bearings inside, it holds 8 at a time, flush them, and forget about messy cloths or anything eles, let the bearings sit on a piece of paper, blow some compressed air into them to dry the solvents used for cleaning, and then lubricate the bearings and you are ready to roll again.

product_title: Coleman 2000019225 Large Dual-Action Quick Pump
review_headline: Works great but needed modification to work with float tube
review_body: Product has worked great so far.  However the adapters supplied did not connect with my fishing float tube. review_headline: Dajo Survivor, One Bad Little Mama Jama
review_body: This is an outstanding knife and kit, except for the sheath (more about this later); the entire package is exactly as described and works as such.  Good to throw in the trunk of a car or toolbox, as another reviewer stated?  Go for it, but I say absolutely not.  I took this to the bush on Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, NC and put it to the test; it performed better than expected.  Can you baton with it?  I batonned the heck out of this knife making small to medium stakes and poles for a lean to.  It is not made for splitting firewood.  I use my K-Bar BK2 or Gurkha Kukri Machete for this.  Much like going to combat, the more \\"tools of the trade\\" you have, the better.  The firesteel is awesome and regardless of what some folks say about the whistle; I found this whistle to be very loud (I took off the key ring and put one small piece of reflective tape on the whistle just in case I dropped it, no use for the key ring myself, but maybe a good fit for some people).  In many ways though I prefer a strong Acorn shell, cannot be beaten in regard to size, abundance, correct pitch level and loudness.  To solve the problem some reviewers had with the firesteel dropping out when carried vertically on the belt and the sheath is opened; turning the steel upside down is the easy answer, or sew its pocket tighter as well. Much like any weapon, it can be abused and damaged if used incorrectly.  Thus, much like a rifle or pistol, it has to be treated with the correct respect.  As far as the sheath goes; I love the design but the belt loop sucks.  Paracord this sheath to your rucksack instead, but be sure to keep the blade facing down; it's not that it's velcro, it's just CHEAP velcro.  I enjoy making modifications to my knife sheaths anyway; much like every Marine, Seal, PJ, Soldier, Police Officer & Bushman, you have to \\"personalize\\" your gear. It's amazing how many Metallurgy experts there are doing knife reviews as well. Some people complain about the comfort of the handle. product_title: Camelbak Quick Grip 21 Oz Hydration Pack
review_headline: It's Okay: A Camelbak Quick Grip 21 oz Hydration Pack Review
review_body:
I signed up with Team In Training and trained with a large group of runners of varying experience levels to compete in my first half marathon. Having never run for sport before, I lacked many items a seasoned runner uses. I had a Polar insulated water bottle from cycling I held while running. This worked fine for low mileage, but as my distance increased, I knew I needed something requiring less effort to hold. I wanted to comfortably carry about 20 oz, and looked at belts with multiple smaller bottles and larger triangular waist packs. Ultimately I chose to stick with a handheld solution.

The Camelbak Quick Grip consists of an insulated water bottle with a lightweight sleeve. The sleeve, made in the Philipines, acts as a handle and includes a small 2.5 x 3.5 inch pocket to hold keys or other small items. My BMW car key fits, but I've got to work it in the pocket and have it angled just right. The removable sleeve fits snuggly around the water bottle, but is difficult to remove and even more difficult to reinsert the bottle into.

The sleeve, opposite from the pocket, allows small hands to grab the water bottle from beneath. My medium sized hand finds this uncomfortably tight and prefers to use the outer adjustable strap. However the adjustable strap needs regular adjustments, as it doesn't effectively lock into place.

The 21oz/610ml BPA-free insulated water bottle with jet valve keeps your beverage cooler longer, and resists flavor retention. On occasion, I'll use a watered down sport drink in my bottle, I've never noticed the flavors lingering from previous uses. Plus, the jet valve locks closed to prevent leaking, but easily twists open allowing a generous flow.

I have mixed feelings about the Camelbak quick grip hydration pack. The pocket could be a little bigger, and the grip is problematic. The insulated bottle keeps my drink cooler, but there are plenty of insulated bottles to choose from. If you have smaller hands, this may work great for you. If y have medium sized hands like me or larger, you may find the adjustable strap annoying and probably should consider other options.

Insulated water bottle
BPA-free
Jet valve prevents leaking and provides a generous flow

CONS:
Small pocket could be a little bigger
Adjustable strap needs regular adjustingyou. If y have medium sized hands like me or larger, you may find the adjustable strap annoying and probably should consider other options. product_title: Sevylor Nautical Pool Chair
review_body:
This product may no longer be available, and is no longer on the Sevylor catalog of current products.

That said, it is an excellent lounge chair. Here are the features: low profile seat, roll-up inflatable leg/foot rest, inflatable back bolster cushion (to prevent you from tipping backwards in the water), welded-on attachments to connect more chairs side-by-side, and grabline to be used as a tie-down to boat decks or the beach (ever had an inflatable go bouncing down the beach due to strong gusts hitting beachgoers and kicking sand all over their faces, or blown off your boat deck into the open ocean?). There are 5 separate chambers: one for the back rest, one for the main chamber and arms, one for the leg/foot rest, and one for the removable back bolster. The 5th chamber (the center of the seat cushion) is intended to be filled with water from underneath. Read further for explanation on this.

It can be used in one of three ways - (1) a water lounge with a footrest, (2) a beach/poolside lounge with leg rest, footrest rolled up, or (3) deck chair with added height with the foot/leg rest folded underneath.

The center cushion area (i.e. under your bottom) can be filled with water as ballast; I like to fill it about 75% full with air though, it's more comfortable and the seams will likely last longer if the seat - already supporting all your weight - doesn't have to support the additional pressure of water. The water chamber is to help hold the chair down in strong sustained gusts.

My favorite thing to do is take this chair about 200 feet off shore (i.e. clear of all the Waikiki near-shore tourists), and anchor it with a short rope and light anchor. Can sit out there with a book, a large bottle of water, and sunscreen all day. The only inconvenience is having to bring an air pump, it's not exactly an inflatable \\"lightweight\\" such as arm bands or even a small air mattress, its main compartment takes a LONG TIME to inflate. The footrest is no sweat.

It's very attractive (I get compliments all the time for it, even got an OFFER from one young lady), very comfortable, the backrest is very supportive (especially when used in conjunction with the removable bolster pillow). Further comfort comes from the fact it has a low profile, and the legrest supports under the knees, and as a footrest it is just the right height (i.e. low enough) so it doesn't discomfort the heels.

So long story short, it's one of the best lounge chairs around, it's just too bad Sevylor is not making them anymore.It's very attractive (I get compliments all the time for it, even got an OFFER from one young lady), very comfortable, the backrest is very supportive (especially when used in conjunction with the removable bolster pillow). product_title: Lazer Magic Buckle: Magnetic Assist Closure
review_headline: Super Upgrade for Kids' Helmets - Parents Rejoice!
review_body:
Wow!

I don't want to overstate my enthusiasm for this gizmo -- it IS just a lowly buckle, after all -- but... Wow!

My son has complained about the stock \\"no pinch\\" chinstrap buckle on his Giro Me2 since the first day he wore it. He's flinched when I fasten it, and he's flinched when I open it. It's regularly accompanied by screams, shrieks, cries, wails, or refusals to wear it. And it's beyond me, because I've never adjusted his chinstrap tight like I would with an adult helmet -- there's always enough slack to ensure separation between skin & buckle. Nevertheless...

I ran into Lazer kids helmets at a local bike shop. The helmets themselves were cool designs with cows, space shuttles, and firefighter helmets, but nevermind that -- my wife and I were both really impressed with these buckles. We eventually settled for another Giro helmet for our son -- the Rodeo -- but found these buckles available separately so \\"upgraded\\" the stock Giro buckles.

To Close: simply overlap the two pieces. The top piece (marked with the 'Z' logo) incorporates a very simple mechanical latch that \\"sucks on\\" to the lower piece (via a very strong rare earth magnet) and that's it! It is truly as easy as putting a magnet on to the refrigerator door -- no clicking, no aligning, no ability to pinch any skin.

To Open: with just very light thumb pressure, the two pieces slide apart (i.e. the 'Z' piece slides forward to the chin). The magnet resists a little (this is what keeps it from opening accidentally) but there is no latch to open, nothing to click, no resistance other than the magnetic force to overcome.

In Use: pull this buckle by the chinstraps in opposite directions and it stays connected -- it's as strong as any chinstrap I've come across.

The straps Giro uses on their infant sized Me2 and toddler/youth sized Rodeo & Rascal are full width, adult sized straps. As such, this buckle adapts over perfectly (though unthreading / rethreading the strap is a mild pain in the kiester). However, it'll probably appear to be a bit \\"chunky\\" compared to the buckle it's replacing. I had my doubts initially, thinking that there must be a child sized version, but rest assured, it works fine with the little ones.

These buckles aren't just for the kids. Lazer uses them on their adult helmets. I like them enough I'm considering buying a few more to adapt over my and my wife's helmets.

If you want to see this contraption in operation, there's a video on you-know-where-Tube. Search for Lazer Magnetic Buckle. They don't show it opening, but they show it basically closing itself. product_title: iBert Safe-T Front Mounted Child Bicycle Seat
review_body:
I was very skeptical at first about a seat mounted to the handlebar stem... but it works very well! Our baby does not mind the movement of the steering wheel. I was also surprised that there is very little affect on the handling of the bike, and I was comfortable (that i was a safe rider with it for baby's sake!) after only a few minutes. A huge benefit of the ibert is being able to interact with your child while you ride. Love being able to talk to my 10 month son and have him look at me... and he likes to play with my gloves (or any thing else) on the handlebars. In fact, we have ordered a second mount from ibert for my wife to use... I am confident she will be a safe pilot also.

I held back on 5 stars because there is a small affect (for me and i assume it would be the same for most...) on your pedaling technique if you are trying to train some while you ride your baby. I do have to bring my knees out a little at the top of their arc and that does not do well with higher levels of effort. But no problems at all with cruising! I Really like the seat and highly recommend it.

product_title: Finger Sleeves Assorted Sizes --- 12

product_title: Drop Women's Opener Gauntlet Glove
review_body: Bought these for my wife on her first ski trip.  Turned out to be a very good pair of gloves. She's usually a cold so I was worried that they wouldn't have enough insulation.  But they kept her warm and dry all day!  Great buy!

product_title: Bones Speed Cream Skate Bearing Lubricant
review_body: I used this on a electric scooter I added bones bearings too and it worked very well. Bones is good stuff.

product_title: Emotion Kayaks Paddle Leash (Black)
review_body: For only $8.12 you can't go wrong; very well-made with clips at both ends; purchased two of these little gems with their own cute little storage bags for our tandem \\"Long-Haul\\" expedition kayak...Very happy with purchase.

product_title: SKS Longboard 45 Full Coverage Bicycle Fender Set
review_headline: Light, functional and long but the silver's not exactly as pictured.
review_body: I ordered the silver, but unlike the stock photo pictured what I received has 2 transparent stripes running the length of the fenders and the 'silver' around them is a sort of brushed-metal looking grey.  Do not expect a chrome or uniform silver color.      Ultimately they fit and seem plenty sturdy.  Installation was nontrivial and you'll probably need to make your own judgments for your particular bike.  One of the black plastic stay-guides broke when I applied pressure on the stay passing through it; I started to panic before realizing that for any of these fenders to be where I wanted them I'd need to cut off the tips of all the plastic guides anyway so that the stays could pass further through.  If you wish to avoid cutting the plastic guides as I did (looks prettier if you don't and would provide some protection from a loosened fender coming down on your tires) you will need to measure and pre-cut the stays to fit your bike before attaching them, Rivendell Bicycle Works has a youtube video that demonstrates this nicely.  Either way you'll probably need a hacksaw or bolt cutter to trim the stays.    The set came with plenty of hardware for various mounting scenarios, the coverage is awesome and they're far lighter than any equivalently sized steel fenders would be.

product_title: Gravity Drop-Carve Makai Complete Longboard Skateboard - 9.5" x 41"
review_body:
I have had a Makai for three weeks. I have been bombing hills, carving up streets and sidewalks and have a blast.
Took it to the skatepark for bowel riding, after waiting a LONG time I got a few good rides... This board is amazing for down hills.
