And I did not want to pay the grossly inflated prices at a brick and mortar store where I could try them on. The sunclouds seemed to fit the bill. Optics are good, price is reasonable and the fit is good. The microfiber case is kind is nice for cleaning the lenses, but doesn't offer any protection when the glasses are stored in them. The bottom of the lenses do touch my cheeks, but I like lenses that fit closely to the face and I've gotten used to that.

product_title: Coleman Fold N Go Stove Carry Case
review_body: This case is perfect for to stove and fuel and a weekend worth of utensils. We love both the case and the fold n go stove!

product_title: SANOXY® 0.2mm Ultra Thin TPU Keybaord Cover, High Transparency LAPTOP KEYBOARD COVER FOR MACBOOK PRO AND AIR, MacBook,MacBook PRO(LATE 2010),MacBook Air 13"
review_headline: AWESOME PRODUCT! Works on my Macbook Alum
review_body: I was a little worried at first since the description only listed Macbook Pros but it works for my MacBook perfectly. I love it! Great product.

product_title: Intex Raised Downy Airbed with Built-in Electric Pump, Queen, Bed Height 22"
review_body: Purchased this Airbed for my boyfriend to sleep on everynight while he was in transition and staying with a friend. His airbed before this one was a joke and would be flat an hr after putting air in it. We were pleasantly suprised when the Intex arrived. The size is impressive and it is definatly comproable to a queen  mattress in size. The first night we blew it up we were VERY impressed. The top of the mattress is fabric covered so it dosent feel like you are just laying on plastic. The built in pump is very convienent and allows you to easily achieve the firmness you want. The only reason this product gets 4 stars instead of 5 is because it does lose some air. It may be user error on our part and not closing the vents properly but i suspect this is not the case since it appears others have had similar issues. Fortunatly because of its size and height off the ground, you will never wake up on the floor because even when it does lose a little air, you are so elevated to begin with there is still pleanty of air to support your body. Overall for the price, we are very satisfied. In the future if we ever need to purchase another airbed we may spring for the more expensive one just to see if it has anything to do with the ability to hold air, but for now, this one is still the best airbed we have used.

product_title: Park Tool PT-03 Double Ended Cone Wrench
review_body: I am glad I was able to get this in the 13mm/15mm size to save from buying two wrenches.  I bought this for my cheapo big box store bike which came with a wobbly front hub and I was easily able to adjust it with this wrench plus a regular 17mm opened end wrench. I read that the most common cone sizes are 13mm (front) and 15mm (rear).  Not all sources carry this combination forcing you to buy two wrenches to overhaul a typical bike's hubs.

product_title: Genuine Rum Runner Flask Kit 1 16oz and 2 8oz Flasks Plus a Funnel
review_headline: they work great, but a bit small
review_body: We put these in our checked suitcase and had no problem going through security at the airport.  We then checked it at the cruise terminal and they were, again, not found.      These flasks are great and do what they say they will, but they're a bit smaller than we expected, especially since you're only supposed to fill them to about 80% capacity.  Regardless, I'm very happy i purchased these flasks :-)

product_title: Grandoe Men's Updown Mitt
review_body: I'm a long distance runner with very sensitive hands to the cold and have found these to be the best gloves yet by far for keepings fingers warm down to even sub zero temps. A bit on the bulky side so end up using them only when I expect I wont be taking them off during the run. Very light-weight and very soft leather. Feel these are worth every bit of the cost and would highly recommend them.

product_title: Schwinn Crest Urban Women's Hybrid Bike (700c Wheels)
review_headline: A few problems, but over all a good bike
review_body: I bought this bike last June when walking just wasn't cutting it anymore.     Pros:  Fast- it has 21 gears and it's meant more for speed, not at all as slow as a cruiser.  Reliable- i've beaten this poor bike up and it took the hits like a champ: crashing it, knocking it down, etc.  Handles New Orleans roads decently- despite it's thin tires, it goes over bumps pretty smoothly.  Pretty good gear shifting- a little difficult sometimes, but over all pretty awesome.  Awesome metal peddles- not those cheap plastic pedals that eventually crack. really sturdy.    Cons:  Heavy- biking uphill is semi difficult with a bike that weighs 45 pounds, but it could be worse.  Rusts easily- after 8 months of riding it, it was COVERED in rust.  Brakes- the brakes are good, but it's really difficult finding the sweet spot to where your brakes work awesomely and your front tire can still come off without having to tweak the brakes. really annoying.  Bolts- some of the bolts didn't even come with the bike and some mysteriously disappeared while riding.    Over all, it's a good bike. It is fast and sturdy. Just make sure to wipe it down when you get out of the rain. Don't ride in the sand because the tires are too thin. Don't worry about your tires when going over big bumps, they can handle it. However, it just got stolen and for me, the pros didn't outweigh the cons enough to buy the same bike again.

product_title: Rothco G.I. Type Plastic Canteen & Pistol Belt Kit
review_body: Wanted a holder and belt for a Tritan 32 oz. canteen-style water bottle [[ASIN:B002PLWE2E Nalgene BPA Free Tritan Oasis Canteen 32 Oz Narrow Mouth Bottle]]. Wasn't anything labeled for such, selection of canteens and belts at Amazon very small (if you eliminate over-the shoulder, and MOLLE style). Description says 1 qt and web belt. Dimensions given are 8 1/2\\" H x 4 9/10\\" x 3 1/10\\". Product delivered is 7 1/4\\" x 4 3/8\\" x 2 3/4\\". Guess I should have bought local. The canteen delivered is 28 oz. or less, holder is snug on this smaller canteen, the belt is maximum size 40 (so am I). For many adult males, this allows no slack to put over clothes, etc. Should be labeled \\"belt for women and youths\\", and \\"maximum canteen size 28 ounces\\". Will use this as backup, but am disappointed. Could have bought better for less at local surplus (and now I will). Maybe you should look at the 589: [[ASIN:B001CWCISM 589 CANTEEN & PISTOL BELT KIT]] instead.

product_title: Victorinox Swiss Army Climber Pocket Knife
review_body: I bought one few weeks go. It looks very nice and has great functions. I like it very much. The tools included are enough for daily use. And it can also be a good present for friends.

product_title: Columbia Women's Whirlibird Parka
review_body:
\\"But Mom, I don't get cold in my jacket.\\" The words my daughter spoke to me are the words every Fairbanks, Alaska mom would like to hear from their children when asking about how this years winter jacket is holding up. My daughter spoke these words to me regarding her Columbia Whirlibird Parka with Omni-heat at the end of a -25 degree F school day. (That -25 is not a typo; we get many winter days like this in Fairbanks.)

Columbia has launched an extensive marketing campaign over its new insulating textile, Omni-heat. The Omni-heat lining is a black breathable fabric with silver reflective dots that send your heat back to your body while allowing moisture to escape. Columbia claims that it has the highest heat retention in the industry, while being lighter in weight and breathable.

That is a pretty big claim for cold-weather clothing.

Often, heat retention comes with a loss of breathability. This means that when you get warm, you will sweat and then the moisture trapped near your skin will cause you to get cold. Layered systems that are designed to keep you warm often wind up being very heavy, using a combination of materials to insulate and pull moisture away that adds pounds and bulk packed over your body.

When I saw the videos for the Omni-Heat products, the one that I really paid attention to was of a guy in a testing facility who works up a sweat and then stops in the cold. Thermal imaging shows that he is able to retain his body heat. After watching this, I thought it would be worth trying one of these jackets out for my daughter's winter gear this year.

product_title: MSR Mutha Hubba HP 3-Person Tent
review_body: I bought the Mutha Hubba for Boy Scout camping with my son's troop.  I am an assistant scoutmaster and go on most campouts with the troop.  The tent is large enought to bring my wife along and hold a queen size air mattress when she camps as well.  With just self-inflating air mattresses, this tent is a mansion for one or two persons.  The weight is very comparable to a lot of two person backpacking tents, such as the REI half dome, and carries in about the same size stuff sack.  It is not an ultralight tent by any means, but most of my camping involves short treks in.    On a camporee last weekend, we were hit with 40+ mph winds as a storm came through.  The Mutha Hubba took on the winds with flying colors and harldy shook at all.  The eight points of contact with the fly, an dthe two vestibules creates a solid tight package.  The tent comes with only two guy lines and no extra stakes, so you will need to invest in some extra line and stakes to be able to fully guy down the tent, but that should only be needed in very high winds, as the 10 stakes around the tent provide a pretty stable base.  Speaking of stakes, the quality of stakes provided by MSR are top notch.  Forget about the flismy stakes provided by most tent manufactures, MSR knows how to build a tent system.  I have bought MSR stakes to replace the stakes with on son's REI Half Dome.    After out last campout, I have had several folks ask about the MSR Mutha Hubba, and I have responded that it was the best investment I could have made.

product_title: Coghlan's Magnesium Fire Starter
review_body:
Okay so your cold, it's gonna get colder, you need fire and your matches are soaked... You probably wont care how long it takes to get one going.

PROS:
It works! If you have the time and patience to sit there and scrape the side of this little wonder for 20 or 30 minutes until you have enough shavings to get started, it WILL get you a fire going. You'll need a pile big enough to cover between a quarter and a half dollar. Once you have it the flint striker does wonders as the pile will flash after just a few quick strikes. Make sure your tinder is already covering it or only a second away as the magnesium burns quite hot but also quite fast! With some basic fire builders skills you'll be warm in no time.

CONS:
Time, collection, noise, knives, and wind... As I mensioned, 20 to 30 mins to get a pile big enough to burn. Add to that the time it takes to find wood and tinder and this could be an all evening process. Trying to collect these little shavings into a pile is kind of a pain. Though a little trick I thought of works well. Lay down a coffee filter and use that to collect them. The filter doubles as added starter. Even wet the filter wont hinder the burn ability of the magnesium. Noise, for the duration of the scrapting your have to listen to a very loud squeek with every pass of your knife. Just think metal on metal. Speaking of knives, your going to have to dull a knife doing this. So I recommend carrying a \\"cheap\\" lock blade just for this purpose. (Not too cheap though, as the cheapest in my collection actually got a notch carved in it by the magnesium and you do want a locking mechanesem that can withstand the downward pressure your going to have to put on it.) The final issue is any firestarter's worst enemy. Wind... Gathering a pile of shavings is tough enough but having them blow away is just insult to injury. So if there's any breeze at all, you might consider doing this from inside a tent or shelter.

This truely is a survival tool but one worth having. If your outdoors in the fall or spring without a fire you'll spend every sleepless minute of that seemingly never-ending cold night wondering what made you decide NOT to get a flint and magnesium fire starter.l tool but one worth having. review_body: This headlamp was a replacement for another which was misplaced during our move.  We have lots of power outages in our area and so when the lights go out, this comes to the rescue! product_title: Eureka! Grand Manan 9 - Tent (sleeps 4-5)
review_headline: Downsizing our tent but still need quality
review_body: My wife and I have tent camped for almost 30 years.  Usually we had upwards of three kids in tow so the tents we've used in the past tended to be large and relatively heavy duty.  Early on we discovered the quality and features of the Eureka tents and had a manufacturing presence in Binghamton, NY.  Since we lived on the East Coast, we would travel there to buy our tents directly. Up until 2009, we were tenting in one of the Eureka \\"Kahuna\\" tents.  Now that there's only the two of us, we've \\"downsized\\" to the Grand Manan.  It's about 1/2 the weight of the Kahuna and it eminently easier to erect.  The Kahuna requires two people, period.  The Manan can easily be done by one.      The design of the tent is intriguing with lots of ventilation especially for condensation; something you'll get a lot of in cool weather camping.  The floor plan is roomy and the big \\"D\\" doors are accessible from either front or back. The zippers and tieoffs are typically high-quality Eureka items.  The one area that this tent suffers, however, is that the \\"bathtub\\" floor is made of much lighter material than I'm used to seeing on the Eureka.  Don't get me wrong...it's waterproof but it's just about 50% lighter than all the past Eureka tents we owned.  Of course with a good ground cloth that's not going to be an issue.  Still, I would prefer to see a heavier, more typical Eureka quality bottom. The only reason it doesn't get five stars is due to this issue.  I am relieved, too, to see that Eureka has included a rain cover that includes a fly. For some time now Eureka has designed out a rain fly over the main door.....a mistake on their part, I think.  So, all in all, I would buy this tent again as its lightweight, easy to erect, and roomy.  It's not heavy duty, however, and will survive four or five seasons of moderate camping but the price reflects that.

review_body: Fantastic bag - really well thought-through.  I bought a large bag and it fits my really big laptop from work w/ portruding battery pack.  I liked the funky looks of the Crumpler bag better, but this bag is more functional.  This bag has become inseparable from me since I bought it!

product_title: Zero Degrees InnerCool 12 Can No Ice Folding Cooler, Black
review_body: I got my cooler almost 15 months at Walgreens.  I lucked out as they were doing a clearance on \\"summer\\" items in July and only paid $5.00 for it. What a deal.  To be honest I've never put it in my freezer due to lack of space. However it does keep food cold. On any given day the cooler portion of this will hold a container of soup or leftovers, 5 pieces of fruit, string cheese, a can of pop, a frozen bottle of water, another bottle of water and the cup of my tea mug. One of the side pockets holds my tea mug, the other pocket has a book. The zippered pocket holds my ipod, vitamins and other assorted stuff. I've taken this to the beach and using 1 frozen water bottle, kept cold 2 other waters, 2 pops, 2 sandwiches and assorted fruit. I would not hesitate to buy another one although I do agree with the reviews that not being able to choose the color is ridiculous.  Also the side pocket were not that useful until I hot glued some elastic straps around them. Now I can turn this puppy upside down and nothing falls out.

product_title: ICEtrekkers Shoe Diamond Grip (1 Pair)
review_headline: I should have gotten these years ago
review_body: I have a very steep driveway, with my house at the top.  After checking all the reviews, I decided on the Diamond Grip Icetrekkers as the best slip-on cleats.    Last week, I got to test them for the first time.  My driveway was a sheet of ice.  I got down into a crouch, and using my hands for balance, slid down the entire drive, barely stopping before I hit the street.  I then put on the ICEtrekkers.  Wow.  What an incredible difference. I was able to walk up and down the entire driveway as if it was bone dry.    They were easy to put on and take off, and I did not notice any slipping around my shoe.  I could not feel them shifting, even on the steepest part of the driveway, and they were low enough so that I did not feel \\"tippy\\" on them.  I was able to just walk normally.    These are now going to stay in my backpack until winter is over.  I do not want to be without these again.

product_title: I Renew Energized Well Being Health Bracelet Black
review_body: My grandfather has had Vertigo, Knee Replacements, and surgery on his neck. He is unable to walk without assistance for years now. He can walk super slow with his walker but I mean slow. I bought this for him and for the first time in 3 years he was able to slowly get around the house on his own without the walker. I have the other Irenew bracelet. I notice slight effects but not like his. I have always had poor blood circulation and got cold hands from the high caffeine intake. I have noticed they are warmer now. Not a big deal but it is something. The balance has increased too but once again not a big deal. I bought this for my grandfather not me.    For the price I say its worth it to the average person. If your like my grandfather its a priceless must own product.

product_title: Yaktrax Pro
review_body: These are great for slick, icy sidewalks. I put them on my shoes and walk right over sheets of ice that I normally would fall on or be clenching my teeth walking over. However, please beware: DO NOT go indoors and walk on any other surface but carpet with these. For some reason, they turn into ice skates on tile, wood, or vinyl floors! I took a dive in these after stepping onto some ceramic tile after being outside!

product_title: Therm-a-Rest Camp Seat
review_body: First and foremost, I love that this cushion is made in the USA. I really hate to purchase items made in China, and avoid doing so at every chance. Secondly, this cushion is very comfortable, and very adjustable. Different situations call for different amounts of air, and this is easily adjusted. It even works well when folded in half (I have a seat with a large \\"dip\\" in it that this fills perfectly when folded).I was surprised how large it is, though. The other Thermarest camp seats sounded like they might be too small for my use, but in actuality may have been better. I am planning on purchasing a smaller one as well, so that I will have all my bases covered.

product_title: Osprey FlapJack Pack
review_headline: Best commuter bag i've had yet.
review_body: I tried to find something I didnt like about this pack, but I think its one of the best packs I've owned to date.  It's perfect for commuting to work, school, library, or anyplace that your going to need quick access to your stuff without having to unzip a bunch of pockets and look for things.  It has one large main compartment, and a laptop compartment as well.         Space is not wasted if you dont use this pack for a laptop however.  The main compartment is further secured by a drawstring at the top, and when you put the flap down you can rest assured that everything is safely tucked away.       There are two pockets in the front of this pack, one secured by a small bit of velcro for easy access, and one zippered pocket, both are fairly deep and compliment this pack nicecly.  There is a zippered pocket to the side that is more suited for small flat rectangular things like a cellphone, checkbook, etc.       This pack stands up nicely when propped up against the wall or table leg, which is great.   The back of the pack has some ribbed ventilation for airflow, I couldnt say how well this works since my bike commutes are not all that far, but it rides comfortably even with a laptop and library books, with a change of clothes for work to boot.       As with all the Osprey packs i've owned, the stitching is superb and the pack is well made in general.  I thought about knocking my review down one star due to the lack of colors, but I think it would be an injustice.

product_title: Beyond Coastal Active Spf 34 Sunscreen
review_headline: Rubs in well. Slight smell as the only downside.
review_body: PROS:   *Rubs in really well, and doesn't leave you white unlike most \\"physical block\\" sunscreens. In fact, this rubbed in better than the other tube of regular \\"non-natural\\" sunscreen I used (Coppertone Water Babies, Pure & Simple).  *Not greasy, shiny, or heavy. Comfortable to have on my skin all day.  *Waterproof, as promised on the tube.  *Protected me well. I had no sunburns.  *Natural ingredients. No parabens etc. Good EWG ratings. Though note, this is still a chemical-block sunscreen, and not a physical block.     CONS:   *Stock up, because you'll have to use a little bit more of this sunscreen than your regular \\"non-natural\\" sunscreen, because this sunscreen is thicker. But note, thicker does not mean harder to rub in. This was much much easier to rub in for me! (See 1st bullet point.)  *Slight smell, which bothered my slightly but may not bother others. I don't know if it's the shea butter (which I don't like) or something else in the ingredient list. The smell stayed on my swimwear slightly too, until I finally came home from vacation and washed my swimsuit in the washing machine on gentle cycle.

review_body: We purchased two of these for xmas, they are great. The kids love them, and we have not any issues with them, and they have been ridden almost every day since Christmas.

product_title: Michelin Pro 3 Race Road Tire
review_body: After years of riding the Pro Race 2 on my Giant TCR C1 with Mavic Equipe and Elite wheels I decided to go  with the Pro race 3 on my Kestrel RT-800 and my Columbus steel cafe bike. Here's the skinny: there are no  grippy-er tires on the market. Rain or shine these are the best. The tread is very durable, in spite of the  stickiness, which is very cool.    However, the puncture resistance is poor. The sidewall strength is poor. I have had too many pinch flats going  through potholes in the city. I keep them pumped up above 110# to combat the flaws in our pavement here in SF  and get decent rolling resistance for my 170# weight (my top weight has been 178#). But I still get bead breaks  and pinch flats.    They are extremely light. This makes them fast in a race. However, the max pressure is only 116#'s which is low  for a race tire at this price point. My other wheels with Vittoria Diamante Pros, which go safely to 145#'s   offer less rolling resistance and have NEVER had a flat.    Since I no longer race I am changing tires to the Diamante Pro and the Ultremo DD.

product_title: Fenix TK35 High Performance 860 Lumen Flashlight
review_body:
I received my TK35 today and I was very excited. In the pictures it looks completely plastic (IMO) but to my surprise it was not. I put my 4 CR123A batteries into it and I turned it on and wow it was very bright. There was some smoke in the house which came from a cigarette (I don't smoke) and I decided to shine the light through it, and I seen a beautiful beam coming from this little monster, this was around 3:00PM so soon I will check it out in the dark since it is now 7:53PM. I spent plenty of time trying to decide on a light that I should get and I came across this and I said to myself \\"This is it\\".

The TK35 is a very durable feeling light, I have not yet dropped it and I don't plan to. The light comes with a lanyard, nylon holder, and a spare o-ring. It also comes in a very nice box. The light is has 2 buttons on the tail of the light. The big button is for turning the light on and off. If you just want temporary lighting you can just slightly press the button in and it will stay on as long as you are slightly pressing on the button. There is also a little button on the back which was a wonderful idea. Once you have the flashlight turned on you can press the little button to change brightness The brightness modes are low, medium, high, and turbo. You can also hold the little button and it will cycle between SOS and strobe. Another wonderful feature is the fact that it has a memory feature, and by that I mean if set your flashlights brightness to low then once you turn it off and back on it will still be on low.

Okay, I just decided to test it out while the dogs were outside in the back yard and I shined it at a house (Sorry!) and it lit the whole house up. The house is 2 stories but it looks like it could be a 3 story house. So, I went upstairs and grabbed my Maglite 4D LED because I wanted to compare, so I shined my maglite at the same house and it did not do bad, but it did not light up the whole house. I never thought that I would get into flashlights and spotlights but after being exposed to them and seeing what they could do I fell in love.

I really recommend the TK35 if you are on a tight budget. It's also a great if you want a flashlight that is fairly small but is a monster. This is my first 'real' flashlight, so I don't have much knowledge. I am trying not to turn flashlights into a hobby, because flashlights are not cheap but they are wonderful. This light is simply amazing, well worth my money. It also got here pretty quick.and spotlights but after being exposed to them and seeing what they could do I fell in love. I really recommend the TK35 if you are on a tight budget. It's also a great if you want a flashlight that is fairly small but is a monster. This is my first 'real' flashlight, so I don't have much knowledge. I am trying not to turn flashlights into a hobby, because flashlights are not cheap but they are wonderful. This light is simply amazing, well worth my money. It also got here pretty quick.

product_title: Diamondback Serene Women's Comfort Bike (26-Inch Wheels)
review_body: This is a great bike for tooling around the neighborhood. I live in the country and ride this bike on the irrigation ditch roads, gravel roads and pavement. The seat is VERY comfortable. The smooth shifting 21 speeds make this bike a joy to ride. I did have to take it to a bike shop to complete assembly...I couldn't figure out how to release the brakes to fit the front wheel on. Very well built and sturdy. I did order a kickstand from Amazon at the same time as the bike does not comeMy dog LOVES to go on bike rides:)

product_title: CamelBak 0.75- Liter Stainless Steel Better Bottle
review_headline: If I could give 6 stars I would
review_body: I use this every morning for iced coffee then put water in it later in the day.  I have a cover that keeps condensation from dripping all over everything so I didn't care about the design.  Only once in a while does it leak, I think it's when I have over filled it.  I have a large cup holder in my car which fits this perfectly.  I absolutely love this bottle and have piece of mind knowing I'm not adding to the landfill with disposable cups and that there aren't any health side effects from stainless steel.

product_title: Wenzel Stocking Foot Waders
review_body: I ordered these to wear while retrieving my boat at the ramp. I thought they were of good quality and originally rated them 5 stars after using them a couple times with no problems. Upon using them a third time, I noticed that the foot-area seams had split open and allowed water to enter. I checked the seams after that use and they separated just by placing your feet in them. Other areas are also separating and not worth the repair cost. You get what you pay for, don't waste your money unless you only need them for a one or two time project.

product_title: Liberty Mountain Winter Sports Helmet
review_body: Have used this helmet 5 full days of snowboarding. After many falls, this helmet is still holding up perfectly. Very comfortable, keeps you warm, I would highly recommend it.   Everything is great, straps are easy, very breathable... Buy it!

product_title: BioGreen Biodegradable BPA-Free Sport Bottle with Wide Mouth DuoFlow Lid (26-Ounce)
review_body: I LOVE this water bottle. Decided to add it to my last purchase to qualify my price for super saver free shipping and was very pleased with the quality of this bottle. The wide mouth duoflow lid is GREAT and very easy to use while running on the treadmill or on the eliptical. GREAT BUY!

product_title: thirtytwo Women's Lashed Fasttrack Snowboarding Boot
review_body: My boots just arrived.  They are even better than i expected. They are really light, super comfy and your foot goes in and out really easy.  Has a good comfy calf fit that isn't hard like soom boots if you lean back. The only negitive- if there has to be one is that they are a tiny bit small. I am a 7.5, ordered a 7.5 and when standing up my toe only just scuffs the end. If i am bending my leg like going down the mountain it is fine. I got the green. Its an awesome aqua like colour. Enjoy!

product_title: Jansport Trinity Backpack
review_body: I have owned this backpack for more than four months and it holds my 15inch laptop, 3 inch binder and plenty of small (reader's digest sized) books with room available for more supplies. The color (I purchased the pink/white) is exactly how it appears in the picture. I estimate the pack will last through all four years of college.

product_title: Leki Rubber Fitness Walking Tip
review_body: I've got about 20 miles on these tips now and I love them. They are very quiet on concrete and have a very nice grip on most concrete/asphalt surfaces. I do not have Leki poles. They fit perfectly on my Yukon poles that came with my snow shows I purchased from Costco. The angle on the tread is perfect. Helps hold your grip even when your pole is at a very low angle. This has taken my power walking to a new level. I go much faster and burn more calories per minute. A really great add to my work out. They are easily removed when you need to go back to the steel tips or put on a snow basket. Nice work Leki! I recommend these if you do any pole walking on concrete or asphalt. They look like they're going to hold up really well. I used Prime second day free shipping. Bam! They're here!

product_title: Snow Rage 48" Snow Blaster
review_body: These tubes are awesome!!! Very fast cushioned ride. The fastest is to ride 2 people on it, especially if they lay on top of each other on the tube face down.

product_title: Mighty Alloy MTB Pedal (Pack of 2)
review_body: I ride my bike daily here in Iraq, and these pedals have lasted me for over 8 months, and are still going.  I broke the old pair of plastic ones by smashing them in the side of a wall, but I've hit them in to walls, smashed against the ground, and even fell right on them and they're still going strong.  Great Product!

product_title: Yakima SKS Lock Keys & Cores
review_body: Trust me, having one key for a set of 8 lock cores is helpful. I use this on my Q-towers, Raptor bike racks, and Big Stack kayak rack.

product_title: Smartwool Women's Secret Sleuth Socks
review_body: Got these for a gift for my daughter who is always cold but doesn't bundle up.  These are perfect!

product_title: Rio Brands WWWC5-4670 Wonder Wheeler Plus
review_body: We used this for the first time when went to the beach on 9/25/2010.  It is ok to assemble except for a problem inserting a bar because a couple holes did not line up. Glad I had someone strong around because I couldn't assemble it.     All that aside, this is wonderful!  We had 2 kids & 3 adults and this carried everything, except for the kids of course!  We had a HUGE 9' wide beach umbrella, towels to sit on, waterproof mats for under the towels, towels to dry off with and assorted beach toys.  It held all of that plus some minor odds and ends.  It is light weight and easy to fold for storage.  Wish I knew about this years ago.

product_title: U.S. Divers Diva Women Snorkeling Set, Ladies Silicone Mask, Trek Travel Fins, Dry Top Snorkel + Gear Bag
review_body: I got these as a gift for an upcoming vacation. After looking at rental prices, it made sense to get a snorkle set of my own. It doesn't hurt to know that no one else has shared your snorkle too. If I lived near the ocean I'd spring for a higher quality set but this is perfect for my intermittant needs. I love the hot pink and everything was in good space on arrival.

product_title: Cadillac Escalade Freestyle Bike (20-Inch Wheels)
review_headline: Also had a fork that was too narrow and had to be returned
review_body: I bought this bike to donate to a benefit for a sick child in our neighborhood, and so when it was delivered we left it until 2 weeks from the benefit to assemble, hoping to keep it shiny and new until delivery.  Unfortunately, like the case of another reviewer, we found that the front fork was too narrow for installation of the wheel, and it was missing a kick stand and a set of pegs.    I immediately wrote to Amazon, as out return window (30 days post receipt) expired 2 weeks before, asking them to allow us to return it and also asking them to ship us another right away so that we could make our deadline.  The other reviewer seemed to have had better luck than we did.  They did make an exception to the return policy, but my only option for replacement was to order another bike and pay for expedited shipping, which I have done.    The order process did not include a way to ask them to check the fork before they ship, and to inspect to make sure all the part were there.  I did write back to customer service asking them to forward the request to anyone that could help, because if it happened a 2nd time (as it did with the other reviewer), we would have no time left to deal with this before the benefit.    Before re-ordering we did call the manufacturer to see if we could deal directly with them, but apparently this is a discontinued model, and they have no parts to send us.      I am hoping that everything comes in this shipment, and am expecting the quality to be that described by the other customers.  But I think it's important to let other people know that this bike seems to have inventory problems inside Amazon, and it is no longer has manufacturer support.  And also - if you order one - open and inspect immediately as sports equipment is limited to a 30 day return window.    The bike did have strong parts, and looked very nice when we tried to assemble.  But since you can't use it without a wheel, 3 stars is the best I can do.

product_title: Nite Ize Flashflight LED Light Up Flying Disc, Glow in the Dark for Night Games, 185g
review_body: It's not for frisbee golf, but good for ultimate frisbee. If you're like me and play well into the evening, this would be worthwhile to have to extend the game. Flies well.

product_title: Mountain Khakis Men's Alpine Utility Short Relaxed Fit
review_body: By far the most versatile pair of shorts I own!  I work in a warehouse, and the utility pocket has proven helpful for holding several things (box cutter, cellphone, pens, etc).  But I can also wear these great fitting shorts to the beach, on the river, or while I'm remodeling my house. Simply put....I can, and will, wear these everywhere!  Great job Mountain Khakis!

product_title: Lafuma Extreme 600 Synthetic Sleeping Bag, Right Zip
review_body: I was very impressed with the compactness and weight of this bag when I first opened the package.  However, I found out you will not be warm in this bag.  I tried it out at home in a 65 degree room and was cold all night.  I was wearing a t-shirt and pajama pants and freezing, I was not warm until I put a sweatshirt and socks on.  This bag should be ok in cooler temps if you dress warm while sleeping.      Positives:  Very light and compact.    Negatives: Will not keep you warm.

product_title: Coleman StormBeam Dynamo Deluxe Flashlight With Radio and Cellphone Charger
review_body: I bought this flashlight for those occasions when my apt. complex loses power or the surrounding area does.  It fits comfortably in my left hand, and it's very easy to crank with my right. This is important to me because I have rheumatoid arhtritis, so ease and comfort of use is essential, and I would recommend it for anyone with mild to moderate problems with their hands.  The radio is quite good, drawing in many stations, which I didn't expect.  I thought local stations would come in~~and that's all I hoped for~~but it's good receiving the news from other locales as well, especially during violent storms.  My only criticism is that the charger doesn't fit my phone because it's a flat connection.  There are several kinds of round connections, and I wish there were more than one type of the flat connector as well. Since I couldn't test its use for my cell phone, I can't make any remarks about how well this function works. The flashlight and/or radio hold a charge for quite a while, and if the light or reception runs low, it's very easy to give it a few cranks to return to bright light and good reception.  I already had a small crank flashlight in my car, so now I'm glad to have one handy for the house for those unpredictal power outages.  This device is easy to use, reliable, and convenient, and the price is very reasonable. I highly recommend it, with the caveat about the cell phone charger.

product_title: Dakine Flip Flop Beanie
review_body: This wonderfully crafted, reversible beanie is versatile enough to be an comfy everyday beanie, and warm enough to take on a snowboarding/skiing trip. It's very thick, soft and still breathable. Great buy.

product_title: Super Bright XT Flashlight
review_body: Looking at the discreption of the item, it appears that it will charge an iphone and all other cell phones. However, that is not the case. Perhaps it is iphone specific, but a mesage appears that said charging is not supported by this device. It may very well charge other phones perfectly, but since I bought it for an iphone, it will not serve it's intended purpose. I can only assume that other smart phones will have the same results. Maybe it is the fluctuation in DC current from the servo? Regardless, it is a neat idea but will not work on iphones.

product_title: Bell Emergency Quick Bike Tool
review_body: I'm not handy and I get my bike worked on by folks who know what they're doing, but carrying this has come in handy a few times on rides. I bought it a few years ago and it's held up well.

product_title: ExOfficio Men's Give-N-Go Flyless Brief
review_body: Good materials and workmanship.  A bit pricey.  Tried out the Sport Brief cut and found it too be a little too tight for my tastes.  The brief itself is well stitched throughout,  The material is light and comfortable and it does dry quickly.  The only con was I found the Sport Brief cut is not for me.

product_title: Timbuk2 Commute 2.0 Laptop Messenger Bag
review_headline: It isn't good as a laptop bag
review_body: I got this bag today and found that the laptop compartment's layers are so thin. I do not feel secure to put my laptop into the compartment at all. I ordered small size though, so I don't know if it is just for the small size.

product_title: Zippo Butane Fueled Lighter, High Polish Chrome
review_body: When the Zippo arrived there was quite a bit of manufacturing debris inside and the seals were dry and stiff. Thought of returning it but after cleaning and using it for a few days it seems somewhat better, though not what I was expecting. I wanted a piece of American craftsmanship. It's a good lighter for the price. Kind of like a Chevy Nova in that it's cheap and doesn't work all that well. Uses a good amount of fuel too. The fuel window is imposable to see in any light. No intention of ever buying another. There are much better lighters to be had that are cheaper, more reliable and better built.

product_title: Topeak Red Lite 4-LED Ultra-Bright Rear Bicycle Light
review_body: i can't say too much for it's water resistance.. i was doing a 30mi ride in a very light drizzle, and by the time i got home, i realised that the light was on, and it could not be switched off. taking it apart, i noticed that the batteries were a little wet from the road spray.    i think my light is gone..

product_title: Coleman 2000016462 Camp Oven, 13.5 x 12.9 x 3.3 Inch
review_headline: Bought my over at a yardsale the rack was missing but...
review_body:
You can watch my test of my oven on you tube same name cdltpx. Video is named \\"coleman oven test\\" you can search using that title. I am really frugal got my oven at a yardsale is had never been used well today I tested it(after letting it sit for years) found that the oven is lacking its rack (GOT IT USED FROM YARD SALE $5 NO PROBLEM) but I found something to work and got on with the test. Grands biscuts in my home preheated electric oven it takes exactly 14 min cook time from when I toss them in.
With the coleman oven 4 biscuts the cook time was more in range 15 min so I have to say this is nearly as good as a home oven and that is impressive in my book for such a low cost portable oven.When it gets in your temp range it holds that temp very well. Now this thing is not air tight it leaks all over the place but that is the design and it works have some foil on hand to plug some holes to assist in temp control I give it a A- my home oven gets an A plus.

product_title: Horny Toad Women's Oblique-V Long Sleeve Top
review_headline: Horny Toad Womens's Oblique-V Long Sleeve Top
review_body:
Shopping experience:
Great item but probably better to buy it elsewhere than Amazon. I purchased it for $25 less on another website. By the way, Google shopping search is limited and will NOT show you the better sellers. You have to just search website by website.

Item review:
I don't know why they chose a name like Horny Toad but whatever, at least the logo isn't plastered anywhere on this top. I purchased both olive and gray. I tried the deep blue but it was disappointingly dark, more like navy rather than the brighter, richer hue as photographed.

The colors are not plain, dead-end solid colors though: There's a barely perceivable pattern but the effect is extremely subtle and uniform. It's a wonderful soft fabric with a nice drape. Thin but not too thin nor sheer. The style can pass for business casual. The sleeves are generously long. Online the color looked like a rich, bright green but in person it's nicer, earthier, more like the olive description, truly a lovely color. The modesty panel is a great design and balances the open neckline. Like wrap dresses and V-necks, this is very flattering to busty ladies but it will probably look good on any type.

product_title: MSR Alpine Stowaway Pot
review_headline: Perfect Large Pot for Camping or Backpacking
review_body: This is a LARGE pot for a pack so it is not one for a single person.  It's better suited to two or more people that are splitting up and sharing cook gear and cook wear.  I've only boiled water in it so I can't speak to how easy it is to clean.  But I can speak to the fact that the handle stays cool and the lid fits quite nicely.  It's a good all around pot.  As I said, I'm not a big fan of cleaning messes in the field so I use it to heat water for dried food but if I had to guess I'd say it would clean with about the same effort as a trational piece of stainless cook wear.

product_title: 9 Series Snowshoe Kit - Men's by Atlas Snowshoe
review_body: I have been looking around for a while for a good pair of snow shoes that wouldn't destroy my wallet. These shoes are great. They arrived promptly anbd in great condition. Thank you

product_title: Go-Ped City Sport Gas Powered Cruising Scooter (Red)
review_headline: Should not buy, look at another scooter.
review_body: First pull and pull start breaks.  Then notice there are no returns on this item. Being stuck with the scooter we used what they referred to as a \\"bump start\\".  Essentially running down the road pushing until the engine starts.  Actually solid engine and frame, but the big catch is there is stationary while the engine is running.  Either you are moving forward or the engine is off.  There is no idle.  The minute the engine starts the back wheel takes off.  Whether you were using the pull start or a bump start the immediate take off is rediculous.  I am stuck with the scooter now and will still need to get another scooter that my son would actually use.

product_title: Sigma BC 1009 Bicycle Speedometer
review_body: I have had this only a month so far, so I can't give it more than 4 stars.  Easy to read while biking and it was relatively easy to set up.  I like that it comes with elastic bands for a temporary setup and then you can make it permanent with the black plastic ties, after you have ridden with it a few times and positioned to your liking.    I'm just getting into biking, so I can't give all the technical reasons why this is a good computer, but I decided to go with a wired computer instead of wireless after reading several reviews about problems with wireless computers.  The installation of the wired pickup was easy and now I have one less battery to replace.

product_title: Outdoor Research Snoqualmie Sombrero Rain Hat
review_body:
Ill make this short and sweet. If your looking for a rain hat then get a Seattle Sombrero and if your looking for a rain hat for colder conditions then get the Snoqualmie, period. The Snoqualmie is basically a Seattle Sombrero with ear flaps. Not only are they extremely comfortable, they are also practically indestructible. I purchased my first Seattle Sombrero back in the early 90's and my first Snoqualmie back in 2002 and I still have both and they are still in great shape. You can literally crumble these up into a ball and shove them in your pocket. That is because they are basically made of nothing but Gor-Tex and a soft liner. You can roll it up, crumble it up, bend it any way you want and it will immediately go right back to its original form. Of course all of this would be meaningless if it didn't keep you dry and fortunately these things perform flawlessly in this regard. Whether your out in a downpour or whitewater rafting, if you have a Seattle Sombrero on your head then your head is going to stay dry. If you have a Snoqualmie on your head then your head is going to stay warm and dry. The rope assures it wont fall of your head when you need them the most. I have used them storm chasing in 60 mile per hour winds and so long as the rope is tightened, this hat isn't going anywhere. The Seattle Sombrero is the model that the entire industry tries to mimic and its really what put Outdoor Research on the map in regards to outdoor equipment. Its basically legendary in the outdoor equipment world. The Snoqualmie is the latest iteration of that design.

The bottom line - There simply is no substitute for these hats. If you want the best then the Seattle Sombrero and the Snoqualmie are what your looking for.

5 Stars and then some!

product_title: Kelty Beat Backpack
review_body: This backpack is the best school/college backpack I've ever owned or seen used by friends, and I got it for under $60. Best feature - the chest and hip straps to help balance the weight, the wicking material on the back, and the expandable front open pocket with the snap straps that can cinch all your contents very tightly. A comparable Jansport would probably be well over $100.     Like most reviews, though I love it and would buy it again I'll probably spend most of my time talking about what I don't like... but don't let that fool you, I do really like the bag! These are quibbles mostly, though if Kelty is out there listening, I hope they solve some of these tiny issues.    I love the roomy interior with the divided pockets that are very versatile (more like thin dividers than actual compartments, so they don't force you to use them or waste space), and the padded spot for the laptop - I have a 13\\" MacBook in a sleevecase (from WaterField - BEST sleevecase ever by the way, go check them out at [...]) and it fits really snugly in the padded spot, so if you have a large laptop it may not work out for you. I regularly haul a large textbook, binder, and a few notebooks in that back compartment, there is a little space left. Personally though I think the size is just right for what it is, a daypack.    The large front section is well utilized and fits most everything I've wanted to put in there. The expandable front open \\"pocket\\" is only useful if you don't have the rest of the pack crammed full, but it works for me to put my work shoes in there for the commute in snow boots. The outside of that pocket has a very thin pocket that doesn't hold much more than a travel pack of wet wipes (good use of the space IMO :) - wish that it had carabiner loops on it, then it would be more useful.    The very top media pocket is nice, but can get annoyingly in the way when you are trying to get at the inner padded pocket - I think the media pocket should perhaps have been smaller,however, I can't complain too much because I like being able to put a lot of items that I need frequently in there. I do wish there were two zipper pulls on it so that one could \\"lock\\" it more securely with a carabiner or something... kind of risky having your iPod so accessible to the world behind you like that.    Anyway, great pack and highly recommend it!

product_title: Malone Auto Racks Universal Car Roof Rack
review_body: Purchased to fit my 2009 Murano roof rails. They fit securely and are generally esy to install in concert with my kayak carrier by the same manufacturer. Pricing and shipping was satisfactory and the cross rails are easy to install/remove with my kayak trips. Only issue but not a deal breaker is noise from wind resistence,

product_title: Columbia 50 Can High Performance Rolling Cooler
review_body: Cooler does exactly as described.  We have not owned this very long.  We have used this cooler once on a 3-day trip.  Number one concern is of course \\"leakage\\" and this one doesn't leak.  We filled the cooler with ice daily but at the end of the day there was still ice remaining.  We placed the cooler in the back seat of the car, then it went inside the hotel room at our destination.  The weather was not overly hot as the high was in the 70's but the important thing is that it didn't leak.  A plus for us is that the cooler folds pretty compact for storage when not in use.  It has velcro tabs on the sides (near bottom) that keep the cooler folded flat after you compact it down.  And when driving on a road trip it's convenient to just reach thru the small opening on the top to grab a bottled water. (Don't have to unzip the whole top).

product_title: Petzl Zipka Plus 4-LED Headlamp
review_body: This light is great.  I decided to get one after a three day hike with a friend and his wife.  She wore it on her wrist in her sleeping bag.  No need to hunt for a light for that midnight bathroom break.  I've used mine down to 24 below zero with no problems.  It fits nicely over a stocking hat.  Excellent for tying on hooks in a dark ice house.

product_title: Flexible Flyer Snowball Maker, colors may vary
review_body: These are really fun and work great at making the perfect snowball.  The plastic is thick and sturdy--well worth the $$.

product_title: Advanced Elements 2.5 Gallon Summer Shower / Solar Shower
review_body: Worked well, and quicker than my other shower.  Liked the small size easier to carry than the other large one I had.

product_title: c-sport fortress front panier set
review_body: I purchased a pair of SunLite's C-Sport Fortress Front Panniers. They're good build quality, but the hardware wouldn't hold the panniers onto the rack. Even with bungee cords, the hooks would let go over pretty small bumps. Obviously, a simple locking hook would solve this problem.    After contacting SunLite's customer service, I was given the run-around. They refused to address the issue, offering only to let me return it to them at my expense. They said they would fix it if it was a warranty issue, but offered no hope that they would address the obvious design flaw. If they saw nothing wrong with it, they would simply return the unusable bags back to me.    I love to give glowing reviews, but I simply can't recommend a company that hides from responsibility like that. I just want to try to save others from wasting their money on a potentially poor purchase from a company that clearly doesn't value service, or their products.

product_title: Block Wrap-Rax Deluxe Single Soft Rack
review_body: Great buy!! Easy to put on vehicle, super strong staps to hold your board down while traveling. Ridiculously inexpensive and extemely portable......smaller than a backpack. Best way to get from home to the beach and back without ruining your pricey board

product_title: Guide Gear Twin Air Bed Fitted Cover/Sleeping Bag
review_headline: Great idea, not so well thought out
review_body: I loved the idea of getting into a real bed at the end of long day of hiking and whatnot.  The fabric is very nice and lightweight for muggy evenings and unlike many other sleeping bags is soft and smooth without being slippery. Unfortunately, there is not enough slack between the zippers to sleep really comfortably.  I put it on a high twin inflatable mattress just as pictured but it was obvious that there was not going to be enough room between the zippers. I had to unzip it in order to turn over and sleep on my side and that left a severe breeze since it wouldn't cover me. I ultimately had to go to  the car and get an extra blanket just to keep the draft off.  You might be thinking to yourself that I'm a big girl and thus the sleeping bag isn't the problem, but I'm 5'6'', 140lbs. I defy a larger woman or a man to sleep in this bag comfortably. Its unfortunate because its a great idea and aside from the size issue a great product.

product_title: Reliance Products Double Doodie Plus Large Toilet Waste Bags (6-Pack)
review_body: I always have 5gal. clorene buckets,so I use the waste bags when camping they are leak proof and very handy.Also use cat litter to soak up the liquid.

product_title: Paricon Lightning Sled
review_body: The sleds are reliable and durable.  Bought them for my extremely tall 11 year old nephew.  They have taken a beating so far and have been a value.  They are made of heavy duty plastic.  Throw in 3 for a decent price and it's a great deal!

product_title: Sigma Micro Front and Rear Light Set
review_body: these lil bad-ass are the best! ive been looking for something small, bright and stylist and this is it! plus when i saw how much it is, you definitely cant beat the price! i have a fixie bike, i like my bike simple and clean no accessories dangling too much of it and these lights are perfect as u barely notice them on my bike but once you turn them on WOW BLINDING AWESOME! LOVE IT!

product_title: Hot Headz No-Slip Ice Cleats
review_body: Strong grip, fits shoe well.  However, a little difficult to put on without the use of two hands.   Great for use on sloped driveways, slick parking lots.

product_title: Coleman 2000020931 1-Burner Low-Profile Stove
review_body: I love this stove! I bought it for a camping trip and it worked great. Easy to set up, easy to use and easy to clean up. The little propane tanks last for a long time too. I would definitely recommend this stove to others.

product_title: BONFIRE Men's Baker Jacket Ski & Snowboard Jacket
review_body: Nice design, good quality construction...great look..but runs lager in sizes. While I might wear a large in a winter coat...this jacket swallowed me up in large!

product_title: Pearl iZUMi Men's Elite Cycling Short
review_body: Disclaimer:  This is my first pair of PI Elite shorts.  I've primarily used the (less expensive) \\"Attack\\" shorts.      I agree with some of the other reviews that talk about the \\"fit\\" of other PI shorts verses these.  I've ridden with PI shorts exclusively since 2004.  The fit is just doesn't seem right for me and some of the new features just don't cut it.    The good:  Really great padding (felt like I was elevated a few inches on the seat too); sorry, that's it.    The not so good:  The fit in the waist seems especially wrong.  Slightly low and to tight (I'm a relatively skinny guy - 32\\") and the mediums were way tight;  They've added a draw string in the waist - Wha?;  If you like extreme \\"compression\\" on your privates, you may like these;  \\"Mamel Toe\\", as a previous review mentioned, was the first thing my wife mention when she saw me in them.  I really don't need that.  I would have prefered \\"you look fat\\".    Mine are new (only two rides) so maybe they'll loosen up (or maybe I'll be asking for an exchange).  Or maybe I'll just revert back to the \\"Attack\\" style and save a few bucks.

product_title: Topeak JoeBlow Max II Floor Bike Pump
review_body: Bought one of these a few months ago and it's been hanging in the garage waiting for me to need to use it. Due to an injury I have not been riding my bike.    So today I *try* to use it for the first time. The stupid plastic screw-on ring on the Schrader side of the valve broke as I was operating the locking lever. Of course all the air was let out of my tire by the time!    Don't buy! Total junk! This plastic valve is a weak link in what seems to be an otherwise OK pump design.    I submitted a ticket with the manufacturer. Depending on how they respond, I will update my rating.

product_title: Heat Factory Foot Warmers, Box of 40 Pairs
review_body: purchase of this item was a mistake. I had been given some free samples of stickon toe warmers which was what I thought I was purchasing from Amazon. I will use up the the toe warmers I purchased but will not order them again.Also they did not hold heat for six hours as advertised.

product_title: Esbit Coffee Press/Mug
review_body: It is fair to middlin.  Washed it in the dishwasher once and half the paint came off.  Not really impressed with it.

product_title: MAXSA Innovations 20062 AC/DC Rechargeable Luxeon K2 LED Flashlight
review_body:
When I received this product I wrote the following review. \\"I do not have any affiliation with Amazon or one of its competitors. product_title: Suisse Sport Yosemite Tent
review_headline: Fine once up but getting it up ..
review_body: Manufacturers in general would be well advised, having created assembly instructions, to have someone unfamiliar with the product to try to assemble it just following the instructions. Following the instructions I was able to assemble the main part of the tent but with difficulty. The instructions were there just not clear. Assembling and attaching the rainfly that protects you from rain was another matter. Just relying on the instructions you plain do not have enough information. review_body:

product_title: Basil Tour XL Double Bicycle Bag (Black/Silver)
review_body: Having just bought this based on various pictures and no tangible reviews, aside from \\"Basil is a good brand\\" on various bicycling forums, I have to say I'm somewhat disappointed.  There are a few issues with this item.      First, the bags are attached to each other, this I knew.  However, what I didn't have any way to tell is that the spacing between them is about 3\\" more wide than the width of my fairly standard rack.  There is no way to shorten this distance, short of physically modifying the bags, which I'm able, but not willing, to do.  As such, the bags hang over the sides of the rack a good bit, causing them to tip out toward the sides and pushing the bottom of the     Secondly, the bags attach with straps and a cinch-style fastener, like the type found on the bottom of back-pack straps. The lower attachment point attaches with only a strip of velcro, rather than bungies and a hook, which makes it a pain to attach.  I'd either be ok with a semi-permanent, but rock-solid attachment system, or a less-solid, but easily removable one.  This bag had neither.    Lastly, the buckles used to hold the top closed are made from a very thin, very soft plastic.  Within the first trip to the store, loaded with a gallon of milk on one side and a few random, light items, and a bag of flour on the other with more random, light items, the clasp cracked when buckling the top closed.  I don't know if it was previously cracked or not, but it is certainly very thin and flimsy plastic.  I'd hardly think less than 20lbs per side should be an issue, seeing as the volume of these bags is quite large, 15-30lbs per side is a reasonable guess for the amount of weight they should be able to carry safely, otherwise you'd have to leave them mostly empty to avoid putting more than a few pounds in each side.    I bought this item to carry small amounts of groceries home, and it is not at all suited for such tasks.  Being unable to easily remove it, combined with it not at all fitting the topwidth of a fairly standard rack make this item sub-par.  I'm not sure what would be an ideal usage for it, but anything that involves loading more than 2-5lbs per side will lead to frustration, as will trying to mount it on a standard sized rack w/o heavy modification, or buying a hard-to-find European style rack with a much wider top.    For those looking for a grocery-getting, this is the best I've found so far: [[ASIN:B000YO7LTK Basil Cardiff Rear Basket, Black]].  Slides on, slides off, take it right in the store, load it up (and know when you run out of room easier), then take it right into the kitchen when you get home.  Will post a review of said item when I get it in, but I'm quite sure it will be vastly superior for getting groceries.

product_title: SteriPen Emergency Online Pack
review_body:
I've had my SteriPEN Emergency UV Water Purifier for a few months and used it this past summer on 2 camping trips. I still packed enough water at our campsite for the weekend and carried the SteriPEN for emergencies but I made it a point to test the purifier out on a few liters of water.

There's a lot to like about the SteriPEN. First it's lightweight and even though it's about 8\\" long, can easily fit into a pack. The purifier uses 2 'AA' lithium batteries which have a long life and can purify around 90-100 liters of water before needing a charge or replacement. Additionally, using UV purification doesn't add an unpleasant taste to water like iodine tablets do or chemical purification can. UV purification is also more effective in cooler temps than the chemical alternatives. The SteriPEN works automatically - you switch the unit on and it begins emitting UV light immediately and shuts off when finished. All told it takes about 1 minute to purify a typical 16oz bottle of water.

The SteriPEN does have limitations inherit to UV purification. First, you need to use relatively clear water (the water used should be as free of particulate matter as possible) for UV purification to be effective. Also, my understanding is that with UV purification you'll want to consume the purified water soon after treatment or treat the water again if it has been sitting for an extended period.

As a long-term solution boiling water is still the better option but not always possible. All told the SteriPEN is a helpful product that is best suited for emergency situations when you have no easy access to potable water.

product_title: Selle Italia Saddle SLR T-1 Triathlon 04
review_body:
I have tried MANY high dollar seats but have not been happy with any of them and always ended up back on my factory Bontraeger seat. I need a saddle that is fairly flat, not raised or rounded like the Fizik's are. Even their \\"tri\\" saddle was too rounded and got very uncomfortable after about 2-3 hours of riding.

I was doing some searching and found the new SLR T1 Model from Selle Italia, and based on the pictures and descriptions, I figured I'd give it a shot. I got it within a few days and loved it instantly! It is fairly light, super flat, and has a slightly wider nose then most seats out there, so it's not putting any unwanted pressure anywhere and even has a slight indention to help with that. I have put several hundred miles on it in the last month and a half, have had no numbness and have been very happy! It has a bit of gel throughout the seat and in the nose, so that it gives just enough, yet is firm and stable for hard seated efforts. It is great for short and long rides, male or female.

product_title: Steripen Adventurer Opti Retail Pack
review_headline: Excellent Product, but requires CR123 batteries
review_body: I bought this on sale, and overall I am very happy with it.  I own a SteriPEN Classic, and decided I needed a second unit.  Plus this one can serve as a flashlight as well.      I am slightly discontented because the SteriPEN Adventurer Opti requires CR123 batteries.  Well, to be precise, I am unhappy because I learned it requires CR123 when I got home and after I opened the blister pack.  I double checked the packaging, and sure enough the back of the package does mention that it takes CR123, but it is not advertised at all prominently.      I bought this product more for emergency preparedness than for ultralight weight camping.  I have lots of AA and AAA batteries in reserve, but I do not tend to stockpile CR123.  You can't find 100 packs of CR123 on sale.  Well, who knows, maybe if I looked...    I'm going to keep the unit, even though it takes CR123.  BackPacker magazine has done a serious amount of field testing of the unit, and they report that it holds up perfectly to all of the field conditions they have subjected it to.      Net-net, it's a superb sterilizer.  It can act as a flashlight.  And it is very lightweight.  I have to pack extra CR123 for my SureFire flashlight anyway.  I won't go into \\"why CR123?\\" for field applications.  They have lots of specific benefits for backpacking and other 'away' activities.      So my SteriPEN Classic is now primarily for emergency preparedness.  Ready to sterilize water in the event of hurricanes, floods, and any other disaster that makes public water unavailable or of dubious quality.

product_title: Hillsound Cypress 6 Crampons
review_body: April, 2011: I only tried it once so far at the Adirondacks but it feels it's just as good as those heavy duty expensive crampons.  They are easier to carry on the outside of the pack and they come with a little \\"pouch\\" so you can put them inside your pack (I don't because they become icy and muddy at this time of the year).  They obviously don't have the front teeth so it's not really \\"ice climbing gear\\" but if you just want to get to the peaks of the Adirondacks without climbing technical ice, then those are more than adequate.  The \\"tightening mechanism\\" is awesome too as it takes literally a few seconds to tighten.  I saw that the same company made a \\"full size\\" crampons with the same tightening mechanism so if these are still \\"standing\\" next fall, I will get those crampons for next winter.  Update: Dec. 22, 2011  After using these again earlier this week in the mountains, I noticed that they formed some snow balls on wet snow even with the anti-balling pad - the snowballs were not difficult to get rid of: a good kick on the rocks did it but it was still something to be careful of as it could be dangerous if gone unnoticed on steep hills. I ordered [[ASIN:B005OFFL7S Hillsound Trail Pro Crampons]] for steeper climbing or technical ice however I still like to carry these as they are so compact.  The ratchet buckle bindings on both is what \\"sold\\" them to me as it makes the tightening and releasing so much easier than [[ASIN:B000T26OMC G10 New Classic Wide by Grivel]] with the \\"traditional\\" binding - in the freezing mountains it's really difficult to tighten the crampons with those \\"strings\\". For years every time I tried to do it, my hands would be frozen and last week although it was -20 at above 4000 ft I didn't even need to take my hands out of the gloves to tighten my [[ASIN:B004BN97IS Hillsound Cypress 6 Crampons]] as it was so easy. :)

product_title: LotFancy® New 36V 1.5A 1500mA Electric Bike Motor Scooter Battery Charger Power Supply Adapter For Rad2Go Sunbird (older models)
review_headline: 36 Volt EBike / Scooter Charger better than original
review_body: After blowing up a couple of chargers in the past due to shorting the output of those chargers, this model simply resets itself immediately.

product_title: Kryptonite Keeper 880 Chain & Padlock
review_body: This item arrived super promptly and is as sturdy as I was hoping. Problem is the lock is really tricky to use, I'm afraid of how long it'll take me to get used to it!

product_title: HotHands Hand Warmers
review_body: My husband works in a freezer and the temps are -30.  This brand is the only one that holds up to those temps.  I have ordered other brands in the past only to be disappointed.  We order a box of each, foot and hand warmers every month,  and the quality has always been consistent.

product_title: Coleman 3AA High-Tech LED Mini Lantern
review_body: This is a great little lantern, but I do stress LITTLE. It's pretty bright and the brightness level is adjustable. It was well worth the money.

product_title: Pedco UltraClamp Assembly Camera Mount Accessory for Cameras, Scopes, and Binoculars
review_headline: Got this to troubleshoot my shooting
review_body: Solid, strong assembly.  Very happy with the construction and quality.    Clamped to the stock of my rifle, removed the arm and set screw, screwed the video camera on the base mount, and it lines up beautifully with my scope eyepiece.  To keep the camera from moving I'll use a small rubber shim between the camera and mount.    Very happy with the purchase.  Wish hitting the bullseye was as easy.

product_title: Beyond Coastal Active Spf 34 Sunscreen
review_body: As a conscientious mother to a very active toddler, I have tried many different sunscreens, basically by picking from the EWG's recommendations [...]. The Beyond Coastal is our favorite so far! It absorbes better and is less greasy than some of the other brands. California Baby was our favorite before we found this, but that one is hard to rub in and leaves what I call a \\"moon glow\\" look - the minerals make the skin look a little purple-y, which doesn't matter so much for a kid, but I felt a little odd as an adult. Literally my only complaint with Beyond Coastal is that it has a slightly odd smell - almost like warm milk. Not much of a complaint when you think of all the benefits of using a safe product for your family!

product_title: Sleep Cell Sleeping Bag The E Bag Premium Extra Large
review_headline: Some neat features, but not a dependable bag.
review_body: It's not necessarily a bad bag, but it could definitely use some redesigning.  The pillow setup is well done, and a very cozy place to rest your head.  However, the bag suffers from some serious drawbacks in the warmth department.  Even when zipped up, I was chilled on a number of nights where the mercury never dropped below 32F, and I am very warm by nature, so I know this thing isn't going to qualify at 10F.  Even if it was capable of sustaing that kind of heat, the fact that the zippers absolutely would not stay up really tears apart any possibility of warmth.  You just look at those things funny and they unzip halfway down the bag.

product_title: SpareHand Head Shot Flashlight with Head Band
review_body: This head  band flashlight is so comfortable I could wear it all day.  And you can easily tilt the light upwards or downwards by just positioning it with your hand.  You can hear the clicks as it locks into position, so there's no angle slippage.  It comes with 3 AAA batteries which has not gone dead yet after several hours of usage.  When they die out I will replace them with rechargeable batteries.  It has a pushbutton on top for off, low, med, hi.  I use the high (3 clicks from off) but I guess the other modes are to extend the life of the batteries.  The battery replacement is the only bad part of this headband.  Instead of a recharger stand you need to replace the batteries when they become weak.  And to access the batteries you need a coin to unscrew the battery holder.  But I like that it uses common AAA batteries instead of those expensive coin batteries.    If there is a rechargeable version of this with a recharger stand it would probably cost more.  So, for its price it's perfect the way it is.

product_title: Pearl iZUMi Barrier Lobster Cycling Glove
review_headline: Still the warmest cycling glove available
review_body: I have an old pair of these I use each winter that have lasted about eight years or so. Despite some of the negative comments saying that these gloves aren't as durable, I took the plunge in buying a pair for my father, who cycle-commutes daily in all four seasons and had gone through several inferior pairs of winter cycling gloves. He's had them since Christmas and has been very pleased; aside from normal wear and tear, he's had no problems. Recommend you get these only if you have circulation problems or are cycling in sub-freezing temperatures. Once temperatures go above 30F, I switch to middle-weight gloves. Cycled to work one day this past January when the air temperature was -2F, and my hands still felt toasty!

product_title: Planet Bike Protegé 5.0 bike computer
review_body: It does what is suppost to do.  If you stop for about 5 minutes, it goes to sleep mode to save battery.  The screen is about 1.5\\".  The numbers are easy to see.

product_title: Techni Ice HDR 4 Ply Reusable Ice & Heat Packs 6 Sheet Special
review_body: This is the greatest way to keep foods cold with little space. We put these in a cooler and put them on the plane to St. Croix and everything was still frozen when we got there!

product_title: Yukon Charlies Trail Series Snowshoe
review_body: Sorry to gripe here but dealing with this Yukon Charlies company has left me totally frustrated.  I bought two pairs of these snowshoes, one for myself and one for my wife, for Christmas.   I'd never heard of this company but I bought them through a local private school's fund raising winter sale. On Christmas day, on closer inspection, I realized that the buckle to one of the heel straps was broken. I also noticed that the binding web straps for both pairs were not assembled properly. The way the webbing is sewn and riveted, this is not a fix the customer can perform.  I took pictures of the broken buckle and sent them and an email to YC's customer service. After three emails, one phone call and a month of waiting time (meanwhile during our four feet of snow my snowshoes were not usable), I received an email from YC customer service stating that since the snowshoes had been \\"donated\\" to the school's sale, they were not under warranty.  How is that for standing behind your product?    I had no problem with buying last year's model and maybe saving a few bucks - it was to support a good cause. But to buy a defective model, actually, two defective models, with that lack of customer service attitude, I will never buy one of their products again.  By the way, I looked up the unit cost of a replacement buckle and it was something like fourteen cents.  So, for that price, plus a couple of rivets - maybe twenty five cents worth of Korean plastic parts, I could have done the work myself and they could have retained a happy customer.  I'm going back to Tubbs.

product_title: Cammenga D3-T JP Destinate Triton Protractor Compass
review_body: These are the discs that are possibly in a lawsuit?? they aren't worth the high price I paid for them!! Waiting all these years for Classic Memphis footage and this is what I get? My husband's VHS tapes look better than this. Sad.

product_title: Columbia Men's Gallatin Range Wool Pant
review_body: Excellent, warm, quiet pants. Unhemmed and long for exact length fit. Excellent snow camo. Quickly became a favorite of mine.

product_title: iBert Safe-T Front Mounted Child Bicycle Seat
review_headline: Does not fit every bike as claimed, and seems unsafe if ridden without seat
review_body:
With the incredible number of positive reviews, I was really excited to buy this seat. Unfortunately, I am most likely going to return it unless I decide to get a new bike. The iBert seat does fit onto my bike, as they say it will, but I do not fit on the bike when the seat is attached. To me, their claim that it fits every bike is a half truth.

The iBert seat was very easy to attach to my bike (less than 10min), but there is no room for me once the seat is attached. I am 5'10\\" and put the seat on an a Trek 830 with a 21\\" frame. With the iBert seat on, there is so little space between the back of the iBert and the front of my seat that I cannot stand over the bike when it is at rest. This means if I come to a red light, I would have to lean onto one leg while balancing the child rather than standing over the center bar with both feet securely on the ground.

Also, iBert claims the seat is easy to remove so you can ride when your child is not with you. While the seat does come off easily, this leaves the \\"Stinger bar\\" exposed and moving when you turn your handle bars. If you have to stop suddenly, it would be very easy to gore yourself. The entire Stinger assembly can be removed in less than 5min, so it may not be a big deal, but iBert claims you can leave it on when you ride without the child seat. I think this would be very unsafe.

I will look for a different bike that might fit the seat as I love the idea of it. For now, however, I am simply disappointed.

product_title: Yakima Q-111 Clip for Yakima Q Tower Roof Rack System
review_body: It stays put very well, and it allows for a wide array of adjustment.  What else could you ask for?

product_title: Truvativ Noir WC Riser Bar (Carbon, 15mm, 31.8)
review_body: This handlebar is great for racing. Light weight carbon fiber at a hair under 26\\" length and just enough rise. I mounted it on a 26'er hardtail, but will fit nicely on a 29'er too. Recent price drop on this product increased its value against newer, and still pricier, carbon fiber handlebar offerings on the market. Buy one.

product_title: Thule 598 Criterium Upright Rooftop Bicycle Carrier
review_body: Buyer beware!!!     Locks must be purchased separately, of which 2 are required to secure bike  to roof rack. Description on here is very misleading as it states \\"The Criterium is also high security, with a double locking system for bike and rack\\"     I bought 2 bike racks and discovered the locks were NOT included, contrary to product description. Amazon have undertaken to amend this mistake.     Apart from that the product itself is fantastic, very easy to use and install, however do not consider installing with out the locks

product_title: Topeak Comp 140 14 Function Cycle Computer
review_body: One of the few computers that shows the three functions (at the same time) I am most interested in..... rpms, speed, and ride time.  Simple to use and you can toggle easily to distance, time of day, avg. speed.  Cannot believe other more expensive computers show less.

product_title: Bones Reds Precision Skate Bearigns 16 pack
review_body: Best bearings ever! I'm a derby girl, and these are used for my derby skates. They are fantastic, very smooth. I love them.
