review_body: This suit isn't worth $1.  It fell apart within one hour.  Ended up using a cheap poncho from Walmart and had a much better experience.

product_title: Topeak SmartHead Bicycle Floor Pump Upgrade Kit
review_headline: Smarthead works if you understand it
review_body: Pay no attention to those reviews that suggest that the smart head does not work properly - they just don't know how to do it.    I just took delivery of the Joe blow Pro model Floor pump. The \\"smart head\\" has a small learning process.  Once you understand it, it is excellent.  Unfortunately, the manual is quite sketchy and it took me a while to learn the process.  A major advantage is that the same head works for both Presta or Schrader valves.    Start with the lever parallel to the hose and, for Presta, press the head down over the valve as far as it will go comfortably.  Now cock the lever, (lever perpendicular to the hose), and inflate the tire.  For Schrader, there is a difference and it took me a while to get the hang of it.  Do not push the head down as far as it is capable of going - if you do, it will be impossible to cock the lever.  You will rapidly learn how far to push the smart head.  It should be possible to cock the lever without having to strain.    I too thought that there was a problem with the design as my first few attempts, both with Presta and with Schrader valves, were awkward.  Once I learned the system I really like it.  In fact, I'm probably going to order the upgrade kit so that I can put it on the Blackburn floor pump that I am replacing.

product_title: Sunlite Sport Helmet/Glasses Mirror
review_body: A pretty decent mirror if you don't want to spend much.  Moves around more than I would like and the entire thing (except for the part 3M taped to the helmet) pops off occasionally.  For $3 I can't complain too much.

product_title: Coleman 16-Piece Cutlery Set
review_body: I needed a set to use at work, got tired of creating my own land fill with plastic utensils, and also wanted something nicer than the shiny version of standard plastic utensils, but did not want to buy a true silver ware or cutlery set made of metal.  These utensils are great.  They are sturdy, don't get stained by coffee, and the knives are actually usable for meat.  I'll use this at work and when I go camping.    Update: first 6 months of daily use at work and no signs of wear whatsoever.  They don't stain and the only problem is I have lost all but one fork somehow...

product_title: CamelBak Podium 21-Ounce Chill Jacket Insulated Bottle
review_headline: MADE IN CHINA - And tastes like it lol
review_body:
The country of manufacture has nothing to do with my 1 Star Review. However this \\"innovative\\" American company has decided that y'all (and me apparently) are dumb enough to keep buying this Chinese crap. I don't see it mentioned anywhere on Amazon - SO I THOUGHT YOU SHOULD KNOW. Let's hope (pray) the Chinese spend all that American money wisely shall we.

I paid US$13 to \\"own\\" this for a little while. Used a dozen times but the taste is so bad, it's got to go. I called China and they said they don't want it back, thanks anyway. Fortunately - even in Texas! - there are recycling programs (ie. jobs for Americans - yay!). Forget about the taste for a moment - I am wondering how much this product would retail for if it was MADE IN THE USA? Does anyone have any idea? Let's say it cost $20 - ***BUT*** they could put a big sticker on it promoting how they are supporting the US Economy and keeping jobs here - do you think people would pay an extra few bucks for that? Maybe 10 years ago they wouldn't (ie. didn't care) but times are changing and people are waking up. I actually think people would support a company like that!

Enough of the rant. Here is the reason it get's 1 Star. I use tap water via my Brita pitcher chilling in the refrigerator. It tastes pretty awesome and delicious actually - but the minute a drop of it goes anywhere near this Podium thing it tastes and smells of plastic. Drinking water from this becomes very unpleasant. Commercial bottled water from a plastic bottle tastes like water, yet water from this bottle tastes of plastic. A possible clue is that I have noticed it more on warm days. Could North American Summer heat be doing something to the plastic? VERY LIKELY, I hear you all say. Yet this Podium thing is designed to be specifically used on a bicycle water cage (outdoors presumably). Surely they (or the Chinese) took that into consideration?

One positive though, is that the mouthpiece did an excellent job of shooting plastic flavored water down my throat while on a ride.

************ UPDATE MARCH 7TH 2013 *********************

Well 2 years later I am still using this bottle so have upgraded the stars to \\"Four\\". I was more than a little frustrated initially for paying $13 to literally leave a bad taste in my mouth.

I did a web search on how to remove taste & odors from plastic and if memory serves (this was a while back) I filled it with baking soda & white vinegar and let it sit overnight. This corrected the awful taste issue and it has not returned since. I think what happened is that I let the bottle sit outside in the bottle holder while my bike was locked up. In Texas it gets hot and the sun beating down on the plastic caused some sort of leaching or reaction that remained even after fresh water was used. I have since made sure not to leave it outside and haven't had the problem return.

I am deducting one star as there should be some sort of caution that this might happen in warm weather. We have all seen the melted VHS tapes left in cars, and it's common sense that plastic doesn't do well in the sun, however this product IS designed with outdoor & hot weather use in mind.

Overall it has stood up very well to repeated use and I can highly recommend it. My sincerest apologies to the people of the People's Republic of China and the company that feels it must use foreign labor rather than shoot the work over to US-based manufacturers (CamelBak).

product_title: Thule 515 Prologue Fork Mount Rooftop Bike Carrier (2-Pack)
review_body: Does what it's supposed to.  I have a Pontiac Vibe and i had to put it backwards on the car so the bikes wouldn't hang off the back and I could use my trunk.  No big deal though.  Comes with the locks which is nice and holds both my road bike, mountain bike, and heavy hybrid just fine.

product_title: Yakima Mako Saddles Rooftop Kayak Carrier with Straps with Tie-Downs
review_body: We have 2 kayaks and use 2 sets of these saddles to transport our kayaks. We have them mounted on Honda Pilot and there is enough room for both kayaks. We have found this system to be fairly easy to use and they hold the kayaks well.

product_title: Shimano CN-7701 Dura Ace XTR 9-speed Chain
review_body: Used this chain for 3 years on my mountain bike before recently replacing it with the exact same one.  It held up fabulously as long as the system is well adjusted and lubricated, never had a problem with shifting or anything

product_title: Camelbak Alpine Explorer 100 Oz Hydration Pack
review_body: Well designed, lots of storage, comfortable carry.  Hip belt not perfect for load shift to hips, but works reasonably well.  Some slippage of the hip belt straps.  Hydration system works well.  Very satisfied overall.

product_title: ENO Eagles Nest Outfitters - DoubleNest Hammock
review_body: This is a great hammock; breathable, lightweight (without the stock rope and carabiners...more on this later), quality construction.  Great for lounging around the backyard or using it to camp in the backcountry.  If you're planning on using it around the yard or car camping, then you can easily use it as-is.  However, if you plan on using it for backpacking you might want to think about changing out the stock rope and carabiners for something lighter, such as Whoopie Slings or Cinch-buckles.  Great product either way though!

product_title: Nikwax Nubuck and Suede Duo-Pack
review_body: I bought this product based on a recommendation from the Keen shoe website. I have a pair of Keen clogs that are my absolute favorite, and they don't seem to sell them anymore.  These shoes had obvious stains and spots on them, so much so that I only wore them at home.  A few days ago I tried both Nikwax products.  They were very easy to use, I couldn't believe they would work.  My shoes look new again!  I wish I had taken \\"before\\" and \\"after\\" photos, but trust me, these shoes looked too dirty to wear away from home.  I also tried it on a cheaper pair of nubuck sandals which also look great, although they were not very dirty.  This pair is a light sand color, and the product did not seem to darken the color at all.  Although I used the waterproofing product, I can't comment on its effectiveness because I haven't worn them since I cleaned them.

product_title: Animal Edwin DeLarosa Flangeless BMX Bike Grip - Black
review_body: These grips are so comfortable. I used to get blisters from the stock grips on my bike, but with these I can ride without gloves. Durability I'm not sure because I don't throw my bike around, but definitely the best comfortable grips ever!

product_title: Eco Ball Chalk
review_body: I was looking for a product to help keep my grip sticky when swinging clubbells and kettlebells. Chalk seemed too messy to use indoors in my apartment. This \\"eco ball\\" does the trick and looks like it will last for a long, long time. I had no idea how much my grip was slipping when swinging my 15 lb clubbells. Now my grip stays in one place.    Note: Make sure to wash your hands well after and then put some lotion on.

product_title: Delta MegaRack Ultra Frame Mounted Bicycle Rack
review_headline: Well designed, well made, well priced rack
review_body: Hard to find fault with this rack. Simple sturdy design - adjusts to fit so well that it seems custom made for my bicycle with 26 inch wheels and an extra large frame. Install is simple, step-by-step instructions clear and easy to follow. The rack's construction and finish are excellent. Once installed the rack is solid and flat.

product_title: Coupler Attachment - InStep & Schwinn Bike Trailers
review_body: The product is what it is.  I just needed a Second one for my wife's bike so she could tow around the trailer as well.  If you are purchasing this you should know what this product is for and I am happy to tell you it is exactly as advertised.

product_title: Cozy Products TT Toasty Toes Ergonomic Heated Foot Warmer
review_body: I got this to keep my feet warm in my office. It only has two settings (low and high). The low setting is too hot to be able to put your feet on it, even with socks and slippers on. I've tried wearing shoes on it and while it makes it more bearable I end up with sweaty feet. Based on other reviews it appears that the Low/High settings are not consistent. Some people complain it's too hot and others that it's too cold. It doesn't feel like a sturdy piece of equipment, the price is definitely too high for the quality you get especially with the inconsistent heating.    I have stopped using mine for now but I may switch to using it as a panel on High without putting my feet on it.

product_title: Hearos Ear Plugs Xtreme Protection, 14-Pair Foam
review_headline: These ones work great for me!
review_body: I like these! I have tried many others, but these ones work the best for me. The most important thing is to roll them into a skinny tube and while lifting the top of your ear up with one hand, put the hearo way in and allow it to expand, then let go of your ear. My husband snores so these really help drown out the noise. I change them out about twice a week because I think fresh ones work the best. The only problem I have had, is when I don't take the time to insert them properly and they work their way out of my ear in the middle of the night. They are still in, but not as effective.

product_title: Avenir Flower Bike Basket

product_title: U.S. Divers Proflex II Diving Fins
review_body: I am giving these a 4 star review even though I couldn't use them. Be careful they run big. I am an 8.5 and these which were supposed to fit 8-9.5 were too big. Perhaps that are 8-9.5 men's. (That's what I get for rushing to buy these things a few days before a trip.)

review_body: While this may not matter for non-collectors, the zippo does not come is a padded box. The design is fine and fluid along with the flints is also nice. When I order a zippo I typically keep them inside the box which this one does not come with.

product_title: Kenda John Tomac Signature Series Nevegal Mountain Bike Tire
review_headline: Big fan of the Kenda Nevegal DTC and StickE
review_body: I'm a big fan of both the DTC and the Stick-E Nevagals.  Avoid the UST tubeless...they feel like you are dragging an anchor behind you! The UST doesn't roll very good at all. The DTC and the Stick-E have never let me down!  I ride singletrack, tubes at about 36 lbs, and never pinch flat or slide out! review_body: do noy buy this trap made by shelter logic its panels were poorley built im goin to reinforce it,do not buy

product_title: Long Free Diving Soft and Powerful Fins | GARA 3000 made in Italy by Cressi: quality since 1946
review_body: These were my first true freediving fins I have bought. I have been spearfishing for years but have never bought my own pair of long blade fins. I have used them before but seeing I owned my own scuba fins I never purchased a pair because of the price. But given the price of these fins and the quality they are so worth it. The blades are a little softer than other fins and work great in colder water.    I ordered size 10-11 in the fins. I wear size 11-12 in shoes. If you want to wear the fins with neoprene booties I would suggest you order fins of the same size shoes you wear. I wear mine with bare feet and they are very comfortable. They might be uncomfortable if you have wide feet.    If you have never used long blade fins for freediving, spearfishing or even scuba I would strongly recommend trying them out. I get so much more power and use less effort. They can be awkward on the bottom or in tight areas when grabbing fish that you have speared but I never have much trouble.     I live in Australia and the Amazon international shipping was fast as well as very reasonably priced.    If you are looking for reasonably priced freediving/spearfishing fins that offer plenty of power and are comfortable to wear these are the fins you should get.

product_title: Under Armour Youth Cold Gear Mock Boys
review_body: As with all of our under armour cold gear products, this mock T is fantastic.  My son wears it all of the time.  He loves not having to wear as many layers and not getting sweat-soaked while hiking the hills after the devil birds.  It is even stylish enought that he wears it to school and around.  For the active individual, when the temps dip, this is a must have, IMO.

product_title: Timbuk2 Gripster Strap Pad
review_body: For around 10 bucks this strap pad is a must have! The two main benefits of this pad are it's grippy texture, which keeps your bag from sliding around on certain jackets, and thick comfy foam that makes the heaviest bags feel 10x better than the standard pad that comes with Timbuk2 bags. It's nice to have both to change depending on your load.

product_title: Comfort Zone The Heat Solution Instant Portable Heat Pack
review_headline: Fun novelty, but not practicle for us
review_body: Kids and friends love watching the transformation!  However, we never seem to remember to recharge it to have it ready for next time.  I suppose we would do better if we had a daily use, but for occasional use it seems like too much trouble.

review_body: Great quality, lightweight. Keeps water cold for a long period of time.     Pretty easy to fill up. Small front pouch.

product_title: iBert Safe-T Front Mounted Child Bicycle Seat
review_headline: Day one, but love love love!
review_body:
The seat arrived today, and despite having way too many things to do, I HAD to install it immediately. I put it on the bike myself in a few minutes. My 19 month old daughter was crying because she didn't want to put on her helmet, until the second we took off on the bike. She was yelling \\"weeee\\" and when I asked if she was ready to stop, I got a \\"no, no, no!!!!\\" When her daddy got home she wanted to go again with dad and it was just as big of a hit.
I'm 5'9\\" and my knees do not hit the seat, her head is far enough below mine that it's not an issue. I thought that turning while the seat was on the handle bars was going to be an issue, but I didn't even notice it. My sister (who is shorter than I by about 5 inches) also tried it with no problems. We're looking forward to many more rides! My husband now wants to get a second stinger (attachment bar) so he can easily take her with him too, without having to switch the whole mounting system.

product_title: Fizik Superlight Soft Touch Microtex Bar Tape
review_headline: Fizik Microtex Soft Touch Bar Tape
review_body:
Outstanding bar tape. In thirty years of cycling, the Fizik tape is the best I've found. Plenty of length. Moderate thickness. It's grip is relentless, even when wet.

This tape is intended for a thinner application -- I prefer thinner tape, and I can't stand sponginess, so I put some stretch on the tape when wrapping. You can wrap without as much stretch if you like a little extra thickness.

Very tough and much easier to care for and clean up than cork. If you like white bar tape, this is the tape to get. I've always been die-hard \\"black bars,\\" but actually tried and tolerated the white tape for a while, because it was easier to keep clean. Back to black, and there is no substitute.

The icing on the cake is the very unique textured look and feel of this tape. Really looks good, no sheen, but without being too monochrome. The texturing gives the bars and the bike a very \\"high end\\" look and feel.

My absolute highest recommendation.

product_title: Stoneman Sports QSP-610 Sparehand Adjustable Bike Bar Adapter, Black Finish
review_headline: Mounts in seconds. No more pinched fingers.
review_body: This product does exactly what it is supposed to.  It is well built and easy to use.  It works very well with 2 women's bikes that we have that have very large down tubes.  Bikes that were previously difficult to mount on a bike rack can now be mounted in just a few minutes.  The jaw release / closure mechanism works easily and closes securely. Take 5 seconds to attaché the \\"Sparehand Bike Frame Adaptor\\" and then proceed to mount bike on your bike rack with the same method you would use to mount a man's bike.    I was a little hesitant on the price, but now I am happy to have made the purchase.  I will probably buy a second one for another bike.  One note of caution.  Not that I had a problem, but it would be wise to make sure both the seat (and seat post) and the handlebars (and handlebar post) are tightened securely. The weight of the bike suspends from these two points when the bike is mounted to a bike rack using the \\"Sparehand Bike Frame Adaptor.\\"

product_title: Osprey FlapJill Mini Shoulder Bag
review_headline: Good quality, but not that good practicality
review_body: I accidentally ordered this item, because I did not realize the \\"mini\\" word in the title. Although, as a first sight I was happy with the product. The size is just perfect, because it can accommodate my 13inch MBP in its sleeve. However, I miss a divider for the laptop and more importantly a waist strap. In this way, this bag is not for an everyday bicycle commuter! I could imagine a hidden pocket on the back part of the bag from outside, an easy accessible one. Personally I am also missing a pen holder, which could make your stuff more organized. If you do not hold the newest 4 inch wide mobile phone, you might find the cellphone pocket too big to your phone, and it is the same with the mp3 player. Since you can't close fully the middle layer with your phone and music player, you should be concerned to ride a bike, because if the bag turns upside down, your belongings (especially if you own an old style cell) could end up falling out.   So overall it seems I have lots of practicality issues with the bag, but if you just want to walk with your small laptop and papers, it might be a good choice.

review_body: I purchased this hat for my Caribbean vacation.  Having very fair skin, I was concerned about sunburning on my shoulders and face. review_body: Well all in all this pot is awesome! When I purchased this pot it would be bigger than it is. I would describe it as short and stout. Lol. I like to eat pasta sides and instant mashed potatoes on the trail and this pot is the perfect size, also great for ramen. The locking lid is solid and enables you to pack the inside with anything you want from a stove to food! I opted for a little of both considering I only use an alchohol stove. Handle is even long enough to cook over the fire if you wanted to, but be careful it gets HOT!! All in all I have no complaints and you wont either. product_title: New Wave 2.2 Liter BPA Free Plastic w/Sturdy stainless steel cap (Blue)
review_headline: I like but it's not perfect
review_body: While I like these bottles and own about a dozen of them altogether (among the round 1-gallon, milk-jug 1-gallon, and 2.2-liter), I have had problems with them cracking.  Obviously, if they fall, they will crack.  One might think that they'd be stronger, but they aren't.  In my case, however, I have acquired many cracks through ordinary transportation of the bottles to/from Whole Foods to get my reverse osmosis water.  Oftentimes they are small, hairline fractures.  For this reason, I DO NOT recommend someone purchase these bottles online.  Rather, I buy locally, save the receipt, and return and exchange when the bottles break.  And they break often.  In the past two years, I have returned upwards of ten bottles.  I only own 12, so almost every bottle I own has been replaced at one point.

product_title: Swagman RV 2" Bumper Adaptor
review_headline: Pro's and Con's of the Swagman RV Bumper Bike Rack!
review_body: PRO'S:  The Swagman RV Bumper Bike Rack Adaptor is very well made with heavy duty material.  It is very easy to install and looks great.  CON's  The (4) four nuts fit very, very tight and appeared to damage the threads of the bolts as you turn the nuts to tighten. You wouldn't have to worry about them falling off.  However... I was concerned about getting them off if/when I wanted to move or remove the Swagman Adaptor.  So I purchased (4) four new flat washers and (4) four new lock washers and (8) eight new nuts. (It takes \\"Metric\\" nuts).  After putting the four bolts through the receiver and down through the bottom plate... I place the flat washer first, then the lock washer, then the first \\"Metric\\" nut and tightened all four nuts.  The second Metric\\" nut was then placed and tightend up against the first nut. This is called double nutting. It may sound like an over kill but it works without any worry of the Swagman receiver comming loose on it's own.  However... it is very easy to remove the Swagman without any of the threads on the (4) four bolts being damaged.  Caution! This is NOT THE FAULT OF THE SWAGMAN ADAPTOR! My Outback RV bumper is made of steel and is a continuous weld the full length of the bottom of the square bumper. It is covered on the top and front with aluminum for looks. The bumper is welded to the RV steel frame in (2) two places about 18\\" in from the left and right ends of the bumper.  Our first trip with the Swagman Adaptor in place and a bike rack attached with (2) two bikes on board was nearly a disaster.  We drove about 375 miles on our first leg of the trip and when we stopped for the night... the bumper was nearly torn off the RV frame.  The bumper... spare tire... and bike rack with (2) two bikes were at a 45 degree angle.  The steel bumper was ripping off the RV frame.  A few more miles down the road and all would have been lost and perhaps caused an accident for following traffic. For the next 1,600 miles we had to load and unload the bikes from inside the RV each time we stopped. I now have to have a shop weld the bumper back on to hold the spare tire and then purchase a full receiver hitch that will bolt directly to the sides of the RV frame and locate it under the existing RV bumper!  UPDATE: Had a heavier gauge steel bumper welded on the rear of the travel trailer for $90 and all is perfect now!

review_body: Fit my mountain bike perfectly and served me well by protecting my back from dirt, since the winter (Chicago-style) of 2010-11!

product_title: Dahon Boardwalk Folding Bike, Obsidian
review_body: I bought this bike to travel around campus quicker without having to wait for shuttles. I've had it for over a week now and have used it daily. The longest I distance I ride it is 2 miles. The bike is very sturdy and looks very nice. Assembly was quick and relatively painless. It truly does fold up in less than 20 seconds, and is very light. review_body: I bought this for my 7 year old grandaughter, so she would have something to do this summer. She hasnt rode it yet but I have! She is going to have a blast! Would recommend this scooter.

product_title: HotHands Toe Warmers (40 Pair)
review_body:
I love HeatMax Toasti toe-warmers. I live in NYC and my feet often get cold when the temperature drops below 40 degrees.

Toasties last 5-7 hours as advertised, but duration varies depending on the temperature (e.g., if its really cold, they stay hot less than 5hrs, and when its warm they stay hot longer, etc.)

The adhesive strips work great and stick to my socks well (other heat pads and hand warmers do not stick to my toes as well and therefore are not able to distribute heat to my toes evenly and consistently).

I would recommend Toasties toe-warmers to anyone who wants to keep their toes nice and toasty.

product_title: Lorpen Liner Coolmax Socks
review_body: I've used these for a few hiking trips now for liners under my wool socks, and they have worked well.  I've had no blisters, and my feet have been nice and comfy.

product_title: Avenir Thorn-Resistant Schrader Valve 700c Tube (700x35-45)
review_body: I can't comment on how well this tube will resist thorns, however upon first impression the rubber is very thick and heavy.  Don't buy if you intend to carry this tube as a spare on your bike.  It is too big to fit in most seat bags and is quite heavy compared to normal tubes.

product_title: Thule Rapid Crossroad Roof Racks
review_headline: By far the easiest rack to mount
review_body: Just removed my bike rack for the winter and it was so easy.  Not like my last rack which scratched my roof up.  The rubber grips very secure and there is no movement or vibration. I bought these used and will probable be able to sell them for the same price if my next van can not use them.  Thule makes the best well thought out products.

product_title: OnGuard Bulldog MINI DT 5015TC Bicycle U-Lock and Extra Security Cable
review_headline: No problems.  Gets the job done.
review_body: I bought this lock for commuting in downtown Austin on a new $300 bike and have used it for about a month.      Having read reviews on here, I was a bit wary that there would be problems with the lock and key.  Well, I'm happy to report that my lock has worked fine.  Sometimes I have to jimmy the key a little to turn it, but it's not a big deal at all.    The lock itself is fairly hefty (I think someone said 2 pounds...sounds about right) and feels very sturdy.  It also comes with a thin metal cable that you can loop through a wheel for a little additional security.    In short, all I can say is \\"so far, so good.\\"

product_title: VDO MC1.0+ Wireless Altimeter/Cycle Computer
review_body: I love this computer - it shows me everything I need and is very easy to view and scan thru.  The only reason it's my 2nd one is that my first got knocked off my bike on a VERY bumpy road and run over by a SAG vehicle!  It's take me a few times to feel fluent about progamming it, but that's not something you do very often, so it's not important (and the manual is easy to follow.)

product_title: HotHands Hand Warmers
review_body: We live in Virgina Beach and take our dog to the bay every weekend, all year long.  In the winter, the winds are so bad down there that the wind chill always makes it miserable.  It will be 30 degrees with, anywhere from 10 to 40 mile an hour winds.  It's just brutal.  My hands are always cold and it's unbearable.  With the hand warmers I can bear the cold and wind. review_body: I purchased this because the Coleman name has always meant good quality to me. The bed only lasted about a dozen uses before it began to leak air right at the seam. product_title: Primus Coffee and Tea Press
review_body: Just came back from a 3-day backpacking trip at Twenty Lakes Basin loop. I'm so glad I took this French press! It makes awesome coffee. (I hate instant coffee!) It weighs 2 oz, and collapses into 2 flat pieces and a rod, and you're good to go. Sadly, it does not come with a pouch, nor does it fit inside the EtaExpress cooking system pot. You can however squeeze it into the sack on top of the pot, but it's a tight squeeze.    Here's how you use it. You put the coffee in the EtaExpress pot after boiling water. Let steep a few minutes. The opening of the Coffee press lid goes over the pot's pour spout/lip. Press down on the plunger. Pour out your coffee. That's it! The coffee is AWESOME. Some things to keep in mind:    1. You MUST have a Primus EtaExpress cooking system, EtaPower 1L pot, or LiTech Trek Kettle, as this is designed for and fits those pots.  2. The lid leaks quite a bit while pouring, as the coffee seems to follow the lid's lip, circumnavigating the pour spout on the pot, and leaking out.  3. Making 2 cups spills a lot less than 4 cups at a time  4. Pour slowly to minimize spill.    Why a 4 star rating for a product that spills so much? 1) Excellent fresh brewed French press coffee, and 2) 2 oz and folds flat. If you already have a Primus EtaExpress, EtaPower 1L pot, or a LiTech Trek Kettle, where else are you gonna find a quality coffee maker that weighs 2 oz?    Make sure you get coarse ground coffee, freshly ground before your trip. We took Coffee-mate creamer powder, delicious! Enjoy!

product_title: DryGuy Circulator Footwear Dryer Warmer
review_headline: They kinda work, but very slowly
review_body: I bought these to dry my kitesurfing boots. Just for reference, my boots are made of 5 mm neoprene rubber with a thin fabric lining on the inside. After use I rinse them and put them upside down for about an hour to let most of the water drip out. In the past I would use a hair dryer for about 15 minutes to get the inside completely dry. This is a pain because it is noisy and you have to keep an eye on it to make sure nothing overheats.     The (only) good thing about my new Dryguy Circulators is that I can put them in and forget them. They put out very little heat, just a bit more than your feet would, and do not move the air, other than through natural convection. The down side is that they are slooooow. After 8 hours the area at the bottom of the boots, right where the device sat was \\"mostly\\" dry, but the shaft of the boot was still pretty wet. This means that on tall or large boots you will have to reposition the Circulators a couple of times, or possibly leave them in even longer.    The build quality seems pretty good, and since they do not get very hot it is nice that they each have an LED so you can see whether they are working.    I have not had these Dryguy Circulators long enough to determine if they leave my boots any smellier, but I am afraid that 8+ hours of gentle warmth, and very very slow drying may just be the perfect conditions for the dreaded stinkyfeet bacteria to multiply....

product_title: Intex Pillow Rest Raised Airbed with Built-in Pillow and Electric Pump

review_body: I was looking for a multi fuel stove that could burn (unleaded) gasoline. I looked at the external tank models (like the MSR whisperlite) and many of the ones I looked at no longer were able to use gasoline. I really did not care for that style and all the messing around that is necessary with those external tank units. This one is easy to use and no assembly is required!

product_title: Insta-Bed Queen Raised Air Mattress with Sure Grip Bottom & Built-In Pump
review_headline: The 1st one leaked but the second one is great!
review_body: The first bed that I ordered leaked badly within the first 24 hours. I returned it and took a chance and ordered another from Amazon. It arrived just in the nick of time for my house guests. That was 3 weeks ago and since I was expecting another house guest soon, we decided to leave it inflated. It has inflated for three weeks now and I haven't had to add any more air!  We have been lounging around on it and I'm happy to say that it is quite comfortable.  I did notice that the \\"sure grip bottom\\" doesn't really grip on a hardwood floor. I put a very small \\"no-slip\\" rug pad under a portion of it and now it stays put.

product_title: Bell No-Mor Flats Bike Inner Tube, 24-x 1.75-Inch to 1.95-Inch
review_headline: The kids will be able to ride bikes all they like now
review_body: I got a total of four of the Bell No-Mor Flats in the 24\\" size for my twin grandson's bicycles. The instructions were pretty sparce, but by the time I was getting the fourth one mounted, the process went quickly. It took me a total of two and a half hours to get all four mounted, and to get both bikes back together.    Helpful Hints - 1 . make sure the tubes are warm because when they are cold, they are as hard as rocks; 2 . use retention straps / strips to cinch down sections of the tire that you have got the tire bead seated on both sides of the rim on, or else the tire bead will pop out of areas you have just done.    I would get six inches of the tire's bead into both sides of the rim, then strap down the section with the velcro strips I used. Then I'd pop in the next 6\\" of bead, and cinch down that section with the third velcro strap while keeping the bead in place with the screwdrivers I was using as tire spoons. Then I'd remove the strap that was in the middle now, and use it to cinch down the next 6\\" section of bead.    Lubricant was only helpful getting the second half of the bead seated once half the tire was seated.

product_title: Hot Chillys Men's Hi Volume Sock
review_headline: Kept my feet warm in bitter cold
review_body: My feet tend to get cold quickly and painfully. I needed socks quickly before a last-minute ski trip and took a shot at these- not only were they sized right but they stayed up and kept my feet warm in 20 degree temperatures over an 8 hour ski day.

product_title: Coleman 2000018295 8-Person Instant Tent, Black (14x10 Feet)
review_body: Excellent quality and instant set up as advertsied - the toughest part is getting it backl in to the carrying bag!

product_title: Sorel Women's Joan Of Arctic Boot
review_headline: Sorel Joan of Arctic black boots
review_body: Just got my Sorel Joan of Arctic black boots. I've tried them at home and they are very comfortable, does not hurt the back of my ankle and I do not think I have to wear them out, does not fit tight I ordered a size 7 and I typically wear a 7-7 1/2, there's a little wiggle room if I want to wear thicker socks so I believe it fit true to my shoe size.  The suede is very comfortable and not stiff at all. The fur is removeable if you want to replace the felt liner as the fur is attached to the liner not the boot itself. I do not feel that they are really clunky as compared to my timberlands maybe a little heavier than my classic Uggs.  When I tie the laces loosely, I am able to slip in and out of the boots without having to tie the laces again.  The front of the duck boot does look a little wide though but overall, I am glad I bought these boots for this crazy winter snow storms.  I am looking forward to wearing these boots and know that it will last a long time.

product_title: Batman Begins Batarangs & Halloween Safety Light
review_headline: Worked for only a few minutes
review_body: Gave this to our son as part of his Easter basket this morning.  The light stopped working literally an hour after the batteries were installed.  Put in new batteries, still did not work.  Could not see how to access the bulb, so can only assume it is burnt out.  Very disappointed, as is our son.

product_title: 2 Standard (MATCHED ZIP TOGETHER SET) EXTREME 0 DEG. BACKPACKING MUMMY BAGS
review_body:
The husband and I just took these out for the first time this weekend for an overnight backpacking trip.

I'd give them 5 stars, for sure, for weight/warmth and packability. They come packed TINY (a little smaller than a 2 liter soda bottle) and I was able to repack them down to the same size as factory shipped. They fit great in the sleeping bag compartment of our packs.

For the price, I was not really expecting these to actually be 0 degree bags. But temps dropped into the low 30s the night we were out and we stayed toasty warm in just normal pjs. We zipped them together and it was me, my husband and our dog (we're pretty little so there was room for all of us.) I should mention we had them on top of a thermarest trail lite sleep pad.

The only drawbacks I see are 1)these might keep you from dying from hypothermia at 0 degrees, but if your looking for a true 0 degree bag, I don't think this is what you want. 2) the zippers don't \\"click\\" into place when you marry them, so the top zipper kept creeping down as we slept and kept needing rezipped. 3) like almost all bags, you have to be careful with the zippers, they will catch on the cloth, but not any more or less than other bags. 4)if your a really big/tall guy, they might be a tight fit.

If you are looking for backpacking bags, at a great price, and are just going to be flirting with the edges of 3 seasons I would not hesitate to get these.

product_title: Petzl E91 Tikkina 2 Headlamp
review_body:
The light is okay. Easy to insert batteries, two modes, pretty bright. In fact, my argument isn't with the lamp itself (which works), but with the strap. The strap is designed to be used by stretching over a helmet, a head, whatever. I wanted to use it by unbuckling it and wrapping it around a cylindrical item (from time to time) and was surprised to see that it couldn't be done. The strap is heat-sealed onto a plastic size adjuster, but there's no way to unbuckle it. The good thing is that the lamp is detachable from the strap which allows for some flexibility.

So lamp = good, strap = adequate but limited. A buckle would have been nice. If there had been a buckle, this would have been five stars.

product_title: Razor Special Edition Steel Scooter
review_body: My son is almost 9 yrs old. The height of the handle bars fit him perfectly. So this was a good deal for me. With a smaller child this scooter may not work as the handle bar is not adjustable. It was too tal for my 7 year old daughter. but for my son this turns out to be a good deal. He loves it.

product_title: Hot Wheels Boys Bike (16-Inch Wheels)
review_body: Awesome bike for lucky little boys who get one! They can \\"rev\\" the engine and show off, it is well constructed and handles easily for beginners. My 4 year old son is the only one in the neighborhood with one, and he likes the attention he gets from the bigger kids. We have had problems with the use of the handbrake vs. the foot brake, but I think given another season of bike riding he will have it all figured out.

product_title: DMM Wallnut Nut
review_body: these are, not only in my opinion, the best nuts on the market. You may want a different brand as a second set (or not) to give you more options, but these are an excellent staple on any rack.

product_title: Avenir Universal XL Rear Rack (Black, Universal)
review_body: We bought two of these racks to accompany our Amazon panniers. They've worked great, really sturdy. The only thing that made them difficult to use was that they were quite tricky to attach to our two bikes - required a great deal of creativity. On one of our bikes, the rack wouldn't fit at all until we borrowed parts from an old rack to help us attach it. So from our experience the rack won't work at all for some bikes, and won't work easily for quite a few bikes. But once we'd secured them, the racks worked quite well.

product_title: Stainless Steel Water Bottle Sports Cap
review_body: The caps fit and work great, and the price is awesome; a-penny-a-piece is hard to beat...  except the shipping was OVER TEN BUCKS! Together-Bottle may not be the best option. Don't be fooled when the \\"price\\" is this good.

product_title: JanSport Eternal Tote
review_body: Such a handy and pretty bag, I love that it's not huge but not too small either. Very practical and pretty at the same time.  Thank you Amzon. Your jeans by \\"NYDJ\\" really have enriched my wardrobe, but did not break the bank ! Awesome !

product_title: Saris Bones 805 (2-Bike) Trunk Mount Rack
review_body: Certainly looks cool. It does leave paint scuff marks on bumper and trunk. Great for one bike. However, seems unstable with two bikes.

product_title: CamelBak 0.75- Liter Stainless Steel Better Bottle
review_body: Great bottle.  Gave it to my daughter for a gift (she requested a Camelbak bottle, but I picked which one.) and it was a huge hit.  Well made and the art looks great.

product_title: U.S. Divers Mariner Diving Gear Bag
review_body: This is the worst product I'll ever bought in my life.  It arrived with a 5 inch hole in the bottom because of an open seam.  That was not a big deal, nothing that I cannot fix with a needle and thread.  But anyway I'm not supposed to be doing that in a new item.  Anyway that is not all, in the first use, carrying 2 pairs of fins, 2 masks and 2 snorkels no heavy equipment or leads one of the plastic pieces in the shoulder strap snapped only under the weight of the bag.  I don't know if it was just bad luck but If this keep going I'll have to remake the whole bag for the end of the summer

product_title: Polar Bottle Insulated Water Bottle - 24oz (discontinued colors)
review_body: Happy with this bottle. It does the job. It won't keep water ice cold for hours in 30 degree celsius + heat, but it helps if the bottle and contents are previously kept in the fridge for 12 hours or longer. The water would then stay cold for a couple of hours. Also, the water doesn't have any unpleasant aftertaste. There isn't much choice in Australia for insulated bottles, and I am quite happy that I ordered this one from Amazon. Seller was very prompt with shipping and costs were reasonable.

product_title: Wenzel Ridgeline 3 Person Tent
review_headline: girls night out at tent city
review_body: The package was shipped and received as projected. The item's carton came not damaged. Grandaughter loves the color and size. Grandpa liked the price. Will use and recommend this supplier.

product_title: Schwinn Pillow Top Cruiser Bicycle Seat
review_body: This seat is somehow even less comfortable than the regular seat that came with my bike.  It is not soft or springy at all, and the grooves from the design make it even worse than just a flat surface.  The name \\"Pillow Top\\" is nowhere close to accurate.

product_title: Third Eye Bar End Bicycle Mirror
review_headline: I have these on my Motorcycle and they are great!
review_body: I use them on motorcycles. They are at least a $100 cheaper then bike shops charge and just as good.

product_title: Platypus Soft Bottle with Closure Cap
review_body: This is a great water bottle, and I prefer it to the standard hard-plastic water bottles. The hardest part is getting used to the fact that it's a soft bottle. In other words, it's incredibly easy to get a feel for this thing. Unless you're a die hard fan of hard-plastic water bottles, you'll love the Platypus.

product_title: Victorinox Signature Lite Pocket Knife
review_body: I bought this to put on my keychain.  I carry it everywhere with me.  It is nice and small.  You don't even know it is on your keychain.  I bought it mainly for the light, which works great!  I love this thing!

product_title: Schwinn High Timber Women's Mountain Bike (26-Inch Wheels)
review_body: I'll say right off that I bought this bike in purple for $190 and I see that the price has changed to $220 ish. Even for the old price of $190 I sent it back. First of all, it came from Wsports and had the wrong part on the left hand shifter. The counter sprocket grip shifter had 7 clicks where it should have had 3 clicks to accomodate the 3 counter sprockets. There are coincidentally 7 rear sprockets which is why I know they had put the wrong left hand shifter on the bike. I'll also say that even if the bike had been shipped with all the right parts I still would have sent it back. It wasn't absolutely horrible but nothing on the bike seemed to warrant its price tag. Derailleurs, v-brakes, kickstand, forks, handlebars, most all hardware seemed like the type of stuff you'd find on a 90 dollar bicycle at a superstore like walmart or target. Also the frame was very heavy. It says the shipping weight is 25 pounds but I will approximate that this bike weighs near 40 pounds. I bought this bike along with a Schwinn Solution FS AL and the Solution is 100 times better bike. The difference in quality and parts of the two bikes greatly outweighs the 20-50 price difference. All the good reviews baffle me. I guess people just psyche themselves into being happy with what they got, but I know better and sent it back. Dont waste your time here. BTW I got a refund and bought another Solution FS AL instead.

product_title: Liquid Logic Nautilus BPA Free Water Bottle with Flipper Top and Carabiner (25-Ounce)
review_headline: I wish it worked better and longer
review_body:
[[ASIN:B001G7QSNE Liquid Logic Nautilus BPA Free Water Bottle with Flipper Top and Carabiner (25-Ounce)]]

Worked well for less than month and the rest is history. A perfect size bottle for me but I had to replace it because the flipper top keeps coming off after less than a month of use which is just horrible! Would not recommend this! I was stuck with this bottle while looking for a replacement and I had to use some adhesive to keep my water from spilling. Fail!

product_title: Bones Bearings Swiss Ceramic Labyrinth Skate Bearings (7mm, 16-Pack)
review_body: These were the first ceramic bearings I've ever purchased.  They were costly but worth every penny.  They are fast right out of the box.  They are smooth as well and it feels almost like there's no friction at all between the bearing and the wheels.  Since they are ceramic there is no metallic dust so servicing them is less of a chore.  Wonderful investment.  It is very likely that I may get new skates in the future but the bearings will last me a life time.

product_title: Thule 835XTR Hullaport Rooftop Kayak Carrier
review_body: I purchased this carrier for an Ocean Kayak Malibu Two XL.  Bad bad idea.  The rated specs for this carrier were for kayaks under 36\\" wide and less than 75 lbs, no problem as ours was 34\\", 61 lbs.  The j-hooks went on easy and the long bolts included fit our Santa Fe perfectly as indicated in the instructions.  Our first hiccup came when we put the kayak up and the j-hooks were just barely tall enough to hit the midpoint of the hull.  Okay.  Then the included straps weren't long enough to strap in the kayak.  That should have been our clue not to use it, but no we went to Lowe's and bought some longer tie downs.  Let's just say that we got to the lake 15 miles from our house fine.  And on the way back we almost lost the kayak to the freeway (we never went over 55).  There were some light winds, and a gust caught the kayak and pulled the front j-hook sideways about 6\\".  It seems like a sturdy system for a smaller kayak, but I have to start shopping for something better suited to ours.

product_title: U.S. Divers Proflex II Diving Fins
review_body: I purchased these fins for a diving/snorkeling vacation in Belize. They performed as expected and got me where I needed to go! After a full week of diving/snorkeling, my feet had gotten a bit raw in spots but that is due in part to sand getting caught in the pocket also. I think for longer vacations I will have a setup that includes neoprene booties to protect my feet better but for shorter trips and general playing these fins do an excellent job for the price!

product_title: Soma Tire Lever Steel Core Card (Pack of 2)
review_body: Used these one time and plastic tip on the lever side broke off while changing tire, steel core remained but not very useful afterward.

product_title: GORE BIKE WEAR Women's Power Lady Tights Short
review_body: Especially comfortable on longer rides... Good quality chamois.  Perfect fit - I like the slightly lower rise.

product_title: Primus Super Pouch
review_body:
purchased to protect my vintage Optimus 111 brass stoves - works very well.. will also use to hold my Primus Gravity MF stove and bottle w/its misc bits... good price...

but i can't figure out what the little loops on each side are for?

product_title: Shimano FH-6700 Ultegra Bicycle Freehub (10-Speed, 32-Hole, Silver)
review_body: I bought this 6700 rear hub and built a custom wheelset. Changing hubs has made a very large difference - smoother, less noise and less rolling resistance. This was well worth the money. I highly recommend this hub. It isn't DuraAce, but the price is right and the value is excellent. Highly recommend this 6700. The wheelset is awesome and, though it is probably in my mind, I seem to have added a couple of mph to my average on long rides.

product_title: Nirve Starliner Men's Hybrid Cruiser Bike
review_headline: Overall, I have not made up my mind yet.
review_body:
With gas prices being what they are, not to mention the health benefits, I decided to buy this one, which is the first for me without trying it out first from a local bicycle shop. I was not fooling myself into thinking that I was going to park the car in the garage and use this as my primary form of transportation, but I did want something that would get the job done with regard to buying a small amount of groceries, Circle K, Starbucks, an occasional outing, including the local \\"watering hole\\" all located within a five mile radius from my home.

With that being said, I knew what I wanted and what would appeal the most to me from my own personal past experience. I was in the market for a large frame bicycle, but wanted the hybrid wheel. I wanted a little bit more \\"gity up\\" then just the typical single speed beach cruiser with the large diameter tire. As you all know, it is somewhat slim pickings to find something that fits the bill for us tall guys. I looked at the Diamond back as well, but I liked the retro \\"old school\\" look of the Nirve, not to mention the reviews were decent, so I went with it. I have PRIME, so the package arrived in two days at my door step. Amazon always comes through in that regard. On the side of the box were listed the tools needed for assembly, which was nice. Keep the Alan wrenches and metrics handy. The assembly directions were straightforward. Plan on about one hour for assembly.

What needs to be assembled is as follows: Front tire, front tire fender, pedals, handle bars, seat, and reflectors. The breaks front and rear are assembled, but need fine tuning. I also opted to go with the front basket, in black of course, which really was a nice touch. I put air in the tires, looked everything over and off I went. During the first few miles, the chain fell off about three times. The shimano will need to be tuned up as well, since it was not ready to go out of the box even though the rear tire and chain were attached and did not need assembly. Synopsis as follows:

Pros:
1. large frame, retro styling, the fenders really set this thing off.
2. Frame true to size. Opted with the large frame. First time I don't feel like my knees are going to hit my chin on a bicycle.
3. Not as heavy as I originally thought. Very light and responsive for this size bike.

Cons:

1. I read these bikes were made in Huntington Beach, California, but I must have gotten the Chinese version because there was a sticker \\"made in china\\" on the downtube of the bike.
2. The seat is not as comfortable as you would think.
3. I think the components could have been a little better when compared to other hybrid bikes even in this price range.

Overall Impression: I think if you just want something with a nice \\"old school\\" look that appears to be well made, to get you around town to the nearest grocery store, Circle K, Starbucks, including a longer outing on occasion, then this bike is for you. If you you plan on downgrading from your old street bike or plan on doing time trial racing then shy away from this one.and did not need assembly. product_title: Klean Kanteen 27 oz Brushed Stainless Steel Water Bottle with Sport Cap 3.0 and Bike Cage
review_body: Perfect combination of bottle, cap, and cage. It's easy to fill, drink from, and get into and out of the holder.

product_title: Intex Raised Downy Airbed with Built-in Electric Pump, Queen, Bed Height 22"
review_body: I guess you get what you pay for but I was hoping for the best despite the many negative comments on here. Nevertheless, my worse fears were realized!. I slept on the mattress two days trying to give it a chance but after the first night, I woke up in extreme back pain and with a mattress that somehow during the night sinks in the middle! The second night I could barely walk after sleeping on it and again waking up with the mattress sunken in the middle. I immediately contacted amazon.com, got my RMA and returned the thing!

product_title: Schwinn Training Wheels 16" - 20"
review_body: As with others the item received was not what was pictured. I was hoping to receive the wheels with the two different length black angle iron, sturdy leg-bike attachments that are pictured. What I received was much flimsier stanless steel. Our Schwinn childs bike came with the training wheels that is pictured on Amazon, so I was hoping to replace the orignals which my wife threw out once my boy graduated beyond training wheels. Our youngest is now using the bike and needs trainers. Already had an accident with substandard stainless supports, so we are not going there again. Apparently from the messages there are some who got the pictured product, but obviously there are quite a few others, like us, who did not.

product_title: LEDwholesalers 51-LED 395nm Ultra Violet Blacklight UV Flashlight 3xAA, 7202UV395
review_body: This product works well and is worth buying more than one. The price is right  and the delivery was speedy even during Christmas rush.

product_title: Zippo Color Ice Lighters
review_body: Zippos are great and this one is nicer looking than I figured it would be. It was delivered very quickly too.

product_title: Spaz Spinning LED Hand Held 3D Rave Show
review_body: I really loved this toy and bought it for my grandchildren.  One of the toys worked perfectly - when you pushed the button it would spin and light up. The other one had a bad battery connection and would only spin if you pushed the button and pushed up on the door to the battery compartment.  It is fantastic when it works.

product_title: 3200 Cubic Inch K-cliffs Moderate Hiker Internal Frame Backpack, Maroon/grey
review_body: Cheap light weight pack. Nothing fancy, but for the price I'm happy. Bought for my wife to try and get her interested in backpacking. Great first pack for someone starting out.

product_title: Under Armour Liner Glove Black
review_headline: When kept in perspective they're AMAZING
review_body: As a college student who when walking across campus in 30 degree temperatures and rarely less than 10 MPH winds I was often cold and looked into things to keep me warm.  My roomate convinced me to get a North Face Triclimate jacket (highly reccomend btw) so I did that but I also wanted something to keep my hands warm.  I didn't want a big pair of gloves because I was simply walking across campus, not playing in the snow, but I wanted something just as effective.  So I narrowed it down to the UA Cold Gear Liner and the North Face Power Stretch pair.  In the end I got the UA Cold Gear Liner because I had experience with UAs Coldgear material before.  I was a little nervous about it though because after a lot of research I had seen several people state that it didn't block the wind which was a big problem for me since the winds are ALWAYS 10 MPH, though usually more.    I got the pair and initially was very pleased upon opening.  I love the way it fit snugly to my hand and wasn't bulky.  So I tested it the very next day going to class.  At first I kept my hands in my pocket and was very impressed how warm my hands STAYED.  Previously I would keep my hands in my pockets but they would, without failing, get sweaty and then they would freeze again.   ColdGear prevents that; it rocks!  I highly reccomend anything from UAs Coldgear line.  Unfortunately, my research was right, the wind pierces right through it.  So if you ride a bike or something where you can't shield your hands these won't be ideal.  Other perks of the glove include a grippy palm side, felt around the thumb and pointer fingers, and the ability to use a touchscreen phone/screen through the material.  For those times Im just rushing to get dinner from the dining hall its nice having the gripy palms to hold my drinks and stuff and not have to worry about it spilling.  The felt around the fingers are awesome for wiping glasses, goggles, and quite frankly... your nose.  But my favorite side perk is the abilityto use my phone without having to take off my gloves.  My roomate was stunned when he first saw me do it.      So in the end it was NOT the do-it-all machine I was hoping it would be.  It couldn't block the wind.  But lets be perfectly honest.  As a liner its NOT supposed to do that.  If I wanted something that would block the wind I would need a bigger set of gloves and I had no desire to wear big heavy set.  Fact is a lightweight pair will NEVER be able to do what a heavier set can.  So as light-weight set of gloves, it is perfect.  I'm not sure its worth $25 but I don't have any regrets about getting it either.  I'm glad I did.  I love 'em.  I highly reccomend the pair as long as you keep in mind what its designed to do.  If you expect them to be a do it all pair then you will be disappointed but when kept in perspective they should make you very pleased you got them... especially if you can find some that are discounted.              Another Nice product by Under Armour!    EDIT:  Forgot to mention that these are excellent gloves for driving when its cold.  Everyone knows driving with a cold steering wheel sucks.  These keep your hands warm and the tacky palms grip the steering wheel for extra control.

product_title: Lorpen Merino Light Hiker Socks
review_headline: Favorite Socks for Hiking And, Well, Everything Else!
review_body: These are my all around favorite socks - period.  I wear them with jeans, shorts, khakis, etc and all kinds of shoes.  They are a great weight, thinner than some other wool socks I own (hence the \\"light\\" adjective in the name) which makes them more versatile as they don't make my shoes fit too tight and they are a little less warm during summer use.  I read about the benefits of wool socks and these prove their worth: they are cool in warm weather and warm in cool weather.  I can use these in any conditions and would only opt for a thicker sock when the temps get sub freezing.  They control moisture very well & remain dry under heavy use in hot weather (unlike cotton socks).  I've been pretty blown away when I remove them after a full day of hiking and they are bone dry.  They control odor well too and can be worn for a couple of days without any major stinkage (once again, unlike cotton socks which get funky quickly).  I intentionally wear these for at least two days before washing them, which cuts down a bit on laundry volume.  They also wear more graciously against the skin than cotton & are much less prone to causing blisters - a big advantage on the trail.  All in all these are a great hiking sock & a great everyday sock.  Unless you need something thicker for extra warmth, these are it.

product_title: Extreme Pak Digital Camo Bag
review_body: It's made in China, but for $24.99 its a great deal. The backpack feels VERY solid. It comes with compression straps, a chest strap, and a waist belt, which is not shown in the Amazon picture. It has one large compartment, and two front pockets. I wish they would have added more pockets. The top of the backpack has two holes that can be used to put an antenna through it, or a hydration tube. I would buy this again.

product_title: Klean Kanteen with Loop Cap, (40 oz)
review_body: I never received my product because the supplier did not ship the item. I was credited the funds. Three stars is somewhat of a neutral rating for a product I never received.

product_title: Long Range S.O.C. Gear - BLACK (T27 SEC D RW 2)
review_headline: Solidly built pack for daily use
review_body:
I use this pack to carry about 30 lbs of gear with me into work five times a week. I walk about a half a mile with it each day. So far after almost a year of service, its as good as the day it was bought. No fraying, no zipper issues, no tearing.

Its not cheap but in this case you get what you pay for.

On the down side, it looks like you have a window air conditioner strapped to your back. Its BIG.

EDIT: November 2012. Still used 5 times a week just as I said above. 3 years of daily service, and still looks great. Outstanding quality! How odd is it that if it was cheap garbage I would never buy another one, and since its so darn good I won't need to buy another one either. Doesn't seem fair does it, to punish success? Just kidding SOC, keep up the good work.

product_title: Victorinox Swiss Army Spartan Pocket Knife
review_headline: After 25 years, I had to replace it
review_body: 25 years in my pocket, it's cut through and fixed everything. I lost it last month....to the TSA. I would still be carrying it if I didn't have to surrender it. Yesterday, i bought the replacement Spartan. Same knife as the original except that it has a tweezers and toothpick. I'm hoping for another 25 for this one.

product_title: Nalgene Tritan 32oz Wide Mouth BPA-Free Water Bottle
review_body: I bought this bottle to replace a metal bottle that i kept denting when going to work. So far this hasn't dented and i don't really expect it to. Volume markings are nice and let me keep track of the amount of water i've consumed. product_title: Suisse Sport Adventurer Sleeping Bag
review_body: I bought it for less than 40 bucks on Amazon, and had my doubts. When it arrived it seemed larger than in the product description, but still fit well in my backpack with plenty of room for other equipment. I've only used it once so far, which was last night, but so far I'm very happy with it. It did it's job well, and now I'm confident that I can rely on it again in the future. I still take a hand woven Mexican traveling blanket with me, for lining if it's cold, or to lay down on the ground if there are sharp rocks since I'm not sure how well the sleeping bag will deal with sharp rocks.... but overall I'm very happy.     The only significant discomfort I found in this sleeping bag is that the shape can be a bit restricting. I'm 5'7, weighing 195 lbs. I expected the legs and feet to be restricted a bit, but the bigger problem was my arms and shoulders. A portion of the night I had to sleep with the bag open and my arms outside. When it got colder though I was more than happy to bring my arms in and zipper up. I really like that I can close everything up leaving just a bit of room to see and enough room to breath comfortably out of.

product_title: Victorinox Swiss Army Classic SD Pocket Knife, Hunter Green, 58mm
review_body: The perfect entry level pocket knife for people of all walks of life. With scissors, tweezers, a toothpick (which is in fact disposable; replacements can be ordered quite cheaply from the Victorinox web site), nail file, screwdriver/nail cleaner, and basic blade, this is a durable, reliable, and--dare I say it?--stylish accessory that will serve you well whether you're in a pinch for some simple tools or just trying to keep your appearance neat. I've had my own for almost a decade; the one I purchased from Amazon was a gift for a friend. It's incredible how often you'll find yourself saved from the trouble of running to the kitchen or basement and reaching into your pocket instead. But what I like the best about this knife over others is the look. With this size and style you won't be self conscious about taking out your knife in the office or on a busy street, whereas bigger blades and more intimidating designs have the potential to put the user in awkward situations. It's only a few inches long, but if you're looking for a helpful knife to carry around in almost any everyday setting, the Victorinox Classic is your best friend.

Cons:
(none so far)

product_title: Global Vision Eyewear Escort Safety Glasses
review_headline: Tough to find tinted "over the glasses" safety glasses
review_body: For those of us who wear corrective lenses, HAVING sunglasses, period, is a big issue.  There are a lot of solutions out there that just don't work that well.    -  Clip-ons suck.  They never fit right, and they allow too much light in from the sides.  -  Prescription sunglasses are expensive.  I'm tough on glasses, and will easily break or lose them  -  Regular sunglasses don't fit correctly on top of corrective lenses  -  Auto-tinting lenses are never quite at the correct light level.    The solution I've used for years is to wear tinted safety glasses over my glasses, and this works EXTREMELY well.    I decided on safety glasses about 10 years ago, when I found a pair of AO safety lenses whose wrap-around design fit around my normal frames, and coincidentally had a \\"notch\\" in the lenses that allowed the hinge of my frames to protrude.    I went through NUMEROUS pairs of these AO safety lenses over a period of about 9 years, always glad that I had a new pair ready to go.  I had stocked up on them, so that as they got lost, broke, or wore out, I always had a new pair.    I finally ran out of my \\"stash\\" of old-style AO glasses last year, and needed something new because AO no longer makes that design.  I spent 6+ months looking, and finally bought two pairs of these on Amazon, one smoked, one yellow.    THESE ARE EXCELLENT glasses.  They fit cleanly around corrective lenses without significantly limiting field of view, while blocking light from bleeding around the sides, DRAMATICALLY enhancing visibility.  If I have to cut, grind, or solder something, it's nice to either not have to switch glasses, or just flip down my safety glasses.  Since they are \\"high impact\\" (Z87.1+ ... the \\"plus\\" is high-impact), I use them as shooting glasses.  These are the best all-around sunglasses / tinted safety glasses I've ever had.    Both of my sons have the OCC-style AO safety / sunglasses, and my younger son wears corrective lenses.  Needing something that allows him to wear corrective lenses for sports, he asked me to get him a pair of these as well.

product_title: Sigma BC 1609 STS Double Wireless Bicycle Speedometer
review_headline: Needs more range for taller folk
review_body:
I was unable to get this unit to work properly on my large frame bike.

The instructions specify a maximum range (90cm) between the speedometer pickup and the handlebar head unit. For those (like me) who do a lot of riding on a trainer, the pickup needs to be on a rear wheel... and that really pushes the 90cm distance.

I'm 6'8, and ride a custom frame. The closest I could achieve was about 92 cm.

As a result, the head unit gets intermittent signals from the pickup. There are frequent \\"freezes\\" when the velocity doesn't read correctly, and the odometer doesn't advance. Then, after an interval of 10 - 120 seconds, the odometer updates in one big jump. The velocity also jumps around, typically at a unit fraction (1/2 or 2/3) of the actual velocity. After an hour of riding, the mileage is less than it should be, perhaps 10% less.

The cadence unit has similar difficulties. Frequent \\"zero\\" displays, infrequent updating of the cadence...

For those of you who are normal sized people, feel free to buy it. It's a solid unit, installs easily. The instructions were easy to follow.

Would it have been so hard to give the units an additional 30cm or so of range? Or perhaps a Min/Max button, trading off battery life for increased output?

I feel a little guilty giving it only 3 stars. After all, it probably works great for normal folks. But we larger people exist too, and the engineers shouldn't have designed it to such a close tolerance.
