product_title: Deluxe Party Tent, Sun Shelter 20ft x 12ft in Green
review_headline: Party tent- this was a great deal
review_body: I was looking for a lighter colored tent, since the party was going to be held on one of the hottest days of the summer in an already hot year.  The reviews for what appeared to be an identical light tan tent were uniformly horrible, so I looked at this dark green one, which had gotten excellent reviews.  They were right.  I had a helper (that is a necessity) but though I expected more time, it took us less than an hour to set it up.  It became very breezy in the afternoon,with no effect on the tent.  It's size is perfect for a few tables, an outdoor birthday party, a crab feast, any kind of cookout, and provides shade and protection from insects if needed.  When we took it down, it fit easily in the huge storage bag included, with room to spare. We took it down in about 1/2 hour, again,much less time than expected.  I think this will be a family favorite for years to come, and I have already had requests to borrow the tent for fall gatherings.  Well worth the cost.

product_title: Stanley Outdoor Vacuum Drink-Thru Bottle 16 ounce/  473ml
review_headline: ...but will it last? (answer: nope) - STAY AWAY
review_body: Expensive for a vacuum bottle - is it worth it?  Here's my take: the design appears to be excellent, though it took me a while - and several disassemblies and reassemblies of the complicated lid - to figure out how to use it and clean it. As advertised, it closes with a secure click and appears watertight.  It does a fine job keeping hot things hot, cold things cold.  But it's made in China -- not known for high-quality consumer goods -- and at this price, I might have expected Japanese, European, or even USA manufacture.  So I'm looking skeptically at this complicated lid mechanism and wondering how long it'll last.  Now here's the hooker - it has the lifetime guarantee, meaning that -- like certain other consumer goods of high-quality manufacture (think Sears Craftsman tools or Jansport packs) -- you can send back the defective part at any time and get a free replacement.  So my bet is that this is the new corporate strategy for higher-end consumer goods - make 'em in China but offer to replace parts as they give out, and it'll still be cheaper for the corporation than having them manufactured someplace where workers get a fairer share.  That said, as of right now I'm happy with it.  ------------------  UPDATE: after several months' using this bottle almost daily, I'm upgrading its rating.  I've finally got the lid figured out.  It has performed perfectly, it never leaks, it's actually easy to clean once you're comfortable with how the parts fit together.  I suspect that the people who report its leaking have it assembled incorrectly.  I'm very pleased with it and plan for it to be the last Thermos-type bottle I ever buy (assuming I don't lose it).  -----------------  SECOND UPDATE (9/23/10): Answer to lead question is no, it won't last.  The plastic part which threads the cap into the bottle has disintegrated.  It has had no more stress than regular daily use.  I will say that I called Stanley's toll-free number, got a human right away, and they are sending a replacement cap without any fuss, no return or receipt required.  So I'm downgrading the rating; if you want to use this thing for the long haul, be ready to call for a replacement cap every 6-12 months or so.  ----------------  THIRD UPDATE (11/4/10): So today the replacement lid broke - again, it was the main part of the lid, the one with the handle attached, and again a small part of the plastic just disintegrated - this time it comprised the edge of one of the locking tabs, so it won't lock anymore and therefore is useless.  I've called for another replacement lid, but this is getting old.  I've downgraded my rating again.    ---------------  FOURTH UPDATE(11/15/10): Third replacement lid in place, and now the vacuum is apparently gone - cold iced coffee warms up in about an hour.  I'm going to request a replacement, but as of now I'm downgrading its rating as low as it'll go.  BEWARE THIS PRODUCT!  A HIGH-PRICED, POORLY-MANUFACTURED FAILURE.

product_title: Outdoor Designs Summit Pro Mittens - Black, Small
review_body: I got tired of having freezing fingers with gloves so I decided to try wearing mittens when I walk my dog.  The difference is profound and I'm so happy I got these.  My hands and all my fingers stay warm in freezing and even windy weather.  I think they are very well made and bet they will last for years.  These mittens already survived my dog's sneaky trip under the bed to use them as a chew toy.  This dog cracks whole coconuts in her mouth but didn't manage a single hole in the mittens.  She did chew off a buckle but I didn't use it before that so I don't miss it.  I should have gotten these years ago and saved myself so much misery.

product_title: InStep Safari Swivel Wheel Double Jogger
review_body: When I had ordered this stroller  it was on back order & I had waited a month to get it.  I am so glad I waited! It is the BEST stroller ever! I have a 1 year old & (very tall) 3 year old & they LOVE this stroller! It is the only double I seen that had trays for children & mom & seperate sun shades for each child. It rides smooth & I have not 1 single complaint about this stroller! You will not be dissapointed, I promise! :)

product_title: Allen Sports 102S Premium 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack
review_body: Just finished my first trip with the Allen bike rack.  It worked great!  Mounts on the back of our 2006 Accord and hauled two bikes 1300 miles.  No problems whatsoever.  A great product.

product_title: Coleman Rechargeable Portable Blender and Lid
review_body: We got this to take out on the boat and make blender drinks with ice - always important when the heat index is 110.  It is a little heavy and we use an ice bucket to stabilize it, but works GREAT!.  We went with the heavier one that will blend whole ice cubes and make a greater amount.  This item a must for hurricane parties -- with or without the hurricane.

product_title: Coleman 2000020931 1-Burner Low-Profile Stove
review_body: Great single-burner stove with large cooking area and powerful flame.  Very happy with it.

product_title: Terry Men's Cite Y Gel Saddle Black
review_headline: good for the price but not leather
review_body: I have Terry seats on each of my three bikes. This is an excellent design and comfortable, however the price keeps going up. I got my first one, leather, in 2001 for $24, another leather one in 2005 for $40 and my first Cite Y (artificial) in 06 for about $30. It lasted only 2.5 years even though I use it less than the others which are still fine. It cracked, so I bought a replacement -- $40. I would have preferred a leather one, but at $80, it costs  more than the bike (which I got used). A good product, but high in price and not as durable as I would like. (I weigh 180lbs, so the short life-span is probably not due to excessive weight).

product_title: Wenger Lugano 16- by 10-Foot Two-Room Eight-Person Family Tent with Canopy
review_body: This tent goes up quickly and is very sturdy.  So far we have not camped out in the rain, so I cannot attest to watertightness.  The first time we took down the tent, we got the folding instructions wet and could not use them again, consequently we had some problems fitting the entire tent, stakes and all back into the bag.  The instructions to put up the tent are on the tag, sewn into the bag, so they don't get lost or ruined.  If you're camping with a family or a group, this tent is very spacious.   It even comes with a door mat... :)

product_title: Airhead VISE Wakeboard Binding
review_body: This may be a dumb question, but is this just for one boot?  Or is it the pair?  I know it just says binding and not bindings but its not clear.     Let me know.

product_title: Yakima KingJoe 2-Bike Trunk Rack
review_body: I purchased the Yakima King Joe 2 after heavily considering the advantages and disadvantages of this vs. a roof rack.  Ultimately, it came down to my estimated frequency of use (intermittent) and the cost (~5x less than a new roof rack).  I use this rack for short jaunts (< 10 miles) twice per month and have used once on a long road trip of 1000+ miles each way.  During the long road trip, the rack held up quite well and I did not observe any loosening of the straps.      The foam pads are fairly robust and support the weight of the rack.  I didn't see any scratches on my paint from the pads but I made sure to clean the trunk surface very well before installing.  I also used painters tape to cover the edges where the clips contact the car and did not see any scratches from the metal clips.     My major knock on this rack is the adjustable frame supports.  These are the plastic pieces that contact and hold the bike frame in place.  These supports are able to move up and down the arms of the bike rack and sometimes the bikes will end up at different angles than what you put them on at.  Other than that, I have been satisfied with my purchase.    This bike rack is a great choice for you if you: want bike-transporting ability and don't have $700 to outfit a roof rack, want to be able to remove your bike rack on occasion, are not an idiot and can read instructions, have sufficient arm strength to tighten the straps of the rack to hold it in place.

product_title: Quik Shade Canopy Weight Plate Set
review_headline: A MUST if you own a pop up tent!
review_body: NO more tie downs or staking into the ground, just use these universal weights! I bought mine at Dicks Sporting store. The good thing about these weights is that they are universal- which means you can use them for any pop up tent- and they are easy to cart around. You must have some form of a tie down or weights for these kinds of tents because they will blow away with the slightest burst of wind!  I learned the hard way so you didn't have to. Hope this helps :)

product_title: Columbia Cougar Flats II 15-Foot by 10-Foot 8 Person 2 Room Family Cabin Dome Tent
review_body: Columbia Cougar Flats II 15x10 2 Room is a fantastic tent. Decided to write a review following another great camping trip with a friend who owns this tent. We camp together every summer a few times. This last time we had quite a bit of rain.   * This tent is easy to put up. My friend follows the directions.   * We love the bay windows which allow you to have them open when it rains  * Very roomy. We sleep in the one room with another half to store items  * The screened in area we put our two chairs and a table and played cards during the rain  * The only problem we had was that some water accumulated under the tent and came in through one of the floor seams.  + The fly over the tent is great for diverting the rain away from the tent  * I like the storage pockets on either side of the tent.  * We like the loft for storing items overhead.  * The option of having the dividing walls open or closed is nice.  * Have not had the poles break in the bays as some have  We highly recommend this tent.

product_title: Topeak Road Morph G Mini Pump
review_body: I purchased this pump a little over a year ago. Since then I have used it on AT LEAST one tire a day. Many times I would go through my entire fleet and air all the tires up within the same hour. The pump gets warm, but not hot like some pumps do. This pump has held up great. My last mini pump had issues getting over 90 pounds into a tire and the foot rest broke off the first time I used it. This pump will put well over 90 pounds in and the foot rest is still as good as new. Very durable pump.    It works flawlessly on both types of valves. Takes less than 20 seconds to change to the opposite style of valve. It fits both valves snugly and securely. I keep this pump attached to my commuter at all times and it has never bounced out of its bracket. It's light weight, so I don't even notice it being there.    The only negative I have is that on rare occasions the pressure gauge will stick until you put another 5 pounds or so in. This is a minor inconvenience at most, so it doesn't affect my 5 star rating.    Over all, this is an amazing pump. So amazing that I ordered 2 more today. You can't go wrong with this pump.

product_title: Guide Gear Director's Chair with Side Table
review_body: This purchase was probably on of the smoothest internet buying experience that I can recall. I was told it would take 3 to 6 days for delivery, would you believe the next day! The camp chairs were everything that I was led to believe. Comfortable, ease of set up and fold up, easy to get out of, and the very handy side table. Five stars isn't enough I would give it 10 stars out of ten easy.

product_title: Pacific Evolution Girls' Mountain Bike (20-Inch Wheels)
review_body: It looks nice and the quality is pretty good. I bought this for my 8 year old daughter and she is quite happy with it. The only problem she got with it is that the shifting wheel is hard to turn for her.

product_title: Heat Factory Fleece Face Mask for use with Hand Heat Warmers
review_body: this face mask is great for shoveling snow in the winter, it keeps your face warm.

product_title: Princeton Tec Corona 8 LED Headlamp
review_body:
Well thats what my wife calls me now. I have always been a serious flashlight guy and have or have had all the best streamlight and surefire lights. This thing is awesome. It takes some tweaking to get the fit just right, or it could be my huge head Im not sure. Anyway when you do get fit right it its just so cool. It is nothing short of liberating to have your hands free to do other things. Ok now for performance it is sooo much brighter than I ever thought it would be. I was thinking awhile back on getting an led light for my bicycle, now this will work just great as it throws a huge amount of light. what like 80 or 85 lumens, that is the same as surefires new led two cells; and for much less cash. The great part is that you can cut the power down as well as shut off leds until you find the light you are comfortable with. It is also very efficient with power. I use rechargeables for most my stuff and am still using the batteries it came with a few weeks ago. Use it everyday for something. What sold me was the reveiw on here of the medic in the military who uses this headlight in total darkness to set up medical field units, and now I can see how you coiuld. Also made in USA. I am also thinking about getting one of Princetons 4 led versions (lighter) with the red lens that slides up for stealth missions like hunting my reading glasses without annoying the wife more than usual. Warning... On high mode you do attract alot of flying creatures because you have a beakon on your forehead.
Get it you will not be sorry.

UPDATE 7-9-2013 Still going strong and use it all the time.

product_title: KRYPTONITE KryptoFlex 7 ft. Cable
review_body: This cable along with a mini U-lock is good for low-crime areas and only for a couple hours at a time. The 7 foot length is great to go through the saddle rails, front wheel and the frame. I wouldn't leave it overnight though. The inherent problem with using a security cable with a U-lock is that once the U-lock is broken there goes everything else. I've since moved on to using a keyed cable lock to go along w/ my mini U-lock for leaving my bike overnight on the street.

product_title: Klean Kanteen 40 oz. Sling
review_body: I decided to get away from plastic containers for health and environmental reasons.  Threw away all the Lexan and bought a few of these.  In all it does what it is supposed to do - it will carry your drink and not leak.  There are definitely things that could have been done better, though.  For one the cap - it is unnecessarily difficult to screw on.  The threads are just too loose and it does not go on smoothly.  Next, the cap has no way to be secured to the bottle when it is off and is very easy to lose for that reason.  I can't even count how many times I have misplaced the cap already.  How hard would it have been for them to put a little plastic loop attaching this to the neck of the bottle?  Also, the mouth is rather small.  Yes, it will take an ice cube...one at a time, but the Lexans have much wider mouths making it considerably easier to get ice in.  I wish they had a size that was closer to one liter.  This is just too big to be handy lugging around everywhere.  Finally, there is no insulation at all.  The thin stainless steel conducts cold away rapidly so drinks do not stay cold very long.  the Lexans seemed to be better at that.  I all I don't think I would buy this again unless the design comes along and they fix some of these issues.

product_title: Kelty K.I.D.S. TC 1.1 Transit Child Carrier
review_body: I'm pleased with this product. It's relatively easy to get the child in and out, it's comfortable for both wearer and the child, and the backpack has PLENTY of space for me to pack some diapers, wipes, a change of clothes for each child, my wallet, phone, and camera, and a small lunchbag. I'm currently using it with a 15 month old on walks and trips and even on public transportation. Much easier then taking a single or double stroller.     He tends to fuss when I first try to put him in, but once he's in it and on my back he's very comfortable and happy. He sat in it for over an hour today while the three of us (me, him in the pack, and his 3 year old brother walking) went for a walk to the library and back. The library is 3/4 of a mile away, and he was very content to sit and look at the scenery.    It's nice that it gives the child a view other then your back, and they have their own \\"space\\" so they are not pressed right up against you. They can move, play with some toys (toy loops are included) or you can attempt to latch a sippy cup to the toy loops so they can have a drink without sending the cup sailing into the street or onto other people.  Also, I can reach back and access the cupholders. Nice when you're walking and everyone needs a drink.    Some negatives - as someone else commented if the child gets sleepy they will end up doing the head-bob, and if they fall asleep they will end up uncomfortably sagging in one direction or another.     No accessible front pocket for holding keys or your phone. You'll have to keep those things in your pocket, or use some other system with the carrier. Also, in order to access the contents of the backpack you'll obviously have to remove the backpack. The child can remain in the pack, but you'll have to set them against a firm surface and keep a hand on them so that they don't tip over.    Some tips:     Be careful not to overpack, as the maximum weight for this carrier is 30 pounds total (child and gear). Newer models have a maximum weight of 40 pounds.    When putting a child in the pack, I set it on a couch, using pillows to help support it. Also, pack it beforehand as the weight will help keep it upright (and it's difficult to pack it up with a squirmy child in it).     You'll have to play with the adjustment of the straps. Adjust it on yourself first, then your child. It took some playing around with to get us to be both comfortable and snug. Make sure the waist belt is tight and snug, as that will support the majority of the weight and you'll have less weight on your shoulders.     It's not for long extended trips or hardcore backpacking. It is more suitable for day trips, trips to the fair or market, walks, etc.    I'm only 5 feet tall, but felt comfortable wearing this carrier. Unlike newer models, this model does NOT have torso adjustment which could make fitting tricky for people who are extremely tall or extremely short. Also, I felt comfortable with the little one on my back in the Kelty and could move freely and even pick up his brother (who is petite like me, but still a 3 year old). This came in handy when his brother got tired of walking and needed a short break. I wouldn't recommend doing this if you're not strong enough though, for obvious reasons. Just saying that I felt comfortable doing so, and I didn't feel that it jeopardized the safety of the littler one.    Honestly, I don't think this model is made anymore as it's been replaced by newer models. But, if you happen to find it used or on sale from some outlet (as I did) hopefully this review helps.

product_title: SALE FIRE STARTER
review_headline: Truly a prime example of a RIP OFF!!!
review_body: I have never been so disappointed in any item I've purchased anywhere as I have been with this miserable excuse for a lighter. I had one of these types of lighters years ago and carried it for quite some time and it performed admirably, but these units are an abomination and should not be offered to anyone who thinks they would be acquiring a product that should work or last. The wires in the wick do not work properly nor do they have enough strength to last. Striking to light is an impossibility and they leak horribly. Do not buy!!!

product_title: Coghlan's Bug Jacket
review_body: I haven't used a bug jacket previously.  But I took a trip to Churchill, Manitoba in July and I had heard it could get pretty buggy.  When I got there, very, very buggy would be more accurate.  I used this bug jacket on half a dozen days and I was very pleased with the results.  No mosquito or flies got through.  (Flies are called 'bulldogs' up there and the name fits).  Overall, I would recommend this jacket.

product_title: Giro Xen Bike Helmet
review_body: I finally had to replace my cheap 6-year-old Louis Garneau helmet. After looking at reviews at  [...], I decided to spring for the Giro Xen.  I first tried on a Giro helmet at a local bike shop, to gauge the size. After ordering it on Amazon, it arrived across the border within 3 days!  The Xen is superior to the Garneau in almost every way -- comfort, styling, and especially ventilation.  I chose the Matt Chalk/White Weathered Camo, as the lighter tones won't heat up as quickly in the summer sun, and they are  a bit more visible on the road than some of the darker colours. Recommended!

product_title: Schwinn High-Density Foam Mountain Saddle
review_headline: Excellent choice regardless of the price
review_body: I ordered 2 of these for my kids' bikes.  I was very impressed with the item right out of the box.  The design is very high tech and sturdy, yet soft enough.  I have not seen seats like these installed on any new bikes.  They exceed standard bike seat quality.  The installation was very easy and took a few minutes.  In our case I did not need to make any adjustments and they both went in at the correct angle the first time.  I tested both bikes with the new seats and was very impressed with the exact comfort.  The kids love them too.  I highly recommend this item and at this price I don't think you can go wrong.  The only word of caution would be that someone else complained it was too small for them.  I think for a standard-weight person there shouldn't be any such issue.

product_title: Klean Kanteen 40 oz. Sling
review_body:
Every thing about this 40-ounce bottle is great!. but for one thing....
When you walk around with it it bounces around and would be better if it had another strap to go around you to keep it steady. Other then that. It's Aces.............

product_title: Foam Maverick Pogo Stick
review_headline: Fun, but a little hard for a 7 year old
review_body: This pogo stick is a little hard to work, which makes it difficult for anyone under 75 pounds or so to make it jump.

product_title: Surly Track Cog
review_body: Great cog. I'll probably stick with Surly's for the rest of the time I have my current bike. Works great with the Surly lockring. Takes a beating and rides smooth.

product_title: Laken ISO 70 Insulated Water Bottle
review_body: The bottle does a good job of keeping the water cold.  I like all the laken bottles I've bought.  I guess the only thing that detracts from this bottle for me is that it doesn't come in a 1 liter size.  Or, 16.9 oz size.  I use those drink packets alot with my bottles and I have to either leave a little water out, or let the drink mix be diluted out because of the bottle size.  Not a big deal really, but just one little thing that detracts from it.  Otherwise, it's a well made bottle, wide mouthed making it easy to drink from and add ice to, and keeps drinks cold.  I drink so much water it never stays in the bottle long so I can't tell you how long it keeps water cold.

product_title: Schwinn Coronado Men's Comfort Bike (26-Inch Wheels)
review_body: I've purchased this bike for almost three months and ride it everyday to school (about 5 miles round trip with a deep uphill on each way). It's a good bike with decent build and nice look. Occasionally I hear compliments of this bike on the street. And in the past three months it had no problems except one flat. As a short-distance commuter it does a good job.    But this bike has the following weaknesses:    * It came half-assembled. This is not a problem for me because I assemble furniture and computers at home all by myself. But you have to buy tools to do the job (I bought an allen wrench set and a 10-inch adjustable wrench for $15 and these are all I need to assemble the bike). And you have to be careful on each screw because Amazon may have installed some screws but left them loose. If you are not experienced in assembling bikes you'd better take it to a local bike shop for setup. Count these extra expenses in your budget.    * I'm 5'7\\" and the seat is a bit too high for me even if I lower it to the minimum. I had to take out the plastic stick in the seat post and cut short about 2 inches so that the seat can be further lowered to fit me.    * It's too heavy at about $38 pounds. This makes it impossible to ride as fast as those road racers. Again, this is not a problem for me because I'm not a racer anyway and the weight gives me good exercise even in the short-distance commute. Instead, I have another problem: I live in an apartment in upper Manhattan NYC on the 5th floor with no elevator. Carrying this bike to the 5th floor in the narrow staircase everyday is really a pain.    * The brake is not really responsive. So you can't go down a deep hill to enjoy high speed.    I'd say I'm generally satisfied with the purchase ($240 including shipping) although I later realized I might have paid $20-30 more than its actual value. I recently bought a Marin Belvedere road bike for $300 incl. shipping from another online store for my wife which has higher-quality partsand includes aluminum fenders and LED light at 10 pounds lighter. If I have another chance to choose my bike I'd buy myself a Marin Belvedere unless the Shwinn Coronado is priced at $210 or lower including shipping.

product_title: Schwinn Scorcher Boys' Bike (16-Inch Wheels)
review_body: Our son received this bike for his 4th birthday and is in love with it.  So far, so good.

product_title: Planet Bike Protege 9.0 Wireless Bike Computer, Black
review_headline: Great product, great price. Mount is not good
review_body: I installed this on my Recumbent Trike, and it works great. The installation was pretty straight forward, all you had to do was read the directions and follow them. It was easy to program, much easier than my last computer, a Trek, and the display has everything you would need to know during a ride. I had no trouble aligning the magnet and transmitter, and actually got it first shot after about 1 minute of adjusting.     My one concern was, would this work in combination with a Polar Heart rate Monitor, because I have had other wireless computers where the computer and the heart rate monitor interfered with each other. I put my Polar unit on, fired up the computer, and there was no interference from one to another. Excellent product at a great price.    I revised this review after 1 year. The mount is problematic on this computer. Many times, when carrying my trike, the computer would fall out of the mount if I just brushed it the wrong way.  This past weekend, on a 20 mile ride, I looked down and the computer was gone. I rode back to the starting point, but never found it. I replaced it with a Cateye Enduro, which has a mount that securely locks the computer in position. I did not think it was a good idea to get another PB 9.0, thinking that it would be only a matter of time, before I lost another one.

product_title: Bolle Nova Goggle
review_body: i missed it, but i don't see no darn modulation to these lenses.  seems like a gimmick.  and i'm the sucker that got gotten.  at least i got em for like $25!  haha     no fog, no problems.

product_title: MSR MiniWorks EX Microfilter
review_body:
I purchased this product upon the strong recommendation of my brother, who has extensive backcountry hiking and camping experience. The filter is simple to use, pumps quickly, and is very easy to disassemble, clean, and reassemble.

Unlike some other reviewers I feel it's sufficiently robust, especially considering it's relatively light. Keep in mind it requires regular cleaning and drying for optimal performance.

My only request (and a minor one, at that) would be for the little instruction guide to be printed on waterproof paper.

product_title: Outdoor Products Firefly External Frame Pack
review_body:
This is a perfect pack for a person just getting into camping/hiking. The only reason i say this is because of its size. I can pack enough materials (including food and water) for about three-four days. If your going to be out longer it may be difficult.

Very sturdy! VERY VERY COMFY! Has flaps over all the zippers for added water protection.

Though the double water bottle design is a little bit of a let down, its slanted to allow you to easily get at them but that just makes it easier for the water bottle to fall out, lol.

product_title: Strider ST-2 PREbike Balance Running Bike
review_body: Our 2.5 yo daughter has mastered the tricycle, but isn't quite ready for a 'big' bike. The Strider bike is perfect for her. She gets around easily, and it's a great energy-burner! Several of our neighbors used these with their younger kids, and raved about them. We are very pleased with our purchase.

product_title: Stansport Aluminum Percolator Coffee Pot
review_body: Difficult to find a pot of this size anywhere without paying a fortune. Now we won't have to make so many pots of coffee in the morning at camp.Great price--great product.  Thanks amazon.

product_title: Cloud-9 Cruiser Select Airflow ES, 11.25" x 9"
review_body: This seat was really quite comfortable, even on longish rides (40 miles or so is my limit) and was great for my 7 mile commutes.  It didn't last forever, alas, as its suspension bar on the bottom snapped at the bracket leaving me with a rather lopsided seat.  This was after a bit over a year of steady biking on rough pavement (and a not-so-small rider at 195lb), so perhaps the 1300 miles I got out of it is not unreasonable.  I've ordered up another one, which indicates my satisfaction...  Update: Yep, this seems to have a 1300 mile survival time.  This seat broke the same way as the last (and at the same mileage) and again I have ordered a replacement...

product_title: Blantex XK-3 Heavy Duty Steel Folding bed with 2-1/2-Inch Mat
review_body: I bought this folding bed. I am not at all happy with this bed. I do not recommend this bed. Many reviews says it is very sturdy. This is not correct. The frames are very fragile and can bend any time with slightest stress. The four legs are not fixed properly and hence may bend and collapse with slightest movement of weight. The bed platform is made up of metal mesh. These mesh are not firm and hence one will get a feeling that they are sleeping in a narrow hole. One cannot easily move or twist their body. If you sleep more than 4 or 5 years you will get body ache. I am afraid on a long term use one will get orthopedic problems.

product_title: Schwinn Free Runner LT Jogging Stroller (Blue/Black)
review_headline: Nice but didn't get any instructions
review_body: The stroller is great, but we didn't receive any instructions with it and we could tell it was an already opened and re-taped box.  Had to go online to find the instructions which took a while and still not sure how to use a few of the extras it has.  Overall the stroller works great, my husband and I like it and our baby does as well, the fact that it was an already opened item and then didn't even come with the instructions was very upsetting.  I have sent an email into Amazon and have not heard back from them yet, it has been almost 3 weeks.

product_title: Board Dudes Magnetic Dry Erase Surfboard, Includes 6 Magnets, Design and Color May Vary (17070UA-4)
review_body: Ordered this for my daughters \\"Surfer Girl\\" themed bedroom.   They offer it in pink and blue but don't give the customer the choice.  Called their customer service line and they simply stated \\"you get what you get!\\"  I took my chances hoping and praying it would be pink........it was blue!   Did the return/replacement option stating that I wanted to exchange it for pink.  Won't allow it.   I don't understand why it's so difficult to set up the product so that customers have the choice of color!!  You'd think they'd try to accommodate their customers.   Very irritating!

product_title: Seattle Sports E-Pod Dry Pocket (Carbon)
review_body: The online info says waterproof, the packaging says splash resistant... two entirely different things if you are going to be taking it in a canoe or kayak where you can tip.  Tested the product just to be sure.  The cloth seams used to attach the fabric backing and the clear window leaks water creating harmful fogging inside the pouch.  Package arrived yesterday, it is back in the mail today.

product_title: Mirrycle MTB Bar End Mountain Bicycle Mirror
review_body:
Ordered two mirrors.
One was cracked. Messaged shipper, without even request of product sent a replacement.
Still sent broken one back.

product_title: Planet Bike Men's A.R.S. Anatomic Relief Bicycle Saddle
review_body: This seat is actually identical to the Bell Sports Mountain Bike Saddle except for the covering. Bell is available at [...] for couple bucks less (I bought both not realizing) and may prove more durable due to the tougher material for the covering. As for comfort, they are identical. No significant sit bone discomfort and certainly no crotch pressure but unless you are used to narrow seats, it does feel like its not wide enough to support your butt. I expect this seat to perform well and last a while. (NOTE: this seat does not come with a seat clamp - minus 1 star)

product_title: STOP Flats2 MTB Bicycle Tire Liner
review_body: These liners seem well built, although I had a flat about a week after I installed them.It seems hard to keep the liners centered when installing tube, therefore I think the liner was not centered properly when I hit a shard of glass it went right to the tube.  There might be a secret to installing them that I don't know about.

product_title: Dakine Mens ON White
review_body: i want to buy this product but the seller's coment says that is a 6'6\\" bag and the amazon descriptions says this is a 6'3\\" bag, so someone could tell me whats the real size thank you

product_title: Kelty Shadehouse
review_body: I was looking for a sun/rain shelter for family car camping. I chose this product because of the advertised size (12' x 12') and the unique design which looked quite stable as well as attractive.  In spite of many other reviewers' complaints about the difficulty of assembly, I bought the Kelty Shadehouse and two side walls.    The other reviewers were right! It was extremely difficult to put up. We are experienced campers, Boy Scouts, and Scout leaders. Even with the numerous suggestions from other reviewers, which did help with assembly since the directions included are incomplete and confusing, it took almost an hour of trial and error to erect the shelter.     Then we discovered the space and size issues. In order to get 12' x 12' of space under the shelter, the center height is around 5 feet tall, the openings even lower. We had to duck to get inside, and I could not stand up except at the very center.  In order to raise the height, we bent the side poles in a tighter arc which effectively decreased the floor space to about 8' x 10'. Then we discovered the side walls, which thanks to another reviewer I knew only fit 2 of the 4 sides, hung about 18\\" off the ground.    I gave the two stars because the shelter is well-made of quality materials, it is attractive, stable in the wind and it does repel water.     I returned the shelter and bought a Swiss Gear shelter, side walls, and screen kit. I am very happy with the Swiss Gear product.

product_title: Xboard Illuminators LED Lighted Risers
review_body: These are alot of fun, I got a pair and they really are very bright. After a few weeks of use they are still working well, but the build quality is not 5 star. Its not that they are poorly built, just not quite as husky as they should be. If you are putting these on a longboard they will last alot longer due to the fact that you wont be thrashing on them as hard. Deff worth the price!

product_title: Sportz SUV Tent with Screen Room
review_body: This tent set up easily with two people. It is high quality with durable zippers. It is easy to drive away from and return to. The hookup to the van was simple and quick. We used it with a 2004 Mercury Monterey Premier and it fit perfectly. It is luxurious tent camping to be able to sleep in the back of the van and have the tent for room and eating when wet. I would recommend this to all minivan people. Shipping was very fast.

product_title: Osprey Airporter LZ Duffle
review_body: Kept our packs safe as we transported ourselves from Texas to Utah on a recent trip. Plenty of room for a large extended pack. Our only trouble was that the airport security folks removed our airport approved locks. Nothing else was missing.

product_title: Mirrycle Road STI Bicycle Mirror - Only Compatible w/ 2010 or older
review_body: I was very impressed with how easily the mirror mounted and how well it integrates into the brake/shifter hood.  Looks like it belongs.  I travel a lot of fairly high-speed, busy roads, and really wanted this as an \\"early warning system\\" before I have to start thinking about changing lanes or making a left turn.  It is NOT a substitute for looking back before you go, but definitely helps with timing when you want to make a move.  Plus, I want to know if and when I'm about to get run over... just a personal preference.    It does vibrate, but unless you're on a really rough road, it serves it's purpose very well.  I've been experimenting with stem and bar positioning and find the mirror very easy to adjust.    If you don't mind \\"purists\\" scoffing at you, get this mirror.  You'll feel safer, and in my opinion, be safer.  Pedal hard!

product_title: Coleman DayTripper Beach Shade
review_body: This beach tent is the best for price, design, features, and quality. The beach shelters/tents that sell for less are usually not as sturdy and large as this one. Plus the others are depicted more as \\"shelters\\" wheras this one is lite and airy like a shelter but has more tent-like features. In the design description it is the only one I found that can handle light to moderate rain so that was the best selling point for me as it makes a chancey day at the beach worth it. I just climb inside and wait for the drizzle to stop and out comes the sun again.  The ones designed as just shelters let in the rain and have no privacy door.     All the other reviews are fair too except for folks that say it's hard to put together. It is really easy. I do it myself, but it would take half the time with a partner. And yes the wind makes it more difficult to set up but that's why I bring it to the beach in the first place so I can stop getting sand in my mouth/eyes and take a break from the sun. Even have a nice lunch inside sans the sand in my sandwich and the seagulls who swipe my food. The only other option is to check out those \\"pop up\\" versions. But they cost twice the price as the Coleman.    Here are the perks: sturdy for wind and some rain, sun protection 50+, back door can be switched to an open or screened window, clothes drying line in side, large enough for two adults to lay down in even when fully zipped up, roomy enough for entire family of 3 to 4 if you have children.        So bring on the wind and let me enjoy my beach time.  And yes if you are wondering, the front door zips up so there's privacy for changing clothes or whatever else you care to do depending on what beach you are at. Thanks to the other reviewers who recommended this product!

product_title: Table-Mate II Woodgrain Folding Table
review_body: I was hoping for  a tray that would work better with my lazy boy chair and couch as far as holding my laptop but the furniture leg design won't allow for the optimum location but its still nicer than a tippy tv tray

product_title: New 17" LAPTOP Computer Photo Video Digital SLR Camera Backpack Rover BAG AW 200mm LENS All WEATHER
review_body: My laptop and camera fit as advertised, but I am not sure how to secure the tripod so that it will not fall off.  A small manual with a few words and some pictures about securing the tripod would be helpful.

product_title: Blackburn Mars 3.0 Rear
review_body: This small light clips onto my helmet for great visibility. It has 3 settings......access is easy while you ride and my level of safety has gone way up! This light really delivers!

product_title: Origin8 Joe-2-Go Standard Drink Holder Bronze
review_body: Best purchase of 2010 thus far.  I use it every day and I couldn't be happier.  I bike the streets of Minneapolis-let's just say they aren't always exactly smooth-and my coffee has never bounced out of the holder.  I love it!!  I'd also like to note that it can hold a pint of ice cream-barely.

product_title: Razor A2 Kick Scooter
review_body: My kids love this- bought 2 from amazon- my kids 9 and 6 are riding it around the house- enjoying themselves in the winter months. Does not scuff the floors- no damage to anything yet. Great braking mechanism. Best of the christmas presents.

product_title: Schwinn Meridian Adult 26-Inch 3-Wheel Bike
review_body: What a surprise!  I purchased this bike for my wife who lost her inner ear or balance when she was a child.  She has always wanted to ride bike and now she can.  Watching her ride gives me pleasure.  Most importantly, this tricycle has become a way to realize one of her childhood wishes come true.

product_title: Safeguard Home Base Two Person Emergency Preparedness Kit
review_headline: Be Sure to Check Expiration Dates
review_body: The food and water in the kit have 5-year shelf lives, however, the first kit I recieved only had 2 years, 8 months left. I reported the problem to Amazon, and they promptly sent a replacement, but the 2nd kit was the same. Don't waste your time.

product_title: SteriPen Emergency Online Pack
review_headline: Compact solution to a vexing problem
review_body:
Whether caused by earthquakes, hurricanes or other natural disasters, interruptions in the drinking water supply can promote panic and pose a threat to public health. So in an uncertain world, it's nice to have the reassurance of the SteriPen.

The SteriPen uses UV technology to destroy or inactivate microorganisms like bacteria, viruses, algae and mold in contaminated water, theoretically making it safe to drink. I say theoretically because there are some contaminants, such as heavy metals, that are unaffected by UV treatments but the SteriPen does a good job of removing most of the more worrisome contaminants and it does it without the use of chemicals.

The unit itself is small and easy to carry as well as simple to use. Just remember to keep a stock of batteries on hand and you're minutes away from safer drinking water in an emergency.

product_title: Planet Bike 3018-1 Rack Blinky 5- 5 LED Tail Light with Rack Mount and Batteries
review_body: I bought one of these so I could get a mount for my rack but after I installed the light and liked it more than the super flash as it had more lighting I use it now. It is bright but just has two modes, flash and steady but I use the flash mode only, which I think will get you noticed sooner. I like and have several super flash but wanted more lights on the rear of my bike for night riding. I now have three of these lights (not all on the same bike) and would recommend these to others. I have changed all three of my bikes lights over to Planet Bike lights so I can move them from one bike to another if I need to. I have not found anything that I don't like or would change with this light except I wish that they had a Amber replacement lense so I could have a amber rear light. You'll like this light.

product_title: JanSport Elefunk Metro Messenger Bag (Black/Black)
review_body: This is a really big bag. Expect the same quality of a JanSport backpack in a huge sidebag. It has pockets for everything although the outermost pocket is a bit too big to quickly retrieve a ringing cell phone. If you don't have any binders or hard flat items inside, then it'll lose its shape.

product_title: Igloo Pink Ribbon Chilly Wrap 1-Liter Bottle
review_body: The bottle it cute but have to be careful with the lid, it breaks easy and no replacement is available

product_title: Easton EA70 Road Bike Wheel Set (700c, Shimano)
review_body: I love these wheels.  They role great.  I have riddin them on rough and smooth roads.  One thing about easton is that they don't have rider weight limits and being 220 lbs when I got them was great.

product_title: Timbuk2 Outtawhack Day Pack
review_headline: This bag is not for me
review_body: I previously used a Timbuk2 classic messenger that is about 5 years old. I acquired a laptop that was too big for that bag so I researched the Timbuk2 website and settled on this pack. I am writing this review mainly to add a hearty second to the first reviewer.    The bag is the same high-quality construction found in every Timbuk2 bag. It is probably indestructible and would last forever. The design is a fail for me though. I got a large, which said it holds a 17\\" laptop, and a 15.6\\" PC barely fits. A 17\\" Mac fits fine. The volume of the bag is also quite limited. Laptop, a few file folders, a book, and power supply have it stuffed pretty full. This appears to be caused by the \\"narrow\\" design or lack of front-to-back depth. The backpack straps are quite terrible and the first reviewer really nailed the issues with them. For reference, I am 6' and 165 and find the bag just as difficult to carry as the smaller reviewer. Additionally, the included shoulder strap is too short to carry messenger style and I can only use it on one shoulder.    This is a high quality bag that may very well fit many needs, just not mine.

product_title: Park Tool BBB-2 The Big Blue Book of Bicycle Repair - 2nd Edition
review_headline: Best book I've found for maintaning your bike.
review_body: I've found this book to have all the illustrations I need to properly maintain my bike.  The book most frequently recommended on this site, [[ASIN:1579548830 The Bicycling Guide to Complete Bicycle Maintenance and Repair: For Road and Mountain Bikes(Expanded and Revised 5th Edition)]] I've found to be great on theory but horrible for practical applications.    This book, the Big Blue Book, on the other hand has tons of practical applications.  I feel its the perfect book for people who want to spend more time fixing their bikes and less time discussing what angle a fork or seatpost should be at.    One picture that stands out is taking apart the rear hub, how many different types of fittings you can expect to find.  It's very straight forward and something a beginner mechanic definitely needs, and a good reference for anyone of any skill.

product_title: Saris Bones 805 (2-Bike) Trunk Mount Rack
review_body: The Saris bike rack worked out great.  I had borrowed a three bike Saris rack from a friend and decided to get one for myself.  I only needed a rack to carry two bikes so thats what I ordered.  When it arrived I was taken aback by the fact it wasn't quite like my friends although it looked exactly like it in the online picture.  It only had one upper arm rather then two like my friends.  Over wise it was identical.  I almost sent it back but decided to try it out instead.  Glad I did because my concerns about stability with just one upper arm was quickly dispelled.  Great rack, rock solid.

product_title: Spiral Column Windsock, 60"
review_body: For those of us who love wind socks this is perfect!  Good quality, great colors, good, strong tie strings.  Blows out without crossed or knotted tails.

product_title: Coleman Rechargeable Portable Blender and Lid
review_body: I purchased this blender three times hoping I would find one that works, but I ended up returning it to Amazon because they all failed. The battery requires 18 hours to be fully charged, and then it only holds the charge for a few hours at most. When I turned on the blender, it didn't have enough battery power to even start the motor. I called the manufacturer, Coleman, and the representative informed me that the battery does not hold a charge very well and suggested that I return it. I would not recommend this product to anyone!

product_title: NALGENE Tritan OTG BPA-Free Water Bottle 24 Oz
review_headline: I can't say enough good about these bottles!
review_body: I really wanted to stop buying bottled water at the grocery but could never find a bottle that 'worked' for me.  I hate the ones with the built in straws or the lids you had to unscrew to drink from, and especially the sippy cup styles. I carry water with me all the time so they have to be easy to carry, use and clean.  I'll admit I'm picky but after trying about 10-15 different types that were all either a pain to use, or a pain to clean, I had just about given up. With each new one we'd try, we were back to the bottled water within the week. While on a shopping trip about 40 minutes from our home, I ran across these Nalgene water bottles. They looked to have a perfect design to counter everything I hated in previous bottles, they were also sturdy, attractive and reasonably priced.  I decided to try.  My search was over.    These bottles are THE BEST.  I've been using them for about 18 months now and can't imagine using anything else.  Love the finger hole for carrying,. They're the perfect size for my bike/car/gym have a great cover to keep germs at bay. They are ultra easy to wash with no nooks and crannies to wonder if it REALLY got clean.  Dishwasher safe & BPA free too!  We haven't bought bottled water since buying these!  I have mine with me 24/7 and they have held up great. After buying one for each of us in the store we found them and discovering these would be bottles we would actually use, I turned to Amazon to order back-ups.  Even though my original bottle still works great, I did recently order new, \\"fresher\\" ones.  I thought I got my 10 bucks worth and deserved a new one ;) I've even had friends ask me to order some for them since they loved mine so much.  Although have all 3 colors (one for each of us so we don't get them mixed up) my favorite is the green, my icewater looks so refreshing in it!  I hope Nalgene never quits making this style.  Perfect!

product_title: Thule 912XT Roadway 2 Bike Hitch Carrier
review_body: I got this rack when I got a new (small) SUV, and the old trunk-mounted bike rack wasn't compatible. We wanted something a lot sturdier anyway, and this is definitely it. I have complete confidence in the Thule brand -- we didn't even consider another. And this particular rack is the one that works well for us. It's easy to install and remove, and it's very easy to mount your bikes. A couple of well-placed levers make it easy to fold the rack section down when not in use and to slant the whole device back (without the bikes mounted) so you can open the hatch of the SUV. (You can buy longer hitches that keep the bikes farther away from the back of the vehicle if you have a larger SUV.) This is a solid piece of equipment. I did two hours of highway driving with the bikes secured to the rack -- they didn't move! No wobbling, no wheel spinning -- nada! I feel very secure with this rack, and of course, love the fact that we don't have to deal with the inconvenience of a roof rack.    Bear in mind that you need to have a trailer hitch. And if you're going to be leaving your bikes unattended for any length of time, I would definitely recommend locks for the bikes AND for the rack. It's so easy to remove the rack, that a thief could very easily take it and the bikes with very little effort.

product_title: Big Agnes - Sleeping Giant Memory Foam Pillow
review_headline: Back Country Luxury with little added weight
review_body: This pillow is amazing. I use it backpacking every time I go. It is comfortable, adjustable, and hardly weighs anything which makes it perfect for carrying up a mountain.  I use it while on the ground and in a hammock, and with it's foam pad it makes the pillow comfortable even when barely inflated while in the hammock. This pillow is the most comfortable addition to my pack.

product_title: Big Agnes Insulated Air Core Mummy Sleeping Pad
review_body: Although this mattress does not self-inflate, it only takes a few breaths to fill.  Provides much more comfortable sleeping than my 10 yr old therma-rest; I can sleep on my side.  Insulation keeps ground chill & dampness away too.  Also packs small so it stows away easily.

product_title: Brunton 9041 Glow Compass
review_body:
When I opened this package, I immediately thought it looked like a $1 or $2 trinket I could have picked up at dollar store.

I kept it for a day, decided it was nothing special, and told Amazon I wanted to return it.

At that time, I was told by Amazon that I could not return the item because it contained hazardous materials that were against Amazon's Shipping Policy, rendering it non-returnable. I was shocked, because this was ...just a compass! I had to send a couple of emails back and forth with Amazon before being told that the liquid inside the compass is \\"absolute ethyl alcohol\\" - a hazardous item that they would not accept as a return. I am still interested to learn how Amazon managed to ship this in the first place, however.

This item, I feel, is overpriced. Maybe not 1 Star, but this way someone will spot it among the 4 and 5 star reviews that exist for this item.

product_title: Currie Technologies e-Zip E400 Electric Scooter
review_body: This is a great electric scooter for teens, not for adults. It has agressive styling, fat durable wheels and tires and can be used standing up because the seat is removable or in a less agressive seated position. My kids really enjoy the Ezip E400. Currie offers other models like the Ezip 500, 750, 900 and 1000 that are much better suited for young adults through aging boomers like me.

product_title: McNett Folio Cotton Sleep Sack,Single
review_body: I wanted to feel comfortable in hotel rooms but sent this right back after it arrived the fabric was not very nice.

product_title: CamelBak Classic 70 oz Hydration Pack
review_body: I bought this to replace an older and smaller CamelBak that I had. Works great.  Keeps water colder, longer.  I received this for around $10 cheaper that anywhere else I've seen it and for free shipping!

product_title: M-Wave Classic Alloy Bicycle Floor Pump
review_body: The pump was a gift for my husband who loved the last one we had from years ago and it made him really happy. He loves it! He said it was the best gift ever. It was shipped in a timely matter and easy to pay for.

product_title: Thule 430 Tracker II Roof Rack Foot Pack (Set of 4)
review_headline: Pricey, yes but Excellent quality with great warranty
review_body:
When searching for a rooftop rack system to fit on my 2003 Honda CRV, I didn't seem to have too many options. The factory rack was overpriced and not very flexible as there weren't many attachments for it to handle the various types of things I wanted to carry...bikes, canoes, kayaks. I decided to buy the Thule system because of it's great reputation and variety of fittings available for it.

I love my Thule rack. The quality and fit of the foot pack is just amazing. Installation was a breeze and the included plastic covers match the existing roof line nearly perfectly. Once the feet are clicked in place, they are very solid and feel incredibly secure...that's something reassuring when carrying a $3,000 kayak! I would hate to see my kayak flying off my roof at 65mph.

It would be nice if locks were included in the package instead of being an expensive option, but other than that, this is a quality rack system that you cannot go wrong with. Highly recommended.

product_title: Sevylor 1 Person Inflatable Pool Boat
review_headline: Meets my Expectations for Pool Use
review_body: I bought this for my grandchildren to use in our large pool.  It is a perfect size for two small ones, and does all I ask of it.  I imagine one could place up to three small children in the boat for pool use.  I would likely upgrade to a larger size if I was looking for a boat to use in open water.

product_title: DRY PAK Dry Bag with Belt Strap for Cameras, Cell Phones, iPhone, Android, 6" x 5" Blue & Yellow
review_body: Guess when I read \\"dry pack\\" I figured it would be waterproof - it's not.  This pack is big enough to hold a passport but not much more.  The instructions clearly say \\"do not submerge\\" which means that it's use was pretty limited on our vacation.

product_title: Coleman Diamondback Sleeping Bag
review_body: have the item in perfect condition. Have not given it to the recipient yet, so we shall see if it is liked!

product_title: Kenda Kross Plus Front/Rear Slick XC Tire, 26 x 1.95"
review_body: I have this very same tire on the back of my old American made Huffy. With a knobby mountain tire on the front. When this tire arrives from Amazon. Which I just purchased, it will be going on the front. It has an exceptionally smoothe ride to it on pavement. Which is where I do most of my bike riding. Dirt trails are not for this guy. Yet, you can use it for dirt trails. It has a center road tread, and a trail tread on the outside edge of the tire. Gives it some versatility, for those who are adventurous.

product_title: Master Lock Resettable Combo Cable Bicycle Lock (4-foot x 6mm )
review_body: I thought it would be thin but not quite SO thin! It looks not much thicker than my laptop cable lock. I guess you're getting what you paid for, but I wouldn't leave my bike with this lock outside at night or for more than a couple of hours! Also, the number combination area looks very cheap and the actual lock area is plastic too. Probably quite easy to break! Lastly, comes with a preset combination which you cannot change!!     Overall, a thin, cheap lock that's useful for a quick ride to the grocery store but if you're looking for security and peace of mind, stay away!

product_title: Mongoose MG102 Wolf Skateboard
review_body: I bought the skateboard for my nephew's Xmas present. It shipped fast and was in great condition upon receipt.

product_title: Satori Harmony Bi Fold Hemp Wallet
review_body: The wallet seems fine but the design is not the same as what I ordered.

product_title: Kelty Starfish 600 Backpack
review_body: My son and daughter love their packs. Just big enough to carry some essentials. Kids will bite through the bite valve, but you can replace them with Nalgene replacement sheaths (part #2353-0012) 2/$4.00. Not a bad deal.

product_title: Balance Buddy (Adjustable)
review_headline: A very handy accessory which I could not find in local stores.
review_body: If you are serious of getting your kid to bicycle, get rid of the training wheels and use this instead. My kid learnt to cycle within 2 days using the balance buddy.

product_title: Wenzel Omega II/Great Falls Mummy 0-Degree Sleeping Bag with Hood (Blue, Black Charcoal, Berry)
review_body: I bought this sleeping bag to go on a cub scout freeze out.  I was very happy with the bag because it is a very warm, seemingly durable product.  I didnt get to try it out in zero degree weather but I was warm enough that I had to leave it unzipped so I didnt sweat to death in 40 degree weather.  The one thing I found alittle difficult was how to get it back in the little storage bag it comes with.  Once you take it out it is a real trick to getting it back in that little bag because it puffs up so nicely!  Over all a very nice bag, reasonable priced, and worth the small investment if you want a nice sleeping bag for cold weather.  I would recommend passing up the higher priced bags as this one definetly does the trick!

product_title: CoPilot Taxi Bicycle Child Seat
review_body: The instructions for this suggest one can simply slide the seat onto the rack.  That's not the case, however.  After a maddening hour or so, I used a flat-head screw driver to leverage the seat on the front of the rack.  Looks like a design or manufacturing flaw prevents one from sliding it on.  I haven't used it yet, but I came within minutes of packing it back up and returning it.  Let's hope its flaws do not extend to how safe it is.

product_title: Topeak Mini G MasterBlaster Bike Pump with Gauge
review_body: it is small so it fits in a backpack or hooks onto your bike. it takes a while to pump bike tires up and the pressure gauge doesn't work so you have to have a pressure gauge with you.

product_title: Zippo Color Lighters
review_body: If you have or have seen a chrome Zippo (polished or otherwise), this is its sister, and names aside, she is hot. It's as if a Zippo designer was out at some party with his shades on and took out his lighter and said \\"Heh, too bad it can't look like that when my shades aren't on\\", then went to work in the morning, shared his brain child, and got it made for the rest of us. High polished chrome \\"with charcoal overtones\\" as a wine snob might put it. The pictures don't really do it justice, but at least they're something to compare with the stock photo and other chrome Zippos to drive home the difference. Definitely top notch for breaking the ice...

product_title: Coleman Montana Big Sky Elite Tent, 16'x7'
review_headline: Coleman Montana Big Sky Elite Tent
review_body: We have a camper so was hesitant when we were asked to go camping but had to use a tent.  I bought the Coleman Montana Big Sky Elite Tent, 16'x7' for this trip.  We were so pleased at the time it took to set this up!  It only took maybe 15 minutes. It rained all one night and we stayed totally dry inside the tent. There was plenty of room for all of our things inside the tent also.

product_title: Kryptonite Kryptoflex 1218 Combo Cable Bicycle Lock (1/2-Inch x 6-Foot)
review_body: Used this lock for a long time on a Bianchi Xtracycle in Los Angeles, until my number was up and I parked my bike on a busy stretch of Melrose Avenue, and I came out of a class to find my cut lock lying on the ground taunting me.  Moral of the story - if you live in a city, do not use this lock to actually lock a bicycle you care about in the least.  Any decent bolt cutter will cut through this.

product_title: Klean Kanteen Stainless Steel Water Bottle
review_headline: A great product made even better
review_body: An excellent product made even better by the improved top. The new version does not trap water as the old one did.

product_title: Topeak Bike Cover (Mountain Bikes)
review_body: It has been a month since I bought this bike cover and so far, this products proves to be worth it. The only issue I had was when I received the package, it came with the wrong order slip. For some reason, the order slip was for a red bag worth $11.28, so there was no way I could return the bike cover in case we didn't like it. It's a good thing the bike cover was exactly what was promised it would be like.

product_title: Sigg Lifestyle Loop Top Water Bottle (1.0-Liters)
review_body: I purchased this water bottle as a gift and the person who received tit loves it, we have since purchased a second one.

product_title: Therm-a-Rest NeoAir Air Mattress
review_body: this is a great product.. as lond as you can protect it from holes. i have gone through 2 therm-a-rest, the first one i loved, i hiked with it for 1,000 miles of the pacific crest trail and it held up great, i did get a few holes, but i was able to patch it up easy, maybe once a night put new air in it, i felt like i was sleeping in an actual bed. this year i felt like i need a ned one so when i recived it i took it right to the trail in freezing weather, well there must of been a defect cuz it never heald the air, i froze my butt off!  if you can protect it and are comfortable patching, get it, it was my favorit piece of gear on the PCT

product_title: Zippo Butane Fueled Lighter, Vertical Chrome
review_body: Within a very short period of time, within a week, I needed new flint. Even after replacing the flint, it still can not be relied on to light.

product_title: Custom X Fin Tethers
review_body: I purchased a pair of these [[ASIN:B001DXKKLW Custom X Fin Tethers]] two years ago and they've held up very well. I've never come close to losing a fin, never had my fins ripped off when I was \\"rag dolled\\" in a big wave, but I know I can rely on these tethers. They come in a variety of colors so you can coordinate them with your other gear if that's your thing. The velcro tabs make them easy to wrap around your ankle, but difficult to take off if you wear neoprene gloves. Other than that I have no complaints.

product_title: Razor E300S Seated Electric Scooter
review_body: Bought scooter, worked fine, we use it daily. Three weeks into it, c/b conotinues to pop. Scooters goes 5 minutes max then has to stop and reset c/b. Went on line two days ago, ordered new battery. Hopefully that is it. The two battery combo package costs approximately another $[...]. I hope that is the fix.

product_title: High Sierra Airhead Backpack
review_body: This has become my gym bag. The material is all mesh material, so there is a lot of air flow. (And not much security if that is important to you). My towel gets nice and dry between workouts. Lots of pockets for gym card and padlock, workout book and towel, cell phone, etc. A good little bag at the right price.

product_title: Body Glove Amaze Purge with Quick Adjustable Strap/Siren/Expanse II Fin Snorkel Set
review_body: The snorkel worked great. Better than I expected.  The mask leaked, I think it is just my face. A friend used it and he was fine with it.  Fins, TERRIBLE! They are entirely too stiff and hurt my feet.   I ended up ditching the fins after trying them twice.  Still have the tube but will get a new mask and fins.

product_title: O'Brien Double X-Wing Inflatable Towable
review_headline: Great Fun Stability Even On The Ocean
review_body: I have a boat on the ocean and your standard donut speed tube is way too violent on the ocean.  This obrien tube was the first thing that actually permitted me to remain on it while actually having fun.  It also permits for you to just tie up to the boat and relax on it with up to 3 people adult size.  It's very comfortable and a great deal for the money.

product_title: High Sierra Expandable Wheeled Upright
review_body: This bag was exactly what I was looking for.  High quality canvas and rolls easily when packed to the maximum capacity.

product_title: Women's Classic Padded Bike Shorts Cycling Bicycle BikingMade in USA
review_body: Wow, what a difference riding my bike.  I'm not a cyclist to be sure, but these shorts made me understand how you could be - much more comfortable than even gel bike seats (which I have) and a fleece cover over that!    If you want to just try a lower cost padded bike short - these are the ones!

product_title: Coleman Rechargeable Portable Blender and Lid
review_headline: Coleman Blender 850 **  JUNK   JUNK   JUNK  JUNK  JUNK **
review_body: I bought my first Coleman 850 blender at Costco.  It worked great for first two weeks, then unable to recharge the battery.  Costco refunded immediately.  The second, third, and fourth were bought at a local retailer.  Each failed to recharge properly.  The last one lasted through the summer so I kept it over the winter but found it failed to work in the spring.  Coleman sent a new one immediately under the warranty.  This was the marine model with a larger , more powerful battery.    Spring 2010, my silver Coleman 850 failed to charge initially; but, after a few attempts , it held it's charge.  Until I needed it a week later.  DEAD.    I am ZERO for FIVE with this unit.  Coleman has created a piece of trash and proudly placed their name on it.

product_title: Greenfield Kickstand
review_headline: Excellent, but not if you need to cut
review_body: This kickstand is wonderful and easy to install. Fortunately, I didn't need to trip the length of the kickstand for my bike. If I had needed to shorten it I'm not sure how I would have done it.

product_title: SportRack A90095 Explorer Roof Box
review_body: The seller was great but the container was a bit cumbersome being that the knobs that hold the container to the vehicle obstruct the bottom of the holder and limit space for solid storage containers like boxes.

product_title: Gear Aid ReviveX Down Cleaner, 12 Ounce
review_body: Both down comforters and an old mountaineering Duvet (the real thing - a hooded jacket) fluffed up like new. The Duvet needed some encouragement during drying but worked out great.

product_title: Large Sunshade
review_body:
Before considering a purchase of this product, it's helpful to understand what it is and what it isn't. Depending on your intended application, you could find it light in weight or heavy, a good design or unusable. This is a review of the medium-size sunshade, but most of what I say should apply to the large model as well. (See update below.)

At 10+ pounds, this is not something anyone is likely to take on a backpack trip. A backpacker looking for shade will more likely choose something akin to Kelty's Noahs Tarp at under 2 pounds and half the price.

Since people may have to duck to enter this structure, and the walls hinder lateral visibility, and the dome shape does not cover the entire footprint, this would not be a great choice for a vendor setting up shop at an outdoor market. The vender would be better off choosing a much heavier portable structure with a rectangular canopy suspended on poles.

So, who would find this product useful? Well, perhaps a family spending a day at the beach, but if it's windy they will need to find ways to anchor the corners, perhaps with coolers or a car bumper, etc. But anyone setting up any kind of sun shelter on a sandy beach would have a similar issue to deal with. This structure does have the advantage of being free standing when erected; you just have to prevent it from blowing away.

I bought the Kelty Sunshade to use on river trips. It is small and light enough to easily take along in a canoe. It proved its worth the first night out when a storm blew in. I wish I had a video of my wife and me setting this thing up for the first time in gale-force winds and pelting rain. I know it would be a huge comedy hit on YouTube.

We got nowhere using the stakes and finally had to rely on a cooler and heavy water containers to hold down the windward side of the structure. The wind finally subsided, but it continued to rain all night. Without the Sunshade we would have been lying in our tent eating granola bars for dinner. With the Sunshade we cooked a hot dinner and enjoyed it seated in our outdoor dining room. It was pretty sweet.

We also set up the Sunshade to provide shade from the sun (novel idea) on layover days when we remained at camp. It did provide sun relief, but not as much as we would have liked. There is an inherent problem with using a lightweight fabric to block the hot rays of the sun; the sun's heat will penetrate the fabric causing the area underneath to heat up. If there is little wind to move the air, or if you are sitting within a few few feet of the fabric, you can become uncomfortably hot. In the future I will bring along a highly-reflective mylar sheet to drape over the sunshade during the hottest part of the day.

Other considerations...
I recommend buying a supplementary side wall. It is easy to attach and can be moved around the structure to match the movement of the sun or breezes.

I'm confident I could set up the Sunshade by myself, but it's a lot easier with two people - even then, not very easy. The problem is stretching the taut fabric over the fiberglass rods or poles. My wife held the pole while I used my strength to pull the metal grommet over the end of the rod. Maybe the fabric will loosen-up over time, and this process will become easier. On disassembly, do not pull the rods out of the fabric sleeves because the shock-corded sections will come apart and fight you. Bunch the fabric and push it off the pole instead. After we got the hang of it, we could unpack and assemble the Sunshade, or disassemble and pack it away, in about six or seven minutes (maybe a little longer in a gale).

Well...since I wrote this review, I replaced the Kelty Sunshade with Kelty's Noah's Tarp. I have to supply poles for use with the tarp, but I can erect the tarp in various configurations, and it is lighter in weight than the Sunshade. So, the Sunshade languished in the basement until I had an occasion to use it on the beach recently at South Padre Island, TX, where I LOVED it! The fabric seemed looser now, so it was easier to stretch over the supporting poles. It was breezy that day, but to my surprise, the stakes held. We hung out under the Sunshade sipping cervezas and blabbing all day long, and it was GREAT! Oh, by the way, one of the fiberglass poles started separating during a canoe trip a few years back, and I duct-taped it.l I had an occasion to use it on the beach recently at South Padre Island, TX, where I LOVED it! The fabric seemed looser now, so it was easier to stretch over the supporting poles. It was breezy that day, but to my surprise, the stakes held.
