Oh, by the way, one of the fiberglass poles started separating during a canoe trip a few years back, and I duct-taped it.

product_title: Winter Sleeping Bag
review_headline: Nice bag for the money, but "winter" is a stretch
review_body: I bought two of these for my kids because the price was right.  While they are comfortable with their brushed lining and extremely compact when stuffed in their sacks, I was disappointed to discover that the 0 degree rating was in fact 0 degrees Celsius, not 0 degrees Fahrenheit.  So this is a 3 season bag at best, not for use in sub-freezing temperatures (so \\"winter sleeping bag\\" is a stretch, at least for where I camp in the Rocky Mountains).  I decided to keep them to use in warmer weather since their compactness makes them great for car camping.

product_title: Coleman Girls Catnap Sleeping Bag
review_body: This sleeping bag is fine for the money.  My only complaint is that it uses strings to tie it closed (when are they going to come up with something that kids can actually do - like velcro wrappers?) and the strings totally unraveled within a day of owning it. I returned it (and the other Coleman bag I bought that had the same problem) and when I got the new ones just melted the ends of the strings with a lighter.

product_title: Advanced Elements Double Action Pump with Pressure Guage
review_headline: should have gotten an electric pump!
review_body: The pump works, but you do get a workout inflating a 2 person Kayak. I also have lower back problems and more than a few times I had to stop pumping for a short rest. My biggest complaint the PRESSURE GUAGE does not work. The needle don't move. If anyone knows a trick to get the guage to work please let me know.

product_title: Planet Bike Superflash bike tail light
review_body: I've always had good luck with Planet Bike rear lights.  This one is no exception.  Nice, bright and works well.  Buy this light.

product_title: Kelty FC 3.0 Child Carrier
review_headline: Great Backpack with Amazing Kelty Warranty
review_body: I love this pack and I will tell you why but if you read anything... read the end of my review about the warranty.    I began using this pack when my kid was 21 lb's and 7 months and he is now 1 year and about 25 lb's. He rides safe, secure and comfortable in this pack. When I first began using the pack he would fidget or whine a tiny bit when strapping him in but once in he is quiet and happy. Once I used the pack for a couple of weeks he was thrilled to be put in it. I have carried him around for three hours in a theme park and he was content and excited to see all of the action from a grown-ups point of view. He has fallen asleep in it with his head forward and face turned to the side resting on the very soft and plush dribble pad (removable and machine washable). Security and comfort are certainly not an issue with this backpack. There are circulation worries with some packs because of dangling feet. On the FC 3.0, the childs feet have a resting area. For larger children you can use the optional Kelty stirrup accessory when your childs is tall enough that their feet have to go to the outside of their seating area. The stirrups are an older item but the rings they clip onto are present on this pack. You shouldn't need these until your child is closer to two or older.    Next... I am very comfortable wearing the pack. I am 5'11\\" and about 180lbs. When I first tried out the pack with the factory settings it felt good. I put my kid in it and tightened some straps up and it was fine although the shoulder and chest area seemed to be carrying the lion share of the load. Then I raised the torso belt some and it was better. I went to a theme park for a day and pulled the shoulder straps even tighter and it raised the pack a little higher on my back. At this point the torso buckle was just about at my belly button and the pack just sort of hugged my back and the weight distributed nicely and I knew I found the sweet spot. This was our first major outing. We logged three hours on a sunny 70 degree day.    On the subject of sun; The sun/rain hood is well designed. The child will have a great view off to both sides. I have heard some grumbles from fans of other brands about the Kelty hoods because they obstruct the front view a little. What these people do not realize is that the child does not need to see straight ahead very well because Mom and Dads head is in the way anyhow. They will have a good view of the back of your head so they are comfortable knowing it's you carrying them and they will have a great view on the sides to see everything else.    The generous storage areas consist of four compartments. One compartment stores the sun/rain hood which is included. One compartment holds an included padded changing pad and has room for a jacket or extra clothes etc.. The third compartment is a small compartment and the last is a very big one at the bottom. I can fit a small picnic blanket in there. You can actually leave the diaper bag at home. I fit diapers, wipes, toys,  bottles, extra clothes... I really do not bring a diaper bag with me when I use this pack.    Putting on the pack is generally safe and fairly easy after you practice a few times, take your time and use caution. The FC 3.0 pack is tall so the shoulder straps are higher off the ground. I have very little trouble strapping on the pack from the floor. I can just loosen the shoulder straps, squat down and put the shoulder straps on. Then I lean forward to get him off the ground and shift his weight onto my back (rather than have him flop over to a side) and then stand and buckle the torso and buckle the chest and tighten the shoulder straps. I am a little overprotective yet I feel very confident and safe loading this pack onto my back with my little guy in it. Unloading involves loosening the shoulder straps, squatting down and resting the kickstand on the ground. With that said... Loading and unloading from a raised area such as a bed or the back of an SUV is far easier. Also, you will find park benches make is easy to load and unload.    This pack is perfectly designed for neighborhood walks, a day at the park or zoo and even serious hiking and overnight camping. I originally thought it was overkill for grocery shopping or a mall but after using this pack for several months now I take it and use it everywhere. My kid makes it about 10 minutes in the grocery store/Target shopping cart. He is good for 30 minutes or more in the pack.     Finally; I need to tell you about my warranty experience with Kelty. One of the best reasons to buy a Kelty product is their Lifetime Warranty. I had an older Kelty child-carrier backpack in which a strap and buckle wore out (this was a less important strap not jeopardizing child safety and the new models have a reinforced version of this strap and buckle). Kelty has a lifetime warranty and they advised me that they do not usually repair the child carriers but will replace them. I was instructed to cut the straps off of my pack (making it unusable), the tag from the pack showing the model number and mail them to the company along with a simple form I filled out from their website. One week after mailing the straps I received a brand new FC 3.0 from UPS. The model they replaced was an older and somewhat less expensive model. I was shocked at how fast they shipped it out to me and that they sent me their top of the line carrier. I paid about $5.00 to ship the straps back and they paid the shipping on my replacement pack. Wow. There are a lot of choices out there for child carriers but I have not seen a lifetime warranty on any brand but Kelty.    This warranty experience has made me a big fan of Kelty as a company. My experiences with this pack has cemented that loyalty. This child carrier provides a generous amount of storage, a comfortable carry for Mom and Dad and most importantly a comfortable and safe ride for your child. If this is what you are looking for than you have found your carrier.Update Feb 1, 2011. My son is now 18 months and and 26 lb's and still likes being in the pack. I put him in it for hiking and walks. It is still a good choice for theme parks because of all the storage it has. He likes to run around a lot more these days but never gripes when I put him in the pack!

product_title: Seattle Sports Square Pack Sink
review_body: Who knew I would need a sink? Until I cooked bacon for the first time when camping, I had no idea that I would need to boil water and have a place to do dishes. This little sink does what it should. And as long as you have all 4 sides on a firm surface it will not collapse on you when even partially filled.

product_title: OnGuard Bulldog DT 5012 Bicycle U-Lock and Extra Security Cable
review_body:
This lock is a beast. It feels sturdy and secure and has kept my bike safe. I have had no problem at all with the keys being sharp - some of the teeth are, however they are recessed into the key and have presented no problems after two weeks of use and a spot on my keychain that goes in my pocket. The lock also works perfectly and smoothly. And you get five keys, one with an LED light. Bonus. Now the cons.

1. Huge, the mounting bracket is flimsy and I have a water bottle cage - it will not mount on my 56 cm top tube specialized sirrus (road bike with commuter handle bars.) anywhere that will not interfere with my pedaling motion. Forget about the bracket if you have a waterbottle cage.

-However, I use a trunk bag/panniers so this is not a problem for me and I was aware of this going in.

2. The warranty (bike replacement) is crap. You must send them the broken lock for them to honor the warranty... Gee if someone ever steals my bike I hope the thief is nice enough to leave my lock lying around. The warranty also states the lock must be broken into and is voided if power tools such as an angle grinder, dremel, or blowtorch is used. Industry standard but still crap.

product_title: Columbia Cougar Flats II 15-Foot by 10-Foot 8 Person 2 Room Family Cabin Dome Tent
review_body: I was able to set this tent up with the only assistance coming from my 5-year-old son and my 7-year-old son in about 30-45 minutes.  Easy enough to set up without reading the instructions, but would have appreciated if the diagrams in the owner's manual were color-coded as well.  Most of the poles are color coordinated with the sleeve on the tent itself.  Easy enough for us three do to though.  I completely enjoy the fact that the case the tent goes in has a hard plastic bottom and has wheels on it as well, as it is not a light tent to carry.  I also liked that the zipper pulls are glow-in-the-dark.  Very helpful.  A feature I also like is the zipper cover or lining.  The way the fabric lays over the zipper helps protect the seam from water coming in.  I also like that the tent is big enough for two queen-sized air mattresses and all of our stuff.  Can't wait to use it more often!!  I'm only giving it 4 stars because we haven't taken it out camping other than our back yard.  It rained and was cold the whole time it was up so we slept in the house!!

product_title: Topeak The Mini Plus 18-Function Bicycle Tool
review_headline: All you need for your bike on the road
review_body: This set of tools is all a biker needs for a modern bike, period. Either on a trail or at home, the tool has it all. (Or course you would need an air pump, hydraulic disc brakes bleeding set, a pedal wrench, etc..)    The tool is very compact for a 18+ function, and is getting that from pretty short keys.    The included soft case while makes it slightly bigger, is nice to keep it from banging against other stuff in your backpack.    P.S. I shopped around for a while before got this one and do not regret a bit. (Now having been using it for over a year I don't regret.)

product_title: Blackstone 36-Inch Commercial Griddle/Grill
review_body: bought this grill for a chruch funtion, works great, cooks allot of food all at the same time, works very well in low setting, heats up very quickly and hold heat steadly, recommend for everybody, even the pro cooks, great craftsmanship, built very well.[[ASIN:B000OQMNNC Blackstone 36-Inch Commercial Griddle/Grill]]

product_title: Buh-Bump 2.5-Ounce Heart Rate Monitor Electrode Cream
review_body: When I do get a small window to work out, I don't have time to waste to get my heart rate monitor to work. Water usually works but when it doesn't I can waste 1/2 my workout trying to get the device to read my pulse. I found Spectra 360 Electrode Gel to be only slightly better than water. Buh-Bump cream, on the other hand, works perfectly every time, no issues ever. It takes so little to work the tube should last a long time. I highly recommend this stuff for use with heart monitors.  12/17/2015 update: At some point the cream does stop working for me but it's not the cream's fault. In my case, every Polar chest strap (and every Polar watch) I have ever purchased eventually failed. I've since switched over to Garmin compatible chest straps with Polar or Wahoo Fitness sensors and don't need the cream any more. The cream is still great. I just don't need it with Garmin or Wahoo Fitness style chest straps.

product_title: Pacific Outdoors 17-LC130 La Chaise Folding Recliner
review_headline: Poor Quality of Materials - Cloth Tearing around Grommets
review_body: Received this chair as an Xmas present this year so it spent several months in the box prior to being used, which unfortunately took us beyond the Amazon Full Refund period.  This chair has only seen occasional use now for a little over a month and a half (weather finally warmed up to used it outdoors) and already the plastic, woven cloth like material is tearing around the grommets, especially around the ones on the bending flex points of the chair (under the knees). All of the material around all the grommets should have been reenforced more and especially where the chair experiences repetitive movement.     Maybe you'll be lucky to get one that doesn't tear on you but for the price one would expect something that should hold up for more than a month and a half's use with average weight people and a 45 lb child. We are disappointed with this product and would not buy another item from Pacific Outdoors.

product_title: HeatMax EverCool Cooling Bandanas. AMERICAN FLAG. Pack of 4 Bandanas - Reusable
review_body: Product really helps beat back the excessive heat from the summer sun.  Simple to use, wrap around you're neck and you are good to go.  Keep a couple in your cooler.

product_title: Razor E300 Electric Scooter
review_headline: Poor on POWER. Save Your Money!
review_body: my kids each got these last year for Christmas. they are incredibly fun for VERY SHORT runs; they STINK on anything less than perfectly flat roads or for any length of time. So, if you go somewhere down hill--you're walking that thing back home.  also, if you carefully read the manual it states that the average ride time is 45 MINUTES!!!  \\"Average ride time\\" really translates to \\"you're lucky if you can ride for 25 minutes.\\"  Additionally, it must be stored in a place where it won't get too cold--so your garage is out.  it'll look just lovely in your front hall. LOL  great concept, terrible product. buy a bike or take a risk on a gas powered scooter--this thing just doesn't cut it.

product_title: Brunton Polaris LED Lantern (Silver)
review_body: As always, I've no complaints about the pricing or speedy delivery from Amazon. Paid for normal ground shipping but it was delivered only two days after ordering.  Can't ask for anything better than that.    I ordered the Brunton Polaris LED lantern as a light source for backpacking and moto-camping (motorcycle) The backpackers reviews suggest this emits a light source similar in color and warmth of a gas lantern (Coleman style) but without the obvious bulk, weight, and need for fuel and fragile mantles.    Upon receipt, the lantern would not switch on until fiddling with the battery cap screw tension.  Seemed there is a sweet spot somewhere between the 'good n' snug' adjustment and simply loose.  A small thing but that was my experience.    Tried it in a darkened bedroom. On the HI setting it seemed to be suffcient for a small camp and the LOW setting would be fine inside a tent for reading. Felt it would work fine for my trip planned to the Sierras the following week.    First night at camp could NOT switch the unit on no matter how snug or loose the battery well cover screw was.  Seting up camp the following day after 300+ miles of riding I find the lantern in my saddlebags turned ON and the batteries quite warm.  The jostling in the side bags apparently turned it on, maybe even fixed it??  Tried turning it ON/OFF several times and it seemed to work fine.  Figured now I can use it.    Tried it again once darkness set in and again it will not work. Tried switching the batteries around, fiddling with the battery cover screw tension again, even tried both a light and firm force on the rubberized on/off switch.  Nothing.  Tried pounding it firmly in the palm of my hand and it flashed on/off for just a millisecond and that was it. Was never to illuminate again.    Once home, wrote to Brunton and waited over a week before receiving a reply from them.  Took another week of exchanging email before given an authorization for return and hopefully, replacement.    If and when I receive the new lantern, I'll update this.

product_title: Avenir AirSource Sport Floor Bike Pump (Silver)
review_body: I bought this pump before looking at the reviews on here and man was that a mistake. The only thing it's got going for it is the price. Aside from being cheap this bicycle pump has no positive qualities. If you ride a road bike forget about using this pump. Pumping to around 80 psi is not an issue, but if you need to go above 100, which most road bike tires do, it's nearly physically impossible. You practically have to sit on it to get it to get to 100 psi, and the pumping handles dig into the skin on your palms. This bicycle pump is going straight in the trash. Money is well spent on a good bicycle pump, and this is certainly not one of them.

product_title: M-Wave Quick Release & Universal Mount Water Bottle Cage
review_body: This Bottle Cage works just as it should.  It holds securely and the bottle can be retrieved easily.  The camlock on the mount will fit and hold on other than round tubes as well (i.e. it fits perfectly on the triangular grab bar on my tractor).  I just ordered two more of them.  'Nuf said!!!

product_title: Victorinox C-Cell LED Flashlight
review_body: I waited some time for this flashlight to finally come in at Amazon.  They had the best price on it by far.  I have used the smaller \\"AA\\" version of this flashlight for years now and love it.  It outlasted by comparable Maglight by a long shot.  The Maglight bulb is exposed when you remove the head, something my 2 year old loved to do.  When it then gets dropped or tossed around, the bulb, even the LED bulb breaks.  Victorinox seals up the bulb in the head so when you remove the head, all the critical parts are protected.  When I got this light I was surprised at the nice weight and balance of the light.  It is also fairly compact.  More compact than my LED \\"C cell\\" Mag.  This also has a superior 5.8 Watt LED versus the 3 Watt in the comparable Mag.  The beam is not focusable but in defense of it, they have channeled the light in a dual pattern.  part of the light is dispersed to the fringes providing enough light by which to see where one is going when walking in the dark.  The other part of the light is channeled in a beam providing directed energy to what you want to point at.  I am very please with this light and if it proves as durable as my other Victorinox light, it is a definite winner.

product_title: Mountain Boy Sledworks Bambino Grande Pull Sled
review_headline: Nice but will have to return
review_body: As a previous reviewer stated, this is a nice sled but our 15 month old kept tipping over on uneven or unpacked snow. We ended up having to push her instead which was not as much fun. Maybe if she were heavier or could hold onto the sled to prevent herself from falling off it would have worked better. Unfortunately we had to return the sled. Quick ship and easy returns as always on Amazon.

product_title: Thule 667ES Excursion ES Rooftop Cargo Box
review_body: We purchased this carrier for our Acura RDX and headed out on a 3 week road trip.  It not only held 4 regular size dufflebags, but two razor scooters/the blankets we purchased along the way/a bag of cleaning supplies/and a bag of stuff for the pool.    The product arrived earlier than the promised time and came by truck.  The two drivers opened the box in front of me to ensure it was not damaged and it wasn't.  Putting it on the car was quick and easy.  Once we figured out what holes to use, it took about 15-20 minutes to secure it in place.  The lid opens from the back and lifts up toward the front.  It did not fit in one of the hotel parking garages, so we emptied it, took it off, and brought it to the hotel room on a luggage carrier :-).  It fit nicely standing up in the closet and was out of sight.  It also has a lock, which gave us peace of mind when we left it full at a hotel stop.     Cons:  The lid is very light and feels a little loose when you open it.  We lost a few mpg's (but you probably will with any carrier).

product_title: Energizer Weather Ready Rechargeable LED Light
review_body: The area in which we live recently experienced an all night electrical power failure. The Weather Ready LED light provided illumination throughout the night enabling us to safely travel within the house.

product_title: Thule 982 Bicycle Frame Adapter for Strap and Hitch carriers
review_headline: User Review: Thule 982 Bicycle Frame Adapter for Strap/Hitch Carriers
review_body: I purchased two Thule 982 Bicycle Frame Adapters for Thule 964 Revolver 4-Bike Hitch Mount Rack from the Amazon retailer, Rack Attack. PROS: 1) Because of the numerous different bicycle frame configurations, it will quickly become apparent to the strap/hitch carrier user that mounting the bicycles level is difficult. Attaching the Thule 982 Bicycle Frame Adapter ends to the bike's handle bar and seat stems will make this procedure much easier.  For this application, the product seems well designed. CONS: 1) One of adapters I received from the Amazon retailer had rusted bolts while still inside the packaging! However, shortly after being exposed to the ouside environment during use, all the lock bolts on both adaptors quickly rusted. At the stated MSRP, stainless steel hardware would have been the fair and better choice. 2) The rubberized coating on the metal ends of the adaptors will ultimately tear or wear down due to use, UVA exposure, etc.. As a result, the exposed metal ends of the adaptors could damage the bike's finish. Take care to protect the rubberized coating during use and storage. In conclusion, it is my opinion that the Thule 982 Frame Adaptor is both a well designed and needed accessory for the strap/hitch carrier user.

product_title: Park Tool Tire & Tube Repair Kit
review_body: Sadly, I have used these a bunch and the good news is they work fine.  I like that they stack together to keep in a seat bag or CamelBak pocket.  Have not had one break so I would say they are made very well.  Can not go wrong if you need some.  Park Tool make some good stuff.

product_title: OGIO Crunch Pack
review_body:
Received the item three days after I ordered it. Outstanding job to Amazon once more for an incredible service.

The bag itself is gorgeous. On one end of the bag, you've got the shoe compartment to keep your footwear completely separate from the rest of your items; perfect for those rainy days where mud and grime are prevalent. On the other side, you've got another large pocket, perfect for your post-workout toiletries, shower sandals, and so on. On the front, you're given another pocket where you can store your PMP, wallet, watch, or any other items not mentioned here.

The primary compartment, even with all those other pockets, is incredibly spacious, giving you ample room for your workout gear, a hanger, towels, and so on.

The interlocking handles are a touch of brilliance I've never seen on any other bags, and make carrying it a breeze. Though if you'd like other means of doing so, you're also given a shoulder strap.

All in all, this is a gorgeous bag, with more than just a few color choices to pick from.

Highly recommended.

product_title: Strider ST-2 PREbike Balance Running Bike
review_headline: No need for training wheels! The best bike ever!
review_body: I bought this bike for my daughter's 2nd birthday. She fell in love with it. It took her about 10 minutes to figure out how to ride it, at first she walked it, then she sat down in the saddle and finally started striding. She had used the bike almost every day for a 1 1/2 years and at 3 1/2 we transferred her directly to a regular two wheeler with pedals - 12\\" (no training wheels, as she had the balance and was able to go down our driveway with her legs up on the Strider). After 25 minutes she was riding a bike!!!! She's almost 4 now and people stop us often in awe that my 3year old is riding a bike without training wheels.   Once she knew how to ride a bike, it was easy to introduce her to inline skating and ice skating.

product_title: Razor E125 Electric Scooter
review_body: easy to assemble, my kids ride them for a long time without charging. So far no complains! Goes pretty fast and looks real durable.

product_title: Optimus Hiker + Stove
review_body: I don't know what happened.  But when the tanks went from brass to a green painted finish a world class product become unreliable.  I've been using camping stoves since the early 70's.  This is the first time I've had a stove stop after 5 minutes and never work again.  Katadyn that now owns Optimus was also very unhelpful.  For the price the fuel tank should not be full of junk.  When I emptied the fuel tank to return it to Amazon the coffee filter I used to strain the fuel through turned black with all the junk in the tank.  If you want an Optimus buy a brass tank vintage model. Another once great product that has gone down hill.

product_title: Schwinn 20-Function Bike Computer
review_body: I bought this bike computer some few weeks ago, and I am very pleased.  Once you enter the tire circumference in mm, it calculates the distance, speed, and etc. I checked my bike route i took with google maps, and compared it to what the computer gave as the distance traveled and it was quite accurate. I like the auto start/stop feature.

product_title: Third Eye Pro Helmet Bicycle Mirror
review_body: This very light weight miror is positioned so that I never really need to turn my head more than a couple inches to see what might be coming up from behind.  The purchase of this mirror has turne out to be one of the most valuable pieces of my cycling gear.  I will never ride without a mirror again.  I use the same bike helmet for roller skiing, and the same is true under those circumstances.  The one thing that I did differently than instructed is that I actually used some small sheet metal screws to more securely hold it to the inside my helmet.

product_title: Timex Expedition Outdoor Metal Field (Full)
review_body: Ordered this last week and just received it today.     I needed a cheap watch for every day wear as I hate to always reach for my bulky Blackberry Bold to check the time. The Timex Field Watch fit the bill.    This is a very nice classic looking time piece that goes well with any outfit and the Indiglo does a great job illuminating the face. My only complaint is the stiff leather band, but I suspect it will soften with additional wearing. Thanks Amazon!

product_title: Solio Mono Emergency Hybrid Solar Charger
review_headline: Charges too slowly to be useful
review_body: Before I bought this product, my expectation was a solar charger that could be clipped to a backpack or left in a car under the sun and maintain enough charge to top off a cellular phone battery once every few days.  My expectation was not met.  The device does not charge whatsoever when left inside a car, even under direct sunlight (perhaps the windows block too much UV light).  It requires several hours of direct, uninterrupted sunlight to charge completely, which means leaving it outside unattended.  In an urban setting, this is not realistic.    Since buying it a couple months ago, I have left it at home and not used it since.

product_title: Stearns Youth Boating Vest (50-90 lbs.)
review_body: I was worried after reading reviews that it wouldn't fit my 10 year old.  However when it arrived I was pleased that what I had read was incorrect.  Excellent life jacket - easy to use and secure - added to our sense of safety on the boat knowing that we had our own life jacket and not some generic sized one from the tour company.  Thank you!

product_title: Schwinn Hinge Folding Bike
review_body: I can say that this product isn't misleading in the sense that, Yes it is a bike, and Yes it does fold; aside from this i cannot speak more so on its behalf but i can say the 4 star rating is ill-deserved. It came with a bent wheel, a bent front gear(complete with dangling chain) and a general feeling of hate and disdain for the customer when you opened the clearly abused packaging. Quick work with a hammer and I was able to salvage it, but i cannot say this product is for anyone suffering from anger issues or a history of violence. If you want a bike that folds, and have time, you can easily have this fixed at a shop. For its hefty price tag, as compared to other similar products, it was the mediocre cousin of sub par. Buyer beware unless you are willing to invest money beyond the initial cost of the bike.

product_title: Kent Adult Westport Folding Tricycle
review_body: I purchased this for my daughter who is 8 years old and visually impaired.  It was difficult for her to ride a 2 wheeler due to her vision, and this is absolutely perfect for her!  She loves it and we go bike riding practically every day now!  The seat and handlebars are both adjustable so the bike will grow with her.  This was the best investment I ever made just to see the smile on her face now that she can ride a \\"big kid bike\\"!  As far as assembly, it was a bit of a pain.  The directions could have been a little bit better.  But all in all, it was worth the stress of putting it together to see her enjoy her trike!

product_title: Yellowstone Driftwood Basket Picnic Picnic Baskets
review_body: DON'T LET THE LITTLE PICTURE FOOL YOU, THIS BASKET IS LARGE...THE QUALITY OF THE BASKET IS SUBSTANTIAL.  LOADS OF ROOM FOR FOOD, A BOTTLE OF WINE, ETC.  THE CUTLERY, GLASSES AND DISHES ARE REALLY NICE, IT EVEN HAS A NICE SMALL CHEESEBOARD.  FANTASTIC FOR A WEDDING PRESENT, BUT I BOUGHT IT FOR A SECOND HONEYMOON MY HUSBAND AND I WERE TAKING TO THE MOUNTAINS...VERY ROMANTIC, WILL GIVE YOU A LIFETIME OF PICNIC MEMORIES!!!

product_title: Coleman 8-Person Red Canyon Tent
review_body: Great tent for the money...It's a good idea to apply seam sealer to the tent and rain fly...little leaks here and there...

product_title: Topeak QR Beam Rack MTX Bicycle Rack
review_body: So far so good. Works well with other topeak accessories. i ride a road bike to work, about 15 miles. Little sway, lock to seat well. So far its a smart purchase. Quick release rubs leg just a little.

product_title: CamelBak H.A.W.G. NV 100-Ounce Hydration Pack
review_body: Our guide was wowed by my Camelbak once he realized I had water, raincoat and room to stow camera and bins when the rain started.  At one point while I looked thru his scope, he lifted my bag from my back. (I guess checking the weight).  He begged us to bring him one on a future trip--we've sent him the men's version (h.a.w.g.)

product_title: Wind Ridge Instant Tent
review_headline: Great Deal, Quick to put up
review_body: Basically this tent is put up with one quick twisting motion.  No poles to pull out and shove through anything (besides the rain flap).  In all honesty, you can have your tent set up and ready to go (staked, with rainfly, etc) in less than 2 or 3 minutes.  I bought it because I end up leaving late from work to go camping a bit and have to set up in the dark, which with this tent is a breeze.    My only complaint is that it is a little bit more complicated to fold up than a normal tent, but once you do you will have no problems fitting it back into the case it came in (because it forces you to do it the right way).    Also, after using it twice, i realized it has two external zip up pockets on each side to throw your shoes in so they dont get wet but also dont dirty up the tent.  cool

product_title: To-Go Ware Bamboo Utensil Set - 2 Pack - Blue Recycled PET Carrycase
review_body: I love the idea of eco friendly utensils. I was surprised how much the flavor of bamboo came out on everything I ate.

product_title: Coleman 14 x 12 Insta-Clip Screen
review_body: THis screen room was pretty easy to assemble, but one person would have a hard time with it. Seemed very sturdy and roomy. Even went back into the carrying case with no problem. We took it camping and left it up for about 3 days. Very nice!

product_title: Berkey Sport Bottle Portable Water Purifier
review_body: The Sport Berkey portable water bottle came free when I purchased a counter top system for my kitchen.  I have used it for 6 months with municipal water from work, 5 days a week.  It is awesome!  The water taste great every time, no chlorine taste ever!  The only place I have found on care and use of the water bottle is  [...]\\"Fill the Sport Berkey Portable Water Purifier with water, screw on cap and tighten securely to eliminate leaks. Flush water through filter by pulling down lever, so that straw is exposed, and squeeze water thru filter & out the straw. Repeat this flushing process twice before drinking.  This removes excess process dust from the filter.  After 2 flushes, rinse the bottle & cap. Your filter bottle is now ready to use. Enjoy!\\"  I only wish I'd had these instructions when I started using the bottle. According  to this website it last thru 160 refills from ANY source. A very GREEN way to drink filtered water, instead of disposable water bottles.  Get the Sport Berkey water bottle, you'll be glad you did!

product_title: Sea to Summit Ultra-Sil Stuff Sack
review_body: I love Sea to Summit Cordura stuff sacks. They are incredibly durable and lightweight. They also have a little tab near the top that you can use to hang the bag (if you are using it for food) so you don't have to overly stress the closing mechanism.

product_title: Schwinn High-Density Foam Mountain Saddle
review_body: I don't ride much, but wanted to do more. I bought this seat to make it more comfortable to start riding.  It isn't as comfortable as I was hoping, but I think I just need to get used to riding.

product_title: Intex Pillow Rest Raised Airbed with Built-in Pillow and Electric Pump
review_headline: not as good as the wenzel
review_body: I owned a Wenzel airbed previously that was far more comfortable. In hindsight i shouldve purchased another one instead of buying the intex. My fault for trying to be cheap.

product_title: Avenir Nylon Bicycle Cover (Mountain Bike)
review_body: A good quality product. Perfect fit for my wife's small frame bike, but a tight fit for my medium frame full suspension bike. Light weight and seems durable. I purchased the second one after being satisfied with the first, but should have checked fit on BOTH bikes.

product_title: Giro Transfer Sport Helmet
review_body: Great helmet!  Nice looking, easy to adjust.  Worn on several long rides (1:30+) and comfortable the entire way.

product_title: LEKI Nordic Walking Speed Pacer Vario T2 Poles (110cm)
review_headline: top of the line nordic walking poles-- does not disappoint
review_body: I was turned on to nordic walking by a European friend three years ago & own a set of Leki speed varios.  Have enjoyed them in the city & on trails for fun & weight loss --25 pounds.  Am a volunteer nordic walking evangelist & have enjoyed turning people on to the sport.  Have a collection of poles for groups & urge them to try different kinds & models including my own 110 varios.  These are the poles they like the best because they are so light & you can swing your arms easily & know you have gotten a great fullbody low impact workout.  When they were on sale on Amazon in August 2010 I bought two pair of 110 varios.  Of course I'm still using my own (estimate 1,800 miles )but sold the two discounted new sets to fellow enthusiasts who used to borrow mine.  I'd say it's a win win.     sfsusan

product_title: Case Yellow CV Sod Buster JR Pocket Knife
review_body: My first sodbuster was the large model, about 30 years ago.  It was a little large for my pocket, but what I like about these knives is the fact that the steel can take a seriously sharp edge.  As a woodworker a steels ability to sharpen well is more important then how long it will keep the edge.  Case has picked the right steel for my use.  I use the Sodbuster Jr. now.  I have two of them; one of which I custom ground for woodworking in tight spots.  They last forever.

product_title: Topeak Presta Valve Extension
review_body: I was living overseas when I bought this and had a family member send it to me to save money on shipping. I was desperate to get something that would allow me to pump the super short valves on my bike since the tubes I was getting were the only options available in country. I was super impressed by the ease of use, the solid design and the ability to be removed and reused on each tire. I had no problems for the year I used this extender and would recommend it to anyone looking for a valve extender.

product_title: Bell KEVLAR Key Cable Lock
review_headline: Awesome Lock if you don't want your property!
review_body:
If you like losing all your posessions, this lock is for you! Not only does it optimize thievery, but it also gives you that invaluable false sense of security that everyone longs for!

Seriously, I used this lock to chain up my custom hand built single speed bike. 3 month build, 700 in components. Last night, thief came in, picked/cut the lock, and took my bike.

Worthless. Bell should pay for my bike.

product_title: Hammers HP9 Anti-shock Hiking Pole with Compass & Thermometer
review_headline: Great hiking poles for the price
review_body: I bought these hiking poles for my father-in-law 4 years ago, and they still come in handy. I bought two, and for the price, they are definitely great hiking poles. He hiked both Half Dome and Mount Whintey using these hiking poles and said they worked like a charm. They fold and become compact and are sturdy. Highly recommended!

product_title: Alps Snowshoes Combo B - S21+S30
review_body: My husband and I got this set to try out. We weren't sure what to expect from the price. We were pleasantly surprised with the quality of the snowshoes. We had an 8\\"  snowfall last weekend and tried them out. We'd never used snowshoes before and were really impressed with how easy they are to walk around in. My husband was even RUNNING! These snowshoes are lightweight and seem durable. I would recommend them and the company who sells them. They came in just a few days, and the company sent them out the same day we ordered them!

product_title: Kettler Sprint Balance Bike (Multiple Styles)
review_body: I can't say enough great things about this balance bike. It was worth every single cent.  I'll be honest, we used to live in Manhattan and in May 2008 we bought one for our son's 3rd birthday and he used it sporadically for that spring and summer.  Once the winter months hit he didn't use it at all so I wasn't too sure if we made the right purchase.  This past May he turned four and with the warm weather we brought the balance bike out, again.  The reception was better but still not great.  We would take it to the playground and he started using it more but still the reception was lukewarm.  We moved to the suburbs where he had a lot more room and space and everything changed!!!!  Once he gained his confidence and got the full hang of the balance bike he was zipping around the yard like a true champ.  Now's he's only 4 yrs and 3 months old and he is able to ride a \\"big boy\\" bike without ANY training wheels!!!! Within the first hour of trying to ride his older cousin's bike he was able to ride unassisted.   It's amazing.  When I say it's amazing I mean it is AMAZING.

product_title: SPOT Personal Tracker
review_body: I think we'd had ours for about 3 weeks when we accidentally left it on the roof of the truck on an off road stop.  Of course, we did not realize it until we got home.  We thought the unit was malfunctioning, as it \\"moved\\" about 1 mile overnight.   Using the coordinates that the Spot transmitted, our regular GPS, and a picture of where it was located from the Spot website, we were able to locate it the next day... inside a packrat's nest.  The buttons have been chewed on a bit, but it's still going strong.  I certainly don't worry about it not transmitting my location accurately.  Great for when the husband is out in the woods.

product_title: CamelBak H.A.W.G. NV 100-Ounce Hydration Pack
review_body: Having owned multiple other Camelbak products since the beginning, I've ceom to expect some pretty rugged build quality, clever features(like the integrated rain hood, bladder hanger, tab for my rear red blinking light, removable waist strap...etc.), and also light weight from their products.  This one did not dissapoint in any of those departments.  The reason I got this pack was because of the N.V.I.S. system, that allows ample airflow across my back while I'm hiking, riding my motorcycle to work or using my commuter bike, and just for general use.  I run hot anyway, and live in the heat, and this is by FAR the most comfortable backpack I've ever owned.

product_title: Swiss Gear Smart Shade 10- by 10-Foot Screenhouse
review_headline: Hope You Never Need Replacement Parts
review_body: We bought this screen tent last summer and found it to be a huge improvement over other screen tents we have owned.  Putting it up the first time was challenging, but now we can do it without much trouble.  This summer while camping in heavy rain (no wind), a large pocket of water accumulated in one corner of the tent roof over night and broke one of the metal frame pieces. I called the phone number listed for replacement parts and on the third day, after being on hold for over half an hour, I finally got to speak to someone. They were pleasant, but I learned that replacement parts for the frame are not available. I also learned that the warranty does not cover problems that they believe are weather related. (Does that mean if your roof leaks, too bad, the rain caused the problem??!) I didn't know I was buying a product that becomes worthless if one piece breaks! For this reason I would not buy from this company again.  I will be figuring out a way to make a replacement part; I can't afford to throw away $169 plus shipping for a new tent.

product_title: Pacific Shorewood Women's Cruiser Bike (26-Inch Wheels)
review_body: Despite some of the complaints I read in other reviews, I went for the bike anyway.  It arrived with most of the bolts missing.  After a trip to Home Depot and calls to 2 engineering friends, I brought it to the local bike shop.  Apparently, the manufacturer pre-assembed it backwards and the entire bike had to be taken part and put back together.  One day in the rain, and it has already rusted.  I guess you get what you pay for.

product_title: CamelBak Octane XC 70 oz Hydration Pack
review_body: I bought the Octane XC because I needed more water than what my FlashFlo's 45oz. during long marathon training runs.  Additionally, I had a hard time reaching behind my back to get at my energy gels.  Most times I had to slow to a walk, loosen the waist strap, slide the fanny pack to the front or side to get at the zippered compartment.  I previously used a Nathan Labs HPL #020 hydration vest, but didn't like it since it felt like I was wearing another layer of clothing.  So with the start of my long runs, I got the Octane XC.     First, be aware that there are two Camelbaks called Octane; the Octane XC and the Octane 8+.  The Octane 8+ is slightly heaver (1.3lbs dry for XC vs. 1.98lbs dry for the 8+) due to it has a larger compartment to hold gear.  Probably great if you need a lot of stuff, but I have a Camelbak Cloud Runner if I need to lug around a lot of stuff for hikes or biking.  For me on a run all I need is to take my energy gels, cell phone, and lots of water.  So to same some weight I went with the XC.       My first run with the XC was a 12-miler.  The XC loaded with a full 70 oz. didn't slosh or move around on my back.  The air channel design on the inside back panel kept me comfortable.  The XC's design allows full arm swing without bumping into the side storage areas on the waist straps.  Speaking of which, the side storage is great for keeping the energy gels handy.  I was able to easily access those area without having to slow down or move the XC.  The top storage area is a small, but was great for holding my cell phone, ID, and  keys.  Halfway through my run, the sun broke through the clouds and the vest I was wearing was becoming too hot to wear.  While the XC has a criss-cross bungy cord to hold stuff, I'm always paranoid of having things fall off.  Instead I was able to store the vest in the same compartment as the hydration bladder with no problems.       One bit of advice, Camelbak did an outstanding job of using elastic band or velcro strapsto keep all the strap ends from dangling.  As such, it's best to adjust all the straps (to include the sternum strap which I had to move to a lower loop on the shoulder straps) before running with it.  In my excitement, I just filled up the hydration bladder and went on a run.  So each time I adjusted a strap, I had to undo the elastic/velcro band, make the adjustment, roll up the excess strap and redo the elastic/velcro band.  All that while running isn't easy.  Also, the drinking tube has a clip on the right shoulder strap, I didn't like the way the end would hit me if I pulled the tube all the way down.  I slid the tube end up, closer to the clip, so it didn't bounce around.        Bottom line:  This one's a keeper.  12-miles and once I got the straps adjusted, I hardly noticed I was wearing it.

product_title: Thomas Flashlight
review_body: My little boy completely enjoyed playing with this Thomas flashlight.  Seems pretty durable too.  My son left it on overnight, and it's still working properly.  I agree with another review, it has some vintage feel to it.  But overall, great buy for the price.

product_title: WeeRide LTD Kangaroo Child Bike Seat
review_body: I love the WeeRide!  Biking with my 1 year old daughter has been a great bonding experience.  I am able to easily talk to her as we are looking at the same things.  I love having her in front of me, instead of behind where we wouldn't be able to communicate well.  The first time we went biking I was the one saying, \\"Weeeeee\\" the whole time!  I'm so happy with this purchase.        Attaching the mounting bar that the child seat sits on was a little difficult.  I have a mens bike that didn't have a lot of room from the bottom of the handle bar to the top of the bar to easily fit the mounting bar of the WeeRide in between that space.  I also had to permanently raise my seat up so the WeeRide mounting bar could attach underneath it, which now makes it hard for me to reach the floor comfortably.  If I was taller (5'3\\") then it wouldn't be a problem.        Other people have mentioned having to ride with your knees pointing out and that was true for me too.  Although it wasn't a problem and barely noticable since I am on the short side.  These two slight problems are both due to the type of bike I have, not the product in particular.  The riding experience is well worth the slight troubles.  I highly recommend the WeeRide!!

product_title: Serta Elevated Diamond Coil Airbed
review_body: The mattress holds air and inflates easily.  That is the good part.  But it says it has a felt top which it doesn't, it is cheap vinyl. We specifically did not want the vinyl because it the sheets and blankets slip more and the cold transfers easier.  We were stuck in the situation of keeping it because we bought it just before a bunch of company was coming to town for my retirement from the military.  So we were faced with not using it and going shopping around town the next day trying to find what we wanted impacting our family time together or keeping it and using it as is.  We used it as the family time was much more important and I will just be disappointed in Amazon for having an advertisement that lied.

product_title: RX Trunk Bag EX
review_body: I used the Amazon reviews when purchasing this product.  The reviews were more accurate than the manufacturers description, the manufacturers description of the size is larger than the actual item.  It is the perfect size for my biking trips.

product_title: Razor Pocket Rocket Miniature Electric Bike
review_body: This is a really great product for children, especially children of parents who ignore safety warnings about the appropriate age for riders.  The product is powerful enough to haul a full grown adult, which means it's AWESOMELY overpowered for a small child. Putting that much torque and acceleration in the hands of an inexperienced rider, along with the absence of shocks makes this really fun to watch if you like really dramatic crashes and road rash.    I'd recommend avoiding a helmet as well, as it could decrease the Darwin effects of this technology.

product_title: LEDwholesalers Uv LED Ultra Violet Blacklight Flashlight 3 Aaa Urine and Scorpion Detector
review_headline: Not good for urine detection in carpet.
review_body: Bought this flashlight to try it out on urine detection in carpet and even in a fully blacked out room it hardly gives any results. I tested it in a room with known urine contamination but not much showed and I still had to place the light within 4-6\\" of the carpet in able to see anything. Would not recommend it at all.

product_title: TETON Sports Outfitter XXL Camping Cot; Perfect for Base Camp and Hunting; Cots for Adults; Free Storage Bag Included
review_body: Great cot! My wife and I shared it but it wasn't big enough for our 3 year old to climb on as well! I am goind to get a pad before we use it again. I think that will improve our comfort. Both of our backs were hurting before the camping trip and so it wasn't a very good test for the cot. We weren't feeling any better on the trip home! I wouldn't advise sleeping double unless you like being close, though. We fit, but there wasn't any room to move. Very well built. Looks like it will last many years. Setup was good.

product_title: Planet Bike Cascadia Front and Rear Bicycle Fender Set with Mud Flaps
review_body: I bought the 45mm fenders for my hybrid, which has 700x35mm tires. I've ridden that setup for about 6 months. The coverage has been absolutely excellent. The mudflaps extend quite low and really keep the bike clean and my feet dry.     Fenders are almost always fussy to install. These were easier than most. I like that they came packaged with locknuts for every bolt; on past fenders I've had to go over every single bolt with Locktite. These fenders were very easy to adjust, and they stayed in adjustment with no excess rattling.     The 45mm fenders say that they are for \\"hybrid/touring\\" but they did not make the transition to my new touring bike well. New bike (Surly LHT, 52cm) has 26\\"x1.5\\" tires. The fenders are just barely not wide enough; although the bike stayed reasonably clean, my feet really got soaked. The fender circumference is also a poor fit and makes an unpleasing visual line around the 26\\" tires. I've ordered the Cascadia ATB fenders to try because I was so pleased with how the 45mm fenders worked on my hybrid.    Edited to add: The ATB fenders give much better rain coverage on my Surly. After going through some mud and light rain today my bike was clean and my feet dry. However, the fenders sit very far out from the wheel - almost an inch out. I could wish for a longer L bracket at the top of both the front and rear fenders, and a spacer at the chainstay bridge to decrease this excess amount of clearance and even further improve the rain protection.

product_title: Saris Bones 805 (2-Bike) Trunk Mount Rack
review_headline: You get what you pay for.
review_body: Don't use this rack on a nice car.  I bought it to use with my \\"beater.\\"  I don't see how you could use this and not scratch your car.  The 6 straps are going to pull on your trunk lid and the three rubber feet are going to alter your paint.  I was not surprised or disappointed but want you to know.  Also, my wife's hardtail (yeh, it's kinda funny) fit on the rack fine, but my full suspension Kona wouldn't fit on the rack even if I loosened the carrying arms and moved them in.  So, yeh, I guess I am a little disappointed.  Road bikes and hardtails with big, open frames will fit nicely.

product_title: Park Tool MLP-1 Master Link Pliers
review_body: Makes disassembly and reassembly of a chain with at master link quick and easy.  Trying to squeeze the chain together prior to having this tool was a real pain.

product_title: Rollerblade Bladerunner Girls Phaser 4-Size Adjustable Skate
review_body: I bought these for my daughter (age 4, size Y11 shoe) and they work great. I've skated for about 20 years and used to teach kids to skate, so I'm tremendously pleased to be teaching my own kid this time.    The boot is a mix of soft shoe and stiff plastic around the heel and ankle. It looks comfortable, much better than the all-plastic boots that typified early inline skates. My daughter doesn't complain about the skates hurting at all.    I'm doubtful that the laces are useful. I removed them. Between the heel strap and ankle buckle there's plenty to keep this skate secure on the feet.    Contrary to other reviewers, I believe the skates fit true to size. I've got the skates dialed to Y11, same as my daughter's shoe size, and they fit perfectly. Note that most kids wearing skates wear them much too large! When standing, the skate should look like an extension of the leg, there should not be side-to-side play.    Wheels are fine, they're on the small side of course (72mm) and hardness (durometer) is appropriate for outdoor skating. They've got plenty of grip on typical asphalt surfaces. My daughter has no problems with slipping due to the wheels losing grip.    My one criticism, and this is more a difference of opinion than a quality issue, is that I think the smaller skates should have a three wheel frame instead of four. On the smallest size skate, the frame is long enough relative to the boot that it's comparable to a speed skate. This makes it very stable at speed, but has the disadvantage of giving the skater very little leverage on the heel brake. Rollerblade used to make a three wheel skate for kids back in the 90's; now nobody does.    The heel brake looks like a standard Rollerblade brake and therefore should be easy to find replacements for. I doubt kids will have enough weight to burn through brakes quickly, however. (I mow through them, but I'm 170lbs.) I consider a heel brake essential to skating in urban environments; the alternative is trashing your wheels with power stops, and I'd rather trash a brake than my wheels.    Note that this skate does *not* come with an extra axle for the brake wheel, so you can't remove the heel brake even if you want to. (The axle used for the brake wheel is longer than the rest.) Most skates come with an extra regular-length axle to give you the option of removing the brake. I'm indifferent on this, however, seeing as I'd keep the brake on there.

product_title: Thule Fit Kit for 400XT and Rapid Aero Foot
review_headline: Thule ........I would expect better quality.......but it works - Fit Kit 2187
review_body: I also purchased the 2187 fit kit for a 2nd generation scion xB. I agree the instructions from Thule are poor quality.  I have been using Thule racks on multiple vehicles for about 10 years and the quality of the instructions and the fit kits has diminished.  I also extended the distance between the feet by ¾ of an inch both front and back.  I also extended the distance between the front and back bars from 26 inches to 30 inches, for added stability. Lastly are the clamps (brackets), yes the front and back are different sizes.  But the problem with the door gasket sticking out is because the angle of the clamp (the part that hooks on to the door opening) is incorrect.  It's obvious if you look at the gap in the back of the clamp against the car body (and for you skeptics - no this has nothing to do with changing the distance between the feet, because I tried it both ways).  I used a vice lined with some thin cardboard (to prevent damaging the protective coating) and readjusted the angle of the clamps and it cured the door gasket issue and made the rack more secure.  After all is said and done, I feel the rack is secure, but I would expect better quality instructions and fit kits from Thule.  I noticed a 2nd generation xB a few days ago with what I thought was a Thule rack and it turned out to be an Inno rack, which appears to be a knock-off Thule style rack.  The fit kit appeared better than the Thule and it looks like the feet will accept Thule Load Bars - Watch out Thule it looks like someone took your design and made it better..... Comments welcome..

product_title: Coleman Queen-Sized Quickbed with Wrap 'N' Roll Storage
review_body: I love this Coleman Bed!  When guests come over to my house, and I feel that they shouldn't drive home (too late, or too much alcohol) I just pull out the bed (it only takes 1/2 cubic foot to store in the closet) inflate it, and throw sheets, blanket and pillows on it, in less then 5 minutes.  Then they can crash for the night, and sleep very comfortably.    I've even slept on the bed many times when family has come to visit.  It can be adjusted firmer or softer, depending on the amount of air that you put into it.      I would recommend that you buy the matteress and the pump seperately, as one or the other will probably out-live it's partner, and if they are combined in one unit, if one fails, you have to throw out the other too.      The electric pump inflates the mattress in just 3 minutes, and deflates it in less then 2 minutes.  If I need to pack it up quickly I use this feature of the seperate electric pump. If I am just deflating it at my house, I just open the valve, and it deflates completly on it's own.  It just lays down flat, so you can fold it over in quarters and then roll it up.    I simply love it!

product_title: Pearl iZUMi Men's Cyclone Cycling Glove
review_body: These have been fine for this november like weather. I don't think they would be warm enough for the northern Illinois winter. Free shipping from Amazon not as fast as it used to be but still a great deal.

product_title: Tracks Sherlock Staff
review_body: Excellent stick. Replaces an older, identical stick that has been misplaced or lost. It was for my wife and she loves it. Quick adjustment and includes camera attach bolt in handle and metal point at the bottom for great grip and stability.

product_title: CatEye - Strada Cadence Cycle Computer
review_body: Like a number of other reviewers, I was initially impressed with this product when I took it out of the box.  Slim, attractive, easy to read, etc...   It took me about ten minutes to mount, which was great.  Wheel magnet....WAY too far away from the chain stay where the sensor is supposed to be mounted.   So, with a rigged up extra centimeter of shim, I got the speed to work.  Ugly, but working.  For the next week, it worked like a charm for my commute to work on the road.  On Saturday, I took it out on some gravel paths, looked down, and it was GONE!   Bounced right out.  I can't imagine this being a sturdy enough for even a causal off road mountain biker.   The computer uses a button on the back and a bracket that allows the whole unit to tilt slightly and depress the back button to change the readout.   So, I can't speak to the longevity of this unit, but I can say it has a least two major design flaws, and that in my book, makes this a poor choice.    On the plus side, Cateye's customer service was great.  I just called, and without even actually asking them for another, they sent one out for free.  I will continue to use it, I will just remove it before going off road.

product_title: Pelican LED Tactical Flashlight
review_headline: Bright. Practical. Versatile. Durable. Efficient. The Glock of flashlights.
review_body: The 8060 is perfect for me.  I love that I can change to alkaline in the field if need be.  It's a larger flashlight but not overwhelmingly brighter than the 7060 (which I also own).  I depend on my equipment to run in adverse conditions in isolated areas for 18+ hour days.  The 8060 is a serious piece of gear.  Actual quote from warranty info: \\"Guarantee does not cover shark bite, bear attack or children under 5\\"  HAHAHAHA!

product_title: Serfas Bike Transport Case
review_body: I hesitated for a while between the Serfas and Thule Bike case. I went with the Serfas after reading other sites reviews and, believe it or not, based on zooming the product picture.  The case is built with strong plastic composite. Both side fit clamp nicely to each other. My favorite feature is the 2 locks on each side (that's the main difference I saw with the Thule).  The case fits my XL Kuota K-Factor perfectly and I can't wait to ship it UPS or Fedex to wherever I do an ironman. The rates are much cheaper that trying to accomodate flying with it (airlines will charge oversize + overweight and might not even accept the box based on the linear dimension being over 84\\".

product_title: ENO Eagles Nest Outfitters - DoubleNest Hammock
review_body: I bought this hammock as a gift for my brother and he absolutely loves it! He's 6'3\\" and 180lbs and he fits very nicely in it. It's comfortable, durable, supportive and easy to carry around. For a minimalist that doesn't want to tote around a tent/sleeping bag, this is a great choice. Just grab a pillow and blanket if necessary, and you're set!

product_title: Intramatic Malibu Mosquito Inhibitor Refills (Pack of 2)
review_body: The product is effective, came in a well packed container as shown in the purchase description.

product_title: Fenix 6 Level High Performance Cree LED Flashlight, Black, 4-Inch
review_body: I have carried this light nearly every day in the 5 months that I have owed it.  This is a small flashlight (can fit comfortably in a pocket) that is well built. Honestly I nearly didn't buy it because of the cost but after reading the reviews I took a chance. I'm glad I did. This light had been dropped quite a few times onto hard surfaces and it has not affected operation in any way. Included is a very sturdy clip that securely clips the light to a shirt pocket.    The one downside is that the battery life could be better. I tend to use the light on HIGH most of the time because of the fantastic light output (when you need to see you need to SEE!) and the battery sometimes dies on me. The way the current regulation works is that the light DOES NOT get dimmer until the battery is dead, so what happens is that you have light then suddenly no light (or flickering light) when the battery is dead. I am using a quality rechargeable battery (Sanyo Eneloop) so the battery is not the problem. This is probably because the flashlight uses a SINGLE \\"AA\\" battery (which is why it's so small).    Also I wish the partially untwisted lens cap position would be the \\"medium\\" brightness setting instead of \\"low\\". That way I could extend battery life. I find it difficult to set the light to \\"medium\\" brightness because the lens cap must be partially untwisted (doing this sets \\"low\\" brightness) and then the button pressed once or twice to gradually increase brightness above \\"low\\". The problem is when you click the button the light turns off for a short time making it hard to determine what brightness setting you are on (unless you keep track of how many times you press the button). I find the low brightness setting useless because it doesn't output sufficient light.     Still, it's a good small flashlight despite these flaws and the fact that it uses a standard AA makes it better than some of the other Fenix models that use \\"weird\\" batteries (like CR123A). I also wouldn't bother with anyLED flashlight that uses AAA batteries because AA batteries have a higher AmpHour capacity rating (i.e. AA last longer than AAAs)    A slightly cheaper version of this light that gets rid of the strobe mode (which I never use) and has a brighter \\"low\\" setting is the [[ASIN:B001GAOOFA Fenix L1T 2 Level High Performance Cree LED Flashlight]]  This one is slightly different but still uses 1 AA (no pocket clip though)

product_title: Yaktrax Pro
review_body: I live in New Hampshire and we have a lot of snow followed by melt, ice, snow. The yak trax are pretty easy to get on. They stay on well. They're easy to store. I wouldn't get them if I had weak or really arthritic hands because it does take some strength to pull on. Otherwise, I love being able to walk at full speed and not have to slow down just because it's icy out.

review_body: Only one tray fits on the twin stroller - very poor design and a headache for a busy mom.

product_title: High Sierra Classic Series Cirque 30 Frame Pack
review_body: Bought this a few months back and have used it for several 3-5 hour hikes as well as day long hikes. Great backpack for the price. I've carried about 20 lbs (mostly as water) in it a few times and its held up pretty well. The padding on the back and waist belt is pretty good. Good purchase overall.

product_title: Sea to Summit TravellingLight Garment Mesh Bag
review_body: This is the latest in travel bags from the folks at Sea to Summit and it is extremely light and durable. I found something similar two years ago at the Muji store in Yokohama and wondered when somthing like this would be available in the US...Now it is!   Highly recommended

product_title: Pacific Shorewood Women's Cruiser Bike (26-Inch Wheels)
review_body: For the money this is a pretty good bike.  The dificulty in putting it together was a 4, things were bent and had to be corrected.  Once all together, the bike had problems moving another bent part that had to be fixed.  It still makes a clicking noise when being peddled from the gear area.  I guess you get what you paid for.  My daugher only uses this bike when here on weekends, so it is OK for that.  I would not buy this if this is a daily use bike.  My mom always said, \\" you get what you pay for\\"  This statement would apply to this bike.

product_title: Bolle Performance Swiftkick Sunglasses (Black/Modulator Rose + TNS Gun)
review_body: I purchased the Swiftkick to use with my SOS prescription adapter that I have with my Bolle Vigilante. Unfortunately, each frame that uses the SOS adapter has a special adapter. I can see well enough without my adapter that I can still use the glasses at least to run (I bought an adapter for the frames, so I can now use them to drive in as well).    That being said, I like the styling of the frames, and really liked the Modulater lenses for the glasses. The Modulater Rose is unlike most other Rose lenses I have had in the past, in that when I remove them on a bright day everything is not green!    I just want to make sure that you know that the prescription adapters for the various frames are NOT interchangeable. The Bolle website does not make this readily apparent.    I like the fact you can interchange lenses. I use a clear lens to run in at night and on trails. I wish that someone would come up with a package deal to get 3 or 4 lens colors in a package instead of buying them 1 at a time.

product_title: Black Diamond Rocklock TwistLock Carabiner Twist Lock (Colors May Vary)
review_headline: This is one of my favorites
review_body: This biner is great. Its a little on the heavy side, but i've never had a problem with it.

review_body: I had many knives my entire life and I always wanted one that had many gadgets and one that gave me protection. I have about 4 swiss knives and one hunting knife. I would trade all of them for my new hercules swiss. It has all , no more than you could ever want from a knife. It is very useful and well crafted and it also makes you feel safe. I spent 2 weeks looking for a good swiss and found the hercules. I searched for the best price. The lowest I could find was $80. I was about to purchase it because I spent so long searching for the best price. But then I saw it on amazon for this cheap price. About $50 is the dream price. I amvery stisfied with my purchase and I love this brilliant knife.

product_title: Fuzion LandShark 4-Wheel Kneeboard
review_body: My son saw the Shark Board at Walmart Xmas 2009.  When I went to Walmart in Palm Beach County,  all the shark boards were sold out.  I found the shark board on Amazon, purchased it and still saved 30 dollars including shipping.  Now we are the only family in our community with a shark board and a happy son I have.  Amazon's the Bomb!

review_headline: Nice size for kid's lunch box, but not leak proof
review_body: I bought these bottles (5 of them) after searching high and low for a small and durable bottle for my kids' school lunch boxes. These looked good for the price, and fit quite nicely. The only problem is that they do start leaking after a few weeks of use, especially if they drink out of the nozzle.

product_title: Mountain Boy Sledworks Bambino Grande Pull Sled
review_body: I bought the sled for my 6-year-old daughter as a Christmas present.  It snowed two days ago so we opened it early and went sledding on a neighborhood hill.  It is a great sled!  It was the envy of all the other kids sledding.  It was fast, went straight, and did not spin or tip.  It worked well on thick or thin snow.    I notice that one of other reviewers said it's too heavy for her to carry from her condo to the park.  We also live in a high-rise condo, but I didn't find it heavy at all (I'm a 5'2\\" woman and not particularly strong).  It is 10 pounds and very easy to carry.

product_title: Mini-Logo Skateboard S4 101A Wheels
review_body: got these for my son, he likes them. Been using them for about 6 months now.
