review_body: Despite the confusion on the website, this is the correct type for my amazing walking stick that I love

product_title: Darkstar Spike 7.7" Complete Skateboard
review_body: The board had barely any pop, it flexed when it shouldn't have and the trucks were speed demons, which are cheap and only last around three months. I went on vacation and forgot a board, so I bought one of these. The Darkstar wheels were terrrible. They are super soft and ride like they were made out of rubber, not urethane. The only positive part was getting a complete for less than $70. If cheap is your game, then get one, but find better wheels. The bearings are dope however, and I think they were speed demons too.

product_title: WeeRide Mounting Bar for Center Child Carrier (Grey)
review_body: I and my wife often ride bikes together. Before we bought this bar, I used to ride her bike with the carrier, and she rode mine. Since we are different height, she had to lower the seat on my bike each time we went for a ride, and I had to pedal without being able to fully straighten my legs because it's very hard to change the height of a seat on a bike with the mounting bar installed. The additional mounting bar for my bike completely solved this problem. All we have to do now is just swap the seat between bikes which is very easy. With this bar you can even do things such as drop-off your child at some place leaving the seat there, and then someone can come to pick-up him/her on another bike with the bar installed.

product_title: CamelBak 100-Ounce UnBottle
review_body: Maybe it is my bad for not reading the spec carefully. But anyway, this thing does not come with straps. So if you need to buy straps separately if you plan to use it while you ride your bike.

product_title: CamelBak Insulated 0.75-Liter Bottle Sleeve
review_body: This water bottle is amazing. I feel like I drink more buy using a straw than tipping a water bottle up to drink. This is the PERFECT solution. Its easy to clean, water stays fresh. I buy these as gifts for people I love it so much!

product_title: Bolle Fusion Sidney Sunglasses,Shiny Black/TNS
review_body: these fit perfectly, thats hard to find for me. overall very happy with this purchase. prompt delivery too.

product_title: Shimano Ultegra PD-6700 SL Pedal
review_body: This is my second pair of clipless pedals, my former being crank brothers candy pedals. So going from those to the Shimano Ultegra took a little getting used to. It's similar to driving a stick shift.  It takes a few times to get it down, but once you do you realize that it is so much more fun. I would recommend sitting on your bike next to a wall to support yourself on and practiced clipping in and clipping out. The two biggest things I notice is one, getting clipped back in from a stop can take a little practice and the second, I found that these are way more comfortable then my former pair of pedals. They sport a bigger platform and I found that I could pedal longer with less strain on my feet. I'm really glad that I purchased these and I am looking forward to many miles with them.

product_title: Texsport Willowbend 2 Person Backpacking Camping Trail Tent
review_body: nice tent for the kids.  Easy to set up and store.  Only problem was the center poles moved out of position easily.  The kids sometimes knocked it down climbing in and out.  Great because they could set it up on their own with a little assistance.  Big enough for a twin air matress, but nothing else.

product_title: Zippo Flexneck Utility Lighter , Black
review_body: Nice, heavy, solid lighter. It is a Zippo so it should work well. I dig the dual flame and Zippo's lifetime warranty is nice.

product_title: Coleman 4D Rugged Personal Size Rugged Lantern
review_body: I bough this lantern when I was living in Florida and suffered a bunch of power outages. It it light, real bright, and it works great. The batteries last long.     This is a good lantern to have to be able to go around the house, read a little, cook a sandwish... This lantern really fit the bill for an emergency light.

product_title: Sawyer Products Premium Permethrin Clothing Insect Repellent
review_body: We've been using this for the past 3 years. Works great. Great for the outdoors person (i.e. backpacking, hunting, fishing, hiking, biking etc...) It really keeps the bugs off!

product_title: iBert Safe-T Front Mounted Child Bicycle Seat
review_body: Love it and my son (18 months) loves it too. Only one thing I could think of to improve this it to make locking the saftly belt little easier. Once toddler is in seat its difficult to access belt clip.

product_title: Gravity Threads Unisex Warm Half Finger Stretchy Knit Gloves
review_headline: Do what they are supposed to do
review_body: These are my 'Kindle' gloves. I love these gloves for bus commuting in fall/winter/spring. They allow you to read with the Kindle and handle an MP3 player while keeping your hands reasonably warm.     For the price the quality seems OK. These are not gloves for super low temperatures (e.g. 20 F). The material is thin. This allows for moving your fingers freely. And they take little space in your bag. But it comes at the expense of insulation.     Overall a good product that I would recommend to others.

product_title: M-Wave Bicycle Frame Bags
review_headline: Does not Fit bikes with small frames
review_body: This did not fit my Bike that has a 49 cm Frame.  I wish it said in the description which size frames this bag fits.  When I tried to attach it to my bike, it kept hitting the water bottle holder.  Do Not Buy if you have a smaller frame size.  The quality of the bag itself is ok, that is why I gave it two stars.

product_title: InStep Ultra Runner 2 Double Jogging Stroller
review_body: I bought this stroller for my 3 1/2 yr old and my 1 yr old and they love it!  It's a great running stroller because the front wheel is fixed, as oppposed to an unstable and shaky swivel wheel.  I also love that it's easy to fold up and pop the wheels off. The only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of five is because, as other reviews have stated, it needs better seat cushions.  My older daughter complained immediately that it was uncomfortable, but I gave her a little blanket to rest her head, problem solved!  Oh well, other than that it's a great stroller and I would recommend it to anyone who is looking for a reasonably priced jogger.

product_title: CamelBak 0.5-Liter Insulated Stainless Steel Better Bottle
review_body: I've had a plastic Camelbak bottle for a while and have always liked the setup.  Yesterday I bought this stainless insulated version.  Filled it up w/ cold water from my refrigerator when I left for work this morning (no ice).  8hrs later it's still very cold.  Unreal, 5 stars for sure.

product_title: Avenir Cone Wrench Set
review_headline: Two wrenches, 4 sizes on each.  Sizes 13,14,15,16.
review_body: Ignore the description about the Avenir Saddle.  You will get two wrenches with 4 sizes on each.  They seem to work fine.  It would have been nice to have a 17 & 18 in this set too.

product_title: Delta Botticelli Four Bike Storage Rack
review_body: Very weak rack, leans badly with 3 lightweight mountain bikes.  Had to reinforce several holes with much larger screws and it still leans.   Customer service provided me with spare parts at no charge, but the rack is not well built.  It is for small bikes only.  I would have bought the Brookstone rack if it was available at the time of purchase.

product_title: Kent Adult Westport Folding Tricycle
review_body: I ordered this \\"bike\\" for my 11 yr old grandson - he is a special needs kid with Fragile X syndrome, a hereditary learning disability.  He has wanted a bicycle but has gotten too big for training wheels.  I wasn't sure if he would use the break on the handlebar - but he got on it, we showed him what to do and he took off.  It has done wonders for his esteem and loves the wind in his hair and face as he races up and down the street.  The ablility to fold the bike in half is excellent for transporting it - the handle bars do not go down so it is still abit tall to get into your vehicle.  It is very well made and I recommend it to anyone, it is cool looking on the road - an excellent bike for touring too!

product_title: Fenix FNX-E01BK E Series LED Flashlight, Black
review_body: Basically, it's GREAT! Small, portable, reliable, cheap.  Way better than Maglite Solitaire in all senses.    Once you get used to it, you'll love it.  The only black spot is that it doesn't come with the reuqired AAA battery, but it's not a big deal (just the fact that you want to start using it ASAP :P )

product_title: ALPS Mountaineering Camp Chair
review_body: I have also purchased the Slumberjack SJK Big Chair, 99% of the people out there will find the ALPS chair far more comfortable. Chair is rock solid, fit & finish is great. Back uprights pop out and fold into the chair to reduce size a big plus over the Slumberjack.  The back is also sloped back much better feel than the Slumberjack, the upper edge of the back tends to cut into my back on the Slumberjack and it's straight back was bothersome after the first 45miin of sitting.      Arm rests are very comfortable although I'm sure the foam padding will have to be taped over with cloth tape at some point as it will undoubtedly end up cut up with trips in and out of the car.  The round tube of the Slumberjack (also padded) does not even compare - I found them unusable.  The ALPS chair with the wave arm rests seems to pull your elbows into the perfect position.  Chair also has a hanging cup holder, not the best and would not work with open glasses but still better than nothing as with the Slumberjack.    The Slumberjack does have a couple advantages in regards to size. It's seat height is a couple inches taller, and the seat is also wider and deeper since the back canvas is separate from the seat (one piece contoured padded canvas in the ALPS chair).    All that said I am 6'5\\" tall and weigh 250lbs and would much prefer sitting through 4 hours of soccer in the ALPS chair over anything I've ever sat in before.     Worth every cent, buy it.

product_title: Petzl MYO RXP Headlamp
review_body: I *love* this headlamp. I bought it specifically for nighttime trail running and it definitely does the job. It's amazingly bright at it's highest setting; I'm able to run nearly as fast in full dark as I do during the day. It takes 3 AA batteries so it's not as light as some lamps, but with the battery pack in the back it balances well on your head. I don't have any problems with the comfort, and I'm notoriously picky about anything on my head.    As another review mentioned, the controls are tiny so it's not that easy to toggle it with gloves on. Once you get used to the placement it's not too bad though. And for me this quirk is minor given how well the unit performs.     If you need a *very* bright headlamp that is comfortable and lightweight enough for active sports this is the product for you.

product_title: Coleman Fold 'N' Go Camp Pillow
review_body: I recently purchased 2 of these little buggers for a weekend camping trip in Joshua Tree.  Both me and my wife were very satisfied with the comfort of the pillow.  I almost wish it was a hair bigger, but it packs so nice as is.  I would recommend this to any camper on the lookout for a quality pillow.

product_title: Coleman Queen-Sized Quickbed with 4D Pump and Wrap 'N' Roll Storage
review_headline: the bed has a little bit leaking, but overall it is a great deal
review_body: The bed is very comfortable, but I have to inflate it after over-night use. It leaks especially when a huge man was sleeping on it. But it is fine for a skiny one (like me). I still love this bed and I use it quite often.

product_title: Therm-a-Rest Dream Time Sleeping Pad
review_headline: Very comfortable, easy to use, too big for hiking
review_body: Best camp mattress I have tried.  Very close to a normal bed feel.  I tried getting my own memory foam topper and adding to the lower priced model, but I like this \\"package\\" better for both sleep feel, convenience, keeping everything clean, and packing size.

product_title: Relaxo-Bak Original Orthopedic Comfort Seat - Gray
review_body: I damaged my tailbone about 2 1/2 years ago, and have been searching for relief since then. Have tried the cushions with a piece cut out, but they haven't helped much. I ordered this to help in long car rides (8 hrs plus), and I would say it helped a little bit. However, I have taken it the last couple of evenings to a tennis stadium where I sit on hard surface chairs. It has been amazing! Trying to get up has not resulted in the searing pain that usually accompanies rising after sitting on anything hard for more than a few minutes. I realize that everyone's pain is different, but I highly recommend giving the relaxo-bak a try.

product_title: Serengeti Velocity Sunglasses
review_body: I am very impressed with the performance of the Serengeti Velocity Drivers.  I have worn nothing else for the last 10 years and have found no reason to switch.

product_title: Coleman Aluminum Non-stick Griddle
review_body: Have had two of these griddles. They warped easily. Go with a TFal griddle for about $30. Much better quality, same size, deeper sides (about 1\\" deep compared to about 1/4\\" on this Coleman), and better handles. The nonstick surface on the first one we owned got trashed when I overcooked some eggs and underapplied sufficient oil. Get the TFal!

product_title: Camelbak Better bottle 0.5 L
review_body: Love the size, color choices and price.  Having to bite the straw, not so much fun.  Like that it fits in all of my cup holders.

product_title: Osprey Mutant 38 Pack
review_headline: Well built and still light weight
review_body: I have been a little rough with this bag so far and it has fared no damage. I bought it as I wanted a smaller pack for when we go top-rope climbing. I am no miraculous climber or anything but we are sometimes hiking out a bit to get to bluffs. I could have just got a rope bag but this pulls double duty. this pack works well despite the fact that it is essentially frame less. there is a plastic panel to firm it up a bit but that is quite flimsy. There is also a removable tri-fold foam pad that I can't imagine using for anything but I leave it in place none the less for added rigidity. when you pack it in tight and cinch up the compression straps making it solid then it carries well on the back, the load lifters work etc...    I do like the Z pattern compression straps and the fact that they are open ended, more manufactures (and osprey, on there other packs) should do this. it proves to be very useful at times.     There are no external pockets of any kind. I suppose If I where into alpine climbing I would appreciated the waste belt configuration a bit more but I don't do that so to me it is a place a pocket could be but is not. It is not the most light weight pack for it's size but it comes in pretty good. I have used the haul loops and an accessory cord to pull it up the face of a bluff after climbing up so my climbing partner did not have to drag it up the slope when we where leaving out. it dose seem to hold up well to this abuse. so far...    Check out the Osprey website for a bit more about this pack and a short video.

product_title: Princeton Tec Torrent Xenon 8AA Dive Light
review_headline: Bright flashlight, good size, nice switch, poor redesign (cheaper)
review_body:
UPDATE: Contacted Princteon Tec regarding the beam quality. A real person answered the phone, took my information, send me a replacement reflector and cap with no questions asked. Was genuinely concerned and wanted to fix the issue. This took 5 mins and cost me nothing. While I still have reservations regarding the new design, I have NO concerns regarding customer service.

I also sent in a Princeton Tec keychain light which did not work properly after a battery change and they replaced that, no questions asked as well. I like the way this company does business.
----------------
I would have given it 5 stars had PrincetonTec not decided to cut costs at the expense of product quality.

Good size and shape for holding while diving.

The included cord is great to attach to a clip of some sort so that you don't lose it while moving around. Though I would recommend a tougher cord if you are hard on your toys.

The previous model I use as my primary has the battery tray/circuit board that snaps into a notch cut out of the threads. This makes for secure fit. Very important, as the first one I received from Amazon was defective and the tray would not stay far enough back in to provide enough focused light. It created a dead spot in the center of the beam. I didn't realize it until I had left on a trip. Thankfully Amazon exchanged it for another one, which is MUCH better but still has a slight dark spot in the center of the beam where it should be brightest.

If you can find an older model that has the battery tray snap in to the body, I would recommend that one wholeheartedly.

If you purchase a new one, make sure the center beam is bright and does not have any dark spots or halo's.

The LED model does not seem to suffer from this condition, but it could be that the two I tried were just improperly made.

product_title: Camp Chef Outdoor Camp Oven
review_body: We have a full size RV kitchen but when the weather is hot, we prefer to cook outdoors to limit the excess heat in the unit. This used to mean the grill or the ubiquitous Coleman stove we all use. I bought this item for the oven and am very pleased with it so far. The molded in handles and (relatively) light weight make it easy to move. The oven size surprised me by accepting an 11 x 13 cake pan. The oven temp control is iffy at best but manageable, more like a grill than an oven. Like all lightweight ovens, you have to be aware of hot spots and I'm getting a pizza stone for the bottom to temper the heat concentrated on the thin metal bottom. The major advantage is being able to cook the entire meal in one spot, outdoors. The included tank adapter was a nice touch.

product_title: Therm-a-Rest Lite Seat
review_body: It's great, it really works well, I don't even need the full inflation, and it rolls up for easy carrying.  I tend to use it on hard park benches.

product_title: Sixsixone Veggie Elbow Guard
review_headline: Great protection, but I wish it would stay put
review_body: I use this for all sort of trail riding.  They've saved me quite a few times already.  I like how it's got a lot of padding, so falling on your elbow doesn't transmit the full force of the impact to your shoulder.  My biggest beef with these pads is that they continually ride down your arm until they end up on your wrists.  If I'm going down Rock It or the San Juan trail with these on, I'm inevitably spending half my time pulling these pads back into place.  They fit tight enough on my arms, but when I start sweating, I can't keep 'em on my elbows.

product_title: Flexible Flyer Snow Screamer
review_body: Fun to ride. After about one month, all the handles broke. We loved the sled other than that.

product_title: Razor A2 Kick Scooter
review_body: Scooter was exactly what we wanted for our 5 year old daughter who has been riding her big brother's very old Razor for the last few months.  Small problem:  one of the handles did not fit into the cylinder.  Of course we did not try to put it together until Christmas Eve and were stuck with it so my husband hammered it in . . . it can never be taken apart, but the scooter works just fine.  It's purple and that is really all she cares about.  We purchased her brother's Razor about 10 years ago and it still works great, so we think Razors are good products.

product_title: Evergreen Design 002 | Clean White
review_body: This is my first stainless water bottle. The bottle doesn't leak, gets cold when cold water is put in and very hot when washing with hot water. other than that i am very happy with this purchase.  for the money, it was totally worth it! great buy, reasonable price! Water tastes great coming out of it & keeps it cold.  love it!

product_title: Ergon GP1 Hand Grip
review_body: My Ergon grips are perfect.  They relieve the pressure on my wrists and shift it to the palm and heel of my hands.  They don't interfere with my grip shifters or my brakes, either.  I highly recommend them.

product_title: Coleman Full-Sized Quickbed with Wrap 'N' Roll Storage
review_headline: Great bed.. but but the one with the pump
review_body: This is a great bed.. but the only problem is pumping it. Buy the bed with the pump its worth the extra 18 bucks.

product_title: Sun Ez-1Sc Recumbent Fenders Black Ss Stay 16/20
review_body: Easy to install and the bike looks great with the fenders. Be positive, no instructions.

product_title: Wigwam Merino Rugged Hiker Socks
review_headline: You get what you pay for
review_body: I searched for these socks high and low. My local outlet store doesn't sell them anymore because they can't make enough money on them. They are more expensive than other work socks on the market, but nothing is tougher or more comfortable. The last few pairs of these I bought were several years ago and I'm just now replacing them. If you wear work boots and are on your feet for the better part of the day. These are the ones you are looking for. Nothing else will do for me. Worth the price, they last for years!

product_title: Eureka Pine Lodge Tent
review_body:
Easy to put up and very roomy.
The vertical walls give you much more space inside than dome tents.

product_title: Cateye HL-EL220 LED Bicycle Headlight
review_body: I ride in the city at night quite a bit, and I wanted a nice light to increase my visibility on lit roads, as well as for use as a good light source to ride unlit park trails.  This light does well at both.  It is quite bright, though somewhat less so than I hoped.  Easy tool-free installation was a snap.  Worthwhile buy for the price to be sure!

product_title: Texsport Lakeway Hammock
review_body: I read the reviews and ordered this hammock. I'd read it took a few days to break-in, but I've had it a month, and it remained as tippy as the day it arrived. Although the fabric was nice, and it appeared to be well made, it was simply miserable to lay on it and feel as though you could tip over at any time. We tried it at a varity of tensions, and the problem remained the same. I can't tell you how many people ended up in the garden unintentionally. I finally faced reality, dumped this hammock, and got one from Hammocks Rada which isn't tippy at all. This was a waste of money, and precious summer days.

product_title: Flagler Films Walking The Great Divide 2 Dvd
review_body: For someone hoping to walk the CDT himself, it was a great video.  The amazing vistas shown confirmed my desire to hike the trails and see the scenery in person.  The tips he gives seem very helpful also.  Well done.

product_title: Hyperflex Wetsuits Men's Cyclone 1.5mm Jacket
review_body: Easy to get in and out of, that's what I wanted.  No need to wear a skin underneath it.  Sizing chart is good.

product_title: Storm Women's 2mm Shorty Snorkel/Scuba/Water Sports Wetsuit
review_body: Fine fit, comfortable, well insulated. Upon the advice of friends, I bought one-two sizes smaller than I usually wear in street clothes. Wear the shortie for water aerobics in winter in an outdoor pool - air temperature 48-55 degrees in California. I have asthma so did not want to take any chances on getting too chilled - no flare-ups with this suit.

product_title: JanSport T501 Superbreak Backpack - Navy Weave
review_headline: Perfect for a large tote size backpack
review_body: I have a broken leg and am on crutches so I needed a light weight backpack to carry all my stuff and have my hands free.  This has been perfect.  It is very light but big enough to hold a sweater, etc as well as the former contents of my purse.

product_title: SportRack A90275 Aero XL Roof Box
review_body:
Same as everyone else I shopped around and chose this unit based on:
-good price
-relatively large amount of storage (for $500+ you can get more!)
-good reviews

It shipped pretty quickly. The local shipping company in Dallas (CEVA I think was their name) was awesome. The truck called me before their dispatch even did. They wanted to come by earlier than I'd been told (!!). I called them back on their cell phone and said what time would work for me. There came within 15 minutes of that time. What an exceptional delivery experience. Kudos to them.

I just installed the unit. Easy. I'll be able to do it in 5 minutes with practice. Only took 20 the first time. That included moving the bars on my roof rack. Now that they're in the right place installation will be a breeze.

Here's some observations I didn't see in any reviews.

On my 2003 Toyota Sequoia I set the roof bars all the way to the back and 30\\" apart. That's the widest apart the box can accomodate and it seems very stable.

It opens from the back vs the side so I'll have to stand on my bumper to load it. No biggie. Just thought I'd share.

The box only closes if you have the key in it and it's turned to a locked position. Don't lose your key :D. Think I'll go make a spare for my glove box.

Important piece of information... when installed on my Sequoia the total height is 7'10\\" (94\\") total. Certainly won't fit in under my garage door and we'll see if I can fit in any under cover parking.

I'm 6'4\\" and not strong or weak (40+ years old) and had NO problems lifting the sportsrack out of the shipping box, nor putting it on the roof of my car by myself. If you're under 6' it will probably not be as easy but for me it's perfect.

Oh yea, the box it comes in is HUGE... my 5 and 7 year old are LOVING it right now. They've decided it's a clubhouse and are all gathered around it with paints and crayons. What a great bonus :D

I'll come add more to this review after I use it a bit and decide if the 4 stars stays.

So far, installation and order/shipping experience was great.bit and decide if the 4 stars stays. So far, installation and order/shipping experience was great.

product_title: Transformer Bumble Bee 16-Inch Kids' Bike
review_body: We got this for my 5year son for Xmas! He loves it and rides it all the time!  The assembly was not difficult from what I understand,( my younger brother did the honors! ) The seat is easily adjusted as well as the handlebars! I have no complaints!!

product_title: CycleOps Mag Trainer w/o Adjuster
review_body: My husband and I each have a trainer and we think they are great.  They do need a bit of tweaking to get them just right and you can't coast but they still make for a great work out.  Some mornings are too cold and too dark to ride outside and I find the trainer to be a great safe alternative.  This product is our first trainer and I doubt we will be needed another.

product_title: Giro Zero Cycling Glove
review_body: I did have to reinforce a couple of the seems at the finger tips but only took like 15 minutes.  I've used them about 20 hours on road and mountain rides (intense and easy).  So far, I really like the fit and feel.  The nose wipe material is very soft and stays that way through the ride too.

product_title: Intex Pillow Rest Raised Airbed with Built-in Pillow and Electric Pump
review_body: i bought 2 of these for my family when they came to visit. they worked out great. i never slept on it myself but my family did and they liked it. it automatically inflates and deflates, you can adjust the firmness, etc. people complained about how the air leaks, but wouldn't all air mattresses do that after a while? just pump some more air into it...i think it's a good buy for the price if nothing else.

product_title: World Industries Flameboy V2 Mini (Complete)
review_headline: This is a mini and not mid - mixed product description
review_body: I purchased this for an 8 year old thinking I was buying the mid size.  The top level product description does say mini but in the body of the product info, it says mid with a size of 7.4.  Measuring it at home, this seems to be Micro as the width is 6.75 and the length is 27.

product_title: Guide Gear Queen Air Bed Fitted Cover / Sleeping Bag Green
review_body: I also purchased the Deluxe 100% Cotton Damask Stripe Mattress Pad, Queen, so the thin bottom layer didn't much matter.  Fit great on a 60x80x18 insta-bed and didn't creep up or slide all night.  I only gave four stars because it doesn't have a tremendous amount of insulation and will likely require an additional blanket for tent camping.

product_title: The AMAZING 95 LED Aluminum Flashlight
review_headline: Great Power!  Really Bright!!  Don't look at it directly!  It hurts!
review_body: This light is really bright and makes a great flood light.  I read several reviews in which they said to insert a piece of paper into the light housing around the batteries to stop the batteries from rattling inside.  I found a better solution.  Take the plastic package that the lights come in and cut the plastic out of the mold of the flashlight and insert them into the housing around the batteries.  You will have to cut them to fit.  They work great!  No rattling and no flickering of the light. All is well.  The light is well worth the money and should last a long time on a set of batteries.

product_title: Fenix Accessory Kit - LD and PD Series (4 Piece Kit)
review_body: Bear in mind that these accessories are mentioned to fit only on LD and PD series lights. I tried them on my TA21 and they do not fit. Having said that, the accessories, if they were to fit, are nice and should function as advertised. It's a shame that Fenix didn't supply an adapter to make these fit on other series lights.

product_title: Master Lock Key Cable Bicycle Lock (5-foot x 8mm )
review_body: this is a nice basic lock. Of course it is not a \\"super lock\\" but it is all you see in the picture and works well for basic situation.

product_title: Coleman 15 x 15 GeoSport Screen
review_body: This tent is relatively easy to put up, especially after you have done it once or twice, but like most tents, it takes two people.  It is very large and sturdy.  I am happy I spent a little more money and got what I paid for.

product_title: gearup The Grand Stand Single Bike Floor Stand, Black
review_body: This is a very helpfull tool to hold your bike at any place, easy to build up and strong enough for a big bike

product_title: Paricon Snow Castle Kit (20-Inch)
review_body: Got for my sister's family. The boys needed something to do outside, and this encouraged them. No need to treck up and down hills, can be used anywhere.

product_title: Klean Kanteen Stainless Steel Water Bottles
review_body: What I didn't realize before buying my 40-oz klean kanteen is that because it has no insulating liner, any cold beverage will create a lot of condensation on the bottle.  I bought this to have at my office, so that I can keep drinking water close at hand without having to waste a bunch of paper cups or plastic bottles.  I'm in a very dry environment, yet every time I pick up the bottle, there is a fresh puddle of water on my desk where it was sitting.  It has something to do with how the bottom of the bottle is slightly concave - moisture collects there when the bottle is sitting on a flat surface.  I dry everything off completely, set the bottle down on a new spot on my desk, and in 2 minutes, voila - new puddle.  I've even tried using slightly warmer water to minimize the condensation effects, and setting it on a napkin, but the puddles still appear.  I can only imagine that it will get worse during the humid summertime.    Besides my water bottle's little bladder problem, I love my klean kanteen.  It's attractively designed, lightweight, environmentally friendly, supposedly free of health risks, and it doesn't affect my water's taste.  It would be great for use in any setting in which it's not set down on a flat surface.  But if you plan on keeping this on a desk like I do, you might want to consider something else.  Now that I've got it, I guess maybe I'll try to find a way to hang or suspend it from a hook or cradle or something to curb its little peeing problem.

product_title: CatEye - Strada Cadence Cycle Computer
review_body: I notice this happened to another reviewer.  My computer arrived without the cadence magnet.  So, I returned it with the appropriate explanation.  I received a replacement within days.  That was great.  But, it was missing the cadence magnet too!  So, I returned it and requested they make note of this problem so they didn't just ship me a 3rd defective unit.  Instead, I received an email informing me that my order was canceled.  (So I wouldn't have the same problem.)  I felt a bit as though I was being blamed for an obvious error on the manufacturer's part.  I wish I'd taken Ms. Gaitin's approach (see her review: she contacted Cateye and they sent her the magnet).

product_title: Bones Bearings Super Reds Bearings
review_body: Have been riding these for years - they are the best bearings you can get for the price! :D

product_title: Intex Prestige Downy Airbed Kit with Hand Held Battery Pump, Twin
review_body: 1st one leaked flat 1st nite.returned by ups while replacement was enroute.it has held up fine with daily use for past month.seems well made.i would recommend.this is re intex twin airbed.

product_title: Wenzel Ponderosa 10- by 8-Foot Four-Person Two-Room Dome Tent
review_headline: You Get What You Pay For
review_body: Purchased 2 of these for a weekend camping trip.  Rain fly on both tents was saturated under light rain and leaked through the screen top. Zippers on the entry doors were defective and came off track numerous times.  Rip cords pulled through the tent poles when simply folding the poles back up upon departure.     I've created a return/refund request for these.

product_title: Slider The Unscooter - U8 - Three Wheel Action Scooter - Black
review_body: My sons, ages 8 & 11 love this unscooter. We live on a culdesac and it's always used. They always have friends over and even though the garage is filled with riding items, they argue over who gets to ride this and for how long. I enjoy sneeking rides on it too!

product_title: Seirus Innovation Blizzard Hat
review_body: Great looking cap that does the job. Just large enough to cover my ears. Also, easy to wash. Just use gentle cycle and place on a bowl to dry.

product_title: OnGuard Beast 5018 Bicycle Chain Lock
review_body: I bought this lock to secure either my motorcycle or bicycle when I commute into work.  Upon receiving the package, I was stunned at the weight.  I had read other reviews stating as such, but this sucker really IS heavy.      After deciding the size/weight of the chain was simply too much for bicycle use, unless entering  a bicycle cage match battle to the death, I decided it would be dedicated to motorcycle use. Day one of commuting with it, I found the gargantuan chain was too bulky for my backpack. Leather jacket on, backpack on, sling the chain over my shoulder and ride off feeling quite like an extra from Road Warrior. After about 10 miles it was rather uncomfortable. \\"Not for wearing,\\" I thought, so no big deal. Day two, I placed it in a saddle bag. Much better.     The lock comes with 5 keys, one with a very bright LED light. The chain cover, a woven nylon, is of high quality and protects whatever you're locking from the chain.  Overall, I like the chain and lock for security, but the size/weight has been significant enough to make it less than convenient. I'm sure its more convenient than walking home because my motorcycle was   quickly thrown in the back of a truck, never to be seen again, though.

product_title: Body Glove Brilliant Recreational Diving Mask
review_headline: Broke in the 1st Hour of Use
review_body: I bought these goggles thinking I could trust Amazon, and that the brand was also reliable. What a disappointment! I barely got an hour of use out of them before the strap broke. It seems like there was a weak spot in the strap and it broke quite easily. DO NOT BUY!

product_title: 1 Liter Better Bottle
review_headline: I FINALLY have a favorite water bottle!!
review_body: I have tried many water bottles, trying to find one that would fit into the cup holder in the car, had a straw, and wouldn't allow air bubbles up through the straw while you were drinking.  The CamelBak does all of these and it doesn't spill.  I love this bottle so much that I purchased a second one and it wouldn't surprise me if I purchased more in the future.  I wash the entire bottle in the dishwasher on the top rack.  I remove the bite valve and the straw so that all pieces and parts get cleaned and sterilized.  I've owned the original bottle for about 3 months now and the 2nd bottle for 2 weeks and haven't had a single issue with either.

product_title: Stearns Watersports Vest (Barbie, Weight- 30-50 Lbs)
review_body: This is a great lifejacket. The sides are full and it has three buckles so it fits snug around the upper chest. This is slightly shorter than other lifejackets that are the 30 to 50 pound size so fits my girls really well.

product_title: Coleman Fuel Filler
review_body: When my Coleman stove arrived, it came with a funnel.  There was no need to purchase this additional funnel whose shipping charge was about the same as the cost of the funnel.

product_title: Grabber Performance Peel N Stick Body Warmer 1 Pack
review_headline: Great safe heat source & economically priced.
review_body: The products last, it's easy to use and much cheaper than other brands and styles.  I've used other name brand warmers and this one is by far superior in heat source and overall quality of product.  Great for back spasms or other body parts that are acting up and creaky.  The shape and size is compact, yet covers a good area without hindering movement.      The adhesive is strong and you can even remove it and put on a different garment, as I use them mainly for muscle spasm issues and can sleep with one, then remove the patch that is still quite warm and use it another 6 hrs. during the day.  You do need to be aware that it gets pretty warm, so adhere it to the clothing, not the skin, unless you're \\"tough\\" like another reviewer stated he uses it, but adhering it to your clothing helps eliminate any skin issues from constant contact, as when you move around, the pad on the clothing will heat up other areas and the surrounding air will help cool you off.    I'd like to know if the contents are organic and can be used in the garden, as iron may be beneficial to plants.  One less thing in the dump site.

product_title: Coleman 36 Quart Xtreme  5 Cooler
review_body: Very good... excellent cooling performance.    Great product... some might wish for wheels at this size for transportation, but was fine with me.

product_title: Coleman Pet Hibernation Sleeping Bag, Extra Large
review_body: I have 2 bags, a large for my Rhodesian Ridgeback bitch and xlarge for the male. We have tent camped in both extremes of temperature and the dogs use the bags in both. When it's cold they burrow in head first and stay that way all night. If it is warm they sleep with their heads out or we unzip it most of the way. As other reviews stated, the sleeping bags are well made and very warm. I highly recommend them!

product_title: Delta Cycle Delta Airzound Bike Horn , colors may vary
review_headline: BE HEARD, STAY ALIVE, A Commuters Savior
review_body: In a time of sound proof tank sized SUVs where drivers are usually fiddling with their GPS, texting, blasting their music or talking on their cellphones you need to be heard CLEARLY and QUICKLY before they run you over or side swipe you.    This horn can save your life. It has prevented many an accident from: drifting drivers who coast into the bike lane to jaywalking pedestrians with the their Ipods on full blast cutting out in front of me from behind parked cars when I have a green light!    Buy it. Use it.     It is removable too. This prevents theft and potential damage when you lock your bike up.    Beyond a  good helmet and lights for night riding this horn is next must have.    A commuter's best friend.

product_title: Kestrel Portable Tripod
review_headline: Kestrel makes good stuff but should leave tripods to the pros
review_body:
I'm with the other reviewer here. I looked over the kestrel accessories and bought their portable weather vane which needs a smallish tripod to hold it on the ground, or a large tripod if you are sheltered and want accurate wind data.

This is overpriced for its size. Small metal tripods cost less and have more features. And they hold the kestrel windvane fine.

Put your money into the windvane and you will get a better return - then find a tripod suited to your use. if you are on clear ground 30 cm - 1m is fine, but if you have buildings or fences, consider a 2-3 meter tripod because the winds up there are much stronger than down low. My permanent weather station is attached to the back of my security camera above my house - it has nothing blocking it just like the camera has no shadows.

Also keep in mind you can buy the tripod without a head if its just for the kestrel, since you want it level and thats it. Opteka makes a very nice 80 cm - 2.4 m tripod with a built in bubble level and magnetic compass in the \\"head\\" (but it remains level and has no handle) - it's meant to have a head attached and is built from super strong reinforced carbon fiber. with the compass you can check your kestrel's internal compass in \\"Magnetic\\" mode as opposed to \\"true\\" mode quite fast. If you just want to do level photography and weather data you don't need a head on the tripod section, but if you want pan and tilt functions, the head is manditory and adds weight. By itself the tripod weighed a KG at most and came with a protective bag that will hold you kestel sub-bags for data gathering and for windvane. It's in the products I've reviewed - look for a tripod by itself (no head attached) and ideal for this application.

Otherwise, small (1 foot) tripods are dirt cheap these days so a specialized version just for weather data is not a good investment when you can get kestrel's windvane version with the precision pivot for rotation and a cup to hold the tripod.

product_title: Sixsixone Mullet Skate Style Helmet
review_body: If you are tired of those aero helmets you see everyone on the trails with, this is perfect. It also gives my head the added protection down the back. Sixsixone's lifetime return policy is also a nice addition. Mail them back the helmet and $10 and they send you a new helmet. Can't ask for much more.     The helmet breathes well, though it is a little warmer than an aero helmet. When it comes down to it though, when I go flying off my bike I feel better with this on my head than one of those lightweight aero helmets.     Only comment I have is that it does take some adjustment to get the fit right, so take your time. It will feel weird out of the box with no adjustments. Get the right pads in (mix and match if needed) and get it cinched down properly.

product_title: Lezyne Metal Patch Kit
review_body: I had cleaned the surface and roughened it as well.  The patch did not stick well.  I will try it again with more time available.

product_title: Fox River Outdoor Thermal Heavyweight Mid-Calf Boot Wool Socks
review_body: Warm, comfortable and inexpensive! What can't you like?

product_title: Coleman Sundome Tent (10-Feet x 10-Feet)
review_body: I bought this tent to take on RAGBRAI in Iowa. It worked out fantastic! We used a large queen size air mattress and it fit easily plus had plenty of room left over on either side. It was also very east to put up. As someone who dosent use a tent very often, it went up and came down very fast and easily. It even fit back into the bag without much problem. One night we had a pretty bad wind/rain storm and the tent held up nicely. We didn't do any extra water proofing of the tent, just took it out of the bag and put it up. There was no rain inside the tent when we woke up in the morning and all was fine. There were many other people in our camp that weren't as lucky so I was very thankful. I will definitely recommend this tent to people in the future.

product_title: Bravo Sports 12 x 12 Quik Shade Weekender 144 Canopy
review_body: Purchased this canopy for my son's youth group. The company's website says it is good for camping, and we took it camping. The first day we had it up, it stormed for about 30 minutes, so we sought shelter in our cars. When we returned to our campsite, we discovered that the canopy had collapsed under the weight of rain that had pooled under the roof. At least two of the legs were severely bent and the metal had split. We reasoned that rain pools on the roof because there are no solid supports extending from the corners to the roof. We were able to perform a make-shift repair using lots of duck tape and our flag poles as splints, but it was destroyed when we took it down. Unfortunately, the company says I am not eligible for a warranty repair. BOTTOM LINE: DO NOT USE THIS CANOPY IF RAIN IS IN THE FORECAST. I recommend spending a little more money and getting an all weather canopy from another manufacturer.

product_title: Mountain Hardwear Monkey Woman™ Jacket
review_body: I love this jacket, I have two of them actually. That being said, I can't really wear them out in public anymore because after a couple of months of wearing it frequently, parts of the fuzz matt down and the damage is not fixable. It's just how the fabric wears. So I still wear them at home, but I don't really wear them out because the matted fuzz makes it look like you've been wearing the jacket for at least a week without taking it off once. It's a lot worse with the light colored ones, I have a black one and the matting is not as apparent.

product_title: Seattle Sports Paddlers Bilge Pump
review_body: works at a very good pace to empty the kayak also have used it to drain a small flower pond. great deal for the price.  dave in Pittsburgh pa.

product_title: Tech4o  Accelerator Women's Fitness - Watch (Carnation)
review_body: I purchased this watch in hopes that it would help with just going out and running without having to measure out a course. I have calabrated and recalabrated and recalabrated, but it does not seem to get the accuate measure for mileage or pace. Although, the \\"chono\\" is great for getting all my mile splits for races and already measured training courses. I really do like the watch. I can use it for more than just running. DO NOT purchase this product if you are wanting to get accurate measure of pace and distance.

product_title: Coleman SunDome 7-Foot by 7-Foot 3-Person Dome Tent (Orange/Gray)
review_headline: Good tent but not for cool weather
review_body: This is a good little tent for my husband and myself. We go camping in the mountains only a couple times a year. This time we went over Memorial Day, when it can still be chilly. Putting up the tent was easy and intuitive. We waterproofed the tent and everything stayed dry despite a couple hours of rain and hail. We were even able to get the tent back into the tent bag when we were done and took it down. My only complaint, and it is unfortunately a big one, is that you can't close all the windows in the tent. It has two large vents (screens) on the top half of the tent that cannot be sealed. That made for some very cold nights. I can also foresee some problems if there was a windy day in a dry area, as the rainfly barely covers those vents and dust/dirt particles could get in there. Unfortunately, our new tent will be replaced sooner than later due to those problems.

product_title: Pearl iZUMi Women's Quest Cycling Short,Black,X-Large
review_body: Comfortable fit, legs do not ride up. Like the longer length. Appear to be holding up well even after multiple washings.

product_title: Coleman Pheasant Dog Toy (Large)
review_body: My Dog loves it. Walks around with it in his mouth and pretends he is a mighty hunter. Of course the pheasant is as large as him so he can't figure out how to make it squeak though.

review_body: I have 6 grandsons, bought each one and they have enjoyed them more than I ever imagined.  Even their parents have taken a spin or two on them.  Friends visit the boys and begin to beg their parents for one!  Great fun and very durable!

product_title: Superlight 2 Oz Backpacking Shovel Trowel
review_body: Convenient & lightweight.  Great to bring backpacking or camping, or to use around the yard at home.

product_title: Cycleaware Viewpoint Eyewear Mirror, Round
review_body: I mainly ride at night, and use these with a pair of clear lensed glasses.  My wife rides with me, and behind me, and with these it is easy to tell if she is behind me or lagging behind.      To use, look left, and turn the head slightly.  I can see everything from directly behind me, even the right side of the road.  A quick glance can show me if head lights are coming up behind, and my wife's little headlight is easily seen.    The problem with these is the image is so small that it is impossible to tell how far back a car is.  The second problem is that, when turning left, the lack of trust makes me turn my head to actually look at the coming car, but the placement of the mirror is directly in the line of sight!  It blocks the view, so I have to turn even farther to see the traffic, which makes the bike hard to control. I'll even turn my head and body to the right to look behind me for a left hand turn.    All in all, the mirror gives an added level of awareness of what is going on behind the rider.  Since I ride at night (3 am) there usually isn't a car coming and I don't have issues with the blindspot.  I can't comment on these for daytime use.  I have 20/10 vision (for reference).

product_title: Bell Fraction Adult Multi-Sport Helmet
review_body: I ordered a small for my 5 year old son and it fits great.  After reading a few of the reviews I was nervous it would be too big but it ended up being perfect.  My son looks real \\"professional\\" and loves to wear his helmet.  Great purchase.

product_title: Sea Eagle 330 Inflatable Kayak with Deluxe Package
review_body: My wife and I enjoy being on water, but hadn't spent too much time kayaking in the past.  We decided on the 330 primarily for the small storage space needed, price, and strong reviews we've read.  In our opinion this boat more than delivers on our expectations.  In fact, we plan to buy another one so we can take our two daughters out at the same time.      The Pros  This boat is light, easy to blow up (<10 min), paddles are quick to assemble, seats are more than supportive, stable in water, easy to deflate and pack up (< 5 min), and very comfortable on the water.    The Cons  It is not a \\"professional\\" kayak.  It does not track as well, is on the smaller side for two people, is slightly awkward to paddle due to \\"pontoon\\" like sidewalls, and works much better with a passenger in front.    The foot pump that comes with the boat is more than adequate.  Before our first use, we bought a cheap electric air pump at Target ($14) that can plug into the car.  It is definitely not needed, but is a big help at getting the 330 blown up quickly.  We let that pump start the three chambers while we use the foot pump to blow up the chairs.  Once the chairs are blown up, we turn off the electric pump, and finish inflating the boat to optimal pressure with the foot pump.  All is done in well less than 10 minutes.      Because we wanted the 330 to get our family outside on weekends (and away from the tv), we have achieved our goal.  Our girls love being on the water, watching fish jump, seeing all the wildlife, and spending time together.  We can easily store the boat in our garage when not in use, and we did not break the bank to make it happen.  We would recommend to others looking for the same type of activity.

review_body: I actually bought this from a consignment shop for a far cheaper price, but in as new condition and I put the helmet on my infant and he was all smiles. I can see this is going to work just great for when I tow him behind my bike in his bike trailer once he turns a year old.    It is very cute too!

The moving from left to right is annoying but not something that would have prevented me from buying it.  It is built well and should last for as long as I ride. product_title: Park Tool PCS-4 Deluxe Home Mechanic Repair Stand
review_headline: Great stand for the do-it-yourself mechanic.
review_body: I checked out some of the less expensive bike repair stands in local stores and did not like the wobbly construction or the clamping mechanism. I also looked at the less expensive Park Tool model. It would work well, I am sure, but I noticed that the clamp on this model is nearly identical to the commercial model used in my local bike shop. Also, the legs--which fold together when not in use--offer a very stable footing when the bike is in place. The stability is further enhanced by the fact that the rubber end caps are eccentric, allowing you to adjust them individually to counter any irregularities or slope in the floor.    As with all the Park Tool products I have tried out, the Deluxe model is solidly designed and constructed and will doubtless outlast its original owner.

review_body: When I first saw a bike up the road that had the brightest rear flashing light I'd ever seen I had to chase them down and ask them about the light.  This is that light.     This is an extremely bright and visible rear light especially on dual flash mode.  I've used many different kinds of rear lights from several makers and previously preferred Bike Planet Superflash lights but this light is definitely brighter and better.   Run time seems to be pretty good which is impressive given the energy output.      I really like the flexible mouunt that comes with the light.  However I've also found out that this light will clip into a Superflash fixed mount and,  if you zip tie it, it will stay there.      With a Light and Motion 200 light up front and a couple of these behind (one bike mounted and the other on my helmet) if someone hits me it will not be because they didn't see me.

review_body: I needed a bike rack compatible with the spoiler on my honda accord and this does the job.  Because I'm concerned about the slightest scratches on my paint I still drape a towel over the spoiler first. product_title: Allen Sports Deluxe 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack
review_body: I drove over 1300 miles with my bike on this rack, on local roads and on freeways, at speeds of up to 70 mph, and had no issues whatsoever. It is a little nerve-wracking because it is so light and your bike tends to bounce a little while you're driving, but it is quite sturdy. I drive a hatchback, and the ropes were long enough for my car. It is pretty easy to assemble (I have no experience in assembling racks as my husband usually does it for me, but I was able to assemble and disassemble this rack with no problems). You do have to follow the instructions carefully though, including making sure the ropes are perfectly straight and taut. You also have to make sure to knot the three ropes that hold the rack to your car, per the knotting instructions included with the rack. I also knotted the ropes holding the bike to rack, and to prevent the wheels from spinning/bike from swinging and hitting my car, I used rope to secure the bike wheels to the rack. Once you get the hang of it, it only takes about 5 minutes to set up.

The body of the light has excellent craftsmanship but the on / off switch can be difficult to find and press if you wear riding gloves, etc.  Overall, I would recommend the product even with that one short coming.

product_title: CamelBak Men's RaceBak 72-Ounce Hydration Pack
review_headline: Kept me hydrated but at a painful price
review_body:
After hearing about how Camelbak packs tend to cause chafing on the neck and/or shoulders, I saw this and thought it was going to be perfect. Please read this if you are thinking about getting one, especially for running which is what I bought it for. I went on a long run today (14 miles in super humid weather) and although it kept me well hydrated, it caused a bit of chafing at the top of my back just below the shoulders. The chafing appears to have been caused by the movement of the straw even though it's on the outside of the Racebak. I noticed it only 3-4 miles into the run and had to keep adjusting the shirt but after awhile and a ton of sweating, I stopped noticing it. When I got home, I looked in the mirror and I had been rubbed raw - it was about the size of a nickel. Needless to say it stung a little. So, fail #1.

I bought a medium which they say is for chest size 38-41\\". I'm 5'9\\" and 155 lb. I wear a 38\\" suit jacket and since this material is supposed to be stretchy anyway, I thought it wouldn't be a problem but it was super tight fitting. It was so tight fitting that it was practically impossible to put on, nevermind WITH a full reservoir inserted. It's also very difficult to take off. The only way to take it off without ripping it is to pull the bottom of the shirt up and off yourself first (instead of grabbing it by the neck and removing that first). It also looks pretty weird - makes me look like a hunchback. Probably should've realized that before buying it. They say this is supposed to be a base layer (i.e. you wear something over it). GOOD LUCK. You think you look weird wearing a fully loaded Racebak? You look much worse when wearing something over it. I tried putting my running sleeveless shirt over it and took it off right away. It's bad enough looking like a hunchback but at least without anything over the Racebak, people can tell you're wearing one. If you put something over it, you just look like a monster. Fail #2.

So if I can't put anything OVER it, how would I stay hydrated in the winter time? It's so tight fitting, I can't possibly put anything underneath it. I can't think of any way to use this in the winter time when running outdoors. Fail #3.

Someone I work with said it looks like \\"The Bro\\" from Seinfeld. Fail #4.

Because it's not a backpack, it has no storage. All fuel belts provide some form of storage. My Nathan belt allows me to store my ID, keys, gel packs, etc. Fail #5.

The straw, when threaded through both of the shoulder loops, kept bouncing and hitting me in the chest. At first I thought I could deal with it but after only a mile, it felt like I was being water boarded on the chest. I took it out of the front loop and threw the straw across my back which worked fine. One time though, I threw it across my back but it kept swinging back up front. Eventually it stayed. Fail #6.

Towards the end of my run, the water level was getting low and I guess when that happens, you have to suck for a little bit to get the water into the straw and into your mouth. This can REALLY ruin your rhythm when you're running especially your breathing if you have to struggle to get your drink. I got pretty good at sucking while breathing through my nose though. Fail #7.

Overall, it didn't exactly turn out to be a great investment and because I got chafed despite Camelbak advertisting the shirt as anti-chafing, I think I'm going to contact them to at least get a credit towards a hydration pack or something else. The reason why I wanted something wearable (either a backpack of Racebak) was because my hydration belt doesn't fit well and it chafes my hips. So the search continues for the perfect tool for staying hydrated during my long runs

=========================
UPDATED
=========================

Well, I did contact someone at Camelbak and Liz from the warranty servicesdepartment was able to hook me up with an Octane XCT hydration pack. I know it won't do me much good using it to run but at least I can use this for hiking and biking (without looking like a weirdo). Thanks Camelbak for taking the time to read my message and responding. Stay tuned for my Amazon review of the Camelbak Octane XCT hydration pack!w it won't do me much good using it to run but at least I can use this for hiking and biking (without looking like a weirdo). Thanks Camelbak for taking the time to read my message and responding. Stay tuned for my Amazon review of the Camelbak Octane XCT hydration pack!

product_title: iBert Safe-T Front Mounted Child Bicycle Seat
review_body: My son is now 2 1/2 and he loves this seat. I highly recommend it. Plus the installation was a cinch. Well worth the price.

product_title: TRANGIA 28-T Mini Trangia
review_body: I purchased this stove for a solo bike tour I took because it was small. I was very impressed with its capabilities and size. Plus the entire kit nests into the pot. Does not work very good with Iso-Alcohol as I tested and rarely would a flame burn longer than a minute. Methyl Alcohol is ideal but I decided to try using Heet (a gas line anti-freeze) based on some suggestions I read online. It worked fantastic and was a bit more convenient than purchasing a vat of Methyl Alcohol. This setup also comes with the simmer ring which give you a little control of the output and can also be used to extinguish the stove. At first I thought the pot holder would be flimsy but it is more than adequate.

product_title: Therm-a-Rest Compack Chair
review_body: I had been using the older version of this chair for about 15 years and I would not consider backpacking without it. It's just too light to be a weigh weenie about considering leaving it home because of the invaluable comfort you get from it. When I upgraded my camp chair to the new ultra light version I also upgraded my sleeping pad from a foam pad to the full length ProLite, (I had to make up for the weight savings from my old chair). The highly rounded edges on the ProLite make setting up the chair a breeze, and it's super comfortable once set up. My wife has the ProLite Plus which is a bit thicker and the edges are not as rounded and setting up the chair requires that you pay attention while you do it or you will get in a fight with your camp chair.    The very first day I used my chair an over zealous fire tender (there's one in every crowd) accidentally tossed a coal that bounced onto my chair. The bad news is it burnt a hole in my chair, the good news is it didn't burn my new thermarest. I've used the chair about 15 times with the centimeter sized hole in it and it has not been an issue. I'll patch it once it's too hot to camp.    Buy this chair, you will be happy you did, or buy two and carry both, then sell it to a jealous campmate at an inflated price as you lounge comfortably after a long hike.

product_title: CatEye Compact Safety Light Bicycle Rear Safety Light SL-LD100-R
review_body: With the unique fastener you can attach this light to almost anything. Easy to put on, easy to release.

product_title: Osprey Resource Veer Shoulder Bag
review_body: I'm using this for a Nikon SLR camera and a couple of lenses. It's perfect for events. If you're worried about padding, there's space to add it, but personally, my padded camera bag always ended up in a corner at events. This bag allows me to tote around a couple of extra lenses, flash, batteries, etc while using my camera. The only issue I have is that the strap is made for right handed people. It's made to wear across your left shoulder, but I wear it across my right - which means the little strap pocket is behind my back, and the buckle is in my side. As long as the strap isn't tight-this seems to work fine, and obviously won't be an issue at all for most people.

product_title: Balance Buddy (Adjustable)
review_body: I was developing back pain by running behind my 4 yr old holding the seat - as he learnt to control the bike's handle - due to the awkward bent over postion. This product is the perfect remedy. It takes about 2 minutes to install - takes away all the bending and helps the child's confidence (fear of toppling is not there). My son is now riding by himself within 3 days of using this!

review_body: I paid approximately $13 for 2 Pepper Sprays and $10 for Shipping & Handling for the ever so reliable USPS. I waited over a week and never received the items.  I went to Amazon's website to track the package and found out the USPS mailed it to the wrong address.  I had a difficult time in reaching the vendor and thus I gave up on the purchase.  I learned my lesson and I will never shop from Amazon again.  I am quite certain that this situation has occurred to countless others.    Julio P.    Brooklyn, NY

product_title: Super Bright XT Flashlight
review_headline: There are better products out there...
review_body: I got this as a gag gift from a friend.  It looked way cool.  But...    1. It has no batteries, just a dynamo generator.  That means you have to crank this thing if you want light from the flashlight.  If you stop, the light goes out.    2. This is meant as an emergency device not as an alternate way to charge your phone.  It does not produce a lot of power so it will take you hours, and when I say hours I mean upwards of 8 hours, of constant cranking to charge your phone fully.  I got tired after a couple of minutes.    3. There are better products out there. For about 20-30 bucks more I've seen ones that have a light, radio, cell phone adapter, and even solar panels to help charge.  Much more useful as an emergency tool than this...

product_title: Blackburn Camber CF Bottle Cage
review_body: Very well made bottle cage. Holds bottles very secure but not too tight.  Bottle go in and come out well, and i have no fear of a bottle coming out.     looks great and works awesome.

product_title: OnGuard 5017LPT Beast Chain Bicycle Lock (140cm x 12mm)
review_body: I use this lock on my 2009 Vespa LX150 and it works great.  The lock works on my Vespa by sliding the steel bar through the rear wheel and then locking the T-head to the end of the steel bar.  The lock through the rear wheel alone might be enough to deter theft, but it's probably better to first wrap the chain around a solid object.    The lock is easy to use, although it is quite heavy and sometimes I wish the chain was longer.  Of course, a longer chain would be even heavier, so the chain length is probably a good compromise between functionality and weight.    As far as I know, no one has tried breaking the chain or the lock to steel my Vespa, so I can't testify to the product's resistance to a determined thief.  I'd prefer to never find out.

product_title: Origin8 Pro Uno-S Saddle
review_body:
The saddle is very pretty, but of all the saddles that I have (about 15), this one is the most uncomfortable by a great margin; in fact, it almost feels defective. The discomfort is not within the normal \\"like-dislike\\" range - the saddle is generally unusable. Granted, saddles are subject to very personal preferences, and I wouldn't base so categorical an opinion on my own experience alone; however, several other experienced riders who tried to ride the bike returned with the same puzzled look: \\"there HAS to be something wrong with the saddle...\\".
The nexus of the problem is somewhere in the midsection, where the saddle narrows very sharply and loses all support - it sort of \\"hammocks\\" under you. I might try to inject some foam under the shell, perhaps this helps - I like the look of the saddle a lot, and would like to be able to use it, but I really can't.
